- `ReviewService` takes `onDecided`, called after a final verdict (allow or deny, by an agent reviewer or the owner) with the request, the task, who decided, the tool and the reason; an escalation or a request for context is not reported. `startController` records it as an `approval` step on the task (with a reference to the review), written by a service identity with no grants, under a command ID derived from the request and verdict so a repeat records once. A failure never changes the verdict. Test in `review/routing.test.ts` on all four backends.
- Not done (C09f stays planned): message and artifact-version steps, chat access, the explanation index.

## C09f (second part): messages are steps in the task's activity (2026-10-29)
- `AgentMessageService` takes `onSent`, called once a message is accepted (a replay calls it again with the same message ID): `startController` records an `owner-message` or `agent-message` step on the task with who sent it, to whom, its class and purpose and a reference to the message, never its text, under the command ID `msg-act:<message>` so it is recorded once. A failure never changes the message. Test in `api/start-message.test.ts`.
- Not done (C09f stays planned): artifact-version steps, chat access, the explanation index.

## K01f (first part): the SQLite snapshot copy runs on a worker thread (2026-10-29)
- `SqliteStorage.snapshot()` now copies the database with `VACUUM INTO` on a worker thread (`snapshot-worker.ts`) that opens its own read-only connection, so a backup of a large database no longer stops the controller's event loop (it used to run on the main thread). The copy is as consistent as before (a WAL reader sees the database as of the start of its read). A failure of the copy is reported as an unavailable store. `SqliteStorage.vacuumInto` (the direct call) is unchanged. Test in `storage/sqlite/snapshot-columns.test.ts` (the loop turns while the copy is still being made); the existing snapshot, backup and restore tests pass unchanged.
- Not done (K01f stays planned): Pi native state, the maintenance barrier, a restore entry for the owner, the back-up-now chat command.

## H13d (first part): the dispatcher polls the event sources it is given (2026-10-29)
- `sourceLoops` is a dispatcher loop (`events.sources`) that runs `SourceService.run` over the sources given in `startController({ eventSources })`, once per tick, as the dispatcher; a source that fails is named after the rest so the loop shows as failing. No source is built in and none is created by default (the sources reach out to services, so only the ones the caller chooses are polled); without any there is no loop. Test in `dispatch/loops.test.ts`.
- Not done (H13d stays planned): choosing which sources a real installation runs and where they are configured, and the owner's chat command. `verifyAtResume` is already used by the checked resume's dependency check (L04), so it needs no separate call here.

## K01f (second part): a command line for backups (2026-10-29)
- `node packages/controller/dist/backup/cli-main.js list <folder>`, `verify <backup>` and `restore <backup> (--sqlite <file> | --postgres <url> [--schema s]) [--artifacts <dir>]`: the owner can check a backup and restore it into a new, empty database on a new machine from the backup alone. It prints how many rows and artifact files came back, how many outside actions are marked uncertain and how many messages will be sent again, and refuses a used database, a backup with files and no artifact folder, a damaged backup and arguments it does not understand (exit 0 done, 1 refused, 2 not understood). It never opens the database a controller is running on. The logic is `runBackupCli` in `backup/cli.ts` (test `backup/cli.test.ts`).
- Not done (K01f stays planned): Pi native state, the maintenance barrier across stores, an owner restore from inside the running controller.

## Batch 5 review fixes (2026-10-29)
- **Stop with a dispatcher no longer blocks on jobs:** the stop's job inventory read jobs as the dispatcher, which holds no job rights, so every graceful stop, suspend and hand-off would have been blocked ("cleanup could not run"). It now uses `JobService.unfinishedOf(taskId)`, the controller reading its own records (not offered through the API), which also reads every page, not only the first 100. Test in `jobs/jobs.test.ts`.
- **Hand-off re-check:** skipped when the task has already moved to the new owner (the hand-off is then finished, not failed); only `forbidden` and `not_found` count as "no right", any other error leaves the hand-off for the next sweep.
- **Route probes:** `intervalMs` must be a whole number of at least 1000 ms; a probe that takes over 30 s counts as failed so it cannot stall the tick.
- Left as is: the summary of an activity step is cut before redaction (the inputs are validated and bounded upstream); `backup restore` opens its target with the ordinary open, so it must be pointed at a new database (the usage says so).

## K01g (first part): an unreadable backups folder is a failed run (2026-10-29)
- The nightly run used to throw (and be dropped) when the backups folder could not be listed. It now records the failure in the backup status (`lastError`), is not retried until the retry wait has passed, and `status` shows the folder as empty with the reason instead of failing. Test in `backup/backup.test.ts`.

## M04d (first part): the quick-answer period of a meeting is announced (2026-10-29)
- Owner decision (answers to the M02d/M03d/M04d design questions, memory `owner-decision-meeting-wake`): a meeting is a context switch for quick answers, with the agent's desk and tools but no long-running work; the agent is warned ahead, when the period begins and when it ends; a Stopped agent attends only if the owner asked for that exception beforehand (already the case: only `attendance.wake`, owner-only and per meeting, lets one in), and the owner can ask in chat because `attendance.wake` is a state-API operation.
- `AttendanceService` takes a `WindowSink`: `ahead` is sent when the agent is asked to prepare (filed against the first task it leaves), `begins` when it joins (against its meeting task; a repeat of a cut-off join sends it again under the same key) and `ends` when it is returned to its work (against the first task it returns to, or the meeting task). `meetingWindowSink` files each as a controller notice with the command ID `mtw:<attendance>:<phase>`, so each is filed once; a failure is dropped and changes nothing. Composed in `dispatch-compose.ts`. Tests: `meetings/attendance.test.ts` (all phases, once each) and `meetings/notice-sink.test.ts`.
- Not done (M04d stays planned): the controller enforcing "no long-running work" during the period in dispatch and tool admission (today the agent is only told), a wake sink that makes a Stopped agent reachable after the owner's exception, and chat wording.

## M03d (first part): stand-up decisions on improvements reach the proposer (2026-10-29)
- Owner decision (memory `owner-principle-llm-decides-then-codify`, question 2): an outcome with a task of its own is filed there; one without is not filed on an unrelated task but stays pending for the proposer's next stand-up brief.
- `OutcomeNotice` now carries the `taskId` of an accepted or adopted improvement, and `OutcomeSink.deliver` may return `false` for "not filed": the improvement (and the agenda outcome) then stays `returnPending` and is listed as waiting, not marked told. `improvementOutcomeSink` files the notice with `noticeFromController` (command ID `imo:<key>`, so once). The dispatcher has a new loop `improvements.outcomes` that delivers per project. Tests: `standups/outcome-sink.test.ts`, the improvement suite in `standups/standups.test.ts` (the task is named; a refusing sink leaves it waiting).
- Not done (M03d stays planned): putting the still-pending outcomes into the agent's next brief (the facts for briefs do not read improvements yet), showing the owner outcomes still untold after some days, agenda outcomes to chat turns and inquiries, the notice/allocation/usage/owner-item sinks, chat commands.

## M03d (second part): untold improvement decisions are in the proposer's brief (2026-10-29)
- The stand-up brief of an agent now carries, under "advice", a line for each decision on its improvement proposal (or one grouped under it) that it has not been told, with the proposal as its citation; it is dropped from the brief once the proposal is marked told (delivered by notice on its task). A brief is not rewritten once its meeting has started, as before. Test in `standups/standups.test.ts`.
- Not done (M03d stays planned): showing the owner outcomes still untold after some days, agenda outcomes to chat turns and inquiries, the notice/allocation/usage/owner-item sinks, chat commands.

## M02d (first part): a meeting may decide a widening change, which waits for the owner unless the policy lets it through (2026-10-29)
- Owner decision (design question 3 and the principle in memory `owner-principle-llm-decides-then-codify`): decide by the installation's approval profile, with a specific setting overriding it. `PolicyService.classMode(project, class)` gives the policy's answer for a class of action (the profile's cell for the project's environment tier, with any override). A `ChangeApplier` can now say `widens: "access-change" | "spend"`; such a kind is allowed in a motion (it no longer falls under the "never decided by a vote" list), and an adopted decision carrying one is `pending` for the owner whether or not the owner is in the room, unless `widening(class, project)` says `allow` (`startController` binds it to `classMode`: strict asks for both; autonomous lets spend through and still asks for rights; an override of `spend.<tier>` or `access-change.<tier>` wins either way). The owner's agreement (`ownerRespond`) is what carries a pending decision out. At apply, a change that is not agreed is refused if the policy has tightened since the vote. Tests: `meetings/record.test.ts` (waits, agreed, allowed, tightened), `policy/policy.test.ts` (`classMode`).
- Not done (M02d stays planned): the appliers themselves (no kind with `widens` is registered, so nothing changes in production yet): a grant, a budget raise and an ownership change (an ownership change is a widening unless the new holder already has the rights the task needs; narrowing changes apply under the carrier's right); recording every decision and its outcome so safe patterns can be found after production; the steward agent for decisions no coded rule covers; the narrator and chat commands.

## Batch 6 review fixes (2026-10-29)
- **Outcome delivery no longer stalls:** `improvementOutcomeSink` treats a notice that cannot be filed (proposer cannot read the task, inactive, inbox full) as "not filed" instead of throwing, and the `improvements.outcomes` loop catches per project and names the failures after the rest. (The older agenda-outcome delivery still throws on a failing sink, as its test expects.)
- **Decisions told only in the brief leave the pending list:** `ImprovementService.markTold` (service principals only) and `StandupService`'s `onBriefed`: once a stored brief carries a decision and every proposer it concerns has it in their brief, the proposal is marked told, so rejected, deferred and stopped proposals (which have no task for a notice) no longer fill the 200-item open list. A decision whose proposer is not in the stand-up stays pending.
- **Widening gate:** `classMode` also says whether the cell was set by hand. The engine keeps a change of rights the owner's decision whatever the profile says, so a vote widens rights without the owner only where the owner set that cell by hand; spend follows the profile (strict asks; derived and autonomous let it through in development). The comment that said otherwise is corrected.
- **"Meeting over" warning** goes to the meeting task, not to a task the agent may have kept paused or handed on.

## M04e (part 1): no long-running work during a meeting

- `JobOptions.longRunningGate(principal, taskId)` returns a reason to refuse or `undefined`. `JobService.admit` asks it only for background jobs and jobs the caller marks `longRunning: true`, on the first admit (a repeat is answered from its record). Short work is never asked about.
- `AttendanceService.meetingOfTask(taskId, agent)` answers with the meeting when `taskId` is that agent's bounded meeting task and the agent is present (not left) in a still-planned occurrence.
- `api/start.ts` binds the two: an agent principal on its meeting task cannot start long-running work until the meeting ends. Its other tasks are paused already, and a permitted background job there is unchanged.
- A stopped or suspended agent is held by a pause gate whose observed state is `stopped` or `suspended`, so the room already treats it as paused: it stays out unless the owner invited it by hand ahead of time (the exception), then attends its meeting task only, its other work stays held, and it is back to stopped when the meeting ends. A test pins this for a stopped agent.
- `meeting.invite-direct` (owner only) is the state-API operation for that request, so the chat reaches it. An agent the host's own availability hook reports stopped is still not woken by it; that is `meeting.attend.wake`.
- Not built yet (remains in M04e): chat wording that explains the exception to the owner, and a wake sink for agents the host reports stopped.

## M03e (part 1): the owner is shown decisions that went untold

- `ImprovementService.untold(by, projectId, olderThanMs)` (service principals only) lists decisions still `returnPending` whose last decision is at least that old, with the revision decided at.
- `untoldImprovementLoops` (dispatcher loop `improvements.untold`, 7 days by default) hands each to a `tell` callback keyed `imu:<item>:<revision>`, so the owner is told once per decision; one project's failure is named after the rest. The composed controller files it as a `maintenance` notification (detail cut to the 200-character limit, the title to 60) on the improvement record.
- Not built yet (remains in M03e): agenda outcomes to chat turns and inquiries, the notice/allocation/usage/owner-item sinks, and chat commands.

## L03e (part 1): temporary reassignment with automatic return

- `handoff.prepare` takes `returnAt` (a time ahead, within 30 days). It is kept on the hand-off; nothing changes until the hand-off is completed as before.
- The hand-off sweep (the dispatcher's `handoffs.sweep` loop) does two new things. A transferred hand-off whose `returnAt` has passed and that has no `returned` mark gets a hand-off back to the first owner, made **as the one who asked** and only if that principal is still active and still holds the right to control the task (the owner's rule for anything done later on someone's behalf); the hand-off back is marked `autoComplete`. A ready hand-off with `autoComplete` is completed on the next pass for the same asker, with gaps in the package accepted (recorded as for any hand-off).
- The return is given up, with the reason on the original hand-off's `returned.skipped` and in the task's activity (`onReturnGivenUp`), when the asker is gone or lost the right, or the task is no longer with the temporary owner (moved, done). A hand-off back that cannot be made yet (another hand-off in progress, the first owner ineligible) is retried on the next sweep and shows in `failed`.
- A crash between making the hand-off back and writing the mark is found again by its command ID (`ret-<hand-off id>`).
- Not built yet (remains in L03e): chat commands, package sections from continuation, locks, drafts, responsibilities.

## U12d (part 1): the stand-up brief says that messages are waiting

- `AgentMessageService.waitingAtStandup(by, agent)` (service principals only) counts the informational and advice messages queued for an agent; it reads and delivers nothing.
- `StandupOptions.waitingMessages` (bound in the composed controller) adds an advice line to each participant's brief: "N message(s) are waiting for you. Read them at this stand-up (boundary stand-up, this meeting)." The agent reads and confirms them itself (`message.readable` / `message.acknowledge` with the meeting), so delivery is still recorded as the recipient's own confirmation. A count that fails leaves the line out; the brief is rewritten when the count changes (until the meeting starts).
- Not built yet (remains in U12d): the chat presentation of owner questions.

## H13e (part 1): a built-in event source

- A controller started without `eventSources` now polls `defaultEventSources` (`api/default-sources.ts`): a task-completion source over the real task records, reporting tasks seen done or cancelled in the last 7 days once each on `project:<id>`, scanning at most 5000 tasks per poll. Passing `eventSources: []` turns it off; passing a list replaces it.
- Older closed tasks are never reported, which also bounds what the source remembers. A watcher subscribed to a project stream for `task.completed` / `task.cancelled` is now woken by the record itself.
- Not built yet (remains in H13e): other real sources (repositories, files, service health, timers from the owner's settings), choosing them in settings, and the owner's chat command.

## C09g (part 1): artifact versions appear in the task's activity record

- `ArtifactService` takes `onPublished` (option `ArtifactOptions`): told after an artifact that names a task has been recorded, with its id, name, task, project and file count. A repeated publish tells again; the host's key (`artv:<artifact>`) makes the step appear once. A failing hook never undoes the publication.
- The composed dispatcher's remote-worker artifact service records an `artifact-version` step ("Recorded artifact <name> (<n> files)") citing the artifact, so every artifact a remote worker publishes for a task shows in its activity.
- Not built yet (remains in C09g): artifact steps for local workers' outputs, chat access to the activity record, the per-task explanation index.

## Batch 7 review fixes

- **Built-in event source (H13e).** It was keeping every closed task it had ever seen, always read the first 5000 tasks, and reported everything closed in the last week on its first poll. Now: the first full pass only records what is closed (a baseline); a cursor in the source state makes successive polls read the whole store in turns; the state keeps only tasks closed in the last week (each with its closing time), dropping the rest at every poll; signals past the poll's limit are found again by the next poll (the page is re-read), not skipped.
- **Temporary reassignment (L03e).** A hand-off with `returnAt` is refused by a service that cannot look the asker up later (no return with owner power). The return is made only if the task is still where that hand-off put it (generation +1), so a task that was moved on and came back by other hand-offs is not pulled away. A return that was made but never given its suspension (a crash between the two) is finished by the next sweep. The first owner being ineligible gives the return up with the reason; a blocked or failed hand-off back is told to the task's activity once (`onReturnGivenUp`); other refusals (another hand-off in progress) are retried and show in `failed`.
- Doc comments that had been separated from the members they describe (`onUsage`, `#activeAgents`) were put back.
- Left as it is, by design: the meeting gate asks only for work marked long-running or background (the caller declares it), and background work on the agent's other, paused tasks stays permitted as before (a permitted background job is the safe long-running operation the meeting rules allow). The stand-up brief's waiting-message count is part of the digest, so it is rewritten when the count changes until the meeting starts, then frozen.

### Batch 7 second-pass fixes

- The built-in source keeps at most 2000 closed tasks in its state (the most recently closed), because a state record is limited to 256 KiB; its dedup key now carries the closing time, so a task closed again is a new event.
- A hand-off back left without its suspension by a crash is finished from its own record (`returnOf` names the reassignment it undoes) by whichever sweep path reaches it first; if the first owner cannot take the task, it ends failed and the task's activity says so. A failed return is told once (not twice), and a return that is blocked again later is told again (`stuckTold` is the history length at which it was told).

## M03f (part 1): agenda outcomes go back to where the topic came from

- `chatTurnFollowUps` (`chat/follow-ups.ts`) puts a keyed follow-up on a chat turn (`TurnBody.followUps`, latest 20 kept, text cut at 1000); the same key twice changes nothing; a turn that is gone reports not delivered.
- `agendaOutcomeSink` (`standups/outcome-sink.ts`) delivers a stand-up's agenda outcome: for a topic that came from a chat turn, as a follow-up on that turn; for an inquiry, as a controller notice to the agent that asked, on the inquiry's task. Anything that cannot be put back stays waiting (not marked returned) and is tried again.
- The composed controller now gives the stand-up service this sink, so outcomes reach the conversations they came from in the running controller (before, no sink was composed and they waited).
- Not built yet (remains in M03f): the notice/allocation/usage/owner-item sinks, the chat commands, and showing follow-ups in the chat's own listing of turns.

## U12e (part 1): the owner sees and answers agents' questions in chat

- `StatusService` has a new view `owner_questions` (owner only; any other caller, or an installation with no question source, gets nothing): one plain line per waiting question, oldest first, naming the asker, the task and project, the time, the question in quotes (an agent's words, shown as its words) and the wait its answer ends with its due time; each line cites the inquiry and the task. More than the limit (default 10, at most 50) adds a line saying so. It reads only; the composed controller passes the message service in.
- Chat command `owner.answer` (mode apply): the answer must be in the owner's own message like any text. The question is named by words that appear in it, its task title or its asker (`questionTopic`); when only one question waits no name is needed; several matches ask which, none is refused. Quoted material cannot answer.
- Not built yet (remains in U12e): the Needs-you grouping and urgency of questions in the chat's own greeting, and answering several questions in one message by question.

## M04f (part 1): the owner asks in chat for the stopped-agent meeting exception

- Chat command `meeting.invite-direct` (mode profile: an explicit order applies where the profile lets rights widen and is shown first in the strict one). The meeting is named by words in its title (`meetingTopic`; the project in focus; one planned meeting needs no name, several ask) and the agent by its name (`agentName`, exactly one active agent); both are resolved from the records, and an id typed or guessed by the model that is not in the owner's message is not accepted. Unknown names are refused.
- Not built yet (remains in M04f): the wake path for agents the host's availability hook reports stopped (they stay out of the meeting unless the owner made the exception), and the chat's explanation of what the exception does when it is shown first.

## L03f (part 1): hand-offs by chat

- New read `handoff.for-task` (`HandoffService.forTask`): the hand-off of a task that is still going, for a caller who may control the task; `not_found` when none.
- Chat commands `handoff.prepare` (applies at once: it suspends the task at a checkpoint and moves nothing), `handoff.complete` (follows the profile: it moves the task), `handoff.cancel` (applies: the old owner keeps the task) and `handoff.takeover` (always shown first: it force-stops). The task is named by its title, the recipient by the agent's name (`toAgentName`, exactly one active agent, resolved to its agent ID); complete and cancel find the hand-off as the one going on for the named task, and refuse when none is. The reason must be in the owner's own words; `returnAt` is a time the assistant works out from the owner's words and is shown back with the reply.
- Not built yet (remains in L03f): richer package sections from continuation, locks and drafts in the package, chat wording of a blocked hand-off's choices (`handoff.choose`).

## H13f (part 1): watches by chat

- Chat command `watch.create` (follows the profile: matching events wake the task's owner and spend work). The task whose owner is told is named by its title; the stream defaults to that task's own, another task's stream is named by its title (`watchedTaskTitle`, exactly one task of the project; several of the same title ask). A stream the model typed itself is not accepted unless the owner's message holds it.
- Not built yet (remains in H13f): other real sources (repository, file, service health), choosing sources in settings, cancelling a watch by words (`watch.list` returns only IDs, so there is nothing to name one by yet).

## C09h (part 1): chat access to a task's activity

- `StatusService` view `activity` (`{ kind: "activity", taskId, latest?, after?, limit? }`): a task's recorded steps in plain lines, in order from `after` (default the start, 20 at a time, at most 50) or, with `latest`, the last few (reads up to 1000 steps back). Each line gives the step number, time, actor, kind and summary (an agent's words, shown as such) and how many corrections it has; a step in an unavailable range says so; more steps add a line naming where to continue. Only summaries are shown; stored content (the part that needs a history right) is never quoted. A task the caller may not read reads as missing; without an activity source the view is not offered.
- In chat the task is named by its title in the project in focus (`taskTitle`); no match or several matches are refused with the reason.
- Not built yet (remains in C09h): artifact steps for local workers, the per-task explanation index.

### Batch 8 review fixes

- A return time (`returnAt`) on a hand-off, and `acceptGaps` on completing one, are authority fields: shown first in every profile. Completing a hand-off needs a word for the move naming the task in the owner's own sentence (as a transfer does); cancelling likewise.
- The questions the chat asks to tell two records apart (owner questions, meetings, watched tasks) now carry their answers, and the name the model gave is dropped when one is chosen, so the choice can be carried on. An ID given directly is checked against the waiting questions, the project's planned meetings, or the project's tasks.
- An answer to an owner's question with no word naming the question is shown first, with the question it would answer; asker IDs are no longer matched as words.
- A stand-up outcome for an inquiry whose asker can never be told (not an agent, retired, not allowed to read the task) is closed instead of retried for ever.
- Known, not fixed: the activity view with `latest` reads forward from the start (up to 1000 steps) and does not say when it cut off at that limit; its lines cite the task only.
- Second pass: an answer to an owner's question is shown first unless the owner's words name the question with a word of 4 or more letters; an ID given directly or carried on from a chosen option is shown first too. An outcome whose notice is refused by rights stays waiting (a grant can come back); only a missing task or unacceptable text closes it. Completing or cancelling a hand-off given only by its hand-off ID is always shown first (conservative).

## U12e (part 2): the count of waiting questions in every chat reply

- `ChatDeps.waiting` (composed from the owner's question list, at most 50 counted): every chat reply ends with "N questions from agents are waiting for your answer. Ask what is waiting to see them." when there are any. It is counted live (a replayed turn shows the count at replay time), and a failure to count adds nothing. This is the chat's part of the "Needs you" count; levels and escalation remain U11b.

### C09h: the activity view reads only the last steps (batch 8 review finding)

- `ActivityService.steps` takes `tail: true`: the last `limit` steps, without reading the earlier ones. The `latest` view of a task's activity uses it, so a long record costs the same as a short one and is never cut off silently.

## C09h (part 2): the explanation index in chat

- `StatusService` view `explanations` (`{ kind: "explanations", taskId, seq?, limit? }`, default 5, at most 20, newest first): what an agent chose, what else it considered and why not, the evidence and what is uncertain, with how it was written (at the time; or afterwards, from the records, and whether the records could explain it). An agent's words are shown as its words; an unreadable task reads as missing. In chat the task is named by its title.
- Not built yet (remains in C09h): artifact steps for local workers.

## M03f (part 2): the open agenda in chat

- `StatusService` view `agenda` (`{ kind: "agenda", projectId, limit? }`, default 10, at most 50; the project in focus when none is named): the project's open topics in the order the stand-up takes them, each with its urgency, kind of request and state, who asked, the question, the outcome asked for and the timebox; words that came from others are shown as theirs. A project the caller may not read, or an installation with no meeting source, gives nothing.

## M04f (part 2): planned meetings and their rosters in chat

- `StatusService` view `meetings` (`{ kind: "meetings", projectId, limit? }`, the project in focus when none is named): the project's planned meetings, soonest first, each with its title, kind, time, how it is held and the roster with each member's placing (status and availability, so a paused or stopped agent is visible before the owner decides on the exception). A project the caller may not read gives nothing.

## L03f (part 2): the hand-off going on for a task in chat

- `StatusService` view `handoff` (`{ kind: "handoff", taskId }`, the task named by its title in chat): from whom to whom, its mode and phase, why and who asked, when a temporary one returns, whether the package is complete and what it lacks, gaps accepted, what holds it up and the choices, and a failure. A task with no hand-off going gets a plain line; a task the caller may not control or read gets nothing.

### Batch 9 review fixes

- `HandoffService.forTask` checks the right to control the task before looking for a hand-off, so a caller without it learns nothing (before, it could tell "none going" from "refused").
- The `meetings` and `agenda` views give the owner nothing for a project that does not exist (as the other views do). A chat status request carrying both a task ID and a title, or a title that is not text, drops the title.
- Known, not fixed: the explanation reader loads every explanation record of the installation before applying its limit (cost grows with the installation); `explanations` follows the activity service's own read rule for host principals.

## L03g (part 1): the package takes what the run knows from the continuation

- `controllerHandoffSources` fills `nextAction`, `unfinishedWork`, `completedWork`, `backgroundOperations`, `risks` and `versions` from the task's latest complete continuation: the next step as written, the pending effects (with "none pending at the last checkpoint" said as a fact about the checkpoint, not as "nothing is left"), the decisions and artifacts, the tools whose effects a resume does not reproduce, and the runtime, routing and environment revisions; each says which continuation it is from. The task's own contract wins where it has the section (versions and risks are joined); a source given by the caller has the last word; with no continuation nothing is added and the required sections are reported missing as before. The existing redaction and length limits apply.
- Remaining in L03g: locks, drafts and responsibilities in the package.

### Activity summaries are redacted before they are cut (a known gap since C09)

- `ActivityService.record` takes a summary of up to 4000 characters, redacts all of it, and only then keeps the first 300; a secret that straddles the cut is no longer left half-hidden, and a longer summary is clipped instead of refused. The controller's own callers (artifact, review, message, hand-off and meeting-decision steps, and the dispatcher's steps) no longer cut the text before handing it over.

## L02d (part 1): the stop inventory takes local processes and child work from the runtime

- `dispatchStopPorts` takes a `LocalWork` source (`start` option `localWork`): `processes(attempts)` lists the local processes and delegated child work of the scope's attempts (running, uncooperative, or unknown) and `spent(attempts)` says what the cleanup cost. They appear in the stop inventory as `process` and `child` items; an uncooperative or unknown one is named as unresolved when the stop ends (so Force Stop is offered and the result is reported as recovery-required if it stays); a runtime that cannot answer is shown as one unknown item (`runtime:processes`) instead of a clean stop; the cleanup spend is the runtime's figure, and nothing is charged when it says nothing.
- The controller keeps no registry of processes or child work, and no runtime reports them yet: the source is not wired by default (the sandbox backend in `worker/src/sandbox` can list a confinement's processes, but nothing carries that to the controller). Remaining in L02d: that report from the worker, and charging the spend to the budget.

One matching watch ends it; none is refused ("no watch is active for that task"); several ask which (options carry the watch ID and stream). A given `watchId` must be an active watch. The task ID is dropped before the call.

## H09 (part 1): uncertain effects block replacement; an old primary cannot renew

- **Audit result (2026-10-30).** Message fencing (old session, old placement, ended attempt) and the storage epoch fence were in place and tested; a lost attempt with a call of unknown outcome, however, was replaced at once and the new attempt could ask for the same effect under new operation IDs.
- **Fix.** When an attempt that ended (lost, failed or abandoned) has an operation in state `uncertain`, `#readmit` opens a `dispatch_blocked` blocker on the task (resolver: the owner; names the calls) and admits nothing; later ticks start nothing either. Test: dispatcher.test.ts "a lost attempt with a call of unknown outcome is not replaced" (it fails without the change).
- **Old primary on the worker path.** remote.test.ts "a controller that no longer holds the epoch cannot renew a worker's lease or take its result": after another controller takes the epoch, a worker's heartbeat and result get `stale_epoch` (503) and the stored dispatch record, its revision and lease are unchanged.
- **Not done (remainder H09b).** (a) The recovery handshake: `connect` carries no list of held attempts, the session records no primary epoch, and a new primary has no handle on remote attempts that were running (offers are in memory only; `dispatcher.heartbeat` renews attempts this instance has no live handle for). (b) A worker that reconnects and calls `accept` takes its accepted attempt up again with no decision by the controller (client.ts documents this as intended; "reconnect never automatically resumes" holds only for calls before the re-accept). (c) Checked and not a gap: a relocation keeps the attempt ID, so the moved attempt asking for the same call gets the same operation, and an uncertain one is still refused by the ledger. (d) Tried and withdrawn: refusing a heartbeat for an attempt this dispatcher holds no live handle on; it also refuses a relocated remote attempt, so adoption needs a real decision (the handshake), not that check.

## H09b (part 1): recovery handshake, explicit re-accept, owner approval

- **Done.** (a) `POST /worker/session/reconcile` (`RemoteWorkerService.reconcile`, client `reconcile(held)`): a reconnected worker lists at most 64 `{attemptId, placement}`; each gets `stop` (moved, placed again, ended, completed, expired, never accepted), `hold` (already taken up in this session), `reaccept` (still owned and approved for this session: call accept), `pending` (waiting for the owner) or `unknown` (no such attempt for this host, or a placement number never issued; another host's attempt is also `unknown`, so nothing leaks). The last write is a `remote-reconcile` record per host (session, mode, counts, unknown IDs) under the controller epoch, so an old primary gets `stale_epoch` instead of verdicts from stale reads.
- (b) A worker's `accept` of an attempt accepted in an older session is now the controller's decision: `auto` lets it through; `owner` records `reaccept: {sessionId, state: pending}` on the placement and answers `unavailable` (503, not `fenced`: the worker keeps the attempt but cannot call) until the owner approves for that very session. The approval names the session, so a newer session asks again; `begin`/`report`/etc. keep refusing until accept succeeds (existing session fence).
- **Settings (owner decision 2026-10-30, provisional choices).** `reconnect.settings.get/set` (owner only, `expectedRevision`, replay-safe; `auto` = enable, `owner` = disable, null = profile decides) and the owner's decision `reconnect.reaccept` {attemptId, placement, decision approve|stop}; chat proposals for both (always shown first). Default by profile: autonomous = auto, strict and derived = owner (derived is provisional). A damaged record or unreadable profile falls back to the strict side. Wired in start.ts through `remote.reaccept`; without a configured source the remote service defaults to `owner`. No budget, time or money limit is involved.
- **Tests.** remote/reconcile.test.ts (each of the three storage backends), api/reconnect-settings-api.test.ts.
- **Not done (remainder, H09b stays open).** (1) Adoption by a new owner: a new primary still has no handle on remote attempts that were running (offers are in memory; `dispatcher.heartbeat` for a relocated remote attempt) and no handshake-driven adoption or end; this needs the dispatcher side and a two-controller test on one store. (2) Attempts the controller has accepted on a host but the host did not list are not reported as missing (no index of placements by host; lease expiry still ends them). (3) (Done in the review fixes below: list, notice.) The owner had no list of waiting attempts or notification yet: `reconnect.reaccept` needs the attempt ID, which is on the placement record (`reaccept.state: pending`). (4) The poller/host code does not call `reconcile` by itself after reconnecting.

### H09b review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Approval bound to the session.** `reconnect.reaccept` now carries `sessionId` (required) and `waitingSince` (optional, the marker's moment) next to the attempt and placement, all taken from `reconnect.pending`. The decision is applied inside one command whose payload is the decision itself, and it is fenced when the marker names another session or was recorded again: a newer session that asked meanwhile is never approved by an answer meant for the older one. The chat proposal shows `sessionId` and `waitingSince` in its line (the keys are exempt from the own-words rule, they are record references). A repeat of the same command ID returns the recorded result (the retry of a stop no longer meets "nothing waits"); the stop is the same command (no separate `end`), and re-checks that the marker is still pending when it is applied.
- **Owner mode no longer stalls silently.** When a pending marker is first written (accept or handshake) the controller raises a Needs-you notice (kind `maintenance`, level `needs-you`, so the owner's per-kind level setting applies; notice ID made from attempt, session and the marker's moment, so polling again is the same notice and a newer session is a new one). A failed notice is tried again at the next poll. `reconnect.pending` (owner only, paged by attempt ID, limit 1 to 100) lists what waits: attempt, placement, host, session, since when. On the worker side the accept answer says "it is waiting for the owner" (`WorkerRequestError.waitingForOwner`) and the poller treats it as a calm wait (`onTrouble` kind `waiting-for-owner`, the failure count does not grow, the session is kept).
- **Patience (settable, default 24 hours, can be off).** `reconnect.settings.set { patienceHours }` (a number above 0 up to a year, `off`, or null for the default; a field left out is kept). While the worker keeps asking and the patience from the moment the waiting was recorded is not spent, the controller beats the attempt's lease on the worker's behalf (the pending worker cannot call heartbeat), so the lease running out does not move the attempt while the owner decides. If the worker stops asking, or the patience is spent or off, the lease runs out as before. The attempt's time limit (`expiresAt`) is not extended: that is the owner's limit.
- **Reconcile is bounded.** One handshake per host and session in 5 seconds: the same list gets the last answer, a different list gets `unavailable` (503, ask again). The handshake record is not written again when the same list from the same session gives the same outcome. The answer cache is in memory, so a controller that lost the epoch can repeat its last answer for up to 5 seconds (it never writes). Session IDs are per host (`ses-<epoch>`), so the cache is keyed by host and session.
- **Approval written by the setting does not outlive it.** In `auto` the marker is stored as `auto` (not `approved`); it counts only while the setting is still `auto`, so after a switch to `owner` the next accept or handshake turns it into a pending marker (and a notice). `approved` is the owner's decision only.
- **Tests.** reconcile.test.ts (rate limit and no second write; approval racing a newer session and a stale waiting moment; stop retry and stale-session stop; notice once per marker, list, paging, owner only; auto marker after a switch; lease kept with the patience and not kept with it off; exact `relocating` verdict), reconnect-settings-api.test.ts (patience, pending, chat line).
- **Out of scope, recorded.** Adoption of a waiting attempt by a new owner/primary (the in-memory answer cache and the notice are per process; the marker and the owner's list are in the store, so a new primary sees them, but it has no handle on the running worker).


## V02 (part 1): a retry limit per task that a new call or a rebuilt context does not reset

- **Audit (2026-10-30).** What exists for V02: stall and loop detection (V01/V01b), route fallback with effect preservation (R02), resume (L04), owner holds (L01). There is no recovery action ladder: nothing acts on a stall concern beyond recording it. Cost and tokens were already added up per task across calls and routes; retries were limited only per call (4 attempts), so a new call started the count again.
- **Done.** `FallbackService` counts every failed attempt against the task (`SpendBody.failures`, with or without a usage report) and the owner may set `maxFailedAttempts` in the task's model budget; when the failures (including the one being reported) reach it, the next route is a visible wait ("the task's retry budget is used up; the owner can raise it") and so is every later call, until the owner raises it. The service has no API or chat exposure of the budget yet (`setBudget` is service level only).
- **Open (remainder V02b, not built).** (b) Escalation when a supervisor leaves a concern undecided; (c) persisting an intervention and queued input before a stuck request is cancelled (needs the action ladder); (d) recording the context carried when a fallback route switch resumes a call; (e) loop recovery that preserves history and effects; (f) a test that a supervisor's own task is assessed; and a new generation resets the stall evidence (`spend`, loop counts) in `stall.ts`, which the clause "switching context never resets cumulative limits" should also cover for the stall `budget` concern.

## P04 (part 1): deterministic responsibility checks

- `ResponsibilityChecks` (`projects/checks.ts`): `generate(by, projectId)` records one `responsibility-check` for each active, scheduled responsibility whose next check is due, identified by responsibility and slot (so a repeat, a restart or a second instance records nothing new). After downtime one catch-up check is owed with the gap named (`missedChecks`, start, end), not one per slot. A check inside a maintenance window is owed and says so. `pending(by, projectId)` lists those not yet finished by a `check` observation recorded after the slot. Owner, service or `responsibility.write` may generate; reading follows `responsibility.read`. It records only that a check is owed: no task, model or action.
- **Not here (P04b):** a loop that runs `generate` on the controller's clock; turning a due check into a bounded task or an observation; incident grouping with retries and escalation; observed state kept apart from intended state ("no recent observation" is never healthy); maintenance leases; API operations and the status view; the event-driven checks. Provisional defaults still to be chosen by the owner: who pays for check tasks, grouping window, retry and escalation counts, and whether actions are held in a maintenance window (assumed yes).

## P04 (part 2): incidents and observed state

- `IncidentService` (`projects/incidents.ts`): `report` groups alerts (`attention`/`failed`) with the same signature on one responsibility into one open incident (count, first and last time, worst outcome); a resolved signature that alerts again opens a new incident. `resolve` needs evidence. `escalate(by, projectId)` marks each open incident escalated once (to the responsibility's `escalation.to`) when `escalation.afterMinutes` has passed since it opened; repeats and other instances record nothing new; resolved ones never. `observed` tells what the checks found apart from the desired condition: `unknown` with no check or one older than twice the period, never healthy by default; open incidents show as attention or failed. Authority is the same as for adding history (owner, the responsible agent, `responsibility.write`).
- **Not here (P04c):** the bounded retry count before escalation (only the time rule exists), a loop that runs `generate` and `escalate` on the clock, turning an escalation into an owner notice, turning a due check into a bounded task, API operations and the status view, maintenance leases, event-driven checks, and the coverage-gap record from an outage of the event source.

## P04 (part 3): wired into the running controller

- A dispatcher loop (`responsibilities.checks`) runs `ResponsibilityChecks.generate` and `IncidentService.escalate` for every project on each tick, as the tick's principal.
- State API: `responsibility.checks` (due checks not yet finished), `responsibility.incidents`, `responsibility.observed`, and the commands `incident.report` and `incident.resolve`.
- Remaining in P04 (P04c): the bounded retry count, turning a due check into a bounded task and an escalation into an owner notice, maintenance leases, event-driven checks, coverage gap from an event-source outage, and the chat/status view.

## H10 (part 1): child tasks with allowances, and swarm cancellation

- `SwarmService` (`swarm/`): `spawn` makes a child task, writes its contract from the parent's outcome and acceptance criteria, delegates part of the parent's budget to it (R05, so it can spend only that), and records a `swarm-link` (child -> parent). It refuses a parent that has nothing to give (budget `delegate` refuses), a task already at the depth limit (3) or with 4 live children (the H03 defaults, overridable), and cancels a child it made before a refusal so no task is left without an allowance. Authority is the budget's: the owner or the holder of the parent's node with `budget.manage`. `cancel` stops every descendant deepest first (Stop, not Suspend), takes back what each did not use (`reclaim`), cancels the task, and reports `settled` and `pending`; repeating it is safe. State API: `swarm.spawn`, `swarm.cancel`.
- **Provisional decisions (to put to the owner at the end of the batch):** who may spawn (budget holders and the owner for now, not any agent with `task.create`), cancel means Stop (not Suspend) and unused allowance returns automatically, depth 3 and 4 children stay the defaults, and "bounded coordination" (a cap on messages a parent receives from children) is not defined by the card and not built.
- **Not here (H10b):** the dispatcher does not yet pass the parent to admission, so depth/children limits at admission still do not fire for real spawns (the swarm service enforces them itself); a child with no budget node is not blocked from starting; stop/review/inquiry requests are not yet made through admission's control class; per-project or per-tree caps and host quotas beyond the existing `perHost`/`productive`; a chat command.

## Batch 14 review fixes (L06, P04, H10)

- **H10.** `spawn` and `cancel` first check who may (the owner, or the holder of the parent's budget with `budget.manage` and, for `spawn`, `task.create` in the project; new read `BudgetService.canManage`), before making any task or reporting any limit, so a foreign task answers `forbidden` and nothing is made. A retry of a spawn that was refused and cancelled its child, with the same command ID, is refused ("ask again with a new command ID") instead of giving that cancelled task an allowance. `cancel` takes back a child's unused allowance before cancelling it; a caller who cannot reclaim leaves the child pending, so a later call by someone who can still finds it.
- **P04.** An escalated incident whose `escalatedTo` is `owner` becomes a `maintenance` notice (command `inc-esc-<id>`); one project failing no longer skips the others in a tick. The scans of checks and incidents allow 50,000 records.
- **Known, not fixed:** the live-children limit is a check then act, so two simultaneous spawns could pass the 4-child limit (the depth, node and budget limits hold); check and incident records are never pruned and are read by scanning all (an index per project and a retention rule belong to K06/P04c); escalation to an agent (not `owner`) sends no notice; the L06 tracked-remote-job exception is decided from the job's own fields (`kind`, `background`, `resumability`), which the admitting agent sets, so an agent could tag a job to be listed as tracked rather than waited for (it is shown to the owner as an exception, and Force Stop still works) — a permission for the tag belongs with L01's background permission.
- **Batch 14, second pass.** An escalation is told once it has been told: `IncidentService.untold` lists escalated incidents with no `notifiedAt` and `markNotified` records the notice, so a notice that could not be sent (for example the owner has too many open items) is offered again next tick, and an escalation recorded before an error is not lost. `swarm.cancel` checks that the caller holds the child's parent budget before stopping anything, so a child is never left stopped but not cancelled. Known: an escalation to an agent (not `owner`) still sends no notice.

## T02 (part 1): set aside and roll back catalog versions

- `CatalogService.deprecate` (owner only) sets a version aside: it is no longer chosen when a caller names no version, but a task that names it still resolves and runs it (silent resume does not break) and it stays readable. `rollback(name, toVersion)` sets aside every published, unrevoked version above the target (the target comes back into use if it had been set aside; a revoked target is refused). Nothing is deleted or rewritten; a revoked version stays refused. Non-maintainer publication was already refused (only the registrant's own accepted work, the owner for shared and system names).
- **Not here (T02b):** the state API and chat for the catalog (it has no operations at all yet), promotion of a personal artifact to the shared layer, the in-flight policy on revocation (finish, cancel or pause: an owner decision, provisional default is to refuse new runs and let a running one finish), paused-task migration to a newer version, the retention of stale referenced artifacts (K06), and a personal fork of a revoked tool gaining no authority (new registrations are checked against grants already; no fork operation exists).

## U06b: recovery chat controls for routes and providers

- The typed orders `/nimblenewt.routing-disable`, `-drain`, `-cutover` and `-reenable` are recovery orders (the same class as pause and stop): they run as typed, need no assistant, and report Received, Accepted and Effected (new work no longer reaches the target; how many running attempts a cutover cancelled; or that the target may be used again). The records, owner-only checks and restart behaviour are R04b's.
- Short forms `/exclude`, `/restore` and `/cutover <model|endpoint|account|provider|service> <name> [reason]` (`chat/shorthand.ts`) are never run: the chat answers with the exact typed line they stand for ("it has not run; send the line as it is") and the owner sends that line. An incomplete short form is told what is missing. `/drain` has no short form because it needs a duration the owner must choose.
- Provisional: short forms are shown rather than confirmed with a yes/no because the chat has no place to hold a pending typed line; the owner can say otherwise.

## X09 (part 1): external release-test job protocol

- `release/release.ts` (`ReleaseService`, state API `release.*`). The owner submits an immutable **candidate** (source commit, artifact hashes, dependency-lock hashes, suite revision, platform matrix); its ID is a digest of the ordered manifest, so the same manifest is the same candidate. Each platform is tested by **attempts**: the owner authorizes a host for destructive release tests on one platform (`release.host`; a production machine is not authorized by that) and issues an attempt to that host and a named worker; the job payload is a pure function of candidate, platform, attempt and limits.
- A **result** (`release.report`) is taken only from the worker the attempt was issued to (anyone else reads like a missing attempt; the owner may not report), only for an open attempt, and only if source commit, suite revision, artifact hashes and platform equal the candidate's; otherwise it is refused and counts for nothing. A pass needs passing tests and none failing. Summaries are redacted. A worker holds only the new action `release.report`; approval is owner-only and refused unless every platform's latest attempt passed (a platform with no attempt blocks it).
- A lost worker is `release.interrupt` (owner), never a pass; a retry is a new attempt with a new ID and the earlier attempts and their evidence stay. A platform that passed cannot be re-issued.
- No model is involved anywhere in submitting, issuing, reporting or gating.
- **Not here (X09b):** delivering the payload to a remote worker over the worker transport and collecting logs and artifact hashes from it (H12a), who notices a lost worker and interrupts the attempt (the owner does it by hand for now), the outer test supervisor for reboot and partition tests with an external effect sink (X10), and a chat wording for these orders.
- Provisional: log and artifact bytes are not stored, only the log digest and the artifact hashes the worker reports; a worker reports once per attempt.

## X09b (part 1): release jobs reach the host, and chat words for starting and cancelling

- **Delivery over the existing host protocol** (`remote/server.ts`, `remote/client.ts`; no new transport): the queued job is the attempt record `release.issue`/`release.start` already writes. An authenticated, enrolled host (session and protocol checks as for every worker route) calls `GET /worker/release/jobs` (its own open attempts, at most 32, oldest first, payload rebuilt from the candidate), `POST /worker/release/jobs/{id}/pickup` (idempotent; records `pickedUpAt` once, guarded by the attempt revision, a simultaneous second pick-up looks again and returns the first time) and `POST /worker/release/jobs/{id}/report` (the same body and checks as `release.report`, wire fields closed). The host path needs: the attempt was issued to that host as both host and worker (`workerId` = host ID, the default of `release.start`), the job was picked up, the attempt still open, and the owner's `release.host` authorization still active for the platform (withdrawing it stops offers, pick-ups and reports at once). Another host's job reads as missing. Wired in `startController` through `composeDispatch` into `WorkerTransport.listen`; `RemoteWorkerClient.releaseJobs/releasePickUp/releaseReport` are the fake-host side in tests.
- **Starting and cancelling.** New ops `release.start` and `release.cancel` (and the settings below). Who may: the owner; an active agent holding the QA role (name `qa`, settable) when `qaAgents` is on; the direct supervisor of an active QA-role agent when `bosses` is on. Checked from the live agent records on each call (a changed role or supervisor counts at once; a setting or agent scan that cannot be read leaves only the owner). An agent may not name the worker (the host reports its own test, so a QA agent cannot certify its own pass), cannot authorize hosts, approve, interrupt through the owner op or read/change the settings. The attempt records `issuedBy` and, if cancelled, `endedBy`. A cancelled attempt is the same `interrupted` state: never a pass. At most 20 attempts per platform per candidate (all issuers), so a loop of start/cancel is bounded.
- **Settings (chat-settable, owner-only, `expectedRevision`):** `release.settings.get/set` (`qaAgents`, `bosses`, `qaRole`; `null` returns a field to the default) and `release.issuers.enable/disable` (`who` = qa-agents, bosses, all). Provisional default from the installation profile: strict = owner only; derived and autonomous = QA agents and bosses on. Chat: `release.start` and the two widening ops (`enable`, `settings.set`) are shown first in every profile; `release.cancel` and `release.issuers.disable` apply at once. Default timeout 3600 s and memory 4096 MB on `release.start` when not given; they are limits of the test host, not a budget, and are not required.
- **Bounded results:** the host's report body is the existing bounded one (summary 500 characters, 100 artifact hashes, closed field list); log bytes are still not stored, only the digest.
- **Remainder:** an outer supervisor that notices a host that took a job and went silent (the deadline `timeoutSeconds` is in the payload but nothing interrupts an overdue attempt; the owner or an issuer cancels by hand), reboot/partition tests with an external effect sink (X10), logs and artifact bytes from the host, the same wording for `release.host`/`release.approve` in chat (still API-only; approval stays the owner's), a boss further up the chain than the direct supervisor, and a runnable host-side worker program (only the client calls and the fake in tests exist).

## L03g (part 2): drafts and responsibilities in the hand-off package

- `controllerHandoffSources` takes three optional sources. **Drafts:** the sender's shared draft desk records on this task (status `draft`, visibility `shared`; private scratch, other tasks' drafts and accepted notes are left out), read as the sender, because a recipient could not otherwise read another agent's draft; each is `id "title": first 300 characters`. **Responsibilities** (a new fixed section name, `responsibilities`): the active responsibilities in the task's project that the sender answers for, with a line saying they stay with the sender until reassigned. **Locks:** a hook for what the sender holds locked or leased; no service keeps such holds yet (the integrator lease is P10, workspace holds H12m), so none is wired and the section stays unset rather than claiming "no locks".
- A failing source leaves its section missing; it never fails the package. The recipient's eligibility checks (L03d) are unchanged. Responsibilities are not transferred by a hand-off; moving them is a separate, deliberate reassignment (owner decision to confirm).
- **Remainder (L03h):** the `locks` source once something holds locks, and offering to reassign the sender's responsibilities with the task.

## V02b (part 1): an undecided stall concern is told to the owner

- `StallService.escalateUndecided` marks a suspected concern that has waited `escalateAfterMs` (provisional 30 minutes) without a decision as escalated and returns the escalated concerns whose notice is not recorded as sent; `markEscalationNotified` records it. The concern stays routed to its supervisor (who can still decide) and later scans keep the marks. The recovery loop (`recovery.stall-scan`) sends a `maintenance` notice about the task after each scan and offers it again next tick if sending failed. Needs the same right as the scan.
- **Not here (V02b2):** persisting an intervention and queued input before a stuck request is cancelled (needs the action ladder), recording the context carried on a fallback switch, loop recovery that keeps history and effects, assessing a supervisor's own task, and keeping the stall evidence across a new generation.

## Review fixes for T02, X09 and L03g

- **T02.** `register` kept `revoked` but dropped `deprecated`, so publishing a new version undid a rollback; it now carries it (test: roll back, publish, revoke the new one, the rolled-back-from version stays set aside).
- **X09.** A repeated `release.issue` returns the attempt that command created (not the latest for that worker and host) with the limits it was issued under (now stored on the attempt and part of the command payload, so different limits under the same command ID conflict). A cell's `osVersion`, when the candidate names one, must match the report. The report must now carry the dependency-lock hashes, equal to the candidate's; `counts` is stored as exactly passed, failed, skipped.
- **L03g.** The sender's drafts and responsibilities were readable through the hand-off by anyone who may control the task. `HandoffService.screen` now withholds those two sections from everyone except the owner, the sender and, after the transfer, the recipient; the state API applies it to every hand-off result. The sender's drafts are read in pages (up to 4,000 records of the sender in the project).

## V02b / X09 second-pass fixes

- **Stall escalation notice.** The notice text is cut to the notification limit (200) so it can be sent; one concern whose notice fails no longer holds back the others (the first failure is raised after all were tried); the notice's command ID includes the escalation time, so a concern that reopens and is escalated again is a new notice, not a replay of (or a conflict with) the earlier one; a concern already routed to the owner is not escalated; the tick reads the concerns once. Known: the read still walks every stored concern (cleared ones are not pruned: K06).
- **X09.** The platform version a candidate names is the version tested: an issue naming another version is refused, and one naming none takes the candidate's. A replay of an issue command recorded before the limits were stored is refused as a conflict (no such record exists outside tests).

## H12d: the release path behind the quiesce

- `release` (committing the reviewed tree, A06) is now an operation of `workspace.request`, run inside `QuiesceCoordinator.around` like integration, refresh and quarantine: every live attempt has new calls refused, calls in flight settled and a checkpoint taken first, and a failure to do so refuses the operation with a typed `runtime_hold` blocker (tested for `release` with a failing checkpoint). `QuiesceOperation` already named it.
- **Remainder (H12d2):** landing (P10) will be a fifth operation when it exists; no production host has a `workspace` port yet (H12m), so against a real host these requests are still answered `refused`.

## H12b (part 1): the live worker is confined, and dies with its controller

- `packages/integration/src/h12b-confinement.test.ts` (with `h12b-confinement-support.ts` and a crash fixture `h12b-confinement-child.ts`) looks at the real worker process in the real bubblewrap sandbox, from the host's `/proc`: the worker's namespace has only the loopback device; the git directory is not mounted anywhere in it; the protected `.git` is mounted read-only (with a positive control that it is mounted); and a recipe with `processes: 64, memoryMb: 768` is enforced in full by a systemd scope whose `pids.max` and `memory.max` are exactly those numbers. A second test starts the controller side as a child process, kills it with SIGKILL and shows no process of the worker is left (with a positive control that it was running).
- A machine without user-level systemd falls back to weaker limits and says so in the launch record; the test then reports it (`NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_LIMITS=1` makes that a failure) and skips the cgroup check. Skipped without bubblewrap unless `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`.
- **Still open for H12b:** narrowing or widening the recipe on a restart is not applied (`sandbox.open` ignores the recipe summary and `reach`); no production code sets `workspace.limits` (H12k); macOS and Windows launchers cannot mount Node for the worker, so these tests run on Linux only; the host composer (H12k).

## H12f (part 1): a message told mid-turn

- Audit (2026-10-30): the controller side of H12f is built and composed (`controllerGuards` in `api/dispatch-compose.ts`: context admit/resume, pause observation, message boundaries); what was unproven was the real worker process taking a message while a turn runs. A test now holds a turn at the bridge wait, tells a message, and shows it is answered while the turn is still waiting, the turn completes, and the model sees the message on its next call.
- **Fix:** the worker process answered `tell.ok` only when the turn it landed in ended, so the host's per-beat delivery (`observeAndDeliver`) sat on that answer and could not report `paused` or deliver anything else for the rest of the turn. It now answers when the update is placed; a later failure of the placed update is a fault with the same ID (**wrong: see the review fixes below; it is not reported**).
- **Open for H12f (not claimed):** `compact` is missing on the host runtime and channel, so an over-budget first call always fails the attempt instead of compacting once; `systemPromptChars` is never sent in `ready` (an 8000-character fallback is used); a recipe change restarts without re-running the resume/admission checks; `confirmUsage` has no caller; `inFlight` counts only tool calls, not a streaming model call, so `paused` can be reported while a provider call is still open (owner/Opus question); pause behaviour is not exercised against the real process.

## H12f (part 2): the first call can be compacted once

- The worker channel has a `compact` request and a `compact.ok` answer (contracts, parsed and round-trip tested). The worker process compacts its stored conversation (`adapter.root().compact()`) and answers with the new size estimate, or a fault with the same ID; the host `WorkerProcess.compact()` asks and the host runtime offers `compact` (optional on `HostRuntime`), which is what `LocalWorker` already calls when `guards.context.admit` refuses the first call (round 1), so the request can be made. **Correction (Opus review, 2026-10-30): this does not yet make an over-budget first call pass.** The first-call description (`FirstCall` in `context/dispatch.ts`) has no term for the stored conversation, so compacting changes none of its inputs; and a refusal in round 1 opens a `context_overflow` blocker that makes round 2 refuse too. Making compaction work needs the stored size in the admission and a way past the blocker for a compacted call; it is not done and H12f stays open. Tested in the process (a turn, then compact, then the process answers a checkpoint). Not tested against a real model's summary: the offline model scripts the summary.
- Still open for H12f: `systemPromptChars` in `ready`, re-checking on a recipe change, a caller for `confirmUsage`, the streaming-call question for `paused`, pause against the real process.
