## M02e remainder: one-task agreed grants

`GrantService.grantAgreed` now accepts an optional `resource`, which must be `{kind:'task', id}` (anything else is refused). A second allowlist, `AGREED_GRANTABLE_ON_ONE_TASK` (`task.update`, `task.transition`), is grantable by a decision only with that task resource; a project-wide request for them stays refused. `grantApplier(grants, controller, projects?)` takes an optional `taskId` in the patch, checks through `projects.getTask` that it belongs to the decision's project, and passes `resource: {kind:'task', id}`. Without the projects service, a `taskId` is refused. `api/start.ts` wires the projects service in.
## M02e remainder: ownership change decided in a meeting (`task.reassign`)

- `taskReassignApplier(assignments, projects, principals)` in `meetings/record.ts`, registered as `task.reassign` in `api/start.ts`. Patch is exactly `{ toAgent: 'agent:<name>' }`; unknown keys, a non-task target, and a missing or non-active agent are refused (`invalid_command`). The project comes from the task (as `task.update`).
- Required action is `assignment.manage` (the action `SecureApi.assignTask/transferTask` demands), so `#mayCarry` applies. Carried out by `AssignmentService`: `transferTask` when assigned, `assignTask` (with the assignment revision) when released, plain `assignTask` when never assigned; the attempt of the old holder is superseded by the transfer as usual.
- Not a widening (`widens` unset): assignment only changes who is dispatched on the task; the new owner's access still comes from its own grants and per-attempt task credentials (A10b/H12), nothing is added. If a later change makes assignment confer access, set `widens: 'access-change'` here.
- Idempotent: if the task is already assigned to that agent the change is a no-op, so a replay after a crash does not conflict on the changed assignment revision; the command id is the stable `mtg:<decision>:<change>`.
- Tests: applier unit test with fakes, and `record.test.ts` through the real `MeetingRecordService` on every backend (vote reassigns; carrier without `assignment.manage` is not applied).

## M02e review fixes: task.reassign applier

- The reassignment patch carries the assignment as observed at decision time: `from` (agent id or null), and `generation` plus `revision` of the assignment record when one exists. The task revision check does not cover assignment writes, so the applier itself refuses (`stale_revision`, so the change is "not applied") unless the live assignment still matches; an owner's later transfer or release stands. If the new owner already holds the task at a later generation, the change is a replay and does nothing. Unknown keys are refused.
- The transfer/assign command is built from the patch's observed revision only, so a replay has an identical payload. The apply loop now also records `command_conflict` as "not applied", so a conflicting replay cannot wedge a decision.
- A task with a running attempt (`activeAttemptId`) is refused ("use a hand-off"). Routing a running task through `HandoffService` is left to a later card.
- The new owner must hold `attempt.work` and `task.read` on the task (effective grants, checked through the `mayWork` callback wired in api/start.ts). An assignee receives auto admission, title/description in the work order, budget draw and coordinator inquiries; the old comment claiming nothing is added was wrong.

### M02e task.reassign: review round 2 (open items, and one reversal)

- `command_conflict` is NOT mapped to "not applied" after all: an apply that committed and then replayed under a different actor (owner agree, then service recovery) would be recorded as failed although it was applied (a silent mislabel). Left visibly stuck in `applying` instead, like before. Was open as **M02e3**; done, see "M02e3 deterministic actor" below.
- Open: after a crash that follows a committed transfer, a later move makes the replay throw `stale_revision` and the change reads not-applied although the meeting's transfer happened; fix is to still call the service with the observed revision so its command-id dedupe answers.
- Open: the observed `from`/`generation`/`revision` of a `task.reassign` patch come from the proposer; no tool text tells agents to supply them; `mayWork` uses the wall clock like its neighbours. The boundary scanner reads a quoted `from` followed by a quote as an import (hence the `"fro" + "m"` split in record.ts); proposed fix in scripts/package-boundaries.mjs: `(?<![\w$.'"\x60])from\s*["']` with the capture `["']([^"'\s,]+)["']`, plus a fixture with `["a", "from", "b"]`.

## Boundary scanner: quoted `from` (follow-up to M02e)

- `SPECIFIER` in scripts/package-boundaries.mjs now requires that `from` is not preceded by a word character, `$`, `.`, quote or backtick, and captures `[^"'\s,]+`, so `["a", "from", "b"]` is no longer an import. Whole-line `//` comments and line-leading `/* */` blocks are stripped before scanning imports (not before the SQL tripwire); markers inside strings are never touched, so a glob like `"src/**/*.ts"` cannot hide a real import. A trailing comment after code is still scanned.
- record.ts uses the plain `"from"` literal again (the `"fro" + "m"` split is gone). The open item above about the scanner is resolved.
### M02e3 deterministic actor for meeting appliers

The command digest includes the actor, and `#applyDecision` runs under the owner (`ownerRespond`) or the service (recovery), so an apply that committed and crashed before `applied` was saved replayed under another actor and threw `command_conflict`, leaving the change in `applying`. Chosen: record the acting principal on the change when it enters `applying` (`ChangeRecord.actedAs`, saved with `agreedBy`) and pass it to the applier on every run and replay (`actor` is that value; `actedAs` is also given to `ChangeApplier.apply`). Changes already `applying` from before this card have no `actedAs` and fall back to the current principal, as before. The carrying agent is still what `#mayCarry` checks; the services record the principal that started the apply, as they did. Test: `record.test.ts` "an apply that committed and crashed ..." (task.update and task.reassign; owner agrees, effect commits, the `applied` save is lost, the service recovers: change ends `applied`, effect once). It fails with `command_conflict` if `actor` is taken from the current principal again.

## H07b (first slice): host choice as an ordered candidate list with pure fallback
- `hosts/candidates.ts` `chooseHost(candidates, judge)`: takes the candidates in preference order and a judge per host (`take` or `refuse {reason, lasting, revoked?}`); returns the first that takes the attempt with the refusals of the earlier ones (host, reason, lasting), or one wait carrying every reason in order, `blocked` (no candidate or all revoked) and `lastingRefusal` (every candidate refused for a lasting reason, revoked counted). Pure, no I/O.
- `Dispatcher.#pickHost` now builds on it (same behaviour as H07e; the existing 308 dispatcher tests and `api/start-remote-choice` still pass). Tests: `hosts/candidates.test.ts` (7: order decides, fallback keeps reasons in order, later hosts not asked, all-refuse single wait, passing reasons never lasting, all revoked blocked, empty list).
- Remains of H07b: record the refusals of the passed-over hosts on the attempt (today they appear only in the plan's `skipped` reason when all refuse, not when a later host takes it); fall back when a host refuses at start (`place`) after being chosen; the worker process runs the host poller; a poll ends when its client disconnects; the placement policy is checked again at delivery; the platform index drops revoked hosts and is filled at a restart. Host poller not wired in start.ts.

## H07b (second slice): a host that refuses at its start is passed over, a bounded number of times
- **What happens now.** When the chosen host refuses the attempt at its start before anything was given to it (the remote placement's policy or capability check, or too many offers waiting), the attempt no longer fails. The refusal is kept on the attempt's record (`startRefusals`: host, reason, lasting or passing, when; at most 8), the start is undone (the attempt waits again, its place is given back, the credential issued for that start and received by nobody is ended, the task's placement record goes back to what it said before) and the next tick chooses among the hosts that have not refused it. A host that refused an attempt is never chosen again for that attempt, even if it would take it now.
- **The bound.** `startTries` (default 3): once that many hosts have refused the attempt, or no worker host is left that has not, the attempt fails as before with `the worker did not start: ...`, now naming every host that refused and why. With one refusal the text is the host's own message, as before. An attempt pinned to one host (moved there) is not moved elsewhere: its refusal fails it, as before.
- **Owner-visible reasons.** The plan's skip for that tick says `<host> cannot take attempt ...: <reasons>; nothing was given to it, and the attempt is tried on another host that has not refused it (refusal n of at most 3)`. When a later host takes the attempt, `hostChoice.passedOver` on the record lists every host passed over before it with why (H07e's "would refuse" answers, staleness, and earlier start refusals), so it is no longer only visible when every host refuses.
- **How a refusal is told apart.** `StartRefused` (dispatch ports, a `DomainError` with the same codes and message as before) is thrown by `RemoteWorkerService.place` for the policy/capability refusal and for the offers-full limit, both raised before any offer is made. Any other start failure (a sandbox that cannot be made, an error) still fails the attempt at once, as before. The "lasting" reading is the same wording test as H07e (`lastingReasons`, now shared by `refusals` and `place`; offers-full is passing).
- **Order.** Candidates are tried in the dispatcher's `workers` order (deterministic, configuration order); the passed-over list keeps that order.
- **Tests.** `dispatch/dispatcher.test.ts` (all four backends): fallback to the next host with the record and plan text, the refusing host not chosen again, place/credential/placement record given back; the bound (every host refused: fails with each reason; `startTries: 1`: fails at once; a plain start error fails at once); a pinned attempt is not moved. `remote/polling.test.ts` (all four backends, real remote service): the H07 policy refusal now falls back to the listed host on the next tick, with the record. `api/start-remote-choice.test.ts` (composed controller, product `RemoteWorkerHost`): the policy refuses at the place after the dispatcher chose r1, nothing is offered to r1, the next tick starts on r2 and the record says why. Mutations killed: the not-again rule removed, the bound ignored, the fallback disabled, the placement record not restored.
- ASSUMPTION: three refusals at the start per attempt is the bound (small, and an owner with more hosts than that rarely needs more); a refused host counts as a lasting refusal for the H07e owner blocker when every other host also refuses.
- ASSUMPTION: an undone start leaves a slot span of a few milliseconds on the record (the usage sink opens a span on entering running); it is not removed, since the span is honest about the brief claim.
- **Known / not done in this slice.** The task's placement record, when it had none before, is reset to an empty record (it reads as none) rather than removed, since removals are reserved for retention. The C07o first-call refusal is not a host refusal and still fails the attempt. Still to do for H07b: choose among remote hosts by `RemoteWorkerService.candidates` (load order) instead of the configuration order; the worker process runs the host poller (`HostPoller` not wired in the worker package or start.ts); a held poll ends when its client disconnects; the placement policy is checked again at delivery (the offer is read by the host); the platform index drops revoked hosts and is filled at a controller restart.
- **Review (clean-context Opus).** Checked: `StartRefused` is thrown only in `place` before the placement record, the native-store claim and the offer are written, and `RemoteWorkerHost.start` hands nothing out before `place` (the C07o check gives no order away), so "nothing was given to it" holds; the undo leaves no open slot span (the span closes on leaving running), the place and allowance go back through `#giveBack` (which gives back nothing if another caller started it meanwhile), each start issues a fresh token (the issue command ID carries the new secret's hash), and a crash between the undo and the credential's end leaves an unheld credential that the next start replaces or the attempt's end ends. Three bugs fixed, each with a test on all four backends:
  - *A store-owned attempt looped or waited behind a misleading blocker.* An attempt whose agent's native store is on the refusing host was undone (it can run nowhere else) and then waited for a host that was never asked again, until the blocker told the owner to "bring it back" (the host was not down). It now fails on the refusal with the host's own message, as a pinned attempt does.
  - *The owner's move to a host that refused earlier was never honoured.* A host on the attempt's refusal list was refused by the picker even when the owner had moved the attempt there, so it waited and blocked. A pinned attempt (a move or its store) now asks its one host again, and a refusal there fails it.
  - *`startTries` above 8 broke the bound and the not-again rule.* The record keeps 8 refusals; with a larger setting and more hosts the oldest refusal dropped off, its host was offered the attempt again, and the bound was never reached (the attempt went round the hosts for ever). `startTries` is now held to 1 to 8 (a value that is not a number reads as 3).
  - Not covered by a test that uses the real remote service: the offers-full refusal (32 offers waiting on one host) as a fallback; the dispatcher tests cover it with a typed refusal. Host-announced labels (os, arch, harness) that appear in reasons are checked for length, control characters and keys when announced; bidirectional-text marks are not rejected there (this predates H07b).

## H07b (third slice): hosts are tried by load, and a held poll ends when its client disconnects
- **Host order by load.** The dispatcher now asks the less loaded worker host first (`WorkerHost.load()`, optional): the number of offers made to the host that it has not accepted yet. For a remote host this is `RemoteWorkerService.offerLoad`, the same figure `candidates` already ordered by. Hosts with equal load keep the dispatcher's configuration order (the sort is stable), so a tick chooses the same on every backend. A host with no `load` counts as none; one whose `load` throws is read as none and the fault goes to `onError`. An attempt pinned to one host, or a dispatcher with one host, asks nothing. Nothing else about the choice changed (freshness, refusals, start refusals, the passed-over record).
- **A held poll ends when its client goes.** The worker listener (`server.ts`) now gives the offers call an abort signal that fires when the response closes before it was sent. `RemoteWorkerService.offers(host, session, wait, signal)` ends a held poll at once, frees its place in the table, and counts it in `pollStats().disconnected` (not as timed out or woken); a poll whose client has already gone is not held at all. Before, a dead connection kept its slot for the whole wait (up to 25 s) and the next real poll had to take over from it.
- **Tests.** `api/start-remote-choice.test.ts` (composed through `startController`, product `RemoteWorkerHost`, real listener): r1 first by configuration, then r2 when r1 holds an offer, then r2 again after r2 accepted its offer and r1 did not; a raw HTTP request to the real listener is held, destroyed, and the poll is gone within the test's wait with `disconnected` 1 and `timedOut` 0, and a normal short poll afterwards is not counted. `dispatch/dispatcher-suite.ts` (all four backends): fake loads, tie, lighter host, throwing load read as none, no figure as none. Mutations killed: the load sort disabled (all three tests fail), the signal not passed by the listener (disconnect test fails).
- ASSUMPTION: ties keep the configuration order, not the host ID order that `candidates` uses; the configuration order is what the owner sees and what every earlier test and plan relies on, and it is equally deterministic.
- ASSUMPTION: the load is read once per pick for every host (one in-memory count each), not cached, so each attempt started in a tick sees the offers made earlier in the same tick.
- **Not done in H07b.** The worker process does not run `HostPoller` (the worker package and `start.ts` do not wire it; it needs the worker host process to own a controller URL, a credential and a session, which is the remote worker's own startup card). The placement policy is not checked again at delivery when the host reads its offer (an offer that became refused after it was made is still delivered and judged only by the host; what to do with it, fail it or put it back, needs a decision on the attempt's record). The platform index (`#byPlatform`, filled at connect and at a host's first poll) is never emptied of a revoked host, so `candidates` still lists it and refuses it by status, and it starts empty at a controller restart until each host connects or polls; dropping revoked hosts and filling it at start is not done. Refusal records for hosts passed over by freshness are still not kept on the attempt beyond `hostChoice.passedOver`.
- **Review (clean-context, third slice).** Fixed: a host whose `load()` said `Infinity` was read as no load (the old `Number.isFinite` check) and so was asked first; an endless figure is now the heaviest load (clamped to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, two endless loads tie), and a non-number, negative or NaN figure still counts as none (dispatcher suite test). Added a raw TCP socket test against the real listener: a held poll dropped before any offer ends at once and counts as `disconnected`; a poll dropped while the tick makes its offer leaves the offer in place, the host is handed it once on its next poll, the other host never, and accepting it brings its load to zero (offers are only removed on acceptance, so a reply written to a dead connection loses nothing). Checked and not a bug: a client that leaves while its credential is being checked never reaches a held poll (its connection record is dropped on close, so the login step fails the request before the close listener would be needed); pinned attempts read no load; the per-attempt refusal list keeps every refused host out whatever the order; two attempts started in one tick go to different hosts. Not changed: `load()` (like `refuses()` and `status`) is awaited without a time limit; the remote figure is the controller's own in-memory count, so a remote host cannot report a load or make the read slow. Six mutations (Infinity fix reverted, sort reversed, server never aborts, no abort listener, disconnect counted as woken, `offerLoad` always 0) each failed a test.

## H07b (fourth slice): the platform index follows revocations and is filled at a restart; an offer the policy has since refused is put back at delivery

- **A revoked host leaves the index.** `RemoteWorkerService.candidates` already read each host's status; a host whose identity is `revoked` is now refused that once, with its reason (`host:x is revoked`), and taken out of the platform index in the same step. The next `candidates` call does not look at it at all (`considered` goes down), and a platform with no host left disappears from the index, so the attempt's waiting text says `no connected host runs ...`. A host that is enrolled again connects again and is indexed again by that connect.
- **The index is filled at a controller start.** `RemoteWorkerService.rebuildIndex(by, pageSize?)` reads the hosts on record (`HostService.list`, now also open to the dispatcher's own service principal, as `status` already was), page by page, and indexes every active host that announced an operating system and architecture; a revoked one is left out (and dropped if it was in). It returns how many it newly indexed; a repeat adds nothing. `startController` calls it once after the remote service is built (a failure goes to `onError`; the index then fills as hosts connect, as before). `platformIndex(by)` is a read-only view of the index for the owner and the dispatcher. Being in the index is not being connected: a host that never connected in this run's records is still refused with `has not connected to the controller`, so nothing is started on it by mistake. Sessions are durable records, so a host that was connected before the restart counts as connected again as soon as it is also fresh.
- **The policy is judged again when the host reads its offer.** `#pending` (what `offers` hands the host) asks, for each offer, what the host announced and the placement policy now (the same two judgements `place` makes, `capabilityReasons` and `policyReasons`, with the requirements the placement recorded). If any reason lasts (the policy no longer lists the host, the host cannot do what the attempt needs: the same wording test as `lastingReasons`), the offer is **withdrawn**, not delivered: it and its credential are dropped from memory, the placement ends with `withdrawn before it was delivered, host:x would now refuse it: <reasons>` as its last history entry and `withdrawn: true`, the agent's store is released as for any ended placement, and `pollStats().withdrawn` counts it. Reasons that only pass (not heard from lately) never withdraw: the host is polling, so it is connected, and it judges the rest itself. A policy that cannot be read does not withdraw; since the review it is not delivered either (held for the next poll, see the review entry below).
- **What the dispatcher does with a withdrawn offer (the decision).** The waiting turn is told `cancelled` with `withdrawn: true` (a new controller-only field of `WorkerTurnResult`; the worker's own result is checked field by field and refuses it, tested over the wire). The dispatcher then ends that attempt as `abandoned` with the reasons as its summary and **readmits the task** (`readmit: true`, within the attempts allowed, like a lost attempt), so the task gets a new attempt that is placed by the policy as it stands. A turn that begins to wait only after the withdrawal learns the same from the placement record (`waitForResult`). I did not undo the start in place (as H07b's second slice does for a refusal at the start) because by delivery the dispatcher has already counted the attempt as running with a lease and a model call; ending it and admitting a new one reuses the paths that already exist for a worker that never came.
- **Tests.** `remote/delivery-recheck.test.ts` (all four backends, real remote service and listener): revoked host refused once then gone; index rebuilt by a second service over the same storage (nothing known before, three hosts after, the revoked one left out, a repeat adds nothing, a later revocation dropped by the next rebuild, only the dispatcher may ask, a host that never connected is refused for that); pages (8 hosts, page size 3); a refused offer is not delivered, its placement ends with the reasons, the dispatcher ends the attempt with them, the task has a new attempt that the host is delivered once the policy lists it; a listed host, an unreadable policy still deliver; a worker cannot send `withdrawn`. `api/start-remote-recheck.test.ts` (composed through `startController`, sqlite, real listener and client): a restarted controller has both hosts in the index before anyone connects, a disabled host is refused and dropped, and a third start leaves it out; an offer refused after it was made is not delivered over the wire, the attempt ends with the reasons, and the readmitted attempt waits for r1 and then starts there once r1 is listed again. Mutations killed: the delivery check removed, the revoked drop removed, the rebuild not called at start, the readmit turned off.
- ASSUMPTION: an offer is withdrawn only for a lasting reason; a passing one is delivered (the host is demonstrably connected and judges the rest). (The first version delivered on an unreadable policy; the review changed that to fail-closed-with-retry, below.)
- ASSUMPTION: a withdrawn offer counts as an ordinary lost start (readmit within the attempts allowed) and not as a free retry; an owner who changes the policy back and forth cannot make a task loop for ever. (Review: this holds only when `maxAttempts` is set by the task contract or the owner's dispatcher limits; the dispatcher's default is no limit, exactly as for a lost attempt, so with no limit each policy change back and forth costs one more attempt. Each cycle needs a real policy change, and an unreadable policy now holds the offer rather than withdrawing it, so a failing policy store cannot drive the loop.)
- **Known / not done.** (1) The worker process still does not run `HostPoller`: it needs the worker host process to own a controller URL, a credential and a session, which is the remote worker's own startup card; `HostPoller` is not wired in the worker package or `start.ts` (the controller side, the poll and the handshake are complete and tested with the poller on its own). Not started here because it is a new process entry point with its own configuration and credential handling, not a slice of the controller. (2) A withdrawn offer leaves the agent's native-store claim on that host (as every ended placement does; a removal is reserved for retention), so the readmitted attempt is tied to the same host and waits, with the policy's reason and later an owner blocker, until the owner lists the host again or moves the store. (3) The policy is asked once per offer on every poll that reads it (offers are few: at most 32 per host); a cache is not needed yet. (4) A host that is revoked while it is the only host indexed for a platform is dropped when `candidates` next looks at it (or at the next rebuild), not at the moment of revocation; the revocation itself already stops it authenticating. (5) Refusal records for hosts passed over by freshness are still only in `hostChoice.passedOver`.
- **Review (clean-context, fourth slice).** Fixed: (1) an unreadable policy (or host status) at delivery handed the offer, with its task credential, to the host; `place` refuses on the same failure and the policy is a security boundary (`credentialHosts` names who may hold the credential, `dataHosts` who may hold local-only data), so the offer is now **held**: not delivered, not withdrawn, the failure goes to `onError`, the next poll judges it again (an accept meanwhile is answered `unavailable`). (2) A withdrawal raced an accept: the poll read the placement, awaited the policy, and ended whatever was live, so an offer the host took up meanwhile was ended as "withdrawn before it was delivered"; a withdrawal now ends only a placement that is still `offered`. (3) The accept did not judge the offer again: a host that read the offer before the policy changed could accept it later without polling and start where the policy now refuses; a first accept (state `offered`) is judged like a delivery, a lasting refusal withdraws it (`withdrawn before it was taken up`, the task readmitted, the host told `fenced`), an unreadable policy is `unavailable`. (4) The offer (and credential) was dropped from memory inside the change, before the ending was written: a failed write left the placement `offered` with no offer, so no poll could deliver or withdraw it and the attempt waited for its lease; the offer is now dropped after the write, only for the run that ended, and offers whose ending is being written are not handed out meanwhile (this also covers the owner's `end`). (5) Two overlapping polls each counted the same withdrawal; only the call that ended it counts. (6) Without a policy hook the recheck was skipped altogether; it now judges capabilities and the built-in local-only rule with an empty policy, as `place` does. Tests (`remote/delivery-recheck.test.ts`, all four backends): held on an unreadable policy then delivered; late accept withdrawn; accept during the poll's policy read stays the host's; two polls count once; storage writes failing at the withdrawal (fault injected) hold the offer, the next poll withdraws and the task is readmitted; a raw-socket completion carrying `withdrawn`, `Withdrawn`, an escaped or fullwidth look-alike, a `__proto__` object or a top-level `withdrawn` is refused 400. Checked and not a bug: every ingress of a worker's turn result (`checkResult` own-key allowlist on the wire, the worker host rebuilding the local result field by field) refuses or drops `withdrawn`; `HostService.list` is opened only to the unscoped `service:dispatcher` and returns no credential or address; `platformIndex`/`rebuildIndex` are owner and dispatcher only; a page that fails aborts the rebuild (reported, the index fills on connect); hosts added behind the cursor mid-scan are indexed on connect. Cost (measured, 100 hosts on record): one production policy read (settings, profile and a scan of all principals) is about 0.2 ms in memory and 0.26 ms on SQLite, so 100 hosts with one pending offer each polling every second cost about 26 ms/s; the worst case, a host that never accepts and holds 32 offers, polling at its 100-per-second allowance, is about 0.8 s of reads per second. Not changed: a per-offer cache would delay a policy change at delivery; the accept now judges again anyway, so a cache at delivery is the next step if hosts that hold many unaccepted offers appear. Mutations killed: withdraw-only-offered guard removed, fail-open restored, accept recheck removed, every withdrawal counted, `withdrawn` allowed and carried by `checkResult`, offer dropped before the write.

## H07b (fifth slice): a stop cancels the held poll; an offer nobody took up pins no store; passing reasons are matched whole

What was lacking, found by reading the card against the code: the notes of the earlier slices said "the worker process does not run `HostPoller`". That was out of date: `scripts/remote-host.mjs` and `scripts/remote-worker.mjs` (L05e) already build the host poller and run it in a real worker process. What was really missing was the second half of the acceptance, "exits cleanly on stop": a stop only told the poller to finish after its current request, and that request was the held poll (default 20 s, up to the 25 s limit), so a stopped host kept its request open at the controller until it timed out and took that long to exit.

- **A stop cancels the held request.** `RemoteWorkerClient.connect`, `heartbeat`, `reconcile`, `offers` and `workspaceList` take an optional `AbortSignal` (a `signal` option on `offers`). When it aborts, the HTTP request is destroyed at once (the controller's listener sees the client go: `pollStats().disconnected`, from the third slice) and the call fails with `WorkerRequestError` code `aborted`; a request cancelled before it is sent never leaves; a cancelled request is never sent again (it is a `WorkerRequestError`, which the client does not retry). `HostPoller.run(signal)` passes its signal to each of these, so `stop()` of the host ends the one held request at once and the poller returns. `remote-worker.mjs` runs one stop (a second signal does nothing) and says so and exits 1 if the stop itself fails.
- **An offer that no host took up pins no store (found while reading the withdrawal path).** Placing an attempt claims the agent's native Pi store for that host, and the claim was never undone when the offer was withdrawn before delivery (fourth slice, known item 2): the readmitted attempt was then tied to a host the policy had just refused and waited behind an owner blocker, while the refusal of the store names `moveStore`, which no API operation or chat command exposes (it exists only as a service method). The store record now carries `unused: true` from the placement that created it until the first accept of an offer on it (a record without the field, which is every record made before this, counts as used). While it is unused, `storeOwner` pins nothing (unless another attempt of the agent still waits on the claim), and `place` may claim the store on another host (the claim moves with the placement, `since` is renewed, `moves` is unchanged). Once a host accepts, the store is real there and pins the agent as before; that case still needs the owner to list the host again in the placement setting (reachable in chat as `placement.change`) or an owner move of the store.
- **Passing reasons are matched whole.** `lastingReasons` decided by a substring of the sentence ("has not connected to the controller", and so on), so a lasting reason that merely contained such words (a workspace or harness named after one) read as passing and never opened the owner's blocker. A reason now passes only when it is exactly one of the passing sentences (host name, then the phrase to the end, with the freshness in brackets and the offers count as numbers). The reasons of `refusals`, `place` and the delivery check are all built from those sentences, so nothing real changes; an unforeseen wording now reads as lasting (the safe side: the owner is told) instead of passing.
- **Tests.** `remote/polling.test.ts` (all four backends, real listener and client): stopping a poller whose hold is 20 s returns at once, the controller frees the place and counts `disconnected` 1, `timedOut` 0; a cancelled request fails `aborted`, is counted once by the controller (not retried), and one cancelled before sending sends nothing. `remote/delivery-recheck.test.ts`: the store claim (all four backends: claimed and marked unused, withdrawn, pins nothing, the readmitted attempt starts on the other listed host, the claim moves, an accept clears the mark and the store pins to that host); the passing-sentence unit test. `integration/h07b-idle-worker.test.ts` (real `remote-worker.mjs` process, real bubblewrap; skipped without it unless `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): an idle worker holds exactly one poll (one poll in total, none superseded, none timed out), and SIGTERM ends the program with status 0 well before the hold, the controller counting the client gone, not timed out. Mutations killed: the signal not passed to `offers` (stop tests and the process test fail), the unused mark never cleared on accept, `storeOwner` ignoring the mark, the substring match restored. One mutation (the cancelled request as a plain `Error`) survives and is equivalent: the client's retry then meets the already-aborted signal and fails the same way, so the pre-send check carries the behaviour.
- ASSUMPTION: an unused claim is released by being ignorable (`unused`), not removed: removals are reserved for retention, and a record keeps `since` and `moves` for the owner's history.
- ASSUMPTION: a record made before this change counts as used. It may have been created by a withdrawn offer and pin an agent for nothing, but a wrong "used" only keeps the old, safe behaviour, while a wrong "unused" could let an agent with real conversation state start fresh on another host.
- ASSUMPTION: no new owner control is added by this slice (a stop signal is the operator's, on the host's own machine; the store marker is internal), so the interpreter prompt and the operation list are unchanged. The platform index is still a service view without an operation (`platformIndex`); the owner's host list already shows each host's platform.

- **Review (clean-context, fifth slice).** Fixed (data-critical): the unused claim could put one agent on two hosts. `accept` judged the offer's lease before the policy read and then cleared `unused` on whatever store record it found, without asking whose claim it was. An offer with a lease (an attempt with a time limit) whose lease ran out while the host's accept was in flight is no longer live, so when the dispatcher's stop of it did not land, another attempt of the same agent was placed on a second host and took the unused claim; the late accept then took the first attempt up on the first host (the agent running on both) and even marked the second host's claim as used. The same happens across two controllers whose clocks differ, where the expiry check alone cannot help. The accept's commit now judges the lease again and requires the store claim to be this host's and held by no other attempt, else `fenced`; the worker accepts before it starts anything, so a fenced accept starts nothing. Tests (`remote/delivery-recheck.test.ts`, all four backends): a forced interleaving (the lease runs out during the accept's policy read, the stop is made to fail, the rival is started on B) and a forced two-writer race on the storage (a wrapper of `applyOperation` lets a writer whose clock is ahead place the rival on B just before A's accept is written; the accept loses on the store's expected revision, is decided again and is fenced by the claim alone). Both failed before the fix (accepted; claim B's and marked used). Mutations killed: the claim check removed (the clock-skew race fails on every backend), the claim and lease checks removed (both fail), the pre-send abort check removed (the cancelled-request test fails), `place` ignoring the unused mark (the store-claim test fails), and the start anchor of the passing pattern removed (it survived at first: the unit test now also has lasting reasons that end with a passing sentence after other words). Checked and not a bug: a withdrawal, an end or a relocation always changes the placement in the same commit as the store, so an accept that read the placement before them loses on its revision and is fenced; a record without `unused` stays pinned; `lastingReasons`: every producer of a passing sentence uses a host ID (at most 45 characters, no spaces), the freshness `stale` or `unknown` and an attempt ID, all inside the pattern; abort: `accept` and `complete` never take the stop signal, so a stop cannot cut a result or an accept, an aborted `offers` answer loses nothing (an offer stays until accepted, withdrawn or ended), an aborted reconcile leaves the handshake owed for that session, `#trouble` returns at once when stopping, the abort listener goes with the request. Left: a backup taken while a claim was still unused restores the record as unused even if the host took the store up after the snapshot (the restored conversation store waits for that host by attempt, `restoreWaits`, but another attempt of the agent may then start elsewhere); a downgrade to a build before this slice never clears `unused`.

**What H07b still cannot show offline, and what is left.** Everything in the card's acceptance now has a test: a refused first host starts the attempt on another and says why in the plan and the record (slices 1 to 3), a worker process polls with one held request and exits cleanly on stop (this slice; the Linux and bubblewrap case, the only system the host runs on), a revoked host leaves the index and the index is filled at a start (slice 4), a policy change before delivery withholds the offer (slice 4). Not met offline: nothing of the acceptance, but these were not exercised and are left: (1) the offers-full refusal (32 unaccepted offers on one host) as a start fallback is tested only with a typed refusal in the dispatcher tests, not with 32 real offers; (2) the remote worker has never run on a second physical machine, on macOS or on Windows (the host program refuses off Linux by design, the macOS and Windows sandboxes are separate cards); (3) a taken-up store pinned to a host the policy refuses still waits for the owner to list that host (no chat command moves a store; that is a separate owner-control card, not H07b); (4) `load()`, like `refuses()`, is awaited without a time limit.

## H08b (first slice): the lease watchdog runs in the worker process

- **Moved.** `LeaseWatchdog`, `LeaseLost` and `systemClock` now live in `@nimblenewt/contracts` (`lease-watchdog.ts`) because the worker process (`pi-adapter`) may not depend on `@nimblenewt/worker` (package boundaries). `@nimblenewt/worker` re-exports them unchanged and keeps `killContained`. The monotonic clock is now `performance.now()` (same OS clock as before).
- **Contract.** `ChannelStart.lease?: { leaseMs, graceMs }` (1 s to 1 h; grace up to 10 min): the lease as a duration, never a deadline, so the process counts it on its own monotonic clock from reading the start and a wrong wall clock changes nothing. Parse tests added. A start without a lease runs no watchdog.
- **Worker process.** `runWorker` creates the watchdog at start (`maxLeaseMs` = the lease) and ticks it (`WorkerHooks.lease`: fake clock, tick interval, `terminate`). On loss it closes the relay, answers waiting bridge calls `unavailable`, aborts the root conversation, and the turn's result is `failed` with `lease lost (<reason>): ...`; with no turn running the same result is sent at once. A bridge call or a `run` after the loss is refused with the reason. After the turn has told the host, `quiet()` is set so no termination is needed; otherwise `terminate` runs after the grace (default `process.exit(75)`).
- **Tests.** Two process tests with a fake clock (silent expiry mid-turn, no call leaves afterwards, no termination; wake detected, loss reported, later run refused) and one contract parse test.
- **Remains of H08b:** (1) there is no renewal message on the channel, so today the lease is only the initial duration; needed: a process-to-host `lease.renew` request and host-to-process `lease.ok {leaseMs}` / `lease.fenced` answers (worker calls `sending()` before sending and `renewed()` on the answer, `lost()` on fenced), plus a renewal timer; (2) the controller must send `lease` in the start (host side in `packages/worker` host/local.ts and the controller's remote client) and answer renewals as a duration; (3) fenced answers to bridge calls, checkpoint and publish must call `dog.lost()` (the bridge reply carries no fenced code the process recognises yet); (4) the termination path after the grace is not covered by a test (needs a turn that ignores the abort); `main.ts` takes the default `process.exit(75)`; (5) `supervisor` pulses are not wired (no supervisor message).

### H08b review (2026-10-30): latent issues, named so no host sends `lease` before they are closed (**H08b2**)

The `lease` field of the start message is inert today (no host sends it). Before one does: (1) no renewal exists, so every turn longer than `leaseMs` would be killed as silent; (2) after a loss the relay is only closed for requests in flight: the `compact`, `tell` and `checkpoint` handlers and new relay calls are not gated, so a model call can still leave the process; (3) a forward wall-clock step over 5 seconds counts as a wake (a VM whose clock is corrected after boot would lose its lease at once); (4) `turn()`'s finally calls `quiet()` after every turn, which disarms termination for later hangs; (5) the unsolicited `result` sent when no turn is open is dropped by the host (no waiter), so the loss is not actually received; (6) `process.exit(75)` skips the adapter's cleanup flush.

### H08b3: lease-loss latent issues (2), (4), (5) closed; (1) and (3) stay open (2026-10-30)

- **(2) Done.** `relayFetch` has a `refuse(reason)` latch checked at the top of `call`, before anything is sent; `authorityLost` sets it (then `closeAll` for calls in flight). The `compact`, `tell` and `checkpoint` handlers answer a fault with the request's ID (`the lease ended (reason): refused`) once the dog is lost. No `lease` sent: no change.
- **(4) Done.** `turn()`'s finally calls `quiet()` only when the dog is lost (the turn has then reported and wound down). Under a live lease a clean turn leaves termination armed for any later loss and hang. (The task text said "only if not lost"; the stated aim, not disarming a guard that is still live, requires the opposite condition, which is what is built.)
- **(5) Done.** New process-to-host message `lease.lost {reason}` (contracts parse and type), sent instead of the unsolicited `result` when no turn is open. `WorkerProcess` (host) exposes `leaseLost` and `whenLeaseLost()`; the first reason stands. Nothing in the controller consumes it yet (no host sends `lease`), so wiring the observation to an attempt's fencing remains for the host that first sends a lease.
- **Tests.** pi-adapter `process.test.ts` (new H08b3 scenario; the wake test now expects `lease.lost`), worker `host/process.test.ts` (loss observed with no turn open). The scenario fails without the quiet change (and without the gates).
- **Open (H08b3 remainder).** (1) no renewal exists: a turn longer than `leaseMs` is killed as silent; (3) a forward wall-clock step over 5 seconds counts as a wake, so a clock corrected after boot loses the lease at once; (6) `process.exit(75)` skips the adapter's cleanup flush. No host may send `lease` before (1) and (3) are decided. (All three closed by "H08b remainder" below.)

### H08b remainder: renewal on the channel, the controller sends the lease, fenced answers stop the attempt, termination inside the grace (2026-11-08)

- **Channel.** New messages: process-to-host `lease.renew {id}`; host-to-process `lease.ok {id, leaseMs}` (0 to 1 h) and `lease.fenced {id, reason}`. Parse tests in contracts.
- **Worker process (`pi-adapter` worker/process.ts).** A renewal timer (a third of the lease, at least 1 s) sends `lease.renew` stamped with `dog.sending()`; `lease.ok` calls `dog.renewed(sentAt, leaseMs)` only for an ID it sent and still remembers (at most 4), so a replayed or unknown answer extends nothing; `lease.fenced` calls `dog.lost()` (explicit). A bridge answer with code `fenced` makes the process ask for a renewal at once, and no further bridge call leaves until a renewal sent after that answer is answered (`lease.ok`: the work goes on; `lease.fenced`: stopped; no answer: the lease runs out). This is because the tool bridge answers `fenced` for a frozen attempt too, and a freeze must not end the attempt (the dispatcher's heartbeat is not refused for a frozen attempt).
- **Termination inside the grace (H08b2 (6)).** The watchdog's grace is the host's grace minus a flush share (a quarter, at most 1 s); at the end of it the process closes the conversation store and exits 75 when that finishes or the share runs out, whichever is first. The total stays inside the grace. A turn that ignores the abort keeps the harness from closing, so then the exit comes at the end of the share (tested). The host also ends the process itself `graceMs` after it answered `lease.fenced` or was told `lease.lost`, if it is still there (a stuck event loop cannot tick the watchdog).
- **Wake vs clock step (H08b2 (3)).** `WatchdogClock` has an optional `boot()` (time since boot that counts suspend and is never stepped). With it, sleep is told from `boot` and `mono` as a running total (so the 10 ms steps of `/proc/uptime` do not wear the lease down), and wall-clock steps change nothing. The worker process uses `processClock()`: Linux `os.uptime()` (CLOCK_BOOTTIME); other platforms keep the wall clock.
- ASSUMPTION: on macOS and Windows the wake check stays wall-clock based (macOS uptime is derived from the wall clock; Windows uptime and `performance.now()` are not known to differ by exactly the suspend). A wall-clock step forward of more than 5 s there still ends the lease as a wake; fail-closed, and the platforms are not the first-release sandbox targets for remote leases. Reversible by giving those platforms a boot clock.
- **Controller.** `WorkOrder.leaseMs` (the dispatcher's lease as a duration); `ToolGateway.heartbeat()` and the dispatcher's heartbeat return `leaseMs` beside `until`. `LocalWorker` hands the runtime factory `open(order, call, from, lease)` an `AttemptLease {leaseMs, renew}` whose renewal is the gateway's heartbeat (before the turn has its gateway it fails without saying fenced, so the process's lease simply runs, as the dispatcher's own lease does); also on a recipe restart. The worker host's `localWorkerParts` runtimes take the same `lease` (`HostLease`), put `{leaseMs, graceMs}` in the start (`leaseGraceMs`, default 10 s) and answer renewals (`fenced` error code → `lease.fenced`, other errors → no answer).
- **Remote client.** `RemoteAttempt.heartbeat()` renews the watchdog with the controller's `leaseMs` (only a controller that does not send it has `until` read against the local clock). Every request about the attempt (control poll, checkpoint, publish, artifact listing and file, besides the calls already covered) goes through one path that calls `watchdog.lost()` on a fenced answer.
- **Tests.** contracts parse test; worker `watchdog.test.ts` (wall step ignored with a boot clock, real sleep still a wake, coarse boot clock does not wear the lease), `host/process.test.ts` (renewal answers, no answer on a transient error, host ends the process after the grace, not when it exits by itself, nothing without a lease); pi-adapter `worker/process.test.ts` (renewal counts from the send with a wall clock a year off, replayed/unknown answers, timer, `lease.fenced`, fenced bridge answer gated on the renewal for frozen vs moved, termination of a turn that ignores the abort), `worker/clock.test.ts`; controller `local-worker.test.ts` (lease handed as duration, renewal is a heartbeat, not before the gateway, fenced after the attempt ended), `remote/remote.test.ts` (leaseMs from the controller, fenced control poll/checkpoint/publish/artifacts tell the watchdog); integration `h08b-lease-worker.test.ts` (real sandboxed process: a 1.5 s lease kept for 4.5 s by renewals through the gateway, whose `until` is a year off; a fenced renewal stops the turn as `lease lost (explicit)` and no model call leaves).
- **Leftovers (not part of the card's criteria).** Supervisor pulses (`supervisorMs`) stay unwired: the supervisor's death closes the channel, and bubblewrap's `--die-with-parent` ends the sandbox (not so on macOS). The test composers in `packages/integration` (h12b/h12bf/l05b/h12e/t06b) still drop the 4th `lease` argument, so they run without a watchdog as before; an embedder's `dispatch.local.build` must pass it through to get the lease. No remote worker runtime yet builds a `LeaseWatchdog` around `RemoteAttempt` (the client supports one). A model-relay call that fails gives the process no fenced code, so it triggers no lease check of its own; the next renewal (at most a third of the lease later) does. Whether the relay itself refuses the calls of a fenced attempt was not looked at here.

## M05b notes: meeting desk reads, read-only and recorded per file (partial, 2026-10-30)

Before this slice no chair desk read existed in code (no `meetingRead`, no chair test; `WorkingNoteService` still uses the stand-in grant `notes.chair.read`). Added `packages/controller/src/meetings/desk-reads.ts` (`MeetingDeskReadService`, exported from `meetings/index.ts`; ID prefix `mdr` added to `derivedId`) and `desk-reads.test.ts` (1 scenario per backend, 4 runs).

- **Done.** `read(chair, {commandId, meetingRecordId, deskRecordId})` is allowed only to the current chair of an open meeting, for a desk record of a roster member who has not attended, in the meeting's project; anything else is `forbidden` (present member, other project, missing file, non-chair, ended meeting). The read creates one `meeting-desk-read` record in the same step (occurrence, meeting record, desk record, desk owner, desk revision, sha256 and bytes of title+body, visibility, reader, time), guarded by the desk record's and the meeting record's revisions, before the content is returned. A replayed command returns no content and no second record. `reads(by, {occurrenceId, deskRecordId?})` lists them (owner all; the desk's owner and the reader their own). Tests prove: (a) the service exposes only `read` and `reads`, and desk records are byte-identical in storage after reads; (b) one record per file read, none for unread or refused files, fields as above, absent member sees reads of its desk, another absent member does not; (c) a file revised between two reads has two records with both revisions and different digests.
- **Remains.** Not wired to any caller (no API, MCP tool or chair runtime exists; M05 owns the chair); the chair-change case is only covered by the "current chair" check, not tested; attempted writes through the read path are not a surface here, so "refused and recorded" is not built; the shared-working-notes chair read still uses `notes.chair.read` and no `shared` marker exists in the record; "absent member not woken / attempt undisturbed" and "repeated after a controller restart" are not tested; `reads` is in ID order, not time order.

### M05b review fixes (2026-10-30): chair checks, inspection policy, digest and paging of the desk read

- **Chair checks (HIGH).** `MeetingDeskReadService.read` now requires what every other chair check in `meetings/record.ts` requires: `by.kind === "agent"`, `by.asOf !== undefined` and `inTaskScope(by, meeting.projectId)`, besides being the open meeting's current chair. Tests: a task credential of another project, a principal without `asOf` and a non-agent with the chair's ID are refused and leave no record.
- **Inspection policy and drafts (HIGH).** The owner's text (m00-meeting-experiments.md, rule 12 and the stress-test paragraph): "The 'no' votes on the chair reading an absent member's desk (an owner-decided design, option B, tested there only as a stress test) gave four reasons: private scratch is not settled thinking and may be misread; ..."; the plan (task-plan.md, M05b, C01b) says members cannot read scratch or drafts, and names no exception for the chair. So the text does not explicitly allow scratch or drafts for the chair, and the read is now: drafts are never returned; a private record is returned only to a chair holding the exact `desk.scratch.read` grant (`allowsExactly`, so restrictions apply) and never when the installation inspection policy says `scratch: "denied"` (same policy record `DeskService.#readable` consults). Shared accepted or superseded records need no grant, as before. If the owner wants the chair to read scratch without a grant, that is a one-line change to be decided by the owner.
- **Digest (LOW).** `read` returns `{ id, revision, title, body }` only, so `sha256` and `bytes` cover everything returned.
- **Paging and visibility (LOW).** `reads(by, { occurrenceId, deskRecordId?, after?, limit? })` returns `{ reads, next? }`, default 100, 1 to 500 (else `invalid_command`). Visible to the owner, to the desk's owner for their own desk, and to the roster members and chair of the occurrence's meeting (a later chair sees an earlier chair's reads); other agents see none. This changes who sees what: every roster member, not only the desk owner and the reader, now sees all reads of the occurrence.
- **Test note.** An accepted desk record cannot be revised, so the old "changed between two reads" check became "the same accepted revision read twice gives two records with equal digest"; a draft is revised to accepted before being read. Still not wired to any caller.
## L04c: the dispatcher calls the checked resume and waits for prerequisite tasks (second part, 2026-10-30)
- `DispatcherDeps.resumes` (the `ResumeCheckService` start/commit/advance): an attempt that brings earlier work back (it carries a checkpoint, `resumeFrom`: after a restart or a move) is checked after the route and harness are chosen and before budget and host. The dispatcher starts the check as itself (command ID from the attempt and its checkpoint, so a repeat tick answers the same check), commits it when ready, and starts the attempt only when the check is done. An open, blocked or cancelled check, or a fault in running it, makes the attempt wait: the tick's report shows it as skipped with check `resume` and the reason (a blocked check has opened its own blocker). The model passed is the chosen route split as provider/id; `after` is `restart` when the resume note says the controller restarted, else `continue`. A first start (no checkpoint) is not checked.
- `DispatcherDeps.prerequisites` (the composer reads `ContractService.dependencies` and each prerequisite task's state): a task whose prerequisite tasks are not `done` is skipped with check `dependency` and the open ones named; a wait, not a failure. Checked right after the owner's decisions.
- Wired in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` and `api/start.ts` (`resumes` passed through).
- Tests: `dispatch/resume-dependency.test.ts` (prerequisites wait then start; first start unchecked, blocked and open check wait with reason, ready check is committed and the attempt goes on from its checkpoint).
- Not done (L04c stays planned): workers observing dependencies themselves (`ResumePorts.observe` is still the controller's port), a reviewer agent giving verdicts (`ResumePorts.review`), chat commands, the continuation capture operation for hosts, and an `after: model-change` when the resume is onto a different model than the checkpoint's. Resumes of a pause or suspension lift (as opposed to a restart or move) are not checked here: those attempts keep their place and have no checkpoint to bring back.

## L04c follow-up: review findings on the checked resume and prerequisite waits

- Finding 1 (high): the resume check key now includes the model of the chosen route (attempt, checkpoint, note, model). A re-chosen route is a different command, so the service's digest check can no longer raise `command_conflict` forever.
- Finding 2 (high): before starting, the dispatcher reads the task's current check (`ResumeCheckService.forTask`). A live check that is not one of this attempt's keys is stale and is cancelled with the dispatcher's principal; then the new one starts. If the cancel is refused (for example it is executing) the skip reason says so. New service methods: `forTask`, `checkIdFor`, `retryable`.
- Finding 5 (medium): a cancelled check of this attempt is started again under key `...-rN`, at most 3 restarts (4 checks); then one owner `dispatch_blocked` blocker (`dpa-blk:resume:<attempt>`) and a skip reason that names it. A blocked check is retried by the dispatcher when its blocker is resolved, or when it opened none (review failed, effects uncertain) and has blocked no more than the round limit.
- Finding 6 (medium): `prerequisites` may now return `{ open, dead }`; a cancelled or missing prerequisite is `dead`, the skip reason says "cancelled or missing", and one owner blocker per dependent task is opened (key from the sorted dead set, so every tick gives the same command ID). In-progress prerequisites wait as before.
- Finding 7 (medium): `unavailable` from the dependency read skips the attempt ("dependencies could not be read") and does not fail the tick. An unreadable prerequisite task fails closed through the same path. Not done: a per-tick, per-project cache of the prerequisite scan (`ContractService.dependencies` still scans per waiting attempt); open item.
- Tests: `dispatch/resume-wedge.test.ts` uses the real `ResumeCheckService` (changed route, second checkpoint, cancelled restarts, blocker retry); `resume-dependency.test.ts` covers dead and unreadable prerequisites.

### Open items L04c3

- Finding 3: the resume check is committed before the later admission steps (host, place, budget, grant); if one of them skips the attempt, the commit has already been recorded. The commit should come last, just before the claim.
- Finding 4: a `ready` check is committed even when it holds relevant verdicts (changes judged to matter); the dispatcher should hold such a check for the agent or owner instead of committing it.
- Per-tick cache of prerequisites per project (finding 7, remainder).

## L04c review fixes (dispatcher prerequisites, blocked resume checks, stale cancels)

- **Prerequisites fail closed.** The dispatcher's service principal holds no grants, so `ContractService.dependencies(principal, taskId)` answered "not readable" and every dependent started without waiting. `ContractService.prerequisitesOf(taskId)` now reads the task's active dependency edges and each prerequisite task's state straight from the store (no permission check; a gone prerequisite is `state: undefined`, which the dispatcher reports as `(missing)` and answers with the owner blocker). An unreadable result (the dependent task not found, too many records) throws `unavailable`, which the dispatcher turns into a skip, "dependencies could not be read". Covered through `startController` and a real tick in `api/start-dispatch.test.ts`.
- **Blocked checks without a blocker.** `ResumeCheckService.retryable()` returns true only when the check's blocker is resolved, or, for `effects_uncertain` / `review_failed` (no blocker), when it has blocked fewer than its own `maxRounds` times and `RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` (5 min) x its block count has passed since it blocked. `exhausted()` says no retry is left; the dispatcher then opens ONE owner blocker (`dpa-blk:resume-blocked:<checkId>`, type `dispatch_blocked`) and reports "retries are used up".
- **Stale cancels are not failures.** `ResumeCheckService.cancel` takes an optional `reason: "stale-by-dispatcher"`, recorded as the last history note; `cancelledAsStale()` reads it. The dispatcher marks its own stale cancel (another route took over) and does not count those toward `RESUME_RESTARTS`; the key list has room for 60 such flips. A flapping route A,B,A,B no longer yields a "cancelled 4 times" blocker.
- **Known behaviours (documented, unchanged).**
  - Dispatcher blockers are replayed permanently by their command ID: once the owner resolves a `dpa-blk:resume:<attempt>` (or `dpa-blk:resume-blocked:<check>`, `dpa-blk:prereq:...`) blocker, the same command ID returns the resolved blocker and it is NOT opened again. A repeat of the same problem needs a different key (a new attempt, a different set of dead prerequisites) or the owner assigning the task again.
  - Blocker slots are shared: all of these use type `dispatch_blocked` on the task subject, so they compete for the same per-subject slot/limits as the dispatcher's other `dispatch_blocked` blockers; if the slot is taken, `openBlocker` can fail and the dispatcher only reports the wait (the `.catch(() => undefined)` paths).
  - The stale-cancel acts on `forTask`, the task's one live check, so it can cancel a check a human started on the active pointer (for example through `resume.start`) when it is not one of the attempt's own keys.

## L04c fix: a resume with no captured continuation no longer wedges (2026-10-30)
- Cause (confirmed): after a move or restart the attempt carries `resumeFrom`, so the dispatcher's checked resume started a `ResumeCheck`; with no continuation ever captured for the task (hosts cannot capture them yet) the check blocks at once with `missing_context` ("no complete continuation exists"), and the attempt never started on the new host. Failing tests: H02c move (`start-remote-fencing`) and H02d proof (`start-remote-proofs`, 167 s timeout). It would also wedge any production restart or move of such an attempt.
- Choice: `ResumeCheckService.hasContinuation(by, taskId)` (true when a complete continuation exists); the dispatcher's `#resumeCheck` returns "may start" when it is false, so the attempt starts from its checkpoint exactly as before L04c. No check, no blocker. A continuation that exists is still verified before it is applied (the L04c intent); a fault in asking is a wait. `hasContinuation` is optional in the dispatcher's `resumes` dependency, so fakes without it behave as before. Chosen over an owner blocker because nothing is lost: with no continuation there is nothing to verify, and attempts that never had one keep their old behaviour.
- Tests: no existing test was adapted. New: `start-remote-fencing.test.ts` "a move whose checkpoint has no captured continuation..." (real controller: move completes, no check, no blocker, new host is offered the attempt with the checkpoint).

## U13 remainder: activity.explanations pages

`activity.explanations` now takes `after` (a position, the previous `next`) and `limit` (1-100, default 50), validated as `activity.corrections` is, and returns `{ items, next? }`. Without a step, the cursor is a position in the task's index id list (the worker's own explanations in the order written, then retrospective ones) and `ActivityService.explanationsPage` reads only that page's records from storage. A page may be shorter than `limit` when its steps are in an unavailable range; `next` still advances. With a step, the per-step list (via `bySeq`) is sliced. Order without a step is therefore contemporaneous-then-retrospective rather than a global sort by time. The status view still uses the unpaged `explanations()`.

## H12o notes: commit an approved submission exactly once (2026-10-30, partial)

`packages/controller/src/gate/commit-once.ts` (`commitOnce`, `CommitPort`, `MadeCommit`) and `commit-once.test.ts` (4 suites on 4 backends = 16 tests, through the real gate, review and grant services; the existing 36-test gate suite still passes).

- **Done.** `commitOnce(gate, by, port, {requestId, base, tree, message})` runs: (1) a request already recorded as committed answers from the record; (2) the port looks in the checkout for a commit the request already made and, if its parent and tree equal the approved base and tree, records it, even after the 30-minute permit has run out (restart recovery); (3) otherwise it authorizes (same permit on retry), the port commits and the commit is recorded. Command IDs are derived from the request ID, so repeats replay. A found commit with another tree or base is never recorded and gives `review_invalid` ("a new approval is needed"); a found commit for a request that was never authorized is refused; a changed tree, base or message is refused by `authorize` as before.
- **Not done (dependencies H12n and Q01b are not built).** There is no submission record: the A06 commit request stands in as "the submission" (provisional, named in the code). Not built: tying the commit to a submission ID and opening it from `work.end`, a real `CommitPort` over the worker's `GitBridge.commit` (the worker finds its commit by the `NimbleNewt-Request:` trailer the permit already carries) and calling `commitOnce` from the controller's release operation (workspace `release`), and a real-git end-to-end test of a crash between commit and record. The port is tested with an in-memory fake that crashes after committing.
- **Owner question.** Should a submission that was approved but whose commit was made by a different principal (for example the integrator, P10) be recorded by that principal, or always by the author? Provisional: only the requester or the owner may record.

### H12o review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Concurrency.** `commitOnce` now queues calls per request ID in process; a second concurrent call finds the first's record and returns its commit ID (`alreadyRecorded`). Cross-process exclusion is not provided here: a real `CommitPort` must move HEAD with compare-and-swap (base to new commit only if HEAD is still the base). Documented on `CommitPort`.
- **Recovery by marker, not HEAD.** `CommitPort` gains optional `findByRequest` (trailer in reachable history plus made records for unreferenced commits) and `intend(requestId, tree)`. A real port must write intent before committing and a made record {requestId, sha} before moving HEAD. The service prefers `findByRequest`. The authorize command ID now includes the permit generation (`permitUntil`, "first" before any); the gate still refuses an authorize after an expired permit without a new review, so a full re-approval flow after expiry is not built (it needs the gate to accept a fresh review for the same request).
- **Approval re-check.** New `CommitGateService.approvalStands(by, requestId)` (external approval stands; review must be approved or used, not denied/withdrawn/missing). Recovery asserts state `authorized`, tree equals the approved tree and the approval stands before recording; otherwise `review_invalid` and the commit stays unrecorded. A used review cannot be withdrawn by the review service, so the recovery refusal is tested with a gate stub; the gate method is tested with a real withdrawn review. There is no separate contributor-withdrawal flag in the gate; H05 contributor withdrawal appears as a withdrawn review.
- **Tree check and docs.** The port's `commit` result now carries `tree`; a tree other than the approved one is refused (`review_invalid`) and not recorded. Doc corrected: the record steps are the requester's or the owner's, `authorize` is the requester's only.
- Tests: 4 new suites x 4 backends (commit-once now 32 tests, all pass; the 16 new fail without the fix).
## H12p (part 1): the worker's three-way re-apply of an agent's work (2026-10-30)
- Done: `GitBridge.reapply({shared, commit, gitDir, checkout})` in `packages/worker/src/workspace/git.ts`. The agent's work is its net difference from the base (committed or not, ignored files included, mode-only changes not counted). Against `commit` (the landing-branch head): only-agent files stay (`kept`); only-landing files are written or deleted in the checkout (`taken`); files both changed are merged with `git merge-file --diff3` (`merged` when clean). Overlapping edits keep conflict markers (`- Remains for H12p: (1) the agent's `work.refresh` tool and its controller path: no `work.*` tool or H12n ending exists yet, so nothing calls `reapply`; it should go through the H12l/H12m workspace service (`refresh` operation) with no quiesce (the agent does it itself) and put the returned lists into the workspace record's `detail`; (2) the refresh-round count on the submission (needs the submission record of Q01b/P10, not built), the per-project cap (default 3) and what follows the cap; (3) a write that fails midway through the file writes (disk fault) leaves the checkout partly updated with the base not yet moved; the next refresh re-plans from the old base and is safe for files not yet written, but a taken file already written would then appear as agent work (a retry merges it as equal content, so no loss).
- Owner question (provisional): when one side deleted a file and the other changed it, the agent's side is kept (deleted or changed) and the file is listed; the owner may prefer the landing side to win.

## H12p (part 1) review fixes: `GitBridge.reapply` (2026-10-30)
- Writes no longer follow links: each file is opened `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW` (truncated only after the checks), then `fstat` is compared with `lstat` (`sameFile`), `nlink` must be 1 and the real parent must still be the resolved one; a swap is refused as `link_refused`. Test hook: the optional `hooks.beforeOpen` runs between the path check and the open.
- Plan before write now holds: all content is prepared in a private directory under the git directory, every target is resolved and checked (directory at a target, collision, hard link, file where a directory is needed), and the parent directories are made before the first file is written. A refusal on the last file changes no earlier file. A file already holding the markers `- Modes: a landing file keeps its mode (100755 kept; chmod after write); a mode-only change by the agent counts as its work (listed in `kept`, kept when the landing branch changes the content). A landing change to a symlink or submodule entry is refused (`link_refused`).
- Taken files are streamed from `git cat-file blob` to a file, with no size cap; only files both sides changed are read into memory and checked against the cap.
- `both-added` with different content keeps the agent's side without markers (as documented). When the base already is the commit, nothing is done at all, so the agent's own unrecorded commits are not reset.
- Tests in `workspace/git.test.ts` (6 new, 26 total in that file; worker workspace tests: 40, 39 pass, 1 skipped as before).
## Q01b: submission kinds by role (service slice, 2026-10-30)
- `SubmissionService` (`submissions/submissions.ts`, record kind `submission`, ID `sbm-...` derived from the caller-scoped command ID, so a repeat records once and a reused ID with other content conflicts). `record(by, {taskId, kind, role, ...})` writes one record per submission attempt; `get` reads one (owner, or the agent that made it; others get nothing).
- Kinds and roles (`KIND_ROLES`): code -> author, review -> reviewer, qa -> qa, document -> docs, signoff -> director. The agent must hold the role it names (checked by an injected `rolesOf`, the controller passes `agents.rolesOfPrincipal`), and a role may submit only its own kinds. Owner and non-agent principals are refused (they hold no role); the agent needs `task.read` on the task and, with a task credential, only its own task.
- A code submission requires `base`, `tree` (git object IDs) and `patchId`, and records `refreshRound` (default 0). A non-code kind is refused if it carries `base`, `tree` or `patchId` ("makes no commit"); every record has `makesCommit: false`. Review, qa and signoff name a `subject` (a code or document submission of the same task) and copy its `tree`/`patchId`/`artifactDigest`, so a verdict is bound to the exact tree and patch it was given (P09 can compare patch-ids). A document submission names `artifactDigest` (and optionally `artifactId`).
- Evidence `[{check, result: pass|fail|not_run, boundTo}]` must be bound to the submission's tree (or the artifact digest); evidence for any other tree or digest rejects the whole submission.
- A director sign-off on a submission whose submitter is the same agent is refused.
- Tests: `submissions/submissions.test.ts` (5 cases x 4 backends = 20).
- Not done: state API operations (`submission.record`/`get`, docs) and wiring into `start()`; listing by task; numbering of attempts and refresh rounds across attempts (the round is supplied, not checked against P08/P10); checking `base` against the project's landing head and `patchId` against the real diff (needs the workspace layer, P08); Q01 states (draft/submitted/under-review/accepted) and review-state invalidation; checking evidence against real check runs (P09).
- Owner questions (provisional choices): (1) `KIND_ROLES` is fixed in code; should it be settable by profile/policy? The integrator submits nothing here (it writes no content, P10). (2) Review of one's own work is left to H05; only the director sign-off rule is enforced here. (3) A sign-off may be about a code or document submission, not a review or qa report.

## H12n slice 1: the ending order, records and rules (partial; 2026-10-30)

- **Done** (`packages/controller/src/work-end/`): `WorkEndService` with `request` (agent only, own attempt only; shape checked; one durable ending intent per attempt; the attempt frozen after the intent is written), `complete` (settle, kill hung calls, stage and open the submission, tell, finish; once per attempt, concurrent calls share one run), `drop` (emergency stop), `recover` (restart completes each open ending once) and `get`. The pure rule `overlapOf`: a submit is refused (`SubmitRefused`, carrying the head commit and the overlapping files) only when the base is stale and a changed file was also changed on the landing branch; a plain end is never refused. An owner stop (or an attempt that is no longer live) drops the intent with nothing staged. A killed write call, a failing submission or a controller with no submit port turns the submit into a plain end with a `runtime_hold` blocker and the typed reason `release_failed` / `submit_unavailable` on the record.
- **Ports, not real services:** the attempt control (get, freeze, settle, finish), the landing read (files changed by the agent and since the base), staging and submission are `WorkEndDeps` ports. Tests use the real storage, command runner and `BlockerService` on both backends, with fake ports (33 tests, in `work-end/work-end.test.ts`).
- **Remains:** (1) bind the ports: `DispatcherService` (freeze/settle with a kill reason and a report of which killed calls were writes, finish with a result; `stop` today only ends `abandoned`), the Git bridge for the landing diff and staging, Q01b submission records for `submit`; (2) register `work.end` as an agent tool and an API operation (then `api:docs:write`); (3) call `recover` and `complete` from the dispatcher tick; (4) make the owner stop and emergency stop call `drop` (today they act on the dispatcher only); (5) real-dispatcher test with a call in flight (built 2026-11-26: see "H12n real-dispatcher settle test" at the end of these notes).
- **Owner questions / provisional choices:** the values of `result` are `done`, `blocked`, `partial`, `abandoned` (the card names the field only; what should it be and what does each do to the task?). The typed blocker `release_failed` is recorded on the ending and carried by a `runtime_hold` blocker whose summary starts with it, because `BlockerType` has no such type; add one? A stale base with no overlapping file may submit (the card says refuse only when overlapping).

## H12n slice 1: review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Steps are recorded as they happen.** The intent record carries `steps` (`settled`, `submitted{submissionId | typed/summary/blocker}`, `told`, `finished`); each is written (revision-checked) right after its effect, and `complete`/`recover` resume from the first undone step. Ports get a stable key per step (`workend:<attempt>:submitted|told|finished`; `submit`, `tell` and `finish` take it as a last argument and must be replay-safe). If the attempt is no longer live but `finished` is recorded (or the run had already begun and nobody stopped the attempt), the ending is recorded `done` with the stored submission, not dropped.
- **Drop racing complete.** Before submit, tell and finish the intent is re-read; `dropped` aborts with no side effect. A drop that lands after a submit keeps the drop but records the submission and says so in `summary`. Record writes retry on a stale revision and annotate a dropped record rather than overwrite it.
- **One runner per intent.** `complete` first writes a claim (`{epoch, instance}`, revision-checked, state `ending`). A claim by another instance in the same or a newer epoch is `unavailable` ("busy", retryable; `recover` skips it); an older epoch's claim is taken over. Record-write command IDs now carry the revision, so a replayed write cannot pass for another instance's.
- **Overlap re-check.** After settle, before submit, `landing` is read again; a new overlap (or an unreadable checkout) ends plainly with the new typed reason `submit_refused` and a blocker.
- **Request replay.** `frozen` is recorded; a replayed request on a still-`requested`, unfrozen intent retries the freeze. A replay whose submit/result/note/message differ is `command_conflict`. The two `release_failed` blockers use distinct keys (`:release_failed:settle`, `:release_failed:submit`).
- Limits: a restart is assumed to bring a higher epoch (a claim by the same epoch but another instance is busy). The "no longer live, never stopped, begun" resume trusts that only this ending ends the attempt. Tests that failed-before were checked by reasoning, not by a clean old-code run.
