- **Tests.** backup/encryption-review.test.ts (appended chunk; bounds; size caps; manifest field by field, MAC removed, skipped list; retention with forged and renamed manifests; unlock flag on a plain backup and `--allow-plain`; no parser text; setup rollback; link, pipe, directory, size; warnings and fingerprint; pin and rekey), encryption.test.ts (the downgrade and memory-bomb cases now assert the specific `SealedFileBad`; the never-failing assert replaced by a byte comparison), api/start-backup-encryption.test.ts (pin across restarts, rekey owner only, status).

## V02c: the supervisor recovery action ladder (smallest slice)

- What it is: the ordered recovery actions on a stall concern, lowest rung first: `nudge` (a controller notice to the agent working the task), `rebrief` (a new brief, same channel), `reassign` (to another agent), `pause` or `stop` the agent, `hand-to-owner`. A concern climbs them one rung at a time; a rung taken is not taken again. `StallService.recover` (API `recovery.step`) takes the step.
- Who: the same people who may decide the concern (owner; holder of `assignment.manage`; the supervisor it was routed to; the current escalated holder while it can see the task). The task's own owner never acts on its own concern. The existing services then check the caller's own rights again (pause/stop `authorizeControl`; reassign needs `assignment.manage` on the task).
- Setting (owner only, `RecoveryLadderService`, record `recovery-ladder-settings/main`): `levels` = allowed actions at escalation level 0, 1, 2 ... (at most 16, `[]` clears), `owner` = allowed actions while the owner holds the concern, `enabled` = whether agents may take steps at all (default on), `autoStep`/`autoStepMinutes` = whether the controller takes the next rung by itself when nobody answers (default off; see "Automatic stepping" below). API `recovery.ladder.get/set/enable/disable` with `expectedRevision`; chat `recovery.ladder.set` and `.enable` (propose), `.disable` (apply, it only narrows). Damaged record: steps are refused.
- Defaults (provisional): level 0 nudge, rebrief, hand-to-owner; level 1 and up add reassign and pause; owner level everything including stop. Agents must take exactly the next allowed rung above the last step; the owner is exempt from the level lists and the on/off switch but may only go up (any higher rung).
- Record: the concern gains `recoveryRung` and `recoverySteps` (last 20: n, action, by, at, level, text, to, warnings). Dropped when the route changes or the concern reopens (new episode). `hand-to-owner` parks the concern with the owner and has the owner told once (same notice path as a climb).
- Replay/crash safety: the effect runs inside the command that records the step, under a key made from the actor's command id; a repeat of the command is answered as recorded and does nothing again; a failed effect records nothing and the rung stays. Bounded: at most 6 rungs, 500-character text, 5 warnings.
- Reassign uses the meeting reassign applier (`reassignApplier` in `api/start.ts`, now shared): moved at once, a new holder lacking `attempt.work`/`task.read` is warned about (owner notice) and the warning is also kept in the step. A task with a running attempt is refused (use a hand-off), as in the meeting path.
- Remains: no per-project ladder. (Chat for the step itself and for answering a concern: see the review below.) (Fixed since: pause/stop act on the task, the nudge goes to the pinned agent, and the effects wiring has end-to-end tests in `api/v02c-recovery-ladder.test.ts`.)
- Owner questions: (1) should `disable` need a proposal like the rest? (2) answered by the review fixes: pause and stop act on the task. (3) answered by the ASSUMPTION below: the owner is not held to the rung order.

### V02c: automatic stepping (timed, controller-driven) (2026-11-07)

- **What.** `StallService.autoStep(by, { afterId?, limit? })`, run by the dispatcher's tick (loop `recovery.auto-step` in `dispatch/loops.ts` `recoveryLoops`, fed the stall service by `api/start.ts`; renews the dispatcher principal each tick and needs the scan right, `recovery.stall-scan`; without it the loop takes nothing and the scan loop's "stall detection is not running" notice already tells the owner). A suspected concern held by an agent (the supervisor it was routed to, or the agent it climbed to) whose holder has not answered for `autoStepMinutes` gets the next rung that holder is allowed, one rung per concern per interval. The wait counts from the latest of the concern's last change (opened, reopened, re-routed, a recovery step) and its last climb, so a new holder gets the full interval and a manual step restarts it.
- **Setting.** `recovery.ladder.set` gains `autoStep` (true/false, default off: absent = off) and `autoStepMinutes` (1..10080, null = the default); `recovery.ladder.get` shows `autoStep`, `autoStepMinutes`, `autoStepDefaultMinutes`. Fields left out stay. Chat: the same `recovery.ladder.set` (propose in every profile, so switching it on is shown first); the chat verb names `autoStep`/`autoStepMinutes` and what they do, and the interpreter's prompt is generated from `CHAT_OPS` and `acceptedArgs`, so it lists both (tested). The owner says it in any words ("when nobody answers a stuck agent for an hour, let the controller take the next recovery step by itself"): no fixed phrase, no ID.
- **Rules (the same as a manual step).** The step goes through `recover` in the HOLDER's name with the holder's own effective rights (read fresh from the principal record): the own-concern guard, `#mayRead`, the holder's own level list (`actorLevel`, the same function the manual path now uses), the agents' on/off switch (`enabled`: off means no concern is even read), `minGapMinutes`, the rung order, the two-phase pending/effect/done record. The effects run as the holder, so the pause and stop services check the holder's own right to control the task; the controller can never do what the holder could not. The owner's own rungs (the `owner` list, `stop` by default) are never taken: a concern held by the owner (handed to it, climbed to it, or routed to it) is never stepped. `reassign` is always passed and recorded as skipped ("the automatic recovery steps never choose who takes the task over; a person must"). A rung the holder cannot take (`unavailable`) is passed and recorded as for a manual step, but only when a later allowed rung can be taken; otherwise nothing is taken. An effect refused as `forbidden` (for example a nudge to an agent that can no longer be told) passes the rung, recorded with the reason, for an automatic step only (left free, it would be begun and refused again every tick). Re-checked under the revision guard of the begin: still suspected, still held by this holder, automatic stepping still on, the wait over.
- **Stops** when the concern is decided (confirmed or dismissed: the answer), clears, re-routes (starts again), or is handed to the owner. A step begun before an answer whose effect is not yet made is not made: just before the effect the concern is read again, and if it is no longer suspected the step is recorded as skipped ("answered ... nothing was done"); a skipped hand-to-owner hands nothing. Residual: an answer committed between that read and the effect call itself (one storage read apart) does not stop that effect; the step was begun before the answer.
- **Replay, crash and race safety.** The step's command ID is `auto-<sha256(concern|rung|reopened|recoveryGen|revision read)>` (scoped to the holder), the effect key is the existing one (concern, rung, episode, reset counter). Two ticks or two controllers on one concern read the same revision: one begin commits, the other loses on the revision guard (or replays the same command); a repeated effect carries the same key. A step begun and not finished (a crash after the effect, or a failing effect) has `recoveryPending.auto`; the next call finishes it at once, without a new interval, in the name it was begun in and under the same effect key, so the effect is made once. Steps and pending steps are marked `auto: true`.
- **Bounds.** Off (or `enabled` off): nothing is read. On: one page of concern records per call (`limit` default 100, at most 500) from a cursor kept in memory by the loop, at most 5 pages a tick, at most 20 steps or refusals per call (a backlog after an outage is worked off over several ticks); a due concern waits at most one lap of the cursor. At most 6 rungs per concern episode. No notice is added: the effects themselves (the nudge, re-brief, pause notice) are keyed per rung, and hand-to-owner tells the owner once through the existing escalation notice.
- **Clock.** The stall service now reads `options.stall.clock` (new in `StartOptions.stall`), else the dispatcher's clock (`options.dispatch.clock`), else the system clock, so the tick and the concern times agree.
- ASSUMPTION: the provisional default interval is 240 minutes (4 hours) when the owner switches automatic stepping on without a time: with the default ladder (nudge, re-brief, hand-to-owner at level 0) a concern reaches the owner in about 12 hours; with all six rungs at least a day, the default wait at each supervisor. The owner changes it with `autoStepMinutes` in chat.
- ASSUMPTION: the owner is not held to the rung order (smallest, reversible: no change): the owner may take any rung above the last one, may not go back down, and is not held to the level lists, the switch or the gap. The automatic stepping never acts as the owner.
- ASSUMPTION: the automatic stepping acts in the holder's name (recorded `by` = the holder, `auto: true`), with the holder's rights, under the owner's standing setting; it never acts on a concern the owner holds and never chooses a reassignment target.
- **Tests.** `health/stall.test.ts` (all four backends: reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker, PostgreSQL), fake clock: off by default reads nothing; on, one rung per interval and each only after its full interval; in the holder's name, marked automatic; reassign passed; stops at the owner and the owner's notice is owed once; agents' steps switched off take nothing; the level list bounds it (the owner's stop never taken; an unavailable rung with nothing after it takes nothing); an answer stops it; owner-held, owner-routed and disabled-holder concerns are not stepped; a crash after the effect is finished by a restarted service under the same key, once, without a new interval; an answer while a step is pending is recorded as skipped and makes no effect; a forbidden effect passes the rung once and writes nothing while the next waits; two services and three concurrent calls take exactly one rung per interval. `api/v02c-recovery-ladder.test.ts`: through `startController` with the dispatcher's fake clock and real effects: off by default, switched on in free-form chat (proposed, nothing until applied, other fields kept), the dispatcher's tick takes nudge then pause (the task really paused with the supervisor's own right), passes reassign, hands to the owner (told), nothing more; and the interpreter prompt lists `autoStep, autoStepMinutes` with the verb.
- **Second check's test gaps closed (2026-11-08).** The clean-context double-check found no bugs and four untested lines; each now has a test that fails under its mutant: (1) a holder the concern climbed to gets the full interval from the climb (`autoSince`'s `escalatedAt` term; a climb does not move `lastChangedAt`): level 0 nudge at 4 h, climb at 28 h, the new holder's re-brief at 32 h, not 28 h (`health/stall.test.ts`); (2) a manual hand-over is announced as "handed to you by agent:..." (`api/v02c-recovery-ladder.test.ts`); (3) at most 20 steps a call and the cursor after the 20th, 26 due concerns stepped once each over two calls (also caught: the cursor set to the unstepped row); (4) the loop's per-tick paging: pages read until one steps or refuses, at most five, the next tick goes on from there and wraps (`dispatch/loops.test.ts`; also caught: five rounds raised to ten). Follow-up, not fixed (no small safe fix): an automatic step left pending stays pending when automatic stepping or agents' steps are switched off (`autoStep` returns before finishing it, and finishing it would make an effect the owner just switched off), when the holder it was begun for loses its identity, or when the holder loses sight of the task after a climb. Nothing else is stepped on that concern meanwhile; the owner can replace it with another rung through `recovery.step` (also in chat), which is the way out. A later card may finish such a step as skipped ("automatic stepping was switched off") without its effect.
- **State (2026-11-08, after the review and the second check's test gaps).** Built, reviewed and tested. Runs on the head: NIMBLENEWT_TIER unset (all four backends) api + health + chat + status + dispatch/loops 1550/1550; `NIMBLENEWT_TIER=typical` api 313/313; `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` 74/74; `roadmap:check`, `check:deps` ok; `api-docs` unchanged. The clean-context double-check is done (no bugs; its four test gaps closed above).
- **Review (2026-11-08, single reviewer-and-fixer).** (1) Owner controls by chat: a stall concern could not be read, answered or stepped by the owner at all through the API or chat (`stall.decide` had no operation; `recovery.step` was API only). Added `stall.concerns` and `stall.concern.get` (queries, the service's own read rules) and `stall.decide` (command), and chat ops `recovery.step` (propose in every profile: it acts on work) and `stall.decide` (profile mode: it changes no work), both with a new chat revision kind `concern` read for the owner (`stall.concern.get`); `concernId` is a record reference and a step's `action` a fixed choice, but its `text` must be the owner's own words. The interpreter prompt lists both (generated from `CHAT_OPS`, tested). (2) False statement to the owner: a concern handed to the owner by a recovery step was announced as "waited too long for its supervisor to decide"; the needs-you item now says it was handed over by that agent, or by the automatic recovery steps because the named holder did not answer in time. Tests: `api/v02c-recovery-ladder.test.ts` (chat list/step/answer with the revision filled, made-up words refused, hand-to-owner shown first, a reader with no part sees nothing; the automatic hand-over's notice text). Mutation checks (each caught): notice wording reverted; concern revision not filled; the step's action exemption removed; the step applied without proposal; the automatic stepping not passing over reassign when choosing. Checked and left: the climb timer of a level-0 concern restarts on each recovery step (it counts from `lastChangedAt`; pre-existing, and the concern reaches the owner by the ladder anyway); an automatic step left pending by a holder that has since lost its identity stays pending until the owner replaces it (`#agentPrincipal` refuses to act for it).
- **Next steps from a cold start.** (1) In the worktree: link `node_modules` (a real directory whose entries link to the main checkout's, except `@nimblenewt/*`, which link to this worktree's `packages/*`; the same in `packages/integration/node_modules/@nimblenewt`), then `npx tsc --build --force`. (2) Run, NIMBLENEWT_TIER unset, from `packages/controller`: `node --import <abs>/scripts/offline-guard.mjs --test --test-timeout=600000 dist/api/*.test.js dist/health/*.test.js dist/chat/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/dispatch/loops.test.js` (expect all pass), then the api files with `NIMBLENEWT_TIER=typical`. (3) If green, the card's clause is met (an unanswered escalation climbs one rung at a time, each recorded): add the `V02c` entry before `C07h` in `scripts/generate_task_plan.py` `progress` (format of `H12e`, commits = the V02c automatic-stepping SHAs), run `python3 scripts/generate_task_plan.py`, `npm run roadmap:write`, `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs`, commit the plan files separately.
- **Mutation checks** (each change made, the tests failed, restored): on by default; no wait (tick and guarded write); answered concerns stepped (tick and guarded write); agents' switch ignored (tick and recover); a pending automatic step not resumed; the answer-before-effect re-read; reassign not passed; owner-held concerns acted for; a forbidden effect left free; acting as the scanner instead of the holder; the loop not running; the chat verb without the setting; the stall service off the dispatcher's clock; a skipped hand-to-owner still parking the concern. Survived, and why: removing the last step's time from the wait (equivalent: the done-mark sets `lastChangedAt` to the same time); removing the derived command ID, the begin's revision check and the done-mark's key check together (the storage's own revision check on every update still lets one begin win; the race test was checked to be really concurrent: all three calls enter `recover` and one step is recorded).

- Review fixes (2026-10-30): (1) pause and stop act on the concern's TASK (task scope), never the agent scope (which needed an `agt-` ID and paused the agent's other work); the agent the concern is about (`stalledAgent`) is pinned on the concern when it is opened (or at the first step for older records) and used for nudge/re-brief and the own-concern guard, not whoever holds the task after a reassignment. (2) A supervisor may reassign (the ladder, set by the owner, is the authority; no `assignment.manage` needed); a task with a running attempt moves by a prepared hand-off (the attempt is suspended and the package collected; the step warns that the hand-off must be completed); the audit reason says "recovery step". A rung the actor cannot take (the service says so: no right to pause, no agent to nudge) or that a service refuses on a precondition (forbidden, invalid_transition, not_found) is passed and recorded as skipped with the reason, so the ladder can always go on; a rung that can be taken must be taken first. (3) The allowed rungs come from the ACTOR's own level (the routed supervisor 0, a holder its climb level, a manager the concern's level, never above it); the owner is not held. (4) Two phases: the step is recorded as pending (with an effect key from concern, rung and episode, not the command) under the revision guard, the effect is made, then the step is marked done; a retry under any command finishes the pending step (other callers may not finish another's, the owner may, or drop it by asking for another action). (5) A confirmed concern handed to the owner is told to the owner once (the notice loop includes it). (6) `minGapMinutes` in the recovery ladder setting (chat-settable through `recovery.ladder.set`; absent/0 = no gap, the default; the owner is not held); one owner notice per concern per episode stands (`notifiedAt`). (7) A repeat of a recorded command is looked up before any check, so it is answered as recorded after the setting is switched off or rights are lost. Open: when two actors race on the same pending step the effect may be repeated once under a second actor's scope (services scope command IDs by actor).
### Quiet-host and scratch-cleanup: second review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Checkpoint must cover the attempt's last activity.** `checkpointVerdict` / `checkpointByAttempt`: besides "by the attempt's agent, at or after its start", the checkpoint's `capturedAt` must be no older than the attempt's last sign of life (last heartbeat; else the end time) minus `CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_MS` (2 min). The dispatcher records no time of the last write, the heartbeat is the nearest signal (provisional). A checkpoint at start+1 min followed by hours of work and a crash keeps the scratch; the reason is recorded (`older than the attempt's last activity`).
- **Quiet hosts: one stale sample moves nothing.** A not-fresh sample counts (breaks a recovery run, opens an episode, moves work) only when the host is genuinely unheard: `now - lastSeenAt >= quietAfterMs`; a run in progress is also a bar to moving. The "last look" before a move applies the same test.
- **Move budget.** The 10-move budget is charged only for moves made. Attempts that cannot move (no host, changed, transient) are bounded by a separate per-pass try count (`attemptsPerPass`, 60). The start of the move stage and of the pending-finish stage rotates per pass (in memory), so a host with many unmovable attempts does not starve another.
- **Cursor.** Kept in memory, saved after the batch, and written only at a reset to the start of the list or every `cursorEvery` (20) passes; an exception for one host no longer stops the others (the first one is rethrown after the batch and the cursor).
- **Episode notice.** A new episode with a timer ("moves after Xh") always sends its notice, once per episode (it bypasses the notice interval); with automatic moves off the interval still holds it back. The "cannot move" notice is held back by the notice interval at most `graceHours`.
- **Scratch: states.** The cleanup record now exists (`deciding`, listed) before anything that can throw is read (`begin`), so the sweep can always retry it (`ports.decide` rebuilds the decision). `awaiting-stop`: everything else is in order but the worker never confirmed it stopped; the sweep re-asks (`ports.workerStopped`, a repeat host release via `DispatcherService.confirmStopped`) every 5 min and orders once confirmed. After the owner's patience (`cleanup` setting `awaitStopHours`, default 24, 1..8760, `null`/`disable` = never tell; chat-settable like `scratch`) the owner is told once (`scratch-stuck:<attempt>`); the scratch stays and the record stays open.
- **Scratch: order claim.** Before an order, the record is claimed with a revision-guarded lease (`SCRATCH_LIMITS.leaseMs` 5 min, longer than the order's own time limit `orderMs` 2 min); a second run or sweep does not send the same order. The sweep runs the same `before` (dropped-ending) check. A host answer `busy: true`, or no answer in time, leaves the record `ordering` (the lease is given up, retried, at most 20 times then kept); a later answer never overwrites a `removed`.
- **Scratch: attempt-unique contract.** `ScratchOrder` carries `attemptId`, `hostId`, `generation` and `key = scratch:<attemptId>`; the host MUST derive the scratch location and the idempotency from the attempt, never from the task alone, so a replay for an older attempt cannot touch a successor's scratch. Stated in the type's doc and tested with a per-attempt fake host.
- **Ended hook.** The dispatcher passes an `AbortSignal` that is aborted at the hook's timeout; `cleanupAfterEnd` starts nothing more once it is aborted (the sweep finishes the record). `shutdown()` waits (bounded by the hook timeout) for the hook calls still running.
- **Late checkpoint (LOW 10).** `DispatcherService.#checkpoint` discards a checkpoint that returns after the attempt's worker was replaced or its host changed (the move committed meanwhile); it is neither handed to the checkpoint hook nor returned.
- **SAFE_OUT (LOW 11).** Letters, marks and digits of any script, spaces (not collapsed) and `. _ - / \ : @ + = , ~ # % ( ) [ ] ' & $ ! ;` survive in host text; control characters become spaces, everything else (double quote, backtick, angle brackets) `?`. The message framing (delimiter, numbered lines) is what prevents forging.
- **ordersHostMove (LOW 13).** `take`/`pull` order a move only when what is taken is the work (`work`, `attempt(s)`, `task(s)`, `everything`): "take the work off host:r1" yes, "pull the logs from host:r1" / "take a backup from host:r1" no.
- **Known limits (LOW 12).** The crash-loop controller (a controller that keeps restarting) never judges hosts: each restart resets `upSince`, so no host is warned until it has run for the quiet threshold. That is intended (a restart is not evidence about hosts) and means a controller that restarts more often than every 5 minutes never moves work.
- **Revoke replays (LOW 14).** Revoke records written before the running-call total fix (T02b review fixes, commit 5121b0e) could carry `runningCalls: null`. The feature was added (dad6c52) and fixed in the same unreleased series: no release and no tag contains it, so no such record can exist outside a developer's own store; no migration was added.
- The sweep's `before` check keeps scratch when the attempt's ending was dropped (it cannot tell which path began the record); `cleanupAfterEnd` itself still cleans up after a dropped ending under the usual conditions. So a crash between a stop and its cleanup leaves that scratch kept (safe side).


## P04d (part 1): coverage and a settable coverage-lapse alert

- `CoverageService` (`projects/coverage.ts`): for a project, the active responsibilities with a coverage gap. Reasons: `no-holder` (no `ownerId`, or the holder's principal is missing or disabled, or its agent is retired), `no-recent-check` (none since creation, or the last older than twice the period: the same rule as `observed`, so silence is never counted as covered), `unscheduled` (no check schedule). Each gap carries the earliest `since`, the minutes lapsed and `beyondPeriod`. Paused and retired responsibilities are not listed. Read: query `responsibility.coverage` (`projectId`, `afterId`, `limit` 1..100 default 50, paged by responsibility ID; needs `responsibility.read`, a project the caller cannot read looks the same as none).
- Setting `CoverageSettingsService` (global, one record): `enabled` (default **off**) and `afterMinutes` (1..525600, default 1440 when on). Owner-only API: `coverage.settings.get` and `coverage.settings.set` (`enabled`, `afterMinutes` or null for the default, `expectedRevision`, command ID replay). Chat: `coverage.settings.set` in `CHAT_OPS`, mode apply (it only tells the owner, and is reversible); no revision lookup yet, so a chat edit is last-writer-wins. A damaged stored record is `unavailable` on read and does not stop the other loops; setting it again repairs it.
- Alert: loop `responsibilities.coverage` (a separate loop, so a failure does not hold back checks or escalation). While enabled, a gap past the period becomes one `maintenance` / `needs-you` notice to the owner, command ID `cov-lapse-<hash(responsibility, since)>`: the same lapse is told once across ticks and restarts, a new lapse after recovery has a new `since`, so it is told again. Text carries no changing numbers (a replay with other text would conflict).
- **Provisional choices:** off by default; one global period for all responsibilities (no per-responsibility override yet); default period 1 day when turned on without a number; stale check = twice the period; the start of a no-holder or unscheduled gap is the responsibility record's `updatedAt` (any edit moves it) or, for a disabled holder, the principal's `updatedAt`; at most 500 lapses are told per project per tick; every chat change applies at once (not a proposal).
- **Not here:** per-responsibility period; a provider-outage or NimbleNewt-downtime gap record with start, end and reason (only the existing check catch-up `gap`); a status-view line; an index instead of scanning all responsibilities (bounded by the 50,000 scan limit); the lapse start for holder loss is approximate as noted.

- Review fixes (2026-10-30): (1) The start of a lapse is kept (`coverage-lapse/<responsibility>`: the time each reason was first seen, written by the sweep, emptied when the gap closes; first seen = the earlier of the moment it is known to have begun and now): `since`, `lapsedMinutes` and the alert ID come from it, so editing a title no longer hides a lapse or makes a duplicate notice. The sweep keeps this even while the alert is off (a bounded slice a tick; no notices). (2) One notice per project per period (`coverage-project/<project>`: when it was last told; lapses that grow past the period inside it wait), naming up to 10 responsibilities with the count of all; a responsibility with `eventSources` and no schedule is not "unscheduled". (3) The sweep is `sweep(by)` (dispatcher only, replacing `lapsed`): one slice of 200 responsibilities a tick with a kept cursor (`coverage-cursor/main`) going round, so the 50,000-record failure no longer exists and no tick scans every project; a report examines at most 2,000 records a call and answers `partial` with `next` when it stops at that bound. A notice is marked told only after it was sent (`markTold`). (4) `responsibility.coverage` answers `alert.status` `on`/`off`/`damaged`; a damaged setting makes the sweep raise its error after the bookkeeping. Remains: a lapse found in a slice waits at most one lap of the cursor to be told (about responsibilities/200 ticks).


### Third review fixes: scratch and quiet hosts, recovery ladder, coverage (2026-10-31)

- **Scratch sweep (A1).** Every record the sweep reads counts toward `perRecover` (20), the pass stops starting work after `passMs` (30 s real time), and where it starts rotates (in memory), so a silent host cannot hold the dispatcher's tick or starve the records behind it. Every call to the host has its own limit and cancellation: the order (`orderMs`) and the stop confirmation (`callMs`, 20 s), both given an `AbortSignal` (also passed on to `host.release`). An unanswered or busy order sets `retryAt`: a wait that doubles from 5 minutes up to 6 hours, so the 20 retries span about four days of outage rather than an hour. Limits are overridable per service (`options.limits`) for tests.
- **Scratch unresolved (A2).** A `deciding` record that cannot be decided and an `awaiting-stop` record that is never confirmed (a host that cannot release) are looked at no more often than the recheck time and are closed as `kept` with a recorded reason after `unresolvedMs` (14 days, provisional), reported once through `ports.unresolved` (a needs-you notice; `scratch-unresolved:<attempt>` is the key) and leave the open list. Nothing is removed by this; the scratch just stays.
- **Heartbeat is not activity (A3).** The dispatcher keeps `lastActivityAt`: a heartbeat moves it only while no call of the attempt waits parked for an approval (otherwise it keeps its earlier value, first the start). `checkpointVerdict` compares the checkpoint with `lastActivityAt ?? lastHeartbeatAt ?? outcome.at`, so a worker that parked and went on heartbeating is covered by the checkpoint it took before parking. An attempt from before the field has only the heartbeat: the conservative reading. Chosen over recording every tool call (a write per call).
- **Shutdown (A4).** The signal reaches the order, the stop confirmation and `host.release`. `DispatcherService.shutdown` aborts every running ended hook at once (not only at its timeout) and waits; a run cut off while an order is out gives up its lease without using a retry, so the next controller takes the order at once. `ScratchCleanupService.close()` (called by the controller's `close`) does the same for sweeps and waits for them.
- **A removal is recorded (A5).** When the host says removed (or already removed) and another run closed the cleanup as `kept` meanwhile, `kept` becomes `removed` (the leftovers it reports are kept). A `removed` record is never changed.
- **Quiet-host notices (A6).** With automatic moves on, a new episode inside `noticeHours` repeats the timer notice only when the grace figure changed since the last timer notice (`lastTimerHours`) or the episode before outlasted it (`priorLong`). Otherwise the warning is recorded without a notice, like the moves-off case. This replaces "a new episode always tells the timer".
- **Recovery ladder order (B3).** `RECOVERY_ACTIONS` is now `nudge, rebrief, pause, reassign, stop, hand-to-owner`. Reason: a reassignment changes the task's generation and so closes the concern, ending the ladder, and pause/stop act on the TASK (the pause and stop services have no scope of one agent's work on one task), so they must come while the stalled agent still holds it. Default: level 0 nudge, rebrief, hand-to-owner; level 1 and up nudge, rebrief, pause, reassign, hand-to-owner; stop is owner-only by default (configurable). A stored `recoveryRung` of a concern in progress when this was deployed is an index into the old order: provisional product, accepted. The scan does not clear a concern of a task the ladder itself paused (a non-skipped `pause` step), so reassign or hand-to-owner can still follow. `unavailable("reassign")` now gives a reason when the target is not an active agent, or the task has a running attempt (a prepared hand-off) and the actor may not control it.
- **The pause covers every agent on the task (B7).** Task-scope pause and stop halt all work on the task, including other agents working on it, not only the agent the concern is about. The earlier comment said otherwise. This is also in the `recovery.step` text.
- **Recovery step mechanics (B1, B2, B4, B5, B6).** The owner replaces a pending step in one call: the pending step is dropped (guarded by the revision the owner read and the pending key) and the new one begun from the revision that produced. Effect keys include `recoveryGen`, which goes up on a route change, a reopening and an abandon, so a key is never used for two different requests; `command_conflict` from the effect re-keys the pending step once. A `forbidden` effect drops the pending step and refuses it, leaving the rung; only `invalid_transition` and `not_found` pass a rung as skipped. A concern without a pinned agent is acted on only if the assignment is still of the concern's generation (else `invalid_transition`: the next scan closes it). A step whose effect was made but whose done-mark failed is reported through `options.onNote`; the retry finds the pending step and marks it done under the same key (the effect is not made again). The abandon of a step whose effect may have run is also noted.
- **Coverage (C1-C5).** The sweep gathers the lapses beyond the period per project over the whole lap (`coverage-project/<project>`: lap count, untold count, the few oldest, last full lap's total, `toldAt`, and the built `notice`, which is offered again each tick with the same ID until `markTold`). A notice is built when the lap completes (or the lap has outlasted the period), at most once per period per project, with the true total. A lapse first seen beyond the period after the last notice (`beyondAt` in the lapse record, reset when its set of reasons changes) is told at once but not more than once an hour (or the period, if shorter). A check recorded after the kept first-seen time of "no recent check" resets that time. Records of paused, retired or gone responsibilities and of archived or gone projects are deleted (25 of each per tick, from kept positions); closed gaps delete their lapse record. A report page may come back with no items and `partial` (the records it looked at had no gap): callers go on from `next` until there is none; a report that stops exactly at its bound with nothing left is not partial.
## H12k (part 4): host enforcement of the owner's limits for local agents; best effort; launch record (2026-10-30)

- Host builder (`LocalHostOptions` in `worker/host/local.ts`): new `limits(order)` (read at each launch of the worker process, combined with `workspace(...).limits` by taking the smaller figure per limit, `strictestLimits`), `bestEffort(order)` (whether a limit the OS cannot enforce in full may go ahead; absent keeps the static `requireEnforced`, default strict) and `onLaunch(record)`. Any of them throwing refuses the launch: nothing starts unlimited and nothing starts unrecorded (if `onLaunch` throws for a started process, the process is ended). Wall time is the launcher's time limit (the attempt's remaining time, at most 24 h) and is recorded as `wallTimeMs`.
- Translation to the sandbox is the existing `limitedPlan` (cgroup scope for memory/processes/cpu time, prlimit and core affinity as fallbacks, a per-file size cap for disk which is reported partial, `none` on other operating systems). `SandboxRun.enforcement` and `WorkerProcess.enforcement` now expose the launcher's per-limit report (full/partial/none, mechanism, detail), the same figures as the launch audit record.
- Default: strict. A limit that is not `full` refuses the launch (so a disk limit always refuses on Linux until quotas exist, and every limit refuses on macOS/Windows) unless the owner switched best effort on. Setting: `bestEffort` in the existing `worker-limits-settings/main` record (kept by `workers.limits.set` and `workers.limits.change`, which no longer drop it). API `workers.limits.besteffort {enabled, expectedRevision?}` (owner only, replay-safe, stale revision refused), `workers.limits.get` now returns `bestEffort`. Chat: `workers.limits.besteffort` is `propose` in every profile (enable/disable). Damaged flag or unreadable record: launch refused.
- Record: `worker-limits-enforced/<attemptId>` (count plus the last ten launches: outcome started/refused, limits requested, best-effort flag, per-limit enforcement, wall time, refusal reason, time), written through a command per launch; read with owner-only `workers.limits.enforced {attemptId}`. Strings bounded and the shape checked on write.
- Controller services given to `build`: `currentLimits` (unchanged), new `bestEffortAllowed()` and `recordLaunch(record)`; a host passes them to `localWorkerParts` as `limits`, `bestEffort` and `onLaunch` (what `integration/h12k-limit-enforcement.test.ts` does). There is still no controller-owned default workspace; the repo does not wire this itself.
- Tests: `integration/src/h12k-limit-enforcement.test.ts` (8): through `startController` with the real recipe building and `limitedPlan`, a fake launcher for the process start: default strict and recorded, refusal with reason and nothing started, best effort on/off with the record naming what was not enforced in full, owner only/validation/races/replay, unreadable or damaged setting refuses, smaller-figure combination, unrecordable launch ends the process, and the real `SandboxLauncher` refusing a disk limit.
- Provisional choices (owner questions at the end): (1) strict by default, best effort chat-settable and proposed (not auto-applied) in every profile; (2) a damaged or unreadable setting refuses rather than assuming strict-and-going-ahead; (3) the workspace's own limits and the owner's combine by the smaller figure; (4) no separate wall-time setting (the attempt's expiry is the wall limit); (5) best effort is installation-wide, not per limit or per role.
- Not done: running agents keep the limits they started with; no real-process end-to-end test of a limit being hit (memory kill) through `startController`; no per-limit best effort; macOS/Windows still enforce nothing (every limit refuses in strict mode); the MCP transport and `context`/`handoffFacts` default composition remain. H12k stays planned.

## H12k review fixes: the owner's policy must reach the host, cpu pinning is partial, records name what failed

- **Policy reaches the host or the start fails.** There is no default host builder in the controller (the operator's `dispatch.local.build` makes the host over the worker package). `startController` now refuses a built host that does not say it applies the owner's policy: `WorkerHost.ownerPolicy` must be true (the worker package's `localWorkerParts(...).ownerPolicy`, true only when `limits`, `bestEffort` and `onLaunch` are all connected; `ownerPolicyOptions(services)` spreads all three from what `build` is given). A refused host closes what `build` made, and the dispatcher does not run (`dispatchProblem` says why). `dispatch.local.acceptUnenforcedLimits: true` is the operator's explicit opt-out.
- **cpus via taskset is `partial`.** An unprivileged process can widen its own affinity, so a core pin is a request, not a quota; strict mode (the default, no best effort) refuses it unless a cgroup scope is used. The pinned set rotates per launch (`nextCoreOffset`) instead of always 0..n-1.
- **Unreadable settings are recorded.** The limits and best-effort settings are read inside the guard that records a refusal, so an unreadable setting writes a `refused` record with the reason.
- **The effective figure says why.** When the host's own start-up figure is stricter than the figure the owner set, the launch record's `stricter` lists owner figure, applied figure and why. A refusal for limits has `failed` (limit, how far enforced, detail) beside the reason.
- **Records.** `recordLaunch` retries on contention (a started process is never ended because the record lost a race) and keeps the newest 20 attempts per agent (older records removed, audited).
- **Wall time.** `wallTimeMs` (1000 to 604800000, optional, off) is part of the same limits setting (`workers.limits.set/change/get`, chat via `change`); it caps the launcher's timeout for the launch and is recorded as `wallTimeMs` enforcement `full` by the launcher time limit.
- **Chat.** `workers.limits.besteffort` with `enabled: false` applies at once when the owner's words say it; enabling is shown first.
- **Tests.** The plan arguments are asserted exactly (systemd-run units, prlimit options, taskset list); the Windows/macOS test shows every limit `none` with the plan untouched; the real-launcher test matches the specific reason and skips without a confined launch.
- **Remains:** macOS and Windows have no per-process limits wired in (every limit reports `none`, so a strict launch refuses there until best effort is allowed).
## X09b review fixes: per-issuer limits, controller-side timeout, indexed attempts, flaky gate

- **Per issuer, not per cell.** The cap of 20 attempts per platform now counts the issuer's own attempts (`issuedBy`); the owner is held only by the hard bound of 500 per platform, and agents stop at 200 so the owner always has room. A start/cancel loop by a QA agent can no longer lock the owner or anyone else out. Starts plus cancels per agent per hour are rate limited by `startsPerHour` (release.settings.set; default 12; `0` is no limit; the owner is never limited).
- **Cancel scope.** An agent cancels only attempts it or an agent reporting directly to it started; the owner's attempts are cancelled by the owner. The right to start or cancel is now checked inside the transaction that acts (a setting narrowed a moment ago is never raced).
- **Timeout on the controller.** `ReleaseService.expire()` (loop `release.expire`, also run for a host on each of its job fetches) ends an attempt that ran past `timeoutSeconds` plus a 10 minute grace (from pick-up, or from issue if never picked up) as `timed_out`: never a pass, the platform is free for a retry. Withdrawing a host's authorization (or moving it to another platform) ends its open attempts at once. `GET /worker/release/jobs` now answers `{ jobs, cancel }`: `cancel` lists picked-up attempts ended without a result (at most 32, repeated for a day) so the destructive test stops; `RemoteWorkerClient.releaseWork()` returns both.
- **No scan of all attempts.** Attempts are read through a per-platform index (`release-cell`) and per-host index (`release-hostjobs`) written in the same transaction; the "more than 5000 records" failure is gone. The boss check pages through agents and stops at the first match (never "unavailable"). Test seeds 5,200 attempts and agents.
- **Who is a QA agent.** The role name can be put on any agent by every holder of `agent.manage`, so the `qaAgents`/`bosses` switches reach all of them (documented on release.settings.set). The owner may name the QA agents (`qaAgentIds`, chat/API-settable); when set the role is ignored.
- **Retry until green is visible.** The gate reads all attempts of a platform: a platform that passed after a failed attempt is `flaky`, with the earlier failures beside the pass, and `release.approve` needs `acknowledgeFlaky: true` (recorded in the approval).
- **Chat.** `attemptId`/`candidateId` of release commands are no longer exempt from the owner's-words check; `release.cancel` names an attempt ID the owner said, or a candidate the owner said with exactly one test running. Remains: starting a test from chat needs the owner to give the candidate ID in the message.
- **Remains:** the host-side agent that acts on `cancel` (the worker host runner is not in this card); `timed_out` attempts need no new owner action.



## H10b (first slice): optional capacity caps with "waiting for capacity" and fair queueing

- **Caps** (`admission/caps.ts`, `CapacityLimitsService`): `perProject`, `perAgent` and `fanIn` (running child attempts whose parent task is owned by one supervising agent; reviewers are not counted), each 1 to 1000, all OFF by default. Per host stays the existing admission limit `perHost` (default 2, always on; the card's "max per host" was already there). Owner-only API `capacity.limits.get` / `capacity.limits.change` (`set`, `enable`, `disable`, `unset`, `expectedRevision`, merge-style, replay-safe, same shape as `dispatch.limits.change`); chat `capacity.limits.change` is a `propose` command (shown first, applied on the owner's word). A change sweeps admission at once so a raised or removed cap lets waiting work in; a lower cap stops nothing that runs.
- **Enforcement** is inside admission's single guarded step (`policy.ts` `blocker`: new blockers `project`, `agent`, `fanin`, after lane and host), so concurrent requests cannot both take the last place. Requests carry `project`, `agent`, `reportsTo`; the dispatcher fills them (attempt's project and agent; `reportsTo` = owner of the parent task found through the `swarm-link`, via the new optional dep `reportsTo`, wired in `dispatch-compose.ts`). Caps are read from the settings record at every decision and never copied into the admission record (stripped in `#built`).
- **Waiting, not failing:** `AdmissionService.where` gives a `reason` ("waiting for capacity: project X already has N attempts running (the owner's per-project cap)"); the tick report has `capacityWaits` (also in `waiting`); nothing is skipped or failed.
- **Fairness:** the existing patience mechanism now covers the new blockers: a request passed over `patience` times is served first and holds back only the thing it waits for (lane, host, project, agent or supervisor key), so other work goes on.
- **Failure behaviour:** a damaged caps record makes new requests fail with `integrity` (nothing starts on a guess), `where` says why, and `release`/stop still work; a change that sets, unsets or disables the damaged cap repairs it.
- **Tests:** `admission/caps.test.ts` (7 cases x 4 backends: off by default, per-project/agent/fan-in waits with reasons, no starvation, lower/raise/disable, owner-only/stale/replay/validation, damaged record); `api/start-capacity.test.ts` through `startController` (per-project cap via real ticks, chat proposal then apply, fan-in through a real `swarm-link`, forbidden/invalid/stale). Mutations killed: patience ignored, project cap check removed.
- **Provisional choices (chat-overridable):** all caps off by default; per host remains the admission limit; "fan-in" means simultaneously running child attempts whose parent task's owner is the same agent (not messages or submissions received); there is no per-installation startup default.
- **Known / not done:** one agent has one native store on a host, so two attempts of one agent seldom run together; `perAgent` is mostly meaningful for hosts or harnesses without that exclusivity (tested at admission level only, not end to end). Fan-in counts running attempts, not review requests or submissions sitting with a reviewer; stop/review/inquiry control traffic is unaffected (caps apply to the productive lane only), but the swarm service's own depth/children limit is still separate. No cross-host (distributed) view beyond admission's single record. The caps sweep after a change is best effort (the next admission decision also promotes). Storage statement counts were not changed, qualification tests not run.

- Review fixes (H10b, 2026-10-31): (1) What a request asks for (priority and supervisor) is decided once per request number and kept on the attempt (`ask`) BEFORE the request is made, so a replay after a crash asks for exactly the same thing and no longer gets `command_conflict` while the committed entry holds a place; if a conflict still happens (the committed entry was made with different figures), the entry under that command ID is adopted when it is for the same host, otherwise released and the request number moves on. Tests: two dispatcher cases (changed supervisor after a crash; changed digest, orphan adopted), both fail without the fix. (2) `blockers()` lists everything holding a request (`blocker()` is its first); a starved request bars every key it is blocked on (host and the caps), and the skipped-count uses all of them. As caps and hosts are keyed alike, the outcome only differs for hosts (CPUs and memory); the test asserts the full list and the promote result. (3) Fan-in is no longer frozen: each tick the dispatcher reads the supervisor again for every waiting request and sends changes through the new `AdmissionService.annotate` (a released parent clears it); a request that already runs keeps what it ran under. Documented: fan-in counts running child attempts per supervising agent (the owner of the parent task); reviewers are not counted (op summary, docs, comments). (4) Requests from before the caps (no project or agent) get them from their attempt through the same `annotate` (fill only when missing, never overwrite). (5) `capacityWaits` and `Where.capReason` list only waits on the owner's caps (per project, per agent, fan-in), also when a host is full too; a plain full host or lane, or a host with no declared capacity, is in `waiting` and `Where.reason` only. (6) The misplaced comment in `chat/commands.ts` is fixed. Not done: a dispatcher-level end-to-end test of the supervisor re-read (tested at admission level through `annotate`).


## U11b remainder: the escalation and expiry run in the controller, bounded

- Found: `NotificationService.runDue` (escalation of unattended Needs-you items, Notice expiry, digests, delivery retries) was never called by the running controller, and `start.ts` passed no channel adapters, so none of it happened in production. Now the dispatcher's tick runs it as the sweep `notifications.run`, and `StartOptions.notifications = { channels?, clock? }` hands the channel adapters (the existing sinks) to the service; Urgent escalations are delivered through the channel the owner set (`channel: external`, `channelName`), at most once per item (delivery id is derived from the item and its first time).
- Bounded: `NOTIFICATION_LIMITS.escalationsPerRun` (25) escalations per tick, oldest first; the rest follow on the next ticks.
- Settings already existed and are unchanged: `escalateAfterHours` (default 24, `null` = off) and `noticeRetentionDays` (default 7), owner-only `notifications.configure` with expectedRevision, and the chat command with enable/disable.
- Test (end to end through `startController` with the dispatcher): `api/start-notification-escalation.test.ts` (not raised at 23 h, raised and sent once at 25 h, not again on later ticks or after a restart, bound of 25 per tick, off by the owner stops it). It fails with the bound removed.
- Provisional choices: escalation still waits out quiet hours (existing behaviour; the card says Urgent also interrupts in quiet hours: left for the owner, would be a new chat-settable switch). The sweep runs only when the dispatcher is started. Not done: de-escalation on resumed work, the "agent has nothing else to do" trigger, other Urgent triggers (K01, H01/H09, A08, denials).

- Review fixes (U11b, 2026-10-31): (1) First deploy no longer floods: the state record keeps `escalationEnabledAt` (set by the first sweep with escalation on, cleared when escalation is switched off, so switching it on again starts the clock afresh) and a wait counts from the later of the item's creation and that time; the sweep sends at most `escalationsPerHour` (setting, default 10) Urgent messages an hour (window kept in the state record): beyond that in one run the items are raised in the inbox but told in ONE "N more items escalated" message (counted among the hour's messages); with none left nothing is raised until the hour turns. (2) A hung adapter: each send runs under `sendTimeoutSeconds` (setting, default 10) with an abort signal passed to the adapter and the promise abandoned; at most 5 sends a run, a 30 s run budget after which nothing new is started; adapters were already called outside any storage transaction (the test reads the store from inside an adapter); `notifications.run` is now moved to the END of the dispatcher's loops (`dispatch-compose.ts`). (3) Cost: the dispatcher calls `runDue({ throttled: true })`: a full sweep at most every `sweepEverySeconds` (setting, default 60) decided from the state record's `nextSweepAt`; between sweeps only digest and delivery work runs. A full sweep examines at most 200 open items from a persisted cursor (`sweepCursor`), so a backlog of 1000 is covered in about five sweeps; Notice expiry still reads the open Notices list (at most 500). Direct callers (`runDue()`) always sweep fully. (4) One damaged item no longer blocks the rest: per-item try/catch in the escalation and settling loops; the first failure is kept with `??=` and raised after the others were tried. (5) Configure refuses an external `channelName` with no registered adapter (and lists the registered names); a delivery given up on (not one dropped because the channel was changed) raises ONE Needs-you maintenance item (`notification-delivery/failed`) that coalesces while open. Not done (remainder): a built-in webhook adapter with an owner-set host allowlist through the network profile: `start.ts` still gets adapters only from `StartOptions.notifications.channels`, so in a stock install `external` cannot be set at all (the refusal says so). (6) Escalation only applies to kinds the owner answers (blocker, review request, owner question) or a kind the owner set to Needs you; maintenance and presence are not raised on their own. New `settleFromController({ kind, ref, projectId })` lets the producing service close what it reported once the condition is gone (it leaves the inbox; a later report is a new occurrence). (7) Quiet hours are read in the owner's `meeting.timeZone` (UTC when none is set or the zone is unknown; digest times stay UTC). New setting `urgentInterruptsQuietHours` (default true): an escalated Urgent item is raised and its message and retries are sent inside quiet hours; false: they wait. Deliveries carry `urgent`; a digest or other message retried in quiet hours is held. The older rule for an Urgent REVIEW (waits out quiet hours) is unchanged and is left to the owner. (8) The tick report redacts the error text of a failing loop (`dispatcher.ts`). (9) `digestsPerRun * digestItems >= openItems` is checked when the module loads (and in a test). All new settings (`escalationsPerHour`, `sweepEverySeconds`, `sendTimeoutSeconds`, `urgentInterruptsQuietHours`) are in `notifications.configure` and therefore chat-settable. Existing tests changed because of the new rules: waits count from the first sweep, maintenance is not escalated unless the owner set its level, an unregistered channel is refused, and switching escalation on again restarts the clock. Tests: 9 new cases x 4 backends in `notifications.test.ts`, a second end-to-end case and changes in `api/start-notification-escalation.test.ts`, a redaction case in `dispatch/loops.test.ts`.

## Q01: versioned deliverables and their acceptance (2026-10-31)

- `AcceptanceService` (`submissions/acceptance.ts`; kinds `deliverable`, `deliverable-version`, `deliverable-event`, `deliverable-index`). A deliverable belongs to one task and records type (code, document, report, design, operational-outcome), title, responsible agent, audience (owner, director, reviewers, project, external) and access scope (owner, task, project). Each VERSION has a state: draft, submitted, under-review, accepted, rejected, superseded. Every move is its own immutable event `deliverable-event` numbered per deliverable (`<id>.<seq>`), written in the same storage operation as the move; an `invalidated` event (a seventh kind) records a voided review. Versions are numbered 1..100; at most 100 deliverables per task (the index record).
- Operations (`api-v1.md`): `deliverable.draft`, `.revise`, `.version.new`, `.submit`, `.review.start`, `.accept`, `.reject`, `.check` and the reads `deliverable.record.get/list/events` (the older `deliverable.get/list` are the U13 artifact reads and are unchanged). Chat: `deliverable.review.start` (apply), `deliverable.accept` and `deliverable.reject` (propose, PROVISIONAL: the owner sees an acceptance before it lets dependent work go on).
- Tool completion cannot accept: the only path to `accepted` is `deliverable.accept` by the owner, an agent holding the director role, or the reviewer that started the review. Never by the responsible agent, the creator, the version's submitter or the submitter of a linked submission (no self-review, no override). A review is started and decided by different calls; deciding needs `under-review`. The tests finish the task by the owner's transition and show nothing is accepted.
- Review disabled for a single-agent project (owner decision): on submit the version records `review: {required: false, reason: review_disabled_single_agent}` when no other agent could review (`reviewersAvailableIn`); the worker cannot review itself, so only the owner decides there. An `external` audience is accepted or rejected by the owner only (PROVISIONAL, no setting: the deliverable leaves the project).
- Missing or changed artifact: submit, start-review and accept verify every artifact of the version (manifest digest recorded at draft time against the artifact record, then `ArtifactService.verify` of the bytes). Damage at submit or start-review refuses with `integrity` and writes nothing. Damage at accept voids the review: an `invalidated` event returns the version to `submitted` and the call fails with `integrity` (the voiding is its own replay-safe command derived from the accept's command ID). `deliverable.check` does the same check on demand and also voids an ACCEPTED version. Without an artifact directory (`verifyArtifact` absent) a version that names artifacts cannot be submitted or decided (fail closed). Verification hashes up to 20 artifacts per call with no byte cap (not bounded by size; PROVISIONAL, no budget imposed).
- Rejected history: a rejected version keeps its state, decider and (redacted) reason; `deliverable.version.new` supersedes every other earlier version but leaves a rejected one rejected. Content of a version is immutable once submitted (`revise` only in draft).
- Contract (S10): `deliverable.submit` takes `contractVersion`, which must equal the version in force (`stale_revision` with the current one otherwise); it is stored on the version. Not re-checked at accept (a later contract change does not void an accepted or submitted version; the version records which one it was checked against).
- Operational outcome: `outcome {reference, systemVersion, observedAt}` is required to submit an `operational-outcome`; time must be UTC ISO. The reference is text; it is NOT checked against the effect ledger or the target system (that is P03's adapter). Source and exported artifacts are grouped under one version (`role` source/exported, `exportedFrom` names a source of the same version). Linked submissions (code or document) must be the responsible agent's own submissions of the task (one message for missing, other task, other agent), and a document submission's `artifactDigest` must be `sha256:` plus the manifest digest of one of the version's artifacts. A code deliverable must link a code submission.
- Visibility: owner always; `owner` scope = responsible agent and creator that can still read the task; `task` = agents with `task.read` for the task; `project` = also any agent holding a role in the project. Task credentials reach their own task only. Anything unreadable is `not_found`. Deciding needs the same read right.
- No setting was added (nothing here is a limit or budget); gating the task's own `done` on acceptance is NOT done (a setting would be needed: default off).
- Tests: `submissions/acceptance.test.ts` (4 backends), `api/start-acceptance.test.ts` through `startController` (flow and events, authorization, replay, stale revisions, tampered blob voiding the review, rejected history, owner-only external, single agent, access scope, task credentials, code and document submissions, concurrent decisions).
- Plan dependencies: Q01 lists P02 and P03 (still planned). Q01 needs neither to work: P02 (workspace and integration) and P03 (non-code and sandbox adapters) are PRODUCERS of code and operational-outcome deliverables. See the final report for the proposed split.

## Q01 fixes (review scope, disabled review, stale checks)

- Review disabled means the owner decides: a version whose recorded `review.required` is false, or for which no OTHER agent could decide now, is decided by the owner only (an agent gets `forbidden`, even after a second agent joins later). "Could decide" is computed with the exact set the acceptance service lets decide (`AgentService.decidersAvailableIn`: reviewer role with a live grant in the project or `*`, or director role with a live grant naming THIS project), minus everyone who did the work. It is evaluated again at start and at decision, not only at submission.
- Deciding power is scoped: a director decides only in projects where one of its live grants names the project (a project-wide `*` grant is not enough); a reviewer needs to be asked to review this deliverable or one of its submissions (`reviewAssignments` port, deliverable ID or submission ID) or hold `review.decide` naming the project; at decision it must also be the reviewer that started the review. The `reviewAssignments` port is NOT wired to a source yet (there is no record of "asked to review a deliverable"), so today a reviewer gets in through an explicit `review.decide` grant for the project; the owner can always decide.
- Acceptance commits with `check` changes on the artifact records read for the verification and on the task contract record, so a change between the check and the commit refuses the acceptance.
- A new version over a version that is under review or accepted records the reason in the `superseded` event (who replaced it, the reviewer or decider) and sends a Notice-level maintenance item to the owner; behavior is unchanged.
- Outcome `reference` and `systemVersion` pass through `redactText`; the responsible agent must be an active agent principal.
## H12b and H12f: completing the blockers (2026-10-31)

Proof: `packages/integration/src/h12bf-composed.test.ts` starts the controller with `startController`, builds the local worker host from the real bubblewrap launcher, the real worker process (Pi) and the controller's relay, and drives it through the dispatcher and the API (`message.send`, the pause service). It runs where bubblewrap works (`NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` makes a machine without it a failure); the recipe and network cases read the sandbox from `/proc` and are Linux-only (skipped with the reason elsewhere).

**H12f (done).**
- *Compaction at start now works.* Three faults kept the old "compacted or refused" from being true. (1) The first call counted only the new text, not the conversation already stored: the host now adds the stored size (`contextTokens`) to `startupTokens`, so a resumed conversation over the startup share (a quarter of the window) is refused in round 1. (2) A round-1 refusal opened the `context_overflow` blocker, which made round 2 refuse too: `ContextEnforcementService.admit` takes `retry: true` (service level only, no API operation), the refusal is recorded but opens no blocker, and the final round opens it. A compaction that throws is reported and round 2 asks about the unchanged call (refused, blocker). (3) The size the process reported counted the whole stored history, which compaction never shrinks; it now counts only what the model still sees (entries from the latest `head`, a new optional field on `TranscriptEntry`). Pi also kept 20,000 tokens verbatim by default, so nothing was ever cut on a small window; the process sets `keepRecentTokens` to a tenth of the window (provisional).
- `systemPromptChars: 0` is sent in `ready` (Pi Durable renders no system text and the process gives it no prompt layout; the provider's reported count still calibrates the estimate through `confirmUsage`, which the test shows recorded end to end).
- A restart (recipe change) now admits the new process's first call again (round numbering goes on from the start; an unfit conversation is compacted once, else the restart fails and the dispatcher keeps the attempt frozen).
- Pause and interrupts are proven against the real process mid-turn: an interrupt told while a model call is open reaches the agent and is in the next model request, labelled as the owner's; a pause shows as `pausing` (written by the agent's runtime) while the call is open and `paused` with `finished` only after it settles; a second interrupt is not delivered to the paused attempt.

**H12b (done for Linux; macOS and Windows proof is H12r).**
- *Recipe changes are applied by the launcher.* `RecipeSummary` has `reach` (names) and optional `limits`. The host turns each reach name into read-only mounts and environment through `LocalHostOptions.reach` (an unknown or duplicate name, more than 32 names, or a mount outside `/inputs` and `/opt` refuses the sandbox: a recipe is never applied in part; every mount still passes the A03 recipe checks), and `limits` replace the workspace default for that launch. `changeRecipe` validates the shape. The test narrows and widens a running attempt: the new worker process has (or lacks) the `/inputs/a` mount and the cgroup limits, each launch records its recipe revision, the agent is told on the widening and the tell is still in its conversation after a later restart.
- *The turn survives the restart.* `LocalWorker.run` waits for the restart and runs the same request again on the new runtime (same request ID, so it is the same turn and keeps its number; the cache figures of the cut part are added to the final report). Restarts are serialised and a stop during a restart closes what the restart opened. A first turn has no completed turn to checkpoint, so the host returns a checkpoint with `midTurn: true` (the conversation is in the agent's home on this host; a resume elsewhere is refused because the store is not there). The start message carries `recover: { reason }` when the controller restarted the sandbox or resumed from a checkpoint; only then does the process release Pi's hold on interrupted work. Without it a store with unfinished work is refused.
- *Platforms.* `LocalHostOptions.guestPaths: "host"` makes the host start the process by the host's own paths and store (Seatbelt shows no private view); this is unit-tested with a capturing launcher, and the composed test picks Seatbelt on macOS. It has not been run on a Mac. Nothing is provided for Windows. Their proof is the remainder card **H12r** (split from H12b on 2026-10-31); no dependent of H12b depends on H12r except D05.
- From inside the sandbox the model endpoint, loopback and an outside address all fail (a real probe in the sandbox); the relay is a function the host takes, so it is replaceable without changing the worker, and its streaming is covered by `relay.test.ts`.
- Provisional: keep-recent share of a tenth of the window; the startup share applies to a resumed conversation as well as to new text; a recipe revision is the launcher's digest of the recipe body (limits are recorded in the launch record, not in the digest, so narrowing back to the first mounts gives the first revision).
- Not covered: the macOS and Windows runs (H12r); H12j's "all six CI cells" part is the same gap and needs the same narrowing to H12r before it can be flipped.

### H12b, H12f review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Each start is judged afresh.** An admission (`admit`, `confirmUsage`, `changeRoute`) takes an optional `launch` part; the local worker makes a random one per `LocalWorker.start`, so an attempt resumed after a restart, a host loss or a move (same attempt ID, round numbering back at 1) no longer gets the recorded `admit` of the time the conversation was small, and the open-blocker check is no longer skipped because an older record exists. Rounds inside one start (and the restart rounds, which go on in the same start) still repeat to their recorded answer.
- **The recipe is kept on the attempt.** `DispatchBody.recipe` (revision, reach, limits) is written when the worker starts and when `changeRecipe` succeeds; every start (resume, move) builds the work order's recipe from it, never from `{reach: []}`. The remote `restart` control message keeps `limits` (validated like `changeRecipe`'s) instead of rebuilding revision and reach only.
- **The label of a recipe change is checked.** `recipeWidens(current, next)`: a reach that is added, a limit that is raised or dropped (when the current recipe states one) is a widening. A change labelled `narrow` that widens is `invalid_command`. A real widening needs the owner, or the dispatcher option `mayWiden(by, attemptId, what)` (the embedder's policy; absent = strict, owner only). Provisional: dropping a limit counts as widening (the host default may be higher); stating a limit where none was stated is not (the default is not known here).
- **Pi's hold is not bypassed.** The host asks the process to recover (release the hold, abandon nothing) only when `heldForReview(order)` answers false (the dispatcher offers `heldForReview(attemptId)`: an unsettled or uncertain call in the ledger); absent or throwing means held, the hold stays and `onHeld` reports it. Also fixed: the recovery reason always said "restarted".
- **Reach environment.** A reach may not set start-up or loader variables (NODE_*, NPM_*, GIT_*, BASH*, ENV, PYTHON*, RUBY*, PERL*, LD_*, DYLD_*, JAVA_*, PATH, HOME, ...); names must be plain identifiers; the workspace's own environment wins over a reach's.
- **A failed restart closes what it opened** (new runtime and sandbox) on a refused re-admission or an open failure.
- **Stored size.** A checkpoint without `contextTokens` is estimated from the stored conversation (bytes / 3, bounded to 20,000 files) rather than taken as 0. The compaction summary's text counts (checked by a test: the size after an extractive compaction is at least 1,000 tokens).
- **Tests.** The composed tests fail instead of skipping where `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` and the sandbox is unusable (the Linux-only ones still skip off Linux), run with `acceptUnenforcedLimits` and the ledger's `heldForReview`, and the recipe test narrows with explicit lower limits (dropping limits is now a widening). Not added: a composed replay-after-restart run (covered by the enforcement unit test of the same attempt asked under two starts).

### H12m review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **A request the controller stopped waiting for is not started later.** Each workspace request carries `expiresAt` (the time the controller stops waiting); `WorkspaceHost.run` refuses to start one past it, checked again after any wait behind another request on the same checkout (so a long request A cannot let a timed-out B run under a freed agent). The poll answer also lists `withdrawn` request IDs (timed out, no answer, kept an hour); `WorkspaceResponder.handle(requests, withdrawn)` drops a withdrawn or expired request it has queued and not started (a running one cannot be stopped; its answer is accepted and dropped). `WorkspaceHost` takes an optional `attemptsQuiet(attemptIds, call)`: when given, a request runs only if it says true (false or a throw refuses it, unrecorded). **Not done:** the product's real remote worker main does not exist in this branch, so whoever builds the host must pass `attemptsQuiet`; without it the host trusts the controller's quiesce.
- **A repeat of a timed-out request ID** fails fast (`unavailable`, "timed out earlier and was withdrawn"); a late answer that did arrive is still returned. Ask again with a new ID.
- **Host journal** records the task and refuses a repeat of an ID for another operation or task. **Integration** reads a path whose folder is gone in the shared workspace as ABSENT (a delete there is skipped as already done), not as unknown.

## H12m test flake: checkpoint pump (2026-10-31)
The remote-host case of `h12m-workspace-host.test.ts` failed intermittently with "the worker did not send a checkpoint in time". Not a product race: `RemoteHostHandle.checkpoint()` polls correctly. Two test faults: the host's `checkpointWaitMs` was a fixed 500 ms (too short on a loaded machine), and the test's pump advanced its read position before answering, so one failed `putCheckpoint` (swallowed by the catch) lost the request for good. Now the wait is a generous 30 s bound (returns as soon as the checkpoint lands) and the pump marks a message read only after answering it. No sibling tests use this pump.

## K06: retention, quotas, archive, export and deletion (2026-10-31)

Code: `packages/controller/src/retention/` (`settings.ts`, `guard.ts`, `references.ts`, `service.ts`), wired in `api/start.ts`; ops `retention.*` in `api/operations.ts`; chat in `chat/commands.ts`. Tests: `api/start-retention.test.ts` (end to end through `startController`), `retention/guard.test.ts`, `chat/retention-chat.test.ts`.

**Policy (defaults, all chat-settable).** `retention.settings.get` / `retention.settings.set` (owner only, `expectedRevision`, command-ID replay-safe, audited with each old and new value, answer and chat line say "field old -> new"; `"default"` returns a field to the installation default, `null` clears an optional one). The chat reads the revision itself (new revision kind `retention`); `retention.settings.set`, `.run`, `.delete`, `.archive` and `.restore` are chat mode `propose` (shown first, applied on an explicit request). Installation defaults come from `StartOptions.retention.defaults` over the built-in ones. A damaged stored record is `unavailable` (the runner and the guard do not guess); setting again repairs it.
Provisional values (owner to confirm): everything that deletes is OFF (`derivedDays` null, `autoRun` false, incident archive/purge null, quotas null); `thinkingDays` 14 (owner decision 2026-10-22; recorded and shown, nothing deletes thinking yet, card K06c); `backupDaily` 7 and `backupWeekly` 4 (the K01 rule, now the owner's: the nightly prune and the runner read them; the newest backup, pre-upgrade snapshots and untrusted names are still never deleted); `quotaWarnPercent` 80; `reserveBytes` 16 MiB (0 turns the reserve off). `derivedDays` 7..3650, incident purge 30..3650.

**Runner.** `retention.run` previews by default (derived summaries `summary-record`, `meeting-summary`, `standup-brief` last touched more than `derivedDays` ago, and the backups outside the counts; the incident rules are listed by their ages, not counted) and returns a `digest`; running for real needs `dryRun:false` and `confirm: digest`, so what is removed is what was shown (a changed set is refused). Each removal is a guarded storage delete with a tombstone and an audit entry (`retention.expire`, ID/project/age, never content); the run is recorded (`retention-run`). The dispatcher loop `retention.sweep` (a) warns, (b) sets the reserve aside again when room was made, (c) runs the same thing when the owner set `autoRun`, at most once per hour (`autoEveryMs`), without the digest step (the owner's setting is the consent). Incident archive and purge (K06 first slice, K06b first slice) now run from the same pass per project when their ages are set; before this they were never called.
**Retained material** (`references.ts`): a task that is not done or cancelled is resumable. Held: its desk records, artifacts, history scopes and paged-out spill; what its compactions cite (sources, pinned, summary); what its checkpoints (`continuation`) list (artifacts, scratch records, summary lineage, source ranges); the compactions and checkpoints themselves. `retention.check {kind,id}` answers `retained` with reasons; the runner, the deletion and the archive skip it and show it as retained. The scan is bounded (100000 per kind); a scan that did not finish answers "retained" for everything. The check is made once per request, so a live task that starts citing a record between the check and the removal is not seen (small window; the cited text then reads as changed and is withheld).

**User-requested deletion** (`retention.delete {recordId, reason, dryRun?}`, owner only). Only desk records can be deleted; history entries and owner decisions are append-only and refused. If anything standing on the record is held by a resumable task, nothing changes and the request is recorded as `retained` with the reasons (the owner cancels or finishes the task, or waits). Otherwise: the record and the copies other agents made of it (`copiedFrom`/`origin`) lose title and body (stub: private, `deleted {at, by, reason, contentDigest}`; an agent can no longer revise or copy it), the summaries that cite it are removed (tombstone), compactions that cite it get their summary text blanked and `sourceDeleted`, and an archive of any of them is removed. Derived records keep their project. One operation per record, each repeat-safe; the `retention-deletion` record is written last. The answer and the record say how backups are handled: existing backups are NOT altered, they hold the text until they fall outside the backup counts ("left to expire", how many hold it, at most `max(daily, weekly*7+6)` days; pre-upgrade snapshots longer, K03), and a backup made afterwards no longer has it. Indexes: none exist (search reads live records). Cached replies: none are stored (the inference cache holds prompt markers). Both facts are written into every deletion record so a later store is noticed; `DERIVED_KINDS` and `EXPORT_KINDS` are the registries a new derived store adds itself to.

**Archive / restore** (`retention.archive {taskId}`, `retention.restore {taskId}`, owner only). A done or cancelled task's desk records move into `retention-archive` records (id `arc-<record id>`, original body kept) and leave a stub (`archived`); summaries made from them go with them. A record another resumable task needs is left and shown as retained. Restore puts the original body back exactly (one operation per record: update plus delete of the archive) and leaves a record that changed since (and a deleted one, whose archive was removed with it) listed as a conflict.

**Export** (`retention.export {projectId, after?, limit?}`, owner only, paged, 512 KiB and 5000 records per page): project, tasks, desk records, summaries, artifact metadata and archived originals of one project. Secret-named fields are replaced and key-shaped text masked (`redact`, count in `redactions`); principals, credentials, grants and keys are not in the kind list at all. It is a read in the API's JSON, not a file or archive format, and there is no import.

**Quotas and reserve** (`guard.ts`, in front of `applyOperation` of the controller's storage; `Controller.storage` is the guarded one, `unguarded(storage)` gives the one under it for fault tests). Quotas are optional, per project and per agent, in bytes of content written: desk records, working notes, summary records, history entries (to their scope's project), spill, artifact metadata plus blob bytes.
