Usage is one pass over those kinds (cached 60 s, raised by what is admitted meanwhile, an update counted at its full new size, so the figure is conservative between passes; a pass reads at most 50000 per kind and says `partial`). A write over a quota is refused as `unavailable` with the reason and nothing is written; a repeat of an operation that already committed is still answered. Visible warnings: `retention.status` lists scopes at or over the warning percent, and the sweep sends one needs-you notice per scope and level per week. NOT metered: messages, model calls, audit, effects, outbox and the other bookkeeping kinds.
The reserve is a real file (`.nn-reserve`, random bytes) in the data directory, set aside at start and on every change of `reserveBytes`, and only when twice its size is free. A write that finds the disk full (the adapters' `unavailable` whose cause chain says SQLITE_FULL / ENOSPC / PostgreSQL 53100 / "disk is full") is retried once with the same operation ID after giving the reserve back, but only for CRITICAL operations: the audit type starts with `continuation.` (checkpoint capture and resume), `stop.`, `recovery`, `resume.`, `stall.recover`, `pause.`, `quiesce`, `shutdown`, `checkpoint`, `notification.emit` (so the disk-full warning itself can be recorded) or `retention.` (so the owner can always change settings and delete to make room). An ordinary write never takes the reserve. After the reserve was taken, ordinary writes are refused up front ("protected") until the dispatcher's pass has set it aside again (room was made); a critical write that still fails is an error, never a success, so a disk-full checkpoint is not reported done (and `continuation.capture` already records an unverified checkpoint as incomplete). Critical writes are also exempt from quotas.

**Not done / what remains.**
- K06c (new card): deleting stored model thinking 14 days after a task is done, dropping chat thinking, and the resume-without-thinking handling; needs adapter support (the Pi conversation is append-only; `ThinkingService` has a read-only source that is not wired).
- The disk-full behaviour is proven with injected driver errors and a real reserve file, not by filling a real filesystem (needs a small dedicated volume; do it in X01). The reserve protects the database disk only: Pi checkpoint files and workspaces on other disks are not covered; with PostgreSQL and no `dataDirectory` there is no reserve (quotas still apply).
- Quota metering covers content kinds only (above). Tiered per-kind retention, archive-before-expiry and the dangling-reference clean-up of notifications are K06b. Archive covers desk records and their summaries of finished tasks, not notes, histories, artifacts or whole projects (P06). Archived rows stay in the same database (no space is freed) and in backups.
- Backups: the counts are the owner's setting; targets, age limits, purging named backups and the recovery-file rules are K01c.
- Known race: see "Retained material" (check once per request).

## K06 fixes (deletion lineage, holds, resumable deletion, backups)

- Deletion follows the lineage: compactions that cite the record AND every later compaction built on one of them (`parent`/`lineage`, transitively, at most 64 rounds; a longer chain makes the scan incomplete and the request retained), the summary records those compactions published (`summaryId`), meeting summaries and stand-up briefs that quote the text (a match of the first 120 characters of the body), and desk records that supersede or are superseded by the record when they quote it. All are blanked or removed together and listed in `derived` (`others` for meeting summaries and briefs).
- Summaries and holds: a summary is retained when it names a resumable task (`taskId`, set by the controller on summaries published by a compaction; never accepted from a caller) or when one of its sources is a desk record of a resumable task. The check "a task whose replay is needed" still means a task that is not done or cancelled; a finished task's replay is not protected.
- Deletion is resumable. The first write is a `retention-deletion` record "in-progress" with the plan and an attempt number; step command IDs derive from the command ID and the attempt; the final record is an upsert by the deletion ID, so a repeat of the same command ID after a "retained" answer or a crash continues and ends with the proper "deleted" record (earlier code failed with `command_conflict`). One request does at most 400 operations: more gives `partial` with `remaining`, and the same command continues. Holds are read again before every batch of 25 removals (the runner does the same per batch of 25 expiries); a hold that appears stops the work with a "retained" record, and what was already removed stays removed.
- Backups: existing backups are not altered and hold the deleted text until they expire (the delete answer says for how long). To keep an old backup from bringing the text back, every deletion is also appended (IDs, who, why, when; no content) to `retention-deletions.ledger` in the backup folder, outside the database, and `backup restore` applies that ledger to the rows as they are restored (`--deletions <file>` names another ledger); it prints how many records were blanked or removed again. A backup folder whose name time cannot be trusted now ages out by its folder time like the others, and an untrusted backup older than the oldest backup the rules keep is deleted. SQLite stores run with `PRAGMA secure_delete = ON`; PostgreSQL has no equivalent (autovacuum reclaims space, and a `VACUUM FULL` after a deletion is the owner's choice); the SQLite WAL is cleared by its checkpoints.
- Quotas and reserve: only delete, run, expire and the retention settings are critical; archive and restore add bytes and are ordinary writes (refused when the disk is full or protected). The usage scan has a single pass in flight; an update or a delete changes the kept figure by the difference to the record it replaces. The reserve file is in the data directory; with PostgreSQL and no local data directory there is no reserve file (a database-side reserve, such as reserved rows, is not built).
- Archives and listings: expiring an archived summary stub deletes its `arc-<id>` archive with it; `retention.restore` returns `conflictDetails` (a reason for each conflict, including "deleted at the owner's request"); the recent-deletions list in the status is sorted by record time (ties by ID) over the whole scan; an export includes artifacts that name a task and no project (through the task's project); `passcode` and `pin` fields are masked like other secrets.
- CI fixes (exhaustive run 41173915277): the sealed artifact index is read with its label taken by `basename` (a `/` split gave the wrong label on Windows, so a sealed backup with blobs could not be verified there); tests that assume POSIX behaviour now say so: file modes (600 refusal, recovery file mode), named pipes, links that need a privilege, and the `/blobs/blobs/` path form; on macOS `/etc` is a link and is refused as such. The composed narrowing check now looks only at the new launch's processes and names the processes and mounts it saw when it fails.


## P03: non-code and service-operation adapters (controller side, 2026-10-31)

Audit of the acceptance text, sentence by sentence, against `main` before this work: (1) "Non-code task produces accepted artifact": acceptance (Q01) existed but NO operation let an agent create an artifact (only tests and the remote checkpoint code called `ArtifactService.publish`); (2) "operational effect records verified target": the effect ledger (S05) existed, Q01 took a free-text `outcome.reference` ("NOT checked against the effect ledger ... that is P03's adapter") and nothing performed or read back an operation on a service; (3) "scoped repair cannot affect collateral service": nothing existed.

- **`artifact.publish`** (`artifacts/task-artifacts.ts`, `TaskArtifactPublisher`): the agent that does a task that is not code (or the owner) publishes UTF-8 text files for THAT task. Needs the `artifact.publish` grant in the project (roles name the capability but do not grant it; a meeting decision may grant it) and the right to read the task; a task credential reaches its own task only; path tricks are refused by the manifest rules; repeating the command ID publishes once. Files are text only through the API (binary export files are P03b).
- **`service.operate` / `service.observe`** (`service-ops/`): `ServiceTarget` is the port to the outside system (`observe`, `affects`, `neighbours`, `apply` once per key, `applied`, `verify`); `SimulatedServices` is the deterministic in-process sandbox target (actions `set` and `restart`; a restart cascades to the declared dependents; armable faults: lost answer, leak into a neighbour, wrong write, refusal). It reaches nothing outside the process. `startController({ serviceTarget })` connects a target; without one the operations answer `unavailable`.
  - Scope is a per-resource right: `effect.perform` with `resource { kind: "service", id: "<service>/<resource>" }` (or project-wide). The target says every resource the action reaches; the caller needs the right on EACH, otherwise `forbidden` naming the collateral resource, BEFORE any ledger row or call to the target. An agent must own the task's current attempt (its fence is stored on the effect); the owner may always.
  - The intent (full input, the scope it was judged against, the state before, the versions of everything next to it) is recorded first. The bridge refuses again if the target's reach is beyond the recorded scope (defence in depth), applies once per key, reads the resource back and compares neighbour versions. Verified: `confirmed` with evidence `{verified: true, systemVersion, observedAt, stateDigest, affected, collateralChecked, collateralUnchanged}` taken from the TARGET. A read-back that does not match, or a neighbour that moved, is NOT confirmed: the effect becomes `uncertain` (never retried blindly, `effect_uncertain` on repeat) with `verified: false` and the reason, for a person to resolve. A lost answer is settled by asking the target (`recovered: true`), never by applying again. A target refusal is `failed`, nothing changed.
  - Replay of a command ID looks the effect up first and runs it (it does not re-judge against the state that has moved on); the same ID for a different operation is `command_conflict`.
- **Operational outcomes are verified** (`AcceptancePorts.verifyOutcome`, `ServiceOperations.checkOutcome`): `outcome.reference` must be the ID of a `service-op` effect of the SAME task that is `confirmed` with `verified: true` evidence, and `systemVersion` and `observedAt` must be those the target reported. Checked at draft, revise, new version and submit (a confirmed effect cannot change afterwards). A person-resolved effect (`EffectService.resolve`) lacks `verified: true` and so cannot back an outcome (PROVISIONAL: a hand-checked outcome the owner wants to accept can be added as a separate owner path later). Without the port an outcome cannot be named (fail closed). The old free-text outcomes of the Q01 tests were replaced by real operations.
- **Owner decisions applied (delegated)**: no new setting, limit or budget was added (scope is a grant, so it uses the existing grant operations and their chat commands, narrowing at once and widening proposed, with expectedRevision as for every grant); the operations are agent-facing and are not chat commands. Provisional: default is deny (no `effect.perform` grant, no operation).
- **Tests**: `api/start-p03.test.ts` through `startController` (3 tests: the document path to acceptance by an independent reviewer; operation, ledger, replay, lost answer, wrong write, refusal, outcome naming rules incl. a hand-resolved effect; scoped repair, collateral refused, leak caught, bridge defence in depth, cascade allowed with the right on every resource, no target). `submissions/acceptance.test.ts` (4 backends) covers a missing and a refusing outcome check. Mutation checks done: removing the scope check, the read-back judgement, the neighbour comparison, the confirmed check, the verified-flag check and the same-task check each fails a test.
- **Not done (moved to P03b)**: the agent-facing tools in the protected bridge (T06) and the Pi extension (its tool list is fixed and tested), chat commands for the owner to see an outcome, a real service connector (only the simulated target exists), binary files for artifacts, a real-model trial on a non-code task. Dependency Y02 (QA checkpoint 2, needs the owner's real-hardware run on Linux, macOS and Windows) is still planned, so P03 cannot be flipped while it stays a dependency unless the owner waives or removes it.
- **Collateral limits**: the neighbour comparison covers the resources the target lists as neighbours (the simulated target lists every other resource); a real connector must bound that list. The reconcile path compares against the baseline recorded at intent time, so an unrelated change to a neighbour between intent and recovery makes the effect `uncertain` (conservative).

## A09 notes: reviewed environment changes and maintenance requests (2026-10-31, slice)

`packages/controller/src/maintenance/` (`MaintenanceService`, `MaintenanceApplier` port, `FakeApplier`), 13 API operations (`maintenance.request/get/list/decide/revoke/apply`, `maintenance.settings.get/set/enable/disable`, `maintenance.site.set`, `maintenance.catalogue.add/remove`), chat commands for decide, revoke, apply, enable, disable, site and catalogue; wired in `startController` (`services.maintenance`, `StartOptions.maintenance.applier`). Tests: `api/start-maintenance.test.ts` (3 end-to-end tests through `startController` with SQLite, mutation-checked: digest binding, protected class, site denial at apply and at decision, the claim lease, the pending counter, supervisor standing).

- **Flow.** A request returns a maintenance ID at once (the apply of a rule-approved one runs after the answer, `MaintenanceService.idle()` waits for it). Kinds and classes: `skill` (skill-draft: allowed and recorded, rule `skill-draft`), `package`/`extension` (dependency), `mount`/`network` (access), `host-policy`/`base` (protected). Statuses: pending, approved, applying, applied, rejected, withdrawn, failed, revoking, revoked. Every command writes an audit entry (type `maintenance.*`, subject the request).
- **Deciders.** Strict profile: the owner. Other profiles: also the requester's supervisor, if the chat/API-settable switch `bosses` is on (default off in strict, on otherwise), and never for `protected` (a supervisor role alone cannot change the protected base), never for one's own request, never with a task credential. The owner's rules decide without a person: `rules` (default on) enables the preapproved catalogue (exact name, version, digest; install scripts need an entry with `installScripts: true`) and allowed sites; a denied site always rejects, even with `rules` off; a site denied after the approval stops the application, reverts an applied change and cannot be approved by anyone until the owner clears the rule.
- **Binding.** The verdict carries `specDigest` (sha256 over agent, kind, spec and rollback plan); the apply step recomputes it and re-checks that the approval still stands (a supervisor approval needs the supervisor's standing now, a rule approval its rule); if not, the request goes back to pending with a reason. Specs are closed forms (no host path, no free command, no capability field), so a skill or extension cannot carry a self-grant.
- **Applying.** A claim (approved to applying, revision-guarded, with epoch and lease of 10 minutes) comes before the applier call, so two drivers never both apply; the applier must be idempotent by request ID. `applied`: effect recorded (redacted, at most 4 KB). `unsupported` (safe restoration impossible) or a throw (offline): stays `approved` with `pendingReason`, retried by `maintenance.apply`, `enforce()` and the start-up `resume()`. `failed`: recorded with the rollback the applier reports. Five claims without a result fail the request. A restart finishes a cut-off application (older epoch). A revoke during the application is carried out when it ends.
- **Provisional choices (owner delegated).** Every new setting is off or at the profile default and chat-settable; no time or money budget exists. Widening in chat (enable, site allow, catalogue add, decide) is a proposal; narrowing (disable, site deny, catalogue remove, revoke) applies at once, deny and revoke only when the owner's own words say it and name the site or ID. At most 20 requests of one agent wait for a decision. The pending notice for the owner is filed as a `maintenance` notification (U11b kind not in code).
- **Not done (remainder card A09b).** (1) The real applier: staging, disposable trial environment, Suspend without release, checkpoint, restart, validate and restore keeping session, compaction and prior Pause/Suspend intent, writing the new environment revision through `EnvironmentService`; the default applier leaves every approved change pending. (2) The bridge tool (T06) that lets a worker call `maintenance.request` (today: the state API with the agent's own credential). (3) An "administrator" role for host policy and the base (today the owner only). (4) The scoped-review reviewer view of install scripts: the request shows `installScripts` as a flag only. (5) "Review outage leaves the approved environment working": nothing here touches the running environment before an apply, but no test with a real review service is in. (6) Standing permissions beyond the catalogue and site rules (a grant that already covers the change).


### A09 review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Scan horizon and flood.** Requests that still need the controller (approved, applying, revoking, apply-uncertain, and applied network changes a denial can revoke) are kept in an index kind `maintenance-live`; `resume` and `enforce` read it, never the hash-ordered request list. Every request of an agent counts toward `requestsPerDay` (default 200, owner exempt, 24 h window, chat/API-settable, null = default), however it was decided.
- **Claim fence.** The claim carries a random token, an epoch and a heartbeat (`renewedAt`, renewed every third of the lease while the applier runs). Lease default 30 minutes (`leaseMinutes`, 1 to 1440). Only the token holder completes; any other result is discarded, recorded in `stale` ("stale apply result", last 5) and, where the request is no longer live, reconciled by `revert`. A claim of an older storage epoch counts as dead (the old controller is fenced out of storage); a same-epoch claim is reclaimed only after its lease ran out. The claim write also checks the settings revision seen by the standing check, and an applied network change is re-checked against the site rules when the application ends. The applier contract now says it must be idempotent by ID, must verify `spec.digest` against the fetched artifact and answer `failed` on a mismatch.
- **Unknown state.** A throw is `apply-uncertain`: a `revert` (verify and restore) pass runs before anything else; only when it succeeds does the request return to approved (and `tries` still counts, 5 then failed). A revoke of an approved or pending request that was ever claimed, and of an uncertain one, calls `revert`. A standing check that fails for a request with a possible application starts a revert, it does not simply send it back.
- **Who decides.** `agent.supervisorSetBy` is recorded (create, clone, import, update). A supervisor never decides for an agent it created or whose supervisor it set. Supervisors decide only the kinds in `bossKinds` (package, extension, mount, network; empty by default; host-policy and base never). A mount is scoped: the requester's own resource (`<agent key>.name`) or `shared.name` read-only; another agent's, `owner.` and shared write are the owner's.
- **Closed forms.** Names forbid `/`, `..`, leading `.`, uppercase and `@` (a package may be `@scope/name`); versions are exact; sources are https URLs without credentials (rejected without echoing them); catalogue entries carry a source and an automatic approval needs the same source. Site rules: `host` (deny: every port and every subdomain; allow: port 443), `host:port`, `*.host` (allow only).
- **Settings and chat.** A settings write only marks the work; the 30 s maintenance tick (`MaintenanceService.tick`, bounded by `driveBatch` per round, `maintenance.tickMs` in the start options) or a background tick right after the answer does it (tests: `idle()`). The chat decision preview always shows installScripts, short digest, version, name and source (cut at 90). A request that a supervisor may decide files a notice-level owner entry naming the supervisor; agents have no inbox outside a task, so the supervisor sees it with `maintenance.list`.
- **Limits stated.** Removing a catalogue entry or switching `rules` off stops future automatic approvals only; applied packages stay until revoked. The digest check itself is the applier's duty (the fake applier checks a supplied content digest); the controller only enforces the closed forms and the catalogue match. `delete` of an index entry carries an audit entry.
## K02 (first slice): release staging and activation with a journalled atomic switch (2026-10-31)

- **What is built** (`release/activation.ts`, wired in `startController` by the new `releases: { root }` option, off unless given). Under the release root: `incoming/<candidate>/` (where the build leaves artifacts; the owner names no path, so no chat or API argument can point the controller at an arbitrary file), `releases/<candidate>/` (the staged, read-only release plus `MANIFEST.json`) and the pointer the launcher reads (`current`, a relative symlink replaced by renaming a new one over it, or `current.json` replaced the same way where symlinks need a privilege; chosen by option, default symlink except on Windows).
- **Staging** (`release.stage`): copies exactly the artifacts the submitted candidate's manifest names into a temporary folder (no-follow open, size bound, hashed while copying, files mode 0444), refuses any file whose digest is not the manifest's (nothing is left behind), writes a canonical `MANIFEST.json` whose digest is the release's digest, and moves the folder in with one rename. Unsafe names (`..`, empty parts, backslash, `MANIFEST.json`, case collisions, file-and-folder clashes) and links are refused. A release directory that exists is never written into; a leftover directory with no record is replaced, never trusted. Temporary folders left by a dead run are swept at start.
- **Activation** (`release.activate`): owner only (an owner token confined to a task is refused too), bound to the candidate, to the staged digest the owner quotes, to this installation's platform (the candidate must list it in its matrix) and to the owner's approval (`release.approve`) unless the owner switched that requirement off. Sequence: journal intent in the database (revision guarded; one open switch at a time) -> verify every file against the manifest (changed, added, removed, non-regular files refuse) -> switch the pointer -> commit. At start `recover()` resolves an open journal by what the pointer says: at the new release -> committed, at the old one -> closed as not done, anything else -> left open and shown by `release.status` (never guessed). A pointer moved by hand outside a switch shows as `diverged` and is not rewritten. `release.rollback` goes to the previous release named by its ID, verified first, journalled the same way.
- **Settings** (all owner-only, `expectedRevision`, chat-settable): `requireApproval` (default on) and `maxStagedBytes` (optional cap on all staged releases, off by default). Ops: `release.staging.settings.get/set`, `release.approval.enable` (narrows, applies at once in chat) and `release.approval.disable` (widens, proposed). Chat: `release.stage` applies at once (changes nothing running); `release.activate`, `release.rollback`, `release.staging.settings.set` and `release.approval.disable` are always proposals. The chat layer already requires the candidate ID and digest to appear in the owner's own words.
- **Tests:** `release/activation.test.ts` (48 runs: reference store and SQLite, symlink and pointer switchers, real temp folders; stage, digest mismatch, unsafe names, links, authority, binding, rollback, tamper, crash at three points, unresolved journal, divergence, concurrency, replay, settings, sweep) and `api/start-activation.test.ts` (end to end through `startController`, including a process death right after the switch and before it, with restarts, chat proposals and the tamper check). Mutation checks done: removing the manifest-digest check, the pre-switch verification, the digest binding, the platform check, the open-journal guard, the recovery commit and the task-scope refusal each fail tests; removing the `recover()` call in `startController` fails the end-to-end test.
- **Provisional choices:** release management is the owner's alone for now (a separate grantable permission distinct from `toolbox.manage` is a remainder); source folder fixed at `incoming/<candidate>`; approval required by default; no byte budget unless set; hard internal bounds (100 files, 4 GiB a file, 200 staged releases, 2000 entries per verification) are safety bounds, not budgets.
- **Remainder (K02 stays planned):** the separate launcher and updater programs that read the pointer and the current and candidate directories on macOS and Windows (only the pointer contract and both writers are here; the Windows pointer file is tested on Linux only); signature verification of the artifact set (digests only); controller-worker protocol compatibility check before activation and mixed-version rollback test; a failed-startup watchdog and a last-known-good record (K07 health and commit-or-revert); maintenance scope and window enforcement (K07); target-installation binding beyond the platform; agent-built candidate of NimbleNewt itself (B06 relies on the owner-only rule here); Pi runtime changes (G11).
- **Review fixes (2026-10-31).** (1) `release.activation.resolve` (owner, chat-proposed, `expectedRevision` required, audit and a `resolved` history entry) closes a switch whose pointer names neither release: `commit`, `abort` or `set-pointer`; the old or new files are verified first and the pointer is moved. A close that fails (plain error) leaves the journal and the next `recover` retries it. (2) `release.stage.remove` (owner, chat-proposed) removes a staged release, refused for current, previous (rollback target), either end of an open switch and the pointer's release; `keepStaged` (chat-settable via `release.staging.settings.set`, off by default) prunes the oldest non-live ones after staging. (3) `incoming` is a configurable path (put it outside the release root, under the build's uid); staged folders are 0555 on POSIX; `verifyReleaseDirectory` and the `release.verify` query re-check a release against the manifest digest the activation record keeps (`current.digest`), which is what a launcher should run at launch; activation re-derives the candidate ID from the manifest and needs the approval record for that ID. The uid trust boundary is documented in the module comment: the same uid or root can still change files, which the digest checks detect but do not prevent. (4) Staging is refused when the pointer or the record names that release. (5) The sweep deletes `.tmp-*` only when this process left it (pid in the name, not in use) or it is older than `tmpStaleMs` (one hour). (6) A missing candidate record at activation is `not_found`. (7) Chat activation takes the digest from the staged record (the interpreter's and the owner's words are not used) and shows it in the preview. (8, 9) The unsigned manifest model is stated in the module comment; approvals are bound to the candidate ID (the digest of its manifest) and the owner's word to the staged digest. A withdrawn approval state is not built (remove the staged copy instead).

## H12a notes: the dispatch contract carried to remote workers (2026-10-31)

`packages/controller/src/remote/contract-wire.ts` (the worker's half: format, digest, `contractProblems`, `enforcementFor`; imports nothing of the controller, so `client.ts` may use it), `contract.ts` (the controller's half: `sealContract`, `checkContract`), edits in `dispatch/ports.ts`, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `remote/{service,server,client,host}.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`. Tests: `remote/contract.test.ts` (3 plain + 5 per backend), `api/start-remote-contract.test.ts` (3, through `startController`, the real transport and the owner API).

- **What travels.** `WorkOrder.contract` (`DispatchContract`, plain JSON): format, the task contract's version, permission ceiling and budget (`maxMinutes`, `maxAttempts`, `maxCost`, and what the allowance holds for this attempt), the owner's limits (`cpus`, `memoryMb`, `diskMb`, `processes`, `wallTimeMs`) and best-effort flag as read for this launch, `requires` (`limits`, `wall-time`) and a SHA-256 digest over the contract plus the order's identity, route, recipe (revision, reach, limits) and expiry (never the credential). The dispatcher seals the task part; `RemoteWorkerHost.start` reads the owner's limits and best effort afresh (the same `workers.limits.*` settings that bind local agents, so no new setting) and seals again. A read that fails refuses the start (the attempt fails with "the worker did not start", nothing is offered): nothing goes out unlimited.
- **Worker side (`RemoteAttempt.honorContract(order, abilities)`).** Refuses an order with no contract, an unknown format, a digest that does not match the order, a `requires` name it does not know, a limit it enforces less than in full while best effort is off, or an expired order. It refuses with `POST .../refuse {digest, reasons}` (the run ends failed, reasons on the placement and in the owner's launch record, the dispatcher ends the attempt without a new one) or confirms with `POST .../launched {digest, enforcement[]}` naming, per limit, how far it is enforced.
- **Controller side (enforced there like locally).** The placement stores the digest (`PlacementBody.contract`). Until the worker confirmed that digest for this placement, `begin` is refused (`invalid_transition`): no call is judged, recorded or run. The controller does not take the worker's word: it checks the confirmation itself (every limit named with the contract's figure, none extra, none short of `full` unless best effort was allowed) and ends the run when it is not so. The confirmation is recorded in the owner's launch record (`workers.limits.enforced`) before it counts; a refusal is recorded too. A new placement (move, restart, second placement) starts over: the old host's confirmation does not carry over and a delayed confirmation of an older placement is fenced. The same confirmation again is the same answer; other figures for a confirmed placement are refused. Results (`complete`) and usage (`usage`, idempotent by `turnSeq`) were already carried; the failed result of a refusal reaches the dispatcher through the normal `waitForResult` path.
- **Provisional choices (owner questions at the end).** (1) No new setting: remote hosts follow the existing limits and best-effort settings (chat-settable, API with `expectedRevision`); strict by default. (2) A worker that does not confirm gets no tool calls (rather than a time-out ending the attempt; the lease still ends a silent worker). (3) An order without a contract is refused by a worker built for H12a (`requireContract` is not optional in `contractProblems`). (4) The permission ceiling and budget are shown to the worker but judged only by the controller per call (as for a local worker).
- **Limits and what remains.** (1) The product worker process that takes an offer, calls `honorContract`, launches the sandbox with the confirmed limits and runs Pi is not built (it needs a real host and sandbox; the worker package has no remote runtime): a worker author calls `honorContract` with `enforces` taken from the launcher's real report. (2) A recipe change by a `restart` control message that changes reach or limits needs a new confirmation (see the review fixes below). (3) Limits changed by the owner later apply to the next launch only, as for local agents. (4) Two concurrent identical confirmations may write the launch record twice (the placement itself is guarded by revision). (5) Effect-class tools from remote workers are still refused (H02 limit; a controller-run effect form is not part of this slice). (6) The mid-attempt wall-time limit is the expiry in the order; the worker is trusted to stop at it, and the controller's lease and expiry fence a worker that does not.

### H12a review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Nothing counts before the confirmation.** Until the worker has confirmed the contract of its placement, the controller also refuses usage, checkpoints, a heartbeat (so the lease is not extended: a worker that never confirms is ended by the lease), reports and a `completed` result (`invalid_transition`), not only `begin`. A `failed` or `cancelled` result is still taken (a worker giving up is not a turn).
- **Trust model, stated plainly.** The controller cannot measure a remote worker's limits (no cgroup or rlimit of the other machine is visible to it, and the worker reports none the controller could compare). Limits rest on the worker's attestation (`launched` names how far each limit is enforced), bounded by what the controller does itself: it checks the attestation against the contract's figures and best-effort setting, judges every tool call, ends a silent worker by the lease, and fences an expired order. A worker that lies about enforcement is not caught by this slice. If a worker later supplies cgroup/rlimit evidence, the controller can compare it; nothing is built for that now. The test that shows it says so in its title.
- **A remote placement needs a contract.** `RemoteWorkerService.place` refuses an order with no sealed contract, so the confirmation gate cannot be skipped by leaving the contract out.
- **A restart that changes the recipe needs a new confirmation.** A `restart` control message whose reach or limits differ from the recipe the worker was given clears the confirmation and replaces the digest with `restartDigest(previous digest, new recipe)` (the worker computes the same value); no call is decided until the worker confirms that digest (`RemoteAttempt.confirmRestart`). A restart into the same reach and limits changes nothing. A restart that raises a limit above the owner's contract limit is refused outright. The placement keeps the recipe it was given (`contract.recipe`) to compare against.
- **Launch record order.** `started` is recorded only after the confirmation is on the placement (and once, not again for the same confirmation); a confirmation that is fenced while it is being kept is recorded as `refused`.
- **The digest is not authentication.** It binds a confirmation to the order and recipe; with no TLS between the worker and the controller (plain `http`) nothing protects it from someone who can change both the order and the confirmation in transit. The transport's own authentication and, for a network that is not trusted, TLS are what give integrity.
- **A tampered order.** A worker that sees an order whose contract does not match (its digest cannot be the controller's) refuses it with the digest it computed; the controller no longer answers `fenced` and leaves the run accepted: it ends the attempt as failed with the reasons (the stale-placement fence by placement number is unchanged).
- **Tests.** The import check of `transport.test.ts` now covers `contract-wire.ts` and `protocol.ts` (the files a worker carries) as well as `client.ts`. The test world records the owner's launch records (`world.launches`). Callers of the earlier tests that completed a turn without confirming now confirm first.

## H12a (part 2): effect calls from remote workers run on the controller (2026-11-11, Claude agent)

Closes the limit the first slice left open ("effect-class tools from remote workers are still refused"). Code: `remote/service.ts` (`RemoteWorkerService.effect`, `RemoteDeps.bridges`, `EFFECT_INPUT_BYTES`), `remote/server.ts` (`POST /worker/attempts/{id}/effect`), `remote/client.ts` (`RemoteAttempt.effect`; `call()` now sends an effect executor over the wire instead of throwing), `api/dispatch-compose.ts` (the remote service gets the dispatcher's own `bridges`). Tests: `remote/effects.test.ts` (6 per backend, through the real transport and dispatcher), `api/start-remote-effects.test.ts` (2, through `startController`). Test world: `world.bridges`, `started(..., { tools })`.

- **What travels.** `{ placement, request: ToolCallRequest, effect: { kind, target, input } }`. The controller looks the kind up in its own `bridges` (own properties only), judges the call like a local one (placement, dispatch-contract confirmation, generation fence, pauses, owner decisions, decision revision, policy, approval), writes it on the S05 ledger and runs its bridge. The worker supplies words (kind, target, input, tool name and arguments) and nothing executable: no bridge, no address, no credential; unknown fields are refused (`invalid_command`, 400). An unknown kind, `""` or `constructor` is refused before anything is recorded or run. `input` is capped at 64 KiB.
- **Duplicates, delays, drops.** The call ID is the identity: a message sent again after a lost answer, several at once, or a delayed one is answered from the record and the bridge runs once. The same call ID with other figures gets the recorded answer and applies nothing. A refusal (decision revision, pause, policy) is recorded under its call ID, so the agent calls again under a new ID after the worker acknowledges the decisions (`acknowledge` over the wire, now tested for the effect path and for a stale placement).
- **Lost link.** An effect that started and whose answer never reached the worker stays `in-progress` on the ledger; when the lease runs out the dispatcher finds the attempt lost and settles the call from the ledger and the target's `reconcile` (as for a local worker), the old attempt is fenced, and a late duplicate or a new call from the old placement is `fenced`. Tested with a replaced dispatcher over the same storage; the bridge applied once.
- **Review fixes (2026-11-11, clean-context review).** (1) The bridge is bound to what was judged: `effect.kind` must be the call's tool name (a call judged as `git-push` could otherwise run any bridge the controller has, such as `deploy`) and `effect.input` must equal the call's arguments in canonical JSON (the policy's protected-branch check and an approval see the arguments; input naming `main` under arguments naming `feature-x` would have pushed `main`). Both are refused `invalid_command` before anything is recorded. ASSUMPTION: one bridge per tool name, named after the tool; a mapping from tool to bridge kind can come with the T-card bridges. (2) The effect (kind, target, input; never the bridge) is part of the call's identity: `invocation.effectDigest` on the operation (written for local effect calls too, so the ledger is the same), compared when the call is asked again and when two asks join in one process. The same call ID naming another effect is refused `command_conflict` (409); before, a finished call answered with the first call's result and a parked call, once approved, would have run the new effect. (3) The 64 KiB cap is measured on the canonical JSON in bytes (the transport's 1 MiB body cap is checked before parse). Tests: kind/input mismatch, prototype and case/unicode kind names, non-string kinds, bytes against characters, another target under a finished and under a parked call ID.
- **Still open (bridge work).** `effect.target` is the worker's text, bound to the call's identity but not judged by the policy: a real bridge (T-cards) must resolve it only within the task's project and refuse any other address.
- **No new owner setting.** Which effects a remote worker may cause is decided by the existing policy, grants, approvals and pauses, all already reachable by chat; the bridges are code the operator composes (`dispatch.dispatcher.bridges`), not an owner control. ASSUMPTION: no chat command or interpreter change is needed for this slice. The composed controller still has no production bridge (as for local workers: the tests supply one), so a remote effect call is refused with "no bridge" until a bridge is registered.
- **Not done.** (1) The product worker process that takes an offer, runs Pi in a sandbox and calls `honorContract`/`effect` (needs a real host; unchanged from the first slice). (2) The controller cannot tell a remote worker's own claim about the branch or spend from the truth any more than for a local one: it uses the same `protectedBranch` hook where wired. (3) No chunked transfer for large effect inputs (64 KiB cap). (4) A real effect bridge per kind (git push, merge, deploy) is T-card work; the lost-link settle needs the bridge's `reconcile`, and a bridge without one leaves the effect `uncertain` for the owner. (5) A controller restart while a worker's request is open drops that HTTP request; the worker's retry with the same call ID gets the settled answer.

## L02d (part 2): the worker reports what it holds, a Stop ends it, and the cleanup is billed (2026-10-31)

- **Worker report.** `WorkerHost.localWork?(attemptIds)` returns `{ processes, costs }`: the local processes and child work still held for those attempts (running, uncooperative, unknown) and the cleanup cost so far as a running total per attempt. `LocalWorker` implements it from its sandbox sessions (`SandboxSession.work?()`, optional; asked also after `close()`, so a process that outlived its confinement is found; the sessions are kept for 500 attempts, oldest dropped). `DispatcherService.localWorkOf(by, ids)` (staff only) asks every host, bounds it (500 attempts, 200 entries per host), drops cost figures that are not whole numbers of zero or more or are for an attempt not asked about, and lets a host that throws fail the whole look (the stop then shows the unknown item `runtime:processes`). `startController` uses it as `localWork` unless the composer passes its own (`hostLocalWork` in `lifecycle/dispatch-ports.ts`). A real sandbox backend that lists a confinement's processes still has to supply `SandboxSession.work` (remainder, needs the OS).
- **Stop ends what it counts.** For mode `stop` the preparation waits only for calls in flight (and anything already asked to stop that did not); processes, child work and jobs are ended in the ending step. `terminate` now asks each background job of the task and of its swarm children to stop (`jobs.requestCancel`, as the principal advancing the stop; a Force Stop escalates one already asked; a permitted remote job the controller tracks is the named exception and is never cancelled; a job the asker may not control is unresolved). Pause does not touch jobs (owner decision). A job that has been asked and not confirmed shows as `uncooperative`, so the stop is `recovery-required` and Force Stop is offered until the host confirms (`confirmCancel`). A Suspend still waits for everything.
- **Swarm children.** A Stop of a task includes the live attempts of its swarm descendants (`swarmDescendants`, read from the `swarm-link` records, deepest first, at most 200): they are quiesced, listed as `child` items while their attempt is live, and stopped with the task. Not done: pausing the children's own gates (a child could start a new attempt during a long preparation) and children of the tasks under an agent, team or installation scope; for those `swarm.cancel` remains the way to settle a swarm.
- **Cleanup spend.** `StopPorts.charge` and the `costs` of `cleanup` and `terminate`: the stop charges the part of each attempt's running total it has not charged yet to that attempt's task budget (`budget.charge`, activity `stop-cleanup`, recorded even on a closed budget), at the end of every cleanup pass and after the ending. What was charged is kept per attempt (see the review fixes below), the command ID derives from the totals, so a repeated pass, a retry or a restart charges nothing twice and a crash between the charge and its note replays. A charge that fails is kept for the next pass; one still failing after the ending makes the result `recovery-required` with "cleanup spend not charged". The part counted against `spendBudget` is what was charged. `spendBudget` stays a per-request option (optional, none by default, unit: millionths of the budget currency, cost only); no new global setting was added, so no new settings op or chat command is needed (provisional).
- **Restart.** Attempts seen are already kept on the request (L06b), the `charged` totals are too; the sweep carries on from there.
- Tests: `api/start-stop-local-work.test.ts` (through `startController`: a host's process named and redacted, job asked to stop, cost billed once and not again after a sweep, a host that cannot answer is unknown, a Force Stop still ends the attempt, a swarm child's attempt and job are ended by the parent's Stop and a Pause leaves them), `lifecycle/stop.test.ts`, `lifecycle/dispatch-ports.test.ts`, `dispatch/local-worker.test.ts`.
- Remains in L02d: a real sandbox backend's `work()` (processes of a confinement, OS needed), pausing swarm children during a stop, children under agent/team/installation scopes, confirmation of job stops by a real job host (`confirmCancel`), a chat view of the charged cleanup spend.

### L02d review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **A stopped parent keeps its swarm children from starting.** The dispatcher asks `heldBy(taskId)` before it starts an attempt; the composer answers from the task's swarm ancestors (up to 50 levels): if one has a Stop or Suspend request that is not cancelled and the ancestor's own pause gate still holds, the attempt is skipped with the reason "its parent task X is stopped". Resuming the parent, or a cancelled request, lets go; a child spawned after the Stop is held the same way. No pause gate is written on the children (so nothing is left behind to release, and a Pause of the parent alone still leaves the children as they were). `StopService.holding(taskId)` is the question. A child the asker may not control is held too: the hold is a consequence of the parent's Stop, not an act on the child.
- **Authority per child.** A Stop of a task ends a child's attempts and jobs only for the owner or someone who holds the budget of the child's parent (like `swarm.cancel`) or may control the child's own scope (`mayControl`). The others are named in the unresolved list ("child T: not stopped, X may not control it", the attempt that keeps running, "job J: not stopped ...") and are neither quiesced nor have their ending dropped, so the result is `recovery-required` rather than a silent partial stop.
- **What was charged is kept per attempt**, in a `stop-charge` record (not per request): Suspend then Stop, overlapping task and agent stops, and a Stop after a resume never charge the same total again. Each step is written before it is done (outbox): the new total is noted as pending with the command ID derived from (attempt, total charged so far, new total), then the charge is made, then the note is cleared; the next try (a pass, or `sweep`) finishes a pending charge with the same command ID first. So a crash after a charge followed by a larger total charges the part already paid once and only the rest as new. A host figure above 10^12 is cut to it. A charge that failed counts once against `spendBudget` and is retried by every later pass and by `sweep` (also for a request that already ended); when it succeeds the "cleanup spend not charged" mark is taken off that request's result (the state stays what it was). A charge to a budget the owner has closed is not refused: the budget ledger records the spend flagged as such, by design, so there is nothing to skip.
- **A replaced sandbox is not forgotten.** `LocalWorker` keeps every sandbox session of an attempt (at most 8, oldest idle first) and asks all of them; an older one that reports nothing left is folded into the attempt's running cost and dropped. The attempt's cost is the sum over its sessions. `HostLocalWork.known` names the attempts the host has a record of: an asked attempt that is not finished in the dispatcher's records, on that host, and not known to it (a controller restart emptied its memory) reads as one `unknown` item, never as nothing running. `RemoteWorkerHost.localWork` reports one `unknown` item for each live remote placement (the controller cannot see the other machine's processes and no worker report exists yet); once the Stop has ended the placement the item is gone. A Suspend of a live remote attempt therefore waits on that item (it is unknown until the worker reports; Stop is not held up, it ends the attempt itself).
- **Limits of the lists.** More than 200 descendants, or links beyond the 40 pages (20,000) read, add an `unknown` child item ("swarm:descendants-truncated"); a list of an agent's jobs cut at 1,000 adds "jobs:truncated". `localWorkOf` drops processes of attempts that were not asked about, as it does for costs.
- **Agent, team and installation Stops** find jobs through the attempt that owns each job (`jobs.unfinishedAll`), so only that agent's (or those agents') jobs are asked to stop, also on a task with no live attempt, and never another agent's job on the same task. A job with no attempt has no known owner and is left alone.
- **Jobs and the checkpoint.** A Stop asks the task's background jobs to stop before the checkpoint is taken (preparation does not wait for them; the ending step asks again, escalates and names what stays). A Suspend leaves jobs running while it checkpoints, so the checkpoint is of the conversation and files at that moment and anything a job produces after it is not in it; this is by design (Pause and Suspend do not touch background jobs).
- **Cosmetic.** `#update` has its own doc comment again; the swarm walk is done once per port call (`inventory`, `cleanup`, `checkpoint`, `terminate`).

## H12q: landing behind the quiesce, and the production workspace port (2026-10-31)

Code: `landing` in `WORKSPACE_OPERATIONS` (`workspace-ops/workspace-ops.ts`, `dispatch/quiesce.ts`, `remote/protocol.ts`), the host side in `packages/worker/src/workspace/host.ts`, the production port in `packages/worker/src/workspace/local-host.ts` (`LocalWorkspaces`), and `LocalWorker.busyAttempts()`. Tests: `host.test.ts` (landing cases), `local-host.test.ts`, and `packages/integration/src/h12q-landing-quiesce.test.ts` (through `startController`).

- **Landing is a sixth operation of `workspace.request`** (same right, `workspace.manage`; same record, replay, open index, crash recovery, freeze tag and `isBusy` hold as the others), so it runs inside `QuiesceCoordinator.around`: the task's live attempts have new calls refused, calls in flight settled and a checkpoint taken before the host is asked, and an attempt of the task is not started while the request runs or is left open. The running agent is told "was landed on the landing branch". Proven through the state API: the host is asked only after the call in flight has ended (the call ends only on the stop signal), and a waiting second attempt is held back and then started.
- **What the host does for a landing.** An integration (A04 bridge, file by file, no commit) that is made only (1) while the checkout's base is the landing branch's current head, otherwise refused with nothing written ("the author refreshes onto the head first"), and (2) when the checkout holds no uncommitted file (only committed work lands). The detail adds `landed`: true only when nothing was kept for review and the base moved (`markIntegrated`). Provisional choices: the head check is strict equality (after a landing the base is the agent's commit, so a second landing of the same work is refused rather than repeated); landing makes no commit in the shared repository (promotion is P10c).
- **The production workspace port is `LocalWorkspaces`** (worker package): one layout `<root>/<project>/<task>/{checkout,task.git,complete}`, `<root>/shared-state/<tree>` (the bridge's state, one per shared tree), `<root>/.making`, `<root>/quarantine`, `<root>/journal`. `ensure({taskId, projectId})` makes the attempt's checkout from the shared head once and finds it again for later attempts (it refuses a task whose checkout was quarantined, rather than start an agent on an empty folder); `locate` serves the operations from the same layout; `port.run` is what `LocalWorker`'s `workspace` option and a remote worker's responder take. Its `attemptsQuiet` is built in: a request names attempts, the host asks `busy()` and refuses to start if one of them has a call in flight, or if `busy()` throws. `LocalWorker.busyAttempts()` is the source (tool calls plus model calls, the same count the pause logic uses).
- **Not done, said plainly (new card H12s).** No product code builds a `LocalWorker` over `localWorkerParts` and `LocalWorkspaces` yet (only tests do); `HostOrder` carries no task or project, so the worker host's `workspace(order)` cannot yet ask `ensure`; a remote worker's real main does not exist, so nothing forces it to give the responder the busy check (the host trusts the controller's quiesce when `attemptsQuiet` is absent). The landing lease, queue, reservations, mechanical re-apply of disjoint files and the escalation after the refresh-round cap stay with P10; the host's landing is a single carry onto the current head, not a queue.
- Known limits: superseded by the review fixes below (the busy check now sees sandbox processes; `ensure` is serialised and atomic).

### H12q review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Serialised by the shared tree.** The host runs integration and landing one at a time per shared tree (a second queue inside the per-checkout one, always checkout first), and `LocalWorkspaces` keeps the bridge's locks and kept changes in `<root>/shared-state/<hash of the shared path>`, one per tree, so two tasks of a project share them; the bridge also takes a tree-wide lock (`exclusive("landing")`) so a second host process over the same folders waits or is refused.
- **The tree is checked, not just the head.** A landing leaves its files uncommitted and the head does not move, so before any write the shared tree must be on the named landing branch (policy `branch`; no policy or no branch = refused, never guessed from what the tree is on), not detached, and hold no uncommitted or untracked non-ignored file. The branch, head and cleanliness are read again inside the locks just before the first rename (a change refuses the landing, nothing written) and the branch and head again after the last (a change is reported: `detail.partial: true`, `landed: false`, "look at the shared workspace"; the files are not rolled back because a commit may already contain them). **Decision (provisional): the integrator or owner commits the landed files.** A landing reports `waitingToCommit: true` and its summary says "landed changes are waiting to be committed"; the next landing is refused with that text until the tree is clean, and the running agent is told the same. A real owner notice for the integrator (a blocker or notification of kind `landed-changes-waiting`) is not built; it needs the notice-level setting (`owner-decision-notice-level-per-kind`) and is left for the card that makes P10 promotion commit.
- **Planned once from committed objects.** `GitBridge.landingPlan` reads `git diff base..HEAD` of the checkout's own git directory and the blobs of its HEAD commit; the live working tree is never read for a landing, so a file a sandbox process writes after the dirty check is not landed (test: a hook writes after the check). The checkout must still be clean, including ignored files, as before. A mode-only change is listed and not carried. `LocalWorker.busyAttempts()` is now asynchronous and also counts an attempt that has a process running in any of its sandbox sessions (`localWork`, L02d); a sandbox that cannot answer makes it throw and the host treats the attempt as not quiet.
- **All or nothing.** `WorkspaceBridge.writeSet` locks every path in a fixed order, reads every file, and if any file is not at its expected version, or is held for review, writes nothing and keeps those files (pending records); otherwise it makes every new file beside its target and renames them, putting back the earlier ones if a later step fails. The host answers `landed: false`, `written: 0`, `changed: false` and lists what was kept; the agent is told "was NOT landed: N written, M kept (paths)" instead of "was landed". The state is still `done` (the host did what it was asked: nothing unsafe was written): **`done` can mean not landed; callers read `detail.landed`** (documented in `workspace.request` and api-v1.md). At most 500 files and 64 MiB per landing. Folders made for new files stay when a landing is stopped late (empty).
- **`ensure` is atomic.** The folder is built under `<root>/.making/<random>` (git directory, checkout, then the `complete` mark) and renamed to `<root>/<project>/<task>`; `locate` and `ensure` use only folders with the mark, so a crash leaves nothing that looks like a checkout (leftovers older than ten minutes are swept) and a folder without the mark is refused, not adopted. Calls for one task in one process are queued; another process that finishes first wins the rename and the loser uses its folder.
- **Permit and protected paths.** Policy `requirePermit` (default true): every commit between the base and the checkout's head must carry the review gate's `NimbleNewt-Request:` trailer and `NimbleNewt-Task: <this task>`; otherwise refused (work reaches the shared tree through review). Protected paths (`.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`, hook directories `.husky/` `.githooks/`, `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.travis.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`) are held: the whole landing writes nothing and those files are kept for the owner's review. **Settings (every setting chat-settable): `workspace.landing.branch`, `workspace.landing.requirePermit`, `workspace.landing.protectedPaths`.** The host takes them as one callback (`WorkspaceHostOptions.landing`, `LocalWorkspacesOptions.landing`); the registration of these keys in the controller's settings and the wiring of the callback to them are not done here (no product code builds `LocalWorkspaces` yet, see H12s), so they are a host-configuration seam today.
- **Names.** Task and project names go through `plainName` (names.ts: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, the path-component rules of `nameProblem` including no `:` and no trailing dot, no device names, not Git's name), a project cannot be called `journal`, `quarantine`, `shared-state` or `.making`, and a task or project folder is refused when another folder differs only in case or Unicode form (`fold`). The assignee still allows `:` (`agent:ann`).
- **Docs.** The `localWork` doc comment is back above `localWork`; the operation lists in headers name landing; `workspace.request` documents `detail.landed`, `kept`, `partial`, `waitingToCommit` and that `done` can mean not landed.
- Tests: host.test.ts (serialisation, same file two tasks, tree/branch/detached/untracked/no policy, untracked and ignored checkout files, plan from committed objects, commit during the landing before/after the writes, all-or-nothing with a kept file, protected paths and the setting, permit, names), local-host.test.ts (crash before the checkout is filled, unmarked folder, concurrent ensure, shared state, case collision), workspace.test.ts (`writeSet` including the put-back, protected path matching), local-worker.test.ts (sandbox process makes an attempt busy), workspace-ops.test.ts (not-landed is told as such), and the integration test, whose head-check scenario now commits the landed file and a new file as real separate commits.
## U09 (part 3): replay of one task, read only (2026-10-31)

- `activity/replay.ts`, `ReplayService` (built on `ActivityService`'s own read operations, so rights, redaction and unavailable ranges are the same as reading the steps): `open` (summary first: steps by kind, outcome, branch line and actor, unavailable ranges, redacted / replaced / corrected / no-context counts; then a window from `from`, filtered by lane, actor or kind, with `next`), `step` (one step in full with its explanations, written-at-the-time and asked-for-afterwards kept apart and labelled), `led` ("what evidence and instruction led to this change", answered with links: manifest refs, evidence refs written at the time, the nearest five earlier instructions, messages, sources and approvals on the same line, what it replaces; links are references, never resolved here), `search` (summaries only), `export` (`nimblenewt-replay/1`; stored content and thinking never in it), `thinking` (owner only).
- Data contract for the web view: the TypeScript types `ReplayView`, `ReplayStep`, `ReplayDetail`, `ReplayLink` and the `REPLAY_LABELS` texts (exported from `activity/index.ts`); operations `activity.replay.open|step|led|search|export` (queries) and `activity.replay.thinking` (command: a recorded look); chat/status view `replay` (`{ taskId|taskTitle, seq?, from?, limit?, lane?, agent? }`).
- `activity.record` takes three new optional fields: `outcome` (proposed, dispatched, confirmed, uncertain), `branch` (a name; no branch = main line) and `supersedes` (an earlier step number). A step without `outcome` shows "not-recorded", never "confirmed". A step that a later step supersedes is `authority: "superseded"` with `supersededBy`.
- Branch lanes: a step on another branch is on its own lane with `previousInLane` / `nextInLane`; when more than one lane exists the view carries `REPLAY_LABELS.concurrent` (numbers show recording order, not that one came before another). No timing overlap is computed.
- No effect: the service holds no port that can run a tool, send, submit a job or call a model. The test counts every `applyOperation` on the storage while opening, stepping, linking, searching, exporting and building the chat lines: zero. (The effect ledger, deliveries and timers all go through that call, so zero writes covers the ledger and outbox; the router is not reachable from the service at all.)
- Thinking: never read by opening or stepping. The owner's step view says only whether retention removed it (`thinkingRemoval.removedAt`, a port); `thinking` is the explicit expansion through `ThinkingService.read` (policy check, redaction, recorded look), returned `collapsed: true` and labelled as model output, not an explanation. Retention removed it: `removed-by-retention` and nothing else, timeline unchanged (tested).
- Provisional choices: scan limit 1000 steps per task (the summary says `scanLimited`); page 20 (max 50); the nearest five earlier leading steps for `led`; step view reads up to 500 retrospective explanations; lane name pattern `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,79}`; a gap has no known lane or actor so it is shown only in unfiltered windows. Thinking is per task, not per step (stored blocks carry no step number).
- Not built (U09b): the web view (packages/ui has only an empty `index.ts`, so there was no view pattern to follow), producers that set outcome / branch / supersedes (today nothing does), composing `ThinkingService` and the K06c retention marker in `startController` (so `activity.replay.thinking` answers "no stored thinking" in the running controller), links resolved to diffs and comments, rerun or simulation (P07), and the validation scenario through the running controller.

## U09 (part 4): review fixes for the replay (2026-10-31)
- **Who reads (finding 1, 12).** `ActivityService.#mayRead` is now async. A principal that holds the `reviewer` role (and not `director`) reads only a task it has a review assignment for (the same `reviewAssignments(principalId, taskId)` port the submissions use, Q01c); with no such port nobody is assigned, so a reviewer reads nothing (fail closed, same as submissions). Integrator, QA and docs agents keep the project-wide `history.read`; a director keeps it because it signs off for the whole project. Sensitive content needs the owner, a service or the new `history.sensitive.read` grant: a project-wide `history.read` (several role bundles carry it) reads ordinary content only. Size and redaction count of sensitive content are shown only to a reader who may read the text (`ActivityService.contentReadable`). `activity.steps` itself still returns the raw payload metadata to history readers; only the replay view hides it. A host principal reads a task's steps when the optional `hostOwnsAttempt` port is absent (hosts are infrastructure that carries out attempts across projects and already record their steps) and only tasks it holds an attempt of when it is given; the port is not composed yet. **Not composed in `startController`:** `reviewAssignments` (nor is it for submissions), so in the running controller a role-reviewer sees no task's activity until that source exists.
- **Task credentials (finding 2).** `activity.replay.*`, `activity.steps` and `activity.payload` refuse a task credential for any task but its own.
- **Supersedes (finding 3).** A step may supersede a step only when it is by the same actor, the owner or a service, and on the same line (branch); otherwise `forbidden`.
- **Outcome and branch (finding 4).** The view says `outcomeNote: "reported by <kind>"` unless the actor is a service, and `laneStatus` (`main`, `controller`, `verified`, `unverified`; `unverified` carries `laneNote: "unverified lane"`). `ReplayDeps.branchKnown(taskId, lane)` is the registry hook; it is not composed (the context branches are keyed by branch ID with no lookup by task and name), so every agent-named line reads unverified. `led` for a step on a side line also links the owner's main-line instructions and owner messages.
- **Windows and bounds (finding 5).** A view reads a window by step number: by default the newest `scan` steps, from `from` when given, around the step for `step`/`led`. `step`/`led` for any step number work. `summary.range` says what was read; an export or a detail cut by a page bound says `truncated`/`retrospectiveTruncated`. The bounds (`scan` 50000, `exportPages` 200, `stepPages` 100) are a setting (`ReplayLimitsService`, ops `replay.limits.get/set/enable/disable`, chat commands, `expectedRevision`); `enabled: false` removes all of them. A `led` main-line search reaches back half the window.
- **Chat (finding 6).** A title that fits several tasks, or only part of a title, lists the candidates and asks; nothing is read. **Status (7, 9).** `status.ask` documents `replay`; `next` of `open` is the next step to show (pass it as `from`), the status line says "continue from step N". **Thinking (8).** The owner is told `unavailable (not wired)` when the thinking store or the retention marker is not part of the controller; everyone else still gets "no stored thinking". The `start.ts` comment now names U09b (U09c does not exist).

## U11c: the Urgent triggers the controller watches for itself (2026-10-31)

- **Built** (`notifications/urgent.ts`, `UrgentWatch`): the dispatcher's tick runs the sweep `urgent.watch` (just before `notifications.run`, so an Urgent item is delivered in the same tick). (1) No good backup within `backupMaxAgeHours` (default 48): measured from the newest good backup (`BackupService.lastGood`: the rule the nightly run uses, not a pre-upgrade snapshot and trusted by its folder name, with the time taken from the name, not the manifest; a time in the future or unreadable counts as no backup); with none at all, from when "no backup" was first seen, kept in the notification state so restarts do not give it a fresh 48 hours; an unreadable backups folder decides nothing. (2) A host whose identity is active and that has been silent (stale) for `hostDownAfterMinutes` (default 10; a host never heard from or revoked is not "down"). (3) Repeated policy denials: the tool path's "denied by policy" now tells `DispatcherDeps.denied`, and `reportDenial` counts per agent in a window (`deniedWindowMinutes`, default 60); the denial that reaches `deniedThreshold` raises one item, later ones only add to its count. (4) `reportSecurity({ kind, key })` for a sandbox escape attempt, a credential used from the wrong task or host, a protected path touched, a failed integrity check (always Urgent, once per key).
- Each is an item of kind `maintenance` raised by `emitFromController` with the new controller-only `interrupt` flag (level Urgent, sent at once, also in quiet hours) and a controller-only `label` (the text that may leave the installation, built from names and counts; the reason is in the inbox-only detail). `interrupt` honours the existing `urgentInterruptsQuietHours` setting (default true; false: it waits for the end of quiet hours). An agent cannot set `interrupt` or `label`. A cleared condition (a backup made, a host heard from) closes its item through `settleFromController` (de-escalation of these items); a new episode is a new item.
- **Settings (owner-only, chat-settable through `notifications.configure`, with `expectedRevision`):** `backupMaxAgeHours` (1 to 8760), `hostDownAfterMinutes` (1 to 1440), `deniedThreshold` (2 to 10000), `deniedWindowMinutes` (1 to 1440). A number sets or turns a trigger on, `null` turns it off. `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Provisional choices (for the owner):** the denial trigger is off until the owner sets a threshold (the card says "owner-set"; no default invented); the host default of 10 minutes is mine (the card gives none; the host freshness window itself stays 90 s); a backup "good" means the newest listed backup, not a freshly verified one; a failed backup run does not by itself raise Urgent (only the age does; it is named in the label and detail when the age does raise it). Denial counts live in the process: a restart starts them again.
- **Tests:** `notifications/urgent.test.ts` (all backends: backup at 47/49 hours, quiet hours, told once, closed by a new backup, limits moved and switched off, host silent 5/11 minutes, revoked and never-heard hosts, recovery and a second outage, denial threshold/window/per-agent/off, security events, quiet-hours wait when the owner chose it, agents cannot set `interrupt`/`label`); `api/start-urgent-watch.test.ts` (through `startController` and the dispatcher tick with the real backup service and an external channel). Not tested: the tool-path hook that reports a denial (no existing test builds a policy denial).
- **Not here (card U11d):** owner-marked critical tasks and the goal-based critical path; ranking the Needs-you view by it; the Urgent trigger for a blocked critical path and for work stopped with nothing else to do; de-escalation of escalated Needs-you items by the dispatcher; the controller-down watchdog; callers of `reportSecurity` (A08, sandbox, credential and protected-path detectors do not call it yet); denial reports from refusal points other than the tool approval policy; the 09:00 digest only when no stand-up is scheduled; answering in place from the Needs-you view; deferred meeting items from M03.

### U11c review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Occurrences.** An event keeps 50 records (derived IDs); when all 50 are closed the one closed longest ago is used again, so a trigger that clears and raises for ever (a host flapping) is never muted. The watch reads what it has open from the notification state (`openRefIds`), not from process memory: restarts forget nothing, a host that is no longer listed has its item closed after a whole pass, and setting a trigger to `null` closes its open item (chosen; the owner turning a trigger off means "stop telling me about it").
- **Rate limits for the controller's Urgent triggers (interrupts).** They count against the hourly Urgent limit (`escalationsPerHour`, default 10, now `null` = off, shared with escalations): beyond it the item is raised in the inbox, still Urgent, not sent, and ONE "N more" summary goes out per hour window (not counted against the limit). A per-record minimum gap `urgentMinGapMinutes` (default 30, `null` = off) holds a repeat of the same record (a flapping host); a gap-held item is a repeat, so it is not named in the summary. Held items are never sent later. Both settings are chat-settable through `notifications.configure`. Interrupts still bypass quiet hours unless `urgentInterruptsQuietHours` is false (then the release after quiet hours is held to the same limits). Across agents, `deniedAlertsPerHour` (default 5, `null` = off; in process memory) caps how many agents' denial bursts page in an hour; the rest are raised in the inbox as Needs you.
- **Denials.** Reported once, by the tool call that wrote the refusal (`ToolPath` passes a callback to `#refuse`), so a judgement redone after a stale revision or the same call made twice at once is one denial. A run of denials pages once; later ones only add to the item (label and count move); when the denials stopped for a whole window and a new run reaches the threshold, the open item is closed and a new one raised (told).
- **Sweep.** The dispatcher runs it at most every `sweepEverySeconds` (the existing setting, default 60); hosts are read 100 per sweep from a cursor; each host is tried on its own, so one failing host does not hide the others (the first failure is raised after). Each read of the backup folder or the host list gives up after 20 seconds (`stepTimeoutMs`) and the dispatcher gives every loop `loopTimeoutMs` (default 60 s, 0 = off); a loop that timed out is reported failed and not started again until it ends.
- **Security events** have a reference per key (hash of kind and key), so two events of one kind are two items.
- **Tests.** `urgent.test.ts` (60 flap cycles, one failing host, restarts with and without a backup, future/unreadable backup times and the failed-run label, 100 hosts down, the gap, 250 hosts by cursor with gone hosts, throttle and hung read, second burst and cross-agent cap, security keys); `dispatcher.test.ts` (denial told once, also for the same call twice at once); `loops.test.ts` (hung loop); `backup.test.ts` (`lastGood`); `start-urgent-watch.test.ts` (a stale host through the real `HostService`); `start-urgent-denial.test.ts` (a real policy denial through `ToolPath`, `start.ts`, `dispatch-compose` and `DispatcherDeps.denied`, counted once; the restriction is placed between the grant check and the policy, the only way the policy itself denies).

## U11c (completion): security events reported by other services; limits all chat-settable (2026-11-11)

- **Found, not rebuilt.** The backup, host-silence and denial triggers, the Urgent interruption (also in quiet hours), de-escalation and the chat-settable limits were already on main from the first slice and its review fixes (above). This pass checked each against the card and added what was missing: the card's fourth trigger had only an in-process method (`reportSecurity`) and no way for another service to reach it.
- **Done.** New state API command `security.report` (`kind`, `key`, optional `projectId`), callable only by a host or a service principal (an agent, a task credential and the owner are refused). It goes to `UrgentWatch.reportSecurityFrom`: the kind is checked, the key is 1 to 200 characters and is hashed together with the reporter's ID (one reporter cannot mute or fake another's event; the same key from the same reporter is one event, told once, and costs no allowance). The item is Urgent, sent at once, also in quiet hours (unless `urgentInterruptsQuietHours` is false), and only the kind and the reporter's name leave the installation, never the key. New owner limit `securityReportsPerHour` (default 20 per reporter, 1 to 1000, `null` = off) set through `notifications.configure`, so by chat; beyond it a reporter's further distinct reports go into ONE collected Needs-you item for that reporter (not paged, count rising), so a wrong or compromised reporter cannot fill the inbox. Tests: two new `urgent.test.ts` cases (all backends), a `start-urgent-watch.test.ts` case through the running controller, and the chat test now sets every U11c limit (backup hours, host minutes, denial threshold, security allowance) and turns two off by free-form chat. `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a host or a service may report; agents may not (an agent is the thing being watched). Default allowance of 20 separate reports an hour per reporter is mine; the owner changes or removes it by chat.
- **Not done (stays in U11d):** the detectors themselves. Nothing in the controller or the worker yet calls `security.report` or `reportSecurity` (A08 integrity failures, sandbox escape attempts, a credential used from the wrong task or host, a touched protected path); the worker-side hook that sends a report over the host channel is not built. Security items are closed by the owner's answer; there is no automatic de-escalation because these are events, not conditions. Denial counts remain in process memory.
- **Review fixes (clean-context review, 2026-11-11).** (1) The command ID of a report held the raw key (`urg-sec:<kind>:<reporter>|<key>`) and command IDs are limited to 120 characters, so any key longer than about 40 to 80 characters failed with an internal error although 200 are allowed; the command ID is now the event's hash (fixed length, and the key is no longer kept in the command log). The in-process `reportSecurity` had the same fault and is hashed apart from reporters' events (`controller|...`). (2) The kind was checked with `in`, so `toString` or `constructor` passed and put function source into the label; it is now an own key of the table. (3) `projectId` was free text (up to 100 characters) that went into the item and its identity; it must now be a project ID, and the project is part of the event (same kind, key and project). (4) The same event reported again after the owner closed its item reused the command ID with a different item and was refused with `command_conflict`; it now answers with its first item, not raised or paged again (told once), and costs no allowance; the allowance is counted only after the item was raised. Test: `urgent.test.ts` "card U11c review" (200-character key, prototype names, a non-project ID, a closed event retried, another project, the controller's own event against a reporter's).
- **Known limits (not changed).** The per-reporter hourly counts are in memory (a restart or more than 1000 reporters starts them again); Urgent (`interrupt`) items are not held to the open-items limit, so separate security items stay bounded only by `securityReportsPerHour` per reporter per hour until the owner answers them. The key length is counted in UTF-16 units (a character outside the BMP counts twice).

## U11d (security slice): the detectors the controller can run itself, and the hook that reports (2026-11-11)

- **Base.** The `security.report` command (U11c completion) was not on `ac53bd2e`; it sat on `card5-u11c` (`c113161e`, `d6f3d9cb`). This branch merges it first and builds on it.
- **Done: the reporting path.** `notifications/security-detect.ts`, `SecurityDetectors.signal(source, { kind, key, projectId? })`: synchronous, never throws, never waits.
