A signal is deduped in memory (source, kind, project, key; 5000 keys, oldest forgotten first) before any work, queued (200 waiting, 4 reporting at once), and reported through `UrgentWatch.reportSecurityFrom` as a service of its own per detector source (`service:detect-<source>`), so the U11c rules apply: Urgent at once (also in quiet hours unless the owner chose otherwise), once per event, an hourly allowance per reporter (`securityReportsPerHour`, default 20, chat-settable) and ONE collected Needs-you item beyond it. What overflows the queue is counted and comes out as ONE `overflow:<hour>:<n>` event per source and hour. A report that failed is forgotten and may be tried again. One noisy detector cannot use another's allowance.
- **Done: owner switch.** New setting `securityDetectors` (true by default) in `notifications.configure`, so by chat ("do not tell me about wrong-task credential use for now"); read at each report; false drops signals (and forgets them, so the same sign reported again once it is on again is told); a failing settings read counts as on. The refusals themselves never change. Chat test and `api-v1.md` updated.
- **Done: detectors the controller runs itself (signals that already existed).** (1) A task credential naming another task: `ownTask` and `ownTaskOnly` in the state API (every activity, replay, job and task operation that reads as missing/forbidden for a sibling) tell `Context.detect("credential", { kind: "credential-misused", key: "task:<own>><target>" })`; the refusal is unchanged; the key holds the two task IDs and never the credential. (2) A host naming an attempt it never held (`RemoteWorkerService.#holds`, the "no such attempt" for anyone else): `detect("host-channel", credential-misused, "host:<id>>attempt:<id>")`; a former holder (fenced) and an attempt that does not exist are routine and silent. (3) A stored artifact or checkpoint file whose bytes no longer hash to its record (`integrity` error of the artifact store) on its way to a worker: `detect("artifact-store", integrity-check-failed, "artifact:<id>")` (A08).
- **Done: worker-side hooks.** (a) `WorkspaceHost` option `security` (and `LocalWorkspaces` option `security`): a request that meets a path inside Git's own data in the agent's checkout (`protected_path` from the landing plan, integration plan, refresh or the bridge write) reports `protected-path-touched`; a file that was swapped or became a link while a refresh read it (the new `WorkspaceError.tamper` flag, set only at those two places) reports `sandbox-escape-attempt`. The key is `ws:<operation>:<24 hex of a digest>` (no path, no content). A commit that merely carries a link, a stale file or an invalid path is an ordinary refusal and is not reported. The hook is fire-and-forget; a throw or rejection is dropped. (b) The controller hands the local host builder `services.reportSecurity` (`dispatch.local.build`), which reports as `host:local-worker`; spread it into `new LocalWorkspaces({ ..., security: services.reportSecurity })`. (c) A remote worker: new route `POST /worker/session/security` with `RemoteWorkerClient.reportSecurity(event)`; the report is the host's own (its ID is in the event hash, so it cannot mute or fake another's). (d) The remote worker's `fetchFile` reports `integrity-check-failed` (`fetch:<artifact>:<digest of the path>`) when the bytes do not hash to the controller's digest, then refuses as before.
- **Tests.** `security-detect.test.ts` (dedupe, never throws, switch, retry after failure, flood bounds, overflow event, key memory bound); `remote/security.test.ts` on all four backends (wrong-host signal and its silences, host report as itself and shape checks, damaged blob by artifact, worker-side digest mismatch report); `api/start-security-detect.test.ts` through the running controller (wrong-task credential: one item per pair, told once on the channel, no credential or task ID in what leaves, off and on by `notifications.configure`, the hourly allowance and the collected item; the local worker hook: Urgent, once per key, bad project dropped, never throws); `host.test.ts` (a planted `.git` in a real checkout reports `protected-path-touched` once per event and the answer is identical without the hook; tamper vs ordinary refusals; a throwing or rejecting sink changes nothing); `urgent.test.ts` (the setting takes true or false only); `chat.test.ts` (set off and on in free-form words).
- **Review fixes (clean-context review, 2026-11-11).** (1) The overflow event's key held the count, so every drained burst was a new event; it is now `overflow:<hour>` and remembered: one per source and hour, as stated. (2) The 200-signal queue was shared: a flood from one detector put every other detector's real sign into overflow (its key and project lost); a source now holds at most 50 of the 200. (3) A hostile agent naming made-up task IDs minted a new key per name and, in seconds, used up `service:detect-credential`'s hourly allowance, so another agent's real wrong-task sign that hour was only collected (needs-you, not Urgent). A signal now names its `subject` (the credential's task; the naming host): one subject raises at most 3 distinct events per source and hour, then ONE `many:<digest>:<hour>` event; a share is given back when the report was switched off, failed or overflowed. A call that names no task (a non-string `taskId`) is not a signal. (4) The local worker's hook went straight to the Urgent watch, so `securityDetectors: false` did not silence it although the setting says it does; with the detectors present it now goes through them (source `local-worker`, reported as `service:detect-local-worker`). Tests: `security-detect.test.ts` (one overflow per hour, per-source share, subject cap and give-back), `start-security-detect.test.ts` (switch silences the local hook; 30 made-up targets are at most one more item).
- **ASSUMPTION:** only Git's own data in a checkout (`.git` in any spelling) is a "protected path touched" event. The default protected list (CI files, hooks, `.gitattributes` and so on) is held for review by the landing policy as a routine; making that Urgent would page the owner for ordinary work. Their review hold is unchanged.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a task credential naming another task is a credential-misused event even when it is an agent's mistake (the card asks to tell the owner; the once-per-pair rule and the owner's allowance bound it). The owner can switch the detectors off by chat.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a link in a commit is not a sandbox escape (ordinary repositories hold links); only a file swapped or turned into a link while a request read it is.
- **Not done (stays in U11d / later):** the sandbox runtime has no escape signal of its own (the launcher/backends refuse and return errors; nothing separates an escape attempt from a failed launch), so the only `sandbox-escape-attempt` signal is the swap race above; a staged restore that fails its integrity check, a malformed manifest and the other `integrity` errors of the stores (maintenance, swarm, route settings) are not hooked (only the artifact/checkpoint file on its way to a worker, and the worker's digest check); the wrong-task detector covers `ownTask`/`ownTaskOnly` (not the tool bridge's own job lookups); an embedder must pass `services.reportSecurity` to `LocalWorkspaces` (the product's own host composition does not construct one in this repository; the integration rigs do not yet); the remote worker executable does not wire a `WorkspaceHost` `security` sink to `client.reportSecurity` (the client method exists); security items still close only when the owner answers; denial counts stay in process memory; the detectors' own key memory and hourly counts are in memory (a restart starts them again, the watch still tells one event once from the notification state). The rest of card U11d (critical path, stopped-work Urgent, watchdog, 09:00 digest rule, answering in place, deferred meeting items) is untouched.

## Re-review fixes for L02d, A09, K02, H12a and P03 (second pass)

- L02d. A Suspend is not held by a host-side placeholder (`remote:<attempt>`: a remote placement exists; `attempt:<attempt>`: a restarted local worker forgot a live attempt) once the cleanup quiesced the attempt: it is recorded in the history as "unverified, not waited for" and the checkpoint goes on. A Stop still ends the attempt and lists what is left as unresolved. The checkpoint port quiesces only attempts the asker may control. `StopService.holding(task, child?)` requires the request to be the cause of the gate as it stands (same gate request ID, still paused) and, with a `mayHold` hook, that the requester may control the child, so a finished Stop followed by a plain Pause of the parent holds nothing. Charge notes are written with their index entry (`stop-charge-open`) in one operation; a lost race on a note is re-read and retried (never `failed`), a sweep reads the index instead of every charge record, and any request whose charges are all settled gets its mark removed. The per-attempt running totals (`stop-charge`) are kept on purpose: they are what stops a later Stop from billing twice (index entries written before this change are not found by the sweep; a charge left pending by an older build is paid by the next Stop of that attempt). Agent/team/installation Stops list jobs with no attempt on the scope's tasks as owner-unknown and end them only for the owner; the unfinished-jobs list is paged to the end. The local worker keeps a sandbox session past the cap of eight unless a look found it empty.
- A09. A decider created by the requester, by someone the requester controls, or by the hand that made the requester or chose its supervisor is refused; an agent whose supervisor has no recorded author (legacy) is unknown, so bosses do not decide for it. New settings, all through `maintenance.settings.set` (also a chat command, with `expectedRevision`; null returns to the default): `requestsPerDay` (no cap by default; 0 or null = none), `pendingPerAgent` (20; 0 = no cap), `attempts` (5), `applyTimeoutMinutes` (60; 0 = none: an application that runs longer is marked uncertain and verified or reverted, and its heartbeat stops), `closeWaitSeconds` (30; 0 = until they end; what is left keeps its claim for the next start), `maxApplies` (4), `tickSeconds` (30). Ticks never overlap; the live index is covered over several ticks with a cursor; the settings record is created at start (marked `base`, and the revisions the owner sees do not count it) so every claim is checked against a revision.
- K02. Prune spares the release the launcher's pointer names; an unreadable pointer refuses staging, removal and pruning. Temporary staging folders carry host+pid+start-time instead of the pid. `maxStaged`, `maxFiles` and `maxFileBytes` are settings of `release.staging.settings.set`. Staging also refuses at the cap itself now (it allowed one more).
- H12a. `publishArtifact` is gated like checkpoints. Usage before the confirmation is booked and confirms nothing. A heartbeat before the confirmation is accepted for `confirmWindowMinutes` (`reconnect.settings.set`, default the attempt lease) from the acceptance or from the restart that cleared the confirmation. `RemoteAttempt.confirmRestarts(messages, held, contract, abilities)` is the worker-flow helper that confirms every restart that changed the recipe. A restart cannot drop a limit the attempt ran under. A confirmation whose launch record failed keeps a `recordPending` mark; the worker's retry writes the record.
- P03. A grant for one service resource survives on a task credential (the use site asks for the exact resource), and a decision may agree `effect.perform` for one service resource. The operation settlement after a lost answer compares neighbours with the versions at the moment of applying (kept by the target through `apply(..., context)` / `applied(key)`). One confirmed effect may still back several deliverables of the same task; binding an effect to one deliverable is not done (the reference is verified, not consumed).
### Re-review fixes for H12q, U09 and T02c (third pass)

- **C1 revoked-bytes blanking.** Off by default: new setting `revokedBytesBlank` (chat-settable; `revokedBytesDays` applies only while it is on). A record is blanked only if its current text digest and revision equal the ones the version recorded at registration (a record edited or superseded since is somebody's live work), and `RetainedMaterial` holds it back when (at the time of its read; see "Blanking race" under T02c) a resumable task, checkpoint or (new) dependency manifest entry of kind `record`/`decision` cites it. The deletion-ledger entry is now written after the guarded command succeeded, so a record left alone never has an entry a restore would apply.
- **B1/B2 activity.** `timeline` (and so the status timeline view) now applies the same per-task reader scope as `steps`, checked in recency order (bounded at 500 checks, `truncated` when cut). No project event stream carries activity content (events carry no step text), so nothing more to scope there. `explanations`, `corrections` and `explain-later` are own-task-only for a task credential; `explainLater` needs the right to add to the task's activity (owner, host, service, `history.append` or `attempt.work`), a reader is refused.
- **B3/B4.** `hostOwnsAttempt` is wired in `start.ts` from the dispatcher's live attempts (a host reads only a task it has a live attempt of; with no dispatcher no host reads any). Replay applies the record-time authority (writer, owner or service; same line) to supersede links, and a step shown as current says when later steps were not read.
- **C2-C4.** The bridge refuses to launch a call whose version is revoked whatever the owner chose (`finish` covers only calls already running); `#decided` is gone. A `dropping` claim stamped in the future is void. A revocation pause counts a task as held only when its own task-scope pause stands (a wider pause is not enough).
- **A1** The permit check needs the commit in a host-side ledger (`nn-permit-ledger` in the checkout's git directory, written by `GitBridge.commit` before the branch moves) as well as the trailers. **A2** A landing that leaves files waiting uncommitted, is refused for a dirty shared tree, or leaves a mixed tree tells the owner (needs-you notice, once per request, via `WorkspaceDeps.notify`). The "committed/cleared" state is read from git itself, so no extra owner operation exists: committing or clearing the files is the clearing. **A3** `writeSet` throws `partial` (restored, not restored) when a put-back fails; the host returns it as `landed:false, partial:true` with a blocker and the exact files; modes are kept on put-back, and a landed 100755 file is executable. **A4** `workspace.landing.branch`, `.requirePermit` (only tightened by lower layers) and `.protectedPaths` are real settings. **A5** The shared-tree lock and bridge state use the real path; integration takes the landing hold; the after-check compares the tree's entries with the landed files. **A6** Default protected paths now cover all of `.github/`, ownership, dependency-bot, ignore and package manager files.

### H12q completion check (2026-11-07)

Checked against the card's one clause ("a landing waits for running attempts to quiesce and an attempt cannot start during one"); two start races and one release gap were found and fixed.

- **Start that passed the busy check (fixed).** The dispatcher read `workspaceBusy` (H12m) once, early in `#advance`, then asked for a place, held the allowance and pinned the checkout before `#start`. A landing that began in that gap froze the still-waiting attempt, but `#start` did not look at the freeze, so the worker came up during the landing (shown by a test: `tick().started` held the attempt while the host was inside the landing). Now the write that marks an attempt running refuses an attempt with a (non-ending) freeze: the attempt stays `waiting`, its place and allowance are given back, and a later tick starts it once the freeze is lifted. This also means any frozen waiting attempt (an owner's freeze, a recipe change that failed) is not started until released, where before it started and had every call refused; a Stop's ending freeze still lets the start go on so the stop ends it.
- **Worker still coming up (fixed).** An attempt already marked running whose worker was still opening was frozen and "settled" by the quiesce with nothing to checkpoint, and the host was asked while the worker was still starting (shown by a test: the host was entered before the worker was up). The dispatcher now keeps the starts in progress (`#starting`, set before the running record is written) and `quiesce` waits for one (bounded by `strictMs`, default 10 s; a start that does not finish in time makes the attempt not quiet, so the landing is refused with a `runtime_hold` blocker). The checkpoint is then the new worker's own. The worker's turn may begin before the host is asked; it is frozen, so every call it makes is refused.
- **A failed second look (fixed).** `QuiesceCoordinator.around` looks at the scope again up to four times; a look that threw after the first had frozen attempts left those frozen with no record naming them (the request's `held` was dropped and the open index cleared). It now releases what it froze (and opens the usual blocker if a release fails, naming the attempt in `status.unreleased`) before the error goes on.
- **Checked and found sound.** Two landings of one task: the second is `unavailable` while the first runs (`#busy`, set with no await after the record lookup). Landings of two tasks over one shared tree: serialised by the host's per-tree queue and the bridge's tree-wide lock; a task's landing does not make another task busy. A call in flight: settled before the host is asked (integration test). A crash during the landing: the record and open index keep it busy until `recover` marks it `uncertain` and lifts only its tagged freeze (H12m tests). Every failure path of `around` releases: the operation throwing, an attempt that cannot be made quiet, and now a failed look.
- **Limits, said plainly.** The host's own check (`attemptsQuiet`) only looks at the attempts the controller named, and counts model calls as busy, so a landing asked while a frozen agent is waiting on a model reply is refused by the host (fail closed; ask again). The two holds are both needed: the freeze check covers an attempt the dispatcher had already claimed when the quiesce looked; the H12m `workspaceBusy` check covers an attempt claimed by the dispatcher after the quiesce's last look (an admitted attempt has no dispatch record until a tick claims it, so the quiesce cannot see it).
- Tests: `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-h12q.test.ts` (all four backends: a landing that begins after the busy check holds the attempt back; a landing that begins while the worker opens waits for it, freezes it and takes its checkpoint), `dispatch/quiesce.test.ts` (a failed second look releases, all backends). Mutation-checked (each change made, the named tests fail, restored): the freeze check in the start (h12q test 1 on every backend; the integration test still passes, as its waiting attempt is claimed after the quiesce); the wait for a start in progress (h12q test 2); the release on a failed look (the new quiesce test); the landing run without the quiesce (integration test `h12q-landing-quiesce`: the host is asked while the call is in flight); the `workspaceBusy` check skipped (H12m held-back test, h12q test 1, integration test); `isBusy` always false (H12m tests, integration test).

## L05b: the model stream feeds revision-bound generation (2026-10-31)

Code: `dispatch/model-stream.ts` (`ModelStreamDecoder`, `ModelStreamTap`, `ModelStreamRefused`), the tee in `dispatch/relay.ts` (`feeding`), `generation/stream-feed.ts` (`streamTapFor`), `generation/stream-settings.ts` (`StreamSettingsService`), the binding in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` (`attemptRelay` passes `stream` to `forAttempt`), operations `generation.stream.get` and `generation.stream.change` (chat: `generation.stream.change`, propose). Tests: `dispatch/model-stream.test.ts`, `generation/stream-feed.test.ts` (four backends), `generation/stream-settings.test.ts` (API and chat), and `packages/integration/src/l05b-model-stream.test.ts` (the real worker process in the sandbox). Mutation-checked: relay ignoring a held reply, ignoring the cut setting, not refusing a held task, the revision fixed at 1, a tool call never marked done, a non-streamed reply not held; each fails a test, and the first also fails the real-process test.

- **Where the stream is read.** The worker process has no network; its model calls go through the controller's `ModelRelay` (H12b), so the relay sees every byte of every reply. That is where the events are read (the worker process itself is unchanged). `ModelStreamDecoder` reads OpenAI-style chat completions and Anthropic-style messages, streamed or whole, and yields text, tool-call pieces (name with the first, `done` with the last) and the end; bytes are passed on unchanged. A reply in another format yields no events and is not recorded.
- **One model call is one generation.** Before the call is sent the feed reads the task's context revision and calls `begin` with it and the attempt's fence (so a stale attempt cannot record), as the dispatcher's service principal. Each piece of the reply is decoded and recorded (`record`, text coalesced per piece, numbered without gaps), the end is `complete`. A call that ends early or fails part way is also completed, so a half-written tool call is `dropped` for good and never `complete`.
- **A late or superseded stream is held.** Each piece is forwarded to the worker only after it was recorded as applied. If the generation was interrupted meanwhile (an owner's correction, a cancel, a newer generation) the record says late, nothing more is forwarded, the worker's call fails with "the model reply was held back: generation N of task T was corrected by owner:rob (reason)", and the rest of the reply lands in the run's `late` list (digest and 200-character preview) with the completion marked late. A reply that is not streamed is read whole and recorded before any of it is passed on. The next call begins a new generation under the new revision (shown with the real worker: Pi retried and the second generation, revision 2, finished; the late text is in nothing the model was shown later).
- **A task that is held starts no generation.** `begin` refuses a task held by L05's `interrupt` (`held`); the relay then refuses the call before it is sent. A correction landing between reading the revision and `begin` (`stale`) is read again once, then the call is refused.
- **Settings (owner only, chat-settable).** `generation.stream.get` and `generation.stream.change` (`enable` / `disable` of `record` and `cut`, `expectedRevision`). Both are on unless turned off; neither is a limit or a budget. `record` off: no generation per call, nothing held. `cut` off: still recorded, a late reply is shown late but still reaches the worker. Read at the start of each call; a setting that cannot be read leaves both on.
- **Change in L05's service.** The dispatcher's service principal may `begin`, `record` and `complete` (it streams on the worker's behalf) and read the runs it owns; no new right was given to anyone else.
- **Provisional choices.** (1) The relay cuts the reply by failing the call, so the worker sees a model error (Pi retries); an alternative is to end the reply quietly, which would look like a finished answer. (2) Recording is awaited before each piece is forwarded: strict, but a slow store slows the reply; text of one piece is one record (the run record is rewritten per chunk, the quadratic cost named in L05). (3) A task whose pause gate (L01) is paused, a task the generation service does not know, a done or cancelled task and an attempt that is no longer current are not recorded and not stopped (no refusal): a pause lets the current step finish, and the fence already stops a stale attempt elsewhere. (4) A chunk the service will not take (credential-shaped text, over a limit) ends the recording of that reply; the reply still reaches the worker. (5) Run IDs are per task and numbered; command IDs carry a per-relay random nonce so a restarted controller does not replay an earlier begin.
- **Not done (new card L05c).** (1) A remote worker (H02) makes its own model calls and does not pass through `ModelRelay`, so its streams are not recorded or held. (2) Nothing at the tool bridge compares a tool call with the recorded generation; a call from a held reply never runs because the worker never receives the reply, not because the bridge checks, and `admitEffect` is still not called from the stream. (3) A paused task's calls are not recorded. (4) The test of a partial call "never runs" is at the record level (state `dropped`, `admitEffect` refuses) and by the hold in the real-process test, not by a worker process that is cut in the middle of a tool call.

### L05b review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Refused chunk (1).** A piece the generation service refuses (a credential-shaped text, the 16K argument / 64K text / 32 call limits) stops the recording with a visible placeholder text (`[recording stopped here: ...]`); the check for an interruption does not depend on recording, so the cut still works afterwards.
- **Batching (2).** `GenerationService.recordMany` applies up to 64 pieces in one commit. The feed writes a batch when `batchChars` (2000) are waiting, `batchMs` (250) have passed (a timer also writes what waits when the model pauses), or a completed tool call or the end of the reply is about to be passed on (always applied before it is forwarded). Whether the generation was interrupted is one read of the task's gate, at most once per `batchMs` and always before a completed call or the end. Text received just before a correction may therefore be recorded as late; that is the price of batching, and `batchMs`/`batchChars` of 0 record every piece. Limit of the cheap check: a cancel that was released again before the next check is only seen by the next write.
- **Store failures (3).** Every store call has a timeout (`storeTimeoutMs`, 20 s, 0 = none). Fail mode `onStoreFailure` (`failClosed`, default closed): closed refuses a call that cannot be bound to a revision and cuts a reply being read when the store stops answering, with the reason; open sends and passes on unrecorded and reports the error. Settings `generation.stream.change` take `enable`/`disable` of `record`, `cut`, `failClosed` and `set` of the four numbers. The end of a failed or cancelled reply is not waited for (the cancel is not held up). While a store call runs the monitor is told (`CallMonitor.waiting`); the dispatcher answers with a repeat of the last output count so the stall detector does not blame the model for the wait.
- **Refused beginnings (4).** Held, paused, waiting for the owner's decision (C08), fenced, and done/cancelled tasks refuse the call before it is sent. Tasks unknown to the service or not the principal's are not recorded and not stopped.
- **Held buffer (5).** A response with content type `text/event-stream`, or whose first line is an SSE comment/event/data line, is a stream at once (keep-alive comments are forwarded immediately). A reply that cannot yet be told from a whole one is held at most `heldBufferBytes` (16 MB, 0 = no cap); past it the reply is passed on unrecorded with a note.
- **Decoder (6).** Null elements are skipped; any throw stops decoding, the reply is passed on and a note is recorded.
- **Retention, labelling, reading (7).** Runs are labelled `sensitive`; retention rule `generationRunDays` (K06; null = keep, chat-settable through `retention.settings.set`) removes ended runs (never one streaming, held, or with a call that could still be admitted). Reading a run is limited to the owner, the dispatcher, the streamer, the task's assigned agent and (with the `roles`/`reviewAssignments` options, not yet wired in the composition) a reviewer asked to review the task; `assignment.read` alone reads the gate, not the text. The recorded text and tool arguments can contain personal or confidential data (PII): sizes are capped (64K text, 16K per call, 32 calls) and the credential filter runs, but personal data is not detected; use `generationRunDays` to age it out.
- **Retry after a correction (8).** A request whose reply was held because of a correction and that is sent again unchanged (same digest) goes out with the correction as a last user message and is bound to the new revision; a body without a `messages` list is refused.
- **Held tokens (9).** A reply that fails or is held reports an output estimate from the bytes received (4 characters per token) to the monitor.
- **Run state (10).** `complete` takes `failed`: a broken reply ends `failed` (not `finished`) and its already complete calls become `unused`. An empty argument string of a finished call is `{}`.
- **Decoder details (11).** Multi-line SSE data is joined; comment lines show a stream; only the first choice is recorded (others noted); lines over 1 MB and bodies over 4 MB are noted; text is cut without splitting a surrogate pair. Not done: bare `\r` line ends and thinking deltas (thinking is not recorded at all).
- **Late chunks (12).** Only the first late piece of a held reply is recorded: the relay stops reading the body when it holds the reply.


### macOS sandbox: libraries of a Homebrew node (own-hardware run 41228808621, 2026-10-31)

- **Cause.** The Seatbelt profile lets a program read only the system places and the agent's own directories and mounts. Homebrew's node links libuv, openssl, icu and others by `/opt/homebrew/opt/<formula>/lib/...` (symbolic links into `/opt/homebrew/Cellar`), outside those, so dyld was refused `open()` and the worker aborted at start (SIGABRT) in `h12bf-composed` tests 1 and 2. GitHub-hosted runners use a self-contained node, so CI never saw it.
- **Fix** (`sandbox/libraries.ts`, `sandbox/seatbelt.ts`). When the seatbelt backend plans a launch of an absolute program path, `dependentLibraryReads` runs `otool -L` and `otool -l` (run paths) on it, follows `@rpath`, `@loader_path` and `@executable_path`, and recurses through the libraries found. System places (`/usr`, `/System`, `/Library/Frameworks`, ...) and paths already readable (workdir, home, scratch, read-only mounts) add nothing. For every other library the profile gets `(allow file-read* (literal (param "LIBn")))` for the path as named, each symbolic link on the way, and the real file: exact files only, never a directory or subpath, never write. Results are cached per program path, mtime and size. If `otool` fails or a library cannot be found the launch is refused (`invalid_recipe`) with a message naming the program and the library; at most 256 libraries. No new setting. `file-read-metadata` was already allowed everywhere, which covers looking at links and directories on the way.
- **Tests.** `sandbox/libraries.test.ts` (any OS, fake `otool` and a fake Homebrew tree): parsing, link chain, rpath/loader_path, system libraries skipped, already-readable skipped, read-only literal parameters only, otool failure and missing library refused, cache. A macOS-only live test runs the machine's own node confined (skipped elsewhere with a reason).
- **Verified only by reasoning (no Mac here).** That `literal` rules on the named path, the links and the real file are what Seatbelt needs for dyld's `open()` (it checked the path as named, per the dyld message; the real file is added as well in case it checks that); that `otool -L/-l` output has the formats parsed; that the Homebrew node's `bin/` is allowed to exec through the existing read-only mount. The libraries are read through `mmap`, which I expect to need only `file-read*` as for system libraries. Rerun `h12bf-composed` on the Mac to confirm.

## Seatbelt dependent-library read set: security review fixes (follow-up to 89ac770)

- Programs under the agent's writable directories (workdir, home, scratch), directly or through a link, are never inspected with otool. Every library, link and real path must lie under /opt/homebrew, /usr/local, the program's own install root (two levels above the real program) or `SeatbeltOptions.libraryPrefixes`, and begin with a Mach-O/fat signature. otool reports must start with exactly `<file>:` (or `<file> (architecture X):`) and not say "is not an object file".
- Walk: a dylib's own LC_ID_DYLIB name is skipped; `@rpath` uses the whole loader chain (run paths resolved where written); weak libraries may be absent; universal binaries use only the host-architecture slice.
- Cache: LRU of 64 programs, keyed by program path only (the answer is for the system alone; the run's directories are applied on every call), revalidated by stat of the program and every listed file. Resolution has a 30 s total allowance. `plan()` is synchronous, so the first resolution of a program still blocks (bounded, then cached); pre-warming at worker start is not done.
- Errors name only the program and library file names. The scratch `.tmp` creation tolerates races and fails as SandboxError.
- Not verified without a Mac: the real otool header form for fat files and for dylibs (`-L` own name first), `otool -l` field layout for LC_ID_DYLIB / LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB (`name X (offset N)`), exit codes and output for non-Mach-O input, Homebrew layouts outside /opt/homebrew, the install-root heuristic on a real Homebrew node, and that sandbox-exec still runs node end to end.


## K01h (first slice): Pi state in backups, a maintenance barrier, an owner restore from inside the running controller (2026-10-31)
- **Pi native state (`backup/pi-state.ts`):** `StartOptions.backup.piState` is a port (`list()` of `{ id, dir }`) naming the agents' own conversation stores (Pi Durable JSON-lines folders) on this machine. Every backup copies each regular file (links and special files are skipped) to `pi-state/f-<n>` (`.enc` and sealed when the backup is encrypted, so no path or name is in the clear) with an index `pi-state.jsonl` (store, relative path with forward slashes whatever the platform, size, digest, stored name), listed in the manifest as `piState` (so an encrypted backup's manifest MAC covers it). A `.jsonl` file is copied up to its last complete line: a worker writing at that moment leaves half a line and the copy drops it (provisional; the quiet restore path never has one). Verification checks the index against the manifest and every file's size and digest; the index is shape-checked (store id, relative path without `..`, `\`, drive letters or empty parts; stored name `f-<n>`), a restore refuses a target folder that already has files and a path that would leave its store, and writes through a temporary name, checking each file's digest. `restoreBackup` takes `piTarget(id)` (required when the backup has Pi state); the command line takes `--pi-state <new folder>`. Nothing about a remote host's state is copied (only the listed folders).
- **Maintenance barrier (`backup/barrier.ts`):** participants are held in the order added and released in reverse; one that cannot be held releases those already held and the raise fails naming it; one barrier at a time; `held` is true from the start of a raise. No time limit (optional, off: `holdTimeoutMs` exists in the constructor but is not wired to a setting). Participants wired: `backups` (no new backup starts, the running one is awaited; the restore's own pre-restore snapshot is `safetyCopy`, which is not stopped by the hold) and `dispatcher` (the driver is paused by `DriverOptions.hold` without counting a failure, its running tick is awaited, and the raise is refused with the count while any attempt is live: stop or pause the work first). While held, every state-API command except `backup.restore.cancel` is refused as `unavailable` (queries still work), which covers the other writers (retention runner, notifications, sweeps run inside the dispatcher tick, which is paused).
- **Restore from inside the controller (`backup/staged-restore.ts`, SQLite only):** a running controller owns its database, so it cannot write into it. `backup.restore.preview { name }` (owner only, query) shows the exact plan and a `token` (a hash of the backup's name, time, MAC or file digests and the installation epoch): rows, artifact files, conversation files, effects that come back uncertain and messages sent again (counted for a plain backup; an encrypted backup's rows cannot be read before the unlock, so they are absent from the plan), the steps and warnings. `backup.restore.apply { name, confirm, method? }` (owner only) needs that exact token, unlocks an encrypted backup from the host passcode or recovery file (`BackupEncryption.unlock`, same rate limit and file rules as the proof; the secret is never an argument, a result or an error), verifies, restores into a NEW database and new conversation folders under `<data>/.nn-restore/<time>/`, then raises the barrier, takes a `pre-upgrade`-kind snapshot of the current state (provisional: reusing that kind keeps it from retention without a new kind), writes `pending-restore.json` and leaves the barrier up. The live data is not touched. `StartOptions.backup.restore.onStaged` tells the host; the controller does not end its own process (provisional). On the next start `applyPendingRestore` runs before the database is opened: conversation folders then database files (with `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`) are moved aside as `<name>.before-restore-<time>` and the staged ones renamed into place, then the marker is removed; every step checks what is already done, so a crash is finished by the next start, and a marker for another database or with paths outside its staging folder is refused. Nothing is deleted. `backup.restore.cancel` removes the marker and staging and lowers the barrier; `backup.restore.status` reports it. Blobs from the backup are put into the live artifact store before the barrier (content-addressed, harmless).
- **Chat:** `backup.restore.apply` is always a proposal (every profile); `backup.restore.cancel` applies (the safe direction). The preview is a state-API query, so the proposal shows the exact plan; nothing applies from an interpreter's words. No new setting was added (no budgets or limits).
- **Provisional choices to confirm:** pre-restore snapshot as `pre-upgrade` kind; the preview token includes the epoch but not the live database's content; a half-written last line of a Pi JSONL file is dropped in a live backup; restart is left to the host; a restore is refused while any agent attempt is live instead of stopping them for the owner; unknown conversation stores restore under `<data>/restored-pi-state/<id>`.
- **Tests:** `backup/k01h.test.ts` (Pi files byte for byte and the torn line, tampering, target not empty, traversal and Windows-style paths, sealed Pi files with the passcode and the manifest MAC, the barrier's order/rollback/exclusivity, preview/token/snapshot/barrier/swap/kept-old-data, cancel and a refusing participant, an interrupted swap and a foreign or escaping marker, an encrypted restore with the passcode file and no secret in any result), `api/start-backup-restore.test.ts` (owner only, wrong token refused, commands refused during the barrier, cancel, restart swaps the data in, conversation folder restored). Mutation checks: skipping the token check, copying a torn line, disabling the command gate, skipping Pi verification and allowing `..` in an index path each fail a test.
- **Not done (K01h narrowed; remainder K01i):** PostgreSQL staged restore, remote hosts' Pi state, composing the local worker host's conversation folders as the production `piState` source and `piFinal` mapping (the option exists; nothing in the production composition passes it yet), holding the remaining writers as barrier participants (today the dispatcher pause and the command refusal), an automatic restart, and stopping live attempts for the owner.

## K01h review fixes (restore swap, marker, Pi-state copy, token, ledger, lock)

- **Swap (finding 1).** Staged copies now sit BESIDE what they replace (`<db>.nn-staged-<stamp>`, `<conversation folder>.nn-staged-<stamp>`), so every rename is inside one folder and one device; apply still stats both sides and refuses a different device. Paths in the marker are absolute and link-resolved (`canon`), so a relative data directory no longer fails the check at every start. `applyPendingRestore` plans the moves, journals them (`restore-journal.json`, HMAC-signed, rewritten after each move), retries EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES, and on any failure undoes the moves made (last first). After a rollback the controller starts on the data it had and the marker carries `failed` (shown by `backup.restore.status`); `backup.restore.cancel` clears it. If a rollback step itself fails the start throws (half-swapped, said plainly) and the next start continues the rollback from the journal. A failed restore is retried by cancelling and preparing it again (no automatic retry).
- **Marker (finding 2).** HMAC under `.nn-restore.key` (mode 600, made at the first restore) over every field; the targets must be exactly where the same `piFinal` function (or `<data>/restored-pi-state`) puts the store, and may not be the data directory or above it. Names are checked against the backup-name pattern before anything prints them. Provisional: the key lives beside the marker, so this stops a writer who can write the marker but not read the key, and the target rule bounds the rest.
- **Pi state copy (findings 3, 4, 13).** Store roots are `lstat`ed (a link is refused), files are opened `O_NOFOLLOW` (where the platform has it) and measured and copied from that one handle; a hard-linked or special file is skipped; a file that shrank, was replaced or (for non-logs) was written to during the copy is tried again three times, then left out as inconsistent. Every skip, unreadable folder and missing store is named in the manifest (`piState.problems`, `problemCount`) and shown in the plan. `validRel` refuses Windows device names and trailing dot/space segments on every platform.
- **Token (findings 5, 6).** The chat computes the plan and token at proposal time from the controller's own preview (the interpreter's `confirm` is dropped); the token is an HMAC (per-process key) over the whole manifest digest, the epoch, an expiry and a nonce, is used once, and is re-checked at apply. Expiry is the retention setting `restoreConfirmMinutes` (default 30, null: none). The restore verifies the backup once, inside `restoreBackup`, pinned to the approved manifest digest. The plan states how many recorded changes since the backup will be lost (audit-trail count); the apply returns the exact number. Provisional: the files are not copied to a private snapshot, so a file changed between that one verification and its read is caught by the per-file digests but not earlier.
- **Ledger (finding 7).** `restoreBackup` skips the blobs of artifacts on the deletion ledger (unless a live artifact holds the same bytes) and drops their rows; delete, restore, cancel leaves them deleted.
- **Visibility (finding 8).** `backup.status.piStateIncluded`, `backup.list` items `piState` ("not included" / "included"), the plan's `piStateIncluded` and warnings (conversation memory may be AHEAD of the restored records), and the pre-upgrade snapshot now includes Pi state when it is configured. A worker host can supply `dispatch.local.piState` (`source`, `final`) and `start.ts` composes it; without either, backups say Pi state is not included.
- **Lock (finding 9).** `startController` takes `.nn-data.lock` (pid, host, nonce) for sqlite installations for its whole life; `applyPendingRestore` uses that lock (or takes its own). A live holder refuses with its pid; a dead one on this host is taken over.
- **Pre-restore (finding 10).** Snapshots taken before a restore are kind `pre-restore`, labelled in `backup.list`, never the nightly backup; retention setting `preRestoreKept` (1 to 1000; null, the default, keeps all).
- **Smaller (findings 11 to 13).** An unlock refusal maps to a typed error with its reason; the preview refuses another schema version; `status()` reads the marker; `cancel()` always lowers the barrier and reports a marker it could not remove or leftovers. The encrypted in-controller restore test runs everywhere with an unlock function (the secret-file variant stays POSIX-only, mode bits).
- **Tests.** `backup/k01h-fixes.test.ts` (relative directory, injected EXDEV/EBUSY and rollback failure, device check, forged markers, symlink/hard link/fifo, unreadable folder, shrinking file, token binding and expiry, ledger, lock, kinds, cancel) and the chat/list/lock case in `api/start-backup-restore.test.ts`.
## C07f review fixes (2026-10-31)

- A route-change decision is named by everything it was made from (route, window, fixed figure, items), and each archive batch by its contents, so asking again with another route or window is a new decision and never a `command_conflict`.
- The route's measured fixed part is written after the admission in its own best-effort command, only for an admitted call, per route and harness, keeping the latest five and using the largest; a lost race or a failure never fails the admission. `contextRouteKey` is now injective (`~` plus four hex digits), so `a/b` and `a:b` differ; callers pass the raw route name to `fixedPartOf`.
- A route nobody measured counts a floor (8000 characters of prompt plus an estimated 6000 of bridge tool schemas, 14000 in all) instead of 0. Consequence: an unmeasured route with a window under about 19000 tokens is refused until measured or until the owner turns the floor off. Settings `context.route.get/change`: `check` (on) and `floorChars` (on), enable/disable/set/unset, chat-settable.
- Check 5c now runs after budget and grant checks, and an accepted move is remembered per attempt, route and routing/contract revision, so a start waiting for a host does not read the owner's decisions every tick. Not built: feeding a refusal into route choice (a fallback route is not tried when the context refuses a route); the refusal only blocks with the remedies named.
- A task back on the route it ran on closes a stale route-change `context_overflow` blocker (`routeKept`). Cut text of goal, human, decision and permission items is read only with `history.read`. K06 `contextRouteDays` (default off) removes route archives and route-change decisions.

## K01h re-review fixes (second round: swap recovery, lock, key, token, retention)
- **Swap (findings 1, 2, 6).** The conversation folder's real place (links followed, a dangling link followed to where it points) is resolved BEFORE the backup is written out, so the copy is made beside the real folder and is never renamed afterwards; a staged folder that is not there fails the prepare. A first start (no journal) whose marker names a staged database or folder that is missing records `failed` (nothing moved) instead of swapping the database alone. A journal is read first and resumed or rolled back from its own stored paths, before the marker's places are checked again; a journal without its marker is refused, never ignored; the journal is marked `done` before the marker and journal are removed; the `failed` marker is written atomically (temp + rename) before the journal goes. `cancel` also undoes a journal when the marker no longer checks out.
- **Lock (findings 3, 4, 12).** The lock file is linked into place complete; a stale one is taken over under a short guard file and re-read to confirm ownership. Stale means: another boot, a reused pid (Linux start time), a dead process on this host, or, when the host name differs, not refreshed for `dataLockStaleMinutes` (default 10, null never; the holder refreshes the mtime and writes the setting into the lock). Locks are taken on the data directory and the database's folder, and by the offline `backup restore` for the folders it writes into. Provisional: boot id and process start time are read on Linux; elsewhere the boot is told from the uptime (2 minutes' slack) and the start time is not checked.
- **Smaller.** Staged folders are removed when the restore fails part-way; the busy flag is reset in `finally`; the key file is written complete and linked, a torn or linked key is replaced only when no marker or journal depends on it; the token carries its issue time and the CURRENT `restoreConfirmMinutes` applies at use; apply refuses and asks for a new preview when the discard count grew by more than `restoreChangeMargin` (default 20, null off; provisional); a store file reached through a folder swapped for a link is not copied; pre-restore snapshots fill no daily or weekly slot and expire with `preRestoreMaxAgeDays` (default null).
- **Tests.** `backup/k01h-review2.test.ts` (uses a child process that really dies mid-swap, `backup/k01h-crash.ts`).

## K01h re-review fixes (third round: lock hosts, lazy lock, links, heartbeat, crash tests)
- **Foreign hosts (finding 1).** The boot id and the pid mean something only on the machine that wrote them: they are now looked at only when the lock's host is this host's name. A lock of another host (a shared NFS/SMB data folder, a container under a new name) is judged by its age alone, so a second host no longer takes over a live lock at once. Staleness margin: never less than twice the holder's refresh period plus `LOCK_SKEW_MS` (30 s). The refresh stamps the file with the HOLDER's clock (`utimes`) and a reader compares it with its own: hosts whose clocks differ by more than the allowance need a larger `dataLockStaleMinutes` (chat-settable).
- **Unlocked second start (finding 2).** `keepDataLocks` (data-lock.ts) holds the lock for the life of a controller. A start that finds a LIVE holder (typed `DataLockBusy`, not any `unavailable`) goes on without it only when no marker or journal waits (card F04i: the second controller takes the epoch), says so once, and retries every refresh period: when the holder closes the keeper takes the lock; a lock that is lost (file removed or replaced) is retaken the same way. A torn lock file, a takeover in progress or a lock that could not be taken refuse the start. `StagedRestore.apply` calls `require()` first: it takes the lock then if it can and refuses with a clear message (nothing staged, barrier not raised) when it cannot.
- **Real paths (finding 3).** `canon` / `canonSync` moved to backup/canon.ts (re-exported from staged-restore.ts); `acquireDataLock` / `acquireDataLocks` use them, so a data directory that is a link to the database's folder (or `/var` vs `/private/var`, Windows case) is one lock, not two. start.ts and cli.ts get this through `acquireDataLocks`.
- **Heartbeat (finding 4).** `setStaleMinutes` re-arms the timer (and the record carries `refreshMs`); a refresh that fails or finds the lock gone is told once per episode through `LockEnv.warn` (start.ts prints it) and the keeper retakes a lost lock.
- **Reused pid (finding 6).** Where the process start time cannot be told (Windows, macOS), a same-host holder whose pid exists is live only while the heartbeat is current (age within 2 x refresh + skew), so a killed controller's lock cannot block for ever. Linux still compares the start time. Injected-clock tests.
- **Cancel, done, doc (finding 7).** `cancel()` no longer swallows a journal that cannot be read or authenticated: it refuses (journal and marker kept) instead of reporting `cancelled`. A swap recorded `done` is cleaned up even if the marker no longer authenticates. The rollBack doc now says progress is recorded only when a move cannot be undone (each undo is checked against the disk, so a rollback is simply run again).
- **Margin (finding 8).** `restoreChangeMargin` counts audit rows, not operations (the storage lists audit rows only), so the default is now 200 (was 20) and the doc says so; the margin is checked again after the backup was written out (rows written during the restore itself) and before the marker.
- **Link fallback (finding 9).** `LINK_FALLBACK_CODES` (data-lock.ts, shared by the lock and the key file) adds EISDIR (libuv's mapping of ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION on FAT/exFAT; unverified off Linux) and EINVAL; tests inject the link function.
- **Tests (finding 5).** `k01h-crash.ts` has a timeout, puts the child's stderr in the failure and removes the dead child's lock file; it can die between the done record and the marker removal, or between the marker and the journal (the "journal done" branch was never exercised before). The dangling-link test cannot show journal-first (canon follows a dangling link), so a separate test resumes after the marker's places would no longer be accepted. `backup/k01h-review3.test.ts`, plus a start-level test in `api/start-backup-restore.test.ts`.

## C07f second review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Stale "kept" (finding 1).** The dispatcher drops the remembered answer for an attempt before it asks the context about a move, so a refusal or an error leaves nothing behind: a flap A to B (refused) to A asks `routeKept` again and the stale `[route change]` blocker is closed. The remembered "fits" key also carries the revision of the project's decision record (`decision-context`) and of the route settings, so new decisions or goals, or a toggled check or floor, are asked again.
- **Blocker closed by a mark (findings 2, 8).** A route change's refusal is marked by its own record (`ctx-route-block`, one per task, naming the blocker it opened); only a blocker named there is closed, never by the text of its summary (a blocker open from before the mark existed, with no mark record for the task, is still recognised by its text prefix, once). It is closed by `routeKept` and now by any `changeRoute` that fits (the owner raised the window with the blocker open, or another route fits). An admission refusal that was already open is not taken over and is never closed by a move.
- **Unmeasured route (finding 3).** The floor still sizes the cut, but an unmeasured route is not refused on it: if the essentials do not fit beside the floor but fit without it, the view is built without it, the decision is admitted (basis `unmeasured`, the warning is in its reasons) and the owner gets a notice (`maintenance`, level `notice`, once per attempt and route); the first call is then checked with its real size. Essentials that do not fit even alone are still refused. A measured route behaves as before. Consequence for tests: a route is "measured" only by an admitted first call, so a test of a measured too-small route measures it on a larger window first. The floor stays settable.
- **Median (finding 4).** The fixed figure is the median of the last five samples (the lower one of an even count, one whole sample so the parts stay consistent), so one task with a very large tool set no longer refuses another task's move. `fixedSamplesOf` returns the kept samples.
- **Retention (finding 6).** `contextRouteDays` holds `ctx-route-archive` records of tasks that are not done or cancelled (reference scan in `RetainedMaterial`, so the hold is re-read before every batch); they show as retained with the reason.
- **Route key (finding 7).** `contextRouteKey` now always starts with `c~r` (the encoding writes `~` only before four hex digits, so `~r` cannot occur in an encoded name) and a cut name ends in `~h` plus a digest (`~h` cannot occur either); injective, tested on colliding and forged names. Calibration records written under the previous release's key or the older colon form are found by decoding the key (`legacyRouteKeys`) and carried into the new key on the next confirmation. Not migrated: `ctx-route-fixed` figures (re-measured by the next admitted call) and calibration of routes whose name was cut to a digest.
- **Window under 1,024 tokens (finding 9).** `routeMoved` answers a window the budgets cannot be made for with one refusal and one marked blocker (asked again: the same blocker; closed when a real window fits); `admit` and `changeRoute` refuse such a window as `invalid_command` instead of a RangeError.
- **Best-effort figure (finding 10).** Non-conflict errors are reported through `onError` (at most once a minute) and never fail the admission. A `command_conflict` is retried only when the record was absent when the try began (two creations racing); the same command ID used for another payload is permanent, reported and not retried. This also fixed a loss the stricter concurrent test showed: a creation race lost samples (only one of four was kept) when the loser gave up.
- Tests: `context/enforcement.test.ts` (route blocker scenarios A and B, mark vs admission blocker, unmeasured proceeds / measured refused, outlier, window, key injectivity and legacy calibration, error reporting, concurrent samples all merged), `dispatch/route-change.test.ts` (flap after refusal and error, cache key revisions), `api/start-route-change.test.ts` (owner raises the window with the refusal open), `api/start-retention.test.ts` (live task's archive kept). Mutations killed: no delete of the remembered answer, no close on a fit, no unmeasured fallback, max instead of median, cache key without revisions, no legacy keys, no window check, retrying every conflict, never retrying a conflict, no live-task hold.

## Windows CI fix for K02 release activation tests (not verifiable without Windows)

- The "symlink" switcher variants of the release activation tests failed on windows-latest (CI run 41236956725), a new failure from K02: Node's readlink returns backslashes (`releases\rcn-...`), and rename cannot replace a directory symlink on Windows (EPERM). Production already defaults to the pointer file on win32, so the symlink switcher is never used there.
- Fix: SymlinkSwitcher.read normalises backslashes; the symlink test variants are skipped on win32 with a reason; the end-to-end API test uses the pointer switcher on win32 and reads current.json.
- Not verified: the Windows run itself (only Linux was run); whether the end-to-end test passes in pointer mode on Windows beyond the link assertions.
## Sweep b36 macOS/Windows test fixes (unverified off Linux)
- h12k disk-limit test: the macOS launcher shows host paths, so the test now uses guestPaths "host" on darwin (the command is the real node, not /opt/node/bin/node, which does not exist on macOS and made the Seatbelt library lookup fail first: "node cannot be read to find its libraries"). Needs a macOS run to confirm.
- workspace-ask "fifth is not sent": the four waiting asks now last 2 s and the test waits until all four are listed; a slow runner let the 300 ms asks expire first. Needs macOS/Windows runs to confirm.


## Windows fix, K01h restore tests (CI run 41236956725)

- Root cause 1 (production): `canonSync` used `fs.realpathSync` (JS implementation, keeps 8.3 short names such as `RUNNER~1`) while `canon` used `fs.promises.realpath` (native, expands to the long name). The marker stored the target through `canonSync` and the start compared it with `canon`, so on Windows every restore with a conversation folder was refused ("a conversation folder is not where this installation keeps att-1"). `canonSync` now uses `realpathSync.native`, the same spelling as `canon`. This also explains the child-process crash helper returning 1 instead of 3 (the child hit the same refusal).
- Root cause 2 (tests): rigs in `k01h.test.ts` and `k01h-fixes.test.ts` removed the temp folder while the SQLite file was still open (EBUSY on Windows). Rigs now open through `openTracked` and `cleanup` closes every tracked database before removing the folder.
- Not verified without Windows: that no other mismatch hides behind the first refusal (tests that failed only as a cascade: relative data dir, mid-swap rename, EBUSY retry, lock takeover, encrypted unlock, failed-marker order, missing staged folder, crash helper). Each was traced to one of the two causes from the log text; a Windows run is the proof. If `realpath.native` returns a `\\?\` form for some path, `canon` and `canonSync` would still agree (both native).

## C07f third review fixes (2026-10-31)

- Retention: `RetainedMaterial.build` reads the `ctx-route-archive` records only when asked (`routeArchive: true`; the context-route-days rule, the explain call for such a record, and the removal batches that include one). The scan has its own completeness flag: hitting the 100,000-record limit holds the archives, never the other rules' material. An archive nobody scanned is held, not freed.
- A refused first call is a real measurement and now records the route's fixed part, so a route whose first call overflows becomes measured. A call with no prompt and no tools is not recorded; zero-size samples are ignored when the figure is read. The figure is the upper median for an even count.
- A route nobody measured whose floor does not fit beside the essentials is built with the room the essentials leave (not the whole startup budget); the warning says how much was set aside.
- The route blocker is marked by what it is (its text), after it was opened or found: an admission blocker found in a race is never marked; a route blocker with a lost or stale mark is marked on the next refusal and then closed when a move fits.
- Legacy calibration keys: `admit` takes an optional `routeName` (the dispatcher passes the route's own name; checked against the key) so the previous release's cut key is found. The oldest colon form is read only when nothing in the name was replaced or cut (`a/b` and `a:b` shared it); calibration written then under a slash name (`provider/model`) is therefore no longer read and is rebuilt by the next confirmed call.
- Found while testing: the owner notice for an unmeasured route was never delivered (the notice detail was over the 200-character limit and the error was swallowed). It now carries a short fixed text.


## M04g (first slice): a real safeLongRunning from the job records (2026-10-31)
- **Superseded by "M04g review fixes" below.** The first version asked the predicate per task at attempt admission, counted `admitted` jobs as safe and let a safe task start a new attempt during a meeting; none of that holds now. What stands from it: the setting `meeting.safeLongRunning` (installation boolean, default true, chat-settable, not a limit); an unreadable job list, malformed answer or the setting being off is "not safe"; composition through `ComposeInput.safeLongRunning`, replaceable by `options.dispatch.dispatcher.safeLongRunning`; the tests are in `meetings/safe-long-running.test.ts`, `api/start-safe-long-running.test.ts` and `dispatch/dispatcher.test.ts`.
- **Not done (card M04h).** A real host for the wake: composing an availability that reports `stopped`/`suspended` from L02/L03 (the pause gate answers `paused` first for a stopped scope, so today the host's hook is the only source of `stopped`) and a `meetingWake.recover` that brings the agent up for the one meeting and back to stopped afterwards; needs the local worker host's lifecycle and a decision on what "up for one meeting" starts.

### M04g review fixes (2026-10-31)
- **Semantics (1).** `safeLongRunning` no longer takes part in admission: a NEW attempt is never let through a meeting by it (it would start the agent's own long conversation); the dispatcher's meeting check passes only `yieldsAtBoundary`. The predicate now answers `Dispatcher.carriesOnDuringMeeting(attemptId)`: true only for a RUNNING attempt, when a meeting concerns its agent (read lazily: no job-store scan otherwise, finding 4) and the predicate `(taskId, attemptId)` says its remaining work is background jobs. Provisional gap: nothing in the controller yields a running attempt for a meeting by itself (the agent interrupts its own tasks with `prepare`), so no production code calls `carriesOnDuringMeeting` yet; remainder on M04h.
- **Gate (2).** The jobs service's long-running gate now also refuses a NEW background or long-running job admitted by an agent on ANY task from the notice before a meeting the agent attends (the lead window, found through `attendance.admission`) until it ends, not only on the meeting's own task. Owner, host and service principals are unaffected. It is the owner's rule (no long tasks during a meeting), always on; the `meeting.safeLongRunning` setting controls only the carry-on.
- **Ownership and state (3).** Only the unfinished jobs of THIS attempt count (`attemptId`); jobs of other attempts or without one are ignored; a job still `admitted` (not placed on a host) is not moving; only `dispatched`/`running` count. Not modelled (remainder on M04h): an attempt that waits on its background jobs' results (handling a finished job's result needs the agent).
- **Wiring (5, 6).** An explicit `options.dispatch.dispatcher.safeLongRunning` wins; an explicit `undefined` key leaves the composed predicate in place. `start.ts` uses `SAFE_LONG_RUNNING_SETTING`. M04g's title is now "Compose a real safeLongRunning from the job records".
- **Tests.** Unit (attempt ownership, admitted, others' jobs), dispatcher (admission never passes the flag or reads the predicate; carry-on only for a running attempt with a meeting, lazy, fail closed, not after it ended), composed (running attempt with a background job carries on, setting off/on, foreground job yields, new attempt deferred, agent-admitted background and long jobs refused on a non-meeting task during a meeting while owner and short jobs are allowed, agent allowed with no meeting, explicit option wins). Mutation checks: no running check, gate extension removed, attempt filter removed, `admitted` counted, spread fix reverted, meeting check removed each fail a test.

### M04g second review fixes (2026-10-31)
- **Gate fails closed (1).** For an agent principal, an error from the meeting check refuses the long or background job ("whether a meeting is near could not be checked ... try again"). ## H12s (narrowed): the landing policy from the settings reaches the host builder (2026-10-31)

- The three settings (`workspace.landing.branch`, `.requirePermit`, `.protectedPaths`) were already registered as chat-settable configuration settings (H12q); nothing in the running controller read them for a host. `api/landing-policy.ts` (`landingPolicyFrom`) reads them for the task (`taskValue`: installation, the working agent's team and agent, the task; a task the configuration does not know falls back to the installation value), fresh at every call, and `startController` passes it to `composeDispatch`, which hands it to `dispatch.local.build` as `services.landingPolicy`. A host composer passes it as the `landing` option of `LocalWorkspaces`/`WorkspaceHost`.
- Behaviour: no branch set gives no `branch` (the host then refuses the landing, nothing guessed); `requirePermit` is true unless the value is explicitly false; an unset `protectedPaths` leaves the host's built-in list, an empty list protects nothing; an unreadable setting throws and the host treats that as no policy (landing refused).
- Tests: `api/h12s-landing-policy.test.ts` (unit: precedence, defaults, failure; through `startController`: the builder's `landingPolicy` follows the owner's staged-and-applied settings). Mutations killed: `requirePermit` defaulting to false, not wiring `landingPolicy` in `start.ts`.
- **Not done, now card H12t:** no product code builds a `LocalWorker` over `localWorkerParts` and `LocalWorkspaces`; `HostOrder` carries no task or project; a remote worker is not forced to give the responder its busy check; there is no project layer, so the landing policy is one per installation (read per task). H12s is narrowed to the policy wiring above; status not changed.

### H12s review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **requirePermit can now be turned off, by the owner only.** New `SettingDefinition.installationMayWiden`: the installation layer is not limited by the fallback (true) when written, and its value REPLACES the fallback in the combination; lower layers still combine as before (a team, agent or task can only keep it true, and cannot set false when the installation or the default requires true). `fallback: true` stays, so the default view shows true. Other restrictions (provider.*.enabled, budget.paidAllowed, deniedTools, reloadPreservesPause, ceilings) do not set the flag and behave as before (configuration tests all pass).
- **protectedPaths ADDS to the built-in list.** It is now a restriction where each layer adds to the ones above (like deniedTools; nothing can be removed by a lower layer). `workspace.landing.protectDefaults` (default true, installation layer only, chat-settable) turns the built-in list off. The host protects `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS` (unless `protectDefaults` is false) plus the owner's paths; an empty list no longer means "protect nothing". Provisional: the way to protect nothing is protectDefaults=false and no paths.
- **branch and protectDefaults are installation-only** (`SettingDefinition.installationOnly`, refused at stage and apply for other layers, so a `config.write` holder cannot redirect landings or switch protection off per task). Consequence: one landing branch for the whole installation until a project layer exists (H12t).
- **Path patterns** with a `.` part (`./CODEOWNERS`, `.github/./`) are refused with the other bad parts; lists are sorted and de-duplicated.
- **Wording:** the policy is per task (installation, team, agent, task), not per project; host.ts and the settings text say so, and H12t records the need for a project layer.
- Tests: `configuration.test.ts` (real ConfigurationService, both backends: owner sets false and the policy reads false, task and agent layers refused when the installation or default requires true, task over installation with a real task, additive paths, installation-only, `.` parts), `host.test.ts` (additive protection), `h12s-landing-policy.test.ts` updated. Mutations killed: no installation replace, no installation-only check, host replacing the built-in list.

### H12s second review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Installation-only is enforced when reading too.** `#combined` skips any non-installation entry of an `installationOnly` key and lists it under `ignored` ("can only be set for the whole installation"), so a task-layer `workspace.landing.branch` stored while H12q still made it a plain default no longer wins.
- **Chat text.** `ConfigurationService.settings()` exposes `installationOnly` and `installationMayWiden`; the chat explanation says "only for the whole installation" for such keys, says only the owner can set `requirePermit` past its default, and a chat proposal to set an installation-only key at a team, agent or task layer is refused with that sentence.
- **One combination per landing.** `ConfigurationService.taskValues/installationValues` return the keys from one combination; `landingPolicyFrom` uses them (a task the configuration does not know reads the installation values for all four keys). The team and agent layers apply only when an agent owns the task (`#chainOf`); documented in `landing-policy.ts`.
- **Stored values change meaning (upgrade note).** `workspace.landing.protectedPaths` values stored in the H12q era were a replacement list (an empty list meant "protect nothing"); they are now additions to the built-in list (an empty list means the built-in list only, and several layers' lists are added together). An installation that relied on a short or empty list now protects more; to protect nothing set `workspace.landing.protectDefaults` to false. Task-layer `workspace.landing.branch` values stored earlier are ignored (see above).

### H12s third slice: a real landing follows the owner's chat-set policy, and the owner can see it (2026-11-11)

- **What was missing.** The policy reader reached `dispatch.local.build` as `services.landingPolicy`, but no test built the production workspace port (`LocalWorkspaces`) from it and landed, nothing in the chat prompt said how to set the landing settings in free words, and the owner had no way to see the policy in force in chat. All three are now done.
- **Chat (free-form).** The interpreter's system prompt has a paragraph on landing: the four installation settings (`workspace.landing.branch`, `.protectedPaths`, `.requirePermit`, `.protectDefaults`) as one `policy_edit` setting template, example wordings, what each value means, that the branch is copied from the owner's words and nothing lands until one is set, that the `protectedPaths` value replaces the installation's whole list (so the model first reads the view and gives the full new list), that only the owner can turn the permit off, that there is one branch for the whole installation (not per project), and that a setting is shown first and counts from the next landing. As before, a chat setting edit is owner-only, shown first, carries the layer's revision and applies as one write.
- **New status view `landing`** (owner only; chat status kind and `status.ask { request: { kind: "landing" } }`): the landing branch (or "none set, so nothing lands"), whether the review permit is required, whether the built-in protected files apply, and the owner's extra protected paths, each marked as the owner's setting or the default, citing the installation configuration layer. It reads `ConfigurationService.installationSettings` (one combined view). When the settings cannot be read it says so in one line ("every landing is refused until they can"). Anyone else, including an agent with `config.read`, gets `not_found`.
- **Composed test** (`packages/integration/src/h12s-landing-settings.test.ts`, SQLite and embedded PostgreSQL): a started controller with the product-style host builder (`LocalWorkspaces` with `landing: services.landingPolicy`, under a `LocalWorker` with its busy check) and the real `ModelInterpreter` behind a stand-in model that only uses the template the system prompt gives. With nothing set, a landing is refused even though the shared tree is on a branch (none is guessed). The owner names the branch in chat (shown first, then applied), and the next landing gets past the branch and is refused by the default permit. A `config.write` holder can neither write the installation layer, nor turn the permit off for a task, nor set the branch for a task. The owner turns the permit off in chat; a stale revision written against the layer before that edit is refused; the landing then writes the file. The owner protects `docs/` in chat, the view shows all four values, and the next landing with a `docs/` change writes nothing and keeps the file for review. The owner moves the branch to `main` in chat, and the next landing is refused because the shared tree is on another branch. When the configuration reads throw, the landing is refused and the view says the settings cannot be read; once they read again the owner's policy applies again.
