- Mutations killed: the host builder given an empty policy instead of the controller's (composed test); the prompt paragraph removed (composed test and prompt test); the owner check removed from the view (view test).
- ASSUMPTION: the view shows the installation's policy only, not a task's combined view. Task, agent and team layers can only add protected paths and keep the permit required, and the branch and `protectDefaults` are installation-only, so the installation values are what the owner sets. This is the smallest view that answers "how is landing set up". A per-task view can come with the project layer (H12t).
- ASSUMPTION: `protectedPaths` set in chat replaces the installation layer's list (a setting value is a whole value). There is no add-one or remove-one change: the model reads the view first and gives the full list, and the proposal shows the value in force before the owner agrees.
- **Third review (2026-11-11).** (1) Adding one protected path in chat could not work as the prompt described: every value of a chat proposal must be in the owner's own message, so the full new list (`["docs/","scripts/"]` for "also keep the scripts folder for my review") was refused because `docs/` was not in it, and "the docs folder" was refused because `docs/` with its slash was not either. Now (`PolicyEditService.#ownPartOf`) the entries of a list setting already in force in that layer count as a record and need not be retyped, and a protected folder may be named without its trailing slash as a whole word of the message; a path the owner never said is still refused, so text an agent wrote cannot add one. (2) A list value replaces the whole list, and leaving entries out needs no words: the proposal now names every entry the new list (or a remove) drops ("these 2 entries are no longer in it: ...") before the owner agrees. (3) A landing whose policy could not be read was refused as "no landing branch set", which would send the owner to set a branch that is already set; it now says the landing settings could not be read (the internal error is not passed on). Tests: `chat/policy-edit.test.ts` (list kept, folder in words, invented path and part-of-a-word refused, drops named), `worker/workspace/host.test.ts` (unreadable policy), the composed test (add a folder in chat, a narrowing proposal names what it drops, the unreadable refusal's words).
- ASSUMPTION: a list entry already in force in the layer being changed may be kept without the owner retyping it. It is a record, not new text, and keeping a protected path only protects more; what the new list drops is named in the proposal.
- Interplay with H12t: once a project can name its own landing branch, the view's first line ("there is no per-project landing branch yet") and the installation-only branch line must say so; whichever card merges second updates the view.
- **Not done (H12t and beyond):** no product code (a real `main` of a worker host) builds `LocalWorker` with `LocalWorkspaces`; only tests do. `HostOrder` carries no task or project. A remote worker is not forced to give the responder its busy check. There is no project layer, so one landing branch and one protected list serve the whole installation. The landing lease and queue are still P10.
## L03i: reassigning responsibilities with the hand-off (2026-10-31)

- Built: `handoff.complete` takes `reassignResponsibilities` (a list of responsibility IDs, at most 50). The package's responsibilities section now says how. `check` runs at completion as the one who completes, before anything moves: each ID must be readable, in the task's project, not retired and answered for by the sender, the recipient must be an agent, and the caller needs `responsibility.assign` (the owner has it); otherwise `invalid_command` and the hand-off stays ready. The list is stored in the hand-off (`reassign`).
- Carried out in the `transferring` step, after the task has moved and before the hand-off is marked transferred, as the principal who completed it (looked up again; if gone or inactive nothing moves and each entry is reported failed). Each entry is moved by an ordinary `responsibility.update` (so the update's own `responsibility.assign` check applies again, and claims on managed resources stay with the responsibility and move with it). Entries move independently; a failure leaves that responsibility with the sender and never undoes the task's move. The outcome is recorded as `reassigned { moved, failed[{id, reason}] }` in the hand-off and a history line. Repeating after a crash is harmless (an entry already answered for by the recipient counts as moved; the command ID follows the revision).
- Provisional choices: a hand-off with `returnAt` (or the return itself) refuses `reassignResponsibilities` (responsibilities would not come back with the task); a forced takeover has no completion step and does not move responsibilities (the owner reassigns them directly); there is no "all" shortcut and no default policy: moving is always an explicit choice per hand-off (nothing widens by default). The "owner question surfaced with the package" is the package section text plus the refusal messages; no separate inbox item.
- Locks: the integrator lease (P10) and workspace holds (H12m) do not exist (both still planned), so the locks section now always ends with a line saying they are not tracked yet and any held are missing, not absent (a gap, not an absence). Wiring them as sources is the new card L03j (deps L03i, P10, H12m); L03i was narrowed to the responsibilities offer, so its acceptance ("the owner can reassign responsibilities with the hand-off package") holds; the lock-source half of the original wording is L03j.
- Tests: `api/start-handoff.test.ts` (package text, refusals before anything moves incl. other's duty / unknown / bad shape, chosen vs unchosen, claim stays with the responsibility, temporary reassignment refused, per-entry failure, repeat, gone asker, caller without the assign right); the L03g/L03h tests expect the gap line. Mutations killed: no check at completion, no move, no ownership guard in apply, no temporary-reassignment refusal, no assign-right check.

### L03i review fixes (2026-10-31)

- Warning (owner decision 2026-10-30, reassignment is immediate and warns): after a duty moves, the recipient's rights are checked (provisional set: `responsibility.read`, `responsibility.write`, `attempt.work` in the project); if any is missing a needs-you maintenance notification names them (command ID from hand-off and duty, so a repeat records nothing new; a failure to record propagates and the step is repeated). Nothing is held back by it. The hand-off's activity line now also says how many duties moved and which stayed with the sender and why.
- `check` now needs `responsibility.assign` and `responsibility.write` (what the update needs) and an active agent recipient, all before anything moves.
- A storage error (anything but a typed refusal) while moving is thrown: the hand-off stays in `transferring` and the next pass or sweep repeats the step; only typed refusals are stored per entry. A repeat `complete` naming another list than the recorded one is refused. An entry whose answerable agent is no longer the sender is reported as "already moved or changed since".
- Chat: `reassignResponsibilities` stays outside the exempt keys (the interpreter may not pick which duties move); the refusal now tells the owner to give the rsp- IDs. Moving duties is shown first.
- Tests added for the asker re-lookup, the crash/replay through the sweep, other project's/retired duty, caller with the hand-off right but not the assign/write rights, warning once, non-typed error rethrown. Mutations killed: asker not looked up, non-typed error stored, repeat-list guard, project check, retired check, write right, warning, chat message, rethrow in the mover.
## T05 (second slice): the MCP door on the conversation listener (2026-10-31)

T05's adapter (`mcp/conversation-adapter.ts`, notes of 2026-10-22) had no way in: nothing carried a message to it. What is built now: `POST /mcp` on the U02b conversation listener (`transport/http.ts`, `#mcpRoute`). One JSON-RPC message per request, one JSON body back; a notification gets 202 and no body. The bearer credential is passed to the adapter for every message (it authenticates afresh, nothing is cached), and the listener's host check, address and principal rate limits, body bound and its refusal of host/service credentials (403) apply before it. No `Mcp-Session-Id` is issued: a connection owns nothing and a reconnect resumes from the cursor. `GET /mcp` and `DELETE /mcp` answer 405 (there is no event stream and no session). Wrong content type 415, bad JSON a JSON-RPC parse error, a batch the adapter's refusal, an oversized body 413. It exists exactly when the conversation listener does (`conversationTransport` in `startController`), so remote exposure stays opt-in with TLS and public host names.

- Tests: `transport/mcp-door.test.ts` (four backends, real sockets: both directions, a retried commandId is the same message, a reconnect reads on from the cursor and the REST door sees the same record, another project's agent learns nothing, host 403, bad or missing credential 401, a disabled client refused on its next request, framing cases) and `api/start-mcp-conversation.test.ts` (through `startController`, the owner's credential). Mutations killed: POST-only check removed, 202 for notifications changed.
- **Review fixes (Opus security review).** (1) The per-address allowance now counts only FAILED sign-ins (an address already over it is refused before the slow credential check); authenticated requests no longer share one loopback bucket. MCP messages have their own per-principal allowance (`mcpPerPrincipalPerMinute`, default 1800), apart from REST. (2) `ConversationService.read` also returns `scannedSeq`; the adapter's `cursor` is the last item, else `scannedSeq`, so a read that found only hidden messages moves on (tested at small scale with hidden messages; the 5000-message scan cap itself is not reproduced). (3) New installation-only setting `conversation.mcp.enabled` (default true, effect next-request; generic settings path, so the policy-edit chat lists it); `startController` passes `mcpEnabled` to the listener, checked first on every `/mcp` request (404 when off; 503 when the switch cannot be read); the REST door is not switched. (4) The listener's authenticated principal is handed to the adapter (`handle(token, message, principal)`), so one credential check per request; nothing is kept across requests. (5) `initialize` with an unsupported version answers with the newest supported (none given is still an error); a present `Origin` that is not one of the listener's own is refused (403) on `/mcp`; the Bearer scheme word is case-insensitive. (6) Tests: no-listener case, chunked oversized body, import tidy. T05b text narrowed to the stock-client test, the event stream, resources/prompts and stdio. Mutations killed: address check, MCP bucket, switch, Origin, scheme case, stream bound, cursor fallback.
- Not done (card T05b, added; D05 waits for it): conformance against a stock MCP SDK client (MCP-Protocol-Version and Accept headers, streamable-HTTP expectations), the optional server-to-client stream and push notices, thread resources and prompts, and stdio. Plan statuses were not changed.

## M02g: per-decision limit on widening, guarded refusals, chat reading of the decision log (2026-10-31)

- **Limit.** `MeetingRecordService` option `policyWideningLimit(projectId)`: before a widening change (grant, budget raise) is started on the approval policy's leave (`ownerResponse !== "agreed"`), the decision's changes already started under `policy:<class>` are counted (recounted inside the start's save, so a concurrent start is seen on the retry). At the limit the decision goes back to `ownerResponse: pending` (as a policy "ask" does, so `needs_you` shows it); the changes already applied stay applied and the rest stay `adopted`. The owner's agree lifts the limit and carries out the rest (logged `applied`, decided by owner); a decline refuses them (`declined`). Nothing is logged as refused by the limit. Settings, installation layer only, chat-settable, in `MEETING_SETTINGS`: `meeting.decision.limitPolicyWidening` (default true; false = no limit) and `meeting.decision.maxPolicyWidening` (0-50, default 3). Provisional: default 3, grants and raises counted together; a failed read of the setting counts as limit 0 (fails closed); `policy:none` changes (widening nothing) are not counted.
- **Guarded refusals (the M02e2 item).** Until a change has been started, `refuse()` saves with the same guard as the start (still `adopted`, owner's answer unchanged); if the owner answered meanwhile the pass reads the decision again instead of overwriting a change the owner's agreement started. Refusals after the start are unguarded as before. The other M02e2 items (a lost `applying` save uses up a loop turn; `notes.chair.read`) are untouched.
- **Chat reading.** `status.ask` gains `{ kind: "decision_log", projectId?, changeKind?, outcome?, after?, limit? }` (owner only; anyone else, and a task-scoped owner credential, reads nothing; default 10 lines, max 50): one plain line a change (time, kind, target kind, outcome and code, who allowed it) citing the log line, decision and project. Wired in `start.ts` through a late reference to the record service (built after the status service).
- **Tests.** `record.test.ts` (all four backends): limit none/2/0/owner-agrees; refusal not saved over an owner-started change. `api/start-decision-log.test.ts`: status line text and cites, empty reading, agent refused, setting validation, defaults and owner override. Mutations killed: no guard on the refusal, no limit comparison.
- **Not done, now card M02h (M02g stays planned until reviewed/flipped by the owner):** the steward agent (`decidedBy: "steward"` stays reserved), the narrator, chat commands for meetings beyond the log reading, learned auto-apply rules from the log, the aggregate cap across decisions. The per-decision limit does not bound the total across many decisions.

### M02g review fixes (2026-10-31)

- HIGH: over-limit changes no longer end as final refusals; the decision waits for the owner and the agree carries them out (see Limit above). Test: 5 raises, 3 applied, agree, 5 applied with the last two decided by owner; decline; limit 0; fail-closed; mixed decision with `policy:none`; and through `startController` (`api/start-widening-limit.test.ts`: default 3, max 7, limit off, 0).
- MED: the chat reading takes a window of up to 100 stored entries (the log is stored in ID order, not time order), shows the newest of the window first, accepts `after`, and says so when the window is empty but the scan was limited. Entries of a window beyond the shown limit are not repeated by the cursor (ask for a larger limit up to 50). Bad `changeKind` is refused with that field name.
- LOW: the recount in the start's save is a defensive race guard; it has no test (it needs two passes interleaving on one decision), mutation-removing it is not caught.
- Splitting grants across several decisions is not bounded by the per-decision limit; that is the aggregate cap in M02h (kept in the card text).

### M02g second review fixes (2026-10-31)

- The owner is now shown a decision held for them: `MeetingRecordService.ownerPending` (owner only; scans up to 10 pages of 100 decisions, `truncated` when the end is not reached) feeds the `needs_you` list (`status` dep `meetingDecisions`), for every pending in-scope decision with a change left, including the conclude-time pending path. It leaves the list once agreed or declined. No separate notification is opened.
- A decision put back to waiting part way (the limit, or the policy asking at apply time) carries `held: true`; only widening changes wait, a change already started and changes that widen nothing go ahead. A decline refuses only the waiting ones. A policy that tightened after the vote no longer ends in a refusal: the decision is held for the owner (this replaces the earlier "refused, unauthorized" result; logs of such decisions now show `declined` or the later outcome).
- The limit counts only changes applied or applying; a change refused after the policy started it is kept with its `agreedBy`/`actedAs` (was lost with the stale copy), so the log shows `decidedBy: policy` for it. Log lines of changes the policy started no longer claim an owner response of pending/declined (`not-asked`). The summary reads a held decision with applied changes as part-applied.
- Chat reading of the decision log: a page is `limit` stored entries (no window beyond what is shown, so `after` loses nothing), newest first within the page; the text says the stored order is by entry ID, not time. Order across pages is still not time (a time index is not built).

## F04e (first slice): chat-controlled controller database transfer (2026-10-31)

- **Built.** `transfer/transfer.ts`: `DatabaseTransferService` moves the whole store between SQLite and PostgreSQL (either direction) through the backup's logical table rows (`snapshot()` and `restoreRows()`), so bodies arrive byte for byte. Owner operations `database.transfer.status|preview|apply|rollback` (owner only; apply and rollback are proposals in every profile in chat; the chat fills the confirmation token from a plan worked out at proposal time, never from the interpreter). Targets are named by the host in `StartOptions.transfer.targets` (a PostgreSQL address holds a password and never comes from chat); with none the commands answer "not configured" (that is the enable/disable: no target, no feature).
- **Apply, in order.** Preview checks (and apply repeats them): source IDs and kinds, timestamps, JSON bodies, audit counter equals the last audit record, delivery counters, receipts (a delivered message has one, an undelivered one has none), the effect digests, policy records readable, recovery points name an existing task, attempt and artifact, artifact files exist in the artifact store (start wires `FileBlobStore.has`), conversation checkpoints through an optional port (`references.checkpoints`, not wired to the Pi stores yet: card F04l). Destination: empty (epoch 0, no rows), same schema version, free room (rows' text x `CAPACITY_FACTOR` 2; a SQLite destination whose free space cannot be read is refused, a PostgreSQL one only warns). Then the maintenance barrier is raised (the existing participants: running attempts must have ended, loops stop), the source is snapshotted, copied table by table (claimed deliveries and timers become pending; claims belong to the drained controller), read back (count and SHA-256 per table), the source's counters are compared with those at the start, the source is fenced (its epoch is taken: a deposed writer gets `stale_epoch`) and the authority file is written. The barrier stays up (as for a restore) until the host restarts the controller on the new database.
- **Failure.** Before the fence any failure leaves the source byte for byte as it was (tested at every stage and every table with an injected failure, and with a write racing the copy): barrier down, destination emptied through the target's `discard` if it has one, journal `failed` with the stage and reason, a retry works. After the fence and before the authority file, the barrier stays up and `resolveAtStart` settles it from the journal at the next start: on the destination it finishes the switch, on the source it abandons.
- **Authority.** `storage-authority.json` (data directory; generation, active, previous, transfer ID) is what makes the destination the only database: `start.ts` calls `resolveAtStart` and `assertStorageAuthority` before anything is opened, so the old configuration after a move, or a copy restored from a backup onto the old path, is refused with where the data is now. Fingerprints are `sqlite:<canon path>` (links resolved with the backup's `canon`) and `postgres:<host>:<port>/<db>#<schema>` (no user or password).
- **Rollback.** Allowed only for the latest switched transfer and only while the destination's epoch, audit and delivery counters equal those recorded after the copy (a controller that started on it has already recorded something): then the authority goes back to the source (new generation) and the destination is fenced. Otherwise refused with the counts and the advice to transfer back. Reverse transfer is the same operation from a PostgreSQL controller into a NEW empty SQLite file (a SQLite file a controller has owned is never reused: not empty).
- **Chat.** `applyProposal` of a proposal containing `database.transfer.apply` reports applied even though the proposal record cannot be updated in the database that was just fenced (`stale_epoch`).
- **Tests.** `transfer/transfer.test.ts` (SQLite to real PostgreSQL and back with new work on the way; injected failure at every stage; settle at start four ways; eleven source-check refusals; destination not empty, partial, schema skew, capacity; confirmation and barrier refusals; a racing write; rollback and its refusal; damaged authority file) and `api/start-transfer.test.ts` (real controller: rights, preview, wrong token, apply, maintenance refusal, old configuration refused, new one starts, chat proposal with the token from the record and an over-large move refused). Mutations killed: no read-back digest compare, no fence, source-unchanged check removed, no authority guard at start, rollback without the new-work check, claims not released, receipt check, capacity check.
- **Provisional choices.** (1) Drain = the restore's barrier, so a transfer is refused while an agent attempt runs (stop or pause first). (2) No time or money caps and no confirmation expiry; the token is bound to direction, both places, schema version and authority generation, and apply repeats every check. (3) Uncertain and intended effects are carried unchanged (reported as warnings), never rerun. (4) `CAPACITY_FACTOR` 2. (5) Targets are host code, not chat-settable; the settings of this feature are the presence of targets. (6) Journal and authority files are plain JSON written atomically (no HMAC).
- **Not done, new cards.** F04l: read targets from the configuration (PostgreSQL address as a secret reference), a real PostgreSQL target helper (free room, schema discard), checking Pi conversation stores against checkpoints. F04m: restart hand-over after the switch, the `apply_proposal` path inside a chat message (its turn record fails in the fenced database), resumable or self-cleaning partial copies, integrity mark on the journal and authority file, transfers for a PostgreSQL controller without a data directory. F04e's status is not changed.

### F04e review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Durable fence (high 1).** The fence is now also inside the database: `assertNotFenced` runs after the database is opened and before the epoch is taken (start.ts), and refuses when `state.holder` starts with `transferred-out:` or `rolled-back:` unless the authority file names THIS database for that very transfer (or the transfer was abandoned/failed and this is its source). Without a state directory such a database never starts. The journal and authority file live in ONE fixed folder, `StartOptions.transfer.stateDirectory`, never derived from a database path (mandatory when targets are given; the start throws otherwise). `guardStart` replaces `resolveAtStart` and `assertStorageAuthority`. Tests use separate folders for the source, the destination and the state; PostgreSQL has no data directory and is held by the in-database fence (reverse-transfer test). A destination controller started without the transfer state directory cannot finish a switch or roll back (documented limit: the host must give every controller the same state folder).
- **Partial destinations (high 2).** `guardStart` refuses a start whose database is the `to` of a journal the authority file does not name (copying, failed, abandoned, rolled-back or never-switched): the message says it may hold only part of the data. Tested with a target that has no discard.
- **Rollback reachable (med 3).** Rollback is now run by the controller running on the NEW database (`database.transfer.rollback`, owner API or the chat there; the chat proposal on that controller works because that database is live). At the end of a start `recordFirstStart` notes the counters in the journal (`firstStart`); the rollback is allowed only while the audit and delivery counters equal them (the start's own records and epoch are not work), then it fences the new database (`rolled-back:<id>`), points the authority at the previous database for the same transfer id and keeps the barrier up. The refusal message and the start message say "from a controller running on <new> that has not recorded work". The chat's applied-despite-fence rule covers the rollback too. Provisional: work done by the dispatcher in the moments after `firstStart` is noted counts as work.
- **Ambiguous fence (med 4).** If the epoch change errors, the state row is read again; holder `transferred-out:<id>` counts as fenced and the switch goes on.
- **Files (med 5).** The directory is flushed after each rename (POSIX). A journal in `switched` whose authority file does not name its destination is an error that stops the start (before: "nothing transferred").
- **Discard (low 6).** `discard` runs only when this transfer wrote rows (not after a refused barrier, not when the first write was refused).
- **Fingerprints (low 7).** PostgreSQL: a `host` query parameter (unix socket) and `port` count; an address that cannot be read, or names no server, is refused instead of mapping to a shared string.
- **Digests (low 8).** The scan hashes every table; after the copy the source is read again and every table must have the same digest (catches an in-place change with equal counters).
- **Open proposal (low 9).** The chat proposal copied to the destination stays `open` there; applying it again fails (the token no longer matches: the authority generation moved). Not marked.
- **Preview (low 10).** The text now says the destination is opened and a new one gets its empty tables; the preview does not clean up (production targets own their databases).
- **Token expiry (low 11).** Accepted: no expiry, bound to places, schema and authority generation; every check repeats at apply.
- **Owner switch (12).** `database.transfer.enabled` (installation setting, default on, installation only, chat-settable); preview, apply and rollback refuse when off. Targets stay in the host configuration.
- Tests added or changed: transfer.test.ts (separate state folder, fence in the database, rollback on the restarted controller, work refusal, partial/failed/abandoned destinations, switched without authority, ambiguous fence, in-place change, discard spy, switch, fingerprints) and start-transfer.test.ts (separate folders for each database, old database refused with and without transfer configuration, new one starts, real rollback and restart on the old one, rollback refused after work, owner switch).

### F04e second review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **1. Fence first.** The source's epoch is taken (with the re-read for a lost answer) BEFORE the journal says `fencing`. A crash between leaves journal `copying` and a source whose holder is `transferred-out:<id>`; a start on the source abandons the transfer, `assertNotFenced` admits it (the journal says abandoned and no authority file names another database) and the normal epoch take puts a normal holder back (tested). The destination never finishes a switch from `copying` (it is refused). New test point `fencing-recorded`.
- **2. Admission and locking.** An abandoned or failed source is admitted only if no authority file names another database. The journal and authority file are single-writer across processes: a lock in `<stateDirectory>/.transfer-lock` (the data directory lock's machinery: live holders, stale takeover, refresh; in a sub-folder because the state folder may be the data directory) is held by apply, rollback and by every start from `guardStart` to the end of `assertNotFenced`. A start waits (up to 5 minutes), an apply or rollback that finds it taken is refused at once. Test: two starts at once on a fenced source and its verified destination, exactly one is admitted and it agrees with the authority file. Residual: a lock of another host is stale after the data lock's stale minutes (10 by default); a transfer on one host and a start on another that wait out that time are not excluded.
- **3. Pending holder.** The copy writes the destination's `state` row with holder `transfer-pending:<id>` (the read-back digest is over the rows as written). `assertNotFenced` refuses it unless the authority file names the database for that transfer; the destination's first start takes the epoch and the holder becomes normal. A failed transfer with no `discard` that wrote a full copy therefore never starts as a normal database (tested).
- **4. First-start baseline.** `recordFirstStart` runs in `composeDispatch` right before the driver starts (new `beforeLoops`), or before the maintenance loop and transport when there is no dispatcher; the start's own provisioning writes (which happen inside composeDispatch) are before it. It records only when the epoch is the copied one plus one (so a start without the state folder in between makes it never record and a rollback is refused: "no clean record") and when growth since the copy is within `START_WRITES_MAX` (1000 audit records, 100 messages; provisional). Work done before the driver starts is the one window left.
- **5. Rolling back.** A `rolling-back` journal phase is written after the no-work check and before the new database is fenced; any start finishes it (authority to the previous database for the same transfer id, journal `rolled-back`). Crash points `rollback:journal`, `rollback:fenced`, `rollback:authority` are tested; each converges. If the crash was before the new database was fenced, only the authority file keeps it from starting (a start without the state folder is not stopped).
- **6. Writes between check and fence.** After the fence the source's counters and the digest of every table except `state` are checked against the scan; a mismatch takes the epoch back with the original holder and fails the transfer (journal `failed`; the controller's services hold the old epoch and are deposed, so the barrier stays up and a restart follows). Same for rollback (counters). Tested with a write injected between the last check and the fence, both ways.
- **7. Backups.** A backup restored from before a transfer carries a normal holder. The refusal text says so; keeping `transfer.stateDirectory` configured is what makes the authority file refuse the old database. A restore cannot keep a fenced holder (it writes a new store from the backup). Not done: refusing to start without a state folder when a journal exists (nothing can read the journal then).
- **8-10.** `transfer.stateDirectory` must be absolute and is canonicalised (links resolved); the journal and authority files are 0600 and the folder 0700 (POSIX, best effort elsewhere); the destination is checked empty again after opening it for the copy, and is not emptied when that check refuses.

### F04e third review (2026-10-31): fixes and recorded gaps

- Fixed: a start on the destination of a `failed` transfer whose destination is clean (emptied by `discard`, or never written) is no longer refused; a pending-holder leftover is named as such in the "not empty" text; an unrecorded first start is caught and printed by `start.ts` (it only turns rollback off and cannot degrade `composeDispatch`); the rollback refusal for "no first-start record" names the crash/record-failure case; the 0600 test covers the authority file.
- Recorded, not done (card F04m): (2) the holder check and the epoch take are separate steps, so a second start on PostgreSQL could slip in between (milliseconds; take the epoch inside the state lock or with `expectedEpoch` from the row `assertNotFenced` read); (3) writes that bump neither the audit nor the delivery counter are invisible to the rollback check; (5) a failed take-back after a late write leaves a half-settled transfer (journal `copying`/`fencing`, source fenced); (6) the state lock is held across slow start work (migrations, restore swap), so a second start waits up to five minutes; and there is no owner-facing way to wipe a pending or failed destination (the host empties it).
## L05c: remote workers' model streams and the check of a tool call against the recorded generation (2026-10-31)

Code: `generation/generation.ts` (`checkCall`, `BeginRun.whilePaused`, `RunBody.beganPaused`), `generation/stream-settings.ts` (three new switches), `generation/stream-feed.ts` (paused retry), routes `stream-start`, `stream-events`, `stream-end` in `remote/server.ts`, `RemoteWorkerService.streamStart/streamEvents/streamEnd` (`remote/service.ts`, option `streams`), `RemoteAttempt.streamTap()` (`remote/client.ts`), the bridge check `ToolExecutionService.#generationRefusal` (`toolbridge/service.ts`, options `generations`, `callCheck`), wiring in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` (`streams`, `DispatchHandle.generation`) and `api/start.ts`. Tests: `api/start-remote-stream.test.ts` (composed controller, a worker over real HTTP with its own `ModelRelay`), `generation/stream-feed.test.ts` (paused recording, `checkCall`), `toolbridge/service.test.ts` (bridge refusals and switches, four backends).

- **Remote stream through the protocol.** A remote worker makes its own model calls, so its `ModelRelay` takes `attempt.streamTap()` as its `stream`. `stream-start` (placement and session checked like every message, contract must be confirmed, idempotency key: a retry does not begin a second generation, which would supersede the first) calls the same `streamTapFor` the local relay uses, with the attempt's fence read from the placement record, and answers `recorded:false`, `refused` (the worker must not send the request) or a `streamId` (plus the correction `amend` for a retried request and the held-buffer cap). `stream-events` carries the decoded events (shape-checked, at most 500 per message), numbered `n`: the same message sent again is answered again and recorded once, a gap is refused. The answer's `held` makes the worker's relay fail the call with the reason, exactly as for a local worker. `stream-end` completes the generation (a half-written tool call is dropped for good); sending it twice is harmless. A stale placement or session is `fenced`. At most 4 calls of an attempt stay open; the oldest is ended as failed.
- **Bridge check.** The bridge asks `GenerationService.checkCall(taskId, callId)` (the model's own tool call ID is the bridge's `callId`). A call found in a recorded generation is refused with the reason (code `generation_refused`, "it was not run") unless that generation is the task's current one at the current context revision, uninterrupted, the task is not held, and the call is `complete` (or `admitted`). Interrupted generations' calls were already `withdrawn` by L05; the check reads the same record. Applies to every bridge operation, reads too. If the check cannot be made the call is refused as `unavailable` (fail closed). The extension's own `decl-` declaration reads are exempt.
- **Settings (owner only, chat-settable, in `generation.stream.change`).** `recordPaused` (on), `checkBridge` (on), `requireRecorded` (OFF). `requireRecorded` is off because a stream that was not recorded (recording off, an unknown reply format, a task the service does not know) says nothing either way; with it on the bridge also refuses a call no generation recorded. None is a time or money limit.
- **A paused task's call is recorded.** `begin` with `whilePaused` (dispatcher only) skips the pause refusal and marks the run `beganPaused`; admitting its calls as effects is still refused while the pause stands (and the bridge's writes are refused by the pause). This changes L05b's behaviour (which refused a paused task's call before sending it) when `recordPaused` is on; turning it off restores the refusal.
- **Provisional choices.** (1) `recordPaused` defaults to on (the card says the call is recorded, which needs it sent). (2) A remote worker that cannot reach the controller refuses the call (closed); the controller's `failClosed` setting is not consulted by the worker. (3) A bridge call ID the Pi extension rewrote (`d:` for a repeated ID, `h:` for an unsafe one) matches no recorded call: passes by default, refused under `requireRecorded`. (4) `checkCall` searches the task's newest 20 generations.
- **Not done (new card L05d).** (1) Admitting a bridge call as an effect (`admitEffect`) from the bridge, so a partial call can never start an effect by that route as well as by the record. (2) A remote worker host that runs Pi in a sandbox over the protocol, with this tap wired into its relay, shown with a real worker process (the test uses a real HTTP client and the real relay class, not a sandboxed Pi). (3) Matching rewritten call IDs (`d:`/`h:`) in `checkCall`. (4) The stall-detection `waiting` signal for a remote relay's store waits. (5) Batching means a piece just after a correction may be recorded as late and still pass (L05b note); the test sets the batch settings to 0.

### L05c review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **Worker batching (HIGH).** `RemoteAttempt.streamTap()` no longer sends one request per piece. Events wait on the worker and go out when `batchChars` (4000) are waiting, when `batchMs` (250) has passed since the last send (a timer sends what waits when the model pauses), and always before a completed tool call or the end of the reply is passed on; adjacent text and same-call tool pieces are merged. Whether to hold the reply is the answer to the latest message; a background send that found the generation late holds the reply at the next piece (the same price of batching as L05b: a piece right after a correction may pass). Options `batchMs`/`batchChars` (0 = every piece). Test: 5000 single tokens in under 300 messages.
- **Message size (MED).** A message carries at most 400 events and about 700 KB of JSON; a longer string is cut into 100,000-character slices (a 3 MB text is a handful of messages). Test: 2000 unmergeable events and a 3 MB text.
- **Overlapping retries (MED).** `stream-start` keeps its answer as a promise under the idempotency key before awaiting it; `stream-events` keeps the latest message's promise with a digest of its content, so an overlapping copy gets the same answer and is recorded once; the same number with other content is refused. Tests with `Promise.all`.
- **recordPaused default OFF (MED).** A paused task's model call is refused before it is sent, as in L05b (model spend is new work). On, it is sent and recorded (`beganPaused`). The L05b tests are back at the default; the on case is its own test. Chat verb text and operation docs name the new switches.
- **checkCall cost (MED).** The search ends at the first run begun under an older context revision (that run is still read, so the latest corrected generation's calls are refused). A call from a generation older than that reads as unrecorded (passes unless `requireRecorded`). The settings read in the bridge is one small record per call; not cached (a cache would make an owner's switch lag).
- **Held task, no record (LOW-MED).** `checkCall` answers `{ recorded:false, held }` for a held task and the bridge refuses such a call (when `checkBridge` is on).
- **Declaration reads (LOW).** Exempt by operation: under `requireRecorded` an unrecorded `tool.discover` passes (the extension's `decl-` IDs may be rewritten to `h:`); recorded-but-withdrawn IDs are still refused for any operation.
- **Attempt end (LOW).** When a placement ends, completes or moves (`#wake`), and when the service closes, its open model calls are ended as failed, so no generation stays streaming.
- **Known limits (for L05d).** A worker that never sends `stream-start` is not recorded and so (without `requireRecorded`) not checked; the bridge cannot tie a call's tool name and arguments to the operation it asks for (the recorded call's name and arguments are not compared with the bridge request); the stream-id-of-another-attempt case is tested only for another host (an agent runs one attempt at a time, so a second attempt of the same host could not be started in the test).

### L05c second review fixes (2026-10-31)

- **checkCall scans on (HIGH).** The early stop is gone: the newest 20 generations are read, so a call withdrawn in an older generation (superseded, then the task corrected) is still refused. The cost is up to 20 reads of runs per bridge call; a cheaper index is left for L05d. Test: superseded, corrected, the old call refused and the new one passes.
- **Held first.** A held task is reported held before anything else, also when it has no generation (the gate exists from the hold). The held check comes BEFORE the `tool.discover` exemption, so a held task's catalogue reads are refused too (when `checkBridge` is on).
- **Message size** counts UTF-8 bytes (`Buffer.byteLength`), test with CJK text.
- **Accepted, for L05d.** (1) The worker's batching uses fixed figures (250 ms, 4000 characters), not the owner's `batchMs`/`batchChars`; pass them in the `stream-start` answer when wired. (2) With the worker's batch and the controller's, up to about 500 ms or 6000 characters of late text can pass after a correction, against about 250 ms for a local worker. (3) A controller restart loses the start/events idempotency maps and the open calls (a retry after a restart begins a new generation). (4) Recording a paused task's call is owner-settable (`recordPaused`), off by default.

## F04l (first slice): transfer targets from configuration (SQLite) (2026-11-01)

Code: `transfer/targets.ts` (`sqliteTargetsFromConfig`, `SqliteTargetEntry`, `SqliteTargetDeps`, `TARGET_ENTRIES_MAX`), exported from `transfer/index.ts`. Tests: `transfer/targets.test.ts`.

- **Configuration entries.** `sqliteTargetsFromConfig(entries, deps)` turns `{ name, kind: "sqlite", path }` entries into `TransferTarget`s. The entries may come from untrusted JSON, so every field is checked: name 1 to 64 characters of `[a-z0-9-]` and unique in the list, path absolute, no other fields, at most 16 entries. A refusal is an `Error` naming the entry's index and the problem; one bad entry returns no targets. A `postgres` entry is refused until that half lands.
- **The targets.** `fingerprint` is `sqliteFingerprint` (links resolved, one place one spelling), taken at build time; `open()` opens a new store at the path through the injected `openStorage`; `freeBytes()` reads `statfs` of the nearest existing directory at or above the path's folder (the folder may not exist yet) and answers nothing when the file system cannot be read; no `discard` (the host empties a failed destination). `deps` injects `openStorage` and `statfs`, so the tests need no disk beyond a temp dir.
- **Left for later slices.** PostgreSQL entries (`postgresFingerprint` plus the `PostgresStorage` wiring; the URL never comes from chat); building `StartOptions.transfer.targets` from the configuration in `api/start.ts`; and the check that a transfer leaves the Pi conversation store alone.

## M03h (first slice): stand-ups in the chat's meetings status answer (2026-11-01)

- **How stand-ups are stored.** A stand-up is a `meeting-schedule` with a `standup-config` record keyed by the schedule ID (the window and coverage the meeting service does not know); its occurrences are ordinary `meeting-occurrence` records, told from other meetings only by their schedule having that record. So "the project's stand-ups" means the occurrences of schedules that carry a `standup-config`.
- **New read.** `StandupService.recent(viewer, projectId, { limit })` (`standups/standups.ts`): for someone who may read the project's meetings (the right asked directly through `meetings.planned`, so a readable project with no stand-ups answers an empty list and nothing else answers undefined), each stand-up of the project by its latest occurrence (`schedule.lastOccurrenceId`): the occurrence id and revision, title, `startsAt` and state — when it ran or is planned — sorted most recent first, at most `limit` (default 20, at most 50), `more` saying some were left out. A stand-up whose schedule has not made an occurrence yet is left out; ended stand-ups are listed too (their last meeting was still this project's stand-up).
- **Status answer.** New optional `StatusDeps.standups`; `meetingLines` adds, after the planned-meeting lines, one line per stand-up in the same style — `Title: stand-up, <startsAt>, <state>.` — citing the occurrence (`meeting`) and the project, and "There are more stand-ups than shown." when the page was cut. The same `limit` (1 to 50, default 10) is asked of both reads. `api/start.ts` wires the dep lazily through `dispatch?.standups`, since the stand-up service exists only once the dispatcher runs.
- **API docs.** The `status.ask` summary in `api/operations.ts` now says the meetings answer also lists the stand-ups by their latest occurrence; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated (`npm run api:docs:write`).
- **Tests.** `status/status.test.ts` (all backends): two stand-ups and one ordinary meeting — the stand-up lines follow the meeting line, most recent first, citing meeting and project; `limit: 1` leaves one stand-up line plus "more stand-ups than shown" and the same page is asked of the stand-up source; a caller without the meeting right gets nothing, and one who may see the meetings but not the stand-ups gets the meetings answer unchanged; a project with no stand-ups gets no extra line. `standups/standups.test.ts`: two stand-ups with occurrences (one settled held, one planned) and one stand-up that has not met yet — newest first by the latest occurrence, the limit and `more`, a reader of the project's meetings sees them, a manager of another project sees none, an empty list for a project with none, and a bad limit is refused. Mutations (dropping the stand-up block in `meetingLines`, dropping the sort, dropping the right check in `recent`) each fail a test.
- **Provisional choices.** (1) One line per stand-up (its latest occurrence), not one per occurrence: there is no per-project index of past occurrences, and scanning every `meeting-occurrence` record is the cost the M03g notes already flag; `lastOccurrenceId` is the only indexed handle. (2) Ended stand-ups are listed. (3) A planned stand-up occurrence appears twice — in the planned-meeting line (with its roster) and in the stand-up line (as its stand-up's latest); the lines say different things, and deduplicating is left for a later slice.
- **Not done (remains of M03h).** The chat commands that pause, resume, rename or end a stand-up named from the status answer (naming by title already exists via `standup.list`), and the usage sink.

## T05b (first slice): threads as resources on the MCP conversation door (2026-11-01)

Code: `mcp/conversation-adapter.ts` (`#listResources`, `#readResource`, `#threadText`, `#who`). Tests: `mcp/conversation-adapter.test.ts`, `transport/mcp-door.test.ts`.

- **What answers now.** `resources/list` and `resources/read` on the conversation door's adapter; `initialize` advertises `resources: { listChanged: false, subscribe: false }`. `resources/templates/list` and `prompts/list` still answer empty, and there is still no event stream. Nothing else changed: no settings, no transport change, no new limit.
- **A thread is a resource.** URI `nimblenewt://thread/<thr-…>`, name the thread's subject (redacted, then cut to `MCP_LIMITS.name` = 80 with the same `clipText` the activity feed uses), `mimeType: "text/plain"`. A read is ONE text item: the thread's newest messages (at most the adapter's `RECENT` = 50), oldest first, each line `<sentAt> <sender>: <text>`. The window is asked from `nextSeq - 51`, so a long thread is never scanned from the start.
- **The bound.** The lines must fit `MCP_LIMITS.text` (20 000). Lines are kept from the newest backwards, and the room for the marker is reserved before the first line is kept, so a thread that does not fit starts with `[older messages left out]` and stays under the bound; when even one line does not fit, the newest message alone is cut with `clipText`.
- **Permissions are the service's.** Both methods go through `ConversationService` (`threads`, `thread`, `read`) as the authenticated principal, exactly as the tool handlers do, so what a caller may list and read is what it may see through the tools; nothing reads storage directly. The transport's checks come first: with `conversation.mcp.enabled` off these methods answer 404 like every other one, and they spend the per-principal `mcpPerPrincipalPerMinute` allowance, not the REST one.
- **Existence is not revealed.** A URI that is not a thread URI, a thread that is not there and a thread the caller may not read answer the identical JSON-RPC error `-32002 "no such resource"` (the code `mcp/state-adapter.ts` already uses for the same case). A credential that is not accepted, and a host's or the controller's own, are refused `-32602`, as the state adapter refuses an unreadable resource.
- **Paging.** `resources/list` takes the MCP `cursor` (the thread id the last page ended at) and an optional `limit` (a whole number 1 to `CONVERSATION_LIMITS.page` = 100, mirroring the `conversation_threads` tool); `nextCursor` appears only when the service has more. A cursor or limit of the wrong shape is `-32602`, not an empty page.
- **Tests.** `mcp/conversation-adapter.test.ts` (four backends): the list shows only the caller's threads and nothing to an outsider, a long subject shortened and a short one kept whole, two pages with a cursor and no thread twice, a bad cursor and bad limits refused, a read's one item with who-and-when lines oldest first, five 8000-character messages bounded under 20 000 with the left-out marker and only the newest kept, six unreadable/unknown/malformed URIs answered one identical JSON error, refused credentials and principal kinds, the advertised capability. `transport/mcp-door.test.ts`: the switch answers 404 for both methods when off and 200 when on, a `resources/list` uses the MCP allowance (429 after it, REST still open), and over a real socket another project's agent is shown no thread and gets the same `-32002` for a read.
- **Not done (rest of card T05b).** Conformance against a stock MCP SDK client, the optional server-to-client stream and push notices (which is why `listChanged` and `subscribe` stay false), prompts, and stdio.

## M02h (first slice): the end of a part-applied decision's wait is told truthfully (2026-11-05)

Code: `meetings/record.ts` (`#applyDecisionTally`, `ownerRespond`), `meetings/summary.ts`, `meetings/record-types.ts` (`SummaryDecision.waitingForOwner`). Tests: `meetings/record.test.ts` (the M02g limit suite and the apply-in-two-steps suite), on all four backends.

- **`waitingFor` at the tenth change.** The apply pass ends after `RECORD_LIMITS.changes` (10) changes. When the last of them was the one that put the decision back to waiting for the owner, the closing answer lacked `waitingFor: "owner"` (the early returns had it). The closing tally now carries it whenever the owner's response is pending. Test: nine plain changes then a widening one with a limit of 0.
- **The `held` flag.** It was written when a decision was put back to waiting part way and never removed. The owner's answer (agree, decline or an alternative) now drops it from the record, so a decided decision does not carry it. Nothing reads it except the pass's own check while the response is pending, so records written before this change that still carry it behave as before and need no migration.
- **The summary.** A part-applied decision that still waits for the owner (some change applied, some still adopted or applying, response pending) now has `waitingForOwner: true`; its `status` stays `part-applied` (a reader that only looks at status is unchanged). It is absent once the owner has answered. Test: the held decision in the M02g limit suite, before and after a decline.
- **A decline and a change already started.** A change already `applying` when the owner declines carries on under the agreement it started with (a decline never cancels it), but nothing finished it until someone applied the decision again, since a sweep does not apply decisions. `ownerRespond` now drives the decision after a decline or an alternative when a change is `applying`; the owner's answer is already saved by then, so a failure of the applier leaves the change `applying` for the next apply and is not thrown to the owner. A failure of that drive is not thrown to the owner (the answer is saved) but is no longer hidden: the answer carries `stillApplying: true`, and the change stays `applying` until the decision is applied again (the apply operation is open to the owner too, but the owner has no chat command for it yet, see the second slice). Tests: the drive succeeds (the change is applied at once) and the drive fails (`stillApplying`, then a later apply finishes it).
- **Not done (rest of card M02h).** The steward and the narrator, chat commands for moving and voting, learned auto-apply rules, the aggregate cap across decisions, the pending index, expiry of stale holds, the order of the hold against the gate, rights and target checks (owner question), and the order dependence of widening changes.

## M02h (second slice): the owner answers a held meeting decision by chat (2026-11-06, reviewed and corrected 2026-11-07)

Code: `chat/commands.ts` (`meeting.record.owner-respond`, propose mode; `describe`, `proposalReason`, a per-command exemption), `chat/chat.ts` (`#resolve`, `#expandAnswer`, the apply of a proposal, the step list of `submit`), `chat/model-interpreter.ts` (the prompt), `api/operations.ts` (`meeting.decisions.waiting`; the answer's `shown` lines; the `stillApplying` text), `meetings/record.ts` (`ownerPending`; `ownerRespond`: the counts, `stillApplying`/`passFailed`/`replayed`/`ownerDecisionDisputed`, a reused alternative command ID, `orphanError`, `pendingAlternatives`), `meetings/record-types.ts` (`pendingAlternatives`), `decisions/decisions.ts` (`refusal`, the meeting decision in `origin`), `decisions/records.ts` (`DecisionOrigin.meetingDecisionId`), `status/status.ts` (the `needs_you` line). Tests: `chat/meeting-decision-chat.test.ts` (all four backends, the chat path), `meetings/record.test.ts`, `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts`, `api/start-widening-limit.test.ts`.

- **The chat operation.** `meeting.record.owner-respond` is a chat command, always a proposal, so the owner sees what will happen and confirms. The reason shown says why: the answer is final (a decision cannot be answered twice), and agreeing lets its changes go ahead. The model gives `response` (agree, decline or alternative) and `decisionTopic`, the owner's own words for which decision (any part of what was decided or its topic). No ID is needed. Matching drops words that say nothing about which decision ("change", "one", "decision", "that", ...), matches whole words only ("art" is not "start") and lets a plural fit its singular; every remaining word must fit, and if none does a single fitting word is enough. Several fitting decisions ask which; none, or nothing waiting, refuse with `not_found`. A `decisionId` must be one of the waiting decisions; one the owner did not write or pick from the question is the model's own, and with several waiting the owner is asked. A list the service cut short (50 read, or the scan limit) is never read as "nothing waits": with no match the owner is told more decisions wait than could be read and is asked for more of the words; with one match a note says so.
- **The preview.** `describe` names the decision (its wording and how many changes are left), says what the answer does, and for an alternative shows `alternative="<the owner's words>" on topic "<topic>"` first (never the record's fields). A decline or an alternative refuses only the changes not yet started: changes already started are finished, those done stay done; the preview gives the number started (`applying`, from the waiting list). `standup.prepare` and `standup.add-statement` (M03h) had fallen through to "a role's capabilities are shown first"; their reasons now say what they do.
- **The list.** Owner-only query `meeting.decisions.waiting`: the same decisions as `needs_you`, with the decision's wording (300 characters), its topic (the motion's own, else the topic of the agenda item it answered, the topics an owner decision is checked on), `left`, `applied` and `applying`. An agent, a host or a task-scoped owner credential is refused; so is `ownerRespond` for a task-scoped owner credential. The `needs_you` line now quotes the wording and topic, so the owner can tell decisions apart and use the words in the answer.
- **An alternative.** `alternativeStatement` (and, only if the owner names one, `alternativeTopic`) is the owner's own decision, at most 150 characters so the preview can show it whole (the line for this command has room for the decision, the alternative and a topic of 80 characters; the decision comes before the alternative). It must be in the owner's message, and before anything is proposed the checks the decision service will make are made here: at least two words and six characters, not a question or hypothetical, not words that follow a negation, and from the topic's history that the topic does not hold another kind of decision (goal, permission, gate), has no unsettled conflict and does not already hold exactly these words. A failing alternative is not proposed; the owner is told `Nothing was proposed: <reason>. The meeting decision still waits for your answer; say what you decide instead as its own sentence (for example "Keep the staging server until May.").` The topic is the owner's topic words, else the topic of the held decision (the motion's, else its agenda item's); a decision with neither is not given a topic made from the agents' words: the owner is asked to name one. The controller builds the record: the held decision's project, category `decision`, `basedOn` read from the topic's history, the chat turn as source, a command ID of the turn. When the proposal is confirmed `basedOn` is read again, the way a decision step does, so a decision stated earlier in the same message on the same topic is not turned into a dispute. The model cannot give an `alternative` object (it is not an accepted argument).
  - **Superseded in part (see "Landing on main with no human step is a shown proposal, not a phrase"):** the refusal quoted above no longer hands the owner a sentence to copy. It now reads `Nothing was proposed: <reason>. The meeting decision still waits for your answer; say what you decide instead, in your own words — a plain sentence of at least two words`, and the topic refusals say `in your own words` instead of `(for example: topic staging server)` — the word `topic` was never required, so that example taught a word that does nothing. Everything else in this entry (the 150-character bound, the two-word minimum, the topic's history checks, `basedOn`) is unchanged.
- **Exempt values.** `response` and `decisionId` are fixed choices and a record reference, so they need not be in the message (no magic word "agree"). The exemption is for this command only (`OWNER_RESPOND_EXEMPT` passed to `foreignValue`), not every command.
- **What the owner is told afterwards.** `ownerRespond` returns what the answer did, counted from the record before and after (`carriedOut`, `refused` as the codes, `alreadyDone`, `refusedBefore`, `stillOpen`; each change is in exactly one: see Final behaviour (c)), and the operation turns that into `shown` lines (`ownerAnswerLines`, tested for every code): after an agreement how many changes were carried out now and how many had been done before, and for each reason a change was not carried out (moved on, the agent no longer holds the right, a gate, gone, failed, recommendation) how many; after a decline or an alternative what was refused and how many already started changes were finished. An agreement whose applier fails no longer throws after the answer was saved: like a decline it keeps the answer and returns `stillApplying`, and the line says the change stays applying, that nothing applies it again by itself and that it is finished by applying the decision again through the API (`meeting.record.apply`); the owner has no chat command for that.
- **The prompt.** One line says when to use the operation and what `response`, `decisionTopic` and `alternativeStatement` are; argument names come from `acceptedArgs`. Tested.
- **Docs.** `stillApplying` and `shown` are in the owner-respond summary and result, `stillApplying` in the apply summary. `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **The drive after a decline.** Checked by replacing the `else` branch (the decision log when nothing was applying) with nothing: the record tests fail on all four backends, so it is covered; the drive that succeeds and the one that fails (`stillApplying`) have their own assertions. A decision that waits with a started change is a real case, not only a theory: a decision of [widening, plain] changes whose widening change is asked of the owner while the plain one is started in the same pass and fails waits with [adopted, applying]; the list gives `applying: 1`, the decline's preview says so, and the decline finishes the started change (end-to-end test). A decision whose change had started before the owner came is not held for the owner (joining does not hold it) and is not in the list.
- **Not done (rest of card M02h).** The steward and the narrator, chat commands for moving and voting in a meeting, learned auto-apply rules, the aggregate cap across decisions, the pending index (`ownerPending` still scans up to 1000 decisions), expiry of stale holds, the order of the hold against the gate, rights and target checks (owner question), the order dependence of widening changes. The owner's other meeting controls have no chat command either: opening or closing a vote, amending or tabling a motion, adding an owner message to the discussion, finishing a meeting and `meeting.record.apply` (which matters for `stillApplying`: nothing re-drives a change that stays applying, and the owner can only apply through the API). A revision guard on the proposal is not added: the service refuses an answer to a decision already answered, and a decision that moved otherwise only means fewer changes left than the preview said.
- **Final behaviour (after thirteen review rounds).**
  - **(a) The alternative and its command ID.** The alternative's command ID stands for one owner decision (`derivedId("dec", scopedCommandId(owner, id))`). It must differ from the answer's own command ID (both are scoped to the owner the same way, so a shared one would record the owner decision and then collide with the answer): the same one is refused (`invalid_command`, field `alternative`) before anything is written. What the decision service would refuse (a stance that is not a decision, words that are not a decision, a source that is not the owner's own words) is refused first, through the service's own checks (`DecisionService.refusal`, which `record` uses too), so a refused alternative writes nothing. Then the meeting decision is marked: the owner decision's ID is appended to `pendingAlternatives` (its own guarded command `meeting.decision.owner-pending`, allowed only while the owner response is pending or not-asked; oldest first, no repeats, at most `RECORD_LIMITS.pendingAlternatives` = 8; every marked attempt counts, recorded or not (one may have stopped before the record or been refused after the marker); at the bound a new alternative is refused with "8 earlier alternatives of yours to this meeting decision were begun and never saved as its answer (K of them recorded); answer it with agree or decline (to decide otherwise, decline and say what you decide on the topic), or send one of them again through the API", K being the listed decisions whose origin names this meeting decision, and a listed one is still accepted; a chat confirm can send an earlier alternative again only while its proposal is still open, since the chat makes the command ID per turn). Then the owner decision is recorded with `origin.meetingDecisionId` = this meeting decision (set by the meeting record through a third argument of `record`, never from the caller), then the answer is saved and links it (`ownerDecisionId`). The marker list stays after the answer. A call that fails after the marker but before the record (the service itself refusing for a state reason, such as the same decision already standing) leaves a marker that points at nothing or at a decision that is not this one's; such a marker tells nothing (it is not an orphan) but it counts toward the bound of 8. Dropping markers of attempts that never recorded is not safe (the record may be in flight, or a crash may follow it), so they are kept. Repeat: the same command ID and content on the same meeting decision (linked) resolves to that decision and is not recorded twice. Crash recovery: the same ID after a crash between the record and the answer finds the recorded decision (chat too: the chat's `from` plumbing and its re-read `basedOn` are why `basedOn` is left out of the comparison). A recorded decision is used for this meeting decision only if it is linked to it, or it is listed in `pendingAlternatives` AND its own origin names this meeting decision. Otherwise it is refused (`invalid_command`): "...but for another meeting decision, not for this one" when its origin names another, or "...but nothing shows which meeting decision it was for (it was recorded before that was kept), so it is not used for this one" when it has no origin (see the old-record decision below), each with id, topic, state and the repair hint. Content compared with what the service stored: project, task, category, gate, topic (the gate topic for a gate, else the normalised topic), statement and wording exactly as given (stored untrimmed), source channel and turn, and session; a different one is `command_conflict`. The reuse path makes the service's input checks too: an object (`null`, a string or a list is `invalid_command`), no unknown field, `basedOn` a whole number. **Old records (decided):** the first version of the marker was one field, `pendingAlternative`; it is read as a list of one. An owner decision recorded by an earlier version carries no `origin.meetingDecisionId`, so the marker alone is never taken to mean it was recorded for this meeting decision: it is not reused through the marker (an existing record in crash-recovery state, recorded and still pending, is now refused with the "nothing shows" reason instead of being accepted; the owner repairs it with a later `decision.record` on the topic, or answers with agree or decline) and it is not told as an orphan. The slice is unreleased, so no such record exists outside tests; the choice errs towards never attaching one owner decision to a meeting decision it may not belong to.
  - **(b) Orphans.** An owner decision recorded for a meeting decision (its own origin says so) and not linked to its answer stands (nothing here withdraws it; the decision service replaces a decision only by a later one). Every such decision listed on the meeting decision is told, as `orphanedDecisions[]` (id, topic, state), one line each, in the answer that is given differently after a crash (agree, decline or another alternative), read from the list as it stood before the call, so a repeat tells them too. One recorded for another meeting decision, one that has no origin, and one never recorded is never told as this one's. They are also told in a refusal when the alternative's ID is used for a meeting decision that no longer waits ("...no longer waits for an answer (<response>)") or never waited ("...does not wait for your answer (it was not adopted for the team to carry out)"). The wording gives the decision's id, topic and state (in force; conflicts, so nothing on the topic is in force until the owner chooses; replaced) and says it is not linked. Repair: for one in force, "say what you decide on topic ... now (a later decision of yours replaces it)" (a later `decision.record` on the topic); for a conflict, "settle that conflict to choose". An answer that loses the race after recording is told the same way.
  - **(c) What the owner is told.** Each change is in exactly one of `carriedOut`, `refused` (codes), `alreadyDone`, `refusedBefore`, `stillOpen`, counted from the record before and after the call. A repeat of an answer (`replayed`) still runs the pass and counts what it did: it says "nothing more was done now" only when it carried out and refused nothing and no pass failed; otherwise "this call finished what was left" (nothing is left), "this call did this much of what was left" (it moved things on and work remains) or "what was left could not be finished now". `stillApplying` only when a started change stays applying; `passFailed` when carrying out stopped with changes still adopted ("any of the remaining changes" when some were done or refused before). The disputed line and the orphan lines are told on the first call and on a repeat. Texts for refused codes (`NOT_CARRIED_OUT`) are true for every use of a code.
  - **(d) Assumptions and what is left.**
    - ASSUMPTION: the alternative is recorded in the `decision` category and the topic is the held decision's topic when the owner names none.
    - ASSUMPTION: an alternative longer than 150 characters is not proposed.
    - ASSUMPTION: an orphaned owner decision is told and left standing (the owner's own confirmed words), not withdrawn; the marker list stays after the answer so a repeat tells it too.
    - ASSUMPTION: at the bound of 8 unresolved attempts a new alternative is refused with the way out (agree, decline, or send a listed one again) rather than dropping the oldest, so no attempt is ever forgotten.
    - Remaining, in order: (1) a chat command for `meeting.record.apply`; (2) withdrawing an orphaned owner decision (needs a decisions operation; repair today is a later `decision.record`); (3) the alternative's record and the answer are still two steps (recovered through the marker list and the origin, not atomic); a refusal by the service for a state reason after the marker was written (the same decision already standing) leaves a marker that tells nothing but counts toward the bound, and the validation before the marker covers the service's input and wording checks only; owner decisions recorded by an earlier version of the marker (no origin) cannot be recovered or told (see the old-record decision above); then the not-done list above.
  - **(e) Verification.** Seeded tests on all four backends: answering held decisions by chat (21 samples, forced cases) and alternatives through the API (10 samples with padding, crash, conflict, reuse on a finished decision, reuse on a second waiting decision, a crash then a different answer, a crash before the record then the same ID on another decision), plus deterministic sequences for taking over an ID, several attempts kept and told, the bound, a refused alternative leaving no marker, and markers pointing nowhere, to another's decision or to an old record. The reviewers' two-meeting-decision sampler (350 seeds) and probes S1-S4 pass. Mutation checks, each killed by a test: the content comparisons (category with goal and permission, project, topic, source, gate, session, stance, unknown field, `basedOn`), the origin write, the origin check on reuse and on the orphan report, the list append, the read of the old single field, the bound and its count of recorded attempts, validation before the marker, the orphan self-link guard, one line per orphan, the never-waited, elsewhere and no-origin wordings, the non-object guard, the orphan line in both line paths, the disputed hint, and the earlier repeat/count/header/wording fixes.
- Review history: thirteen rounds (2026-11-07); corrections are folded in above.

## M02h (third slice): the owner's other meeting controls by chat (2026-11-10)

Code: `meetings/record.ts` (`ownerControls`), `api/operations.ts` (query `meeting.owner-controls`; `api/state-api.ts` type list), `chat/commands.ts` (`CHAT_OPS` entries, `MOTION_CONTROLS`, `MEETING_CONTROLS`, `MEETING_CONTROL_EXEMPT`, `acceptedArgs`, `proposalReason`, `describe`), `chat/chat.ts` (`#resolveMeetingControl`), `chat/model-interpreter.ts` (one prompt line). Tests: `chat/meeting-controls-suite.ts` (run by `meeting-controls*.test.ts`, one backend per file, as the M02h answer suite is). `api-v1.md` regenerated.

- **Done.** Five owner chat commands, all reachable in free words (no magic phrase), all `propose` mode (shown first with a reason that says what it does): `meeting.record.open-vote`, `meeting.record.close-vote`, `meeting.record.table`, `meeting.record.finish`, `meeting.record.apply` (the chat command the second slice listed as missing: it finishes a change that stays `applying`). The model gives the owner's words (`motionTopic`, `meetingTopic`, `decisionTopic`); the thing acted on is found among what the owner can act on and the operation can still do something to (a motion waiting for a vote, a motion with a vote open, a motion not yet put to a vote for tabling, as the records service allows, an open meeting, an adopted decision with changes left). Matching is the one the answer to a held decision uses (significant words, whole words, every word then any word); several fits ask which, none refuses with `not_found`, nothing listed is `not_found`. A project in focus narrows the candidates. An ID the owner did not say or pick from the question is the model's own: with several candidates the owner is asked. The version a vote is opened on is read from the record, never said or taken from the model.
- **The list.** Owner-only query `meeting.owner-controls` (not a task-scoped credential; `limit` 1 to 50): `meetings` (each open meeting with its non-final motions: id, number, text cut to 300, topic, state, version) and `unfinished` (adopted in-scope decisions not waiting for the owner with changes `adopted` or `applying`; a declined decision with a started change is in it). Reads the open-meeting index and up to 1000 decisions; `truncated` says more exist, and the chat then says so in its refusal instead of reading a short list as "none".
- **Reasons shown.** Opening a vote starts the clock on a decision the team will carry out; counting settles the motion and an adopted decision is carried out (or waits for the owner as the policy says); tabling and ending cannot be taken back and ending voids motions not concluded; applying carries out changes a vote or the owner agreed to (each checked again against the rights and state it relies on). `describe` says the same in the line.
- **Tabling.** The reason is the owner's own words if the model gives one that is in the message (the usual unseen-text check refuses one that is not), else the owner's message (cut to 500 characters).
- **Not done (rest of card M02h).** The steward agent for decisions no coded rule covers (`decidedBy steward`) and the narrator; learned auto-apply rules from the log; the aggregate cap across decisions on policy-agreed grants and raises; the pending-decisions index (`ownerPending` and `ownerControls` still scan up to 1000 decisions); expiry of stale holds; the order of the hold against the gate, rights and target checks (owner question); order dependence of widening changes; re-driving an applying change after a decline in a held decision beyond the new apply command. Chat commands not added: amending a motion (needs the new text and a version, and a material change restarts a vote), adding an owner message to the discussion, setting the chair, the length of a vote (`limitMinutes` is not accepted from chat; the default stands), the casting vote (the chair's, not the owner's), and casting a ballot (the owner is not on the roster and has no vote). Moving a motion by chat is not added for the same reason: only a roster member or the chair may move one, and the owner has no seat; an owner's wish goes in as a topic or a decision (`agenda.capture`, `decision.record`).
- **Review (clean context, 2026-11-10).** Fixed: picking a motion or meeting from the chat's question did nothing useful (the answer kept `motionTopic`/`meetingTopic` beside the picked ID, so it was refused as named twice over, and the pick did not count as the owner's words); tabling offered a motion whose vote was open, which the records service refuses after the owner confirms; words that fit every word of a motion in another state (say, still waiting for its vote) fell back to a one-word fit on another motion and proposed acting on that one (now refused, saying the state); a list cut short gave no note on a single fit. Tests: "the owner's pick from the question …", "a motion whose vote is open is not offered for tabling …".
- **ASSUMPTION:** "moving and voting" in the card is read as the controls the owner holds over motions and votes (open, count, table) plus ending a meeting and carrying a decision out; the owner moving or casting a vote would change who votes, which is a product decision the card does not make.
- **ASSUMPTION:** all five commands are always shown first, in every approval profile; a vote opened or counted produces a decision the team carries out, and the cost of one extra confirmation is small.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the length of a vote is not set from chat (the default of 10 minutes stands) so no number has to be taken from the owner's words.
- **Known gaps.** The matching text of a motion includes its meeting's title, so a title word fits all of that meeting's motions (the owner is then asked). `meeting.record.apply` has no command ID, so two confirmations of the same proposal rely on the service's own idempotence (changes already in a final state are not carried out again). No test for the "list cut short" note in the new resolver (more than 50 open meetings or unfinished decisions; the note is added on both the words and the ID path). Counting a vote early is refused by the records service while members have not voted and time remains (the chat does not read ballots to say so first). ## M02h (fourth slice, finish): cap across decisions, steward agent, narrator, learned suggestions, hold expiry, pending index, order and check order (2026-11-13)

Code: `meetings/record.ts` (apply loop, `#askSteward`, `#expireHolds`, `#sweepNarration`, `#liveDecisions`, `learnedPatterns`, `patternsOf`), `meetings/agents.ts` (model-backed narrator and steward helpers), `meetings/record-types.ts`, `meetings/meetings.ts` (settings), `api/start.ts` (wiring, `StartOptions.meetingRecords.narrate|steward`), `api/operations.ts` (`meeting.decisions.patterns`, sweep text), `status/status.ts` (`decision_patterns`), `chat/model-interpreter.ts` (one prompt line), `budgets/budgets.ts` and `security/grants.ts` (accept `steward:<class>` and hold it to the same ceiling as the policy).
