- **Aggregate cap.** Per project, in a 24-hour window: `meeting.decision.maxPolicyWideningPerDay` (default 10, 0 to 500; the same switch `limitPolicyWidening` turns it off). The count lives in a small `meeting-widening-window` record per project and is read and raised in the SAME save that starts a change on a delegate's leave, so two decisions started at once cannot both take the last place (tested). At the cap the decision is put back to the owner exactly as at the per-decision limit; the owner's agreement lifts it. A cap that cannot be read counts as reached.
- **Steward agent.** `StartOptions.meetingRecords.steward` is a host function that answers allow or ask for a widening change the policy would leave to the owner. It is used only while the owner has set `meeting.decision.steward` true (default false), and for rights only if `meeting.decision.stewardRights` is also true. It is shown the kind, class, a cut redacted summary, a digest of the patch and safe counters, never the patch. A failure, a slow answer (60 s), nonsense or "ask" send the change to the owner. An allow starts the change as `steward:<class>`, counted against both limits, logged `decidedBy: steward`, with the reason kept on the change. Where a class is steward-enabled, the vote no longer puts the decision to the owner up front; the steward is asked when the change is carried out. `meetings/agents.ts` (`stewardFrom`, `narratorFrom`) builds the texts and reads the reply strictly from a host-given `complete(system,user)`.
- **Narrator.** `StartOptions.meetingRecords.narrate` is now wired into the record service. The sweep writes the summary (with overview) once for an ended meeting still waiting for its hand-back, at most 3 a call; a failing narrator leaves the summary marked `overviewFailed` and is not asked again by the sweep.
- **Chat commands.** The owner-facing controls were added in earlier slices; this slice adds the settings above (reachable in free words through the setting proposal; the interpreter prompt now describes all the widening settings, which it did not before) and a status request `decision_patterns` ("what has my approval of meetings been like").
- **Learned rules.** `meeting.decisions.patterns` and the chat status `decision_patterns` read the decision log and suggest letting a class through where the owner agreed at least 5 times (changes the policy asked about) and never refused, overrode or lost one. It only suggests; it never changes the policy.
- **Order dependence and check order.** A held decision now marks the specific changes put aside (`waiting`) instead of freezing every widening change, so [allow, ask] and [ask, allow] give the same result. Gate, rights, missing and moved-target checks now come BEFORE the hold, so a change that could never be carried out is refused, not put to the owner.
- **Hold expiry.** `meeting.decision.holdExpiryDays` (default 14, 0 never). The sweep ends a held decision unanswered for that long as a decline made by time: unstarted changes get code `expired`, `holdExpiredAt` is set; a started change finishes.
- **Pending index.** `ownerPending` and `ownerControls` read the projects' unlogged indexes (decisions that may still need something) instead of up to 1000 decisions of all history, capped at 200 reads.

- **ASSUMPTION:** the cap is per project, 24 hours, and a started change that later fails still counts (conservative).
- **ASSUMPTION:** an unanswered hold ends as a decline after 14 days (safe side: silence never widens); the log records it as not-applied with code expired and the decision's response as declined.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the owner question "gate/rights/target checks before a hold" is answered yes (an owner is not asked about what cannot happen).
- **ASSUMPTION:** narration is automatic only for ended meetings listed for hand-back; others by `meeting.record.summarize`.

## F04m (first slice): a database move applied from a chat message is reported as applied (2026-11-05)

Code: `chat/chat.ts` (`#execute`). Test: `api/start-transfer.test.ts` ("applying the move from a chat message, not only by applyProposal, …").

- **The defect.** `applyProposal` already told the owner the move was made when the record of it could not be written to the database just retired (`stale_epoch`). A message whose plan is `apply_proposal` ran the same move through `#do`, then `#finishTurn` wrote the turn as done into the fenced database, failed with `stale_epoch` and the owner saw an error for a move that had been made.
- **The fix.** `#execute` treats `stale_epoch` from `#finishTurn` as success only when an outcome of this very turn is an applied proposal with a `database.transfer.apply` or `database.transfer.rollback` result; any other `stale_epoch` still propagates. The turn record and the context lines that would follow are not written (the old database refuses them); the next message writes to the new database.
- **Known gap (review finding).** The turn is not written to the new database, so it stays `planned` there and the proposal stays `open` (as in the earlier F04e path). If the client resends the same `messageId` after the restart, the plan runs again against the new active database and the owner is likely to see a refusal for a move that succeeded. The context line and the resumed-question marker the message would have written are not written either; nothing writes them later (the comment in `#execute` said otherwise and has been corrected). To be closed with the card's restart hand-over.
- **Not done (rest of card F04m).** Restart by the host, a copy that starts over, the integrity mark on the journal and authority file, a controller-level PostgreSQL start with a state folder, taking the epoch under the lock, the lock held across start work, a guarded take-back after a late write (split out as card F04n and flagged to the owner in build-decisions-for-owner.md on 2026-11-05; note: in the rollback path the journal says `rolling-back` before the take-back, and a failed take-back would leave a start to finish the rollback over work recorded meanwhile; the order of the journal write and the take-back needs a design before it is changed), re-hashing the other tables on rollback (needs digests noted at the first start), and the owner's wipe of a failed destination.


## F04m (second slice): restart hand-over, integrity marks, self-cleaning copies, the owner's wipe, the epoch take (2026-11-10)

Code: `transfer/transfer.ts`, `transfer/targets.ts`, `transfer/index.ts`, `api/start.ts`, `api/operations.ts`, `chat/chat.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`, `status/status.ts`, `configuration/settings.ts`, generated `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md`. Tests: `transfer/transfer.test.ts` (eight SQLite tests and one PostgreSQL test marked F04m), `transfer/targets.test.ts`, `api/start-transfer.test.ts` (three new controller tests).

- **The host restarts the controller by itself (opt-in).** `StartOptions.transfer.restart = { run(event), delayMs }` (default 1500 ms). After a move or a rollback was answered, `run({ reason: "switched" | "rolled-back", transferId, to })` is called once; the host stops the controller and starts it again from its configuration (the integration test is such a host). The journal records `restart: requested`, or `failed` with the host's reason (the move stands and the owner is told to restart by hand, as without an opt-in); closing the controller cancels a restart that is waiting (`dispose`). The answer says `restart: scheduled | off | not-offered`. The owner can turn it off and on: installation setting `database.transfer.restart` (default on, only matters when the host offers one), reachable in chat as the proposal `database.transfer.set` (`{ restart, enabled }`, which also gives chat the existing `database.transfer.enabled` switch it did not have), read as `database.transfer.settings`. `ASSUMPTION:` default on when the host opted in, because the host's opt-in is the real decision and the owner's switch only narrows it.
- **The message path is closed, including a resend.** The first slice reported the move as applied; the turn and the proposal stayed `planned`/`open` in the new database. Now `database.transfer.apply` and `database.transfer.rollback` keep the command ID in the journal (`appliedBy`, `rolledBackBy`, plus a short summary); the same command sent again, also to the controller restarted on the new database, is answered with the recorded result and `replayed: true` before any other check. A client that resends the message then gets "applied" and the chat finishes the turn and the proposal in the new database. `ASSUMPTION:` a command ID is the idempotency key for a move (as for every other command); the replay needs the journal to say `switched` with that ID and does not check the target name again.
- **A copy that failed starts over.** `#inspect` tells a left-over copy from a used database: the destination's holder is `transfer-pending:<id>`, or (the state row is copied last) the journal from BEFORE this apply says that transfer's destination was this one and it was `copying`, `abandoned` or `failed` with a dirty destination. Such a copy is a warning in the plan ("it will be emptied first") and the apply empties it through the target's `discard(id, { leftover: true })`, then copies. Never emptied: a database with a non-zero epoch, a destination the authority file names, the copy of a `switched`/`fencing`/`rolling-back` transfer, a target without `discard`. Configured SQLite destinations now have a `discard` (removes the file and its `-wal`/`-shm` only when its state row carries the pending mark or no controller ever owned it); a configured PostgreSQL destination can empty a copy left by an earlier process (before, only a schema its own open had created in this process). If the leftover cannot be emptied the new transfer stops with the reason (address hidden) and the source is as it was. `ASSUMPTION:` no true resume (continuing a half-written copy after verifying it): the card allows "resumes or is cleaned", and re-copying from a fresh snapshot cannot carry a stale row into the destination.
- **The owner's wipe.** `database.transfer.wipeplan` (query) and `database.transfer.wipe` (command, owner only, a proposal in every profile in chat; the token comes from the controller's look at the destination, never from the interpreter) remove the leftover of an unfinished move without a hand edit. A failed journal of that transfer turns to `failure.destinationClean: true`, so the destination may be started or moved to again. The new status question `database_transfer` (free words: where does my data live, what happened with the move) tells the database, the destinations, the last move, a dirty destination ("ask to remove it"), the restart setting and a host restart that failed.
- **Integrity marks.** The journal and the authority file are written with `integrity: hmac-sha256:<hex>` over their content, keyed by `transfer-integrity.key` (random, 0600, in the transfer state folder, made `wx` by the first write). A file that does not match, has no mark once the key exists, carries a mark with no key, or a key that is not a key is rejected by every reader (start, status, preview, rollback) naming the file. Files written before this change have no mark: accepted while no key exists, and marked when the first write makes the key (so an upgrade does not lock anyone out). `ASSUMPTION:` an HMAC with a key kept beside the files stops accidents, partial edits and casual tampering, not someone who can read the folder and rewrite both files and the key; the key could be given by the host (a secret) later.
- **Review fix: making the key survives a stop.** The key was opened `wx` and then written, and the old files marked after it: a stop in between left an empty key (every reader refused it) or a key beside unmarked files (refused as "no integrity mark"), so the controller would not start. Now a whole key is first placed as `transfer-integrity.key.new` (temp file, flushed, hard-linked so the name never shows half a key and never overwrites one), the unmarked files are marked with it, and it is then linked as the key and the pending name removed. Readers accept, while only the pending key exists, a file not yet marked or marked with it; the next write finishes a step left half done. Test: `transfer/transfer.test.ts` ("making the integrity key survives a stop at any step").
- **Review fix: a rollback does not keep the move's restart note.** The rolled-back journal kept the move's `restart: requested` when the rollback's own restart was off or not offered, so the status said the host was asked to restart and a resent rollback answered `scheduled`. The rollback now writes its own note or none, and a replay says `scheduled` only for a restart still `requested` (a failed one reads `not-offered`: restart by hand). Test: the host's restart test in `transfer/transfer.test.ts`.
- **The epoch take.** The start no longer holds the state lock across a staged restore's swap and the database open (it can no longer make a second start wait five minutes): the journal is settled under the lock, the slow work runs outside it, then the settle and the holder check run again under the lock and the first `acquireEpoch` is made with `expectedEpoch` from the row the check read (`expectEpochOnFirstTake`). A second start or a transfer's fence that got in between makes the first start stop with "another start or a database transfer took this database". The transfer's own fence already used `expectedEpoch`.
- **Writes the counters miss.** `firstStart` now also holds the count and digest of `operations` and `effects`; the rollback (and its re-check after the fence) compares them, so a command admitted with no audit record and no message is found. `ASSUMPTION:` only those two tables: timers, aggregates and deliveries are rewritten by loops on their own, so comparing them would refuse every rollback; deliveries are covered by their counter. Cost: one read of both tables at the first start (before the loops).
- **No data directory.** The transfer state folder is the configured `transfer.stateDirectory` (the configuration gives `<dataDir>/database-transfer`), never derived from a data directory, so a PostgreSQL controller started with no data directory runs transfers (the controller tests start with none).
- **Mutation checks: not run in this slice** (the machine was loaded by the benchmark and each test round took minutes); the reviewer should plant: mark not verified, replay check removed, leftover emptied without the authority check, restart not cancelled by `dispose`, digest compare removed, first-take `expectedEpoch` removed.
- **Not done.** (1) Taking the epoch under the state lock itself (the guarded take covers the race; the lock still is not held at `ProjectService.open`). (2) F04n (a failed take-back after a late write in a rollback) stays its own card. (3) A host that really restarts a process (the launcher is card U14): the tests restart inside one process. (4) Resuming a half-written copy instead of re-copying. (5) The integrity key from the host's secret store. (6) Aggregates, timers and deliveries are not compared at rollback beyond the counters. (7) A PostgreSQL leftover whose schema was made by someone else is still not dropped (the existing narrow-drop rules apply).

Code: `api/start.ts` (the settings port of `DatabaseTransferService`), `transfer/transfer.ts`, `api/operations.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`, `chat/chat.ts`, `chat/model-interpreter.ts`, generated `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md`. Tests: `api/start-transfer.test.ts` (three new composed-controller tests: the switch on SQLite and on an embedded PostgreSQL controller database, and a PostgreSQL controller restarted by its host onto the SQLite file it moved to), `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts` (one).

What was there already (second slice): the host's opt-in `StartOptions.transfer.restart`, the installation setting `database.transfer.restart`, the chat proposal `database.transfer.set` and the launcher entry's exit 75 (card 17). What was missing is closed here:
- **Revision checked.** `database.transfer.settings` now gives `revision` (the installation settings layer the two switches live in; 0 before anything was set there), and `database.transfer.set` takes `expectedRevision`: the change is made only while the layer is still at that revision, else `stale_revision` and nothing changes. The chat pins the revision when the message is planned (`CHAT_OPS` revision kind `database-transfer`), so a proposal the owner confirms after anything changed the installation settings is refused, not applied over a change they did not see; they ask again. A resend of the same confirmation is answered from the record and changes nothing. Without `expectedRevision` (an API caller) the layer as it is now is used, as before.
- **Others' staged changes are not applied with it.** Applying a layer puts its whole draft into force, so the switch used to carry any installation change someone had staged and not applied into force with it. Now `database.transfer.set` refuses while such a draft exists, naming its settings ("apply or discard them first").
- **A refused apply is reported.** The configuration's refusal (`applied: false`) was ignored and the owner was shown the unchanged settings as if done. It is now an error with the configuration's reasons, and the staged switch is discarded so it cannot go into force later with someone else's apply.
- **Owner only**, as before, now tested on the composed controller: an agent's credential gets `forbidden` for the read and the change. In chat, planning it with a session that cannot read the settings is refused (`forbidden`); that branch is not tested on its own (the chat is the owner's).
- **Free-form chat.** The interpreter prompt has a paragraph (no magic phrases) on moving the database, the host's automatic restart after a move or rollback, turning it or moves off and on in the owner's own words (`restart` and/or `enabled`, only the ones spoken of; `expectedRevision` left to the system), the wipe and the `database_transfer` status kind.
- **On PostgreSQL.** A controller on an embedded PostgreSQL database with the host's opt-in moves to a SQLite file named in its configuration; the host is called once with `switched`, closes it and starts a controller on the file, which has the data; the owner then turns the restart off and back on there from chat.
- `ASSUMPTION:` the revision is the whole installation layer's, not the two switches' own: any installation change between proposal and confirmation makes the proposal stale. This refuses more than strictly needed but never applies over an unseen change, and a re-ask costs one message; giving the switches a record of their own would need a configuration migration.
- `ASSUMPTION:` a foreign staged draft is refused rather than applied or set aside: the smallest, reversible choice (the owner decides about the draft).
- Mutation checks (each applied, built, run, restored; each fails the named tests): the caller's revision ignored (both backend tests); the foreign-draft check removed (both); the chat's revision pin removed (both and the prompt test); the service not passing `expectedRevision` on (both).
- **Not done.** (1) An API caller that leaves out `expectedRevision` and resends after a success gets a stale stage instead of the replay (its read revision moved; the chat always pins, so the chat is not affected). (2) A resend after a success is refused, not replayed, if someone staged other installation changes in between (the draft check runs first). (3) Two `database.transfer.set` steps in one chat message: the second is planned at the same revision and is refused as stale (one message per change). (4) The rest of F04m's list in the second slice's "Not done" (epoch under the lock, F04n, a real process restart outside the launcher, resuming a half-written copy, the key from the secret store, rollback comparison of aggregates/timers/deliveries) is unchanged. (5) The card's status in the task plan is not changed.
- **Review fix (clean-context review, 2026-11-11): a switch left staged no longer blocks the switches for good.** The switch's stage and apply are two writes; a stop between them leaves the switch staged in the installation layer. The draft check counted any staged key not in the current call as someone else's, so a left-over `restart` blocked every later change of `enabled` with "apply or discard them first", and no operation (API, chat, MCP) lets the owner discard a staged draft: the test cleared it through the service. Now a draft holding only the two transfer switches is discarded first (at the revision the caller quoted or read; an older revision is still `stale_revision` and discards nothing), so it is neither a block nor put into force with the new change; the chat's proposal planned while it waited still applies. Staged keys of anything else are still refused. An apply that throws after the stage now discards the stage as well (best effort). Test: `api/start-transfer.test.ts` ("a switch left staged by a change stopped between its stage and its apply ..."). The bad-revision check now asserts the owner-facing wording for -1, a string, a fraction, 2^60 and null (the configuration's own check refused -1 too, so the old assertion passed with the service's check removed).
- Review mutation checks (each applied, built, run, restored): left-over keys counted as foreign again (new test fails); the left-over discard skipped, so the old value merges (new test fails: `restart` went into force); the stale check before the discard removed (new test fails); `setSettings`' revision validation removed (the strengthened bad-revision check fails; before the change it passed).
- Review findings left as they are: (a) a stray staged draft of OTHER installation settings (only possible after an interrupted chat setting edit, `chat/policy-edit.ts`, which stages and applies the same way) still blocks this switch, and the owner has no operation to discard it; a chat setting edit of the same layer would instead put that draft into force with its own change (pre-existing in `policy-edit.ts`, not changed here; a `config` discard operation or a single-write stage-and-apply would close both). (b) An API caller resending after a success that first discarded a left-over draft gets `idempotency_conflict` instead of the replay (its stage was recorded at the revision after the discard); the chat is not affected. (c) `ownerOnly` checks the principal's kind and not `taskScope`; task credentials are always issued as agents, so no task credential reaches these operations.

## F04l (second slice): configured destinations are built at start, and the host answers the checkpoint check (2026-11-05)

Code: `api/start.ts` (`StartOptions.transfer.targetEntries`, `.references`). Tests: `api/start-transfer.test.ts` (two new tests).

- **Entries.** `transfer.targetEntries` takes the configuration's `{ name, kind: "sqlite", path }` entries as they are. `startController` builds them with `sqliteTargetsFromConfig` (real `SqliteStorage.open` and `statfs`) and joins them to the `targets` a host gives; a bad entry stops the start with its index and problem, and a name or a place used twice (across both lists) is refused. A state folder is still required. A repeated name or place is now refused among the host's own `targets` too (it was accepted before), and the target list is a snapshot taken at start rather than a read of the host's live array. The tests show a move to a configured destination through chat, and the three refusals.
- **Checkpoints.** The controller cannot read Pi's conversation stores (only the Pi adapter knows their layout, and the controller does not depend on it), so `transfer.references.checkpoints` is the host's answer to "which of these recovery points' checkpoints are missing", passed straight to the transfer check. The host receives each checkpoint as the JSON text the record holds. A missing one refuses the plan with the recovery point named, and nothing is moved. The test seeds a real database with a recovery point and starts the controller on it.
- **Not done (rest of card F04l).** The PostgreSQL entry (address as a secret reference, redaction from errors, logs and the journal, free room read from the server, emptying its schema); the `controller.databaseTransfer` entry in the configuration schema of `@nimblenewt/config` and the host that hands those entries to `startController` (no host in this repository does that yet); and the Pi adapter's `checkpoints` answer for the host.

## F04l (third slice): PostgreSQL destinations from configuration, the configuration entry, and the Pi checkpoint check (2026-11-07)

Code: `transfer/targets.ts` (`transferTargetsFromConfig`, `hideAddress`; `sqliteTargetsFromConfig` stays as another name for it), `storage/postgres/admin.ts` (`postgresDatabaseBytes`, `discardPostgresTransferCopy`; `dropPostgresSchema` is for tests' clean-up only), `storage/postgres/schema.ts` (`CONTROLLER_TABLES`), `api/start.ts` (`transfer.secrets`), `transfer/transfer.ts` (`TransferTarget.redact`), `@nimblenewt/config` (`controller.databaseTransfer`, `transferOptionsFromConfig`), `@nimblenewt/pi-adapter` (`missingCheckpoints`). Tests: `transfer/targets.test.ts`, `transfer/transfer.test.ts`, `api/start-transfer.test.ts`, `config/src/config.test.ts`, `pi-adapter/src/store-check.test.ts`, `integration/src/f04l-transfer-checkpoints.test.ts`.

- **Configuration.** `controller.databaseTransfer.targets` (optional, at most 16): `{ name, kind: "sqlite", path }` or `{ name, kind: "postgres", url: { secret }, schema?, maxBytes? }`. The address of a PostgreSQL entry can only be a secret reference (a plain string is refused without echoing it, as for every other secret). The secret is listed with `secretReferences`, so a start that cannot find it fails by name before anything else. A name used twice is refused; a public profile may not carry the list and a shared export omits it. `transferOptionsFromConfig(config, resolver)` gives the two things `StartOptions.transfer` takes (`targetEntries`, and `secrets`, a lookup that answers ONLY the secrets those entries name, so the controller never gets the whole secret store). The host that calls `startController` is outside this repository (package rules keep `config` and `controller` apart), so that call is the one line the host has to write.
- **PostgreSQL target.** `startController` passes the entries to `transferTargetsFromConfig` with the real `PostgresStorage.open`, `pg_database_size(current_database())` and `discardPostgresTransferCopy` (both in the storage folder, the only place allowed to touch the driver; the schema name is checked against the storage's own rule before it is placed in the statement; nothing is ever dropped with CASCADE, see the drop rule below). The fingerprint is `postgres:host:port/database#schema`, so two entries for one place, or an entry that is the controller's own database, are refused/hidden as for SQLite. The `discard` empties a failed copy only when this target's own open created the schema and the copy is still this transfer's own (see the drop rule in the review fixes below); a successful retry then starts clean (tested: failure at `copy:deliveries`, schema gone, journal `destinationClean`, second attempt moves).
- **Free room.** The preview reads the size of the destination database from the server and subtracts it from `maxBytes`; below zero is zero. Without `maxBytes` it answers nothing and the preview warns, as before. `ASSUMPTION:` PostgreSQL gives a client no portable way to ask how much disk is left (that needs a superuser program call or an extension), so the "room" is a cap the owner writes, measured against what the server reports for the database. The plan compares it with the same bytes-needed figure as SQLite (2x the rows' text).
- **The address never shows.** The address is resolved once at start and held in closures. `open`, `freeBytes` and `discard` rethrow with `hideAddress` applied (the address, the password in raw, decoded and percent-encoded form, `user:password@`, a `password=` or `sslpassword=` query value, anything shaped like `postgres://...`; the user name alone is not hidden as a bare word, because a short one would mangle ordinary text); the stack and every other property of the original (a driver's `detail`, for one) are dropped, also when the message holds no address. One rule for where the password goes: an address whose query string has `password=` or `sslpassword=` (any case) is refused when the entry is built, naming the secret and not the value (the driver honours `?password=`). The transfer service applies the target's `redact` to the whole reason and then cuts it to 500 characters (cutting first could leave the start of a password at the cut), and writes it into the journal and tells the owner. The tests check the chat answers, print lines, the journal and the authority file of a real start (SQLite to PostgreSQL) for the address, its password and `postgres://`, and the error from a copy failure whose message carries both. `ASSUMPTION:` the fingerprint (`host:port/database#schema`, no user or password) is not "the address": it is what the authority file compares and F04e already decided to keep it; if the host name itself must stay out of the journal, the fingerprint needs a hash, which would change the stored authority format.
- **Pi conversation stores.** `missingCheckpoints(adapter, points)` in the Pi adapter returns the recovery points whose checkpoint does not hold: not JSON or not an object, no checkpoint recorded, conversation or entry missing, not a turn boundary, history changed, other runtime. It uses the adapter's own `verifyCheckpoint`, and throws if the store cannot be read (a failed look is never "nothing missing"; the transfer then refuses with "could not be checked"). The controller keeps only the part of a format-2 checkpoint that names the history (conversation, entry, digest, runtime, format); the history layout and the informational contracts version are filled in with the ones this adapter writes before verifying (`ASSUMPTION:`; the runtime name and version are still compared, so a different runtime is reported). The host passes `references.checkpoints: (points) => missingCheckpoints(adapter, points)`. The refusal text now reads "is not in the conversation store, or does not match it", because a changed history is not "missing". Integration test: a real Pi adapter and a real controller; a recovery point with a wrong digest refuses the move, the checkpoint as the controller stores it passes.
- **Backends.** The target tests run the SQLite and PostgreSQL stores (the transfer service works from the snapshot interface of the real stores; the in-memory and worker SQLite stores cannot be a transfer source or destination, since a destination is a file or a server). Real PostgreSQL through the test harness: capacity, over-cap refusal, failure and clean-up, `PostgresStorage.open`'s `createdSchema`, a schema the owner creates just before or during the open never dropped, both directions through a real start (SQLite controller to configured PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL controller to configured SQLite file).
- **Owner controls.** No new operation: the existing `database.transfer.*` operations and their chat route show configured PostgreSQL destinations by name and kind like SQLite ones, so the interpreter prompt needs no new text.
- **Mutations killed.** Redaction removed from `hiding` (targets and transfer tests), from the service's `reason` (transfer test), `redact` removed from the target; free room not subtracting the server size; `discard` doing nothing; the secrets lookup not passed by `startController`; `missingCheckpoints` not calling the verifier / ignoring the verdict; the filling-in of the stored checkpoint removed.
- **Not done.** Nothing in the card's text is left except what needs a host outside this repository: the process that loads the configuration file, resolves secrets and calls `startController` with `transferOptionsFromConfig(...)` and `references.checkpoints` (no such host exists in this repository). A real disk-free figure for a PostgreSQL server (see the assumption). The PostgreSQL destination is opened without the unsupported-server override; a destination server older than the supported minimum is refused.

### F04l third slice review fixes (2026-11-07)

- **Which schema a failed copy may drop.** `PostgresStorage.open` accepts an existing schema with no tables (it creates its tables there), so `DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE` on whatever the entry names could destroy `public` of a new database, a schema the owner prepared with grants, or one holding sequences, functions or types. The rule: a schema is dropped only if THIS target's own open created it, learned from the open itself, and that is forgotten after a drop. `PostgresStorage.open` reports `createdSchema`: true only when its migration transaction found the schema absent in `pg_namespace` and its `CREATE SCHEMA` committed (a schema another session creates at the same moment makes that `CREATE SCHEMA` fail, so the open fails and claims nothing). The target sets its flag only from an open that resolved with `createdSchema` true (a failed open claims nothing; a later open of the schema this target made, such as the apply after the preview, keeps the claim), and clears it after a successful drop, so a schema of that name made later is someone else's until an open creates it again. There is no separate existence check before the open. Otherwise `discard` refuses, the journal says `destinationClean: false`, and the next preview tells the owner the destination holds a partial copy to empty first.
- **The drop rule now (fresh review, 2026-11-07).** The claim above stays from the preview's open until the apply (in chat, the whole time a proposal is pending), so what is in the schema by the time a copy fails may not be only the transfer's. `discard(transferId)` therefore never uses CASCADE: in ONE transaction, `discardPostgresTransferCopy(url, schema, "transfer-pending:<id>")` locks the schema's `state` row (`FOR UPDATE`) and requires it to be the open's own (holder NULL at epoch 0: the copy failed before the state row, which is copied last) or this transfer's `transfer-pending:<id>`; then drops the controller tables (`CONTROLLER_TABLES`: `schema_migrations` plus every table a migration's `CREATE TABLE` names, read from `MIGRATIONS`; indexes go with their tables) with `RESTRICT`, then `DROP SCHEMA ... RESTRICT`. Another table, sequence or any other object in the schema, or a view or foreign key elsewhere that depends on a controller table, makes a drop fail; the transaction rolls back, so there is no half-done state: nothing is dropped, the journal says `destinationClean: false`, and the owner's error ends "The partial copy was not removed from the destination (<why>); empty it by hand before another transfer there." (also said, without a reason, when a target has no `discard`). Someone else's holder or a taken epoch refuses the same way, so a copy another controller (another state folder) has finished writing, a database it switched to, or one a controller runs on is never dropped. A schema already gone is a success, so a re-run is a no-op; a schema without a `state` table is refused. `ASSUMPTION:` a second controller's copy that is still before its state row (holder NULL) can be dropped by the first one's clean-up; that copy has not switched, and its own read-back or writes then fail, so nothing in use is lost. A future migration that creates something other than tables or indexes must add it to the list, or every clean-up is refused (safe, not clean). Tests (`transfer.test.ts`, real PostgreSQL): a view in another schema selecting from `schema_migrations`, another table with a row in the schema, someone else's `transfer-pending:` holder, and a taken epoch each stop the drop, keep every copied row and the foreign object, and give the not-clean journal and text; a failure before and after the state row was copied (holder NULL, then the transfer's own) drops everything and a second run passes; `targets.test.ts` checks the target passes its own pending holder. A controller restart between preview and apply forgets the claim, so the drop is then refused too (conservative); so is an open that created the schema and then failed in a later migration step. Tests: `targets.test.ts` (fake server: a schema there before, the schema this target created dropped once and claimed again only after another creating open, a failed open followed by the owner's schema, a drop followed by a foreign schema of the same name) and `transfer.test.ts` (real PostgreSQL: `createdSchema` true then false; the owner's schema created just before the open's own check, and in a transaction committed while the open waits on its `CREATE SCHEMA`, both survive `discard`; a schema the owner created with a sequence of their own survives a failed copy, journal not clean).
- **Preview probe errors.** An error from the destination's store while the preview probes it (after `open`) reached the owner unredacted; it now goes through the target's `redact`. Test in `transfer.test.ts`.
- **One wiring.** `postgresTargetDeps(resolveSecret)` (`transfer/targets.ts`) is the real PostgreSQL side used by `startController` and by the real-server tests, so the start's wiring is what those tests exercise.
- **Configuration tests** (`config.test.ts`): a plain address is refused at the entry's path without echoing any part of it, a name used twice, malformed entries, more than 16, the secret listed by `secretReferences` and reported missing by `resolveSecrets`, the export omits the list, a public profile is refused.
- **Server size answer.** `databaseSizeFrom` (`storage/postgres/admin.ts`) accepts only a string of digits that is a finite number; anything else (empty, negative, `NaN`, exponent, an overflow to infinity) is an error, so a bad answer can never become a `NaN` room that passes the check.
- **Further tests.** A PostgreSQL entry's name is taken like a SQLite one's (a later SQLite entry of that name is refused); a stored checkpoint with another `historyFormat` is reported (the stored layout is used when present).
- **Mutations (fresh review fixes).** Each fails a test: the holder check removed, the NULL/epoch-0 case refused, epoch not checked, the transfer's own holder refused, the tables or the schema dropped CASCADE, the already-gone early return removed, the not-clean owner text dropped, the target passing the bare id; the secret-reference check without its one-key rule (the test now uses a secret that resolves, `{ secret: "transfer.pg-url", extra }`, and checks the extra value is not echoed), `user:password@` not hidden or the secrets not replaced longest first (`hideAddress("x nnuser:hunter2%2Fx@db y", ...)` must give `x [address hidden]db y`), the percent-encoded password spelling removed (`u:a&b@`: `a%26b` must be hidden; kept). Equivalent: the missing-`state` message (the following read fails and rolls back anyway). Second fresh review, four more tests in `transfer.test.ts` (now 35 tests, 0 skipped): `FOR UPDATE` removed fails a race test (another copy's uncommitted state row at epoch 3 commits once the clean-up is seen waiting on a lock in `pg_stat_activity`; the clean-up must refuse and the schema stay; 10 runs, no flake); the no-`discard` owner text removed, the clean-up's reason not passed through `redact`, and `CONTROLLER_TABLES` one table short or long each fail a test.
- **Mutations.** 27 mutants of this slice (redaction, the drop rule, free room, place and name checks, the configuration checks, the secret lookup, the Pi check) each fail a test; so do the claim taken always or before the open, the claim not forgotten after a drop, `createdSchema` always true, `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS` (the race), cut-before-redact, the query-password refusal or hiding removed, the PostgreSQL name not recorded, the original error rethrown, the size check removed and the stored `historyFormat` ignored.
- **Judged.** The six `ASSUMPTION:`s stand (cap minus server size; fingerprint with host kept; layout filled in for stored format-2 checkpoints, consistent with the adapter's own upgrade of format 1; a missing named secret stops the start, as for every secret reference; the user name not hidden as a bare word; no unsupported-server override for a destination). No production host exists in this repository (`startController` is called only by tests and test worlds, `@nimblenewt/api` is a placeholder and no package may depend on both `config` and `controller`), so the two lines that pass `transferOptionsFromConfig(...)` and `references.checkpoints` belong to the card that creates that host.

## F04l (fourth slice): a start from a configuration file, the state folder and the schema from the configuration, the room in chat (2026-11-10)

Code: `@nimblenewt/config` (`transferOptionsFromConfig` now also gives `stateDirectory`; `TRANSFER_STATE_FOLDER`; optional `schema` on a PostgreSQL `controller.storage`), `controller/src/chat/chat.ts` (the transfer proposal's note), `scripts/package-boundaries.mjs` (integration may depend on `@nimblenewt/config`). Tests: `config/src/config.test.ts`, `controller/src/api/start-transfer.test.ts`, `integration/src/f04l-config-start.test.ts` (new).

- **Everything from the configuration.** A host had to invent the transfer state folder; `transferOptionsFromConfig(config, resolver)` now gives it as `<installation.dataDir>/database-transfer`, so `StartOptions.transfer` is `{ targets: [], ...transferOptionsFromConfig(config, resolver), references: { checkpoints: (p) => missingCheckpoints(adapter, p) } }` with nothing else to choose. The folder is given also when the configuration lists no destination, so a start keeps checking which database a past transfer made active after the owner takes the destinations out. `ASSUMPTION:` the folder name `database-transfer` under the data directory; a relative `dataDir` gives a relative folder, which the start refuses by name.
- **Pointing the configuration at the moved database.** A transfer to a PostgreSQL destination with its own `schema` could not be named by `controller.storage` afterwards (it had no schema), so the start's "Point controller.storage at <name>" could not be followed. `controller.storage` of kind `postgres` now takes an optional `schema` (the storage's own rule; absent means the controller's default `nimblenewt`).
- **The room in chat.** The proposal of a move now says `room: about N bytes needed, M free at the destination` (or that the free room is not known). For PostgreSQL M is the entry's `maxBytes` less what the server reports for the database; a destination without enough room was already refused with both figures.
- **A start from a file, as a host does it** (integration test; the glue is test code). The configuration file names a SQLite controller database and two PostgreSQL destinations whose address is the secret `transfer.pg-url` in a secret directory (`directorySecrets`). The host loads the file, resolves its secrets, builds the storage and the transfer options from it and passes the real Pi adapter's `missingCheckpoints`. In free-form chat the owner's move to a destination whose cap is just over the server's current size is refused for room; a move to the other is proposed with the room the server figure gives (checked against `pg_database_size` within 1 MiB) and applied. The authority file is in `<dataDir>/database-transfer`. The same file started again is refused with "Point controller.storage at big-pg"; the file pointed at the PostgreSQL schema (address still a secret reference) starts with the data and offers the way back to a file. The chat answers, print lines, the refusal and every file in the state folder hold neither the address, its password, `postgres://` nor `postgresql://`. A second test: a recovery point whose checkpoint the Pi store does not hold refuses the move from a configuration-file start, and the same record with the real checkpoint is proposed.
- **Package rule.** `integration` may now depend on `@nimblenewt/config` (test package, no product code, nothing depends on it); `config` and `controller` stay apart.
- **Mutations killed.** `stateDirectory` not given (both new integration tests fail); the room note removed from the proposal (`start-transfer.test.ts` and the integration test fail); `schema` not accepted on `controller.storage` (config test fails).
- **Not done.** The launcher process that reads the configuration file for an installation, resolves secrets from the operating system's store and calls `startController` is card U14; the integration test's host is the shape it takes. A real disk-free figure for PostgreSQL stays the owner's cap (the earlier `ASSUMPTION:`).

## T05b (second slice): a stock MCP client uses the conversation door (2026-11-05)

Code: none changed in the door. Test: `transport/mcp-sdk-client.test.ts` (four backends). Dependency: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1 (MIT), a devDependency of `@nimblenewt/controller`, added with the owner's approval of 2026-11-05. Not dev-only in effect (review finding): `@google/genai`, reached through `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, lists it as an optional peer dependency, so the lock file marks the SDK and its 92 companions `devOptional` and `npm ls --omit=dev` shows them; an install of this repository with `--omit=dev` still contains them. Published `@nimblenewt/controller` does not depend on it. The owner chose to keep it as it is (2026-11-05); moving it to the test-only `integration` package was tried and changes nothing, because that package reaches `pi-ai` too. Gemini support does not need it (`pi-ai` never mentions it; `@google/genai` uses it only in its `mcpToTool` helper). An install from this source tree that must not contain it uses `npm ci --omit=dev --omit=optional`: the only other optional package is `pg-cloudflare`, which is for Cloudflare Workers and not used on Node.

- **The dependency.** Pinned exactly to 1.32.1 (published 2026-10-05) rather than the newest 1.32.2 (2026-10-23, under two weeks old). Installing it adds 93 packages to the lock file (its HTTP-server pieces such as express and hono are unused by the test); `npm audit` reported 0 vulnerabilities and the install ran with `ignore-scripts`. It is allowed for the controller in `scripts/package-boundaries.mjs` and listed in `license-inventory.md` (227 packages, all permitted licenses). Only a test file imports it.
- **Under the package runner.** `scripts/offline-guard.mjs` replaces the global `fetch` with one that always refuses, and the SDK's transport sends through `fetch`, so the test passes the transport a loopback-only `fetch` built on `node:http` (the guard allows loopback sockets). It was first run outside the runner and passed there; the review found it failing inside the runner, and it now passes with the guard loaded (`node --import scripts/offline-guard.mjs --test …`).
- **What the test shows.** The SDK's `Client` with `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` connects with its own headers and handshake (initialize, the initialized notification, its attempt to open a stream that the door answers 405 to), lists the tools, starts a conversation as an agent, reads and answers as a second client, lists the thread as a resource and reads it, and a second connection (the first closed) reads on from the cursor and sees a later message. Nothing in the door had to change for a stock client to work.
- **Prompts: none, by the owner's decision of 2026-11-05.** `prompts/list` stays empty and the capability is not advertised. A prompt would be text a client's model follows, built from other agents' messages, and the door's resource already gives a client the same thread text; it is polish for third-party apps that show server prompts. It can be added later (a read-only `catch_up` taking a thread id was the candidate) without changing anything else. This concerns NimbleNewt as an MCP server only; prompts of outside servers used by NimbleNewt's own agents stay untrusted source material (mcp-integrations.md).
- **Event stream: not built, by the owner's decision of 2026-11-05.** `GET /mcp` stays 405 and `listChanged` stays false. The conversation service has no change feed to drive a stream (it would need a new in-process notifier, per-caller stream limits, a heartbeat and closing every stream when the switch goes off), and the notices would do little for outside apps, which at most refresh a resource list. A client reads new messages with the tools from its cursor, which the stock-client test shows. The card text was amended to match.
- **stdio bridge (owner's choice, 2026-11-05: token from an environment variable).** `mcp/stdio-bridge.ts` and `mcp/stdio-main.ts`: `node dist/mcp/stdio-main.js [door-url]` reads one JSON-RPC message per line on stdin, posts each to the controller's `/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer $NIMBLENEWT_TOKEN`, and writes each answer as one line on stdout (messages one at a time, in order). It opens no database and adds no way in; the door's own checks apply to every message.
  - The credential comes from `NIMBLENEWT_TOKEN` only (never an argument), is deleted from the process environment at start, and is never written. The address comes from `NIMBLENEWT_MCP_URL` or the first argument and must be http(s) without a user name or password; plain http is accepted only for a loopback address.
  - A refusal by the door (401, 403, 404 for switched off, 413, 429, 503) becomes a JSON-RPC error for that request with a plain message; an unreachable controller likewise, without node's own error text. A refused notification goes to stderr. A line over 64 KiB is answered here without being sent.
  - Tests: unit tests with a fake door (ordering, refusals, no credential in any output, size bound, address and token checks) and the stock SDK `Client` over `StdioClientTransport` against a real child process and the real listener on all four backends (tools, a two-party exchange, resource read, a bad credential refused at the handshake, the chat switch off and on again).
  - **Not covered:** the bridge keeps no session (the door has none), a very slow answer is cut off after 120 s, and a credential file is not supported.
- **Card T05b is now complete as amended** (no stream, no prompts); it is not flipped, which waits for the green exhaustive CI run.

## M03h (second slice): the stand-up review measures worker-slot time (2026-11-05)

Code: `standups/standups.ts` (`#slotUsage`, used by `#review` when no `usage` hook is given). Test: the P/PC balance review suite in `standups/standups.test.ts` (four backends).

- **The measure** (the owner chose "sum attempt run time", 2026-11-05). For each dispatch record of the project that ran in the period, the time it held a slot is cut to the period and added up by the class of its task (the task contract's `workClass`, P by default). An attempt counts from `startedAt` to the exact end the dispatcher recorded when it finished (`outcome.at`; the record's last update only for a record that has none); while it runs, to the end of the period. The review then says `actual PC share 33% (worker-slot time of 2 attempts)`.
- **Attempts that parked or were placed again are left out** (review finding). A resumed attempt keeps its first `startedAt`, so its record cannot tell run time from waiting time (an hour of work, twenty hours waiting for an approval, an hour of work would count as 22 hours). Parked attempts and those with more than one placement request or a resume are not counted in the share, and the basis says how many were left out. If nothing measurable remains the review counts tasks. Attempts of other projects are left out.
- **Known limits.** The scan is the stand-up service's usual bounded one (25 pages of 200 records, in id order, over every project's dispatch records), so past 5,000 records the review is marked partial and the share rests on whichever records were read; the class is the task's contract at review time, not at the time the attempt ran.
- **No attempt in the period.** Nothing is measured and the review counts tasks as before ("worker-slot time is not measured here"). A host can still pass its own `usage` hook, which wins. A scan cut short marks the review partial like the other figures.
- **Not done (rest of card M03h).** An agenda outcome that asks the owner a new question; chat commands to prepare a stand-up now, read a brief and add a statement (the API operations `standup.prepare`, `standup.brief`, `standup.briefs` and `standup.add-statement` already exist; what is missing is how the owner names the occurrence and the brief in chat, and a chat answer for a read); one end-to-end controller test with every sink.

## Test-clock fix: the meeting service reads the dispatch clock (2026-11-05)

- The M04g test "the gate refuses an agent's new long job from the notice before a planned meeting" failed from 2026-11-03 on. It fakes time through `dispatch.clock`, but `MeetingService` in `api/start.ts` was built without a clock, so it used the real one and never made the occurrence for a one-off meeting dated 2026-11-02; attendance then found no meeting. With the system clock shifted back to 2026-11-02 the unchanged test passed, which confirmed the cause.
- `MeetingService` now takes `options.dispatch.clock` when one is given (nothing changes without it). Full controller suite: 8,725 of 8,725.
- **Other services built in `start.ts` still use the real clock** when a test gives only `dispatch.clock`. None fails today; a similar date-dependent test could appear for them.

## M03h (third slice): the chat model is told what it can do; the owner may leave a note on a brief (2026-11-06)

- **Owner rule recorded (2026-11-06):** everything in NimbleNewt is controlled by free-form chat with a model; no fixed phrases. See the owner's words in the build decisions file's chat section.
- **Gap found and closed in part: the interpreter prompt.** `ModelInterpreter` told the model only the operation *names*; it never saw argument names, the names the chat resolves from words (`taskTitle`, `standupTitle`, `meetingTopic`, `agentName`, ...), or the kinds of status question. A real model could only guess them. The prompt now lists every chat operation as `name(args) - what it does`, built from the same tables the chat validates against (`CHAT_OPS`, `acceptedArgs`), and every status kind with its keys (new `STATUS_KINDS` in `status/status.ts`), and says plainly that the owner uses no fixed phrases and that an unclear project, task, agent or stand-up is a `clarify`, not a guess. A test checks that each operation and kind appears in the prompt, and another that every listed status kind is one the service knows.
- **Still not done (card U03b):** the prompt is about 19,000 characters (roughly 4,000 tokens) on every chat message, which is a cost to watch; no run against a real model has checked that it produces correct intents from natural wording (the recorded-model scenarios of U03b were never written).
- **The owner may add a note to an agent's brief.** `addStatement` accepted only the agent the brief is about. The owner may now leave a note, advice or priorities on any agent's brief; it is stored with `by: "owner"` and never reads as the agent's own words. Other principals (hosts, services) still cannot. The limit of ten statements counts both.

## M03h (fourth slice): run, annotate and read a stand-up by chat, in the owner's own words (2026-11-06)

- **What the owner can now say.** Prepare a stand-up now, leave a note on an agent's brief, and read the briefs, each by naming the stand-up and the agent in loose words ("get the morning one ready", "tell the morning agent: look at the cache", "what did the morning brief say?"). The chat's model turns the words into `standup.prepare`, `standup.add-statement` or a `standup_briefs` status question; the code only looks up the names the model extracted.
- **Looking things up.** A stand-up is found by any part of its title (words such as "stand-up" or "meeting" and small words are ignored; case does not matter) among the project's stand-ups (new read-only operation `standup.recent`). Preparing accepts a planned or reported occurrence, a note only one still ahead (a brief closes when the stand-up starts). An agent is found by name, exact first, then by any part of it. Words that fit nothing ask, listing what exists; words that fit several ask which. The brief's revision is read when the proposal is made, so the proposal is for exactly that brief.
- **Shown first.** Preparing and noting are proposals in every profile (the owner can reword them in chat before they run). Reading is a status question and changes nothing.
- **Guards that still apply, by design.** Every text value the model gives must appear in the owner's message (so a note is the owner's own words and the model cannot invent a name); the fixed choice `section` (advice, priorities, note) is exempt. The prompt now tells the model to copy names and note text exactly.
- **Reading a brief.** New status kind `standup_briefs` (`occurrenceId|meetingTopic`, `agent|agentName`): per brief, counts of done, unfinished, blocked, advice and priorities with the records each entry cites, then the statements, each marked as the owner's or the agent's own. With no stand-up named, the next one coming up is meant; with an agent named who has no brief there, the answer says no brief was found.
- **Tests.** `chat/standup-commands.test.ts` (all four backends): a note before preparation is refused as having no briefs; preparing by loose words is a proposal naming only that stand-up; words that fit none or both ask; a note by part of an agent's name is a proposal and, applied, is stored as the owner's; the briefs are read back with the owner's note marked, and a wrong agent finds no brief. The stand-up service in that test now runs on the test world's clock (it ran on the real one, which made the note look too late).
- **Not done (rest of M03h).** An agenda outcome that asks the owner a new question; an end-to-end test of a stand-up through the running controller with every sink; a per-project index (`standup.recent` and `standup.list` read every stand-up record); the status answer names agents by their principal ID, not their friendly name; no run against a real model has checked that natural wording leads to these commands (card U03b).


## C07h: the 50-hand-off test of the hand-off package

`packages/controller/src/lifecycle/handoff-hops.test.ts` hands one task A to B to A fifty times with the real hand-off service and the real controller package source. The continuation holds four decisions per attempt as record IDs (the shape the continuation service accepts, at most 200), and a simulated desk answers what each ID stands for. Checked at every hop: only the fixed sections, each within the 4000-character limit; the owner's words, goal, permissions, open question, acceptance criteria and next action present; the assignment is with the agent it was handed to. After hop 50 the seeded early decision and early failure are found again by their reference.

Findings (their checks are in the test as `todo`, named to the card that fixes them; remove the `todo` when the card lands): a section is cut at its tail with a plain slice, no marker and no archive (`lifecycle/handoff.ts` line 492), so the completed-work section is cut from hop 29 and the latest diagnosis is lost from that hop (C07j); the package grows with every hand-off, first ten hops averaging 1507 characters and the last ten 4707, because nothing summarises the decisions (`lifecycle/handoff-sources.ts` lines 48-49) (C07k). Not covered here, and moved to C07l: first-call size, stored conversation size, resume note, lease timeouts, compaction and the smaller-window fallback, open blockers, and the audit's other candidates.

Mutation checks: removing the section slice fails the section-limit test (completedWork 4094 over 4000 at hop 29); cutting the brief to its title fails the retention test at hop 1; dropping the brief leaves the package incomplete and the hand-off is refused without `acceptGaps`.

entry still lists the request with an unpaid note, a mark whose clearing crashed after the owed figure was taken off (the figure already covered by another request's charge) cleared by a later sweep,
