directions, a paid note that covers the wanted cost but not the compute keeping the want, an entry kept when a request it lists raises its want after the sweep read the page, a wanted figure that cannot be recorded anywhere keeping the marks of the requests on its entry, figures above the cap waited for at the cap (both wait paths), and the owed limit; and for the index scan and the remaining per-dimension and race rules: an open index longer than one sweep reads (neither a mark on an entry past the cut nor one on no entry read is cleared, and the view reports the cut), a sweep run without a charge port, the owed compute not lowered by a later figure, a higher compute owed while the lower is charged kept, an entry whose wanted compute was raised after its page was read kept, the wanted raise with cost and compute in opposite directions both ways, a higher figure merged (not refused) for a request already owing for the limit of attempts, and a figure owed between the read and the write of either clear keeping the mark; and, from the sixteenth review, one request listed on 2100 paid entries (the window's paid entries are taken off, the rest paid by the next sweep, each charge once, the mark cleared only then), a request listed only on an entry more than a page past the cut keeping its mark while an older record's mark on a cut scan reads as cut, an index of 150 entries read to its end by the view (a request's own note on page 2, an ended marked request on no entry reading mark only) and by the sweep's clear, and an index of exactly 2000 entries read as complete by both), `status/status.test.ts` (every backend, including a table of mode x phase x scope kind that checks each sentence), `chat/status.test.ts` (task found by title, every backend), `api/start-stop-local-work.test.ts` (through `startController`, after a real Stop with a held process).

- **What it shows.** For the latest Suspend or Stop of a task, agent, team or the installation (`{ kind: "stop_cleanup", taskId }` or `{ kind: "stop_cleanup", scope: { kind, id } }`): the mode and phase, what the preparation cost against the request's limit (`spent`, with the limit if one was set), each attempt the request saw with the cleanup total charged to its task's budget (`stop-charge`, all stops of that attempt counted once; it includes the ending, so it can be more than the preparation figure), and whether a charge is still unpaid or being made. A scope with no request of its own gets one line saying so (naming only the wider scopes that exist for its kind); a viewer who may not control the scope gets nothing (same rule as `lifecycle.get`). Read only, no new command and no new setting.
- **Free-form chat.** The owner asks in words ("what did stopping Order seeds cost?"). `stop_cleanup` is in `STATUS_KINDS` (`status/status.ts`), from which the interpreter prompt is built (tested: the prompt names it, and every kind `ask()` handles is in `STATUS_KINDS`). A task title is resolved to the task by the chat as for the other task views. The scope form (agent, team, installation) needs an ID the chat cannot resolve from a name, so in chat the task-title form is the usual one.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the figure on the first line is the request's `spent`, the figure of its current cleanup budget window (what counts against `spendBudget`), not the full cost: a `wait` on a blocked preparation restarts it (a wait after a failed ending does not). Billed but NOT counted in `spent`: a pass that went stale (the request moved while the cleanup ran), a checkpoint that throws, a second loss of the cleanup model, and a preparation pass whose note and wait both lose every race on an attempt (the figure is then owed on the request, see the ninth review; only if the request's own record also cannot be written does the pass end with the retryable `stale_revision` error, after charging some attempts and before `spent` is written), and a crash between the charge and the write of `spent` (a re-run then adds only what was not yet charged); counted in `spent`: a checkpoint that is not durable. The view says so ("a wait on a blocked preparation starts it again") and adds "the cost of ending the work is charged on top" for a Stop whose ending has run (`ended`, written after terminate and its charge), "when it runs, is charged on top" for a Stop still going, and nothing for a Suspend, a Force Stop (its own sentence), or a Stop that never reached the ending (restart from an earlier boundary, a resume). A Force Stop that took over any Suspend or Stop (preparing, blocked, prepared or already terminating) keeps that request's figure and limit and says "Its last cleanup budget window before the Force Stop (a wait on a blocked preparation starts it again) used ..." (so a wait that restarted the window, or a pass that went stale, shows as a smaller figure than the attempt totals); one that began as a Force Stop says "A Force Stop has no preparation". A Stop that reused a Suspend's checkpoint says so and points to the attempt totals (its own `spent` is 0); that is read from a `reusedFrom` marker written at creation, not from the capped history. The per-attempt lines are the running totals actually charged (all stops of that attempt, once). They are shown side by side, not merged, because a total per request would need the charge records indexed by request.
- **Wider scopes named.** A task can be stopped through its agent, a team above that agent, a parent task of its swarm or the installation; an agent through its team, a team above that or the installation; a team through a team above it or the installation.
- **Scope in chat.** A chat request has no nesting, so besides `scope: { kind, id }` (API clients) the view takes `scopeKind` and `scopeId` (what the interpreter prompt lists); a title given beside a scope is dropped. The ID must be known: the chat does not resolve an agent's or team's name.
- **Unpaid, two kinds.** `unpaid` is true when this request has charging of its own left (its own pending note is open, or an open entry that lists it holds a `want` above what was charged on that attempt) or its outcome still carries the "cleanup spend not charged" mark. When only the mark is left (another request's charge, for example a Stop of the agent over the same attempt, paid the note it waited on; `#retryCharges` clears the mark at the next sweep) the view says "A charge failed when the request ended; this request has nothing left to charge, and the next sweep checks it again and clears this." (tested: Stop fails its ending charge, the agent's Stop pays it, the task's view reads mark only, a sweep clears it). That sentence is given only where a sweep does clear the mark: the record carries `ended` (this build marked it) or an open entry lists the request. A marked record written by an older build (no `ended`) on no open entry (`markKept`) reads instead "A charge failed when the request ended. This request was recorded by an older version, which did not note where that charge went, so no sweep will clear this; compare the attempt totals above with the task's budget spending to see whether it was charged." A view whose index scan was cut (`scanCut`, see the next point) and found nothing of the request's own reads "A charge failed when the request ended. More charges are open than this view reads, so whether this request still has some of its own to make is not known." when marked, and adds "More charges are open than this view reads, so a charge this request is still making on an attempt not listed above may not be shown." when not (each sentence tested exactly).
- **Index scan rule.** Every read of the open index (`stop-charge-open`) pages by 100 and stops after `RETRY_PAGES` (20) pages; a scan is complete when it ends on a short page, or when every page was full and a read of one more entry after the last (`#nothingAfter`) finds none (so an index of exactly 2000 entries is read as complete, not cut). Nothing is concluded from the absence of an entry in an incomplete scan: `#payOwed` keeps the mark (a later sweep looks again) and `cleanupSpend` reports `scanCut` instead of mark only. `#retryCharges` pays only the first 2000 entries, then reads the rest of the index (read only, no paying, no page cap) and puts every request listed there in `pastCut`: such a request's mark is not cleared by this sweep, but a paid entry in the window that lists it is still taken off (only `stuck`, a request with an unpaid entry in the window, an unfinished one or one that still owes, holds an entry back). That is safe because the entry past the cut keeps listing the request, so its mark is cleared only once that entry is paid, and nothing is charged twice (taking an entry off leaves the attempt's running total). Sixteenth review: holding the window's paid entries back for a request listed past the cut (the earlier rule) wedged the window: when the first 2000 entries all listed such a request, every sweep re-read the same 2000 entries and the entries past the cut were never paid (probe: one request on 2100 entries charged 1999 on every backend). Entries past the first 2000 are paid once the entries before them are dropped, which now happens for every paid entry whose requests are cleared or listed past the cut. `#nothingAfter` is pinned by a test of 2000 settled entries and ONE more listing a marked, ended request with a failing pending note: the view reads cut (`[unpaid, markOnly, markKept, scanCut]` = `[true, false, false, true]`), a sweep keeps the mark, and a sweep once charges work pays the entry and clears it (the mutants `limit: 2 ... <= 1`, `return after !== undefined` and an always-true return each fail it on all four backends).
- **Known limit / follow-up card (window starvation by unfinished requests, sixteenth review).** Condition: the first 2000 open entries by attempt ID all list a request that has not finished (for example a Stop blocked waiting for the owner). Such a request goes in `stuck` (`#retryCharges`, the `TERMINAL` check in the clear loop), and the drop loop keeps every entry that lists a stuck request, even a settled, fully paid one with no pending note and no unmet `want`. No entry in the window is dropped, so the window never moves and the entries past it are never paid while those requests stay unfinished (probe D: 2000 settled entries listing a `blocked` request, then entry `zzz` with an unpaid 7 for another request R: after 4 sweeps `zzz` was charged 0). Impact: charges past the window are delayed, not lost or doubled: cleanup spend is not charged to the task budget (and those requests keep their marks) for as long as the window's requests stay unfinished, which for a blocked Stop is until the owner acts. Candidate fixes for the follow-up card: (a) a settled entry with no pending note and no unmet `want` whose only reason to stay is an unfinished request does not count toward the 2000-entry window (the scan reads past it to fill the window with entries that need paying), or (b) the rest-scan past the cut also pays entries that carry a pending note or an unmet `want` (still without clearing marks for requests listed past the cut). Do NOT take the shortcut of not treating unfinished requests as stuck (dropping their entries): that breaks the brute-force probe's `marked-not-indexed` case (brute22), because the entry is what lets a later sweep clear the mark a request writes when it finishes; without it the mark is stranded.
- **A request that waited on another request's note is indexed too.** When a request's cleanup finds an attempt's pending note written by another request and cannot pay it, the request is added to that attempt's open index (`#waitOn`), so the sweep clears its mark once the note is paid; before this its mark stayed for good. Tested with the sequence force (charges failing), stop, force.
- **A higher figure behind an unpaid note is charged (review fix, money).** When a request's ending reports a higher total for an attempt while an earlier pending note (its own, or another request's) cannot be paid, the figure used to be dropped and the sweep later cleared the mark, so the view said "paid" for money never charged. Now `#waitOn` also keeps `want` on the attempt's open entry (a running maximum of the figures reported meanwhile, with the request that raised it); `#retryCharges` pays the note, then charges the rest up to `want` (`#charge`), and clears the requests, and takes the entry off, only when that succeeded. A `want` stays on the entry until the attempt's charged total covers it. The same record is written when six races for the note are lost. The 20-request cap of an entry no longer drops a request that still needs the sweep (see the sixth review below). `cleanupSpend` finds the request's own pending note, and a `want` above what was charged on an attempt that lists the request, through the open index, so it is found on an attempt the request's record does not list and such a request reads "retried until it is", not mark only. Limit (not a fault of this slice): a figure a runtime reports while it has no charge port at all is not recorded anywhere and so is never charged later. The sequence test now ends at a fixed point and requires that the highest figure the runtime ever reported for each attempt is charged (and no more), no command ID reached the budget twice with another figure, nothing is pending or marked, the index lists only requests that have not finished, and one more sweep changes nothing. That is true because the test runtime always has its charge port; it says nothing about a runtime without one.
- **Sixth review (concurrency and storage faults).** (F1) A wait's command ID now carries a digest of the entry it writes (the figure included), so two passes that wait at the same revision with different figures are different commands and the loser re-reads, instead of the higher figure being answered as a replay of the lower. (F2) The sweep clears a request's mark only once the request has finished (a request still going has no outcome to clear, so it stays listed until it settles), counts a clear that failed as stuck, and drops an entry only when every request it lists was cleared and none is stuck, so a failed write or a sweep between the ending's charge and its settling no longer strands a mark with no entry. (F3) Past 20 requests an entry keeps every request that is unfinished, marked, the owner of the pending note or the one whose figure is wanted. (F4) The attempts a pass charged are recorded whatever phase the request has reached, so a pass that finishes after another pass settled the request still lists them. Two more faults the large concurrent run found: a pass that had just paid one note re-read the record, found another request's new note there and wrote its own note over it, so the other request's charge was made twice (an overcharge; now a pending note found after paying is paid first), and a note write that lost a race against the sweep dropping the entry failed the whole pass (`not_found` is now a lost race like `stale_revision`). Limits, stated plainly: a record written before `want` existed that lost a figure cannot be repaired (the view may say "paid" while that figure is uncharged); a figure reported while the runtime has no charge port at all is never recorded (the rule for a deployment is that a charge port is always configured); an entry for a request that stays blocked stays on the index until it finishes. (Seventh review.) A wait that loses six races in a row no longer returns with nothing recorded (see the ninth review: the retryable error the seventh review introduced did not hold when another pass finished the request). The ending update (`ended`, attempts) does not need the request to still be terminating.

- **Ninth review (a figure that no write could record).** When a request's own pass loses six races on an attempt's charge note AND six on its open entry, it used to throw and leave the figure nowhere; that was only safe if the same request's pass was the one to finish it, and a second pass of the same request could settle it first (an undercharge, with the view saying nothing was unpaid). Now `#charge` calls `#wait`, which tries the open entry and, when that keeps changing, writes the figure on the request's OWN record as `owed` (per attempt the highest figure in each dimension; a record only that request's passes write, so charge traffic cannot starve it; older records have none). The list holds at most the inventory limit (100) of attempts and is never cut: a figure for one more attempt is refused with the retryable `stale_revision`, so the pass is left unfinished and retried, and no older figure is dropped. The pass reports the charge as failed and goes on (it no longer throws); a Stop's ending then carries the "not charged" mark as before. The sweep calls `#payOwed` for every request that owes something (finished or not) and for every finished request this build marked (it carries `ended`, written before the mark), owed or not. `#payOwed` charges each owed figure through the ordinary `#charge` (same derived command ID, so a replay or two sweeps at once never pay twice), takes an entry off only after it is charged and only if no higher figure was added meanwhile, and once nothing is owed takes the mark off a finished request that no open entry lists. So a mark whose clearing failed after the last owed figure was taken off, or one a request settled with after a sweep had already paid what it owed, is cleared by a later sweep. `#retryCharges` never clears a request that still owes a figure: the request stays listed (its entry is not dropped) and keeps its mark until `#payOwed` has charged what it owes. A marked record written by an older build (no `ended`) and listed on no entry keeps its mark: nothing says where its figure went. `cleanupSpend` counts `owed` as the request's own unpaid charging (`markOnly` false). **ASSUMPTION / limit:** a record that cannot be written either (six lost races on the request's own record, which needs six other writes in a row by passes of that same request) still ends the pass with the retryable `stale_revision`, and so does a figure refused by the owed limit; nothing is lost then only if the request is still live for the sweep, which is the case for a pass that nobody else finishes. Limit kept from main: `#charge` takes only the first 100 figures of one report (`costs.slice(0, 100)`), so a runtime that reports more attempts in one cleanup or ending has the rest ignored. The call tree is: `#waitOn` is called only from `#wait`, `#wait` only from `#charge`; `#charge`'s callers are a request's own pass (`advance`, preparation or ending) and the sweep (`#payOwed`, and `#retryCharges` for a wanted figure, where a failure keeps that entry for the next sweep and the other entries go on).
- **Older records.** `afterPreparation`, `reusedFrom` and `ended` are new. A stored request without them degrades without a false statement: a Force Stop carrying a limit, a spent figure or a checkpoint counts as after a preparation (a pure Force Stop is created with none); no `reusedFrom` reads as "not a reused checkpoint" (the Stop's own preparation figure is then shown, which is what it had); no `ended` reads as "ending not recorded", and the view still treats a done stop or force stop as ended.
- **Unpaid is the request's own.** A pending note belongs to the request that wrote it (`pending.intentId`); another request's further charge on the same attempt shows on that attempt's line ("a further charge is still being made") but does not make this request unpaid. The mark-only sentence says "this request has nothing left to charge".
- **A wait keeps the preparation's figure unless the preparation was blocked.** `choose(wait)` zeroes `spent` only when the block was in preparation; after a failed ending (blocked in `terminating`) the figure stays, because the window that produced it is over.
- **Older records (more).** A Force Stop also counts as after a preparation when its history shows a preparing or prepared step; a request settled as "unresolved work remains" is known to have run its ending even without `ended`. Where nothing says whether the ending ran, a Force Stop line says "no ending of the work is recorded", and an empty attempt list says "No attempt with a charged cleanup cost is recorded on this request."
- **Force Stop tail.** A Force Stop sentence ends "what ending the work cost is charged to the attempts below" only when the ending ran; "what ending the work costs, when it runs, is charged ..." while it is going (its terminate may have failed and the request be blocked); "no ending of the work is recorded" when it did not (restart from an earlier boundary, a resume, an older record).
- **Scope read (review fix).** The view reads the `stop-active` pointer of exactly the scope named, and a Suspend or Stop is recorded only for the scope that was requested. A task stopped through its agent, team or the installation therefore answers "No Suspend or Stop was requested for task X itself; one made through a wider scope ... is read by naming that scope"; looking up the enclosing scopes the caller may control is left for a later slice. More than 20 attempts say how many are not listed. *(Superseded by L02e below: the view reads those enclosing scopes itself and says which one the figures come from.)*
- **Authority (review fix).** `cleanupSpend` calls `authorizeControl` first: an asker who may not control the scope, or a task that does not exist, is refused (`forbidden`/`not_found`, shown as missing by the status view), never told "not stopped". Tested with the real `StopService` and through `status.ask` with an agent holding no grants.
- **Attempts (review fix).** The attempts an ending charged (a Force Stop, or a Stop that reused a finished Suspend's checkpoint, which now also carries the Suspend's list) are merged into the request's `attempts`, so the view lists them; the cost attempts of the preparation are merged the same way (`costAttempts`), also when the runtime does not list them.
- **Not done (L02d stays planned; follow-up split).** (1) A real sandbox backend's `SandboxSession.work()` that lists a confinement's processes (needs the OS; the worker host contract and Stop end are done). (2) Children under agent, team and installation scopes (their swarm descendants are not walked; `swarm.cancel` remains). Part 2's item "pausing swarm children during a stop" is settled, not open: the review fix there holds a stopped parent's children back through `heldBy`/`StopService.holding` without writing gates on them. (3) A real job host's `confirmCancel` for background jobs. (4) A per-request cumulative cleanup total (the view shows the budget-window figure and per-attempt totals). (5) A task's view of a Stop made through its agent, team or the installation. (6) Chat resolving an agent's or team's name for the scope form (the ID has to be given).

## L02e (first slice): a Stop of an agent, team or the installation walks the swarm below it, the charge window is not starved, and the cleanup view says which scope the answer came through (2026-11-09)

- **What remained** (this card splits seven leftovers from L02d; its Acceptance names three checks, so those three are done here and the rest are named as follow-up). Each was reproduced first with a test on this branch:
  (1) **Scope.** `lifecycle/dispatch-ports.ts` resolved a stop's scope to the live attempts of the scope itself and, for a task only, of that task's swarm children (`more.descendants(taskId)`, wired in `api/start.ts` from `swarmDescendantsInfo`). Nothing walked `swarm-link` for an agent, a team or the installation, although the file's own comment says "an attempt on a swarm child is not found by listing the parent's assignments". A Stop of an agent left every descendant task's attempts and jobs untouched while the request went `done` and the owner was told the scope was stopped.
  (2) **Sweep window.** `StopService.#retryCharges` reads `RETRY_PAGES` (20) x 100 open entries a sweep and the rest wait; an entry is taken off only when every request listed on it is cleared, and clearing needed a *terminal* phase. An entry keeps the note of every request that ever waited on it, so requests that never finish (a Suspend or Stop that blocks on an uncooperative process, or whose scope was asked again) leave settled entries on the index for ever: 2000 of them fill every window and the first real unpaid charge behind them is never reached, only read past.
  (3) **The owner's read.** `cleanupSpend` and `status.stopCleanupLines` read `stop-active` for exactly the named scope, so a task stopped through its agent answered "No Suspend or Stop was requested for task X itself; one made through a wider scope ... is read by naming that scope". L02d part 3 wrote that lookup down as left for a later slice.
- **The walk** (`lifecycle/dispatch-ports.ts`, `lifecycle/index.ts`, `api/start.ts`): `swarmDescendantsInfo` is split into `childIndexOf` (the `swarm-link` index, read once) and `tasksBelow` (deepest first, each task once, a cycle cannot loop, at most `max`), and `swarmDescendantsOf(storage, taskIds, max = 200)` walks the children of several roots together, deduplicated. `dispatchStopPorts` gains the optional `descendantsOf` hook (without it each root is walked on its own and the results merged, so a runtime offering only the single-task hook still walks) and one `resolveScope(scope)` per port call: `own` the tasks the scope's own live attempts run (a task is itself; an agent's, a team's or the installation's tasks are known only from what runs for them), `kids` the tasks below them, `truncated` when the walk was cut, and `attempts` the live attempts of both. `attemptsOf`, `jobsFor`, `inFlight`, `askJobs` and `controllable` all go through it, so a child's attempt is listed and quiesced, its jobs are asked (a refusal keeps it, as the scope's own do), its processes are listed so Force Stop reaches them, an ending dropped for one of its attempts is carried on by the request that covers it, and `controllable` keeps saying "not everything is stopped" while a child is left out. A child the asker may not control (`more.mayControl`, the rule `swarm.cancel` uses) is not asked, not ended and not named; a cut walk is the existing `child` unknown item. A task's own Stop behaves as before, and the link index is still read once per port call.
- **The window** (`lifecycle/stop.ts` `#retryCharges`): an entry is held only by requests that may still need it. A listed request whose record cannot be read, that still owes a figure of its own, or that the sweep could not pay stays in `stuck` and holds the entry; one that has merely not finished has no debt on a settled entry and goes to `live` instead, so the entry is taken off like one that lists nothing (its own note, when it finally writes one, puts the entry back). The charge record, its audit and the budget ledger stay; only the open index changes.
- **The read** (`lifecycle/pause.ts`, `lifecycle/stop.ts`, `status/status.ts`, `api/operations.ts`): `PauseService.chain(scope)` is exposed as a read (only the private `#chain` and `guard()`, which lists *paused* gates, existed) because the stop must ask what covers a scope, not what is paused now. `cleanupSpend`, when the named scope has no request of its own, answers from a new `#coveringRequest`: the covering scopes nearest first - a task's assignee agent and the teams above it, its swarm parents (up to `PAUSE_LIMITS.chain` links; a cycle or a missing link ends the walk), and the whole installation last because it covers everything and explains least - newest `requestedAt` wins, ties keep the nearest. The answer carries `through: { kind, id }` and `requestedAt`, and its `spent`, `spendBudget` and `attempts` are that request's for its whole scope. A request on a covering scope the asker may not control (`authorizeControl` refusing `forbidden` or `not_found`) is skipped, so they are told nothing, exactly as if it did not exist. `status.stopCleanupLines` says so first ("Nothing was asked for task X itself: this is the stop of agent agt-y, asked <when>, which reaches it. Every figure is that scope's, not task X alone.") and names the wider scope in every sentence after; the attempt, unpaid and scan-cut lines are unchanged. The scope it came through goes through `shown()` like every other borrowed name. `STATUS_KINDS.stop_cleanup` and the `status.ask` summary changed, so `npm run api:docs:write` regenerated `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md`.
- **Chat**: nothing new. No operation, no phrase, no registry change; `stop_cleanup` was already reachable from free-form chat by task title, and the interpreter's line for it is generated from `STATUS_KINDS`.
- **Tests.** `lifecycle/dispatch-ports.test.ts` (+2 tests, 20 in the file; unit tests over a fake dispatcher, as the file was): an agent's Stop lists and ends a child's attempt, asks a child's job, leaves a child the asker may not control (`controllable` false, nothing quiesced or terminated), Force Stop kills what a child holds, a cut walk is said as an unknown item, and the walk is asked for once per port call, for the tasks the agent runs; a team's and the installation's Stop walk the children of every task they cover, the links read once for the lot. `lifecycle/stop-suite.ts` (+3 suites, run on all four backends by `stop*.test.ts`): one sweep takes all 2000 settled entries that list nothing but a blocked Stop off the index, leaving only the entry with a charge still to be made, and the next sweep pays that charge (30) and clears that request's mark while the blocked Stop is left as it was; a task stopped through its agent is answered from that request (`through` the agent, its figure and attempts) and the manager who may control the task but not the agent is told nothing, and the task's own request then wins; the installation's stop answers for a task and for an agent, a later team's stop takes over for the task, and a later swarm parent's stop answers for the child. `status/status.test.ts` (every backend): the exact lines and cites of an answer that came through an agent, and a `through` id carrying an ANSI CSI shown as `\u001b`; the "nothing requested for this scope" sentence reworded, since a wider request is now found rather than asked for. `lifecycle/stop-sequences.test.ts`: the seeded invariants now compare `through` with the request's own recorded scope (`through-mismatch`, `through-not-told`) and read the sentence about the request after the explanation.
- **Mutation checks** (each restored exactly and rebuilt): `resolveScope` not walking for a non-task scope (both new dispatch-ports tests fail); `cleanupSpend` not consulting a covering scope (both new read suites fail); the status view not saying where the answer came from (`through-not-told` in the seeded sequences, and the cleanup-view suite on all four backends fail).
- **Counts** (this worktree, `NIMBLENEWT_TIER` unset, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, all four backends): lifecycle 715 (711 pass, 4 todo - the C07k hand-off TODOs), chat 997, api 373, status 171, none failed; `dist/dispatch` plus `dist/domain` 1365 (1351 pass, 14 todo) for the `PauseService` change; `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6; `npm run roadmap:check` and `npm run check:deps` ok; `npx tsc --build --force` clean.
- ASSUMPTION: an agent's, a team's or the installation's Stop walks the swarm children of every task it covers, not only the tasks listed for those agents; the card asks for a wider walk and nothing narrower was chosen. Authority is still checked once, for the scope the Stop was made for; per child only `mayControl` (the rule `swarm.cancel` uses) applies.
- ASSUMPTION: unknowns from the walk go through the request's existing channels - `inventory` items, `unresolved`, the retryable `unavailable` refusal while a child cannot be reached, and the `child` unknown item when the walk was cut. No new `StopIntentBody` field, so the cleanup view needed no new sentence for the walk.
- ASSUMPTION: a settled charge entry is dropped from the open index even while a request it lists never finished. The charge record, its audit and the ledger entry stay; nothing claims the dropped note was charged, because the `Charge` the budget holds is the amount taken.

(b) The covering read answered with any older wider request: a task created after the installation was stopped and resumed, or given to an agent after that agent's Stop, was told that Stop "reaches it". A covering request made before the asked scope's record was created, or (for an agent or team) before the task's current assignment generation began, is skipped. Checked and left: removing an entry while a listed request is live (drop is revision-checked; the request's later note or wait re-creates the entry; its "not charged" mark is cleared by `sweep` through `#payOwed` once no entry lists it, since the mark is written only after `ended`); walk bounds (40 x 500 links read, 200 descendants, cycles); a child also stopped through its own task is reached only through its live attempts, and a second stop of one joins the end already under way (`dispatcher.stop`). Left as known limits: a wider scope's tasks are those with a live attempt, so a child of an agent's task that has no live attempt right now is held from restart by (a) but not ended; the inventory and `unresolved` still name child attempts, jobs and task IDs the asker may not control (as the task-scope walk of L02d did); the covering read follows the task's current assignee only.

So once the scope was resumed and later merely paused, the finished Force Stop held the swarm children again - for a task (L02d) and, through the wider look, every child of an agent's or team's tasks, under another agent too. `force` now records the gate's request ID like `request` does (older Force Stop records keep the old reading). Checked and left: a resume or cancel lets a wider hold go (the gate must still be paused by the request's own pause); Suspend, Stop and Force Stop hold alike, as for a task's own; `mayHold` is still asked per child for the requester; the hold follows the parent's current assignee and is bounded by the pause chain (no scans); the covering read's times are the runner's one clock (`createdAt` and `requestedAt`), a tie counts as reached, and a reassignment back to the same agent starts a new generation, so an older stop of that agent is not its answer; `swarm.cancel` keeps the own-task look.

## L04c (third part): commit last, hold for the owner, host ports and capture operations (2026-11-07)

**Built**
- **Commit comes last (open item finding 3).** The dispatcher's `#resumeCheck` no longer commits. A ready check with nothing judged to matter is handed back as a pending commit; `#advance` commits it after the place and the allowance are held and before the checkout pin and the start. An attempt that waits for the checkout, a place or an allowance records no resume. A commit that fails or does not reach `done` is a skip with check `resume` (not a failure) and the place is given back; the commit's command ID is the check's key, so a crash and retry (or a commit made just before a crash) records one resume.
- **Changes judged to matter hold the attempt (finding 4).** A ready check with any verdict `relevant: true` is not committed by the dispatcher. The tick reports a skip (`resume`) naming the check and the changes, and the owner gets one `needs-you` notification (command ID from the check, so every tick answers the same one) naming the task and up to three changes.
- **`resume.approve` (owner only; `taskId`).** Commits the task's current check when it is ready; a done check answers as it is; none or not ready is refused with where it stands. `ResumeCheckService.commit` now refuses a non-owner when any verdict is relevant, so neither the dispatcher, a host nor the agent being resumed can bypass the hold with `resume.commit`.
- **`resume.decline` (owner only; `taskId`).** The owner's "no": the task is released FIRST (while the held attempt is still its active one; its waiting attempt ends and nothing works on it until it is assigned again), THEN the check is cancelled (history note "declined by the owner") and the notice that it is held is closed at once. Release first because the dispatcher takes any cancelled check of its own key as a reason to start the next one: with the old order (cancel, then release) a tick in the gap, or after a crash in it, started a new check and, when nothing was judged to matter, committed it and started the attempt the owner had declined. Once the attempt has ended, `commit`/`approve` refuse the check (attempt guard) and the dispatcher no longer looks at the attempt (generation check), and a crash before decline's own cancel leaves the check to the dispatcher's drop of the ended attempt (`attempt-ended`). After the release, decline re-reads the assignment: if the task moved meanwhile (nothing released) it is refused (`invalid_transition`) and nothing is cancelled. A cancel that finds the check already moved after a successful release (dropped by the dispatcher, or committed by an approval just before the release) is not an error: the release stands and the attempt never runs. A check an approval committed but whose resume is not yet recorded is carried on by the decline (before its checks and again after its cancel): its record is refused now that the attempt has ended, so it ends cancelled (`attempt-ended`) and the decline answers that, never `executing`. Declining again finishes an interrupted decline: when the check's attempt was ended by a release and the task is still released, the check (ready, or already cancelled by the drop) is cancelled if still live and the notice closed. Refused with where it stands: none (`not_found`); a check not tied to an attempt (`invalid_command`, "cancel it with resume.cancel or release the task"); a done/executing check ("already approved"), a check in another phase (for example one the owner cancelled), or a ready check with nothing judged to matter (`invalid_command`); a check whose attempt was transferred, given another attempt, or released and assigned again (`invalid_transition`, "nothing to release; the task is left as it is"). Each completed decline writes a `resume-decline` record keyed by its scoped command ID (the check and attempt it declined): the same command ID again answers with that check, even after the task was assigned again and has a newer held check, which is left alone. Belt and braces in the dispatcher: a check of this attempt's keys whose history carries the declined note is never followed by a new key (the tick waits: "the owner declined this resume; the task is being released"), so a record left by the old order cannot start the work either. The release is the controller's (`ResumeCheckDeps.release`, wired in `startController`); without it a dispatcher's check is refused as `unavailable` before anything is written.
- **Approve and a release never both win.** The commit's write to `executing` carries a revision check of the check's attempt (read active), and so does the write that records the continuation resume (`ContinuationService.resume` takes a `guard` whose changes it writes with the record; a lost race asks the guard again, which refuses once the attempt has ended). Every way an attempt ends is written with the assignment, so a release (a decline's or any other) that lands anywhere inside an approval or the dispatcher's commit either refuses the commit (nothing written; `approve` says "not approved: the attempt ... is no longer the task's active attempt") or refuses the record (the check ends `cancelled` with `attempt-ended`; nothing recorded; `approve` says the same). A record already made answers as made after a crash. An approval that finds the check cancelled meanwhile says so ("the resume was declined meanwhile (the task is released)", or "cancelled meanwhile"), never that the inputs changed.
- **Chat.** `resume.approve` and `resume.decline` are in `CHAT_OPS` (mode `propose`: shown first, applied on the owner's word). The interpreter prompt lists chat ops from `CHAT_OPS` with their argument names and verbs (`model-interpreter.ts` `OPERATION_LINES`), so it describes both, including that declining releases the task; the owner names the task (`taskId` or `taskTitle`), never a check ID, and no fixed phrase. The dispatcher's skip reason, the notice and the needs-you line all say "approve, or decline (which releases the task)". The notice and the needs-you line name the task by its quoted title (`held()` returns it), never by its ID, as the other needs-you lines do.
- **A held check never outlives its attempt.** A dispatcher's check records the attempt it is for (`ResumeCheckBody.attemptId`, kept out of the start payload so a check started before this change answers its own command again instead of conflicting). It stands only while that attempt is active (every way an attempt stops being the task's active one ends it in the same write): `held()` does not list it otherwise, `commit()` and `approve()` refuse it (`invalid_transition`, "no longer the task's active attempt (released, transferred or given another attempt)"; nothing is recorded), and when the dispatcher ends an attempt that has a checkpoint to resume from (superseded, released, transferred, expired) it cancels that attempt's own live check (reason `attempt-ended`; a newer attempt's check is left alone) and closes its notice, also for a check approved but not yet seen by a tick. The guards hold without a running dispatcher; the cancel and notice close need it, or come from `approve`/`decline`, which close the notice at once (`ResumeCheckDeps.settle`).
- **Host ports.** `StartOptions.resume` (`observe`, `review`, `missingContext`, `uncertainEffects`) is passed to `controllerResumePorts`. A host that watches dependencies supplies `observe`; a reviewer agent supplies `review`. Without them behaviour is as before (unknown observations; every change treated as relevant, so the owner decides).
- **Continuation capture for hosts.** New operations `continuation.capture` (command; host, service, owner, or an agent for its own run; an agent's durability claim is stored as not verified, so the capture is incomplete) and `continuation.latest` (query). API contract doc regenerated.
- **Sweep at start-up:** already present (`resumes.sweep` is a dispatcher loop, run on every tick including the first); not changed.

**Tests** (new): `dispatch/resume-hold.test.ts` (5 x 4 backends: commit last while the checkout is busy, failed commit retried with one command ID, crash after commit, hold + notification once + bypass refused + owner approve + repeat, approve refusals); `api/start-resume-ports.test.ts` (capture/latest through the API, host ports reach the check, hold vs no hold); `chat/resume-approve-chat.test.ts` (4 backends). Mutation-checked: commit not run, hold removed, commit guard removed, approve owner check removed, approve-when-done removed, chat op removed, ports not passed: each fails a test.

ASSUMPTION: a resume check with any change judged relevant needs the owner (default with no reviewer connected: every change is relevant, so a resume that follows a changed dependency waits for `resume.approve` until a reviewer is connected). Chosen as the most reversible reading of "never passed off as a judgement".
ASSUMPTION: the owner is told by a `needs-you` maintenance notification, not a blocker, because no operation exists to resolve a dispatcher blocker and a blocker left open after approval would be untrue.
ASSUMPTION: `resume.approve` is a chat proposal (shown first) in every profile.
ASSUMPTION: only the owner may commit a check that holds relevant verdicts (host, service and agent are refused), including `resume.commit`.
ASSUMPTION: declining a held resume releases the task. A bare cancel would be started again by the dispatcher on its next tick and held again with a new notice (and after RESUME_RESTARTS such cancels the owner gets a blocker), so "decline" would not mean anything; releasing is the smallest reversible step (assign the task again to try again, with a new check) and is what the needs-you line already offered. `resume.decline` is a chat proposal (shown first) like approve.
ASSUMPTION: a check started before checks recorded their attempt (no `attemptId`) is treated as standing for the task, as before; the dispatcher does not cancel it on an attempt's end (a new attempt's check still cancels it as stale).
ASSUMPTION: `resume.decline` refuses a check with no `attemptId` (started through `resume.start`, or by a dispatcher before checks recorded their attempt) instead of guessing which attempt to release: declining it would only cancel it, and the dispatcher would start a new check on its next tick and hold it again, while the owner was told the task was released. The owner cancels it (`resume.cancel`) or releases the task. Chosen as the smallest, most reversible choice (no release of an attempt the check does not name).
ASSUMPTION: a decline whose check's attempt was released and whose task is still released counts as done (an interrupted decline, or a release made some other way): the owner's "do not go on; release it" holds, so it is finished and answered, not refused.
ASSUMPTION: a retried decline command is answered from its own record (the check it declined), never re-read through the task's current check, so a stale retry cannot decline or release a newer attempt.

**Not done (L04c stays planned)**
- No real worker-side dependency observer and no real reviewer agent exist in the controller: only the ports (`StartOptions.resume`) are wired and tested with fakes. Someone must supply a host-side observation of files and a reviewer agent that gives reasoned verdicts.
- Hosts do not yet call `continuation.capture` (no host process captures checkpoints); the operation is ready for them.
- Chat cannot retry a blocked check; what a held check changed is read through the needs-you list (up to three changes named) or `resume.get`.
- The per-tick prerequisite cache (finding 7 remainder) is still open.
- A decline's record is written last: a crash after the cancel and before the record leaves no record, so that command ID retried answers through the ordinary path (check cancelled as declined, task released: answered as done); only after the task is assigned again would such a retry be refused (`invalid_transition`) rather than answered as before.

### L04c (third part) review fixes (2026-11-07)

- **One resume whoever carries the check on (bug).** `continuation.resume` scopes its command ID by the caller, and the executing step called it as whoever advanced the check: an owner's approval that failed after the resume was recorded, finished by the dispatcher's sweep, recorded two resumes (shown with the real `ContinuationService`; also reachable without a crash when the sweep ran during an approval). The resume is now recorded by one internal principal (`service:resume-check`); who committed stays in the check's history. Test: `continuation/resume-recorded-once.test.ts` (4 backends).
- **Hold judged on what is written.** `commit` refused a non-owner on the check it read, then wrote `executing` on whatever was stored; a check started over and reviewed again in between (relevant verdicts now) could be committed by the dispatcher. - **Approve tells the truth.** An approval during which the inputs changed again started the check over and answered "applied" with a ready check; it is now refused (`invalid_transition`, "not approved ... approve again"). A check left `executing` by a crash is finished by approving again (it was refused as "not ready").

## H12k (part 5): the MCP transport to the checked address, and the end-to-end test through startController (2026-11-08)

- **What remained** (against the acceptance text "an end-to-end test starts a controller, runs an attempt through the real relay, guards and bridge, quiesces it around an integration, and connects to a remote MCP server only at a checked public address"): no MCP transport existed (the connector handed a checked target to a callback nobody supplied), the host builder was not given the MCP connector, and no test ran the real worker process, the real tool bridge and a quiesced integration together through `startController`.
- **Transport** (`controller/src/mcp/http-client.ts`): `RemoteMcpClient` over `RemoteMcpConnector` speaks streamable HTTP (one JSON-RPC message per POST; JSON or event-stream answers). Every socket goes to `target.address` (the checked one); the name is only the TLS server name (the certificate is checked against it, system CAs unless `ca` is given) and the Host header. One call is one session: `initialize` at the server's pinned revision (another revision is refused before anything is called), `notifications/initialized`, the request, then `DELETE` of the session if the server gave one. A redirect is refused (never followed), an answer is bounded (`maxBytes`, default 4 MiB) and timed (`timeoutMs`, default 30 s), a JSON-RPC error is passed on marked as the server's words with credentials redacted, and the caller cannot set the transport's own headers (Host, content type, session, protocol). `callTool`, `listTools` (first page only) and `request`. `RemoteTarget` now carries `path` and `protocolRevision` (`McpService.remoteEndpoint` returns the pinned revision).
- **Composition** (`api/dispatch-compose.ts`): the MCP service, connector and client are built before the local host; `dispatch.mcp.transport` takes the transport settings; `DispatchHandle.mcp.client` is new; `local.build` receives `services.mcp: { connector, client }` (the same objects as the handle's). `controller/testing` exports `selfSigned`.
- **Tests.** `mcp/http-client.test.ts` (3): the stock SDK server (stateful, event-stream and JSON answers) over TLS reached at the checked public address with the name's certificate, session id and pinned revision carried, session ended; untrusted CA refused; internal address never dialed; redirect, other revision, oversized answer, certificate for another name refused; server error text framed and redacted; own headers protected. `integration/h12k-composed-host.test.ts` (1, real bubblewrap, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` fails instead of skipping): `startController` composes the host from the services it hands `build` (relay through `attemptRelay`, `guards`, `context`, `ownerPolicyOptions`), the checkout comes from `LocalWorkspaces`, every tool request goes through the controller's `ToolExecutionService`; the provider key is added by the relay, the first call is admitted, a desk record written through the bridge returns to the agent, an urgent owner message is delivered; `workspace.request` integration runs with the attempt frozen and nothing in flight, a tool request arriving meanwhile is refused as frozen, the work reaches the shared tree with no commit, the agent is told and released and finishes; then the controller's MCP client reaches a TLS MCP server only at the checked address, a rebinding name and an internal one are refused with nothing dialed, a revoked server gets no connection. 8 + 6 consecutive runs green.
- **Mutation checks** (each restored exactly, rebuilt): dialing the name instead of the checked address (unit 3/3 and e2e fail); `rejectUnauthorized: false` (unit 3/3 fail); redirect check removed, revision check removed, size bound removed (unit test 3 fails each); session header dropped (unit tests 1-2 fail); `services.mcp` not passed to `build` (e2e fails); the quiesce not freezing (e2e fails); the bridge ignoring a freeze (e2e fails). Equivalent mutant noted: TLS `host` set to the address while `servername` stays the name (Node checks the server name first).

- **What remained** (part 3's list, against the deliverable "repository, file, service-health and timer sources chosen in settings, the owner chat command; a real model-availability source" and the acceptance "events from a real source wake the right agent"): no real probes for repositories, files or service health; nothing configured a timer; no model-availability source in the running controller; no chat view of the setting; no way to add a source without a restart.
- **Defined sources** (`events/defined-sources.ts`): the owner defines a `timer` (`everyMinutes`, counted from the definition, or once `at` a time not already past), a `file` or folder (`path`, absolute), a git `repository` (`path`) or a `service` health address (`url`, http(s), no user name or password), reporting into the project's stream or, with `taskId`, a task's of that project. Real probes: a folder is walked (symbolic links not followed, `.git` and `node_modules` skipped, at most 1000 files; version = size and modification time in ns, never content); a repository's branches and tags are read from its files (working copy, linked worktree through `commondir`, bare; packed refs with loose ones overriding; no git program is run; at most 1000); a health address gets one GET (10 s limit, redirects not followed, body not read; 2xx/3xx healthy). File, repository and service sources are looked at every `checkSeconds` (default 60, 10 to 86400) unless the last look had more to report. A repeating timer fires once for the latest slot after a pause, not once per missed slot. The saved state carries a digest of the definition, so a source redefined under the same ID (another path) starts from a baseline. A state over 200 kB is refused with a reason (one record has a size limit).
- **Setting and API** (`events/source-settings.ts`, owner only): `events.sources.define` (replaces a defined source of the same ID; may not take a host source's ID; the project and task are checked; at most 50), `events.sources.remove` (also clears it from the off-list; a host or built-in source cannot be removed, only turned off). `events.sources.get` lists defined sources with `defined`, `watches` (one line) and `definition`; `set`/`change` validate turning off against host and defined sources as the setting stands inside the command.
- **No restart.** `sourceLoops` takes a function read at every tick; `startController` gives it the host's list plus the defined sources. When the read fails, the last list read is polled (the same fail-open-on-last-good rule as the off-list); with none, the tick fails.
- **Model availability** (`api/default-sources.ts`, built in as `models`, not critical): reads the router's own health records (`CutoverService.healthStates`, accounts, endpoints and models) and reports `model.unavailable` once per outage and `model.available` on return on every active (not archived) project's stream; a route that never failed is not reported. Each project keeps its own position, so a poll cut at the limit tells the rest next time. At most 1500 project-and-route pairs (otherwise the source fails with that reason).
- **Chat.** Ops `events.sources.define` and `events.sources.remove` (both shown first in every profile, like turning sources on and off); the project comes from the focus, the task by its title. The `path` or `url` must be in the owner's message exactly (case included); `type`, `sourceId` and `at` are exempt from the own-words check (a fixed choice, a name the assistant may choose, a time worked out from words; all shown first). `watch.create` gains `watchProject` (the focused project's stream) so a project-wide source can be watched by words. Status kind `event_sources` (owner only) lists each source, on or off, built-in or defined, and what a defined one watches. The interpreter prompt says how to have something watched and woken on.

- **Mutation checks** (16, each restored exactly and rebuilt; each fails a named test): the exact-case path check in chat; the source list read at every tick; the `checkSeconds` throttle; `more` bypassing it; the definition digest (redefinition re-baselines); the latest timer slot; 5xx counted healthy (fails the unit and the composed test); `.git`/`node_modules` skipped; credentials in an address refused; the model source telling every project; `startController` adding the defined sources; the task-in-project check; a host source's ID refused; remove clearing the off-list; turning off a defined source; the `event_sources` status view. ### H13f Windows fix (exhaustive run 42469337913, Windows Node 24)

- **Paths read the same on every platform.** A watched path is kept exactly as the owner wrote it (it was `path.normalize`d, which on Windows rewrote `/srv/data/in` to `\srv\data\in`, so the setting no longer matched the owner's words or what was shown back). It must be absolute by the controller machine's own path rules (`checkDefinition` takes the path module, default node:path): on Windows `C:\data`, `C:/data`, `\\server\share` and a root-relative `/data`; on POSIX a Windows drive path is refused when defined instead of being watched as missing for ever. Filesystem access still uses the platform path.
- **Names inside a watched folder use `/`** (`insideName`), so event text and saved state do not depend on the platform (`sub\b.txt` leaked before). Ref names already used `/`.
- **Repository source.** The `.git` pointer of a linked worktree is parsed by `gitDirFromPointer`: first line only (CRLF), `gitdir:` resolved against the working copy with the platform's resolve (git on Windows writes `C:/...` or a relative path); `commondir` likewise takes its first line. `readSmall` now looks at the file with `lstat` before opening it on every platform: Windows has no `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_NONBLOCK` (both 0), so a link would otherwise be followed by the open; the handle is still checked as a regular file after the open, and on POSIX the flags close the gap.
- **Tests** (`events/defined-sources.test.ts`, now 8): path rules and kept-as-written for both `path.win32` and `path.posix` on every machine; `insideName` and `gitDirFromPointer` with both syntaxes; `readSmall` opened with plain read-only flags (what Windows has) refuses a link, a directory and an oversized file; `packed-refs` as a directory is refused on every platform. Symbolic links that Windows refuses to create without the privilege (EPERM/EACCES, win32 only) leave out only the link checks, with a diagnostic; any other error fails. The pipe and `/dev/zero` checks stay POSIX-only, after the parts that run everywhere.
- **Mutation checks** (each restored, each fails the file): the machine's path rules replaced by POSIX's; normalizing instead of keeping as written; names without `/`; the whole pointer file instead of its first line; the look before the open removed; the pointer resolved by node:path instead of the given rules. - **Other hazards checked:** the chat's own-words check compares the path exactly as typed, which with the path now stored as written also holds for backslash paths; `start-defined-sources.test.ts` builds every path with `join` and expects only names without separators; no file modes or case-only names are used.

## R04c: model calls, probes and cancellation bound to drain and cutover (2026-11-08)

What the card asked and where it is now (dependencies R04, R04b and H12k are implemented):

- **The dispatcher's model calls go through the fallback service.** With the default route resolver (difficulty profiles), `startController` gives the dispatcher a `modelCalls` port (`api/route-calls.ts`, `routeCallsOf`). Every run of an attempt on a route is one call of `FallbackService`: (1) at every claim and advance the dispatcher asks the gate (`RouteGate.blocked`, reads only) for the configured route and then the further routes the configuration allows (`RouteChoice.alternatives`, the difficulty decision's other table-eligible candidates, in order) and uses the first one the owner's controls and the routes' health leave open; all closed is a visible wait (`skipped`, check `route`, "every route allowed for the task is closed to new work: ..."), never a blocker; (2) just before the worker starts it begins the call (`FallbackService.begin` with the new `routes: [route]`, judged once more by the table rules, the gate, a half-open trial claim and the task's model budget; `budgetWait` is asked first so a task waiting for a raise does not leave a call per tick); (3) once the worker is up it marks the call `sent`; (4) the end is reported once: a completed turn is `succeeded` with the money the attempt was charged since the call began, a failed attempt is `failed` with a neutral message (so a task, tool or worker failure is never taken for a provider outage), any other end (stop, lost worker, orderly shutdown, cutover) is `abandon`ed (a possible charge on a paid route), a call whose worker never started is `withdraw`n (new: skipped, no charge, not counted). An attempt's route can now change while it waits (`#beginCall` records the route the call is on); the record keeps `modelCall` and `modelCallSeq` (`dispatch/model.ts`). An attempt that parks for approvals ends its call and begins a new one when it goes on.
- **A drain or cutover changes where the next attempt goes and cancels the running one.** A drain or disable closes the target to new work at the next look; running work is left alone. A cutover abandons the running calls on the target (R04) and its listener (`cutoverListener`, bound in `composeDispatch`) cancels the task's current generation (`GenerationService.interrupt`, mode `cancel`, with the owner's authority since the owner ordered the cutover), ends the attempt (`DispatcherService.cutOver`: worker stopped, or the host told to let go when this process has no handle; a replacement is admitted within the attempts allowed and goes to the next open route), then lifts the generation hold it put on (only a hold with its own words; an owner's pause is left alone). Every step is idempotent; a failure leaves the cutover pending and the listener is called again. The relay of an attempt whose call was taken back refuses further model calls before they are sent, even if the worker has not been stopped yet. An attempt that was waiting (not started) when its call was cut needs nothing: its next advance begins a call on an open route.
- **Probes run on a timer.** The dispatcher's tick runs `routes.probe` (R04c part 1; still off unless the operator supplies `routeProbes` and turns it on) and now also `routes.tick` (`CutoverService.tick`): a drain past its deadline becomes a cutover and cancels what still runs; a cancellation a crash left pending is carried out again.
- **A role whose list is empty is refused at configuration.** The routing table already had the list rules; the cutover service now has them too (`CutoverService.withEpoch(..., {}, {})`), so a topology change that would put a whole list on one endpoint or account is refused as well. Tested through `ConfigurationService.bindRouting`, `RoutingService.setTable` and `CutoverService.setTopology` of a started controller.
- **Chat.** `routing.drain` (follows the approval profile, like `routing.disable`) and `routing.cutover` (shown first in every profile) are chat commands; with the existing `routing.disable`, `routing.reenable` and `routing.failback.set` every routing control is reachable by free-form chat. The interpreter's instructions say how to name the target and that a drain's `drainSeconds` must come from the owner (ask if missing). A new status kind `model_routes` (owner only) shows the controls in force, the failback policy and the targets that are down; with `level` and `name` it gives the three facts of the drain report.
- **Tests.** `api/start-route-calls.test.ts` (5, SQLite, about 10 s): the composed flow (a run is a sent call counted by the drain report; drain sends the next attempt elsewhere and leaves the running one; cutover ends the running attempt, stops its worker, lifts the hold, records a late reply as late, and the replacement runs on the next open route; a crashed process's running call is found and cut over by the next controller, which tells the host to let the worker go; every route closed is a wait, re-enabling one starts the waiting attempts; an orderly restart ends the calls and starts the same attempts again on an open route); the relay refusing a cut call; the list checks; probes and drain expiry on the tick; drain and cutover by chat and the status view. `routing/fallback.test.ts` +2 per backend (the caller's list, `withdraw`, `call`, `budgetWait`).
- **Mutation checks** (16, each restored exactly and rebuilt; each fails a named test): the gate look at claim; the listener ending the attempt; the listener lifting its hold; the call ended at an orderly shutdown; the cutover's list rules; the `routes.tick` loop; `routing.drain` in chat; `routing.cutover` shown first; beginning the call; marking it sent (survived at first: the test now checks the fallback service's `sentAt`); the relay refusing a cut call; binding the listener; the caller's own list in `FallbackService`; `withdraw` refusing a sent attempt; the `model_routes` view. Controller fast tier: 9775 tests, all pass (the 12 `not ok` lines are the known TODO cases of C07j/C07k).
- ASSUMPTION: `routing.cutover` in chat is shown first in every approval profile (it cancels running work and may leave charges to settle); `routing.drain` follows the profile like `routing.disable`. The typed recovery order `/nimblenewt.routing-cutover` still runs at once.
- ASSUMPTION: only the default (difficulty) route resolver goes through the fallback service; an operator who passes their own `dispatch.route` keeps choosing routes by themselves, as before (their routes need not be in the routing table).
- ASSUMPTION: a cutover's replacement attempt counts against the task's attempts like any re-admission.
- ASSUMPTION: token counts are not known at the dispatcher's level, so a run's call reports 0 tokens and only money; a task's model budget (`model-budget.set`) now binds dispatched attempts through `begin` (it did not before, because nothing called `begin`).
- **Not done, said plainly.** The relay does not report provider failures to the gate, so health is learned only from what is reported through the fallback service elsewhere and from probes (no request-level failover within a run: a run stays on its route, and the next attempt is the fallback). No real probe sender ships (owner decision). The routing table and topology still have no state-API or chat operation (a configuration card); remote workers' runs are tracked and cancelled the same way, but tested only with the scripted host.

## H09b (part 2): adoption by a new primary, sessions bound to the primary, the poller's handshake

- **Which primary owns a running attempt.** The dispatch record of a running attempt now carries `primaryEpoch`: the epoch of the controller that started it (written with the move to `running`) or took it over (`adoptedAt`). `DispatcherService.heartbeat` renews only an attempt whose `primaryEpoch` is its own; any other is refused `unavailable` ("this controller has not taken it over yet; send the heartbeat again"), a passing condition for the worker, not the end of the attempt, and the lease the earlier controller gave runs on. The controller's own keep-alive for an attempt waiting for the owner (part 1's patience) goes through the same heartbeat, so it does not renew an attempt that is not taken over either.
- **Takeover (adopt or end).** A new step 0 of the tick looks at every running attempt in the live list with no handle in this process and another `primaryEpoch`. The host it runs on is asked (`WorkerHost.adopt`, new and optional): the remote host answers with a handle on the placement the worker accepted, or on one that already completed (its stored result is taken at once, so a result sent while no controller had the attempt is not lost). With a handle the record is stamped with this epoch and given one fresh lease from the takeover, and the dispatcher waits for the result as for an attempt it started (`TickReport.adopted`). When the host no longer runs it (the placement ended or moved, or was only offered: the offer and its credential lived in the old controller's memory), the attempt ends as lost (`lost`, a replacement is admitted within the attempts allowed, and H09's hold for calls of unknown outcome applies); the placement is released, so the agent's native store is free. An attempt on a host that cannot be taken over (a local worker, which died with its controller) is left to its lease. An attempt taken over in a tick is not judged by its lease in that same tick. Concurrent takeovers of one attempt in a process are joined.
- **A session belongs to the primary that opened it.** The session record and the connect answer (`SessionInfo.primaryEpoch`) name the controller's epoch. A controller that took the store over refuses a session opened with another one (`fenced`, "connect again"), and a deposed controller refuses a session of the new one. So a worker that kept its session across a takeover cannot carry on: it connects again, and what it holds is taken up only through the handshake and `accept`, which part 1 made the controller's decision (`auto` or the owner).
- **The handshake reports what is missing.** `reconcile` answers `missing`: the attempts the dispatcher runs on this host whose placement the worker accepted and did not list (read from the live list, at most 64, not worked out when the list is full), and the handshake record keeps their IDs. Nothing is ended for them: nobody beats them, so their lease ends them (ASSUMPTION below).
- **The poller makes the handshake.** `HostPoller` takes `held()` (what the host still holds) and `onReconciled(answer)`: in every new session the handshake is the first request after `connect`, before heartbeats and offers; it is tried again before the next poll if it fails or `onReconciled` throws (a repeat within 5 s gets the controller's cached answer). Without `held` the poller behaves as before.
- **Bug fixed on the way.** A controller that lost the epoch while it held a remote attempt hung in `close()`: `dropWorkers` stopped the handles (the stop could not be written) but left the turns, which waited for a result only the new primary receives, and `idle()` waited for them. `dropWorkers` now lets go of the turns too; a turn that ends later finds its handle gone and changes nothing.
- **Tests.** api/start-new-primary.test.ts (two `startController` instances on one SQLite store): the new primary refuses the worker's old session and its own heartbeat before the takeover (record unchanged), the old primary's heartbeat gets `stale_epoch`, the reconnected worker's handshake is `pending` (strict profile), waiting does not renew the lease, the tick takes the attempt over, the owner approves through `reconnect.pending`/`reconnect.reaccept`, and the worker's result ends it `succeeded` on the new primary; a second test: an attempt only offered when the first controller was replaced is ended as lost with a replacement admitted, and with a third controller a result the worker sent before the takeover is taken (`succeeded`). remote/new-primary.test.ts on every backend: the session fence both ways (also over the wire), the `missing` report and record, the poller's handshake first in each new session.
- **Mutation checks** (each broken alone, the two new test files run, then restored): the own-epoch check in the heartbeat (2 failures), the session fence (3), stamping the epoch at takeover (2), `adopt` accepting an offer (1), `adopt` refusing a completed placement (1), the tick step (2), the listed filter of `missing` (2) and its host filter (2), the poller's handshake (2), the epoch written at start (1), and the `dropWorkers` fix (the test file hangs at the deposed controller's close and is killed by the timeout).
- ASSUMPTION: a restart of the controller is a new primary like any other. A remote worker connects again after it, and under the owner setting (the strict default) each attempt it held waits for the owner's approval, as after any reconnect (part 1); the patience keeps its lease once the new controller has taken it over. Chosen as the conservative reading of "a worker that reconnects does not resume until the controller decides"; the owner who wants restarts to pass by themselves sets `reconnect.settings.set { reaccept: auto }` (already reachable by chat).
- ASSUMPTION: an attempt the worker does not list in the handshake is only reported (`missing`), not ended at once: a worker's list can be incomplete, and the lease ends the attempt within a minute anyway.
- ASSUMPTION: the takeover gives an adopted attempt one fresh lease from the moment of the takeover, so a worker that was cut off while no controller was primary has one lease to reconnect and be heard; an attempt past its own time limit (`expiresAt`) still ends.
- **Not done.** Nothing owner-facing is new (the takeover is the controller's own decision; the owner's controls are part 1's settings and decision, already in chat), so no state API operation or chat entry changed. The product worker process does not yet hold attempts across a reconnect (no product code passes `held` to the poller; the worker side that resumes a held run is the worker package's).
