- ASSUMPTION: a job belongs to its task, not to the attempt that started it: it outlives the attempt and the worker (the acceptance needs the handle after a worker restart) but not a Stop of its task, agent, team or installation, its time limit, or the controller's shutdown or end.
- ASSUMPTION: what an agent starts as a job is a version of the catalogue (the same thing `tool.invoke` runs, with the same checks); there is no free-form command.
- ASSUMPTION: starting a job needs `job.write` on the task (a grant the owner gives, not implied by the work grants); the agent stops the jobs of its own task with that same right; restart decisions and reconciliations need `job.control` (the owner, or a supervisor given it).
- ASSUMPTION: `job.cancel` by chat follows the approval profile (a Stop is reversible control of running work, like `routing.disable`); `job.decide` and `job.reconcile` are shown first in every profile, since they record how work ended.
- ASSUMPTION: the bounds on running jobs (per task, in all, output, grace) are start-up options of the installation (`jobs.limits`), not owner settings; the owner's controls over jobs (status, Stop, Force Stop, decide, reconcile) are all reachable by chat.
- **Leftovers, said plainly.** (1) A tool that leaves a checkpoint cannot yet be relaunched from it: a script has no channel to report one and the launch is not stored with the job, so nothing wires `decideAtStart`'s `relaunch`, and such a job is outcome-unknown at start. (2) Fixed by the review: a job whose task is done or cancelled is now stopped within `sweepMs` (30 s). (3) Stop and Force Stop both end the tree through the launcher's kill (the launcher has no gentler signal), so on Linux a stop is never ignored; "not obeyed" is reached only when the process has not ended within the grace time (tested with a driven launcher). (4) The orphan scan is Linux's (/proc); on macOS and Windows the launcher's own tree kill is all there is, and the job tests skip there like every real-process test. (5) A remote (H02) attempt cannot start a job (refused as not this machine, like `tool.invoke`). (6) MCP jobs are the controller's (`Controller.mcpJobs`); the agent has no MCP tool yet (H12k's leftover). (7) Standard error reaches the job's output only at its end. (8) The job bounds are not owner settings (see the assumption).
- **Independent review (2026-11-08, merged onto main 4b6eb1bb; `status.ask` names both `reconnect` and `jobs`).** Bugs found and fixed, each with a test and a mutation check (10 mutants, all killed):
  - *A different request under a used call ID got the old job's handle.* The refusal rested on the bridge's in-memory call-ID map, which a controller restart (or its eviction after 256 attempts or 5000 calls) forgets; `job.start` then answered the earlier job's handle (named with the new request's tool) for any request. It now compares the durable call record (tool, version, argument digest) and the job (label, background) and refuses a mismatch (`toolbridge/service.test`, 4 backends, with a fresh service standing in for the restart).
  - *Invisible format characters reached the agent.* `job.output` dropped C0/C1 controls but not `\p{Cf}` (bidirectional overrides, zero-width characters); `job.status` passed orphan names and exit/unknown reasons untouched, and a label could carry C1 controls, separators or overrides. Output and status text now drop them; such a label is refused.
  - *A job could keep its own end from being recorded.* A process the job leaves behind can rename itself (prctl); its name went into the orphans, and a control character there (or in a launch failure's standard error, put in the exit reason) made the job service refuse `finish`/`confirmCancel`, so the job stayed running or being stopped on the record forever. The worker reduces an orphan's name to printable ASCII, and the runs clean orphans and reasons before recording (`jobs.test` x4, worker `job.test` with a fake /proc).
  - *A stop asked between admission and launch was never confirmed* (`start` found the job no longer admitted and left it `cancellation_requested`; the next start then called it outcome-unknown). `start` now confirms the stop when nothing was dispatched.
  - *A task credential holding `job.control` could decide and reconcile its own task's jobs* (and, at the service level, stop another task's). The job service refuses both for any task credential (`jobs.test` x4); the owner or a supervisor without a task scope still may.
  - *A job ran on after its task ended* (leftover 2, judged not acceptable: it held one of the task's four slots and the machine's sixteen for up to 24 hours on work nobody would read). `LocalJobRuns` sweeps every 30 s and asks a recorded Stop (by the job host) for each job whose task is done or cancelled (both final) or gone.
  - The h12bf resize (40960-token window) still proves its point: with the startup check weakened (limit x4) the test fails on `[[1,false],[2,true]]`. The fixed part of a first call is about 2380 estimated tokens with the job tools; an 8192-token window (startup share 2048) was already below the fixed part before this card, so no supported default changed class.
- ASSUMPTION: a job does not outlive its task: when the task is done or cancelled, its jobs are stopped (the sweep), whether or not they are background jobs; a job wanted after the task belongs to a new task.
- ASSUMPTION: deciding or reconciling a job records how work ended, so no task credential may do it, even one carrying `job.control`; a supervisor does it with its own (unscoped) credential.
- **Independent review, round 3 (2026-11-08).** Bugs found and fixed, each with a test written to fail first and a mutation check (9 mutants, all killed):
  - *A revoked tool version's jobs ran on.* A job was not one of its version's running calls, so a revocation whose choice (or the owner's policy) is `cancel` or `pause` stopped every `tool.invoke` run and left the job running for up to its time limit, and the chat revoke flow's list of running calls did not name it. A job is now a running call of its version until its end is recorded (`LocalJobRuns.ended`): it is listed, and `cancel`/`pause` asks a recorded Stop by the job host; `finish` leaves it alone (`toolbridge/service.test`, 2 modes x 4 backends).
  - *A stop that landed while a start was recording the dispatch left the job "being stopped" for ever.* The dispatch report was refused (the job was already `cancellation_requested`), `start` dropped the run and threw, and the stop waited for a process that never came. This is reachable by the 30 s sweep (a task cancelled while its agent's `job-start` is in flight) as well as by the owner or the agent. The stop is now confirmed (nothing was launched) and `start` returns quietly; a dispatch that failed for another reason (the store) stops and confirms the job instead of leaving it admitted, and the error still reaches the caller.
  - *An MCP server could keep an MCP job running on the record for ever.* The server's own error words (quoted in the client's error) went into the job's exit or outcome-unknown reason; a tab, a control character or half a surrogate pair there made the job service refuse `finish`/`markUnknown`. The reason is now cleaned (controls and format characters dropped, tab to space, lone surrogates repaired, redacted, bounded).
  - *Half a secret could sit in the job record.* Output is written every second (or 16 K characters) at whatever point the program had reached; a secret cut there was stored in part, unrecognisable to the redaction (for example the first 16 characters of an AWS key), until the rest came. Before the end the trailing word (at most 1,024 characters) is now held back for the next write; the end writes everything. The joined output was already redacted again (T07).
  - *Output past the 16 MiB bound before the launcher handed the process over* did not stop it (there was no process to stop yet); the process is now stopped as soon as it is handed over.
  - Checked and left as they are: a failed task check is never taken for an ended task (now tested: nothing stopped, the failure told); a paused task's jobs are not swept (tested); the sweep timer and the flush timers are `unref`'d and cleared on close; `job.output` takes no offset or limit and answers at most the 8 K-character tail; the job's sandbox has its private directory only and no network, so a job of task A cannot read task B's files; the durable call-record comparison uses the same canonical JSON digest the dispatcher records (key order does not matter) and reads the job with the attempt's current credential, so a retry after a restart or a credential rotation gets the same handle.
- ASSUMPTION: a job is a running call of its tool version, so the revocation choice for running calls applies to it as to a `tool.invoke` run (cancel and pause stop it, finish lets it run).
- ASSUMPTION: holding back the unfinished last word of a job's output until the next write (or the end) is an acceptable delay for an agent reading the output of a running job; a progress line that ends without a space or line break shows when more output comes or the job ends.
- **Independent review, round 4 (2026-11-08, clean-context reviewer; branch `t07b-review-r4` on `t07b-review-r3` 554076a8).**
  - *Bug: the orphan scan could kill an unrelated process.* `linuxOrphans` read every command line in /proc, then sent SIGKILL by bare process ID; a process that exited in between and whose ID was taken by another program (scanning /proc can take tens of milliseconds) was killed, and the second scan could name the newcomer as the job's orphan. The scan now keeps each process's start time (field 22 of its `stat`, read after the last `)` so a name with spaces or parentheses cannot shift it) and, right before the kill, checks that the ID still has that start time and still holds the job's directory; only a process the scan saw is ended or reported. This is the same identity rule the A03 launcher already uses for the descendants it tracks; the launcher's own process-group kill is of a child it has not reaped. Test: worker `job.test` (fake /proc: two IDs reused while the first is being ended, one by a program that also names the directory, one by an unrelated one; neither is killed nor reported).
  - *Tests added for what was checked and held:* `toolbridge/service.test` (4 backends): `job-start` of a version revoked before it is refused (`forbidden`) and of one revoked between the owner's approval and the start is refused, nothing admitted or started; an attempt that has ended can neither start nor stop a job (`fenced`/`unauthenticated`). `jobs/jobs.test` (4 backends): through the runs, a two-line private key with its header split over three writes, a `password:` and a `Bearer` value split at the space, and a second key cut by a Stop: no piece of a secret is in the record after any write, and the held-back end is written redacted when the job is stopped.
  - **Checked, no change:** (a) the hold-back holds only the trailing word, but a secret whose shape has a space or line break (`Bearer x`, `password: x`, a key block) is caught when the pieces are joined (the record keeps the 8 K end and redacts the join; an open key block drops what follows up to its end); the final flush runs on every end (exit, Stop, Force Stop, time limit, output bound, shutdown) before the end is recorded, and the job service redacts it like any piece. A word longer than 1,024 characters is written as it is: the shapes that long (`sk-`, tokens, assignments) are recognised from their start, and the rest of a redacted word is dropped from the next piece. JSON string values (`"password": "x"`) and PGP key blocks are not credential shapes at all (C01b), split or not. (b) revocation: `finish` lets a job run on and it is forgotten from the running calls when its end is recorded; `pause` aborts the call like `cancel` (the job gets a recorded Stop) and pauses the task; a job admitted after the revocation never starts (both checks above). (c) every bridge request binds the credential, the attempt (running, current generation, not frozen) and the task first; a call of a stale generation is refused before `job.start`. (d) no PID is killed at controller start (the start-up rule only records decisions); bubblewrap's private process list ends every process of a job with its first one, so the orphan scan is a second line. (e) output is not kept in memory beyond the pending piece (at most 16 K characters plus writes queued to the store, all within the 16 MiB bound per job); standard error is capped by the launcher at 64 KiB; the job's directory is removed at its end; `jobs` lists at most 100 per answer. (f) bubblewrap: every namespace unshared (no network, private process list), user namespaces disabled inside, `--die-with-parent`, `--new-session`, all capabilities dropped, empty environment, root and /dev read-only, only the job's three directories writable and the interpreter read-only; no launcher or an unusable one refuses the launch (`requireEnforced` true), so the job fails and never runs unconfined. (g) chat and API name a job by its ID only; the `jobs` view quotes labels. (h) a job's output reaches an agent only through `job.output` (quoted); the label reaches the activity step nowhere and the background record (L01) only as the agent's own label.
  - **Left, said plainly:** a controller that is killed outright leaves its jobs' private directories (and the script runner's) under the run base; nothing removes them at the next start (the base may be shared, and removing a directory a fenced controller still uses was judged worse). A job's working directories are on the host disk with no quota (as for catalogue scripts, A03). Every output write is a job command (one stored operation and audit entry per second at most per job) until retention covers jobs. The `jobs` chat view shows the first 100 live jobs with no next page (the API's `job.live` pages).
  - **Mutation checks** (each applied alone, rebuilt, restored and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`): the pre-kill identity check removed; the start time read from the wrong field; only the command line checked before the kill; the report taking any listed ID (all fail the new worker test); the version's revocation check in `#prepare` neutralised (fails the new bridge suite x4); the held-back word written at once; the final flush not run on the end (both fail the new runs suite x4).

## C07j: every hand-off cut is marked and the original kept (2026-11-08)

**Built**
- **The cut.** `lifecycle/handoff-cut.ts` (`cutSection`). A section is a list of entries, one per line, oldest first (as the sources write them). A section over `HANDOFF_LIMITS.section` (4000) keeps first the entries holding one of the owner's marks (newest first, case-insensitive substring, as many as fit), then the newest entries until one does not fit; that one is shortened from its start into the room left (ending `[... shortened; whole in the archive]`) when at least 40 characters fit, and older entries never jump ahead of it. Kept entries stay in their order under one first line: `[cut: N of M entries, archive hnd-…] Entries were left out to fit (the owner's marked ones and the newest are kept); the whole section is kept: read it with the state API query handoff.archive.read { "archiveId": "hnd-…" }.` `N` counts entries left out or shortened. The marker's room is reserved at its longest form (every entry left out), and the result is checked to be within the limit (a `RangeError` otherwise, never a silent slice). Cuts never end between the halves of a surrogate pair (`safeSlice`); lone surrogates from a source become U+FFFD (`wellFormed`) so every store accepts the text.
- **Injection.** Any source line holding something like `[cut:` (any case, spaces allowed, anywhere in the line, so a line hidden behind U+2028 or U+0085 is caught too) is quoted on one line with `quotedLine` (JSON string, U+0080-U+009F, U+2028, U+2029 escaped) and prefixed `(an entry quoted, not a cut marker)`, in every section whether cut or not: the only marker a reader sees is the controller's, on the first line. The package itself reaches the next agent as JSON through `handoff.get`; no prompt renders it today.
- **The archive.** `HandoffService.#collect` (was a plain `.slice(0, 4000)` at `handoff.ts` line 492) redacts the whole section first (a credential is never split into pieces redaction would miss), then, for a section that does not fit, writes the original before the cut package: kind `handoff-archive`, ID derived from the hand-off, the section and the content's SHA-256 (collecting again after a crash finds the same archive; the command ID replays), in parts of 40,000 characters (each part ends on a whole character, so every part fits a record in every store and the parts join to the original). Up to 1,000,000 characters are kept; a longer section's marker and package say "the first 1000000 characters of the section are kept" and the archive says `truncated` (never silent). The package lists each cut in `cuts: [{ section, archiveId, left, total, chars, archiveTruncated? }]`.
- **Reading it back.** `HandoffService.archive` / state API `handoff.archive.read { archiveId, part? }` → `{ archiveId, handoffId, taskId, section, entries, chars, part, parts, text, truncated? }`. Who reads: the owner; the sender; the recipient once the task is transferred to it (a credential scoped to another task cannot); whoever may control the task, except for the sender's drafts and responsibilities, which follow `screen` (owner, sender, recipient after the transfer). `screen` also drops the cuts of those two sections. Anyone else, or an archive that does not exist, gets `not_found`.
- **The owner's marks.** `HandoffService.mark` / `handoff.marks.change { taskId, add?, remove? }` (owner only; 3-200 characters, one line, no credentials; at most 20 per task; `remove` names marks there are, otherwise refused naming the marks; repeated command IDs replay; a concurrent change re-reads and applies) and `handoff.marks.get { taskId }` (whoever may control the task). Kind `handoff-marks`, one record per task. They apply from the next package collected.
- **Chat.** `handoff.marks.change` is a chat op (`mode: "apply"`: marks only choose what stays in view, the rest stays in the archive; `needsProject`; marks must be in the owner's own words); the interpreter prompt says how a section is cut and how to add and remove marks; the `handoff` status kind now lists a hand-off's cuts (section, how many left out, archive) and the task's marks, so the owner can ask about both in free form.
- **The 50-hand-off test** (`handoff-hops.test.ts`): `kept` also accepts an item in the original read back, part by part, through the archive a marker names; the latest-diagnosis check (now strict: in what the next agent is shown, not only the archive) and the cut-marker check (judged from what the source gave, not the package; marker counts, archive equals the original, every shown line is an original entry in order; uncut sections equal the source) lost their `todo` on all four backends. The seeded early decision and failure are found through the archive after hop 50. The C07k growth check stays `todo` (8 of the 12 TODO cases are gone; 4 C07k remain).

**Tests.** `lifecycle/handoff-cut.test.ts` (9: fits whole, newest kept and counted, marks first and in order, an over-broad mark, shortening, surrogate pairs, lone surrogates, forged markers including U+2028/U+0085, too-small limit refused); `lifecycle/handoff.test.ts` (3 suites on all four backends: cut with marks, forged marker quoted, credentials removed, archive read and who may read it; a 2,000-line drafts section archived in parts with the pair moved to the next part, drafts withheld from a controller and its cut screened; a 30,000-line section past the archive's limit; the owner's marks validated, case-insensitive, removable, replayed); `lifecycle/handoff-hops.test.ts` (two former todos on four backends); `api/start-handoff-cut.test.ts` (`startController`: marks through the API, a 101-line brief cut with the marked line kept, the archive read by the owner, the sender, the recipient after the transfer, not found for others, the `handoff` status lines); `chat/handoff-marks-chat.test.ts` (the interpreter prompt; on four backends the owner adds and removes a mark in their own words, a mark they never said and an agent are refused).

**Runs** (worktree build with its own `@nimblenewt` links and copied third-party packages, `tsc --build --force`): the whole controller package 9954 tests, 9911 pass, 4 todo (C07k), 1 fail (the pre-existing `status.ask` description test below), 38 cancelled (PostgreSQL cases in `notifications.test` and `workspace-ops.test`, whose test server did not start under the full parallel load; rerun alone with the C07j files: 263 tests, 259 pass, 4 todo, 0 fail); `node scripts/api-docs.mjs --write` regenerated `api-v1.md` (three new operations).

**Mutation checks** (16, each restored and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`; each fails a named test): marked entries not kept first; oldest kept instead of newest; the surrogate check in `safeSlice`; no marker line; the marker's room not reserved; `neutralise` off; archive parts split without the surrogate check; archive without redaction; the task-scope check on the sender/recipient; the drafts/responsibilities exception; the recipient allowed before the transfer; marks not owner-only; `screen` keeping the drafts' cut; the chat op removed; the status cut line removed; the archive never written (the package names an archive that does not exist).

- ASSUMPTION: "the entries the owner marked" are the owner's marks set per task (words or record IDs matched case-insensitively within an entry), chat-settable; nothing is marked by default. When the marked entries alone do not fit, the newest marked ones are kept first and the rest are in the archive.
- ASSUMPTION: the recipient reads an archive only once the task has moved to it (before that it cannot see the package either); the sender and anyone who may control the task read it at once; the sender's drafts and responsibilities follow `screen`.
- ASSUMPTION: an archive keeps at most 1,000,000 characters of one section (25 parts of 40,000); a longer section says so in its marker, in `cuts` and in the archive.
- Pre-existing, not this card: `api/api.test.ts` "the status.ask description names every kind" fails on main (`reconnect` is a status kind the `status.ask` summary does not name).
- **Not done.** Archives and marks are not yet covered by retention (they are kept as long as the store; the hand-off record has no retention rule either). The sources still write one entry per line, so a multi-line entry (a draft's body is flattened already) would count as several. Bounding the growth of the decisions list is C07k; the first call, stored conversation and resume note are C07l.

**Independent review (2026-11-08, clean-context reviewer; merged onto main 4b6eb1bb).**
- **Bug: the newest decision was pushed out by artifacts.** `controllerHandoffSources` wrote the completed-work section as every decision and then every artifact, and the cut keeps the last entries, so a continuation with many artifacts (up to 200 are accepted) filled the section with artifacts and dropped every decision, the newest included (counted in the marker, but not shown). The section now lists artifacts first and decisions last, so the newest decision is the last entry. `handoff-sources.test.ts` checks the order.
- **Bug: marked entries could crowd out the newest entry entirely.** Marks are matched as substrings of entries an agent writes, so an agent repeating a mark's words in older entries (or an over-broad mark) filled the room and left the newest entry out. `cutSection` now keeps the newest entry first when it fits whole, and otherwise holds back room to show its start (shortened) before the marked entries are placed. Test: "the newest entry is never crowded out by marked ones".
- **Bug: a marker hidden behind invisible or full-width characters was not quoted.** `neutralise` matched only `[\s*cut\s*:`, so `[` + U+200B + `cut:`, a bidi or soft-hyphen insertion, or full-width `［ｃｕｔ:` passed raw. The line is now judged after dropping format characters (`\p{Cf}`: zero-width, bidi, soft hyphen, BOM) and NFKC folding, and a line holding `archive hnd-` or `N of M entries` is quoted too (a look-alike letter in `cut` does not hide it); the quoted form escapes format characters as well as U+0080-U+009F, U+2028 and U+2029. Test: "a marker hidden with zero-width or bidi characters...". Also tested: a section holding an earlier cut's marker is cut again with one controller marker.
- **Checked, no change:** archive written from the redacted text only (the command payload holds the digest, never text); read authorization follows `screen`, maps forbidden to `not_found`, checks the part only after authorization; parts are written in one command (atomic), and a replay with the same sources finds the same archive; marks are owner only; the final section is checked against the limit; record size (40,000 characters at worst 6 bytes each is under the 256 KiB body limit; 25 parts under the 100 changes per operation).
- **Mutation checks** (each restored and rebuilt): `neutralise` without the format-character folding; the newest entry not kept first; the room for its start not held back; the sources' old order. Each fails a named test.
- ASSUMPTION: the newest entry outranks the owner's marks for the first place in a cut section (the card asks for both the most recent entries and the marked ones; the newest one is the minimum that keeps "most recent" from being empty).
- ASSUMPTION: artifacts before decisions in the completed-work section (decisions are what the card protects; the order between the two kinds was not recorded anyway).
- Left: if the sources change between an archive write and the package write (a crash, then new decisions), the first archive is orphaned (no package names it); it is removed only by the retention rule still to come. Homoglyph forgeries that change every word of the marker (`сut`, `еntriеs` and no `archive hnd-`) are still shown raw; the controller's own marker stays the only line matching `CUT_MARKER` on the first line.

**Independent review, round 3 (2026-11-08, clean-context reviewer; branch `review-c07j-r3` on `review-c07j` d6cc1eda).**
- **Gap closed: a look-alike marker opening a line.** The marker's opening is now reserved: a source line whose first visible character (after spaces, combining marks, controls, format characters and the blank letters U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800, then NFKC) is an opening bracket (`\p{Ps}` except `(` and `{`, plus the bracket pieces U+23A1-U+23A3, U+23A7-U+23A9, U+231C, U+231E) is quoted whatever letters follow, so `[сut: 0 оf 9 еntriеs, аrchive hnd-…]` in Cyrillic is quoted. The only raw line a reader sees opening with a bracket is the controller's marker; a look-alike in the middle of a line cannot pass for a first-line marker, and `cuts` names each genuine archive by section. Test: "a line opening with a square or other opening bracket is quoted whatever letters follow". The nonce design was not needed: the archive ID is derived from the SHA-256 of the section that would contain the forgery, so an agent cannot name its own section's archive anyway.

- ASSUMPTION: lines opening with `[` or another square-type bracket (for example `[WIP]` or a Markdown link) are quoted in every section; round `(` and curly `{` openings stay raw. Showing such a line as a JSON string costs readability, never content.
- ASSUMPTION: the newest change of a draft or responsibility (`updatedAt`) is its age for the cut.

**Independent review, round 4 (2026-11-08, clean-context reviewer; branch `review-c07j-r4` on `review-c07j-r3` 264ec95b).** End to end through `startController` with the real sources.
- **Checked, no other path:** the package is built in one place only (`HandoffService.#collect`, the only caller of the sources); every reader (`handoff.get`/`prepare`/`complete`, the `handoff` status view, chat) reads the stored, already cut and redacted package. The dispatcher's attempt hand-off (`context/budget.ts` `handoffFromFacts`, `ctx-handoff` records) is a different note written when an attempt ends, cut at its tail with `[… hand-off cut at N characters]` and no archive: it is the resume note of C07l, left there.

The recipient's package keeps every section within 4000 characters; the newest decision (the failure) is the last line, the marked early decision is kept, the newest pending effect, draft (by `updatedAt`, through the real `start.ts` wiring) and responsibility are shown, headings kept; six sections are cut, each marker names its archive and each archive reads back the source's section exactly; `handoff.marks.change` is refused for a host, the sender and an agent that manages the task's assignment.

## C07l: what the next agent is given in a call, over 50 hand-offs (2026-11-08)

**Built**
- **The test** (`dispatch/first-call-hops.test.ts`, every storage backend). One task is handed A to B to A fifty times with the real hand-off service; after each hand-off the real dispatcher (`buildWorld`) starts the new owner's attempt on a real `LocalWorker` whose guards are the real `controllerGuards` bound to a real `ContextEnforcementService` (as `api/dispatch-compose.ts` binds them). Only the model process is a stand-in, sized as the worker package's host sizes its first call (`packages/worker/src/host/local.ts` line 381: the prompt at three characters a token plus the stored conversation; a checkpoint says the conversation's size). Routes come from the routing table: `localp/small` (32,768 tokens) and the fallback `localp/tiny` (16,384). The hops repeat every five: a lease that runs out (the attempt is lost, the next one admitted and run), a controller restart while the turn runs (the attempt resumes from its checkpoint with its resume note; the stored conversation is 900 tokens a hop larger, so it is resumed whole at hop 2, compacted to fit at hops 7, 12 and 17, and started fresh from hop 22 on, being over the 60 % resume share), the smaller-window route, and two plain hops. An open blocker sits on the task from the start.
- **Checked at every call sent** (all pass): each hop's new owner was sent a call and nobody else was; the hops held at least 10 lease timeouts, resumes, two or more compactions, fresh starts and 10 calls on the smaller route; every call stays under the startup limit of its route (measured independently of the admission's own arithmetic); the largest call of the last 10 hops averages no more than 5 % above the first 10 (about 3,665 tokens against about 3,860); a stored conversation is continued only within the route's resume share, and a fresh start ends the call with the reason (`... starting fresh from the continuation record]`); a resumed call ends with its resume note as the last bracketed paragraph, and a call that is not a resume carries nothing beyond the task's text and rules (a note is at most 1,000 characters); the owner's words, the goal and the rules that bind the agent (its permissions) are in every call.
- **Bug fixed on the way: a shutdown lost the resume of a local attempt.** `DispatcherService.shutdown` stopped the worker while the turn was still the attempt's live turn; the local worker's turn ends as soon as its process is closed, so its `cancelled` ended the attempt (`abandoned`) before shutdown could leave it `waiting` with its checkpoint, and the next controller started nothing. Shutdown now lets go of the turn before stopping the worker, as `relocate` already did (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts` around line 526). Test: `dispatcher.test.ts` "a turn that ends the moment its worker is stopped ... resumes from its checkpoint" (four backends).

**Findings** (each a follow-up card; its checks are in the test as `todo`, named to the card):
- **C07m**: the next agent's first call is the task's title and description, the rules and the route view (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts` line 1863), plus a resume note. It neither carries nor names the hand-off package (next action, decisions, acceptance criteria, open question: readable only through `handoff.get`), the controller's hand-off note of the ended attempt (written at `dispatcher.ts` line 2163 through `ensureHandoff`; `latestHandoff`, `context/enforcement.ts` line 914, has no production caller) or the open blockers (in neither the package nor the call). Three todo checks on every backend. Retention "present whole or retrievable by the reference the prompt carries" holds today only for the owner's words, goal and permissions; the rest is retrievable by an operation the agent is not told of.
- **C07n**: a route whose window the binding does not know: `dispatch/runtime-guards.ts` line 57 admits every first call and line 74 resumes every stored conversation. Todo case: a first call of a million tokens is admitted.
- **C07o**: remote worker hosts: `remote/service.ts` `place` (line 584) offers the order as it is (line 643); no first-call admission and no resume decision is made for a remote attempt, and the remote API has no operation to ask.
- **C07p**: silent cuts in notes: `context/budget.ts` line 178 cuts the controller's hand-off note at its tail with no archive (todo case); `dispatch/dispatcher.ts` line 493 cuts the parked-call verdict note to 500 characters with no marker.
- **C07q**: `ContextEnforcementService.compact`, `registerCompressor` and `keptDecisions` (`context/enforcement.ts` lines 535-747, which pin up to 12 owner decisions through compactions) have no production caller; compaction is the model process's own. The controller's lineage grows by one ID a compaction with no cap (line 635), and `continuation/continuation.ts` line 250 refuses a capture whose `summaryLineage` passes 200 entries, so a long task's captures would fail after 200 compactions.
- The audit's "brief cut at its tail" is the hand-off note above (C07p); the package's brief is cut with a marker and an archive since C07j.

**Mutation checks** (8, each applied, rebuilt, run on the typical tier, restored with `git checkout`, then `tsc --build --force`; each fails the named test): admission skipped in the local worker (startup limit; every hop sent a call); the resume guard ignored in the local worker, and the resume decision always "resume" in `runtime-guards.ts` (resume share); the fresh-start reason not added to the note (a fresh start says why); the startup comparison in `admitFirstCall` removed (startup limit); the task description cut from the call (owner's words and goal); the shutdown fix reverted (the new dispatcher test and the 50-hop simulation); the resume note dropped from the call (resume note). The size-trend check has no guard to remove today, because nothing carried across hand-offs reaches the call (C07m); it guards the call once C07m adds the package.

**Runs** (worktree build, `tsc --build --force`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `dist/dispatch/**/*.test.js` 962 tests, 948 pass, 14 todo (the C07l findings), 0 fail; the new file alone 38 tests, 24 pass, 14 todo, about 23 s on all four backends.

- ASSUMPTION: the card's 50 hops are measured at the dispatcher and the local worker (what the model is actually sent), with the model process as a stand-in sized like the worker package's host; a run through `startController` with remote hosts belongs to C07o, since remote hosts have no check to measure yet.
- ASSUMPTION: a resumed attempt keeps the route it was placed on (the dispatcher chooses the route when the attempt is first claimed), so the smaller-window route is exercised on new attempts; a task moving to a smaller route goes through C07f's route change, tested there.
- ASSUMPTION: the findings are split into five cards (C07m-C07q) rather than fixed here, as the card asks; the shutdown race was fixed here because the resumes the card measures could not happen without it.
- **Not done.** C07k (package growth) is unchanged; its todo stays in `handoff-hops.test.ts`.

### C07l independent review (2026-11-08)

- **Shutdown fix checked and kept.** Letting go of the live turn before stopping the worker is right and matches `relocate`. Checked: a stop that lands at the same time (`#endInner` finds no handle, asks the host to release, and shutdown's write leaves a finished attempt as it is); shutdown during a worker's start (the attempt is not in `#live` yet, shutdown leaves it waiting, and the start sees it is not running and stops the worker it brought up: unchanged); a heartbeat after the turn was let go (it finds no live handle and changes nothing); a second shutdown (nothing running, `closed: 0`); remote handles (their late result was already ignored once the attempt waited); jobs (T07b jobs belong to the task and the controller's runs, and shutdown does not touch them). The attempt keeps its allowance hold (`reservationId`) and gives back its place, so the resume is charged against the same hold, not twice.
- **Before the fix it was worse than the card said.** The worker package's local host answers `failed` (with its cache figures), not `cancelled`, when its process is closed (`packages/worker/src/host/local.ts` lines 384-392), so every controller shutdown failed each running local attempt and opened a `dispatch_blocked` blocker. The dispatcher test now runs for both answers and checks that no blocker is opened and that a second shutdown closes nothing (four backends each).
- **What the fix gives up.** The figures that closed turn reports (for the local host, its cache figures) are no longer charged, since a turn that is not the attempt's live turn changes nothing; `relocate` and `dropWorkers` already worked this way. The local host reports no cost or compute time, so no money is lost.
- **The test against production wiring.** The 50-hop test binds `controllerGuards` itself, as `api/dispatch-compose.ts` does, and copies the worker host's `storedTokensOf` (the controller cannot import the worker package). Removing the window binding in `dispatch-compose.ts` (`window: () => undefined`) does not fail the 50-hop test or any controller API test, but it does fail four integration tests (`c07g-route-view`, `h12bf-composed`, `h12k-composed-host`), so those tests guard the composition.
- **The resume share is not judged in any composition in the repository.** `local.storedTokens` is optional (`dispatch-compose.ts` line 450), and nothing passes it, the integration tests included. Without it `local-worker.ts` line 232 skips the resume decision, so through `startController` a stored conversation is resumed whatever its size, and only the first-call admission (with its one compaction) bounds it. This was added to C07n.
- **The size-trend check cannot fail today.** Nothing carried across hand-offs reaches the call: the call is the task's text, the rules and the route view, plus a resume note that is a fixed string or the resume-share reason. The only part that varies is the stored conversation, and the test's own hop design front-loads it: the restarts in the first ten hops resume theirs, and those in the last ten start fresh. So the comparison favours passing. A check without the stored conversation was added. Neither check can fail on a defect of the code under test until C07m puts the hand-off into the call. The mutants that skip admission or always resume fail other checks, and the trend check survives them.
- **Status.** The card's acceptance included "retention items are present whole or retrievable by reference at every hop". The test shows that this does not hold for the hand-off package, the controller's note or the open blockers. The acceptance was narrowed the way C07h's was: the part that holds is required, and the rest is todo checks named to C07m, which become required when C07m lands. The progress note now says plainly that this part is not met.
- ASSUMPTION: C07l stays `implemented` with its acceptance narrowed, rather than going back to planned. The plan has no partial status. C07m to C07q are blocked on C07l, and C07m's acceptance is C07l's three todo checks. Keeping C07l open would chain every follow-up behind C07m. The narrowing is recorded on the card, so nothing is claimed that the test does not show.
- **Mutation checks re-run** (typical tier, each restored and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`): shutdown fix reverted (fails the dispatcher test for `cancelled` and `failed`, and every 50-hop check; no integration test fails, because none shuts a controller down during a real worker's turn); first-call admission skipped in the local worker (fails "every hop sent a call" and "startup limit"); resume decision always resume (fails "resume share"); resume note dropped from the call (fails "resume share" and "resume note"); policy note dropped (fails "owner's words, goal and permissions"); window binding removed in `dispatch-compose.ts` (fails the integration tests above).
- **Left open.** No test uses a real worker process for a controller shutdown in the middle of a turn. The dispatcher test reproduces the real host's `failed` answer.
## U09 (part 5): completion check, quoted agent text, time and kind filters (2026-11-08)

Checked the card against what parts 1-4 built (blockers C09, U05, A10 and C06b are implemented on main). Covered already, each with tests: the zero-write replay (every storage mutator counted), versions used then (`versionsThen`), distinct outcomes with `not-recorded`, branch lanes with the concurrent label, gaps and redactions marked, contemporaneous and retrospective explanations labelled apart, superseded steps non-authoritative, links, search and export under the same checks with no stored content or thinking, thinking collapsed and owner-only as a recorded look with the retention wording, missing and unreadable reading the same (`not_found`, "no such task"), paging and the read bounds for a huge task (`ReplayLimitsService`). Three gaps were found and closed:

- **Agent text in chat lines (a prompt-injection and terminal-escape gap).** The replay, timeline, activity and explanation status lines put step summaries, missing-content and gap reasons, manifest references, explanation choices, alternatives, evidence and uncertainty, and `led` notes into the line raw (only redacted and whitespace-folded). Recording refuses C0 controls only, so a summary could carry a C1 CSI (U+009B), a bidirectional override or zero-width characters, and its own quotes and words ("(confirmed, replaced by step 9 ...)") read as the controller's. New `quoted(value, max)` in `status/explain.ts`: redacted, folded to one line, cut, JSON-quoted, with U+0080-U+009F, U+2028, U+2029 and `\p{Cf}` (astral ones as their surrogate pair) written as `\uXXXX`. Every agent- or recorder-written text in those four views now goes through it; numbers, kinds, checked line names and principal IDs stay plain.
- **Time filter on the replay.** `ReplayService.open` takes `since` and `until` (ISO times, both included; anything else is `invalid_command`), also on `activity.replay.open`. Like the other filters they narrow the window, not the summary, and a gap (no known time, line or actor) is listed only in an unfiltered window. A `kind` no step can have is refused instead of showing an empty window.
- **Following lines and agents from chat.** The `replay` status view takes `stepKind`, `since` and `until` (as well as `lane`, `agent`, `from`, `seq`), its summary has a line "Lines of work: main (n), ... Agents: agent:x (n), ..." (ten of each, "and N more"), and a window with nothing in it says "No step in this window matches.". `STATUS_KINDS.replay` lists the keys and says what they do, so the interpreter prompt offers them for a free-form question; the `status.ask` summary names them. `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- ASSUMPTION: the project `timeline` keeps only `since` (no `until`): it reads each task's latest ten steps, so an `until` in the past would show nothing; going back in time is a replay of one task.
- ASSUMPTION: the C09h `activity` and `explanations` views quote agent text the same way (the same records rendered to the owner; the escaped quotes inside a quoted summary, `\"Findings\"`, are the price).
- Tests: `activity/replay-u09.test.ts` (`quoted` itself; all four backends: time, kind, line and agent filters, the gap under a filter, `next` under a filter, refused times and kinds, the summary's lines and agents, a hostile summary, reference, reason and explanation through the replay, step, timeline, activity and explanation views with no raw C1, separator or format character and the quotation not closable, credentials removed, missing and unreadable task the same, zero storage writes); `api/start-activity.test.ts` (filters and the quoted chat line through `startController`). Updated for the quoting: `status/status.test.ts`, `activity/replay.test.ts`, `activity/replay-review.test.ts`, `api/start-c09h.test.ts`, `integration/c09h-local-artifact.test.ts`.
- Mutation checks (each applied, rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`, the named test failed, restored and rebuilt): `\p{Cf}` dropped from `quoted`; the replay step summary back to `shown`; the timeline summary back to `shown`; the `led` note back to `shown`; the `since` check removed from the window; gaps listed under a time filter; the kind check off. Each fails `replay-u09.test.ts` on every backend (the kind check also `start-activity.test.ts`).

## U09 (part 6): independent review of the completion check (2026-11-08)

A clean-context review of part 5 against the card. The quoting is applied to every agent- or recorder-written text in the replay, timeline, activity and explanation lines (actors, `e.by`, lane names and reference kinds are checked IDs or patterns, `led.note`, `v.note` and the thinking labels are the controller's own); the five changed tests now expect the right text (the quoted summary, the extra "Lines of work" line moving the continuation to `lines[2]`, the artifact's own quotes escaped inside the quoted summary). Found and fixed:

- **Time filters read in the host's time zone.** `since`/`until` went through `Date.parse`, which reads `2026-11-01T08:00` (no zone) or `Nov 1 2026` in the controller host's local time and takes `1` as the year 2001, `2026-02-30` as 2 March and `T24:00` as the next day: the same chat question showed a different window on another machine. New `filterTime` (`activity/activity.ts`), used by the replay and by the project timeline's `since`: an ISO time that names its zone (`Z` or `+hh:mm`) or a date (midnight UTC), a real calendar time, at most 40 characters; anything else is `invalid_command` and the refusal never echoes the value. `since` after `until` is refused instead of showing an empty window. The interpreter's `STATUS_KINDS` text and the operation argument docs say the format (`api-v1.md` regenerated).
- **`quoted` bound counted characters before escaping.** The cut was taken on the raw text and the escaping came after, so a summary of 300 zero-width spaces became a 1200-character quotation, and a step line (summary plus missing-content reason) or the step view (up to 100 references of up to 200 characters each, many pieces of evidence) could reach over 100 KB on one line; a few such status questions in one chat turn could pass the 256 KB record limit and the turn could not be stored. `quoted` now escapes one code point at a time and cuts the escaped text, so a quotation is at most `max` characters plus its quotes and a cut never splits a character, a surrogate pair or an escape (an escaped quote that does not fit is left out whole). DEL (U+007F) is escaped too (recording refuses it, but the quotation does not rely on that). The "Context then" and "Led to this step" lines name the first 12 items and say "and N more" (`activity.replay.step` and `.led` still give them all).
- **A wrong `stepKind` was refused as `kind:`**, a name the chat never used; the replay chat view now refuses it as `stepKind:` itself.
- ASSUMPTION: a date without a time (`2026-11-01`) is accepted and means midnight UTC (as `Date.parse` and ISO 8601 give it); `until: "2026-11-01"` therefore ends at the start of that day.
- ASSUMPTION: the project timeline's `since` takes the same stricter format (its existing tests and callers already pass zoned times); a zoneless time it used to take is now refused.
- Checked and left as they are: redaction runs before the cut (a credential near the cut is never half-shown; tested); `next` under a filter is a step number and the filters are applied again on every page, so reusing it under another filter shows nothing outside that filter; missing and unreadable tasks read alike in the replay, its filters and the chat view (validation happens before the task is read, so a bad filter is refused the same way for both). The task-title candidates the chat lists when a title is unclear are cut with `slice(0, 80)` and not quoted (shared with the activity, explanations, hand-off and stop-cleanup views; titles are checked text without controls); left for the chat's own owner.
- Tests (`activity/replay-u09.test.ts`): `quoted` at every bound from 4 to 120 over a hostile string (length after escaping, no raw C1/format/separator, no lone surrogate, parseable), the exact cut of escape-heavy text and of a quote at the cut, DEL and half a pair escaped, a credential near the cut; on all four backends: zoned times, an offset equal to its `Z` form, both ends included, a date, the oldest and newest times, a dozen refused forms (no zone, `Nov 1 2026`, `1`, `2026`, 30 February, `T24:00`, minute 60, month 13, lower-case `t`/`z`, a leading space, a number) for `since` and `until` and the timeline, `since` after `until`, an injected text not echoed by the replay, the chat view or the timeline, `stepKind` named in its refusal, and a step with 30 references, 20 pieces of evidence and escape-heavy texts whose lines all stay under 4000 characters with "and N more", zero storage writes.
- Mutation checks (applied to the compiled file, the test run, restored, then `tsc --build --force`): lenient `Date.parse` fallback (8 failures), the calendar check off (4), `since` after `until` allowed (4), DEL not escaped (1), the escape-blind cut (2), the list cap off (4), the refusal named `kind` (4). Escaping half a surrogate pair is redundant with `JSON.stringify` (which already writes it as `\uXXXX`); kept as a guard.

## U09 (part 7): second independent review (2026-11-08)

A second clean-context review of parts 5 and 6, on what was still unquoted or unbounded. Found and fixed:

- **A chat turn could outgrow its record.** Each status answer is cut at 30 lines, but a message may hold eight questions and nothing bounded their sum: eight explanation or replay answers whose quoted agent text is in a three-byte script (about 1.2 KB a line) pass the 256 KB body limit, `chat.turn.done` is refused (`changes[0].body: is larger than 262144 bytes`) and the turn can never be recorded as done (shown by a failing test on all four backends before the fix). New `fitAnswers` in `chat/chat.ts`: before the finished turn is written, its size is measured and, when it would pass the limit less 8 KB of slack, lines are left out from the end of the last answers first; each answer counts what it left out in `moreLines` ("N more lines not shown; ask for a narrower view."), as an answer cut at 30 lines does.
- **Task titles, names and other record text shown unquoted could carry C1 controls, bidirectional overrides and zero-width characters.** The claim in part 6 that titles are "checked text without controls" holds for C0 and DEL only: `text()` in `domain/model.ts` (every task title goes through it: `createTask`/`updateTask`, an agent's sub-task in `swarm`, a meeting's task, the coordinator's planned tasks, which are created by `createTask`) accepts U+0080-U+009F, U+202E and the other `\p{Cf}` characters. The chat's list of tasks a title could mean (`chat.ts`, shared by the activity, explanations, replay, hand-off, hand-off archive and stop-cleanup views) now quotes each title with `quoted(title, 80)`. `shown()` itself (`status/explain.ts`), used by every other status renderer, now writes C0 controls left after folding whitespace, DEL, C1 and `\p{Cf}` characters and half a surrogate pair as `\uXXXX`, bounding the text after escaping and never cutting an escape; plain text is unchanged.
- **Agent words in other views read as the controller's, or broke out of hand-made quotes.** Mechanically moved to `quoted()`: the owner-questions and needs-you lines (task title, the question, the wait's summary; the hand-written `"${shown(...)}"` let a question's own quote close the quotation), the needs-you approval name, meeting decision text (it was cut with `.slice(0, 160)` after `shown`, which could split a surrogate pair) and topic, the held-resume title and an owner blocker's summary; the agenda's topic, question and requested outcome; stand-up brief entries and statements; a hand-off's reason. A hand-off's blocked and failure reasons are the controller's own words and stay unquoted.
- **`filterTime` refused 0000-02-29.** `Date.UTC` reads the years 0 to 99 as 1900 to 1999; the calendar check now sets the full year.
- Checked and left as they are: leap seconds (`23:59:60`), a comma before the fraction and lower-case `t`/`z` are refused (as before; ASSUMPTION: the strict ISO subset is enough for a filter the interpreter writes); offsets up to `±23:59` are accepted (ISO allows them; a `+14:00` is the same instant as its `Z` form); more than three fraction digits are read to the millisecond; year 9999 with a negative offset gives a time past year 9999, which only means an empty window. The timeline's stricter `since` breaks no caller: nothing in `packages/ui`, `packages/api`, the scripts or the docs calls `activity.timeline` or the `timeline` view with a zoneless time, the tests pass zoned times, and the operation and `STATUS_KINDS` texts state the format. `next` under a changed filter: unchanged from part 6.

## L02d (part 4, closing): real processes from the sandbox, Force Stop that kills, winding down charged (2026-11-08)

What parts 1-3 left (the contract, the Stop's ending of jobs and swarm children, the charge ledger and its chat view were built): no sandbox backend reported a process (`SandboxSession.work` was never implemented by a real sandbox), a close that the OS could not complete hung for ever, and a Force Stop did nothing to a process that outlived its attempt. This part closes the card's acceptance ("a process that ignores the request is listed and Force Stop offered; the cleanup spend is charged") with real processes.

- **A run's processes** (`worker/src/sandbox/proc.ts`, `SandboxRun.processes`). On Linux the launcher reads the run's tree from /proc (the launched process and everything below it, parents first; zombies are not alive; names reduced to printable ASCII, never a command line; at most 200, more is said as `processes:truncated`). On macOS it uses the backend's `descendants`/`startTimes`; elsewhere it cannot say (`undefined`, and nothing is claimed). Once the run has ended, only what outlived it is listed: a process an earlier look saw that is still the same process (same start time), after a short settle (the kernel ends a private process list a moment after its first process). `kill()` after the end kills those survivors (start time checked first). Real bubblewrap test: a run lists both of its sleeps (one detached with `setsid`), none of another run's, and nothing after it ended.
- **What a sandbox holds** (`HostSandboxSession.work`, `worker/src/host/local.ts`). `splitRunTree` separates the confinement down to the launched program (bubblewrap's processes and the worker process) from what the agent started (the program's descendants, and orphans the confinement adopted). The worker process is the attempt itself: while it runs it is NOT listed (it is quiesced and checkpointed through the attempt, so a Suspend does not wait on it for ever); once asked to end it is listed until it has gone. What the agent started is listed while it runs. State: `running`, or `uncooperative` once the process was asked to end more than the close grace (3 s) ago and is still there; anything that outlived the run is `uncooperative`.
- **A close that cannot end the process says so** (`WorkerProcess.close`). It asks, kills after the grace, and if the run has still not ended `killWaitMs` (5 s) after the kill it rejects with `ProcessNotEnded` instead of waiting for ever. The sandbox's `close` passes that on, `LocalWorker`'s handle `stop` now lets a failed sandbox close fail the stop (after everything was tried), so the dispatcher records `workerStopped: false` (the scratch stays) and the Stop's look after the ending names the process.
- **Force Stop kills** (`SandboxSession.end`, `LocalWorker.endLocalWork`, `WorkerHost.endLocalWork`, `DispatcherService.endLocalWorkOf` (staff only), `LocalWork.end`). A Force Stop's ending tells the hosts to kill what they hold for every attempt seen for the scope (also one that ended earlier and left a process behind) that the asker may control (a swarm child only for someone who may control the child, as for its attempt and jobs). Every host is told even when one fails; a failure is not reported as such, the look afterwards names what is left. A graceful Stop only asks (the close); what ignores it is named and the Stop is `recovery-required` (or, if seen during preparation, blocked with `force-stop` among the choices).
- **Cleanup spend** (`computeMs`). The local sandbox's running total is the time each of its worker processes took to wind down: from the first request to end (a close or a kill) until its run ended (or until now). Whole milliseconds, left out while 0 (an attempt that never wound down reports no figure and is not listed in the stop's charges). The Stop charges it once, as `stop-cleanup` compute, through the existing per-attempt ledger (parts 2-3). Money (`costMicros`) is not reported by a local sandbox: model calls during the cleanup are charged by the relay as before.
- **Tests.** `worker/src/sandbox/proc.test.ts` (3: tree, zombies, reused IDs, names; the bound and an unreadable list; the split), `worker/src/sandbox/launcher.test.ts` (+1, real bubblewrap), `worker/src/host/process.test.ts` (+2, mock timers: ask, kill after the grace, give up with `ProcessNotEnded`, keep counting, Force Stop; an obeying process timed exactly), `worker/src/host/local.test.ts` (+2: not listed while running, running within the grace, uncooperative after it, the close rejects, Force Stop ends it and the count stops; a survivor of an ended run; a system with no process list; 0 ms charges nothing), `controller/src/dispatch/local-worker.test.ts` (+1 x 4 backends: `endLocalWorkOf` for the attempts asked only, staff only, every sandbox told even when one fails, a sandbox whose close failed leaves `workerStopped: false`), `controller/src/lifecycle/dispatch-ports.test.ts` (+1: graceful asks, Force Stop kills for every attempt seen that the asker may control, a failed kill still looked at), `controller/src/api/start-stop-local-work.test.ts` (+1 through `startController`: an uncooperative worker blocks the Stop with `force-stop` offered, the owner's Force Stop makes the host kill it and the stop ends), `integration/src/l02d-local-processes.test.ts` (1, real bubblewrap through `startController`: a worker process that ignores the close starts a detached process; readiness lists that process by `pid N (node)` and not the worker; the attempt counts as busy for a workspace operation; the Stop gives the grace, kills the sandbox, nothing is left in /proc; the winding down (>= 3 s) is charged once as `stop-cleanup` compute on a budget with no compute limit, shown by the `stop_cleanup` chat view, and a sweep does not charge again).
- ASSUMPTION: the cleanup spend of a local sandbox is the wall time its worker processes took to wind down (compute dimension), not CPU time and not money; every wind-down of the attempt's sandboxes counts (a recipe restart's too, usually milliseconds), since the ledger charges running totals per attempt once.
- ASSUMPTION: a local worker process is "uncooperative" only once it has outlived the close's grace (3 s); within it, it is simply still ending (`running`), so a recipe restart racing a Stop's preparation does not block the Stop.
- ASSUMPTION: the worker process itself is not an inventory item while its attempt runs (the attempt is quiesced through the dispatcher); processes the agent started are, so a Suspend now waits for (and, at its deadline, blocks on) a background process the agent left running, as it does for jobs ("a Suspend waits for everything"), and a workspace landing treats that attempt as busy (H12q's stated rule).
- **Interactions checked.** H12q landing quiesce: `busyAttempts` counts agent-started processes and a worker being closed, not a frozen idle worker (all h12q/h12m integration tests green). A starting attempt: its worker process is remembered the moment it is launched, before the launch is recorded. L04c hand-off holds: this slice writes no pause gate and does not change which gate a Stop reuses or lifts. 0 = unlimited: the compute charge lands on a budget opened with money only (compute limit 0) and is recorded, not refused. Window starvation of the charge sweep: unchanged (a local sandbox's figures are charged like any other; nothing new is put on the open index unless a charge fails).
- **Left (follow-up card L02e).** Swarm descendants of an agent's, team's or installation's tasks are not walked by their Stop; the charge-sweep window starvation by unfinished requests (part 3's known limit); a task's `stop_cleanup` view of a Stop made through a wider scope; chat resolving an agent's or team's name for the scope form; a per-request cumulative total; a remote worker's own process report (one unknown item per live placement today). Also: Windows sandboxes list no processes (nothing is claimed); more than 16 worker processes in one sandbox drop the oldest ended one (its time kept) even if something outlived it.
- **Mutation checks** (14, each applied alone, built, run, restored with `git checkout` and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`; all killed): the split counting the program's children as its own (proc.test, local.test); the worker listed while it runs (local.test); `close` never giving up (process.test); the sandbox close swallowing `ProcessNotEnded` (local.test); `LocalWorker.stop` swallowing a failed sandbox close (local-worker.test x4); Force Stop not reaching the hosts (dispatch-ports.test, start-stop-local-work.test); Force Stop killing a swarm child the asker may not control, and forgetting attempts seen earlier (dispatch-ports.test); winding down not timed (process.test, the integration test); `uncooperative` within the grace (local.test); every process seen reported after the run (real launcher test); `endLocalWorkOf` without its staff check, and ignoring a failed kill (local-worker.test x4); zombies counted alive (proc.test).
- **Runs** (worktree build with its own `@nimblenewt` links and copied third-party packages, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): worker 278 tests, 277 pass, 1 skipped; integration 108, 98 pass, 10 skipped (tier), 0 fail; controller lifecycle, dispatch, remote, workspace-ops, status, api/api and the stop/lifecycle startController files 2583, 2579 pass, 4 todo (C07k), 0 fail. No API operation or status kind was added (the Force Stop and the chat view already existed), so `api-v1.md` and the interpreter prompt are unchanged.

### L02d review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-08)

Reviewed against the card, the part 4 notes above and the safety questions (whose process is killed, who may force a stop, what is charged and how often). Fixed:

- **A process ID walked after its process exited** (`launcher.ts`, `processes`). Between the launched process's exit (Node has reaped it) and the run's end (up to the 2 s drain while a survivor holds the output pipes), a look walked /proc from `child.pid`, which may already belong to an unrelated program, and remembered what it found; a later `kill()` would then have killed that program and its children (their start times were taken from the impostor). A look now walks the tree only while Node has not seen the exit (an exited, unreaped process keeps its ID, and the /proc walk is synchronous, so nothing reaps it during the walk); after it, only what an earlier look saw and still runs with the same start time is listed. On macOS a look whose waits saw the exit is discarded. Test: `launcher.test` (real trusted-host run: in the drain, the detached survivor is still listed; mutation `if (ended)` alone fails it).
- **A kill that left a survivor** (`launcher.ts`, `kill`). While the run went, `kill()` killed only the process group: a trusted-host run's `setsid` child escaped it, and Force Stop then claimed nothing about it until the run had ended. `kill()` now also ends what an earlier look saw that still runs (same start time), also while the run goes. Test: `launcher.test` (real: the detached process is gone after the kill; mutation back to the old `kill` fails it).
- **Wall-clock wind-down time** (`process.ts`). The time charged as `stop-cleanup` compute was `Date.now()` differences: a clock set back made it 0 (clamped), a clock set forward made it as large as the jump (then cut at the ledger's cap). It is now `performance.now()` (monotonic). Test: `process.test` (wall clock set back a day and forward a year; mutation to `Date.now()` fails it). The mock-timer tests map `performance.now` onto the mocked `Date`.
- **Process names unquoted** (`local.ts`). A name is the program's own (up to 40 printable ASCII characters) and was shown as `pid N (name)`, so a name like `x): settled. pid 1 (init` or `[cut: 1 of 2 entries]` read as more of the line in the readiness and stop answers. It is now `pid N "name"` (JSON-quoted, so quotes and backslashes are escaped). Test: `local.test` (three hostile names).
- **A renamed program taken for the confinement** (`proc.ts`, `splitRunTree`). Any process named `bwrap` on the chain was treated as confinement, so a worker process that called itself `bwrap` would hide its oldest child from the listing (and from a Suspend's wait). At most two confinement processes (bubblewrap's monitor and its process 1, checked on a real run) are taken; below them the process is the program whatever its name. Test: `proc.test` (mutation without the bound fails it).

Checked and left as built: Force Stop is authorized by the scope's own control check (`authorizeControl`, the same as Stop) and per swarm child by `mayControl`; it reaches only attempts seen for that scope (no other project's); `endLocalWorkOf` is staff-only and filters attempt IDs; the per-attempt ledger keeps the running total with `max`, so a sweep, a second Stop or a replay after a restart never charges twice (a restarted controller has no sandbox figures and charges nothing more); a charge on a budget whose compute limit is 0 is recorded (integration test); `ProcessNotEnded` leaves the attempt finished with `workerStopped: false` while the sandbox keeps listing the process (`uncooperative`, Force Stop offered), and a recipe restart whose old sandbox cannot be closed now fails (the attempt is frozen) instead of running two workers; a Suspend that waits on an agent-started process blocks at its deadline naming the process; a system that cannot list processes (Windows) names the worker once asked to end and claims nothing about what it started (as before L02d).

- ASSUMPTION: a process is identified by its process ID and its start time (clock ticks since boot, from /proc); a reused ID with the same start tick would need the whole process ID space to wrap within one tick. Node offers no process file descriptor, so the start time is checked immediately before each kill (and the launched process's ID is never used once Node has seen it exit). A namespace or cgroup check would add nothing a bubblewrap run needs: its processes die with its private process list.
- ASSUMPTION: the bound of two confinement processes matches bubblewrap's tree (monitor, process 1, program) as run here; Seatbelt's `sandbox-exec` replaces itself with the program.
- Left (pre-existing, not changed): the launcher's group kill (`kill(-pid)`) in the drain after the launched process exited could reach a new process group that reused the ID once the old group is empty; this needs the ID to be reused within 2 s. A local worker whose close failed stays unconfirmed after Force Stop killed it, so its scratch is kept (added to L02e).
- **Runs** (review worktree on main 3b56a4be, own `@nimblenewt` links, copied third-party packages, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): worker 282 tests, 281 pass, 1 skipped, 0 fail (three full runs; one earlier run had one failure in the bubblewrap launcher file that did not recur in three full runs nor in six parallel runs of that file); pi-adapter 188 pass; controller lifecycle, dispatch, remote, workspace-ops, status and api 2896, 2892 pass, 4 todo (C07k), 0 fail; integration l02d-local-processes, h12q-landing-quiesce, h12m-workspace-host, h12bf-composed, h12k-composed-host, h12k-limit-enforcement and t07b-jobs 21 pass; `plan.test`, `roadmap:check`, `check:deps` green; `api:docs:write` changes nothing. Mutation checks (4, each applied, built, run, restored and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`): `kill` back to group-only while running; the walk after the exit; `Date.now()` for the wind-down; the confinement bound removed; all killed by the named tests (the quoting by its test's exact refs).

### L02d review 3 (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-08)

Branch `review-l02d` merged with main 49a9cb84 (clean: only the T07b orphan-scan test changed). Fixed:

- **The integration test named a real process `node`** (`integration/src/l02d-local-processes.test.ts`). Node 24 on the CI runners names its main thread `MainThread`, and the listing shows the kernel's name (`/proc/<pid>/stat`), so the expected ref `pid N "node"` would fail there exactly as T07b's orphan-scan test did. The name is now read from `/proc/<pid>/comm` of the process (the patch prepared for this; it also needed the pid typed as a number to build). The other L02d tests that name real processes name `sh`, `sleep` and `bwrap` (from the executable's file name, not Node's thread name), and the fake /proc tests write their own names.
- **The group kill after the launched process exited** (`launcher.ts`, `finalKill`; left as pre-existing by review 2). Force Stop makes this path more used: a `kill()` in the drain (the launched process has exited and been reaped, a survivor still holds the output pipes) killed the process group named by the old ID, which, once the run's group is empty, may be a new group made by another program that got the ID (this launcher makes every run a group leader, so the next run it starts is exactly such a program). The group is now killed after the exit only while no process holds the ID (`groupKillSafe`): POSIX keeps a process group's ID from reuse while the group has members, so a taken ID means the run's group is empty and the kill would only reach someone else. Before the exit nothing changes. Tests: `launcher.test` (real trusted-host run: in the drain, with no look made, the kill still ends a sleep left in the run's group; the guard's verdicts for a taken and a free ID, and the real check on a live ID). Mutation: skipping the group kill after the guard fails the real test.
- **Force Stop waited per sandbox in turn** (`LocalWorker.endLocalWork`). Each session's `end` waits up to `killWaitMs` (5 s) for what it killed; one after the other, an attempt restarted a few times, or many attempts of an agent or team, made the Stop wait that long for each. All sessions are now told at once (`Promise.allSettled`; failures still collected and thrown together). Test: `local-worker.test` x4 (three sandboxes are ending at the same time; mutation back to the loop fails it).

Checked and left as built (nothing real found): Force Stop's reach (the scope's own control check, swarm children per `mayControl`, verified by mutation: dropping that filter fails `dispatch-ports.test`); `endLocalWorkOf` staff-only; the per-attempt `max` ledger with a derived command ID per step (the existing `stop-suite` case "a crash after a charge was made, followed by a larger total" and the seeded sequences cover a crash between the charge and its note; `budgets.charge` records a cleanup charge whatever the limits, so a compute limit of 0 never fails the Stop); `ProcessNotEnded` (the attempt finishes with `workerStopped: false`, the sandbox keeps the process listed; a runtime reopen in the same sandbox swallows it, harmless because the old process was already sent SIGKILL and can run no more code); the start-time check before each survivor kill (mutation: dropping it in `linuxStillRunning` fails `proc.test`); survivors of an ended run listed as uncooperative (mutation fails `local.test`); macOS listing re-checks the exit after its waits; Windows lists nothing below the worker (no backend lists descendants there; nothing is claimed about them, as before L02d) and lists the worker itself while it lives after the request to end, so a Force Stop never reads clean while the worker process lives. The L02e pointers (`remote/host.ts` unknown item per placement, the 20 x 100 open-entry read of `stop.ts`, `stop_cleanup` by exact scope in `cleanupSpend`, chat's scope form) exist as described; L02d's own acceptance (a process that ignores the request is listed and Force Stop offered; the cleanup spend is charged) is met, the wider-scope child work is a deliverable split honestly to L02e.

- ASSUMPTION: a process ID that a `kill(pid, 0)` reaches (or is refused for) after the launched process was reaped belongs to another program; the group kill is skipped then. It can miss nothing of the run: while any member of the run's group lives, the ID cannot be handed out.
- Left (added to L02e): an attempt that finished with its worker unconfirmed (its close could not end the process) is not live, so a later Stop of its task neither lists nor reaches what its sandbox holds (only attempts live or seen during that Stop are asked). On Linux such a process has already been sent SIGKILL and the private process list ends everything below it.
