## Capacity view in chat (Pi)

The owner can already change the capacity controls in chat (`capacity.limits.change`, `capacity.quotas.change`,
`swarm.limits.change`) and read them through the state API, but no status kind showed them, so a free-form "what are
my capacity limits?" had no view to answer from. One new owner-only kind, `capacity`, answers all three groups in
plain lines.

- **`packages/controller/src/status/status.ts`**: `capacity` in `STATUS_KINDS` (keys `[]`, the `about` text is what the
  chat model is told), `{ kind: "capacity" }` in `StatusRequest`, `case "capacity": { onlyKnown(request, ["kind"]); return this.capacityLines(by); }`
  in `ask`, and `capacityLines` built the way `eventSourceLines`/`retentionLines` are: `if (settings === undefined || by.kind !== "owner") return undefined`,
  so a caller that is not the owner reads exactly what it would read if the kind did not exist (the chat answers `not_found`,
  `status.ask` throws `not_found`). It calls the same service methods the operations call - `CapacityLimitsService.get`,
  `AdmissionService.quotas`, `SwarmLimitsService.get` - and reads nothing else, so the view cannot drift from the API.
- **What each line says**: every figure with its meaning in words, then `(the default)` or `(you set it)` (caps: an entry
  the owner never made is the default; quotas: compared with the `defaults` the service returns; swarm: an absent entry is
  the default, a `null` fan-in total is `off, no total`), plus what holds them now (`N running now`, `N of them in use now`,
  `N waiting now`, `N productive attempt(s) running on it`). A cap that is off says `off, nothing is capped`, and a cap
  turned off keeps saying which figure would turn it back on. A host that has declared nothing is named as such, because
  work needing a host is then refused. A figure that means the whole thing is off says so in words rather than as a bare
  nought: `depth ...: 0 (you set it): no child task may be spawned at all` and `liveChildren ...: 0 (you set it): no new
  child task may be spawned now`, the same two things `SwarmService` refuses a spawn with. The quotas header names whose revision it
  shows - `the admission record is at revision N, which every request and release also raises` - because the number is the revision of
  the whole admission record, not the version of a setting (a test walks it 0 -> 1 with a request and 1 -> 2 with its release while every
  quota line stays the installation's own).
- **Damaged or absent is one line, never a throw, and says what the damage stops**: a group whose service is not composed in
  says `this controller does not offer them`, and a damaged record is told with the consequence its readers really produce,
  checked against them rather than worded generally:
  - *caps* - `CapacityLimitsService.get` throws `integrity` through `capsOf`, and `AdmissionService.request` reads the same
    record before it admits anything: with `{ perProject: { enabled: true, value: "many" } }` stored, an inquiry, a review and
    productive work are all refused `integrity` while what already runs is left running and can still be released. The line
    says nothing new is admitted, inquiries and reviews included, until `capacity.limits.change` repairs it (it used to say the
    record "applies to nothing", which reads like a harmless setting).
  - *swarm limits* - `SwarmLimitsService.get` does not throw, but `SwarmService` takes its limits from `effective()` before it makes any
    child, which does: a damaged record spawns nothing at all (probed through the composed controller - the spawn is refused `integrity`, and
    once the record is readable again the same call gets past that gate and on to its next check). The group line says that; a name whose stored
    figure cannot be read is marked `damaged: the figure stored cannot be read` and never `(the default)`; the sound names in the same record are
    marked `- not in force while the record is damaged`, because none of them is in use while one name is unreadable.
  - *quotas* - `AdmissionService.quotas()` hands back the admission record without checking it, so damage reaches the view as it
    is: `{ capacity: null }` used to throw `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` out of the view and lose the
    whole answer, a record whose `limits` lack `queue` printed `queue: undefined (you set it)`, and a host entry that is not a
    record printed `undefined CPU(s), undefined MB declared`. Every figure is checked before it is shown (`quotaProblem`): every
    record a record, every count a finite number, and every quota a whole number inside `LIMIT_BOUNDS` - the table `checkLimits`
    and `capacity.quotas.change` enforce - because a stored `productive: -1`, `0` or `1.5`, `control: 0` or `queue: 0` is no figure
    the owner could have stored (the command refuses the same value - `set.productive: must be a whole number from 1 to 64`, the words
    `checkLimits` uses for the whole record too) yet used to print as `(you set it)`. Anything else - or a read that fails outright, such as
    a `running` that is not a list or a per-host count that is not a figure - is one line naming what cannot be read. Such records
    are not inert: admission works from the same figures and applies no bound it cannot read (a record with no `queue` let a queue of
    any length build up where a sound one refused; a stored `productive: 0` leaves productive work waiting for ever while inquiries
    still run; a stored `queue: 0` refuses anything that has to wait with `the queue is full (0 waiting); try again later`) - all
    three asserted through `AdmissionService` itself. The line says the record needs repair and that `capacity.quotas.change` cannot
    mend every damaged shape, rather than telling the owner to repair it with that command: the command merges `set` into the stored
    limits and checks the whole record with `checkLimits`, so it needs `depth`, `children` and `patience` - figures no quota command
    can set - to be there (probed, and both halves are tested: a record with no limits is refused `limits.depth: must be a whole number
    from 0 to 8` even with all four quotas set, while one whose limits are whole but that lacks `queue` is mended by the same call).
    The caps and swarm lines may keep naming their command because those two really do always mend: `capacity.limits.change` and
    `swarm.limits.change` read their records leniently (`readCapEntries`/`readEntries`), keep the sound entries and refuse only until every
    damaged name is named in the change (`set, unset or disable it in this change to repair it`).
  The other two groups are still read in all of these cases. `forbidden`/`unavailable` say the group cannot be read here; anything
  else about the read itself is thrown, as every neighbouring view does - but nothing the records hold throws out of this view.
- **Text from outside is quoted**: host IDs go through `quoted()`, so a host ID holding a double quote, a newline, U+2028, U+202E
  and `[cut: ` stays on one line inside one quotation (the newline and U+2028 are folded, the quote escaped, the override written
  as `\u202e`). Numbers are shown as themselves. Every lookup by a name read out of a record is an own-property one (`Object.hasOwn`:
  the per-host running counts, the quota `defaults`, the `N running now` words, `CAPACITY_WORDS` and `LIMIT_BOUNDS`), because those
  records are plain objects - a host declared as `constructor` used to print `function Object() { [native code] } productive
  attempt(s) running on it`, and now counts nought, with a per-host count that is not a figure called damaged. The revision of each
  record read goes into the cite, and the three cite kinds are
  `capacity-limits-settings/main`, `admission-state/admission` and `swarm-limits-settings/main`.
- **Bounds**: the caps (3) and swarm (3) names are all shown, the quotas (4) likewise, and at most 10 declared hosts are listed
  (`CAPACITY_HOSTS`), in host-ID order, with one line counting the rest - `capacity.quotas.change` takes at most 50 hosts in one change (probed)

## X09b (part 2, Pi): chat words for the owner's release actions and the release status view (2026-11-08)

- **Chat (`chat/commands.ts`):** `release.host` (authorize a host for release tests, `active: false` withdraws it), `release.approve` and `release.interrupt` join `CHAT_OPS`, all `mode: "propose"` — shown first in every profile, so nothing happens until the owner confirms the proposal. The proposal reason reads "a release action is shown first". As with `release.start` and `release.cancel`, no ID is ever the model's to pick: `attemptId` and `candidateId` are release keys not exempt from the evidence check (`RELEASE_ID_KEYS`) and `hostId` was never exempt, so a host, attempt or candidate the owner did not name in their own words is refused (`unsupported_value`) — each is checked by test.
- **Listing (`release/release.ts`):** `candidates(owner, {limit})` returns the submitted candidates newest-first with each one's approval state and a `more` flag; it reads at most `CANDIDATE_SCAN` (200) candidate records and says so when cut. Owner only, like the rest of the release read path.
- **Status view (`status/status.ts`, wired in `api/start.ts`):** `release` joins `STATUS_KINDS` (keys `candidateId`, `limit`), owner only: `ask` returns nothing for anyone else and `status.ask` answers `not_found`, the same as for a subject that is not there. Per candidate: a header (approved or not, ready or not, the flaky caveat), one line per platform — pass, flaky pass (naming the earlier failures it took), fail, interrupted, timed out, running or not run — one line per attempt (state, platform, host, started and ended, what the host said, an interrupt reason), and one staging line from `ReleaseActivationService.status` (current release, what rolling back would return to, staged count, whether activation needs an approval, and the pointer when it diverges from the record). A named candidate is read by ID; otherwise the newest `limit` (default 5) are listed and a cut list says how to see more. The answer is bounded to 30 lines with a last line saying what was not shown and how to read it. Every host-, platform-, pointer- and agent-written value goes through the existing `quotedLine` helper (quoted, escaped, one line), so none can split a line or forge structure.
- **API documentation:** `status.ask` describes the `release` view; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated with `npm run api:docs:write`.
- **Tests (`chat/release-owner-words.test.ts`, all four backends, real services — the real StateApi, ReleaseService and ReleaseActivationService over the same storage the chat turns on, with a real staging folder on disk; nothing mocks the implementation):** `release.host` is proposed (the machine cannot take a test while the proposal waits) and applied only on the owner's confirmation; `release.interrupt` likewise, and the named attempt ends interrupted, never as a pass; `release.approve` without `acknowledgeFlaky` is refused at apply time when a platform passed only after failing (the gate stays unapproved), and the acknowledged approval is applied only on the owner's word; a host, attempt or candidate not in the owner's words is refused and changes nothing; the release view answers in chat (gate, attempts, flaky, staging, every line cited) and a stranger's `status.ask` reads `not_found`, exactly like a candidate that is not there. The second test: the flaky pass is labelled and counted, a hostile host ID and a forged agent-written summary (quotes, a fake `": pass"` structure, U+2028) stay inside one quoted line and split nothing (the only `win32` text in the answer of a linux/darwin candidate is inside the one escaped summary), an unreadable pointer file is reported quoted as `pointer says "invalid"`, the listed view cuts at exactly 30 lines with the "more line(s) are not shown" tail, and a caller who may not read release records gets nothing. The chat harness now takes `apiExtra` as a function of `(storage, epoch, built services)` so real services can be wired into the API before the owner token exists. The interpreter prompt listing and the `status.ask` description are checked by the existing loops (`model-interpreter.test.ts` over every `CHAT_OPS` and `STATUS_KINDS`; `api.test.ts` over every kind) — both pass with the new entries.
- ASSUMPTION: `release.host`/`release.approve`/`release.interrupt` reuse the existing API operations unchanged; the chat table only lets the owner's words reach them, still proposed first.
- ASSUMPTION: the view quotes the platform label even though `os` and `arch` are a fixed vocabulary the service validates (defence in depth; the quoting is asserted).
- ASSUMPTION: a controller running without a release root says "Staging: not set up on this controller" — reads like nothing staged, not like an error.
