## X09b part 2 review fixes (Pi): the flaky word, the paged candidate list, a view that keeps its own lines (2026-11-08)

The independent review of `daca3f52` returned eight defects. All eight are fixed; each was written against a test that was seen to fail first, and three claims made in the section above are corrected here.

- **1 — `acknowledgeFlaky` had to be the owner's word (`chat/commands.ts`, `chat/chat.ts`, `66df3c06`).** Before, any approval of a flaky candidate passed if its reason merely contained "flaky" *or* an accepting verb next to "fail"/"failures", so "approve it, the failures are not mine" and even a reason that only repeated a preview word could authorize it, and the preview said nothing about which platforms were flaky. `saysAcknowledgeFlaky(words)` now reads the owner's own message only: the word `flaky`, or accepting / approving / acknowledging / understanding the failures or the result, with the negated forms ("not accept", "won't accept", "never accept", "don't accept") refused. `release.approve` carrying `acknowledgeFlaky` is refused before a proposal is drawn up when the message does not say it, and the `release.gate` preview names each platform that passed only after earlier failures and says approving needs `acknowledgeFlaky`. **Corrected:** the section above said "each is checked by test" — the flaky rule was not: the only flaky test used words that happened to contain "flaky", which is exactly how the over-permissive rule survived review. Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (the wording itself, including the negations), `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (three refused approvals through the real chat and API, the accepted wording still proposed, and the gate preview naming the flaky platform).
- **2 — the blind-interrupt test was proved to be a real check.** The turn where the owner never names an attempt now takes the model's `reason` from the owner's own words ("stop the release test that is running now, it is not needed" → reason "it is not needed"), so nothing but the `attemptId` can give the command away; leaving `attemptId` out of `RELEASE_ID_KEYS` was run and the file failed 4 of 8 (all four backends), and restoring it and rebuilding made it pass 8 of 8 again. A check that only works because the test leaks an ID is not a check.
- **3 — `release/release.ts candidates()` pages (`3b3e3fb9`).** It read 200 candidate records once, in digest-ID order, and stopped. **Corrected:** the section above's "newest-first … a `more` flag" and the view's "the newest `limit` are listed" were both false: the scan could stop before the newest candidate (IDs do not follow submit time), `more` was then 0 with candidates left, and the cut line told the owner to ask for a larger limit that could not help. Now it reads pages of `CANDIDATE_SCAN_PAGE` (200) up to `CANDIDATE_SCAN_PAGES` (25) — `CANDIDATE_SCAN` (5000) records — sorts what it read by submit time newest first, and `scanLimited` says when the bound was reached. **`more` is a boolean, not a count**: it says only that a submitted candidate is not listed, and it is exact while `scanLimited` is false; the view's cut line says which of the two it is. Tests: 205 candidates whose newest has the highest sort position in the store, exactly 200, and a store that fits in one look.
- **4 — the release status view (`status/status.ts`).** Attempts were listed oldest first and a candidate with more than `limit` attempts never showed its newest one; the 30-line budget was spent on attempts and could cut off the staging line and the cut line itself. **Corrected:** the section above's "one line per attempt … one staging line" happened in that order and could stop before the staging line. Now attempts are newest first, room is kept for the gate lines, the staging line and the cut line, reading stops when the budget is used up, and the cut line no longer tells the owner to name a candidate they already named — it points at `release.attempts` for one candidate. Test: a named candidate with 39 interrupted attempts and one open attempt is answered in exactly 30 lines with the open attempt and the staging line both present.
- **5 — fewer reads, same gate (`release/release.ts`, `status/status.ts`, `api/start.ts`).** `gateAndAttempts(owner, candidateId)` returns the gate and the attempts from one read of the attempt records (the gate is computed by the same `#gateOf` as before, so no gate rule moved), the view takes it when the service offers it and falls back to the two reads when it does not, and the candidate list no longer reads an approval record per row — the gate the view reads anyway says whether a candidate is approved. Tests: `gateAndAttempts` agrees with separate `gate` and `attempts` reads, candidate rows carry no `approved` field, and the view's read counter shows one combined read per candidate.
- **6 — `decisions/records.ts quotedLine` hides nothing (`1471b84b`, `13830b54`).** It escaped C1 controls and the two line separators only; `\p{Cf}` (bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width space, soft hyphen, BOM) and DEL reached the owner's view, a status line and a worker's first prompt alive. **Corrected:** the section above's "every host-, platform-, pointer- and agent-written value goes through `quotedLine` … so none can split a line or forge structure" was only partly true — nothing could split a line, but an invisible character could still reorder or pad what was read. The class is now `[\u007f-\u009f\u2028\u2029\p{Cf}]`; `decisions/quoted-text.test.ts` tests the escaping itself from code points (it fails 0/1 when the class is put back to the old one), and the release view test puts a bidi override, an isolate and a zero-width space into a host's summary and an interrupt reason. Chat, status, activity and decisions suites rerun green.
- **7 — a name is the owner's whole word (`chat/commands.ts`, `chat/chat.ts`).** `foreignValue` compared with `includes`, so an owner saying `host:rig2` authorized `host:rig`, and a shorter release ID hid inside a longer one. IDs that the check looks at (release and maintenance IDs, and `hostId`) must now stand as whole words (`wholeWord`, the same rule the hand-off and grant wording already used); sentences such as a reason or a summary are still compared as text, and record references the check does not look at (a reconnect attempt) stay as they were. The cheap option was taken for `release.host`'s exempt `os`/`arch`: the chat refuses when the owner's message does not name the platform the model asks to authorize. Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (pure), `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (`host:rig2` refuses `host:rig`, the named host and platform are proposed, an unnamed platform is refused).
- **8 — the view on the running controller (`api/start-release-view.test.ts`, `a220fe15`).** One test through `startController`: a candidate whose platform passed only after a failure is labelled flaky, attempts are newest first with what the host said quoted, a platform with no attempt is said rather than left out, the staging line is there, every line cites its records, the answer is bounded, a candidate that is not there and a worker who may not read release records both read `not_found`.
- ASSUMPTION: `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` judges what the message says, not what it argues — the word `flaky` counts even in a question, and these are the same owner words `foreignValue` already trusts; the approval is still a proposal the owner confirms, which is where a misread is caught.
- ASSUMPTION: the candidate scan is bounded at 5000 records (25 pages of 200) rather than unbounded; past that the view says the older candidates were not read and tells the owner to name one, which is honest and keeps the read finite.
- ASSUMPTION: `limit` in the release view counts *candidates*; a candidate's attempts are shown newest first while the 30 lines last, and the rest is read with `release.attempts`.
- ASSUMPTION: `gateAndAttempts` is optional on the view's release dependency, so a caller that supplies only `gate`/`attempts` keeps working and falls back to two reads; gate semantics were not touched.
- ASSUMPTION: `release.host` takes item 7's cheap option — `os` and `arch` must appear as whole words in the owner's message; `active` stays exempt because the proposal shows it either way.
- ASSUMPTION: escaping every `\p{Cf}` character also changes how those characters look in worker prompts and the decision log; nothing that was readable becomes less readable, only text that was invisible becomes visible.
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): full controller package suite (`npm test` in `packages/controller`) 10142 tests, 10138 pass, 0 fail, 4 todo (the pre-existing C07k hand-off size todos); the per-item commands and their counts, including the two mutation runs that were seen to fail, are in the working report `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/x09b-fix-REPORT.md`; `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with no change to it (no operation signature moved).
- Not here: `release.stage` / `release.activate` still have no chat words; the view still shows five candidates by default; paging the *attempt* list of one candidate through the view (rather than by `release.attempts`) is not done.

## X09b part 2 review 2 fixes (Pi): an approval tied to the failures it showed, a host taken off by chat, a format character above the BMP (2026-11-08)

The second independent review of the part 2 work (`4e90317f`) returned six defects. All six are fixed; each was written against a test that was seen to fail first, and two claims made above are corrected here.

- **1 — `acknowledgeFlaky` had to accept something, and be tied to what the owner was shown (`chat/commands.ts`, `chat/chat.ts`, `release/release.ts`, `api/operations.ts`).** Two holes. First, `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` said yes to any sentence containing `flaky`, so "approve rcn-a, the flaky test fixtures are fine", "approve rcn-a. Is rcn-b the flaky one?", "approve rcn-a unless it is flaky", "approve rcn-a if nothing failed" and "approve rcn-a, it isn't flaky" each authorized a release; the negation list was also missing the contractions (`isn't`, `aren't`, `wasn't`, `doesn't`, `didn't`, `hasn't`, `can't`, …). It now needs one sentence that carries an acceptance (`accept`, `acknowledge`, `agree to`, `fine with`, `ok`/`okay with`, `all right with`, `despite`, `waive`) *and* a failure or `flaky`, that is about the candidate being approved (its ID as a whole word, or an "it" straight after the sentence that names it), that asks nothing, conditions nothing and denies nothing; the extended negation list tightens `saysMainAutomatic` the same way. Second, the approval was bound to no set of failures, so a platform retried green between the proposal and the owner's confirmation was approved with a gate nobody had read. The chat now writes the earlier-failure IDs it read from `release.gate` into the approval as a new `expectedFailures` argument — always, `[]` when nothing had failed and passed — and `ReleaseService.approve` refuses when the gate's earlier failures are not exactly those, naming both sets; the owner is shown the gate as it is then and asked again. A gate that cannot be read is refused at proposal time rather than approved unbound. **Corrected:** the ASSUMPTION above that "`saysAcknowledgeFlaky` judges what the message says, not what it argues — the word `flaky` counts even in a question" is dropped: a question about flakiness authorizes nothing. Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (the wordings themselves), `release/release.test.ts` (shown none, shown another ID, shown the right one, and a gate that gained a second failure, every backend), `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (naming `flaky` refused, a question about another candidate refused, an acceptance proposed; then the drift sequence on all four backends: acceptance drawn up while nothing had failed-then-passed, linux retried green, "confirm that approval" refused, asked again with the failure named in the preview, applied).
  - **Superseded in part:** the negation-list sentence about `saysMainAutomatic` no longer applies — that check, and `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` itself, are removed. The `expectedFailures` binding and the gate-drift refusal stand.
- **2 — `quotedLine` corrupted a format character above the BMP (`decisions/records.ts`, `lifecycle/handoff-cut.ts`).** It escaped a `\p{Cf}` match with `c.charCodeAt(0)`, which for a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is the *high surrogate alone*: `U+E0041` (a tag character, invisible by design) came back as `\udb40` followed by the low surrogate left raw in the line, so the escape was a lone surrogate that `JSON.parse` cannot take and the quoted text no longer read back as what the host or agent wrote. The escaping is now one function, `escapeInvisible`, which writes an escape for **each UTF-16 unit** of the match, and `handoff-cut.ts`'s private copy of the same bug is gone (it quotes through `quotedLine` now). Tests: `decisions/quoted-text.test.ts` and `lifecycle/handoff-cut.test.ts`, both built from the code points `0xe0041`, `0xe0001` and `0x1d173` (a tag character, another tag character and a musical beam mark — `\p{Cf}` with the `u` flag matches each as ONE character written in TWO UTF-16 units), with the two halves computed in the test from the code point, so no source file carries an astral character; each asserts the line is printable ASCII, that both escapes appear in order, and that the text survives `JSON.parse` intact.
- **3 — a host taken off the release machines by chat needed no platform (`chat/chat.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`, `release/release.ts`, `api/operations.ts`).** `release.host` with `active: false` asked for `os` and `arch` it does not use, so "withdraw host:rig" from the chat was refused and the service refused a withdrawal that named no platform. Withdrawing now asks for neither, at either layer; a withdrawal of a host that was never authorized is refused with a word about it rather than written as a record. And the platform an owner types is read as they type it — `linux-x64`, `linux/x64`, `mac`/`macOS`/`darwin`, `windows`/`win32`, `x86_64`/`x86-64`/`amd64`/`x64`, `arm64`/`aarch64` — so a natural spelling is no longer refused as "not in your message"; naming no platform of a kind asks for it (an answer counts as the owner's own words, as `runningCalls` and `decisionId` answers already do), and naming a *different* one is refused with what they said. Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (the spellings), `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (withdrawal proposed and applied with no platform named, `mac`/`arm64` accepted, `windows` refused for a darwin host, every backend), `release/release.test.ts` (withdrawal with and without a platform at the service, and a worker refused).
- **4 — the candidate page's bound was one page off (`release/release.ts`).** The scan probed one record past its own bound, so an installation of exactly `CANDIDATE_SCAN` (5000) candidates reported `scanLimited: true` for nothing. Paging is now `scanPages(records, readPage, limit)`: full pages until one comes back short, then one probe; `CANDIDATE_SCAN_PAGE` is exported and the bound is tested from the constants. Tests: `scanPages` alone below, exactly at and one past the bound, an empty store, and `candidates()` at `CANDIDATE_SCAN` (`scanLimited: false`) and one past it (`true`).
- **5 — `candidates()`'s owner check had no service-level test (`release/release.test.ts`).** It was only ever proved through the status view, so a `candidates()` that stopped checking could pass. The service now refuses an agent and a worker directly and still answers the owner.
- **6 — a name joined to punctuation, and these notes (`chat/commands.ts`).** `wholeWord` treated any non-word character as a boundary at the end but required a letter or digit at the start, so an ID written as `**rcn-1a2b**`, `` `rcn-1a2b` ``, `rcn-1a2b:` or `candidate:rcn-1a2b` — the way a client and the view itself write an ID — was refused as "not in your message". A name may now be preceded by punctuation that cannot be part of one, while what joins names is still a letter, a digit, or a dash, underscore, dot or colon with more of the name after it: `host:rig2` is not `host:rig`, `rcn-1a2bc` is not `rcn-1a2b`, `rcn-1a2b_old` is not `rcn-1a2b`. **Corrected here as well:** the claim above that the candidate list returns each candidate "with … a `more` flag" needs the truth of it — `more` is a **boolean**, not a count, saying only that a submitted candidate is not listed; it is exact while `scanLimited` is false. And the part 2 line that `candidates(owner, {limit})` "returns the submitted candidates newest-first with each one's approval state" has not been true since item 5 of the first review round: a candidate row carries no `approved` field at all, and the view takes the approval from the `release.gate` it reads for each listed candidate. `api/start-release-view.test.ts` closes its controller in the `finally`, so a failed assertion no longer leaves the database open.
- ASSUMPTION: the acceptance `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` looks for is one sentence long and about the candidate named in it (or the "it" of the next sentence). An owner who accepts in a roundabout way — "the earlier failures were the flaky network, approve rcn-a" — is refused and told the form of words that works; that is a refusal to approve, never an approval given without one.
- ASSUMPTION: `expectedFailures` is the chat's own reading of `release.gate`, so a value the interpreter writes for it is dropped before the gate is read (as `release.activate` drops a digest the model writes). A direct API caller may still approve a flaky gate with `acknowledgeFlaky` and no `expectedFailures`; the API caller is the owner reading `release.gate` themselves, which is what the argument exists to remember for the chat.
- **Mutation checks** (each applied to the compiled `dist`, run, then restored and rebuilt with `tsc --build --force`): acceptance not required (a sentence naming `flaky` alone returns true) → `chat/release-words.test.ts` fails on "the flaky test fixtures are fine"; the `expectedFailures` comparison removed → both new `release/release.test.ts` suites fail and the chat drift sequence applies the approval; the escape written for `charCodeAt(0)` only → `decisions/quoted-text.test.ts` and `lifecycle/handoff-cut.test.ts` both fail on the astral character. The `scanPages` probe was also mutated (`more` always true) against the bound test, for item 4.
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): full controller package suite (`npm test` in `packages/controller`) 10167 tests, 10163 pass, 0 fail, 4 todo (the pre-existing C07k hand-off size todos); `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` — this time with a change: `release.approve` gained `expectedFailures` and `release.host`/`release.approve` read as described above.
- Not here: `release.stage`/`release.activate` still have no chat words; a direct API approval without `expectedFailures` is still accepted (see the ASSUMPTION); the view still lists five candidates by default.

## X09b part 2 review 3 fixes (Pi): a negation a phone types, and an acceptance that really is one (2026-11-08)

The third independent review of the part 2 work returned four remaining defects in the shared word checks. All four are fixed; each was written against a test that was seen to fail first. D1 and D2 are below; D3 (a message that names two platforms, and the ordinary words that spell one) and D4 (a withdrawal that rewrote a host's platform) are in the section after this one. The drift binding of review 2 item 1 (an approval carrying the earlier failures it showed) was not touched.

- **D1 — the shared negation list only knew the straight apostrophe (`chat/commands.ts`, `9a4040ca`, `9a89fb76`).** `NEGATED` is written with `'` (`don'?t`, `won'?t`, `can'?t`, `is'?n'?t`, …), so a message typed with the curly apostrophe a phone produces slipped past it: "approve the release candidate rcn-X, I don’t accept the earlier failures" with the interpreter's `acknowledgeFlaky: true` was PROPOSED and then applied, while the same sentence with `'` was refused. `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` and `saysMainAutomatic` now normalise `‘ ’ ʼ` (U+2018, U+2019, U+02BC) to `'` before any word check (`plainApostrophes`), which also fixes "don’t send it straight to main" — the same rule `NEGATED` guards. Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (won’t / can’t / don’t / isn’t / donʼt / don‘t in both functions, each against the identical sentence written with `'`); `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (the curly and the straight denial both refused through the real chat with the interpreter's `acknowledgeFlaky`, gate left unapproved, and "I’m fine with the failures that came first" still proposed); `chat/landing-words.test.ts` (new, through `ChatService`: "don’t send it straight to main", "don't …", "we won’t land finished work on main automatically" and "it isn’t automatic to main" each refused by the words check, and the owner's own order "land finished work on main automatically" not stopped by it).
  - **Superseded:** `saysMainAutomatic` and `chat/landing-words.test.ts` are removed — landing on main is a shown proposal now (see "Landing on main with no human step is a shown proposal, not a phrase"). `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` was already removed with its own tests (`ec84768e`).
- **D2 — `saysAcknowledgeFlaky` accepted sentences that accept nothing (`chat/commands.ts`, `0cb240bc`).** Five rules, each with the review's own sentences:
  - **a verb, not a noun.** `accept\w*` / `acknowledg\w*` / `waiv\w*` matched "the **acceptance** suite", "the **acknowledgement** of the failures" and "the **waiver** file". Only the verbs are matched now (accept(s|ed|ing), acknowledge(s|d)?, waive(s|d)?, agree to, fine/ok/all right with, despite, notwithstanding).
  - **no condition.** `FLAKY_CONDITIONAL` had no `once`, `after`, `before`, `until` or `whether`, so "approve rcn-1a2b once QA has accepted the failures", "…only after the failures are acknowledged" and "…ask QA whether they accept its failures" each authorized a release. Those five condition the acceptance when they stand in front of it with nothing closing their clause first — a time clause of its own only describes what happened, so "rcn-1a2b failed before it passed and I accept that" still accepts.
  - **the acceptance belongs to the candidate it sits nearest to.** "approve rcn-1a2b and rcn-9f9f; I accept the failures of rcn-9f9f" accepted for `rcn-1a2b` because the sentence named it somewhere. The acceptance is now bound to the `rcn-` ID nearest to it and counts only when that is the candidate being approved.
  - **a question accepts nothing,** with or without its mark: `[?？]` anywhere in the sentence (so a sentence ending `?!` or typed with a full-width `？` counts), plus the inverted order of an asking sentence typed without any mark — `did|do|does|would|should|could|can|will|shall` followed by a subject ("did you accept the failures", "does QA accept the failures").
  - **whose acceptance it is.** "…, Bob accepted the failures" was the owner's acceptance of nothing. An acceptance is the owner's own when the sentence says I / we / my / our / me / us, or when it names nobody else ahead of the acceptance and simply accepts ("accept the earlier failures", "go ahead despite the failures"); a third-person pronoun, an agent noun (QA, the team, the reviewer, …) or a capitalised name ahead of it makes it that person's acceptance and the chat refuses. The rule is written down in the comment above `FLAKY_FIRST_PERSON`.
  - **D2b, still accepting what owners say.** "approve rcn-1a2b, I accept the earlier failures", "approve rcn-1a2b anyway, I accept that linux failed first", "…go ahead despite the failures", "…acknowledge the flaky pass" and — the part that needed the binding widened — an acceptance in the sentence *after* the candidate was named, with no pronoun in it: "approve rcn-1a2b. Yes accept the earlier failures". **Corrected here:** the review-2 ASSUMPTION that the acceptance is "about the candidate named in it (or the 'it' of the next sentence)" is now the precise rule instead — a sentence that carries the acceptance and names no candidate belongs to the candidate of the sentence before it, and a sentence naming several candidate IDs binds to the nearest one. The doc comment above `FLAKY_WORD`, which still listed the word `flaky` and "I know it failed first, go ahead" as acceptance, says the opposite now: naming or knowing about a flaky pass accepts nothing, as the code has done since review 2 item 1.
  Tests: `chat/release-words.test.ts` (a true/false table of every wording above plus the nearest-candidate and previous-sentence bindings) and `chat/release-owner-words.test.ts` (the other-candidate acceptance, "did you accept the failures", "Bob accepted the failures", "once QA has accepted the failures" and "the acceptance suite failed on linux first" each refused through the chat with the gate left unapproved, and the acceptance in the sentence after the candidate's name proposed).
- **The interpreter's `expectedFailures` is now tested, not just believed (`chat/release-owner-words.test.ts`, `17840de4`).** The chat drops the argument before reading the gate, writes the earlier-failure IDs it just read into the approval when the owner acknowledged a flaky pass, and writes none when they did not — nothing proved it. A flaky candidate approved with an invented attempt ID is now proposed with the gate's own ID in the preview and no trace of the invented one, and the owner's confirmation applies it (had the invented list been kept, `ReleaseService.approve` would have refused the approval as a gate that had changed); a clean candidate approved with `acknowledgeFlaky: false` and the same invented list is applied too, which is only possible because the list was dropped.
- **Mutation checks** (each applied to the compiled `dist`, run against `chat/release-words.test.js` or `chat/release-owner-words.test.js`, then restored and rebuilt): the always-conditional rule removed, the time-condition rule removed, the question rule removed, the nearest-candidate binding removed, the owner's-own-mouth rule removed, the acceptance verbs put back to `\w*` nouns, the previous-sentence binding put back to the pronoun-only rule, and the apostrophe normalisation removed — each fails a test; `delete args["expectedFailures"]` removed from `chat.ts` fails the clean-candidate assertion on all four backends, and the refill line removed fails the flaky approval and review 2's drift sequence.
- ASSUMPTION: the acceptance rules are heuristics over owner English, and each of the new ones errs towards refusing — a refusal to approve, with the form of words that works read back to the owner, never an approval given on a guess. A first-person sentence with somebody else's acceptance inside it ("Bob accepted them and I accept them too") reads as the owner's own; a third-party acceptance whose subject is written after the verb ("the failures were accepted by QA") reads as nobody's, and is caught by the question or condition rule when it is phrased as one.
- ASSUMPTION: normalising `’ ‘ ʼ` is limited to the two word checks that read the owner's intent (`saysAcknowledgeFlaky`, `saysMainAutomatic`); `durationInWords` already had its own narrower normalisation and was left as it is.
  - **Superseded:** both of those word checks are removed — accepting a flaky pass and landing on main are shown proposals now, not wording questions. Nothing is lost by dropping the shared normalisation: the word checks that remain carry their own apostrophe handling (`DENIAL` and `platformsNamed` match `don't` and `don’t`, `policy-edit.ts` has `CURLY`, `durationInWords` and `wholeWord` never needed it).
- **Left open (deliberately, not fixed here):** an ID embedded in a URL still counts as the owner's own whole word — `wholeWord` takes the `/` of `https://nn.example/candidates/rcn-1a2b` as a boundary, so a link pasted into the message names that candidate (it does not by itself approve anything: `acknowledgeFlaky` and the proposal still need the owner's words). And `timed_out` or `interrupted` attempts before a pass are **not** earlier failures: the gate's `earlierFailures` are the attempts whose reported state is `failed`, so a platform that timed out twice and then passed is not flaky and needs no `acknowledgeFlaky` — by design, since those attempts carry no host-reported failure to accept; the release view still lists them.
- **Runs** (that batch, this worktree, `npx tsc --build`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; the sweep line below supersedes these counts): `dist/chat/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/decisions/*.test.js dist/release/*.test.js dist/lifecycle/*.test.js dist/activity/*.test.js dist/api/*.test.js` — 2396 tests, 2392 pass, 0 fail, 4 todo (the pre-existing C07k hand-off size todos); `chat/release-words.test.js` + `chat/release-owner-words.test.js` 34 pass / 0 fail; `chat/landing-words.test.js` 4 pass / 0 fail; `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with no change to it (no operation signature moved). Counts and commands are in `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/x09b-fix3a-REPORT.md`.

## X09b part 2 review 3, second batch (Pi): two platforms in one message, and a withdrawal that names none (2026-11-08)

The same third review's items D3 and D4, both about the platform an owner's words name for `release.host`. Both are fixed, each against a test that was seen to fail first.

- **D3 — `mac` and `windows` are ordinary words, so a message could name a platform it never meant (`chat/commands.ts`, `736cd4f1`; `chat/chat.ts`, `bf6bcd1f`).** Three things, all in the owner's words:
  - **a denied platform names nothing.** "let host:rig run release tests for linux x64, **not the mac**" with the model's `os: darwin` was proposed. A plain negative (`not`, `no`, `never`, `neither`, `nor`, `except`, `without`, `instead of`, `other than`, `rather than`, exclude/avoid and the contractions with either apostrophe) within its own clause and within 30 characters of the alias takes that name away; the same message still names linux, so the refusal reads "Your own words say os \"linux\", not \"darwin\"".
  - **an ordinary word that merely spells a platform names nothing.** "…on linux x64, its **MAC address** is on the sticker" with `os: darwin` was proposed; `mac` followed by "address"/"addresses" is a printed number, not macOS. Other spellings of the owner's own mac are untouched ("my mac", "mac mini", "macOS").
  - **two platforms of one kind is a question, not a choice.** "…on linux **arm64**; the old one was **x64**" with `arch: x64` was proposed, and "on **mac or linux**" with `os: darwin` likewise. `platformsNamed(words, key)` returns the platforms of that kind the message names (denials and ordinary words excluded), and the chat refuses with both of them named — "which arch is `host:old` authorized for (x64, arm64)?" — instead of taking the interpreter's. Naming none of a kind is still the question it was, and naming one that is not the model's is still refused with what the owner said.
- **D4 — a withdrawal rewrote the platform on the host's record (`chat/chat.ts`, `bf6bcd1f`).** "stop letting host:yard run release tests" reached `release.host` with the model's `{active: false, os: "darwin", arch: "arm64"}`, review 2 had stopped asking the owner for a platform it does not need, and `ReleaseService.authorizeHost` takes a named cell as the platform to write: the machine came off the list with darwin/arm64 recorded for it. A withdrawal now carries no `os` or `arch` unless the owner's own words name them — the model's are dropped from the command before it is drawn up, so the record keeps the platform its authorization on record names. A platform the owner did say on a withdrawal is kept ("stop letting host:box run release tests on linux x64"), and one their words contradict (`os: win32` in that same message) is refused rather than dropped or sent. An authorization (`active` not false) still asks for a platform it cannot guess, so it is never silently sent without one.
- **What an approval carries is read from its own arguments (`chat/release-owner-words.test.ts`, `df2b797f`).** The behaviour was already there and the owner's view of it was tested; what the test did not say outright is the proposal's own `steps[0].args` — the earlier-failure IDs replaced by the chat's reading of `release.gate`, and no `expectedFailures` key at all when the owner's words acknowledge nothing.
- **Mutation checks** (applied to `src`, `npx tsc --build`, run, then restored and rebuilt): `DENIAL` and the "mac address" rule removed → the new word tests fail; the platform refill (`args["expectedFailures"] = shown`) removed → the new assertion fails on all four backends with the approval going out carrying no earlier failures at all. A withdrawal whose `os`/`arch` are not dropped was proved by the D3/D4 chat suite failing before the fix (`proposed` where a refusal was required, and the interpreter's `os` still in the stored proposal).
- ASSUMPTION: a denial counts only inside its own clause and within 30 characters of the name, so "linux, not windows; the mac mini is the one" still names the mac — the reading that keeps the owner's affirmative. A platform named twice, once denied and once not, counts where it was said.
- **Still left open, unchanged from the batch above:** an ID embedded in a URL still counts as the owner's own whole word (`wholeWord` takes the `/` of `https://nn.example/candidates/rcn-1a2b` as a boundary), and `timed_out` or `interrupted` attempts before a pass are **not** earlier failures — the gate's `earlierFailures` are the attempts whose reported state is `failed`, by design, since they carry no host-reported failure to accept; the release view still lists them. Nothing in this batch changed either.
- **Runs** (this batch, `npx tsc --build`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): the sweep of `dist/chat/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/decisions/*.test.js dist/release/*.test.js dist/lifecycle/*.test.js dist/activity/*.test.js dist/api/*.test.js` — 2402 tests, 2398 pass, 0 fail, 4 todo (the same pre-existing C07k hand-off size todos); `chat/release-words.test.js` 8 pass / 0 fail; `chat/release-owner-words.test.js` 32 pass / 0 fail; `chat/chat.test.js` + `chat/release-words.test.js` + `chat/host-move-words.test.js` + `chat/landing-words.test.js` 117 pass / 0 fail; `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with no change to it (no operation signature moved). Counts and commands are in `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/x09b-fix3b-REPORT.md`.

## A grant with no limit or no end is a proposal that says so, not a phrase (Pi, 2026-11-09)

`chat/policy-edit.ts` had two keyword gates on the terms of an approval grant. `NO_LIMIT_WORDS` scanned the owner's own message for `no limit`, `no cap`, `as much as it wants`, `unlimited` and nineteen other spellings, and `NO_END_WORDS` for `no end`, `permanent`, `forever`, `until I revoke it` and their neighbours; each read sentence by sentence through `saysWords` (negation, question, musing, a quote inside the sentence). Without a match, `spendLimit: null` and `lengthDays: null` were refused (`needs_limit`, `needs_end`) and the refusal told the owner what to say: `Say the limit, or say there is none.`, `Say how long, or say it has no end.` Free-form chat cannot work that way — the interpreter, not a phrase table, decides which operation the owner asked for — so a phrase test is a magic word with the owner blamed for not knowing it. This is the same fault fixed on the flaky release approval (`c4f023a6`, `ec84768e`), on landing on main (`56ce51b1`) and in the brief's Owner decision of 2026-10-28 ("no magic words"), and it is fixed the same way.

- **What was removed (`chat/policy-edit.ts`).** `NO_LIMIT_WORDS`, `NO_LIMIT_CLAUSE`, `NO_END_WORDS`, `NO_END_CLAUSE`, the two `prepare()` gates and the `needs_limit` / `needs_end` refusal codes. Nothing else in `prepare()` changed: the grantee, tool, class, environment, audience and amount invention guards are kept (an ID or figure the owner never gave is still not the chat's to invent), as is the `evidenceInText` quotation check. `saysWords` is kept for one caller, `ordersHostMove`, which asks whether the owner *ordered* work moved off a quiet host — a different question, still open, listed below.
- **The consequence is a term of the grant, and it is on the proposal (`#grant`).** `spendLimit: null` draws up a grant with `spendUnlimited: true`; `lengthDays: null` one with `permanent: true`. Their lines say what happens rather than what was said: `Spend limit: none. This grant has no spending limit; it can pay any amount the work asks for, however large.` and `This grant has no end: it never runs out on its own and stays until you revoke it.` `chooseGrantLength`'s reasons, which used to claim the owner had asked for it ("you asked for it to have no end"), now describe the record ("nothing in it expires by itself", "it is drawn up to end `<iso>`"), because on `apply_proposal` the wording being read is the confirmation, not the original ask. The consequence sits in the first line the owner is shown, in the proposal's `preview`/`explanation`, in the stored `summary` and in the grant's recorded `basis`, so it cannot be truncated away or added after the fact.
- **Nothing is applied without the confirmation, in any approval profile.** A grant has always been "loosening", so it is shown first in `strict`, `derived` and `autonomous` alike; the message that asked for it never applies it. `chat/grant-consequence.test.ts` (new, four backends) walks each profile: an ordinary sentence ("Rex keeps stopping to ask me about payments. Let Rex pay for what the work needs and do not put a ceiling on it.") produces the proposal, nothing is held, and only the owner's confirmation of *that* proposal (`apply_proposal`, with the ID the interpreter chose) writes the grant. The no-end suite does the same for "Make it a standing thing so I am not asked again", adds the owner's no ("No, that is more than I wanted." → discarded, nothing held), an interpreter that reads a flat denial backwards, and a question about it: shown or asked, never applied.
- **What a grant is missing is asked, not demanded (`#grant`).** A spending grant with no ceiling stated asks `How much may Rex spend under this grant — a figure, or no ceiling at all?`; a send or publication with no audience asks `Sending out is granted per account and audience: which account or audience may Rex send to?`. Both go through the existing ask mechanism, `status: "asked"`, with no options list — there is nothing to say back, an answer in ordinary words is read by the interpreter like any other. The guard messages that stayed were reworded from `Say how long.` / `Say the limit.` / `Say which environments.` into the question they were always asking ("How long should the grant last?"); their refusal codes (`invalid_length`, `unsupported_value`) are unchanged.
- **What is still guarded, and why that is not a phrase gate.** A length must be a length the owner gave (`lengthInWords`), a spend figure a figure they gave (`amountInWords`), an environment one they named (`platformChoices`/`wholeWord`), a grantee or tool one that appears in their message (`foreignValue`/`wholeWord`). Each refuses a *value the model invented*, and answers with a question. `chat/grant-consequence.test.ts` proves the invention guards survive the change: `lengthDays: 40` and `spendLimit: 9999` the owner never said are still refused, and the refusal ends in a question mark, not a sentence to copy.
- **Nothing the owner is shown may dictate wording (`chat/grant-consequence.test.ts`).** Every message, question, preview and explanation line the tests produce is run against a list of phrase-instruction shapes: `for example "`, an imperative to say a thing (`say the limit`, `say how much`, …), `only … when your own message says so`, `your own words must`, `as you said`, `use the words`. A statement that the owner did *not* say something ("you did not say how long, so the 30-day default is used") is a fact about the record, not an instruction, and is excluded on purpose.
- **Three other owner-facing lines that dictated a sentence (`chat/chat.ts`, `chat/policy-edit.ts`).** No project in focus asks `Which project do you mean?` instead of ordering the owner to say it (four refusals; nothing there reads their wording for a project name). A shown proposal is offered as its two outcomes (`Edit pedit-… waits for your word: apply it, or discard it?`) instead of `say to apply it, or to discard it`. A stale policy edit asks to be asked again. Tests: `chat/status.test.ts` updated; the proposal line and the stale line are asserted nowhere by phrase, so no other expectation moved.
- **Left alone on purpose, and recorded.** Several more `Say `/`for example "` lines are still in the controller, each backed by a check that reads the owner's words, where softening the message would only hide why it was refused: `routing.drain` (`durationInWords`) and the `wholeWord`/`foreignValue` "say it exactly" refusals, the host-platform refusals that name the platforms their message did name, and `remote/quiet-hosts.ts`, which tells the owner to say `move the work off <host>` because `ordersHostMove` really does require the order and the host in their words. The meeting-decision `for example "` refusals are already fixed on main by `c42bbe67` and were deliberately not re-done here. Each of these needs the same proposal treatment as its own card.
- **Review fix: the chat's `grant.create` phrase gate (`chat/chat.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`).** It demanded "give <who> the <action> right everywhere permanently" through a leftover-word scan and `/permanently/`, `/everywhere/` checks, in the free-form chat path (the interpreter emits `grant.create` as an ordinary command). Removed: the right is a proposal in every profile, and `describe` now states on it `no end: it never runs out and stays until you revoke it` and, for `project: "*"`, `everywhere: it covers every project, including ones made later`. A missing scope asks `Which project should this right cover, or should it cover every project?`. `api/start-chat.test.ts` now drives a hedge, a dropped time limit, an ordinary sentence, no "permanently", and a scope said about something else: each is proposed with both consequences shown, grants nothing, and the owner's no discards it.
- **Second review fix: a right's project, named in ordinary words, and said first (`chat/chat.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`).** A right scoped to a project the owner named by its name ("let service:scanner do recovery.stall-scan in Garden") was refused with "a right names its scope as `project`: a project ID, or * for everywhere", i.e. the owner had to give an ID. `projectName` is now resolved for `grant.create` like everywhere else: it must stand as a whole word of the owner's message (so "Gardening" is not "Garden"), the project with exactly that name is the scope, several with that name are asked about, and a name together with a different `project` (for example `*`) asks which scope was meant instead of picking one. The `grant.create` line also states a single project in its leading parenthesis (`no end …; only in "Garden"`), as it states `everywhere` for `*`, so the scope is said before the names and the basis and a cut line cannot hide where the right reaches. Tests: `api/start-chat.test.ts` (named project proposed, applied, reaches only that project; part of a longer word refused; two scopes asked), `chat/commands-preview.test.ts` (a cut line still names the project).
- ASSUMPTION: the interpreter's `spendLimit: null` / `lengthDays: null` is treated as a *proposed term*, not as consent, because nothing can be applied from an interpreter's field alone — a grant is shown first in every profile, so the worst an invented `null` can do is put a proposal in front of the owner that says plainly what it would do. No `expected*` binding of the confirmation to a snapshot is added: a grant carries its own terms and its own default end, and a proposal the owner confirms is applied with the terms it showed. If a later review wants the confirmation bound to the records read at proposal time (the way a flaky approval is bound to its failure IDs), that is a small follow-on.

## Landing on main with no human step is a shown proposal, not a phrase (Pi, 2026-11-09)

The last phrase gate on an owner's release-side choice in chat. `chat/commands.ts` had `saysMainAutomatic(words)` (line 239), which looked in the owner's own message for `main automatic(ally)`, `automatic to/onto main` or `straight/directly to main` in a sentence carrying no negation; `chat.ts` refused any `landing: "main-automatic"` its interpreter sent unless that matched, and the refusal told the owner what to say: `only when your own message says so (for example "land finished work on main automatically")`. Free-form chat cannot work that way: the owner says what they want in their own words and the interpreter picks the operation, so a phrase test is a magic word with the owner blamed for not knowing it. This is the same fault the flaky release approval was fixed for (`c4f023a6`, `ec84768e`, whose own record went into its report file rather than here), and it is fixed the same way.

- **What the gate really guarded (`chat/chat.ts`, `chat/commands.ts`).** `landing` is a fixed choice, so `foreignValue` never required it to be in the owner's words (`EXEMPT`); `saysMainAutomatic` was the only thing standing between an interpreter that invented `main-automatic` and the project's record. Removing it without a replacement would have left the model's guess free to promote work to main with no human step, so the replacement is the proposal itself, not another wording test.
- **The operation is now a shown proposal that states its own consequence (`chat/commands.ts`).** `LANDING_MEANS` says, for every landing the policy accepts, what happens to the owner's work — for `main-automatic`, "finished work goes to main by itself once its required checks pass, with no human step". `describe()` puts that sentence in the proposal line before the field names, so a long project name can never push the consequence off the line, and it is the same table `#integrationQuestion` reads when it asks how a new project should land, so the question and the proposal cannot drift apart. `project.create`'s `integration` section is now rendered as the settings it holds rather than a JSON blob. `proposalReason` gained a landing-specific reason ("finished work would go to main by itself with no human step, so this is shown first for you to confirm") instead of falling through to the role-capabilities wording it used to inherit; `integration.set`, `integration.default.set` and a drafted `project.create` with that landing are shown first in every profile, `strict` through `autonomous` included.
- **What the owner is shown is read from the records, never from the model (`chat/chat.ts`).** When the landing offered is `main-automatic`, the proposal carries a note naming what gates the automatic promotion — the `requiredChecks` given, or those on the project's own integration record read there and then — and whether the installation lock (`forbidMainAutomatic`) stands, in which case the owner is told the change will be refused while it does. So the confirmation is bound to facts, the way a flaky approval is bound to the failures it listed. `landing` itself is not a consent flag the chat can drop: it *is* the value being set, and the guard on a wrong one is the owner's no.
- **Nothing is applied without the confirmation, in any wording (`chat/landing-proposal.test.ts`, new, four backends).** An ordinary sentence ("Garden's finished work should stop waiting on me — get it onto main by itself once the checks pass") yields a proposal whose text says the consequence and names the project's checks, and the record is unchanged until the owner confirms *that* proposal. An interpreter that guesses `main-automatic` from "make Garden's landing as quick as you can", or reads a flat denial ("don't ever put Garden's work on main without me asking first") backwards, gets the same treatment: shown, stated plainly, and no record touched; the owner's "no" discards it. A question about it applies nothing. With the installation lock on, the proposal says it will be refused, and confirming it is refused with the lock named — not with a phrase to say. Every outcome the owner sees is asserted not to tell them to word anything in a particular way (no "for example", no "your own words say/say so", no "only set when", no quoted example wording).
- **The old assertions are replaced, not deleted (`api/start-integration.test.ts`).** What used to be "a vague or negated sentence is refused, a plain one passes the words check" is now the rule that actually holds: any wording produces the same shown proposal, and none of them — order, denial, negation or look-alike — applies anything until the owner confirms that one. `chat/release-words.test.ts` keeps the whole-word ID and platform evidence checks and loses its phrase tests.
- **Operation summary and prompt table (`api/operations.ts`, `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md`).** `integration.set`, `integration.default.set` and `project.create`'s `integration` argument now say what the chat shows and that the owner's confirmation of the shown proposal applies it; nothing in them tells the owner (or the interpreter) to use a particular form of words. `npm run api:docs:write` regenerated `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with those three changes and no other.
- **Superseded entries marked above:** the P08b `SAYS_MAIN_AUTOMATIC`/`saysMainAutomatic` bullets, P08c's "picking it from the list counts as saying it", review 2's negation-list sentence about `saysMainAutomatic`, the D1 apostrophe bullet (`chat/landing-words.test.ts`) and the ASSUMPTION that limited the curly-apostrophe normalisation to those two word checks. The `precheck`, installation-lock, `heldFrom`, `expectedFailures` and gate-drift parts of those same entries all stand.
- ASSUMPTION: `landing` needs no replacement consent flag and no `expected*` binding of its own. The proposal is a settings write the owner confirms, the checks it names are read at proposal time for information, and if the project's checks change in between the landing the owner confirmed is still the landing they agreed to — `main-automatic` already cannot be stored with no required check at all (`policy/integration-policy.ts`), and the installation lock is re-checked by the service when the proposal is applied, so a lock imposed in between still refuses it. If a later review wants the confirmation bound to the exact settings shown, the way a flaky approval is bound to its failure IDs, that is a small follow-on: bind `integration.set` to the record's `expectedRevision`.
- **The other owner-facing messages that told the owner what to say (`chat.ts`, same sweep).** Every refusal and question in `chat/chat.ts` and `chat/commands.ts` was read. Fixed here, where no check depends on the wording it illustrated: the four meeting-decision `instead(...)` messages, which used `say what you decide instead as its own sentence (for example "Keep the staging server until May.")` and `(for example: topic staging server)` — they now say what is missing and that the owner's own words are wanted; the suite asserts the new wording and that no such refusal dictates a phrase. Left as they are, because softening the message while the check behind it still reads the owner's words would hide why they were refused (each needs the same proposal treatment as its own card, not a reword): `routing.drain` (`durationInWords` must find the owner's own length; the refusal quotes "drain it over the next hour"), `grant.create` in chat (a leftover-word scan, `/\bpermanently\b/` and `/\b(everywhere|all projects|every project)\b/` on the owner's message, with refusals that dictate `give <who> the <action> right everywhere permanently`), and `release.host`'s platform refusals and the `wholeWord`/`foreignValue` "say it exactly" refusals, which are the allowed ID-invention guards naming fixed choices or a name the owner must supply. `chat/shorthand.ts` and the typed-command JSON example are command lines, not free-form chat, so their syntax examples stand.
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): the sweep of `dist/chat/*.test.js dist/release/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/api/*.test.js` — 1632 tests, 1632 pass, 0 fail, 0 todo; the files this change touches, measured together (`chat/landing-proposal.test.js`, `chat/release-words.test.js`, `chat/release-owner-words.test.js`, `api/start-integration.test.js` and all of `dist/release/*.test.js`) — 205 pass / 0 fail; `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` — 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with no further change after the three entries above. One honest note on the first sweep: it reported 4 failures, all of them the *orphaned compiled* `dist/chat/landing-words.test.js` (its source was deleted in this batch and `tsc --build` does not remove the output of a deleted source); removing that stale file and rebuilding gave the counts above. Counts and commands are in Pi's `REPORT.md` for this change (kept out of the tree).

## M03h part 1 (Pi): a status view of the stand-ups themselves, and chat that reaches a stand-up before it has met (2026-11-08)

The card asked for two things: the owner's chat reaching a stand-up — prepare it now, read its brief, leave a note for an agent — and a `standups` status view. The three controls were already in `CHAT_OPS` and the meeting-side view already listed stand-ups among a project's meetings, so what was left was the view that answers "what stand-ups does this project have?" and, once that was written, the reach: the owner's words could not name the stand-up they were most likely to name, one set up this morning.

- **`standups` answers from the schedules (`standups/standups.ts`, `status/status.ts`, `3f98d6d5`).** `StandupService.overview` tells every stand-up a project has set up — whether it is active, paused or ended, how often and at what time it is held, how long it lasts and how wide its window is, who is on its roster, how many meetings it has made, the one coming up next and how the last one ended. Unlike `recent`, which knows a stand-up only through an occurrence and leaves one that has not met out of the list, a stand-up waiting for its first meeting is shown, and the one with a meeting ahead is told first. Ended ones are counted and left out unless asked for. The view is two lines each: the schedule as set (its title quoted, because an agent that set one up wrote it), then its meetings. The right to it is the right to read the project's meetings, so a readable project with none is answered "No stand-up is set up in this project." rather than with nothing at all, and a roster longer than ten is listed to ten and counted after. `STATUS_KINDS.standups`, the `status.ask` summary and `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` name the kind; the interpreter's prompt is drawn from those tables, so the model is told it exists, and the chat takes the project for it from the focus as it does for the other project views.
- **Reaching the stand-up the owner named (`chat/chat.ts`, `c740fbaf`, `426b8227`).** Preparing, noting on and reading all looked the owner's words up in `standup.recent`. A project with two stand-ups waiting for their first meeting therefore answered "no stand-up in this project can be prepared now" — untrue of a project that has two — and asking what one of them had briefed answered that its name fits nothing, in a project that has exactly that stand-up. All three now start from the project's schedules through one read (`#standupTitles`: every stand-up, ended ones left out, in one order so a list the owner reads does not shift between answers), and the three ways the chat had of listing them were joined into one phrase (`5e2363fa`). Words that fit one of them are answered about that stand-up ("… is set up in this project but has no meeting to prepare right now") instead of being asked which one they meant; words that fit none are refused with the titles the project has, quoted; a stand-up that has ended is not named as one the project runs. The meeting worked on is still the one the records say it is — the planned one, or, when it has passed unprepared, the last, so a catch-up still works — and an agent who is not on that stand-up is still refused rather than answered with someone else's brief, with the owner's note coming back on the read-back as the owner's own words.
- **Tests.** `standups/standups.test.ts`: the new read on four backends — a stand-up that has not met shown where `recent` leaves it out, the next and last meetings and their revisions cited, the roster and window as set, the limit paging and `more`, ended ones counted and hidden until asked for, rights (a manager of another project and an agenda writer without the meeting read see nothing), a readable project with none answering empty, and a bad limit refused. `status/status.test.ts`: the two lines word for word, what each cites, a title with a quote in it, a twelve-strong roster cut to ten plus a count, an end date told, the ended count, the empty answers, rights, and the kind refused with a key it does not take. `chat/standup-commands.test.ts`: three suites of ordinary sentences — "what stand-ups do we have", "can you get the morning one ready", "tell the morning agent: the demo is at four", "what did the Friday review brief say" — with the project taken from the focus, an invented stand-up and an invented agent refused, another project's note refused, and a name that fits two asking. Nothing scans the owner's text for a word: the model's `meetingTopic` and `agentName` are still checked against the owner's own words, and every sentence the chat says about a stand-up uses the title from the records, quoted.
- **Still open in this card, untouched here:** the usage sink; an owner's question raised by a stand-up; an agenda outcome that asks the owner a new question; an end-to-end controller test with every sink fitted; and the per-project stand-up index — `list`, `recent` and `overview` all still scan every stand-up record of the installation, which is why `overview` shares `recent`'s paging note rather than promising a cheap read.
- ASSUMPTION: the view shows ten stand-ups and ten roster names, and the read behind it defaults to twenty (at most fifty); more are counted in the answer rather than squeezed into it, because the owner is reading this in a chat reply, and a narrower ask (`limit`) is honoured up to twenty-five.
- **Runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `dist/chat/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/api/*.test.js dist/meetings/*.test.js dist/standups/*.test.js` — 2063 tests, 2063 pass, 0 fail; `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with the `standups` kind named in `status.ask`. Counts and commands are in `REPORT.md` on `pi-m03h-chat`.

## Chat: a proposal line quotes the names it borrows, so no one else's text can forge a second line (Pi, 2026-11-09)

The line the owner is asked to confirm is `describe()`'s (card U03). Two earlier rounds made the line's **values** safe (`4fe056ae`, `6c8229ed`): everything shown bare goes through `short()`, which folds breaks, writes controls, `\p{Cf}` characters and half surrogate pairs as escapes, and cuts only between whole characters and whole escapes; the line's own cut stopped splitting a surrogate pair. What was left was the text the line **borrows**, which was interpolated raw — and that borrowed text is written by someone else: an agent, or the interpreter.

- **What was raw, and what could really reach it (`chat/commands.ts`, `6257697a`).** `labels[value]` was printed as `taskId="<title>"` with the label untouched, and the alternative to a meeting decision as `alternative="<statement>" on topic "<topic>"`. The labels are built in `chat.ts` out of records: a project's name (763, 792, 798, 803), an agenda item's topic (838), a stand-up's title (852, 868), a waiting decision's wording (947), an agent's name and `…'s brief` (987, 1030, 1063, 1158, 1206), a stand-up meeting's title and time (1015), a task's title and a prerequisite's (1195, 1201), and a maintenance request's description (1281). The record checks (`domain/model.ts` `text()`) refuse C0 controls, DEL and lone surrogates but **accept U+2028/2029, the C1 controls and every `\p{Cf}` character**, so a title an agent wrote could carry a bidirectional override that reorders the rest of the owner's line, or a C1 CSI that reaches a terminal as an escape sequence. The interpreter's own text is bounded by length alone: the alternative's statement and topic, a grant's `expiresAt`, an argument's own name and an unknown operation name are not record text, and a message is checked for length only. Three smaller holes sat beside them: a right's end time (`grant.create`'s ` (ends …)`), the argument names (`${key}=`) and the `spec?.verb ?? op` fallback.
- **The rule now.** Every text a proposal line prints goes through exactly one escaping helper — `short()` for a value shown bare, `quoted()` (card U09, `status/explain.ts`) for text shown between quotes, the same helper the chat already quotes a task title or a stand-up title with in its questions and options. Labels, the alternative's statement (150 characters) and its topic (80) — the bounds the chat accepts them within, so what is shown whole is what would be recorded — argument names, an unknown operation name and an end time are all shown through one of them. A name is bounded by the line's own room rather than a shorter cap of its own: `chat.ts` builds some labels out of several fields of one record in a deliberate order (1278: install scripts, digest, version, then name, site and source), so a 200-character quotation bound hid the source a maintenance proposal was showing — the first run of `api/start-maintenance.test.ts` failed on exactly that, and the bound is `CHAT_LIMITS.line` so the line's own cut stays the only trim.
- **What is shown is still what is set.** `quoted()` folds whitespace and cuts credential-shaped runs out, as every shown text in this product does (`shown`/`quoted`, card U09). For a label that is a display name, so nothing is misquoted; for the alternative, which *is* what would be recorded, the owner's whole message is refused when it carries a credential shape (`refuseCredentials`, `chat.ts:237`) and the statement must be a substring of that message, so the redaction has nothing to cut and an accepted 150-character statement is still shown whole (the test says so outright). Nothing is escaped twice: each text passes one helper here and the preview is stored and joined as it is, never escaped again — and a test asserts no doubled backslash, which is what a second pass would leave.
- **Tests (`chat/commands-one-line.test.ts`, new, `d796d14a`).** Several operations named by a record (task update, transition, budget raise, agent update, stand-up prepare and note, project update, workspace request, grant, landing), each with a name carrying a newline, U+2028, U+202E, U+200B, a lone surrogate and an emoji: one line, no raw control or invisible format character, no half character, no half escape, no doubled backslash; a `"` inside a name cannot close the quotation and invent a field; the alternative is quoted and whole; a long name is swept across its own bound and the line's with an emoji and an escaped override at the cut. One turn through the real `ChatService` on four backends titles a task with U+2028, U+202E and U+200B (all of which the record checks accept) and reads the proposal back escaped once. All seven fail against the previous `commands.ts` (proved by stashing the fix, rebuilding and rerunning).
- ASSUMPTION: a line or paragraph separator inside a name is folded to a space rather than written as an escape, because both helpers already fold whitespace and the owner reads one line either way; writing it out as well would be a display change with no safety gain. A name's cap is the line's own room (400), not a tighter bound of its own, for the label-composition reason above.
- **Still open, the same fault elsewhere in the chat's own words (`chat.ts`).** The which-one questions and refusals still interpolate record text raw: an agenda topic (833), a stand-up's title (868), an inquiry's question (888), a meeting's title (1054), a watched task's title (1092) and the `More than one task is called "…"` wordings (819, 1092). Other places in the same file already quote through `quotedText` (453, 479, 486, 997, 1008, 2027), so the rule exists but is not applied everywhere. These are questions rather than proposals the owner confirms, so they were left for their own pass with tests rather than changed here.
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `dist/chat/*.test.js dist/status/*.test.js dist/api/*.test.js` — 1528 tests, 1528 pass, 0 fail, 0 todo (146 s); `chat/commands-one-line.test.js` alone — 7 pass / 0 fail, and 7 fail / 0 pass against the pre-fix `commands.ts`; `chat/landing-proposal.test.js` + `chat/commands-preview.test.js` — 29 pass / 0 fail; `api/start-maintenance.test.js` — 3 pass / 0 fail; `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` — 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with no change to it. Counts and commands are in Pi's `REPORT.md` for this change (kept out of the tree).
- **Review (Opus, 2026-11-09).** Two holes fixed with tests that fail without them: the line's own final cut (`cutAt` in `describe()`) was pair-safe but not escape-safe, so a long line could end `\u{20...` or `\u20...` or `\...`; it now steps back to the start of any escape it would split (`chat/commands.ts`, swept across the bound in `commands-one-line.test.ts`). And the coordinator's plan note `"<title>" is not assigned`, which joins the owner's decompose proposal preview, printed the coordinator model's title raw; it is quoted through `quotedText` now (`chat/coordinator.ts`, `coordinator.test.ts`; a plain title reads exactly as before). Runs: chat/status/api 1528 / 1528 pass; plan 6 / 6; roadmap ok.

## C07m (Pi): the first call of an attempt says what the task was handed with — the hand-off, the note before it, and what holds it up (2026-11-09)

C07l left three checks `todo` in `dispatch/first-call-hops.test.ts`, and they said the same thing three ways: an agent started on a task it was handed was told nothing of the hand-off. The package (brief, acceptance criteria, decisions, unfinished work, next action) is readable only through `handoff.get`, which no call named; the controller wrote a hand-off note when an attempt ended without one and never gave it to anyone (`context/enforcement.ts` had a `latestHandoff` with no production reader at all); and an open blocker was in neither. The card asked for the first call to name the latest hand-off package, the controller's hand-off note for the previous attempt and the task's open blockers — bounded or escaped, **or by ID with the operation that reads them**. That is what was taken: the call names the records, it does not carry them.

- **One bounded paragraph, built apart from the dispatcher (`dispatch/handoff-brief.ts`, `handoffBrief`, `c2dc7a95`).** It is a bracketed block of its own — so the worker's resume note still lands last — of at most `HANDOFF_BRIEF_LIMITS.chars` (1500), with a heading that says it is the controller's record and not an instruction. One line names the hand-off the task arrived in (`hnd-…`) and says to read the package with `handoff.get`; one names the note the attempt before left (`hof-…`, whose `source` the line quotes as the controller's or the attempt's own) and says to read it with `context.handoff.read`; one lists the task's open blockers with their IDs, their type, who can resolve them and a quoted summary, and (since the review below) says the owner's task status view holds the whole list, which the task credential may not open. Nothing is dropped in silence: more than five blockers and the line says how many are not shown, and if the summaries will not fit the bound they are shortened and, past that, the IDs go out alone. Every person-written text goes through `quoted` (one line, credentials removed, controls escaped) and then through `bracketless`, which writes `[` and `]` as escapes — `quoted` leaves them alone, and inside a paragraph of its own one `]` from a blocker summary would close the block and let the rest of the summary speak as controller text. Record IDs and blocker types are checked against their shape and quoted when they do not match it.
- **The note has a reader now (`context/enforcement.ts`, `lifecycle/handoff.ts`, `40faa3df`).** `latestHandoffFor(principal, taskId)` answers the task's latest note as `{id, attemptId, source}` without the text, on the dispatcher's own gate (`#dispatch`) — the gate that writes the note is the gate that reads it back, and an agent is refused it, like every other dispatcher method. `readHandoff(principal, noteId)` gives the whole note to whoever may work on the task, and reads a note it may not show the same as one that does not exist, the way `latestHandoff`, `latestCompaction` and `keptDecisions` already do. `HandoffService.latestForTask(taskId)` is the same shape for the hand-off record — ID, phase, from, to, taken from the pointer `cutsForTask` already reads, with nothing of the package. The old `latestHandoff` keeps its behaviour and is now the same private read, so the two cannot drift.
- **The operation and the wiring (`api/operations.ts`, `api/state-api.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `api/start.ts`).** `context.handoff.read` (`noteId`) is a query of the same family as `context.spill.read` and `context.route-archive.read`: an agent's read of a record of the task it works on; a controller running without a dispatcher answers `not_found`, exactly as the spill read beside it does. `npm run api:docs:write` regenerated `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with that entry and no other change. The dispatcher takes two widened deps (`handedIn`, and `context.latestHandoffFor` beside the `blockers` pick it already had) and `composeDispatch` is handed the `handoffs` service it now needs.
- **Where it goes in the call (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`).** `#startNow` reads the three things once, best effort (each read that fails is left out, never guessed at), and puts the paragraph after the task's own text and the rules and **before** the route view: `dispatch/local-worker.ts` rebuilds the *tail* of `order.content` when a route was never measured (line 304 keeps everything before the view and writes a new one), so anything placed after the view is the first thing a rebuild would drop, and the room it asks the rebuilt view for is `content` minus the view plus the resume note — which now counts the hand-off paragraph as it is. The same string is reused for the order, so the paragraph whose size was passed to the view is the paragraph that goes out.
- **The route view is made room for it again (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `context/enforcement.ts`, `1b08c719`).** The view is cut to leave room for the rest of the prompt, and until now that rest was guessed at with `PROMPT_NOTE_RESERVE_CHARS`. The first run of the C07g tests with a bigger reserve showed the honest problem with guessing: the hostile-question test's three long items stopped being *cut* and started being *left out*, because the estimate had swallowed their room. The estimate is now what it should have been — the dispatcher passes `noteChars`, the size the paragraph actually is, and the composed hook keeps `PROMPT_NOTE_RESERVE_CHARS + noteChars` (it first kept the larger of the two; the review below made it the sum), so the constant stands for what is not measured here (the project's rules, a resume note) and stays where C07g measured it.
- **Tests.** `dispatch/handoff-brief.test.ts` (new): empty when there is nothing to hand over; each line's record and operation; a hand-off named to the agent it went to and not to the one it did not; blockers counted, summaries shortened, IDs alone past the bound; hostile summaries whose brackets, newline and credential cannot close the block or speak as controller text. `dispatch/handoff-call.test.ts` (new, four backends): through `composeDispatch`, the first call of the agent a task was handed to names the package, the note of the attempt before it and the open blocker; a call for a task with none of that carries no paragraph at all; a note of this very attempt is not passed off as the previous one. `api/start-handoff-call.test.ts` (new, the whole path): a real attempt ends and the controller writes its note, the owner hands the task over through the API, the new owner's order names all three, and the note it names reads back through `context.handoff.read` for that agent and for no one else — with the package itself readable by the sender and the recipient, as `handoff.get` has always judged it. `context/enforcement.test.ts`: the two reads' rights (the dispatcher's gate refuses agents; whoever may work on the task gets the note; anyone else reads nothing) and both shapes of missing ID. `lifecycle/handoff.test.ts`: `latestForTask` before any hand-off, while one is only prepared, after it completes, and after a second one supersedes it, with its keys asserted so no package can ride along. `dispatch/first-call-hops.test.ts`: the three `C07m` todos pass and lost their todo, and the check that used to say "a call carries nothing but its resume note" now says what is true — the task's own text and rules, then the hand-off paragraph within its own bound, then the resume note last.
- ASSUMPTION: the first call *names* the package and the note instead of carrying them. Carrying them would make the call grow with the hand-offs it survives (C07k shows the package growing already) and would break the size trend C07l just measured; naming them costs one bounded paragraph whatever the records hold, and each named read is one the agent in front of it may actually make — `handoff.get` answers the sender and the recipient, `context.handoff.read` whoever may work on the task.
- ASSUMPTION: only blockers whose subject is the task itself are named, read through the per-type open slot (one read a type, thirteen types). A blocker on one of the task's effects, attempts or artifacts is real but is not "what holds this task up" in the same sense, and widening the read to every subject of the task is a separate card; the line says the owner's task status view holds the full list (it is not open to the task credential, so the agent is not sent there).
- ASSUMPTION: `context.handoff.read` is not an owner chat control, so `CHAT_OPS` and `STATUS_KINDS` are unchanged. It joins `context.spill.read` and `context.route-archive.read`, none of which is a chat operation: it reads one record of the caller's own task and needs the right to work on it. The owner already sees the hand-off in `status.ask { kind: "handoff" }` and the blockers in the task views.
- ASSUMPTION: a paragraph whose reads all failed is left out rather than replaced with "the controller could not read its records". A first call that says nothing was handed is the truth the agent can act on (it may still ask), and a refusal line repeated on every start of a task whose records are unreadable would be noise; the failure is reported through the dispatcher's own `onError` as everywhere else in that path.

The files this card adds or changed, each run alone: `dispatch/handoff-brief.test.js` 7 / 7 (0.8 s), `dispatch/handoff-call.test.js` 8 / 8 (30 s), `api/start-handoff-call.test.js` 1 / 1 (12 s), `dispatch/first-call-hops.test.js` 38 tests, 36 pass, 0 fail, 2 todo (94 s) — every one of them well inside the 600 s a file is allowed. That last four together (54 tests) were run again with one thing taken away — `#handedInNote` building the paragraph and throwing it away, nothing else changed — and 17 fail: the twelve C07m checks across the four backends, the four of `handoff-call.test.js`, and the composed-controller test; the first-call limit, the size trend and the resume-note checks that were there before still passed. `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` — 6 pass / 0 fail; `npm run roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` rewrote `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` with the one new operation and nothing else.
