Known limit, not changed: an adopted attempt whose worker finished early in an outage counts the rest of the outage until the new controller takes its result, since nothing records when the worker finished.

## C07q (Pi): a bounded compaction lineage, and the owner's decisions kept through the process's own compaction (2026-11-09)

C07l's finding 5 had two parts. The controller's compaction lineage grew by one ID each compaction, and a continuation capture refused a `summaryLineage` of more than 200 entries, so a long task's captures would fail after 200 compactions. And `ContextEnforcementService.compact`, `registerCompressor` and `keptDecisions` (which pin up to 12 owner decisions through compactions) have no production caller, because the model process compacts its conversation itself.

**Built**
- **The lineage is bounded (`context/lineage.ts`, `context/enforcement.ts`, `8caa4bbf`).** A compaction record lists its newest `LINEAGE_KEEP` (50) earlier compactions in order. The older ones go into `earlier: { count, digest, through }`. `digest` is a chained `sha256` over the folded IDs, oldest first, so later folding continues it without the IDs folded before. `through` is the newest folded ID. `earlierLineage(principal, { taskId, from?, limit? })` reads the folded part back, newest first, by following each record's `parent`, one page at a time (`next`). Whoever may not work on the task reads nothing. `compact` returns `earlier`, and so does `latestCompaction`. Pinned decisions were already capped at 12 and carried forward, and that is unchanged.
- **A capture accepts a long lineage (`continuation/continuation.ts`, `8caa4bbf`).** `manifest.summaryLineage` now takes up to 10,000 record IDs. The newest 200 stay listed and the rest are folded into `manifest.summaryLineageEarlier` the same way. A host may also pass `summaryLineageEarlier` itself, as the controller's compaction records give it. Folding then continues from it: the counts add up and the digest goes on. A list longer than 10,000 is still refused, and so is a malformed reference. Retention (`retention/references.ts`) keeps the folded `through` compaction of a resumable task. A resumable task's compactions were already all kept. `continuation.capture`'s manifest description and `api-v1.md` are updated.
- **The owner's decisions go to the process's own compaction (`decisions/records.ts` `compactionKeep`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `contracts` `worker-channel.ts`, `worker/host/local.ts`, `pi-adapter/worker/process.ts`, `b3680886`).** The composer's `context(order)` is now async. It reads the owner's current items for the task as the controller, the same read the route view uses (`decisions.controllerContext`). Those items are decisions, gates, goals, permissions and unresolved conflicts, never an agent's open question. Up to 12 are passed as `compaction.keep`. Each line is the item's ID and its wording, quoted with `quotedLine` and cut to 200 characters. A note goes with the lines. It names the decision version, says how many were left unlisted, and says the current ones are read whole with the state API query `decision.context`. The channel bounds `keep`: at most 12 single lines of 600 characters and a note of 1,000. The host reads the context once at each process start. The process's extractive `beforeCompact` writes the note and the lines after every summary it makes. A decision record that cannot be read is reported through `onError` and left out. It never fails the launch.
- **Tests (each fails without its change).** `context/compaction-lineage.test.ts` runs the real decision, retrieval, enforcement and continuation services on all four backends, about 1.5 to 5.5 s each. It does 250 compactions with 12 owner decisions pinned over the first 12. At every step the lineage lists at most 50, and the listed and folded IDs together are exactly the earlier compactions. After the last compaction the folded part reads back whole and in order through `earlierLineage`, and it matches the digest. `keptDecisions` returns all 12, available and with the wording whole, and the 250th summary names each one. A capture with all 250 summary IDs is accepted, keeping 200 plus the reference. The controller's bounded form is accepted as it is, and a host-passed reference is continued. Past 10,000 entries, or with a bad digest, the capture is refused. `compactionKeep` gives 12 lines and counts the extra ones. Before the change this test fails at compaction 52, where 51 were listed. Other tests: `api/start-dispatch.test.ts` checks that the composed controller gives nothing when nothing is decided and gives the decision quoted (a line break folded, a quote escaped) once one is recorded. `worker/host/local.test.ts` checks that an async context reaches the process's start message and is read once. `pi-adapter/worker/process.test.ts` checks the lines come after every summary, even when the extract cut the decision out of the middle, and checks the channel bounds. Mutation checks (each applied, rebuilt and restored): drop the `await` in the host, drop `${kept}` in the process, or drop `keep` in the composer. Each fails its test.

**Not done, stated exactly**
- **The controller's summariser still has no production caller.** `compact`, `registerCompressor`, `keptDecisions` and `earlierLineage` are called only by tests. The conversation being compacted lives in the sandbox, in Pi's store. The controller never holds that text, and `compact` needs its sources as stored records the summary can cite (desk records, history entries, owner decisions). Routing Pi's `beforeCompact` through the controller would need a new process-to-host-to-controller request on the channel. It would also need a way to cite a conversation that is not a controller record. Calling `compact` with made-up sources would produce a retrieval summary that claims records it was not made from, so that was not done. What is wired instead is the acceptance's alternative: the process's own compaction is kept, and the pinned decisions are given to it.
- **The decisions given to the process are a snapshot taken when the process starts.** A correction made later is not in the lines of a compaction that runs before the process restarts. The note says so and names `decision.context` for the current ones. The dispatcher already holds calls after a decision change until the worker has put the new context in front of the agent (C08). Refreshing `keep` mid-process would need a new channel message.
- **Only the extractive compaction carries them.** Pi's own model summariser runs only when the host gives no `extractive` fallback. The composer gives `extractive` for every route with a known window, and C07n refuses a route with an unknown window. So in the composed controller every process that compacts carries the decisions. A host built without the composer's `context` gets neither.
- **No production host captures a continuation yet** (L04d). Nothing in the repository builds `summaryLineage` from the controller's compaction records, so the bounded form is accepted but not produced by any host today.
- **`earlierLineage` has no state-API operation.** No compaction read (`latestCompaction`, `keptDecisions`) has one either.
- **Not run:** a real Pi process compacting with the decisions through the whole local worker. The integration tests that compose the host (`c07g-route-view`, `h12bf-composed`, `h12k-composed-host` and four more) pass with the async context, but none of them records a decision before the process compacts.
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build --force` clean, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` with the offline guard): controller `dist/{context,continuation,dispatch,lifecycle,api,chat}/*.test.js` had 3,588 tests, 3,584 pass, 0 fail and 4 todo (C07k's, unchanged). Controller `dist/{retention,decisions}` pass. `contracts` had 11 of 11 pass, `pi-adapter` `worker/process.test.js` 18 of 18, and `worker` `host/local.test.js` 13 of 13. The seven integration tests that compose the local host pass, 10 tests in all. `scripts/plan.test.mjs` had 6 of 6 pass, and `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` are ok.
- ASSUMPTION: the alternative branch of the acceptance is taken: the process's own compaction is kept and the pinned decisions are given to it. The other branch, routing compaction through the controller's summariser, is not taken, for the reason above. It is a larger channel change with no honest set of sources.
- ASSUMPTION: 50 compactions kept by ID on a compaction record, and 200 on a capture (the capture's old limit, kept). The rest are kept by count, chained digest and a reference, because every compaction record names its parent, which makes the parent chain the complete list. 10,000 is the most a capture accepts in one list. It is a bound on input size, not on the task: a host past it passes the reference instead.
- ASSUMPTION: the decisions given to the process are each cut to 200 characters with their ID, not given whole. They are written into every summary, so their size is paid at every compaction, and the full wording is one named read away.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09).** One fix in `compactionKeep` (`decisions/records.ts`), tested in `decisions/quoted-text.test.ts` (fails without it). Each line was cut to 200 characters *before* `quotedLine` escaped it, and an escape writes one character as up to twelve, so an owner's wording rich in format characters (a family emoji's zero-width joiners, bidi marks, tag characters) made a line past the channel's 600 (721 for forty family emoji), and `parseToChild` then refused the whole start message: every launch of the task failed. The line is now cut further until the quoted line, ID included, fits `COMPACTION_KEEP.line` (600, the channel's `CHANNEL_KEEP.line`). With it, unresolved conflicts and gates now come before the other items, so a task with more than 12 items never leaves out the one that says what must not be done. Checked, no change: the digest chain is oldest first and continues across folds and captures; one ID folds per compaction at 51; old records with a longer lineage fold at once; `earlierLineage` stops at a missing parent or another task's record and is bounded by `limit` (so a cycle cannot loop), and reads nothing for a reader who may not work on the task; a capture's list length is checked before any ID is read or hashed; retention keeps `through`; every `context` call site awaits (the host awaits inside its launch `try`, and the composer catches a failed decision read and reports it); only owner principals record decisions and agent questions are filtered out.

## W01 (first part): the Pi completion bench, built; the baseline is not run yet (2026-11-09)

What is built (`scripts/pi-eval/`, plain Node ESM, no new dependencies; the README there is the manual):

- **One command:** `node scripts/pi-eval/run.mjs` runs every pinned task in variants A and B, three repeats each, one at a time (`--concurrency` at most 3, Pi's limit on Radiance), and prints the report; `report.mjs` reprints it from `results.jsonl`; `--calibrate` checks a task with no agent (hidden tests fail at the base, pass at the solution). Results live outside the repository, in `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/eval-results/` (one JSON line per run plus the prompt, Pi's whole log, the hidden-test output and the diff stat); throwaway checkouts are `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/eval-<run>` and are removed after the run.
- **The pinned task set (`taskset.json`):** nine merged Pi cards, three per size: S quote-lines (081248b7), flaky-proposal (212db814), grant-proposals (eac67f71); M landing-proposal (0e84a1b9), c07n (b3851601), phrase-hints (9bb923b4); L m03h-1 (e78581b6), l02e-2 (1c8816fe), c07m (eb19ba95). Base is the merge's first parent and solution the merge; hidden files are the test files (and test suites) the merge added or changed; full SHAs are pinned and checked at load. Task texts are the prompts Pi was actually given for those cards (`~/.local/pi-cli/runs/*.prompt`) without their process steps, plus the names the hidden tests import and what the review rounds added. Variant templates: A plain, B a PLAN.md with a checkbox per small step and a commit per step. C and D are refused with "needs W04".
- **The hidden tests are kept out by construction:** each run `git init`s a new directory and fetches only the base commit, so the solution commit is not in its object store at all (the run refuses to start if it is reachable or a hidden file already holds the solution's content). After the agent ends, the solution's hidden files are written in, the repository is rebuilt, and the hidden test files run with the offline guard.
- **Classification (`lib/classify.mjs`):** timeout, error, verified-finish (hidden tests pass on a changed worktree), length, empty (no visible text and no work, or "No response requested"), stopped-early (unchecked PLAN.md steps, thinking-only after work, an announced next step, no done claim, or a log without `agent_end`), wrong (a done claim and failing hidden tests), and unclassified for anything else. Each run also records wall time, tokens, turns, tool calls, plan progress, commits ahead, nudges (0 until W04), the route and model and the bench's own commit.
- **Gates (`lib/stats.mjs`):** verified finish at least 90 % S, 85 % M, 70 % L per variant; false done at most 5 %; zero unclassified; each rate with its Wilson 95 % interval; a size with no runs fails as not measured; a PASS/FAIL line per variant and a RESULT line.
- **Tests** (`node --test "scripts/pi-eval/*.test.mjs"`, 25 pass): the classifier on five logs trimmed from real runs (the smoke run's false done, c07p stopped-early thinking-only, x09b-fix3 length, capacity-view-pi empty, flaky-confirm finish or false done by the hidden tests); the aggregation and gates; and the runner end to end on a tiny repository with `stub-agent.mjs`, where **the deliberately broken agent that stops after its first turn is scored stopped-early, never finished**, and a thinking-only stop, a false done, a crash, a hang (timeout) and an honest solver come out as such. The checkout is shown to hold no hidden file and no way to reach the solution.
- **Calibration** (`run.mjs --calibrate`, bench commit 4abd2e0d, no agent): all nine tasks are sound. Their hidden tests fail at the base and pass at the solution. Hidden tests passing at base and at solution: quote-lines 139/154 and 154/154; flaky-proposal 30/38 and 38/38; grant-proposals 239/275 and 275/275; landing-proposal 6/8 and 34/34; c07n 46/74 and 61/74 (the other 13 are todo, 0 fail); phrase-hints 354/371 and 376/376; m03h-1 284/316 and 316/316; l02e-2 179/189 and 189/189; c07m 294/321 and 357/358 (1 todo). Each task takes about 3 to 6 minutes of CPU.
- **Smoke run** (one run, variant A, quote-lines, Radiance qwen3.8-flash-next-iq4r, thinking medium). The first attempt was scored error in 4 s: Radiance answered "the engine stopped on an error and is not serving (device error)". Nothing was restarted, and Radiance was answering again within 10 minutes. On the second attempt Pi worked 30.5 minutes (100 turns, 110 tool calls, 1 commit, +222 -10 across 6 files) and ended with a 3332-character report that opens with "Done.". The hidden tests passed 153 of 154; the line-cut sweep in `commands-one-line.test.ts` failed. Outcome: **wrong** (a false done). The classifier first scored it stopped-early because it read only the report's last 600 characters for a done claim. It now reads both ends, a fixture from this run pins that, and `rescore.mjs` re-scored the saved record. The run proves the pipeline end to end; it says nothing about rates.

What is left:

- **The baseline of variants A and B over the whole set** (54 runs, about 20 GPU hours), at a quiet time on Radiance. Record its batch, commit, route, model and the report here; that is what W01's acceptance asks for.
- Before trusting the M and L rates, read their hidden tests against the task texts: hidden tests pin exact wording and names, and only quote-lines was checked test by test.
- Variants C and D after W04. `nudges` and the W02 end kinds come from the worker once W02/W04 exist; the bench reads the CLI log only.

- ASSUMPTION: base = the merge commit's first parent, and the hidden tests are the merge's own test files. That is what was accepted at merge, review rounds included, so the task texts name what the review rounds added.
- ASSUMPTION: a test file that exists at the base stays in the agent's checkout in its base version. Only the solution's version is held back, because removing existing tests would change the task. The solution's version replaces the agent's at grading.
- ASSUMPTION: c07m holds back `dispatch/handoff-brief.test.ts` from grading. It unit-tests the internal shape of a module the agent has to invent, and the card's own acceptance test (`first-call-hops.test.ts`) and the composed-controller tests still run.
- ASSUMPTION: "empty" means no visible text and no work done (or "No response requested"). A thinking-only ending after tool calls is stopped-early (c07p), because the agent was mid-work and its next step is visible in its thinking.
- ASSUMPTION: the gates are judged on the point rate, and the Wilson interval is shown beside it with a warning when it reaches below the gate. Requiring the lower bound to clear 90 % would need over 35 consecutive successes per size.

W01 review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09). Fixed, each with a test that fails without the fix (31 bench tests pass):

- A verified finish now needs the rebuild with the hidden files in to succeed. tsc emits despite type errors, so hidden tests could pass on code that does not typecheck, or on a stale dist file the agent built from its own test of the same name.
- An honest partial report ("could not complete step 4", "still fails", "remaining work", "incomplete") is no longer read as a done claim, so it is stopped-early, not a false done (it inflated the false-done gate). A closing "Let me know if ..." is a sign-off, not an announced step (it hid false dones as stopped-early).
- Pi's stderr goes to `pi-stderr.log`, no longer into the JSON log where a stray line could split or swallow an event.
- Processes left running in the checkout when the agent ends are killed (Linux, by /proc cwd): Pi starts bash tools in their own process groups, so the group stop missed a hung test or a background server, which then kept writing into the checkout during grading and outlived the run.
- Checkouts moved to `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/eval-work/`, so the agent's parent directory is not the one holding the merged worktrees; Ctrl-C removes active checkouts and stops setup and hidden-test runs too.
- Contamination detection widened: any absolute path in a tool call under the reference checkout, a directory holding checkouts, the results or the home directory (except Pi's install) flags the run and is listed in `foreignPaths`. It is still detection, not isolation: relative walks, run-time paths and searches from `/` are not seen. A bubblewrap sandbox was ruled out because the controller's own tests need bubblewrap and AppArmor refuses nested user namespaces here.
- The report shows tasks per size beside runs and says that repeats of one task are not independent samples. `rescore.mjs --write` writes a temporary file and renames it.
- ASSUMPTION: the bench isolates the checkout, not the machine. Pi can read other checkouts, so a run whose tool calls name one (or the solution's short SHA or the results directory) is flagged `contaminated` and still scored.
- ASSUMPTION: the bench's tests are not added to `npm test` (`scripts/*.test.mjs` only). They spawn git and child processes and take about 10 s, and the bench is an operator tool, not product code.

## C07k: a hand-off package summarises its completed work, so it stops growing with the number of hand-offs (2026-11-09)

C07h found that the package grows with every hand-off (first ten hops averaging 1507 characters, last ten 4707): the controller's source lists every artifact and decision of the run's latest continuation in `completedWork` (`lifecycle/handoff-sources.ts`), and nothing summarised them until C07j's cut at the 4,000-character section limit.

**Built**
- **A digest of the completed work (`lifecycle/handoff-cut.ts` `digestSection`, `lifecycle/handoff.ts` `#collect`).** `completedWork` (the one section that only grows across hand-offs) is summarised once it holds more than `HANDOFF_LIMITS.digestWhole` (8) entries, before it reaches the section limit. The newest 8 entries stay whole and in order (so the latest decision is still the last line the next agent sees), and so do older entries holding one of the owner's marks (newest first, while the section stays within the limit). The older entries are counted by kind on the first line, which is C07j's cut marker (`[cut: N of M entries, archive hnd-…]`) followed by `Older entries are summarised so the package does not grow with every hand-off: 192 decisions and 1 artifact left out (the owner's marked ones and the newest 8 are kept); the whole section is kept: read it with the state API query handoff.archive.read {…}`. The whole section, every decision's reference in its order, is archived first exactly as a C07j cut is (same archive, same `cuts` entry, same readers), so every existing reader of a cut (`handoff.archive.read`, the chat's `handoff_archive` view, `cutsForTask`) reads a digest without change, and no decision is lost. A section whose newest 8 entries do not fit beside the marker is cut as before. The counted kinds are the controller's own `Decision: ` / `Artifact: ` labels; agent text is not interpreted, and a quoted (neutralised) line counts as an "other entry".
- **Tests.** `lifecycle/handoff-hops.test.ts` (four backends): the size-trend check lost its `todo` and passes (first ten hops average 1319 characters, last ten 1375, +4.2%; the only growth after hop 2 is the digits of the counts). The cut-marker check now treats a `completedWork` of more than 8 entries as cut (it was "given whole while under 4,000 characters"); its other assertions (marker counts, archive equals the original, every shown line an entry of the original in order) apply unchanged, and the seeded early decision and failure are found through the archive after hop 50. `lifecycle/handoff-cut.test.ts`: six new cases (whole up to 8 entries; newest 8 kept and the rest counted by kind under the marker; the same size at 20, 60 and 199 decisions; the owner's marked older entry kept; fallback to the ordinary cut; a digest keeping nothing refused). Mutation check (applied, rebuilt, restored): with `DIGESTED_SECTIONS` emptied the size-trend check fails on all four backends, and so does the cut-marker check (an 8-plus-entry `completedWork` given whole).
- `dispatch/handoff-brief.ts` and `dispatch/dispatcher.ts` comments no longer say the package grows with every hop. No operation changed (`api-v1.md` unchanged).

**Not done**
- The digest is a count and a pointer, not a written summary: older decisions are listed by reference only in the archive. The continuation's decisions are record IDs (`dsk-…`) with no state, so "open" and "resolved" decisions cannot be told apart here; only the newest 8 and the owner's marked ones are kept whole. The controller's summariser (C07q) is still not used for the package.
- Other sections are unchanged: they are bounded by the section limit (C07j) but not digested; the drafts and responsibilities lists can still grow up to it if the sender keeps adding to them.
- The 5% acceptance holds with a small margin in the 50-hop fixture (4.2%) because the first hop's package has only 5 entries and no marker; the steady state is reached at hop 2.
- ASSUMPTION: 8 entries kept whole (two attempts' worth of decisions in the C07h fixture, and room for the latest diagnosis plus the decisions around it); the digest is applied in the hand-off service, not in the source, so it can archive the whole section and reuse C07j's marker, archive and readers instead of adding a new read.
- ASSUMPTION: only `completedWork` is digested; it is the one section that accumulates per hand-off by construction (a run's continuation keeps every decision, up to 200).
- **Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build --force` clean, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` with the offline guard): controller `dist/{lifecycle,context,dispatch,decisions,api,chat}/*.test.js` 3,700 tests, 3,700 pass, 0 fail, 0 todo (the 4 C07k todo cases now pass); `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6; `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` ok. No operation changed, so `api:docs:write` was not needed.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09).** Two fixes in `digestSection` (`lifecycle/handoff-cut.ts`), each tested in `lifecycle/handoff-cut.test.ts` or `lifecycle/handoff-hops.test.ts` (all fail without them). (1) The source lists every artifact before every decision (`handoff-sources.ts`), so "the newest 8 lines" left out every artifact, the run's newest one too, at every hop from the second: the next agent no longer saw what the run had produced, only a count. The 8 kept entries now always include the newest entry of each kind (`Artifact: `, `Decision: `, other), so a run with one artifact keeps it and its newest 7 decisions; the marker says "the newest 8, among them the newest of each kind". New hops check (four backends): the hop's newest artifact is shown in every package. Keeping the newest 8 of *each* kind was tried and rejected: it gives hop 2 (1 artifact, 8 decisions) whole with no marker and moved the size trend to +7%. (2) Each marked older entry re-rendered the whole section to measure it, quadratic in the entries: a 20,000-line section under a mark matching every line took 75 s (the controller source caps at 400 lines, but other sources and a 1,000,000-character archive do not). Sizes are now running sums; 50,000 marked lines take milliseconds. Also: a digest whose every older entry is marked and kept says "no entry left out" (it said ": left out"). Size trend now first ten 1341, last ten 1397, +4.2%; deterministic (fixed clock, fixed-length record and archive IDs; only the hop number's and counts' digits grow, and continuation lists are capped at 200 each, so the marker counts stay at three digits however many hops). Checked, no change: the marker carries only controller numbers and fixed labels (an agent's "Decision: " text only shifts a count; continuation decisions are record IDs, never multi-line); marks cannot crowd out the newest entries; the archive is the redacted original, written before the package, with an ID derived from hand-off, section and digest (idempotent on retry); C07m's paragraph names the package by ID only; the changed cut-marker assertion still checks counts, archive and order.
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09).** Two fixes, each tested and failing without it. (1) A `completedWork` of more than 8 entries that fits the 4,000-character limit while its newest 8 beside the digest marker would not (one short old entry, eight long new ones) falls back to `cutSection`, which gives a fitting section whole; `#collect` had asked only whether it had more than 8 entries, so it archived the section and recorded a cut of "0 of 0 entries left out", which the handoff status reported as a section cut to fit. `givenWhole` (`lifecycle/handoff-cut.ts`) now answers whether the digest gives a section as it is, and `#collect` and the hops check both ask it before anything is archived (tests in `handoff-cut.test.ts` and `handoff.test.ts`). (2) An entry's kind is read from the line as the source wrote it (`matchOn`), not from the `neutralise`d line: a decision whose text read like a marker was quoted and then counted as an "other entry" (and could not be the newest decision kept). Also: a property test over 3,000 random sections (kinds, lengths, astral characters, marks) checks every entry is shown whole in its order or counted, the counts by kind sum to what was left out, "no entry left out" exactly when none was, the newest of each kind and the newest entries are shown, and the limit holds; the status line now says a section "was cut to fit or summarised", and the chat interpreter's description of cuts mentions the completed-work digest. Checked, no change: the size trend (first ten 1341, last ten 1397) is real and fails with the digest off (1540 to 4714, +206%, eight failures over four backends); the +4.2% comes almost wholly from hop 1 (909, five entries, no marker), every later hop is 1385 to 1397. The running sums equal the rendered length exactly (header plus each kept entry and its newline, in UTF-16 units; nothing is sliced, so no surrogate is split). "Newest of each kind" is the last entry of that kind in the list, which matches the sources' oldest-first order within a kind; with fewer kinds than 8 it adds at most one entry per kind beyond the newest lines and still keeps 8 in all. Runs after the fixes: controller `dist/{lifecycle,context,dispatch,decisions,api,chat}/*.test.js` 3,714 tests, 3,714 pass, 0 fail, 0 todo; `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6; `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` ok.

## C07o: a remote host's first call and stored conversation are judged by the controller before the order is offered (2026-11-09)

C07l's finding 3: `RemoteWorkerHost.start` placed the order as it was (`remote/service.ts` `place`), so for an attempt on a remote host the controller made no first-call admission and no resume decision, and the remote API has no operation through which a host could ask. The card allows either a state-API operation for the host or a check by the controller before the offer; this change takes the second, so the remote API is unchanged (`remote/server.ts` still has no route that admits work, and `npm run api:docs:write` leaves `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` unchanged).

- **One resume rule for both hosts (`dispatch/local-worker.ts`, `9010522c`).** The local worker's resume decision is now the exported `judgeResume(context, order, report)`: the embedder's reader, else the worker package's `nn.contextTokens`; unknown size or a failed check is a fresh start with the reason in the resume note; a size over the resume share is a fresh start with C07b's wording. `LocalWorker.start` calls it; behaviour is unchanged (its 82 guard tests pass unchanged).
- **The controller's check before the offer (`remote/host.ts`, `dispatch/runtime-guards.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `d99edfb1`).** `RemoteWorkerHostOptions` gains `window` (the operator's figure for the host, the counterpart of `local.window`), `context` and `onGuardError`. The composer binds each remote host to `controllerGuards` with the same window order as C07n (the host's figure, then the routing table's `contextTokens`, then a non-retryable refusal with a `context_overflow` blocker naming the route), `routeWindow` letting a table read error through (refused as "the context check failed", no blocker), and `checkpointStoredTokens`. Before `place`, `#judge` runs `judgeResume` (a stored conversation not carried is removed from the order and the reason added to `resumeNote`, so the host starts fresh and the agent is told), then `guards.admit` with round 1, a fresh launch per offer and `retry: false`, so a refusal is written as a `ctx-admission` record and opens the blocker as the local worker's does. A refused first call is never placed: the host never sees the order or its task credential, and the attempt fails with `the first call was not sent: …`. The first call is estimated by `estimatedFirstCall`: the order's text plus resume note in tokens at the budget's characters per token, plus the carried conversation's tokens, plus the route's measured fixed part (`fixedPartOf`), all passed as `startupTokens` with no prompt or schema characters so the estimate is never stored as a measurement of the route.
- **Tests (`4d738abe`).** `remote/host-context.test.ts` (new; reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker thread, PostgreSQL) uses the real context-enforcement and blocker services. It checks: a 3,000,000-character order is not placed, fails with the startup-limit reason, and leaves a refused admission record and an open blocker; a short order is placed unchanged and admitted; a conversation that fits is carried; one over the resume share, or with no size, is removed with the reason appended to the existing note and the host told; a conversation that fits alone but makes the first call too large is refused; and a route with no window is refused with no admission record and a blocker. `api/start-c07o.test.ts` (new; SQLite and PostgreSQL) runs `startController` with a real remote worker client over the transport and a host window of 4096 tokens. An 8,000-character task is never offered, fails, and leaves `["first-call", false, 4096]` and a blocker. A short task is offered with `["first-call", true, 4096]` and no blocker. Mutation: with `#judge` disabled in `dist/remote/host.js`, all 6 new tests fail; restored, they pass. The wait in the startController test is bounded so a regression fails rather than hangs.
- **Existing tests changed, and why.** Every composed remote world (11 files, including `api/testing/remote-world.ts` and `integration/src/h12m-workspace-host.test.ts`) now states `window: () => 131_072` for its hosts. These worlds use a route resolver with no routing table, so under C07n's rule their remote attempts are now refused, as local attempts already were. The moved checkpoints in `api/start-remote-fencing.test.ts` and `api/start-resume-capture.test.ts` now state their size (`nn: { contextTokens: 500 }`); without it the controller rightly does not carry it to the new host.
- ASSUMPTION: the check runs in the controller before the offer rather than through a new host-facing operation. Remote hosts are untrusted for what they report, and the controller already holds what the check needs (the order, the checkpoint, the route's window and measured fixed part). A host-reported figure would be the host's word. No operation or field was added to the remote API.
- ASSUMPTION: a route whose fixed part nobody has measured counts no fixed part in the remote estimate, rather than C07f's 14,000-character floor. Remote hosts never measure the route, so a floor would refuse every first call on a small remote-only route based on a guess; the route-move check already avoids refusing on that floor.
- ASSUMPTION: no reply reserve is counted, because the controller does not know the remote host's model settings. The estimate is a lower bound: it refuses only what cannot fit.
- ASSUMPTION: a composed remote host with no stated window and a route the routing table does not size is refused, the same as for the local host after C07n. Embedders that relied on unchecked remote placement must state `window` on the host or `contextTokens` on the route.
- **Left.** (1) The remote host's real first call (with its own system prompt and tools) is not measured or confirmed: no remote operation reports the provider's input count, so `confirmUsage` and calibration are not fed from remote hosts. (2) The remote host cannot compact before a second round; a refusal is final for that offer. (3) Fixed in review, below. (4) A restart through control messages (`RemoteWorkerHandle.restart`, which carries a checkpoint to a host already holding the attempt) is not judged; only a start or re-placement through `start` is, and that includes relocation's new offer.
- **Runs** (this worktree; `npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard as an absolute `file://` URL; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`). `dist/remote dist/dispatch dist/context dist/api dist/chat` (`*.test.js`): 3363 tests, 3362 pass, 1 fail, 0 todo, 243 s. The one failure was `api/start-resume-capture.test.js`, whose moved checkpoint stated no size. With its size stated it passes (1/1). `remote/host-context.test.js` 4/4 and `api/start-c07o.test.js` 2/2, each well inside the 600 s bound. `integration` `h12m-workspace-host` 2/2 and `h12k-composed-host` 1/1; `lifecycle/dispatch-ports` and `status/status` 188/188. `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6/6; `npm run roadmap:check` reports "roadmap ok"; `npm run check:deps` reports "package boundaries ok"; `npm run api:docs:write` makes no change.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09).** One fix in `controllerGuards` (`dispatch/runtime-guards.ts`), tested in `dispatch/runtime-guards.test.ts` (fails without it). The admitted round of each attempt was kept until a `confirm` that never comes for a remote host, so a long-running controller grew one entry per remote attempt forever (and a local attempt that lost its process before confirming left one too). `GuardBinding.confirms: false` (set by the composer for every remote host) now keeps no round, and the kept rounds are bounded at `KEPT_ROUNDS` (10,000, oldest forgotten: only that attempt's calibration is lost). Checked, no change: every offer goes through `RemoteWorkerHost.start` (`remote.place` has no other caller, relocation's new offer included), so a refused order and its task credential never reach a host; the window comes only from the operator's host figure and the routing table, never from a host; `judgeResume` is the local rule moved whole (same share, unknown size and failed check both start fresh, with the note appended); repeated or many-host refusals reuse the task's one open blocker. Accepted as is: (a) the restart path (4 above) carries back to the same host the conversation that host already holds, so it gives the host nothing new; a remote restart that overflows fails at the provider rather than being refused first, and judging it would need the order on adopted handles. (b) The size of a stored conversation is the one the previous host wrote in its checkpoint (`nn.contextTokens`); a host that understates it can make the next host's first call overflow at its provider, which costs a failed call, not access. (c) The estimate is a lower bound with no measurement feeding back, so a remote call can still be refused by the provider where the local worker would have refused it first.

## W02: a turn's result says how the turn ended, from the worker process to the attempt (2026-11-09)

Before this card a turn's result said only completed, failed or cancelled. Pi Durable answers a reply that stopped on the output limit as it answers a natural stop (`pi-durable/dist/harness/generation.js` about line 362: `stopReason === "length"` goes to `answer`), so a cut-off reply, a thinking-only reply and a full report all looked the same to the controller.

**Built**
- **The channel (`contracts/src/worker-channel.ts`).** The `result` message has two new optional fields: `endKind` (`TURN_END_KINDS`: `length`, `empty-visible-text`, `no-work-end`, `announced-step-without-tool-call`, `normal`) and `visibleChars`. `HostEndKind` adds `unknown`. `endKindOf` reads a missing kind, or one this side does not know, as `unknown`. The parser leaves out a kind it does not know (from a newer worker), so it is never read as `normal`. `visibleChars` must be a whole number.
- **The classifier (`pi-adapter/src/worker/end-kind.ts`).** `classifyTurnEnd` takes the last reply's Pi stop reason (the last assistant entry of the transcript), its visible text and the turn's tool calls. The rules are tried in this order: `length` if the stop reason is `length`; `normal` if the turn called work.end and the controller accepted it (a refused call renders as `refused (…)`, so it does not count); `empty-visible-text` if the trimmed text is empty; `announced-step-without-tool-call` if the last 600 characters match the W01 bench's `ANNOUNCES_STEP` rule (a final reply has no tool call after it, or Pi would have run it); otherwise `no-work-end`. `visibleChars` is the trimmed length. The worker process (`worker/process.ts`) sends both with every completed turn.
- **work.end as a bridge tool (`pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts`, `controller/src/toolbridge/service.ts`).** Before this card the agent had no way to call `work.end`: H12n's "register work.end as an agent tool" was still open, so no turn could be `normal`. The bridge now offers `nimblenewt__work-end` (`WORK_END_TOOL`; `submit`, `result`, `note`, `message`). The controller's bridge sends it to the existing `work.end` API operation with the worker's task credential, for the attempt the request came through (`attemptId` in args is refused), with command ID `bridge:<attempt>:<call>`. The operation's own checks apply as before: only the attempt's own agent may call it, a pause or stop refuses it, and a repeat returns the recorded ending.
- **The host (`worker/src/host/local.ts`).** `HostTurnResult.endKind` is required: the process's kind for a completed turn, and `unknown` for a failed or cancelled turn, a process that ended, or a worker that sent none. `visibleChars` is passed on when the process sent it.
- **The attempt (`controller/src/dispatch/{ports,model,dispatcher}.ts`).** `WorkerTurnResult` has optional `endKind`/`visibleChars`. The controller restates the kinds as `TURN_END_KINDS` with `unknown` (it does not depend on `contracts`). `#run` holds `turnEnd { endKind, visibleChars?, at }` from the turn's result (`turnEndKindOf`: missing or unknown → `unknown`; a negative or fractional length is dropped). The write that finishes the attempt (`#end`) or parks it (`#yield`) records it, so there is no write of its own. A first version wrote it separately, and the PostgreSQL `dispatch/quiesce.test` caught a lost update: `#update` names its command `dpa-up:<attempt>:<revision>:<instance>`, so two updates read from the same revision in one process share a command ID, and the second (a quiesce's release) is taken as a replay and dropped. That hazard in `#update` predates this card; it was fixed in review (below). This is a record only: the outcome is decided exactly as before.
- **Tests (each fails without the change).** `contracts/worker-channel.test.ts`: every kind round-trips; an unknown kind is left out; bad lengths are refused. `pi-adapter/worker/end-kind.test.ts`: each kind and the order of the rules; a refused, failed or unknown-tool work.end is not an ending. `pi-adapter/worker/process.test.ts`: the five kinds from a faux provider through `runWorker`, plus a refused work.end giving `no-work-end`. `pi-adapter/bridge.test.ts`: the tool list includes `work-end`. `worker/host/local.test.ts`: a scripted process's kind is passed on; an older process's missing kind, a newer process's unknown kind and a failed turn are each `unknown`. `controller/dispatch/turn-end.test.ts`: on all four backends, each kind is recorded, missing or unknown is `unknown`, and the outcome stays `succeeded`/`failed` as before. `controller/toolbridge/service.test.ts`: work.end goes to the API for the attempt's own ID, with the task credential and a command ID from the call, and a named attempt is refused. `integration/w02-end-kinds.test.ts`: one fixture per kind (a `length` finish, a `reasoning_content`-only reply, a plain stop, an announced step, and a work.end call followed by a report) through the real sandboxed worker process, the host and the controller's `LocalWorker`. The shared scripted endpoint (`integration/h12-worker-support.ts`) can now play a `length` finish and a thinking-only reply. `integration/h12bf-composed.test.ts`: the work.end tool's schema made the fixed part larger, and the second attempt's first call went 68 tokens over the startup share (10,308 of 10,240). The fixture's answers are now 440 repeats instead of 450, the same kind of change T07b made; 4 of 4 pass.

**Left**
- Nothing acts on the kind yet. W03 ends an attempt `stopped-early` on it, and W04 continues the turn.
- The parked path (`#yield`) records the kind too, but no test covers it; an end that joins another end already under way may not record it.
- A remote host that sends no `endKind` is recorded `unknown` (since review, one that sends it is carried; see below).
- The kind is on the dispatch record (`dispatcher.get`). No status line or chat view shows it yet, so no operation or status text changed, and `api:docs:write` was not needed.
- Not checked end to end: the composed controller with a real task credential calling `work.end` through the bridge. The routing is unit-tested, and the `work.end` operation already accepts a task-scoped credential for its own task (H12n), but the two are not run together in one test.
- ASSUMPTION: `normal` means the turn called work.end and the controller accepted it. The card defines `no-work-end` as "a natural stop without work.end", so without the tool no turn could be `normal`. Offering the tool (H12n item 2) is the smallest change that makes the kind reachable. It lets an agent end its attempt as H12n designed, and changes nothing for a turn that does not call it.
- ASSUMPTION: a turn that called work.end is `normal` even when its last reply has no visible text or announces a step, because the agent's ending carries its report. A reply cut off at the output limit is `length` even after work.end.
- ASSUMPTION: only a completed turn is classified. A failed or cancelled turn is `unknown`, since the five kinds describe how a completed turn ended.
- **Runs** (this worktree; `npx tsc --build --force` clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard given as an absolute `file://` URL). contracts: 12 of 12. pi-adapter (whole package): 194 of 194. worker (whole package): 285 tests, 284 pass, 1 skipped. controller `dist/{dispatch,api,toolbridge,work-end}/*.test.js`: 1,719 of 1,719. integration `w02-end-kinds`, `h12bf-composed`, `h12b-worker-process` and `t06b-composed-worker`: 12 of 12. Before the last dispatcher change, `c07g-route-view`, `h12e-*`, `h12k-composed-host`, `t07b-jobs`, `c09h-local-artifact`, `c06b-cache-stability`, `h08b-lease-worker`, `l05b-model-stream` and `h12j-worker-gaps` also passed (29 tests, the one failure being h12bf, fixed above). `scripts/plan.test.mjs`: 6 of 6. `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` ok. `api:docs:write` made no change.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-09).** Three fixes, each with a test that fails without it.
  1. `#update` (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`) lost writes. The command ID was `dpa-up:<attempt>:<revision>:<instance>`, so two writes in one dispatcher that read the same revision had the same ID and the same payload. The second write was answered as a replay of the first and dropped, and its caller was told it had been written. This happened on every backend, not only PostgreSQL: four concurrent `heartbeat`s counted 1 (`dispatch/update-race.test.ts`, 4 backends). The ID now ends with a per-dispatcher write number (`:<n>`), so the losing write gets `stale_revision`, reads again and is written. The ID stays unique (the instance is random per process) and short (under 70 characters).
  2. An attempt ended by the agent's own `work.end` usually had no `turnEnd`. The `workend.complete` sweep runs every tick and completes the ending (settle, then `finishWith`) while the turn is still producing its last reply. That stops the worker, so the turn never reports how it ended. `finishWith` now passes `agentEnded`, and `#endInner` records `{ endKind: "normal", at }` when no turn ending is held. When the turn's own result is held (the ending was completed from the turn's end hook), the worker's kind is kept. Tested in `dispatch/turn-end.test.ts` (4 backends).
  3. A remote host could not send an end kind. `WorkerTurnResult` (and so the remote `StoredResult` and `RemoteAttempt.complete`) now has `endKind`/`visibleChars`, but `checkResult` in `remote/service.ts` refused both as unknown fields. A host that passed its local result through would have had the whole turn result refused. Both fields are now accepted for a completed turn. A kind this controller does not know is left out (read as `unknown`). A negative or fractional length is refused. Tested in `remote/remote.test.ts`.
  Checked, no change: the work-end tool cannot name another attempt (`attemptId` is refused and the attempt comes from the bound credential). It goes through the API with the worker's task credential, so H12n's agent, task-scope, live-attempt and pause checks apply. Its arguments are bounded by the bridge (`BRIDGE_LIMITS.args`) and by H12n (note 1,000, message 2,000, and a credential-shaped text is refused). A repeat returns the recorded ending, and a different repeat is refused. `done` and `partial` end the attempt `succeeded`, exactly as a plain completed turn already does. A submit only opens an author-role submission, which still goes through review and landing, so the tool grants no approval. The classifier reads the stop reason from the last assistant entry, thinking is not counted as visible text, and a length stop after an accepted work.end is `length` (as the ASSUMPTION says). The h12bf fixture change (450 to 440 repeats) is the same sizing fix as T07b's and keeps the test's claim. The three changed `process.test` assertions only add the new fields to exact-match results.
  Left (not fixed): `lastStopReason` scans the whole stored transcript once per completed turn (Pi Durable exposes no direct read of the answer entry). A malformed (non-string) `endKind` or a fractional `visibleChars` on the worker channel still fails the result line, like any other malformed field. A turn ending held in memory is lost if the controller dies before the end write, so the attempt then has no `turnEnd`. `work.end` is not in the bridge's `WRITES` set, so a pause is refused by H12n's own check (code `unavailable`) and not by the bridge's (code `paused`).

## Owner decisions on completion, 2026-11-10 (Rob, in conversation)

- The completion gate runs on the Radiance route, which is the owner's local AI server; no cloud route is used (an earlier line here wrongly said Radiance was dropped). W09 now blocks the macOS, Linux and Windows fresh-install qualification cards (X04 to X06).
- An agent must always give a report when it ends, coding or not, built from running notes it keeps as it works; a second agent questions a done before it is recorded succeeded (new card W10). ASSUMPTION: the questioning agent can send work back to the same agent within the W03 limit and then raises a CTO blocker; it does not approve work (acceptance stays with the independent review) and does not ask the owner.
- A standing grant expires only after it goes unused and renews on use (card A07h).

## A07h: a standing grant lapses only after it goes unused, and each use renews it (2026-11-10)

Owner decision of 2026-11-10 (Rob): a hard end date makes long unattended work stall at an arbitrary moment. A standing grant now has an idle window instead: it lapses once it has gone that long without being used, and each use starts the window again.

**Built**
- **The grant record (`security/grants.ts`).** `GrantRecordBody` has optional `idleDays`, `lastUsedAt` (set to the time the grant is made, or its `notBefore` if later) and `lapseNoticedAt`. `grant()` and the `grant.create` operation take an optional `idleDays` (1 to 36,500). One shared `holdsWith` replaces the two copies of the "does this record hold" check in `heldRecords` and `effectiveOf`; it adds "not lapsed from non-use" (`lapsedFromNonUse`, `idleEnd`). A derived grant falls with a lapsed parent, and `derive` refuses a lapsed parent. A grant without `idleDays` (every grant stored before this card) and a grant with an explicit `expiresAt` behave as before.
- **Use (`recordGrantUse` / `GrantService.recordUse`).** Writes `lastUsedAt` on each grant with an idle window that still holds; a derived grant renews the grant it rests on. The command is named `grant-use-<grant>-<UTC day>` and is skipped when `lastUsedAt` is already that day, so a grant is written at most once a day however busy the work. A lapsed, revoked or ended grant is never renewed.
- **Where use is recorded.** The dispatcher's grant check at placement (`#missingGrants`, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts` about line 1478): when nothing is missing, the grant records that cover what the task needs are renewed. The approval policy (`PolicyService.evaluate`): an approval grant that decides an action is renewed.
- **A stalled task says why.** A `grant_needed` blocker whose missing right was covered by a grant that lapsed from non-use reads "the task needs X and agent:… no longer holds it; the right lapsed from non-use (X: grant grt-… lapsed on D after N days unused, last used D): grant it again to let the task go on". An approval that asks again because its grant lapsed has that as its last reason. The old wording stays for a right that was never given.
- **The owner's notice (`dispatch/loops.ts` `grantLapseLoops`, `lapseNotice`; composed in `api/dispatch-compose.ts`).** At most every ten minutes the loop finds grants that lapsed from non-use and were not yet reported (`GrantService.noticeLapsed`), tells the owner one plain `maintenance` notice per grant (command ID `grant-lapsed:<grant>`), then marks the grant `lapseNoticedAt`. The text names the agent and project, each quoted once with `quoted()`, the right, the window and the last use, within the 200-character notice limit.
- **Chat (`chat/policy-edit.ts`).** A length in days on a standing-grant edit (owner-stated, picked on apply, or `grants.defaultDays`/30) is now the idle window: `decided.idleDays` is stored and the grant is made with `idleDays`. A day the owner names (`until`) stays an end date, and "no end" stays no end. The proposal says the grant lapses only once the agent has not used it for N days and that each use restarts the count, and that the owner is told once when it lapses. Only `grants.maxDays`, unset by default, refuses a length (the existing 36,500-day ceiling stays as a bound on the number). The `grant.create` chat line says "lapses once unused for N days, each use renews it" when `idleDays` is given, and the interpreter prompt says when to give it. The setting descriptions of `grants.maxDays` and `grants.defaultDays` say what the length now means.
- **Standing-rule proposals (`policy/load.ts`, A07d).** The length chosen on accept is the grant's idle window (`idleDays`), not an end date. The A07d history counts a grant that lapsed from non-use as having run its full term, and a lapsed grant is no longer live.
- **What agents are told (`policy/policy.ts`, `policy/describe.ts`).** The approvals an agent holds show "lapses after N days unused; each use renews it".
- **Tests (each fails without the change).** `security/grant-idle.test.ts` (all four storage backends): used every four days, still live after 100 days; unused, lapses exactly at its window; use after a lapse does not revive it; 40 uses in a day write once (revision counted), the next day once more; an end-dated grant still ends and is never written; a derived grant renews its parent and falls with it; the owner is told once, a revoked or live grant is not reported, a failed tell is retried; `lapsedCovering`; `idleDays` checks; a retry of a pre-A07h grant under the same command returns it. `dispatch/grant-idle.test.ts`: placement renews once a day and keeps the task running past the first window; a task after a lapse is blocked with the lapsed right named; a never-given right keeps the old wording. `policy/grant-idle.test.ts`: an approval grant used every five days for 60 days with a 7-day window, one write per day of use, then the lapse named in the decision. `dispatch/grant-lapse-notice.test.ts`: the notice text (quoting, limit) and the loop telling once. `chat/policy-edit.test.ts`: a 1000-day window applied without a cap, renewed by use past 100 days, an `until` day still an end date, refused once `grants.maxDays` is set. `chat/commands-preview.test.ts`: the `grant.create` line with `idleDays`. Updated: `policy/load.test.ts`, `chat/policy-edit.test.ts` and `chat/grant-consequence.test.ts` assertions that read `expiresAt` now read `idleEnd` (same instants).

**Left**
- The reviewer and decider availability checks (`agents/agents.ts` about lines 417, 437, 461) read the effective grants, so a lapsed grant no longer counts there, but being listed as an available reviewer is not a use and does not renew a grant. A reviewer's grants renew when its own attempts are placed or its approvals decide actions.
- The window of a chat grant retried after a crash starts when the grant is actually made, not at the time first fixed for the edit (the length fixed then is kept).
- `grant.create` from chat without `idleDays` still makes a grant with no end, as before; the interpreter is told to use `idleDays` only when the owner asks for a grant that lapses when unused.
- The lapse loop scans every grant record each time it runs (at most every ten minutes); the dispatcher's own grant check already scans them per agent.
- Not checked end to end: the composed controller ticking the lapse loop into the owner's notification inbox (the loop and the text are tested; the composition line is the same shape as the other notice loops).
- ASSUMPTION: "use" is the dispatcher placing a task that needs the grant and the approval policy deciding an action by an approval grant; a grant is renewed only while it still holds.
- ASSUMPTION: "at most once a day" is per UTC calendar day, so a window can end up to a day earlier than the last use would give.
- ASSUMPTION: an idle grant whose record has no `lastUsedAt` (not written by this code) counts as lapsed, so a right nobody can date does not stay open.
- ASSUMPTION: a retry, after the upgrade, of a grant step that was made before it (same command ID, now with `idleDays` instead of `expiresAt`) returns the grant already made rather than failing as a conflicting command; a retry that would grant something else still fails.
- **Runs** (this worktree; `npx tsc --build --force` clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard as an absolute `file://` URL). controller `dist/{agents,chat,dispatch,api,status,security,policy,configuration}/*.test.js`: 3,185 tests, 3,181 pass; the 4 failures were `chat/grant-consequence.test.ts` reading `expiresAt` of a 30-day chat grant, updated to `idleEnd` and re-run with `chat/model-interpreter` and `policy/load` (110 of 110). The longest file, `chat/policy-edit.test.ts`, took about 186 s. `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6, `roadmap:check` ok, `check:deps` ok. `api:docs:write` run (the `grant.create` `idleDays` argument).

**Review fixes (clean-context Opus review, 2026-11-10)**
- Use at placement was recorded at the grant check, before the route, context and host checks, so a task waiting for a host renewed its grants every day without running and kept an unused right open for ever. The dispatcher now records the use only when the task is placed (`#missingGrants` returns a `recordUse` step that the admission runs on its `ok` path). Test: `dispatch/grant-idle.test.ts` "a task that waits for a host ...".
- The upgrade-retry branch of `GrantService.grant` returned the existing grant for any `command_conflict` with the same grantee, action and project, so a retry with different terms, resource, reason, source or end date was silently given the old grant. It now applies only when everything else is the same and the length moved from an end date (stored) to an idle window (asked). Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts`.
- `noticeLapsed` reported a grant that had already ended on its own `expiresAt` as "lapsed from non-use" once its idle end also passed. Such grants are skipped. Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts`.
- `recordGrantUse` walked from a derived grant to its parent even when the derived grant itself no longer held; a grant that does not hold now renews nothing. Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts`.
- A chat `grant.create` took any `idleDays` the interpreter supplied. Like every other value, it must now be a length the owner's own words give (`lengthInWords`), as a whole number; otherwise a plain question is asked and nothing is drawn up. Test: `api/start-chat.test.ts`.
- Noted, not changed: a recorded use bumps the grant's revision, so a revoke (API or chat) holding an older `expectedRevision` can fail with `stale_revision` once in a day of use and must be retried. With the at-most-once-a-day write, a 1-day window can lapse between days for a grant in steady use (see the ASSUMPTION above). A09's `approve.maintenance.<kind>` auto-approval should count as a use once that branch merges.

**Second review fixes (clean-context Opus review, 2026-11-10; branch merged with main at A09 slice 2 first)**
- The owner's revocation could be refused by a recorded use: a use writes the grant record, so a revoke holding the revision the owner saw (the API, or a chat revocation drawn up before the use) failed with `stale_revision`. An active grant's terms never change after it is made (the only writes before a revocation are a use and the lapse notice), so `GrantService.revoke` now accepts any revision from the one expected up to the current one of a still-active grant, refuses one it never had, and returns the revision it left; the chat revocation reports that revision instead of `expected + 1`. Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts`.
- A one-day window lapsed in steady use: a use was written at most once per UTC day, so a grant made at 00:30 and used every 20 minutes was recorded as last used at 00:30 until the next day's first use, by which time it had lapsed. A use is now written once the recorded one is `useWriteInterval(idleDays)` old: a day, or a 24th of a shorter window (an hour for one day). The command is named by the use it replaces (`grant-use-<grant>-<lastUsedAt>`). Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts` (three days of use every 20 minutes, about 72 writes).
- A long attempt lapsed its own rights: use was recorded only at placement, and an attempt may run up to `time.maxMinutes` (a week), so an agent working one task for longer than a short window lost `attempt.work` mid-run (and the bridge refused its tools). Every presentation of a task credential (`TaskCredentialService` `#present`) now records a use of the grants covering `attempt.work` and `task.read` on its task, and the tool bridge's start check passes the access the tool asks for (`principalOf(..., { uses })`), counted only when all of it is held. `noteUseOf` skips a grant looked at in the last hour, so a request costs no extra reads. Test: `security/task-credentials.test.ts`.
- A reviewer's review right never renewed: deciding a review checks `review.decide` but recorded nothing, so a reviewer whose only standing grant was that right lost it after one window however many reviews it decided. `ReviewService.decide` now records the use. Test: `review/review.test.ts`.
- A09's standing permission (`approve.maintenance.<kind>`) is a use when it approves a request: the grant records it rests on are renewed after the request is written. Test: `maintenance/maintenance.test.ts`.
- A lapse notice that failed was raised at once, so one notice that could never be given stopped every later grant from being reported. The pass now goes on past a failed tell (at most `limit` failures and `limit` notices a pass) and raises the first failure at the end. Test: `security/grant-idle.test.ts`.
- Lengths in words: "fifteen days", "forty-five days", "twenty one days" (21, not 1), "sixty days", "a couple of weeks", "a hundred days" were not read, so a chat grant with such a length asked again and again. Teens, tens, compounds, "a couple of" and "a hundred" are read. Test: `chat/policy-edit.test.ts`.
- Checked, unchanged: the review binding's policy digest holds grant IDs and end dates, not revisions, so a use does not invalidate a reviewed approval; the derive and maintenance fences on a grant revision can fail with `stale_revision` in a race with a use written at the same moment, and succeed when asked again (the maintenance claim loop judges again by itself); the reviewer and decider availability lists still do not count as a use (being listed is not using the right).
- ASSUMPTION (replaces the UTC-day one above): a recorded use may be up to `useWriteInterval` (one day; an hour for a one-day window) older than the real last use, so a window can end that much earlier than the last use would give.

## A09 second slice: maintenance requests through the bridge, and standing permission (2026-11-10)

**Built.** (1) Two bridge operations (T06's closed list, `toolbridge/service.ts`; declared in `pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts` as `nimblenewt__maintenance-request` and `nimblenewt__maintenance-status`). `maintenance.request` goes through the state API with the worker's own task credential (`maintenance.request`, command ID `bridge:<attempt>:<call>`, so the same call is the same request), takes only `kind`, `spec`, `reason`, `rollbackPlan` (an `agentId` is refused: an agent asks for its own environment only) and answers the maintenance ID and status at once; the application of a rule-approved request runs after the answer, so a call whose own worker the application replaces has already returned. It is a write: a pause refuses it like the others, and it is recorded as an activity step. `maintenance.status` reads one of the agent's own requests (`maintenance.get`; the ID must be `mnt-` plus 20 base32 characters) and returns kind, class, status, digest, the decision's verdict/via/rule, applied time and the pending or failure reason with control and format characters removed. (2) Standing permission (`maintenance.ts`, `#standingGrant`): a `package` or `extension` request **without install scripts** is approved by rule `standing-grant` when the agent holds, as stored now, a grant of exactly `approve.maintenance.<kind>` for project `*` and no resource, not restricted; `approve.*`, a wildcard or a grant for one project do not count. It is judged again at application (`#standing`), so a permission revoked between approval and application sends the request back to pending. The owner's `rules` switch turns it off with the catalogue and site rules. The API summary of `maintenance.request` says so (`api-v1.md` regenerated).

**Tests.** `maintenance/maintenance.test.ts` (one test per backend: kinds, install scripts, other agents, broad and one-project grants, self-grant and derive refused, restriction, revocation re-checked at apply; mutation-checked by removing the re-check), `api/start-maintenance-bridge.test.ts` (through `startController` with a real dispatched attempt: the ID comes back while the applier is held open, the standing permission approves, the package waits, `agentId` and a capability field in the spec are refused, status read; the application finishes after the attempt), the pause suite of `toolbridge/service.test.ts`, the tool list in `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts`.

ASSUMPTION: standing permission covers only the dependency kinds (package, extension) and only without install scripts: README's table puts broader access under a scoped review per change and host policy and the base under the owner, and the card says install scripts never run before an approval of the exact artifact. It is installation-wide (project `*`) because an environment belongs to an agent, not to a project.

**Left (A09 stays planned).** (1) The real applier: stage, trial in a disposable environment, Suspend without release, checkpoint, reload or restart, validate and restore keeping session, compaction and prior Pause/Suspend intent, writing the revision through `EnvironmentService`, rolling back a failed activation; install scripts inside the boundary. The default applier still leaves every approved change pending (acceptance: unsupported safe restoration leaves it pending, which holds today). (2) An administrator role for host policy and the shared base (the owner only today). (3) A reviewer view of install behaviour beyond the `installScripts` flag. (4) A test that a review outage leaves the change pending while the approved environment keeps working.

**Review fixes (2026-11-10).** (1) A standing permission counts only when every term its grant record carries can be judged by the maintenance check: a time window (met now) and `delegation`; a grant with `environments`, a spend limit, audiences, branches or the owner's free-text `conditions` leaves the request to a decider (before, terms were ignored, so a grant the owner limited to office hours or "only from our registry" approved anything at any time). A grant given at enrollment has no terms and counts. (2) The approval is fenced: the request write and the claim at apply carry a revision check of the grant record (and every record a derived grant rests on), or of the principal record for an enrollment grant, so a revocation written between the check and the write fails the write and the request is judged again (it waits for a decider). A new restriction written in that window is not fenced (restrictions are found by a scan); it counts from the next drive. (3) `maintenance-status` reads the agent's own requests only: the state API shows a supervisor its reports' requests, and through the bridge those read as not found. (4) The applier contract now says `installScripts: false` is the requester's claim: the applier installs with every install and lifecycle script switched off and should fail an artifact that declares them. (5) The API summary of `maintenance.request` no longer says 200 requests a day are accepted: the daily cap is the owner's setting and off by default, so an agent holding a standing permission is bounded per day only when the owner sets one (pending requests stay capped at 20; rule-approved ones do not count as pending).

**Second review (2026-11-10).** (1) Fixed: the terms of a derived standing permission were read from the derived record only; every record of its chain is now judged (a derived record that lacks its parent's terms, such as an older one, no longer sheds the owner's conditions or window). Tests: that case, and the fences (a revocation between the check and the request write refuses the write; the root of a derived grant and an enrollment grant, through the principal record, fence the claim; each mutation-checked). (2) Checked, no change: the fenced records change only on a revocation or an owner's edit of the principal, so unrelated writes do not keep failing requests; a failed fence leaves the request refused (asked again) or approved and re-judged, never applied. `delegation` is not enforced anywhere and a grant record is its grantee's alone, so it lets no other agent use the permission. Window bounds are UTC, end exclusive, as in the approval policy. A request approved inside a window that closes before application lapses to pending (it is not told to anyone; the same holds for any rule that lapses). (3) Recorded: a restriction written between the drive's check and its claim (milliseconds) is not fenced, and one written after the claim does not stop that application, as for a revocation. An agent holding a standing permission can still make any number of rule-approved requests while the owner's daily cap is off; controller work stays bounded (each tick drives at most 50, applications run at most `maxApplies` at once, and the grant scan is the one every authenticated call already makes), so no new cap was added against the recorded decision. `installScripts: false` stays the requester's claim until the real applier exists: the controller never sees the artifact, so the applier contract (scripts off, fail an artifact that declares them) is the only enforcement point.

## C07i: each attempt's starting size is watched across a task's hand-offs, and the owner is alerted before it becomes a slowdown (2026-11-10)

C07h's repeated-handoff test proves the bound in a simulation; this watches the real thing. Every first call the controller's guards judge is recorded per task and hand-off, and a run of rising sizes or a size close to its route's limit raises one alert. The watch only records and tells: it never trims, cuts or compacts anything, and it writes no record but its own.

- **The record (`context/start-size.ts`, `StartSizeService`).** One `ctx-start-size` record per task: per attempt its hand-off number (0 for the first attempt; another round or launch of the same attempt replaces its point and is not a hand-off), size in tokens, route, local or remote worker, window and startup limit with the share used (absent, never 0, when the route's window is not known), whether the call was admitted, the parts it was made of (stored conversation, hand-off package, notes, project rules, task text, rebuilt route view, system prompt and tool schemas, the rest) and the records that hold their originals. The newest 50 points are kept whole and older ones are rolled up (count, hand-off range, smallest, largest, sum), so the record is bounded however long a task runs.
- **Alerts.** A trend alert opens when the size rose over `risingHandoffs` hand-offs in a row (default 3), each at least `minRisePercent` larger (default 1, so noise of a few tokens is not a rise); a share warning opens when a call passes `warnPercent` of its route's startup limit (default 80; the startup limit is the 25 percent share of the window, above which the call is refused). Each stays open while its condition lasts and is raised once, not per attempt; it clears when the run breaks or the size falls back, and the next run raises a new one. Only the newest point is judged. The alert names the trend, the three largest contributors (by growth over the run for a trend) and the records that keep the originals.
- **Where it is fed (`dispatch/runtime-guards.ts`, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `dispatch/local-worker.ts`, `remote/host.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`).** `controllerGuards.admit`, which both the local worker and the controller's check before a remote offer (C07o) go through, gives every call it judges to `startSize.record`: the context service's figure and limit when judged, the same estimate made without a window when the route has none (refused as before, C07n). `estimatedFirstCall` now sizes the text of a remote order on a route of unknown window instead of answering zeros, so that figure is not recorded as 0. The dispatcher sends `WorkOrder.startParts` (the lengths of the task text, project rules, hand-off paragraph and route view, and the `hnd-`/`hof-` IDs the paragraph names); the remote host strips it before the offer. The local worker now asks the guards about the order as it is sent (without a stored conversation that is not carried, with the note that says why), so the stored conversation counts only when it is carried. A failure of the watch is reported through `onError` and never changes the decision.
- **The owner and the task (`api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `status/status.ts`).** Each opened alert is one notification (command ID from the alert, ref `ctx-start-size`): a trend is a Notice, a share warning is Needs you. The task's status shows `Warning: ...` while an alert is open, to the owner and to whoever may work on the task. The `start_size` status view (chat: the task by its title) shows the newest ten points, the roll-up, the open alerts with how to read each original (`handoff.get`, `context.handoff.read`, `context.note-archive.read`, and the `handoff_archive` view for cut package sections) and the thresholds.
- **State API (`api/operations.ts`).** `context.start-size.read` (the owner, and whoever may work on the task); `context.start-size.get` and `context.start-size.change` (owner only; `set`/`unset`, bounds `risingHandoffs` 2 to 20, `minRisePercent` 0 to 100, `warnPercent` 50 to 99). The change is a chat command (applied at once: a reversible setting). `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `dist/dispatch/*.test.js dist/remote/*.test.js` 1575 tests, 1572 pass and 3 fail on the first run (stub context services without `limits` read by the watch while no watch was bound; fixed by reading the limit only when a watch is bound, the 56 tests of those files then pass); `dist/{chat,status,api,context}/*.test.js` 2022 / 2022 (528 s at concurrency 4). New files alone: `context/start-size.test.js` 37 / 37 (14 s), `dispatch/start-size-watch.test.js` 4 / 4, `api/start-start-size.test.js` 1 / 1 (3 s), `chat/start-size-chat.test.js` 4 / 4. Mutation: the guards no longer give a judged call to the watch: the watch and composed tests fail 5 of 5. `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 / 6; `roadmap:check` ok; `check:deps` ok; `api:docs:write` added the three operations and the `start_size` view.
- **Tests.** `context/start-size.test.ts` (4 backends): one alert per run with trend and contributors, a new one after a break; flat and falling raise nothing; the 80 percent warning before refusal, once; unknown window recorded with no limit or share, local and remote; validated owner thresholds; repeats; the roll-up; no task change and no record but its own written; who may record and read. `dispatch/start-size-watch.test.ts` (4 backends): the guards record admitted, refused and unknown-window calls with their parts, local and before a remote offer, the host is not given `startParts`, and a failing watch changes no decision. `api/start-start-size.test.ts`: four hand-offs through `startController` raise one notification and a task warning, read through the state API, with the task text untouched; thresholds through the API, owner only. `chat/start-size-chat.test.ts` (4 backends): the trend read and thresholds changed in free words.
- ASSUMPTION: a "hand-off" is a new attempt on the task (the C07h hops); a restart or another round of the same attempt is the same point.
- ASSUMPTION: a trend alert is a Notice and a share warning is Needs you: a rising trend asks nothing of the owner yet, while a call near its limit is one growth away from a refusal. The owner can change a kind's level as for any notification.
- ASSUMPTION: the parts are what the controller can tell apart from the order; whatever the runtime adds beyond them (its own startup builder's pieces) is "the rest". "Links the archived originals" is met by naming the records and the operations that read them; the stored conversation itself is kept in the attempt's checkpoint by its host.
- Left: the parts of a remote first call are the controller's estimate (remote hosts report no provider count, C07o); the alert is not pushed into the running agent's context (it is the owner's and the task's); there is no installation-wide list of tasks with an open alert beyond the notifications.
- Second review (2026-11-10). An alert whose notification failed after its record committed was never told (a repeat of the record opens nothing): `startSizeRecorder` (`context/start-size.ts`, used by the composition) now tells every alert open on the task after each record, with the alert's command ID, so a failed telling is retried at the task's next first call and a told one is a repeat that notifies nobody again (a repeat refused as another command, once the owner's item moved on, is taken as told). The guards waited on the watch without bound: a watch held up (a database that does not answer) held the first call; they now wait at most `START_SIZE_WAIT_MS` (2 s) and the record goes on by itself. Left as they are: a share that rounds to the line (79.95 percent shown as 80.0) warns, which is early, not late; an attempt rolled up past the 50 points and admitted again would count as a new hand-off (attempts of a task are sequential, so this is not expected); a record that outlives the wait can land after a later round's record of the same attempt and replace its point with the earlier figure.

## W03: a natural stop is not success; the run ends stopped-early and the attempt goes on from its checkpoint (2026-11-10)

Before this card a completed turn ended the attempt `succeeded` (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `#run`), whatever W02 said about how it ended, and the work-end hook (`work-end.ts` `resolveOnEnd`) had nothing to say for an agent that never called work.end.

**Built**
