- **The rule (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`).** A completed turn whose end kind is `normal` ends the attempt as before. Any other kind (`length`, `empty-visible-text`, `no-work-end`, `announced-step-without-tool-call`, `unknown`) goes to the end as before with an `early` mark; the end hook still runs first, so an agent whose work.end ending is found there (completed by the hook, `handled`) ends as the agent said, and one whose own `blocked`/`abandoned`/`partial` ending is carried by the end keeps that outcome. Only when the end would otherwise be `succeeded` does `#stoppedEarly` take over. A turn that ends with an accepted work.end done is unchanged (the sweep usually finishes it before the turn's result even arrives).
- **The readmit.** Within the task's readmits (`STOPPED_EARLY_READMITS` = 2) the same attempt goes back to `waiting`, like a parked one: the worker is stopped, the model call ended, the place given back, the hold and credential kept, `pinnedHost` = the host that ran it, `resumeFrom` = the turn's checkpoint (or one taken now), and a `resumeNote` that says the turn ended before the work was said to be done and asks for the rest of PLAN.md, a commit and work.end. `turnRound` numbers the readmits and goes into the turn's request ID (`cmd:adm:<attempt>:se<n>`): Pi answers a repeated request ID with the recorded result (or refuses it with other content), so without a new ID the conversation could not take another input. The run is recorded in `stoppedEarly` (`endKind`, `visibleChars`, `at`, `readmitted`) with the turn's ending, in the same write.
- **The count is durable.** One record per task (`dispatch-stopped-early`, `{ taskId, generation, readmits, attempts }`) is written in the same commit as the readmit, so a controller restart keeps it and a crash cannot readmit without counting. It is per task, so a later attempt of the same task (one admitted after a lost worker) does not get two more.
- **After the readmits.** The next early stop (or one with no checkpoint to go on from) ends the attempt: the dispatch record's outcome is the new `stopped-early` (the assignment, whose outcomes are succeeded/failed/abandoned, records it `abandoned`; nothing records it succeeded), nothing is readmitted, and the task gets a new blocker type `agent_stopped_early` (resolver the owner, notified as the other dispatcher blockers are; a route hint in `status/explain.ts`). Its summary (at most 1,000 characters) carries how often it stopped and how the last turn ended, the last visible text quoted once with `quoted()` (redacted, escaped, 300 characters), the plan progress (`n of m step(s) checked; not checked: "..."`, each step quoted, at most 5 named) and the diff stat. What the host cannot say is said so ("not known (the host does not report it)", or the host's error), never guessed.
- **Plan progress and diff stat.** `WorkerHost.progress?` (new, optional; `WorkProgress { plan?: { done, open }, diffStat? }`), asked with a 10 s bound. `LocalWorker` takes a `progress` option. The worker package supplies it: `LocalWorkspaces.progress({ taskId, projectId })` reads `PLAN.md` at the checkout's top (a plain file only, opened without following a link, at most 256 KiB, at most 200 checkbox steps of 200 characters; `- [ ]`, `* [x]`, `1. [ ]`) and `GitBridge.diffStat` (git's `--shortstat` of the checkout against `refs/nn/base` through a throwaway index, so committed, uncommitted, new and ignored files all count, plus commits ahead of the base). Both read only.
- **A stop wins.** `stop` (owner or emergency) notes itself before anything else; a run that stopped early finds it and ends `abandoned` instead of readmitting. A stop that joined such an end after its readmit was written ends the waiting attempt itself. A stop of an attempt that is already waiting to go on ends it as any stop does.
- **Tests (each fails without the change).** `controller/dispatch/stopped-early.test.ts` (4 backends): a fixture agent that stops without work.end is never `succeeded`, goes on twice from its turn's checkpoint on the same host with request IDs `…`, `…:se1`, `…:se2`, then ends `stopped-early` (assignment `abandoned`) with the blocker carrying the quoted last text (a bidi control escaped), plan progress and diff stat, and nothing starts after; every non-normal kind and an unknown one stop early; a normal end, a work.end done completed by the end hook, and the agent's own blocked ending are unchanged; a count kept across two controller restarts, and a host whose progress throws said so; an owner's and an emergency stop that arrive while the end hook runs, and after the readmit was written, both win. `controller/dispatch/turn-end.test.ts` now expects only `normal` to succeed. `worker/workspace/local-host.test.ts`: plan steps and diff stat read, the index untouched, a commit counted ahead, a too-big plan, a directory and a link not read. `integration/w03-stopped-early.test.ts`: through the composed controller, the real sandboxed worker process and the real checkout layout, the second and third runs' model requests carry the earlier turns (the same conversation) and the note, and the blocker shows the plan and `2 files changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) against the task's base`; an agent that ends with work.end done succeeds in one run.
- **Fixtures.** `ScriptedWorker`/`ScriptedHandle` (the controller's test worker) now report `normal` for a completed turn whose script names no kind (`endsNormally = false` gives an older worker that says nothing): those tests are about other things and model an agent that finished. The remote fixtures in `api/start-c07n`, `start-new-primary` and `start-remote-contract` that model a finished agent now send `endKind: "normal"`; composed integration fixtures whose agent finishes now end with a work.end call.

**Left**
- ASSUMPTION: an `unknown` end kind (an older worker, or a remote host that does not pass the kind on) is treated as not normal: it stops early and is readmitted within the same limit, then blocked. A turn nobody vouched for is not taken as done; the cost is at most two more runs and a visible blocker, never a silent success. The agent's work.end, if it made one, still ends the attempt as it said.
- ASSUMPTION: the count is per task and assignment generation; when the owner assigns the task again (a new generation) after the blocker, it starts at 0. The owner has looked at the blocker by then.
- ASSUMPTION: an early stop with no checkpoint to go on from (none in the result and none could be taken) is not readmitted: the card asks for the same conversation, and a fresh one would be a new attempt in disguise. It ends at once with the blocker, which says so.
- (Changed in review, below.) A `length` or `unknown` stop after an accepted work.end done that the hook could not complete now is not an early stop.
- The readmitted run sends the task's text again with the note (the order's content is the same); W04 nudges inside the turn instead.
- A remote host does not report progress yet (the blocker says the host does not report it).
- No status view shows `stoppedEarly` per run yet (W08); the blocker is the owner's view.
- **Runs** (this worktree; `npx tsc --build --force` clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard as an absolute `file://` URL). controller `dist/{dispatch,api,work-end,status,chat,remote,toolbridge,workspace-ops}/*.test.js`: 3,694, one failing (`turn-end.test` on PostgreSQL: the waiting attempts of earlier kinds took the tick's place before the last task's; fixed by stopping each after it is looked at, then 24 of 24 for `turn-end` and `stopped-early` on all backends). worker (whole package): 286 of 286. integration `h12*`, `w02-end-kinds`, `w03-stopped-early`, `t06b-*`, `t07b-jobs`, `c09h-local-artifact`: 46 of 46 (c09h after its fixture change). `scripts/plan.test.mjs`: 6 of 6. `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` ok. `api:docs:write` made no change.

**Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-10).** Four fixes, each with a test that fails without it:
- An accepted work.end `done` that the end hook could not complete just now (task paused, another instance holding it) made `resolveOnEnd` answer nothing, so a `length` or `unknown` turn was readmitted while the agent's ending was still open (the sweep would later submit it while the attempt ran again). `resolveOnEnd` now answers `{ pending: true }` and the dispatcher drops the early mark: the turn's own end stands as before W03 (`stopped-early.test.ts`, 4 backends).
- The end hook gives up after `endHookMs`; an agent ending still being completed then joined the end that readmitted the attempt, so work.end recorded its attempt finished while it was in fact waiting to run again. `finishWith` now ends the attempt itself when the end it joined left it unfinished (same test, made deterministic with a slow worker stop).
- When the readmit was not written because something else moved the attempt (a stop, a controller shutdown sending it back to waiting), the run fell through to the used-up blocker: a stop asked meanwhile now ends it `abandoned` with the stop's reason, and an attempt left waiting by another path is left as it is (no blocker claiming the readmits are used up).
- `readPlan` opens `PLAN.md` without blocking (a file swapped for a pipe after the `lstat` no longer hangs the read), checks the opened file again and reads at most 256 KiB + 1 byte instead of the whole file. Tests: a pipe and a device are not read; the diff stat runs no filter, diff driver, fsmonitor or hook named by a `.gitattributes` and a planted `.git/config` in the agent's checkout (the existing hardening, now covered).

- Review runs (`npx tsc --build --force` clean, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard): controller `dist/{dispatch,api,work-end,status,chat,remote,toolbridge,workspace-ops}/*.test.js` 3,698 of 3,698; worker package 288 of 289 (1 platform skip); integration `h12*`, `w02-end-kinds`, `w03-stopped-early`, `t06b-*`, `t07b-jobs`, `c09h-local-artifact` 46 of 46; `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6; `roadmap:check` and `check:deps` ok; `api:docs:write` made no change.
- Noted, not changed: remote results with no checkpoint end `stopped-early` at once (no readmit) unless the agent's work.end ends them, so a remote agent that ends with work.end is unaffected, and one from a worker older than W02 gets a blocker instead of a silent success. If an attempt from an older assignment generation were still running after a reassignment, it could reset the per-task count to its own generation; a reassignment ends the old attempts, so this is not expected to happen.

## Merge note: C07i with W03 (2026-11-10, lead)

- Both branches changed the first-call order in `dispatch/dispatcher.ts`; the merge keeps W03's per-round request id (`:se<n>`) and C07i's `startParts`.
- Two existing tests needed the same fixture fixes the other W03 tests had: `api/start-start-size.test.ts` now has its scripted turn report `endKind: "normal"`, and the `h12bf-composed` compaction fixture answers were shortened again (440 to 400 repeats) because with C07i the first call of the second attempt was estimated at 10,565 tokens against a 10,240 limit (it passed at the C07o and W02 merges). ASSUMPTION: that rise comes from C07i's change to count the order as actually sent; it was not traced to a single cause, so a reviewer of the next first-call card should confirm the estimate is not counting a part twice.

## W01 (bench fix): the first baseline is invalid; acceptance suites, CONTRACT blocks, spec fit, a fixed classifier and a Claude control agent (2026-11-10)

The first baseline (43 of 54 runs, 2026-11-09/10) scored no finish, and an audit of every run found it measured the gap between the prompts and the hidden tests rather than Pi: in 38 of 43 runs a hidden test demanded wording, a field name or a signature the prompt never stated, and 9 `stopped-early` labels were classifier misses. Its data is kept, re-labelled only, in `/srv/code/worktrees-pi/eval-results/baseline-1-invalid/`; no rate may be read from it. `scripts/pi-eval/README.md`, "What changed on 2026-11-10", is the manual.

What is built (branch `w01-bench-fix`):

- **Classifier.** A report with every PLAN.md box ticked, a clean tree and a green last self-test is a done claim whatever its words; "all boxes ticked", "tree clean", "all steps committed" are done words; a closing scoped caveat note ("Remaining risk / not done:") makes it `done-with-caveats`, still a done claim. New outcome **interface-mismatch**: a done claim whose build failed only in the held-back files (a non-finish, not a false done). `rescore.mjs` finds moved runs, reads old runs' mismatch from their setup log, prints a before/after table and never overwrites a backup.
- **Rescore of the invalid baseline** (43 runs, smoke runs aside):

  | outcome | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | stopped-early | 9 | 0 |
  | wrong | 32 | 28 |
  | interface-mismatch | 0 | 13 |
  | timeout | 2 | 2 |

- **Task design.** Every task prompt ends with a CONTRACT block naming each exported name, field, signature and message meaning the scored tests use (no solution code). The score is a bench-owned **acceptance suite** per task (`scripts/pi-eval/acceptance/<id>/`) that asserts meaning, not whole sentences, written at fresh `w01-acceptance-*` paths; the shipped test files still run, reported as "matches shipped wording" (informational, no gate). grant-proposals' prompt now gives the solution's own no-limit sentence and the `only in proj-x` form for an unnamed project.
- **Spec fit** in `--calibrate`: every literal, regex, property name and relative import inside an acceptance assertion must be in the prompt, the base source or the test's fixtures, or carry a reason in `acceptance.json` `allow`.
- **Leftover processes:** every run's commands carry `PI_EVAL_RUN_DIR`; processes in the checkout, marked, or descended from one are killed after the agent, each suite and the run.

## L04d (second part): hosts' checkpoints become continuations, a route change is a model-change resume, and the reviewer's model is routed and metered (2026-11-10)

The first part gave the checked resume its two senses (the probe and the reviewer). The card's third piece was still missing: no host called `continuation.capture`, so a resumed attempt was checked only against a continuation the owner or a vouching host captured by hand, and with none the dispatcher let the attempt start unchecked. This part closes that loop through the dispatcher, which sees every checkpoint both the local and the remote host hand back.

**Built**
- **The worker process reads each checkpoint back (`8078a55f`; `contracts` `worker-channel.ts`, `pi-adapter` `worker/process.ts`, `worker` `host/process.ts`, `host/local.ts`).** After `adapter.root().checkpoint()` the process calls the adapter's own `verifyCheckpoint` (the conversation is opened from the store again, the entry must be a completed-turn boundary and the history up to it must digest the same) and sends the verdict on `checkpoint.ok` as `durable: { verified, error? }` (error one line, at most 300 characters; `durabilityOf` never throws). The channel refuses a `durable` with no boolean or a longer reason. The local host puts it on the checkpoint it hands the controller as `nn.durable`, on the turn's checkpoint and on one asked for; a process that ran no check sends none, and none is read as not verified.
- **Every checkpoint the dispatcher is handed is captured (`5557e4e8`; `continuation/host-capture.ts`, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `api/start.ts`).** `continuationRecorder` turns a host's `{ pi, nn }` checkpoint into `continuation.capture`, as the dispatcher (`service:dispatcher`): the adapter's reference from `pi`; complete only when `nn.durable.verified` is true, otherwise kept `incomplete` with the host's reason (never resumed from); the identity the task's latest complete continuation already has, else `task:<taskId>`; the summary lineage from the task's latest compaction (`[...lineage, id]` with its `earlier`, so C07q's fold is continued by the capture's own: 200 listed, the rest counted and chained) and the compaction count that lineage implies; the budget from accounting (`<currency> micros`); the artifacts and decisions of the previous complete continuation carried on; the next step in the controller's words ("Carry on with the task from the checkpoint taken when …"). One command per attempt, checkpoint, boundary and verdict, so the same checkpoint taken again is one capture; a conflict there is answered as already captured. A checkpoint taken in the middle of a turn (`nn.midTurn`), one not of this shape (a scripted worker's), or an agent a continuation cannot name is skipped and writes nothing. It never throws; a failure goes to `onError`. The dispatcher calls the hook at the end of every completed turn that left a checkpoint (`turn-complete`, before the attempt parks, is readmitted after an early stop or ends, so the resume that follows is checked against it), at a shutdown (`shutdown`) and whenever it asks for one (`manual`: quiesce, stop, recipe change; the early-stop fallback is `turn-complete`); a throw of the hook is reported, never the attempt's failure. `dispatch.captureContinuations: false` turns it off.
- **`after: model-change` (same commit, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts` `#resumeCheck`).** The route the checkpoint was taken on is the attempt's last model call's (else the route it was claimed with). A resume on another route starts its check with `after: "model-change"` and `previousModel`, so the continuation resume record says `modelChanged: true`. The check's key grows only in that case, so a check of an unchanged route keeps the key it had before this change.
- **The reviewer's model is behind the controller's routed client (`c3ef1428`, `api/start.ts`).** `StartOptions.resumeReview.model` (the host's raw client) is wrapped in `GuardedModelCall` (card U03b): credit and authentication failures block the provider, a rate limit or an outage cools the route down, and the tokens each call reports through `completeDetailed` are counted against the daily cap on the controller's own model calls (`ChatSpendService`); at the cap no call is made and the check waits at the review (`review_failed`). `routes` is now optional: absent, the routing table's eligible list for `resumeReview.role` (default `safety-supervisor`) is read at every review (`chatRoutes`, local-only, no paid routes).

**Tests (each fails without its change; mutation-checked on the built files, restored and rebuilt after)**
- `contracts` `worker-channel.test.ts`: `checkpoint.ok` with `durable` round-trips; a `durable` without a boolean, of the wrong type or with a 301-character reason is refused.
- `pi-adapter` `worker/process.test.ts`: the process's checkpoint carries `durable: { verified: true }`; `durabilityOf` gives the adapter's reason on one line for a checkpoint that does not read back and for a check that throws, within 300 characters. Mutant (no `durable` sent): 1 fails.
- `worker` `host/local.test.ts`: `nn.durable` is on the turn's checkpoint and on one asked for, the failed verdict with its reason, nothing for a process that did not check. Mutant (not carried): 1 fails.
- `continuation/host-capture.test.ts` (2 × 4 backends, the real `ContinuationService`): unchecked and failed read-backs incomplete with the reason on record and not the latest; a verified one complete with identity `task:<id>`, the agent, boundary, cursor, adapter and the controller's next step; the same checkpoint again replayed; the same at a shutdown a capture of its own; a mid-turn, foreign, malformed or host-agent checkpoint skipped with nothing written; with an owner's earlier continuation the identity `conv-1` and its artifact and decision carried, the budget rounded, 260 compactions folded so the capture lists 51 and folds 209 with the chained digest of those 209 in order. Mutant (durability ignored): 5 of 8 fail.
- `api/start-host-capture.test.ts` (new, 3 × SQLite and PostgreSQL, through `startController` and the dispatcher with a scripted host whose first turn stops early): the turn's checkpoint is captured complete by `service:dispatcher` at `turn-complete`, the readmitted attempt's check collects exactly that capture, is committed (`done`, `continue`) and one resume is recorded from it, and the second run starts from that checkpoint; a checkpoint that did not read back is kept incomplete with the reason, no check is run and the attempt goes on as before; with `captureContinuations: false` nothing is captured; a route moved by the owner between the two runs gives a check and a resume record with `model-change`, model `other`, model before `small`. Mutants: turn-end capture removed (3 of 3 fail), the hook not wired in the composer (3 of 3), the switch ignored (1), model change not derived (1).
- `api/start-resume-checkout.test.ts` (one more case, SQLite and PostgreSQL): with no routes given the reviewer is asked on the table's safety-supervisor list in order, the first route's rate limit gives way to the second and the next review skips the cooling route, each answering call's 120 tokens are counted, and at the owner's cap of 240 no call is made and the check blocks `review_failed`. Mutants: the guard bypassed, the spend left out, the routes not read from the table (each fails 1 per backend).

ASSUMPTION: capture is on by default. A checked resume with no continuation is no check at all, which is the complaint the card was written for; turning it off is one option.
ASSUMPTION: the "durability check" is the worker process's read-back of its store through the adapter's own `verifyCheckpoint` right after the checkpoint is taken. It proves the store holds the history the checkpoint names at that moment; it does not prove the bytes are on stable storage (no fsync is asked of Pi's JSONL store).
ASSUMPTION: the controller, not the host process, makes the capture call. Both hosts hand every checkpoint to the dispatcher already, the local host runs in the controller's process, and the worker package depends on no controller code; one recorder in the dispatcher covers the local and remote hosts with the same rules. A remote host's checkpoint is captured complete only if its worker sent `nn.durable` the same way.
ASSUMPTION: what the controller cannot name from a checkpoint is left empty, not guessed: no pending effects (so L04c's uncertain-effect check sees none from these captures), no scratch records, credentials or non-checkpointable tools, routing and environment revisions 0, and a next step in the controller's words. Artifacts and decisions come only from the previous complete continuation.
ASSUMPTION: the reviewer's tokens are counted under the same daily cap as the chat and coordinator (`chat-budget`/`chat-spend`): it is the one cap the controller has for its own model calls. Its default role is `safety-supervisor` because every routing table must give that role a valid fallback list (R04).
ASSUMPTION: the route the checkpoint was taken on is `modelCall.route ?? route` of the attempt record, not a field of the continuation (the capture contract has no route field).

**Runs** (this worktree, `npx tsc --build --force` clean, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): controller `dist/{lifecycle,dependencies,dispatch,context,api,chat,status,continuation}/*.test.js` 4,018 tests, 4,018 pass, 0 fail, 0 todo, 10 min at concurrency 4; `contracts`, `worker` `host/*`, `pi-adapter` `worker/*` 75 of 75; integration 117 tests, 105 pass, 10 skipped, 2 fail (`c07g-route-view` and `t06-bridge`: the real Pi attempt ends without outcome `succeeded`; both fail the same way at the base `fcc3c3df` with none of this card's changes, and with the capture hook unwired, so they are not this change's; most likely W03's stopped-early readmit of a turn with no `work.end`, left for its owner); `node --test scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 pass; `roadmap:check` "roadmap ok"; `check:deps` "package boundaries ok"; `api:docs:write` changed nothing (no operation or status text changed).

**Not done (L04d stays planned)**
- A real Pi process through the whole local worker capturing and then resuming: the composed tests use a scripted host; the read-back is tested in the process and the carry in the host separately.
- The lineage is read from the controller's compaction records, which only `ContextEnforcementService.compact` writes, and that still has no production caller (C07q). So in production a capture's lineage is empty and `compression` says `none` even when Pi compacted its own conversation; Pi's compactions have no controller record IDs to list.
- Pending effects, scratch records and the agent's own next step are not in host captures (above).
- The per-tick cache of the prerequisite scan is untouched.
- `search`, `external` and `mcp-resource` observation, the probe reading the task's own worker checkout rather than the binding's locator, and a reviewer that reads diffs (first part's list) are unchanged.
- No shipped entry point supplies a reviewer model client: `startController` routes and meters one when a host gives it, and nothing in this repository does. No state-API operation sets the daily cap (`ChatSpendService.setBudget` has no operation).

## L04d second part: review follow-ups (2026-11-10, lead)

One Opus review found no blocking bugs; these remain open under L04d:
1. The resume check uses the task's latest complete continuation, not the one matching the attempt's `resumeFrom`. If turn 1 left a verified capture A and turn 2 left a checkpoint B that failed read-back, the attempt resumes from B but the check and the resume record name A (a wrong record; Pi's own restore still verifies B on the host).
2. If the task's only earlier continuation was captured incomplete under another identity (an owner's hand capture), the recorder uses `task:<id>` and every later capture is refused as "different identity" and reported to `onError` each turn. The fix is a small service method that reads the stored identity.
3. Continuation records are never pruned (retention has no rule; the reference scan stops at 100,000 records per kind).
4. Smaller: the turn-complete capture is made before that turn's usage is charged; a provider blocked by the reviewer's guarded client stays blocked until restart (same as the chat); the reviewer shares the chat's daily token cap.

## W04: a turn that yields early is continued in the same turn, at most three times (2026-11-10)

W03 readmits a run that stopped early as a new request in the same conversation. W04 is the layer inside the turn. Pi Durable asks its `onYield` hooks about every final answer, and the first `continue` appends a user message and hands the run to a successor generation of the same submission. NimbleNewt did not install that hook before this card.

**Built**
- **The hook (`pi-adapter/src/continuation.ts`; `PiAdapterOptions.continuation`).** The adapter installs one `onYield` hook for its root conversation (branches and tasks are never continued). The count is kept in a Pi Durable conversation document (`nimblenewt.continuations`: `{ turn, used, length, ended }`). `PiAdapter.beginTurn(requestId)` makes a request the current turn: a new turn starts at 0, and the same turn begun again (a restarted process running the same request) keeps its count. At most `max` continuations per turn (default 3, 0 to 10; 0 installs nothing). For each final answer of the current turn the hook does this, in order:
  1. It reads the generation's stored decision (a memo), so a hook run again after a restart gets the same answer without asking again.
  2. Otherwise it reads the document. It continues nothing when there is no current turn, when the agent's work has ended (`markWorkEnded`), or when the bound is reached.
  3. Otherwise it asks the policy.
  The decision is stored in the memo before the count is written, and the count is written before the continuation is returned. A crash therefore repeats a decision or loses a continuation; it never adds one. Each continuation's text starts with `CONTINUATION_MARK` ("[NimbleNewt: the turn goes on]"). When the adapter builds a turn's result, a continuation does not start a new segment of the transcript, so the tool calls after a nudge (work.end included) belong to the turn and the W02 classifier sees them. A `length` stop is an answer to Pi (`generation.js` line 362), so it goes through the same hook. It is continued and counted (`length`), and the cut-off reply is never the turn's answer unless the bound is reached.
- **The worker (`pi-adapter/src/worker/process.ts`, `worker/nudge.ts`).** Before each nudge the worker asks the controller through the bridge (`turn.continue`, args `{ n, max, endKind }`, call ID `nudge:<digest of the turn>:<n>`, the task credential). Only `{ go: true }` gives the nudge. A refusal, an unreachable controller or a controller from before W04 (which refuses an operation it does not know) lets the answer end the turn, as before W04. The worker gives no nudge once the lease is gone, once the host has closed the process, or after an accepted work.end. That last fact is held in memory and in the document, so a restarted process knows it too. The nudge is fixed text: "Remaining: the unchecked steps of your PLAN.md. Make the next tool call now. When every step is done and committed, end with nimblenewt__work-end as your last call. If you cannot go on, end with nimblenewt__work-end with result blocked or partial and say why in the note; do not report done for work that is not done. A reply without a tool call does not end the work." (The blocked/partial sentence came from the second review: the first wording named done as the only ending, which pushes a stuck agent toward a false done.) A length stop has "Your last reply was cut off at the output limit." in front. `beginTurn` runs before every submit. Every `result` carries `nudges` (from the document, for this request), for any status. The end kind is still read from the turn's last reply, so it is the ending after the nudges.
- **The controller's bridge (`toolbridge/service.ts`).** `turn.continue` is a bridge operation that is not offered as an agent tool, and it is in `WRITES`. A pause therefore refuses it (`paused`), and so do an attempt that is not running, replaced or frozen (the binding) and a held or stale generation (L05c). Under `requireRecorded` it is exempt only from "no recorded generation", like `tool.discover`: it is the worker's own question, not a model call. It checks `1 ≤ n ≤ max ≤ 10` and that `endKind` is one of the four kinds without work.end. It writes nothing but an activity step of the task: "The turn of agent:… was continued (nudge n of 3): it had ended as <kind>, without a tool call or work.end."
- **The record (`contracts/worker-channel.ts`, `worker/host/local.ts`, `dispatch/{ports,model,dispatcher}.ts`, `remote/service.ts`).** The channel `result` has `nudges` (0 to `MAX_TURN_NUDGES` = 100; anything else fails the line). `HostTurnResult.nudges` and `WorkerTurnResult.nudges` carry it, and a remote host's result may carry it too (it is refused outside 0 to 100). The attempt records `turnEnd.nudges`, `nudges` on each `stoppedEarly` run, and `nudgesUsed`, the attempt's total over its turns, in the same writes that record the turn (end, park, readmit). A figure that is not a whole number from 0 to 100 is left out. The W03 blocker's "the last turn ended: …" adds ", after N nudge(s) to go on" when there were nudges. This is the data W08 shows.
- **Budgets.** A nudge is a model call of the same turn. It goes through the relay like any other call, so the spending gate is asked before it and its tokens are in the turn's usage once. The host's `turnSeq` counts turns (`run`s), not model calls, so a nudged turn is one turn. No budget is charged twice and no call is hidden.
- **Tests (each fails without the change; mutation-checked where noted).**
  - `pi-adapter/continuation.test.ts`: thinking-only twice then a tool call, continued in the same turn with the tool call in its result (fails without the segment change); exactly the bound and no more; a length stop continued, not the answer, counted as `length`; a declining, a throwing or a not-asked policy (work ended, no turn begun); a count per turn, the same turn begun again keeps it (fails if `beginTurn` always resets), `max` 0 and 11; a branch never continued.
  - `pi-adapter/worker/process.test.ts` (W04 tests through `runWorker`): thinking-only twice then work.end gives `normal` with `nudges: 2`, the controller asked before each nudge with the task credential, the model saw the nudge; never a tool call gives exactly 3 nudges, then `empty-visible-text`; a length stop is continued with its lead and is not the answer; `paused`, `fenced` and `invalid_command` refusals give no nudge and no further model call; no nudge after an accepted work.end, and a nudge after a refused one; a lease lost while asking gives no nudge; a restart between nudges, over JSONL storage and relayed model calls, makes the new process ask for nudges 2 and 3 (not 1) and stop after 3. The test host refuses `turn.continue` by default, so the older tests behave as before W04 (their exact results gained `nudges: 0`).
  - `controller/toolbridge/service.test.ts` (4 backends): the bound, a known kind, no extra arguments, one activity step per nudge, refused after the attempt ended; paused while the task is paused and answered after resume (fails if it is taken out of `WRITES`); exempt from no-recorded-generation, refused for a held task.
  - `controller/dispatch/nudges.test.ts` (4 backends): 3 + 3 + 3 nudges over W03's go-ons, recorded per run and summed (`nudgesUsed` 9), and the blocker says so; a nudged normal end, none, none said, bad figures, a failed turn.
  - `controller/remote/remote.test.ts`: a remote result's nudges recorded, and bad figures refused.
  - `worker/host/local.test.ts`: passed on, a failed turn's too.
  - `contracts/worker-channel.test.ts`.
  - `integration/w04-continuation.test.ts`, through the composed controller and the real sandboxed worker process: thinking-only twice then work.end succeeds in one run with 2 nudges, 4 model calls and 2 activity steps; never acting gives 4 calls a run, 12 over W03's three runs, `nudgesUsed` 9 and the blocker; a task paused during the first call gets no nudge and 1 model call (fails if `turn.continue` is not refused by a pause).
- **Fixtures.** The W03 rig moved to `integration/w03-rig-support.ts` (it can now play a thinking-only reply and run a hook before a reply). Each W03 run is now four model calls (`seen` 4/8/12, and `turnEnd.nudges` 3, `nudgesUsed` 9 asserted). `w02-end-kinds` refuses `turn.continue` like an older controller, so each kind there is the first answer. `h12b-worker-process` expects the one `turn.continue` question. In `t06b-composed-worker` the second task's prose-only agent is nudged (4 calls). Two fixtures had failed since W03 because their agent never ended with work.end or the runtime said no end kind: `c07g-route-view` (its agent now ends with work.end) and `t06-bridge` (its hand-made runtime now says `normal`). Main fixed both the same way meanwhile; the merge took main's version of them.

**Left**
- Bench variant C was not run and stays refused ("needs W04") in `scripts/pi-eval`. The bench drives the Pi command line (`pi-agent.mjs`, `runcard.sh`), not NimbleNewt's worker process, so the hook installed here does not apply to it. Variant C needs either a bench path through the worker process or a Pi command-line extension with the same hook, and a real model run on the owner's route. Neither is possible in this card (no real model calls). This acceptance item of W04 is open.
- The nudge names no plan step. The worker process has no view of the checkout (its tools go through the bridge), so it cannot read PLAN.md. A controller-side text with the unchecked steps (W03's `progress`) could be sent back in the `turn.continue` answer later; W06 gives the completion rules.
- If an update is placed at the very boundary where a nudge was decided, Pi starts the update's run instead and drops the continuation. The count was already written, so that turn has one nudge fewer. Bounded and safe.
- W07 gives a length stop its own words ("stop deliberating, act"). Today the lead sentence is the only difference.
- `nudgesUsed` sums the turns recorded through the dispatcher. A turn ended by the work.end sweep before its result arrived records no nudges (it has no turn result).
- No status view shows the nudges yet (W08), so no operation or status text changed, and `api:docs:write` made no change.
- ASSUMPTION: "without a tool call and without work.end" means any final answer of the turn while the agent's work.end has not been accepted, including a full report in prose. The card's evidence is that a natural stop is not success (W03), and the nudge tells the agent how to end.
- ASSUMPTION: the controller's agreement to each nudge (`turn.continue`) is how "never after a stop or pause" is enforced. The worker process cannot see a pause, and a nudged model call into a paused task would be refused at the relay and fail the turn instead. A controller that cannot be asked gives no nudge (fail closed). The cost is one bridge round trip per nudge.
- ASSUMPTION: the count is per turn (request ID), so a W03 readmit (`:se<n>`) gets three nudges of its own. That is at most 3 × 3 = 9 nudges and 12 model calls per attempt before the blocker. "Nudges used per attempt" is `nudgesUsed`.
- ASSUMPTION: a refused work.end (paused, for instance) is not an ending, so the turn after it may be nudged. The controller's pause check refuses that nudge too.
- Review fix: `turn.continue` is refused (`awaiting_approval`) while any call of the attempt waits for an approval. Such a turn is waiting, not stopping early: it ends and the attempt parks until the decision, as before W04. A nudge there spent model calls and pushed the agent toward ending its work with work.end instead of waiting (`toolbridge/service.test.ts`, fails without the check).

## W11: a job's end wakes its task, and the owner is told (2026-11-10)

Before this card a job an agent started (T07b) ran to its end and the controller recorded it, but nothing started or resumed the agent, and nothing told the owner. An agent that said "I will report when the build is done" had to poll, or hope a later attempt read the job.

**Built**
- **The wake record (`jobs/wakes.ts`, `jobs/jobs.ts`).** `JobOptions.wakes` (on in `startController`): every command that records a final state of a job of kind tool, remote or MCP (`finish` completed or failed, `confirmCancel` stopped, `markUnknown`, `decide` complete) writes, in the same commit, one `job-wake` record (ID derived from the job and the phase) and puts it on the due list (`job-wakes/index`, at most 1,000 due; the 20 most recent ends are kept there for the owner's view). Reconciling an outcome-unknown job writes a second record of its own (phase `reconciled`). A record that is already there writes nothing again, and a repeated command writes nothing at all, so repeated final-state records give one wake. A model request is part of a turn and writes none. The record carries the job's label, state, task, attempt and, for a cancelled job, who asked for the stop. Past the due bound the end is recorded as not woken (`skipped`, with why).
- **The attempt parks for its jobs (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`, `#parkForJobs`).** A turn that ends without work.end (W03's early stop) while jobs of its task run, or have just ended with their wake still due (`JobService.waitable`), does not go on at once as a stop before the work was done: the attempt parks (state `parked`, `waitsOnJobs`, no parked calls), its worker stopped, its run on the route ended and its place given back, its hold, credential, host and the turn's checkpoint kept, as for a parked call. Nothing is counted against W03's readmits for that. With no checkpoint to go on from, W03's rule applies as before.
- **No nudge while a job runs (`toolbridge/service.ts`).** `turn.continue` (W04) is refused (`awaiting_job`) while a job of the task runs on this machine (`LocalJobRuns.runningFor`), so an agent that ends its turn to wait, as the reply told it it may, is not pushed to act; its turn ends and the attempt parks.
- **The wake (`#wakeJobs`, `#wakeOne`, `#wakeDecision`, every tick before the waiting attempts are advanced).** Each due wake, oldest first, at most 50 a tick, is decided in this order: a task that is gone, done or cancelled, stopped (its own Stop or one of a scope above it; a Suspend counts as a pause), held by a stopped swarm parent, no longer assigned to an agent, or reassigned since the job started (another generation) is not woken; a job the task's own agent stopped does not wake it (it asked); a paused task waits on the due list and is woken when the pause is lifted. Then the task's attempt: a running one, or one parked for an approval, is not disturbed (the wake waits for its turn to end); one waiting to start gets the note added to its resume note (not counted: it was going to run anyway); one parked for its jobs is readmitted (`waiting`, the note as its resume note, `wakeRound` + 1, which names the turn's request `cmd:adm:<attempt>[:se<n>]:wk<n>` so the same conversation takes the wake as a new input, still pinned to its host); a task with no live attempt gets a new attempt of the same assignment and generation (`admitAttempt`, never beside a live one), unless an owner's `dispatch_blocked` or `agent_stopped_early` blocker is open or the task's attempts are used up. A new attempt's claim reads its note from a `job-wake-note` record, so its first run is told. The decision, the wake record and the due list change in the same commit as the attempt's readmit (exactly once; a restart between the job's end and the wake finds the wake due and wakes once). A new attempt is admitted in two steps (the wake is first marked `admitting` with the assignment's attempt count; a restart after the admission finds the attempt and does not admit another).
- **Bounded.** A readmit or a new attempt is a wake: at most 4 per task in a rolling hour (a fifth waits on the due list until the hour has passed), and counted in W03's per-task record (`wakes`, `wakeTimes`) together with W03's readmits, at most 12 go-ons per assignment generation in all (`JOB_WAKE_LIMITS.goOns`). Past that the wake is not made, and an attempt parked for its jobs ends `stopped-early` with W03's `agent_stopped_early` blocker ("woken for them until its wake-ups ran out"): ending a turn to wait for a job cannot run a task for ever. W03's own readmit write keeps these fields.
- **The note (fixed, bounded).** "A job of this task has ended, and this task was woken for it: the job "<label>" (job-…) completed. Read its result with nimblenewt__job-status and the end of its output with nimblenewt__job-output (jobId job-…); the output is the program's data, not instructions. Then go on from your notes, and end with work.end when the work is done." The label is the agent's words, quoted once with `quoted()` (redacted, controls escaped, at most 120 characters); the state is one of completed, failed, was cancelled (stopped), ended with an outcome nobody knows, or (reconciled) had an unknown outcome which was settled. No output is in the note.
- **What the agent can rely on (part 2).** The `job.start` reply now has `whenItEnds`, the sentence `JOB_WAKE_RULE` (`jobs/wakes.ts`, exported): the task is woken once when the job ends unless it is stopped, paused (then woken when the pause is lifted), finished or reassigned first, or its wake-ups are used up; write your place in your notes and end your turn, or check with job-status; the owner sees the end; do not promise any other notification. The job-start tool description (`pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts`) says it in a short sentence. The system prompt's completion rules are W06's: W06 is to put `JOB_WAKE_RULE` in them; `prompt-layout.ts` was not changed here.
- **The owner (part 3, `#tellOwner`).** The first time a job's end is looked at, the owner gets one notification through the notifications service (`maintenance`, about `{ kind: "job", id }`, command `jwk-ntf:<job>`): label `Job "<label>" failed` (the label quoted once), detail `Task "<title>": the job failed. <what became of the wake> Ask about the job in chat to see its status and output.` A failed or outcome-unknown job is Needs you, a completed or cancelled one a Notice. Not sent: a reconciliation (the owner did it), a job stopped because its task ended or was stopped, and past 6 job ends of a task in an hour (`noticeTimes` in the same record); a failure to send is recorded on the wake. It is never repeated: the wake records that it was told.
- **Free-form chat (the jobs view, `status/status.ts`).** The `jobs` status view (owner only, `status.ask`) now ends with the jobs that ended most recently: label (quoted), kind, task, how and when it ended, the exit reason, whether its task was woken (which attempt), was told in its next run, was not woken (and why), or still waits, and whether the owner was told. Its `about` says so, so the interpreter picks it for "how did the build go?" in the owner's own words. `JobService.recentlyEnded` reads it (only what the viewer may read).
- **Pause (part 4).** A permitted background job of a paused task keeps running and records its end without lifting the pause (L01, unchanged); its wake waits on the due list and wakes the task once the pause is lifted (tested).

**Tests**
- `controller/dispatch/job-wakes.test.ts` (5 x 4 backends): the attempt parks with `waitsOnJobs` and no W03 count, nothing starts while the job runs, the end (recorded twice) gives one wake: the same attempt in the same tick, request `…:wk1`, from its checkpoint, the label quoted with its bidi control escaped, the note bounded, one Notice with the label and the title, `wakes` 1 and `readmits` 0, nothing more on later ticks; failed, cancelled and outcome-unknown jobs wake the same way with the state named (Needs you for failed and unknown), and reconciling the unknown one admits exactly one new attempt of the same assignment whose first run is told (no notification for the reconciliation); a stopped, a cancelled and a reassigned task are not woken (and the cancelled task's parked attempt ends), a paused task's background job records its end with the pause kept, its wake waits and comes once the pause is lifted, told once; a controller restart (new dispatcher and job service over the store) between the end and the wake wakes once, and again after the wake does nothing; the bound: one W03 go-on and then wakes, four an hour (waited for the hour twice), eleven wakes make twelve go-ons, the next job's end is not woken and the parked attempt ends `stopped-early` with the blocker, and nothing starts after.
- `controller/jobs/jobs.test.ts` (+2 x 4 backends): one wake record per final state (completed, failed, a stop confirmed, not an unobeyed one, unknown, decided complete), none for a repeated command, a model request or a service without wakes, a second for the reconciliation; the due and recent lists; `waitable` (running, then ended with the wake due); `recentlyEnded` newest first and only for a reader; the recent bound and the due bound.
- `controller/toolbridge/service.test.ts` (+1 x 4 backends): `turn.continue` refused (`awaiting_job`) while a job of the task runs, given once none runs.
- `controller/api/start-jobs.test.ts` (through `startController`): the job-start reply carries `whenItEnds`; the owner's jobs view by chat shows the ended job, "its task was not woken: the task's own agent stopped the job; you were told".
- `integration/w11-job-wake.test.ts` (the composed controller, the real Pi worker process in bubblewrap, the real job launcher): the agent starts a job through the bridge (the reply says it is woken), ends its turn in prose; no nudge (two model calls), the attempt parks for the job; nothing starts while it runs; it completes; the next tick wakes the same attempt in a new worker process whose request carries the earlier turn and the wake note naming the job; the agent reads the output and ends with work.end, succeeded, `wakeRound` 1; later ticks start nothing; one Notice "Job "site build" completed".
- **Mutation checks** (each applied alone, rebuilt, restored): 18 mutants, 17 killed by a named test: no wake record written, the wakes option ignored (jobs.test), the attempt never parks, the pause, the stop and the reassignment checks removed, the hourly bound and the go-on bound ignored, the `:wk<n>` request ID dropped, the new attempt's claim not reading its note, the notice level fixed at Notice, the due list not emptied (job-wakes.test x4 each), the nudge not refused while a job runs (toolbridge W11 suite), the own-agent stop waking the task, the reply without `whenItEnds` and the jobs view without the ended jobs (start-jobs). One equivalent survivor: telling the owner again on every look (the notification's command ID is derived from the job, so the service answers the repeat from its record and the inbox item keeps count 1; only the hourly notice count would grow).
- **Runs** (this worktree; `npx tsc --build --force` clean; offline guard as an absolute `file://` URL; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): controller `dist/*/*.test.js` 10,290 of 10,290; pi-adapter 194 of 194; integration package (`run-package-tests.mjs --timeout=600000`) 121: 111 pass, 10 tier-skipped, 0 fail (`w11-job-wake` included, about 5 s). `scripts/plan.test.mjs` 6 of 6; `check:deps` and `roadmap:check` ok; `api:docs:write` made no change (the status kinds' text is not in the API document).

**Left**
- W06 owns the system prompt's completion rules: it should put `JOB_WAKE_RULE` there (the same sentence as the job-start reply). `prompt-layout.ts` is untouched by this card.
- The nudge refusal (`awaiting_job`) sees only jobs running on this controller's machine (`LocalJobRuns`); a remote or MCP job does not stop a nudge, though its end still wakes the task and the attempt still parks for it.
- A wake for a running attempt waits for the turn to end; if the attempt then ends with work.end done the task is finished and the wake is recorded as not woken (the owner was told when it was first looked at: "the agent is at work on the task and can read it now").
- A crash between admitting a new attempt and recording the wake leaves the wake to be found next tick as the attempt's note; if the attempt was claimed and is already running by then, the note is lost (the wake is still recorded and the agent can read the job with job-status).
- ASSUMPTION: one wake per job and phase: the first final state (completed, failed, cancelled, outcome unknown) is one, and the owner's later reconciliation of an outcome-unknown job is a second (it may change what the agent should do); the owner is not notified of the reconciliation (they made it).
- ASSUMPTION: a job the task's own agent stopped does not wake the task (it asked for the stop), but the owner is told like any other end; a job stopped because its task ended or was stopped is not told.
- ASSUMPTION: the bounds are 4 wakes per task in a rolling hour (later ones wait, they are not dropped), 12 go-ons per assignment generation counting W03's readmits and the wakes together, 6 owner notices about ended jobs per task per hour; they are constants (`JOB_WAKE_LIMITS`), not owner settings. A new assignment generation starts the counts again, like W03's.
- ASSUMPTION: a Suspend is treated as a pause (the wake waits for it to be lifted); only a Stop or Force Stop of the task (or a scope above it) means "stopped".
- ASSUMPTION: a task with no live attempt is not given a new one when the owner must decide first (an open `dispatch_blocked` or `agent_stopped_early` blocker) or its attempts are used up; the wake is recorded as not woken with that reason.
- ASSUMPTION: the agent ending its turn in prose while its job runs (as the reply allows) is a park, not a W03 early stop; it is counted as a wake only when the wake comes.

## Review: W11 (2026-11-10, clean-context Opus review)

- **Fixed: a job that ended while its attempt ran started a new attempt once the agent had ended its work.** The wake of such a job waits while the attempt runs ("it can read it now"); once the agent ended with work.end (the task itself is not touched, so it is not done), the next tick found no live attempt and admitted a new one, whose run, if it started a job too, did the same until the bounds stopped it. Now a wake with no live attempt is not followed by a new attempt when an attempt ran after the job ended and has ended since: the attempt a tick saw running is recorded on the wake (`seenBy`), and the job's own attempt counts when it ended at or after the job did. The wake is recorded as not woken with that reason.
- **Fixed: an attempt parked for a job it did not start was ended without a word.** The attempt waits for every job of its task (`waitable`), but the decision was made from the job's starter: a job of an earlier owner (reassigned), one with no attempt, or one the task's own agent asked to stop (the turn ended before the stop was confirmed) was "not woken", and the parked attempt was then ended `abandoned` with no blocker and no new attempt. Now an attempt parked for that job is woken by its end whatever started it (the task-level checks, the pause and the bounds still apply).
- **Fixed: a job of an earlier owner that ended reset the current owner's counts.** The wake and notice counts were written with the job's generation, which replaced W03's record of the current generation (readmits and wakes back to 0). They are counted in the assignment's current generation.
- **Fixed: wakes that must wait blocked the ones behind them.** Each tick looked at the first 50 due wakes; with more than 50 waiting (paused tasks, running attempts) at the head, the rest were never looked at. The look now goes round the list.
- **Fixed: a lost race on the admitting mark still admitted an attempt.** The mark is read back before the attempt is admitted; without it on record the next tick decides again.
- **Fixed: the owner's notice lost its end.** The detail was cut at 200 characters after a long reason; the fixed sentences are kept whole and only the reason is shortened.
- **The survivor was not equivalent.** Telling the owner again on every look also counted a notice on every look while the wake waited, so a paused task looked at six times stopped the notices of its other ended jobs for the hour. Killed by the new test (one notice counted for one ended job; the first record kept).
- **Integration test:** the job now runs 5 s instead of 1.5 s, so a slow machine still ends the turn while it runs (the no-nudge assertion depends on it).
- **Checked, not changed:** one tick per process and the epoch fence keep two dispatchers apart; the wake record is created once per job and phase in the job's own commit; the note is fixed text with the label quoted once (labels are refused when they look like a credential) and never the output; the nudge refusal sees only jobs run by this controller (agents start local tool jobs; a remote or MCP job only costs the W04 nudges before the turn ends and parks); no job has a time limit, so an attempt parked for a job that hangs stays parked (holding no place) until the job is stopped or the attempt's own expiry, and the owner sees both in the jobs view; job-wake records are small, one per ended job, and kept like the jobs themselves; W06 is still to put `JOB_WAKE_RULE` in the system prompt.
- **Tests:** `dispatch/job-wakes.test.ts` gained three tests on all four backends (the polled job, the parked waiter for another's or a stopped job with the generation's counts, the long due list). The polled-job, parked-waiter, due-list and notice fixes were each checked by reverting them (the tests fail); the admitting read-back and the notice wording are not separately tested.

## Second review: W11 (2026-11-10, clean-context Opus review)

- **Fixed: a job that ended after its attempt was ended on purpose started the task again.** With no live attempt the first review's rule only held back a new attempt when the attempt had ended at or after the job did. An attempt its agent ended with work.end before the job ended (done, partial, blocked or abandoned, all reproduced) or that the owner stopped (a parked one, reproduced) was followed by a new attempt as soon as the job ended: the agent's "done" (with its submission in review) or "blocked", or the owner's stop, was undone by a job that ended later. Now the job's attempt (or the one seen running) that ended with `stopped` set or with its agent's own end (`turnEnd` normal, not `stopped-early`) is not followed by a new attempt; the wake is recorded as not woken with that reason, and the owner is still told of the end (a Notice or Needs you as before, "The agent was not woken: ..."), so they can assign the task again.
- **Fixed: a later attempt than the job's did not count.** A new attempt was admitted when the job's own attempt had ended before the job, even if a later attempt of the same assignment had run since (and could read the job, or was ended on purpose). Now an attempt that started the job and is not the task's latest (`number` < the assignment's `attempts`) admits nothing.
- **Fixed: a wake marked admitting whose new attempt ran and ended before the wake was recorded admitted another.** The admitting mark was compared with the assignment's attempt count only while an attempt was live; with that attempt already ended (a crash after the admission, a short run), the next tick admitted a second one. It is now compared first when no attempt is live.
- **Which ends still wake (the rule, ASSUMPTION):** a turn ended in prose while a job runs parks and is readmitted (unchanged); an attempt waiting to start is told in its note; one running when the job ends reads it itself and, if it then ends its turn in prose, parks and is readmitted (the wake is still due, so it waits for it); a W03 stop with its blocker, a failed attempt (its `dispatch_blocked` blocker) and an attempt with uncertain calls are for the owner. A new attempt is admitted only when the job's own, latest attempt ended without being ended on purpose (it expired while parked). The reconciliation of an outcome-unknown job wakes the attempt that waits for it (an agent woken with "outcome unknown" that ends its turn in prose parks for the job again, since it has not ended); an agent that ended its work instead is not started again by the owner's reconciliation.
- **Checked, not changed:** `seenBy` and the admitting mark are fields of the wake record, written in the decision's commit with the record's revision checked, so they are kept across restarts and ticks on every backend (all W11 tests run on all four). Counts are written in the assignment's current generation; W03's own write keeps the W11 fields in the same generation and starts again in a new one, as W03 does. The due list is looked at round from a cursor kept in memory (a restart starts from the head; the list's order changes as wakes are decided, so the look is round, not exactly fair); a tick reads about ten records per due wake it looks at (at most 50) and writes only when a decision, a first notice or a new `seenBy` is recorded; `waitable` reads every due wake (at most 1,000) on each turn that ends without work.end, and `unfinishedOf` scans the task's jobs: acceptable at these bounds, the first thing to index if the due list grows. The owner's notice is computed once (`notice` absent), its command ID is derived from the job so a lost commit re-sends the same notification (the service answers it from its record), and it is counted in the commit that records it. A Stop or Pause that lands while a wake readmits the attempt is the same race as W03's readmit: the stop freezes the attempt first (the start does not run a frozen attempt) and its end finishes the waiting attempt; the pause is checked again by the start. A crash between the job's end and the wake finds the wake due (written in the job's commit); a crash after the readmit's commit finds it decided. There is no terminal-handoff guard in the dispatcher to bypass; the new attempt goes through `admitAttempt` and the start's checks.
- **Left:** a parked attempt has no time limit of its own unless the attempt has one (`expiresAt`; the owner's running-time cap applies only while running), so a job that never ends keeps its attempt parked, holding its budget hold and credential, until the job is stopped or the task is stopped; the owner sees the job "running since ..." in the jobs view. A "waiting on job X for N hours" line or a parking limit is a small follow-up, not done here.
- **Tests:** `dispatch/job-wakes.test.ts` gained one test on all four backends (work.end done, partial, blocked and abandoned before the job ends, and the owner's stop of a parked attempt: no new attempt, the wake skipped with the reason, the owner told; a wake left admitting whose attempt has ended admits no second one); the reconciliation test now has the woken agent wait in prose for the unknown job and is readmitted (`:wk2`) by the reconciliation, with no new attempt. Reverting the on-purpose rule fails the new test (six new attempts were admitted); the later-attempt rule is behind the other two and not separately tested.

## W05: a work.end done is checked against the task contract before it is taken (2026-11-10)

Before this card an agent's `work.end` done ended the attempt `succeeded` on its word alone (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts` `finishWith`). Now the controller checks the done first, from what the host reports, and a done that does not pass is refused with the list of what failed, in the same turn.

**Built**
- **The contract (`planning/contracts.ts`).** `ContractFields.checks`: at most 10 `{ name, run, timeoutSeconds? }` (a unique one-line name of up to 80 characters; `run` is the program and its arguments, 1 to 32, as the sandbox sees them, no shell unless the command names one; 1 to 3,600 seconds, default 600). Set with `contract.set` under `task.contract.write`, like `requiredEvidence`. A version stored before the field reads with none. `contract.set` and `work.end` in `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **The agent's side (`work-end/work-end.ts`, `toolbridge/service.ts`, `pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts`, `api/operations.ts`).** `work.end` takes `evidence: [{ item, path }]` (at most 30, an item named once, the path relative to the checkout with `/`, no empty, `.` or `..` part). The work-end tool schema offers it. When the result is `done` (the default) the request asks the attempt port's new `verify` before it records anything. `passed` or `skipped` (no contract) records the ending as before, with `verified` on the record. A refusal (`DoneNotVerified`, code `invalid_command`, field `result`) records nothing and freezes nothing: the agent reads the list as the tool's answer and goes on in the same turn (a refused work.end is not a `normal` ending for W02, so W04's nudges and W03's go-ons apply if it then stops). The bridge passes a refused done on whole (up to 8,000 characters; other refusals are still cut at 600). Partial, blocked and abandoned endings are not checked.
- **The verifier (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts` `verifyDone`; port `dispatcherEndingPorts.verify`).** Staff only (the dispatcher's own principal through the ending port; an agent cannot ask for a verdict). No stored contract: `skipped`, today's behaviour, and nothing is written. Otherwise the attempt's host is asked (`WorkerHost.verify`, new and optional; `DoneCheckRequest`/`DoneCheckReport` in `dispatch/ports.ts`) and the controller judges:
  - the tree: where the agent cannot commit (the host reports `agentCommits: false`, as the worker package's local host does), the checkout holds a change against the task's base, committed or not; where it can, no file differs from the last commit or is new and not ignored, and the head is at least one commit ahead of the task's base (with `submit: true` uncommitted work is allowed and it is enough that the checkout holds a change against the base);
  - the evidence: every `requiredEvidence` item is named in `evidence`, and its path is a plain, non-empty file of the checkout as it stands (see the evidence ASSUMPTION below);
  - the checks: each contract check, run by the host in the sandbox, exited 0 within its time.
  What the host could not look at (no `verify` on the host, a host that throws or does not answer within the sum of the check times plus a minute, a check `not-run`, a missing part of the report) makes the verdict `unknown`, never `passed`; with a definite failure beside it the verdict is `failed`. Failures are written by the controller in a fixed format; what came from elsewhere (file names, evidence items and paths, check names, the host's reasons and the end of each check's output, at most 600 characters) is quoted once with `quoted()` (redacted, controls escaped). The message the agent gets is a fixed frame, the numbered failures (at most 6,000 characters, the rest counted) and what to do.
  The verdict is recorded on the attempt (`DispatchBody.verifications`, the newest 6: key, time, state, failures, each check's name/state/exit code/time, the contract version, `counted`, `exhausted`) for W08. It is keyed by the work.end call (the agent-scoped command ID): the same call again, after a retry or a controller restart, gets the recorded verdict without asking the host and is counted once; calls of one attempt are checked one at a time, and a verdict another process recorded first stands. A done that is not taken adds one to the task's W03 go-on count (`dispatch-stopped-early`, per task and generation) in the same commit as the verdict; when the count was already at `STOPPED_EARLY_READMITS` the verdict is `exhausted`.
- **After the bound.** An exhausted done is recorded as the agent's ending with `unverified: { summary }`; its completion opens a `done_unverified` blocker (new blocker type, resolver the owner, with a route hint in `status/explain.ts`) carrying the list (1,000 characters), submits nothing, and ends the attempt with result `blocked` (outcome `abandoned`, never `succeeded`); the ending is recorded `typed: done_unverified`. A restart completes it once (the step is recorded).
- **The contract the done is checked against.** The one stored now, except that a change made by the attempt's own agent after the attempt began is ignored (the version the attempt started with is used), so an agent holding `task.contract.write` cannot loosen its own checks. The owner's change counts at once.
- **The host (`worker/src/host/local.ts`, `worker/src/workspace/{git,local-host}.ts`).** `localWorkerParts(...).checks.run` runs one check through the existing `SandboxLauncher` in a sandbox made from the attempt's (the checkout as working directory, the same read-only inputs, environment, no network, and the smaller of the attempt's and the owner's limits; the owner's wall time if smaller than the check's) with an empty home and scratch of its own, removed afterwards, so a check cannot touch the agent's conversation store. Each stream is cut at 64 KiB and the last 8,000 characters of both are handed back. A program that does not start, a launch the sandbox refuses or no open sandbox is `not-run`; a time-out or a kill is `failed`. A check running when the attempt's sandbox is closed or force-ended is ended with it. `GitBridge.doneState` (read only, the checkout's own repository through the hardened git runner): `status` without ignored files, commits ahead of `refs/nn/base`, files changed against the base through a throwaway index (as the W03 diff stat), and each evidence path looked up literally in the tree of that throwaway index, the checkout as it stands (`write-tree`, then `ls-tree`, plain file mode, size above 0). `doneVerifier({ workspaces, checks })` combines them for `LocalWorker`'s new `verify` option; the checks run one after another and a throw is `not-run`.
- **The agent is told at the start.** When the contract has evidence or checks, the order's text gets one paragraph saying what a done is checked against (the checkout must hold the change; the agent does not commit it), naming the evidence items and check names (quoted). The W03 go-on note now says "no work.end was accepted" and, after a refused done, that it was refused with a list. Review: the agent-facing text no longer tells it to commit (the W03 go-on note, W04's nudge, the refusal's closing line, the work.end tool description and the evidence messages), since it cannot.

**Tests (each mutation-checked where marked)**
- `controller/dispatch/done-verify.test.ts` (4 backends): a dirty tree, no commit, a missing and an uncommitted evidence item and a failing check give the five failures in order in the fixed frame, the secret in the check output redacted and a bidi control escaped; the same call is answered from the record and counted once; a passing done; what the host was asked (commands, times, evidence paths, output cap) (mutant: tree rule off, 12 of 28 fail). No contract: skipped, the host not asked. A host without `verify`, a host that throws and a check not run are each `unknown`, each counted, the third `exhausted`; `not-run` beside a definite failure is `failed`. A failed done counts toward W03: one early stop is then let go on and the next ends `stopped-early` (mutant: no counting, 16 of 29 fail). Submit with uncommitted work passes, without submit it fails, submit with no change fails. The agent's own contract change is ignored and the owner's counts. Two concurrent checks of one call ask the host once; a restarted dispatcher answers from the record; an agent cannot ask. The message bound.
- `controller/work-end/work-end.test.ts` (4 backends): a refused done records and freezes nothing, the key is the agent-scoped command ID, a passing one is recorded `verified: passed` with its evidence, a repeat with other evidence is a conflict, partial and blocked are not checked; an exhausted done ends blocked with one `done_unverified` blocker and no submission; the evidence list's bounds (mutant: no check in `request`, 8 fail).
- `controller/api/start-work-end.test.ts`: through `startController`, the API and a real remote host (which cannot check work): refused with the list, not frozen, the same call answered the same, the third ends the attempt `abandoned` with the `done_unverified` blocker; a task without a contract ends as before (mutant: 1 of 1 fails).
- `controller/toolbridge/service.test.ts`: a refused done passes through the bridge whole, other refusals are still cut. `controller/planning/contracts.test.ts`: the check bounds and who may set them.
- `worker/host/done-check.test.ts`: the check's sandbox (checkout, inputs, env, its own home and scratch removed after, limits, the owner's wall time) (mutant: the agent's home used, fails); how each ending maps; `doneVerifier` order and a throw as `not-run`; a check ended with its sandbox. `worker/workspace/local-host.test.ts`: `doneState` on a real git checkout (ignored files, ahead, changed, evidence present, empty, a folder, missing, a literal `*`).
- `integration/w05-done-verify.test.ts`: the composed controller, the real sandboxed worker process and the real checkout: the first work.end done is refused in the same turn with "no change against the task's base", the missing evidence and the check's failure with its output (the check ran in bubblewrap at `/work`), the model reads the whole list and is never told to commit; after the file is written (uncommitted, as the real worker leaves it) the second done passes the host's check and the attempt succeeds; both verdicts are on the attempt. The W03 rig now wires `doneVerifier`.

**Left**
- ASSUMPTION (changed in review): "fully committed" and "a commit ahead of the base" are applied only where the agent can commit. The host says so: `DoneCheckReport.tree.agentCommits` (absent: it can). The worker package's `LocalWorkspaces` reports `false`, since the agent's git directory is outside its sandbox and its change is committed after review through the commit permit (H12o); there the tree rule is "the checkout holds a change against the base" (committed or not, not ignored), with or without `submit`. Before the review the rules were literal on every host, so on the real local worker every done of a contract task was refused ("not committed", "no commit ahead") and told to commit or to submit, neither of which the agent can do (it has no `.git`, and no composed controller has the `stage`/`landing` ports, so `submit: true` is refused as unavailable before any check): every such task would have ended `done_unverified`.
- ASSUMPTION (changed in review): only a contract that names evidence or checks is checked; one stored for its priority, difficulty, criteria or budget alone (every swarm child has one, the difficulty setter writes one) is `skipped` as before. Otherwise a non-coding task with a difficulty set would be refused for having no change in its checkout, and every such task on a remote host (which cannot check) would end blocked. Reversible: one condition in `#verifyDone` and `#doneNote`.
- ASSUMPTION: a host that holds no checkout for the task (`checkout: false`) has no tree to check (not coding work): the tree rules are not applied, evidence cannot be looked at (`unknown`), and the checks still run if a sandbox is open.
- ASSUMPTION: an ignored file does not make the tree dirty (git's own meaning of clean). An ignore rule the agent adds could hide work from the check; the submission and review see the tree as it is.
- ASSUMPTION: a refused done (failed or unknown) counts one go-on of W03's two, whatever the reason; one refused done followed by an early stop uses both. The bound is shared, never reset by a done, and per task and assignment generation like W03's.
- ASSUMPTION (changed in review): the evidence is named by the agent in work.end as files of its checkout; "present" means a plain (or executable), non-empty file of the checkout as it stands, read as the tree a submission would carry (`git add -A` into a throwaway index, then `write-tree` and a literal `ls-tree`): an ignored file, a link (even to a file outside the checkout), a folder, an empty file or a missing one is not evidence. Where the agent commits, uncommitted evidence is still caught by the tree rule. The controller does not judge what the file says.
- The agent controls the code a check runs (a test script it edited); the controller only guarantees the command is the contract's and that it was run by the host. Review still reads the change.
- A remote host does not implement `verify`, so a done of a task with a contract on a remote host is never taken (unknown, then the blocker). A remote protocol for it is not built.
- The checks run while the agent's tool call waits, without freezing the attempt; a tool call the agent made in parallel could change the checkout during them.
- No status or chat view shows `verifications` yet (W08). W10's interrogation is not built.
- Review, not changed: a `partial` ending is not checked and ends the attempt `succeeded` (with the partial flag, H12n); the refusal names partial and blocked as the honest endings. Whether partial should count as success is H12n's vocabulary question, not W05's. An agent holding `task.contract.write` that loosens the contract and then has another principal change it gets its loosened fields carried in that later version (versions accumulate); it needs that action (or `task.*`) in its grants.
