## CMP: compaction thresholds scale with the model window; a window under 8,192 is refused (2026-11-11)

Found in the U14 review: Pi Durable's background compaction starts at `window - reserveTokens (16,384) - backgroundTokens (32,768)`, which is zero or below for every window under 49,152 tokens, so on a 32,768-token route (U14's placeholder window for configuration providers) a background summary call started before nearly every request once a cut existed (a compaction loop).

- **Done.** `pi-adapter/src/compaction-thresholds.ts` is the one place the figures are computed: `reserve = max(1,024, min(16,384, window/8))`, `background = max(1,024, min(32,768, window/4))`. On a small window the background threshold is 62.5% of the window and the blocking threshold 87.5%; from 131,072 tokens up they are Pi's defaults (16,384 and 32,768), so large routes (the 200,000-token Radiance route, 1M) behave as before. Between 49,152 and 131,072 they are also scaled (e.g. 65,536: background at 40,960 instead of 16,384), so those windows compact later than before. `worker/process.ts` passes the result to Pi next to `keepRecentTokens` (a tenth of the window, unchanged), and `begin` refuses a window under 8,192 (`WindowTooSmallError`, reported as the worker's "could not start" fault with the reason in words) before anything is opened.
- **Setup.** `routing.provider.add` (U14) refuses a `contextTokens` under 8,192 in plain words (`MIN_WORKABLE_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, equal to the worker's `MIN_WORKABLE_WINDOW`; `integration/cmp-small-window.test.ts` checks they are equal, since the controller does not depend on pi-adapter). The setup assistant's model-route question and the chat interpreter's prompt now ask the owner for the model's real window and never to guess it; the launcher's note says 32,768 is only a placeholder that matters most when the real window is smaller.
- **Tests (fail before, pass after).** `pi-adapter/src/compaction-thresholds.test.ts` (windows 8k, 16k, 32k, 49,152, 128k/131,072, 200k, 1M: no zero or negative threshold, background below blocking, exact figures, defaults kept for large windows, refusal under 8,192 and for non-integers); `worker/process.test.ts` (a 32,768 window makes exactly the two scripted model calls with no summary call in between, and a 4,096 window is refused at start; both fail on the old worker); `t06b-composed-worker`, `h12b-worker-process` and `h12j-worker-gaps` are back on a 32,768-token window (W06/W10 had moved them to 65,536 to dodge this very behaviour); `start-setup-u14.test.ts` refuses 4,096.
- **Not done.** (1) `keepRecentTokens` stays a tenth of the window (H12f, provisional); on an 8,192 window that is 819 tokens, and the fixed part of a first call (system rules, tool schemas, about 3,400 tokens) is already over the controller's startup share (a quarter), so an 8,192 route will block with `context_overflow` at the controller instead of working: 8,192 is the refusal floor, not a promise it is comfortable (16,384 is the smallest sensible window). (2) A table edit that does not go through `routing.provider.add` can still store a smaller `contextTokens`; the worker refuses it at the start. (3) `h12bf-composed` (41,984) is left as it is; its refusal case used a 1,024-token window, which the worker now refuses at start with the window message instead of the controller's blocker, so it uses 8,192 (the fixed part of a call is still over its startup share there). (4) Windows between 49,152 and 131,072 now compact later than they did; no test depended on the old earlier start except the three fixtures above, which were small windows.
- **ASSUMPTION:** reserve at one eighth and background at one quarter of the window, floors of 1,024, minimum window 8,192 (the figures the task suggested); the sharing of both thresholds is not tuned against a real small model.

- **Runs.** pi-adapter 225/225; integration 139 tests, one failure (the h12bf refusal case above) fixed and the file rerun 4/4; the controller files touching providers, launcher, setup and chat 128/128; targeted CMP tests 2+4+1 pass, the two worker tests fail on the old worker.
- **Review (clean-context, 2026-11-11).** (1) **Reserve too small for a reply (fixed).** Pi sizes each reply as `min(model.maxTokens, window - estimated input - 4,096)` (pi-ai `CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS`), at least 1, and takes a `length` stop as the answer. With `reserve = window/8` the 4,096 margin used up the whole reserve on windows up to 32,768, so a request just under the blocking threshold (no compaction started for it) went out with a reply limit of 1 token and the turn ended cut off; on 49,152..131,072 the reply room at blocking shrank to 2,048..12,288. The reserve is now `min(16,384, max(window/8, 4,096 + reply))`, where `reply` is the model's `maxTokens` capped at `window/8` (the whole eighth when not given); `worker/process.ts` passes `start.model.maxTokens`. A test calls pi-ai's own clamp (`clampMaxTokensToContext`, loaded from its file) one token under the blocking threshold for windows 8,192..200,000 and reply limits 1,024..32,000 and checks the constant is Pi's; it fails on the old figures ("8192 tokens, reply limit 1024: Pi grants 1"). New exact figures (no reply limit): 8,192 -> 5,120/2,048, 16,384 -> 6,144/4,096, 32,768 -> 8,192/8,192, 49,152 -> 10,240/12,288; 131,072 and up unchanged (Pi's defaults). (2) **Owner text claimed 8,192 and 16,384 work (fixed).** Measured, the worker's fixed part is 12,582 characters (10,045 of tool schemas, 2,537 of system text), about 4,194 tokens at the controller's 3 characters a token, over a quarter of 16,384 (4,096) as well as of 8,192: every task on such a route stops at its first call with a `context_overflow` blocker. The setup question, the interpreter prompt and the launcher note now say 32,768 or more is needed in practice and a smaller window is accepted but its tasks stop with a context blocker. **ASSUMPTION:** the refusal floor stays 8,192 (the card's figure; below it the worker cannot run at all) rather than being raised to a figure that tracks the fixed part, which grows with cards. (3) Checked, no change: Pi's background figure is a band below the blocking threshold (`blocking = window - reserve`, `background = blocking - backgroundTokens`, pi-durable `generation.js` `thresholdCompaction`), so the card's sign is right; the figures are continuous at 131,072; the summary call's own reply is `0.8 * reserve` and its input is only the part being cut; a window under 8,192 (or 0) that reaches the worker past `routing.provider.add` fails the attempt with "the worker did not start: could not start: the model's context window (N tokens) is too small..." (`readmit: false`), not a retry loop and not the C07n blocker. h12bf's comment on the 65,536 background threshold corrected (40,960). (4) Old-worker check: with the scaled figures removed from `worker/process.ts`, `h12b-worker-process` and `h12j-worker-gaps` fail (3 model calls instead of 2: an unscripted background summary) and `t06b-composed-worker` fails (an unscripted call, then the file times out); all pass on this branch. **Review runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` after a dist clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard): controller in 3 shards 3,903 of 3,917 (14 cancelled: embedded-PostgreSQL port in use in `inference-cache/markers.test.js`, rerun alone 56/56), 3,483/3,483, 4,090/4,090; pi-adapter 226/226; contracts 14/14; worker 310 of 311 (1 skipped); integration 131 of 141 (10 skipped, the heavy G04 tests), 0 failed.

## M04h (first slice): the controller is the host for the owner's meeting wake (2026-11-12)

Done:
- **A stopped agent reports `stopped`, not `paused`.** `StopService.agentRest(agentId)` answers `suspended` or `stopped` when a finished Suspend or Stop of the agent, or of a team above it, is still the cause of the gate (a resume, a newer pause, an unfinished or `recovery-required` stop all end it). A stop of the whole installation is never a rest: it is the emergency brake and keeps reporting `paused`. `PauseService` has a new option `pausedAvailability`, asked only for an agent a pause holds, that replaces `paused` with its answer (undefined keeps `paused`). This is the hook the pause gate used to answer ahead of, so the attendance now says "stopped: it stays stopped unless the owner authorizes waking" for such an agent.
- **`MeetingWakeHost` (`meetings/wake-host.ts`)** is the host composed by `startController` when the embedding application supplies no `meetingWake`. `recover(request)` writes a `meeting-wake-lease` record per agent (one entry per meeting, at most 20; the command ID comes from the key, so a repeated key is the same wake) and refuses an agent not at rest, a meeting that is not open or one whose roster lacks the agent. `availability` says `available` while a meeting the agent was woken for has an open room, and `stopped`/`suspended` again as soon as the room ends: the agent's gate is never lifted, so its other tasks stay held and nothing has to be undone. It answers nothing (so `paused` stands) under an installation pause, and says the plain rest while any pause besides the stop's own holds the agent.
- Wired in `api/start.ts` (both the controller's and the dispatcher's pause service, through `ComposeInput.pausedAvailability`). An embedding application that passes `meetingWake` keeps its own path exactly as before (composed host off, `paused` answers as before); the owner reaches the wake through `meeting.attend.wake`, which the chat interpreter already offers like every operation.
- `AttendanceService.authorizeWake`: a replay of the command that made the wake is no longer asked what the agent reports now (it reports `available` once woken, which used to make the replay fail).
- Tests: `api/start-wake-host.test.ts` (3: stopped is reported, wake makes it available for the open meeting only, replay, back to stopped after `meeting.attend.end`, other agent untouched; plain pause and installation stop are not woken; the embedder's own host is left alone), `api/start-meetings.test.ts` updated (the composed host refuses an agent no finished stop holds, with the fixed "the host did not wake" message).

Not done (follow-up, remains in M04h):
- A caller for `carriesOnDuringMeeting` (needs the agent's conversation idle, `conversationIdle: true`), and result handling for an attempt waiting on its background jobs.
- T07 follow-ups: `jobs.decide` restart during a meeting without asking; jobs admitted by host or service credentials skip the gate; the gate racing a meeting created after it read; a withheld seat over-refused near a meeting.
- The woken agent stays `available` until the room ends even if it leaves earlier; the real local worker host's own start of the woken agent's attempt (the lease only changes what the controller reports) is the L02/L03 worker side.

Review (clean-context, 2026-11-11), three bugs fixed:
- A wake outlived a newer stop: woken, then resumed and stopped again while the room was still open, the agent stayed `available`. Each lease entry now names the stop intent it woke the agent from, and only a lease for the stop that holds the agent now counts.
- A woken agent could be chosen as a reviewer while its meeting was open (the review service read `PauseService.availability`). `PauseService.workAvailability` leaves the meeting wake out (`pausedAvailability(p, { meetingWake: false })`), and the review service is wired to it; the attendance, meetings, stand-ups, conversations and messages still see the wake (task messages stay held by the agent's gate through the task guard).
- A wake of an agent another pause also holds (a team pause on top of its own stop) was accepted and did nothing. `recover` now refuses it ("the host did not wake").
Tests: two more in `api/start-wake-host.test.ts` (the three cases, and a Suspend of the agent's team woken for one meeting and suspended again after it).

ASSUMPTION: a stop of the whole installation is never woken for a meeting (the brake is not overridden, as for pauses); the owner resumes it first.
ASSUMPTION: the composed host is on by default and replaced entirely by `meetingWake` when the application supplies one; it covers only stops the controller itself recorded, so an agent that only an application `availability` hook calls stopped gets "the host did not wake" unless the application also supplies `meetingWake`.
ASSUMPTION: the lease ends with the room (no timer), the smallest reversible rule.

## M04h (second slice): the controller brings a woken stopped agent into the room and runs it, within bounds (2026-11-12)

Plain words first. The first slice only changed what the controller *says* about a woken agent (available for that meeting). Nothing then made the agent do anything. Now, when the owner wakes a stopped agent for a meeting, the controller itself brings it into the room and starts one attempt for it, only through the paths every other attempt uses, and ends that attempt when the wake ends. The owner can see every wake and stop it in ordinary chat words.

Done:
- **One more loop, `meeting.wake-attend`** (`dispatch/loops.ts`, composed in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` only when the controller's own host is in use). Each pass reads the wake records (`MeetingWakeHost.attend`) and for each wake of an open room: checks the agent is still at rest from the same stop; prepares it (it has nothing to leave) and joins it through `AttendanceService`, which creates the bounded meeting task; asks for ONE attempt on that task through `AssignmentService.admitAttempt` (the admission the dispatcher itself uses to read again) naming the harness the owner's routing gives the task. The dispatcher then claims it with all its ordinary checks (pause, meeting, route, budget, grant, host, lease). There is no other door: the host starts no worker, writes no dispatch record.
- **The stop is passed by an existing mechanism, not a new one.** `AttendanceService.#decide` now treats an agent that is `available` while a stop still holds it (only the composed host produces that) like a paused agent the owner invited by hand: `bounded` attendance with a pause permission that covers exactly the gates held now (their request IDs) and expires with the meeting plus its grace. Only the meeting task runs; the agent's other work stays held, and a later stop is another request and is not covered. No gate is lifted or written.
- **The meeting is not a conflict with its own meeting task.** `Dispatcher` now passes the task to `AttendanceService.admission`, which skips the meeting of that very task for that agent (the bounded meeting task is how it attends). Without this the dispatcher deferred the task for "a meeting the agent attends starts before this work would end".
- **Bounds** (`WAKE_LIMITS`): at most 3 agents brought in per pass, at most 5 woken agents attending at once (the rest wait and are listed as waiting), 3 failed passes and a wake is given up with the reason, 200 wake records read per pass, 50 shown. A wake lasts only while its room is open; the attempt runs under the usual attempt limits and the permission expires at the meeting's end plus grace. The attempt count is one per wake (the admission's command ID is derived from the wake key; a second pass cannot start a second attempt).
- **Crash safety.** Every step is repeatable and re-derivable from stored state: the join is skipped if the seat is already taken (`AttendanceService.seatOf`), the admission is idempotent, each change to a wake record is its own command with an ID naming the step and the wake key. A pass cut off after the join is finished by the next pass (tested: prepare and join once, admission twice). A stop or the end of the meeting is made final only after both the room and the dispatcher stop succeeded; until then the next pass tries again.
- **Ending.** When the room ends, the agent leaves, or the owner stops the wake, the attempt is ended through the dispatcher's own graceful stop (`stop`: freeze, settle, checkpoint, end `abandoned`, no readmit). The attempt is asked of the dispatcher (`liveAttemptsOf`) because the task is already done by then.
- **Owner control.** `meeting.attend.wakes` (query, owner only: agent, meeting, `waiting`/`attending`/`gave-up`/`stopped`, tries, reason) and `meeting.attend.wake-stop` (command, owner only: the agent reports at rest again at once; it leaves the room; a seat that never got in says the wake was stopped; repeating it is the same stop). In chat: a status view `wakes` ("who is woken for a meeting", offered to the interpreter by the view catalog), and chat commands `meeting.attend.wake` (follows the approval profile like the invitation, shown first in the strict one, says "this meeting only, then the agent is back as it was") and `meeting.attend.wake-stop` (applies at once), the meeting named by words (`meetingTopic`, or none when only one is planned) and the agent by name (`agentName`), resolved from the records like `meeting.invite-direct`. The interpreter prompt describes all three.
- **An application that supplies its own `meetingWake`** gets none of this: no loop, `wakes` answers nothing, `wake-stop` is refused in words.
- Tests: `meetings/wake-host.test.ts` (5 cases on all four backends: bounds, give-up, cut-off passes, stop settling, end of meeting, a changed stop), `api/start-wake-attend.test.ts` (composed `startController` with a fixture host and no model: the whole flow with the attempt started by the dispatcher on SQLite and PostgreSQL, owner-only, application-supplied host, chat wake/see/stop). Mutation checks done by hand: removing the admission exemption, removing the stop permission, and removing the give-up each fail a test.

Not done (remains in M04h):
- A caller for `carriesOnDuringMeeting` and result handling for an attempt waiting on its background jobs (unchanged; needs the agent's idleness).
- The T07 follow-ups: `jobs.decide` restart during a meeting without asking; jobs admitted by host or service credentials skip the gate; the gate racing a meeting created after it read; a withheld seat over-refused near a meeting.
- What the woken agent *does* in the room is whatever its attempt does with the meeting task; no new tool or prompt was written for it. The loop and `done` handling for a meeting task that finishes early is the ordinary attempt ending.
- A woken agent that leaves by its own `meeting.attend.leave` cannot be woken for the same meeting again (a seat that left is final); it reports available until the next pass settles the wake (one loop interval).
- The graceful stop waits for the worker's checkpoint (the dispatcher's usual wait); a worker that never answers keeps the wake unsettled and the stop is retried every pass until the attempt's lease ends. The fixture host in the test does not answer, so the test checks the attempt is frozen with the reason, not finished.
- The 3 / 5 / 3 figures are constants, not owner settings.

ASSUMPTION: a wake brings in one attempt, not a standing worker; the figures above (3 per pass, 5 at once, 3 tries) are the smallest bounds that let a handful of agents attend while a mistake cannot start a crowd; they are not settings.
ASSUMPTION: the attempt is ended with the dispatcher's graceful stop (not the emergency one) because a checkpoint of a meeting attempt loses nothing and an emergency stop would be recorded as a Force Stop.
ASSUMPTION: the harness for the admission is the one the routing resolver names for the meeting task at that moment; when it names none (no route) the attempt gate refuses and the wake is given up after three passes with that reason in words.
ASSUMPTION: the wake host acts as the dispatcher's service principal, which is what every other loop uses.

Review (clean-context, 2026-11-12), four bugs fixed:
- **The owner's later stop did not win over the meeting permission.** A Stop, Suspend or Force Stop made while the agent's gate is already paused keeps the gate's pause request, and the permission was keyed on that request only: a woken agent that had joined and was then force-stopped (or suspended, woken, then stopped) kept a meeting task the pause did not hold, and the wake still said attending. Each covered gate of a `pause-exemption` now also records `stop`, the stop in force when it was granted (`PauseService.stopInForceOf`: the stop service's per-scope `stop-active` pointer and the request's mode). The pause chain covers a gate only while that is unchanged, and locks the pointer, so a stop racing a claim fails the claim's commit (a first stop on a gate that was only paused rewrites the gate as it takes it over, which the chain already locks). This also applies to a paused agent the owner invited by hand. A permission an older build wrote (no `stop`) is checked as before.
- **The host loop now ends a wake the owner overtook.** An attended wake whose agent is held by a pause and no longer made available by it (stopped, suspended or paused again) is ended like a stopped wake: the agent leaves the room, the attempt is stopped, and the wake reads `ended` with the reason, said as soon as the room agrees (before the attempt's stop finishes). A wake still waiting is given up with that reason instead of being listed as waiting for ever. A resumed agent (no pause holds it) is left to attend.
- **Wake records grew for good, and a pass stopped reading at 200.** A lease per agent ever woken was kept, and a pass reads at most 200 in ID order, so after 200 agents had been woken a new wake whose lease sorted later was never brought in nor shown. A lease whose rooms are all over and that needs nothing more is now removed (revision-checked, so a new wake racing it wins).
- **A wake that ended still made the agent `available`** until its room ended (an agent that left by itself, or one the owner stopped again). A wake with `endedReason` no longer counts. The note above that said "until the next pass" is now true.
- `task-plan.md` had a progress note typed in by hand. The generator writes that file (CI fails on hand edits), and the generator prints notes only for cards that are flipped. The note is removed; the card is flipped when it is merged.
Tests: `api/start-wake-attend.test.ts` (a later Force Stop, a Stop after a Suspend, and a stop before the agent was brought in, on SQLite and the first two on PostgreSQL), `meetings/wake-host.test.ts` (on all four backends: a replaced stop is given up with the reason; 205 woken agents whose meetings are over do not hide a new wake and only the live lease is kept; a leaver reads `ended` and at rest).

ASSUMPTION: the owner's later stop ends the wake for good (the wake is not resumed if the later stop is lifted while the room is still open); the owner wakes the agent again if it should attend.

## L05d: bridge calls as effects, a remote worker host that runs Pi in its sandbox, rewritten call IDs (2026-11-11)

Code: `generation/generation.ts` (aliases, `#locateCall`, `admitCall`, `executeCall`, `hasStreamed`), `generation/stream-settings.ts` (`bindCall`, `admitCall`, `requireStream`), `toolbridge/service.ts` (`#generationCheck`, `#admitted`, `#silentStream`), `dispatch/model-stream.ts` (`bridgeCallIdOf`, the event `alias`), `remote/service.ts` (alias check, relay monitor), `remote/runner.ts` (new), `api/start.ts`, `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `chat/commands.ts` and `chat/chat.ts` (the owner's chat reaches the new switches). Tests: `api/start-l05d.test.ts` (six, composed remote world), `toolbridge/service.test.ts`, `generation/stream-feed.test.ts`, `generation/stream-settings.test.ts`, `dispatch/model-stream.test.ts`, `remote/runner.test.ts`, and `packages/integration/src/l05d-remote-sandbox.test.ts` (the real Pi process in bubblewrap behind a remote runner).

- **Done.**
  - **Bridge calls are effects.** A write operation of the tool bridge (the `WRITES` set) is admitted through the generation service (`admitCall`, kind "bridge": the call must be complete in the task's current, uninterrupted generation) and run through the effect ledger (`executeCall`), so it is settled `confirmed`, `failed` (the operation's own refusal, as `EffectRejected`) or `uncertain` (any other throw). Asking again is answered from the ledger and does not run again. Reads are not admitted. A generation still streaming is waited for (100 ms steps, 3 s at most), then refused.
  - **Name and arguments are bound.** The call as presented to the bridge must be the one the model wrote (the model-facing name of the operation, and the arguments compared member by member, so key order and numeric strings do not matter).
  - **Rewritten call IDs.** The Pi extension sends `h:` + a digest for an ID it cannot keep and `d:` + a digest for the nth use of one ID. The decoder now records the ID the bridge will see as the call's `alias` (`bridgeCallIdOf`), and `checkCall` finds a call by its ID, an alias, or the `d:` number (`reusedCallId`, bounded by `GENERATION_REUSE_MAX` uses and `GENERATION_REUSE_HASHES` digests) of the newest recorded call with that base (see the review fixes below). A call found by an alias is checked against its own recorded generation.
  - **Remote stream stall reporting.** The remote service reports each remote model call to the relay monitor (start, first output, end, waits on the store), so stall detection and `stall-evidence` see a remote worker as they see a local one. A remote worker that never opens a stream is noticed once in the owner's activity, and `requireStream` (off) lets the owner have its calls refused.
  - **A remote worker host.** `RemoteOfferRunner` takes an offer, confirms the dispatch contract, starts the order in the machine's sandbox, runs the turn through the attempt as gateway, follows tell, checkpoint, restart and stop, sends the result. Its `tap(attemptId)` is the `stream` of the machine's model relay, so every model call of the process is recorded by the controller. The real-process test shows a late reply held at the controller and never reaching Pi, and a corrected generation's call (sent under an `h:` ID) refused at the bridge as withdrawn, without an effect, after which the next generation ends the task.
  - **Owner controls.** The three switches are in the state API (`generation.stream.get/change`) and in the chat command text and the interpreter's operation list; `enable` and `disable` names are not searched for in the owner's words (a fixed list the service checks), so no phrase is required.
- **Not done.**
  - The remote worker's tool bridge still has no route in the protocol: in the real-process test the machine's bridge calls the controller's `ToolExecutionService` in the same process with the remote attempt as gateway. A deployed remote host needs a protocol message for a bridge request (follow-up card).
  - `RemoteOfferRunner` is not composed into a deployed worker program (no CLI or service wiring); it is the tested building block.
  - Remote speed and route reporting for the monitor (the route is empty for remote calls, `request_started` omits it).
  - `d:` matching is bounded: a reuse number beyond `GENERATION_REUSE_MAX` is "not recorded". A call ID of 100 or more characters hits the earlier command-ID length overflow (a pre-existing limit in the effect command ID); the test uses an 82-character ID.
  - No run against a real model (the Pi/Radiance benchmark holds the one connection); the model is scripted. The card is not flipped.
- **ASSUMPTION:** `bindCall` and `admitCall` default on and `requireStream` off, because the first two only refuse what the model did not write and the third would stop every remote worker that has no tap.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a bridge call refused by its own operation is a failed effect (it did not happen), any other error is uncertain (it may have), matching the ledger's rule for local effects.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a superseded generation's call is `withdrawn`, not `complete`, so a later `call_0` of the provider (which restarts its count each reply) finds the newest generation holding it.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the unref on the runner's control sleep was dropped, so an offer in flight keeps the process alive.
- **ASSUMPTION:** `dispatch/model-stream.ts` (carried by the worker) now imports `node:crypto` for the alias digest; the transport test that lists a worker file's imports was widened from none to `node:crypto` for that one file, since the worker already carries `node:crypto` for the dispatch contract and the alternative (moving the digest into the client) would change the event shape.

### L05d review fixes (2026-11-11, clean-context Opus)

- **Parked tool calls (HIGH).** `tool.invoke` and `job.start` answer before they are done: a call parked for a review (`awaiting-approval`) or still running (`in-progress`) is `ok` and is asked again with the same call ID to go on (the dispatcher's operation and the job are keyed by the attempt and the call ID). The admission settled that first answer as a `confirmed` effect, so the second ask was answered from the ledger with the first answer and the approved call never ran (the T07b job test and the W11 job-wake test in the integration package failed this way: the job stayed `parked`). These two operations now run as an idempotent effect bridge, and an answer whose `state` is `awaiting-approval` or `in-progress` leaves the effect `pending` (the answer is still passed back); the next ask runs the operation again, which answers its current state, and a final answer settles the effect. Test: `toolbridge/service.test.ts` (four backends), the real generation and effect services: parked, approved, asked again (confirmed, ran once), asked a third time (confirmed, not run again); without the fix it fails, and so do T07b and W11.
- **`d:` IDs (HIGH).** `#locateCall` read the extension's number for a repeated provider ID off the window (the nth use, oldest first) before anything else. The extension counts only the uses the process was given, so a call the window holds and Pi never ran (a reply that broke off with a `dropped` call, a call held back, a failed reply's `unused` call) or a generation older than the window shifted the count, and the current generation's call was matched to an older generation and refused as "no longer the current one" (for a provider that counts from zero in every reply, after any broken reply, every later call). A `d:` ID now stands for the newest recorded call with that base, each distinct base tried for numbers 2 to `GENERATION_REUSE_MAX` within the digest budget; Pi only ever runs the calls of the newest reply it received. A stale request under an older number is judged as that newest call and must still carry the name and arguments the model wrote for it (`bindCall`); if it does, the newest call's own request is answered from the ledger and does not run again. Test: `stream-feed.test.ts` (four backends), a reply broken in the middle of `call_0`, then two whole ones; the old code fails it.
- **Runner restarts (MED).** When `confirmRestarts` threw (a lost connection), `RemoteOfferRunner` logged it and still applied the batch, so the sandbox restarted under a recipe the controller had not confirmed (H12a), and `after` moved past it. Now nothing of that batch is applied; the same messages are read again at the next look (each confirmation is keyed by its message), and a fenced answer stops the sandbox. Test in `remote/runner.test.ts`; the old code fails it.
- **Remote progress (MED).** The remote service told stall detection the start, the first output and the end of a remote call, never the output that kept arriving (a local relay reports it every 15 s), so a healthy remote reply streaming longer than the difficulty's silence threshold (5 to 90 minutes) read as `silent`. `streamEvents` now reports the output so far at most once per `monitorProgressMs` (`RemoteDeps`, `RemoteStartOptions`; default 15 s, 0 = every message with output). The `start-l05d` stall test holds the reply open twice and waits for `outputTokens`; the old code fails it.
- **Checked, no change.** Double runs: a repeat of an admitted write (same attempt and call ID) derives the same command ID, so admission replays and the ledger answers (confirmed/failed from its evidence, a claim in flight `effect_busy`, a started-then-crashed one `effect_uncertain`); nothing is run twice. A withdrawn or corrected generation's call is refused by `checkCall` and again by the admission commit. Aliases are found only within one task's newest 20 generations, so no cross-task attribution; a remote worker can claim any alias for its own calls, but it already supplies its own stream. The chat exemption covers only `enable`/`disable` of `generation.stream.change`, whose names the service checks against a fixed list, and the change is a proposal. The widened import list is `node:crypto` only (`createHash` for the digest; the file imports nothing else). `requireStream` is off and only judges model-originated calls after a reply was read, so a slow first token does not trigger it; a remote call that `streamTapFor` does not record at all (`recorded: false`, for a task the service does not know) is reported as never streamed (off by default; noted).
- **Left as is (noted).** `sameValue` reads `a[k]` without `Object.hasOwn`, so a `"__proto__": {}` member on one side only compares equal (no bridge operation takes that key). After a controller restart a remote attempt's monitor numbers its reports from 1 again (`relay:<attempt>:<n>`), so the first reports replay earlier command IDs and are ignored or logged as conflicts until the count passes the old one (a local attempt does not outlive the controller). The `admitted` short-circuit in `admitCall` is redundant with the command ID's replay for the same attempt (a mutation removing it fails nothing).
- **Review runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard; after all fixes): controller in 3 shards 4,040 of 4,040, 3,298 of 3,298, and 3,831 of 3,854 (the dependency-probe "no probe starts another" failed once under load and cancelled the 22 tests after it in its file; `dependencies/observe.test.js` alone 66 of 66); integration 132 (122 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed); worker 297 passed, 1 skipped; pi-adapter 218 of 218; contracts 13 of 13; `check:deps`, `roadmap:check` ok; `api:docs:write` no change. Each new test fails on the code before its fix. Mutations of the card's own tests: argument binding ignored (6 fail), no admission (7), alias dropped by the remote check (1); removing `admitCall`'s replay short-circuit fails nothing (redundant, see above).
## L05e: the tool bridge in the worker protocol, the remote worker program, remote route reporting, two review leftovers of L05d (2026-11-11)

Code: `remote/protocol.ts` (`ToolBridgeRequest`, `ToolBridgeAnswer`, `REMOTE_LIMITS.toolBytes`, `toolTokenChars`), `remote/service.ts` (`toolBridge`, the `toolBridge` dep, the placement's `route`), `remote/server.ts` (route `POST /worker/attempts/{id}/tool`), `remote/client.ts` (`RemoteAttempt.toolBridge`), `remote/runner.ts` (`bridge`, `verdict`), `api/relay-monitor.ts` (new: the monitor moved out of `dispatch-compose.ts`), `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, `toolbridge/service.ts` (`sameValue`), and in `scripts/`: `remote-host.mjs` (new: the composition), `remote-worker.mjs` (new: the program). Tests: `remote/tool-bridge.test.ts` (all four backends, 5 tests), `api/start-l05e.test.ts` (4, composed controller, real bridge), `api/relay-monitor.test.ts` (2), `remote/runner.test.ts` (2 new), `toolbridge/service.test.ts` (the L05d binding test extended, four backends), `scripts/remote-host.test.mjs` (4), `integration/src/l05e-remote-worker.test.ts` (a REAL worker process).

- **Done.**
  - **The tool bridge has a route.** `POST /worker/attempts/{id}/tool`, body `{ placement, token, request }` (`request` = `{ op, callId, args? }`, `token` = the task credential the agent's process presented to the machine's bridge). The route is checked like every message about an attempt: the session header and protocol version are the session's own (426 otherwise; protocol 1 stays 1, the route is additive), an `Idempotency-Key` is required, the host must hold the attempt (another host: `not_found`, plus the existing `credential-misused` signal), the placement must be current and the session the one that accepted it (`fenced`), and the worker must have confirmed the dispatch contract. Then the controller's `ToolExecutionService.handle` is called with the credential and a gateway bound to THIS attempt, so the credential is judged against the attempt (a credential of another task or agent is `unauthenticated`), the assignment generation against the task's current one (`fenced`), the call against the generation that recorded it, and a write is admitted as an effect of that generation on the ledger: it is the very same code as the in-process call, shown by comparing answers of the route and of the in-process bridge for the same call.
  - **Idempotent by call ID.** Copies of one request that overlap (a retry after a timeout) share the first one's answer and reach the bridge once; the same call ID with other content is refused as `invalid_command` (the bridge says the same); a repeat after the answer goes to the bridge again, which answers a write from its ledger (confirmed/failed/uncertain) and a parked `tool.invoke`/`job.start` goes on (L05d review). The route keeps no state beyond the overlap map (256 entries). The client's default idempotency key is the call ID plus a digest of the request.
  - **Limits.** Body at most `REMOTE_LIMITS.toolBytes` (160 KB; 413 `too_large` otherwise, the general 1 MB cap still applies below it), credential 1 to 512 characters, `callId` 1 to 120 of the bridge's alphabet, `op` 1 to 40 characters, `args` an object, unknown fields refused at both levels. The bridge's own limits (64 KB of arguments, the operation list) are the bridge's to apply and its refusal comes back as an answer (`ok: false` with a code, like a local worker's).
  - **No secrets.** The credential is in the body of the one request, never in a URL or header, in the placement, an error, a refusal, a log line or a stored record (tests scan answers, wire errors, the placement and the operation records). The client sends nothing else of it; the runner keeps none.
  - **Client and runner.** `RemoteAttempt.toolBridge(token, request, key?)`; `RemoteOfferRunner.bridge(attemptId, token, request)` answers for an attempt it does not run, a fenced answer and a lost connection as bridge answers (`fenced`, `unavailable`: the extension may ask again with the same call ID) and never sends the credential for an attempt that is not running. `RemoteOfferRunner.verdict(attemptId, verdict)` acts on the recovery handshake: `stop` stops the sandbox, `reaccept` takes the attempt up again in the new session.
  - **A deployed remote worker program.** There was none (the notes of L05d said "not composed into a deployed worker program"; the repository had only the tested building blocks), so one was made: `node scripts/remote-worker.mjs --config worker.json`, built from `scripts/remote-host.mjs` (`startRemoteWorker`, like `local-host.mjs` it lives in `scripts/` because the packages do not import each other). It connects with `RemoteWorkerClient` and `HostPoller`, runs each offer with `RemoteOfferRunner` over the worker package's `SandboxLauncher` and `localWorkerParts` (Pi in bubblewrap, `requireEnforced: true`) behind a `LocalWorker`, gives the machine's `ModelRelay` the runner's `tap(attemptId)` as its stream (every model call is recorded by the controller, its progress reaches stall detection), sends the process's bridge requests through the new route (`parts.bridge` is `runner.bridge`), answers workspace requests with `WorkspaceResponder` over `LocalWorkspaces.port`, lists what it holds in the recovery handshake and acts on the verdicts. **The workspace host's `security` hook is `client.reportSecurity`** (kind, key, project ID only; a failure is logged and never stops work). The abilities it confirms for the dispatch contract are found by trying (`detectLimitCapabilities` + `limitedPlan`), not claimed.
  - **Configuration without secrets.** The file names the controller `url`, `base` (the host's own folder), `projects` (project ID to the shared repository's folder on this machine), `routes` (`provider/model` to an endpoint, the NAME of the environment variable that holds the provider key, optional window and token cap), optional `protectedPaths`, `hostId`, `poller` timings. The host credential is `NIMBLENEWT_WORKER_TOKEN` or the file named by `tokenFile`; a `token` in the configuration file is refused. Nothing printed holds the credential, a provider key or a `Bearer` text (the test greps everything the process printed). A `https` address is required unless it is loopback.
  - **Remote route and speed for the monitor.** The placement now keeps the order's `route`; the remote service's monitor is made with the route and the host, so a remote call's `request_started` carries `route` and `hostId` and a finished call can add its sample to the route's speed on that host exactly as a local one does (`stall-speed`). Test: the open request of the stall evidence of a remote call names `localp/small` and `host:r1`. The speed sample itself is the existing code and thresholds.
  - **Review leftover: `sameValue`.** It reads own members only, so a `"__proto__"` member on one side was equal to the other side's prototype and is now a difference (both sides having the same one are equal). Test in the L05d binding test (four backends).
  - **Review leftover: monitor numbers after a restart.** A remote attempt outlives a controller restart and its new monitor numbered its reports from 1 again, replaying the command IDs of the earlier ones (ignored). Rather than persist a counter, each monitor has its own run mark (8 hex characters) in its command IDs (`relay:{attempt}:{run}:{n}`; request IDs keep their form `{attempt}:{n}`, the stall evidence tells a request by being the open one); the order within one monitor is still its sequence and two monitors for one attempt cannot collide (this also fixes a monitor made again by a placement made again). The monitor was moved to `api/relay-monitor.ts` to be tested alone.
  - **Real process.** `l05e-remote-worker.test.ts` starts `scripts/remote-worker.mjs` as a child process against a composed controller; it connects, takes the offer, runs Pi in bubblewrap, the controller records the model call as a generation bound to the remote attempt, Pi's `work.end` goes through the tool route to the real bridge and the attempt ends `succeeded`; the provider key reached the scripted provider from the child's environment by the name the configuration gave; the process ends cleanly on SIGTERM.
- **Not done.**
  - Windows and macOS remote hosts (the program is Linux and bubblewrap only, as the local host is).
  - The owner's `batchMs`/`batchChars` for the worker's stream batching are still the worker's fixed figures (L05d note), and the context limits (C07b) of the process are the process's defaults on a remote host (the local host takes them from the controller's `services.context`); the model's `contextWindow` on the remote host is the route entry's `contextTokens` or 32,768.
  - A tool script that `tool.invoke` runs is run by the controller's script runner (as for a local worker's bridge), not on the remote host; a remote script runner is a later card.
  - Attempts do not survive a restart of the worker program (the sandbox dies with it); the recovery handshake covers a reconnect within a running program only.
  - `requireStream` is still off by default (L05d).
  - The card is not flipped; no run against a real model.
- **Runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` clean; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard; `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` one shard at a time): controller shard 1 of 3: 3,874 of 3,876 (the card V01b relay test expected request IDs in the form `{attempt}:{n}`, which the first version of the run mark changed: kept, the run mark is in the command ID only, test passes; the H12m workspace-ask PostgreSQL test failed once under load and passes alone, 28 of 28 with its file); shard 2: 3,755 of 3,755; shard 3: 3,777 of 3,777; the other packages in shard 1 (worker, pi-adapter, contracts, integration with the real-process test) all passed; `scripts/*.test.mjs` including `remote-host.test.mjs`, `check:deps`, `roadmap:check`, `licenses:check` ok; `api:docs:write` no change. Mutations (each fails its test, or hangs the file until killed: tests since made to release their held call on failure): token check, contract confirmation, shared overlapping answer, same-ID-other-content check, unknown fields, body limit, `toolBridge` not composed, monitor run mark, route kept on the placement, `sameValue` prototype read, runner sending for a non-running attempt, `verdict` stop, client posting to the wrong action, program bridge, program security hook.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the remote worker program did not exist, so building it is in scope of "wire RemoteOfferRunner into the remote worker executable"; it is configured by a JSON file and the environment, not by the owner's state API.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the credential travels in the JSON body of the tool route over the authenticated, TLS (or loopback) worker channel; the controller authenticates it against the attempt and the worker already holds it. It is length-limited and never echoed.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a bridge request goes to the controller's bridge with the controller's gateway for the attempt (as for the local worker); the route has no state of its own, so the bridge's ledger is the only idempotency record.

**L05e review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-11), merged with main 7a88cfc5 first** (one conflict in these notes, both sides kept).
- **An overlapping copy with another credential got the first copy's answer.** The route's overlap memo was keyed by attempt, call ID and placement only, so a second request with the same call and a different (or wrong) task credential, sent while the first was in the bridge, was handed the first's result without its own credential being judged. The key now includes a SHA-256 digest of the credential (never the credential): such a copy goes to the bridge on its own. Test fails by assertion with the digest removed.
- **The remote host built folders from the controller's attempt ID unchecked.** `base/attempts/{attemptId}/home` and `scratch` were made and mounted as the sandbox home from `order.attemptId` as sent; an ID like `../../x` made (and gave the agent) folders outside `base` (the mutation run really created them). An offer whose ID is not `att-` + 20 base32 characters is now not run (logged), and the workspace step refuses it too. Task and project IDs were already checked by `LocalWorkspaces.ensure`.
- **A token file other users can read was accepted.** `tokenFile` must now be a regular file with no group/other permission bits (as ssh asks of a key); the refusal names the field, never the content.
- **Test added:** a chunked over-size body (no content length, never ended) is answered 413 while streaming; the earlier test sent a content length, so a limit applied only after buffering passed it.
- **Checked, holding:** host A naming host B's attempt (404 + `credential-misused` signal), stale placement/session (fenced), ended/expired attempt, unconfirmed contract (refused before the bridge), credential of another task (the bridge binds agent, task and project to the running attempt at the current generation), body limit while streaming, unknown fields at both levels, credential never in placement/ops/errors, `bridge()` maps a lost connection to `unavailable` ("ask again", not "not executed"; the call ID makes the retry the same call on the ledger), the sandbox gets `--clearenv` and an explicit env (the host token and provider keys never reach Pi), `sameValue` own-members change keeps arrays and nested equality, relay run mark bounded (`relay:{att}:{8 hex}:{n}`).
- **Flagged, not changed:** a 401 for the HOST credential reaches the agent as code `unauthenticated`, the same code as a refused task credential (the message differs); no per-host concurrency cap on the route beyond the transport's general rate limit (the memo is bounded at 256).
- **Mutations (each fails a test):** credential digest removed from the overlap key, host-ownership check removed, body limit moved after buffering, the offer and workspace attempt-ID checks removed (each separately).
- **Review runs** (`npx tsc --build --force` clean, no stale dist tests; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`; offline guard; `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`): controller shards 4,280 of 4,281 (K02a supervisor SIGTERM-group timing, 13 of 13 alone), 3,780 of 3,780, 3,702 of 3,702; worker 382 (1 skipped); pi-adapter 226; contracts 14; scripts 87 of 87; integration 139 of 150 with 10 skipped (heavy G04) and W11 job-wake failing under load (1 of 1 alone); `l05e-remote-worker` ran (22 s), not skipped.

## L05d finish: what the card still lacked, and the close-out (2026-11-13, Claude agent)

Code: `remote/client.ts` (`streamTap` takes the owner's figures; `STREAM_MIN_BATCH_MS`), `remote/service.ts` (`stream-start` answers `batchMs`/`batchChars`), `dispatch/model-stream.ts` (`ModelStreamCall.batchMs/batchChars`), `generation/stream-feed.ts` (the feed reports the figures it uses), `toolbridge/service.ts` (`bridgeCommandId`), `remote/server.ts` (`streamEventsPerMinute`), `remote/runner.ts` and `api/operations.ts` (text only). Tests: `api/start-remote-stream.test.ts` (2 new, composed controller), `toolbridge/service.test.ts` (2 new, all four backends), `remote/stream-flood.test.ts` (3, all four backends).

I read the L05d card and every L05/L05b/L05c/L05d/L05e note. The card's deliverables (bridge calls as effects, the remote host that runs Pi in its sandbox with the stream tap, rewritten call IDs, relay waits reported to stall detection, a worker that never opens a stream detected, name and arguments bound) and its acceptance (a REAL worker process in its sandbox: late reply held, a corrected generation's call refused at the bridge, a rewritten ID checked against its recorded generation) were already built and shown by L05d, L05e and their reviews (`l05d-remote-sandbox.test.ts` and `l05e-remote-worker.test.ts` both pass again here with the sandbox required: 2 of 2 and 1 of 1, none skipped). What was left on the card's own lists, and is now done:

- **The owner's `batchMs`/`batchChars` reach the remote worker (L05c second review, accepted for L05d; repeated in the L05e "Not done").** The worker used fixed figures (250 ms, 4000 characters), so with the controller's own batching up to about 500 ms or 6000 characters of late text could pass after a correction, against about 250 ms locally. The `stream-start` answer now carries the owner's two figures and the tap uses them (a figure given in the tap's own options still wins; with neither, the old defaults). The owner changes them by chat as before (`generation.stream.change`, in the interpreter's operation list; its text now says remote workers use them too), so no new control exists. The window is still the worker's plus the controller's, but both now follow the owner (the default 250 ms and 2000 characters instead of 4000).
- **A call ID of 89 to 120 characters was refused by the wrapped operation.** The note of L05d said a 100-character ID "hits the earlier command-ID length overflow": the command ID of the operation a bridge call runs was `bridge:{attempt}:{call}`, over the 120-character command-ID limit from 89 characters, although the bridge takes call IDs up to 120. `bridgeCommandId` keeps the readable form when it fits (byte for byte as before) and otherwise keys by a SHA-256 digest of the call ID. **Review fix:** the first digest form ended in `h-<40 hex>`, which a short call ID can spell, so the two could meet. A command ID has no character left over to mark a digest (letters, digits and `. _ : -` are all valid in a call ID), so the mark is now the prefix: readable `bridge:{attempt}:{call}` and `bridge-run:...`, digest `bridge-h:{attempt}:{40 hex}` and `bridge-run-h:...`. A readable form has a colon right after its prefix, a digest form a `-h`, so no call ID can make one equal the other. The threshold is the real length of the finished text (120), so a longer attempt ID moves it. Test (four backends): a 118-character call and short calls spelling its digest as `h-…`, `h:…`, bare and with the attempt ID get six different keys and the short ones keep the readable form. Test (four backends): a 118-character ID runs a write once, a repeat has the same key, an ID differing only in its last character has another, all within 120 characters; the short form is unchanged.

**Review round (Astra) fixes:**
- **The gap is enforced where a message is sent.** Before, the character count, a completed tool call, the end of the reply and the loop inside `flush` sent at once whatever the last send was (`batchChars: 1` meant a request per character; the first test even expected that). Now `flush` waits until the gap since the previous message of the call has passed before each request (the first message of a call goes at once), in the same serialized chain, so order is kept and the caller of `events` waits (backpressure). A long text split into several requests is spaced the same way. The gap is the owner's `batchMs` held to at least 50 ms (`STREAM_MIN_BATCH_MS`); a `batchMs` the worker is given itself is its own gap (0 for the tests that need every piece). The tap takes an injectable `sleep` as well as `now`. Test: an injected clock that only the tap's waiting advances; the send times of 40 one-character messages (owner `batchChars: 1`, `batchMs: 0`), of completed tool calls and the end, and of a one-million-character text cut into several messages are all at least 50 ms apart; a longer owner time (700 ms) is kept; nothing is lost (the generation holds all 40 characters).
- **Figures are validated, not repaired, at both ends.** A worker's own `batchMs` (whole number 0 to 60,000) or `batchChars` (0 to 65,536) that is negative, fractional, NaN, infinite, oversized or not a number makes `streamTap` throw `RangeError`. The controller's figures in the `stream-start` answer are checked the same way (also when the worker gave its own): an invalid one refuses the call (`ModelStreamRefused`, the call is not sent) and the generation the controller began is ended as failed. The only adjustment left is the documented floor of an owner's valid `batchMs` below 50 ms. Tests for each of negative, fractional, NaN, infinite, oversized and wrong-type values on both sides, with and without a worker's own option.
- **Flood bound at the controller.** The worker transport has its own bound for `stream-events`: `streamEventsPerMinute`, default 1,800 per attempt (an honest worker sends at most 1,200 a minute at the 50 ms gap), counted in the transport's clock window like its other rates and answered `429 rate_limited`; the worker then holds the reply back (a failed record). Test (four backends): a hostile worker sending 12 stream messages in a window gets 5 through to the service and 7 refused, other messages of the attempt are not counted, the next window lets it in, and the default bound is above the honest pace and below the whole-host allowance. The existing request, connection and body limits are unchanged.
- **Round 2 (Astra): one line of messages per attempt.** The controller's bound counts all of an attempt's stream messages, and up to four calls of an attempt are open, but each call paced itself, so two busy honest calls could send 2,400 a minute and be refused (and the transport's own per-address allowance of 3,000 a minute would have refused four). The gap is now kept across all the calls of an attempt: `RemoteWorkerClient.reserveStreamSlot(attemptId, gap, now)` hands each message the next free slot of the attempt (taken at once, so overlapping callers get successive slots), and a call waits for its slot before sending. An honest worker therefore sends at most 1,200 a minute per attempt whatever the number of open calls; the 1,800 bound stays as the aggregate abuse bound. Test (four backends, real streams through the protocol, injected transport clock): two and four concurrent calls of one attempt send 240 messages at a 600 ms gap with the bound scaled to the same proportion (a minute of the honest pace times 1.5, i.e. 150), all are accepted and recorded and take one line of time; the default bound is asserted to be exactly that proportion of the product's pace (1,800 against 1,200). Mutation: no shared slot fails this test (calls add up to 4 times the pace and are refused).
- **Round 2: the flood test is rewritten.** It starts real streams on two attempts of one host (two agents) and records what arrives. Attempt A's first five messages are recorded and its flood is refused without being recorded; attempt B (window opened a second later) records its own five regardless of A's flood and is refused on its sixth; A is refused at 30 s, 59 s and 59.999 s of its window and recorded again at 60 s, while B's window (opened at +1 s) is still closed at +60 s and reopens at +61 s. The world's remote suite got a `streams` option for this. Mutations now failing: one bucket for the whole host (the test fails at B's first message), the window reopening after 30 s (A recorded at 30 s), no shared slot (above).
- **Round 3 (final review, Claude agent): a clock stepped back no longer stalls the line.** `reserveStreamSlot` kept the next slot as a wall-clock time (`Date.now()` by default), so a clock corrected backwards right after a message (an NTP step of an hour) left the slot an hour in the "future" and the next stream message of that attempt waited the whole hour (the reply stalled, every call of the attempt with it). Each line now also keeps the time it was last asked at; a `now` earlier than that restarts the line at `now` (one message may follow the previous one sooner than the gap, once), and the sweep of old lines drops such lines too. The rest was checked and kept: a slot is only a time, so a call that fails while holding one blocks nothing after that time passes; overlapping callers get successive slots; a clock stepped forward only shortens one wait; the table is swept past 256 lines to 128 of lines still in use; the transport window is `>= 60_000` (59.999 s still the old window, 60 s a new one), keyed by host and attempt, and only `stream-events` is counted; `bridgeCommandId` keeps the readable form at exactly 120 characters and the digest form (`-h` right after the prefix) can never equal a readable one (colon right after the prefix). Tests: a unit test of the pacing line (four callers at one instant wait 0, 1, 2 and 3 gaps; another attempt does not queue; a slot whose caller failed blocks nothing once passed; after a clock step back of an hour the wait is at most one gap; a thousand finished attempts leave at most about 256 lines); the flood test now proves that heartbeats and a new call's `stream-start`/`stream-end` of an attempt whose stream messages are refused still go through (the notes above said so, but no test checked it). Mutations re-run on the reference store, each failing its test: one bucket for the whole host; the window reopening after 30 s; the shared slot removed (each call its own line: the two- and four-call test is refused); heartbeats counted in the stream bound; the clock-step fix removed ("waited 3600100 ms"); the readable/digest threshold moved to 119 (the "88 characters still fit" test). All new tests use injected clocks and no fixed pauses, paths or signals.
- **Round 3 runs** (after merging origin/main 847d0a3f; `npx tsc --build --force`, no stale dist tests, `api:docs:write` unchanged, `check:deps` ok; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, controller shards one at a time, load average about 60): controller 1/3 4,548 of 4,549 (encryption-manage "the command line adds a passcode" timed out at 120 s under load; the file alone 9 of 9), 2/3 4,424 of 4,424, 3/3 4,240 of 4,240; worker 440 of 443 with 2 skipped (the known sandbox-launcher flake; the file alone 32 of 32); pi-adapter 247; contracts 18; config 52 (24 skipped); ui 30; registry 15; `scripts/*.test.mjs` 154 (1 skipped); integration 163 (10 skipped, 0 failed).
Mutations (each fails its test, restored after): the tap ignoring the controller's figures; the floor removed; the wait before a send removed (the character-count test fails); validation of the controller's figures removed; the transport bound removed (the flood test); `bridgeCommandId` always returning the plain form; the digest form changed back to `h-…` after the same prefix (the collision test).

- **ASSUMPTION:** a worker that follows the owner's figures never sends two stream messages of a call closer than 50 ms apart (`STREAM_MIN_BATCH_MS`), whatever triggers the send and whatever the owner's valid `batchMs`: the owner's 0 means "check every piece" for the controller's own recording, but a request per token would pass the transport's rate limits and the failure mode is a closed (refused) call. A worker's own `batchMs` option is its own gap and can be 0 (tests).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the first message of a call is sent at once; the delay a completed tool call or the end of the reply can suffer is at most the gap (50 ms by default of the floor), which is also the price of the late-text window the owner's setting already names.
- **ASSUMPTION:** invalid figures are refused (an invalid controller figure refuses the call, as the controller being unreachable does) rather than repaired, because a silent repair hides a bug in one of the two programs.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the stream bound is per attempt and per minute, 1,800 by default, in the transport (not the service), so it counts every message however the service answers it; it is a limit on `WorkerTransportLimits` and can be changed with the other transport limits.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a call ID over the length that fits is keyed by a digest in the wrapped operation's command ID only, under a prefix of its own (`bridge-h`, `bridge-run-h`); the ID itself, the ledger key (`ba-...`) and the job/operation keys (already digests) are unchanged, and the readable form of every call ID that fits is byte for byte what it was.

**What is NOT done (honest list; none is in the card's deliverable or acceptance):**
- No run against a real model or real hardware: the models are scripted and the Pi/Radiance benchmark holds the one connection. This cannot be met offline; the real-process tests use a scripted provider.
- A controller restart loses the start/events idempotency maps and the open calls (a retry after a restart begins a new generation, L05c second review accepted).
- `checkCall` still reads up to 20 generations per bridge call (no index).
- `requireStream` stays off by default (it would stop every remote worker that has no tap).
- Linux and bubblewrap only for the remote host (no macOS or Windows remote host); a script run by `tool.invoke` runs on the controller (L05e).
- `d:` matching stays bounded by `GENERATION_REUSE_MAX` (1,000 uses of one provider ID).
- Windows/macOS: the new tests use temporary folders, an injected clock and sleep (no real waiting, no machine speed), no signals and no POSIX paths, but they have not run on a Mac or Windows machine; the stream-feed L05d flake (L05d "repeated provider ID") has no new evidence.

## U07b: web chat follow-ups: trusted proxy, two-level sign-in limit, revoked in-flight requests, settings, sign-out by chat (2026-11-11)

Code: `web/proxy.ts` (new), `web/door.ts`, `web/sessions.ts`, `chat/chat.ts` (`CallOptions`), `api/operations.ts` + `api/state-api.ts` + `api/start.ts` (`web.access.get`, `web.access.revoke`), `status/status.ts` (`web_access`), `chat/commands.ts` + `chat/model-interpreter.ts`, `packages/ui/src/script.ts`. Tests: `web/web.test.ts` (+17, 37 total), `web/proxy.test.ts` (3), `ui/ui.test.ts` (+1), `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts` (prompt lines). API docs regenerated. Guide: [private-web-chat.md](../private-web-chat.md).

**Done**
- **Trusted proxy (option `webChat.trustedProxy`, OFF by default).** `{ addresses, header? }`. Validated at start (`checkTrustedProxy`): 1 to 8 plain IP literals (no names, ranges, ports, leading zeros, unspecified address), loopback or private only, loopback only for a loopback listener, header `x-forwarded-for` (default) or `x-real-ip`. Without it, forwarded headers are never read. With it, the header is read only when the connecting peer is one of the addresses; then `x-forwarded-for` gives the rightmost entry that is not itself a proxy address (several header lines are one list), `x-real-ip` its single value. A hop that is not a plain IP, an empty hop, more than 20 hops, a repeated `x-real-ip` and an empty header fall back to the peer (the proxy's shared bucket), so a garbled header cannot choose an address. IPv4-mapped IPv6 is the IPv4 address; an IPv6 client is counted by its /64.
- **Two-level sign-in limiter.** Failures count per client address (10 a minute) AND over all addresses (`failedLoginsGlobalPerMinute`, 100). Check and count happen with nothing awaited between them (the burst fix is kept); a success gives both back. A **valid pairing code skips the ordinary ceiling** (it is single-use, 50 bits, five minutes), so the owner can still sign in under a flood of wrong credentials; an invalid code is a guess like any other. (Review: the code is now only looked at inside the per-address allowance and a code ceiling of 10x the global one, see below.) The owner's credential is the path a full counter closes (until the minute passes). Sign-in bodies are read at most 8 at a time per address and 64 in all (a slow sender cannot hold every reader). The terminal chat is a different door and was tested to work during a flood.
- **Revoked in-flight requests.** `ChatService.submit / applyProposal / discardProposal` take `{ stillAllowed }`; the door passes a check of "this session is still in the store and its credential is still the owner's". It runs before the turn is recorded, before each part of a plan, before each step of an applied proposal and before a discard. The error it throws ends the whole call (it is wrapped so a step does not turn it into a refused outcome) and the door answers 401 and clears the cookie. Steps already taken stay taken; applying again carries on (tested).
- **Settings view** on the page (the old Browsers tab): `GET /web/settings` (read only; binding, TLS/proxy, host names, trusted proxy, limits, session limits, the address the door sees you as and whether it came from the proxy header) with the existing per-session sign-out, sign out of all others and pairing-code display. Browsers now have a readable name (`deviceLabel`: "Safari on iPhone"), only that is kept of the User-Agent.
- **Owner chat control.** `web.access.revoke` (browser words or `all`) is a chat command applied at once (narrowing access; a lost phone cannot wait for a confirmation), matched by words in the browser's name, ambiguity and no match asked about, a repeat of the same command ID does nothing (no later sign-in is ended by a replay; a different payload under the same ID is a conflict). `web.access.get` and the status kind `web_access` read the settings and the browsers. Both owner only (an agent gets forbidden). The interpreter prompt describes them (and the op list is derived from the table); tests check the prompt.
- Mutations (each fails a test with the guard removed): peer-is-proxy check, leftmost instead of rightmost, skipping of trusted hops, no-proxy reads the header, IPv6 /64 bucket, loopback-listener proxy rule, public-proxy rule, global ceiling (check and count and refund), valid-code bypass, per-address and global body readers, `isLive` and credential re-check (each alone is covered by the other, both removed fails), guard at record/execute (same), guard at each apply step and at discard, replay memo and its conflict check.

**Not done**
- Changing the trusted proxy, address or network at runtime or by chat: they are start options (a security boundary like the binding); the chat says so. ASSUMPTION below.
- A pairing code in chat: the chat keeps its turns, so a code would be stored. The Settings view and `createPairing` show it.
- "Sign out all OTHER browsers" in chat: the chat has no notion of which browser it comes from, so "all" signs out every browser including the one asking (it signs in again). The page button still keeps the current one.
- The lock-out of the owner's credential by a many-address flood once the ceiling is hit (only the pairing code, or waiting a minute). A rate limit cannot tell the owner's guess from a stranger's.
- The Settings page was not driven in headless Chromium this time (the ui tests check the client calls and that the page code draws text only); no live Tailscale was used. A request already inside a single state API call when the session is revoked still finishes that call.

**ASSUMPTION:** `trustedProxy` is a start option only (smallest, most reversible; a mistake there is a security hole, so it is not a chat setting).
**ASSUMPTION:** a valid pairing code skips the ordinary global ceiling (single-use, 2^50 guess space); changed in the review so it no longer bypasses the per-address limit, and code attempts have their own global ceiling.
**ASSUMPTION:** chat sign-out applies at once in every profile, since it only narrows access.
**ASSUMPTION:** 100 failures a minute overall, 8/64 concurrent body readers: provisional, adjustable in `webChat.limits`.

**U07b review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-11), merged with main 6ca008f7 first** (conflicts in chat.ts kept both `stillAllowed` and the U14b `secrets: false` channel flag: the web door's backend now passes `{ ...options, secrets: false }`, so the door's options cannot switch secrets back on; `#apply` takes both). Fixed:
- **The sign-in limiter did nothing against pairing-code guessing.** `redeem(code)` ran before any limit check, so a client past its per-address allowance and past the global ceiling still had every code guess tried: a wrong one was answered 429, the right one signed in. Now a code attempt is first checked against the client's per-address allowance and a code ceiling over all addresses (`10 x failedLoginsGlobalPerMinute`, key `global:code`), counted on both before it is looked at (given back when valid), and a wrong code also counts on the ordinary ceiling. A code refused by a limit is not used up. Test: `a pairing code is tried only inside the limits` (per client, the code ceiling over all addresses, and the owner's code still working past the ordinary ceiling); both removed checks fail it.
- **Ambiguous sign-out named browsers the owner could not tell apart** ("2 browsers match: Chrome on Windows; Firefox on Windows" gave no way to choose but "all"). The refusal now carries each match's `ws-` handle, which `web.access.revoke` already accepts; tested.
- status.ts: the retention doc comment had been pushed above `webAccessLines`.
- **Checked, holding:** peer-is-proxy (mapped `::ffff:` peers canonicalised on both sides), rightmost untrusted hop, leading-zero/octal/hex/short IPv4, zone ids, ports, quotes and brackets in the header all refuse to name a client (fallback to the proxy's bucket, which only the misformatted requests share); `x-real-ip` doubled lines are joined by Node and refused; IPv6 /64 bucketing; counter maps bounded (a request over a ceiling is refused before a new key is made; `#windows` pruned past 5000; `#revoked` 200); the guard runs before the turn is recorded, before each plan part and before each proposal step (planning only reads); `deviceLabel` output is one of a fixed set of words; the Settings reply and `web.access.get` hold no cookie, CSRF token, credential or pairing code (session handles are not credentials); the three proxy mutations (no peer check, leftmost, no trusted-hop skip) each fail two tests.
- **Flagged, not changed:** (1) the sign-in body readers (8 per address, 64 in all) are taken before the code path, so 8 slow senders on 8 addresses can hold all 64 for up to the request timeout (15 s, checked every 30 s by Node) and refuse even a valid code meanwhile; `maxConnections` 200 is a lower bar for such a flood anyway. (2) Two browsers sending the same `messageId` share one run, so if the first browser is revoked mid-run the second gets the 401 and its cookie cleared (ids are browser-random; harmless in practice). (3) "sign everything out" in chat from a web browser signs that browser out too, and its own request ends with 401 before any later plan part (documented in Not done).

## U07 finish: recorded history, live updates, the cost and blockers pages, and a real-browser check (2026-11-14)

What was lacking against the card's acceptance ("phone browser supports chat, approval, status and recovery; a suspended connection resumes without duplicate commands; a revoked session is denied; local or private binding is explicit; no public exposure or mandatory VPN vendor; blocker and cost views"): the first two slices met binding, revocation, resume and the guide, but (1) the page only knew the messages sent from that phone (a second browser was empty, a reload lost anything the local copy had dropped), (2) nothing arrived without a tap, (3) the cost and blockers views were a plain list of fields, and (4) the page had only ever been run in a real browser once, by a throw-away script.

Code: `chat/chat.ts` (`ChatService.history`, `HistoryTurn`), `web/door.ts` (`GET /web/history`, `GET /web/events`, the stream limits, `liveStreams` on the settings reply), `api/start.ts` (the backend's `history`), `ui/src/script.ts` and `style.ts` (merged conversation, live updates, `pageCost`, `pageBlockers`). Tests: `chat/history-suite.ts` with `history.test.ts`, `history.sqlite.test.ts`, `history.worker.test.ts`, `history.postgres.test.ts` (4 each, on all four storage backends), `web/web.test.ts` (+5, 46 total), `ui/live.test.ts` (10), `web/browser.test.ts` (1, real browser). Guide: [private-web-chat.md](../private-web-chat.md). No state API operation changed (no `api:docs:write` change).

**Done**
- **The conversation from the controller.** `history(token, { limit, before })` (owner only; an agent is refused) returns the newest turns first: the words, the plain reply, the outcomes, status and times, and for every proposal in them whether it is `open`, `applied` or `discarded`. It reads the stored turns by a bounded scan (4000 records, ordered by identity, not time, so a very long history says `complete: false`); the cursor is the time and identity of the last turn shown, so turns made meanwhile never shift a page. Reading writes nothing and calls no model (tested by counting the audit trail and the interpreter's calls).
- **The page** shows turns from this phone from its outbox and every other recorded turn from the controller, in time order, never both; "Show older messages" pages back; an old question has no answer buttons (only the newest line has); a proposal decided elsewhere has no buttons.
- **Live updates** over one server-sent-event stream (see the guide). Only nudges, no content; fingerprints taken with the session's own credential; a failed read keeps its last fingerprint (an outage is not announced as a change); session and credential re-checked at every look; per-session and total caps; closed with the door; the page falls back to a 30-second history read without EventSource.
- **Cost and blockers pages** drawn as labelled regions and tables, a native `meter` with an accessible name on every cost row (no inline style: the policy forbids it), every string as text (hostile names tested), failed reads shown in the controller's words.
- **Real browser.** `web/browser.test.ts` runs the real page in headless Chromium as a 390 x 844 touch phone over the DevTools protocol (Node's WebSocket, no package, its own throw-away profile and loopback listener): the strict content security policy lets the real script run and nothing throws; every tab has no sideways scroll, every visible button a name and a 44 px height; the cookie is HttpOnly (`document.cookie` empty) and the secret is in no storage; a message sent while the browser is offline arrives once; a message whose ANSWER is lost (the request got through, the response was cut) is sent again under the same id and runs once; a second browser in its own context sees the conversation; a message from the terminal chat appears on both pages with no tap; revoking every session returns both to the sign-in. It skips where no browser is found.
- **Mutation checks** (each fails a test with the bug in, then restored): history order flipped; proposal state always open; page cursor repeating the last turn; history open to an agent; no live check on the stream; no per-session stream cap; chat change not fingerprinted; page shows outbox copies twice; answer chips on every line; proposal state ignored; the `ended` event not closing the stream; the `changed` event ignored (also fails the real-browser test); wrong meter share; history text assigned as markup; resend under a new id (fails the real-browser test). One survives and is equivalent: not stopping the streams explicitly on close, because `closeAllConnections` already ends them.

**Not done (what a real device or a human is still needed for)**
- **A real phone.** Chromium with touch and a phone-sized screen is not iOS Safari or an Android browser: Safari's EventSource suspension in a locked phone, the on-screen keyboard, safe-area insets on a real notch, Add to Home Screen and the real feel of 44 px targets were not seen. Nothing here ran on a tailnet or a certificate-trusting phone either (no deployment is authorised); the Tailscale commands are still from the vendor's documentation.
- **A screen reader pass** (VoiceOver, TalkBack): structure is checked (regions named by headings, tables with captions and scoped headers, buttons named, live regions on the log and the status pill, tabs with roles), the spoken result is not.
- **Offline shell** (a service worker so the page opens with no network): not built; a phone with no network cannot open the page, though an already open page keeps its outbox and sends when the network returns.
- **A persistent device record or a second factor**: still not built (see ASSUMPTION). Sessions end at a controller restart.
- **A QR code for the pairing code**: not drawn; the code is ten characters.
- **A designed per-project cost filter and a chart over time**: the cost page shows the controller's breakdowns, not a time series (the usage summary has none).
- A blockers item whose summary names an age (a stale artifact: "recorded 8 d 3 h ago") changes its fingerprint once an hour, so an open blockers or status view is read again hourly with nothing new; harmless (a nudge only re-reads), noted rather than fixed.
- The live-update look runs four reads per open stream every 15 seconds; with many owners that would be shared, but this is a one-owner product, so it is not.
- The history scan is bounded at 4000 turns, read in identity order (the turn ID is a hash, not a time); an installation with more reports `complete: false`, and the turns shown are the newest of the 4000 read, which need NOT be the owner's newest: the page then says some messages, recent ones included, may be missing, and the live-update look at the chat (which reads the same history) can miss a new turn. A time index on chat turns would remove the bound; it is a storage design change left for a follow-up card (tested in `chat/history-suite.ts` with 4100 seeded turns on all four backends).
