- Windows and macOS: the new tests use no signal, path or timing assumption (they wait on conditions and use a loopback listener); the browser test skips without a browser. They were not run on those systems here.

**U07 finish review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-14), merged with main 61d49fb8 first (no conflicts).** Checked: owner-only history and stream (agents and task credentials refused by `ChatService`, non-owners never get a session, revoked, expired and rotated sessions end the stream at the next look), the content security policy unchanged, no content, secret or host path in any event, hostile text drawn as text, the browser test skipping cleanly where no Chromium is found (only Linux paths and the Linux Playwright cache are probed, so macOS and Windows skip). Found and fixed, each with a test that fails with the fault in:
- **The 4000-turn bound was described wrongly.** Turn IDs are hashes, so past the bound the scan reads an arbitrary 4000, and the "newest" turns it shows need not be the owner's newest; the page said "Only the newest part of a very long history could be read". The page, the code comment and these notes now say recent messages may be missing. New test: 4100 seeded turns plus 50 of another owner on all four backends (`complete: false`, a full page, newest first among those read, the cursor pages on, no other owner's turn). Without it, dropping the owner filter from the scan passed every test.
- **A proposal decided elsewhere was not proven to nudge an open page** (leaving the proposal state out of the chat fingerprint passed every test): new web test applies a proposal from the terminal chat and waits for `changed` naming `chat`.
- **A dropped browser freeing its stream place and an expired session ending its stream were untested** (removing the close listener passed every test): new web test.
- **The incomplete-history note on the page was untested**: new UI test.
Deliberate breakages, each caught: close listener removed; owner filter removed; incomplete flag never set; scan bound removed; session re-check on the stream removed; total stream cap removed; `'unsafe-inline'` added to the script policy; proposal state left out of the chat fingerprint; incomplete-history note not drawn.
Left as found (noted above): the bound itself (a time index is a storage design change), the hourly re-read caused by an age in a stale-artifact summary.

**ASSUMPTION:** a nudge stream (no data on the wire, the page reads again with its ordinary requests) rather than pushing records: smallest thing that cannot show the owner something the session could not read, and a lost or repeated nudge is harmless.
**ASSUMPTION:** the history is the owner's whole recorded conversation (terminal chat included), because the controller keeps one conversation per owner; the page does not separate doors.
**ASSUMPTION:** 15 seconds between looks, 2 streams per browser, 40 in all: provisional, adjustable in `webChat.limits`.
**ASSUMPTION:** still no device-token record, no second factor and no service worker; each is a design change with a security or install cost that a human should choose, and none is needed for the card's acceptance as written.
**ASSUMPTION:** amounts on the cost page are shown in the cost unit with no currency symbol, because the usage summary carries none.

## K01b3 (proposed follow-up of K01b, built first): backup signing, the encryption on/off and scope setting, the proof reminder as a notification (2026-11-11)

Which card: K01d (backup scope tiers) is blocked (K01c, the full configurable backup system, is not built; K06b is only partly built). K01b3 is the K01b follow-up listed in the K01b second-slice notes ("proposed follow-up card line K01b3"); its only blocker, K01b, is built. It is NOT a line in the plan yet (see Not done), and no card is flipped.

Code: `backup/signing.ts` (new), `backup/setting.ts` (new), `backup/reminder.ts` (new); changed `backup/{write,service,verify,restore,staged-restore,cli,pin,encryption,index}.ts`, `api/{operations,state-api,start}.ts`, `chat/{commands,model-interpreter}.ts`. Tests: `backup/signing.test.ts`, `backup/setting.test.ts`, `api/start-k01b3.test.ts`, `api/start-k01b3-chat.test.ts`, one test in `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts`.

**Done.**
- **Signing.** Every backup (when `backup.signing` is given at start) carries `signature.json` beside the manifest: Ed25519 over a fixed label plus the SHA-256 of the canonical WHOLE manifest (so every file digest, the artifact and Pi indexes, and for a sealed backup the keyed MAC, are under it). The private key lives only in the host's secret store (F09; `StartOptions.backup.signing { store: { resolve, set }, secretName? }`, default name `backup-signing-key`); it is read for one signature and dropped, and never wrapped by a passcode, in the database, in a backup, in an answer or in a printed line (tests scan answers, every file of every backup and the start output for it). The public keys are recorded in the database (`backup-signing/main`) per generation, with the time signing began (`since`): that is "the owner's record". A locked, empty or foreign secret store writes NO backup (the signer fails closed, nothing partial is left); a start with an unreadable store or a retired key is refused; a store holding a valid key the record does not list is recorded as a new generation and printed as a warning.
- **Restore checks against keys it already trusts, never the backup's own.** `verifyBackup`/`restoreBackup` take `signatureTrust { keys, since? }`. Checked first (before any file is read): a missing signature is refused unless the backup is older than `since` (then a warning that it predates signing), a key not trusted is refused, a signature that does not verify is refused (the key ID in the file only selects among trusted keys; the maths decides). The staged in-controller restore uses the recorded keys (preview refuses, and the preview warnings say "Signature valid ... only as strong as the running server"; apply passes the trust into the restore itself). The command line takes `--trusted-signing-key-file F` (public keys, one base64 key per line, the owner's copy kept OFF the server; the key IDs are derived, never read) and `--manifest-digest HEX` (the stronger check for hand-exported backups: `verify` prints the digest to keep; a restore with a different digest is refused). Without a trust the result says plainly "its signature was not checked ... only as strong as the running server", so a restore on a new machine from the backup alone still works and does not look authenticated.
- **Rotation.** `backup.signing.rotate` (owner only, revision-checked, recorded, announced to the inbox as a Notice) makes a new key, stops the old one signing and keeps its public key trusted. The new secret is stored first and the record second (until the record names it, `sign` refuses, so nothing is signed with an unrecorded key; a record failure heals at the next start's `ensure`). `backup.signing.status` (owner only) shows generations and public keys, no private key.
- **On/off and scope setting.** `backup.encryption.set { enabled?, scope?, expectedRevision? }` (owner only at the service AND the operation, revision-checked, validated, recorded in the audit log, replay-safe). Off writes plain backups from the next backup; scope `secrets` is accepted but, because no secret values are in a backup yet, also writes plain (the answer and status say so in words); it never touches the key or old backups. A real change is announced to the owner's inbox ("Backup encryption was made weaker" as Needs-you; widening as a Notice). `backup.encryption.status` shows the setting. The writer reads the setting at each backup (`BackupService.encryptionSource`; a failing source fails the backup, never goes plain). **Downgrade guard:** an installation that has pinned a backup key refuses to start when the configuration no longer names the keyring file, unless the owner's recorded setting is off (the K01b review's "a pinned installation should refuse that").
- **Quarterly proof as a notification with escalation.** `BackupProofReminder` (a dispatcher sweep, `backup.proof-reminder`, every 5 minutes): when the proof is due (92 days from the last good proof or the key's creation) a Needs-you maintenance item says what to do (no secret, no path); if it stays due 14 more days a second, Urgent (interrupting) item is raised once; a successful proof closes both. Restarts do not reset the clock or repeat an open item.
- **Free-form chat.** `backup.encryption.set` and `backup.signing.rotate` are in `CHAT_OPS` as proposals (always shown first, applied on the owner's agreement); the interpreter prompt has a paragraph for the owner's own wording and says never to put a passcode, recovery code or key in an argument (the host-only key operations stay host commands). Tests: the prompt lists both with their argument names (generic test plus a specific one); a real `ModelInterpreter` with a stand-in model that acts only on what the prompt describes drives off, "agree", on, "agree" and the next backups follow (`start-k01b3-chat.test.ts`).
- API docs regenerated (`backup.encryption.set`, `backup.signing.status`, `backup.signing.rotate`, the status result).
- **Mutation checks** (each fails at least one test, then restored): signature maths ignored; untrusted key accepted; unsigned backup allowed past `since`; verify ignoring signature problems; setting owner check removed (service); downgrade guard removed; writer ignoring the setting; signer dropped from the writer; sign without the recorded-key check; rotate owner check removed; reminder never escalates; reminder never closes; restore skipping the trust; rotated key no longer trusted; the chat op applying without being shown; the prompt paragraph removed.

**Not done.**
- **Not a plan line.** `K01b3` is still only the proposal in the K01b notes. Adding it to `scripts/generate_task_plan.py` was tried and reverted: the plan tests need the ID format, a single leaf (D05 would have to list it), and the architecture record's counts changed, which belongs to the plan owner. Proposed line (unchanged from the K01b notes): `K01b3|N17|Finish encrypted backups: signing key and signature check, on/off and scope setting, proof reminder as a notification|K01b|...`, with D05 listing it.
- The signing public key is not carried by the recovery file (the card says "the recovery file OR the owner's records"; the records and the owner's saved public-key file are built). The setup command makes the recovery file before the controller has a signing key, so carrying it needs a command that adds it; follow-up.
- No `status.ask` kind or chat read for `backup.signing.status` / the setting (the owner reads them through the API status; the chat can change them). Owner can ask only by command today.
- The pre-upgrade snapshot (taken before the storage opens) is not signed and is sealed per the keyring, not per the setting (the setting lives in the database it is about to snapshot).
- Remaining K01b "Not done" items not part of K01b3: rotation prompted by an exposed passcode from chat (host files), Argon2id, keeping `.generation-N` files in line with retention, applying a rotated keyring without a restart, "secrets only" sealing real secret values (nothing to seal yet).
- A plain backup's time (`createdAt`) is not authenticated, so an attacker who can replace a plain backup AND the signature check's `since` rule could present an unsigned backup as pre-signing only if its stated time is older than `since`; sealed backups are protected by their MAC. Said in the "unsigned before signing" warning text.
- Signing needs `StartOptions.backup.signing` from the host; no configuration key or host wiring (the controller entry point passing the real F09 store) is added here.

**ASSUMPTION:** `signing.since` is the time signing was first switched on; an unsigned backup older than that is allowed with a warning (otherwise every backup made before K01b3 would be unrestorable), and every later unsigned backup is refused where a trust is known.
**ASSUMPTION:** a backup that cannot be signed fails (the failure shows through the usual failed-backup notification) rather than being written unsigned; a locked keychain is more likely than a reason to accept a forgeable backup.
**ASSUMPTION:** scope `secrets` is stored and reported as it is, but seals nothing because no backup holds secret values; the status says so in words rather than refusing the setting.
**ASSUMPTION:** the proof is due after 92 days and escalates 14 days later (provisional, like K01b's 92); `BackupProofReminder` takes both.
**ASSUMPTION:** operation name `backup.encryption.set` (not `.setting.set`): built-in command names allow at most three segments.

**K01b3 review (clean-context, 2026-11-11), merged with main 9c96053f first.** Fixed:
- **A rotation could stop every backup.** `backup.signing.rotate` put the new private key in the secret store before the recorded command, and the command's digest held the new key ID: a client repeating the same command (a timeout) was refused as `command_conflict` AFTER the store had been overwritten with a key no record names, and a rotation whose record write failed (stale revision, a storage error) left the same state; `sign` then refused every backup until a restart. Now the key goes into the store inside the command, after the repeat check (a repeat is answered from the record, `madeBy`, and touches the store not at all); a failed or overtaken write puts the previous key back when it is the one the record names; rotations on one controller run one at a time.
- **An exposed key stayed trusted for ever.** Rotation is the answer to an exposed key, yet the old public key stayed trusted, so its holder could sign a forgery (with any date) that the restore accepted. `rotate { revokePrevious: true }` now marks every earlier key `revokedAt`; `trust()` leaves revoked keys out (their backups restore only with the host command and no trusted key); `ensure` refuses a revoked key put back in the store. Chat: the interpreter prompt says when to give it.
- **Signing downgrade at start.** An installation whose database records signing keys, restarted without `backup.signing`, wrote unsigned backups and its staged restore checked no signature at all. The start now refuses that (as it does for a dropped keyring).
- **The pre-upgrade snapshot was unsigned**, newer than `since`, and in the same folder: on a signing installation the controller's restore refused exactly the copy taken before a bad upgrade. It is now signed with the key in the secret store (`BackupSigningService.storeSigner`; the database and its record are not open yet); no key yet means signing has not begun (the snapshot is older than `since`); a locked store fails the snapshot and so the upgrade.
- **The setting claimed sealing without a keyring.** On an installation with no keyring, `backup.encryption.status` said "on for everything: every file of a new backup is sealed" and `backup.encryption.set { enabled: true }` was accepted (backups stayed plain, and after a pin the next start refused to run). Switching on without a keyring is now refused (`invalid_transition`), and the text says no keyring is configured and backups are plain.
- **Chat:** `backup.encryption.set` values other than a boolean `enabled` and `everything`/`secrets` (a passcode the owner typed in passing, say) are refused before a proposal is made; `revokePrevious` must be a boolean.
- The proof reminder's 5-minute throttle no longer holds off the next look for as long as a clock was set back.
- Tests: `backup/signing.test.ts` (repeat/failed-write/concurrent rotation, revocation, pre-upgrade signer, the signature checked before any file is read), `api/start-k01b3.test.ts` (no keyring, signing option dropped), `api/start-k01b3-chat.test.ts` (a passcode in a chat argument). Mutations re-run, each fails a test: signature maths ignored, untrusted key accepted, unsigned backup allowed, keyring-drop guard off, signature checked after the files, plus the six new ones (no reconcile, no rotation lock, revoked still trusted, signing guard off, enable without keyring, chat value check off).
- **Flagged, not changed:** an unsigned plain backup with a back-dated `createdAt` is still accepted as "made before signing" (noted above; the time is the attacker's to write); restoring an older backup brings back an older signing record, so keys of generations made after it are no longer trusted (the next start records the store's current key again); the "strengthened" notice is also given for off -> secrets, which seals nothing today (the detail text says so).
## K01b (finishing slice): Argon2id, secret values in encrypted backups with a real "secrets only" scope, old key generations, switching on needs a proof (2026-11-12)

Which card: K01b itself. Earlier slices (first, second, K01b3 and their reviews) built the key, wrappers, recovery file and code, extra passcodes, rotation, signing, the on/off and scope setting and the quarterly reminder. This slice closes what the card text still lacked. Code: `backup/argon2.ts` + `argon2-worker.ts` (new), `backup/secrets.ts` (new), `backup/generations.ts` (new); changed `backup/{crypto,format,write,verify,restore,service,staged-restore,setting,encryption,cli,index}.ts`, `api/{operations,state-api,start}.ts`. Tests: `backup/{argon2,secrets,generations,k01b-staged}.test.ts`, `api/start-k01b-secrets.test.ts`, `backup/setting.test.ts` (updated).

**Done.**
- **Argon2id.** The card names it; Node 22 has none, so RFC 9106 Argon2id (one lane, version 0x13) is written out (`argon2idSync`, Blake2b included) and runs in a worker thread (`argon2idAsync`) so the controller's loop is never held for the few seconds 64 MiB takes. It is checked against OpenSSL's own Argon2id (fixed vectors in the test, and a live comparison at 64 MiB / 3 passes when the host's openssl has it) and Blake2b against Python's hashlib values. New passcode wrappers are Argon2id at 64 MiB, 3 passes; floor 64 MiB and 2 passes, ceiling 256 MiB and 16 passes, one lane (a wrapper outside is refused before any derivation). Settings are stored with each wrapper. Older scrypt wrappers still open (the `scrypt` option stays for them and for quick tests); new keys, added passcodes and rotations use Argon2id.
- **Secret values in encrypted backups.** `StartOptions.backup.secrets { store, names }` (the host gives the F09 store and the names the configuration uses). When encryption is on, every backup carries the values in one sealed file `secrets.jsonl.enc` under the backup's own key; the manifest lists only a count and how many names had no value. With encryption off a backup holds references only and the source is not even read. The backup-signing private key is never carried (excluded by name). A locked or failing store fails the backup (no folder left); nothing is written unsealed. The manifest's notes say which case a backup is.
- **A real "secrets only" scope.** `backup.encryption.set { scope: "secrets" }` now seals the secrets file and leaves tables, blobs and conversation files plain (before it wrote plain and said so). "everything" seals all of it, secrets included. A secrets-only backup verifies and restores WITHOUT any key (the rest restores; the secret values are left out and the result says so); with a key the manifest MAC and the secrets file are checked too; `requireEncrypted` with no key on such a backup is refused. The words said back to the owner (setting text, status, announcement) name the scope's effect and what losing every unlock method costs: secrets only, the values are lost and the rest restores; everything, the backups cannot be read. The setup command prints the same.
- **Restoring the values.** Library: `restoreBackup` takes a `secrets` sink; a value already in the store that differs is KEPT (a restore does not roll back a rotated secret), a missing one is put back, `overwriteSecrets` takes the backup's; counts only are returned (`secretsRestored`, `secretsLeftOut` in the `backup.restore.apply` answer). In-controller restore uses the host's store as the sink. Command line: a restore with a key needs `--secrets-out <new file>` (mode 600, never overwritten, written only after the restore succeeded, for the owner to load into the new store and delete) or `--skip-secrets yes`; refused before anything is made otherwise.
- **Switching on needs a proof.** Turning encryption back on (off to on) is refused until the recovery file was proved to open the key in this run within 24 hours (`backup.encryption.verify` method recovery), as at setup; scope changes while on need none.
- **Old key generations.** `backup encryption-generations <keyring> --backups <folder> [--remove yes]` and `oldKeyGenerations` in `backup.encryption.status` say, for each archived generation, how many backups still use its key. Only an archive with no backup is removed, never the live keyring, and never while any backup folder's manifest cannot be read; the output then says the recovery file made for it no longer opens anything.
- **A sealed backup no longer names skipped blobs in the clear:** their digests in the manifest are keyed.

**Tests** (4 storage backends where storage is touched: secrets.test.ts loops all of them): secrets scope (plain tables, no value or name readable in the folder, no-key verify with a note, passcode and recovery restore, no-key restore leaves values out, signing key never carried), everything scope, plain/locked store/tampered/removed secrets file/changed manifest, restore refusal with nowhere for values, kept-different and overwrite, name validation, command line (new mode-600 file, never overwritten, left out without key), started controller (scope and on/off setting followed by the next backup, enable refused until a recovery proof), in-controller restore for both scopes and the no-unlock host, generations (listing, still-used, unreadable folder, removal, Argon2id default and setup wording), Argon2id vectors and bounds.
**Mutation checks** (each fails at least one test, then restored): secrets file written unsealed; overwrite always; signing key not excluded; Argon2 rotation constant changed; generation removal ignoring unreadable folders; switch-on proof removed; secrets file not checked by verify; restore skipping the secrets.

**Not done / limits.**
- Rotation "prompted by an exposed passcode from chat": the chat cannot do it by design (the passcodes and files never travel through chat); the owner runs `backup encryption-rotate` on the host. The chat can read the status, the generation list and the setting, and change the setting.
- The signing public key is not carried inside the recovery file; the card allows "the recovery file OR the owner's records", and the records plus the owner's saved key file (`--trusted-signing-key-file`) are built.
- A rotated keyring still needs a restart to be used by the running controller; the pre-upgrade snapshot carries no secret values (the database and secret store are not open yet).
- The table row counts and file sizes are visible in a sealed manifest (the content is not).
- Argon2id is JavaScript: about 4 seconds for a derivation at the default settings (in a worker thread), slower than a native one. Parameters can be raised later; stored per wrapper.
- Retention (K01c) is not built; the generation removal is a host command, not an automatic step tied to expiry.

**ASSUMPTION:** default Argon2id 64 MiB / 3 passes / 1 lane (the RFC's low-memory recommendation and the card's floor); floor 2 passes.
**ASSUMPTION:** both scopes carry the secret values (the card: secrets are sealed whenever encryption is on); the backup-signing key is excluded even sealed.
**ASSUMPTION:** a secret already in the store with a different value is kept on restore (a rotated secret is never rolled back silently); the owner asks for an overwrite.
**ASSUMPTION:** the restore of values on a new machine goes to a new mode-600 file (the command line has no secret store of its own).
**ASSUMPTION:** the switch-on proof must be a recovery-file proof from the current run, within 24 hours.
**ASSUMPTION:** an unreadable backup folder blocks removal of key archives (deleting key material is never done on a guess).

**Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-12).** Argon2id checked independently: the host's OpenSSL 3.5 first reproduces the RFC 9106 section 5.3 Argon2id vector (four lanes, secret, associated data), then a 57-case differential (m 8 KiB to 256 MiB including sizes not a multiple of 4, t 1 to 9, tag 4 to 1000 bytes, passcode 0 to 5000 bytes, salt 8 to 400 bytes) matched ours byte for byte; a smaller sweep is now a test. Backups written by the pre-change code (0eccbdab: plain, and sealed with scrypt N=2^17) verify and restore with this code by library and command line, passcode and recovery file (checked by hand, not committed: a committed fixture would carry a keyring and its passcode). One-byte flips, truncation and extension of every sealed file, a secrets file swapped between two backups, and ten manifest/wrapper mutations (scope flip, scrypt downgrade, fewer passes, salt, wrapped key, nonce, ephemeral key, secrets count, secrets entry removed, MAC) are each refused with the key, both scopes. Fixed: (1) `encryption-generations --remove yes` with a mistyped or empty backups folder removed every archive (a folder that cannot be listed counted as "no backups"): now a folder that cannot be listed or has no `encryption-set-up` marker makes nothing removable; (2) the removal message said the old recovery file "no longer opens anything (you may destroy it)": it still opens copies of old backups kept elsewhere, so it now says so; (3) a restore put a `backup-signing-key` entry from a backup into the secret store / the `--secrets-out` file: a backup never carries it and anyone with the public keyring can seal one, so it is refused (default name and the installation's configured name) and counted as `refused`; (4) `--secrets-out` checked with access() let a dangling link through until after the whole restore: lstat now; `--skip-secrets` takes only yes; (5) the passcode copies sent to the Argon2 worker are wiped; the argon2.ts comment no longer claims an RFC vector test it cannot run.
**Review limits left:** a "secrets only" backup restored inside the controller on a host that has an unlock method set up still needs the passcode or recovery file put in place (the command line restores it without a key); a "secrets only" backup restored with no key has its plain files checked against a manifest that nothing authenticates but the signature (as with a plain backup; the MAC never authenticated against whoever holds the public keyring anyway). A crafted backup can ask for up to 2 wrappers of 256 MiB and 16 passes each, minutes of work in this JavaScript Argon2id on the command line.

## F04n: a failed fence take-back in a database rollback leaves the new database startable (2026-11-11)

Code: `packages/controller/src/transfer/transfer.ts` (`#rollback`, and the late-write branch of `#apply`). Tests: `transfer/transfer.test.ts` (seven tests marked F04n). No owner control, API operation or setting changed, so the interpreter prompt, the operation table and `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` are unchanged (the API docs were regenerated and are identical).

- **Done: the order.** When a rollback finds work written between its last check and the fence, the journal is now written back to `switched` FIRST and the fence is taken back second. If the take-back fails the state is: journal `switched`, authority file naming the new database, new database still fenced (`rolled-back:<id>`), barrier up. `guardStart` and `assertNotFenced` already accept a restart on the new database in exactly that state, so the next start comes up on it with the late records, and the previous database is refused. Before this change a failed take-back left `rolling-back`, which the next start finished onto the previous database.
- **Done: the lost answer.** A take-back whose commit happened but whose answer was lost is recognised by reading the holder (as the fence take already did) and counts as lifted; the message is the old one ("the fence was lifted and the controller must be restarted").
- **Done: the owner's message.** A failed take-back says what happened (work was recorded while the rollback was being made, so it was not rolled back; the record says the move stands; the fence could not be lifted; nothing was lost) and to restart the controller. The driver's own error text is not copied into it, so a PostgreSQL address cannot reach chat, the journal or a log (the tests make the failure carry a password-bearing address and check message and journal).
- **Done: a failed journal write.** If the journal cannot be written back, nothing else is touched (no take-back, authority file unchanged, journal as it was because the write is temp-and-rename), the new database stays fenced and the barrier up, and the message says NOT to restart until the state folder can be written and the record says the move stands.
- **Done: the apply path.** A late write found after the source was fenced and a failed take-back now also gives a plain message (the source stays the authoritative database; restart). State: journal `copying`, source fenced, no authority file; test shows `guardStart` abandons the transfer and `assertNotFenced` lets the source start. Behaviour of the successful paths and of a successful take-back is unchanged.
- **Tests (fail before, pass after).** The rollback test runs the same scenario on the reference store (`MemoryStorage` as a destination), SQLite, SQLite on its worker thread and PostgreSQL: a late record is written before the fence, the take-back is made to fail, then the journal, authority file, holder and barrier are checked, a restart is simulated (guard, `assertNotFenced`, new epoch) and the late record is read, and the previous database is refused. Mutations planted and caught: old order (tests 1-5 fail), journal failure swallowed (5), lost-answer re-check removed (7), apply path left as it was (6).
- **ASSUMPTION:** if the journal write itself fails we do not fall back to taking the fence back anyway: lifting the fence under a journal that still says `rolling-back` would let the work be written on a database a restart then rolls away; keeping everything as it was and saying "do not restart" is the smallest reversible choice.
- **Not done.** (1) [done in the review, below] (2) The rollback check still compares only the tables named in F04m. (3) `build-decisions-for-owner.md` keeps its "until then" advice; it is marked as superseded there. (4) The card's status in the task plan is not changed.
- **F04n review (clean-context, 2026-11-11).** Fixed: (1) a `rolling-back` journal was finished by the start before the database was opened, so late work on the new database was rolled away silently in three cases: the double failure above (late work and an unwritable state folder), a crash or a driver error after the fence and before the last check (work that slipped in before the fence was never looked at), and (2) below. `guardStart` takes the opened database now: on a start on the rollback's NEW database it waits until the database is open (`"later"` before, the storage after, both in `start.ts`) and compares it with `firstStart` (counters and digests, the rollback's own test); work found puts the journal back to `switched` (the move stands, the start goes on with the work, the previous database is refused); no work finishes the rollback as before. A start on the previous database still finishes it (it cannot look at the new one). (2) In the fence-failure branch, a failed write of the journal back to `switched` let the barrier come down and the controller go on working under a journal that said `rolling-back`: the barrier now stays up and the owner is told to restart. The message for late work with an unwritable journal now says to restart on the new database, not the previous one. The chmod test (skipped under root) is replaced by one that makes the journal's place a folder (works as root and on Windows) and goes on to the restart. Tests added: the stopped-after-fence rollback with and without late work (unit), the fence-and-journal double failure, and a real `startController` restart on the new database after a stopped rollback with slipped work. Mutations caught: no deferral before open, `start.ts` not passing the database, the barrier released on the double failure, the take-back skipped, the authority file written before the last check, the old order.
- **ASSUMPTION (review):** a start configured on the PREVIOUS database while the journal says `rolling-back` still finishes the rollback without looking at the new one (the owner chose that database; refusing would lock the owner out when the new database is gone). Only a write that bypassed the barrier between the rollback's check and its fence can be lost that way, and the messages say to restart on the new database.
- **Checked, not changed (review):** the lost-answer checks compare only the holder name, and every controller uses `controller` unless told otherwise; this is safe because the check runs under the state lock, and any other start waits for that lock and runs the start guard first. Owner-facing errors that are not `DomainError`s are masked by the API ("the request could not be completed"), so driver text reaches only the internal-error log.
## P04e (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5): per-resource maintenance leases, validation outcome, owner chat controls (2026-11-11)

Measured against the card's acceptance text, what was still missing after P04/P04b/P04c/P04d: maintenance leases ("a second agent's update to the same resource blocks visibly on the lease"), failed validation with a recorded rollback or escalation, event-driven checks, turning a due check into a bounded task, coverage gaps for provider outage and NimbleNewt downtime (start, end, reason) with reconciliation of missed events, Suspend / Suspend and Release behaviour, a remote host managed through an approved tool, and chat reach for the owner's responsibility controls (only `responsibility.create` was reachable). This pass builds the leases and the validation outcome and the chat reach.

**Done**
- `MaintenanceLeaseService` (`projects/leases.ts`, kind `maintenance-lease`, one record per managed resource). `acquire` grants a free or lapsed lease, renews it for the holder, and otherwise answers `status: blocked` after recording the block on the lease (who, when, why, whose lease; the last 10 kept, all counted in `blockedCount`). A lease ends at its time (default 60 min, max 1440); a lease past its time reads as `expired` and the next `acquire` takes it over and records from whom (`tookOverFrom`). The resource must be held by an active responsibility's claim; a paused or retired responsibility starts no new maintenance. Authority: owner, the answerable agent, or `responsibility.write`; anyone else is refused as if the resource did not exist.
- `release` takes the validation result. Passed frees the lease and writes an `ok` `intervention` into the responsibility history. Failed needs a response: `rollback` only when the responsibility's `permittedActions` names `rollback` (otherwise refused, escalate instead), or `escalate`, which opens an incident (`maintenance-validation:<resource>`, outcome failed) and escalates it at once (new `IncidentService.escalateNow`: same record as the timed escalation, target = the responsibility's `escalation.to` or the owner, so the existing loop tells the target). Either way a `failed` `intervention` entry is written. The owner may force-release another agent's lease with a reason only (recorded as forced, no outcome). Follow-up records use ids derived from lease and holding, so a repeat or a crash between steps completes the rest and writes nothing twice. NimbleNewt records that a rollback was invoked under the permitted action; the agent performs it with its own authorised tools (nothing here acts on a resource).
- Pausing a responsibility leaves its owner, open incidents, the escalation queue (the escalation still comes due and is still told) and any lease untouched (test).
- API: `lease.list` (query), `lease.acquire`, `lease.release` (commands). Chat (`CHAT_OPS`): `lease.acquire` (apply), `lease.release` (propose: ends a lease by force or with a failed validation), `responsibility.update` (propose; the revision is read for the owner via the new `revision: "responsibility"`), `incident.resolve` (profile). The owner names things in words, never IDs: `responsibilityTitle`, `incidentSignature`, `resourceLabel`, resolved from the project's records (one match, else the chat asks). `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.
- Tests: `projects/leases.test.ts` (10 cases x 4 backends: block visible and counted, bounded blocks, replay, renewal, takeover, authority and validation, passed/failed/rollback/escalate, forced release, pause, new service instance), `chat/lease-chat.test.ts` (force release, pause, resolve by words, refusal for an agent, shown-first vs applied), `api/start-lease.test.ts` (through `startController` with a restart).

**Not done (P04 stays open)**
- Event-driven checks (the `eventSources` field exists; nothing turns an event into a check) and the reconciliation of events missed during downtime.
- Turning a due check into a bounded task or a recorded observation (still only "a check is owed"), and "calling an agent only when interpretation or action is needed".
- Coverage gaps for a provider outage or NimbleNewt downtime with start, end and reason (only the check catch-up `gap` with reason `not-generated` and the P04d lapse reasons exist).
- Suspend checkpoints the responsibility without stopping the service; Suspend and Release naming the new monitor owner (needs L03/handoff-responsibilities wiring).
- A remote host managed through an approved tool with no worker enrolled.
- A sweep that tells the owner when a lease expired unreleased or when rivals waited long; today expiry is visible in `lease.list` and handled on the next `acquire`. Leases and blocks are scanned with the 50,000 limit like incidents (no index, no retention yet). `incident.report` is still API-only (an agent action); no chat words for acquiring a lease on an agent's behalf beyond `lease.acquire`.

**ASSUMPTION:** one lease per resource with a 60 minute default and 24 hour cap (the card names no figure); a blocked attempt is a normal answer, not an error; a failed validation must name its response and `rollback` is allowed only when `permittedActions` lists the literal action `rollback`; escalation on failed validation is immediate rather than waiting for the responsibility's time/count rule; ending a lease with a failed validation or by force is shown to the owner first in chat, taking one applies at once.

**P04e review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-11).** Two bugs fixed, each with a test on all four backends: (1) agents racing for the same lease met a changed record and the loser got `stale_revision` instead of a grant or a visible block; `acquire` and `release` now run again against the new state when their own lease update loses the race (up to 8 times; nothing is ever granted twice, the storage revision check already prevented that). (2) The records after a release (incident, immediate escalation, history entry) were derived from the lease's latest release and its generation, so a repeat of a release command after another agent had taken and released the lease recorded that agent's outcome under the repeating agent (an extra failed intervention, an extra incident report) and never its own; they now follow the command's own validation and response and are keyed by the release command (the release record keeps the command's hash as `key`). Checked and found sound: the who-may-lease rule against task-scoped principals (`responsibility.get` applies the task scope), a non-holder's renewal (blocked) and release after a takeover (refused), rollback only under `permittedActions`, a forced release needing a reason, paused/retired responsibilities, the minute bounds at the API (chat goes through it), chat naming by words (one match, else a question; model IDs fall under the generic foreign-value check). Known limits left as they are: a lease whose responsibility was retired cannot be released (it lapses at its end); a repeat of a release long after the resource moved to another responsibility would record on the new one.

## P04f (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5): due checks become observations or bounded tasks, event-driven checks, coverage gaps for downtime and outages (2026-11-13)

Measured against the card's acceptance text after P04e. Still missing then: a due check was only a record that a check is owed; nothing took it ("each check produces a bounded task or a recorded observation, calling an agent only when interpretation or action is needed"); the `eventSources` field turned nothing into a check and missed events were not reconciled; provider outages and NimbleNewt downtime were not coverage gaps with start, end and reason; and the owner had no control over check tasks. This pass builds those. Nothing in it calls a model, acts on a managed resource or touches the local AI server.

**Done**
- **A due check is taken** (`projects/check-runner.ts`, `CheckRunService`, run each tick after checks are generated, per project, in the loop `responsibilities.run`). A check is first offered to an optional deterministic probe (`CheckProbe`, none is wired into the controller yet: see below): its answer is written to the history as a `check` entry (no agent, no model) and a bad one is reported as one grouped incident (signature `scheduled-check`). Otherwise the agent that answers for the responsibility gets one **bounded task** (created, made ready and assigned under derived IDs, so a crash part-way or a second instance finishes the same task and never makes another). The task text says the objective, desired condition, managed resources, the actions the responsibility may use at most, that changes are held while a maintenance window is on, and how to finish (record a `check` entry). A `note` entry in the history links the task. The check stays owed until the agent records its `check` entry, so a task that never answers leaves "no recent observation", never healthy.
- **Bounds.** One open task per responsibility (a later check, scheduled or from an event, rides on it and starts no agent work); at most the owner's `maxOpen` (default 5) open check tasks in a project; 100 checks looked at per pass. A task that ended (done or cancelled) with no check entry is tried again after a wait (the responsibility's period, at least 5 minutes), at most three tasks per check; the third failure is recorded as a `check` entry with outcome `attention` ("not taken") and an incident. A responsibility with no answerable agent gets the same `attention` entry at once. Paused and retired responsibilities are left alone, so their checks wait.
- **Event-driven checks** (`projects/event-checks.ts`, `ResponsibilityEventChecks`). An event in the project's stream whose source id, kind or `source:kind` equals one of the responsibility's `eventSources` makes it owe a check (`CheckBody.trigger`: source, number of events, first and last sequence number, kinds). **One check per look**, not per event. Each responsibility has its own saved position in the stream (`responsibility-event-cursor`), moved only after the check exists, so a crash repeats the same check and never makes a second; a paused responsibility's position does not move, so its alerts stay queued and are read when it is active again. **Missed events are reconciled on return:** the position is kept across a restart, so events recorded during downtime are read and give their one check. If retention cut events the position had not reached, a closed `events-missed` gap (from the last look to now) says so. A new responsibility looks only at events recorded after it was created. A look reads at most 200 events per responsibility (`more` tells the loop; the rest is read next tick). Reading uses a new controller-internal `EventService.since` (no principal check, never offered through the API).
- **Coverage gaps** (`projects/coverage-gaps.ts`, `CoverageGapService`, kind `coverage-gap`): start, end (open while it lasts) and reason, kept apart from the lapse of one responsibility. Reasons: `controller-down` (the first tick of a process compares with the last time it was seen running, kept each minute in `coverage-liveness`: an absence over 5 minutes becomes a closed gap from then to now, once), `provider-outage` (the model-route health: a route that is down opens a gap at the time it went down, closed at the time it was restored), `event-source-outage` (an event source whose poll failed opens a gap, closed by its next good poll; hooked into `sourceLoops` through the new `ran` option), `events-missed` (above). Closed gaps older than 180 days are removed a few at a time. `covering` answers whether a gap overlaps a time span.
- **API and chat.** Queries `responsibility.gaps` (project's and installation gaps, open first; readers need `responsibility.read` in the project) and `check.settings.get`; command `check.settings.set` (owner only; `enabled`, `maxOpen` 1 to 50 or null for the default). Chat: `check.settings.set` (apply, reversible and a check that is not taken stays owed and shown as not observed); its verb and arguments are in the interpreter's command list, so the owner turns check tasks off or caps them in plain words. (Reading gaps and checks is a query, as for the other P04 reads: the chat is for commands.) `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Tests.** `projects/p04f.test.ts` (12 cases x 4 backends: gap open, close, scope and rights; downtime gap and removal; event checks incl. restart, pause, retention cut, batches; task, crash, ride-on and retry limit, probe and incident grouping, no agent, settings, paused), `dispatch/p04f-loops.test.ts` (4), `chat/check-settings-chat.test.ts` (4 backends), `api/start-p04f.test.ts` (through `startController`: event wakes, one task, restart gap, event read on return). Mutations run, each failing a test then restored: cursor not moved, ride-on removed, setting ignored, retry cap removed, downtime threshold removed, paused responsibilities not skipped.

**Not done (P04 stays open; this cannot be met offline)**
- **No deterministic probe is wired in.** `CheckProbe` exists and is tested, but nothing in the controller supplies one: a real probe needs a managed resource it can reach (an HTTP health URL, a process) and the permission to reach it, which is an approved-tool decision tied to the remote-host item below. Until then every due check is a bounded task for the answerable agent (still bounded by `maxOpen`).
- **A remote host managed through an approved tool with no worker enrolled** is not built: it needs a real tool bridge to a real host (U-cards for the tool bridge, L-cards for hosts), which cannot be exercised offline.
- **Suspend checkpoints the responsibility without stopping the managed service; Suspend and Release names the new monitor owner.** No Suspend-and-Release mode exists in the stop service (only `suspend` and `stop`); the hand-off (L03i) already moves responsibilities to a named agent. Nothing here stops a managed service (NimbleNewt never acts on one); a responsibility-aware Suspend note and a new mode belong to L02/L03.
- **Lease expiry told to the owner** (a lease that ran out unreleased, rivals that waited long) is still only visible in `lease.list`.
- Provider outage is read from the model-route health records the router keeps; an outage the router never saw is not a gap. A gap for a project is not yet put next to a responsibility's "no recent observation" in `responsibility.observed`; `covering` and `responsibility.gaps` give the facts to the reader.
- Event-source outage and provider gaps are installation-wide; they are not narrowed to the responsibilities that name that source.

**ASSUMPTION:** an event matches a responsibility when it equals the event's source id, its kind, or `source:kind` (the card names no matching rule). ASSUMPTION: check tasks are on by default with at most 5 open per project and are charged to the project like any other task (the owner had not chosen who pays); the owner may turn them off. ASSUMPTION: a restart shorter than 5 minutes is not a gap (a minute is the shortest check period, and the last-seen time is only kept to the minute); the start of a downtime gap is the last time the controller was seen, so it can be up to a minute early. ASSUMPTION: closed gaps are kept 180 days, a bounded number removed per tick from the first 200 records read (not owner-settable; K06's retention settings do not cover them yet). ASSUMPTION: a task that ends with no answer is retried at most three times, then recorded as `attention`; "not taken" is never recorded as ok. ASSUMPTION: events of a paused responsibility queue (its position is kept) rather than being dropped, and a check riding on an open task does not count against the owner's switch because it starts no work. The per-responsibility event positions are kept for retired responsibilities too (a few bytes each).


**P04f review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-13), merged with main 97a07961 first.** No path was found where a due check reads as healthy without a recorded `check` entry (the runner's own history entry is a `note`, which does not move the last check; only a probe or the "not taken" `attention` entry is written by the controller), and the retry cap holds (three tasks, then `attention`). `EventService.since`, the sweep, the runner, `noteRun` and `recordEvent` are reached only from the controller's start-up wiring, never from an API operation, chat op or MCP tool. Fixed, each with a test:
  - **A crash could make a second event check (MED).** The event check was identified by its first and last matching event; a crash between writing the check and saving the position, with a new matching event arriving before the next look, made a second check over overlapping events (and two instances at different moments did the same). It is now identified by where the look started (`recordEvent`'s `lookFrom`), so the repeated look is the same check.
  - **Event reads were not bounded per tick (MED).** Each responsibility read its own batch of up to 200 events, so 1,000 responsibilities in one project meant up to 200,000 reads a tick; and a new responsibility read the project's whole history 200 events a tick before it saw anything new (a project with 100,000 events: 500 ticks of lag). Responsibilities at the same position now share one read, a sweep reads at most 2,000 events in all (`EVENT_CHECK_READS`; charged by events actually scanned, so a look at the end of the stream costs nothing), the starting responsibility rotates so each gets its turn, and a new responsibility finds its first event after its creation by halving (holes count as "after", so it can only start earlier, never skip one).
  - **A clock set back hid a later downtime (MED).** The last-seen time was only rewritten when at least a minute had passed, so after the clock went back it stayed in the future, and a real absence after that was never over the threshold. It is now rewritten when the clock went back too. The 5-minute boundary is tested (exactly 5 minutes is not a gap, a moment more is).
  - **Lost source events were not recorded (LOW).** A source whose saved position was older than what it keeps reported a `gap`, but the hook ignored it, though the notes and the code comment said it is an `events-missed` gap. The hook is now `dispatch/loops.ts` `sourceGapHook` (tested on its own): it records that gap once, and one failing source no longer skips the others.
  - **`responsibility.gaps` arguments (LOW).** `limit` was not checked (a string or NaN gave an empty list and `truncated: false`) and `open` accepted anything; both are now refused with `invalid_command`. API-level tests cover `check.settings.set` with NaN, strings, 51, 2.5, an extra field and a string revision, and an agent without the rights reading or changing the settings or reading gaps.
  - **Each tick scanned every check record for every project.** `pending` now returns at once for a project with no responsibilities.
  - Mutations run, each failing a test, then restored: task ID not derived (two passes, two tasks), event position not saved, a closed gap closed again, event check keyed by first and last event, clock set back not handled, no shared read, new responsibility reading from the start, gap limit not checked, lost source events not recorded.
  - **Left as is (noted).** `pending` still scans every check record of the installation (there is no index by project) and gives up past 50,000 records; finished checks are kept unless the owner sets `checkRecordDays`, so a large installation that never prunes them would see the check runner fail every tick after months (hourly checks on 10 responsibilities reach that in about 200 days). A per-project index of owed checks is the fix. Two controller processes at once (the instance lock normally prevents this) could each open one task before seeing the other's, so `maxOpen` can be passed by one. A `close` that races another may return true although the other closed it (the gap is still closed once). Time while the dispatcher is held right after a start counts as the controller being down.

## P04g (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5): lease expiry told to the owner, coverage gaps shown next to the observed state (2026-11-14)

Measured against the card's acceptance text after P04f. Two items from P04f's "not done" list can be built and exercised offline, and are built here: a maintenance lease that ran out unreleased was visible only by asking `lease.list`, and `responsibility.observed` gave a state of `unknown` with no hint that a coverage gap was the reason. Nothing here calls a model, acts on a managed resource or touches the local AI server.

**Done**
- **A lease that ran out unreleased is told to the owner once** (`MaintenanceLeaseService.expiredUntold` and `markExpiryTold`, loop `responsibilities.lease-expiry` in `dispatch/loops.ts`, wired in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` and `api/start.ts`). Each tick, per project, a lease whose time ended with nobody releasing it and whose holding has not been told becomes one `maintenance` notice (`needs-you`, command id `lease-exp-<lease>-<generation>`) saying the resource, how many other attempts met the lease, and that another agent may take it over or the owner may release it by force. The holding is marked told only after the notice was sent (a failed notice is offered again next tick; an already-sent id counts as sent). A lease that was released, taken over before the mark, or that is still live is never told; a later holding that also runs out is told again (the mark is per generation and a new holding starts without it). Telling does not release or change the lease. A reader without the right to the project learns nothing (`undefined`).
- **Coverage gaps next to the observed state.** `responsibility.observed` now also returns `coverageGaps`: the gaps (id, reason, start, end if still open) that overlap the time since the responsibility's last check, or since it began when it has none. The state itself is unchanged (a gap never turns `unknown` into healthy); the list says why a check is missing.
- **Tests (this slice).** `projects/p04g.test.ts` (3 cases x 4 backends: listed once and told once, live and released and taken-over and stale-mark cases, a second holding, rights), `dispatch/p04f-loops.test.ts` (one new case: order, marks only after a notice, `command_conflict` as sent, one failure does not skip the rest), `api/start-p04g.test.ts` (through `startController`: a live lease tells nothing, an aged lease tells the owner once across ticks, still shown as expired, an open gap and a closed gap both appear on `responsibility.observed` while the state stays `unknown`). `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated. Mutations run, each failing a test then restored: the told mark ignored, the mark ignoring the generation, live leases listed, a failed notice swallowed and marked, the gap window started at "now" (a closed gap then went missing; the test was strengthened with a closed gap and the mutation then failed it). A no-op edit as a control passed, as it should.
- **No new owner control, so no new chat verb.** The notice is a fixed rule (it uses the owner's existing notification settings); there is nothing to switch, so there is nothing to describe in the interpreter prompt.

**Checked against the acceptance text (what P04 has and has not)**
Met in earlier slices and re-read here: checks generated idempotently and surviving a restart, a bounded task or recorded observation per check, intended/observed/last check/open incidents distinct and "no recent observation" never healthy, grouped incidents with bounded retries and escalation across restart, provider and downtime coverage gaps with start, end and reason and missed events reconciled, a second agent blocked visibly on the lease, a failed validation causing a recorded rollback or escalation, a paused agent keeping its queued alerts and ownership (P04f), Suspend and Release moving responsibilities with the task to a named agent (L03i: `reassignResponsibilities`, the new monitor owner is the recipient and the move is recorded in the hand-off).

**Not done (P04 stays open; none of this can be met offline)**
- **A remote host managed through an approved tool with no worker enrolled on it.** It needs the real tool bridge reaching a real host and an owner-approved tool; there is nothing to exercise it against inside the offline guard.
- **A deterministic probe supplied to the controller.** `CheckProbe` exists and is tested, but a real probe is an approved reach to a real resource (an HTTP health URL, a process) with a permission, tied to the item above. Until then every due check is a bounded task for the answerable agent.
- **Suspend (not Suspend and Release) writing a responsibility-aware note, and a monitor-owner line on the Suspend and Release stop mode itself.** The hand-off path names the new owner; the stop service has no mode that does, and nothing stops a managed service. This belongs to L02/L03.
- Event-source outage and provider gaps are installation-wide, not narrowed to the responsibilities that name the source; an outage the model router never saw is not a gap.
- A per-project index of owed checks (noted in the P04f review) is still not built.

**ASSUMPTION:** an expired lease is told to the owner as a notice that needs them (`needs-you`), once per holding, with no setting to turn it off, because it blocks every other agent from the resource until someone acts. ASSUMPTION: the gaps shown on `responsibility.observed` are those overlapping the time since the last check (or the responsibility's start), read as the reader, so a reader who may not read the project's gaps sees none. ASSUMPTION: the notice does not name the holder's task or release the lease for the owner; releasing stays an explicit act (`lease.release`, forced with a reason).

**P04g review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-14), on c8f14062 (already on main a3dccc4f).** Checked and found sound: a notice is marked told only after it was sent (a repeat of the same notice id replays, an answered earlier item gives `command_conflict`, both count as sent); the mark is per holding (`generation`), and every new holding (a takeover, or the same agent taking it again after it ran out) gets a new generation and a body without the mark; a released lease has no holder and is never listed; `expiredUntold` follows `lease.list`'s project rights; the observed state is never changed by the gap list. Fixed, each with a test:
  - **Notices of different leases were folded together (LOW).** The notice pointed at the responsibility, and the notification service keeps one open item per kind and record, so a second lease of the same responsibility that ran out (or the hand-off notice "now answers for responsibility ... but lacks rights", also a `maintenance` item on the responsibility) replaced the first one's text and only raised a count. The notice now points at the lease (`maintenance-lease`, the lease id): one item per resource, and a later holding of the same resource is counted on that item. `api/start-p04g.test.ts` now runs two resources of one responsibility (two notices, each naming its own) and ages the second holding it used to leave unchecked (told once more, then not again).
  - **`markExpiryTold` had no rights check (LOW, not reachable today).** It is reached only from the controller's sweep (as the owner), but as a public method it let any principal mark an expiry as told, which would keep the owner from being told. It now refuses anyone but the owner or a service (`forbidden`); test on all four backends (the holder, a rival with write rights and an agent without rights are refused and the lease stays untold).
  - Mutations run on the built files, each failing a test, then restored: the told mark ignored, the rights check removed, the mark ignoring the generation, a failed notice swallowed and marked, the notice pointed back at the responsibility, the gap window started at "now", live leases listed, the project rights skipped in `expiredUntold`. Two controls passed as they should (free leases admitted to the filter: they carry no holder; a no-op edit).
  - **The "cannot be met offline" list above is too broad.** Of the five items, only the remote host through an approved tool and a real probe reaching a real resource depend on things outside the offline guard. These can be built and tested offline and are left for a later slice, not blocked: a per-project index of owed checks; narrowing event-source and provider gaps to the responsibilities that name that source; a Suspend note that names the responsibilities (and says the managed service keeps running) and a Suspend-and-Release mode in the stop service naming the new monitor owner (code in `lifecycle/stop.ts`, owned by L02/L03 but nothing external is needed). Also offline and not listed: P04f's "rivals that waited long" (a live lease that keeps blocking others is still never told; only a lease that ran out is), and settling the expiry notice when the lease is later released or taken over (it stays open until the owner answers it).
  - **Left as is (noted).** Each tick `expiredUntold` scans every lease record of the installation once per project (the same 50,000-record scan as `lease.list`); a single scan grouped by project would be cheaper for many projects.

## P04h (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5): leases that keep others waiting, notices that close, narrowed gaps, an index of owed checks, a Suspend note (2026-11-14)

Measured against the P04g review's list of what could still be built offline. Nothing here calls a model, acts on a managed resource or touches the local AI server.

**Done**
- **A lease still in time that keeps another agent waiting is told to the owner** (P04f's "rivals that waited long"). `MaintenanceLeaseService.untold` finds, in one pass, each lease whose current holding has blocked another agent for at least `LEASE_WAIT_MINUTES` (30) by the oldest block still kept; the holding is told once (`waitToldGeneration`, set by `markWaitTold` only after the notice was sent). The notice (`maintenance`, `needs-you`, ref `maintenance-lease-wait`, command id `lease-wait-<lease>-<generation>`) names the resource, holder, number of waiting attempts, since when, until when the lease runs, and that the owner may release it by force. Blocks of an earlier holding never count. Telling releases nothing.
- **Notices close when their lease moves on.** The `responsibilities.lease-expiry` loop first looks at the open notices (`openRefIds` of both ref kinds) and closes (`settleFromController`) an expiry notice whose lease is no longer expired (released or taken over) and a waiting notice whose lease is no longer held in time. The rule follows the lease's own status, never the "told" mark, so a failed mark cannot close the notice just sent. A lease that is taken over and runs out again between two ticks is coalesced on the one open item (count raised), as before.
- **One pass per tick, not one per project.** `untold` scans the installation's leases once (only held ones) for both lists; the loop no longer takes a project list. `expiredUntold` (per project, with the project's read rights) is kept for readers and the earlier tests.
- **Gaps narrowed to what a responsibility depends on** (`gapAppliesTo`, used by `CoverageGapService.covering` and so by `responsibility.observed`). `controller-down` is about all. `provider-outage` is about a responsibility with an answering agent (one with nobody is recorded as not taken without asking a model). `event-source-outage` and `events-missed` of `source:<name>` are about a responsibility that names `<name>` or `<name>:<kind>` in its event sources; one with none is not affected. A retention gap kept by one responsibility's look (`events:<id>:...`) is about that one. Any other key stays about all. `responsibility.gaps` (the project's list) stays whole.
- **A per-project index of owed checks** (`responsibility-check-index`, `ResponsibilityChecks`). `generate` and `recordEvent` add each new check to the project's index in the same storage operation (retried on a race). `pending` reads the checks of the index when it is complete, instead of every check of the installation; otherwise it scans once and, when the controller reads, writes the index (so an installation that already has checks needs no migration and a record made while that scan ran is never lost: the write is against the revision read first). Only the controller drops finished or removed checks from it; a reader never writes. Past 5,000 entries the index is dropped and the scan is used as before. The index is a hint that is only ever too wide (the owed test is still applied to each record).
- **A Suspend note** (`projects/suspend-notes.ts`, run from the stop service's `onSettled` hook in `api/start.ts`). When a Suspend, Stop or Force Stop of an agent (or of the whole installation) ends in `suspended` or `stopped`, each non-retired responsibility that agent answers for gets one `note` in its history naming it, saying it stays with that agent, that NimbleNewt does not stop the service being maintained (nothing watches it until the agent is resumed), that checks and alerts wait and are taken then, and that Suspend and Release (the hand-off) names a new monitor. Once per request and responsibility (a repeat writes nothing); one failing note does not skip the others. Task and team scopes are not noted.
- **Tests.** `projects/p04h.test.ts` (4 cases x 4 backends: the wait list, one pass and a moved-on lease, the narrowing rules, the index with scan counts, an index missing entirely) plus the suspend note; `dispatch/p04f-loops.test.ts` (the loop's order, marks, closings, one failure not skipping the rest); `api/start-p04h.test.ts` through `startController` (a wait told once then closed on release, an expiry notice closed on takeover, narrowed gaps on `responsibility.observed`, the note on an agent's responsibility after `lifecycle.stop`). `start-p04g.test.ts` keys its gap for the responsibility now. Eight mutations run on the built files, each failing a test and then restored: wait threshold ignored, notices closed whatever the lease status, provider gaps not narrowed, retention gap not narrowed, index never used, `generate` not indexing, the told mark ignoring the holding, the note written for every scope kind.
- **No new owner control, no chat verb.** The new notices are fixed rules that use the owner's existing notification settings, the same as P04g; there is nothing to switch, so the interpreter prompt has nothing to add. The owner already releases a lease by force and reads gaps in plain words through the existing controls.

**Suspend and Release stays with L03.** The card's "Suspend and Release names the new monitor owner" is met by the hand-off (L03i: `reassignResponsibilities` takes the named recipient and records the move). A second Suspend-and-Release mode in the stop service would duplicate that path and its fencing, so it was not added; the Suspend note points to it.

**Not done (P04 stays open; these need things outside the offline guard)**
- A remote host managed through an approved tool with no worker enrolled on it (needs the tool bridge reaching a real host and an owner-approved tool).
- A deterministic probe supplied to the controller (`CheckProbe` exists and is tested; a real one is an approved reach to a real resource, tied to the item above).
- A provider outage the model router never saw is still not a gap; the provider narrowing is by "has an answering agent", not by the route that agent uses (responsibilities do not name routes).
- A kind-only name in `eventSources` (a kind with no source in front) is not matched to a source outage, because the outage names only the source; the gap is then not listed for it.
- The Suspend note does not cover a team or task scope (a responsibility belongs to an agent; the team's agents are not listed there).
- `answeredBy` and the index scan fail closed above 50,000 records of a kind, as the other P04 scans do.

**ASSUMPTION:** a wait is "long" after 30 minutes (provisional, fixed, not owner-settable); the oldest of the last 10 blocks is used, so a very busy lease is told a little late, never early. ASSUMPTION: the waiting notice is `needs-you` like the expiry one, because the owner may need to release the lease by force. ASSUMPTION: an event-source name matches a gap when it equals the source or begins with `<source>:`; names that cannot be matched are left out rather than guessed. ASSUMPTION: a provider outage is about a responsibility with an answering agent. ASSUMPTION: the index keeps at most 5,000 owed checks. ASSUMPTION: the Suspend note is written for Stop and Force Stop as well as Suspend (the managed service keeps running in all three), worded by what happened.

### P04h review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-14)

- **Fixed: the index could lose an owed check for good.** `pending` read the project's responsibilities first and the index after; a responsibility made in between (its check generated and indexed meanwhile, for example by the tick while the owner reads `responsibility.pending`) was not among those read, so its check counted as not owed and the controller's write dropped it from a complete index. Nothing put it back. The index now drops only a check of a responsibility it read whose last check is at or after the slot (or one whose record is gone); an unknown responsibility's check is kept. Test: a read with a list taken before the second responsibility existed leaves its check owed (4 backends).
- **Fixed: a bare event-source name hid source outages.** An `eventSources` name without `:` matches an event's kind as well as its source (`ResponsibilityEventChecks.matches`), and any source can send that kind, so a source outage can be about it. The narrowing now lists every source outage for a responsibility with a bare name (one too many is safe, one hidden is not); `source:kind` names still narrow exactly. A key cut at its 160-character limit matches by prefix. The earlier ASSUMPTION ("names that cannot be matched are left out") is replaced by this. `responsibility.observed` summary and API document updated.
- **Fixed: the Suspend note ran as the one who settled the request, raised to owner level.** `lifecycle.advance` can be called by an agent that may pause the scope; its principal was copied with `kind: "owner"`, so the note was written under the agent's name with owner powers (reading every responsibility of the installation). The note now runs under a fixed controller name (`service:stop-notes`) at the owner's level, as the other controller hooks do. Test: the note's author is `service:stop-notes`.
- **Test added: a reader never writes the index** (an agent with read rights reads the owed checks; the index record is unchanged). A mutation making every reader write survived before it.
- **Checked and left as is.** Crash between check and index: one storage operation. Two writers: every index write is against the revision read (`contention` retried 8 times by `generate`, given up by `pending`, which leaves it too wide). Retention deleting a check: `get` misses it and it is dropped. No other code path creates `responsibility-check` records. Index body at 5,000 ids is about 155 KB (under the 256 KB record limit). Closing notices follows the lease's status only (`settleFromController` closes the open occurrence; its command id is not a key). A stale waiting notice of an earlier holding stays open while the lease is held by a new one (safe direction). Gap narrowing uses the responsibility as it is now: an answering agent removed or an event source taken off after a gap hides that older gap from it (noted; the project's `responsibility.gaps` stays whole). The Suspend note is best effort (a failing note is not retried; the stop is not undone).
