The line says "judged to matter", "not reviewed by a second agent (why)", or "need you: N judged to matter and M not reviewed (why)".
- **The dispatcher's notice and wait reason (`dispatch/dispatcher.ts`)** say "had no second-agent review" or "need you (M not reviewed)" instead of "matter to it" for unjudged changes. Within the 200-character notice, the room for names is never negative.
- **The prompt always fits the shared client (`continuation/resume-reviewer.ts`).** Pieces were 40 changes with no size check. Quoting (backslashes, `\uXXXX` escapes) could push a prompt past the 24,000 characters `BoundedReviewerModel` keeps. Its cut dropped the closing id list and could leave a change line half shown with its id visible. Pieces are now also made smaller to fit `RESUME_REVIEW_LIMITS.prompt` (24,000).

**Tests:** `resume.test.ts` (per-change not reviewed, both directions, 4 backends); `status.test.ts` (mixed and all-unreviewed wording); `dispatch/resume-hold.test.ts` (the notice and wait reason for a not-run check, 4 backends); `resume-reviewer.test.ts` (40 heavily escaped changes: every prompt at most 24,000, more than one piece, every shown id in the closing list). Own mutations, each failed its test: per-verdict marker dropped; mixed wording treated as all unreviewed; dispatcher unreviewed count forced to 0; the size check removed. 4 of 4 killed.

**Seen, not changed**
- The shipped reviewer runs inside the dispatcher's tick (`#resumeCheck` awaits `resumes.start`), as an explicit `resumeReview` did before. With a route set, a resuming attempt holds the tick for at most one slot wait (45 s) plus the host client's bound (60 s) per piece, once per check.
- Two `advance` calls on the same `reviewing` check at once would both call the model and both count spend; only one verdict is written. Not reachable from the single dispatcher loop.
- A file that changes again after the review keeps the same status and note ("the content differs"), so neither the verdict nor the commit's staleness check sees it. This predates L04d (L04b's digest). The reviewer never sees content, so its verdict would not differ.
- The owner naming a route allows cloud data (`data: "cloud-allowed"`, paid allowed), the same consent rule as `report.reviewerRoute` (W10). There is no per-task local-only flag to respect.


## Clean-context review of the one-write settings change and the meetings notice sink (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-11)

Reviewed the "Review leftovers: settings changes in one write" section above (commit d8763d08) after merging origin/main 45dd09ff.

**Checked and sound.**
- `change` against the old stage then apply, check by check: unknown fields refused; layer and scope ID; a value valid for its setting; installation-only settings only in the installation layer; nothing locked above; a restriction no wider than the layers above or its fallback; the owner alone writes the installation layer and locks (the writer rule is the same `#mayWrite`); the scope must exist; at most 200 settings; the whole combination checked by the same `#combined` with the layer as it would be; the guards on the layers above; the history entry with its effects. "No revision given" in the chat was already "the layer must not exist" under the old stage, so `?? 0` keeps it. For `database.transfer.set` with no revision, the old code read the layer and expected that revision; `change` now writes against the layer as it is, which loses nothing because it is computed from that same layer in the same write. A change refused by the checks writes nothing (the old apply left a failure record that the discard followed).
- Nothing in the composed controller calls `stage`, `apply` or `discard` any more (no API operation, no chat, CLI or MCP path, no setup or import step writes a configuration layer otherwise), so no draft is made today and none can be applied over the owner's newer change. A draft an older controller left is never applied; if an embedder applies one later, its revision check is stale after any `change`, and an apply at the new revision would put the draft's absolute values into force over the change (the draft holds values, not differences). That is the meaning of applying a draft, and no product path does it.
- Settings consumers read the configuration when they need it (no cache or listener keyed on `config.apply`), so a `config.change` write is seen exactly as an apply was. The audit record is written once, by the runner, with the caller as the actor.
- Meetings notice sink: `noticeFromController` sets `contention`, so a race on the inbox is `stale_revision`; `command_conflict` can only mean the same `mtn:` key was already filed (or is being filed at that moment). Every other error is rethrown.

**Fixed.**
- A `change` that creates a layer and loses to another write at the same moment (the same layer created by another write, or a layer above changed, such as the owner locking the setting) was answered `command_conflict` "already exists, so this command ID was used by something else": the runner's wording for a create that meets a conflict. The command ID was fine; the settings moved. The chat happened to treat it as stale, but `database.transfer.set` with `expectedRevision: 0` would pass the wrong answer to an API caller. `change` now gives the runner a contention answer when it creates a layer: `stale_revision` with the current revision. (`stage` has the same wording and is left as it is; nothing in the product calls it.)

**Tests added** (`configuration/configuration.test.ts`, all four backends): a change of a value keeps the owner's lock in that layer, and a value locked above is refused in the agent and task layers; a layer of a team or agent that does not exist is `not_found` and nothing is written; a lock above that lands between a change's read and its write (a storage wrapper runs it just before the commit) makes the change `stale_revision` and nothing goes into force under the lock; two changes creating the same layer at once give one success and one `stale_revision`.

**Mutation checks**, each applied alone, built and run: lock dropped by `change`; the check against the layers above removed; the scope existence check removed; the guards on the layers above removed; the replayed answer's effects emptied; the create contention answer removed; the meetings sink swallowing every domain error. Before the new tests, three of these (lock, existence, guards) survived; now all seven fail their tests.

**Not changed.** `change` clears the layer's `lastFailure`, which describes the last refused apply of the draft that is still staged; with no product path staging, it is left as is.

## Credential redaction follow-up: clean-context review (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-11)

Adversarial review of the scanner above, probing with invented keys only.

**Fixed**

- Two inputs took quadratic time. A base64 dump with no private key END (the old `ORPHAN_END` regex, a repeated line group before a lookahead) took 6 s for 256 KB and did not finish for 1 MB. Text with `eyJ-` repeated (the JWT pattern started at every `\b`) took 5 s for 64 KB. The orphan END is now found by walking back from each END line, and a JWT must start at the beginning of a run. 1 MB of either now takes 0.1-0.7 s.
- Misses. `KEY=<random value>`: a `=` before a run kept it from the entropy rule, so `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…` and an Azure `AccountKey=…` stayed. The named assignment now matches at the end of a longer name, after `_` or a quote: `DB_PASSWORD=`, `CLIENT_SECRET=`, `client_secret=<64 hex>`, `"password":"…"`, `_authToken=`, `Pwd=`, and the new `access_key`/`secret_key`/`private_key`/`auth_token` forms. `inputToken`, `max_tokens` and `TOKEN_COUNT` still stay. New shapes: `Authorization: Basic …`, AWS `ASIA`/`ABIA`/`ACCA`, Slack `xapp-`, and the "service token" shape (Hugging Face `hf_`, GitLab `glpat-`, Docker `dckr_pat_`, DigitalOcean `dop_v1_`, Shopify `shpat_`). A combining mark on a key's letter is left out of the matching view; the text keeps it, and a span covers the marks on its last character. A lone carriage return splitting a key is joined like a line break.
- False positives. go.sum `h1:` and `sha256:` + base64 digests stay, and so do SSH public keys (`AAAAB3NzaC1yc2E…`, `AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5…`, ecdsa). The AWS prefix stays case-free but its body must be upper case. A case-free body read a derived ID such as `cmp-a3t…` or `cmp-akia…` (20 lower-case characters) as a key, and the C07q compaction test found it.
- `redactText` no longer throws on a non-string. Three raw error messages are now redacted: start's release recovery line, the launcher's "building it failed", and the MCP stdio bridge's stop message.
- Tests: four review tests in `secret-scan.test.ts`. Mutations, each killed: view offsets shifted by one at the start, and at the end; marks kept in the view; `=` hiding runs; orphan END never redacted; the JWT `\b` start (by the time test); the named assignment `\b`; trailing marks not covered.

**Not done (decided)**

- Homoglyphs (a Cyrillic `о` or Greek `ο` inside a key) are not folded. Such a string is no longer the key, and anyone who swaps letters on purpose can just as well encode it. A key split by spaces, by quotes (`'ghp_ab' + 'cd'`), or written in JSON `\u` escapes or HTML entities throughout is not caught. Joining across spaces would blank ordinary text.
- ASSUMPTION: a random value after `=` is now checked by the entropy rule, so a third-party URL `cursor=<32+ random characters>` is blanked. NimbleNewt's own `~` cursors stay. A secret in `KEY=value` lines (.env files, connection strings, `?sig=`) matters more.
- Still blanked: `xxd -p` hex lines (60 hex), data: URI images, SHA-384/224 hex, PGP signature lines and other long base64 of plain data (as noted above). The prose `the token: expired` is blanked by the named assignment, as before.
- A key at a line's end followed by a short non-word on the next line (`Ok`, `𝐀`) blanks that word too (the line-joined view).
- Older copies that are not the shared scanner remain. config `findInlineSecrets` (`SECRET_SHAPES`) and release `service-units` (`SECRETISH`/`SECRET_VALUE`) keep their own shorter, case-sensitive, unfolded lists. The worker and pi-adapter packages have no credential redaction; pi-adapter prints hook error messages raw. Thinking store and job output keep their own orphan-END literals on top of the scanner. The tool bridge, job runs, MCP job call and scratch cleanup strip controls with their own regexes after `redactText`. `onInternalError` passes the raw error to the embedder's sink.
## L03j: the integrator lease and workspace holds in a hand-off (2026-11-11)

**What this card does, plainly.** When a task is handed from one agent to another (or taken over by force), the controller now accounts for two kinds of hold the sender may have: the *integrator lease* of a landing branch (the right to be the one agent landing work on that branch) and *workspace holds* (a workspace operation running on the task's checkout, or one that ended but could not unfreeze the agent's attempts). The hand-off package lists both, and the "not tracked by this installation yet" gap line is gone. When the task really moves, each lease the sender held for it is let go exactly once, or moved to the recipient if the owner (and only the owner) asks. A workspace hold is never lifted or taken over by a hand-off: it belongs to the operation, which ends it itself (or the recovery loop does).

- **The lease (new, `packages/controller/src/landing/integrator-lease.ts`).** P10 had not been built, so there was no lease to account for. This card adds its smallest part: `IntegratorLeaseService`, one lease per project and branch, with a fence number that grows by one each time the lease changes hands, and an expiry. `acquire` (refused while someone else holds a live lease; of two at the same moment one wins), `renew` and `release` (refused `fenced` for an old fence, a released or expired hold), `handOver` (to another agent and task, new fence, refused for an expired hold, since an expired lease is free and is taken like any other), `valid(leaseId, fence)` for a landing to check right before it writes, and `forTask` (the live leases of a task, from a per-task index of at most 8 leases). It takes no caller: it is for code that builds the services (the hand-off now; P10's landing later). It is on `startController`'s `services.integratorLeases`; there is no state-API operation for it yet.
- **The hand-off (`lifecycle/handoff.ts`).** A new port `LeaseHandover` (`integratorLeaseHandover` adapts the service). Steps, each written before it is carried out, so a crash at any point is finished by the next pass or the sweep: (1) just before the transfer, the sender's live holds for the task are read and written into the hand-off as `leasePlan` (lease, branch, fence, release or move); (2) the task moves; (3) the responsibilities chosen (L03i) move; (4) each planned entry is released or moved under a command ID made of the hand-off, the lease and the fence; (5) the results are written once as `leasesSettled`; (6) the hand-off is marked done and the activity record says what happened ("Integrator leases: released integration."). A repeat of step 4 after a crash answers what it did the first time and writes nothing again; a hold that changed since the plan (expired and taken by another integrator, or released) is answered `fenced` and recorded as `skipped` with the reason, never touched.
- **Who may move a lease.** `handoff.complete` takes `moveIntegratorLease: true`. Only the owner may give it (anyone else is refused `forbidden` before anything moves); it is refused for a temporary reassignment and its return, for a recipient that is not an agent, and on a repeat that makes the other choice. Without it, every lease the sender held for the task is released when the task moves. A forced takeover always releases. In chat it is a "shown first" argument like `acceptGaps`.
- **Stop and resume.** A hand-off that is cancelled or fails (the sender stays the owner) leaves the sender's leases as they are. While the sender is suspended its lease is not renewed, so it may expire during a long preparation: that is the lease's own rule (a lost integrator frees the branch), and the package says until when it is held.
- **Workspace holds.** New `WorkspaceOpService.heldFor(taskId)`: a request that ended but still holds attempts frozen (its freeze could not be lifted). The locks section names it next to the running operation L03h already listed. The hand-off does not end, lift or take over either: the freeze is tagged with the request's ID and only that request (or the recovery loop) lifts it; the record stays attributed to the sender (`assignee`); the recipient's attempts wait (`isBusy`) until it ends.
- **The locks section** now lists the sender's leases for the task, the checkout's workspace operation and any freeze left by one, and the claims of the sender's responsibilities. When every kind was read and nothing is held it says so (`LOCKS_NONE`, "none: ..."), instead of leaving the section empty; a source that fails says that part is missing, not absent.
- **Tests.** `landing/integrator-lease.test.ts` (four backends: race with one winner, expiry frees the branch with a new fence, an old fence cannot renew or release, a repeat answers what it did, a second release under another command is refused, an expired hold is not handed over). `lifecycle/handoff-leases.test.ts` (four backends, real lease service, a fault injected at each step: before the plan, after the plan and before the transfer, after the release and before its record, before the release; a lease that expired and was taken by another integrator is skipped and left untouched; owner-only move with a crash after the move, moved once to fence 2 not 3; the other choice on a repeat is refused; cancel keeps the lease; forced takeover and a temporary reassignment release it). `workspace-ops-h12m.test.ts` (four backends: `heldFor` names the request while the freeze stays and is gone after the recovery). Composed `api/start-handoff-holds.test.ts` (through `startController` and the state API: a refresh held open on the host, a lease, the package lists both, a manager cannot move the lease, the hand-off releases it and leaves the operation running and the owner's, the owner moves the next one with a new fence, "none" when nothing is held). `api/start-handoff.test.ts` now expects the "none" line where the gap line was.
- **Mutation checks** (each applied alone, built, run, restored): the settle step skipped (8 failures); release without the fence check (6); no plan before the transfer (8); no owner check on the move (3).
- **Review (clean-context, 2026-11-11).** Four real bugs found and fixed, each with a test that fails without the fix on all four backends: (1) two acquires by one task for different branches at the same moment raced on the task's index and the loser was refused "leased by someone else" although nobody held its branch: a lost race is now built again, and only a lost race on the lease itself is a refusal; (2) the same applied to `release`, `renew` and `handOver`: a release racing the holder's renew came back `fenced`, which the hand-off takes as a final skip, so the sender kept a lease for a task that had moved: those are now built again too, and `fenced` means only that the hold really changed; (3) the per-task index kept "the last 8" and pushed out the oldest even while it was live, so a hand-off would never release or move it: now only leases that ended (or moved to another task) make room, and a task already holding 8 live leases is refused a ninth (`unavailable`); (4) two `handoff.complete` calls at the same moment (the owner moving the lease, a manager not): the one whose step lost simply advanced the winner's choice and answered success; it is now answered as a repeat, so a choice that lost is refused `invalid_command` (a cancel that won makes it refused as cancelled). Found on the way, pre-existing: two different callers advancing one hand-off at once sent the transfer under the same command ID with different actors, and the loser got "command ID already used for a different command"; that answer now means someone else moved it, like `stale_revision`. Mutation checks of the review (each alone): release every lease of the task whoever holds it (caught by a new test: another integrator's lease for the same task is untouched), settle always releases, complete ignores its lost step, settle command ID not stable across a crash, the index counting a lease that moved to another task (new test), plan written after the transfer: all caught.
- **Remaining risks noted by the review (not fixed, for P10).** After a restore from a backup the lease records go back with it, so a fence handed out after the backup can be handed out again to someone else; `valid(leaseId, fence)` does not compare the holder, so P10's landing should check the holder too or fold the epoch into the fence. `acquire` does not check that the task belongs to `projectId` (no caller can reach it yet; P10 must). An expired hold that a planned move could not hand over stays `held` (expired) rather than being released, which only matters if the controller's clock is set back.
- ASSUMPTION: P10 was not built, so its first part (a fenced, expiring lease per landing branch, without the queue, reservations or landing itself) is built here so the hand-off has a real lease to account for. Reversible: P10 builds on it or replaces it.
- ASSUMPTION: a hand-off releases the sender's leases for the task unless the owner moves them; nobody else may move one (smallest-scope reading of "never taken over without the owner"). A temporary cover releases too; the lease is not handed back with the task.
- ASSUMPTION: a running workspace operation is named in the package, not a reason to hold the hand-off back (the provisional choice of L03h stands); the recipient waits for it through `isBusy`.
- ASSUMPTION: the lease holder is named by its agent ID and works the landing under one task; who may `acquire` (the integrator role, the task's assignee) is decided by P10's landing, not by this service.
- **Not done (remains for P10 and later).** No state-API or chat operation acquires, renews, releases or lists leases; no landing uses `valid` before it writes; no queue, reservations, refresh-round cap or escalation; nothing renews a lease on the holder's behalf; a lease held for a task that is not handed over but simply ends (task cancelled or done) is left to expire rather than released at once; the per-task index keeps the last 8 leases, so a task that held more than 8 different branches over time would not list the oldest (they are on other branches and expire on their own). The activity line is recorded as the one who completed the hand-off, so when that principal may not record activity (a manager with only assignment rights) the line is skipped, as for the L03i sentence (best effort, unchanged here).
## H12t (first slice): the product worker host uses the workspace port under the owner's landing policy (Claude agent, 2026-11-11)

Card H12t, "Compose the production workspace port into the product worker host". Built on H12q (`LocalWorkspaces`), H12s (`landingPolicy`), H12m (the responder), W05 (`doneVerifier`), U11d (the security hook) and U14b (the launcher's host builder `scripts/local-host.mjs`).

- **What was wrong before.** The launcher's host (U14b) and the remote host (L05e) already built `LocalWorkspaces`, but both passed a fixed landing policy, `{ branch: "main", requirePermit: false }`: every landing went to `main` whatever the owner set, and the commit permit was switched off. The launcher's host also gave no `verify` (so a done of a task whose contract names evidence or checks was never taken as verified, W05) and no security hook. A remote worker could answer workspace requests without saying which attempts were busy.
- **Done.**
  - **The launcher's host (`scripts/local-host.mjs`)** now hands its workspace port the controller's own parts when the controller builds it: the owner's landing policy for the task, read fresh at each landing (`services.landingPolicy`; before the host is built, and when the policy cannot be read, a landing is refused), the security hook (`services.reportSecurity`), and the done check (`verify: doneVerifier(...)` over the same port's checkouts and the attempt's sandbox). The busy check stays `LocalWorker.busyAttempts` (tool calls and model calls in flight).
  - **Two projects on different branches.** Configuration has no project layer, but the owner already has a per-project, owner-only record: `project.branches.set` / `.change` with `landing`. It is now the landing policy's branch for that project (`ProtectedBranchService.landingOf`, `landingPolicyFrom(configuration, projectLanding)`); a project that names none uses the installation's `workspace.landing.branch`; no branch anywhere means nothing lands. The permit and protected paths are still the settings' (installation, team, agent, task).
  - **Remote worker.** `WorkspaceResponder` now requires a `busy` check and is refused at construction without one; before it hands a request to the port it asks it, and a request whose attempts must be quiet includes a busy one (or whose check throws) is refused, nothing run. `scripts/remote-host.mjs` passes `local.busyAttempts()`. Its landing policy is now its own configuration's `landing: { projectId: branch }` (checked: a branch name, for a project in `projects`), with the permit required and the default protected paths kept; a project not named is never landed there.
  - Texts updated: the `workspace.landing.branch` description, the `project.branches.set` summary (the chat model reads it), the worker's `host.ts` comment.
- **Tests.** `packages/integration/src/h12t-product-host.test.ts` (1, real bubblewrap, skipped cleanly without it unless `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): the launcher builds the host; an attempt runs in the checkout the port made (its layout beside the data directory, no `.git` in it); a refresh asked while the agent's model call is in flight is refused by the host's busy check; the done is checked on that checkout (the contract's check runs in the sandbox and passes); a landing with no branch named is refused; with the installation's branch `main` a refresh and a landing of project A are answered and A lands on `main`; project B (repository on `trunk`) is refused on `main` and lands on `trunk` once the owner names it; a quarantine moves A's checkout. `packages/controller/src/api/h12t-landing-project.test.ts` (5: the policy combination, and `landingOf` on all four storage backends). `packages/controller/src/remote/workspace-ask.test.ts` (+1 per backend: no busy check refused at start, busy and unknown refused without reaching the port, a quiet one runs). `scripts/remote-host.test.mjs` (+1: configuration checks, landing from configuration, busy given to the responder). The H12s test's call now uses a real-form project ID (a malformed one is refused by the project read, fail closed).
- **Mutations (each alone; all killed):** the launcher host's busy check returning nothing (the refresh ran during the model call); the old fixed `main`/no-permit landing (landed with no branch named); no `verify` (the done was never verified and the attempt did not finish); the responder's busy check removed (4 backends fail); the project's landing branch not read (B refused on trunk).
- **Not done (left for H12t's next slice or other cards).**
  1. **A remote host does not get the owner's landing policy.** The workspace request carries no policy, so the remote host uses its own configuration's `landing` map. Carrying the owner's policy (branch, permit, protected paths) in the request, or a host-channel read of it, is the follow-up.
  2. **The host's busy check and the controller's quiesce differ for model calls.** The quiesce stops gateway calls, not the relay, so an operation asked during a model call is refused by the host and must be asked again (H12m leftover (1), unchanged). Nothing retries it automatically.
  3. **No project layer in configuration.** Only the branch is per project (from the branch-settings record); the permit and protected paths stay per installation/team/agent/task.
  4. **`HostOrder` (worker package type) still does not declare `taskId`/`projectId`**, though the controller's `WorkOrder` carries them and both hosts read them; typing it is cosmetic for the `.mjs` composers.
  5. **No submit/stage in the product composition** (W09). The commit through release is now made by the platform when `release` is asked for (H12o product slice, 2026-11-12, see its section); nothing asks for it automatically after a done.
  6. macOS and Windows hosts (H12r) are unchanged: the builder still says it is Linux only.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the project's owner-set landing branch (`project.branches.set`, `landing`) wins over the installation's `workspace.landing.branch`, because it is the more specific of two owner-only answers and was recorded for exactly this ("which branch finished work lands on"). Reversible: clear it with `landing: null`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a malformed project ID in a landing request refuses the landing (the project read throws) rather than falling back to the installation's branch; the controller only sends real project IDs.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the remote host requires the commit permit for every landing (no configuration switch to turn it off), because the owner's permit setting does not reach it yet; the smallest safe choice.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the responder's own busy check refuses a request as a plain refusal (not `failed`), since nothing was run.

### H12t first slice: clean-context review (Claude agent, 2026-11-11)

Reviewed commit 5667ac9a after merging origin/main (H12s's narrowed slice was already in the branch; no overlap conflicts).

- **Checked and sound.** The landing branch (installation's, a project's own, or the remote host's map) is never written into a git argument: the host only compares it with the branch the shared tree is already on (`git symbolic-ref`), so `refs/` prefixes, leading `-`, `..`, tags or symbolic names cannot redirect a landing; a name that is not the tree's branch is refused. `project.branches.set` / `.change` are owner only (both check), the project ID is checked (`proj-` form) on write and on `landingOf`, and the stored name is checked again when read. A policy that cannot be read (settings or project record) refuses the landing; the dispatcher gives `{}` (no branch: refused) when no policy is wired. The local host's busy check counts model calls; the port's own busy check runs again just before the work (the responder's is a first gate). The done check runs on the checkout `workspaces.ensure` made and in the attempt's sandbox (W05 bounds the output). The remote host's configuration is checked before it starts (a bad `landing` entry stops it) and every landing there needs the permit.
- **Fixed: a busy check that answers something other than a list left the request in hand forever.** `WorkspaceResponder` filtered `quietAttempts` against the answer outside any `try`: a non-list answer threw, the request stayed marked running, was never answered and never retried (the controller waited it out). Now a non-list answer (or a missing `quietAttempts`) refuses the request like a throwing check, and the refusal is sent. Test: `workspace-ask.test.ts` (a `Set` answer, 4 backends).
- **Fixed (test): nothing checked that the product host refuses a landing without the commit permit.** The end-to-end test turned the permit off before its first successful landing, so a local host that forced `requirePermit: false` passed. The test now names the branch first with the permit at its default and requires the landing to be refused ("do not carry the commit permit"), nothing written, before it turns the permit off for the operator's commit.
- **Mutations (each alone; all killed):** the responder's original unguarded filter (the new `Set` case); the responder ignoring busy attempts; the installation's branch over the project's; `set` not owner only; the remote host's permit off; the local host forcing the permit off (killed only by the new test).
- **Leftover (added to H12t's next slice):** 7. **A remote host has no done check (`verify`).** `scripts/remote-host.mjs` gives its `LocalWorker` no `doneVerifier`, so a done of a task whose contract names evidence or checks is never verified on a remote host and the attempt does not succeed there (fails closed, never a false pass).

## U11c (other refusal points): a refused-for-no-grant call counts as a denial (2026-11-12)

Card U11d listed "the denial hook also from the other refusal points (not only the tool approval policy)". This is the smallest complete slice of it, and it needs no new owner control: the existing `deniedThreshold` / `deniedWindowMinutes` / `deniedAlertsPerHour` settings of `notifications.configure` (owner only, with `expectedRevision`, chat-settable in any words; the interpreter prompt is built from that operation table, whose text already says "refusals of one agent") now cover a second kind of refusal.

- **Done.** In the tool gate (`dispatch/tools.ts`, `#judge`) a call the agent made with no grant for it now ("agent X holds no grant for tool.Y on this task now", for example after the owner took the grant away while the agent kept calling) is a denial like a policy denial: it goes to the same hook (`onDenied` -> `UrgentWatch.reportDenial`), once per call (the same call asked again, or twice at once, is not a second one), and is counted per agent with the policy denials. With no threshold set nothing is counted (as before), a single refusal is routine, and beyond the owner's threshold one Urgent item is raised for that agent, with the hourly cap and the inbox-only overflow that already exist.
- **Not counted on purpose (they are not the agent's doing):** a pause, the owner's decisions or gates, a changed decision revision, a route that is no longer allowed, a used-up budget, a frozen attempt. The new suite test checks that a pause refusal is not told.
- **Tests.** `dispatch/dispatcher-suite.ts` (all four dispatcher test files that share the suite: reference, SQLite, PostgreSQL, worker): the new case "a call refused because the agent holds no grant ... is told to the denial hook once". Mutation checked by hand: removing `denied: true` from the grant refusal made the SQLite case fail (103 pass, 1 fail), then restored.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a missing grant is counted as a denial because it is the one other refusal where the agent itself tried something it may not do; the other refusals above are controller or owner states.
- **Not done (stays in U11d):** the refusals of the approved-call path (a call run after an owner approval is judged again without the policy; a grant lost between approval and run is refused but not counted), the state API's own `forbidden` answers to an agent, the per-agent "nothing else to do" half, the controller-down watchdog, answering each Needs-you item in place from the view, deferred meeting items from M03 in the view, the sandbox escape signal, and the remaining security hooks listed above. Denial counts stay in process memory.

### U11c (other refusal points) review (2026-11-12, Claude agent, clean context)

Reviewed 5e82a384 after merging origin/main (3ef91ff7).

- **Fixed (bug): a slow trickle of refusals paged as if they came inside one window.** `UrgentWatch.reportDenial` raised the item when the whole run's count (refusals each within the window of the one before) reached the threshold, so with threshold 3 and a 10-minute window refusals at 0, 9 and 18 minutes paged "refused 3 times within 10 minutes", which is false. A missing grant makes this likelier than before (an agent that keeps calling a tool the owner took away, now and then over a long run). The item is now raised only when the threshold of refusals falls inside one window; once raised the run's count goes on as before, and the text then says both ("3 times within 10 minutes, and N times in all since <time> with no 10-minute gap") instead of claiming all N came inside the window. New test in `notifications/urgent.test.ts`.
- **Fixed (test): "twice at once" never reached the write race.** `ToolPath.call` joins a second ask of the same call ID in the same process before anything is written, so moving the hook call before the refusal's write (a double count across two controller processes) passed every test. The suite case now also asks the same call through a second dispatcher on the same store at once (one denial), and it now exercises each refusal its title names as not a denial (pause, changed decision revision, route no longer allowed, used-up budget), checking each refusal's reason.
- **Checked, no change.** The same call asked again returns the stored refusal (not told); a stale-revision rejudge tells only after the write; the approved-call path does not tell (stays in U11d, as noted); counts are per agent ID, the item names only the agent and the count (no tool name, arguments or reason); the hourly page cap and inbox overflow are unchanged. A grant the owner took away (or one that expired or a restriction) counts as the agent's refusal under the slice's ASSUMPTION; that is defensible because it is opt-in and the item says "refused", not "misbehaved", but the owner who just took a grant away may get a page about it. Noted for U11d: the item could say which kind of refusal it was.
- **Mutations (each alone; all killed):** the grant refusal without `denied`; a pause refusal marked `denied`; the hook told before the refusal is written (killed only by the new two-dispatcher ask); the old whole-run threshold; one count for all agents; the "within the window" text kept for a long run.
## A09 fifth slice: the reviewer's summary, and a review that does not come (2026-11-12)

**Built.** (1) Every maintenance request the state API shows (`maintenance.get`, `maintenance.list`, so the owner's views too) now carries a derived `review` summary (`reviewSummary` in `maintenance/maintenance.ts`, never stored): the exact change (`package name@version`, mount, site and port, skill), source and digest, the access it asks for, install behaviour in plain words, the rollback plan and whether it can be undone. For a package that declares install scripts it says they run only after approval of exactly that digest, inside the sandbox with no network; for one that does not, it says the applier installs with every script off and refuses an artifact that declares one. Host policy and the shared base say "protected: the owner decides" and not reversible. Only the people who could already read a request (owner, requester, requester's supervisor) see it. (2) Tests: `maintenance/maintenance-review.test.ts` (both on all four backends: summary shown to the three readers and refused to others, derived and not stored; a review that does not come through ticks, enforcement and a restart leaves the request pending with the applier never asked; the requester, a peer, a wrong digest and a stale revision change nothing; the late owner decision applies once, a second decision is refused), and an end-to-end test in `api/start-maintenance-env.test.ts` (the approved environment stays the active revision and the agent is not held while the request waits; the agent cannot approve its own request; the owner's approval then runs trial, reload and validate once). Mutation-checked: dropping the digest binding in `decide`, dropping the pending-status check, and ignoring `installScripts` in the summary each fail tests. Dropping the "nobody decides their own request" line alone does NOT fail a test: the later supervisor test already refuses the requester (a requester is not their own supervisor), so that line is a second guard.

**Already in place from earlier slices (checked, not rebuilt).** Request through the bridge with an ID returned at once; owner-visible pending notice; nothing installs without an approval (owner, a preapproved catalogue entry, an allowed site, or a standing `approve.maintenance.<kind>` grant); apply through the real applier and the Linux local environment runtime (trial in a disposable environment, suspend without release, reload, activate, validate, restore, rollback); revoke reverts to the earlier revision; install scripts only in the sandbox after exact-digest approval; offline mirror only, so tests use no network.

**NOT done.** An administrator role for host policy and the base (owner only); a reviewer view that reads inside the artifact (the controller never sees the bytes, so the summary shows the requester's claim and the platform's rules, not the archive's scripts); mount, network, host-policy and base requests still stay pending after approval (no runtime for them); the dispatcher still does not pin the environment revision per attempt; remote hosts, macOS and Windows have no environment runtime.

ASSUMPTION: the summary is added to the existing read operations rather than a new operation, because it adds a field and removes none.

### A09 fifth slice review (clean-context, 2026-11-12)

Reviewed eec560a8 after merging origin/main 3ef91ff7. The whole approval path was traced (owner, catalogue, allowed site, standing grant, supervisor; digest binding, stale revision, double decision, the standing check again at claim time, task credentials, puppets, retired agents), not only the diff.

- **Fixed (security): a package source could carry invisible or direction-changing characters.** `checkSource` refused spaces and quotes but not a right-to-left override (U+202E), a zero-width space or a C1 control, so `https://registry.example.org/x<RLO>gpj.exe` was accepted and shown to the reviewer (in the new summary and in the owner's chat confirmation label) as another address than the one fetched. A source (request or catalogue entry) with any `isHidden` character is now refused.
- **Fixed (security): the summary showed text uncleaned.** The rollback plan (free text; `text()` refuses C0 controls only), the base and host-policy `change` and a source stored before the new rule went out as written, bidi characters included, and a secret-shaped value in a source query string was repeated. Every shown string now goes through `cleanUntrusted` (redact, strip hidden characters, redact again), is bounded, and a `warning` says when something was left out or marked.
- **Fixed (honesty): the summary said more than the platform does.** "Install scripts run once" was false: they run in the disposable trial and again when the agent's revision is built. "Access: none beyond the package files" hid that the installed code runs with the agent's own access. The rollback plan and `installScripts` were shown as facts: they are the requester's words, now labelled (`rollback: "the requester's plan, not checked by the platform: ..."`, `requesterClaims`). A new `checked` line says what is verified (the bytes match the digest and name themselves this package and version) and what is not (who made them). No summary uses the word "safe" (tested for every kind).
- **The "nobody decides their own request" line is a second guard, proven:** `#decider` refuses `by.id === agentId || by.id === requestedBy`, and `#isSupervisorOf` independently refuses `by.id === agentId`; a non-owner `requestedBy` is always the agent itself (`request` refuses another agent), and `agents.update` refuses an agent reporting to itself. Each line alone survives mutation by design; a new test plants a self-supervising record (no command can write one) and is killed when both are removed.
- **Tests added** (`maintenance-review.test.ts`, all four backends): hidden characters refused in sources and catalogue entries; the summary cleaned, warned, claims labelled, never "safe"; a planted self-supervisor and a supervisor's task credential cannot decide; a catalogue entry approves only its exact digest, source, version and script rule; a supervisor approval that waited is judged again at the claim and goes back to pending when the owner switches bosses off or withdraws the kind; two concurrent decisions on one storage (PostgreSQL included) count once, and an approval racing the requester's withdrawal never applies a withdrawn request.
- **Mutations (each alone):** hidden-character check off, summary shows raw text, summary warning never set, `#mayRead` without the supervisor, decide's update unfenced: killed. A supervisor task credential allowed, catalogue ignoring the digest, supervisor approval not re-checked at the claim: survived before, killed by the new tests. Self guards: see above.
- **Leftover (not changed):** the stored `spec.source` (shown raw in the body next to the summary, and in the chat label) is not redacted, since the applier must fetch it as given; `checkSource` could refuse a query string with a secret shape instead. A supervisor whose agent is paused (state `active`, pause gate set) may still decide; whether a paused agent keeps its authority is a policy choice not made here.

ASSUMPTION: a source with an invisible character is refused rather than cleaned, because the digest binds the spec as written and a cleaned address would be a different request than the one stored.

## A09 sixth slice: the environment an attempt sees is the one it was pinned to; no secrets in a source's query string; a held supervisor does not decide (2026-11-12)

Closes three leftovers of the fifth slice and its review: "the dispatcher still does not pin the environment revision per attempt", "the stored source is not redacted / `checkSource` could refuse a query string with a secret shape", and "a paused supervisor can still decide".

**Built (done)**

- **The pin travels with the attempt.** The dispatcher already asked the environment service to pin the agent's active revision when an attempt started (`revisions.environment`, and the launch limits come from that pinned manifest). What was missing is that nothing downstream used it: the host mounted whatever the agent's `active` link pointed to when the sandbox started, so an environment activated while an attempt was parked, or between the claim and the sandbox, changed what that attempt saw. Now (1) `WorkOrder.environmentRevision` (and `HostOrder.environmentRevision` on the worker host) carries the pinned revision; (2) the local environment host's `reach("environment", order)` mounts exactly that revision (`LocalEnvironmentRuntime.packagesOf(agent, revision)`), read-only, verified against its record, not the active one; a revision that is not on this host (while the agent has others) or whose files no longer match their record is refused, so the attempt does not start with a different environment; an order with no pin gets an empty grant (no environment); (3) a restart or resume of the same attempt asks the pin again and gets the same revision (the pin is stored per attempt); (4) an attempt that first started while its agent had NO environment records `revisions.noEnvironment` and keeps none on restart, even if an environment was made meanwhile. A later attempt gets whatever is active then. The remote protocol does not carry the pin (remote hosts have no environment runtime; it is stripped like the starting-size parts).
- **Secret-shaped query strings are refused at request time.** `checkSource` (so a request and an owner's catalogue entry) refuses a source whose query string or fragment has a parameter named like a secret with a value (token, secret, password, api/access/private key, `key`, `sig`, `sas`, auth/authorization, credential, signature, session, bearer, jwt, cookie; any letter case, percent-encoded or `+` forms, `&` `;` `#` separators, fragment `#a=b`) or any part shaped like a credential by the shared scanner (decoded up to twice). The message names the rule and never repeats the value. Ordinary query strings (`?download=1`, `?v=1.2.3`, `#readme`, `?author=bob`, `?token=` with no value) and secret-looking words in the PATH are accepted. Sources stored before this slice are not rewritten (they are still shown cleaned, as in the review fix); the applier fetches stored sources as written.
- **A supervisor held by a pause, suspend or stop gate does not decide.** `MaintenanceOptions.held(agentId)` (wired in `startController` to `PauseService.agentHolds`: the agent's own gate, its teams' and the installation's) is asked inside `#bossFor`, which both `decide` and the claim-time re-check use. Held means no decision as the boss: `decide` is refused (`forbidden`) and an approval that waited and whose supervisor was held meanwhile goes back to pending at the claim, the applier not asked. A lookup that throws counts as held (fail closed). Reading is unchanged (a held supervisor still reads its report's requests). The owner is never held.

**Tests.** `dispatch/dispatcher-suite.ts` (all four backends through the dispatcher suites): the order names the pin; an environment changed and another created while the attempts are parked do not reach them; the restart keeps revision 1, the no-environment attempt keeps none, later attempts get 2 and 1. `worker/src/environment/runtime.test.ts`: the mount for a pin stays the pinned revision after the active one moves; revision 2 is mounted for a pin to 2; a missing or tampered pinned revision is refused; no pin means no mount. `remote/host-environment.test.ts`: the pin is not offered to a remote host. `maintenance/maintenance-review.test.ts` (+2 per backend, all four): 21 secret-shaped sources refused for request and catalogue without repeating the value, 8 ordinary ones accepted; a held supervisor is refused to approve and to reject, a throwing gate lookup refuses, an approval that waited is judged again at the claim, the owner decides while the supervisor is held, a released supervisor decides. The existing summary-cleaning test now plants an old-style source with a secret directly in storage (the request is refused today). **Mutations (each alone, restored; each killed):** the order dropping the pin; a restart ignoring `noEnvironment`; `reach` using the active revision; `packagesOf` without verification; `packagesOf` not refusing a missing revision; the query check off; the parameter-name rule off; the value-shape rule off; the held check off; a failing lookup treated as not held; the remote strip removed.

**NOT done**

- Nothing stops a revision's files from changing on disk after the mount starts; the host verifies them against their record when the sandbox starts, not while it runs (as before). A revision of the same number is rebuilt only for the same manifest (the controller's revision numbers are never reused), so a pinned older revision stays as built; the store and old revisions are still never garbage-collected, which is what keeps a pinned older revision available.
- A claim and the pin are two steps in one start; a change activated in between is possible but harmless: the pin is read once and recorded, and everything after reads the record.
- A held supervisor's earlier approval is judged again only when the application starts (the same moment as the other standing checks); a request already applied is not undone.
- No administrator role, no reader inside the artifact, no macOS/Windows/remote environment runtime (unchanged from the fifth slice).

ASSUMPTION: an order with no pinned revision gets NO environment mount (previously it got whatever was active). The controller always records the pin when it has an environment service, so the only orders without a pin are for agents with no environment; mounting an environment a later change created would be exactly the mid-attempt change this slice stops.
ASSUMPTION: a paused, suspended or stopped supervisor (any gate in its chain, including the installation's) does not stand in for the owner. Fail closed was chosen over "pause only closes task ingress" because a held agent is not meant to act, and a request that waits for the owner costs one decision; the owner can decide at any time and the supervisor can again once released.
ASSUMPTION: a parameter NAME that looks secret refuses the source whatever the value looks like (`?key=abc`), because an address the platform fetches on an agent's word never needs one and a short key has no shape to find; the cost is that a harmless source with a parameter named `key` or `token` must be asked for in another form.

### A09 sixth slice review (Claude agent, clean context, 2026-11-12)

Reviewed 7654c0fa after merging origin/main b48923a4 (clean merge). Checked adversarially: the pin is stored per attempt ID and returned unchanged on every restart of that attempt; a readmitted or handed-off attempt is a new attempt and pins anew (by design); the in-process local worker passes the whole order into `sandbox.open`, so `reach` sees the pin; only the maintenance applier activates revisions and a rollback re-activates the existing number, so a pinned older revision stays as built; `verify` hashes every package's whole tree and refuses extra entries; `held` is passed `agt-...`, which is what `PauseService.agentHolds` takes; revoke as well as decide and the claim re-check go through `#bossFor`, so a held supervisor neither decides nor revokes. The query rule held against percent and double encoding, case, `;` and `#` separators, AWS, GCS, CloudFront and Azure SAS names, and does not refuse ordinary parameters, `#sha256=` links or random digests.

**Fixed**

- **A token in the PATH of a source was accepted** (`https://host/<github token>/simple/pkg.tgz`, the form some private registries use): it is stored, shown and sent exactly like a query-string secret. `checkSource` now also scans the address before the query string, decoded up to twice, with the shared scanner, read whole (a lone content-addressed segment such as a registry's 60-hex directory or an IPFS name looks random out of context, so the scan is not per segment; real registry paths are accepted). The refusal never repeats the value.
- **`?pass=` and `?pw=` were accepted**: both names now count as secret (anchored at the end of a name, so `passage` or `pwa` are not).
- **Tests that could not fail**: nothing proved that `startController` wires the real pause gates (the slice's tests inject a fake `held`); `api/start-maintenance.test.ts` now pauses a supervisor through the real `PauseService` and checks decide and revoke are refused, then allowed after the resume (killed by removing the wiring). Nothing proved the pinned path must lie inside the environments directory; `runtime.test.ts` now moves the pinned revision's packages out and links them back intact (killed by removing the check).

**Mutations of my own (each alone, restored, each killed):** the `held` wiring removed from `start.ts`; the path scan off; `pass|pw` removed; the dispatcher no longer recording `noEnvironment`; `packagesOf` without its inside-the-root check (killed only after the new test).

**Not changed (noted)**

- A pin that names a revision on a host that has NO environment for the agent at all gives an empty grant (the attempt runs without its packages) rather than a refusal. That fails toward less access, not more, and is what the slice's test states; a stricter host would refuse.
- The order carries the revision number only, not its manifest digest, so the host checks the revision against its own record, not against the controller's: a host whose environments directory survived a reset of the controller's state (revision numbers then start again) could mount an old revision 1. Carrying `pin.digest` and passing it to `verify` would close it if the digests are made comparable.
- An attempt that began before this slice without an environment carries no `noEnvironment` mark, so its restart pins whatever is active then.
- A parameter name with a look-alike letter (`tоken` with a Cyrillic o) is not caught; a server does not read it as `token` either.

## H12a (part 3): the owner's landing policy and the done check reach remote hosts (Claude agent, 2026-11-12)

Closes the three H12t leftovers (1: no done check on a remote host, 2: the owner's landing policy does not reach a remote host, 4: `HostOrder` does not declare `taskId`/`projectId`). Code: `remote/{protocol,service,host,responder}.ts`, `workspace-ops/workspace-ops.ts` (`CarriedLanding`, `WorkspaceCall.landing`), `api/dispatch-compose.ts`, worker `workspace/host.ts` and `host/local.ts`, `scripts/remote-host.mjs`. Tests: `remote/dispatch-carry.test.ts` (6 per backend, through the real transport), worker `host.test.ts` (+1), `scripts/remote-host.test.mjs` (+2).

- **The done check on a remote host (leftover 1).** Giving the remote host's `LocalWorker` a `verify` was not enough: the controller's dispatcher asks the *controller-side* `RemoteWorkerHost`, which had no `verify`, so a done on a remote host always read "the host cannot check work". Now `RemoteWorkerHost.verify` asks the host over the existing workspace-request channel (a new ask kind `verify`; same authentication, the same one-answer and withdrawn-when-slow rules, nothing changes on the host). The host's responder runs the host's `doneVerifier` (the checkout state of the port's own checkout, the contract's checks in the attempt's sandbox) and answers with the report. `scripts/remote-host.mjs` builds that verifier over its `LocalWorkspaces` and `localWorkerParts(...).checks`, hands it to its `LocalWorker` (`verify`) and to the responder, and refuses any attempt ID that is not a real attempt ID before looking at a sandbox. The ask is bounded before it leaves the controller (at most 20 checks, 100 evidence paths, command words and timeouts capped). The report is reshaped on the controller (`reportOf`): known fields only, one entry per check asked and none other, evidence only for paths asked, whole-number counts; anything else, a refusal, a throw or no answer reaches the dispatcher as "could not check", so the done does not count (fail closed). The responder cuts a check's output to fit the answer limit (4000 bytes), then drops it. The verify ask is not held back by the busy check (the asking attempt is itself at its end), and it only runs checks in that attempt's own sandbox.
- **The owner's landing policy on a remote host (leftover 2).** `RemoteWorkerHost` has a `landingPolicy` reader (the composed controller gives it the same reader a local host uses: the project's landing branch, else `workspace.landing.branch`, with the permit and protected paths), read fresh at each landing. A landing request carries the four owner-set figures (`landing` on the ask: branch, `requirePermit`, `protectedPaths`, `protectDefaults`). Fail closed on the controller: no reader, a throw, or no branch means nothing is sent. The figures are the reader's, never the caller's (a `landing` a caller put in the call is replaced); any other operation carries none (and a hostile ask carrying one is refused); unknown fields, a path-like branch, wrong types, over 100 paths or 300 characters are refused (`invalid_command`). The ask rides the authenticated host session and is listed only to the host asked; it has no signature of its own (as for the dispatch contract, integrity on a network that is not trusted is the transport's: use https).
- **What the host does with it (`remoteLandingPolicy`, `scripts/remote-host.mjs`).** The host's configuration `landing` map stays a per-project pin: the one branch this machine's operator allows landing on. The owner's policy can only hold that pin and tighten: no policy carried (an older controller), no branch, or a branch that is not the pin means the landing is refused in plain words (a new `refuse` text of the worker host's `landing` option, which stops the landing before anything is read or written); a project not pinned is never landed; the permit is required and the built-in protected list always applies whatever is carried (the owner's "off" does not follow to another machine); the owner's extra protected paths are added. The worker host's `landing` option now receives the carried figures as `carried` (a local host's request carries none and its builder ignores the field).
- **`HostOrder` (leftover 4)** declares `taskId` and `projectId` (required, as the controller's `WorkOrder` always carries them); four test orders were given them.
- **Mutations (each alone; all killed):** the controller keeping a caller's own `landing` instead of the reader's; sending a landing when the policy has no branch; allowing a policy on a non-landing ask; accepting unknown landing figures; the report check taking a check that was not asked or named twice; taking evidence that was not asked; the responder not handling a `verify` ask; the worker host ignoring `refuse`; the remote host following a carried `requirePermit`; ignoring a branch that is not the pin; accepting no carried policy; no `verify` given to the responder; no `verify` given to the worker; a check run for a bad attempt ID.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the owner's landing branch must equal the host's pinned branch (the pin stays the host operator's hard limit); a moved owner branch refuses landings on that host until the operator moves the pin. This is the smallest fail-closed choice and loosens nothing. A looser rule (the owner's branch wins when the project is pinned at all) is a one-line change in `remoteLandingPolicy`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the owner's "permit off" and "built-in protected list off" are not honoured on a remote host (they stay on). The owner can still turn them off for the controller's own host; a remote machine is not the owner's by default.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a verify report is the worker's word, like its work: the controller cannot run the checks on another machine. A worker that lies about a check is not caught here (the same trust statement as the dispatch contract's enforcement).
- **Not done.** (1) The per-project pin is still the host's own configuration; the controller does not push the branch. (2) Nothing retries a verify or a landing a slow host dropped (the dispatcher records "could not check" and the agent calls `work.end` again; a landing times out as before). (3) A real end-to-end run (controller, remote host process, bubblewrap) was not added; the pieces are proven through the real transport with stand-in ports and the script's stand-in packages. (4) Leftovers 3, 5 and 6 of H12t (project layer, commit/submit in the product composition, macOS and Windows) are unchanged.

### H12a (part 3) clean-context review (Claude agent, 2026-11-12)

Reviewed a202c828 after merging origin/main 3ef91ff7 (task-plan.md only). Checked: a hostile host cannot answer another host's request (answers are bound to the asked host), cannot replay an old verify answer onto a new check (every check is a fresh random request ID), and cannot turn a report that says less than it was asked into a pass (the dispatcher counts a missing check or evidence entry as "could not check", `unknown`, and the done is not taken). `reportOf` reads named fields only (a `__proto__` key in JSON is an own property, never read); protected paths are matched as plain strings (no pattern a host could make slow). The dispatcher's wait is its own timer, not the tick.

- **Fixed: a large but honest report could never come back, so a remote done could never be checked.** The responder cut only the checks' output (600, 150, 0 characters), and the answer is limited to 4000 bytes: ten checks that could not run (reasons kept to 200 characters each) and twenty uncommitted files with long names already exceed it, giving "did not fit" on every call. A last stage now sends only what the verdict is decided by (each check's state and exit, the tree's counts with no file names, each evidence path and whether it is there). A report that still cannot fit (a hundred 500-character evidence paths) is refused as before.
- **Fixed: an owner's valid landing policy could be recorded as a failure that may have changed the checkout.** The carried-policy check allowed 100 protected paths and 100-character branches, but the owner's settings allow 200 of each. A policy past the check made `askWorkspace` throw before anything was sent, and the workspace service records a throw as `failed` (the host "may have done part of it"). The limits now match the settings on both sides (controller check and `remoteLandingPolicy`), and a landing the request check refuses is a clean refusal ("could not be carried ... not sent (nothing was changed)").
- **Fixed (regression of a202c828, found by the full run): the W05 end-to-end test `api/start-work-end.test.ts` hung for its whole 600 s and timed out.** It composes the controller with a remote host (`host:pc`) whose test client never answers workspace requests, and expected "the host cannot check work" at once. With this card the remote host has a `verify`, so `work.end` asked `host:pc` and waited the checks' time (600 s default plus 60 s). The product behaviour is intended (a connected remote host is asked); the test now runs a real `WorkspaceResponder` started without a check of a done, which answers at once "this host cannot check work", and the done is still never taken (the same three-refusal path to `done_unverified`). File alone: 9 of 9 in 13 s. Note for the owner: a connected host that does not answer at all keeps the agent's `work.end` waiting for the checks' time (at most an hour), then "could not check".
- **Tests:** `remote/dispatch-carry.test.ts` (+3, all backends): the large honest report; replay and cross-host answering (an old pass sent again is only a repeat of the old request, another host's answer is `not_found`, and the new check waits for its own answer and comes back failed); a 200-path policy with a 158-character branch is carried, and policies beyond that are clean refusals with nothing listed. `dispatch/done-verify.test.ts` (+1, all backends): a report that leaves out an asked check, or an asked evidence path, is `unknown`, not passed.
- **Own mutations (each alone, restored after):** compaction stage removed; any host may answer a request; verify reuses one fixed request ID (replay); the host obeys a carried `requirePermit: false`; the dispatcher takes a check missing from the report as passed (it survived the existing tests, so the done-verify test was added); a pre-send refusal thrown again. 6 of 6 killed.
- **Left as is (noted):** (1) the responder runs requests one at a time, so a long done check (the contract allows up to ten checks of an hour each) holds back later landings and quarantines on that host; the controller stops waiting after an hour (`waitMs` cap), so a contract whose checks add up to more than an hour can never be verified on a remote host (fails closed, `unknown`). (2) A host's `checkout: false` skips the tree rules; a lying host can claim anything anyway (the trust statement above).
## Credential redaction coverage follow-up: every place on the shared scanner (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-12)

Not a numbered card. It finishes the list that the clean-context review of the credential-redaction follow-up left open ("Older copies that are not the shared scanner remain").

**Done**

- **Package boundaries.** The config package may import nothing, and the worker and pi-adapter may import only contracts (`scripts/package-boundaries.mjs`; the controller imports neither). So the scanner (`credential-patterns`, `secret-scan`, `redact`, `clean` in `controller/src/security`) is copied, byte for byte, as ONE generated file into `contracts/src/credential-scan.ts` (the worker and pi-adapter import it from `@nimblenewt/contracts`) and `config/src/credential-scan.ts`. `node scripts/copy-credential-scan.mjs` writes the copies; `scripts/copy-credential-scan.test.mjs` fails when one is stale. A second, behavioural test (`integration/src/credential-scan-drift.test.ts`) runs one shared corpus (keys of every family, fullwidth, hidden characters, split over lines and quotes, hex in and out of key context, private key blocks, normal prose) through the controller's scanner, the contracts copy and the config copy and demands the same answers. Edit the controller files, run the script, rebuild.
- **Config `findInlineSecrets`** uses the scanner (`findCredentialShapes`) for values and for names: any letter case, fullwidth letters, invisible characters, split keys, `Authorization: Basic`, named assignments, service tokens, long random runs. The message says which kind (`looks like a GitHub token`); the URL wording is unchanged.
- **Release `service-units`** takes its "looks like a key" test from `findCredentialShapes`. The word test (`token`, `passw`... in an argument that does not name a file) stays: it is about names, not values.
- **Worker host.** A child's fault message, the stderr tail shown when it ends, an error that quotes a command line, a check's output and its failure reasons go through `safeText`/`safeTail` (contracts, built on `cleanUntrusted`). They are cleaned BEFORE they are cut to a length, so a cut never leaves half a key that the scanner would not know.
- **Pi adapter.** The compaction and continuation hook errors, every `fault` message, the failed-turn error and the model's `detail`, a checkpoint read-back failure, a relayed `fetch failed` message and anything the process writes with `console.log` (redirected to stderr) are redacted.
- **`onInternalError`.** `startController` hands the embedder's sink every error through `redactedSink`/`redactError`: message, stack and cause are cleaned. A clean error is passed on as the same object; a dirty one becomes a copy with the same name and `code`.
- **Orphan key END, one place.** The thinking store and the job output no longer carry their own `-----BEGIN/END` regexes. `redactText(text, { continues: true })` (also `cleanUntrusted(..., { continues: true })`) takes everything up to an END that no BEGIN of that text belongs to, as one mark, through the folded view; `privateKeyOpen` and `afterPrivateKeyEnd` tell a stream whether a block is open and where it ends. A BEGIN or END hidden by a zero-width or soft-hyphen character, or written fullwidth, now opens/closes a block in a job's output too (before, the open block was missed and the next report leaked).
- **One cleaning pipeline.** The tool bridge, job runs, the MCP job call and the scratch cleanup use `cleanUntrusted` instead of their own control-character regexes after `redactText`. Differences you may notice: a lone carriage return is a line break; a control character in a scratch path text is one space (double spaces in a path stay); a lone surrogate in an MCP job error is repaired first as before.
- **Scanner gaps closed.**
  - Keys split over string literals (`"ghp_" + "..."`, `'sk-' '...'`, `"a"."b"`, `&`, a line break between) are found: a third matching view removes only a quote join between two token characters. A comma or other character keeps two strings apart; ordinary quoted words, lists and `"sk-" + name` stay.
  - A hex run of 32, 40, 64 or 128 digits, which the entropy rule leaves alone because digests and IDs look the same, IS redacted when the words right before it on its line end in a key word: `the api key is`, `secret key:`, `"key": "`, `authorization:`, `password =`, `encryption key is`. `sha256:`, `commit`, `hash`, `digest`, `key id` and a bare run stay.
  - An unsigned JSON web token (`eyJ....eyJ....` with no signature) is a token too (the old service-unit test had it).
- **Tests.** `security/secret-coverage.test.ts` (joins, false positives, linear time, hex context, stream helpers, `continues`, `redactError`, `redactedSink`), `config/inline-secrets.test.ts`, `contracts/safe-text.test.ts`, worker `process.test.ts` (fault and stderr tail), pi-adapter `process.test.ts` (a fault that quotes a key), jobs (hidden BEGIN/END across reports), service units (spellings), the drift tests above. Mutation check: switching off the quote view and the hex-context rule each broke the new tests; restored.
- Every secret-shaped literal in the new tests is built at run time by concatenation or from a seeded generator.

**Not done**

- `scripts/remote-host.mjs` and `scripts/remote-worker.mjs` still strip only `Bearer ...` from their own error text, and the other launcher scripts print raw `error.message`. They are scripts, not the packages named by the follow-up; they can import the built contracts later.
- The worker's `console` output inside the sandbox and the child's stdout other than channel lines are not redacted at the source; the host redacts the stderr it reports.
- The end-to-end wiring of `redactedSink` in `startController` has no test that triggers a real internal fault with a key in it (the faults are hard to provoke by hand); the sink and `redactError` are tested directly.
- Still blanked, unchanged: the `xxd -p` style hex lines, data URIs, SHA-384/224 hex. A key whose pieces are joined by something other than a quote join (a variable, a function call) is not found.

**ASSUMPTION:** the generated-copy design (one script, a staleness test and a behaviour test) was chosen instead of editing the package-boundary rules, because the rules are a gate and nothing here is authorised to change them.
**ASSUMPTION:** a key-context hex run is redacted even though it could be a digest called "key" (`key: <sha256>`): losing a display of a cache key is cheaper than printing a real key.
**ASSUMPTION:** the config message names the kind in the scanner's words (`a high-entropy key`, `an API key (sk-)`) rather than keeping the five old phrases.

### Credential redaction coverage follow-up: clean-context review (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-12)

Reviewed commit 7322b43d after merging origin/main (only `task-plan.md` changed there; no scanner conflict). Probed with invented keys only.

**Fixed**

- **Quadratic time in the new hex-context rule.** `keyContextHex` found the start of a run's line with `text.lastIndexOf("\n", at - 1)`, which walks back to the start of the text for every run of a line with no break. One-line JSON or a log line full of 64-digit digests took 2.6 s for 1 MB with no key word at all, and `key:<hex>,` repeated took 7 s. It now looks only inside the 80 characters before the run. 1 MB of either: about 30 ms. The other adversarial inputs (quotes and plus signs, quote joins with long white space, `key` words before hex, thousands of BEGIN or END lines, a BEGIN or END with a long `[A-Z ]` run, a zero-width BEGIN repeated, a base64 dump) were all linear and under 0.6 s for 1 MB.
- **The worker host cleaned whole outputs to keep a short tail.** `safeTail` (a check's output, up to the contract's 64 MiB) and the stderr tails of `WorkerProcess` (`safeText(stderr, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)`) ran the scanner over everything before cutting: 4 MB of ordinary test output took 7 s and 860 MB of memory, 16 MB took 30 s and 1.9 GB, so a large check output could stall the host past its lease or run it out of memory. `safeText`/`safeTail` now clean a bounded window: what can be kept plus 16 KB (`SAFE_MARGIN`), cut at white space so a one-line key is not split, and a tail window that starts inside the output is cleaned with `continues` (an END whose BEGIN was cut off takes everything up to it). The stderr tails use `safeTail(stderr, 8 KB)`. 16 MB now takes a few milliseconds.
- **`redactError` could throw, hang, or hand the sink raw secrets.** (1) A thrown Proxy whose `getPrototypeOf` trap throws escaped (`instanceof` was outside the `try`), so the wrapped sink threw. (2) A thrown plain object with cycles went through `redact()`, which has a depth limit but no visited set: four self-references never finished (4^32 steps) and a 20-level diamond of shared references took 8.5 s. (3) A cause chain deeper than four, or a cause that is the error itself, left the ORIGINAL fifth cause inside the cleaned copy. (4) Only message, stack and cause were read: an error with a clean message but a key in its own fields (a child process's `stdout`, a request's `config.headers.Authorization`) or in an `AggregateError`'s `errors` was passed on as the same raw object, and Node's `util.inspect` prints all of those. `redactError` is now one bounded walk (500 objects, depth 8, a value met again on its own path or past the bounds becomes the mark) over message, stack, name, cause, own fields (sensitive names replaced whole) and `errors`; a clean error, own fields and all, is still returned as the same object; a dirty one becomes a plain `Error` copy with the cleaned own fields (so `code` and the rest are kept). It never throws.
- **False positives of the hex-context rule.** It blanked a 32/40/64/128-digit hex run after `public key:`, `primary key:`, `cache key:`, `idempotency key:`, `ssh host key`, and after any name that only begins with a key word: `tokenizer:`, `"secretaryId"`, `API_KEY_HASH =`, `authorization_code_hash`, `secret_key_id`, `password_fingerprint`. Those name IDs, digests and public values that code review and logs show. The rule now ignores a key word whose name ends in `id`, `hash`, `digest`, `sum`, `fingerprint`, `count`, `izer`, `ary`, `length`, `size`, `type` or `name`, and a bare `key` right after `public`, `primary`, `foreign`, `cache`, `host`, `ssh`, `gpg`, `pgp`, `sort`, `partition` or `idempotency`. `key: <hex>`, `"key": "<hex>"`, `api key`, `auth key`, `access key`, `signing key`, `secret`, `password =`, `client_secret:`, `SECRET_KEY=` are still redacted.
- **The end-to-end sink wiring had no test.** `api/start-internal-error-redacted.test.ts` starts a real controller, makes a service throw an error that quotes a bearer key and carries it in a field, calls the state API, and checks the embedder's sink got it cleaned (message, stack, field; `code` kept) and the caller only `unavailable`. Without the `redactedSink` wrap in `startController` it fails.
- Tests: `security/secret-coverage.test.ts` (+3: linear on one long line, the hex-context exemptions and what stays redacted, `redactError` against proxies, cycles, a diamond, long and self cause chains, child-process fields, request headers, AggregateError, clean errors kept as the same object), `contracts/safe-text.test.ts` (+1: 16 MB tailed fast, a key at every offset around both window edges, a key block whose BEGIN is before the tail window), the start test above. Each new test fails on the reviewed code (checked by putting the old file back).
- Mutations of the reviewed code, each alone (all caught by its own tests): `privateKeyOpen` without the folded view; the orphan-END rule ignoring which BEGIN an END belongs to; the job output's END search back to the literal regex; the thinking store without `continues`; the Pi adapter's `fault` message raw; release service units without the scanner.

**Checked and sound**

- The open private-key state of a job's output lives on that job's own output record (`keyOpen`), is bounded by `JOB_LIMITS.keyBlock` and is cleared at the END line; the thinking store keeps no state between blocks (each block is cleaned with `continues`). One job's or agent's key block cannot change how another's text is redacted.
- The generated copies: the script writes two fixed paths from four fixed sources (no input path, deterministic), and the staleness test compares the whole file byte for byte, so a one-character difference fails. The worker, pi-adapter and config import no controller code (`npm run check:deps`).
- Quote joins: ordinary code (`"foo" + "bar"`, `"ghp_" + name`, `'sk-' + 'proj-' + suffix`, `"task-" + id`, SQL string concatenation, lists) stays; uuids, git SHAs and `Merge:` lines, lockfile checksums, `sha256:`/`oid sha256:`, SRI digests, `monkey`/`turkey`/`keyboard`/`hotkey` before hex all stay.

**Not done (noted)**

- A key quote-joined with a following word (`"ghp_…" "next"`) takes that word into the mark (the line-joined view has a `runsOnIntoWord` exception, the quote view has none). Text is lost, nothing leaks.
- `safeText`'s head window may, in theory, cut a key that is split over a line break or quotes at the window's end; only when cleaning shrinks the kept part by more than 16 KB could a piece of it reach the kept text.
- ASSUMPTION: a hex run after `public key`, `primary key`, `cache key` (and the names listed above) is a value meant to be shown, not a secret; the smallest change that keeps code review and logs readable. Reversible: remove words from `NOT_SECRET_KEY`/`NOT_SECRET_SUFFIX` in `secret-scan.ts` and re-run the copy script.

## H12u: a project layer in the configuration, so the landing permit and protected paths can be set per project (Claude agent, 2026-11-12)

Closes the H12t leftover "the configuration has no project layer". Before this, only the landing branch was per project (the owner's `project.branches.set` record); the commit permit and the protected paths were one policy for the whole installation, with narrower team, agent and task layers that could only add to it.

- **What is built.**
  - A fifth configuration layer, `project`, between the installation and the team (`LAYER_ORDER`: installation, project, team, agent, task). Its ID is `project.<project ID>`. Only the owner may stage, change or apply it (any other holder of `config.write` gets `forbidden`, locks included); it is revision-checked like every layer (`expectedRevision`, `stale_revision`); a project that does not exist or a malformed ID is refused.
  - A task reads the layer of its own project (`taskValue`, `taskValues`, `effective`); another project's layer never reaches it. `effective(owner, { projectId })` and the new `projectValues(keys, projectId)` give the installation plus one project. `taskValues(keys, taskId, projectId?)` throws when the task is not in that project (fail closed: a landing order that names the wrong project is refused, not read under the wrong layer).
