## U14e (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-13): from an empty folder to a finished first task with only the launcher and the chat

What was lacking. An independent audit named one unmet clause of U14: "on a clean machine the launcher starts the controller and the owner reaches a first working agent and first task using only the launcher and the chat, with no code written." The only test where an agent really ran (`u14b-local-host.test.ts`) made the project, agent, rights, task, ready move, assignment and the attempt by direct service calls and ticked the dispatcher by hand; the two chat walk-throughs ended with the host still open and nothing ran. Building the missing walk found three real gaps in the product, all fixed.

- **The walk (`packages/integration/src/u14e-chat-only-first-task.test.ts`).** It starts the real launcher on a state folder that does not exist yet, with the real local worker host (bubblewrap sandbox, the real Pi worker process) and a scripted fake model route behind an injected fetch (no network, no real model). From then on it does nothing but type free-form chat messages that the fixture interpreter reads (the same fixture as the other chat tests; every value the interpreter returns must appear in the owner's words, as in the product, so the messages carry the addresses, names and the folder). Each proposal the strict approval profile shows is confirmed by a second chat message. Steps, all by chat: two model servers (address, models, the NAMES of the secrets); the project; binding the repository; turning on this computer as the host; an agent called Ann; seven rights one by one (`attempt.work`, `effect.perform`, `review.request`, `task.read`, `desk.write`, `desk.read`, `message.receive`); a task; the launcher is started again (the host counts from the next start, as the notes of U14b say); the task is made ready and given to Ann. Then the test only waits: the controller admits the attempt, the dispatcher starts it on the local host, the agent reaches the model at the address from the edited record with the key from the secret store (never seen by the agent, in no file), calls `work.end`, and the attempt finishes. Skipped without bubblewrap and a usable Node install (fails instead with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` on Linux), like `u14b-local-host`.
- **Gap 1, fixed: nothing started an attempt for a task given to an agent.** In the running controller the assignment's event was never delivered to the inbox (the reconciler had no delivery destination), so a chat or API assignment stayed "assigned" for ever unless a program admitted the attempt itself, which is what every test did. New start option `admitAssigned` (`api/start.ts`): the reconciler's pass now delivers `assignment-events` to the inbox, and the inbox admits one attempt naming the installation's one shipped harness. The launcher sets it whenever it builds the local host. Off by default, so a controller driven by hand (tests, embedders that admit attempts themselves) behaves as before; it needs exactly one shipped harness (none or two admit nothing, because the inbox must name one). Once admitted the existing dispatcher places and starts the attempt. A repeat of the same assignment or several passes never make a second attempt (the inbox's rule). Tests: `api/start-admit-assigned.test.ts` on SQLite and on PostgreSQL (the two storage kinds the controller can start on); the delivery, inbox and admission records themselves are the domain's and are tested on all four backends by their own suites, untouched here.
- **Gap 2, fixed: the owner had to know an agent's ID to give it a task.** `task.assign` and `task.transfer` take only `owner: { kind, id }`. They now also take `agentName` (the owner's own words, which must appear in the message like every other value): the chat looks it up among the active agents (exact name, case ignored), refuses an unknown name, asks when two agents share it, refuses an ID and a name given together, and shows and confirms the agent's name. The interpreter prompt describes this and the whole first-run sequence (ready, give, the agent, one right at a time) so free-form words reach it; the operation list in the prompt is generated from the accepted arguments, so `agentName` is listed there too (test in `model-interpreter.test.ts`).
- **Gap 3, fixed: a one-project owner was asked "which project?" for a task title.** With nothing in focus a task named by title, or any project-scoped control, asked "Which project do you mean? There is none in focus." even when exactly one project exists. With exactly one project that project is used; with two or more the question stays. Tests in `chat/u14e-names.test.ts` on all four backends (reference store, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL), together with the two agent-name fixes above.
- **Found by the walk, not a product change:** a repository named in `project.create` is only a name until it is bound as a resource; a task that names an unbound repository is blocked ("repository garden is not bound to the project; bind it first"). The walk therefore includes the chat command `resource.bind` (already reachable and described in the prompt). A later card could bind the repositories named in `project.create` at once; not done here.
- **Own mutations (each alone, restored; each killed):** the one-project fallback disabled (12 of 12 name tests fail); the name resolved to the typed words instead of the agent's ID (4 fail); the "ID and name together" refusal removed (4 fail); the "two agents, one name" question removed (4 fail); `admitAssigned` ignored so the inbox always runs (2 of 3 admission tests fail); the inbox given no harness (2 of 3 fail); the launcher not setting `admitAssigned` (the whole walk fails); the prompt's first-run sentence changed (prompt test fails).
- **NOT done / cannot be met offline.** A real clean machine (a fresh operating system, the real secret store, the real command line `scripts/nimblenewt.mjs` typed by a person) and a real model server answering the interpreter and the agent: the walk uses an in-process launcher call, an in-memory secret store and a scripted model. The walk's chat messages are the ones the fixture interpreter is told to read; whether a real model reads every free-form wording into these commands is checked only by the prompt tests, not by a model. The terminal chat (`runTerminalChat`) is used by the earlier tests; this walk submits through the same chat service the terminal and web door use. The worker host exists on Linux only (macOS and Windows have none, as U14d already says); on them the walk is skipped.
- **ASSUMPTION:** `admitAssigned` is opt-in and set by the launcher (not on for every controller), because many tests and embedders admit attempts themselves and two admitters on one assignment would race; reversible by making it the default in `start.ts`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the inbox admits for the one shipped harness (`pi`); a second shipped harness needs a rule for choosing which, which is a later decision, so with two harnesses nothing is admitted automatically.
- **ASSUMPTION:** an agent is found by its exact name (case ignored), not loosely, because a wrong agent receiving work is worse than one more question; the existing hand-off command does the same.
- **ASSUMPTION:** with exactly one project, that project is meant. Reversible by removing the fallback in `chat.ts` (`#resolve`, "exactly one project").

### U14e review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13)

Merged origin/main fd182537 first (clean). Checked in plain terms:

- **Automatic admission (`admitAssigned`).** It adds no gate of its own and needs none: the reconciler's pass delivers the assignment events to the inbox, and the inbox and `admitAttempt` decide from the CURRENT assignment (same generation, same owner, state assigned, task ready or in progress, no active attempt; the attempt's ID derives from the message, so a repeat, a restart or a second controller finds the same attempt). The reconciler leaves a message alone while the task is under any pause of its chain (the task, its project, its agent and team, the installation; a Stop holds the same gate) or a manual hold, and the dispatcher applies its own checks (pause, grants, harness, route, budget, host) before anything starts. A retired agent is never given work (`assignTask` refuses it). Two controllers on PostgreSQL: only the one holding the epoch passes; the other's pass is fenced. It is a start option only: no API operation, agent or task credential can switch it. Off, the reconciler is built exactly as before (no destination, the inbox with no harness). Only the launcher's local-host start sets it, and that is the only shipped start with a dispatcher (`nimblenewt-controller.mjs` starts none). With none or two harnesses nothing is delivered.
- **Found: the slice's tests did not cover pause, readiness, transfer, release or restart for this path** (removing the reconciler's pause check left all 3 admission tests passing). Added `held()` in `api/start-admit-assigned.test.ts` on SQLite and PostgreSQL: a task given before it is ready waits and starts once ready; a paused agent gets nothing until the pause is lifted, then exactly one; a task moved to another agent before the pass gets one attempt, the new owner's; a released task gets nothing; a restart on the same database admits nothing again.
- **Known behaviour, not changed:** assignment events written while the option was off (before the host was turned on) are delivered at the first start with it on, so a task given earlier starts then. That is what the first-run order needs; a hand-driven database later started by the launcher would get its still-current, unattempted assignments started too.
- **Agent names.** The chat is owner-only (`#owner(token)`), so no agent or task credential reaches the lookup, and the "two agents, one name" question shows only IDs from the owner's own `agent.list`. Matching is exact after trimming, case ignored (`toLowerCase`), active agents only; no Unicode normalization or look-alike folding, so a name in other letters (a Cyrillic "А") or another normal form is refused as unknown, never matched to someone else. Agents are not project-scoped. Errors quote the owner's words through `quotedText` (bounded). **Found: case folding, the retired namesake and "which of two agents" were untested** (dropping case folding or counting retired agents left the 12 tests passing). Added a test on all four backends: lower case and upper case names, a retired "Bob" ignored beside the active one, a Cyrillic look-alike refused, and a `task.transfer` by name with nothing moved before the yes.
- **Found and fixed: a right could not be given by name.** `grant.create` needed `grantee` as the principal `agent:agt-…`, which must appear in the owner's words, while the agents status shows only `agt-…`; a first-run owner with a real model would have to type a form the chat never shows (the walk read the principal through a direct API call). `grant.create` now takes `agentName` the same way (exactly one active agent, case ignored; unknown refused; two asked about; a name with a `grantee` refused); the principal is put in after the owner's-words check, and the proposal is still shown first in every profile. The prompt's first-run sentence says so; `agentName` is in the generated operation list. Test on all four backends (rights to two agents by name, so a lookup that takes the wrong one fails whichever comes first).
- **One project.** `project.list` is the caller's own list (owner only here), so a project the caller cannot read is never chosen; archived projects are listed and counted, so one active plus one archived still asks.
- **The walk.** It now asserts that every step's first message is a proposal (nothing changed before the second, "yes" message) except the move to ready, which the strict profile applies at once; the rights name Ann by name (no API read of her ID); it checks that the seven rights are Ann's. "Key in no file" is proven by reading every file under the test folder (state folder, database, repository) after shutdown for the raw key bytes; added: the launch notes and anything printed, and every message the interpreter saw, hold neither key. The yes messages carry the proposal ID because the fixture interpreter reads only the owner's words.
- **Own mutations (each alone on the built files, restored; each killed):** name match without case folding (4 of 20 fail); retired agents counted (4 fail); the reconciler's pause check removed (2 of 5 admission tests fail); the one-project fallback taking one of several (4 fail); the grant name resolved to another agent, first or last of the list (4 fail each); admission on by default (2 fail); the harness count not checked (1 fails); the assignment name resolved to another agent (4 fail); the launcher not setting `admitAssigned` (the walk fails).
- **Windows/macOS:** the walk skips without bubblewrap (fails only with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` on Linux); its folder name has spaces; its only waits are bounded polls. The admission test uses a manual timer and `path.join`. The walk passed 3 of 3 times alone (about 15 s each).
- **Clause, offline:** with this slice the clause is met as far as it can be offline: from a state folder that does not exist, only launcher starts and free-form chat messages (names, never IDs) lead to a finished attempt on the local host. What cannot be met offline: a real clean machine (fresh OS, the real secret store, `scripts/nimblenewt.mjs` typed by a person) and a real model reading the owner's free-form words into these commands and answering the agent.

## U13 finish (2026-11-13): event subscriptions, stale artifacts, tool activity, message references, checkpoints, command states

What was lacking after the earlier slices: no API operation for event subscriptions (so no cursors a client could keep), no stale-artifact definition, no chat reach for the attention list, no per-task reads of tool activity, message references or checkpoints, and no shared words for long-running command states.

- **Event subscriptions (`events.subscribe`, `.pull`, `.acknowledge`, `.heartbeat`, `.status`, `.resume`, `.trace`).** Thin doors on `EventService`, whose subscription and cursor are stored in the controller's own storage; a test subscribes, pulls, acknowledges, restarts the controller and goes on from the stored cursor (an old acknowledgement never moves it back). The API's `EventService` is now given a hold check: a task stream whose task is paused answers `wake: false, held: true` (the events wait). A task credential may use only its own `task:<id>` stream.
- **Stale artifacts (`stale_artifact` in `status.attention`).** ASSUMPTION: an artifact is stale when (1) a newer artifact with the same name exists on the same task (`superseded`; `at` is when the newer one was recorded), or (2) it is the newest of its name on a task that is still open (not done or cancelled) and was recorded more than 7 days ago (`aged`; constant `STALE_ARTIFACT_DAYS`). No file is read. Artifacts with no task are never listed. Needs the artifact right on the project. The agent filter matches the recorder. Artifacts have no per-task index, so one call reads artifact records up to the scan budget; if there are more, the result says `artifactsPartial` (narrowing by project or task does not shrink the read in this build; it only limits which tasks are shown).
- **Chat reach.** New `status.ask` kind `attention` (keys projectId, agentId, state, attentionKind, since, until, limit), listed in `STATUS_KINDS` (so the interpreter prompt describes it for free-form questions) and named in the `status.ask` summary; the owner may leave the project out.
- **Reads with revision and provenance.** `activity.tools` (a task's tool calls: state in_progress/confirmed/failed/uncertain, caller, server, capability, revisions; filters agent, state, time; paged by call ID; no inputs or outputs), `message.references` (a task's messages without their words; owner sees all, others those they sent or received), `continuation.list` (a task's checkpoints, complete and incomplete, with who captured them and the checkpoint identity, not what the run was doing). Task credentials read their own task only.
- **Command states.** New `api/command-state.ts`: accepted, queued, running, completed, blocked, failed, outcome_unknown. The command envelope now carries `state` (`accepted` when `awaits` is set, else `completed`); job items and suspension/stop items carry `commandState`. ASSUMPTIONS: a job's `dispatched` is `queued`, `cancellation_requested` is `running`, `cancelled` is `failed`; a stop that is `done` with unresolved items is `outcome_unknown`, `blocked` and `recovery-required` are `blocked`.
- **Tests.** `status.test.ts` two new suites on all four backends; `api/start-u13-finish.test.ts` (4 tests); assertions added to `start-lifecycle` and `start-jobs`. Mutation checks (each made a test fail, then restored): drop the hold wiring, drop the open-task condition of `aged`, treat error calls as confirmed, drop the envelope `state`, drop the task-credential stream guard.
- **NOT done / cannot be met offline.** Commands that are deferred to a worker (for example `task.assign`) report `accepted` at the envelope but there is no generic "what became of command X" read that follows them through queued, running and failed; only jobs and stops carry the full vocabulary. Message/continuation/artifact lists scan records (no per-task index) and are bounded. A project-level hold of an event stream is not consulted (only task pauses). The other overview kinds (blocked tasks, open waits, failed events) are still only in `status.ask` views, not in the attention list. Sealed attention cursors still do not survive a restart (by design, earlier fix); event subscription cursors do. No live end-to-end check against a real model or host was made (none allowed).

### U13 finish: review (2026-11-13, clean-context Claude review of a2e83ec6)

Merged origin/main 8f62a2f1 (F04m final slice) first; the notes conflict kept both sides.

**Bugs found and fixed.**
- **A task's own event stream was out of reach (authorization).** `EventService` judged a `task:` stream with no project (the lookup its comment promised was never written), so `allows` matched only a grant over every project: a task credential could not subscribe to or trace its own task's stream, and neither could an agent with the right in the task's project. The API test passed because it ran the operation against a fake event service. The task's project is now read from the task record: `history.read` in it, or `attempt.work` on that task (the same as the task's tool history). A task with no record keeps the old rule.
- **A task credential could use its agent's other subscriptions (authorization).** A task credential carries its agent's principal ID, and subscriptions are owned by ID, so a credential for task A could pull, acknowledge, heartbeat, read, resume and cancel subscriptions the same agent made for task B or for the whole project. The guard was only on `subscribe`/`trace` in the API. The service now uses a subscription only on the credential's own task stream (all six calls), and refuses other streams in `subscribe`/`trace` too.
- **A revoked reader kept receiving (authorization).** The read right was checked only at `subscribe`; `pull`, `acknowledge`, `heartbeat` and `resume` now check it again (hosts and services, which the controller relies on, are not re-checked).
- **No limit on subscriptions.** An agent or client could make subscriptions without end (each a record kept for ever). Now at most 20 active ones per subscriber and stream (`EVENT_LIMITS.perSubscriber`), kept on a small `subscriber-streams` record written in the same write as the subscription, so two subscribes at once cannot both take the last place; cancelled and expired IDs are dropped when it is read. Hosts and services are not capped. A repeat of a recorded subscribe answers as before.
- **A stop that ended with unresolved work read `blocked`, never `outcome_unknown`.** The stop service never records `done` with unresolved items; it records `recovery-required` with them, so the `outcome_unknown` branch could not happen. `recovery-required` with unresolved items is now `outcome_unknown`. `ASSUMPTION:` `recovery-required` with nothing listed (a restart from an earlier boundary) and `blocked` stay `blocked`; reversible in `api/command-state.ts`.
- **Small.** The hold check asked the pause service about any `task:` stream ID, so a stream named for another kind of record failed every pull; it is now asked only for task IDs. The chat `attention` view said "ask again to go on", but the chat kind has no cursor, so asking again showed the same items; it now says to narrow the question. The API document's envelope section and the MCP door's `_meta` now include `state`.

**Checked, no change.** Acknowledgements only move forward, a repeat changes nothing, and nothing past the last event is accepted. Acknowledging further than the last pull is the subscriber's own choice about its own cursor. Two consumers of one subscription get the same batch, which is at-least-once delivery. A pull never moves the cursor, so a held (`wake: false`) answer loses nothing, and the events are served after the pause ends (tested). Restart: the cursor is stored, tested. Event payloads are kind, record reference, key and times only, and keys and IDs are limited by pattern, so there are no free words to redact. `message.references`, `continuation.list` and `activity.tools`: a task credential is held to its own task by `ownTaskOnly` and by the services, a non-owner sees only messages it sent or received, checkpoints and tool calls need the same rights as their existing reads, and no words, inputs or outputs are listed. Stale artifacts are grouped by task, so the same name on another task or project never supersedes. A deleted artifact record is simply absent. The age check uses the record time and the injected clock, and a record dated in the future is never `aged`. `artifactsPartial` can also say "partial" when the records exactly fill the scan budget (accepted: it errs toward saying more may be missing). Paging: limits are whole numbers from 1 to 100, cursors are checked by pattern, and `trace`'s `from` is a whole number from 1. The new tests use no fixed pauses, signals or POSIX-only paths.

**Left open.** Hosts and services may still subscribe to any stream (as before, H06). An agent may still acknowledge past what it pulled on its own subscription.

**Review tests and mutation checks.** New: `events/events.test.ts` "task streams (card U13 review)" on all four backends (task-project rights, task credential on its own stream and refused on the agent's other subscriptions for all six calls, revoked reader, the cap with a cancel freeing a place and a repeat not counting, hosts not capped). The sweep-limit test there now spreads its 101 subscriptions over 8 readers. `start-u13-finish`: `recovery-required` with unresolved items is `outcome_unknown`. Mutations, each made alone on the built files and restored, all made tests fail: (1) a task credential may use its agent's other subscriptions (the new event test fails on 4 of 4 backends); (2) any principal may pull or acknowledge any subscription (17 tests, including the API restart test); (3) no project lookup for a task stream (4 of 4); (4) no subscription cap (4 of 4); (5) an unresolved `recovery-required` stop read as `blocked` (the command-state test); (6) a stranger sees message references (the U13 read test); (7) a revoked reader keeps pulling (4 of 4).

## F04m (final slice): the restarted controller comes up on the new database by itself (2026-11-13)

Code: `packages/controller/src/transfer/targets.ts` (`storageFollowingAuthority`), `launcher/launcher.ts` (`launch`), `transfer/index.ts`. Tests: `transfer/targets.test.ts` (one unit test, "the restart hand-over"), `scripts/nimblenewt-controller.test.mjs` (one end-to-end entry test marked F04m). No owner control, API operation, setting or interpreter prompt changed; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` is unchanged.

**What the card still lacked (measured against its acceptance text and the earlier slices' "Not done" lists).** Every item of the deliverable was built by the earlier slices except one that the in-process tests hid: "The host restarts onto the new database by itself". The tests' own host picked the new storage in code. A real host (the entry under the release launcher: exit 75, the launcher starts it again) restarts from the CONFIGURATION, and the configuration still names the old database (`controller.storage`). The start guard then refused that start ("the controller database was moved to ... this start is configured for another database. Point controller.storage at it"), so after a move the owner had to edit the configuration by hand and the automatic restart led to a refused start in a loop of the launcher's own slowing-down. The same applied to a rollback onto a destination (moved A to B to C, back to B).

**Built.** `launch()` now follows the authority file: when the configuration lists transfer destinations and the (integrity-checked) authority file names a place that is not the configured database, the start uses the listed destination (SQLite entry by path, PostgreSQL entry by the address its secret holds plus its schema; the fingerprint is the comparison, as everywhere) and prints one line naming the destination (never an address). No authority file, or one naming the configured database: nothing changes. A place no entry lists is left to the existing start guard, which refuses with its existing text. An authority file that fails its integrity mark makes the start fail with the existing message, so nobody is started on a database a changed file chose. The entries are untrusted JSON and checked defensively (bad ones are skipped, the real validation still runs in the start). The secret name rule for the owner's credential is the launcher's `named`, as for the destination at transfer time.
- `ASSUMPTION:` follow the authority file inside `launch()`, not inside `startController`: the start function keeps refusing a start on a different database (the safety net and its many tests stay as they are), and only the host that restarts "from its configuration" resolves the destination. Rewriting the owner's configuration file instead was rejected (it holds the owner's text and comments, and a second source of truth could disagree with the authority file).
- Test (entry, in one process, SQLite): the entry under the release launcher's environment applies a move through the API, exits 75, is started again with the UNCHANGED configuration and comes up on the new file with the earlier data; it then rolls the move back (exit 75 again) and a third start is on the configured database, with nothing to follow. Unit test: no file, file naming the configured database, a SQLite destination, an unknown place, no entries, a PostgreSQL destination (schema is part of the place; the password appears in nothing returned), and a hand-changed file (rejected). Only file names and the platform's own temp folder; no signals, no timing assumptions beyond waiting for the exit code.
- Mutation checks (applied, built, run, restored): the launcher's follow switched off (the entry test fails); the PostgreSQL schema left out of the comparison (the unit test fails).

**Judged complete without further code (reasons recorded).**
- Resume or clean of an interrupted copy: the card says "resumes or is cleaned"; cleaning (second slice) is the chosen half. `ASSUMPTION:` no true resume; a copy from a fresh snapshot cannot carry a stale row.
- The epoch take: the card allows "inside the state lock or with expectedEpoch from the row the check read"; the second slice does the second. Not holding the lock across `ProjectService.open` is deliberate (a start must not make another wait five minutes).
- Rollback comparison of aggregates, timers and deliveries: every command admission writes an `operations` row (compared by digest) and effects are compared; deliveries are covered by their counter, audit by its counter. An aggregate or timer changes only through a command (so an `operations` row appears) or through a loop's own rewrite, which a rollback must not count as work. A write that skipped the command path entirely is not the barrier's case. `ASSUMPTION:` not comparing these two tables is final.
- Real process restart: the entry already exits 75 and the launcher starts it again (K02a tests with real child processes); this slice makes the second start land on the right database. The new test runs both legs in one process on purpose (the existing launcher test already covers the child-process leg, and a Windows child process adds no meaning here).

**What still blocks completion.** Nothing that blocks acceptance. Two things are choices left open, not defects: (1) the integrity key lives beside the files (stops accidents, partial edits and casual tampering, not someone who can rewrite the folder; a key from the host's secret store needs a decision on which secret and its rotation, and a migration of marked files, so it is a product choice for a later card); (2) a PostgreSQL leftover whose schema someone else made is still not dropped by the controller (the narrow-drop rules; the owner empties it). The card's status in the task plan is not changed.

### F04m final slice: review (2026-11-13, clean-context Claude review of dc49716e)

Base was already the current origin/main (57c9facd); nothing to merge.

**Bug found and fixed (data-critical).** After a move, a restart whose destination database is missing (the disk it is on is not attached, or the file was removed) came up on a NEW, EMPTY database without a word beyond the "this start uses it" line: opening a missing SQLite file (or an empty PostgreSQL schema) makes a fresh store, the start guard passed (the authority file names that place) and the fence check passed (a fresh store has no holder). The project list was empty and new work would have gone there while the real data sat fenced elsewhere. Reproduced through the entry before the fix (it started, exit 0, `project.list` empty). Fixed twice:
- `storageFollowingAuthority` refuses to follow to a SQLite destination whose file is not there (before anything is created at that path); the text names the entry, never a path or an address.
- `assertNotFenced` (every start with a transfer state folder, both backends, also a configuration pointed at the destination by hand) refuses a database the authority file names FOR A TRANSFER when it is empty: epoch 0 and no holder (or no state row), which is what opening a missing file or an empty schema makes. A copy always carries its source's epoch and the previous database of a rollback was started on, so neither is ever epoch 0. An authority file with no transfer, or none, leaves a new installation's first start alone.
- Tests: entry test "after a move, a destination whose file is gone ..." (refused with exit 1 when followed and when named by hand, nothing created, comes up on the moved data once the folder is back); unit test "a database the authority file names for a transfer is not started on when it is empty" (fake snapshot: both empty shapes refused without the address, a used database and a pending copy pass, no authority / no transferId pass); the implementer's hand-over unit test now also checks the missing-file refusal.

**Checked and found sound (no change).**
- Whatever the launcher picks, the start guard re-judges it under the state lock against the same integrity-checked authority file and journal, so the follow cannot make a start the guard would refuse; it only removes refusals. Crash points: a move stopped before its authority write leaves the authority on the old place (followed: nothing; the guard abandons the move); stopped after it (followed to the new place; the guard settles the journal). A rollback stopped after its fence and before its authority write: the follow now goes to the NEW database, where the guard looks for work first (F04n): with work the move stands (better than before: a start on the previous database would have finished the rollback and dropped that work); without work the guard finishes the rollback and refuses that one start, and the next start (the release launcher restarts it; its crash-loop limit is 20 short runs, then exit 4) follows to the previous database. One refused start in that window is accepted, not fixed.
- A configuration hand-pointed at a third place while the authority file names a listed destination: the start goes to the authoritative destination and says so (the third place would be refused by the guard anyway; no fork).
- Places: SQLite by `canon` (links resolved, native realpath, so case and 8.3 spellings agree on macOS and Windows for an existing file); entry paths must be absolute with a drive letter or UNC prefix on Windows. PostgreSQL by host (lower case, `host` query parameter counts), port (5432 default), database and schema; never user or password. Same address with another schema is another place (tested).
- Secrecy: the printed line has the entry name and kind only; a PostgreSQL secret that cannot be resolved is skipped silently and left to the guard's refusal, which names entries, not addresses.
- Integrity mark: HMAC-SHA256 over the whole body (format, generation, active place with name and kind, previous, transfer id, since), key file 0600 beside it, writes are temp-file + fsync + rename. Residual (not introduced here, recorded): there is no anti-replay anchor, so an OLD authority file restored together with its key by a whole-folder file restore made outside NimbleNewt (K01 backups do not carry the transfer folder) is accepted; with a pre-rollback file the start would follow to the rolled-back database (its `rolled-back:` holder is accepted, because the same holder with the same files is also the legitimate state after a rollback that found late work). A fix needs a generation kept inside each database; left for a later card.
- K01 staged restore: the swap is applied to the database the start uses, which is now the followed one, so a restore staged while running on the destination lands there after the restart.
- Own mutation checks (each alone on the built files, restored): no missing-file check in the follow (unit and entry tests fail); no empty-database check in the start (unit and entry tests fail); the follow takes the authority file's `previous` place, i.e. a stale pointer to the rolled-back database (both entry tests fail); a place no entry lists falls back to a listed entry (unit test fails); the integrity mark ignored by the follow (unit test fails).

## K06 finish: replay holds, stored model thinking, the scratch and transcript tiers, host wiring (2026-11-13)

This closes the last offline-doable parts of the retention card (K06, K06b, K06c, K06d). Earlier slices are not redone.

**What the card still lacked, and what is built now**

- **"Material referenced by a resumable task or by replay is never deleted and shows as retained."** Resumable tasks were held already. Replay was not: a finished task's replay steps (`activity-step` manifest refs and `summaryId`) and explanations (`activity-explanation` evidence) can cite desk records, summaries and other records. `RetainedMaterial` now holds each cited record with a reason `cited by the replay of task T (step N)` or `... explanation of step N`. Expiry and deletion skip it and show it as retained. An archive is not stopped by it (the original is kept and restorable). The owner may release exactly this hold with `retention.delete ... releaseReplay: true`; the deletion record then lists the replay steps that now point at nothing. A resumable task's hold can never be released that way.
- **Stored model thinking (K06c).** Pi Durable keeps the model's own copy of its thinking in a per-attempt conversation store (`main.jsonl` and sidecars) that its API only appends to. New `removeStoredThinking(dir)` in the Pi adapter rewrites those files without the thinking blocks (text, signature and redacted payloads), through a temporary file and an atomic rename; it stops and changes nothing if the file changed meanwhile or a line is not JSON, ignores links, and is safe to repeat. The store still opens and the conversation goes on (tested with the real adapter). The retention rule `pi-thinking` applies it to the attempts of finished tasks after `thinkingDays`, previewed, digest-confirmed, audited as `thinking-store-days` (counts only, never text), and tracked per attempt in a `thinking-purge` record as `purged`, `none` (no store there) or `pending` (a host did not answer, the attempt is running, the rewrite failed). A task with a pending attempt stays a candidate and is tried again. The same is done on remote hosts over the authenticated workspace-ask channel (`pi-thinking-purge`; the host checks the names, refuses path-shaped ones, never opens a running attempt's store). Composition: `local-host.mjs` and `remote-host.mjs` hand the adapter's removal to the host; `start.ts` builds the local and remote ports.
- **Owner decision 2026-10-22 (thinking goes 14 days after done) without the owner turning anything on.** New switch `thinkingAuto` (default true). When `autoRun` is off, the dispatcher still runs a thinking-only pass (at most once an hour). Nothing else runs without `autoRun`.
- **K06b tiers "scratch output" and "old transcripts".** `scratchArchiveDays` and `scratchPurgeDays`: private desk records of a finished task are archived (restorable by `retention.restore`), later removed the same way as a user-requested deletion, with what was made from them; a replay or resumable hold stops removal. `transcriptDays`: an old finished chat turn loses the owner's words, plan and answers and stays as a stub (ID, message ID, state, times), so the same message sent again is still answered as the done turn; a turn that a decision, an agenda item or an open proposal rests on, or a turn still holding commands, is kept. Both are off by default and bounded. Audit and decisions are never touched.
- **Chat.** All new fields are in `RETENTION_FIELDS`, so the chat's settings command and the interpreter prompt (generated from the operation table) name them; `retention.delete` names `releaseReplay`. No magic phrases.
- **Disk-full.** A real SQLite "database or disk is full" error (page limit) is shown to be classified by the adapter and recognised by the guard.

**Tests:** replay holds, thinking stores, tiers (all four backends); the remote ask over the real worker channel (four backends); the Pi adapter rewrite (real adapter, real store, scanStorage clean, the provider request carries no thinking); an end-to-end `retention.run` over a real conversation store; the SQLite disk-full error (storage/sqlite/disk-full-real.test.ts). Mutations applied to the built files and seen to fail, then restored: replay scan off, thinking strip off, `thinkingAuto` sweep off, transcript holds off.

**NOT done, and why**

- A true full file system (needs a small dedicated volume; not portable in CI). The engine's own error code is tested instead.
- Wiping freed disk blocks, and removing thinking from Pi data inside existing backups (a backup is a sealed copy; a restore of an old backup brings the old thinking back, then the next run removes it again).
- Export to a file or archive format and an import (only JSON pages exist).
- Quota metering of messages and model calls (no counting point exists offline).
- A remote host that never answers keeps its attempt pending for ever (the task stays a candidate; nothing is claimed clean).

**ASSUMPTION:** a finished task's replay holds what its steps cite, because the owner reads that replay; releasing it is the owner's explicit choice.
**ASSUMPTION:** an archive ignores replay holds because it keeps the original and restores it exactly.
**ASSUMPTION:** a whole thinking block is removed rather than blanked, since a block without its signature would be refused by the provider; an assistant message left empty keeps one empty text block.
**ASSUMPTION:** `thinkingAuto` defaults on (the owner's 2026-10-22 decision); reversible by one setting.
**ASSUMPTION:** a host with no way to clean stores, or an unreachable host, counts as `pending`, never as clean (the safe reading).
**ASSUMPTION:** the scratch and transcript windows are off by default and bounded (7 to 3650, 30 to 3650); the smallest reversible choice.

### K06 finish: review (2026-11-13, clean-context Claude review of 004c42a0)

Merged origin/main 8f62a2f1 first (notes only conflicted; both sides kept).

**Default on checked.** `thinkingAuto` on by default stays: `provisional-defaults.md` ("stored thinking is deleted 14 days after the task is done ... owner decision 2026-10-22") and the K06/K06c card text record it as the owner's decision. `done` and `cancelled` are final (`TRANSITIONS`), so a store cleaned after its task ended is never resumed; pi-ai drops empty text blocks and assistant messages left empty, so the emptied message is safe for every provider.

**Bugs found and fixed.**
- **A crashed attempt's store could be made unopenable.** Pi Durable cuts off a last line with no line end when it opens a store (an append that never finished) and refuses a complete line that is not JSON. The rewrite read lines with `readline` and wrote every one back with `\n`, so a torn tail became a "complete" garbage line in any store that also held thinking: Pi would no longer open it. The rewrite now works on bytes: a line with no thinking mark is copied byte for byte (line ending, CR, any bytes) and so is an unfinished last line; an unfinished last line that mentions thinking is left out (what Pi's own opening does). Lines with the mark are decoded as strict UTF-8 (Pi does the same) and a CR before the line end is kept.
- **Two removals on one store could put a half-written temporary file in place of the conversation.** Both used the same temporary name and each first deleted "leftovers" with that name, so a manual `retention.run` overlapping the hourly pass (or a host asked again after a timeout) could rename the other's partly written file over `main.jsonl`. A lock file (`.thinking-purge.lock`, taken over after 15 minutes when a crash left it) now makes one removal at a time; the second is `pending` with a plain reason.
- **A file replaced between read and rename went unnoticed when its size and mtime matched.** The file is now opened without following links, checked to be the file that was listed, and compared on device, inode, size, mtime and ctime both through the open handle and by path just before the rename. The new file keeps the old mode (it was 0600 before), is flushed, and the folder is flushed after the rename (POSIX); on Windows the handle is closed before the rename and a rename refused with EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES is tried again up to 8 times with backoff. Pi's own `*.jsonl.reclaim` leftovers (which Pi deletes on open and which may hold thinking) are removed too.
- **The local stores of a still-running attempt were not protected.** The remote host checks its busy attempts, but `start.ts` gives the local port no `busy`. The rule now skips every attempt whose dispatch record still says `running` (a cancel not yet delivered, an end not yet reported), on every host; the task becomes a candidate again once it ends.
- **An unreachable host made the hourly thinking pass write a run record every hour for ever.** Every candidate stays pending, so each pass ran for real and wrote a `retention-run` row with nothing removed (24 a day; the M03h class). The automatic thinking-only pass now writes no run record when it removed nothing; the per-task `thinking-purge` record still keeps what was settled.
- **Old chat turns kept the owner's words in the chat context.** The `chat-context` record keeps a line per recent turn and project (the first 100 characters of the words and the answer, up to 20 per project), so for a quiet project the words outlived the stub. The same command that stubs a turn now replaces those lines with "(the words of this turn were removed by retention)".
- Test hygiene: the integration test removes its folder with retries (Windows keeps the SQLite file busy briefly).

**Checked and found sound (no change).** Replay holds: only the retention service deletes desk, summary or artifact records, so no other path bypasses them; `releaseReplay` is owner-only, goes through a chat proposal, and is ignored when the reference scan was incomplete; resumable holds are never released. Transcript stubs: a message sent again is matched by `turn-<hash(owner, messageId)>` with no text comparison and returns the done turn; decisions (`decision.source.turnId`), agenda items (and so owner questions) and open proposals hold their turns; follow-ups keep a turn. Remote: the controller accepts only attempt-shaped IDs (1 to 50, no repeats), the host validates names again and finds directories from its own listing, never from the request; an old host or one without the removal gives no `purged`/`none` lists, so the attempt stays pending; a host can still lie about "purged" (it is its own data; recorded, not fixable). Dispatcher: the sweep loop has the 60 s loop timeout and is never run twice at once.

**Left open (recorded).** The rewritten file belongs to the controller's (or host's) user, since a rename cannot keep another owner. A backup taken during a purge may hold the old file in its copy (it retries on a replaced file). A backup whose Pi-state copy predates the purge but whose database copy has the `purged` record would not be cleaned again after a restore (retention is not a backup-barrier participant). Closed proposals keep their preview lines. An attempt whose dispatch record is stuck at `running` is never cleaned (the safe direction).

**Mutation checks (each alone on the built files, restored):** the changed-file check off (adapter test fails); a line end added to an unfinished tail (adapter test fails); the lock off (adapter test fails); a running attempt's store handed to the cleaner (4 of 4 backends fail); the hourly empty run recorded (4 of 4 fail); the chat-context copy kept (4 of 4 fail); the remote host opening a busy attempt's store (remote test fails).

## U09b (finish): the replay's web view, honest producers, links, owner correction and a simulated rerun (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-13)

**What was lacking.** The replay existed only as API calls and chat. Three things in the card were still open: the owner's web view; step producers that wrote a real outcome, a real line of work (branch) and a real "this replaces that" claim (before, almost every step said only what it said, so replay could not tell a confirmed result from a mere claim); and the rerun. The links in a step (what it cites) showed only an id.

**What is done.**
- *Producers.* The dispatcher records tool calls with outcome (confirmed, failed and cancelled count as an answer that came back; uncertain stays uncertain; in progress is dispatched) and finishes the earlier "proposed" step of the same writer and line. The tool bridge, reviews, messages, lease force, artifacts, stop, handoff, meeting decisions and compaction (new "compression" step) all write an outcome. The branch registry now tells the host about open, transition and switch, and the host writes a step on that line. A recorded submission writes a "submission" step.
- *Supersedes.* Two honest sources only: a later step of the same writer on the same line that finishes an operation an earlier step proposed, and the owner's correction with `replaces` (owner only; refused for anyone else before anything is written). A retry of the same command is told as it was first told.
- *Links.* `activity.replay.links` (and the chat step view, and the web step route) resolve what a step cites by asking the owning service as the reader: agent messages, submissions, reviews, artifacts, side lines. A record of another task is refused; a code submission shows identity only (base, tree, patch), not diff lines; text written by an agent is marked untrusted, cleaned and bounded. Kinds with no reader say so.
- *Rerun.* A replay never reruns anything: `activity.replay.rerun` always refuses and points to `activity.replay.simulate`, an owner-only command that walks at most 200 recorded steps in an isolated scope (no tool, provider, message or ledger port), can inject a failure at one step, is labelled "Simulated", and is idempotent by command ID.
- *Web view.* A Replay tab: summary first, filters, lines side by side with the "happened side by side" label, one step with its links, search, thinking collapsed behind a button (each expansion is a recorded look with a fixed reason and an Idempotency-Key), and a simulate button that asks first. Owner session only, CSRF on every POST. Everything is drawn as text; the page never assigns markup.
- *Chat.* `activity.replay.simulate` applies at once (it changes nothing); `activity.correct` with `replaces` is shown first and applied on yes. Both are in the interpreter prompt's operation table, so the owner needs no magic phrase.
- *Retention.* After retention removes the thinking the page and chat say only "removed by retention"; the timeline and the replayed steps are unchanged (composed test).

**Tests.** `activity/replay-finish.test.ts` (four backends), `submissions` hook (four backends), dispatcher outcome tests, `api/start-replay-finish.test.ts` (the whole story through the running controller, the door and the chat), `ui/src/replay.test.ts` (hostile text, collapsed thinking, simulate confirm).

**What is NOT done / cannot be met offline.** P07 proper (a simulation scope with simulated tools, events and competing edits) is not built; the simulation here is a labelled walk through recorded steps only. Live thinking from a real model, the Pi-side store copy of K06c and anything on real hardware cannot be checked offline. Agent-message steps have no composed test (they need the tool bridge with a real host); they are covered by resolver unit tests only.

ASSUMPTION (corrected by the review below): a call that came back without taking effect (failed, cancelled, refused) is the new outcome "failed", never "confirmed"; "confirmed" is a success only.
ASSUMPTION: a call awaiting approval maps to "proposed" (nothing happened yet); a state nobody has classified maps to "uncertain".
ASSUMPTION: the minimal isolated simulation stands in for P07 until P07 is built; it is labelled so everywhere it shows.
ASSUMPTION: a link to a diff shows identity only, never the diff lines.
ASSUMPTION: the new replay-simulation records, and the "submission" and "context-branch" references, are small, bounded and owner-created, so K06 retention holds do not cover them.
ASSUMPTION: an agent's own claim of an outcome stays marked "reported by agent"; only a controller service's own step is unmarked.

### U09b (finish) review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-13)

Plain words first. The replay told the owner that a tool call which failed was "confirmed", and counted it with the successes in the summary. That is now its own outcome, "failed". A few smaller things were fixed too, and the gaps in the tests the slice listed were filled.

**Fixed.**
- *Honest outcomes.* `STEP_OUTCOMES` gains `failed`: the answer came back and the action did not take effect (failed, cancelled or refused; the step's words say which). The dispatcher maps a success to confirmed, failed/cancelled/refused to failed, in progress to dispatched, awaiting approval to proposed, and anything else to uncertain (was: failed and cancelled confirmed, refused and unknown states proposed). A meeting decision that could not change a task is failed (was proposed). A failed step is terminal: a later step never marks it replaced.
- *Owner correction at the command-ID limit.* The replacing step's command was `<commandId>-replaces`; a command ID of 112 to 120 characters made it too long, so the correction was written and the replacing step failed with an internal error on every retry. It is now derived at a fixed length (`rpl:` and a digest), and a retry completes it.
- *The tool path is not slowed by the finish lookup.* `recordFinishing` looked back over up to 200 steps one read at a time on every recorded tool call (the common case finds nothing and reads all 200). It now reads them in parallel chunks of 25, newest first, and stops at the first deciding step; the rule is unchanged (test: an open step found behind 60 other steps).
- *Link text.* The server-side cleaner now also removes direction-changing and invisible characters (U+061C, U+200B to U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2060 to U+2069, U+FEFF), never cuts a character in half, and treats a resolver that does not say otherwise as untrusted. The page already removed these; other API readers did not.
- *The simulation walk.* A recorded step with a missing or odd field (no kind, a number as summary, an object as outcome, a non-number seq, a kind named like an object member) is shown as "unknown"/empty and never stops the walk; a page that does not move forward ends it.
- *The page offline.* Opening a step, searching, expanding the thinking and simulating each say "Offline" when the connection drops, and their buttons can be pressed again (before: a button stayed disabled, a step stayed "Loading...").

**Tests added.** Composed: a task credential for another task and another project's agent are refused on `activity.replay.links/step/led`, neither can simulate (a task credential not even on its own task), neither can correct with `replaces`; simulate refuses a missing and a wrong CSRF header, a missing or malformed Idempotency-Key and GET, writing nothing. Activity (four backends): a failed step is not replaced; an agent cannot claim to replace another writer's step on any line (the old check used two services, which may, and passed only because of the line); the 200-step bound and `truncated` with a later `from`; a 120-character command ID correction and its retry; bidirectional and surrogate text; another project's reader gets nothing and no resolver is asked. Unit: odd stored steps in the walk. UI: the confirmed Simulate click (one POST each, CSRF header, a fresh Idempotency-Key per click, empty body), the search query encoding, the next-steps button and the agent and "Show everything" chips, and offline recovery.

**Checked and found sound (no change).** The web routes are behind the owner session (a non-owner credential ends the session), the same-origin check and the CSRF header on every POST; the thinking look carries a fixed reason the page cannot change; the page sets text only and builds no link from a stored ID. Every producer hook is wrapped so its failure never fails the operation (branches, submissions, dispatcher, tool bridge, compaction). A crash between an operation and its step leaves the step missing until the same command is told again (the hooks are keyed by the command or record, so a retry records it once); nothing reconciles a step lost without a retry, as before. The hooks are awaited after the operation commits, so a hanging activity write still delays the caller's answer, as with C09d's existing steps.

**Mutation checks (each alone on the built files, restored):** `replaces` allowed for a non-owner; a confirmed step superseded by a finishing step; the message resolver returning another task's record; the page fetching and showing the thinking without a click; a failed call mapped to confirmed; direction-changing characters kept in link text; the old `-replaces` command ID; the offline simulate button left disabled. All eight were caught.

### U09b (finish) proof of "zero effects" through the running controller (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-13)

Plain words first. An independent audit found that the composed story only checked that the number of audit records and effect records did not change while the owner replayed a task. That does not show that nothing was queued for delivery, that nothing else was written, or that no model was asked. The composed test (`api/start-replay-finish.test.ts`) now shows each of those. Only the test changed; no product code needed a fix.

**What the test now checks.**
- *The outbox.* The delivery table and its sequence counter are read from a consistent copy of the store before and after the web replay reads (open, filter, error answers, step, links, search), after the owner's thinking look, and around the simulation. They are identical each time: no delivery was added, claimed or changed. (The audit counter in the same state row moves with every record, so only the delivery counter is compared.)
- *Writes.* The operations table of the same copy is the write log. The replay reads add no operation. The thinking look adds exactly one (its own recorded look, opening no effect). Refused simulation requests (no CSRF, wrong CSRF, no key, bad key, wrong method) add none. The simulation adds exactly one operation, carrying one audit record and no effect.
- *Models and routes.* The composed controller is given counting stand-ins for every model it can call: the chat interpreter (the scripted one already counts), the resume reviewer, the report questioner and the coordinator, each with its own route name. Across the replay reads, the thinking look and the simulation the stand-in counts do not move, and over the whole story (including the chat turns, which use only the scripted interpreter) no model or route stand-in is ever called.
- *Audit history after retention.* The weak "at least as many records" check is replaced: every audit record taken before the task ended and the retention run is compared, by sequence number and full content, with the same sequence number afterwards. (The retention run's own record is separate and is still asserted.)

**Mutation checks (each applied alone to the built files, seen failing, restored).** The simulation also queues a delivery: "the simulation queued no delivery". A replay read that also starts a simulation: "a replay read wrote an operation" (with the older audit-count line switched off, so the new line is what failed). A replay read that submits a chat turn: "no replay read went through the chat interpreter" (older lines switched off). A replay read that asks the resume reviewer stand-in for a completion: "a replay read called a model". One earlier audit record's type changed directly in the SQLite file after retention: "audit record 3 (principal.provision) changed".

**Limits that remain** (unchanged from the slice, repeated here so a later flip reads them in one place). The simulation stands in for P07, which is still planned. The provider switch and the failed tool call in the composed scenario are written by hand with `activity.record`; their real producers are tested separately. Agent-message steps have no composed test. Live thinking from a real model cannot be checked offline. The composed test runs on SQLite only; the services it reaches are covered on four backends in their own suites.

ASSUMPTION: a counting stand-in for the models is enough for "zero router calls": the controller reaches a route only through a model client, so a stand-in per client, each with its own route name, sees every route call. No separate router object is exposed to count.
ASSUMPTION: the write log is read from the operations table of a store copy rather than by wrapping the storage object, because replacing a method on the live storage object made the composed controller spin and run out of memory.

## M04h (final offline slice): a caller for `carriesOnDuringMeeting`, the idle signal, and a left seat no longer holds work back (Claude agent, 2026-11-13)

**Corrected by the review below:** a carrying-on task IS paused for the meeting (skipping the pause let the agent act on the task meanwhile); `carriedOn` is only a note of the background jobs that continue under the pause. Card status is NOT changed. This finishes everything in M04h that can be built and proven without a real model or real hardware. What still needs the real thing is listed under "NOT done".

Plain words first. When the owner calls a meeting, an agent that is busy has to stop what it is doing and come to the room. That is right for an agent in the middle of work, but wasteful for an agent that is only waiting for a long background job (a build, say): pausing it gains nothing. Since M04g the controller could say "this attempt has only background jobs left", but nothing asked the question, and nothing could tell whether the agent was really waiting rather than thinking. Now both exist.

**Done**
- **The idle signal.** `WorkerHandle.idle?()` (new, optional): "the turn is running and no model call and no tool call is in progress". The local worker answers it from what it already counts (tool calls in flight plus the runtime's open model calls); a runtime that cannot count its model calls, a stopped attempt or a turn that has not started is never idle. A worker without the method (a remote host, an older worker) is never idle, and a failure reads as not idle.
- **The caller.** `Dispatcher.carriesOnTask(by, taskId)` (staff only): true only when every live attempt of the task is running, has no call in flight or parked for an approval, its worker says `idle()`, and `carriesOnDuringMeeting(attempt, { conversationIdle: true })` agrees (a meeting concerns the agent, and the job records say only background jobs remain). Anything else, any failure, a task with no running attempt and any non-staff caller read as false.
- **Where it is asked.** `AttendanceService.prepare` asks the new `AttendanceOptions.carriesOn` hook (composed in `dispatch-compose.ts` as the dispatcher's own `carriesOnTask`, bound lazily) for each task the agent says it interrupts. A task that carries on is NOT paused; it is recorded on the attendance (`carriedOn`, one event naming the tasks), returned by `prepare` (`carriedOn`) and shown in the room status (`participants[].carriedOn`). A task already paused for this attendance keeps its pause (a pause is never lifted here); if a task that carried on is later prepared again while busy, it is paused and removed from `carriedOn`. No hook, or a failing hook, means the task is paused as before. Joining needs nothing for a carried task (only paused tasks are waited for), and the return has nothing to resume for it.
- **A left seat no longer holds work back.** `AttendanceService.admission` skipped an agent only by its current reachability; an agent that had LEFT the meeting (a left seat is final) still made the rest of the meeting hold its new work (and through the T07 gate its long jobs) back. A seat that has left is now skipped. Checked and left as it is: a "withheld" seat (the agent was paused or unavailable when the meeting was called) of an agent that is reachable again is not over-refused, because `openRoom`, `prepare` and `join` decide the seat again from current reachability, so that agent really can attend; an agent that is still not reachable was already skipped by admission's reachability check. So the T07 follow-up "a withheld seat over-refused near a meeting" is closed: its only real case was the left seat.
- **Owner controls.** No new owner switch was needed: the existing chat-settable `meeting.safeLongRunning` (default on) turns the whole carry-on behaviour off (the predicate then says no, so every task is paused as before). What carried on is visible in the room status and the attendance timeline, which the owner reads through the existing meeting status view in chat. `meeting.attend.prepare` and its API docs now name `carriedOn`.
- **Tests (four storage backends where the service touches storage).** `meetings/attendance.test.ts` (2 new suites on reference store, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread and PostgreSQL: carry-on skip, paused-as-before for the others, failing or absent hook, room status, left seat); `dispatch/dispatcher-suite.ts` (1 new suite, every dispatcher backend that suite runs on: no attempt, worker that cannot say, busy, idle, owner may ask, agent may not, foreground work, failing worker, unknown task, ended attempt); `dispatch/local-worker-guards.test.ts` (idle signal of the real local worker); `api/start-safe-long-running.test.ts` (composed `startController` on SQLite, no model: an idle attempt with a running background job is not paused by `prepare`, the task with no running attempt is, and a busy conversation is paused). Mutation checks (each applied, tests failed, restored): worker idle check removed (dispatcher suite and composed test fail), `prepare` never carrying on (attendance suites and composed test fail), left-seat skip removed (the attendance suites fail on all four backends).

**NOT done (cannot be met offline, or by design)**
- **A real worker's idle signal on real hardware.** The idle answer of the local worker is only exercised with fake runtimes. Whether the real Pi runtime's `activeModelCalls` and the tool bridge's in-flight count cover every moment a real model is working has not been observed (there can be a short gap between a model call ending and the tool call starting; see ASSUMPTION). The remote host protocol carries no idle signal, so an attempt on a remote host is never taken to be idle and is paused for meetings as before.
- **Result handling for a job that finishes during the meeting.** What the agent does with a finished background job's result needs the real agent. The existing W11 wake still delivers the result as before; this slice adds nothing to it and no test of a real agent receiving it mid-meeting exists.
- **The real local worker host starting a woken agent's own attempt** (the L02/L03 side of the first two slices) is only proven with the fixture host.
- A woken agent that leaves by its own `meeting.attend.leave` cannot be woken for the same meeting again (a left seat is final); unchanged by design.
- The 3 / 5 / 3 wake bounds stay constants, not owner settings (unchanged).

**ASSUMPTION:** a conversation with no model call open and no tool call in flight is idle for this purpose. A brief gap between steps could be read as idle; the cost of a wrong "carries on" is only that the task is not paused while the agent is in the meeting (its own long jobs are still refused by the T07 gate), the smallest and most reversible harm, and `meeting.safeLongRunning` turns it off.
**ASSUMPTION:** a worker that cannot report idleness (remote host, older worker) is never idle, so it behaves exactly as before.
**ASSUMPTION:** the hook is asked per named task inside `prepare`, so the agent (or the loop that calls prepare) still decides which tasks it interrupts; the controller only declines to pause the ones that qualify. No new background loop.
**ASSUMPTION:** a left seat is final, so its work stops being held back at once; a withheld seat of a reachable agent keeps holding work back because that agent can still be brought in.

### M04h final offline slice: review (2026-11-13, clean-context Claude review of 40a2d318, merged with main 8f62a2f1)

Plain words first. The slice let a meeting skip pausing a task whose agent seemed to be "only waiting for a background job". The review found that skipping the pause is what let the agent keep working on that task during the meeting, so the meeting now pauses every task again. The question the slice added is kept, but only as information: it records which paused tasks still have background jobs running, so the owner can see that a build carries on while its agent attends.

**Bug found and fixed (safety): a "carrying on" task was not paused, so its agent could act on it during the meeting.**
- The task pause (L01) is the one thing that stops an attending agent's work: the tool bridge refuses every write of a paused task ("A pause stops everything the agent writes through the bridge"), and the dispatcher starts nothing for it. A task left unpaused by `prepare` had none of that, and nothing re-checked it later (only a second `prepare` could, and a joined agent cannot be prepared again).
- The idle reading cannot carry the weight put on it. Under W11 an agent that waits for its jobs ENDS its turn and its attempt PARKS (`state: "parked"`, `waitsOnJobs`), so it is never `running`; the `running`-and-idle state the slice looked for is in practice only the short gap between a model call and the next tool call (or the reverse), which the implementer's own ASSUMPTION admits. In that gap the agent's very next step is more work on the task (a model call, then writes, commits or a landing), and nothing stood between it and that step. Requiring the reading to hold for two reads or a grace period would not change this: whenever the reading is right, the next thing the conversation does is still act on the task.
- Pausing costs a waiting task nothing: a permitted background job keeps running under the pause, its result is recorded without lifting it (L01 `recordBackground`), and its W11 wake waits until the pause is lifted (the dispatcher's `#wakeOne`), which the meeting's return does. So README 503 ("long-running operations can continue if safe ... the bounded meeting task without advancing its paused assignment") is met by the pause itself.
- Fix: `AttendanceService.prepare` pauses every named task again. The `carriesOn` hook is asked first (before this attendance's pause would make the answer no) and a task it says yes to is noted in `carriedOn` (still on the attendance, the `prepare` result and the room status), and only when this attendance's own pause holds it. The event now reads "paused for the meeting; its background jobs carry on: ...". The return lifts the pause like any other, so nothing new is needed at the end of the meeting. The warning "ahead" again names the first interrupted task.
- `ASSUMPTION:` the meeting always pauses the tasks the agent leaves, and "carries on" is only a note of the background work that continues under the pause. This is the smallest and most reversible choice that keeps the agent from acting during the meeting. The other choice (a separate meeting gate that holds a running conversation without a pause) would be new machinery, and it would only give back what the pause already gives.

**Smaller fixes.**
- `Dispatcher.carriesOnTask` answered yes for a task the owner had paused (a paused attempt stays `running` with nothing in flight, so it read as idle). It now answers no for any task a pause holds (the pause gate's `guard`). `prepare` also notes only tasks that its own pause holds, so a pause that races in after the question (the owner's) is never described as this meeting's carry-on.
- `carriesOnTask` now also counts the real way an agent waits on background work: an attempt parked for its jobs (W11 `waitsOnJobs`, no approval parked) whose own unfinished jobs are all background jobs already placed (the same M04g predicate, and a meeting must concern the agent). A parked attempt has no conversation running at all.
- Chat: the interpreter prompt did not describe `meeting.safeLongRunning` (or `meeting.leadMinutes`), so although the setting exists, the model had no way to know it can change it. It now has a paragraph with free wording examples and the `policy_edit` shape (placed after the other setting paragraphs, so an older test that takes the first `policy_edit` template still finds the MCP one). The paragraph says the task is paused either way. `meeting.attend.prepare`'s description in `operations.ts` and the API docs were corrected to match ("paused too; its jobs carry on under the pause").

**Checked and found sound (no change).**
- Remote attempts: the remote host's handles have no `idle()`, so they are never idle (the `idle` in `remote/responder.ts` is a different class). A worker without the method, or whose method throws, reads as not idle.
- Several attempts of one task (swarm, another agent's attempt of the same task): every live attempt of the task must qualify, or the answer is no.
- Hook failures: `#carries` catches everything, so a throwing or failing hook notes nothing and the task is paused as before. The attendance is written in one revision-checked update, so a failure cannot leave it half-written. `carriedOn` is an ordinary field of the attendance body, so it is kept on all four backends and survives a restart. The room status shows it to the same viewers who already see `interrupted` (the same task IDs), so nothing new is exposed.
- Left seat (`admission`): a missing attendance record reads as not left, so a seat that never joined still holds work back. Nothing clears an agent's `leftAt` (only the owner's own rejoin drops it, on the owner's record), and `prepare` and `join` refuse a left agent, so a left agent cannot be admitted again. Admission is not used for quorum or ballot counts, so they do not change.
- CI portability of the new tests (the slice's and the review's): no fixed pauses, no signals, no POSIX-only paths (folders come from `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())` and the test worlds); the waits are on conditions or on manual timers.

**Left open (recorded, not fixed here).**
- There is no chat view of a meeting room (who is preparing, present or unavailable, what each waits on, and now `carriedOn`). The `meetings` status kind lists planned meetings and their rosters only, and `meeting.attend.status` is an API query that the chat does not offer. The slice's note that the owner reads `carriedOn` "through the existing meeting status view in chat" was not right. The owner can still see the background jobs themselves (`jobs` status). The room view has been missing since M04 and needs a status kind of its own.
- `WorkerHandle.idle()` stays as built. With the pause always applied it only decides whether a `running` attempt is noted.

**Review tests (each fails without its fix).** `meetings/attendance.test.ts` (rewritten suite, four backends): the carrying task is paused with this attendance's own pause, waits for its boundary, is noted in `carriedOn`, the event and the room status, stays paused through join, and its pause is lifted by the return. A task the owner paused is neither noted nor taken over, and the owner's pause stays. An absent or failing hook notes nothing and the task is paused. `dispatch/job-wakes.test.ts` (new, four backends): an attempt parked for its background job is reported as carrying on. An attempt parked for a foreground job is not, and neither is one with no meeting or a task the owner paused. Under the pause the finished job does not wake the attempt. `dispatch/dispatcher-suite.ts`: an owner pause turns the answer to no. `api/start-safe-long-running.test.ts`: the composed controller pauses the carrying task, notes it (also in the `meeting.attend.status` answer), keeps the background job running, and never notes the owner-paused task. A new chat test shows the owner turning `meeting.safeLongRunning` off and on in free words through the real `ModelInterpreter` with a stand-in model that knows only the prompt (shown first, applied on agreement). `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts`: the prompt names both meeting settings.
