## M05b (finish): the chair's desk read is proved read-only, recorded per file and visible to the absent member (2026-11-13)

Earlier slices (M05b partial and its review fixes, above) built `MeetingDeskReadService.read` and `reads`. This slice closes every item of the card's acceptance that can be checked without a running chair. Code: `meetings/desk-reads.ts`, `meetings/desk-reads.test.ts` (two scenarios per backend, 8 runs), `context/inspection.ts` (a `meeting-chair` kind of look), `status/status.ts` (new view `meeting_desk_reads`), `api/operations.ts` (query `meeting.desk-reads`), `api/start.ts` and `api/state-api.ts` (wiring), `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.

**What was lacking, and what is done now**
- **A record the absent member sees "through its inspections".** Before, a read left only a `meeting-desk-read` record that `reads` listed. Now the same commit also writes an `inspection` record (`via: "meeting-chair"`, meeting record, record read, its revision, owner of the file, reason text, time), so `InspectionService.inspections` shows the file's agent (and the owner) every read of its files with no new reader code. A read whose records cannot be committed returns nothing and leaves nothing (tested with a storage that refuses to commit, then the retry works); every read record names its inspection and the test checks each exists.
- **Attempted writes are refused and recorded.** New `attemptChange(chair, { meetingRecordId, targetId, operation })` with `operation` one of `write`, `revise`, `rename`, `delete`, `lock`: it never does anything, always answers `forbidden` (a repeat too) and, for the current chair of an open meeting only, leaves a `meeting-desk-attempt` record (one per meeting record, target and operation, with a count, first and last time and the last chair), so a chair that keeps trying cannot grow the store. Tests: the desk record is byte for byte unchanged, the number of desk records, notes, reads and inspections is unchanged, the same command repeated counts once, the file's agent and the roster see the attempts (`attempts`), a stranger does not, a non-chair is refused with no record, malformed operation or target is `invalid_command`. The service's public methods are pinned (`attemptChange`, `attempts`, `read`, `readNote`, `reads`), none named like a write.
- **Shared working notes.** New `readNote(chair, { meetingRecordId, noteId })`: needs only being the open meeting's current chair (no desk grant, no scratch grant, no `notes.chair.read`; the test chair holds none), for a shared, undeleted note of the meeting's project whether its agent is present or absent; the record says `source: "note"` and `visibility: "shared"`, and the note's agent sees an inspection by the meeting chair. Private, deleted, another project's notes, a non-chair and a malformed ID are refused with no record.
- **Chair change, end of meeting.** Tested for all three paths (desk read, note read, attempt): after `setChair` the former chair is refused and the new chair works; after the meeting ends nobody can.
- **Absent member not woken, attempt undisturbed.** The test takes the whole audit (every write the controller makes is audited, gap free) around three reads: exactly three audit entries, all by the chair, all about `meeting-desk-read` records; the desk records, working notes and versions, agents, principals, grants and the meeting record are identical before and after; no delivery is queued for any member or the owner. There is no running-attempt model in this service, so the proof is "nothing was written or queued for the agent", not an attempt-level probe.
- **Repeated after a controller restart.** The test takes a new epoch (`ProjectService.open`): the old service is refused as `stale_epoch`, the new one lists the earlier records, reads again (a second record), repeats an earlier command and is answered from its record (`replayed`, no content, no second record), and the attempt counts continue across the restart.
- **Listing in time order.** `reads` (and `attempts`) now list by time, then ID, with a cursor (`after` must be a `next` of the same listing, else `invalid_command`); before they were in ID order, which is a hash. The whole kind is scanned per call (one record per file read), as before.
- **Owner surface.** API query `meeting.desk-reads` (`occurrenceId`, optional `deskRecordId`, `after`, `limit` up to 500; returns the reads, `next` and the refused attempts; the service decides who sees what: the owner, the file's agent, the roster and chair). Status view `meeting_desk_reads` (listed to the interpreter from the one `STATUS_KINDS` table, so the owner asks in free words and the model sends the view): one line per read and per refused attempt, each citing its record, an empty answer saying "nothing read, or none of it is yours" for someone who may see none. Tested through the real API in the chat suite (owner, roster member, bad page size, unknown argument, missing argument) and in the new scenario (all four backends).

**Tests (reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker thread, PostgreSQL)**: `desk-reads.test.ts` 8 runs; `chat/setup-chat.test.ts` 5; the chat meeting-controls files (4 backends). Mutations made on the built files, each killed: chair check removed (all 8 runs fail), note `shared` check removed, inspection record not written, attempt count not accumulated, time ordering removed (3 of 4 backends fail; the fourth keeps the same order by chance of the ID hash, so the order is also pinned through paging), the attempt not recorded.

**NOT done (cannot be met offline or belongs to another card)**
1. **No chair exists.** `meetingRead` as a grant-less path is built and tested, but nothing in the controller runs a chair, absent-member detection (the service uses the meeting record's `attended` list), or calls these methods; M05 (floor control, owner inquiry, chair questions, notes, the question cap, "reads are listed in the meeting summary", "count against the chair-question cap", "the returning member can add a recorded correction", "reported as unverified", "revocable by the owner", "redacted excerpts with source links") is a large engine and is not built here. Those rules need the chair runtime.
