## U11d (integrity failures of the environment service reach the owner) (2026-11-14)

The last clause of card U11d: "hooks that report A08 integrity failures". The state API door, the swarm and route settings reads and the artifact and checkpoint digests were already hooked. Two places were not: the dispatcher's launch (`EnvironmentService.resume`, which throws `integrity` when the pinned environment revision is missing or has changed) and the maintenance applier's activation (`activate`, whose `integrity` error is caught and only rolled back). Neither goes through the state API, so the owner heard nothing.

- **What is built.** In `api/start.ts` the environment service is wrapped once with the existing `watchIntegrity` guard (place `environments`, methods `resume` and `activate`), and that wrapped service is the one handed to the dispatcher, to the maintenance applier and to `services.environments`. A failure raises the same report as the state API: source `integrity`, kind `integrity-check-failed`, key from `integrityKey` (the message with digits and long IDs removed, so no path or digest is sent), subject `store:environments`. The error and the call are unchanged; a failing detector changes nothing. The state API keeps the plain service: it already reports its own failures at its door, and an error told once is never told again (`TOLD_INTEGRITY`).
- **Tests.** `maintenance/environment-integrity.test.ts` (all four backends): a changed pinned revision seen three times (owner, agent, owner) is one report; a bad attempt ID (a refusal) tells nothing; an activation failed inside the real applier (worker reloaded with a different extension on disk) is one report with a key different from the first; a repeat of the rolled-back request, and a later change failing the same way, tell nothing new; a failing detector changes nothing for the caller. `api/start-integrity-environments.test.ts` (running controller, SQLite): the same two failures are exactly one Urgent item each in the owner's inbox, repeats add none.
- **Mutation checks (applied, seen failing, restored).** Wrong event kind (fails all); the guard swallowing the error (fails all); the key made unique per call (fails all); `resume` dropped from the guarded methods (the start test fails); `activate` dropped (the start test fails); `services.environments` handed the plain service (the start test fails). One survived and is accepted: renaming the place string in `start.ts` (the backend tests pin the format `environments:<hash>`, the start test does not pin the place).
- **Not done.** (1) No test drives the dispatcher's own launch call or the applier inside the running controller; both receive the same wrapped object the start test exercises, so what is proven there is the object, not the two call sites (the applier is proven with the guard in the backend test, the dispatcher's `resume` call only through the service). (2) The startup restore recovery is not hooked. (3) The rollback inside `EnvironmentService.rollback` calls its own `activate` internally and is not seen by the guard; its failure comes back as a `problem` result to the API, which does not raise it. Nothing else of card U11d's security list is open as far as the notes show. Not flipped.
- **ASSUMPTION:** one guard on the environment service in `start.ts` is the smallest change that covers both call sites; wrapping inside `EnvironmentService` itself was not chosen, to keep the service free of the notification layer.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the state API is left on the plain service because it already reports at its door and the dedup makes a double report impossible; handing it the wrapped one would change the key's place from `api:<op>` to `environments`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the startup restore hook, offered as optional, is left out: the restore path was not changed and its failure is already an owner-visible failed restore.

### U11d environment hooks, review (2026-11-14)

Reviewed `u11d-integrity` at b745befa after merging origin/main (27e8b4a8, no conflicts). The change is right as built: one guard on the environment service, handed to the dispatcher, the maintenance applier and `services`; the state API keeps the plain service and reports at its own door, and `TOLD_INTEGRITY` stops a second report when the same error passes through both. Access rules are unchanged (the guard only observes; members other than `resume` and `activate` are the service's own). The key is `environments:<hash>` and the subject `store:environments`: no ID, path, digest or secret. Rollback calls `activate` on the unwrapped service, so a failed rollback activation comes back as `problem` and is not reported; this is sensible, because in the applier it always follows the reported failure of the activation it undoes (the same worker damage), and an owner's own rollback shows the problem in its answer.

- **Added.** (1) The start test now restarts the controller on the same database and meets both failures again: still exactly two items (the detectors forget on restart; the Urgent watch tells one event once from the stored notification). (2) It pins the item's reference to the hash of `integrityKey("environments", …)`, so renaming the place in `start.ts` now fails (the one surviving mutation of the implementation) and checks the item holds no path or ID. (3) A second start test drives the controller's own maintenance applier (`maintenance.environmentRuntime`, owner approval through the API): the worker reloads with an extension the manifest does not name, the request fails and is rolled back as before, and exactly one Urgent item is raised. This proves the applier call site, not only the object. (4) The backend test checks that a detector that throws at once leaves the caller's error and a sound call's result unchanged.
- **Mutations on built files (each seen failing, restored).** Place renamed (both start tests fail); applier given the plain service (the new applier test fails); the guard reporting any error code (backend tests fail at the refused attempt ID); a throw from the detector escaping the guard (backend tests fail); the error rethrown as another error (all fail); the Urgent watch making a new item for a repeat it already holds (the restart part fails). One survived and is not a gap: a per-process command ID for the security item, because the item is also kept once per reference.
- **Still not done.** No test drives the dispatcher's own `#launchLimits` resume inside the running controller (it receives the same wrapped object; driving a pinned launch needs a full host). The startup restore stays unhooked, as the implementer recorded.

## U11d (the loader configuration and the sandbox launch signal) (2026-11-14, branch u11d-last)

The two clauses of card U11d that were still open: "a protected path touched" for the loader configuration (only Git's own data was reported), and a "containment violation signal" from the sandbox runtime itself (the only `sandbox-escape-attempt` was the host-side swap race of a workspace refresh).

- **Protected loader configuration (`protected-path-touched`).** New `worker/src/host/loader-watch.ts`: `lookAtLoaderConfig(paths)` fingerprints each path by content (its type, a digest of every file's bytes and every link's target, nested folders included; bounded at 2000 entries and 64 MiB) and `loaderChange(before, after)` names the difference as `linked`, `removed`, `added` or `changed`. The local host (`localWorkerParts`) has two new options: `loaderConfig: { paths }` (absolute paths, normally the controller-owned extensions folder) and `security` (the hook; `ownerPolicyOptions(services)` now passes the controller's `reportSecurity` as `security`, so every host built the usual way gets it). The host looks when an attempt's sandbox opens, after each turn (even a failed one) and when the sandbox closes; a difference from the last look is reported once as `protected-path-touched` with the key `loader:<kind>:<24 hex of a digest of the path number, kind and both fingerprints>` (no path, no content, no project path), then the new state is the baseline, so the same state is never reported again and a later attempt starts from it. The look and the report never change what the caller gets: a look that fails or exceeds the bounds says nothing, and a throwing or rejecting hook is dropped.
- **Sandbox runtime signal (`sandbox-escape-attempt`).** `SandboxError` has a new `containment` marker (`what`, and `id`, a digest of the path), set only by `normalizeRecipe` (the launcher's own check, so the same code runs for bubblewrap, Seatbelt and Windows) in two cases that only the agent's files can cause: (1) the host's own checkout, home or scratch folder for the attempt is itself a link (a leaf link; a link further up, such as a system's own temporary-folder link, is a configuration matter and carries no marker), (2) the checkout's protected `.git` entry is a link. The refusal is the same refusal with the same message as before; the local host reports it as `sandbox-escape-attempt` (key `sbx:<what>:<24 hex>`) from the place where the sandbox opens, the worker process launch and a contract check's launch. A read-only input a reach names that is a link is an ordinary refusal (those inputs are the host's own configuration), as is any missing path.
- **Tests.** `worker/src/host/loader-watch.test.ts` (7: writes, nested writes, additions, deletions, same bytes are not a change, folder or file replaced by a link, bounds, key shape, most serious kind); `worker/src/host/local-security.test.ts` (10: written during an attempt reported once at close, not again by the next attempt, removal and addition with their own keys, folder swapped for a link, a change in the middle of a turn reported at the turn's end with a throwing hook leaving the answer the same, no hook or no paths, `ownerPolicyOptions`, checkout/home/scratch links one key per place, `.git` link, a read-only input link and a missing place are not reported, the process launch and the contract check carry the marker); `controller/src/api/start-security-loader.test.ts` through the running controller with the host built from the controller's own services: a loader write is exactly one Urgent item, a checkout turned into a link tried three times is exactly one more, an ordinary refusal adds none, and neither the label nor the channel text holds a path or a file name. Link cases use a junction on Windows and skip where the system refuses to make a link; no pauses beyond waiting for a condition, no POSIX paths, no signals. The Urgent items' storage runs on all four backends in the existing notification and security suites (nothing here touches storage; the start test uses SQLite like the other start tests).
- **Mutation checks (applied to the built files, seen failing, restored).** Close no longer looks (4 failures); the per-turn look removed (1); the open-time look removed (5); the launch flag removed at the sandbox open (2), at the process launch (1) and at a contract check (1); the leaf-link rule dropped (1); the digest left out of the comparison so content changes are not seen (8); the baseline not updated after a report (5); a read-only input label counted as the agent's place (1, after a first mutation that missed the index and was redone).
- **What cannot be observed, and why (stated honestly).** Bubblewrap, Seatbelt and the Windows job refuse a write under a read-only mount, a path outside the allowed mounts and a connection outside the private network inside the confined process; the host does not see those refusals, and ordinary programs probe such places all the time (a package manager writing to a cache), so reporting them would only produce noise. A connection that does not go through the relay does not exist on a backend with a private network (nothing leaves), and a destination the owner did not grant is refused by the relay as a routine event. None of this is invented as a signal. What the host can see on every platform is what its own checks see before and after: the recipe checks above (a leaf link where the host made a folder) and the content of the loader configuration. The G05 containment suite remains the proof that the backends refuse writes and escapes; it is a release gate, not a runtime signal.
- **ASSUMPTION:** "loader configuration" means the controller-owned protected extensions the worker loads (`LocalEnvironmentRuntime`'s `extensions.directory`) and whatever else the embedder names in `loaderConfig.paths`; the repository has no other loader file. The embedder names the paths (the product's own host composition is not in this repository); the integration rigs do not yet pass `loaderConfig`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a change by content is reported however it was made, including an owner-approved update of the extensions while an attempt is open (rare; one Urgent item, told once). A replacement with the same bytes is not a change, and a change put back before the next look is not seen; both are named limits.
- **ASSUMPTION:** only a leaf link where the host made a plain folder (or the `.git` entry) is a containment marker. A link above it (macOS `/var`, `/tmp`) and any other launch refusal stay ordinary, so a mistaken configuration never pages the owner as an escape.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the optional integrity hooks (startup restore, the rollback's own `activate`) are left out: the startup restore's failure is already owner-visible as a failed restore and the rollback's activation failure follows the reported failure of the activation it undoes (see the environment-integrity review above).
- **Not done.** The remote worker executable does not name `loaderConfig` or wire `security` to `client.reportSecurity` (the hook and the client method exist); the Seatbelt and Windows backends have no signal beyond the shared recipe checks; the product host composition (outside this repository) must pass `loaderConfig`. Nothing else of card U11d's list is open as far as the notes show. Not flipped.

### Review of `u11d-last` at db798701 (2026-11-14, Claude agent)

origin/main (78bb815b) was already in the branch. Problems found and fixed, each with a test:

- **A named path that is a link was looked at only as a link.** An embedder naming a deployment's `current` link (or any link) as the loader configuration had only the link's target text fingerprinted, so a write behind it was never seen. A named (top) path that is a link is now looked at through it once (its target text and what it points to); links further down are still never followed, so a loop of links is one entry. Test: write behind a folder link and a file link is a change, the same bytes are not; a link inside the folder that loops back is one entry.
- **The bounds did not hold while the tree changed.** A file's size was taken from `lstat` and then read whole, so a file that grew between the two could be read far past 64 MiB; a folder's names were all read into memory before the entry bound applied. A file is now read in 1 MiB pieces and given up once the byte bound is passed (counted on what is read); a folder is read name by name and given up past the entry bound. The file is opened without following a link and without waiting, and checked to be a plain file after opening, so a file swapped for a link or a pipe between the type check and the open is not followed or waited on (a pipe already there is an entry of type `other`, by its type only). Tests: the byte bound across files, the name bound, a pipe in the folder, an unreadable folder says nothing.
- **The close looked before the attempt's process had ended.** A write made in the process's last moments (while it was told to close) was missed and, because the attempt was gone, never reported. The last look now runs after the process is closed (also when that close fails). Test: a played process that writes the loader configuration as it is told to close is reported at the close.
- **The running-controller test broke the package boundary.** `controller/src/api/start-security-loader.test.ts` imported `@nimblenewt/worker`, which `npm run check:deps` refuses for the controller. It is now `integration/src/u11d-security-loader.test.ts` (public exports only); since the inbox is not reachable from outside the controller package, each Urgent item is counted as the one message the channel is sent for it (a write: one message; a link tried three times: one more; an ordinary refusal: none; no path, file name or folder name in any message). Seen failing when the escape key was made different at each report.
- **Two looks of one attempt could cross.** A close during a turn's look ran a second look at the same time; if the older one finished last it set the older state as the baseline and the next look would report a change back that never happened. The looks of one attempt now run one after another. (No test: the crossing depends on disk timing; the mutation that removes the ordering survives, stated here.)

Checked and left as they are:

- **False positives.** An owner-approved extension update while an attempt is open, or an editor's swap or backup file created in the folder, is reported once (named in the ASSUMPTION above; a new entry inside the folder is `changed`). Touching a file, a same-bytes atomic replace, mode bits and a path that does not exist yet (until it appears) are not changes. A link higher up the named path (macOS `/var`) is resolved by the system and never seen as a link. A failed look (permission error, bounds, a file gone mid-read) never becomes the baseline, so it cannot flap. Two attempts open at the same time each report the same change; with the same baseline it is the same key, so one item.
- **Stated limits.** A change put back before the next look and a same-bytes replacement are not seen; both are written plainly above. A look on a disk that stalls (a hung network mount) delays the end of the turn or the close until the read returns; it never changes the answer.
- **The containment marker** is built only inside `normalizeRecipe` from fixed labels and a digest of the path; nothing from the agent's text reaches `what` or `id`, and only a `SandboxError` instance carries it (a message from the worker process is never one). Ordinary refusals (missing place, a read-only input link, a link higher up) carry none.
- **Remote worker.** It does not name `loaderConfig` (stated under Not done): it reports nothing for the loader configuration, which is a missing signal, not a wrong one.
- **What cannot be observed.** The argument above holds: the confined process's refusals are invisible to the host and routine; nothing is invented.
- **Mutations on built files (each seen failing, restored).** A named link not followed (the new link test fails); the byte bound removed (2 fail); the marker given to any label (the read-only input test fails); the hook's rejection no longer caught (the file fails); the close looking before the process ends (the last-moments test fails). Survived, not gaps that can be shown without timing or memory measurement: the name bound inside a folder removed (the walk's own entry count still stops it), the ordering of looks removed (above).

## M05 notes (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-14): meeting facilitation and owner control, offline slice

**What was lacking.** Meetings had a record (M06), desk reads (M05b), attendance (M04) and the owner's decision controls, but nothing ran a meeting: nobody decided who speaks, in what order, for how long, what the chair does between rounds, or what happens when the owner interrupts.

**Done.**
- `meetings/floor.ts` (`MeetingFloorService`): one unit of work at a time (claim, ask the model, store the reply, write to the record with fixed command IDs, commit). A crash repeats nothing and spends nothing twice. Blind first round (members answer alone, in parallel, up to `parallel`), then comment rounds, the chair's notes once, chair summary, reminders, an objection check that sees only the motion and the round summary, a chair ruling (proceed, amend, table), a fresh round after an amendment, the vote one ballot at a time (a voter is never shown another ballot; ballots are not transcript entries) and the chair's single casting vote on a tie.
- Pure rules in `floor-text.ts` (visible-token limit with a separate hidden-reasoning budget, cut at a word; shared-first prompts; facts-style summaries above 8 members with verbatim short statements; structural chair-question check; verbatim quote check; checkpoint answers wrapped by the controller as "not live"). Settings in `floor-settings.ts`, all `meeting.floor.*`, registered in `MEETING_SETTINGS` (chat and API through the configuration service) and per meeting with `meeting.floor.configure`.
- Chair desk read by a list of file IDs through M05b (one inspection per file, files read and quoted listed, an unquoted excerpt marked unverified, a member who comes in is asked for a correction).
- Owner commands (owner only; the chair, a manager or a member is refused): ask one agent (next safe boundary, nothing done is undone; an absent member answers from its checkpoint, stamped not live; nobody outside the roster), address the team (heard with each member's next turn; a voter who already voted is offered one revision turn, at most `maxRevisionsPerVoter`), amend the motion (fresh round and vote), open and end an inquiry, change priorities (agenda urgency), extend time or spend, configure, end the meeting.
- Inquiry: the meeting clock and turn limits stop, an open vote is held (record hold/resume), answers are held from the other voters and released at the close, an idle reminder after `inquiryIdleMinutes`, an open inquiry shows on the Needs-you list (`meeting.floor.needs-you`), it survives a restart.
- Timeboxes: time (without inquiry pauses) and model spend/tokens (the owner's own questions are recorded but not counted); at the end the motion is tabled with a reason and the rest becomes follow-up work; nonurgent agenda items not reached are batched to the next meeting; a blocked budget is reported to the owner.
- Chair questions with an owner-set cap, members may ask the chair for one, a member may challenge, the chair or the owner rules. Follow-up tasks (unanswered questions, unanswered chair questions, investigations, tabled research), once each, by stable command ID. A waiting-on view (person, agent or tool).
- API: `meeting.floor.*` operations. Chat: ask, address, inquiry-open, inquiry-end, priorities, extend, configure, start, follow-ups, end, each by the owner's own words (meeting by title words, agent by name); the interpreter prompt describes them and every setting key.
- Tests: `floor.test.ts` (33 scenarios, all four backends), `floor-text.test.ts`, two chat scenarios in `meeting-controls-suite.ts`. Mutation checks (apply a bug, see a test fail, restore): visible limit counting hidden tokens, owner-only check removed, answers not held during a vote, clock not paused in an inquiry, unverified quotes accepted, chair-question cap removed. All six were caught. One mutation (the cap check in the second place) survived because the same cap is checked twice; the first check was then mutated and caught.

**NOT done.**
- No model route has been wired to a real model: `options.meetingFloor.runner` is the port, and without it the floor says "unavailable". Nothing was measured against a real model (no local server was used). The M00 numbers (220 visible tokens, 800 hidden, 120 seconds) are the proposed defaults, not measured here.
- Hidden tokens are only known when the route reports them; otherwise they count as zero.
- Follow-up tasks carry the owner in their description ("Owner: agent:x"), because tasks have no owner field; they are not assigned.
- `checkpointOf`, `persona`, `deskNotes` and `budget` are ports with no production implementation yet. Release/recall of attendees during an inquiry (`work`) is a port, not wired to attendance.
- The loop that calls `advance` and `sweep` on a schedule is not wired; the owner or a host drives it with `meeting.floor.drive`.
- Priorities by chat resolve one agenda item at a time.

**ASSUMPTION lines.**
- ASSUMPTION: the owner has not formally accepted the proposals of `m00-meeting-experiments.md`; they are built as the defaults anyway, and each is a setting the owner can change by chat and API.
- ASSUMPTION: during an owner inquiry the owner's question text is visible to the other voters before the vote closes (smallest change; the answers are held, the questions are not).
- ASSUMPTION: a hang timeout records "no response" and the meeting goes on; a turn waiting on a tool shows as waiting on a tool and is tried again at the next advance.
- ASSUMPTION: the floor writes controller words as a service principal with `meeting.manage` and `meeting.read`; ballots, the casting vote and desk reads use the agent's own principal.
**M05 review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-14), after merging M06.** M05 and M06 were built at the same time and both carry a whole motion state machine (comment rounds, objection check, ruling, tabling, one ballot at a time, revision turns, casting vote) over the same M02 records. M06 was written expecting the floor to be its `MeetingFloor`/`ChairFloor` port; M05 instead runs its own. The records refuse a second ballot by one voter on one version, so no ballot is ever counted twice, but two drivers could write statements and rulings twice and race each other's votes. Fixed now: (1) the procedure refuses to begin on a motion the floor moved, and the floor yields (waits, writes nothing) on a motion that has a procedure; (2) a floor started without a motion only carries the owner's controls (questions, inquiry, address, priorities, timeboxes) and runs no rounds of its own, which is how the owner questions a meeting whose motion the procedure runs; (3) the floor's owner controls act on whichever vote of the meeting is open, not only its own: an inquiry holds (and later resumes) a vote the procedure runs, an answer to the owner is held from the voters while that vote is open and is released once, with a stable command ID, when no vote is open; (4) the owner's words through the floor (ask, address) get the procedure's check: words that repeat a cast ballot's reason while its vote is open are refused with a warning until sent with `acknowledged` true; (5) the four settings both cards have are one choice: the floor follows `meeting.rounds`, `meeting.objection.reruns`, `meeting.tabling` and `meeting.vote.maxRevisions` unless its own `meeting.floor.*` key was set on purpose, and the interpreter prompt says so. Other fixes: the chair (a voter) and a manager agent saw the whole floor state, including who had voted, the turn log and held answers' details; now only the owner, a host and a service do, the chair gets the member view plus its own notes, and the waiting-on view tells everyone else only that the meeting waits on the voters; `advance` no longer tells a manager agent whose ballot was taken. An inquiry opened while a ballot was being answered left the ballot unit failing on every advance and blocked the owner's own questions; the ballot is now set aside (its cost still counted) and asked again when the vote resumes. A model route's own error text (it can carry a host path or key) is no longer kept: the floor records "the model call failed", the hang timeout or the refusal code. A follow-up for an investigation is keyed by its content, not its place in a capped list. Address with an amendment is shown first in chat. Tests: `floor-review.test.ts` (all four backends); 9 deliberate breakages on built files, each caught.

**What should still be unified (not done in review: too large to do safely here).** One motion state machine, M06's `MeetingProcedureService`, with the floor as its `MeetingFloor` and `ChairFloor` port (bounded turns, the blind round, the chair's notes, questions, summary and desk read, timeboxes, the owner's inquiry). The floor's own rounds, objection check, ruling, vote and casting code (`#plan` phases `round` to `vote`, `#apply` cases `objection` to `casting`) and its four duplicate settings would then go. Until then a motion is run by one of them, never both. Still not wired in production: `notifyOwner` (a reached budget and the idle reminder reach the floor's notices, which the owner reads in `meeting.floor.state`, but no notification is sent), the sweep loop, the Needs-you list of the status service, and a chat command for the owner's overruling of a chair-question challenge (`meeting.floor.cq-rule` is API only).

## M06: meeting procedure, roster, quorum and ballots (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-14)

In plain words. M02 already kept the records of a meeting: the fixed roster, the quorum, hidden ballots, the tie rule, decisions. What was missing was the *procedure* that runs a motion through a meeting: the comment rounds, the objection check, tabling, asking each member for its ballot alone, the revision turns after an owner message, and the owner's controls over all that. M06 builds it as `MeetingProcedureService` (`packages/controller/src/meetings/procedure.ts`), a state machine kept in one record per motion (`meeting-procedure`, private, never a shareable citation) and moved one step at a time by `advance` (one member's turn, one answer, one ballot). Each step is saved before the next, so a restart carries on where it stopped and nobody is asked twice. The members and the chair are a port (`MeetingFloor`, `ChairFloor`) so the whole thing is tested with scripted members; the real floor control (bounded model turns, the baton, the owner's inquiry) is M05's runtime and is not wired here.

**Built to the m00 proposals as defaults.** The owner has not formally accepted the proposed changes in `m00-meeting-experiments.md`. ASSUMPTION: M06 is built to them as defaults and every one is a setting the owner can change by chat or API: tabling stays (`meeting.tabling`, default on); a meeting that looked like an echo is flagged (`meeting.echoFlag`, default on); seats prefer different model families, then different information (`meeting.seating`, `diverse` or `listed`, default diverse); two comment rounds (`meeting.rounds`, 1 to 5); the objection check at most two reruns (`meeting.objection.reruns`, 0 to 5); at most three revision turns per voter per vote (`meeting.vote.maxRevisions`, 0 to 10). All six are installation-only settings (the owner's alone), validated, shown to the owner first when set by chat and described to the interpreter in free words. The tie rule is the owner's decision already in the card (a casting vote by the chair, no double vote) and is M02's, untouched and not a setting; the procedure only asks the chair for the vote (`ChairFloor.castingVote`) and waits for the chair when there is none.

What each part does:

- **Rounds.** `rounds` comment rounds. Every present roster member has the floor once per round in seat order and is given the whole transcript up to its turn (read straight from the records by the service, so no ballot is ever in it: ballots are separate records). From round two the request says `deskCheck: true` (the member may check its desk and bring sources, passed through to the statement). A member absent when the record opened is skipped and recorded; one who joins the room before being asked is heard first. A member's reply that is empty, fails, or holds a credential-shaped text is recorded as no answer; the meeting never waits on it.
- **Objection check.** Each present member is asked once per run and receives only the motion version and the round summary (a plain, attributed digest built by the controller from the statements, `roundSummary`; the chair's own neutral summary with verified quotes is M05's). The answer is none, objection (reason) or needs time to research (what it would look into); an answer without its reason, no answer and a failed call are `no-response`: recorded, never blocking. An objection or a request for research enters the transcript. Any of them moves the procedure to `ruling` and holds the vote.
- **Ruling.** The chair or the owner rules with `rule`: `proceed` (the objections left are recorded as dissent, shown in the summary), `table`, or `uphold` with `addressed` clarify or amend (an amendment is a material amendment of the record, new version) after which the check runs again, at most `objectionReruns` times; after that uphold is refused and only proceed or table remain. A model chair, when wired, rules by itself; otherwise the procedure waits and says it waits for the chair. The chair may table only when a member asked for time to research and tabling is on; the owner always may. The check refuses a raw `openVote` by anyone but the owner while the procedure is not `ready` (the record's own `openVote` reads the procedure; the owner's own order to open the vote is the owner's ruling).
- **Tabling.** No vote, no ballot asked. Each request for research becomes an owned follow-up task (created through the project service and assigned to the member who asked) and the tabling reason carries the next step, so the record's hand-back defers the agenda item with its reason and next step (M03). Quorum and roster are unchanged. The owner can overrule a tabling (`overruleTabling`, chat "vote on it anyway"): the tabled motion stays on record, its wording and changes are moved again as a new motion (by the chair, else the original mover, as itself) and its procedure begins at the objection check.
- **Voting.** Each ballot is asked of one member alone, in seat order, and cast as that member (the record's own rule). Its delivery is the transcript, which holds no ballot (tested: no other voter's reason appears in any delivery). An owner message already in the transcript reaches a member that has not voted with its ballot request. Every voter who cast before that message is offered one revision turn (keep or revise with a reason; the short delivery is the ballot, the owner message and what was said since), at most `maxRevisions` per voter per vote; a revised ballot replaces the earlier one in the tally and the table keeps the history with its trigger (M02). The vote closes when everyone asked has answered and every revision turn is done, or when the vote's time is up. A held vote (owner inquiry) waits with `waiting.on: owner`. A tie asks the chair for the casting vote; with no answer the tie fails after the time (M02's sweep).
- **Amendment.** A material amendment through the procedure (`amend`) after the comment rounds starts a fresh pass: one comment round, a fresh objection check and a fresh vote; ballots on the old version are set aside by M02. A non-material change restarts nothing.
- **Owner's message and the warning.** `ownerMessage` (owner only) refuses a message that repeats a run of at least five words (three for a short reason) of a ballot cast in an open vote, with a warning that ballots stop being private; sending again with `acknowledged` goes through and says so. In chat the proposal is shown first and the owner says "send it anyway", then the interpreter sets `acknowledged`.
- **Echo and summary.** The summary has a `procedure` list per motion: rounds, fresh passes, objection runs, who was skipped, who gave no response, dissent from objections, a tabling with its follow-ups and the echo flag (three or more voters, every first-round stance known and equal, every ballot equal). Stances come from the member's comment reply (`stance`).
- **Seating.** `seatOrder` interleaves model families (largest group first, round robin), then information inside a family; with no trait known it is the roster's order. `traits` is supplied by the host (not wired by default).

**Owner and API surface.** Operations `meeting.proc.begin`, `advance`, `run`, `rule`, `amend`, `untable`, `owner-message`, `status`, `owner-controls` (the short prefix is because command names are limited to 28 characters). Begin, advance, run and amend are the controller's or the chair's; rule is the chair's or the owner's; untable and owner-message are the owner's alone; `status` shows the owner, hosts, services and the chair everything and shows a member or reader the stage, rulings and settings but not who has voted or the stances; an outsider sees nothing. Chat: `meeting.proc.rule` (motionTopic, ruling, text, reason, addressed), `meeting.proc.untable` (motionTopic) and `meeting.proc.owner-message` (meetingTopic, text, acknowledged), each found by the owner's words, always shown first, with their own proposal reasons; `ruling` and `addressed` are fixed choices exempt from the own-words check. The six settings and these commands are described in the interpreter prompt (a test checks every key is in it). The state API composes the service (`StartOptions.meetingProcedure` takes `floor`, `chair`, `actAs`, `traits`; settings are read from the installation layer each time a procedure begins).

**Tests.** `procedure.test.ts` (30 scenarios x 4 storage backends), `procedure-rules.test.ts` (6 pure), `api/start-meeting-procedure.test.ts` (composed controller: settings validated and owner-only, rounds from the setting, ruling by the chair only, tabling with an owned follow-up task, overrule, summary), `chat/meeting-procedure*.test.ts` (4 scenarios x 4 backends: rule, table and overrule by words, a message with a quoted ballot, access and proposal reasons), and the interpreter prompt test. Mutation checks, each seen failing on the built files and restored: see "Mutation checks" below.

**Not done / limits.**
1. **No real members.** Nothing asks a real model agent for a turn: that is M05's floor runtime (turn limits in output tokens, time and spend limits, the baton, direct questions, the chair's questions and notes, the inquiry period). The port is exercised only by scripted members; the composed controller has no floor unless a host passes one, and then `advance` says it waits for nobody.
2. **A member absent when the record opened stays absent.** The roster is fixed (M02), so a woken agent (M04h) can join the room and be heard in the comment rounds only if it is not in `withheld`; those woken after the record opened still cannot join (the known gap in M04h's notes) and have no ballot. Nothing here changes that.
3. **The chair's summary and quotes are M05's.** The objection check gets a mechanical round summary; the chair's neutral six-point summary with verified quotes is not built.
4. **Answers voters give the owner during a held vote** (kept out of other voters' deliveries until close) and the idle-inquiry reminder are M05 (the inquiry period). The hold itself, no ballots during it and the revision turns after it are built and tested.
5. **The interface warning is the refusal.** There is no console widget; the API and chat return the warning and the owner repeats the message to send it.
6. **One crash window.** A step writes its record entry and then saves its own state; a crash between them re-asks that member (a different text then meets the stable command ID and is treated as already recorded). The driver should keep one service identity so the derived command IDs match.
7. **Follow-up ownership is best effort.** The task is made first; if the assignment fails (for example the agent is retired) the task stays open and findable by its title and the failure is not raised.
8. **No settings in the console.** Settings are set by chat or `configuration` like the other meeting settings.

ASSUMPTION: the number of revision turns the owner may limit is counted per voter per vote (`meeting.vote.maxRevisions`, default 3) as the card says "at most one revision per owner message, with an owner-set maximum".
ASSUMPTION: a member that joins "before being asked" means joins the room (a presence entry) after the current round began and before its turn; it is then heard first, ahead of the remaining seats.
ASSUMPTION: after an upheld objection is addressed by an amendment, the check runs again straight away (the objection route), whereas a material amendment from anywhere else (owner message, procedural concern) starts a fresh single comment round, a fresh check and a fresh vote, as the card says for an amendment after the comment rounds. Both read the card; the first keeps the rerun count, the second resets it.
ASSUMPTION: the owner's open-vote command (the existing `meeting.record.open-vote`) is the owner's own ruling and bypasses the procedure's checks; everyone else is refused until the motion is ready.
ASSUMPTION: an overruled tabling moves the wording again as a new motion (the tabled motion cannot be reopened in M02), by the chair or the original mover; it keeps the tabled motion on record with a pointer to the new one.
ASSUMPTION: the round summary given to the objection check is built by the controller from the statements (first 160 characters each, attributed); a model summary would be M05's.

**Mutation checks (M06).** Each was applied to the built files, the targeted tests were run on the reference store, the break was seen failing, and the file was restored: the chair may table with no request for research (fails); the rerun limit ignored (fails); the revision cap ignored (fails); a member sees the vote's progress (fails); a no-response counts as an objection and blocks (fails); a member who joined is not heard first (fails); the vote opens round the procedure (fails); one comment round whatever the setting (fails); a quoted ballot is never noticed (the rules test fails); seating never mixes families (fails); the echo flag ignores stances (fails); anyone may overrule a tabling (fails); a material amendment starts nothing fresh (fails); no revision turn is ever offered (fails). One survived and is not a gap: removing the procedure's own "only the chair or the owner rules" check, because every ruling also writes a ruling entry or tables through M02's record, which refuses anyone else; the check stays as the clearer first refusal.

### M06 review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-14)

Reviewed `m06-impl` at 73b6ddf8 (already on origin/main 488c9252, nothing to merge). Problems found and fixed, each with a test:

1. **The chair saw who had voted.** `status` gave the chair the full view (who was asked for a ballot, who cast, who gave none, revision outcomes). The chair is usually a voter too, so it now sees what a member sees; only the owner, hosts and services see the vote's progress.
2. **The live summary named members who gave no ballot while the vote was open** (`procedure[].noResponse` included them). The summary is readable at any time by the meeting's readers, so they are now listed only once the motion's vote is over.
3. **An objection's reason and a member's stance were kept unchecked** in the procedure's own record (and from there in the ruling request, the dissent, the summary and the follow-up task's text). A credential-shaped reason now counts as no response and such a stance is not kept; control characters are folded to spaces.
4. **A model chair's ruling the rules refuse** (table with no request for research, uphold past the limit, unusable text) made every step throw, so `run` could never get past it. Such a ruling is now not taken and the vote stays held for a proper ruling; the chair's answer is reduced to the ruling's own fields.
5. **A material amendment made on the record itself** (`meeting.record.amend`, by the chair or the owner's chat) during the vote put the motion back to proposed, and the procedure then called the motion concluded and never voted on it. `advance` now notices the new version and starts the fresh pass (one round, a fresh check, a fresh vote), as the procedure's own `amend` does.
6. **The casting-vote request told the chair "0 yes, 0 no".** The counts of a tie stay unrevealed (M02), so the request now carries the motion and the deadline only. A tie whose casting time is over now fails at the next step instead of waiting for a sweep, and a casting vote the record refuses leaves the tie waiting instead of failing the step.
7. **Crash windows.** A revision turn answered before a restart was recorded as "no answer" afterwards (its stable command ID met the earlier revision); it is now recorded as revised. An upheld amendment written before a restart made the same ruling fail when repeated; it now goes on from the amended version without amending twice.
8. **Access.** The chair's own commands (begin, rule) now need the chair's credential to be in the meeting's project, as M02's own checks do. The surviving mutation in the notes above (removing the procedure's "only the chair or the owner rules" check) is now caught: a host or a manager upholding with an amendment would have gone through the record's own amend, which hosts may use; the test now refuses both and checks nothing was amended. Members are now also refused at the objection check and during the vote, where a step writes nothing in a member's name.

Also added: two controllers driving the same procedure at once (each statement and ballot written once, the motion concluded). Deliberate breakages on the built files, each seen failing and restored: the chair given the full view; the live summary naming who gave no ballot; the credential check on a member's short text removed; the record-amendment check in `advance` removed; a refused chair ruling thrown again; the tie deadline ignored; the revision conflict counted as no answer; the chair's project check removed; the open-vote gate in the record removed; `advance` open to members; the procedure's own ruling access check removed (the old survivor). The first attempt at the credential breakage (one of two checks) survived because the cut text is checked a second time; removing both failed the test.

9. **M06 broke an existing test (T05b, `api/start-mcp-conversation.test.ts`, every run).** The test's scripted model takes the first setting template in the interpreter prompt, and M06's paragraph, placed before the MCP door's, put its own generic template first, so the scripted model proposed nothing. The test now picks the door's own template by its key; the prompt itself is right (the order of paragraphs is not a contract). A real model reads the whole prompt and is not affected.

## K01c pre-upgrade snapshots and K03's rollback period (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-14)

What was lacking: the last open clause of K01c, "neither rule removes a pre-upgrade snapshot while K03's rollback period needs it". `chooseKept` kept every pre-upgrade snapshot for ever because K03 did not exist when it was written.

What is built, in plain words.
- `MigrationGuardService.preUpgradeNeed()` (K03's guard) says which snapshots the rollback period still needs: the period in days, `notBefore` (now minus the period), `since` (the earliest upgrade still inside its period) and `keepNewest` (a destructive migration is approved and not yet applied). It reads the guard's stored record, so a restart and a second controller on the same database give the same answer. `api/start.ts` hands it to both the backup service and the backup system (every target) through one function; until the guard exists, when its record cannot be read, or when no migration guard is wired, nothing is said and every snapshot is kept, as before.
- `chooseKept` (`backup/retention.ts`, new `Retention.preUpgrade`): with a need given, a pre-upgrade snapshot is kept only while it is needed (made inside the period, or the snapshot taken for an upgrade still inside its period and every later one, or the newest while a destructive approval waits). Every other snapshot falls under the daily and weekly counts and the age limit like any backup. The newest good (manual or scheduled) backup is still never deleted by any rule, and the newest backup of all stays. Targets use the same rule and a target that cannot be read still deletes nothing.
- What `release.rollback.check` reads: the tested pairs, the upgrade records, the migration list and the period (`judgeRollback`). It reads no snapshot: a release rolls back over additive migrations without one. The snapshot is the way back from a destructive migration ("restore the pre-upgrade snapshot"), and it is needed for the same period and while the approval waits, which is what is kept.
- Words: the answer to `retention.settings.set`, `backup.config.status` and the `retention.delete` confirmation (`backups.note`, new `backups.preUpgradeDays`) now say "a pre-upgrade snapshot is kept while the rollback period (N days after an upgrade) is open, whatever the counts and the age limit say; after that the counts and the age limit apply to it", or, without a guard, that it is never deleted here. The owner's `migration.policy.set` period is the one used.

ASSUMPTION: the only K03 approval that can be waiting is the owner's approval of a destructive migration not yet applied (`release.rollback` itself applies at once), so that is the one that keeps the newest snapshot. While it waits the newest snapshot stays whatever its age.
ASSUMPTION: a snapshot made inside the period is kept even when no upgrade was recorded for it (a start that failed before `noteStart`), so a fresh snapshot is never deleted before its upgrade is on record.
ASSUMPTION: an expired snapshot still takes a daily or weekly slot like any backup (as before), so it can stay on the counts; the age limit then ends it.
ASSUMPTION: a guard with no record at all yet (never started) says nothing, so every snapshot is kept.

Not done: the snapshot is not copied to targets (unchanged, K01c's earlier ASSUMPTION), so only a hand-placed copy on a folder target is affected there; Windows and macOS runs.

Mutation checks (built files, one at a time, restored): the guard ignored (10 failures), age limit sparing every snapshot (2), the period comparison reversed (10), the pending-approval rule ignored, the period shortened to one day, the anchor on the upgrade dropped, the start wiring not passing the need (results listed in the final report).

### Review of the pre-upgrade snapshot slice (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-14)

Found and fixed, each with a test on every backend:
1. **A policy record that could not be read shortened the period to the default.** `preUpgradeNeed()` used `effective()`, which falls back to the 14-day default when the policy read fails; with the owner's period at 60 days, a snapshot 20 days after its upgrade could be deleted during a passing storage fault. The need now reads the policy itself and throws when it cannot (the caller then keeps every snapshot); a damaged field in a record that was read still uses the default, as K03 does.
2. **An upgrade record with an unreadable time was taken as closed** (its comparison with NaN is false), while K03's own check treats it as open. The need now throws on it, so nothing is deleted on a guess. `since` and `notBefore` are written as plain UTC instants, so a record in another form still compares correctly with a backup's time.
3. **The retention runner (K06 `retention.run`) did not use the need**: it passes its own counts, which carry none, so it kept every snapshot while the backup run and the targets deleted expired ones, and its preview disagreed with them. `BackupService.rules` now adds the need in force to counts that come without one (none when the source fails), so all three apply one rule.

Checked and left: `release.rollback.check` (`judgeRollback`) reads pairs, upgrade records, migrations and the period, never a snapshot; the way back from a destructive migration is the snapshot (migration-recovery.md), and the destructive step is only approved after the period is closed, takes its own snapshot and is recorded as an upgrade, so that snapshot is kept for the whole period after it (tested with an owner-set 30-day period, then it goes). A target that cannot be listed deletes nothing; the same rule reaches every target. A clock moved far forward would let expired snapshots go early, as it already does for the age limit on every backup (not changed). On the first start of this release an installation's older pre-upgrade snapshots, kept for ever until now, fall under the counts and age limit once the guard has a record (by design of the card).

Deliberate breakages on the built files, one at a time, each seen failing in `backup/k01c.test.js` and restored: the policy read falling back to the default (4 failures); the damaged-time check removed (4); the runner's counts not given the need (4); the anchor on the upgrade's snapshot dropped (1); the waiting-approval rule ignored (5); the newest good backup no longer spared by the age limit (2); needed snapshots no longer spared by the age limit (14).
## M05 and M06 become one service (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-14)

**What was lacking.** Two services each ran a whole motion: the facilitated run (M05, `floor.ts`) and the meeting procedure (M06, `procedure.ts`) both did the comment rounds, the objection check, the ruling, tabling, the one-at-a-time ballots, the revision turns and the casting vote over the same records. The review had only put a guard so they never drove one motion together. The owner also had four settings twice (rounds, objection reruns, tabling, revisions per voter), and some owner controls were not reachable in free chat (start and step the procedure, ask where a motion stands, overrule a challenged chair question, what a meeting waits on), and some production wiring was missing (the owner was not told when a budget was reached or an inquiry was idle, nothing ran the meetings on a schedule, an open inquiry was not on the Needs-you list).

**Done.**
- **One state machine.** `MeetingProcedureService` is the only service that runs a motion. The floor (`MeetingFloorService`) is its members and chair: `floor.asMembers()` and `floor.asChair()` are the procedure's `MeetingFloor` and `ChairFloor`. The floor kept only what is specific to a facilitated meeting: bounded turns (visible-token limit, hidden budget, hang timeout), the blind first round (the other seats are asked at once and their answers are kept, spent once), the chair's notes, questions, desk read and verified summary (given to the objection check in place of the mechanical digest), direct questions between members, timeboxes and the owner's inquiry and questions. The floor's own phases, rounds, objection, vote, stances, amendments and casting code are gone (`FloorBody` shrank; its `phase` is now the procedure's stage as `state` shows it).
- **The seam.** The procedure asks the floor three extra things (all optional, so the plain M06 behaviour is unchanged): `before` (the floor's own work first, or a halt: an inquiry, a used-up time or spend timebox), `between` (the chair's work after a comment round, one step each time), and `setAside` (a ballot answered while an inquiry held the vote is not cast and is asked again). Every answer is stored on the floor before anything is written (`#cached`: claim, ask, store, apply), so a repeat after a restart spends nothing twice and writes the same words; a second driver meanwhile gets "busy". The procedure's own scheduled turn is `driveAll`.
- **Settings.** Retired from the floor: `commentRounds`, `objectionReruns`, `tabling`, `maxRevisionsPerVoter` (now only `meeting.rounds`, `meeting.objection.reruns`, `meeting.tabling`, `meeting.vote.maxRevisions`) and `freshRoundAfterAmendment`. At start the controller moves what the owner had stored under the old names (`ConfigurationService.migrateSettings(FLOOR_RETIRED_SETTINGS)`): a choice made under the old name becomes the new key unless the owner also set the new key (the newer choice stays); `commentRounds` 0 becomes 1; the old keys are removed so the layer holds no key nobody knows; safe to repeat.
- **API.** Every operation name is kept (`meeting.floor.start` now moves the motion and begins its procedure; `advance` and `drive` do the floor's own work, then one procedure step). `meeting.floor.configure` no longer accepts the five retired names. New: `meeting.floor.tick` is not an operation (the loop calls it); the Needs-you answer kind `meeting-inquiry` (`needs-you.answer`, answer `done`) ends an inquiry.
- **Chat.** New owner controls, each found by the owner's words and shown first: `meeting.proc.begin`, `meeting.proc.advance`, `meeting.floor.cq-rule` (the challenged chair question is found in the meeting; several ask which). New reads answered at once: status kinds `meeting_procedure` (where a motion stands) and `meeting_waiting` (what a meeting waits on), the motion or meeting found by words, an unclear one asks. The interpreter prompt describes all of them and no longer lists the retired keys.
- **Production wiring (`api/start.ts`).** The floor and procedure are composed when a model route is given (`options.meetingFloor.runner`). The owner is told through the notifications service when a model budget is reached, when an inquiry opens and when it has been idle; the notices are closed when the inquiry ends. A scheduled sweep `meetings.drive` calls `floor.tick` (reminds an idle inquiry, gives each running meeting a few steps) and the procedure's `driveAll` for meetings the floor does not run. An open inquiry is on the Needs-you list (kind `meeting-inquiry`, one choice: `done`).
- **Guarantees kept.** Ballots are never in a transcript; the chair sees what a member sees while a vote is open (nobody but the owner, a host or a service learns who has voted or whose ballot is next); answers to the owner are held while a vote is open and released once the vote closes (also when the last step closed it); credential-shaped text is refused by the procedure's own checks; an owner's inquiry holds the procedure even when it is driven alone; the timebox holds it too.
- **Tests.** `floor.test.ts` (34 scenarios, all four backends), `floor-review.test.ts` (5), `floor-text.test.ts`, `floor-migration.test.ts` (settings move), `procedure.test.ts` (one expectation widened: the objection request carries routing fields, never a transcript or a ballot), `meeting-integration` chat suite (5 scenarios, four backends), `api/start-meeting-floor.test.ts` (the running controller: the loop finishes a motion, the inquiry notice, the Needs-you item, the reminder). Mutation checks (apply a bug, see a test fail, restore): inquiry hold in `before` removed; the used-up-timebox hold removed (survived: the floor's wrap-up runs first and covers it, so the hold is only a second line); the clamp of 0 rounds removed; absent members no longer skipped; the non-owner view returned in full; held answers not released after the closing step; ballot answers not stored; chair-question ruling no longer asking which. Seven were caught, one survived as said.

**NOT done.**
- No real model was used and no local server was touched; nothing was measured with real models. `options.meetingFloor.runner` is still the port (a worker's bridge in production is not part of this work).
- The settings migration is tested on its own with the old keys defined in a test; the running-controller test does not seed an old key (a started controller cannot be given a key it no longer defines).
- `checkpointOf`, `persona`, `deskNotes` and `budget` are still ports with no production implementation. Release/recall of attendees during an inquiry (`work`) is still a port.
- A meeting whose floor was never started is driven only by the procedure's own scheduled turn, which asks the members through the floor only when a model route is configured.
- Windows and macOS were not run here (Linux only); the new tests wait on conditions and use no fixed pauses, signals, POSIX-only paths or machine speed.

**ASSUMPTION lines.**
- ASSUMPTION: the procedure's rules win where the two services differed: an amendment made by a chair's ruling reruns the objection check only (no new comment round), and a fresh pass (one comment round, a fresh check and vote) follows only an amendment of the motion itself (the owner's `address` with `amend`, or the record's own amend).
- ASSUMPTION: revision turns are the procedure's (one per owner message after the ballot, up to `meeting.vote.maxRevisions`), so the floor's `revisionsOffered` is always 0; the owner's control notes (inquiry opened or ended, priorities) are written as the owner's rulings, not owner messages, so they do not by themselves cost a voter a revision turn.
- ASSUMPTION: the first-round "chair-match" step (does the objection match the motion) is dropped; the procedure's ruling covers it.
- ASSUMPTION: a floor started with no chair means an objection waits for the owner's ruling instead of going straight to the vote. With a chair that can rule, the check hands over to the chair's ruling at once (nothing waits).
- ASSUMPTION: a member who has not come into the room is skipped (nothing asked, one line in the transcript), as the floor always did; the procedure counts the missing answer as no response.
- ASSUMPTION: the four duplicate settings move to the procedure's keys and not the other way, because the procedure's keys are the ones the owner already used for every motion.
- ASSUMPTION: the idle-inquiry reminder repeats every idle period (once per period), and the notice about an open inquiry is closed when the inquiry ends.

### M05/M06 integration review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-14)

Reviewed `m56-unify` at 0005f615 after merging origin/main ac4c65a6 (clean merge). Problems found and fixed, each with a test in `meetings/floor-unify-review.test.ts` (9 scenarios, all four storage backends):

1. **A motion begun without the floor got no real answers.** With a model route the procedure's members are always the floor, but the floor only answered for a meeting it had been started on. A motion begun with `meeting.proc.begin` (the new chat control) and driven by the procedure's scheduled turn therefore asked nobody: every comment, objection answer and ballot was recorded as no response and the vote opened on an empty discussion. The floor now puts itself on such a meeting the first time the procedure asks (as `meeting.floor.start` without a motion does, stable command ID, safe for two drivers); from then on the floor's own turn runs the meeting and the procedure's turn skips it.
2. **A manager agent learned who voted.** `meeting.floor.advance` and `drive` passed the procedure's step text through ("agent:x cast its ballot", "agent:y did not answer"). While the vote is open only the owner, a host and a service get it; anyone else gets "a step of the vote".
3. **A voter waiting on a tool was named.** A ballot turn that waits on a tool set the floor's tool wait with the voter's name, which the waiting-on view (and `meeting_waiting`) showed to members and the chair. While the vote is open, no agent or tool wait is shown with its agent to anyone but the owner, a host or a service.
4. **A revision turn set aside by an inquiry was not asked again.** The set-aside forgot the wrong stored answer (the key lacked the owner message), so after the inquiry the answer given before it was cast. The aside now names the owner message.
5. **An inquiry landing just as a ballot was cast lost that ballot.** The record refused the cast (the vote was held a moment before) and the procedure recorded the voter as giving no ballot, never to be asked again. Such a ballot (or revision) is now set aside and asked again when the vote resumes.
6. **The scheduled turn `meetings.drive`.** (a) It makes model calls but ran inside the dispatcher's tick: it now runs apart from the tick like the resume checks (`apart`). (b) It drove every running meeting each turn with no bound: now at most 20 meetings (`floor.tick` `meetings`) and the procedure's 50 procedures a turn, each going on from where the last turn stopped, so all are reached however many finished procedures are kept (before, the procedure's look stopped after 12 pages, so procedures beyond the first 1,200 would never have been driven). (c) It ignored archived projects: an archived project's meetings are now held (nobody asked, nothing spent, no reminder) until it is restored, read fresh each turn like the other loops (card P06). (d) A meeting closed by other means (the record's own finish, its lease) left its floor running with an open inquiry: the owner was reminded every idle period forever and the Needs-you item could not be ended ("the meeting is closed"). The turn now ends such a floor and closes its notices, and the owner's "done" for it is accepted.
7. **A second inquiry in the same meeting told the owner nothing** (the notice's command ID was per meeting). Each inquiry's notice is now its own.
8. **The integration broke an existing test (T02c, `api/api.test.ts`, every run of shard 3).** The two new status kinds `meeting_procedure` and `meeting_waiting` were not described in `status.ask`; they now are (`api-v1.md` regenerated).

Checked and found sound: one state machine (the floor writes no statement, ruling or ballot of its own; it moves the motion, tables a proposed motion at the timebox and amends through the record, which the procedure turns into a fresh pass); replies stored before anything is written, claims and `busy` for a second driver, restart repeats nothing; the chair and members see the member view; the settings migration (installation layer only, an old value never overrides a new key, out-of-range or wrong values dropped, 0 rounds becomes 1, second run is a no-op, a concurrent start leaves it to the next); owner-only access on the new controls (Needs-you `meeting-inquiry`, `cq-rule` owner or chair, procedure begin/advance service-level); the interpreter prompt names every new control and no retired key; no route error text kept.

The surviving mutation of the implementer (the used-up timebox hold) is now caught: a timebox used up during an open vote must ask no further ballot or revision turn (new scenario). Deliberate breakages on the built files, each seen failing and restored (reference store): the timebox hold removed; the floor not put on by itself; the floor's archived fence removed; the procedure's archived fence removed; the manager's step text unmasked; the tool wait unmasked; the revision aside key reverted; the cast-race aside removed; the closed meeting not ended; the turn's cursor removed; the per-inquiry notice key removed. All 11 caught.

Not done / left as is: a draft (staged, not applied) owner change under a retired key is not migrated; its apply is refused naming the key and the owner stages it again. Floors left mid-motion by the old floor code (before this change) are not converted (no installation has run them). `openInquiries`, `ownerPending` and the reminder sweep still read every floor record (one page loop each), as before. Windows and macOS were not run; the new tests wait on conditions with `setImmediate`, use the suite's manual clock and no paths, signals or pauses.

## K01d (finish): backup scope tiers (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

**What was lacking.** K01d's blockers (K01c, K06b) are built, and nothing of the card itself existed: a backup always held every record of the store, so a long-lived installation's backups grew with scratch output, old chat words and message logs that the owner may not want to keep copying. The card wants: optional, off by default; audit and decisions always in, and anything a resumable task or replay refers to; a restore that says what was left out instead of looking complete; the live retention unaffected; the change owner-only and recorded.

**What is built.**
- `backup/scope.ts`. Three tiers, each a number of days (7 to 3650) or `null` (off, the default): `scratchDays` (private scratch, desk records only their agent reads, of a task that is done or cancelled, not changed for that long), `transcriptDays` (the words, plan and answers of chat turns completed that long ago) and `logDays` (records of messages to the owner that were delivered that long ago). The tiers reuse the live retention rules' own definitions of who is a candidate (same states, same age field), so the two systems agree about what "old scratch" is.
- Always kept, by construction: the writer only ever looks at three kinds (`LEAVE_OUT_KINDS`: desk-record, chat-turn, notification-delivery, pinned by a test), so the audit log, decisions, and every table other than `aggregates` (operations, deliveries, effects, timers, state) are written whole. On top of that every candidate is checked with `RetainedMaterial` (the live retention's own "what a resumable task or a replay needs" scan, run over the SAME snapshot the backup is written from, through a small adapter that reads the snapshot's `aggregates` rows in key order). A record it names is written whole and counted as `heldBack`. A decision's source turn is kept (the transcripts check). If that scan cannot finish (more than the bound of records), nothing at all is left out and the backup says so.
- The writer (`write.ts`, option `leaveOut`) works out the plan before writing a file and applies it to the `aggregates` pages: scratch and delivery records are not written, a chat turn is written as an empty shell (ID, the message it answered, state and times kept; text, plan and outcomes gone, marked `retention.rule: "backup-scope"`), so a message sent again after a restore is still answered as the turn it was (the same reason live retention leaves a shell). The manifest gets `contentScope` (the rules, a line per kind with how many were left out, stubbed and held back, whether the reference check finished, and a plain statement), the statement is also in the manifest's `notes`, and so under an encrypted backup's MAC and a signature like every other field. `backup.list` / `backup.now` items carry `notFullCopy` and `recordsLeftOut`.
- `BackupService` option `scopeSource`, read at each manual or scheduled backup. Safety copies (before an upgrade, before a restore) and pre-upgrade snapshots are always whole. A source that throws gives a whole backup, never a narrower one.
- A restore says what was left out: `RestoreResult.leftOutByScope` and a note, the command line prints "NOT A FULL COPY: n records were left out", the staged restore's plan carries `leftOutByScope` and a warning that starts with "NOT A FULL COPY" (shown to the owner in the chat's restore plan too), so the owner is never told the restored data is complete when it is not. A restore does not bring left-out records back.
- Owner-only and recorded: `BackupScopeSettingService` (record `backup-scope-setting/main`), operation `backup.scope.set` (one op-table entry; the current value is in `backup.config.status` under `scope`), always a proposal in chat (`chat/commands.ts`), described in the interpreter prompt (free wording, no phrase needed; whole-number days or null; says plainly that a restore from such a backup is not a full copy). A change is checked (days 7 to 3650 or null, at least one field, no unknown field), revision-checked, applied once per command ID, written to the audit log with the owner as actor and the old and new values, and announced in the owner's inbox ("Backups now leave out more" at the notification's default level, "less" as a plain notice). An agent, with any grant, is refused for both reading and changing.
- Live retention is untouched: nothing is deleted from the running store (a test checks the live records after a scoped backup).
- Tests: `backup/k01d-scope.test.ts` (all four storage backends: off by default, every tier with every protected case, each tier alone, restore report and what comes back, the setting service, `BackupService` including safety copies and a failing source; plus the reference check that cannot finish) and `api/start-k01d.test.ts` (the running controller: free wording through the interpreter stand-in, shown first, applied on agreement, audit, `backup.list`, restore preview warning, an agent refused). `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.

**The K01 leftovers named in these notes ("nightly VACUUM INTO blocking the tick", "taking the blob lock first", "per-version snapshot column list")** are already built and tested on main (K01e first, second and fourth parts and K01f first part: the nightly run is not awaited by the tick, `createBackup` takes the artifact store's shared lock before the snapshot, snapshots read the columns the database has, SQLite snapshot copies on a worker thread). Their tests (`api/start-backup.test.ts`, `backup/backup.test.ts`, `storage/sqlite/snapshot-columns.test.ts`) pass unchanged here; nothing was left to do for them.

**NOT done, and why.**
- Only three kinds can be left out. Other bulk kinds (tool operation records, generation runs, agent messages and conversation threads, dispatch records, meeting entries, activity steps) are not offered; each needs its own reference rule (a replay cites tool operations and messages) and is a small card of its own. Audit and decisions can never be offered, by design.
- The `operations` table (the record of every command's result, kept for repeat detection) is written whole, so text that a command's result echoed is still in a backup after the record itself was left out. The card names audit and decisions as always-in; the operations table is treated as part of that safety net (a repeated command must be recognised after a restore).
- Summaries and other records derived from a left-out scratch record are kept in full (live retention removes derived copies with their source; the backup scope does not rewrite other records), and they may name a record that is not in the restore.
- A restore does not bring left-out records back from anywhere; the owner's own older, whole backup, if one exists, is the way, and the statement says so. No tool exists to merge two backups.
- No preview of what a scope would leave out before it is set (a backup answers it afterwards, in its statement). No separate per-project scope.
- A scope applies from the next backup; backups already made, and copies on other targets, are not rewritten.
- Windows and macOS runs come from CI only (the new code uses no signals, shell or file-name assumptions beyond the existing backup paths).

**ASSUMPTION:** the three tiers are scratch (private desk records of finished tasks), transcripts (chat turns) and logs (delivered message records), the same three the live K06b tiers name; the card's "logs, scratch output and transcripts" reads that way.
**ASSUMPTION:** age is the live rule's own age field (last change for scratch and delivery records, completion time for a turn), and the same 7-day minimum and 3650-day maximum as the live rules; a smaller value would leave out material that agents may still be reading.
**ASSUMPTION:** a left-out chat turn stays as an empty shell (as the live rule does) and the other two kinds are not written at all (as the live rule removes them), so a restore never mistakes a shell for the real words and never loses the idempotency of a repeated message.
**ASSUMPTION:** the backup scope is owner-announced like encryption (an inbox notice), because leaving data out of the copy is something the owner should see even when it was their own token that did it.
**ASSUMPTION:** when the reference check cannot be finished, or the setting cannot be read, the backup is whole (the safe direction), and says so.

**K01d review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-15).** Branch on base 8851bed6 (origin/main had not moved; no merge needed). Read against the card, the live K06b retention rules and `RetainedMaterial`.
- Checked and sound: the candidate rules match the live K06b rules (same states, same age fields, same held/follow-up turn exclusions); the live scratch rule's filter of the "written for task <own task>" reason is not needed here because that reason only applies to tasks that can still resume, and the backup reads the task state from the same snapshot. The writer's page cursor follows the raw page, so a page whose rows are all left out still moves on. Snapshot tables are flat (no row of another table depends on an `aggregates` row being present).
