## L04d (follow-ups): the check follows the attempt's own checkpoint, captures keep one identity, old captures are pruned, and a turn is captured after its usage is charged (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

What was lacking: four offline items from the L04d finish review's "what is left" list. Areas touched: `continuation/` and `dispatch/dispatcher.ts` only.

**Built**
- **A capture is found by its checkpoint (`continuation/continuation.ts` `forCheckpoint`).** The task's head now keeps a short list of its newest captures (`recent`: record ID, order, complete or not, checkpoint digest; at most `CONTINUATION_KEEP` = 50). `forCheckpoint(by, taskId, digest)` returns the newest complete capture with that digest, never an incomplete one, with the same read right as `latest`. A head written before the list existed (`recentFrom` absent or above 1) is scanned like `history` (pages of 500, at most 20 reads) for the older captures.
- **The resume check follows the attempt's own `resumeFrom` (`continuation/resume.ts`, `dispatch/dispatcher.ts`).** `resume.start` takes an optional `checkpointDigest`, kept on the check. Collecting, verifying and every later verification use `#target`: the complete capture of that checkpoint if there is one, else the task's latest complete capture (as before). So the check and the resume record name the capture the attempt really restores, and a newer capture no longer makes such a check stale. The dispatcher passes the digest of `resumeFrom.pi`; the check's key now includes it (a check of that kind has its own key family, so a check started by an older controller is not replayed with different content: it is cancelled as stale and a new one starts). `capturedCheckpoint` tells the dispatcher whether the checkpoint has its own capture: then the "no complete capture" step in the activity is not written; when it has none, the step is told as before and the check falls back to the latest.
- **Identity of an earlier incomplete capture (`identityOf`, `host-capture.ts`).** The head's identity is fixed by the first capture of any kind, but the host recorder took its identity from the latest complete capture, so after an incomplete first capture (an owner's capture with another identity, a checkpoint that did not read back) every host capture used `task:<id>` and was refused as a different identity. The recorder now asks `identityOf` first (best effort, from the real service; no composer change was needed because the service already has the method).
- **Pruning.** Each capture that would take a task above 50 records deletes the oldest ones in the same write, never the latest complete capture (it stays however many incomplete ones follow), with an audit entry `continuation.pruned` for each deleted record. No scan is needed because the head's list names the oldest. A repeat of a resume command recorded against a pruned capture answers `not_found` ("has been pruned") instead of failing on a missing record.
- **A turn is captured after its usage is charged (`dispatcher.ts` `#run`).** The turn-complete capture used to run before the turn's usage was charged, so its budget figures (spent and remaining) were one turn behind. Usage is charged first now; both still happen before the attempt's next step is written.
- Tests: `continuation/checkpoint-lookup.test.ts` (5 tests; 20 with the 4 backends) and `dispatch/resume-checkpoint-follow.test.ts` (3; 12 with the backends).

**Mutation checks** (built, run, restored): no pruning (4 fail); pruning may take the latest complete capture (4); an incomplete capture offered by checkpoint (4); the check ignoring the named checkpoint (4); the recorder ignoring the identity (4); the dispatcher not passing the digest (8); the step said even when the checkpoint has its own capture (4); the capture made before the usage (4).

**Suites** (all pass): continuation 86, dispatch 1540, api tests mentioning continuation or resume 175, other users of the service (chat resume, branches, handoff sources and hops, compaction lineage) 75. No flakes seen.

ASSUMPTION: 50 records per task is the keep limit (smallest change that bounds growth; one constant, `CONTINUATION_KEEP`). It leaves ample history for the checkpoints a long task needs to resume from.
ASSUMPTION: heads written before this change are not pruned retroactively (their older records stay; only captures made from now on enter the list and can be evicted). A bulk delete of old records is a data operation for the owner, not done silently.
ASSUMPTION: a check that names a checkpoint with no complete capture falls back to the latest complete capture instead of blocking (the earlier decision, unchanged: Pi verifies the checkpoint itself on the host).
ASSUMPTION: a check in progress whose capture is pruned meanwhile (more than 50 newer captures during one check) fails its commit with `not_found` and is retried by the dispatcher; not tested, because it needs 50 captures in the middle of one check.

**Not done**
- The state-API operation for the reviewer's daily cap (left out on purpose: it touches the operation table another agent owns).
- Everything else on the earlier L04d lists is unchanged: a real Pi process through capture and resume, remote hosts' view of search/external/MCP-resource dependencies, the probe reading the task's own worker checkout, a reviewer that reads diffs, compaction lineage in production, pending effects and scratch records in host captures, the reviewer's model call not being cancellable by the dispatcher, the remote hosts' resume path, a real model. The card stays planned (not flipped).
- Windows/macOS: nothing here uses paths, signals or timing; the tests wait on conditions only (no fixed pauses).

**Review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15).** No defect found in the code. Checked: the commit records the resume against the capture the check verified (`continuationId` is passed), so the check and the resume record name the same capture; the digest patterns of `resume.start` and the dispatcher accept every digest `capture` accepts; the composer passes the real service (with `forCheckpoint` and `identityOf`) to both the resume check and the host recorder; branches already treat a missing capture as invalid; retention has no hold that pruning would skip; the usage charge is awaited before the turn-complete capture; a check left under the key from before this change is cancelled as stale by the existing "another check in progress" step. Tests added to `continuation/checkpoint-lookup.test.ts`, because three claims were not exercised: a newer capture between a check's review and its commit does not make a check of an older checkpoint stale (it was only stated in a comment; the test committed before the newer capture), while a check that names no checkpoint still goes stale; every pruned record has its `continuation.pruned` audit entry (task, keep limit, never another task's record); repeating a resume command whose capture was pruned answers `not_found` ("pruned"); a caller without the right gets nothing from `capturedCheckpoint`. Mutation checks on the built files, each caught (4 failures, one per backend): the check ignoring the named checkpoint, no audit entry, the pruned-repeat guard removed, the latest complete capture prunable, the recorder ignoring the kept identity, an incomplete capture offered by checkpoint, `capturedCheckpoint` without its authorization.

**Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-15).** No defect found in the code. One test gap closed: the verifying phase's search for earlier effects of unknown outcome could look at the task's latest capture instead of the checkpoint's own capture without any test failing; `checkpoint-lookup.test.ts` now asserts that the missing-context and uncertain-effects checks are both handed the checkpoint's own capture. Mutation checks on the built files, each caught (4 failures, one per backend) after that addition: the scan of a head from before the list removed; `recentFrom` always 1 (an old capture lost after the head starts its list); the keep limit off by one; the verification before commit following the latest; the effects check following the latest; the collecting phase following the latest. Checked by reading: nothing dereferences a pruned capture unsafely (branches check on open only, handoff sources and `latest` read the latest complete one, which is never pruned, retention only scans what exists); two controllers capturing at once conflict on the head's revision and the loser rebuilds, so a record is never pruned twice. Noted, not changed: for a head from before the list, `forCheckpoint` of a digest not in the list scans every task's continuations (at most 10,000 records) on each call; it is bounded and only affects older heads. Suites: continuation 86 of 86, dispatch 1540 of 1540, the two new files 32 of 32 (4 backends), `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard.

Documentation only: no product code changed. The card asked for architecture, contribution, protocol, troubleshooting and notices; examples that match the current API; dependencies and licenses inventoried; security reporting and compatibility support documented; flush guarantees for process crash, orderly shutdown and power loss; and the rule that a component that is not TypeScript needs a recorded justification, bounded interface and maintenance plan.

- `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs` (runs with the other script tests, no database needed): every link and heading anchor in the ten files resolves; every backticked repository path, `npm run` script, `node scripts/...` program, `--flag`, `NIMBLENEWT_` variable, dotted operation or setting name and snake_case code exists in the repository (operations against the generated `api-v1.md`); the guides repeat the supported environments (Node, PostgreSQL, builds, file systems, git, override switches, MCP revisions, pinned Pi Durable) exactly as `supported.ts`, `mcp.ts` and `runtime.ts` list them; the durability guide matches the settings the storage code enforces (it fails if SQLite's `synchronous = FULL`, PostgreSQL's flush checks or the artifact store's file flush change); SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md have the required parts; every non-TypeScript file in the repository is accounted for in CONTRIBUTING.md; the license guides list the same allow-list as `license-inventory.mjs`.

**What the guides found and say plainly.**

Not changed here (code and generated reference are out of scope); recorded as a known inconsistency for the owner of `api-v1.md`.
- Pi Durable's own conversation store stays at SQLite's default `synchronous = NORMAL`: after power loss its last moments can be lost. The controller's records are not affected. ### D02 review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15)

Checked every factual statement in the ten guides against the code (two read-only passes plus spot checks), ran the D02 tests, and made nine deliberate breakages of my own (built conversation code, guide examples, guide facts, adapter source), each caught by a test and restored.

**Fixed in the guides.**
- Agent history durability was wrong. The agent process opens Pi Durable's **JSONL** store (`pi-adapter/src/worker/process.ts`) with default options, under which nothing is flushed (`fsync` off); it is not a SQLite store, and the `synchronous = NORMAL` the guide cited is set by Pi Durable's SQLite adapter (SQLite's own default is FULL), which NimbleNewt does not use. After a power cut the history can lose more than its last moments and may be found damaged, because unflushed appends need not reach the disk in order. The durability and security guides now say so.
- Pagination was wrong: the list ends when an answer has **no `next`** (a short last page has none, `security/secured.ts`); a page can be short or empty while `next` is present; a full last page still carries `next`. A short-page example was added.
- Smaller corrections: Node 24.21.0, macOS and Windows run in the exhaustive and QA runs, not on every push (the same wording is in `environment/supported.ts`'s evidence text, left for its owner); Linux on ARM added to "not supported"; nothing prints the environment at start-up; HTTP 404 on `/mcp` cannot mean "listener not running"; exit 76/77 are believed from an unproven release only `hostRetries` times; `status` writes a starter configuration; only the supervised controller has a default backups folder; `/mcp` answers bad JSON as JSON-RPC and 403 for a foreign `Origin`; the listener's own error codes listed; `integration` may not depend on `registry`, `ui` or `api`; the MCP SDK is a test-only dependency; `pi-telemetry` comes with `pi-ai`, not `pi-durable`; the protected secret file does not flush its directory; artifact temporary files live in `tmp/`, wrong bytes are refused on read and replaced on the next store; backups are folders; crash tests cover the four main write paths on the three durable stores; SQL is also allowed in `storage/qualification/`; network-mount detection is best effort outside Linux and can be overridden; owner token storage, enrolment with owner-given grants, refusal timing at the listener, license check on full runs (not every build), offline guard scope, package approval paths, the model address check on hand-edited files, the web chat's private-address mode and the remote-worker listener.

**Fixed in the tests.** `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs`'s check that the adapter sets no Pi flush mode could never fail (it searched for "pi-durable" in a string made only of `PRAGMA synchronous` matches); it now checks that the agent process opens the JSONL store with default options, that Pi Durable's JSONL store defaults to no flush, and that no adapter source turns flushing on or opens the SQLite store. `api/d02-guidance.test.ts` matched answers as a subset, so a missing `next` could not be checked; a list answer the guide shows without `next` now must have none, and the guide must show both ways a list ends.

**Verified, for the owner of `api-v1.md` (not edited).** Its sentence "A thing it may not read reads exactly like a thing that does not exist" (generated from `api/docs.ts`) is true only in that the two cannot be told apart. For projects (`project.get`, `project.update`, `task.create`, `task.list` with a project) a non-owner gets `forbidden` "<principal> may not <action> in <projectId>" for a real and a made-up ID alike (`security/access.ts` `requireAction`, no existence lookup); for tasks (`#hide` in `security/secured.ts`) a non-owner gets `forbidden` "may not read that" for both, and only the owner sees `not_found`. Operations whose text says "not found" (thread reads, jobs, deliverables, meetings and others) do answer `not_found` for both; conversation writes answer `forbidden` for both. Suggested wording: existence is never revealed; projects and tasks answer `forbidden` both for one you may not read and for one that does not exist (only the owner sees `not_found`); operations whose text says so answer `not_found` for both.

**Left as is.** `environment/supported.ts` says Node 22.19.0 and 24.21.0 "pass CI on every push" (product text; only 22.19.0 on Linux does). Pi Durable's JSONL store could be opened with `fsync: true` for power-loss safety of agent history; that is a product decision with a cost, not made here.

## U08c: settings and administration pages (2026-11-15)

The browser now has an **Administration** tab with ten sections, one at a time: First run, Settings, Providers, Secrets, Agents and teams, Policy, API access, Operations, Sandbox, Migration. Every section reads the owner-only views `admin-setup`, `admin-settings`, `admin-providers`, `admin-secrets`, `admin-team`, `admin-policy`, `admin-access`, `admin-operations`, `admin-sandbox`, `admin-migration` (the door's fixed view table). Each part is a record or the controller's plain error, so one failed part does not hide the rest. A failed load still shows the section buttons.

**What was built**
- `admin/admin.ts` (`AdminViewService`): owner-only reads that put the existing services together: effective settings with value, default or set, layer it comes from, locked, and when it counts; the provider list with where each runs, address, secret NAME and whether it is set (never a value); secret names and state; the first-run list; sandbox facts. Four new chat read operations and status kinds cover the same data (`status.ask`), so every page is also answerable in free words, and the interpreter prompt describes them and says a secret value is never typed in chat.
- `environment/sandbox.ts`: names the mechanism per platform (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS, Windows Sandbox on Windows) and marks Seatbelt and any unproven host as a weaker boundary (decision G01, 2026-10-21). The warning shows on First run, API access, Operations and Sandbox.
- Editing from the page is the chat's own turn for fixed words: `POST /web/admin/setting|profile|provider` (session, CSRF, one Idempotency-Key, an exact body, anything extra is 400). A setting or the approval profile becomes a `policy_edit` intent, which is shown first and applied on Apply; a provider is `routing.provider.add`. The assistant is never asked. A sentence that the redactor would change (a key-looking value) is refused with 400.
- `ChatService.applyProposal` and `discardProposal` now accept `pedit-` policy-edit IDs, so the page's Apply and Discard buttons reach the same code as typing "apply it". (This was a real gap: they threw "no such proposal".)
- Write-only secrets: `PUT /web/secrets/:name`, body exactly `{ value }`, up to 8 KiB, session and CSRF required; the value goes to the host's secret store only and the answer is `{ name, set, replaced }`. Reserved names (the owner's own credentials) are refused with 403; no store connected is a 503 with a plain sentence; a store failure is a 503 with neither the value nor the store's words. The page empties the field before the request leaves, keeps no copy in the outbox or browser storage, and never shows the value.
- First-run walk-through: what is done, the next step and how, plain explanations of the strict and derived profiles, derived recommended for testing and development, and the same question in chat when there is no browser.

**Tests**: `admin/admin.test.ts`, `chat/admin-views.test.ts` (all 4 storage backends: free-word reads, page edit equals typed edit, non-owners read nothing), `environment/sandbox.test.ts`, `web/web.test.ts` (views, edit route, intent builder, secrets form, no value in views, history, session or the database files), `ui/views.test.ts` (fake DOM: sections, settings states, hostile text as text, outbox keys, secret field emptied, no copy kept).

**Not done**
- Editing agents, teams, grants, API access, operations and migration is read-only on the page; changing them is by chat.
- Writing a secret from the page is possible only when the launcher connects a secret store and the name is not reserved; deleting a secret is not offered.
- Nothing was run against a real model, a real secret store or a real Windows or macOS sandbox (offline fixtures only).

**ASSUMPTION:** a setting edited from the page applies at the installation layer only; narrower layers are edited by chat.
**ASSUMPTION:** a "back to default" on the page removes the installation value and asks for confirmation first.
**ASSUMPTION:** the profile the page offers is derived (recommended for testing and development) or strict; autonomous is chosen only in chat.
**ASSUMPTION:** the secret length bound of 8 KiB and the reserved-name list are the launcher's own choices, not configurable from the page.
**ASSUMPTION:** a provider added from the page is shown first like any provider addition, and carries a secret by name only.

**U08c review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15).** Found and fixed: (1) the backup signing key (`backup-signing-key`, or the host's `backup.signing.secretName`) lives in the same secret store but was not on the reserved list, so the Secrets form could overwrite it and break signing of later backups; it is now always reserved (the backup's own restore of secrets already refused it). ## T7b (T7 follow-up): the running work that relies on a right is listed before the right is taken back (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-16)

**What was lacking.** T7 let the owner take a standing right back from the Administration page, and its second review left one gap: neither the page nor the chat said which running work depends on the right, so the owner decided blind ("work that relies on it may stop").

**What was built.** One read, shown in three places, in the same words:
- `grant.reliance` (new read-only API operation, owner only, `grantId?`): for the named right, or for every active right (at most 50), the unfinished tasks of the agent that holds it that have an attempt running now, in the project the right is for (`*` is every project; a right on one task covers only that task). Each answer carries `total`, at most 10 entries (task ID, title, agent, project, attempt ID and number) and `complete` (false when more than 10,000 assignment records or 500 running attempts had to be left unread, so "nothing" is never claimed from a partial look). `api-v1.md` is rewritten by `npm run api:docs:write` and shows it. Code: `security/reliance.ts` (one scan of the assignment records, grant by grant matching), `GrantService.reliance`.
- The chat's preview of a take-back (`grant.revoke`, typed or sent by the page): after the usual "Revoke grant" line it adds one head line ("2 running tasks may rely on it. Taking it back may stop it at the next check."), one line per listed task and "N more running tasks are not listed." (at most 12 lines, each under 400 characters, so no line is cut; the proposal's preview limit is 40). A read that fails says "could not be checked just now" instead of reading as "nothing relies on it".
- A status answer in free words: new status kind `grant_reliance` (`grantId?`), owner only and not for a task credential, read only. With a `grantId` the same lines as the preview (at most 12); without one, one line per active right that has running work (at most 10, then a count), so "does anything running depend on my rights?" works with no named right. It is in `STATUS_KINDS`, so the interpreter prompt generated from the table names it, and one prompt line says when to use it (and that taking a right back is always shown first). Nobody has to type a command.
- The page: the Policy tab's one read now includes `reliance` (the door's `admin-policy` view); each take-back card shows "Running work that relies on it" with the head, up to ten tasks and the count of the rest, and the question asked before the request is sent repeats the head and the first three tasks. When the read failed, or the right is not in it (newer than the page), the card and the question say that it could not be checked. Titles are drawn as text.
- Titles and names are words someone else wrote: on the chat side they pass through `quoted`/`shown` (credential-shaped runs removed, controls and text-direction characters written out, clipped); the page clips them and draws them as text only.

**Tests** (SQLite, SQLite worker thread, reference store and PostgreSQL, `chat/grant-reliance.test.ts`, 9 tests): the read for a project right, a right for every project, another agent's right, a right on one task and a right whose agent has no work; assigned-but-idle and finished attempts are not running work; the page's take-back preview names exactly the covered tasks and nothing is taken back until Apply; the typed take-back says the same; a status answer for one right and for all rights; after Apply the right reads as taken back with no work; an agent is refused (`forbidden`), a made-up ID is `not_found`, a malformed ID or a stray field is `invalid_command`, a status answer for an agent names no title; twelve running tasks give ten listed and "2 more", a status answer of 12 lines (the limit is 30), a preview of 12 lines under 400 characters, a credential-shaped run and a text-direction override in a title never repeated; the interpreter prompt names the kind. `ui/views.test.ts` (fake DOM, 2 tests): the card lists ten of twelve with the count, the question repeats it, nothing running, a partial read, a right missing from the read and a failed read; `web/web.test.ts`: the Policy view carries `reliance` for exactly the active rights.

**Mutation checks** (built files, each applied, a test failed, restored and compared byte for byte): project filter removed; grantee filter removed; cap raised from 10 to 11; the preview without the list; a right on one task covering every task; the status answer open to a non-owner; the page question without the list; the page view without the `reliance` part; the API read open to an agent; a title shown raw; the page card without the count of the rest; the all-rights status counting rights with no work as busy. All 12 failed a test.

**Not done.**
- It is what the right covers, not what the attempt will use: the controller does not record which action a running attempt takes next, so each entry says "may rely on it". A right on another kind of thing (a service or host principal, a derived right resting on this one, a network or approval grant) lists no agent work; derived rights that stop with their parent are not listed.
- Only attempts running now are listed. A task assigned to the agent with no attempt yet, a waiting or paused task and work that starts after the page was drawn are not; the chat reads again when the owner asks, so its preview is the current one while the page shows what it read when it was drawn.
- (Done in the first review, below: an ended, lapsed or not yet started right, and a derived right whose parent no longer holds, list no work.)
- The page does not poll: the list is read when the Policy tab is drawn (the chat preview is read when the request is drawn up).
- No notification carries the list (a notification's detail is limited to 200 UTF-16 units); the owner sees it in the chat's preview, in a status answer and on the page.
- The scan is one pass over the assignment records (cap 10,000) and gets two records per running attempt (cap 500); nothing is indexed.

**ASSUMPTION:** "relies on a right" means: the agent holds the right, has an unfinished task with an attempt running now, and the right's project (or every project) and resource include it. The controller cannot say more.
**ASSUMPTION:** at most ten tasks are named per right (the preview names ten, the page ten, the question three), with the rest counted; a status answer for all rights names two per right and ten rights.
**ASSUMPTION:** the take-back stays a proposal shown first in every profile; the list is information only and never blocks or changes it.
**ASSUMPTION:** a read that could not be made says so in words and never reads as "nothing relies on it".

**First review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16).** Each claim was driven end to end; four defects were found and fixed with tests and mutation checks.
- *A right that gives nothing listed work as relying on it.* An active right past its `expiresAt`, before its `notBefore`, lapsed from non-use, or derived from a right that was taken back or no longer holds, gives the agent nothing (`effectiveOf` leaves it out), yet the read listed the agent's running work and the preview said "taking it back may stop it". Now `holdsNow` (in `grants.ts`, the same judgement `effectiveOf` makes, walking the parent chain) decides `inForce`; a right not in force covers nothing, the answer carries `inForce: false` and the chat, status answer and page say "is not in force now (it ended, lapsed or has not started), so no running work relies on it now".

- *The page drew a credential-shaped run of a title.* The chat removed it, but the read the page draws from carried the title raw. The read now gives titles through `redactText`.
- *The page cut a title through an emoji.* `clip` in the page script cut at a UTF-16 unit and could leave half a character; it now drops a character it would split (every clipped field on the page benefits).
- Tests added: `security/reliance.test.ts` (stub runner, 5 tests: the 500-attempt and 10,000-record caps, exactly at each cap, more than 50 rights, every not-in-force case and a right on a host, word bounds with hostile and emoji titles); in `chat/grant-reliance.test.ts` on all four backends: an ended and a not yet started right (read and preview), a derived right before and after its parent is taken back, an agent with only read rights and a client refused for the read and the status kind with no data in the refusal, a failed read shown as "could not be checked" in the preview, a credential-shaped title absent from the read; `ui/views.test.ts`: a right not in force and an emoji at the cut.
- Mutation checks (built files, each restored and compared byte for byte; all 12 failed a test): covered work ignoring `inForce`; the head ignoring `inForce`; a derived right judged without its parent; titles not redacted in the read; the 500-attempt cap and the 10,000-record cap not marking the look incomplete; the summary without the partial clause; the summary with the old "50 or more" wording; the owner check removed from the read; the chat preview without the failure line; the page without the not-in-force line; the page clip splitting a character.
- Checked and found right: another agent's work, a finished or idle attempt and a task in another project are left out; a right on one task covers that task only; the read and the status kind are refused to every principal but the owner; bidi and control characters are written out in chat and on the page; the interpreter prompt names the kind from the table.

**ASSUMPTION:** a right that does not hold now (ended, lapsed, not started, or resting on a parent that no longer holds) is reported as not in force with no work, rather than listing work that could not be using it; it can still be taken back.
**ASSUMPTION:** an exact count of 10,000 assignment records is reported as possibly incomplete (the scan cannot tell it from more without one more read); this errs toward "some may not be listed".

**Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16).** One access gap fixed and three gaps in the tests closed.
- *An owner credential narrowed to one task could read every right's running work.* The status kind refused it, but `grant.reliance` (and `GrantService.reliance`) accepted it, so such a credential could read task titles of other projects. Both now refuse it (`forbidden`, no data in the refusal).

All 7 failed a test (the second, third and fifth only after the tests above were added).

## K06b follow-up: the scratch rule holds the records a catalogued tool reads its text from (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

**The gap.** An agent may register a personal tool or skill from its own accepted private desk records (`instructional.recordId`, `executable.recordId` of a catalog version). Those records look like scratch of a finished task. With the owner's scratch archive or purge window set, the live rule could archive or remove them and the tool then failed with "the recorded executable is missing or has changed". The K01d backup scope tier already fixed the same thing for backups (second review); the live rule did not.

**What is done** (`packages/controller/src/retention/service.ts`, scratch rule only):
- A bounded read of every catalog version collects the record IDs they name as instructions or code. A desk record in that set is not a scratch candidate (archive or purge) and is shown in the run's `retained` list with the reason "a catalogued tool or skill reads its instructions or code from this record".
- Fail closed: if that read cannot finish (the bounded scan reaches its limit, or the read throws), the scratch rule makes no candidates at all and the run says `partial`.
- Before every removal batch that holds scratch work the list is read again, so a tool registered between the preview and the confirmed run is held; an unfinished read at that moment keeps the whole batch's scratch work (reported as retained).
- Test: `retention/k06b-catalog-source.test.ts`, on all four storage backends, using the real desk and catalog services: ordinary scratch is still archived and later purged; the source records stay whole and the tool still reads its code and instructions after both; a failing catalog read removes nothing (at plan time and at batch time); a read that reaches its bound removes nothing; a tool registered mid-run is held.
- Mutation checks done (each makes the new test fail on all four backends): drop the plan-time hold; treat an unreadable list as empty at plan time; drop the batch-time check; ignore an unreadable list at batch time; read only `instructional`; treat a bounded scan that hit its limit as complete; treat a failed read as an empty list.

**ASSUMPTION:** revoked and old catalog versions count too (same as the backup tier): their text is blanked by the dedicated revoked-bytes rule, not by the scratch rule, and dropping a version by the catalog-version rule frees its source records for a later scratch run.
**ASSUMPTION:** the hold is local to the scratch rule and not added to `RetainedMaterial`, because that would also stop the revoked-bytes rule from blanking a revoked executable, which is its job.
**ASSUMPTION:** the batch-time read is added for scratch batches only; a user-requested deletion of a record that a tool uses is a separate path (it already removes what stands on a record) and is not changed here.

**Not done.** The hold covers the scratch tier only; other tiers do not touch desk records. A source record that is still `visibility: shared` was never a scratch candidate. `catalogScanLimit` is a test-only dependency.

### K06b follow-up review (Claude agent, Opus, 2026-11-15)

**Found and fixed.**
- The owner's own archive of a finished task (`retention.archive`) went through the same `#archive` as the scratch tier and had no catalog hold: archiving a task emptied a personal tool's code or a skill's instructions until a restore. The hold now lives in `#archive` itself, so both paths share it: one bounded read before the loop (a source is listed as retained), and a second read inside each guarded archive command, the last thing before the write (the `#blankExecutable` pattern). An unfinished read archives no desk record. Summaries made from a record are now archived only when the record itself was (before, also when its archive was skipped).
- Register accepted an archived or deleted desk record (status stays `accepted`; the body is empty), so a tool could be registered with empty code. `DeskService.executableSource` and the owner's `#source` now refuse a record that is archived or deleted. Register's write now also checks the revision of each source record it read, so an archive or removal that commits between register's read and its write makes the register fail (`stale_revision`, "register again"; the retry is then refused as archived).
- The scratch purge (`#tierPurge` → `#delete`) is held by the catalog inside the deletion's own `heldNow` (read before every removal batch of the deletion), not only by the run's per-batch read; a hold found there is reported in the run's `retained` list. The owner's explicit deletion of a named record is not held (decision below).
- A confirmed run whose batch-time catalog read did not finish now reports `partial: true` (before, it removed nothing but said it was complete).
- A hold found inside `#archive` during a scratch run is reported in the run's `retained` list (before, it was a silent skip).
- Doc comment of `beforeBatch` had been moved onto `catalogScanLimit`; restored. New test seam `beforeArchiveWrite` (tests only).

**Race, in plain terms.** Only one controller writes at a time (epoch), so the race is between two commands of one controller. Register-after-retention is closed fully (the revision check). Retention-after-register leaves one small window: a register that commits after the archive's or deletion's last catalog read and before its write. Same accepted window as `#blankExecutable` and the resumable-task holds; closing it would need a shared per-record claim row written by both sides.

**ASSUMPTION:** the owner's explicit `retention.delete` of a record a catalogued tool uses still deletes it (the owner named that record); the tool then reports its text was removed. The owner's task archive, which does not name records one by one, holds it.

**Looked at, not changed.** Catalog skills use `instructional.recordId` and are covered (now tested). Summaries: the catalog names only desk records, and summaries cited by resumable tasks or replays are held by `RetainedMaterial`. ## T8: tests for the two L04d follow-up behaviours no test reached, and one real defect they found (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

Test-only, except for one small product fix that a test showed was needed. No operation table change, no new operation.

**The defect, said plainly.** The L04d follow-up note said a resume check whose capture is pruned meanwhile "fails its commit with `not_found` and is retried by the dispatcher". The test showed that the retry could never succeed. The pruned capture is the check's own (not the latest complete one, which is never pruned), and a check in the `executing` phase keeps naming it. Every later tick asked for the resume again and got the same `not_found` ("no such continuation for that task"), so the attempt never started and nothing told the owner why beyond a skip line each tick.

**The fix (`continuation/resume.ts`, `advance`, `executing` step).** When recording the resume answers `not_found`, the check's capture is looked up; if it is really gone the check starts over (`#restart` now takes the phases it may leave, default `ready` as before; the same round limit applies, so a check that keeps losing its capture ends as `resume_churn`, never loops). It goes back to verifying, follows the latest complete capture, is reviewed again and waits for the next commit. Nothing was recorded by the failed attempt (the resume command fails while it is built), so the command ID `<check>-resume` is free for the new capture. Any other `not_found` is still thrown as before.

**What is tested (new files, each on all four storage backends).**
- `continuation/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts` (2 tests, 8 runs): (a) a capture pruned between review and commit (51 newer captures) makes the commit start the check over against the latest capture, with no resume recorded; (b) a capture pruned after the commit began, before the resume is recorded (the capture is pruned inside the resume call by a wrapper): the resume itself answers `not_found` once, nothing is recorded, the check goes back to `ready` against the latest capture with a history line saying why, and the next commit records exactly one resume.
- `dispatch/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts` (1 test, 4 runs), real continuation and resume check services through the dispatcher: the commit fails once with `not_found`, the attempt does not start that tick (skip line: the check "is ready after the commit; it is looked at again on the next tick"), no resume record exists, and the next tick commits against the capture that exists and the attempt starts.
- `dispatch/resume-scan-failed-read.test.ts` (2 tests, 8 runs): a failed read of the dependency records is dropped from the per-tick scan (unit), and in one tick (storage made to fail once) exactly one task meets "dependencies could not be read" while the next task of the same tick reads again and is held for its real prerequisite ("waiting for ... to be complete").

**Mutation checks** (on the built files, each restored): the failed read kept in the scan (all 8 runs of the scan file fail); the not_found fix removed (8 of 12 runs of the two pruned-capture files fail; the four that pass are the before-commit case, which never relied on the fix); pruning off (`CONTINUATION_KEEP` 5000: 0 pass, the runs fail or time out, because no capture is ever pruned).

ASSUMPTION: a pruned capture of an `executing` check restarts the check rather than blocking it. The smallest, most reversible choice: it reuses the existing start-over path and round limit, and a changed capture is looked at again (by the owner if anything matters) before anything resumes.
ASSUMPTION: no retroactive change to checks already stuck in `executing` on an installation: the next advance after this fix recovers them by the same path.

**Not done.** The earlier L04d lists (real Pi process through capture and resume, remote hosts, a real model) are unchanged. The `not_found` is not tested through a real pruned capture of 50 captures made by a concurrent controller (the wrapper prunes inside the resume call, which is the same window).

### T8 review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-15)

Merged origin/main f2437dc3 (T1, docs only; the notes conflict kept both sections). Checked the fix against `continuation.resume` and the command runner.

**Found and fixed: a recorded resume could be started over.** `continuation.resume` answers `not_found` ("the continuation that resume was recorded against has been pruned") also when it *replays* a resume already recorded under the check's command ID. That happens if the controller stopped right after the record, before the check moved to `done`, and 51 newer captures arrived before the check was carried on. The T8 fix then started the check over although the attempt had been resumed. The check went back to `ready` against the latest capture, and its next commit sent the same command ID `<check>-resume` with another capture: `command_conflict` at every retry. That is the same "never starts" outcome the fix was meant to end, and the owner would have been asked to approve a resume that had already happened. The same end state could come from two advances of one check at once (the resume sweep beside the dispatcher's own commit), when one recorded the resume just before the prune and the other started the check over. Now, on a `not_found` for a capture that is really gone, or on a `command_conflict`, the check first looks for its own resume record (`cnr` derived from `service:resume-check` and `<check>-resume`, same task). If the record exists, the check ends `done` "resumed from <capture> (that capture has since been pruned)", the rule already used for a replayed record. Only when no record exists does a pruned capture start the check over. A `not_found` while the capture still exists, and a `command_conflict` with no record of this check, are still thrown. A resume is never recorded twice: the command ID stays the check's own, so a second record would be refused by the runner.

**Checked, as written.** The start over goes through `verifying`: the new capture's dependencies are checked again, and an earlier verdict is kept only for an item with the same digest (the existing rule for a start over from `ready`). A permission refusal or a deleted task answers `forbidden` and a released or replaced attempt answers ORPHANED, so neither reaches the new branch. Two advances racing the start over or the done write are guarded by `#update`'s phase check (`from: ["executing"]`); the second write does nothing.

**Tests added** (`continuation/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts`, each on all four backends, now 6 tests, 24 runs): (c) recorded, then stopped, then pruned: the next advance ends `done` from the record, same round, one record, repeatable; (d) a check already started over meets a record of its command ID against another kept capture: the commit's `command_conflict` ends it `done` from that record, one record; (e) a `not_found` from the resume while the capture still exists is thrown, and the check stays `executing` in its round with nothing recorded; (f) a capture pruned before every commit: the check blocks as `resume_churn` within its rounds, the resume is tried at most `maxRounds` times, nothing recorded.

**Breakages** (built files, one at a time, each restored; all three new files run): start over removed (pre-fix): 16 runs fail; record lookup removed: 8 fail; `command_conflict` not handled: 4 fail; round limit removed: 4 fail; start over straight to `ready` without verifying: 16 fail; any `not_found` restarts without looking at the capture: 4 fail (test e); failed read kept in the scan: 8 fail.

### T8 second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-15)

Merged origin/main 9f3704f3 (T5; the notes conflict kept both sections). No operation text changed, so `api-v1.md` is unchanged.

**Found and fixed (1): an ended attempt was started over, not cancelled.** `continuation.resume` looks up the capture before it asks the attempt guard. So when the attempt ended (released, transferred, replaced) and the capture was pruned, the resume answered `not_found` and the check started over for an attempt that will never run. In its last round it also opened a `resume_churn` blocker for the owner. The rule everywhere else (`advance`'s ORPHANED handling, `decline`) is that such a check ends cancelled. The start over (and the churn block) is now written with the attempt guard. Its ORPHANED refusal cancels the check with the same note as before, and in the last round the guard is asked before the blocker is opened, so a refused one opens none.

**Found and fixed (2): a resume recorded just after the look was not caught.** The record lookup and the start-over write are separate. Another advance of the same check (the resume sweep beside the dispatcher) could record the resume between them, and the check then went back to `verifying` with its resume already recorded. The owner could be asked to approve it again, or get a churn blocker for it. The start-over guard now reads the record again on every try of the write and refuses with an internal reason when it exists, and the loop then ends the check done from the record (replay `not_found` or `command_conflict`). Storage has no "absent" check (`validate.ts` requires a check revision of at least 1), so a record committed between that read and the write is still not excluded. That narrow window converges as before (the next commit's `command_conflict` ends it done), never with a second record or a second start; it is stated in the code.

**Checked, as written.** (a) The record is found only by its ID, `derivedId("cnr", scopedCommandId("service:resume-check", "<check>-resume"))`. Scoped IDs are `principal:hash`, `continuation.resume` is not an API operation, and the check's ID is unique, so no other task, check or caller can produce it. The `taskId` comparison is a second check. (b) One record at most (deterministic ID, `creates`), and one attempt start (the dispatch test counts starts). (c) A forbidden caller or deleted task is refused before the build and is thrown, as is a storage failure (not a `DomainError`), including one inside the catch's reads. (d) Repeated pruning is bounded by `maxRounds` and the advance step limit. (e) The done write, the start over and the cancel all apply only from `executing`. The loser's `#update` returns false, and its loop reads the new phase and goes on from it. (f) Four backends for every new test.

**Tests added** (all four backends): `continuation/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts` "a resume recorded by another advance after this advance looked for it…" (the check service's storage misses the record once while the other advance records it; done, same round, one record). `dispatch/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts` "a check whose attempt was released while its capture was pruned ends cancelled…", run twice: in an ordinary round, and in the last round with no blocker opened. The three T8 files now hold 48 runs.

## T8b: three narrow items the T8 reviews left in the resume check (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-16)

Branch `card20-t8b`. Only `continuation/resume.ts` changed. No operation text changed, so `api-v1.md` is unchanged.

**Done.**
- *(a) A churn blocker left open when the attempt ends in the middle of the write.* When a check is blocked as `resume_churn` (or `missing_context`), its blocker is opened first and the block is written after. If the attempt ended between the two (the write carries the attempt guard, which answers "no longer the task's active attempt"), the check ends cancelled, as before, but its blocker stayed open and the owner was shown trouble for a check nobody will carry on. Now `#block` closes that blocker with a plain resolution ("the attempt this resume check was for ended before the check could be blocked, so nothing is waiting on this") when, and only when, the failure is that ended attempt and the check does not itself name the blocker (another advance of the check may have blocked it with the very same blocker). Any other failure (storage error, busy check) leaves the blocker open: the retry uses the same command ID and finds it again. `BlockerService.resolveBlocker` is an optional part of the blockers port, so existing fakes still fit; a lost race while closing is ignored, any other error is thrown.
- *(b) Overlapping start-overs could take a check past its round limit.* `#restart` judged "is this the last round" on the round it read, then wrote `round + 1` on whatever round the check had by then. If another advance started the check over and brought it back to the same phase in between, the write skipped the limit and the churn block. The write now refuses when the round moved (internal reason), and the loop reads and judges again (at most 6 times, then `unavailable`, which says the same call can be made again).
- *(c) Six lost races on one write were reported as a bare `stale_revision`.* The commit, the dispatcher's skip line and the sweep's failure then read as a fault of the caller. After 6 tries `#update` now answers `unavailable` ("the resume check was changed by other writers on each of 6 tries; nothing was written, and it is looked at again"). Nothing was written, and the next tick or call goes through.

**Tests** (all four backends: reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker thread, PostgreSQL). `dispatch/resume-pruned-capture.test.ts` gains "a check whose attempt ends while its churn block is being written ends cancelled and its blocker is closed" (the task is released right after the blocker is opened; no open churn blocker remains; the blocker existed). New `continuation/resume-busy-rounds.test.ts`: two commits of one check overlap (the second runs its whole start over inside the first one's window) and the check blocks as churn within its rounds instead of passing them; six lost races give `unavailable` with nothing written, and the same call made again goes through.

Two changes made no test fail: closing a blocker even when the check names it (defence, no test builds that exact interleaving) and 60 tries instead of 6 (the constant-conflict test ends the same way).

**NOT done.** The dispatcher's skip line for a busy check is not tested end to end (it prefixes the error text, as before). A blocker whose close fails for a reason other than a lost race is thrown, not retried by this change. The sweep's `failed` list still carries ids without reasons (changing its shape would change the API contract). The earlier L04d lists (real Pi process, remote hosts, a real model) are unchanged.

ASSUMPTION: a busy check is `unavailable` (the code the runner already uses for "send the same command again") rather than a new error code, the smallest and most reversible choice.
ASSUMPTION: a blocker is closed only for the ended-attempt case; other failures keep it open because the same command ID reuses it on retry.

### T8b second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-16)

Each case was driven with throwaway scenarios on all four backends before any change, then kept as repo tests.

**Found and fixed (3), all in `#block`: a churn blocker opened for a block that is then not written.**
- *Resume recorded meanwhile.* In the pruned-capture start over's last round the blocker is opened, and the block write's guard can then find the check's resume recorded by another advance (`RECORDED_MEANWHILE`). The check ends `done` from that record, but the blocker stayed open: the owner was told "the inputs kept changing ... rounds did not settle" for a task that had resumed. Now closed: "The task's resume was recorded before the check could be blocked, so nothing is waiting on this."

The same holds when another advance committed the check meanwhile. Item (a) only covered the pruned path. The close now also leaves the blocker open when the task's current check (its active pointer) names it, and reads the checks after the blocker.

A storage error or a busy (`unavailable`) block write still leaves the blocker open, as before: a retry of the same check opens it under the same command ID, which would replay a closed blocker.

## A09 follow-up T6: administrators are told of requests, and the claim checks the agent records the administrator check read (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

Card A09 is NOT flipped. Base 16ef7406, branch `task-t6-a09b`. This closes two items the ninth slice and its reviews left open.

**What was lacking.** (1) Only the owner was told when a host-policy or shared-base request arrived; a named administrator had to find it by listing. (2) The claim write that starts an application checked the settings revision and the grant records, but not the agent records the administrator check had read (the administrator, the requester, and the supervisors and creators above them). A supervisor or creator change between the check and the claim therefore did not stop the claim; the next judgement would have caught it only after the application had started.

**Built.**
- *Notices.* After a protected request is stored as pending, the service asks `#adminFor` of every named administrator and sends one `MaintenanceNotice` (`to: "administrator"`, `administratorId`) to each that could decide it. The check is the one the decision uses, so the requester, the one who made the request, an administrator that is held, inactive, a task credential, or in the requester's team gets nothing. Other kinds never produce one; a replayed request produces none (the build, which prepares the notice, does not run again); a notice that fails to send never fails the request. `api/start.ts` turns it into a `notice`-level inbox item with its own command ID (`mnt-adm-<request>-<16 hex of a hash of the administrator>`), so it is one item per administrator per request. The owner's own notice is unchanged.
- *Claim fence.* `#agent` can record the revision of each agent record it reads. `#adminFor`, `#upline` and `#madeByRequesterSide` pass that along, and `#standing` turns the records read into `check` changes on the claim write. A change to any of them between the check and the claim fails the claim; the drive loop then judges again and, if the approval no longer stands, sends the request back to pending without asking the applier.

**Tests** (`maintenance-admin.test.ts`, all 4 backends): the notice test (free administrators told once each; the requester, a held administrator and one in the requester's team not told; a replay, another kind, and no administrators tell nobody extra; the owner notice kept) and the claim test (a supervisor set on the requester, a supervisor set on an agent in the administrator's own line, and a creator set on the requester, each written in the window after the record was read; the applier is never asked; an ordinary claim still applies).

**Mutations (each alone on the built file; tests failed; restored).** Guard dropped from the claim (4 failures); agent revisions not recorded (4); notice sent to every named administrator without the check (4); the requester check removed from the administrator check (4); the upline reads not recorded (4). Three more changes made no test fail and are equivalent by design (defence in depth): the replay guard on the notice (a replay never reaches the build), the protected-class guard on the notice (`#adminFor` refuses other classes itself), the target read not recorded (the upline read of the same record records it).

**NOT done.** The `api/start.ts` wiring (notice to inbox item) has no end-to-end test; it is a one-branch addition of the same kind as the supervisor one. The administrator's notice is an item in the owner's notification inbox naming the administrator (agents have no inbox of their own outside a task), exactly as the supervisor's notice is. `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` did not change (`npm run api:docs:write` left it as it was).

ASSUMPTION: "inbox notice" for an administrator means a `notice`-level item in the notification inbox that names the administrator and the request, as the supervisor notice does; there is no per-agent inbox to write to.
ASSUMPTION: the claim fence covers every agent record the administrator check read (not only supervisors and creators), because a revision check on a record read is the simplest complete rule; an unrelated change to one of those records makes the claim fail once and the loop judge again (up to six rounds), which costs a repeat read and no harm.
ASSUMPTION: administrators are judged for notices after the request is stored, not inside it, so a slow or failing judgement can never make the request itself fail or retry; the cost is that an administrator named or released between storing and notifying may be judged on the newer settings.

### A09 follow-up T6 review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-15)

Merged origin/main f2437dc3 (T1) first; `api-v1.md` unchanged by the regeneration; `check:deps` clean.

**Fixed.**
- *The administrator notice never reached the inbox.* Its text was longer than the inbox's 200-character detail limit (it was trimmed to 400), so `emitFromController` refused every one and the refusal was swallowed. Had it fitted, it would still not have been an item of its own: the inbox keeps one item per `kind|project|ref`, so a second emit for the same request folds into the owner's Needs-you item and replaces its text with one written for an administrator ("that you may decide as an administrator ..."), the last administrator's text winning. Now the service judges the administrators first and puts them on the owner's notice (`administratorIds`); `api/start.ts` writes one owner item whose text names them (`maintenanceOwnerDetail`: as many as fit in 200 characters, then "+N more"; an ID too long to name is counted) and ignores `to: "administrator"` notices (they stay on the service hook for a later agent-side channel). Each administrator is judged in its own try, so one read failure no longer skips the rest. The owner and supervisor texts are trimmed to the inbox limit (200), not 400.
- *Claim fence kept the last revision of a record read twice.* The requester's record is read as the request's agent (where who chose its supervisor is judged) and again in its line of management; a change between those two reads was fenced at the newer revision, so the claim went ahead on the stale first read. `#agent` now keeps the first revision read (test: the administrator becomes `supervisorSetBy` of the requester right after the second read; all 4 backends failed before the fix).

**Checked.** The notice carries IDs and the kind only, and goes to the owner's inbox, which no agent reads; an administrator can read every protected request anyway (`#isNamedAdmin`), so nothing new is disclosed. Reads-map completeness: every agent record the decision reads is recorded (administrator, requester, filer, both lines, the creator chain); an absent record is not fenced, which is sound because a supervisor must name an existing agent, creators exist, and agent records are never deleted. Records read on an incomplete chain only lead to "lapsed" (fail closed, no claim). Loop: `drive` makes at most 6 rounds, then the next tick; agent records are written only by owner or manager actions (field changes, retire), so routine traffic cannot starve a claim. Notice replay: none on a replayed request; the per-administrator command ID scheme is moot now that start.ts does not emit for administrators.

**Tests added.** `api/start-maintenance.test.ts`: through `startController`, one Needs-you item per request naming the administrators who may decide it (not the requester's supervisor), no copy of the request's reason, replay adds nothing, none named when none may decide; the owner text stays within 200 characters with five long IDs. `maintenance-admin.test.ts`: the owner's notice names the same administrators and comes first; the first-revision fence.

**Not done / open.** An administrator itself is still not told: agents have no inbox outside a task (the P04c incident notice anchors on a task the agent holds and has no anchor for an idle agent). A pause placed on the administrator between the check and the claim is not fenced (pause records are not in the guard; it was not before T6 either).

### A09 follow-up T6 second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-15)

Merged origin/main 9f3704f3 (T5) first (notes conflict only, both sides kept); `api-v1.md` unchanged.

**Checked, no defect.** (a) Nothing of the request's reason, spec or plan goes into any notice; the owner's item carries agent IDs and the kind, has no project, so standup agendas never list it, and the `to: "administrator"` notices stop at the service hook. (c) The owner gets one item per request (`mnt-req-<id>`); a replay notifies nobody; with no administrator qualifying the plain text is used. With real 30-character agent IDs every owner and supervisor text is at most 197 characters, so the 200 cut never splits an ID; two administrators are named, then "+N more". (d) Keeping the first revision is the safe direction: the claim commits only if every recorded record is still at the revision first read, and revisions only increase, so every read of that record saw the state at commit; a change between two reads, or between the check and the claim, fails the claim and the loop judges again on fresh reads (a new map each round). ## K06b follow-up T5: the scratch rule, the owner's task archive and the scoped backup keep a plan that a decision link names (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-15)

**The gap.** The catalog-source follow-up (above) left one case "looked at, not changed": a decision link (`decision-reliance` record, `links[].subject = { kind: "plan", id }`) may name a task's private `plan` desk record as its subject. For a finished task the scratch rule (archive or purge) and the owner's task archive could empty or remove that plan, and the link then pointed at an empty record.

**What is done** (`retention/service.ts`, `backup/scope.ts`):
- The same bounded, fail-closed read that finds the records a catalogued tool reads from now also reads every decision link and adds the plans they name (links in any state, current or superseded). Each held record carries its own plain reason: "a decision link names this plan as its subject" (`PLAN_LINK_REASON`); the catalog reason is unchanged. A held record stays whole and is shown in the run's (or the archive's) `retained` list with that reason. A plan with no link still goes.
- All the existing guards cover it, since it shares the one read: no scratch candidates and `partial` when the read cannot finish or reaches its bound; the read again before every removal batch; inside the deletion's own check before each removal batch of a purge; and inside every guarded archive write of the owner's task archive (an unfinished read there keeps the record, reason "did not finish"). The "did not finish" text now says it covers the tools and the decision links.
- Backup scope tier (K01d, `planLeaveOut`): it did need the same hold. The link is always in the backup; a scoped backup that left the plan out would restore a link to nothing. The tier now keeps a plan named by a link (counted as `heldBack`); ordinary scratch and unlinked plans are still left out. An unreadable snapshot already makes the tier leave nothing out.
- Tests (all four storage backends): `retention/k06b-plan-link.test.ts` (preview/archive/purge hold, failing read at plan and batch time, bound reached, link made mid-run, link made in the gap before the deletion's own check, owner archive with a link made inside the first guarded archive, failing read inside the guarded archive, owner's explicit deletion unchanged) and `backup/k01d-plan-link.test.ts` (kept in the backup, left out when unlinked, restored link points at the text).
- Mutation checks (built files, each restored; each makes the new tests fail on all four backends): links not collected; unfinished link read treated as complete; link read unbounded; no re-read inside the guarded archive; no check inside the deletion; no batch-time read; no plan-time hold in the scratch rule; backup tier hold dropped. Two removals are covered by inner guards and so do not fail alone (intended defence in depth): the owner's archive loop pre-check (the in-archive re-read catches it) and the batch-time read (the deletion's own check catches it, as in the catalog follow-up).

**Review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5).** No defect found. Added tests: a superseded link still holds its plan, and a link of another subject kind whose ID equals a desk record's holds nothing, both in the owner's task archive (`k06b-plan-link`) and in the scoped backup (`k01d-plan-link`, planted links; the decision service refuses such a link). Without them, dropping the `plan` kind check or keeping only current links went unnoticed in both places; with them each of those four breakages fails on all four backends. Checked: no retention or backup tier removes the other subject kinds (task, review, effect, context branch), so `plan` is the only one that needs the hold. When a record is both a catalog source and a linked plan only the catalog reason is listed. The shared read now makes two bounded scans (each up to the limit), also inside every guarded archive write of the owner's task archive, so a large task archive reads both lists once per record (unchanged pattern from the catalog follow-up, cost doubled).

**ASSUMPTION:** links in any state hold the plan (a superseded link still names it and a revalidation may re-link it).
**ASSUMPTION:** only the subject kind `plan` is held; other subject kinds (task, contract, review, action, branch) are not desk records.
**ASSUMPTION:** the owner's explicit `retention.delete` of a named record is unchanged (the owner named it), as for catalog sources.
**ASSUMPTION:** the hold is reported with its own reason but shares the catalog read and its `catalogScanLimit` test seam rather than a second helper, so the fail-closed rules cannot drift apart.

**Not done.** The same remaining window as the catalog hold: a link made after the last read and before the write. Decision links are not cleaned up when the owner explicitly deletes a plan. No change to the op table or the API docs (`api:docs:write` showed no change).

**Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5).** One gap fixed: the revoked-bytes rule (`#blankExecutable`, `revokedBytesBlank`) also blanks a desk record, and an agent may register any of its own accepted original records as a tool's executable, a `plan` included. If the owner revoked that version, the rule blanked a plan a decision link names. The link read is now its own helper (`planLinkIds`, the same bounded fail-closed scan, used by `catalogSourceIds`). The rule leaves a linked plan out of `revokedBytes` at the preview, an unfinished read leaves out every item and marks the run `partial`, and the guarded write reads the links again (a link does not change the record's revision). Test: `retention/blank-race.test.ts` (four backends: superseded link at the preview, link made in the gap before the write, failing read). Every other remover of desk records was checked: the scratch archive and purge, the owner's task archive and the scoped backup tier (held by T5); `retention.delete` (the owner names the record, unchanged by design); `retention.restore` and backup restore (put text back or re-apply recorded deletions only); desk supersede (a status change, the text stays); project transfer and retirement (no desk record removal). Breakages on built copies, each run on all four backends: only current links counted; no link re-read inside the revoked-bytes write; no `plan` kind check in the backup scope; unfinished link read treated as complete; scratch purge's deletion without its hold.

Notes, not changed: (1) A linked plan is kept for as long as the link record exists, and decision links are never removed by retention, so such a plan stays until the owner deletes it by name. The growth is one plan per link an agent makes, not unbounded per run. (2) The link read is capped at 50,000 `decision-reliance` records (one per task with links). Beyond that the scratch tier, the owner's archive of desk records and the revoked-bytes blanking stop and say `partial` (fail closed), and the backup tier leaves nothing out. (3) `decisions.link` accepts a plan that is already archived or deleted (`#checkSubject` checks kind, project, task and visibility only), so a link can point at an empty record that retention did not cause. Refusing it would change decision semantics and is left for its own card. (4) The remaining race is unchanged: a link committed between the last read inside the guarded write and that write's commit.

## T2 (L04d follow-up): the owner reads and sets the daily cap on the controller's own model calls (2026-11-15)

Before this, `ChatSpendService` (`chat/routed-model.ts`) already kept a per-day token cap and count and every call made through `GuardedModelCall` with a spend service stopped at the cap (in the shipped composition only the resume reviewer and the work-report interrogator, built in `api/start.ts`; see the review below for the chat interpreter), but nothing outside the service could read or change it: no API operation and no chat command existed.

**Built**
- **`chat.budget.get` (query, owner only).** `{ item: { maxTokensPerDay (number or null), setBy?, setAt?, day, tokens, calls, remaining (null with no cap, never below 0) } }`. The day is the UTC day the count belongs to; `tokens` and `calls` are the provider's own figures that `GuardedModelCall` records. A task credential and an agent are refused (`forbidden`).
- **`chat.budget.set` (command, owner only).** `maxTokensPerDay` is a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000,000, or `null` to remove the cap; the argument must be present (leaving it out is `invalid_command`, not "no cap"). It needs a command ID. The same ID with the same value is a replay (`replayed: true`, no second record or audit entry); the same ID with another value is `command_conflict`. Each real change writes one `chat.budget` audit entry (actor: the owner, subject: the `chat-budget` record, detail: the value). The cap counts from the next call.
- **Service (`ChatSpendService.view`).** One owner-only read of the cap and today's count, so the API and the status answer cannot disagree. The existing `setBudget` is unchanged and is what the operation calls.
- **Wiring.** `Context.chatSpend` / `StateApi` dependency `chatSpend`; `startController` builds one `ChatSpendService` for the API and for the status service (the guards keep their own instances on the same store, so the cap is shared through the store, as before).
- **Chat.** `CHAT_OPS["chat.budget.set"]` is `propose`: always shown first with its number (`maxTokensPerDay=2000000`) and applied only on the owner's yes, in every profile; "remove it" is `null`. Reading is a new status kind `chat_budget` (owner only, every line cites the `chat-budget` and `chat-spend` records, writes nothing). The interpreter prompt lists both from the tables (`OPERATION_LINES` and `STATUS_LINES`, so they cannot drift) and has one added paragraph with free-form examples ("limit your own model use to two million tokens a day", "take the daily token cap off", "how much of today's allowance have you used"), including how to turn "two million" or "500k" into a whole number.
- **Docs.** `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated after the build (24 lines added).
