## Q04: defect records, repair and review cycles, owner overrides (slice 1, 2026-11-18)

- **Built.** `DefectService` (`submissions/defects.ts`; record kinds `defect`, `defect-check`, `defect-override`, `defect-index` per deliverable). A defect is a finding against ONE submitted version of a Q01 deliverable: deliverable ID, version, the finding (text, optionally the number of the deliverable event it came from, such as the rejection, checked to be an event of that version), severity (`critical`, `major`, `minor`), up to 10 evidence references (redacted), and the deliverable's responsible agent, who repairs it. States: `open`, `repair-submitted`, `resolved`, `escalated`, `overridden`. At most 100 defects per deliverable.
- **Who.** Report and check: the owner, or an agent that may read the deliverable (the acceptance service's own read rule), holds the reviewer, qa or director role in the project and did none of the work of the version it judges (responsible agent, creator, the version's creator and submitter, the submitters of its linked submissions). A QA agent that made a repair is one of that version's contributors and cannot pass it (one clause of the card's acceptance). Repair: the responsible agent or the owner. Override: the owner only.
- **Cycles.** `defect.repair` names a newer version (newer than the defect's and than the last repair; submitted, under review or accepted, never a draft). `defect.review` with `fixed` resolves it; with `not-fixed` (reason required) it counts one repair and review cycle and returns it to `open`, or escalates it when the count reaches the limit in force. Each check is its own immutable `defect-check` record with the cycle count and the limit at the time. The limit is the new setting `review.repairCycles` (default 3, 1 to 20, installation or project layer, read per project when each check is made). An escalation tells the owner once (a `needs-you` maintenance notice that names the defect, under a command ID derived from the defect and its revision). A repeat of the check sends the notice again under that same ID, so a controller stopped between the check and the notice still tells the owner and the inbox holds it once; it is not sent again once the owner decided or anything came after that check.
- **Override.** `defect.override` (owner): `accept-as-is` closes the defect as `overridden` with the finding remaining; `repair-again` returns an escalated defect to `open` with the cycle count kept (never reset), so the next failed check escalates again; it is refused while a repair waits for its check (that repair would be dropped unchecked). The decision is its own `defect-override` record: outcome, the owner's reason (redacted), the defect's state, count and last verdict before the decision, and every finding of the deliverable still unresolved at that moment. No check record is touched, so a failed check is never shown as passed; the other defects listed are pinned with `check` changes so the list is the one that stood when the owner decided.
- **API and chat.** Operations `defect.report`, `defect.repair`, `defect.review`, `defect.override` (commands) and `defect.get`, `defect.list` (queries); `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated. Status kind `defects` (`taskId|taskTitle`): each deliverable of the task with its newest version and state, and each defect with ID, severity, state, cycles against the limit, the quoted finding and its latest check (version, verdict, who, the quoted reason); the chat resolves the task by its title like `work_report`. All four commands are chat commands: report and repair apply at once (they add a record and decide nothing), review and override are always shown first (they decide whether work goes on) and are pinned to the defect's revision when shown (second review: a repair checked and repaired again in between, now in another version, made the owner's "fixed" land on a version they were never shown; now the proposal is stale and nothing is recorded; a repair named in the same message counts ahead). In chat the defect and deliverable IDs (taken from the `defects` view) and the fixed-list `outcome` and `severity` are not searched for in the owner's message (`DEFECT_EXEMPT`, like `verdict`); the finding and the reason still must be the owner's words (tested: an invented finding is refused). The interpreter prompt has a line on defects (free words, no fixed phrase), and on setting `review.repairCycles` by a `policy_edit` at the installation or one project's layer.
- **ASSUMPTION:** default limit 3 cycles (reversible: the owner sets `review.repairCycles`). **ASSUMPTION:** a draft has no defects (a finding is against submitted work). **ASSUMPTION:** the owner's two answers are accept-as-is and repair-again; accepting the deliverable itself stays `deliverable.accept` (an override does not accept or reject a deliverable).
- **Tests.** `submissions/defects.test.ts` (four storage backends): authority, the link to version and finding event, redaction, draft refused, repair rules, cycle counting, escalation at the limit with one notice, replay of a check answering with what it recorded, override recording the remaining findings and leaving the checks unchanged, repair-again keeping the count, a changed limit applying at the next check, a QA contributor refused, two checks at once. `api/start-defects.test.ts` through `startController`: the project-layer setting, the ops through the state API, the owner's needs-you notice, the chat `defects` answer by task title equal to `status.ask`, and the override by chat shown first and applied on the owner's word; second review added: the "No repair of it has been checked yet" line, a report by chat from "the latest version" with no number in the message (a version number is not searched for in the message, so it applies), and a stale chat judgement refused.
- **Not done (rest of Q04).** A conflict returned to its author counting as a repair cycle (P10's landing queue is now merged, but it has no entry point into the defect service yet; that link is still not built). Escalation of unresolved disagreements other than a defect's cycles. Periodic and incident-triggered reviews that do not interrupt contributors. Chat answering "what waits for QA" and team-wide risks with evidence links (the `defects` view covers what was checked per task only). Linking defects to Q02 QA evidence (Q02 is not built). A defect is not withdrawn or edited after it is reported; nothing gates a task's `done` or a deliverable's acceptance on open defects; an escalated defect is not on the needs-you list (only notified); defects are not part of hand-off packages, retention rules or the web project view. Second review follow-ups: a check does not look at the repair version's state when it is made, so a repair can be found `fixed` after that version was rejected or superseded by a newer one (the newer version is not checked for the fix; a regression needs a new report); a defect reported by chat applies at once with the deliverable ID and version the interpreter took from the view, and there is no withdrawal if it took the wrong one.
- **Q04 follow-ups (2026-11-19).** (1) The scratch test for a repair and a judgement in one owner message is now `api/start-defects-same-message.test.ts` (both orders: repair first applies and the judgement lands on the repair's version; judgement first is stale once the repair is applied). (2) The chat controller sets the revision of a pinned command (task, project, agent, defect and the other kinds) from its own reading and replaces an `expectedRevision` (or a contract's `expectedVersion`) the interpreter supplied, unless that number is one the owner wrote in their own words (`ownerWroteNumber`: a number standing on its own in the message, "revision 4" or "v4", not the 4 of "14" or "4.5"). An invented or guessed one therefore cannot refuse or mislead the command, and a revision the owner quoted (one a view showed them, such as the standing-rule proposal and retention views do) is the version they decided on and is kept, so a record that moved since they looked is refused as stale and never applied against the newer one. A decision's `basedOn` from the interpreter is still refused outright. Tests: a judgement with an invented `expectedRevision: 9999` is shown and applies; a judgement whose message quotes the revision seen before a repair arrived is stale and records nothing; chat `agent.update` with an interpreter-only stale revision applies, with the owner's own stale revision is `stale_revision`, with the owner's own current one applies, and a different number in the message (12 for 1) does not count; the standing-rule accept with an invented 999 is pinned to the real revision. Mutation (always replace) fails both new tests. **ASSUMPTION:** a number in the owner's message equal to the given revision is taken as the owner's (it can only make the command stricter: a match with the current revision is the same value, anything else is refused as stale); a kind whose controller reading is absent keeps what was given. First review (2026-11-19) narrowed the first version, which replaced every interpreter revision including one the owner wrote. Second review (2026-11-19): the message is NFKC-normalized first, so full-width digits ("revision #２") count as the owner's (tested, stale); the 1 of "1.5" does not count (tested, replaced and applies). Mutations of the helper (always replace; always keep; any single digit) each fail a test. Known limits, left as they are: digits of other scripts (Arabic-Indic and the like) and number words ("revision four") are not recognized, so such a revision is replaced by the current one; the owner's quoted revision is kept only when the interpreter passes it (when it leaves it out, the command is pinned at planning as before); and a kind with no controller reading (a first `task.assign`, notification settings never set, a new documentation obligation) keeps an invented revision, which only makes the command refused (`not_found`, `invalid_command` or `stale_revision`), never applied against something else. (3) The P10 wording above is corrected.

## P07 (first slice): a simulation scope where the effect ledger refuses any real write, send or spend, with results labelled simulated (Claude agent, 2026-11-18)

Plain words first. The owner can now open a simulation scope for a task: a stand-in of the services (built from a layout the owner gives) where actions are tried before any real access is used. Every action in it goes through the same effect ledger as real work, marked with the scope, and the ledger itself refuses to run such an effect through anything real. Every result says it is simulated, and a simulated result can never be named as a real outcome. Card status is NOT changed.

**What is built.**
- *The ledger rule* (`domain/effects.ts`). An effect may be intended with `simulation: <scope ID>` (`sms-...`). `EffectBridge` gains `simulated?: true`, set only by an in-process stand-in. In `run`, before any claim: an effect of a scope offered to a bridge that is not simulated is settled `failed` with `SIMULATION_REFUSAL` and the real bridge is never called (no execute, no reconcile, also for an effect that already started, as a recovery pass that picks bridges by kind would); a simulated bridge offered a real effect is refused `forbidden` and the effect is left untouched. The ledger adds `simulated: true`, the scope and `SIMULATED_EFFECT_LABEL` to the evidence of every effect of a scope when it settles, whatever the bridge or a person resolving it wrote. This is kind-blind, so it covers writes (a push, a service change), sends (a message) and spends (a model call) alike.
- *Not a real outcome* (`service-ops/service-ops.ts`). `ServiceOperations.checkOutcome` refuses an effect of a scope (or evidence marked simulated) by name, so a deliverable of type operational-outcome cannot rest on a simulation.
- *The scope* (`simulation/scopes.ts`, `SimulationService`). Owner only (a credential confined to another task is refused; an agent is refused even with `effect.perform`). `open` validates a bounded layout (1 to 20 services of 1 to 20 resources, state up to 8 KB each, dependents inside the layout) and stores the stand-in's world in the scope's own record (`simulation-scope`), so it outlives a restart. `operate` does one action through the ledger on the scope's stand-in only, with the same read-back and collateral checks as `service.operate` (the `operationBridge` over the stand-in, marked simulated); `inject` arms one failure (`refuse`, `lose-answer`, `corrupt`, `leak`) so the failure paths can be seen. The stand-in saves its world after every apply (even one whose answer is lost) before the ledger settles. A repeat of the command does it once; another operation under the same ID is `command_conflict`. `observe` and `get` are read only and labelled; `close` stops further operations, the record stays readable. At most 200 operations per scope. The scope holds no real service target, tool, model, message port or grant (recorded in its `isolation` field).
- *API and chat.* `simulation.open`, `simulation.operate`, `simulation.observe`, `simulation.get`, `simulation.close` (docs regenerated). `simulation.open`, `simulation.operate` and `simulation.close` are chat commands applied at once (they change nothing real); the interpreter prompt lists them with their arguments. The chat does not ask for the scope ID, the service and resource names, the action type or the injected failure in the owner's words (`SIMULATION_EXEMPT`: a record reference the service checks, names inside the stand-in, and fixed choices); a text given as state must still be the owner's own.
- *Wiring.* `startController` builds `SimulationService` on its own `EffectService` (holder `simulation`, no assignment service: there is no attempt to fence) and passes it to the state API.

**Tests.** `simulation/simulation.test.ts` (four backends, 3 tests): the ledger refuses a write, a send and a spend of a scope and never calls the real bridge, also after the effect started; a stand-in cannot do or settle a real effect; the scope's operations with set, restart, lost answer, refusal, wrong write and leak, repeat and conflict, kept across a fresh service, never on the real target, refused as an outcome, owner only, closed scope refuses; a scope's effect offered to the real service bridge is refused. `api/start-p07.test.ts` (through `startController`): the API path, an agent refused, nothing on the connected service target, the delivery table unchanged, a deliverable naming the simulated effect refused, chat operate and close applied from free words, a text the owner did not say refused, the scope kept across a controller restart, and the real `service.operate` still reaching the real target unlabelled.

**Mutation checks (each alone on the built files, restored):** the scope-to-real-bridge refusal off (domain test 8 of 12 fail, composed passes, so the domain test is the guard); the stand-in-on-real-effect refusal off (4 of 12 fail); the label not added on settle (12 of 12 and composed fail); the outcome check for simulated effects off (4 of 12 and composed fail); the world not saved after apply (4 of 12 and composed fail); the chat exemption removed (composed fails).

**What is NOT done (the rest of P07).** A workflow run end to end by agents inside a scope (a dispatched attempt whose tool calls, events and model provider are simulated stand-ins), provider failure and competing edits as events of such a run, the owner's separate grant of real access as a step after a simulation, and replay reruns in the same scope (U09b's `activity.replay.simulate` still walks recorded steps with no ledger port at all, which is stricter; tying it to a `simulation-scope` record is left to U09b's flip audit). The stand-in is the P03 `SimulatedServices` (actions `set` and `restart`); there is no copy of a real service's state into a scope. No chat status kind lists scopes (the owner reads them by ID through `simulation.get`, and the chat's reply to `simulation.open` gives the ID). The unsettled effect of a scope after a crash is finished when the same command is sent again; the start-up reconciler has no bridge for it (it has none for `service-op` either) and, if one were registered, the ledger refuses it.

ASSUMPTION: a simulation scope is the owner's alone in this slice (agents running inside a scope come with the workflow part); the smallest reversible choice.
ASSUMPTION: the owner gives the stand-in's layout; no real state is copied into a scope (copying would read the real target, which the scope must not reach).
ASSUMPTION: opening, operating and closing a scope apply at once in chat, as `activity.replay.simulate` does, because nothing real changes; granting real access stays `grant.create`, always shown first.
ASSUMPTION: an effect of a scope offered to a real bridge is recorded `failed` (refused, nothing done) rather than left open, so it cannot later reach a real bridge by mistake.

**First review (Opus, finished after a server reboot stopped the first pass; 2026-11-18).** Fixed: a change the scope's record could not keep is refused before it is done (it was confirmed by the ledger and lost from the stand-in); the size trial on a copy now arms the same injected fault as the real run, so a `corrupt` write that would grow the world past the record's bound is refused up front instead of failing its save part-way; a lost save never reads as confirmed (the stand-in answers nothing more, so the effect stays open or uncertain); a closed scope runs no operation it had not finished, it only reports it. The domain test file now has 4 tests per backend (the count above said 3); it also checks that an effect of a scope resolved by hand is still labelled simulated, and that the size is judged on the faulted world. Mutation checks: the trial's fault removed (the new size check fails); the label on a hand resolution removed (the new resolution check fails).
Left for a follow-up: the lost-save guard in the stand-in has no test of its own (with the size trial it is not reachable through the service); a scope's effect that had started on the stand-in and is later offered to a real bridge (a recovery pass) is recorded `failed` although the stand-in may hold the change (simulation only, nothing real; no such recovery bridge is registered today); a repeat of `simulation.operate` with a different `inject` is taken as the same command.

**Second review (Opus, clean context; 2026-11-18).** Checked independently: the ledger refuses a scope's effect on any bridge that is not simulated before any claim and never calls it; a stand-in is refused a real effect and cannot settle one; the label is added on settle and on a hand resolution; `checkOutcome` refuses a simulated effect by name; only the owner (and a task-confined credential only for its own task) uses a scope; the world is kept in the scope's record and size-checked on the faulted world before anything is recorded; the API, chat and `startController` wiring (the start-up reconciler has `bridges: {}`, so no recovery pass offers a scope's effect to anything). Fixed: a repeat of `simulation.operate` with the same command ID and a different `inject` is now `command_conflict` (it was taken as the same command); test added. Added a composed test that the chat opens a scope from free words through `simulation.open` (applied, the scope's task and world as asked, nothing real reached). Mutation checks on the built files, each alone and restored, all caught: scope-to-real refusal off, stand-in-on-real refusal off, label off, outcome check off, inject conflict off, owner check off, world save off, size check off, chat exemption off. Run through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` after `tsc --build`: `simulation/simulation.test.js` and `api/start-p07.test.js`, 17 of 17 (four backends). Skipped: other suites (only `simulation/scopes.ts` and these two test files changed in this round).
Left for a follow-up (unchanged judgement): a scope's effect that had started on the stand-in and is later offered to a real bridge is recorded `failed` with "nothing was done" although the stand-in may hold the change (simulation only; no such bridge is registered today); the lost-save guard in `ScopeWorld` has no test of its own; a resumed operation (intent recorded, then a crash) runs without the injected fault it was asked with.

## P07 simulation leftovers: a resumed operation keeps its injected failure, and the lost-save guard has its own test (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. Two of the leftovers the P07 reviews recorded are closed; card P07 stays planned. The third leftover named in the round-4 list (a repeat of `simulation.operate` with a different `inject` taken as the same command) was already fixed in the P07 second review (`scopes.ts`, the `was["inject"] !== command.inject` comparison, with a test); nothing more was needed there beyond the extra resume case below.

- **A resumed operation runs with the failure it was asked with** (`simulation/scopes.ts`). An operation whose intent was recorded and that never started (the process stopped in between) used to run on the repeat with no fault armed, so a `corrupt`, `refuse` or `leak` asked for was silently dropped. Now, when the ledger's record is `intended` and not started, the recorded `inject` is armed for that run (a leak goes into the first neighbour outside the action's reach, worked out from the scope's world as it stands, which the unstarted operation has not changed). An operation that did start is only finished, never given the fault again. The fault mapping and the reach computation are now one helper each (`faultsFor`, `reachOf`), used by the first run, the size trial and the resume, so they cannot drift apart.
- **The lost-save guard has a test of its own** (`ScopeWorld` is exported from `scopes.ts` for the test only; `simulation/index.ts` is unchanged). Directly: a working save is called once per apply, also when the stand-in's answer is lost; a failing save makes `apply` fail and every later `observe` and `applied` refuse with "could not be saved". Through the ledger: an effect of a scope run on a stand-in whose saves fail is never `confirmed`, also when run again, and the stand-in is changed once only.

**Tests.** `simulation/simulation.test.ts`, two new tests per backend (four backends): the resume with `corrupt` (read-back catches it, state written wrong), `refuse` (failed, nothing changed) and `leak` (the neighbour moved, not confirmed); a repeat of the uncertain one answers `effect_uncertain` and does not touch the stand-in; resuming a recorded `inject` without it is `command_conflict`. And the lost-save test above. Run through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` after `tsc --build`: `simulation/simulation.test.js` 24 of 24, `api/start-p07.test.js` 1 of 1. Skipped: other suites (only `simulation/scopes.ts` and its test changed).

**Mutation checks** (built `dist/simulation/scopes.js`, each alone, restored and compared): resume fault not armed (4 of 24 fail); the guard's check off (4 fail); the failed save not remembered (4 fail); the `inject` comparison in the conflict check removed (8 fail); the save skipped when the stand-in's answer is lost (8 fail).

ASSUMPTION: only an operation that never started gets its injected failure on the repeat; one that started had its fault spent on the first run, and arming it again would report a second failure the stand-in never had. Reversible: arm it on every repeat.
Left as recorded (unchanged judgement): a scope's effect that started on the stand-in and is later offered to a real bridge is recorded `failed` although the stand-in may hold the change (simulation only; no such bridge is registered).

## P10 (queue slice): an oldest-first landing queue per branch, base==head and "nothing beyond the submission" at landing, and a race test (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-18)

Card P10, "Land submissions with one leased integrator per project". The lease (L03j, P10 first and second slices) was built; nothing ordered the work that lands, and a landing carried whatever the checkout's commits held. This slice adds the queue and ties a landing to exactly one approved submission.

- **What was built, plainly.**
  1. **The queue (`landing/landing-queue.ts`, `LandingQueueService`).** One record per project and landing branch (`landing-queue`, ID `lqu-...` from project and branch) holding approved code submissions oldest first, each with its approved base and tree, author and a sequence number. One place per task: a newer approved submission of a task already queued takes the old one's place and keeps its number (an author who refreshes and is approved again does not lose its turn); the same submission again is left where it is. At most 200 entries. Every change is one recorded command (a repeat answers what it did); a lost race on the record is built again from what is stored (up to 40 times, with a short jittered wait), so writers at the same moment are all kept.
  2. **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`, `LandingQueueOps`).** `landing.queue.add` (the owner, an integrator with the exact right `integration.lease` on the project, or the submission's own author; only approved work, only on the branch the owner's policy names as the landing branch), `landing.queue.remove` (owner or integrator any entry, an author its own; others are told nothing exists), `landing.queue.list` (owner or integrator). The controller queues by itself: when a reviewer's `approve` is recorded (and when a code submission that needs no review is recorded), the subject is queued; when a newer `changes` or `reject` takes an approval back, the entry is withdrawn (both best effort, in the submissions' `onRecorded` hook in `startController`; a failure leaves the queue as it was and the door can still add it).
  3. **Landing lands only the oldest (`workspace-ops.ts`, `landingQueue` dependency).** With the queue composed, a `workspace.request` landing (after the lease check) lands the task's queued submission only when it is the OLDEST entry of the landing branch's queue and still approved for the same base and tree; otherwise `invalid_transition` (not the oldest, no entry, a named `submissionId` that is not the task's entry) or `review_invalid` (approval taken back), before anything is recorded or frozen. It is checked again right before the host is asked (a queue that moved during the quiesce refuses the landing, the host is not asked: "no longer the oldest approved one in the landing queue"). The record carries `queued: { submissionId, base, tree, branch }`, and the host is told `submission: { id, base, tree }`.
  4. **base==head and "the integrator writes no content" at the host (`worker/workspace/host.ts`, `GitBridge.treeOf`).** For a landing with a submission the host refuses, writing nothing, when the landing branch's head is not the submission's base ("approved on X but the landing branch is at Y"), and when the checkout's committed work (`base..HEAD`) is not exactly the approved tree on the approved base: a commit added after the approval, by the integrator or anyone, is a diff beyond the submission and refuses the whole landing. A landing it makes answers `detail.submission`, `base`, `tree`.
  5. **The entry leaves the queue with the landing, in one write.** The landing's outcome record and the removal of its queue entry are one storage write (`#settle`'s `also`, like H12o's commit record), and only when the host confirmed exactly that submission, base and tree with `landed: true`. A landing the host does not confirm keeps the entry and its summary says so. A refused or failed landing leaves it.
  6. **Chat.** `landing.queue.remove` (owner, always shown first: it changes what lands next); the owner names the task and the reason in their own words. The chat's description of `workspace.request` says a landing lands the task's queued approved submission when it is the oldest. Adding is done by the controller on approval (and by agents through the API); reading the queue is an API query.
- **Tests.** `landing/landing-queue-p10.test.ts` (5 cases x 4 backends): ordering, one place per task, rights for add/remove/list, the controller's own queueing and withdrawal; **race:** twelve adds at once from three services over the same records all kept with their own numbers, and a take-out racing two adds; the landing gate (no entry, not the oldest, wrong submission, owner's landing of an unqueued task while the queue is not empty, approval taken back), the host told the submission, the entry removed with the landing, an unconfirmed or refused landing keeping it, the owner landing by chat-style request without naming it, an empty-queue owner landing as before; a queue moved during the quiesce; **race:** two integrators taking the branch at once from two services (one holds it), then the holder's landing of the oldest, the other integrator with the holder's numbers, and the holder's landing of the second task all at the same moment from two services: exactly one reaches the host (`done`, `fenced`, `invalid_transition`), and the next lands once the first has. `worker/workspace/landing-submission.test.ts` (real git): a commit beyond the approved tree refused with the shared tree untouched, a submission approved on another base refused, a submission on an operation that neither commits nor lands refused, the exact tree landed with the submission named in the answer. `api/start-p10-queue.test.ts` (composed controller, SQLite): approval queues by itself once the landing branch is set, `changes` withdraws and a new `approve` queues again at the back, rights through the API, an integrator's landing of a non-oldest task refused and of the oldest passed to the (absent) host, the owner's chat removal proposed then applied. `api/start-p10-lease.test.ts` updated: an integrator's landing of a task with nothing queued is now refused by the queue (it was refused only for the missing host before).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the owner may land a task with nothing queued, as before, but only while the branch's queue is empty; an agent (integrator) never lands anything that is not queued. This keeps the owner's existing landings (and the H12q/H12s/H12t integration tests) working, and still makes the queue binding whenever there is queued work. Reversible: refuse the owner's unqueued landing too.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the order is the order of queueing (for the controller's own queueing, the order of approval), not the order of submission; a task keeps its place when its submission is replaced. Reversible in `enqueue`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a head that cannot land (its base is no longer the head, or it is refused by the host) blocks the queue until it is refreshed and approved again (which replaces it in place), or the owner, an integrator or its author takes it out; the queue is not skipped automatically. A head whose approval is taken back leaves by itself.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the permit gate is unchanged: under the default `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true` a submission's commit (H12o's platform commit) is still refused by the host as unpermitted (H12o "Not done 1"); whether an approved queued submission counts as permitted is an owner decision about the human gate, left as it is.
- **Not done (said plainly).** Reservations and the refresh-round cap with escalation to the director; mechanical re-apply of disjoint files and return of overlapping work to the author; reassignment of a retired author's task; the Q04 cycle limit; the "no submission waits forever under steady load" test (with one place per task kept across refreshes, a task cannot be overtaken by later tasks, but a head that never becomes landable still blocks until taken out). A remote host refuses any `submission` field, so an integrator cannot land a queued submission on a remote host yet (the owner's unqueued landing there works as before while the queue is empty). The queue can be read by chat only through the API, not a status view. The `integration` operation still writes the shared tree without the lease or the queue. Nothing commits the landed files (P10c/H12o remain).
- **Mutation checks (each alone on the built files, the new tests run, the file restored and compared): all killed.** The oldest-first check removed (8 failures); replacement in place turned into a new entry at the back (4); the queue's race rebuild removed (4, the race test); the queue entry not removed with the landing (8); the second showing of the queue skipped (4); the host's confirmation not comparing the tree (4); the host's base==head check for a submission removed (1); the host's "exactly the approved tree" check removed (1).
- **Verified (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard):** `tsc --build --force` clean; `api-v1.md` equal to `node scripts/api-docs.mjs`; controller `landing/`, `workspace-ops/`, `chat/`, `submissions/`, `api/start-p10*`, `api/start-submission`, `api/operations*`, `api/state-api*`, `remote/dispatch-carry`, `remote/workspace-ask`: 1915 pass, 1 fail that passes alone and is in an untouched file (`submissions.test.ts` "the cursor is sealed...", SQLite on a worker thread; it depends on the hash order of record IDs); integration `h12q`, `h12s`, `h12t`, `h12o`: 5 pass; worker `workspace/`: 142 pass, 1 skipped (Windows only); `security/secret-scan`: 12; `scripts/plan.test.mjs`: 6; `roadmap:check` ok. **Skipped:** the rest of the controller shards, the other integration suites and the other packages (the diff does not reach them; CI is the net).
- **First review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-18): fixed.**
  1. **An author's take-out was judged on an earlier read.** `LandingQueueOps.remove` looked the entry up, decided the caller could take it out, then removed by task in a later write; an entry of another author added for that task in between could be removed. `LandingQueueService.remove` now takes `allowed(entry)`, judged on the entry inside the write (refused `not_found`, as before).
  2. **The controller's withdrawal removed by task.** `withdrawUnapproved` checked that the withdrawn submission was queued, then removed the task's entry; a newer approved submission of the same task that took its place in between would have been dropped. It now removes only that very submission (`allowed: e.submissionId === submissionId`).
  3. **A confirmed landing could go unrecorded under a busy queue.** `#settle` writes the outcome with the queue entry's removal; any queue change in between loses the race. It had five immediate attempts; now twenty, after a short jittered wait (the queue service's own pattern).
  - Tests: `landing-queue-p10.test.ts` new case (4 backends): the outcome's write loses its race six times to adds and take-outs and is still recorded with exactly the landed entry gone; a non-author's take-out judged inside the write is refused; a withdrawal racing a replacement keeps the newer submission. Mutation checks on the built files, each killed: withdrawal by task (4 failures), five attempts (4), the door's author rule off (4), the service ignoring `allowed` (8).
  - Verified (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard): `tsc --build --force` clean; controller `landing/`, `workspace-ops/`, `api/start-p10-lease`, `api/start-p10-queue`: 342 of 342. **Skipped:** the other suites (the change is limited to the queue service, its door and the outcome write).
  - **Seen, not changed:** when the host lands the files but cannot mark the checkout landed (`landed: false`), the entry stays at the head with no word in the summary, and a repeat would land the same files again; the host's `nothing(false)` answer (no files) also leaves the entry. `landing.queue.list` reads the project-level landing branch only, so a task-level branch override's queue is not listed.
- **Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-18): fixed.**
  1. **A landed submission could be queued again.** A second reviewer approving a submission after it landed (or an author or integrator adding it by hand) put it back in the queue, where it sat at the head and could never land (the branch is past its base), holding the queue up. The queue record now keeps the IDs of the submissions that landed from it (`landed`, the last 200), written in the landing's own outcome write (also when the entry was taken out during the landing); `enqueue` refuses one of those `invalid_transition`, so the controller's own queueing leaves it out.
  2. **An older submission could take a newer one's place.** "A newer approved submission takes the task's place" was "any approved submission": an older submission of the task approved late (reviews out of order) or added by hand replaced the newer queued one, so superseded work would land. `approvalOf` now answers `submittedAt`, entries carry it, and an older submission is refused `invalid_transition` while a newer one of the task is queued.
  3. **A landing the host did not confirm said nothing.** The note "stays in the landing queue" was given only when the host answered `landed: true` for something else; a landing that wrote the files but could not mark the checkout (`landed: false`), or found nothing to land, kept the entry at the head silently. The note is now given for any done landing of a queued submission the host does not confirm, and names `landing.queue.remove`.
  - Tests: `landing-queue-p10.test.ts` new case (4 backends): a landed submission re-approved or added by hand is not queued; an older submission approved late or added by hand does not replace the newer, the newest still does; an unmarked landing keeps the entry and says so; a submission taken out during its landing and then landed is still not queued again.
  - **First review's leftovers, judged.** (a) Files landed but the checkout not marked: asking again does not land twice: the host refuses while the landed files wait uncommitted in the shared tree, and once they are committed the branch is past the submission's base. The entry blocking the head is the general "a head that cannot land blocks until taken out" ASSUMPTION; it is now told in the summary (fix 3). ## P10 landing-queue polish: any branch's queue can be read and cleared, other queues of the project are named, rights before configuration on take-out (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. Three follow-ups from the P10 queue slice's review ("Follow-ups (not changed)") are closed; card P10 stays planned. When the owner names another landing branch, work that was queued on the old one no longer sits out of sight: the owner sees it (in chat and through the API), can read that queue by name, and can take entries out of it. A caller who may take nothing out of the queue is no longer told the project's landing configuration.

- **`landing.queue.list` takes an optional `branch`** (`landing/queue-ops.ts`). Without it, the landing branch's queue as before. The answer now also carries `landingBranch` (the branch the policy names now, empty when none) and `others`: the project's other branches whose queues still hold entries, with their counts (a branch that was the landing branch before the owner named another, or a task's own landing branch). `partial` is set when the walk over queue records stopped early. Same rights as before (owner or `integration.lease`); the branch is one line of 1 to 200 characters.
- **The project's queues are found by walking the queue records** (`LandingQueueService.queuesOf`, `landing/landing-queue.ts`): pages of 200 `landing-queue` records, at most 50 pages (10,000 project branches), filtered by project, only queues with entries, sorted by branch name. No new record or index, so nothing changes in the queue's own writes or its race behaviour.
- **`landing.queue.remove` judges rights first and takes an optional `branch`.** While the project names no landing branch, a caller who is neither the owner nor an integrator is told `not_found` (as for anything it may not manage); the owner and integrators are still told `forbidden` with the reason. With `branch`, the entry is taken out of that branch's queue under the same rules (an author its own entry, judged inside the write; the in-progress-landing guard unchanged), also while no landing branch is named.
- **Chat.** A new status kind `landing_queue` (keys `projectId`, `branch`; the project in focus by default) answers in the owner's terms: the queue oldest first (first lands next), each task, submission and author, and a line per other branch with waiting work that says it does not land now and what the owner can do. The interpreter prompt has a paragraph for the queue in free words (read it; take a task's work out, with `branch` only when the owner names one, copied exactly). `landing.queue.remove` stays a proposal shown first; `branch` is checked against the owner's words like any other value (a branch the owner did not say is refused `unsupported_value`). `startController` passes the queue door to the status service. API docs regenerated (`npm run api:docs:write`).

**Tests.** `landing/landing-queue-polish.test.ts` (four backends, 3 tests): after a rename the old queue is listed in `others` and read by name in order, a new approval queues on the new branch, another project's queues never appear, no landing branch lists every queue with work, rights and the branch's form; take-out with no landing branch (`not_found` for an author and a stranger, `forbidden` for the integrator and the owner), take-out from a named branch by the author (own only, repeat answered), the integrator and the owner, an emptied queue leaves `others`; `queuesOf` over 250 queue records of two projects (more than one page). `api/start-p10-queue-polish.test.ts` (through `startController`): the state API's list with and without `branch` and its rights, the chat status answer for the landing branch and for `main` by name, `status.ask` refused to an author, a take-out by chat from the old branch shown first and applied on the owner's yes, and a branch the owner did not say refused.

**Mutation checks** (built files, each alone, restored and compared by `cmp`; domain file 12 tests, composed 1): rights-first refusal off (domain 4 fail); `branch` ignored on take-out (domain 4, composed fails); `branch` ignored on list (domain 4, composed fails); `others` not filtered of the branch shown (domain 4); `queuesOf` project filter off (domain 8); `queuesOf` reads one page only (domain 4); the status view's other-branch lines off (composed fails); `landing_queue` not given the project in focus in chat (composed fails).

**Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build`): `landing/*` (integrator-lease-review 16, integrator-lease 8, landing-gate 5, landing-queue-p10 52, landing-queue-polish 12, lease-p10 20, lease-p10b 12), `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p09-p10` 12, `status/status` 212, `chat/model-interpreter` 14, `api/api` 58 (its guard that `status.ask` names every status kind caught the new kind first; the description now names it), `api/start-p10-queue` 1, `api/start-p10-queue-polish` 1, `api/start-docs` 1; all passed. `api-v1.md` regenerated. Skipped: worker and integration suites and other controller shards (no host or worker code changed).

ASSUMPTION: entries left in the queue of a branch that is no longer the landing branch are not moved by themselves to the new branch. Their order in the old queue says nothing about the new branch, a submission approved on the old branch's base may not apply to the new one, and the owner may switch back. They are named in the list and the chat view, and the owner (or an integrator, or the author) takes them out or queues the submission again on the new branch. Reversible: move them on the next approval or on the branch change.

## Q02 (first slice): QA evidence bound to a tree, the criteria and the decisions (2026-11-18)

Card status is NOT changed. This slice builds the evidence record and its gate; the rest of Q02 is listed below as not done.

- **What is built.** `QaEvidenceService` (`submissions/qa-evidence.ts`), wired in `api/start.ts` and reached through five state API operations (`qa.evidence.record`, `qa.evidence.check`, `qa.evidence.list`, `qa.evidence.get`, `qa.evidence.gate`; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated).
  - A record (`qa-evidence`, `qae-` ID, index `qa-evidence-index` per task, at most 200 per task) names one CODE submission and so its tree (the exact version checked), the task contract version in force (`criteriaRevision`; any other is `stale_revision`), the owner decisions it was judged against (each active and of the task or its project; every decision the task relies on through `decision.link` must be named; a task relying on a superseded decision is refused until `decision.revalidate`), the environment, when the checks ran (`observedAt`, not in the future) and when it was recorded, and each check with one of four results kept apart: `passed`, `failed`, `blocked`, `not-run`.
  - Who: the owner, or an agent that may read the task AND holds the qa or reviewer role in the project (a role title alone reads as `not_found`). The agent that submitted the code may record a self-check (`source: self`), which is kept and shown and never counted.
  - The gate (`qa.evidence.gate`, read only) for one submission: required checks are the contract's check names plus its required evidence items; each needs `passed` in the newest current independent record that names it. Failed, blocked, not-run and missing are counted separately and each fails; no evidence fails; evidence whose criteria or decisions changed does not count (`stale`) even before anyone invalidates it; a task relying on a superseded decision fails. With no required checks, every check named in any current independent record must pass, each judged by the newest record naming it (changed in the first review, below). A different tree has its own (absent) evidence.
  - Invalidation (`qa.evidence.check`): every current record of the task is compared with what it was bound to. A change of the contract fields that say what the work must be (`CONTRACT_WORK_FIELDS`: expected result, acceptance criteria, required evidence, checks), a superseded or disputed decision, or a decision the task now relies on that the record did not cite, invalidates the record (kept with its results and the reasons) and schedules a re-check (`qa-recheck`, `qrc-` ID, assigned to whoever recorded it); the owner gets a notice (`maintenance`, ref `qa-recheck`). New independent evidence on the same submission settles the pending re-checks. Nothing stale: nothing is written.
  - Owner chat: status kind `qa` (task by title) tells per checked submission whether the gate passes and why not, every record with source, environment, times, revisions and results, whether it still holds, and the pending re-checks; `qa.evidence.check` is a chat operation (applies at once: it only applies what the records already say); the interpreter prompt describes both in free words.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a change of priority, budget, difficulty, class, permissions or recovery does not invalidate QA evidence (the same rule U13 uses for deliverables); reversible by adding a field to `CONTRACT_WORK_FIELDS`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the required checks are the contract's check names and required evidence items matched by exact text; a reviewer or the owner who wants more names them in the record and the gate then judges every check named in current independent evidence only when the contract names none.
- **ASSUMPTION:** invalidation runs when someone asks (`qa.evidence.check`, any reader of the task, or the owner by chat) and the gate never passes stale evidence meanwhile, so nothing passes on a changed dependency even before the check runs. Reversible: a later slice can call `check` from `contract.set` and decision propagation.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a self-check by the author is accepted as a record (the card asks for self-check records) but never counts toward the gate.
- **NOT done (rest of Q02):** the review policy (scope, triggers including periodic and incident, required checks, whether independent review gates completion); a project-wide QA view (the `qa` view is per task); counting independent evidence by original source (`DeskService.independence`: a copy and its original are one source); a reviewer verdict that cites criteria and decision revisions and a rejection that must cite an unmet owner requirement; a team vote never overriding an owner decision in review; carrying a reviewer verdict over only by unchanged patch-id (P09); the task's `done` or landing gated on `qa.evidence.gate` (P09); automatic invalidation on `contract.set` and decision propagation (see ASSUMPTION); dependencies other than criteria and decisions (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) invalidating evidence; relation to the older `submission.record` kind `qa` (pass/fail/not_run evidence) is left as is: that remains the author-side record, this is the QA-side one.

### Q02 first slice: first review (Claude agent, Opus; this round is final)

- **Fixed: an earlier failure could be hidden by leaving the check out.** With no required checks in the contract, the gate judged only the checks of the newest record, so a later record naming only passing checks hid another reviewer's (or the same reviewer's) earlier `failed`, `blocked` or `not-run`. The gate now judges every check named in any current independent record, each by the newest record that names it (`qa-evidence.ts` `gate`; API summary and `api-v1.md` regenerated). Test: `submissions/qa-evidence.test.ts`, task T2.
- **Fixed: a re-check of a self-check could never be settled**, since only independent evidence settled re-checks; the author's new self-check now settles the re-check of its own earlier self-check (and nothing else). A self-check still never counts toward the gate.
- **Fixed: done re-checks dropped out of the index**, so `qa.evidence.list` and the `qa` view never showed them although the operation says "pending or done". They now stay listed (at most one per evidence record, so the index stays bounded by the 200-record limit).
- **Checked, no change:** a role alone opens nothing (task read is checked first and hides the task); an agent without qa or reviewer is `forbidden`; another project's agent sees `not_found`; future `observedAt` beyond 5 minutes is refused; a different submission (tree) has its own evidence; stale criteria or decisions never pass the gate even before `qa.evidence.check`; a superseded relied-on decision fails the gate and refuses new evidence; record and check write with expected revisions on the evidence, the index, the cited decisions and the contract (a concurrent `decision.link` that lands after a record is caught by the gate as `decision_not_cited`); restart: all state is in storage, the module test runs on all four backends; the interpreter prompt names the `qa` status kind and `qa.evidence.check` with the task's title; `api-v1.md` equals `node scripts/api-docs.mjs`.
- **Seen, left for later slices:** independence is judged against the submitter of the submission only; an agent that submitted an earlier code submission on the same task (a contributor to the tree) is counted as independent (Q04 "a QA agent that commits a fix becomes a contributor"). With required checks named in the contract, a `failed` recorded on a check the contract does not name does not fail the gate (the slice's own ASSUMPTION). The owner notice after `qa.evidence.check` is sent after the commit; a crash between the two loses the notice (best effort, as documented). A replayed `qa.evidence.check` whose first run already invalidated everything answers `replayed: false` with nothing invalidated.

### Q02 first slice: second review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context)

- **Fixed: a submission's kind was told before its task's read right was checked.** `qa.evidence.gate` and `qa.evidence.record` refused a non-code submission as `invalid_command` ("recorded on a code submission") even when the caller could not read its task, so a caller without access learned that the submission exists and is not code. `#submission` now reads the task with the caller's read right first; such a submission is `not_found`, and only a reader is told it is not a code submission.
- **Tests added** (`submissions/qa-evidence.test.ts`, all four backends): a decision the task comes to rely on after the evidence was recorded makes it stale (`decision_not_cited`, gate `stale_evidence`), `qa.evidence.check` invalidates it (the author's self-check too) with that reason on the re-check, and new evidence must name it; a decision of another project, or of another task of the project, cannot be cited; the gate and record on a non-code submission of an unreadable task are `not_found`.
- **Mutation checks** of the compiled service against the module test (each restored after; each fails all four backends, the unmutated build passes): no `decision_not_cited` staleness; no project check, or no task check, on a cited decision; the kind check before the read right; self-checks counted by the gate; no staleness when a cited decision is superseded or its version changes; oldest record deciding a check instead of the newest.
- **Verified (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`):** `tsc --build` clean; `submissions/qa-evidence.test` (four backends) and `api/start-qa-evidence.test`: 7 of 7. **Skipped:** other controller and package suites (only `qa-evidence.ts` and its test changed), hosted CI.
- **Leftovers (follow-up, not fixed here):**
  - With no required checks in the contract, invalidated records drop out of the judged check names: a re-check answered by a new record that names different checks passes on those alone (the earlier record's failure was against the old criteria, so this follows the slice's ASSUMPTION, but the gate does not ask that the re-check cover what the invalidated record covered).
  - A re-check is settled only by evidence on the same submission; when the author submits a new tree, the re-check on the old submission stays pending (shown on the old submission's gate only).
  - Two `qa.evidence.check` calls at the same moment: the one that loses the race answers `stale_revision` ("ask again") although the other did the work; asking again answers nothing invalidated.

### Q02 follow-up: a re-check covers what it replaces, a newer tree settles older re-checks, a lost check race answers from the winner (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Card status is NOT changed. Branch `card-q02-leftovers` off origin/main `33d5784d`. It takes the three leftovers of the second review above.

- **A re-check names again what the invalidated record named.** `qa.evidence.record` settles a pending re-check of the same submission only when the new record, together with the other evidence of the same source on the submission that still holds (for a self-check, the author's own), names every check the invalidated record named. When the contract names checks, only the ones it still requires count. A re-check that is not settled comes back in the new `open` field of the result (`{ id, missing }`). The gate does the same: with no required checks, it also judges every check named by independent evidence on the submission that no longer holds and whose re-check is not done (a current record that is stale now, or an invalidated one with a pending re-check). Such a check is `missing` until a re-check names it again, so evidence on other checks alone does not pass. A done re-check's checks are not owed again. The `qa` status view tells, per pending re-check, which checks it must name again.
- **A newer tree settles the re-checks of older code.** `QaEvidenceService.submitted(submissionId)` settles every pending re-check of the task on a code submission submitted strictly earlier (by `submittedAt`). Each is marked `done`, with `supersededBy` set to the newer submission and no `doneBy`. `api/start.ts` calls it from the submissions `onRecorded` hook for each code submission. That call is best effort and repeatable (command `qa-sup:<submission>`, actor `controller`). If the call is missed (a crash after the submission is written), the next QA evidence recorded on a newer submission of the task settles them in the same write. The newer tree has no evidence of its own, so its gate fails (`no_evidence`) until it is checked. Nothing on an old tree passes in its place.
- **A check that loses a race answers from the winner.** When `qa.evidence.check` gets `stale_revision` (at commit, or because its write found nothing left to invalidate), it reads again. If nothing is stale any more, it answers with the records it had found stale that are now invalidated, and their re-checks, with `concurrent: true`. The owner is told once, by the winner. If something else went stale meanwhile, it tries again, at most three times in all.
- `qa.evidence.record` now names its own contention: a lost race on the index, a re-check or a cited record is `unavailable` ("send this one again"), not `command_conflict`, unless the evidence ID really exists.
- **ASSUMPTION:** with required checks in the contract, a re-check must name again only the invalidated record's checks that are still required. A check the contract dropped is not owed. This follows the slice's ASSUMPTION that the required checks are the contract's.
- **ASSUMPTION:** any newer code submission of the task settles the old re-checks, whoever recorded them and whatever they named, and also a self-check's re-check. "Newer" means a later `submittedAt`; equal times settle nothing. The re-check's purpose moves to the newer tree, whose gate needs its own evidence. Reversible: settle only on evidence on the newer tree by removing the `onRecorded` call.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the gate's reasons change for a submission whose only independent evidence is stale. They now read `stale_evidence, check_missing` (the stale record's checks are owed) where they read `stale_evidence` before. The verdict is unchanged.
- No owner control was added. The owner still reads the `qa` status kind and asks `qa.evidence.check` by chat, so the interpreter prompt is unchanged. `api-v1.md` was regenerated (`npm run api:docs:write`).
- **Tests.** `submissions/qa-evidence.test.ts` (all four backends): existing expectations were changed to the coverage rule (a narrower re-check leaves others open, the gate asks for the missing check, two records together settle). A new test covers a check losing at commit and at build to a concurrent check (a storage proxy runs the winner first), a newer tree settling every pending re-check of older code (and not the reverse, and repeatable), the record backstop when the submission's call was missed, and a check the contract dropped not being owed after its re-check is done. `api/start-qa-evidence.test.ts`: the status view names the checks owed, and a real `submission.record` of a newer tree settles the old re-check (`supersededBy`).
- **Mutation checks** (compiled build, each restored after): no coverage check; the gate not carrying owed checks; no answer from the winner; record backstop off; `submitted` ignoring order; no pool of other holding records; the required filter off; carrying done re-checks' checks too (this one survived at first, so the last test segment was added); the `onRecorded` call removed (API test). Each fails its test, and the unmutated build passes.
- **Verified** (one at a time through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `tsc --build` clean; `submissions/qa-evidence` 8 of 8 (four backends), `submissions/doc-obligations` 8 of 8, `projects/p04i` 28 of 28, `api/start-qa-evidence` 3 of 3, `api/start-docs` 1 of 1, `api/start-docs-verify` 1 of 1. **Skipped:** other suites (no other code reads these records), hosted CI.
- **Left:** a missed `submitted` call with no later evidence on a newer tree leaves the old re-check pending (shown on the old submission only, as before). The loser of a race answers only with what it had itself found stale.
- **First review (a different Opus, 2026-11-20).** One fix: once a newer tree settled an older tree's re-checks (`supersededBy`, no `doneBy`), the older tree's gate stopped carrying the invalidated records' checks, so with no required checks a later narrower record on the older tree passed it although nothing named those checks again. The gate now carries the checks of a re-check settled only by a newer tree, as it does for a pending one (only a re-check done by evidence clears them). Test segment added at the end of the follow-up test (mutation `else if (false)` fails 4 of 8). Re-ran the implementer's mutations on the compiled build (coverage off, no answer from the winner, `submitted` ignoring order, record backstop off): each fails its test. Checked: the runner records nothing for a refused build, so `check` retrying under the same command ID is sound, and `qa.evidence.record` contention maps to `unavailable` only when its own record does not exist. Noted, not changed: the `qa` status line "It must name again" lists every check of the invalidated record, including ones the contract no longer requires (the record result's `open` is exact). Verified: `tsc --build` clean, `submissions/qa-evidence` 8 of 8, `api/start-qa-evidence` 3 of 3 (slot, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`). No API text changed.
- **Second review (a different Opus, clean context, 2026-11-20).** Verdict: sound; one display fix and two tests added. Checked: the gate's carried checks only add names to judge, so they can never make a gate pass; with required checks they are not used and the coverage rule filters to the same list; a re-check settled by a newer tree keeps its checks owed on the older tree; self-check re-checks never reach the gate (only independent stale records carry). The runner records nothing for a refused build or a commit conflict (`domain/runner.ts`), so `check` retrying under its own command ID and `submitted` with its fixed ID are sound on all four backends; the loser never notifies and the winner's notices use `qa-recheck:<id>`, so nothing is told twice; `submittedAt` is compared as ISO text, the same on every backend. **Fixed:** the `qa` status line "It must name again" now lists what `qa.evidence.record` would report as `open.missing`: the invalidated record's checks, only those the contract still requires when it names checks, less those other holding evidence of the same source on the submission already names (the required list comes from the gate the view already reads; no API change). **Tests added:** `api/start-qa-evidence` (the first record also names "audit note", which the changed contract no longer requires; the line names only "login works"); `submissions/qa-evidence` (a check that loses at commit while another record went stale meanwhile tries again and invalidates that one itself, each re-check told once; a `qa.evidence.record` that loses a race is `unavailable` and sending it again records it). Mutations on the compiled build, each restored after: `check` never retrying (fails 4 of 8), record contention always `command_conflict` (fails 4 of 8), the status required filter removed (fails 1 of 3). Not mutation-covered: the status line's subtraction of already-named checks (a display hint only). Verified: `tsc --build` clean, `submissions/qa-evidence` 8 of 8, `api/start-qa-evidence` 3 of 3 (slot, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`).

## P03b (first slice): agents repair services and deliver non-code work through the tool bridge (Claude agent, 2026-11-18)

What was there: P03 built the controller side (`service.operate`/`service.observe`, operational outcomes checked against the effect ledger) and C09h gave the bridge `artifact.publish`. A local worker still had no way to read or change a service, or to draft and submit a deliverable: those existed only for API clients.

- **Four new bridge operations** (`toolbridge/service.ts`, declared in `pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts` in the fixed alphabetical order): `nimblenewt__service-observe` `{service, resource}`, `nimblenewt__service-operate` `{service, resource, action}`, `nimblenewt__deliverable-draft` `{type, title, artifacts?, submissionIds?, outcome?, audience?, accessScope?, note?}` and `nimblenewt__deliverable-submit` `{id, expectedRevision}`. Each goes through the same API door as every client, with the worker's task credential, so the per-resource `effect.perform` right, the reach of the action (a cascade onto a resource without the right is refused before anything is done), the attempt's fence, the effect ledger, the read-back from the service, the author/docs/qa role, the task scope and the outcome rules are exactly the API's. The task always comes from the attempt; a `taskId`, a `responsibleAgent` or a `contractVersion` from the caller is `invalid_command`. The call ID is the command ID, so asking again applies nothing again.
- **Contract version at submit**: the bridge passes the version recorded in the attempt's dispatch record (`revisions.contract`, the version the attempt began with), never one the agent names. ASSUMPTION: an agent should not be able to retry a stale submit by copying the current version out of the refusal; if the owner changed the contract mid-attempt the submit is `stale_revision` and the next attempt (which starts against the new version) submits.
- **Pause and steps**: the three writes (`deliverable.draft`, `deliverable.submit`, `service.operate`) are refused while the task is paused; `service.observe` is a read and goes on. Each write is a `tool-call` step of the task's activity; a service operation's step carries the operation's own standing (confirmed, failed, uncertain, or dispatched for pending), never "confirmed" for an unverified change.
- **Tests**: `api/start-p03b-bridge.test.ts` (through `startController`, a real dispatch with a scripted worker calling `services.bridge`, the simulated service target): observe allowed and refused, a confirmed operation applied once on a repeat, a cascade outside the right refused with nothing changed, named task/responsible agent/contract version refused, an outcome the service did not report refused, a report naming the published artifact and an operational outcome naming the verified effect both drafted and submitted, read back by the owner as `submitted` with the agent responsible. `toolbridge/service.test.ts` pause suite (4 backends) now covers the new writes and the read. `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts` the fixed tool list.
- **Not done (still P03b)**: chat commands for the owner to see an operation's outcome (granting and narrowing a per-resource service right already works through the existing grant chat commands, narrowing at once and widening proposed, as P03 noted, but nothing in chat shows an operation); a `ServiceTarget` connector for a real system class (only `SimulatedServices` exists); binary artifact files; `deliverable.revise` / `deliverable.version.new` through the bridge (a rejected draft is changed through the API only); the real-model trial on a non-code task (no model calls were allowed for this slice: the local AI server is out of scope). Y02 remains a planned dependency of P03.
- **First Opus review (2026-11-18)**: the four operations go through the API door with the attempt's credential and the checks were confirmed there (per-resource `effect.perform` and the reach of the action in `service-ops`, the fence of the current attempt, the ledger keyed by the call, `#mayRead` limiting a task credential to deliverables of its own task, the paused writes). The ASSUMPTION on the contract version stands: letting the agent name a version would let it copy the current one out of the refusal and submit work done against the old contract unchecked. Fixed: the composed test never had a contract (version 0), so passing a constant 0 instead of the attempt's version went unnoticed; the task now has a contract (version 1) before the attempt, the owner changes it during the attempt and the next bridge submit is `stale_revision`. The bridge now words that refusal for the agent (the API's "read it and check the deliverable against it" suggested a retry it cannot make): the contract changed after the attempt began, this attempt cannot submit, say so when ending. Added: a service-refused operation (`failed`) and one whose read-back does not match (`uncertain`) are answered with that standing and no outcome, and their activity steps carry `failed`/`uncertain` (a constant `confirmed` went unnoticed before); a deliverable of another task the agent is responsible for is `not_found` through this attempt; the activity counts drafts and submissions and shows no step for a read. Mutation-checked on the built files, each alone and restored: the attempt's version replaced by 0, the step outcome made always confirmed, a new command ID per repeat, the draft field list widened to `taskId`/`responsibleAgent`, the refusal wording, and each of the three new operations taken out of the pause set (pause suite).
