## K07 (first slice): maintenance windows that prepare and activate one exact release at a stated time (2026-11-18)

- **What is built** (`release/windows.ts`, `ReleaseWindowService`; wired in `startController` whenever `releases` is given). The owner sets a window for one exact staged release: its candidate ID and the staged digest (the owner's word binds both; a different digest is refused), a local date and time in a named IANA time zone (the meetings' calendar rules: a time skipped by a summer-time change happens just after the gap, a repeated one is the first), a duration (15 minutes to a day), an optional channel label (the trusted source the release came from; nothing is fetched), the scope (`installation`, the only one for now), the preparation lead (default 60 minutes), the free space the release root must have (default 1 GiB) and a health deadline (recorded only, see below). Who authorized it and when is kept with it. One window may be open at a time; a window must close in the future and open within a year.
- **The sequence** (the dispatcher sweep `release.windows`, its own barrier participant `release-window-loop`; each step is written to the database before the next is taken, revision guarded, so a crash or a second controller repeats a step at most as a replay):
  - `scheduled` -> **Prepare**, from the lead time before the opening and never after the close: the release is not quarantined, its staged files are verified again against the digest the owner named (`release.verify`), its migration plan is still the one the window was set with, and the free space is enough. A digest, file or plan mismatch fails the window AND quarantines the candidate; too little space, a release no longer staged or a free-space read that fails only fails the window. Success is `prepared`.
  - `prepared` -> **Quiesce check**, only while the window is open: while any agent attempt is running nothing is stopped; the window records what it waits for (once per change) and waits. Work is never Force Stopped.
  - **Activate**: the preparation checks are made again, then the existing journalled `release.activate` (card K02) runs under the owner's standing word for this window (principal `service:release-window`, owner level, never a task), so every K02/K03 check applies: approval, signature, platform, targets, migration plan quoted from the record, worker-protocol compatibility, one open switch. A refusal fails the window. Success is `activated` with the way back (`from`, the release the activation kept as previous).
  - `activated` -> `committed` once the release confirmed its start (it is current and the last known good), or `reverted` when the launcher recorded a failed start of it (it fell back) or another release became current first. A failed start quarantines the candidate.
  - A window that closes before the update started is `missed` (or `deferred` when it was prepared and work never went quiet). Neither deploys later: **a delayed window never deploys at an unrelated time.** `cancelled` by the owner at any point before activation (an activated window is rolled back with `release.rollback`).
  - The owner is told each outcome once (needs-you for missed, deferred, failed, reverted; a notice for committed; kind `maintenance`, ref `release-window/<id>`); the window records `toldAt`, and a notice that cannot be filed is tried again at the next sweep.
- **Quarantine** (`release-quarantine` record per candidate, written in the same operation as the window's failure): a quarantined release cannot get a new window and fails a window's preparation. There is no un-quarantine: a changed artifact is a new candidate anyway.
- **API:** `release.window.set`, `release.window.cancel` (owner only), `release.window.get`, `release.window.list` (owner, or a holder of exactly `release.manage`). A window that changed the current release shows `rollback: { to, ok, reasons }` from the K03 check (`release.rollback.check`).
- **Chat:** `release.window.set` is always a proposal; the controller fills in the staged digest from the record (never the interpreter's) and shows the date, time, zone and duration it understood, so the owner confirms the time before anything is set (date, time and zone are the interpreter's reading of the owner's words, which is why they are shown rather than required verbatim). `release.window.cancel` applies at once (it only stops). Status kind `release_windows` answers "how are the maintenance windows" in plain lines.
- **Tests:** `release/windows.test.ts` (5 cases on each of the four backends, real staging and activation in temporary folders: binding and refusals, time zone conversion, replay; lead time, waiting while work runs, activation, commit and a single notice; missed and deferred never activating later; quarantine on a changed file, failed-not-quarantined on space, refused activation; reverted and quarantined after a failed start, cancel). `api/start-release-window.test.ts` (through `startController` on SQLite: agent refused, chat proposal with the digest filled in, applied, the dispatcher sweep activates, cancel refused after activation, confirm commits, one inbox item, the chat status answer). Mutation checks: removing the close check (a late window would deploy), the running-work wait, and the quarantine write each fail tests (4, 8 and 8 of the 20 backend cases).
- ASSUMPTION: windows are one-off (no recurring standing window yet); recurring windows are in the remainder.
- ASSUMPTION: one open window at a time for the whole installation (overlapping updates are refused rather than ordered).
- ASSUMPTION: the release must already be staged when the window is set ("acquire before the window"); preparation verifies it again.
- ASSUMPTION: preparation starts 60 minutes before the opening by default and needs 1 GiB free under the release root by default (provisional numbers; both are set per window).
- ASSUMPTION: running work holds the update back rather than being suspended (the safe reading of "defer and report rather than silently Force Stop"); suspending without release is the remainder.
- ASSUMPTION: only artifact faults quarantine (a digest, file or plan mismatch, a failed start); full disks, an unstaged release and a refused activation (not approved, no signature) only fail the window, because the release itself may be fine.
- ASSUMPTION: after activation the controller does not restart itself; the launcher runs the new release at the controller's next start, and the window stays `activated` until the start is confirmed or fails.
- **Not done (K07 stays planned):** suspending affected workers without release (Quiesce proper) and restoring their prior lifecycle state; the Checkpoint (a consistent snapshot of state, artifacts and configuration taken by the window); testing migrations on an isolated copy with fake services; the independent compatible inbox during downtime or reporting unavailability; the quarantined start with dispatch and effects disabled and a single writer; the verification run (startup, registration, a local admin request, a fake task, checkpoint and restore) and the health deadline enforcement (today the launcher's startup window, `release.staging.settings`, is what decides; the window's `healthDeadlineSeconds` is recorded only); commit-or-revert of the state with the candidate's process tree terminated (today the launcher's K02e/K03 fall-back is what reverts the code); a restart after activation; bounded recovery mode when both releases fail; gates owned by a window and cleared only by it on cancel (no gates are applied in this slice, so cancel touches nothing else); recurring windows and a standing maintenance policy for routine updates; scopes narrower than the installation; pruning old window records (listing reads at most 500 and shows 50); the UI view; the 44-case fault matrix on macOS, Linux and Windows; re-running the G05 macOS cases on a new macOS release.

### K07 first slice: first Opus review (2026-11-18)

- **Fixed: a stop between the switch and the window's record of it.** The window called `release.activate` and only then wrote `activated`; a controller that stopped in between left the window `prepared`. If it came back after the close, the window was marked `missed` and the owner told "it will not be activated later" although the release had switched; if it came back inside the window after the launcher had fallen back, the replayed activation was refused and the window ended `failed` instead of `reverted` (no quarantine). The window now saves `activatingAt` before calling the activation, and a window carrying it is settled from the activation record first (its journal still open: wait; an `activated` or `recovered` entry by `service:release-window` for the candidate since then, or the candidate current: `activated` with the way back; otherwise it goes on, or closes as missed). `release.window.cancel` is refused for such a window once the switch took effect.
- **Fixed: the wait step's command ID repeated.** It was named by the count of running attempts and the history length, and the history is capped at 20, so a count going up and down repeated an ID with a different payload: every later sweep failed with `command_conflict` and the window kept an old "waiting" text. It is now named by the revision it moves from.
- **Fixed (small):** a second cancel of a cancelled window wrote a no-op update under a new command ID (it now returns without writing); `set` read the existing window outside its serial section (two copies of the same command at once could refuse the second as "another window is open"); the interpreter prompt had no words for maintenance windows (now: date and time as the owner's local time worked out from Now, an IANA zone, ask when the zone or length is unclear, leave the digest out, the status kind `release_windows`); a misplaced doc comment in `status.ts`.
- **Tests added** (`release/windows.test.ts`, each on the four backends): summer-time conversion (New York 02:30 on the spring-forward day is 07:30 UTC, 01:30 on the fall-back day is the first, 05:30 UTC; London in July; past a year refused; a holder of release.manage lists); a stop right after the switch settled as activated after the close, cancel refused, then committed; a stop after the switch with a failed start, found after the close, reverted and quarantined; a stop before the switch, found after the close, missed and nothing switched; a 30-sweep wait with the count going up and down. Mutation checks on the built files, each alone and restored: settling from the activation record (8 of 36 fail), the cancel guard (4), the wait ID (4), the close check (8), the running-work wait (12), the quarantine write (12); the chat's digest fill from the record (the `startController` test fails).
- **Follow-ups (not fixed here):**
  - Chat names: `release.window.set` needs the `rcn-` ID and `release.window.cancel` the `rwin-` ID in the owner's own words (`RELEASE_ID_KEYS`), so "cancel the maintenance window" in free words is refused; resolving the one open window (and the one staged release) by loose words would meet the chat-control rule.
  - A switch the window began whose journal a crash left open is finished or aborted by K02's start-up recovery, which can happen after the window closed (the window then truthfully settles as activated, but the switch lands outside the window).
  - The quiet check counts only `running` attempts: waiting and parked attempts and long jobs do not hold the window, and an attempt may start between the check and the switch (harmless while the switch takes effect only at the next start; it matters once a restart follows activation).
  - The one-open-window check and the list read at most 500 window records; beyond that an open window can be missed (pruning is in the remainder).
  - Numbers in a chat proposal (`durationMinutes`, `minFreeBytes`) are not checked against the owner's words (only texts are); the fill note shows the duration, not the free-space figure.

### K07 first slice: second Opus review (2026-11-19)

- **Fixed: chat names (the chat-control rule).** "install the update tonight at 2" and "cancel the maintenance window" now work without typed IDs: with no `candidateId` the chat takes the one staged release waiting to be installed (staged, not current, not quarantined, never failed to start) and says so on the proposal, and asks which when there are several or says none is staged; with no `windowId` cancel takes the one open window, or says none is open. An ID the owner never wrote is still refused. The interpreter prompt says to leave the IDs out unless the owner wrote them, and to give `channel`, `prepareLeadMinutes` and `minFreeBytes` only when named. Set stays proposal-first.
- **Fixed: the proposal shows every number.** The note now gives the local time and zone, the UTC opening and closing instants, the length, the preparation lead and the free space needed (defaults marked), and says when the local time does not exist that day (clocks go forward: when it opens instead) or happens twice (the first). A window without a length is asked for in chat rather than proposed.
- **Fixed: an activation error after the switch began.** `release.activate` can raise an error after its journal opened (the commit not written after the pointer switched, an undo that failed); the window marked itself `failed` ("activation was refused") while K02's restart recovery could still finish the switch, so the owner would be told the window failed while the release became current. After any refusal the window now reads the activation record first (its own switch only): an open journal leaves it waiting, its recorded switch settles it `activated`; only otherwise is it failed.
- **Fixed: the 500-record scan.** Window records are listed by ID (a hash), not by age, so after 500 windows the one open window could fall outside the single page read: the sweep would never prepare it and `set` would allow a second open window. The scan now reads every page (page size an option for tests).
- **Tests added:** `release/windows.test.ts` (each backend): an error raised right after the pointer switch leaves the window `prepared` and untold, and after recovery commits the switch (past the close) it is `activated` with the way back; a page size of one with the open window off the first page: set still refuses a second window and the sweep activates it. `api/start-release-window.test.ts`: scripted interpreter turns from loose words: cancel with none open refused, set with no ID proposed for the one staged release with its numbers shown and applied, "cancel the maintenance window" applied, an unwritten window ID refused, two staged releases asked about. `chat/release-words.test.ts`: the note's numbers, UTC instants and the skipped and repeated New York times.
- **Mutation checks** (built files, each alone, restored, then all three files pass again): ignoring an open journal after a refusal (4 of the backend cases fail), skipping the record check after a refusal (4), a single-page scan (4), taking the first of several staged releases (the `startController` test fails), dropping the proposal's time-and-numbers note (fails), dropping the open-window lookup for cancel (fails).
- **Left (judged, not fixed):** the quiet check counts only `running` attempts (waiting and parked attempts do not hold the window; harmless while the switch takes effect only at the next start, needed once a restart follows activation; Quiesce proper is the remainder). A switch left open by a crash is finished by K02 recovery at the next start, possibly after the window closed (the window then truthfully reports `activated`). The chat's open-window lookup reads `release.window.list` (newest 50 by opening). Numbers are shown, not checked against the owner's words.

### K07 chat names follow-up (Claude agent, 2026-11-21): the window's numbers are the owner's, and the open window is never off the list

Branch `card-k07-s5` off origin/main `61b8434c`. The second review left four K07 items: (1) the chat's open-window lookup read the newest 50 windows only, (2) the numbers of a chat proposal were shown but not checked against the owner's words, (3) the quiet check counts only `running` attempts, (4) a switch a crash left open may be finished by K02 recovery after the window closed.

- **Done: the open window leads the list** (`release/windows.ts`, `list`). The list now puts the open window (scheduled, prepared or activated; at most one) first and then the rest newest opening first. Before, cancelled windows set for later dates came first, so after 50 of them "cancel the maintenance window" said none was open and the status answer's ten lines did not show it. `release.window.list`'s description says so (API docs regenerated).
- **Done: every number of a chat window proposal is the owner's** (`chat/commands.ts`: `windowLengthInWords`, `leadInWords`, `sizeInWords`; checked in `chat/chat.ts`). Texts were already checked; numbers were not, so a length, preparation lead, free-space figure or health deadline the model made up would have been proposed. Now:
  - the length must be in the owner's words, said outright ("for 90 minutes", "an hour", "half an hour"), as hours and minutes ("an hour and a half", "2 hours and 30 minutes", "1h30m"), or as an end time after the start the proposal shows ("from 2 to 4am", "3am until 4:30", "between 2 and 3", "2-4am", "till midnight", "until noon"; an end time without am or pm is read both ways, one marked am or pm only that way);

## Fixed-part sizing after T08: the unmeasured-route floor, the smallest startable window and the owner's words follow the real worker's fixed part (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-19)

Follow-up card found by the CI fix `3b100d87` (C07g, W12, W13 windows). Branch `card-fixedpart-impl` off origin/main `3b100d87`.

Since card T08 slice 2 the real worker's fixed part, measured as the worker measures it at start, is system text 2,537 characters (`sharedSystemText(PI_AGENT_LAYOUT)`) plus 28 bridge tool schemas 15,024 characters (`composeTools`), 17,561 in all, about 5,854 tokens at the budgets' three characters to a token. The floor counted for a route nobody has measured was 8,000 + 6,000 = 14,000 characters, below it, so a route move could be admitted on the floor and refused at the first call; the owner was told "about 4,200 tokens".

- **One source of the figures:** `packages/controller/src/context/fixed-part.ts`. `WORKER_FIXED_PART` (the measured 2,537 + 15,024), `WORKER_FIXED_PART_BUDGET` (3,000 + 16,000: a little room, no more), `WORKER_FIXED_PART_ABOUT_TOKENS` (5,900, the measured figure rounded to hundreds), `MIN_TASK_CHARS` (3,000, an estimate of the smallest task with its rules note and view frame), `windowCanStartTask` / `startableWindow` / `MIN_STARTABLE_WINDOW` (30,720: the smallest multiple of 1,024 whose quarter holds the fixed part, the anchor at its default size for that window and the smallest task), `PRACTICAL_STARTABLE_WINDOW` (32,768: `MIN_STARTABLE_WINDOW` rounded up to a multiple of 4,096 by `practicalWindow`, since the second review; it was the next power of two), `FIXED_PART_WORDS` and `smallWindowWarning`.
- **(1) The floor:** `ROUTE_FLOOR_DEFAULTS` is now `WORKER_FIXED_PART_BUDGET` (19,000 characters, 6,334 tokens), at or above the real fixed part. `context.route.get`'s summary names the figures from the constants. `start-route-change.test` expects 19,000.
- **(2) The smallest window:** `MIN_WORKABLE_CONTEXT_TOKENS` / `MIN_WORKABLE_WINDOW` stay 8,192 (the CMP test keeps them equal). `routing.provider.add` (`SetupProviderService.add`) still adds a provider whose window is from 8,192 up to 30,719 tokens, and its answer then carries `warnings` and the same lines as `shown` (which the chat shows after "Done"): "Provider tiny: a context window of 16,384 tokens is accepted, but no task can start on it: the team's fixed instructions and tools take about 5,900 tokens ..., so 32,768 or more is needed in practice; with the goal anchor and the smallest task the first call needs a window of at least 30,720 tokens. Give the model's real context window, or add a model with a larger one." A replay repeats the warning (it is worked out in the command's prepare step, which runs on a replay too). Under 8,192 is refused as before.
- **(3) The words:** the setup guide (`readiness.ts`, model-route), the interpreter prompt (`model-interpreter.ts`) and the `routing.provider.add` summary build their sentence from `FIXED_PART_WORDS` / the constants; the h12bf comment names 5,900 and the constant.
- **(4) The budget test:** `packages/integration/src/fixed-part-budget.test.ts` measures the real system text and bridge tool schemas (with `toolSchemaCharsOf`, now exported by pi-adapter and used by the worker process itself, so the test and the worker measure alike). It fails when either exceeds `WORKER_FIXED_PART_BUDGET` (the next tool addition raises the budget deliberately), when `WORKER_FIXED_PART` drifts more than 5% from the real figures (so the owner's words stay true), when the floor is below the real part, and when the real part no longer starts a task on 32,768 tokens. At the time of writing the tools have 976 characters of room, the system text 463.
- `packages/controller/src/setup/small-window.test.ts`: the add warning through the API (16,384 warned, 65,536 and 30,720 not, 8,191 refused, replay the same, the chat reply shows it), every accepted window under the startable one warns, and the guide's words.
- c07g-route-view, w12-anchor and w13-recall keep their windows (32,768 / 40,960) and C07g its 20,000 floor; the c07g comment now says the real part is just under the default floor rather than over it.

- ASSUMPTION: for (2) the add-time warning was chosen over raising `MIN_WORKABLE_*` to 32,768: it is the smaller, more reversible change (nothing that is accepted today is refused, no stored route becomes invalid, the CMP equality and the worker's own refusal stay as they are), and the owner still learns the needed figure at the moment the window is given.
- ASSUMPTION: the floor's system part is the real worker's measured system text with room (3,000), not the host's 8,000-character assumption for a harness that reports no system prompt (`UNKNOWN_SYSTEM_PROMPT_CHARS`). The real Pi process always reports its figures, and 8,000 + 16,000 = 24,000 characters (8,000 tokens) would fill a 32,768-token window's whole startup share and refuse every unmeasured route move there. A non-reporting harness is still counted at 8,000 by the host at its first call.
- ASSUMPTION: "derive the tool figure from the bridge tool list at build time" is done as a test, not generated code: the controller does not depend on pi-adapter (and must not, by the package boundaries), so the figures live in the controller and the integration test, which depends on both, measures the real list and fails on drift or growth.
- Two controller tests were sized for the old 14,000 floor: `context/enforcement.test` (C07g view suite) now uses a 40,960-token window (19,000 characters no longer fit beside its twenty open questions on 32,768; it then carries a warning instead of `undefined`), and `api/start-route-view.test` (hostile questions) sets the floor to 14,000 through `context.route.change`, since it is about quoting, not the floor.
- **Checks on this change** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): pi-adapter suite green; integration suite 215 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped (the exhaustive-only kill-path cases), including c07g-route-view, w12-anchor, w13-recall and the new budget test; controller suite 15,632 of 15,637 with the five failures the two tests above (fixed, then those files and small-window/start-route-change rerun: 178 of 178); `check:deps` ok. Worker, contracts, config, ui, registry and scripts suites not run (nothing they import changed except pi-adapter's new export).

### First Opus review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-18)
Checked against the card: the floor (19,000 = budget, at or above the measured 17,561), the add-time warning (worked out in the runner's prepare step, so a replay repeats it; refused under 8,192 as before), the chat display (`routing.provider.add` is proposal-first; on "yes" the applied step's `shown` comes from the result through `shownOf` and is printed after "Done"), and both ASSUMPTIONS. Both are sound: an unmeasured route is never refused on the floor (`changeRoute` builds the view with what is left and the first call decides), so a floor at the real worker's size with room is the right estimate and the host still counts 8,000 for a harness that reports no system prompt; the warning keeps every stored route valid. `windowCanStartTask` checks only the startup limit; the working limit (startup + likely tool output + the route's reply reserve within 60%) depends on each route's `maxTokens`, so 30,720 is a lower bound, which the words ("at least") say.
Fixed in this review:
- **Launcher words:** the note for providers registered from the configuration document said "under about 32,768 tokens" and "8,192" as literals and dropped any warning `add` returned; it now builds them from `PRACTICAL_STARTABLE_WINDOW` / `MIN_WORKABLE_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and appends the warnings (u14-launcher checks the words and that 32,768 is not warned about).

## macOS sandbox: Homebrew OpenSSL's configuration file (own-hardware macOS probe, run 44453704944 job 135323540710, Claude agent, 2026-11-19)

- **Cause.** Homebrew's node@22 on Rob's Mac (Darwin arm64) links Homebrew's OpenSSL (`/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/libcrypto.3.dylib`). When node starts, that OpenSSL reads its configuration file `<OPENSSLDIR>/openssl.cnf`, here `/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3/openssl.cnf`. The Seatbelt profile already allowed each library file (the 2026-10-31 fix above) but not that configuration, so a confined node stopped at launch with `OpenSSL configuration error: BIO_new_file: Operation not permitted ... fopen(/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3/openssl.cnf, rb)`. A missing file is ignored by node; a refused one is fatal.
- **Fix** (`sandbox/libraries.ts`, one comment in `sandbox/seatbelt.ts`). After the library walk, for each library found outside the system whose file name starts with `libcrypto`, the resolver reads the OpenSSL directory that library was built with, from the text `OPENSSLDIR: "<dir>"` that every OpenSSL 1.1/3 libcrypto carries (the same text `openssl version -d` prints; read from the file, nothing is run; only a plain, absolute, already-normal path counts). If `<dir>/openssl.cnf` exists, is a regular file and it, its links and its real path all lie in the places libraries may come from (Homebrew's prefixes, the program's install root, configured prefixes) and not in the agent's writable directories, those exact paths join the same list as the libraries, so the profile gets one more `(allow file-read* (literal (param "LIBn")))` line per path. Nothing else changes: no directory, no write, no network, no environment change, nothing else in `/opt/homebrew/etc`. When node is not linked to such a libcrypto (a self-contained node, as on GitHub's runners) nothing is added and no file is scanned. When the configuration is absent, a directory, or outside the allowed places it is simply not added (no refusal; node then behaves as before).
- ASSUMPTION: the exact file only, not the `/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3` folder (the folder also holds `cert.pem` and `certs/`, which node does not read unless told to use OpenSSL's certificate store).
- ASSUMPTION: the configuration path comes from the linked library itself rather than from `process.config` (a Homebrew node built with `--shared-openssl` does not record OPENSSLDIR there) or from running an `openssl` program (which may be a different OpenSSL). The alternative from the brief, giving the confined process an empty `OPENSSL_CONF` file, was not taken: it would silently change OpenSSL's settings for the agent's programs instead of letting them read the owner's real configuration.
- **Tests** (`sandbox/libraries.test.ts`, run on any operating system with a fake Homebrew laid out as on Rob's Mac): exactly the configuration is added (not `cert.pem`) and only the libcrypto is scanned; the profile has one read-only literal line for it, its `-D LIBn=` parameter names it, and the rest of the profile and the environment are identical to the profile without it; no libcrypto, or a libcrypto without the text, adds nothing and scans nothing; a missing configuration or a directory of that name adds nothing and does not refuse; a configuration outside the allowed places, a link from it to a secret file, a configuration inside a writable directory and one under `/usr` (already readable: Intel Homebrew) add nothing; a configuration that is a link inside Homebrew adds the link and its target; the parser takes only plain absolute paths (relative, `..`, `//`, control characters, unterminated and over-long values refused) and the real file reader works on a written file; and on a machine with an OpenSSL 3 library in a known place (Linux CI's `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.3`) the directory read from the library equals what that machine's `openssl version -d` prints. The macOS-only live test (`the real otool (macOS only)`) is unchanged; it should now pass because the default seatbelt backend adds the configuration. Mutation checks, each failing at least one test: not adding the paths, no allowed-places check, no writable check, no regular-file check, no path normalisation check, a real reader that finds nothing, scanning every library, no length limit.
- **Not verified (there is no Mac here; say so plainly).** None of this ran on macOS. Not seen: that Homebrew's arm64 `libcrypto.3.dylib` carries the `OPENSSLDIR: "/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3"` text exactly in that form (it is how OpenSSL's `cversion.c` builds it and Linux's libcrypto has it), that the one literal rule is enough for OpenSSL's `fopen` under Seatbelt, and that node then starts. Not confirmed either: that the five tests where the dispatcher started no attempt on the Mac (`c07g-route-view` line 107, `h12bf-composed` subtest 1, `l05b-model-stream`, `w12-anchor`, `w13-recall`) had this same cause; it is likely (their worker would hit the same OpenSSL error) but only the next own-hardware macOS run can tell. Rerun the macOS probe (`libraries.test` "the real otool" and `h12bf-composed`) to confirm.
- **Not done.** A configuration that `.include`s further files: only `openssl.cnf` itself is allowed (Homebrew's default has no active include). A self-contained node with OpenSSL built in (no separate libcrypto) is not scanned; such a node's compiled-in directory usually has no `openssl.cnf`, which node ignores. `OPENSSL_CONF` set in a recipe's environment is not followed.
- **First Opus review (2026-11-19).** Checked: the path never enters the profile text (it travels only as a `-D LIBn=<path>` value; the profile line is a fixed `(literal (param "LIBn"))`), so `"`, `\`, `(`, `)`, `;` or regular-expression characters cannot change the profile; the parser refuses newlines (a trailing one too), control and non-ASCII bytes, `.`/`..`/`//` and values over 1024 bytes; a link from the configuration to elsewhere adds nothing, and Seatbelt checks the opened file's resolved path (the assumption the library rule already relies on), so a file swapped for a link after the check is still refused (not verifiable here: no Mac). The remembered answer stamps the configuration like a library, so an edited, replaced or removed configuration is looked at again. Changed: the scan limit is 64 MiB instead of 256 MiB (the whole file is read into memory once per cache miss; Homebrew's libcrypto is about 5 MB). Tests added: the size limit (sparse file over and at the limit), more parser refusals (newline, trailing newline, `/./`, non-ASCII), profile characters kept literally, first mark wins, and the cache re-check of an edited, replaced and removed configuration. Mutation checks on the built files, each failing at least one test and restored: not adding the paths, no allowed-places check, no writable check, the allowed-places check on the configuration alone (not its links and real path), no regular-file check, no normalisation check, no printable check, no length limit, no trailing-slash strip, every library scanned, a reader that finds nothing, the configuration added without its links. Two equivalent mutants survive by design: dropping `exists` (the regular-file check covers it) and the regular-file check on the configuration path instead of its real path (the check follows links).
- **Mac log (run 44453704944, `own-hw-diag/mac/run-1.log`).** The five "no attempt started" tests (`c07g-route-view` 107, `h12bf-composed` 1, `l05b-model-stream`, `w12-anchor`, `w13-recall`) all fail the same assertion (the expected attempt list is empty) in tests that launch the real worker under Seatbelt; the only worker stderr in the whole log is the OpenSSL configuration error (in `h12bf-composed` subtest 2 and in the live `libraries.test`), and no other "Operation not permitted" or sandbox refusal appears. That supports one cause, but a second refusal later in node's start would be hidden behind the first; only the next macOS run can show it.
- **Follow-ups (first review), both fixed in the second review.** (1) A configuration that appeared only after a node's answer was remembered was not picked up until the libcrypto or node changed. (2) A remembered answer whose configuration lay inside a run's writable directories refused that launch, and an answer first computed for a run whose writable directories held the configuration left it out for every later launch.
- **Second Opus review (2026-11-19).** Checked: the allowed set is the one configuration path plus its links and real path, each a `literal` parameter line, only when every one of them is in the library places and the real path is a regular file; nothing in the profile text depends on the path. The library list matches the Mac log (brotli, c-ares, icu4c (data inside `libicudata`), nghttp2/3, libuv, openssl@3, simdjson, sqlite, uvwasi, zstd, each with its `opt` link); the only refusal in the log is the configuration. Node upgrade: the program's stamp changes, so the answer is recomputed; `brew upgrade openssl@3`/relink: the `opt` link's stamp (it follows the link) changes or the old Cellar path disappears, so it is recomputed, and the new libcrypto is scanned again. Changed (`libraries.ts`): the resolver keeps each configuration as a group (file, links, real path) apart from the libraries; the writable-place rule for that group is applied per launch (leave the group out, never refuse), so the remembered answer no longer depends on the first launch's writable directories; the configuration paths looked at are remembered with their stamp, or "absent", so one created later is picked up on the next launch (one more `stat` per launch). Tests added: a configuration appearing after the remembered answer is added; a launch whose writable directories hold it gets it left out without a refusal and the next launch gets it back, in both orders. The host comparison test (`openssl version -d` against the library's text) now skips, with a reason, when there is no `openssl` program, it does not run, it does not print a directory, or its library version text is not in that library file (a different OpenSSL), instead of passing silently or failing. Mutation checks on the built file, each failing a test and restored byte-identical: absent-stamps ignored, no configuration path remembered, the per-launch writable filter removed, the configuration refused instead of left out, the writable filter dropped from the direct lookup, the writable filter applied at lookup time (so remembered), the configuration never added, no allowed-places check. Suites run: `libraries.test`, `seatbelt.test` (the code is only used by the Seatbelt backend). Still not verified without a Mac: everything in "Not verified" above.
- **Re-check of the second review's change (2026-11-19).** Confirmed: the allowed set and its checks are unchanged apart from the writable rule moving to each launch; the remembered answer never depends on a launch's writable places (both orders tested); the extra `stat` of a configuration path turns every failure into "absent" and cannot fail a launch. One gap: the per-launch rule checking only the configuration path (not its link and real path) survived the tests; a test now covers a linked configuration whose real file is in a writable place (left out, no refusal, back for the next launch). Mutation checks on the built file, each restored byte-identical: twelve, all failing a test after that addition.

## P09 (first slice): a landing is gated on the project's required checks, run on the exact integrated tree (Claude agent, 2026-11-18)

Before this slice the integration policy's `requiredChecks` (P08) were stored and shown but never run: a landing went ahead whatever they said.

**Built.**
- **The gate (`controller/src/landing/landing-gate.ts`, `LandingGate`).** Asked by `WorkspaceOpService` for every `landing`, inside the quiesce, after the integrator lease is shown the second time and before the host is asked to write anything. It reads the project's required checks through `IntegrationPolicyService.effective` (new; no caller, the lock and the record made at first read apply, as the P08 note asked), then asks the host that holds the checkout for the change the landing would carry and for the test results. What each check means:
  - `tests`: the task contract's test commands (`contract.set checks`, W05's field), run by the host in the sandbox on a fresh copy of the integrated tree. A contract version the author stored itself is skipped back to the one before (`ContractService.landingTests`), so an author cannot loosen the checks of its own landing. No contract or no commands: `not_run`.
  - `review`: the landing names the reviewed code submission (`workspace.request` `submissionId`, now accepted for `landing` too; only "a code submission of this task" is checked at the door). Its newest review must approve it and its patch ID must equal the patch ID of the change being landed: an approval carries over to a different tree (a refresh onto a newer base) only while the patch is unchanged. Not reviewed yet or no submission named: `not_run`; newest review says changes/reject, or another patch: `fail`. `SubmissionApproval` now carries `patchId` and `newest`.
  - `qa`, `docs`, `director`: not collected at landing yet, always `not_run` (see Not done).
  `not_run` counts as failed: the landing passes only when every required result is `pass`. A host without `landingChecks`, a host that throws or does not answer within the commands' time plus a minute, no checkout, an unreadable change or nothing to land make every required check `not_run`. A project that requires no check is not gated and the host is not asked. Required checks that cannot be read refuse the landing.
- **Bound to the tree.** Every result names `boundTo` (the integrated tree ID); the whole verdict (`required`, `passed`, `base`, `tree`, `patchId`, `submissionId`, `contractVersion`, `results` with each command's state, exit code, time and the redacted end of its output) is kept on the landing's request record as `checks`. When the gate passed, the host is told `checkedTree` and lands only when the checkout's head still has exactly that tree (`WorkspaceHost.#land`); work committed after the checks refuses the landing with nothing written. Results are never reused: each landing runs the checks again, so a different tree never passes on old evidence.
- **A failure goes back to the author.** The landing is `refused` with a summary naming what failed; the author (the agent that made the named code submission, else the task's assignee) gets the results as a controller notice in its inbox (`AgentMessageService.noticeFromController`, command ID `lgc-<request>`, recorded as `toldAuthor`), and a quiet attempt of the task is told the same text (`told`).
- **The host side (`worker/src/workspace/landing-checks.ts`, `landingChecks`).** `GitBridge.committedChange` reads base, head, the head's tree and the stable patch ID of base..head (`patchId` gained a `to` argument; the diff has the same form as a staged submission's, so the same change has the same ID, tested). For each command: a fresh folder, `GitBridge.exportTree` writes exactly that tree into it (throwaway index, neutral attributes, no `.git`), an empty home and scratch, the recipe from `attemptSandbox` (no network, the task's git directory named so nothing reaching it is mounted, only the given read-only inputs), the owner's limits and best-effort setting read at each run, the launcher's time limit (the owner's wall time when smaller); the folder is removed afterwards. ### P09 first slice, first Opus review (Claude agent, 2026-11-18)

**Fixed.**
1. **The review check took the submitter's word for the patch ID.** `submission.record` accepts any `patchId` an agent names next to its base and tree, and the gate compared only that claim with the landed patch: a code submission whose named patch ID did not belong to its reviewed tree could carry an approval to a different change. Now the gate reads the named submission before asking the host and passes its base and tree (`landingChecks` `reviewed`); the host computes their stable patch ID from the checkout's own objects (`GitBridge.patchId` with `to`, answered as `reviewedPatchId`, or `reviewedProblem`). `review` passes only when that computed ID equals both the ID the submission names and the landed change's; a mismatch is `fail` ("names patch X, but its base and tree make patch Y"), an ID the host cannot compute (objects missing, a host that does not answer the field) is `not_run`. The approval is read again after the host's run, so a review that asked for changes while the tests ran still refuses.
2. **The author's own contract versions were skipped only for the assignee.** The gate named only `assignee` as the author, so when the agent that made the reviewed submission was not the assignee, a contract version it stored itself (for example one with no test commands) was used. `ContractService.landingTests` now takes a list of authors and the gate names both the assignee and the submitter of the landed submission. The controller test now covers it with the submitter not the assignee (it only passed before because the test set the assignee to the submitter).
3. The `tests` summary for "no usable contract" said the task had no contract even when it had one stored only by its author; it now says the author's own versions are not used.

**Tests added.** Gate: the host is asked for the reviewed base and tree; a claimed patch ID that its base and tree do not make fails; an uncomputable one is not run; a review turned to changes during the run fails; both authors are named. Controller (4 backends): the submitter's loosened contract is not used, the claimed/computed mismatch and the missing computed ID refuse the landing. Worker (real git): the reviewed patch ID equals the staged one, differs for an older reviewed tree, and a missing object or an empty change is a problem, not an ID.

**Mutants on the compiled code (each restored, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`).** Author's contract version not skipped: 4 failures; the landed patch comparison removed: 5; the claimed-vs-computed comparison removed: 5; not run counted as passed: 10; the host's `checkedTree` comparison removed: 1 (worker); `checkedTree` not sent: 4.

**Left for follow-up.**
1. When the gate gives up waiting for the host (the commands' time plus a minute), the host's check processes are not stopped; they keep running on their own copies after the landing was refused and the quiet lifted.
2. A task whose only contract versions were stored by its own author can never pass `tests`: the author is told, the owner is not (no needs-you notice); someone else has to set the contract.
3. `GitBridge.patchId` takes only a 40-hex base, so on a SHA-256 repository every `review` is `not_run` (fails closed).

### P09 first slice, second Opus review (Claude agent, clean context, 2026-11-18)

**Fixed.**
1. **A whitespace-only change kept the reviewed patch ID, so an approval carried over to code nobody reviewed.** `GitBridge.patchId` used `git patch-id --stable`, which strips every whitespace character from each line before hashing. Shown on git 2.53: moving `b()` out of a Python loop (re-indenting it) and turning the string `"a b"` into `"ab"` gave the same `--stable` ID as the reviewed change, so the `review` check passed for a landing that differed from what the reviewer approved. `patchId` now runs `git patch-id --verbatim` (stable ordering, whitespace kept; available in git 2.39.5, checked in a `node:22.15.0` container, and 2.53). Every patch ID (H12n `stageWork`, the landed change, the host-computed reviewed one) comes from this one function, so they stay comparable; a submission recorded before this change carries an old-form ID and now needs a new submission (fails closed). The two tests that pinned `--stable` (`local-host.test.ts`, `h12n-submit-host.test.ts`) now pin `--verbatim`.
2. **An author's loosened test commands counted once anyone else stored a later contract version.** `ContractService.landingTests` skipped only versions the author STORED, so after the author set its checks to a command that always passes, any later version by someone else that changed another field (the owner's priority, an escalation's difficulty) carried the author's checks forward and they ran. It now finds who SET the checks: it walks back to the version that introduced the checks the newest version holds, and when an author introduced them it continues from the version before that. Bounded at 200 reads and a missing stored version (both fail closed).

**Tests added.** Worker (real git): a re-indented line and a changed string spacing give a different patch ID from the reviewed one, while git's whitespace-stripping ID would not tell them apart. Controller (4 backends): the author's always-passing checks still do not run after the owner stores a priority change; checks the owner set still run after the author stores another field (`contractVersion` names the newest version).

**Mutants on the compiled code (each alone, restored and compared byte for byte, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`).** Not run counted as passed: 10 failures; landed patch comparison removed: 5; claimed-vs-computed comparison removed: 5; host `checkedTree` comparison removed: 1; author versions not skipped: 4; checks setter not tracked: 4; `--stable` instead of `--verbatim`: 1; checks run on the checkout instead of the copy: 2; gate answer ignored: 16; `checkedTree` not sent: 4.

**Judged, left for follow-up.**
1. (first review 1) Check processes outliving the gate's wait: each still ends at its own launcher time limit and works only on its own copy, so what lands is not affected; worth stopping them, not a correctness problem.
2. (first review 2, now slightly wider) Checks set only by the task's own authors never pass `tests`, and an owner who re-saves the same checks does not count as setting them (an unchanged value is not a change). Fails closed; it needs a needs-you notice to the owner or an explicit "accept these checks" step.
3. (first review 3) SHA-256 repositories fail closed (40-hex base only). Acceptable until such repositories are supported.
4. Git older than 2.39 has no `patch-id --verbatim`: staging a submission and every `review` check then fail (closed). The project names no minimum git version; this sets 2.39 in practice for submissions.
5. A mode-only change (Not done 6) means the landed tree can differ from the checked tree in executable bits only; a check that relies on such a bit can pass on the checked tree and not hold on the landed one.

**Verified (after `tsc --build --force`, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`).** Worker suite 551 of 552 (1 skipped, 0 failed). The 42 test files the diff can reach outside the worker (integration `h12*` and `p09`; controller `planning`, `workspace-ops`, `landing`, `submissions`, `policy`, `api/start-submission`, `api/start-work-end`): 749 of 749. Other suites not rerun (the diff does not reach them); session CI is the net.

## P09 + P10 together: the landing gate judges the landing queue's head (merge of origin/main into card-p09-s1, Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-19)

P09 (the landing gate) and P10's queue slice were built side by side and both redefined the landing in `workspace-ops.ts` and the host. This merge composes them by design; neither slice's rules were dropped.

- **One submission for both.** With the landing queue composed (always, through `startController`), the submission a landing lands is the queue's head: `landingQueue.check` decides it (a `submissionId` the caller names must be the task's queued one, else `invalid_transition`, as P10 had; a task that is not the head is refused the same way, before anything is recorded and before the gate or host is asked). The record keeps it as `queued`, and the gate judges exactly that submission (`queued.submissionId`), whether or not the caller named it. P09's `landedSubmission` (checked only as "a code submission of this task" by `#codeOfTask`) is used only where no queue is composed (unit rigs). The author told about a refused gate is the submitter of that same submission (else the assignee).
- **Order inside the quiesce.** The lease, the approval and the queue are shown again (P10), then the gate runs the checks (P09), then, when the gate actually had required checks, the lease and the queue are shown once more (new: tests can run for minutes, the same reason P10 shows them a second time after the quiesce), and only then is the host asked. A queue that moved or a lease that ran out while the checks ran lands nothing (`refused`, the host not asked; the gate's results stay on the record).
- **The host checks both.** `WorkspaceCall` carries `submission` (P10: the landing branch is at its base, and the checkout's committed work is exactly its approved tree on that base) and `checkedTree` (P09: the head still has exactly the tree the checks ran on); `WorkspaceHost.#land` refuses unless both hold. On a landable checkout they name the same tree. The host accepts `submission` on `release` and `landing`, and `checkedTree` on `landing` only.
- **Outcomes.** A refused gate is a `refused` landing: the queue entry stays (nothing is dequeued unless the host confirms `landed` for exactly the queued submission, base and tree), the summary says the submission stays in the landing queue, and the author gets the results (`toldAuthor`). A passing gate lands only the checked tree, and the landing's outcome write removes the entry and records it in the queue's `landed` list, as P10 built.
- **Other files.** `submissions.ts` `approvalOf` answers `patchId` and `newest` (P09) and `submittedAt` (P10). `landing/index.ts` and `api/start.ts` export and compose both the gate and the queue. The chat's `workspace.request` description, the API summary of `workspace.request` and `api-v1.md` (regenerated) now say both: the queue's oldest lands, gated on the required checks for that submission, and the result names `queued`, `landedSubmission`, `checks` and `toldAuthor`.
- **Tests.** New `controller/workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p09-p10.test.ts` (4 backends, the real queue, gate, policy and contract services): a non-head task, a non-head named submission and the head task naming another task's submission are refused before the gate or host is asked; the head with a failing test command is refused, judged for the queued submission though the landing named none, stays queued, and its submitter is told; once the checks pass the host is told both `submission` and `checkedTree` (the same tree), the entry leaves the queue and a repeat does nothing again; the queue moving while the checks run lands nothing even though they passed. `integration/p09-landing-checks.test.ts` now names the landing branch before the review, so the controller queues the approved submission itself; it checks the refused landing leaves it queued and the landing takes it out (before, the approval came before the branch was named and the landing was refused by the queue).
- **Mutants on the compiled `workspace-ops.js` (each alone, restored and compared by checksum), against the new test:** the gate judging only a named submission (not the queue's): 8 of 8 fail; the author looked up from the named submission only: 4 fail; no showing of the lease and queue after the gate: 4 fail; `checkedTree` not sent: 4 fail.
- **Left as before.** Remote hosts answer neither `landingChecks` (P09 Not done 3) nor a landing `submission` (P10 Not done): on a remote host a gated or queued landing is refused (fails closed).
- **Verified (after `tsc --build --force`, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, offline guard, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`).** Controller `workspace-ops/` (with `workspace-ops-p09`, the P10 tests and the new composed test), `landing/`, `submissions/`, `planning/`, `api/start-p10*`, `api/start-submission`, `api/start-work-end`, `api/api.test`: 614 of 614 before the new test, which then passed 8 of 8; controller `chat/` and `api/operations*` (the verb and summary changed) with the new test: 1420 of 1420; worker `workspace/` and `sandbox/host-runner`: 157 of 158 (1 skipped, Windows only); integration `h12*` and `p09`: 40 of 40 after the `p09` change (the `p09` test alone 1 of 1; before the change it was the one failure, refused by the queue). `api-v1.md` equal to `node scripts/api-docs.mjs`. **Skipped:** d01/q04/q02/p07 neighbours (the merge did not touch their code; only an import line in `api/start.ts` sat next to theirs), other controller shards and packages; CI is the net.

- **Follow-up (P09 + P10): an owner landing with an empty queue judges no submission (fails closed).** `checkLanding` lets the owner land a task that has nothing queued only while the branch's queue is empty; it then answers no queued submission, so the landing names no submission and the gate has nothing to judge for `review`. A project whose required checks include review therefore refuses that landing (the `review` check is not met), by design: no approval is assumed. This is a refusal, not a defect. **Intended owner flow:** the author's code submission is approved by a reviewer, then put in the queue (the controller queues it itself when the approval is recorded, `queueApproved`; otherwise `landing.queue.add`, by the owner, an integrator with `integration.lease`, or the submission's author); the integrator (or the owner, for the queue's oldest) lands it with `workspace.request` (`landing`), naming that submission or none, and the gate judges the queue's head (the integrator lease is shown when the request is made, once the task is quiet and again after the checks). An owner landing with an empty queue is for projects that require no review (only test commands), under the host's own rules.
- **Follow-up tests.** `workspace-ops-p09-p10.test.ts` gained a lease case through the `landingLease` dependency (not held at the start: refused, no record, nothing asked of gate or host; held at the start and expired while the checks ran: `refused` with the checks' results kept, host not asked to land, entry stays queued, nobody told; held again: lands) and "no record written" assertions (record count of `workspace-request`) after the refusals before the gate. New `submissions/submissions-approval-submitted-at.test.ts` (4 backends) checks `approvalOf` answers each code submission's own `submittedAt` (before and after approval, unaffected by later reviews), which the queue's ordering and its older-submission refusal rely on.

## Own-hardware workflow: Windows steps use Git Bash, not the WSL launcher (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-19)

Run 44453704944 of `.github/workflows/own-hardware.yml` started no test on the owner's Windows runner: in jobs "Windows Sandbox (real)" (step "Run the real Windows Sandbox tests") and "Probe nimblenewt-windows" (step "Record the machine"; "One run of the whole suite" would have failed the same way) `shell: bash` resolved to `C:\WINDOWS\system32\bash.EXE`, the WSL launcher, which dropped the backslashes of the runner's script path (`/bin/bash: C:actions-runner_work_temp...sh: No such file or directory`). The macOS probe ran normally (its suite run had 7 failing tests; that is a separate matter, not touched here).

Done: both jobs that can run on the Windows runner (`probe` for the `nimblenewt-windows` matrix entry, and `sandbox-windows`) now start, right after the checkout, with a step "Use Git Bash for bash steps" (`if: runner.os == 'Windows'`, Windows PowerShell). It looks for Git's `bin\bash.exe` from the `git.exe` on the PATH (`Git\cmd`, `Git\bin` or `Git\mingw64\bin`), then in `%ProgramFiles%\Git\bin`, prints the bash version it found, and adds that folder to `GITHUB_PATH`. The runner searches the added folders before the machine PATH when it resolves `shell: bash`, so every later bash step in that job runs under Git Bash. If Git Bash is missing the step fails with a clear error instead of reaching the WSL launcher. The steps that run the tests, their commands, environment and artifacts are unchanged; macOS skips the new step. `docs/nimblenewt/own-hardware-runners.md` says bash must be Git Bash and names, as an option only, putting `C:\Program Files\Git\bin` ahead of System32 in the runner service's PATH. No other workflow targets a self-hosted runner (the hosted `windows-latest` jobs in exhaustive.yml, qa.yml and postgres-versions.yml already get Git Bash from GitHub's image).

ASSUMPTION: a PATH step rather than `shell: 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe ... {0}'`. The runner (actions/runner, `ScriptHandlerHelpers.ParseShellOptionString`) splits a custom `shell:` line at its first space and has no quoting, so a path under "Program Files" cannot be named there; the 8.3 short name (`C:\PROGRA~1\...`) depends on a per-volume setting. The PATH step keeps the test steps identical on both systems.

NOT done: the workflow has not been run. This agent may not dispatch workflows, so whether the Windows jobs now get past the bash step is unproven until the owner runs "Own hardware" from main again. Checked here: the YAML parses (PyYAML) and the step order is as intended; no repository test reads this workflow file; actionlint and PowerShell are not installed on this machine, so neither the workflow expressions nor the PowerShell script were checked by a tool.

Review (clean-context Opus 5.5, 2026-11-19): fixed in both copies of the step. (1) The bash check passed `-c 'echo "...$BASH ($BASH_VERSION)"'`; Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape double quotes inside a native argument, so bash would have received a split command and printed only part of the line; the text now has no double quotes or parentheses. (2) A `git.exe` found in `Git\mingw64\bin` gave `Git\mingw64\bin` as the candidate (no bash there); the parent of that folder's root is now also tried, and empty parents (a `git.exe` at a drive root) are skipped instead of stopping the step in `Join-Path`. `Get-Command` now takes the first application match only. Checked and kept: `GITHUB_PATH` is written as UTF-8 without a BOM with a `\n` ending; the runner resolves `shell: bash` with the prepended path (`WhichUtil.Which(..., prependPath)`), effective from the next step; a failing setup step skips the test steps but the `if: always()` uploads still run; the macOS probe skips the step; no test step changed. The YAML parses (PyYAML); PowerShell and actionlint are still not available here.

## Hardware-chain evidence for G05, A03b, G06 and Y02: the missing producers and workflow steps (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-19)

A read-only audit of the four cards found that no run, however green, could produce the evidence their gates ask for: nothing ran the Y02 scenario set in any workflow, nothing produced the Windows block of a G05 report, there was no G06 test for paths over 260 characters and no G06 record, and nothing produced Y02's owner-decisions-per-day and stall figures. This batch builds those, so that ONE later run of own-hardware.yml plus exhaustive.yml plus qa.yml on the same main commit can gather the evidence. No hardware evidence is claimed, no card status is changed and no generated plan file is edited.

**Done**
- `own-hardware.yml`, job `Windows Sandbox (real)` (same guards: by hand, from main, only `nimblenewt-windows`; the Git Bash step is kept first). After the real Windows Sandbox tests it now also, on the same commit: records the filesystem for G06 (`g06-host.json`: filesystem type and cluster size of the checkout's and temporary folder's volumes, `LongPathsEnabled`, 8.3 short names and the checkout's case sensitivity reduced to the words enabled/disabled, OS caption, version and build, Node; no volume label, serial or account name); runs the controller working-directory check; runs `containment-evidence.mjs run` with the Windows block filled from the tests' summary and uploads ONLY the redacted report (the unredacted one goes to a local folder that is never uploaded, as the G05 notes' assumption asked); runs the G06 long-path test; and runs `y02-checkpoint.mjs run` with `NIMBLENEWT_REAL_WINDOWS_SANDBOX=1` (the Sandbox tests inside it write to their own folders, so they cannot replace the uploaded summary). Every one of those steps has `continue-on-error`, so a failure in one does not hide the others; a last step writes a table of every outcome to the job summary and then fails the job if any step failed, so a green job still means everything passed. The job timeout is 300 minutes (the Y02 set runs controller files on four storage backends on the owner's PC). New artifacts: `containment-windows-own-hardware`, `g06-host-windows`, `y02-scenarios-windows-own-hardware`.
- `exhaustive.yml`, new job `Y02 scenarios / ubuntu-latest, macos-latest`: `y02-checkpoint.mjs run` (the 8 scenarios, sandbox required) on the same commit as the rest of the exhaustive run, with bubblewrap on Linux; uploads `y02-scenarios-Linux` / `y02-scenarios-macOS` and puts the per-scenario lines in the job summary.
- G05 Windows block producer, `packages/worker/src/sandbox/containment-windows-evidence.ts`: `windows-real.test.ts` now writes, in its uploaded `summary.json` (booleans only), a schema, the supervisor-ACL mode in use and the escape fixture's controls (the guest wrote the mapped checkout; could not write the read-only input, `.git` or through a junction; the checkout's ACL was given back exactly). `windowsEvidenceFromSummary` turns that into the report's `windows` block: mapped-output ACL positive and negative are true only when the whole escape test passed (its host-side checks included) and each control was seen; the supervisor-ACL check is `strict` only when strict was in use AND its test passed; `featureEnabledOnly` is true when no test that starts a real sandbox passed; the account is always written as `<user>`; logout and reboot are always false (no automation proves them). `containment-evidence.mjs run` takes `--windows-summary FILE [--workdir-check FILE]` and `--redact [--local DIR]` (redaction touches only free text: OS and backend descriptions, the capacity reason, case details, the trusted-host authority and the account; ids, verdicts, commit, time and booleans stay exactly, and a redacted report that no longer reads as a report is not written). With `--redact`, what the command prints is redacted too.
- Controller working-directory check, `scripts/g05-workdir-check.mjs`: generates the real service unit for the platform (on Windows the scheduled task, whose working directory would otherwise default to System32), starts the real release launcher from that unit's working directory against a disposable release root with one installed release, and checks that the controller of that release runs in its own release folder (not the checkout, not the system folder). Output: booleans and fixed texts only. Passes here on Linux.
- G06: `packages/worker/src/workspace/long-paths.test.ts`.
