## P10 queue race test on Windows: a timing assumption in the test, not a store race (Claude agent, 2026-11-19)

- **Symptom.** On the Windows own-hardware runs (44552386792, 44607130723) the test "two integrators racing for the branch, and two landings racing for the queue" got `['done','fenced','done']` instead of `['done','fenced','invalid_transition']`.
- **Cause.** The test held the host's answer, waited a fixed 50 ms, then released it. The third landing (task two, not the oldest) is judged by the queue check when its request is processed. On a slow machine that check had not run yet when the host was released; by then task one had landed and left the queue, so task two really was the oldest and landing it was correct. The queue and lease stores were not at fault: `checkLanding` is a read made when the request is made and again right before the host is asked; with nothing taken out of the queue meanwhile (as in this test), a task becomes the oldest only when the earlier landing's outcome is written, which takes its entry out in that same revision-checked write (`landedChanges`) after the host answered; so here a second landing can reach the host only after the first one's outcome is recorded, never at the same time. The failing runs fit this: the assertion that only one landing had reached the host passed, and the third landing was done afterwards, in turn.
- **Fix (test only).** The second service's queue check is now observed, and the test waits until the later landing's check has finished (an event, not a time) before releasing the host. The interleaving is forced the same way on every OS; the assertions are unchanged and still strict.
- **Run.** `landing-queue-p10` race test three times and `packages/controller/dist/landing/*.test.js` (89 tests, all backends incl. PostgreSQL) through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: all passed. Windows not runnable here.
- **First review (Claude agent, Opus).** Conclusion checked against `workspace-ops.ts` (`request`, the second showing, `#settle`/`#dequeueChange`), `queue-ops.ts` and `landing-queue.ts`: while the queue changes only by landings, no path lets two landings reach the host together or two landings of the queue both be done before the first is recorded. Test hardened: a landing that ends before the point waited for (a fault before the host or before its queue check) ends the wait, so the file reports it instead of waiting for its 900 s timeout; it asserts that the later landing was judged; the held host answer is released in a `finally`, so a failed assertion no longer leaves the first landing waiting. Mutations: a 200 ms delay before task two's check (the Windows timing) still passes on all four backends; the head-of-queue refusal in `checkLanding` removed fails on all four (reference store, SQLite and the worker thread at "only one landing reached the host", PostgreSQL at `["done","fenced","done"]`) without hanging. Runs through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: the race test (4 backends) and `dist/landing/*.test.js` 89 of 89.
- **Second review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** Test change agreed: the waits end on an event or on the landing ending, `ask` turns every failure into a code (no rejection is left unhandled), and `go()` runs in a `finally`. Notes narrowed: the "never at the same time" holds while the queue changes only by landings. Checked by an experiment not kept in the tree: when the owner takes task one out of the queue while its landing waits on the host (`landing.queue.remove`, also `withdrawUnapproved`), task two becomes the oldest, passes both queue checks and reaches the host while task one is still there (2 host calls at once on all backends). Nothing here changes that; whether a landing in progress should keep its place (or the take-out wait for it) is a separate P10 question, not a test fault. Runs through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: the race test (4 backends) unchanged, and again with a 300 ms delay before task two's check (all pass); `dist/landing/*.test.js` 89 of 89.

- **Windows Sandbox cleanup acts only on recorded folders.** Follow-up to the open point (a) above: any local account could create a folder under `%ProgramData%` with the evidence runs' name pattern. Each real test now creates its base folder with `createRecordedFolder` (windows-records.ts): a record file `<name>.json` (folder path, random token, job id) in the runner-owned work area (`<RUNNER_TEMP>\nn-wsb-records`, or the folder in NIMBLENEWT_WSB_RECORDS, else the temporary folder) and the same token in a marker file (`.nn-wsb-token`) inside the folder, both written before the folder is used. `searchEvidenceDirs` (used by `scripts/wsb-cleanup.mjs`) takes control folders only from recorded folders whose marker matches the token, whose path is directly under ProgramData with the pattern's name, and which are not links or junctions. A pattern folder with no record, a record with a different token, an unreadable record or a record naming another place is kept and reported by name only (a count in the log, the names in the local file); a record whose folder is gone is dropped quietly. Without a work area or when a list fails nothing is trusted, so everything is kept. The G05 base under the runner's temporary folder is unchanged. Not exit 1 by themselves: the reported folders do not fail the step, the kept jobs still do. - **In-progress take-out (follow-up to the second review above, 2026-11-19).** ASSUMPTION (Rob's "nothing waits on Rob"; smallest and most reversible choice): an entry whose landing is in progress cannot be taken out of the landing queue until that landing ends, so the queue never has two landings at the host. In progress means the task's open workspace request is a `landing` still in state `started` (from the moment it is recorded, through the quiesce and the checks, to the host's answer). `LandingQueueService.remove` (the one write that `landing.queue.remove` and the controller's `withdrawUnapproved` both use) reads the task's open-request pointer and request inside its own write and refuses `invalid_transition` with a plain reason (it is being landed right now; wait for that landing to end, then take it out if still queued). The same write also rewrites the pointer unchanged, so a landing that starts at that very moment changes the pointer and one of the two loses the race (the take-out is built again and refused, or the landing fails before the host); a task with no pointer yet gets an empty one created in the same write, so there too exactly one of the two commits (first review: before this, a take-out that read "no pointer" and committed after the landing's last showing of the queue could still take the head out while it was at the host, letting the next landing reach the host too; now covered by a test that holds the take-out's read until the landing is at the host). The rewrite bumps the pointer's revision only when the take-out is allowed (no landing started): a non-landing workspace request of the same task starting at that very moment gets `stale_revision` before anything is done, and its `settle` re-reads (20 tries). Because it is in the queue layer it holds on all 4 backends. Effects: `withdrawUnapproved` stays best effort and a refused withdrawal is not retried; a head whose approval was taken back mid-landing that then fails stays queued, and the next landing is refused with `review_invalid` telling the owner to take it out, which is now allowed. A landing left `started` by a stopped controller is resolved by the existing recovery, which also frees the take-out. Reversible: remove the check. Tests: `landing-queue-p10.test.ts` (new test: held host answer, take-out by owner, integrator and withdrawal refused while the head is at the host, second entry never reaches the host (calls stay 1), allowed after the landing ends; the quiesce case and the take-out-during-host case now assert the refusal), `workspace-ops-p09-p10.test.ts` (the queue moving during the checks is now a newer submission taking the head's place). Mutation check on `dist` (guard disabled): 12 failures (3 tests on each of 4 backends); restored. API text of `landing.queue.remove` updated (`npm run api:docs:write`).
- **In-progress take-out, second review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** Atomicity checked: `CommandRunner.command` builds once and maps any `revision_conflict` to the build's `contention`; the storage conformance suite (run on all 4 backends) holds a create of an existing record and a stale update to `revision_conflict` and lets exactly one of concurrent creators or writers win. Once a landing's `started` record and pointer commit, no take-out commits until it ends (a take-out that read before conflicts on the pointer, is built again and refused; one that committed before is seen by the landing's second showing of the queue). The empty `{}` pointer is what every finished request leaves, and every reader (`openFor`, `heldFor`, `recover`, `#resolveOpen`, `#openChange`) treats it as nothing open; no other code reads the kind. Found and fixed: (1) a repeat of a landing's command while its first call is at the host marks the record `uncertain` and leaves the pointer naming it, so the take-out was allowed and the next entry could reach the host too; the take-out now also waits for a landing the pointer names as `uncertain` (also what a stopped controller leaves until recovery closes it, the same rule as `openFor`); new test, fails on all 4 backends without it. (2) A take-out that rewrote the pointer while a non-landing request (refresh, release, quarantine, the author's reapply) of the same task was being recorded answered that request `stale_revision`; the start write is now built again (at most 5 times) while its record does not exist yet; new test, fails on all 4 backends without it. For a landing this is still safe: its second showing of the queue refuses it. (3) `#markUncertain` swallowed a lost race on the pointer alone, leaving the record `started`; it now builds again (at most 5 times) while the record itself is unchanged. The second-review test of a landed submission again covers a submission that is no longer queued when it lands (a newer one took its place during the landing). Runs through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: `dist/landing/*.test.js` 105 of 105, `dist/workspace-ops/*.test.js` 288 of 288, `dist/api/start-p10-queue.test.js` 1 of 1; `npm run api:docs:write` no diff.
- **In-progress take-out, re-check (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** The two bounded loops checked: a failed commit records nothing (the operation is all or nothing), so building the start again under the same command ID cannot write a second record or skip the repeat logic (a record already there ends the loop with the error; the record is a create, so only one can exist); `#markUncertain` builds again only while the request's own revision is unchanged. 'uncertain' blocking a take-out cannot last: the request's own settle clears the pointer, and otherwise the dispatcher's `workspace.recover` loop (`#resolveOpen`) lifts its freeze and clears the pointer. Two tests added (all 4 backends): a take-out that commits while a landing is being recorded wins and the landing, its start built again, is refused before the host (the opposite order to the first review's test); and a stopped controller's left request is still marked uncertain when a take-out rewrites the pointer at that moment (the `#markUncertain` loop had no test: with one try the test fails on all 4 backends).

- The Windows cleanup now gives the G05 base (`NIMBLENEWT_G05_WSB_BASE` or `RUNNER_TEMP\nn-g05-wsb`) the conditions recorded `%ProgramData%` folders get. `searchEvidenceDirs` runs the same `recordDirProblem` (exported from windows-records.ts, now with a label) on the base: a link or junction, an account other than the runner's own that can change it, or an unreadable access list leaves the base out of `dirs`; an unreadable owner does the same. - **First review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** (1) On a default Windows install the drive root `C:\` grants `Authenticated Users` Modify to every folder made under it (`(OI)(CI)(IO)(M)`), so `C:\actions-runner\_work\_temp\nn-g05-wsb` prints `NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(I)(M)` and `parseIcaclsWritable` lists it: the base check refuses on every run on Rob's machine (runner in `C:\actions-runner`), elevated or not, and the step exits 1 each time a G05 control folder exists. An elevated runner then passes: its folders and files are all owned by Administrators (S-1-5-32-544), so the owner comparison holds, and SYSTEM/Administrators are not counted as writers. (2) Found and fixed: the base's own owner was not anchored, so a base another account made in its place (possible while the work folder is writable by all), owned by that account and listing only the runner's account, passed every check, and contents that account wrote matched "the base's owner". The base's owner must now be SYSTEM, Administrators or TrustedInstaller, or the owner of the believed records folder (the runner's own account when not elevated); otherwise held with a fixed text. Tests (windows.test.ts): a foreign-owned base, the same with a records folder of another owner (held), owned by the records folder's owner and by Administrators (released); and the default-inherited icacls print yields Authenticated Users, the fixed one only the runner's account. Folders below that only inherit get the new entries (Windows passes a folder's inheritable entries on when its list changes); entries set directly further down stay. The runner keeps working: its account has its own full-control entry, so `run.cmd` started normally (Administrators is then deny-only) or elevated both have access; SYSTEM keeps full access (Defender, services); git does not depend on these entries. ## T08 (third slice): consumers stay on their pinned shared tool version until they opt in (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

T08 is still **not** complete and stays `planned`; this is the third slice, on base 33d5784d. Verified (Linux, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`): `tsc --build`; controller `catalog`, `dependencies`, `commands`, `environments` 339/339; `toolbridge`, `status`, `retention` 543/543; `chat` 1414/1414; `api` files `api*`, `operations*`, `start-toolbox*`, `start-catalog*`, `start-status*`, `start-tool-bridge*`, `start-revoke*` 100/100 (toolbox suites on all four backends); pi-adapter 270/270; `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs` 27/27; `scripts/api-docs.mjs` output byte-identical to the regenerated `api-v1.md`. Mutation checks: 17 mutations of the new code (pin resolution, first-use pin, the agent-only and revoked opt-in rules, the audience check, each notice, the everyone move, the consumers permission, the listing, the retention hold, the bridge refusal text and argument list, chat name lookup, the status line), each killed by the new tests. Skipped: the remaining controller `api` files and other directories (they do not use the changed catalogue paths), the integration package (real workers), hosted Windows/macOS (CI). It covers the acceptance clause "consumers stay on their pinned version until they opt in" (README 320, 354: "other agents opt into an approved version rather than receiving silent global changes"; "a revoked queued version must be blocked or explicitly replanned, not silently substituted"). Changed: `catalog/catalog.ts` (pin record, resolution, `optIn`, `pins`, `consumers`, notices), `catalog/notices.ts` (two notice kinds), `retention/references.ts` (pins hold versions), `api/operations.ts` (three operations), `toolbridge/service.ts` and `pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts` (two bridge tools), `status/status.ts` and `api/start.ts` (the `toolbox` status line), `chat/commands.ts`, `chat/chat.ts` and `chat/model-interpreter.ts` (owner chat op), `domain/ids.ts` (the `cpn` prefix). Tests: `catalog/toolbox-pins.test.ts` (4 tests on each of the four backends), `api/start-toolbox-pins.test.ts` (one composed test through `startController`: agents' own credentials on the state API, the owner's status and chat), a bridge suite in `toolbridge/service.test.ts` (four backends) and additions to `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts`.

**Done in this slice**

- **The pin record** (`catalog-pins`, one per shared entry, keyed `cpn-` by the tool's canonical name): each consumer agent (`agent:<ID>`, its durable identity), its version, when, who set it and how (`first-use` or `opt-in`). At most 1000 consumers per tool (`CATALOG_LIMITS.pins`).
- **The first run pins.** After `authorizeRun` records a run of a `toolbox.` tool by an agent that has no pin, the agent is pinned to the version it ran, in a separate write. The command ID is derived from the agent and the tool, so once a first-use pin is written it is never written again by a run (a later opt-in or owner move is never overwritten). It is best effort: contention is retried twice, and any other failure leaves the run as it was (the pin is written at the next run).
- **What a call naming no version resolves to.** For an agent, `#resolve` uses the pin of a shared entry when the pinned version is still published, whatever has been released, set aside or rolled back since. Every path goes through it: `get` (and so the bridge's `tool.describe` and `tool.invoke`), `source`, `copy` and `authorizeRun` without a version. `list` (the bridge's `tool.discover`) shows the pinned version as the version, so the agent's tool list matches what a call runs. `toolbox.list` keeps `latest` as the version in use and adds `pinned` (and `pinRevoked`) for the caller. Owners, services and system or personal entries are never pinned. Naming a version runs that version and moves no pin. Proposals keep using the version in use (`chosenVersion`) as their default base, not the author's pin.
- **A revoked pin is refused, not replaced.** `get` without a version returns the pinned version with `revoked` and `pinned: true`. The bridge refuses the call with "... was revoked (reason); it is the version you are pinned to: opt in to another (toolbox-optin) or name a version", and `authorizeRun` refuses it as for any revoked version. A version set aside (deprecated or above a rollback) keeps running for the agents pinned to it.
- **Opt in** (`toolbox.optin`, `CatalogService.optIn`). An agent moves its own pin to a published, unrevoked version of a tool it may read; the default is the version in use now, and an older one is allowed (that is its choice). A tool it may not read is `not_found`, the same answer as for a tool that does not exist. The owner moves one agent (`agentId`) or every agent pinned to the tool (`everyone`), names exactly one of the two, and each agent actually moved is told in its toolbox inbox (kind `pin`). An agent naming `agentId` or `everyone` is refused (`forbidden`), maintainers included: publishing, rolling back or holding `toolbox.manage` never moves a consumer. The pin write checks the entry's revision, so a revocation at the same moment makes the opt-in ask again. A repeat of a committed opt-in is answered from its record and tells nobody again.
- **Notices** (the slice 2 toolbox inbox, read with `toolbox.notices`). After a shared release commits, each agent pinned to a version older than the one now in use is told once per in-use version (kind `release`, naming `toolbox.optin`). After a revocation, each agent pinned to that version is told that calls naming no version are refused until it opts in, and which version is in use (kind `revocation`). After a deprecate or rollback, each agent pinned to a version now set aside is told it still runs for it (kind `pin`). All are written after the command commits, keyed so a repeat sends nothing new.
- **Reads.** `toolbox.pins` (an agent's own pins: version, version in use, `newer`, `setAside`, `revoked` with reason). `toolbox.consumers` (the owner, or a maintainer whose grant covers the tool's audience, as for `toolbox.forks`): each agent's pin with `how`, `by`, `revoked`, `setAside`, and the version in use.
- **Retention keeps pinned versions.** `RetainedMaterial.build` reads the pin records, so `dropVersion` is held for a version any agent is pinned to ("<agent> is pinned to <tool> <version> until it opts in to another version").
- **Bridge tools.** `toolbox.optin` (a write: a pause refuses it, the command ID is derived from the attempt and call, and it is a `tool-call` step of the task's activity) takes only `name` and `version`; the agent moves itself. `toolbox.pins` is a read. Pi tools `nimblenewt__toolbox-optin` and `nimblenewt__toolbox-pins`. The `tool.describe`/`tool.invoke` version parameters say an omitted version is the pinned one for a shared tool.
- **Owner controls by chat and status.** Chat op `toolbox.optin` (`mode: "propose"`, always shown first) with `name`, `version` (left out: the version in use), and `agentName` (the agent's name copied from the message, looked up as for `task.assign`: exactly one active agent, two are asked about, none is refused) or `everyone: true`. The `toolbox` status line adds which version the agents using each tool stay on, grouped by version, with the version in use, a revoked or set-aside version marked, and up to three agents named. The interpreter paragraph gives example sentences ("move Ann to lint 2.0.0", "put everyone on the newest formatter", "who is still on the old lint tool") and says a new release never moves anyone; no fixed phrase.

ASSUMPTION: "a revoked pin falls back as the revocation rules say" means it is blocked and the consumer is told, not moved to another version: README 320 says a revoked version "must be blocked or explicitly replanned, not silently substituted". The agent replans by opting in (it can, through the bridge) or by naming a version.
ASSUMPTION: the consumer is the agent (its durable identity), not the agent in one project or task. A pin is set by the first run, whatever version that run named, and never by discovery or reading.
ASSUMPTION: only the owner may move another agent's pin. A maintainer's authority covers publishing and choosing the shared version in use, and the card's point is that this does not move consumers.
ASSUMPTION: pin notices go to every pinned agent, without checking whether it is still in the tool's audience (that check needs the agent's grants, which the catalogue does not have for another principal). Such an agent learns only that a tool it already used has a new version number. `toolbox.pins` and opting in still apply the audience.
ASSUMPTION: pins of retired agents still hold their versions against retention. The owner can release them with `toolbox.optin` (`everyone`), and dropping a version is a retention decision, not a pin one.

**Not done (later slices or audit)**

- Bridge tools for revise, rebase, withdraw, promote, the proposal list, maintainers' decisions and revocation; the proposal patch snapshot; the per-agent fork lineage bound; walking the README 313-315 list item by item (all slice 4, ready-cards item 2).
- Pins are per agent, not per task: a task that resumes uses the version its call record names (T02), and a new call follows the agent's pin.
- Status lines name agents by principal ID (as the proposal lines do); names are not looked up. No U08 browser page for pins.
- Notices are written after the release or revocation commits; a crash between the two leaves `toolbox.pins` as the only record, as for fork notices.
- Changing the pin record of a retired agent, and removing pins of agents that left the audience, are left to the owner's `everyone` move.

**Changed behaviour of existing code:** for an agent, a call of a shared tool naming no version now runs the version of its first run (its pin), not the newest release; `list` shows that version. `get` may carry `pinned: true`. Notice kinds `release` and `pin` were added. The pinned list of bridge tool names in `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts` gained `toolbox-optin` and `toolbox-pins`. No existing assertion needed changing: the slice 1 and 2 catalogue and toolbox suites (96 tests) pass unchanged.

**First review of T08 slice 3 (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20).** Merged main `cf8a5afe` (conflict in the `start.ts` status wiring: main's `landingQueue` kept, this slice's `toolbox.consumers` added). Checked who can move a pin: only the agent itself (bridge and API take no `agentId`/`everyone` from an agent, maintainers included) or the owner; a replay with the same command ID is answered from its record and tells nobody; a different command under the same ID is `command_conflict`; the opt-in write checks the entry revision and the pin record revision, so a stale or concurrent change asks again. A pinned agent is never stuck: a revoked pin is refused with words to opt in, naming a version still runs, the owner can move it by chat, and a pause only holds the bridge opt-in while the task runs nothing anyway. The notice ASSUMPTION is acceptable: an agent that left the audience learns only a new version number or a maintainer's revocation reason for a tool it already ran, and `toolbox.pins`/opt-in still apply the audience. Worst-case pin record is about 172 KB, under the 256 KiB body limit. Fixed: (1) at the 1000-consumer limit the first-use pin committed a check-only command under the command ID derived from agent and tool, so that agent could never be pinned by a later run although the notes said it would be; it now refuses inside the build (nothing recorded) and a later run pins it once there is room. (2) Two agents' first runs at the same moment on a new pin record lost one pin (a create race gave `command_conflict`, which the retry loop did not retry); the build now gives `contention` (`stale_revision`), so it is asked again. (3) `toolbox.source` and `toolbox.copy` without a version resolve the agent's pin, but their API and Pi argument texts still said the version in use; both now say so, and the release notice says to name the new version when comparing with `toolbox.source`. Test: `catalog/toolbox-pins.test.ts` gains one suite (four backends): Ann and Ben's first runs together (Ann twice) both pinned once; at the limit Rita's first run is not refused and not pinned, her opt-in is refused `unavailable`, and with room her next run pins her and keeps her there after a release. Mutations: restoring the check-only commit at the limit fails it on 4 of 4 backends; removing the contention fails it on 3 of 4. Verified through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: `npx tsc --build`; `catalog/toolbox-pins` 20/20; `toolbridge/service` toolbox and pin tests 8/8; `api/start-toolbox-pins` 1/1; pi-adapter `bridge` 13/13; `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs` 27/27; `npm run api:docs:write` regenerated `api-v1.md`. Left: a replay of an owner `everyone` opt-in that named no version answers `version: ""` (the record keeps no version); pins of retired agents count toward the limit until the owner's `everyone` move (as noted above).

**Second review of T08 slice 3 (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-20).** Merged main `c600045a` (notes only: kept both sides). Checked: who can move a pin (an agent, including one with a task credential or a typed `nimblenewt.toolbox.optin` command, is refused `agentId`/`everyone` in `CatalogService.optIn` itself; the bridge's `onlyKnown` and the Pi declaration take only `name` and `version`; the owner's chat `agentName` resolves to exactly one active agent and the proposal is shown first; the opt-in command ID is scoped to the caller, and the derived first-use ID `tpn-<sha(agent, tool)>` contains no `:`, so a scoped ID cannot claim it). The pin never refuses a run: every error is caught, contention is retried at most twice, and it costs one command lookup per run once written. ## Q03 next slice: the impact check runs by itself on QA evidence, a release candidate flags its project's documents, and a verification is bound to the QA records it read (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Branch `card-q03-s3` off origin/main `33d5784d`. Card status is NOT changed (Q03 stays planned). This reverses the first slice's ASSUMPTION "the impact and release checks run when someone asks" and closes the leftover both Q03 reviews judged open ("the QA gate reads in `verify` are not bound into its write").

- **Impact on QA evidence, by itself.** `QaEvidenceService` gained two optional ports: `recorded` (after `qa.evidence.record`, also for a repeat of the same command, so work a crash cut short after the record is done on the repeat) and `invalidated` (after `qa.evidence.check` invalidated records). The controller wires them to two new `DocObligationService` entry points, which act as the controller's own identity `DOC_AUTO_PRINCIPAL` (`service:doc-checks`, owner level, the same pattern as `service:coverage-gaps` and `service:stop-notes`):
  - `afterQaEvidence`: for independent evidence, `impact` with that submission under command ID `doc-impact:<evidence id>`. The repeat of the same QA command is therefore the repeat of the same documentation check (`replayed`, nothing flagged twice, update tasks not yet opened are opened). A self-check never counts for a gate, so it checks nothing.
  - `afterQaInvalidation`: per invalidated record (command ID `doc-evidence-lost:<evidence id>`), only lost evidence is looked for: a document verified against code of the task whose QA gate no longer passes is flagged `evidence_lost` with an update task. The invalidated code is not treated as new behaviour (running `impact` with that submission would have flagged documents verified against newer code as `behavior_changed` whenever another record still let its gate pass).
  - A check that throws never undoes the QA record and is not the recorder's error: the controller tells the owner with a needs-you notice (`doc-impact-failed:` / `doc-lost-failed:`, ref the evidence) saying to ask `doc.impact.check` again.
- **Release candidates.** `release.submit` takes optional `projectId` and `version` (both or neither). They are part of the command's payload (a command ID reused with another project or version is `command_conflict`), not of the manifest, so the candidate ID is unchanged and the same manifest is still the same candidate. The project must exist (checked inside the command, so a refused submission records no candidate). After the candidate is recorded, the API handler runs `doc.release.check` as the owner under `releaseDocsCommandId(candidate, project, version)`; its result is the new `docs` field of the answer. A repeat, or the same candidate submitted again for the same project and version, is the same documentation check (`replayed`).
- **Owner chat.** `release.submit` now accepts the project (`projectName`, resolved like every other project name, or `projectId`) and `version`, which must be in the owner's words (it is not in the exempt list, so a version the model supplied is refused); the proposal line shows both. The interpreter prompt says to add them when the owner says which product version and project the build is ("this is Garden 3.0"), and not to send `doc.release.check` as well; the docs paragraph says the controller now checks the documents by itself when independent QA evidence is recorded or invalidated, and that asking again finds nothing new.
- **Binding the QA gate reads.** `QaEvidenceService.gateBound` returns the gate with the records its verdict was read from, at the revisions read: the task's `qa-evidence-index`, the `task-contract` and the `decision-reliance` when they exist, every independent `qa-evidence` record of the submission and every `decision` those records cite. `gate` is unchanged (it returns the gate alone, so `qa.evidence.gate` answers as before). The documentation service's `gate` port carries `reads`; `verify` adds a `check` change for each (one per record), so QA evidence recorded or invalidated, a changed task contract or a superseded decision between the read and the write refuses the verification with `stale_revision` ("the QA evidence of the code named changed while it was being verified ...: verify again") through the runner's `contention` answer; a moved obligation still answers with its own revision.
- **Docs.** Summaries of `qa.evidence.record`, `qa.evidence.check`, `doc.impact.check`, `doc.obligation.verify` and `release.submit` say the above; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the automatic checks keep the service's rules unchanged, including that the first passing QA evidence of a task flags its unverified documents (as a manual check always did). So a document change submitted before that QA no longer verifies the document: the keeper submits it again after the flag (the update task says so). This is the smallest change; reversible by not flagging unverified documents automatically.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the automatic checks run as the controller (`service:doc-checks`, owner level), not as the recorder: a QA agent holds neither the docs nor the director role, and the check affects the whole project's documents. The update tasks name `service:doc-checks` as requester.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a release candidate flags documents when it is submitted, not when it is approved, so the documents are updated while the release is tested; a candidate that is never approved leaves those flags (verify for the version, or record the document for another). Reversible: the check could move to `release.approve`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** if the documentation check of a release fails after the candidate was recorded, the error is the answer (nothing is hidden); sending the same command again replays the candidate and runs the same check again.
- **ASSUMPTION:** absent records are not bound (the storage has no "must not exist" guard): a task contract or decision reliance created between the gate read and the verification's write is not caught by that write; the next QA check (now automatic on invalidation) catches its effect.
- **Tests.** New `submissions/doc-auto-checks.test.ts` on all four storage backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL): a self-check flags nothing; independent evidence flags the unverified document with an update task assigned to the keeper and requested by `service:doc-checks`, another task's document untouched; the repeat of the QA command flags nothing twice; new tested code makes the verified document stale against the new tree; QA evidence recorded between the gate read and the write refuses the verification (`stale_revision`), and evidence of another task does not; a task contract changed between the read and the write refuses it; an invalidation where the document's own evidence still passes flags nothing; a contract change plus `qa.check` flags the document `evidence_lost` (not `behavior_changed`), and the repeat flags nothing. New `release/release-docs.test.ts` on all four backends: both-or-neither, a project that does not exist (no candidate recorded), same candidate with and without a project, a repeat, `command_conflict` for another version or for adding a project to a used ID, owner only. New `api/start-release-docs.test.ts` through the running controller: `release.submit` with project and version flags the project's document with an assigned update task, the repeat and the resubmission are replays, `command_conflict`, a version without a project refused; the owner's chat shows the candidate with the project and version first, refuses a version not in the owner's words, and applying flags the document for 3.0. `api/start-docs.test.ts` and `api/start-docs-verify.test.ts` now expect the automatic flags (the first QA evidence flags the unverified page; the old document change no longer verifies it; the owner's own impact check finds nothing new); `start-docs.test.ts` also invalidates the evidence by a contract change through the API and sees the page flagged `evidence_lost` with an update task for the keeper.
- **Mutation checks** (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): the verification without the bound checks, the gate without the contract read, without the index read, the automatic impact off, lost-evidence ignoring the gate, the `recorded` and `invalidated` ports not called (each failed `doc-auto-checks` on all four backends); the release payload without the project and version, no project check (each failed `release-docs` on all four); the API handler not running the release check (`start-release-docs`); the controller not wiring `recorded` or `invalidated` (`start-docs`). Survived, judged equivalent: binding each QA evidence record by itself (every write to a record also rewrites the task's evidence index, which is bound; kept as a guard against a later write that does not); running `afterQaEvidence` for a self-check (a self-check never changes a gate, so the check finds nothing).
- **NOT done / leftovers:** the controller's `gate` port passing `reads` is not covered by a test through the running controller (a read-to-write race cannot be placed there without a test hook; the service test covers the binding); recorded QA evidence on an older code submission after newer code was tested flags the documents for the older code, as a manual `doc.impact.check` naming it always did (only the newest code submission of a task could be considered, which needs a per-task code index); a repeat of `qa.evidence.check` that invalidated nothing new does not re-run the lost-evidence check (the next record or a manual check does); the rest of Q03's own "NOT done" list (documents gating a release or `done`, notices when documents go stale, own record kinds for support and promotional material, reading the document's text, retiring a document, bridge tools).
- **First review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context).** Merged origin/main `6352ed7d` (Q02 leftovers). Conflicts resolved: `qa.evidence.record` returns main's `open` and still calls the `recorded` port; main split `check` into a retried `#runCheck` (a check that loses a race answers `concurrent: true` from the winner), so the `evidence` list moved into `#runCheck`'s report type and the `invalidated` port is called once after the retry loop (a lost race does not call it: the winner did); the API summaries keep main's text plus the Q03 sentences; `api-v1.md` regenerated. Changed: main's gate now also reads the task's `qa-recheck` records (an invalidated record whose re-check is not done keeps its checks owed), so `gateBound` binds each re-check of the submission it reads too (a guard: every re-check settled by evidence also rewrites the bound index, and one settled by a newer tree leaves the verdict as it was, so no test can tell; judged equivalent like the per-record binding). Checked, no change: (1) `service:doc-checks` is used only by `afterQaEvidence` / `afterQaInvalidation`, whose task, submission and evidence IDs come from the stored QA record, never from the caller's arguments; its result never reaches the recorder (the port returns nothing; a failure notice to the owner carries only the error code); its command IDs go through `scopedCommandId` (principal ID plus a hash), so no agent or owner command can meet `doc-impact:` / `doc-evidence-lost:` IDs, and no principal can be created with a `service:` ID (agents are `agent:`). (2) Double flags: `#planned` drops reasons already on the record or on an open update task and opens at most one task per subject, so a second QA record on the same code, a repeat, or an invalidation check after an impact check flag nothing twice. (3) The behaviour change (first passing QA flags unverified documents, so a document change submitted before it no longer verifies) is the existing `flaggedAt` rule and is recorded as an ASSUMPTION; kept. (4) The unbound "must not exist" gap matches how acceptance.ts and routing/difficulty.ts bind a contract (only when it exists); kept as recorded. (5) Chat: `version` is not in the exempt list, so a version not in the owner's words is refused; `projectId` is exempt like elsewhere and `projectName` is resolved. Before, QA evidence recorded late on older code (or the repeat of such a record) moved a verified document back to the older code, and since `verify` takes the newest *flagged* tree, the keeper then had to verify against the older code; once that code's gate stopped passing (a contract change invalidates it and the newer tree settles its re-check, which keeps its checks owed) neither submission could verify the document and no later check could add the newer reason again (already in `reasons`), so the keeper was stuck until another code submission. ## P09 gate leftovers: the owner is told about test commands only the authors set, checks can be accepted, and the host's check processes stop when the gate gives up (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Two items the P09 reviews left for follow-up ("P09 first slice, second Opus review", Judged, left for follow-up 1 and 2). The card stays planned (Y02 chain).

**Built.**
- **The owner is told when a landing has no test commands it can use (`landing-gate.ts`, `workspace-ops.ts`).** When `tests` is required and there was something to land but no command to run, the gate's record says why in `checks.testsNeedOwner`: `authors-only` when the only versions that set the contract's checks were stored by the task's authors (the assignee or the submitter of the landed submission), `no-commands` when no contract names any (or its versions could not be read). The author cannot fix either: its own contract changes do not count. A landing refused with that mark sends the owner a needs-you notice through the existing workspace `notify` (kind maintenance, ref the task; at most 200 characters, the notification limit), with the identity `lgo-<task>-v<contract version>-<reason>`, so further landings while nothing changed do not raise it again. The record says `toldOwner: true` when it was sent (a notice that cannot be sent is recorded as not told; the landing is refused either way), the refusal summary ends with "the owner is asked to set or accept them" (or "to set them"), and the author's inbox text says the owner was told. A failing command, nothing to land or a host that cannot check is the author's or the host's matter and tells the owner nothing new.
- **Accepting checks (`planning/contracts.ts`).** Before this, an owner who wanted the author's commands could not say so: naming the same checks again was refused as no change, so the owner had to change them and change them back. Now `contract.set` that names `checks` equal to the ones the contract holds is a change when someone other than the caller set them: it stores a new version and counts as the caller setting them (needs the same `task.contract.write` as setting them; the command's detail says `acceptedChecks`). Every version stored by a `contract.set` that names `checks` carries `checksSetBy` (the caller); versions that do not name them, and difficulty changes, do not carry it forward. `landingTests` stops walking back at a version with `checksSetBy`, so an acceptance by the owner counts, an acceptance by an author is skipped like its other versions (the owner's accepted checks before it still run), and versions stored before this field are read as before (by comparing checks). It returns `onlyAuthors: true` (and no commands) when only authors set checks that name something, which is where `authors-only` comes from. The caller who set the current checks naming them again is still refused as no change.
- **The host stops its check processes when the gate gives up (`landing-gate.ts`, `worker/src/workspace/landing-checks.ts`).** The gate passes an `AbortSignal` in the `landingChecks` call and aborts it when it stops waiting (the commands' time plus a minute) or when the call fails. The host kills the running check through `SandboxRun.kill` (the launcher's tree kill: the run's process group and any survivor it found), reports it `not-run` ("the controller stopped waiting"), starts no further check and still removes every copy. The signal passes through `LocalWorkspaces.port` and `scripts/local-host.mjs` unchanged (both forward the call object as it is). `LandingGate` takes an optional `marginMs` (tests only).
- **Docs and chat.** `contract.set`'s `checks` argument says a landing runs them unless only the task's assignee or submitter set them, and that naming the checks the contract already holds accepts them; the interpreter reads these descriptions, so the owner can ask in free words to accept the checks the author wrote and the interpreter can answer with that `contract.set`. Checked by reading, not by a chat test: the chat runs `contract.set` with the arguments as given (`checks` is not one of its authority fields, so it applies or is proposed like any other contract edit under the owner's profile). `workspace.request` names `toldOwner` and `checks.testsNeedOwner`. `api-v1.md` regenerated.

**Tests.** Gate: `testsNeedOwner` for authors-only, no contract and empty checks, and absent when commands exist, when there is nothing to land and when tests are not required; the author's text says the owner was told; a host that never answers gets its signal aborted with the reason, one that answers in time does not. Controller (4 backends, real contract, policy and gate services): no contract tells the owner (`no-commands`, version 0); the submitter's own checks are refused with `authors-only`, the owner notice (identity, length, text), `toldOwner` on the stored record, the same identity on the next landing; the author naming its own checks again is refused; the owner naming the same checks accepts them (`checksSetBy`), the landing runs them and passes; a second acceptance is refused; a later criteria change does not carry the mark; the author accepting the owner's checks does not count, the owner's still run; a failing command tells the owner nothing; a failed notice is not recorded as told; an agent without `task.contract.write` cannot accept. Worker: a fake slow run is killed once on abort, the next check is never launched, both are `not-run`, the copies are gone, an already-aborted call launches nothing; in real bubblewrap a check that started a detached child is gone with that child after the abort.

**Mutants on the compiled code (each alone, restored and checked by hash, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`).** Gate does not abort the signal: 1 failure; the host does not kill on abort: 2 cancelled (the run never ends); the host keeps starting checks after an abort (both of its checks removed): 1; `testsNeedOwner` never set: 1 gate + 4 controller; the owner never notified: 4; acceptance off: 8; `checksSetBy` ignored by `landingTests`: 4; `checksSetBy` carried forward: 8; `onlyAuthors` never answered: 4; the setter allowed to accept its own checks: 4. Two first mutants survived because the code checked the same thing twice: the gate's timer aborted the signal and its `catch` did too (the timer's abort was removed, the `catch` aborts), and the host checked the signal both in its loop and before each launch (mutated together).

**Verified (after `tsc --build`, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`).** Controller `landing/`, `workspace-ops/`, `planning/`, `submissions/`, `policy/`: 795 of 795; `api/api`, `api/start-p10*`, `start-submission`, `start-work-end`, `chat-gaps`, `start-commands`, `h12s-landing-policy`: 80 of 80; `chat/`: 1414 of 1414; worker `workspace/` and `sandbox/host-runner*`: 161 passed, 2 skipped (both Windows only); integration `p09-*`, `h12*`, `w05-*`: 41 of 41; after the last gate edit `landing/` and `workspace-ops-p09*` again: 155 of 155. `api-v1.md` equal to `node scripts/api-docs.mjs`; `check:deps` ok. Other suites not rerun (the diff does not reach them); CI is the net.

- ASSUMPTION: the needs-you notice plus the record's `toldOwner` and summary line is the "status line"; the notice appears in the owner's needs-you list like other maintenance notices. Smallest reversible choice, as the brief named.
- ASSUMPTION: the owner is also told when there are no test commands at all (`no-commands`), not only when authors set them: in both cases only someone other than the author can make the required tests pass.
- ASSUMPTION: accepting checks is `contract.set` naming the same checks (no new operation), counted only when someone other than the caller set the current ones; an agent with `task.contract.write` that is not an author of the task can accept too, the same people who could set them.
- ASSUMPTION: one notice per task, contract version and reason; a new contract version that still leaves only author-set checks raises a new one.

**First review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context).** (1) Found and fixed: `onlyAuthors` was decided only at version 1, so in the usual order (the owner makes the contract with criteria only, the author then adds checks) the walk reached the owner's version without checks and answered "no test commands": the owner was asked to "set" commands that already existed, and the notice was keyed to that older version. `landingTests` now remembers whether a skipped author's version named checks; reaching someone else's version without checks then answers `onlyAuthors` (newest version), and version 1 counts only checks that name something (an author's empty list is "no test commands"). (2) The controller test's "notice that cannot be sent" step never reached `notify` (the owner's accepted checks ran, so the owner was not needed); a new test (4 backends) covers the owner-first order, a failed notice not recorded as told (also on the stored record) and the next landing telling the owner. Mutants on dist (the new rule off; `toldOwner` set after a failed notice) each fail it on all four backends; restored. (3) Checked, not changed: an author cannot make its own checks count by the accept step: its acceptance stores `changedBy`/`checksSetBy` as itself and is skipped like its other versions; `checksSetBy` cannot be named by a caller (`parsePatch` takes the known fields only) and a difficulty change drops it; a replayed `contract.set` answers the stored command (no new version); versions stored before the field are walked by comparing checks as before. Accepting when the walk cannot read far enough (`#checksIntroduced` undefined) lets the setter store an acceptance of its own checks, which changes nothing a landing runs. A second identity holding `task.contract.write` that is not the assignee or the submitter could already set the checks before this change. The notice identity is at most about 50 characters (`task-` IDs are fixed length), within the 120 of a command ID. Abort and normal end: the listener is removed once the run's result is in, and a check reported `not-run` for the abort needs both the signal aborted and the run killed. The process-tree kill is checked in real bubblewrap only; on Windows the launcher's kill is not exercised by these tests (the two Windows-only skips). Verified through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` after `tsc --build`: `workspace-ops-p09`, `landing-gate` 39 of 39; `workspace-ops-p09-p10` and `planning/` 64 of 64; worker `landing-checks` 9 of 9; integration `p09-landing-checks` 1 of 1.

**Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context).** (1) Changed: who set a version's checks is read as `checksSetBy ?? changedBy` (`checksSetterOf` in `contracts.ts`), both in the `landingTests` walk and in the accept step. Before, the walk judged a version by `changedBy` only, so keeping an author's checks out of the landing rested entirely on every writer dropping `checksSetBy` (`setContract` and `difficultyChanges` do); a version that carried an author's `checksSetBy` under someone else's `changedBy` would have counted the author's checks. With both writers as they are the result is the same. New test (4 backends): the delegating parent's `difficultyChanges` version over ann's checks carries no `checksSetBy` and leaves `authors-only` (keyed to the newest version); a hand-written version with ann's `checksSetBy` and the parent's `changedBy` is still ann's; ann cannot accept there, the owner can and the landing passes. Mutant on dist (the walk back on `changedBy`): fails on all 4 backends; restored by hash. (2) Checked, not changed: the notice is keyed `lgo-<task>-v<version>-<reason>` with a text that depends only on the task and reason, so a repeat is answered by the command runner and a failed one is retried with the same identity on the next refused landing; it is only retried on a landing, nothing else retries it. An author can raise a new notice per contract version it stores (the recorded assumption). The signal reaches the host unchanged (`LocalWorker` keeps the port object, `scripts/local-host.mjs` forwards the call); remote hosts have no `landingChecks`, so nothing runs there. An abort after a check ended but before its result was read may report it `not-run`; the gate has already given up then, so nothing reads it. `contract.get` now shows `checksSetBy` (it returns the stored fields but `changedBy`). Merges cleanly with main 6352ed7d (Q02 leftovers); the merged tree builds and its `api-v1.md` equals `node scripts/api-docs.mjs`. Verified through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` after `tsc --build`: `workspace-ops-p09` 36 of 36; `planning/`, `landing/`, `workspace-ops-p09-p10` 179 of 179.

**Not done.** Remote hosts still have no `landingChecks` (P09 Not done 3), so there is no stop signal across the remote protocol; the processes there are not started in the first place. The other items of the second review's follow-up list (SHA-256 repositories, git older than 2.39, mode-only changes) are unchanged.

**First review of P07 and P10 polish (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20).** Read both commits against `33d5784d`. No correctness or rights problem found: `landing.queue.list` judges the owner or `integration.lease` before reading any branch or queue (status view and API alike, a task credential is refused); `landing.queue.remove` validates only the form of `branch` before rights, and with `branch` a caller who may not take the entry out is still told `not_found` inside the write; the in-progress-landing guard reads the task's open request whatever branch is named; the walk uses the same id-ordered paging on every backend; the P07 resume arms the fault only for an `intended`, never-started effect. Changed: a test that the in-progress guard refuses a take-out named by branch after the landing branch changed (owner and integrator; `landing-queue-p10.test.ts`); `queuesOf` takes an optional page bound (tests only) and a test that a walk cut short says `partial` (mutation: `partial` always false, 4 of 12 fail); the bound's comment now says it counts queue records of all projects, empty ones included; the status `docLines` comment moved back above its method. Verified: `npx tsc --build`; `landing/landing-queue-polish` and `landing/landing-queue-p10` 64 of 64 through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`. No API changed. Left: `partial` is also set when the bound ends exactly on the last record (conservative).

## Windows per-file limits: quiet-hosts, g04-kill-postgres, g04-tool-postgres (Claude agent, 2026-11-20)

- **Symptom.** In the Windows own-hardware probe (run 44552386792, 7551 s) three test files reached their per-file limit: `remote/quiet-hosts.test.js` (900 s) and `g04-kill-postgres.test.js`, `g04-tool-postgres.test.js` (300 s). The limit is on the whole file (node:test treats each file as a test). Near misses in the same run: `g04-kill-sqlite` 290 s of 300, `g04-tool-sqlite` 236 s.
- **quiet-hosts, cause (measured on Linux).** No fixed sleeps: a CPU profile of the reference-store cases shows the main thread idle 33 of 36 s. Every request over the worker transport authenticates the host again (`PrincipalService.authenticate`, scrypt N=16384 r=8, run on the libuv thread pool), about 40 ms a request on this machine; a quiet-hosts case makes about 20 such requests. With the cost lowered as an experiment (in the build output only, not committed), a request took 4 ms and the 31 reference-store cases 10.7 s instead of 35.8 s. On Windows each case took about 4 s in memory, 4 s on SQLite, 10 s on SQLite on a worker thread and 6 to 8 s on PostgreSQL, about 31 cases on each of four backends, so more than 900 s in one file. How much of the Windows time is scrypt was not measured.
- **quiet-hosts, change (test only).** The suite moved to `remote/quiet-hosts-suite.ts` (`defineQuietHostTests(backend)`), with one file per backend: `quiet-hosts.test.ts` (reference store), `quiet-hosts.sqlite.test.ts`, `quiet-hosts.worker.test.ts`, `quiet-hosts.postgres.test.ts`, as the dispatcher suite already is. The cases are unchanged. Estimated Windows time per file from the run: about 120 s, 125 s, 310 s and 240 s. The scrypt check per request is product behaviour and was left alone: lowering its cost in tests or keeping verified tokens would change what the transport's credential check does, which is a security decision and not part of this card. It is the main lever for the remote suites' run time if one is wanted.
- **g04-kill and g04-tool, cause.** Also no fixed waits: each boundary starts a real Node process (649 modules), runs it to the kill, opens the database again, runs the whole path and compares it with the uncrashed run. On Linux that is about 1 s a boundary (child about 0.75 s); on Windows 7 to 10 s (tool-postgres: 157 s for one sweep of 17 runs). kill-postgres runs 39 of these, tool-postgres two sweeps of 17, plus 21 to 25 s to start PostgreSQL. The work is long, not wasted.
- **g04 change (test only).** Each kill sweep is divided between two files per database (`g04-kill-<db>.test.ts` part 1 of 2, `g04-kill-<db>-part2.test.ts` part 2 of 2), and each tool route has a file per sweep (`g04-tool-<db>.test.ts` for the call presented again, `g04-tool-<db>-not-again.test.ts`). The split files run in parallel under node:test. `share` in `g04-fixture.ts` takes every second sampled boundary per part, so the parts together are exactly the boundaries one file killed at (38 by default, 127 exhaustive); `g04-share.test.ts` checks this (every point once, near-equal parts, each part covering both ends). Each part makes its own uncrashed run first. A new assertion checks that the boundary with the model request in flight is among those sampled, so the resume check runs in exactly one part and cannot be skipped everywhere. Done for SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread (heavy, still skipped by default) and PostgreSQL. `scripts/slow-tests.json` lists the new files; the exhaustive G04 job finds them by its `g04-*.test.js` pattern. Estimated Windows time per file: kill-postgres parts about 200 to 220 s, tool-postgres files about 185 s; kill-sqlite parts about 150 s, tool-sqlite about 120 s.
- **Test PostgreSQL start.** `startEmbeddedServer` passes `--no-sync` to initdb: initdb does not flush the new cluster to disk before returning. The cluster is temporary and no test crashes the operating system; the server still runs with fsync, full_page_writes and synchronous_commit on (the controller refuses a server without them). On Linux initdb takes 0.5 s either way; on Windows it took 21 to 23 s, and how much of that the flush is was not measured.
- **No limit raised.** The per-package limits stay at 300 s (integration) and 900 s (controller).
- **Run (Linux, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build`).** The four quiet-hosts files: 124 of 124 (the same 124 the single file had), 45 s wall time against 157 s for the single file. `g04-share`, all `g04-kill-*` and `g04-tool-*`: 13 tests, 9 passed, 4 skipped (the heavy worker-thread variants), 20 s; each kill part reports 19 of the 38 boundaries. `storage/postgres/postgres.test.js` (servers with the new initdb flag, including the fsync-off refusal): 214 of 214. `scripts/slow-tests.test.mjs`: 1 of 1.
- **Mutation checks (in the build output, restored after).** `share` giving every part the same half: `g04-share` fails. `share` dropping the last point: fails. The in-flight boundary label not found: `g04-kill-sqlite` fails. A changed warning text in `quiet-hosts.js`: 4 failures in both `quiet-hosts.test.js` and `quiet-hosts.postgres.test.js`. Not guarded by a test: the two-line `sweeps` choice in `g04-tool-suite.ts` (a mistake there would run one tool sweep in neither file); the test names in each file's output show which sweep it ran.
- **Untested.** Nothing ran on Windows. The per-file estimates above are taken from the timings of run 44552386792; the next own-hardware run shows the real ones.

## T08 (fourth slice): proposal and revocation bridge tools, a proposal's kept text, the per-agent fork lineage bound, and the README validation walk (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

T08 stays `planned` (the card is not flipped here; the table at the end is the evidence a flip audit needs). Branch `card-t08-s4` off origin/main `85ea823f` (slice 3 merged). Changed: `toolbridge/service.ts` and `pi-adapter/src/bridge.ts` (two bridge tools), `catalog/catalog.ts` (lineage bound, kept text in releases), `catalog/proposals.ts` (kept text), `retention/service.ts` (the owner's deletion gathers kept text), `context/fixed-part.ts` and the tests that pin its figures, three `api/operations.ts` summaries, `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` (regenerated).

**Done in this slice**

- **Bridge tools for the rest of the proposal work and for maintainers.** `toolbox.proposal` is one bridge operation with an `action`: `propose` (as `toolbox.propose`), `promote`, `revise`, `rebase`, `withdraw`, `list`, `get` and, for maintainers, `decide`. `toolbox.revoke` is a maintainer's revocation with `runningCalls` `finish` or `cancel` (a pause, which pauses tasks, stays the owner's and is refused in words). Both act as the agent with its own grants, through the same services and not-found rules as the state API; the agent's own `toolbox.manage` decides what it may decide or revoke, and an author never decides its own proposal. `list` and `get` are reads (a pause does not stop them, they are not activity steps); every other action, and an unknown one, is a write: a pause refuses it, a recorded call is admitted as an effect (card L05d), the command ID comes from the attempt and call, and each is a `tool-call` step ("decided toolbox proposal ...: accepted, released as 1.1.0 (an acceptance authorises nothing beyond that release)", "revoked shared tool ..."). A promotion names the attempt's own task, never one the request names. Proposal text from `get` is clipped at 16 KB per part with `truncated`, as `toolbox.source` is.
- **The separate `toolbox-propose` Pi tool is no longer declared**; proposing is the `propose` action. The controller still accepts the `toolbox.propose` operation, so a worker of the previous version keeps working. Pi tools now: `nimblenewt__toolbox-proposal`, `nimblenewt__toolbox-revoke`.
- **The fixed part.** Slice 3's two tools had already brought the real worker's bridge schemas to 18,887 characters, over `WORKER_FIXED_PART_BUDGET` (18,750) and more than 5% from the recorded 17,714, so `integration/fixed-part-budget.test.ts` failed on main (slice 3 did not run the integration package). Eight separate tools would have added about 4,800 characters and pushed the window the owner is told from 36,864 to 40,960 tokens (step 3 of RAISING THE FIXED PART, with every real-process test window). One tool with an action and shorter toolbox descriptions (same meaning; the version parameters now say "default: your pinned version of a shared tool, else the latest live") keep it at 36,864: measured 2,537 + 19,087 characters (about 7,200 tokens), smallest startable window 36,864, practical 36,864. `WORKER_FIXED_PART` records that; the budget (also the unmeasured-route floor) is 2,800 + 19,400 = 22,200, under 22,248, the largest fixed part that still starts a task on 36,864. Pinned figures updated on purpose: `fixed-part-budget.test.ts` (7,200 tokens, `MIN_STARTABLE_WINDOW` 36,864), `setup/small-window.test.ts` ("about 7,200 tokens"), `api/start-route-change.test.ts` (floor 22,200); comments in `c07g-route-view.test.ts` (its floor 22,750 stays above) and `h12bf-composed.test.ts` (about 1,600 tokens still spare at 98,304).
- **A proposal keeps the text its author wrote** (`toolbox-proposal-text`, keyed by the proposal ID, `PROPOSAL_TEXT_KIND` in `catalog.ts`). Written in the same write as `propose` and `promote`, replaced by `revise` (removed when a revision writes no part), holding only the parts the author wrote (a part left as the base has it is the base's, with the base's own snapshot), with `sources` naming the records. `get`, `rebase` and the release read the author's record while it holds exactly the proposed bytes, and otherwise the kept text, checked against the proposed digest. So the author superseding a record, or retention archiving a finished task's records, no longer strands a waiting proposal (before, both made it `unavailable` and unreleasable). The release pins the kept text it read; the kept text is removed when the proposal is released (the new version keeps its own snapshot), rejected or withdrawn, in the same write and with an audit entry (`toolbox.proposal.text.remove`). An acceptance without a version keeps it for the release that follows.
- **The owner's deletion still wins.** `retention.delete` gathers kept proposal text through `sources`, exactly as it gathers release snapshots, and deletes it with the record; the part is then `unavailable` and a release is refused ("deleted by the owner; the author revises the proposal").
- **Per-agent fork lineage bound.** A copy again into the same copy name from the same base version replaces that lineage entry (a revocation of that base reaches the same copy either way); anything else adds one. Each agent keeps at most `CATALOG_LIMITS.forksPerAgent` (20) entries per tool, so one agent can no longer fill a tool's 500 entries and stop everyone else from copying it (the slice 1 second review's leftover). A new base version in a name already used is a new entry (the older copy versions still run on the old base).
- **API summaries** of `toolbox.copy`, `toolbox.propose` and `toolbox.proposal.get` say the above. No operation was added or changed.

ASSUMPTION: "so the owner deleting a desk record cannot strand it" is read as the record being moved out from under the proposal by archiving (the owner's retention archive of a finished task) or by the author superseding it, not as the owner's explicit `retention.delete`. That deletion promises the text is gone everywhere (it already removes release snapshots made from the record), so it removes the kept text too and the proposal must be revised. Reversible: drop the kind from the gather.
ASSUMPTION: the proposal operations are one bridge tool with an action rather than one tool per operation, because every bridge declaration is part of every prompt's fixed part and separate tools would raise the window every task needs to 40,960 tokens. `baseVersion`, `mine`, `after`, `limit` and `expectedRevision` are not declared to the model (the defaults apply: the version in use, every proposal it may see, the first 50); the controller accepts them.
ASSUMPTION: 20 lineage entries per agent per tool. Twenty copy names or base versions of one tool is more than any agent needs; 25 agents together can still fill 500, which is the tool's own bound as before.
ASSUMPTION: a maintainer's revocation from a run offers `finish` and `cancel` only, as the state API does for maintainers; it has no running-call preview (as on the state API).

**Changed behaviour of existing code:** `toolbox-propose` is no longer a declared Pi tool (the operation remains). A rebase or release after the author superseded a record now succeeds from the kept text; the slice 2 assertion that refused it now checks that text changed in both places is still refused, and that the rebase reads the kept text. Toolbox tool descriptions are shorter. The pinned list of bridge tool names in `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts` gained `toolbox-proposal` and `toolbox-revoke` and lost `toolbox-propose`.

**Not done (later slices or audit)**

- Promotion through the stand-up and a chat form of publishing (from slices 1-2); maintainers' own view and U08 browser pages; status lines naming agents and audiences by name.
- A running-call preview or chat ask for a maintainer's revocation.
- Notices are still read on request, not put into the next prompt; revocation and pin notices written after the command commits have no sweep (slices 2-3).
- Final-state proposals are kept without bound (retention rule; slice 2 second review).
- Snapshots for personal tools and system versions, and a backfill for shared versions released before slice 2.

Integration `fixed-part-budget`, `t06-bridge`, `h12b-worker-process` 7/7 (the budget test failed on the base, see above). `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs` 27/27; `scripts/api-docs.mjs` output byte-identical to `api-v1.md`. **Mutation checks** (source edited, rebuilt, restored): no per-agent bound, lineage never replaces, release ignores the kept text, release after the owner's deletion, the release pinning the kept text it also removes (the storage refuses two changes of one record), nothing kept at proposing, `get` reading no kept text, rebase reading no kept text: each killed. The run was stopped there at the coordinator's request; the remaining planned mutations (revise, withdraw, reject and release keeping the text; the deletion gather; the bridge's read/write split, promote's task, revoke's `pause` and name checks, the steps, the Pi `action` requirement) were not run. **Skipped:** the remaining controller and integration files, other packages, hosted Windows/macOS (CI), the two Opus reviews.

**First review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** (1) Base claim checked: 85ea823f built in a separate worktree measures 2,537 + 18,887 characters against the budget 3,000 + 18,750 (recorded 17,714, 6.6% off), so `fixed-part-budget.test.ts` failed there. The new figures are the measurement (2,537 + 19,087); the tool budget rose by 650 and the system budget fell by 200, so the floor (22,200) is still under 22,248, the largest that starts a task on 36,864; `MIN_STARTABLE_WINDOW` (now 36,864) is derived from the measurement, not a loosened limit. (2) Grants through `toolbox.proposal`/`toolbox.revoke`: every action passes an allow-listed set of fields, the command ID and (for `propose`/`promote`) the task are set after the caller's fields, the principal is the run's agent; `decide` and `revoke` are checked by the services against that agent's own `toolbox.manage` (an author never decides its own; a maintainer's `pause` is refused by the catalog as well as by the bridge). (3) Found and fixed: the write that kept a proposal's text did not check that the source records were still at the revision whose text it copied, so the owner's `retention.delete` landing between that read and the write (it gathers kept text by `sources` and would not find the copy yet) left the deleted text in a `toolbox-proposal-text` record (unreadable through `get` or a release, which see the record's `deleted` marker first, but still stored after the owner was told it was gone). `propose`, `promote` and `revise` now add a `check` of each source record's revision to the same write; the proposal is refused when it moved. New test in `toolbox-proposals.test.ts` ("slice 4, first review: the owner's deletion ... leaves no copy behind", all four backends: a storage proxy runs the deletion right after the last read of the record, for a proposal and for a revision); removing either check fails it. (4) The 14 planned mutations that had not run were run one at a time: 13 killed; "revoke allows pause" survived because the catalog's own maintainer check refuses `pause` too. The bridge suite now also revokes through a catalog whose `revoke` is counted and asserts `pause`, `stop` and an empty value are refused by the bridge without reaching it; the mutation is then killed. (5) Who may read kept text: only `toolbox.proposal.get` (author, owner, deciders: the same people who saw the text before through the record) and the release; nothing else reads the kind. Size: at most two parts of 16,000 characters per proposal, 20 waiting proposals per author; removed in the same write as release, rejection, withdrawal, a revision without a written part, and by the owner's deletion; a retired author's waiting proposals keep theirs until decided (the walk relies on that). Left, not fixed: a proposal accepted without a version keeps its text until a later acceptance releases it, and no action ends such a proposal otherwise (it is no longer pending, so its author's 20 do not bound it); as with final-state proposals, this grows only with maintainers' acceptances. (6) Lineage bound: the fork record is updated with its revision checked, so two copies at once cannot pass the bound; older lineages with repeated entries for one agent, copy name and base are collapsed to one at that agent's next copy into the name. (7) Compatibility: `toolbox.propose` stays in `BRIDGE_OPERATIONS`; the Pi declaration's fields cover each action's allow-list and `action` is required (mutation killed). `node scripts/api-docs.mjs` output is byte-identical to `api-v1.md`. **Second review (Claude agent, Opus, clean context).** (1) Found and fixed: the owner's deletion (`retention.delete`, and the scratch tier's purge, which uses it) gathers kept proposal text and release snapshots by `sources` at its start and blanks the records afterwards; a `propose`, `promote`, `revise` or a release committing in between passed its own revision check (the record was not blanked yet) and left a copy of the deleted text that nothing removed. The first review's check closes only the window between that write's read and its commit. `#delete` now scans `toolbox-proposal-text` and `catalog-snapshot` once more after every record is blanked (neither is made from a blanked record, so this finds the last of them), appends them to the deletion ledger first, removes them and lists them in `derived.others`; a `partial` request needs no such pass (the next one gathers again). New test in `toolbox-proposals.test.ts` ("slice 4, second review: a proposal written after the owner's deletion gathered ...", all four backends, through retention's `beforeBatch` hook): it failed on all four before the fix. (2) Saved-text lifecycle traced on every path: propose and promote create it in the proposal's write; revise replaces or removes it in its write; release, rejection and withdrawal remove it in their write with an audit entry; rebase leaves it (it never changes a part's text; a part that the new base now equals stays in the kept text, harmless, removed with the proposal's end); an acceptance without a version keeps it until a release (as the first review noted, nothing else ends it but the owner's deletion); every path is one write, so a crash leaves either the old or the new state. Proposals made before this slice have none and behave as before. The deletion ledger replays `removed` by kind and ID, so a restored backup loses the kept text too. (4) Budget: computed from `startableWindow`, 22,248 characters is the largest fixed part that starts on 36,864 and the 22,200 floor starts there; the room over the measurement is now 576 characters. (5) Lineage bound with older data: an agent already holding more than 20 entries can still copy again into a name and base it holds (repeats collapse to one), but adds no new one; a replacement never trips the 500 bound.
