## P10 (third slice): reserved places at the refresh-round cap, escalation to the director, and a test that no submission waits forever under steady load (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. A task whose author keeps having to refresh its work because the branch moved now gets a reserved place in the landing queue once it reaches the project's refresh-round cap (`integration.refreshRounds`, default 3). It keeps that place (its turn) even when its approval is taken back, and while its place is first and it has no approved submission, nothing else lands, so the branch stops moving under it. When a reserved task still needs another refresh, or when the first place has held the branch for four hours while other work waits behind it, the project's director is told (and the owner). The director, like the owner and integrators, may take the task out, which ends the reservation; the owner can do the same by chat in any words. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **The queue record (`landing/landing-queue.ts`).** New optional fields: `reservations` (task, place number `seq`, since, the round that reached the cap and the cap then, `escalatedRound`), `front` (the first task and since when, `escalated`), and `away` (the place an entry had when the controller withdrew it because its approval was taken back). `frontOf` decides the first place: the entry or reserved place (a reserved task with no entry) with the lowest number. Every write keeps `front` up to date (the same first task keeps its time; a new first task starts now) and keeps the entries sorted by number. `reserve` (one recorded command; a task already reserved is left as it is) takes the task's entry number, else its `away` number, else the next number. `enqueue` gives a reserved task its reserved number again instead of the back. `remove` ends the task's reservation too, and the owner, an integrator or a director can end a reservation of a task with no entry (`reservationEnded`); the controller's own withdrawal keeps the reservation and remembers the place (`keepReservation`). A landing's `landedChanges` ends the landed task's reservation. `markEscalated` marks a `front` or `round` escalation once. Commands with nothing to write are refused inside and answered outside (the runner commits a change per command).
- **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** `afterRound({ taskId, projectId, round })`: below the cap nothing; at or above it, the task's place is reserved; a reserved task with a round beyond its reserved round is told to the director once per reservation. `checkLanding` lands only the first place's entry; a reserved place without an entry refuses every other landing ("task X holds the first place (reserved after its author reached the refresh-round cap) and waits for its approved submission"). When a landing is refused behind a first place that has held for `holdMs` (default `LANDING_HOLD_MS`, four hours, on the controller's clock), the director is told once per first place. `list` answers `reservations`, `front` (with `waitingForApproval`) and `reserved` on entries. New options: `refreshCap`, `escalate`, `isDirector`, `holdMs`.
- **Where rounds come from (`workspace-ops.ts`).** A new optional `onRound` dependency is told after a counted refresh round of `work.refresh` is recorded (not on a repeat); `startController` wires it to `afterRound`.
- **Composition (`api/start.ts`, `agents/agents.ts`).** The cap is `integration.effective(project).refreshRounds`. `AgentService.directorsOf(project)`: active agents with the director role and a live grant naming THIS project (a `*` grant does not make a director, as in `decidersAvailableIn`). An escalation is a notice in each director's inbox (full text), and an owner notification (200 characters, `ref` the task): `notice` when at least one director was actually told, `needs-you` when none could be (no director, or none can read the task).
- **Chat and owner controls.** No new operation. Ending a reservation is `landing.queue.remove` (already a chat command, shown first). The interpreter prompt's landing-queue paragraph says what a reserved place is, that the director (or the owner) is told, how to end one in free words ("stop holding the branch for the login task", "let the others land"), and that the cap is `refreshRounds` changed with `integration.set` (already a chat command). The `landing_queue` status view names reserved entries, each reservation (since, round, cap, whether it waits for approval and holds the branch, whether the director was told) and an escalated first place. API summaries of `landing.queue.add`, `.remove`, `.list` and the `refreshRounds` argument of `integration.set`/`integration.default.set` updated; `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Tests.** `landing/landing-queue-reservations.test.ts` (four storage backends, 4 tests): (1) reservation at the cap, the place kept across a withdrawal, other landings refused before any host while the reserved place waits, a later task behind it, the re-approval landing first, the landing ending the reservation; (2) escalation of a round beyond the cap once, who may end a reservation (not the author without an entry, not a stranger; the director; an author's own take-out ends it), cap 0, unreadable settings use 3; (3) the hold escalation: not under the hold time, once at it, not for the head's own landing, a new first place starting its own time; (4) **the steady-load fairness test**: three tasks approved together on the current head every six simulated minutes (24 in all), the integrator landing the first place each minute through the real landing path against a simulated branch head, a stale landing going back to its author (approval taken back), who refreshes (a round) and is approved two minutes later; one author goes silent after its place is reserved. Asserted: every other task lands, within a bound computed from the queue length, the cap and the review time plus the hold once; the queue drains; the silent task is told to the director once (`front`) and the director takes it out; no task needed a round beyond its cap. `api/start-p10-reservations.test.ts` (composed controller): the project's cap from `integration.set`, the director's inbox notice and the owner's `notice`, a stranger refused and the director ending a reservation through the state API, the chat view naming the reservation and the owner ending it in plain words (shown first, applied on the yes), and a project whose only director cannot read its tasks: the owner is told `needs-you` and no director is told. `integration/h12p-author-refresh.test.ts` extended: with the landing branch set and `refreshRounds: 2`, the agent's real `work.refresh` round 1 reserves nothing and round 2 reserves the task's place.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored, then `tsc --build --force`): all killed but one equivalent.** A reserved place without an entry not counted as first (8 failures); a reserved task's re-approval sent to the back (8); `afterRound` never reserving (12); the controller's withdrawal ending the reservation (4); hold escalation off (8); the landing keeping the reservation (8); reservation ignoring the withdrawn place (4, the fairness test: a round beyond the cap); `onRound` not called (the H12p integration test); a director not allowed to take out (9); the owner always `needs-you` (composed); the owner's level by director count instead of directors told (composed). Survived and equivalent: the door's "already escalated" check removed alone (`markEscalated` refuses a second mark itself); both removed together fail 4.
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`): controller `landing/*`, `workspace-ops/*`, `status/status`, `chat/model-interpreter`, `api/api`, `api/start-p10*`, `api/start-docs`, `agents/*`: 816 of 816; controller `chat/*` with integration `h12q`, `h12s`, `h12t`: 1418 of 1418; integration `h12p-author-refresh` 1 of 1; new files 17 of 17 after the last change. `api-v1.md` regenerated. Skipped: other controller shards, worker and other packages (no host or worker code changed); CI is the net.
- ASSUMPTION: the queue stays strictly first-place-only (the queue slice's design); a reservation is a kept place (the task's number), not a jump ahead of older work. A task reaching the cap while it is away from the queue gets back the place it had when the controller withdrew it, else the back. Reversible in `reserve`.
- ASSUMPTION: a reservation reaches the cap at round >= cap (`refreshRounds`; 0 reserves at the first round), and the director is told once per reservation, at the first round beyond the round that reserved it. A round missed because the controller stopped between recording it and `onRound` is caught at the next round (>= cap).
- ASSUMPTION: the hold time is a fixed four hours (`LANDING_HOLD_MS`, not an owner setting), checked lazily when another landing is refused behind the first place (no timer); escalation keeps the hold (the director or the owner decides: let it land, or take it out). Reversible: the `holdMs` option, or a setting.
- ASSUMPTION: the director may take out any entry and end a reservation (escalation needs someone who can act); a director is an active agent with the director role and a live grant naming the project.
- ASSUMPTION: the Q04 cycle limit ("a conflict returned to its author counts as a repair cycle") belongs with the slice that returns overlapping work to its author: no conflict is returned yet, so there is nothing to count. The refresh-round cap built here bounds the same loop for stale work. Left for that slice.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) Mechanical re-apply of disjoint submissions by the integrator (a stale first place still goes back to its author). (2) Return of overlapping work to its author as an act of the queue (today a review `changes` does it), and the Q04 cycle count for it. (3) Reassigning a retired author's task (its entry and reservation stay until taken out; the hold escalation tells the director). (4) The remaining items of the earlier slices: a remote host still refuses a landing `submission`, the `integration` operation is not under the lease or the queue, and nothing commits landed files (P10c/H12o).

**P10 third slice, first review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20): fixed.**
1. **A reserved place could overtake a landing already at the host.** The take-out guard keeps an entry whose landing is in progress, but a reservation restored from `away` (or the re-approval that takes that number again) put a task AHEAD of an entry that had already passed its last check; that task's landing then passed both of its own checks and reached the host while the other was still there. `LandingQueueService.landingUnderway` reads the open request of every other entry of the queue (the same `workspace-open`/request reading as the take-out guard), and `checkLanding` refuses the first place's landing `invalid_transition` ("task X's landing on branch Y is in progress") while another entry's landing is `started` or `uncertain`. A landing records its request before its last check, so of two landings that both pass the first-place check one always sees the other. A leftover `uncertain` landing blocks the same way the take-out guard already does, until recovery closes it.
2. **A failed escalation was never told, and a replay counted as a fresh mark.** The door marked the escalation first and then told; when telling failed (the owner's notification threw) the mark stayed and nobody was ever told. It now tells first and marks after, so an unmarked escalation is told at the next refused landing (front) or the next round (round). The notices stay idempotent: the held notice's text no longer contains the elapsed hours (it says "at least" the hold time) and its command ID also names whether the place waits for approval; the round notice's command ID names the round. `markEscalated` answers `false` on a replay of its command, and the round mark is keyed by the reservation's `since` (a later reservation of the same task is marked again).
3. **Wording.** The refusal behind a reserved first place says who may take it out and that this lets the others land; the interpreter paragraph says the director and the owner are told (the owner asked to decide when no director could be told), not "the owner when the project has none".
- Tests (`landing/landing-queue-reservations.test.ts`, four backends, 2 new): a reserved place restored ahead of an entry whose landing waits at the host is refused before any host, and asked once that landing ended (host calls 1, then 2); an escalation whose telling failed is told at the next refused landing, then once, and a round notice that failed is told at the next round (round 4), then not again.
- Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored): guard off (4 failures); mark before tell (4); for the fairness test alone: never reserving (4 of 4), a reserved place without an entry not first (4 of 4), a reserved task's re-approval to the back (4 of 4).
- Verified (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build`): controller `landing/*` and `api/start-p10*` 155 of 155; `chat/model-interpreter` and `workspace-ops/*` 322 of 322; integration `h12p-author-refresh` 1 of 1. `api-v1.md` equal to `npm run api:docs:write` (no API text changed).
- **Judged, not changed.** (a) The hold escalation is checked only when a landing is refused behind the first place (as specified, no timer): a queue nobody tries to land from tells nobody; the owner sees the reservation in the `landing_queue` view. (b) A director may take out entries and end reservations but cannot read the queue (`landing.queue.list` stays owner/integrator); the notice names the task, which is all `landing.queue.remove` needs. (c) A reservation of a task that was cancelled or whose author retired stays until it is taken out (Not done 3); the hold escalation tells the director and the owner. (d) `others` in the list counts entries only, so a branch holding only a reservation (after the landing branch was renamed) is not named; it blocks nothing on the landing branch. (e) Rights and reach checked: `isDirector` needs a live grant naming this project (another project's director is told `not_found`), a director's notice is refused for a director who cannot reach the task (the owner is then asked, `needs-you`), and the reservation-only take-out is open only to callers with no `allowed` rule (owner, integrator, director), never the controller's withdrawal.

**P10 third slice, second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-20): two fixes, the rest checked.**
1. **A full queue could stay held by its own first place.** `enqueue` refused any new entry once the queue held 200, the re-approval of a reserved task too. With the first place reserved and waiting for its approval, nothing else lands and that task could not take its place back, so the queue stayed held until someone took something out by hand. A task with a reserved place now takes its kept place at the bound (reservations are bounded on their own: at most 200 + 200 entries); any other new entry is still refused there. Test (`landing/landing-queue-reservations.test.ts`, four backends): a reserved first place without an entry behind 200 entries, another task refused `unavailable`, the reserved task's re-approval placed first (seq 1, position 1). Mutation (the old bound, in the built file): 4 failures of 4; restored.
2. **Wording.** Landing the reserved task itself while it has no entry (the owner's unqueued landing included: the queue is not empty) was refused with "an integrator lands only queued submissions"; it now says the task holds a reserved place and lands from it once its submission is approved. The reservation test asserts both callers.
- **Checked, not changed.** (a) Two landings at the host: both landings record their request before the second showing of the queue, so for a reserved place restored ahead of an entry at the host, either the newer landing's head check precedes the other's record (impossible: the other's second check would then see the newer one first) or its `landingUnderway` read sees the other `started`; sound. An owner's unqueued landing (queue empty at both showings) is not an entry, so `landingUnderway` does not see it; an entry added after that landing's second showing can reach the host while it is there. This is the queue slice's existing window, not new here; the host's per-tree queue still runs the two one after the other. (b) Leftover `uncertain`: recovery at start marks a left `started` landing `uncertain` and clears the task's open pointer in that write; only a repeat while the first call still runs leaves the pointer naming `uncertain`, and that first call then writes the real outcome. So `landingUnderway` and the take-out guard are held only while a landing is really open. (c) A cancelled task or retired author holding a reservation still holds the branch once its place is first, until it is taken out; the hold escalation tells the director and the owner (`needs-you` when no director could be told), as the first review judged. (d) A reserved place never counts as first while its task has an entry (the entry is the place, with the same number); the landing's own write removes the entry and the reservation together; a reservation-only take-out cannot meet a landing in progress (a task without an entry has no queued landing, and an unqueued one is refused while any reservation exists). (e) Notices: command IDs are derived from the queue, task and `since` (and round), so a restart repeats nothing that was marked; a notice told and then not marked before a restart is told again only for a round notice at a later round (its ID names the round). (f) Rights: directors only through a live grant naming the project, never with a task credential; another project's director and non-members get `not_found`; the director's notice is refused for a director who cannot reach the task. (g) The composed `isDirector`/`escalate` judge grant expiry on the system clock while the queue uses the dispatcher's clock; grants are judged on the system clock elsewhere too. (h) `npm run api:docs:write` leaves `api-v1.md` unchanged; the chat paragraph reaches reservations in free words.

## P10 (fourth slice): mechanical re-apply of disjoint work, overlapping work returned to its author as a Q04 repair cycle, and returned work of a retired author's task (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. When the landing branch moved after a task's work was approved, the integrator no longer has to send that work back to its author for a refresh when none of the work's files changed on the branch in the meantime: the host that holds the checkout moves the approved change, unchanged, onto the branch's head, proves it is byte for byte the change that was approved, the required checks (P09) run on the result, and it lands. When some of its files did change there, nothing lands and the work goes back to the agent that now holds the task: it leaves the landing queue, is not queued again, and the holder is told which files overlap and to refresh and submit again. Each such return is one repair cycle of the task (card Q04's rule "a conflict returned to its author counts as a repair cycle"), counted against the project's `review.repairCycles` (Q04's own setting, default 3); at that limit the project's director and the owner are told, and they decide. A task whose author retired cannot be held by that author any more (retirement refuses while an agent holds tasks), so the returned work goes to whoever holds the task now; when nobody active holds it, the director and the owner are told to assign it or take it out. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **The host (`worker/workspace/git.ts`, `host.ts`, `local-host.ts`).** `GitBridge.restack({ shared, onto, gitDir, checkout, submission })`: the checkout must be at rest and its committed change must be exactly the approved one, either on the approved base or already re-applied onto a later commit of that base's history (a re-apply made by an earlier landing that did not finish counts only after the same proof). The landing branch's head is fetched; it must descend from the checkout's base (a rewritten branch is refused). The submission's paths (`diff --raw --no-renames`) and the paths the branch changed since the base must be disjoint: no shared path, and no path inside a folder the other side changed as a file. Disjoint: a new tree is built in a throwaway index as the head's tree with exactly the submission's entries put in (same modes and objects; a link or submodule entry is refused), it is proven with `sameChange` (every entry's path, old and new mode and old and new object equal to the approved change) before anything moves, a platform commit (release identity, `NimbleNewt-Submission` and `NimbleNewt-Reapplied-From` trailers, not a permit commit) is made on the head, the clean checkout gets the branch's files by a two-way `read-tree -m -u`, and the base and head refs move in one `update-ref --stdin` transaction, each from the value read. Nothing is ever merged line by line. `WorkspaceHost.restack` checks the request, the landing policy (branch named, shared tree on it and clean) and that the task's attempts are quiet, runs in the same order as a landing (the checkout, then the shared tree), and answers `current`, `reapplied` (new base and tree, the old base, whether it was an earlier re-apply answered again, how many branch files were taken), `overlap` (at most 20 paths, the head) or a refusal; no journal is needed because the answer is decided by the checkout's own state each time. `LocalWorkspaces.port.restack` exposes it. A landing call may carry `reappliedFrom` (the approved base and tree, only with a submission); the host then proves again, before anything is written, that the checkout's committed change on the new base is exactly the approved change on a later commit of the approved base's history, and answers `detail.reappliedFrom` when it lands.
- **The landing (`workspace-ops.ts`).** `WorkspacePort.restack` (optional). Inside the quiesce, after the lease and queue are shown again and BEFORE the P09 gate, a landing of a queued submission asks the host to re-apply. `current`: as before. `reapplied`: the gate's checks run on that tree (its `review` check compares patch IDs, which an unchanged change keeps), and the host is told the re-applied base and tree as `submission` plus `reappliedFrom`; the record keeps `queued` (what was approved) and `reapplied` (what landed). The queue entry leaves with the landing only when the host confirms the re-applied base and tree AND the same `reappliedFrom`. `overlap`: nothing is asked of the gate or the host, the landing is `refused` with the paths, and the queue's `returned` is told (best effort, after the quiesce); the record keeps `returned` (paths, who was told, the cycle count and limit, whether the director and owner were told). A refusal from the re-apply refuses the landing; a host without `restack` (a remote host today) lands only on the approved base, as before.
- **The queue (`landing/landing-queue.ts`).** New record fields `returned` (submission IDs returned to their authors, last 200: `enqueue` refuses one of them `invalid_transition`, so neither the controller's own queueing nor a hand add puts work back that would overlap again) and `returns` (per task: the count, and the last return's time, submission and paths; at most 200 tasks). `returnWork` is one recorded command that, in one write, takes out only that very submission's entry (a newer one of the task that took its place stays; `returned: false` and nothing counted when it is no longer queued), remembers its place in `away` like the controller's withdrawals (a reserved place is kept: its re-approval takes the place again), notes the submission in `returned` and adds one to the task's count; a repeat of the command counts nothing more. A landing's `landedChanges` drops the task's returns.
- **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** `returned(call)`: returns the work, reads the limit (`repairCycles`, `REPAIR_CYCLES_DEFAULT` 3 when absent, unreadable or not a whole number of at least 1), tells the holder (`assignee`, only while `activeAgent` says it is active) with the overlapping files, what to do (`work.refresh`, submit again) and "conflict return N of L", and calls `escalate` with `why: "returns"` when the count is at or past the limit (each return from then on, named by its count) or `why: "unassigned"` when nobody could be told. `list` answers `returns`. New options `repairCycles`, `tell`, `activeAgent`.
- **Composition (`api/start.ts`).** `repairCycles` reads `review.repairCycles` as it applies to the project (the defect service's reader); `tell` is an inbox notice from the controller to the holder; `activeAgent` is the principal's state; the escalation's owner notification names the two new reasons ("its work overlapped landed files again, at the repair-cycle limit", "returned work, nobody holds the task"), `notice` when a director was told, `needs-you` otherwise (as the third slice built). `workspaceOps` gets `landingQueue.returned`.
- **Chat and owner controls.** No new operation: the owner's decisions are the existing `landing.queue.remove`, a hand-off of the task, and the existing `review.repairCycles` setting (`policy_edit`). The interpreter prompt's landing-queue paragraph now says, in free words, that disjoint work is re-applied unchanged by itself (the checks still run), that overlapping work goes back to the agent holding the task and counts as a repair cycle, that the limit is `review.repairCycles` (the same as for defects, "give them five tries before asking me"), who is told and what the owner can do. The `landing_queue` status view lists each task's returns (count, last submission and paths) and says the director and owner are told at `review.repairCycles`. API summaries of `workspace.request` (re-apply, `reapplied`, `returned`) and `landing.queue.list` (`returns`) updated; `api-v1.md` regenerated with `npm run api:docs:write`.
- **Tests.** `worker/workspace/landing-restack.test.ts` (real git, 2 tests): disjoint work (a change, a deletion and a new file) re-applied onto a head that changed two other files: the new base, tree and parent, the branch's files in the checkout, the agent's own files kept, a clean checkout, the change from the head exactly the approved one, a repeat answered as recovered, a landing with a `reappliedFrom` the host cannot prove refused with nothing written, the re-applied landing writing exactly the approved change while the branch's own change stays; overlap of the same path and of a folder with a file inside it (nothing moved), a checkout that is not the submission, a dirty checkout, a rewritten branch and a malformed submission refused. `controller/landing/landing-queue-returns.test.ts` (four storage backends, 5 tests, with a simulated branch head and host): a stale disjoint first place re-applied and landed (restack before land, the host told the re-applied base and tree and the approved ones, the entry gone, a repeat asking nothing); a host that does not confirm the proof keeps the entry, and a host without `restack` refuses as before; overlap returned (the host not asked to land, the holder told, out of the queue, the controller's and a hand re-queue refused, `returns` listed, the next task lands, a refreshed submission lands and ends the returns, a return of a submission no longer queued does nothing); ### P10 (fourth slice) first review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. The re-apply is sound in what it proves: the bytes added beyond the branch head are exactly the approved entries on exactly the approved old entries, proven before anything moves and again by the host before it writes. Three gaps in the "disjoint" test and in failure handling were closed.

- **Changed.** (1) **Names compared as the filesystem sees them.** The disjoint test compared paths byte for byte, so a branch file differing only by case (`docs/C.md` against the work's `docs/c.md`) or by Unicode normalisation (NFD against NFC) counted as disjoint; on a case-insensitive or normalising filesystem they are one file, and writing the branch's file into the checkout would have replaced the agent's. Paths are now compared by `collisionKey` (the same fold the bridge uses), for equality and for the folder-and-file rule. (2) **Git attribute files.** A `.gitattributes` changed on one side now overlaps every path of the other side in its folder or below: the landing writes the approved bytes, but committing them later applies the branch's attributes (eol, `text`, filters), which the review did not see. (3) **A failed ref move puts the checkout back.** The checkout's files are written (two-way `read-tree -m -u`) before the base and head refs move in one transaction; when that transaction fails, the files and index are now read back to the head they were read at, so the checkout is not left looking changed (which would refuse every later landing and refresh). A crash of the host process between the two steps still leaves that state (as `refresh` already can); the owner sees a dirty checkout refused, nothing lands.
- **Tests.** `landing-restack.test.ts` gains one test: case-only, NFC/NFD, a branch rename whose source the work changes, and an attribute file over the work's folder all overlap; a locked base ref makes the re-apply fail with the checkout, index and refs as they were, and it succeeds once the lock is gone. Mutations (built file, each alone, restored): no fold, no attribute rule, no put-back: each fails that test. Controller spot mutations: `enqueue` dropping `returned`/`returns`, and a landing keeping its task's returns: each fails 4 of `landing-queue-returns`.
- **Checked, not changed.** Renames and copies: both sides are listed with `--no-renames`, so a rename on the branch shows its source as deleted and overlaps work on it. Symlinks and submodules in the work are refused; a branch link or submodule at a folder of the work overlaps by the folder rule. Mode-only changes, deletions and binary files are entries with modes and object IDs, compared exactly; an empty change is refused. The proof compares against the queue entry's approved base and tree (the controller's record), not anything in the checkout; the host proves again at landing and the existing tree check then binds the checkout's head to the re-applied tree. The branch moving again after the re-apply refuses the landing (base is not head; the write guard checks again) and the next landing re-applies from the earlier re-apply after the same proof. The two ref moves are one `update-ref --stdin` transaction, each a compare-and-swap. Git: `update-ref --stdin` transactions need 2.27, below the 2.39 the P09 patch IDs already require. SHA-256 repositories: commits are matched as 40-hex IDs throughout the workspace code, so a SHA-256 repository is refused, never mis-landed. P09's `review` check compares host-computed patch IDs, which the unchanged change keeps (asserted). Returns: one command per landing request, a repeat counts nothing; the never-queued-again mark names the returned submission only, so a refreshed (new) submission queues. Rights: `returns` is listed only to the project's integrators; the holder's notice goes only to an active agent; directors and the owner as in the third slice. `npm run api:docs:write` leaves `api-v1.md` unchanged.
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build`): worker `workspace/*` 156 of 158 (2 skipped, platform-only); controller `landing/landing-queue-returns` 20 of 20 (with the mutations restored). `npm run check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass.

### P10 (fourth slice) second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

Plain words first. Nothing can land that was not approved: the host builds the re-applied tree from the queue entry's approved base and tree (the controller's record, not anything the submitter can still change), proves entry by entry that the change from the branch head is exactly the approved change before anything moves, and at landing proves it again, then reads the checkout's own base and tree again and requires them to be the re-applied ones. One gap in the "disjoint" test was closed, and two guards that no test held were given tests.

- **Changed.** (1) **Git ignore files** (`git.ts restack`). A `.gitignore` changed on one side now overlaps every path of the other side in its folder or below, as a `.gitattributes` does: an ignore rule the branch added can hide a file the work adds, and since `sharedTree` lists no ignored file, the landed file would not show as waiting to be committed and would be left out of the integrator's commit. The review never saw that rule. (2) **Tests.** `landing-restack.test.ts` gains one real-git test: an executable-bit-only change re-applied with its old and new mode; a link entry in the work refused with nothing moved; a branch `gen/.gitignore` over the work's `gen/x.out` overlaps; hooks planted in the checkout's git directory (`reference-transaction`, `post-checkout`, `post-index-change`, `post-commit`, `pre-commit`) run neither during the re-apply nor during the landing; a branch that moves again after a re-apply refuses the earlier re-apply's landing, is re-applied from it (`previous` = the first re-applied base) and lands only with `reappliedFrom` naming the approved base and tree (the approved tree on another base is refused). `landing-queue-returns.test.ts`: a host that echoes `reappliedFrom` with the approved base and a different tree keeps the entry; returning the old submission while the task's newer one is queued takes nothing out and counts nothing.
- **Mutations** (built files, each alone, restored and compared): no `.gitignore` rule (the new worker test fails); no link refusal (fails; the landing's own plan would still refuse a link); landing proof always true (2 worker tests fail); `returnWork` matching any entry of the task (4 of `landing-queue-returns` fail, survived before the new assertion); confirmation ignoring the approved tree (4 fail, survived before the new variant); no `unassigned` escalation (4 fail).
- **Checked, not changed.** Hooks and configuration: every git command runs with `core.hooksPath` set to an empty folder, no global or system configuration, and the repository is the host's own (outside the sandbox); `read-tree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref` and `fetch` therefore run no hook (the test plants them). The neutral `info/attributes` is written by `status` before `read-tree -u`, so the branch's files are written as committed. Links in the branch are written as plain files (`core.symlinks=false`). Deletion plus re-add on the branch with the same bytes is no change of that path (nothing to overlap); with other bytes it is a change and overlaps. Context the branch changed without touching the work's paths (a function the work calls, renamed elsewhere) is what the project's required checks (P09) run for, on the re-applied tree; this is the first slice's ASSUMPTION, unchanged. Case and normalisation: a branch folder `Docs/` beside the work's `docs/` with different file names overwrites nothing. Crash windows: after `read-tree -u` and before the ref transaction, the checkout looks changed; the next re-apply, landing and refresh refuse it as not at rest (fail closed, as `refresh` already can); after the transaction and before the answer, the next re-apply answers `recovered`. Returns: one command per landing request; the never-queued mark names only the returned submission, so a resubmission (a new ID) queues; the automatic queueing swallows the refusal (best effort) and a hand add is refused. Permit: under the default `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true`, the re-apply's platform commit is not a permit commit, so the landing refuses it as it refuses H12o's release commit (first slice's Not done (2)); the checkout has then moved onto the head, which a later re-apply answers as recovered. `npm run api:docs:write` leaves `api-v1.md` unchanged.
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build`): worker `workspace/*` 157 of 159 (2 skipped, platform-only); controller `landing/landing-queue-returns` 20 of 20. `npm run check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass.
- **Re-check** (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, clean context, 2026-11-20). The ignore-file rule holds: both sides are tested (`attributesOver(t, k) || attributesOver(k, t)`), on `collisionKey` keys (so `.GitIgnore` and other foldable spellings count), a root file (folder '') covers every path, a nested one its folder and below, and added, changed, deleted and renamed files are all listed (`--no-renames` shows a rename as a deletion and an addition). `core.excludesFile` is inert (no global or system configuration) and the checkout's `info/exclude` cannot hide work (a re-apply needs a checkout at rest, ignored files counted). An overlap returns the submission once; after a refresh its base is the head and the re-apply answers `current`, so the rule loops only while the branch keeps changing an ignore file over the work, as for attribute files. Added one test (an ignore file the work changes overlaps a branch path in its folder; a case-folded root ignore file the branch adds overlaps every work path); mutations: no `.gitignore` name fails both ignore tests, no work-side check fails the new one.

## P10 (fifth slice): after a hand-off, the task's new holder answers for its queued work (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. Before this slice, only the agent that submitted a piece of work (besides the owner, integrators and directors) could put it in the landing queue or take it out. After the owner handed the task to another agent, that new agent, who is the one asked to refresh returned work, could not take the task's work out of the queue, while the agent that handed it off still could. Now the agent that holds the task answers for its queued work: after a hand-off the new holder may add the task's approved submission and take it out, and the agent that handed it off may no longer. While nobody holds the task (never assigned, or released), the submitter may, as before. The queue entry still names the submitter as its author (what was approved, and by whom). This closes the fourth slice's Not done (3). Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- ASSUMPTION (the slice chosen): of the remaining P10 items (remote hosts re-apply, a permit commit for the re-apply, the entry's owner after a hand-off, the `integration` operation under the lease and queue, committing landed files), this slice takes the hand-off rule: it is the smallest that is complete on its own, touches no host or git code and needs no new stored field. The others stay listed below.
- ASSUMPTION (who answers after a hand-off): the holder now replaces the submitter, rather than both being allowed. A hand-off moves the responsibility for the task (the returned-work notice of the fourth slice already goes to the holder), so the agent that handed it off should not be able to pull the new holder's queued work. The owner, integrators and directors are unchanged. Reversible: in `#ownAgent` (`queue-ops.ts`), answer `author === by.id` beside the holder check.
- **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** New option `holderOf(taskId)`: the principal that holds the task now, or undefined. `#ownAgent(by, taskId)` decides who is the task's own agent: a task credential counts only for its own task; with a holder, only the holder; with no holder, the submission's author; when the holder cannot be read, nobody (fails closed; the owner, integrators and directors are not affected); without the option, the author rule alone (as before). `add` and `remove` use it in place of the author check. The take-out still judges the entry inside the queue's own write; the holder is read just before it, so a hand-off at that very moment is judged on the holder before it.
- **Composition (`api/start.ts`).** `holderOf` reads the task's assignment: while it is `assigned`, its owner as a principal ID (`agent:<id>`; an owner ID that already carries a kind is used as it is).
- **API and chat.** The summaries of `landing.queue.add` and `landing.queue.remove` say who the task's own agent is; `api-v1.md` regenerated with `npm run api:docs:write`. The owner's chat is unchanged: the owner may always take work out, and a hand-off is the existing owner control.
- **Tests.** `controller/landing/landing-queue-handoff.test.ts` (four storage backends, 3 tests each, with the real assignment service): after a hand-off the new holder takes the entry out (a repeat answered as done) and adds it back with the submitter still named as author, the old author and a stranger refused both, a task credential of another task refused and one of the task itself allowed; a task never assigned or released leaves its work to the author (the earlier holder refused), and a task handed back to its author is hers again; a holder that cannot be read refuses the agent but not the owner, and without `holderOf` the author rule stands. `controller/api/start-p10-handoff.test.ts` (composed controller): the controller queues the approved work; the owner hands the task over with `transferTask` (owner ID stored bare, as the inbox does); through the state API the old author is told `not_found` for remove and add, the new holder removes and adds back, and after the task is released the author removes it and the former holder cannot.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared): all real ones killed.** Holder ignored (5 fail); author allowed beside the holder (5); task credential scope ignored (4); an unreadable holder failing open (4); `add` keeping the old author rule (9); `remove` keeping the old author rule (9); the composition passing the bare owner ID (composed test fails). One equivalent mutation survived and is not a gap: dropping the `assigned` state check in `holderOf` changes nothing, because a release removes the owner from the assignment.
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, after `npx tsc --build --force`): controller `landing/*`, `workspace-ops/*`, `api/start-p10*`, `api/api*`, `api/operations*`, `api/start-docs*`: 561 of 561 (26 files, no flake); `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs` 27 of 27. `npm run check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; the task plan and roadmap regenerate unchanged. Skipped: other controller shards and packages (no other code changed); CI is the net.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) A remote host has no `restack` and still refuses a landing `submission`, so neither re-apply nor return happens there. (2) The re-apply commit is a platform commit, not a review-gate permit commit, so under the default `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true` the landing still refuses it. (3) The `integration` operation still writes the shared tree without the lease or the queue. (4) Nothing commits the landed files (P10c/H12o). (5) From the fourth slice: a reserved place whose work was returned keeps holding the branch until the refreshed work is approved or someone takes it out. (6) The holder is read just before the queue's write, not inside it: a hand-off at the very same moment as a take-out is judged on the holder before the hand-off.

## Prompt growth tests: windows of the real-process tests worked out from the fixed part's budget (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-20)

- **Symptom.** Exhaustive CI run 44841469337 (main b628fe73), shard 1 on Ubuntu: six integration files failed after T08's third and fourth slices brought the worker's fixed part to 2,537 + 19,087 characters (7,208 tokens; 6,751 before, at 2,537 + 17,714). All six reproduced locally.
- **Mechanism, per file.** `c07g-route-view`: at its written-out 40,960-token window the startup share is 10,240 tokens; the measured fixed part plus what must stay whole (goal, decision, newest questions, a reference for each one left out, 3,034 tokens) came to 10,242, so the view was blocked. `g09-retained-context`, `w03-stopped-early`, `w04-continuation` (the shared `w03-rig-support.ts`, 36,864 written out): the first call of the resumed or continued run was 9,449 tokens against a startup share of 9,216, so the attempt failed instead of ending as the test expects. `h12k-composed-host` (32,768): the first call, 8,270 tokens, went over the 8,192 share, so the context check refused it once. `w11-job-wake` (32,768): the woken run's first call, 8,358 tokens, was over 8,192, so run two never reached its last model call. A tool or rule added within the budget leaves these tests startable; one over it fails `fixed-part-budget.test.ts` first, and raising the budget raises these windows. These stay written out, as the RAISING steps already list them. `pi-adapter`'s compaction thresholds and the worker's tests do not depend on the fixed part's size. w07-route-budget's 32,768 is a provider's declared window in a budget test and passes.
