## H12p follow-up: the author's refresh and the submit's stale check go to the owner's landing branch (Claude agent, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. Before this slice the agent's `work.refresh` moved its checkout onto whatever commit the shared working tree had checked out, and a submit was checked for a stale base against that same commit. A landing and the integrator's mechanical re-apply (P10) work only on the owner's landing branch. So if the shared tree was on another branch for a moment (an owner looking at something, a tool), an agent could refresh onto that other branch's work, be told its submit was fine or stale against the wrong commit, and only find out at landing. Now the refresh and the submit's check both go to the owner's landing branch (the project's own branch, else `workspace.landing.branch`), read as that branch's commit in the shared repository, whatever the working tree has checked out. With no landing branch set, both follow the shared tree's head as before.

- ASSUMPTION (the slice chosen): every acceptance clause of H12p was already met on main (the H12p finish and review sections above; the refresh-round cap is P10's third slice). The one place the author's refresh still disagreed with the restack/landing machinery was which commit it treats as "the landing branch", so this slice makes it read the landing policy the same way (one reader, `WorkspaceHost.#policy`, now shared by the integrator's re-apply and the author's refresh) and makes the submit's stale check use the same head. It needs no model server.
- ASSUMPTION (branch, not checked-out tree): the refresh reads `refs/heads/<landing branch>` rather than refusing while the shared tree is on another branch (as the restack does). A refresh only reads the shared repository; refusing would block an agent for something that does not concern its work, and the landing still refuses until the shared tree is back on the branch. Reversible in `WorkspaceHost.landingHead`.
- ASSUMPTION (refusals): a landing branch the shared repository does not have, landing settings that cannot be read, a host that refuses to name a policy (`refuse`, a remote host pinned elsewhere) and a name that is not a plain branch name refuse the refresh and leave the checkout as it was (fail closed, as a landing and a re-apply do). The same refuses a submit's view (`unavailable`); the submit is then refused as unavailable, as it already was when the view could not be read.
- **Worker (`workspace/git.ts`, `host.ts`, `local-host.ts`).** `GitBridge.branchHead(shared, branch)`: the commit `refs/heads/<branch>` names in the shared repository (exact ref name through `for-each-ref`, never a pattern or an option; the name must have the owner's branch shape), `undefined` when absent. `GitBridge.submitView` takes an optional `head`. `WorkspaceHost.landingHead({ taskId, projectId, shared, carried? }, nothing)`: reads the policy through the host's `landing` option (with what a remote request carried), answers `{ head, branch }`, `{ head }` (no branch set) or `{ refuse }`. `#reapply` uses it; its answer names the branch (`detail.branch`, the summary says "onto the head of the landing branch "main""). `LocalWorkspaces.submitView` uses it too.
- **Controller (`remote/host.ts`, `remote/service.ts`, `remote/protocol.ts`).** A remote host cannot read the controller's settings, so the author's refresh now carries the owner's landing policy (as a landing has since H12a): read fresh, a caller's own figures never taken; unreadable: nothing is sent and the answer says the checkout was left as it was; a policy that names no branch is carried as it is; one the request check refuses is a clean refusal ("the refresh was not sent"). The request check accepts `landing` on `reapply` as well as on `landing` (still refused on every other operation).
- **API.** The `work.refresh` summary says which branch it goes to and when it is refused; `detail.branch` added to its result text. `api-v1.md` regenerated. The Pi tool's short description is unchanged (the fixed part does not grow).
- **Owner controls.** None new: the landing branch is the one the owner already sets in free words in chat (`project.branches.set`/`.change`, `workspace.landing.branch` through `integration`/settings), and the refusal text names the missing branch and what to do ("the owner names an existing branch or creates it").
- **Tests.** `worker/workspace/reapply-host.test.ts` (2 new, real git): the shared tree checked out on a side branch with its own commit, the refresh goes to `main`'s head (the side file is not taken, the agent's file kept, the shared repository unchanged, `detail.branch`, `landingHead` agrees, a second ask is "nothing to refresh"); refusals with the checkout unchanged for a missing branch, unreadable settings, a host `refuse`, and five names that are not plain branch names; a remote request's carried policy reaches the host's option; with no branch named, the shared tree's head as before. `worker/workspace/local-host.test.ts` (1 new): a submit's view names the landing branch's head and its changes while the shared tree is on a side branch that changed the agent's file (no false overlap), the refresh through the port, then a view with nothing stale, and a missing landing branch refusing the view. `controller/remote/dispatch-carry.test.ts` (1 new, four storage backends): the refresh carries the owner's policy (not the caller's), carries an empty policy as it is, is not sent when the policy cannot be read, is a clean refusal when it cannot be carried, and with no reader is sent with none.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) The submit's refusal text when the view is refused is the existing generic "unavailable"; the agent is not shown the branch problem there (the refresh shows it). (2) A remote host's own `landing` option decides how it treats a carried policy for a refresh; the shipped remote composition is the operator's. (3) The earlier H12p "Not done" items stand: no end-to-end run with a real model and sandboxed agent (offline), a crash between the host's refresh and the controller's record undercounts a round by one, a file deleted on one side and changed on the other keeps the agent's side, and a host crash in the middle of writing a merged file can leave that one file short.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored, then `tsc --build --force`): all 10 killed.** Landing branch ignored (3 failures); a missing branch falling back to the shared head (2); unreadable settings taken as "none" (1); the host's `refuse` ignored (1); the carried policy not passed on a refresh (1); the submit's view ignoring the landing head (1); the branch-name check off (1); the remote refresh carrying no policy (4, one per backend); the remote refresh sent when the policy is unreadable (4); the request check still refusing a policy on a refresh (4).
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`): worker `workspace/*` 161 of 163 (2 skipped, platform-only); controller `remote/*`, `workspace-ops/*`, `work-end/*`, `landing/*`, `api/api*`, `api/start-docs*`, `api/start-p10*`, `toolbridge/service` 2,070 of 2,070; integration `h12*` (18 files) and `p09*` 40 of 40; `scripts/d02-docs`, `scripts/plan` 33 of 33. `npm run check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; `api-v1.md` regenerated after the build. Skipped: other controller shards and packages (no other code changed); CI is the net.

### H12p follow-up: first review (Claude agent, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. The slice holds up: an odd landing branch name cannot make git read or write anything other than that one branch, a refused refresh leaves the checkout alone, and a submit is checked against the same head the refresh goes to. One small hardening and a test of the branch reader by itself were added; the rest is said plainly below.

- **Merged** `origin/main` d7bcb753 (P10 fifth slice, G04 fifth slice, the own-hardware docs correction); the only conflict was the end of these notes (both sides kept).
- **Fixed (hardening): a branch ref that does not hold a commit.** `GitBridge.branchHead` took any 40-hex object a `refs/heads/<branch>` held. Git does not write a non-commit into a branch, but a ref file written by hand can hold an annotated tag object, and a refresh would then be asked to base the checkout on it. It now reads `%(objecttype)` too and takes only a commit (otherwise "no branch", so the refresh is refused and the checkout left as it was). The comment says why only the exact name is taken (`for-each-ref` treats its argument as a whole-component prefix: `refs/heads/feature` also lists `refs/heads/feature/x`).
- **Test added** (`worker/workspace/reapply-host.test.ts`, real git): the branch reader alone. `main` reads its commit; a tag `trunk` with no such branch, `feature` while only `feature/x` exists, `refs/heads/main` and `heads/main` (a prefix taken as part of the name, so another branch), a prefix `mai`, `HEAD` and the hand-written ref to a tag object all give nothing; twenty malformed names (leading dash, `--all`, `..`, `//`, trailing slash, `.lock`, space, newline, NUL, a non-ASCII letter, glob characters, `@{-1}`, `~`, `^`, `:`, a leading dot, 201 characters, empty) are refused before git runs; the shared repository (head, status, every ref) is unchanged after all of it; and through the host a refresh to the tag-only name and to the non-commit ref is refused with the checkout's base unchanged. The ref file part runs only where refs are loose files (it checks git sees the planted ref, so a reftable repository leaves that part out rather than failing).
- **Checked, no change.** (1) Argument injection: every name reaches git only as `refs/heads/<name>` after the shape check (first character a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`), as one argument with no shell; the refusal texts quote the name with `JSON.stringify` and cut it to 80 characters, so control characters cannot shape the text. (2) The refusal paths (missing branch, unreadable settings, a host `refuse`, a malformed name) all return before `GitBridge.reapply` is called, which is the only writer; the tests check the base and the files after each. (3) No false "fresh": the submit's view uses the same `landingHead`; when it cannot be read the view throws, the dispatcher reads that as unknown and the submit is refused as unavailable (never as fresh). (4) Storage: the carried policy is added in `RemoteWorkerHost` after the workspace service has recorded the request, and the remote service keeps workspace requests in memory, so nothing new is stored; the remote test runs on all four backends.
- **Not done (said plainly, added to the slice's list).** (4) Mixed versions: a host built before this slice ignores a policy carried on a refresh and refreshes onto its shared tree's checked-out head (the earlier behaviour, no error); the protocol version was not raised and the announced capabilities have no field for it, so the controller cannot tell. A controller built before this slice sends no policy, and a new host then reads its own `landing` option. (5) A new checkout (`LocalWorkspaces.ensure`) and the controller's quiesced `refresh` of a clean checkout still start from, or move to, the shared tree's checked-out head. If the shared tree is on another branch at that moment the checkout's base is that branch's commit; the submit's check then sees a base that is not the landing head (stale, never fresh) and the author's refresh moves it onto the landing branch.
- **Deliberate breakages on built files (each alone, restored): all 7 caught.** `branchHead` without the commit-type check (1 failure) and without the exact-name check (1); a missing landing branch falling back to the shared head (2); the submit's view not given the landing head (1); the remote refresh carrying no policy (4 backends); the request check refusing a policy on a refresh (4 backends); the host not passing the carried policy to its `landing` option (1).

### H12p follow-up: second review (Claude agent, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. The slice holds up, with one gap closed: when a refresh went to a remote host, the controller could record it as a refresh onto the landing branch even when the host had not used that branch (a host built before this slice, or a host whose own settings ignore what the controller carried). The host already says which branch it used; the controller now checks that it is the branch it sent, and otherwise records the refresh as failed and tells the agent not to take its checkout as fresh.

- **Merged** `origin/main` ce552529 (Windows redaction re-checks); no conflict.
- **Fixed: a remote refresh that did not use the carried landing branch.** `RemoteWorkerHost` (controller `remote/host.ts`): a `reapply` that carried a landing branch must come back with `detail.branch` equal to it. An answer without it (an older host, which refreshes onto its shared tree's checked-out head) or naming another branch is thrown as `unavailable`, so the workspace service records `failed` ("may have changed the checkout"), never a refresh onto the landing branch, and no refresh round is counted; the text names the branch, says the checkout may now be based on another commit and asks the agent to refresh again once the host is updated. A policy that names no branch expects none. This replaces "Not done (4)" of the first review as far as the controller's belief goes; an old host still moves the checkout (it cannot be stopped from here without a protocol version), but the controller no longer reports that as fresh. A remote submit is still refused as unavailable (remote hosts give no submit view), so no submission can follow from it.
- **Changed: the host names the whole branch.** `WorkspaceHost.#reapply` put the branch in `detail.branch` cut to 80 characters; a branch name may be 200, so the controller's comparison would have failed for a long name. The name is already checked (shape, at most 200 characters) before it gets there, so it is now carried whole; the summary still cuts it.
- **Tests.** `controller/remote/dispatch-carry.test.ts` (four backends): the remote refresh's answer naming the carried branch is taken; one naming no branch or another branch is thrown `unavailable` with the explanation; a policy without a branch accepts an answer without one. `worker/workspace/reapply-host.test.ts`: a landing branch of 98 characters is named whole in `detail.branch`, both for a refresh that moved and for "nothing to refresh".
- **Checked, no change.** Traced submit and refresh with the shared tree on another branch (both use `landingHead`: the landing branch's commit), with the landing branch missing (refresh refused before `GitBridge.reapply`, the only writer; the submit view throws `unavailable` and the dispatcher turns that into "cannot be known", the submit refused), deleted between the read and the re-apply (the commit ID was read once and the re-apply works from that object; the next submit view refuses), and moved between refresh and submit (the view compares the base with the new head: stale, with the landed files, never fresh). Names reach git only as one argument `refs/heads/<name>` after the shape check; no glob or option character passes; the controller's carried-policy check is looser (`//`, a trailing `/`, `.lock`) and the host refuses those before git. Crash/restart: unchanged from H12p (the host journal answers a repeat, a request that began and did not finish is refused as possibly half done). Storage: nothing new stored; the carried policy and the answer check live in `RemoteWorkerHost`, and the remote test runs on all four backends. New real-git tests: no chmod, symlinks, case or fixed pauses; `core.autocrlf=false` throughout; the loose-ref part checks git sees the planted ref first.
- **Deliberate breakages on built files (each alone, restored, then rebuilt): all 7 caught.** The answer-branch check off (4 failures, one per backend); the host cutting the branch to 80 characters (1); `branchHead` without the exact-name check (1) and without the commit-type check (1); the submit view not given the landing head (1); the request check refusing a policy on a refresh (4); a missing landing branch not refused (3).

## Q03 leftovers: retiring a document, and a notice to the owner when verified documents go stale (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21)

Branch `card-q03t08-s5` off origin/main `61b8434c`. Card status is NOT changed (Q03 and T08 stay planned).

ASSUMPTION: of the open Q03 and T08 leftovers, this slice takes the two smallest that need no model server, no new bridge tool (the fixed part's budget) and no change to how notices reach a prompt: Q03's "taking an obligation away (retiring a document)" and "the owner told by a notice when documents go stale". The rest stays listed below. Nothing waits on Rob; reversible by not calling the new operation and leaving out the `notify` port.

- **Retiring a document.** New state API operation `doc.obligation.retire` (`obligationId`, `expectedRevision`, optional `reason`, at most 300 characters, redacted), `DocObligationService.retire`. Who: the same people who record documents (the owner, or an agent that may read the project's tasks and holds the docs or director role there); not from a task credential. In one write the record is marked `retired` (who, when, why) and taken out of the project's list (`doc-obligation-index`), so it is no longer in `doc.obligation.list`, the `docs` view, or any impact, lost-evidence or release check, and no longer counts toward the project's 500. `doc.obligation.get` still reads it. A retired document can be neither verified, replaced nor retired again (`invalid_command`, "record the document again"). Its open update tasks are marked `dropped` (a new value next to `open` and `settled`); after the write, each one not yet started (proposed, ready or blocked) is cancelled, and one already in progress is left to its agent (its verification is then refused) and reported in `running`. Repeating the command answers `replayed` and finishes any cancellation a failure left (the cancel's command ID carries the task's revision, so a repeat after the task moved is a new cancel, not a `command_conflict`).
- **Races with a running check.** Every check's plan skips a record marked retired, so a check that read the project's list before the retirement and the record after it does not flag it. A check that wrote its flags before the retirement and then opens its update tasks does not create the task of a document retired in between (`#open` reads the record before creating).
- **Notice when documents go stale.** New optional port `notify` of `DocObligationService`, wired in `api/start.ts` to a controller notification (kind `maintenance`, level `notice`, ref the first stale document, project set). It is called once per check that moved documents from `verified` to `stale`, when the check was not the owner's own: the automatic checks after QA evidence is recorded or invalidated (`service:doc-checks`) and a docs or director agent's `doc.impact.check` or `doc.release.check`. The owner's own check (chat or state API, and the release check `release.submit` runs as the owner) answers with what it flagged and sends no notice. Unverified documents flagged are not "gone stale" and send none. The text names the documents (`A verified document went stale: "Landing page". Update tasks went to their keepers; the docs view shows why.`, at most 200 characters); its command ID is derived from the check's command, and a replayed check writes nothing, so it is never sent twice. A notice that cannot be sent is not the check's failure.
- **Owner chat.** Chat operation `doc.obligation.retire` (shown first, pinned to the obligation's revision like the other document commands; the reason must be in the owner's words, the obligation ID comes from the docs view). The interpreter prompt's documentation paragraph says when to use it ("we deleted the old FAQ page", "stop tracking the 1.0 install guide", "the quick start was merged into the user guide") and that the owner gets a notice when verified documents go stale on a check they did not ask for. No bridge tool was added; the worker's fixed part is unchanged.
- **Docs.** `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated (the new operation).
- **ASSUMPTION:** a started update task is not cancelled (it may be mid-run; cancelling would stop an agent's work without a word). Its verification is refused once the document is retired, so the agent finishes it some other way. Reversible: cancel it as well.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the stale notice is a plain notice, not a needs-you item: the keepers already hold the update tasks, so the owner has nothing to answer.
- **Tests.** New `submissions/doc-retire.test.ts` on all four storage backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL): no notice for unverified documents or the owner's own check; one notice for a docs agent's check naming both documents, none on its replay; one for the automatic check after QA evidence; a failing notice does not fail the check; retirement refused for an agent without the role, a wrong revision and an empty reason; the unstarted update task cancelled and the started one reported `running`; the record leaves the list, keeps who and why, its updates `dropped`; the replay, `command_conflict` with another reason; verify, replace and retire again refused; impact, release and lost-evidence checks skip it, also when the list still names it (planted); a document retired while a check opens its update tasks gets no task; a cancel that lost a race to the task moving is finished by the repeat. `api/start-docs.test.ts` (running controller) now also checks the notices in the owner's inbox (level `notice`, the page's title), retires the landing page by chat (a reason not in the owner's words refused; applied, Dora's update task cancelled, the docs view no longer shows it), and through the state API: verify of a retired document refused, a QA agent may not retire, the docs agent may.
- **Mutation checks** (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): retirement keeping the document in the list; release, impact and lost-evidence plans not skipping a retired record; a retired document changeable; notice for the owner's own check; notice for unverified documents; the opening guard removed; started tasks cancelled too; no cancellation; open updates not dropped (each failed `doc-retire` on all four backends); the controller's notice wiring broken; the chat operation missing (each failed `start-docs`). Survived, judged equivalent: notifying without the "this run wrote" condition (a replay never runs the build, so nothing is collected to notify).
- **NOT done / leftovers:** a crash between a check's write and its notice loses the notice (the replay writes nothing, so it does not send it again); the rest of Q03's own list (documents gating a release or `done`, own record kinds for support and promotional material, reading the document's text, the docs view per task and the D01 user guide link, bridge tools for the docs agent); the Q03 next slice's leftovers (older-code QA evidence, a repeat of `qa.evidence.check` with nothing new); all of T08's "Not done" list (promotion through the stand-up and a chat form of publishing, maintainers' view and U08 pages, a chat ask for a maintainer's revocation, notices into the next prompt and their sweep, the bound on final-state proposals, snapshots for personal and system versions).

## B03 (first slice): versioned lessons, their links and evidence, stale premises and the proposer told (Claude agent, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. A lesson is something the team learnt in a project ("handlers without error-path tests get sent back"), written once with when it applies and the records that show it. It can be a newer version of an earlier lesson, rest on other lessons, replace them or disagree with them. The controller works out which pieces of evidence are really separate events and which only repeat one already cited. When a lesson stops holding, every lesson resting on it is marked and the accepted ones go back for review. Any proposed lesson can be finished as accepted, rejected or inconclusive, and the agent that proposed it is told the result.

- ASSUMPTION (the slice): the first slice is the lesson record (versions, applicability, premises, supersession, contradiction, evidence with its independence), its evaluation and review, the stale-premise marking, telling the proposer, the state API, the owner's chat view and decisions, and the dispatcher loop that tells proposers. It needs no model server and adds no worker bridge tool (the worker's fixed part is unchanged).
- ASSUMPTION (the improvement backlog): the card's "project improvement backlog linked to meeting agenda items" already exists as M03's `ImprovementService` (proposals, decisions, `bringToStandup` makes the agenda item, the outcome is told to the proposer). This slice links lessons to it as evidence (an improvement proposal can be a lesson's evidence) and does not build a second backlog.
- ASSUMPTION (what counts as independent): the controller decides, never the proposer. A submission or a review is its own event; an observation rests on the submissions and reviews it cites (or is its own event when it cites none); an improvement proposal is its own. (First review: what rests on no event is its author's own word, so an agent's observation with no event behind it and an improvement proposal count as `account:<author>`: the same author's reports, however reworded, are one independent piece; an observation the controller made with no event stays its own event.) A piece that shares an event with an earlier piece is `derived` (and names that piece), and a lesson cited as evidence is always `derived` ("another lesson's conclusion"). Tasks, artifacts and desk records are not accepted as evidence (they are context, not events).
- ASSUMPTION (when links take effect): supersession and contradiction act only when the new lesson is accepted, so a proposal alone changes nothing. Only direct dependents are marked (bounded); a lesson sent to review does not mark its own dependents until it is actually found rejected or inconclusive, or superseded or contradicted.
- ASSUMPTION (premises at acceptance): a lesson is accepted only when every premise is accepted now. A lesson whose premise was superseded cannot be accepted again; it is revised to rest on the successor (or rejected or found inconclusive). Acceptance clears the stale-premise marks.
- ASSUMPTION (who is told): only an agent's own lesson waits to be told (`outcomePending`); a lesson the owner proposed does not. The notice is filed on the lesson's task (the first piece of evidence that names one), as M03 does for improvements; a lesson with no task stays pending, is shown on the lessons view as "Not yet told to ...", and the proposer can read it with `lesson.get`.

**Done:**
- `packages/controller/src/lessons/` (`LessonService`, `lessonOutcomeSink`). Record kinds `lesson` (ID prefix `lsn`) and `lesson-index` (one per project: the current lessons and finished ones not yet told: at most 500 open ones, 1000 in all).
- **A lesson** has title, statement, applicability (all in the proposer's words, credential-shaped text refused), `lineage` and `version` (a lesson that `revises` another is its next version), `dependsOn`, `supersedes`, `contradicts` (five each), `dependents` (written on the premise when a lesson resting on it is proposed, at most 20), `supersededBy`, `contradictedBy`, evidence (1 to 20 pieces, each with `independence`, the events it rests on and what it repeats), `independentEvidence`, the task it is about, proposer, status, finding, `stalePremises`, `outcomePending` and ten history entries.
- **Statuses.** `candidate` -> `evaluating`, `accepted`, `rejected` or `inconclusive`; `evaluating` -> `accepted`, `rejected`, `inconclusive`; `accepted` -> `needs-review`; `needs-review` -> `accepted`, `rejected`, `inconclusive`. Rejected, inconclusive and superseded are final. Every outcome but `evaluating` needs the finding. Managers of the project's meetings (`meeting.manage`) and the owner decide; anyone with `meeting.agenda` proposes and adds evidence.
- **Stale premises trigger review.** In the same write as the decision: accepting a lesson supersedes what it supersedes and sends an accepted lesson it contradicts to `needs-review` (both record who did it); a lesson that is superseded, contradicted, rejected or found inconclusive marks each lesson resting on it with the stale premise and why, and an accepted one goes to `needs-review`. The decision answers which lessons it marked.
- **Scope.** Links and evidence must be of the lesson's project; an agent may cite only what it can read now (an observation it reported or may read, its own submission or one on a task it may read, its own review request, an improvement it proposed, a lesson it may read); missing, foreign and unreadable records are refused alike. Reads: the owner, `meeting.read` or `meeting.manage`, and the proposer (its own lesson, with other deciders shown as "someone else" and no list of what rests on it).
- **The proposer is told.** `deliverOutcomes` (owner, host or service only) hands each pending outcome to the sink with a stable key (lesson, revision, proposer) and marks it told only after the sink filed it, at the revision told; a told final lesson leaves the current list. The dispatcher loop `lessons.outcomes` (in `dispatch-compose.ts`, with the controller's notices) runs it project by project; one project's failure does not stop the others.
- **State API:** `lesson.propose`, `lesson.evidence`, `lesson.decide`, `lesson.get`, `lesson.list`; `api-v1.md` regenerated. Status kind `lessons` (`lessonStatus` keeps one status), named in the `status.ask` summary.
- **Owner by chat, in any words:** the `lessons` view; `lesson.propose` and `lesson.decide` (revision filled in) apply at once (a candidate changes no work, a decision can be reviewed again); one interpreter prompt sentence with free-word examples. As for every chat command, values (title, statement, applicability, record IDs) must come from the owner's own message.
- **Tests:** `lessons/lessons.test.ts` (5 tests on each of the four backends: independence, more evidence later, scope and replay; versions, supersession, stale premise and the second revision refused; contradiction, reconfirmation and an inconclusive premise; finishing as rejected or inconclusive, the proposer told once, a sink that cannot file, the real notice sink, the owner's own lesson not pending; two services proposing on one premise at once, then a rejection marking all four), `chat/lessons-chat.test.ts` (the prompt, and the owner proposing, asking and deciding by chat on each backend), `api/start-lessons.test.ts` (the composed controller with a real failed review and its observation as evidence, a revision and its stale dependent in the status view, a restart, and the outcome loop).
- **Mutation checks** (built `dist/lessons/lessons.js`, each alone against `lessons.test`, restored byte-identical, SHA-256 checked): same-event detection off; the stale-premise marking off; the premise check at acceptance off; outcomes never pending; evidence readability off; a told final lesson kept on the list; an accepted contradiction not sent to review; the proposer seeing who decided. All 8 failed named tests on all four backends.
- **Runs** (Linux, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`): one affected-suite run of the three new files and their neighbours (`observations/observations.test`, `chat/observations-chat.test`, `api/start-observations.test`, `status/status.test`, `api/api.test`, `chat/model-interpreter.test`, `chat/chat-budget.test`, `dispatch/archived-fence.test`, integration `fixed-part-budget` and `t2-chat-budget-launcher`, `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs`): 427 of 427. Not run, by the owner's reduced test-load rule (CI is the net): the rest of `chat/*`, `status/*`, `api/*`, the other controller shards and `scripts/*.test.mjs`. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; `api-v1.md` regenerated after the build.

**NOT done (next slices):**
- No automatic lesson from observations: a manager or agent proposes one, citing them. Nothing groups similar lessons by wording.
- Applicability is words only; nothing matches a lesson to a task or puts accepted lessons into an agent's context or stand-up brief (a later slice: B04 or the brief).
- An outcome for a lesson with no task waits (shown on the view, readable by the proposer); it is not carried in the stand-up brief as improvement outcomes are, and there is no "untold for days" reminder to the owner.
- Only direct dependents are marked; a chain of lessons is reviewed step by step. A premise with 20 open lessons resting on it refuses a 21st (`unavailable`) until some are settled (finished ones leave its list then, first review).
- The list of current lessons holds at most 1000 (500 open, the rest finished and waiting to be told); a project with 1000 finished lessons that can never be told (no task, a retired proposer) would refuse new lessons. Nothing yet tells such an outcome some other way.
- A submission is its own event, so the same patch submitted many times counts many times; nothing compares submissions' contents.
- No bridge tool for agents (the worker's fixed part has no room); agents use the state API.
- Retention has no rule for `lesson` and `lesson-index` yet (nothing is ever deleted).
- Linux only; nothing here depends on the platform (no paths, timers or signals; the clock is the record's ISO time).

## G04 slice 6: a kill inside the model stream before the tool runs, measured (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-21)

Branch `card-g04-s6`, on main `44a85ef1`. Test code only; no production file changed. Card status is not changed.

Plain words first. Until now the G04 tests killed the controller and Pi together inside a tool call, but the record of the model's reply (the "generation") was written by the tool itself, not by the part of the controller that does it in real use. Now the model's reply goes through the real relay and stream recorder, and the process is killed at every step from the moment the model is asked to the moment the tool answers. In 34 of the 36 kills per database the work ends exactly as if nothing had happened: pushed once, and the model told so. In 2, all in the order the real relay uses, nothing is pushed and the model is told the push did not run, because the controller died after Pi had the whole reply but before the controller marked that reply finished. Nothing is pushed twice and nothing is reported wrongly, but the model would have to try again. That gap is pinned by the test and left for a later slice.

- **ASSUMPTION (which leftover).** Slice 5's list leaves (3) to (7) open. (3), "a kill inside the model stream before the tool runs (Pi's side) is not measured", is the lowest numbered and needs no Windows host, no model and no credentials (a scripted model behind the relay's fetch). (4) to (7) change the worker's or the bridge's behaviour. This slice does (3).
- **Done.**
  - **The rig** (`packages/integration/src/g04-stream.ts`). The real Pi adapter's model calls go through the production `ModelRelay` with the production `streamTapFor` to a scripted OpenAI-style streaming server (`scriptedModel`, three body chunks: start, the tool call or text, the finish and `[DONE]`). The tap begins the generation when the call is sent, records the tool call before Pi may see it and completes the generation at the reply's end. The `push` tool (`streamPushTool`) does what `ToolExecutionService#admitted` does: `admitCall` with the bridge's command ID, then `executeCall` through the ledger; a `GenerationRefused` is answered "it was not run", as the bridge answers it. Reused from the tool slice: `toolPath`, `pushTarget`, `toolState` and `toolInvariants`; `viaRelay` and `relayedModels` (now exported) from `g09-radiance-run.ts`. New child scenarios `stream` and `stream-read-first` in `g04-child.ts`.
  - **Two orders of a reply's end** (`EndOrder`). Pi storing the reply and the controller completing its generation race. `recorded first`: the tool waits for the tap's end before it runs. `read first`: the tap's completion waits until the tool was called (Pi stored the reply before it runs a tool), and the tool then waits for the completion, as the bridge's 3 s wait does. This is the production relay's order (`relay.ts` passes the last piece on, then completes). Each run fixes one order, so its boundaries are the same in every run; the waits are on events, never fixed pauses.
  - **Tests** (`g04-stream-suite.ts`; files `g04-stream-{sqlite,sqlite-worker,postgres}{,-read-first}.test.ts`). Each file: the uncrashed run must end with the expected outcome and two model calls; the swept boundaries must be exactly the expected 18 in order (`STREAM_STEPS`); a real SIGKILL at each, the database read before any command (`acknowledgedSurvive`), a new process finishes the path; the tool slice's invariants plus two new ones (the call admitted in at most one generation; no generation left `streaming`); and the result at each boundary must be `expectedResult`'s. ## P10 (sixth slice): an `integration` is made under the landing branch's lease, by the owner, while the landing queue is empty (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-21)

Plain words first. An `integration` (card H12l) copies a task's unfinished, unreviewed work into the shared folder that the landing branch's approved work lands in. Until now it ignored the integrator lease and the landing queue that every landing must respect, so the owner (or any agent with checkout rights) could put unreviewed files into that folder while approved work was waiting its turn, and those files would then block every landing until somebody committed or cleared them. Now, on a project that has a landing branch, an integration needs the same live integrator lease as a landing (the owner can leave it out, as in chat: the current holder's lease is used), only the owner may ask for it, and only while that branch's landing queue is empty (no waiting work, no reserved place). The lease and the queue are checked when the request is made and again right before the host is asked. A project with no landing branch integrates exactly as before. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- ASSUMPTION (the slice chosen): of the remaining P10 items, (a) "the `integration` operation is not under the lease or the queue" was taken, as the first in the preference order and the smallest complete one that runs offline: it touches no host or git code, no stored record shape (only an optional field's use: `lease` on an integration's record) and no worker prompt. (b) the re-apply permit commit and (c) the hand-off racing a take-out stay listed below.
- ASSUMPTION (who may integrate on a project with a landing branch): only the owner, while the queue is empty, exactly like the owner's unqueued landing (queue slice). An integrator or other agent is refused even with a live lease: an integrator lands only queued, approved submissions, so it carries no content of its own, and an integration carries unreviewed content. Reversible in `LandingQueueOps.checkIntegration` (drop the owner check).
- ASSUMPTION (no landing branch): an integration on a project that names no landing branch is not gated (no lease can exist there, and there is no queue or landing to protect); naming a lease there is refused. Settings that cannot be read refuse the integration (`unavailable`, fail closed). Reversible in the `integrationGate` composition (`api/start.ts`).
- ASSUMPTION (the owner without a holder): as for the owner's landing, the owner's integration on a project with a landing branch needs some integrator to hold the lease; with nobody holding it the refusal says so (`fenced`) and names `integrator.lease.acquire`.
- **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** `checkIntegration(by, { taskId, projectId, branch })`: refuses anyone but the owner (a task credential included) and any queue of `branch` with an entry or a reserved place (`invalid_transition`, naming how many wait, how many are reserved, which task is first, and `landing.queue.list`/`.remove`).
- **The service (`workspace-ops/workspace-ops.ts`).** New optional dependency `integrationGate(by, { taskId, projectId, leaseId, fence })`: `undefined` for no landing branch, else the branch and the lease used; throws when refused. `request` asks it for an `integration` before anything is recorded or frozen and records the lease used (`lease`). The second showing, inside the quiesce right before the host is asked, asks it again with the pinned lease and requires the same answer (same branch and hold, or no branch both times): a lease released or taken by someone else, a queue that got an entry, or a landing branch named in the meantime ends the integration `refused` ("... no longer allows this integration, so nothing was written to the shared workspace"), with the host never asked. Without the dependency (the older unit rigs) nothing changes, and a lease named on an integration is still refused.
- **Composition (`api/start.ts`).** `integrationGate` reads the landing branch with the same reader as the landing's lease check; no branch: `undefined`; otherwise `IntegratorLeaseOps.checkLanding` (lease refusals keep their code and get the prefix "an integration writes the shared tree of landing branch X, so it is made under that branch's integrator lease, as a landing is: ...") and then `checkIntegration`.
- **API and chat.** The `workspace.request` summary and its `leaseId`/`fence` arguments say when an integration needs the lease and the empty queue; the chat command's one-line verb says the same (the owner's chat integration leaves the lease out, which the gate accepts). `api-v1.md` regenerated with `npm run api:docs:write`. No new operation, no worker tool, the worker prompt is unchanged.
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p10-integration.test.ts` (four storage backends, 3 tests each, with the real lease and queue services; the gate built as `startController` builds it): (1) no holder refused `fenced` with nothing recorded and no host call; an agent without a lease, with a wrong fence, and the holder itself refused; the owner with the lease left out lands the integration with the lease recorded, a repeat answered from the record, a named hold accepted and a stale one refused, a released lease refused, unreadable settings `unavailable`; with no landing branch as before (no lease recorded) and a named lease refused; without the dependency the old refusal. (2) an approved entry of another task, and the task's own entry, refuse it; after a take-out it goes ahead; a reserved place with no entry refuses it too; after the reservation is ended it goes ahead. (3) the second showing, with a second set of services on the same store playing another controller (on PostgreSQL too): while the integration is held in the quiesce, the other controller queues work, or releases the lease and another integrator takes it, or the landing branch gets named; each ends `refused` with the host never asked; then an unmoved integration goes ahead once under the new holder's lease. `api/start-p10-integration.test.ts` (composed controller): no landing branch as before; with one, the owner refused with no holder (the prefixed text), the integrator refused, the owner's integration with the live hold recorded; a reserved place refuses it until the owner takes it out through `landing.queue.remove`; after the holder releases the lease, refused again.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared by sha256): all 6 killed.** Gate never asked (13 of 13 fail); second showing's answer comparison off (4 fail); second showing skipped (4); the owner-only rule off (5); reserved places not counted (5); the composition not asking the queue (composed test fails). One mutation first survived because it was badly made (`false && a || b` leaves `b`); remade as removing the throw, it failed 4.
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`), one affected-suite run at the end: controller `landing/*`, `workspace-ops/*`, `api/start-p10*`, `api/start-workspace`, `api/start-docs*`, `chat/commands-one-line`, `chat/commands-preview`, `chat/model-interpreter`: 545 of 545; integration `h12m-workspace-host`, `h12k-composed-host` (integrations through the composed controller with no landing branch): 3 of 3. `npm run check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass. Skipped (Rob's test-load rule while Radiance benchmarks): every other controller, worker, scripts and integration file; CI is the net.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) The re-apply commit is a platform commit, not a review-gate permit commit, so under the default `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true` the landing still refuses re-applied work. (2) A hand-off at the very moment of a take-out is judged on the holder read just before the queue's write (fifth slice). (3) A remote host has no `restack` and refuses a landing `submission`. (4) Nothing commits landed or integrated files (P10c/H12o). (5) A reserved place whose work was returned holds the branch until its refreshed work is approved or it is taken out. (6) New here: the queue is shown right before the host is asked, not inside the host's write, so an entry queued in the instant between that showing and the host's write is not seen by this integration; the landing of that entry then finds the integrated files uncommitted in the shared tree and is refused until they are committed or cleared (the owner is told, as for any landing refused on an unclean tree). The same window exists for the owner's unqueued landing (queue slice). (7) The chat interpreter's longer prompt text about landings was not extended; the one-line command verb says it.

## P10 (seventh slice): the re-apply commit is a review-gate permit commit when the work it replaces was one (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. When the landing branch moves after work was approved, the integrator's host re-applies the approved change onto the new head as a new commit (card P10). Until now that commit was the platform's own and not a "permit commit" (the mark the review gate gives a commit it allowed), so under the default setting `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true` the landing refused every re-applied work: the re-apply only worked where the permit rule was switched off. Now the re-apply commit carries the permit when, and only when, everything it replaces already carried it. A re-applied work that the review gate permitted lands under the default setting; anything else is re-applied as before and still refused there.

- ASSUMPTION (what passes the permit on): the host checks, before it moves anything, that every commit between the checkout's base and head (the work being re-applied: the approved commit, or an earlier re-apply) is a permit commit for the same task (the host's own `unpermitted` test: the marks in the message and a line in the host-side permit ledger). Only then does the re-apply commit get the `NimbleNewt-Request:` (the re-apply's own request ID) and `NimbleNewt-Task:` marks and a ledger line (written before the head moves, as `commit()` does). The proof that the change is exactly the approved one (`sameChange`) is unchanged and still made at the landing. Reversible in `GitBridge.restack` (`permitted`).
- ASSUMPTION (release commits): a commit made by the H12o release operation is not a permit commit, so work committed that way is re-applied as a non-permit commit and is still refused under the default. That is the existing rule for release commits (queue slice) and is not changed here.
- ASSUMPTION (no new field): the host's `restack` answer is unchanged (no new field, so no remote or stored shape changes); the permit status is visible in the commit and the ledger. No storage is touched, so the four-backend tests do not apply to this slice.
- **Code.** `worker/src/workspace/git.ts` (`restack` takes an optional `permit: { taskId, requestId }`, returns `permitted`) and `host.ts` (passes the task and request IDs). The already-re-applied answer (`recovered`) reports whether the existing commit is permitted.
- **Tests.** `worker/src/workspace/landing-restack-permit.test.ts` (real git in temporary repositories, default policy `requirePermit: true`, real `GitBridge.commit` permit commits): (1) a permitted submission re-applied onto a moved branch carries the marks and a ledger line, passes `unpermitted`, and lands; a repeat is answered from the checkout; (2) an agent's own commit, a commit with forged marks (not in the ledger) and a commit on top of a permit commit are re-applied without marks and the landing is refused, nothing written; (3) a permit commit marked for another task does not pass on, and a branch that moves twice keeps the permit through both re-applies and lands; (4) with `requirePermit: false` an agent's own commit re-applies and lands as before.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared by sha256): all 6 killed.** Always non-permit (2 fail); the "replaced work is permitted" check dropped (2); ledger line not written (2); marks left out (2); the host not passing the permit (2); a wrong task mark (2).
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) A remote host has no `restack` and still refuses a landing `submission`. (2) An H12o release commit is still not a permit commit, so released work re-applies but cannot land under the default. (3) The `restack` answer does not say whether the commit is permitted (it is visible in the checkout's commit and ledger only). (4) A hand-off at the very moment of a take-out is judged on the holder read just before the queue's write. (5) Nothing commits landed or integrated files (P10c/H12o). (6) A reserved place whose work was returned holds the branch until its refreshed work is approved or it is taken out. (7) The queue-level (controller) test of a restacked landing under the default policy was not added: the host test goes through `LocalWorkspaces`, the same host the controller drives.

### P10 seventh slice review (Claude agent, first reviewer, 2026-11-22)

Reviewed 2cd16bcd; origin/main was db17af05 (nothing to merge); api docs unchanged after the build.

- **Checked and sound.** The permit passes on only when the permit ledger lists every replaced commit and those commits carry the marks of the same task: forged marks are not in the ledger, and another task's marks do not match. An empty change can never pass, because `sameChange` needs at least one entry. The ledger line is written before the one ref transaction moves the base and head, so a commit on the branch is always listed. A line left behind for a commit that never became the head counts for nothing: such a commit is exactly the approved change on `onto` in any case. The task and request IDs come from the controller's call, not from the agent.
- **Fixed (hardening).** `restack` asked `unpermitted` about base..HEAD as HEAD stood at that moment, while the head move compares and swaps against the `head` read earlier. A head moved away and back between the two would be judged on other commits than the ones replaced. `unpermitted` now takes an optional `range` (full commit IDs), and `restack` passes `{ base, head }`, the commits it actually replaces. Landing still checks the live base..HEAD.
- **Tests added.** (1) When the ledger line cannot be written (a read-only ledger), the re-apply fails and nothing moves: not the head, not the base, not the files. Nothing is listed, and a later re-apply lands. This test fails if the ledger write is moved after the head move. It is skipped when running as root. (2) `range` reads exactly the commits named, not the moving HEAD, and refuses IDs that are not full. (3) The "moves twice" case now uses a second task (`tsk-two`), so a re-apply that always wrote the first task's mark is caught.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared by sha256): 9 of 9 caught.** Always not permitted (3 tests fail); the replaced-work check dropped (2); marks left out (3); `range` ignored (1); the ledger check in `unpermitted` dropped (1); the task check loosened to any task (1); the host not passing the permit (3); the ledger written after the head move (1); the task mark fixed to `tsk-one` (1, caught only after the `tsk-two` change).
- **Verified** (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, the offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`): worker `landing-restack-permit`, `landing-restack`, `landing-submission`, `host`, `git`: 77 of 77. `check:deps`, `licenses:check` and `roadmap:check` pass. Under Rob's test-load rule no other suite was run; CI is the net.
- **Left as is (said plainly).** A re-apply made by an earlier build (not a permit commit) that is already on the current head is answered again as `recovered` and stays unpermitted. Under the default policy its landing is refused until the branch moves again and the work is re-applied once more.

## G04 harness on Windows: the late-label probe's grandchild is detached (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

- **Failure:** on GitHub's windows-latest (node 22 and 24) `g04-harness.test.ts` "the run is judged when the output streams close, not at the child's exit" got no label (`the child died elsewhere ( exit 1)`), while the 1 MiB and real-kill probes passed.
- **Cause:** on Windows libuv puts every process a Node process spawns (unless `detached`) into that process's own job object, created with kill-on-job-close. `probe-late` spawned its label-writing grandchild attached and then killed itself, so Windows closed the child's job and ended the grandchild before its write. POSIX has no such tie, which is why only Windows failed. Nothing was wrong in `runChild`.
- **Fix:** the grandchild is spawned with `detached: true` (`g04-child.ts`), which keeps it out of that job on Windows. On POSIX the option only gives it its own session. Its stderr is still the inherited pipe, so the parent's stream stays open until the grandchild writes and exits. The test and `runChild` are unchanged, so the test still proves the same thing.
- **Verified** (Linux, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build`): `g04-harness.test.js` 7 of 7. Mutation: built `runChild` judging at `exit` (calling `finish()` there instead of the drain timer) fails exactly this test (`the child died elsewhere ()`), then restored. Windows itself is checked by the next CI run.

## B04 (first slice): bounded baseline experiments (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-b04-s1`, on main `c9a73654`. The card is not flipped.

Plain words first. An experiment is a proposed change to how the team works ("add a checklist to the coder prompt") tried against what the team does now. The proposer says what problem it addresses, what work it touches, what it changes, the effort, the running cost, the benefit, how it will be judged and when it stops. A manager (never the proposer) then pins the yardstick once: the baseline and the evaluator (each a label, a reference and a hash), the separate evaluation cases, the baseline's own numbers, the budget and the thresholds. From then on the experiment cannot change its own yardstick. The proposer reports runs; the controller, not the proposer, decides whether the result is better, no different, worse or too thin to say. Whatever the verdict, it is kept. When the budget is used up the experiment pauses instead of spending on.

- ASSUMPTION (the slice): the first slice of B04 is the experiment record, its pinned criteria, runs, budget, verdict and savings counting, the state API, the owner's chat view and decisions. It makes no model call and spends nothing: it records what a run reported. Reversible: nothing else reads experiments.
- ASSUMPTION (disposable environment, A08): the controller does not launch or verify an environment. A run must name one (`environment.ref`) and state `disposable: true`; a run that does not is refused. Making the controller start the disposable environment through A08's manifests, and checking the reference against them, is a later slice (below).
- ASSUMPTION (who judges): the owner, or a manager of the project's meetings (`meeting.manage`) who is not the proposer, pins, raises the budget, concludes. An agent proposes with `meeting.agenda` or `meeting.manage`. Runs are reported by the proposer or by a judge, so a run of an owner-proposed experiment is reported by the owner or a manager. The proposer reads its own experiment; other agents do not.
- ASSUMPTION (verdict rule): per pinned metric the candidate's mean over its runs is compared with the pinned baseline number, lower being better except adoption. `worse` if any metric is worse by more than `maxRegressionPct` (default 0) or any case the baseline passes failed in any run; `improved` if no such regression and some metric is better by at least `minImprovementPct` (and above 0); else `no-change`; `inconclusive` when there are fewer runs than the pinned `minRuns` (default 1). A zero baseline moves by 100 percent either way. These are the first rule; owners can tune the thresholds per experiment.
- ASSUMPTION (units): cost and metrics are plain non-negative numbers in whatever unit the proposer and the pinning manager agreed; the controller converts nothing and does not connect them to B01's accounting.
- ASSUMPTION (savings counted once): an improvement's saving on a lower-is-better metric (baseline minus candidate) is claimed per (metric, affected work label) in the project's experiment list; a later improvement on the same pair is saved with `counted: false` and the ID of the first. Adoption is a gain, not a saving. The label is the proposer's `affectedKey` (lowercased), so a rewording of it counts as another piece of work; a manager checks it when pinning.
- ASSUMPTION (paused): a run that reaches the pinned runs or cost is kept and the experiment becomes `paused` (reason budget). Another run is refused with `unavailable` and changes nothing; the owner or another manager raises the budget (only upwards, with a reason; the seal is renewed in the same write and the raise is listed) or concludes it, and the runs it got are judged. A paused experiment is never woken by anything.

**Done:**
- `packages/controller/src/experiments/` (`ExperimentService`, `judge`, `betterPct`, `sealOf`). Record kinds `experiment` (ID prefix `exp`, added to `derivedId`) and `experiment-index` (one per project: the IDs, oldest first, at most 300, and the savings claims). Nothing is ever deleted; withdrawn and concluded experiments stay listed.
- **Statuses.** `proposed` -> `running` (pinned) -> `paused` (budget) -> `running` (budget raised); `running` or `paused` -> `concluded`; `proposed` -> `withdrawn`.
- **The candidate cannot alter its criteria or authority.** The proposer, a manager who proposed it, a reader and another project's manager are refused when pinning, raising the budget or concluding. Criteria are pinned once. The controller seals them (SHA-256 of the canonical criteria); the seal is checked on every run and at the end, and criteria changed in storage are refused as `integrity`. A run must report exactly the pinned metrics and exactly the pinned cases, so the candidate cannot add, drop or swap either. Text fields refuse credential-shaped content.
- **Negative result saved.** `worse`, `no-change` and `inconclusive` results are stored with the runs, the mean metrics, the change per metric, the failed cases, the finding and who concluded, and are listed beside improvements.
- **Budget exhaustion** pauses, as above; concurrent runs from two controllers both keep their run, and two concluders conclude once.
- **State API:** `experiment.propose`, `experiment.pin`, `experiment.run`, `experiment.budget`, `experiment.conclude`, `experiment.withdraw`, `experiment.get`, `experiment.list`; `api-v1.md` regenerated. Status kind `experiments` (`experimentStatus` keeps one) with a line per experiment (status, change, stop condition, runs and cost against the budget, verdict with each metric's change, savings and whether they were counted).
- **Owner by chat, in any words:** the `experiments` view; `experiment.propose`, `experiment.pin`, `experiment.conclude` and `experiment.withdraw` apply at once (nothing is spent or launched by them); `experiment.budget` (more spending later) is always a proposal the owner confirms. The revision is filled in. One interpreter prompt paragraph with free-word examples. Runs are not a chat command: the proposing agent reports them. As for every chat command, values (title, texts, digests, IDs) must come from the owner's own message.
- **Tests:** `experiments/experiments.test.ts` (7 tests on each of the four backends plus one arithmetic test: 33 in all), `chat/experiments-chat.test.ts` (the prompt, and the whole owner conversation on each backend), `api/start-experiments.test.ts` (the composed controller: propose, refused self-pin, pin, a pausing run, status view, restart and a replayed run, conclude).

**NOT done (next slices):**
- The controller does not launch a disposable environment or check the named one against A08's manifests; no worker runs the candidate. A run's numbers are what the proposer or a judge reports (a judge can also report them), not measured by the controller.
- Not linked to B01: a run's cost is not charged to the PC budget, no capacity is reserved and the budget's units are not tied to the P/PC accounting. The pinned budget is the experiment's own bound.
- The baseline, evaluator and cases are references and hashes: the controller does not fetch or run them or check a hash against content.
- The proposer is not told the outcome (B03 does this for lessons); no lesson is created or moved by a result; no automatic experiment from a lesson's applicability.
- Metrics are reported numbers; time to accepted result, rework and cost per success are not derived from task and review records, and adoption and maintenance are not measured over time (B05 monitors).
- A savings claim is not released when an experiment is later found wrong; there is no way to re-conclude.
- Retention has no rule for `experiment` and `experiment-index` (nothing is deleted); a project keeps at most 300.
- Linux only has been run here; nothing depends on the platform (no paths, timers or signals; the clock is the record's ISO time).
- **Mutation checks** (built `dist/experiments/experiments.js`, each alone against `experiments.test`, restored byte-identical, SHA-256 checked): the proposer allowed to judge; the seal not checked on a run; a non-disposable environment accepted; the budget pause off by one; a paused experiment taking a run; a baseline-passing case that failed ignored; a saving counted twice; the budget allowed to be lowered; adoption treated as lower-is-better; an extra or missing case accepted; the verdict never `worse`. All 11 failed named tests (4 failures each, one per backend; 13 for the adoption direction).
- **Runs** (Linux, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, after `npx tsc --build --force`): `experiments/experiments.test` 33 of 33; `chat/experiments-chat.test` 5 of 5; `api/start-experiments.test` 1 of 1; neighbours `chat/lessons-chat.test`, `api/start-lessons.test`, `chat/model-interpreter.test`, `api/api.test`, `scripts/d02-docs.test.mjs`: 144 of 145 first (the `status.ask` summary had to name the new `experiments` kind: fixed), then `api.test`, `d02-docs` and the chat test 90 of 90. Not run, by the owner's test-load rule (CI is the net): every other test file. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; `api-v1.md` regenerated after the build.

## G04 slice 7: a generation left streaming by a dead controller no longer refuses its complete call (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-g04-s7`, on main `db17af05`. One production change (`controller/src/generation/generation.ts`) plus tests. Card status is not changed.

Plain words first. Slice 6 found that when the controller died after the worker had the whole model reply but before the controller marked that reply finished, nothing ever finished it: after the restart the same tool call was refused as "still streaming", nothing was pushed and the model had to try again. Now each generation records which primary epoch (which controller process) began it. When a call is admitted and its generation is still `streaming` under an OLDER epoch, its controller is gone and no stream can end it; the call is admitted if its arguments were recorded complete, and the generation is ended (`finished`, partial calls `dropped`) in the same commit. The two read-first boundaries (76 and 77, "tool: called by the model" and "before generation.complete") now end exactly like the uncrashed run: pushed once, model told so. All 36 kills per engine now have the same result.

- **ASSUMPTION (which leftover).** The pinned gap of slice 6 (the stuck `streaming` generation, which slice 5's item (3) first found) is the one leftover that is offline-doable and complete in one slice. Items (4) to (7) of slice 5 change the worker's or the bridge's behaviour and stay open.
- **Done.** `RunBody.epoch` (optional) is set from the runner at `begin`. `#admitEffect` treats `streaming` with `epoch < current epoch` as ended: it admits a `complete` (or `held`) call, drops partial calls, finishes the run, all in the one commit that already checks the gate and hold. Hold, pause, decision, supersession, interruption and wrong-revision checks run first and are unchanged (a held task still refuses). A same-epoch streaming generation is still refused (its stream may be about to end; the bridge's 3 s wait still applies). A late `complete` or piece from the old relay is refused as `stale` once the run is finished. The harness expectation `expectedResult` now answers the clean result at every boundary in both orders; `NOT_RUN_RESULT` is removed.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a call that was recorded `complete` in a generation whose controller died is safe to run: the worker only runs a tool after it has read the whole reply, and a reply that breaks off is only discarded by `complete(failed)`, which cannot happen once the controller is gone. A reply broken off with a complete call already recorded, then a worker that ran that call, is not possible, since Pi stores a reply before running its tools.
- **ASSUMPTION:** records begun before this field (no `epoch`) keep the old refusal ("still streaming"); no migration rewrites them. Reversible: treat a missing epoch as old.
- **Tests.** `generation/generation.test.ts`, four backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL), two new tests: the older-epoch stream admits its complete call, drops the partial one, finishes in the same commit, answers a repeat of the same command with the same effect, refuses another ask as admitted, refuses the old relay's late end and piece as stale, refuses a partial call as incomplete leaving the run untouched, still refuses under the same epoch, and still refuses under a hold; a streaming record with no epoch is refused. The six `g04-stream-*` sweeps now expect the clean result at all 18 boundaries.
- **Mutation checks** (built `generation.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; each failed tests): the older-epoch test always true (12 failures); the test "not equal" so a missing epoch counts as gone (4); never gone (5); the run not ended (4); partial calls not dropped (4); the epoch not recorded at begin (5); older-or-equal instead of older (8).
- **NOT done.** Slice 5's items (4) to (7) (see slice 5/6 lists). A generation left streaming whose controller died and whose model never calls a tool stays `streaming` until the next generation supersedes it (nothing needs it). Whether `lifecycle/pause.ts` treats such a stuck `streaming` generation as running is not checked. Windows and macOS were not run (Linux only); nothing depends on the platform (no paths, timers or signals beyond the shared harness's).

### G04 slice 7 review (Claude agent, clean-context reviewer, 2026-11-22)

Reviewed 8d70d937; merged origin/main c9a73654 (one conflict in these notes, both sides kept).

- **Safety of the older-epoch rule: sound.** Every storage write is refused unless it carries the current primary epoch exactly (`stale_epoch`, all four backends' conformance), and a process takes its epoch once at start (`api/start.ts`). So a generation under an older epoch can never be added to or ended by the controller that began it, even if that process is still alive next to a new primary on PostgreSQL. Admission and the finish are one commit with the run's revision check, so two requests cannot both admit (the second sees `admitted`, a repeat of the same command is answered from its record). Ordering does not use clocks, only the stored epoch number. Hold, pause, decision, supersession and interruption are checked before the epoch rule and are unchanged; a hold makes `#blocked` refuse first, so the `held` branch of `complete` is not needed here.
- **Fixed: a paused task stayed "pausing" for good.** `lifecycle/pause.ts` `#streaming` counted a generation a dead controller left `streaming` as running, so `observe paused` was refused; with the pause also refusing the call's admission and a new generation, nothing could end it. ## Q01b: a code submission is written only while the attempt it was checked against is still current (Claude agent, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-q01b-s3`. ASSUMPTION: Q01b's own acceptance was already met and the bridge tool was built (previous slice); the one remaining item that needs no local model and no owner decision is the known limit written under the 2026-11-16 re-check ("the attempt check reads the assignment outside the commit transaction, with no revision guard"). Evidence-through-the-bridge and a `submission.get` bridge tool stay out: the prompt head has 2 characters of room (previous slice). The owner question on project-scoped roles (`rolesOfPrincipalIn`) is a policy choice and is untouched.

**What is built.** The attempt check reads the task's assignment and its active attempt, then the submission is written a moment later. If the attempt ended, or the task moved to another agent, in that gap, the record used to be written under an attempt that was no longer current. Now the attempt port (`AttemptOf`) may return `guards`: the records it read and the revision of each. `attemptOfAssignments` returns the assignment and the attempt. `SubmissionService.record` adds one `check` change per guard to the same write, so the write commits only if each is still at the revision read. When it does not, the answer is `forbidden` ("the task's attempt changed while this submission was being recorded, so it was not recorded; check the task and send it again if it is still yours"), not the old, wrong `command_conflict` ("command ID used by something else"). Nothing is recorded. Sent again, the ordinary owner check decides (a task that moved is refused as "not the owner of the current attempt"; an agent whose attempt was merely replaced by a new one of its own is recorded under the new attempt). A repeat of an already recorded submission is unchanged: the runner answers with the first record before the check or the guards are reached. A hand-made port with no `guards` behaves as before.

**Tests** (`submissions/submissions-q01b-guard.test.ts`, 7 cases x 4 backends = 28, real `AssignmentService`, no fake records): no gap records and names the attempt; the attempt finishes in the gap; the task is transferred in the gap (then refused by the owner check on a resend); a repeat after the attempt succeeded answers with the first record; a port with no guards; a refused write followed by the next attempt's submission recorded; the port's guards are exactly the assignment and the attempt at their revisions, and a stale revision on either alone refuses. Mutations of the built file (each alone, restored): checks not added to the write; the port's guards not taken; guard comparison inverted; refusal not returned (each fails 12 to 16 of 28); assignment guard dropped from the port (4 fail); attempt guard dropped (4); the attempt guard carrying the assignment's revision (16); only the first guard checked (4).

**Not done.** The gap between reading the task and the role check is not guarded (those are reads of the task, not of an attempt). A legitimate change to the assignment record in the gap (for example a transfer back to the same agent) also refuses once; the agent sends again. The other not-done items of the Q01b sections above are unchanged (evidence and `submission.get` through the bridge, `KIND_ROLES` and project-scoped roles as owner questions, checking base/tree/patch-id against the repository (P08), evidence against real check runs (P09), `reviewAssignments` wiring).

## H12o (permit slice): a reviewer-approved submission's commit is a review-gate permit commit (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card H12o commits an approved submission in the task's own checkout. Until now that commit was the platform's own and never a "permit commit" (the mark the review gate gives a commit it allowed), so under the default setting `workspace.landing.requirePermit=true` the landing refused it. That was the main thing still keeping H12o from reaching P10's landing: reviewed work could be committed but not landed unless the owner switched the permit rule off. Now, when a reviewer other than the author approved the submission, the release makes its commit a permit commit and a landing under the default accepts it. Everything else is as before. Card H12o stays planned (see "Not done").

- ASSUMPTION (the slice chosen): of the open H12o / H12m / P10 items, "a release commit is not a permit commit so it cannot land under requirePermit=true" was taken, because it is the one that blocks reviewed work from landing, it needs no new storage shape and no real model, and the P10 seventh slice (the re-apply carries the permit on) already built the second half of the chain. Left: see "Not done".
- ASSUMPTION (what counts as the review gate): a submission approved by a `review` of a principal other than its author (the service refuses a self-review when it is recorded, and the newest review decides) is the review gate's decision for this purpose. The approval of one-agent projects (`review_disabled_single_agent`: no reviewer judged the work) is never a permit: that commit stays the platform's own and is landed only where the owner set `requirePermit=false`, as before. Reversible in one line, `reviewerApproved` in `workspace-ops.ts`.
- ASSUMPTION (the human gate): A06's permit is owner-only by default, and this slice lets an agent reviewer's approval stand for it only for the one commit that is exactly the approved tree on the approved base (the host's existing checks). The owner's landing rules (lease, queue, protected paths, required checks P09, the review check on the patch ID) are unchanged and still apply at the landing, so an approval alone never lands anything.
- **How it works.** The controller marks the host call `permit: true` only for a `release` of a submission whose recorded approval is a reviewer's (`WorkspaceCall.permit`, `HostWorkspaceCall.permit`). The host (`host.ts`) refuses `permit` on anything but a release of a submission (and `false` or any other value) before touching the checkout. `GitBridge.release` with `permit` adds the `NimbleNewt-Request:` trailer (the release's own request ID) beside the existing `NimbleNewt-Task:`, writes a line in the host-side permit ledger BEFORE the head moves (as `commit()` and the P10 re-apply do), so a commit on the branch is always listed and a line left behind for a commit that never became the head counts for nothing. The agent supplies none of it: the marks are text anybody can type, and `unpermitted` still requires the ledger line. A release asked again finds the one commit (unchanged) and now says whether it is a permit commit (`detail.permitted`); a commit made earlier without the permit is NOT upgraded (ASSUMPTION: rewriting history to add a mark is the wrong direction; it stays refused under the default and is landed under `requirePermit=false`). `detail.permitRequiredToLand` is false for a permit commit. The controller's `submission-commit` record keeps `permitted: true` only when the host said so (a host that made a plain commit is never recorded as having made a permit one).
- **With P10.** A permit commit that the landing branch moved past is re-applied by the integrator as a permit commit (seventh slice) and lands under the default (tested end to end on a real repository).
- **No storage shape changes** beyond one optional field on the `submission-commit` record (absent on older records), so no migration.
- **Tests.** `worker/src/workspace/release-permit.test.ts` (6, real git in temporary repositories, default policy `requirePermit: true`): marks, ledger line, `unpermitted` empty and landing succeeds; no flag is the platform's commit and the landing refuses it (unchanged); release permit then the landing branch moves, re-apply, landing succeeds; a repeat finds the one commit and reports permitted (and a commit made earlier without the permit is not upgraded); the permit refused on a plain release, an integration, a refresh, a landing, `false`, and `GitBridge.release` without a submission, and a changed tree refuses with nothing listed; the same commit is unpermitted for another task. `controller/src/workspace-ops/workspace-ops-h12o-permit.test.ts` (2 new tests x 4 storage backends, the existing H12o rig): a reviewer's approval asks for the permit and the record keeps the host's confirmation, a repeat is answered from the record, the one-agent approval and a plain release never ask; a host that answers with a plain commit is recorded as not permitted. `integration/src/h12o-submission-commit.test.ts` (extended): through `startController`, the real local worker over real git, the reviewer's approval gives marks, a permit-ledger line, `unpermitted` empty and `permitted` on the record, also for the commit found again after a lost answer.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, tests run, restored): all 9 killed.** Permit ledger line not written (3 fail); marks left out (3); the host not passing the permit to git (3); the host accepting `permit` on any operation (1); the recovered answer always `permitted` (1); the one-agent approval counted as a reviewer's (4); the controller never asking for the permit (8); the record claiming a permit the host did not confirm (8); the answer's `permitRequiredToLand` ignoring the permit (2).
