## Q04 (second slice): a repair in a rejected or replaced version is not found fixed (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card Q04 tracks defects and the repairs that answer them. Until now a repair could be found `fixed` after the version that carried it had been rejected, or had been replaced by a newer version, so the defect could close on work that was no longer the current attempt. Now such a repair cannot be found fixed. The responsible agent (or the owner) names a newer version as the repair in its place; nothing was checked, so no repair and review cycle is counted. A repair in such a version can still be found `not-fixed` (that counts one cycle, as before). Card Q04 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Slice chosen, and why.** Of Q04's open items this one was taken because it is a stated "second review follow-up" gap, needs no new record shape and no model, and keeps the cycle rules the card's acceptance depends on honest. The other items (what waits for QA in chat, withdrawal of a defect, gating a task's `done` on open defects) are larger or need product choices.
- **Built.** `DefectService.review`: a `fixed` verdict is refused (`invalid_transition`, naming the version's state) when the repair's version is `rejected` or `superseded`. `DefectService.repair`: a defect in `repair-submitted` whose repair version is `rejected` or `superseded` accepts a repair naming a newer submitted version (the floor rule still applies: it must be newer than the defect's and than the last repair); a repair in a live version still holds the defect (a second repair is refused as before). No API shape changed, so `api-v1.md` is unchanged.
- **Tests.** `submissions/defects-dead-repair.test.ts` (four storage backends): a rejected repair version cannot be found fixed and nothing is recorded; a newer repair replaces it with cycles at 0 and then resolves; a replaced (superseded) version cannot be found fixed and a newer repair resolves; a dead version can still be found not-fixed (one cycle); a live repair still blocks a second repair. Seven mutations each fail all four backends' tests: empty dead set, only `superseded`, only `rejected`, verdict condition inverted, repair allowed on any `repair-submitted`, replacement never allowed, every check counted as a cycle.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a version rejected for any reason, not only for this finding, counts as dead for a repair (the safer reading: the repair must be in work that still stands). Reversible by removing `rejected` from `DEAD_VERSION`. **ASSUMPTION:** a `not-fixed` check of a dead version stays allowed and counts a cycle (the checker's finding is still true of that version); a replacement repair does not count one.
- **Not done (said plainly).** Everything else in Q04's earlier "Not done" list stands: the P10 conflict return is counted in the landing queue's record, not as a defect record; escalation of disagreements other than a defect's cycles; periodic and incident-triggered reviews; chat answers for "what waits for QA" and team-wide risks; the link to Q02 QA evidence; withdrawal or editing of a defect; gating a task's `done` or a deliverable's acceptance on open defects; the needs-you list, hand-off packages, retention and the web view. A newer version that appears while a repair is still live does not move the repair (only a dead repair version can be replaced).
- **Review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22).** origin/main unmoved (464669e7); clean `npx tsc --build --force`, `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok. Checked, no change needed: only the responsible agent or the owner names a replacement and only the owner, a reviewer, qa or director agent that did none of the version's work checks one (unchanged rules apply to the new path); `rejected` and `superseded` are final states of a version, so the replacement's read of the old repair version needs no revision check, and the defect's own revision check makes two replacements (or a replacement and a check) on two controllers land one at a time; a replacement keeps the cycles counted, an escalated defect is never replaced (it waits for the owner), and every failed check of a dead version still counts toward the limit, so the replacement cannot reset or avoid the cycle limit; the version cap (100) bounds replacements. Fixed: (1) a check carries no version, and the repair can now change while the defect stays `repair-submitted`, so a check written for one repair could land on its replacement: chat already pins the defect's revision, and the `defect.review` summary now tells callers to send `expectedRevision` (test: a check with the revision read before the replacement is refused `stale_revision` and nothing is recorded); (2) the `defect.repair` and `defect.review` summaries (and `api-v1.md`) and the chat interpreter's prompt did not describe the new behaviour: they now do. Tests added (all four backends): the replacement refused for a non-responsible agent and allowed for the owner; a repeat of a replacement answered from the record; the one check names the version it judged; cycles kept across a replacement; two replacements at once, exactly one lands; failed checks of dead versions escalate at the limit and the escalated defect cannot be repaired. Mutations of built files (each alone, restored and checked by SHA-256; all caught): replacement resets cycles, live repair replaceable, no replacement, dead `fixed` allowed, dead `not-fixed` refused, only `rejected` dead, escalated defect replaceable, floor ignoring the last repair, access checked only on `open`. Runs (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, sandbox required, offline guard): `defects-dead-repair`, `defects`, `start-defects`, `start-defects-same-message`, `model-interpreter`: 24 pass, 0 fail.
- **Second review (Claude agent, clean-context second reviewer, 2026-11-22).** Merged origin/main caa479e3 (notes conflict only, both sides kept). Found: `defect.review` named no version, so a `fixed` check written for repair version N could resolve the defect on its replacement N+1, which nobody examined, whenever the caller left out `expectedRevision` (chat was already safe: its proposal pins the defect's revision). Fixed, backwards compatible: `defect.review` takes an optional `version` (the repair version checked); a named version that is no longer the repair is refused (`stale_revision`) after the access check, and is part of the repeat payload. ## P10 (eighth slice): a reserved place whose work is away holds the branch only for a bound (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. When a task's author kept refreshing stale work, the task got a reserved place in the landing queue (third slice). If that task's work was then returned to its author, or its approval was taken back, the reserved place stayed first with nothing approved in it, and every other landing waited behind it until a person took it out. Now there is a bound: when a reserved place has had no approved submission for twelve hours and another landing waits behind it, the controller ends the reservation itself. The landing that was waiting goes on in the same call. The task's holder (while an active agent), the director and the owner are told once; the task's work is not removed, and when its refreshed work is approved it takes its turn at the back like any new work. No submission waits forever behind a place nobody works on. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** Of the open items (5 the reserved place held until approval or take-out, 2 the hand-off racing a take-out, 6 the integration queue window) this one: it is the only one that can leave work waiting without end, it needs no change to the host or the lease, and it is fully testable offline. Items 2 and 6 are bounded windows of an instant that end by themselves.
- **Queue (`landing/landing-queue.ts`).** `front` gets `idleSince`: since when the first place has had NO approved entry (set when a reserved place with no entry becomes or stays first, kept across writes, dropped as soon as an entry is first). `releaseIdle({projectId, branch, taskId, since, olderThanMs})` is one recorded command (`landing.queue.release`) that judges inside its own write, on the stored record: the task still holds the reservation, is still the first place with that `front.since`, has no entry, and has been idle (from `idleSince`; a record without it is never ended on that call, see the reviews below) for at least the bound by the controller's clock. It answers the reservation ended, or nothing (not first, approved work came back, taken out, not yet due, a repeat or the loser of two simultaneous calls). So a take-out, a landing or approved work arriving at the same moment wins, and two calls end it once.
- **Door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** `LANDING_RESERVATION_RELEASE_MS` (12 h) and the option `releaseMs`. `checkLanding`, when the first place is a reserved place with no entry that is not the asking task's own, asks for the release; if the place was ended (by this call, or by another call that got there first) the landing is judged again on the queue as it is then, in the same call. The notices are best effort after the write (the place is ended even if nobody could be told): the holder gets an inbox notice (`tell`, new optional `purpose`), the director and owner a `released` escalation (a `notice`, never a `needs-you`, since nothing is waiting on them). `start.ts` words the `released` notice.

- **ASSUMPTION (trigger).** The check runs when a landing is refused behind the place (like the four-hour notice), not on a timer: a queue nobody tries to land from does not change by itself. A waiting submission's next landing attempt is what ends the wait.
- **ASSUMPTION (the task's own landing).** The reserved task asking to land is not a release; it is refused as before and keeps its place.

## P10 (ninth slice): a take-out is judged on the task's holder inside the queue's own write (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. When the owner hands a task to another agent, the new agent answers for the task's queued work and the old one no longer does (fifth slice). That rule was checked on the holder as read just before the queue was written. If the owner handed the task over at the very same moment the old holder took the work out, the take-out could still go through on the old holder. Now the holder is read inside the queue's own write, and that commit carries a revision check of the assignment record. A hand-off committed in between changes that record, so the take-out is built again and judged on the new holder (the old holder is refused and the entry stays); a hand-off after the commit finds the entry gone. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** Of the open P10 items (a remote host's `restack`/`submission`, a permit commit for H12o, the `integration` queue showing inside the host's write, committing landed files, this hand-off race), this is the smallest that is complete offline: it touches no host or git code, needs no new stored field, and it is the one that could leave work wrongly gone or wrongly kept (a queued submission pulled by an agent that no longer answers for it). The `integration` item needs a host-side lock and the others need host or protocol changes.
- **The write (`landing/landing-queue.ts`, `remove`).** New optional `holder` (`RemoveHolderGuard`: the assignment record's reference and an `allowed(entry, body)` judgment, which may be async). Inside the build, after the entry is found, the record is read and judged; the commit then carries a `check` of that record at the revision read (on PostgreSQL a `FOR SHARE` row lock inside the transaction, so a hand-off's update waits and then finds the entry gone, or committed first and fails the check; SQLite and the reference store apply one commit at a time). A lost race is built again by the existing retry (at most 40). A task with no assignment record yet is not guarded (see the assumption). The reserved-place-only branch (ending a reservation) is only for callers with no own-agent rule, so it is unchanged.
- **The door (`landing/queue-ops.ts`).** New option `holderRecord` (`refOf(taskId)`, `ownerOf(body)`). With it, a take-out by the task's own agent (not owner, integrator or director) is judged in that write: a task credential of another task is refused; the owner of an `assigned` record decides by `isAgentOwner`; with nobody holding it, the entry's author decides; a body `ownerOf` cannot read refuses. Without `holderRecord` the earlier behaviour (read just before the write through `holderOf`) is kept. `api/start.ts` composes it from the assignment record (`assignmentIdOf`).
- **Tests.** `landing/landing-queue-holder-race.test.ts` (four backends, 5 tests each after the second review, real assignment service, no pauses: the judgment itself performs the hand-off between its read and the commit): the old holder judged on a stale record is refused after the commit is built again and the entry stays (judged twice, the record changed only by the hand-off); a new holder judged before the hand-off is refused without any write, and once it holds the task it takes the work out and the owner stays unchanged; the door's rules on the record (old holder refused, new holder allowed, other task's credential refused, never-assigned task goes to the author, unreadable body refuses, owner unaffected); a real take-out and hand-off sent together (six rounds) always end consistent. The existing `landing-queue-handoff` (12) and composed `api/start-p10-handoff` tests run through the new path.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared): 8 killed, none survived.** Write-back (now the check) dropped (8 fail); judgment skipped (12); record body ignored (8); unreadable body allowing (4); task-credential scope ignored (4); author fallback always allowing (4); a stale/guessed holder instead of the record (4); the composition naming the wrong record (composed test fails).
- **Review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22): a check, not a write-back.** The first version wrote the assignment record back unchanged, which raised its revision. Other writes are guarded on that revision: a code submission's attempt check (card Q01b) commits a `check` of the assignment revision it read and is refused `forbidden` ("the task's attempt changed") when it moved, and the inbox's attempt admission and a hand-off do the same. So an agent taking its old entry out while its new submission was being recorded could have its submission refused. The take-out now carries a `check` instead: the same exclusivity against a hand-off, and the revision stays as it is. The test now asserts the revision is unchanged after a take-out and that a hand-off prepared on the earlier revision still applies. Review mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored and compared by SHA-256): 8 killed, none survived (check dropped, check turned back into a write-back, judgment skipped, unreadable body allowed, author fallback always allowing, task-credential scope ignored, guarded path off, composition naming the task record). Runs (Linux, four backends): `landing-queue-holder-race` + `landing-queue-handoff` + `landing-queue-release` + `api/start-p10-handoff` + `submissions-q01b-guard` 117/117; `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok; API docs unchanged.
- ASSUMPTION (never-assigned task): with no assignment record there is nothing to guard, so a first assignment at that very moment is still judged by the author rule on the earlier read. A write-back cannot create the record without inventing its body.
- ASSUMPTION (add): only the take-out is made atomic. A wrongly added entry is visible and takeable out by the new holder or the owner, and it carries the approval already checked; a wrongly taken-out entry is the harm the hand-off rule exists for, so the take-out was the one fixed.
- **Second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22).** Confirmed how each backend applies the `check`: the reference store and SQLite (also through its worker thread) validate every change before writing, one commit at a time (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`); PostgreSQL at read committed takes `SELECT ... FOR SHARE` on the assignment row in key order with the queue's own rows, so a concurrent hand-off either waits for the take-out to commit (and is then not refused, since the revision did not move) or commits first, after which the locked read returns the new revision and the take-out loses, is built again (at most 40 times, then `unavailable`) and is judged on the new holder. A replay is answered from the recorded result before anything is judged. Other readers of the assignment revision (the Q01b attempt check, inbox admission, attempt end, hand-off) are unaffected because the revision never moves; heartbeats write the separate activity record. Own mutation checks on built files (8, each alone, restored): 6 killed at first, 1 equivalent (`ownerOf` ignoring `state`: a released assignment has no `owner`), 1 surviving: the holder guard not stopping the reservation-only path, so the task's own agent could end a reserved place with no entry (only the owner, integrators and directors may). The code was right; the gap was in the tests (the composed reservation test removes a reserved task that still has its entry). Added a four-backend test (holder and author refused, the reservation stays, the owner ends it), and the concurrent test now requires the hand-off to apply in every round (a take-out never refuses it). Both mutants now fail 4 and 5 tests.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) The `add` is still judged on the holder read before its write. (2) A first assignment at the moment of a take-out is not guarded. (3) A remote host has no `restack` and still refuses a landing `submission`. (4) An H12o release commit is still not a permit commit. (5) The `integration` operation's queue showing is still not inside the host's write. (6) Nothing commits landed or integrated files (P10c/H12o). (7) The idle-release bound is still a controller constant checked only on a refused landing.

## P10 (eleventh slice): the stuck-place bounds act on the controller's regular rounds, not only when a landing is asked for (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Two bounds keep a stuck first place in a landing queue from blocking approved work: a reserved place with no approved submission is ended after twelve hours, and the director is told when a first place has held the branch four hours. Until now both were looked at only when somebody asked to land the work waiting behind the place. If nobody did, a place nobody worked on stayed, and so did the notice. Now the controller's regular round (the dispatcher's `landing.queue.bounds`) looks at every project's landing-branch queue that has approved work of another task waiting behind its first place, and does what a landing asked for behind it did: ends an idle reserved place past its bound, or tells the director once about a first place past the hold bound. It lands nothing, queues nothing and removes no approved submission; the place's own task keeps its work and takes its turn at the back when it is approved again. With nothing waiting behind the place, nothing is ended or told (as before). The owner's view (`landing_queue`, `landing.queue.list`) now says this instead of "never on a clock". Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** Of the open items (a remote host's `restack` / landing `submission`, the `integration` queue showing inside the host's write, the `add` race on a first assignment, committing landed files, a timer for the bounds, a release bound for an approved first place) this one needs no host or protocol change, no new stored field and no product decision beyond an ASSUMPTION, and it uses the dispatcher's existing sweep list. It does not change what lands: the same write, the same notices and the same conditions as a refused landing, only without waiting for one. The `add` race on a first assignment cannot be fixed soundly (no assignment record to check a revision of, ninth slice); a bound that removes an APPROVED first place would change what lands without the owner's say, so it was left out; remote host work needs a worker protocol change.

One queue's failure does not stop the others; the call never throws for a queue. A record from before the idle time existed gets its count started and nothing ended. `api/start.ts`: sweep `landing.queue.bounds` in the dispatcher's sweep list, named in the maintenance barrier's participant `handoff-and-resume-sweeps`, so a restore holds it like the others. No new stored field; a queue record is read, never created, by a read.
- **Wording changed** (status line, `status.ask` summary, `landing.queue.list` description, interpreter prompt, `api-v1.md` regenerated): the bounds are checked on the controller's regular rounds and when a landing is asked for behind the place, only while approved work waits behind it. ## P09 third slice: the `qa` required check is collected at landing (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. A project whose required checks include `qa` could land nothing: the landing gate never looked at QA evidence and always answered "not run". Now the gate reads the QA gate (card Q02) of the code submission the landing lands. The landing goes ahead on that check only when independent QA evidence (an owner, qa or reviewer agent that did not submit the work, never the author's own self-check) passed for that submission, and that evidence still counts for the tree being landed: when the work was refreshed onto a newer base the evidence carries over only if the patch is unchanged, by the same host-computed patch ID rule the `review` check uses. Card P09 stays planned.

- **Chosen item and why.** Of P09's Not done list, item 1 (`qa`, `docs`, `director` never collected) is the one that needs no new storage index and no host or protocol change: the QA service already answers a per-submission gate. `docs` and `director` stay as they were (see Not done).
- **What it does** (`landing/landing-gate.ts`, `#qa`; `api/start.ts` composes `qaGate` reading `QaEvidenceService.gate` as the controller). No submission named: not run. No QA gate wired (a unit rig): not run, as before. The gate is read AFTER the host's run (evidence can be invalidated while the tests ran), together with the submission, and must be for this task and the submission's own tree. A failed gate is `fail` with its reasons (`check_failed`, `stale_evidence`, ...), except that "no evidence at all" is `not_run`; both count as failed and go back to the author as before. A passed gate then needs the host's patch ID of the submission's base and tree to equal the submission's claim and the landed change's patch. The host is now asked for that patch ID when `qa` OR `review` is required.
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p09-qa.test.ts` (4 backends x 4: real QA evidence and gate services, real landing gate; none, self-check only, failed, blocked, not-run each refuse and tell the author, a newer independent pass lands; evidence turned to failed while the host runs refuses; carry-over, a different patch, a wrong claimed patch and an unreadable patch; qa beside review). `landing/landing-gate.test.ts` (+2: fake QA gate paths, no gate wired). Mutation checks (each failed tests, then restored): failed treated as pass, no-evidence treated as pass, landed-patch comparison removed, claimed-patch comparison removed, host not asked for the patch ID when only qa is required, gate tree not bound to the submission, missing gate wiring passing.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) `docs` and `director` are still never collected (they need document and sign-off submissions read against the landed patch). (2) The author's claimed evidence is still not compared with the gate's own results. (3) Remote hosts still have no `landingChecks`, so on a remote host a gated landing is refused. (4) The `qa` check needs a named (or queued) code submission; an owner landing with an empty queue names none, so a project requiring `qa` refuses that landing, as for `review`.
- ASSUMPTION (what counts): the QA gate's own verdict (independent evidence only, required names from the contract or the evidence) is the meaning of "qa passed"; the landing adds only the tree/patch binding. Reversible: take `qaGate` out of the composition and `qa` is not run again.
- ASSUMPTION (not run versus fail): a gate with nothing but `no_evidence` is `not_run` (nobody has checked it yet), any other failed gate is `fail`; both refuse.

## H12n (second slice): the staged files are checked against the landing branch after the staging (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card H12n ends an agent's work with `work.end`. When the agent submits, the controller checks that nothing it changed was also changed on the landing branch, and checks again after the agent's calls settle. A process still running in the agent's sandbox could still add a file in the short time between that last check and the staging, so a file the check never saw could be submitted. Now the controller reads the landing branch once more right after the staging and judges the files actually staged: an overlap, or a read that cannot be made, ends the attempt plainly with the typed reason `submit_refused` and a blocker, and nothing is recorded. Card H12n stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Built.** `stagedSubmit` takes an optional `landing` port and, after the staging and the staged-base check, runs `overlapOf` with the staged files as the agent's files; it throws `SubmitRefused` (now also accepting an undefined head and its own message). The ending's submit step records a `SubmitRefused` from the submit port as `submit_refused` with the blocker key `<attempt>:submit_refused` (not `release_failed`). `start.ts` gives the same landing port to the service and to `stagedSubmit`, so the host binding and a composer's own `landing` both get the check; with no `landing` given to `stagedSubmit` nothing changes.
- **Tests.** `work-end.test.ts` (four backends): a refusal from the submit port is `submit_refused`, one blocker, no `release_failed`, the message still told, one finish, a replay changes nothing. A pure `stagedSubmit` test: staged files (not the first check's `mine`) are judged, an unreadable or throwing read refuses, a stale base with no shared file, a current base and no landing read still submit, nothing is recorded by any refusal. `api/start-work-end.test.ts` (through `startController`): the third landing read finds a late file changed on the landing branch; the ending is `submit_refused` with a blocker and no submission.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored): 7, all killed.** Check skipped; the first check's files used instead of the staged ones; unreadable read taken as no overlap; overlap never refused; the `SubmitRefused` catch removed (5 fail); the composition not passing `landing` to `stagedSubmit`; the head taken as the base (stale rule broken).
- **Not done (said plainly).** Remote host answering `submitView`/`stage` (needs a wire protocol); product composition of `LocalWorker` (H12t); P08's re-check of tree and patch ID at landing time; `PLAN.md` still carried in the staged tree (H12o product slice). The new check still has a gap between the staging and the submission record (a landing that moves then is caught at landing by H12q's expected-version check, as before).
- ASSUMPTION: this was the smallest offline-doable H12n item. The other open parts need a protocol, a composition or cross-card changes; this closes the one race the second review named and left. 
- ASSUMPTION: a landing read that fails after the staging refuses the submit (fail closed, like the earlier re-check) rather than submitting unchecked.

## P09 fifth slice: the author's claimed evidence is compared with the gate's own results (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. An author can record its own check evidence on a code submission (card Q01b: for example "tests passed", tied to the exact tree). Until now the landing gate ignored what the author claimed and only ran its own checks, so a submission whose own evidence said one thing while the gate found another went through unremarked. Now, at landing, the author's claim for a required check on the very tree the gate judged is compared with the gate's own result, and a disagreement is named plainly to the author. The author's word never makes a check pass. Card P09 stays planned.

- **Chosen item and why.** Item (a), the claimed-evidence comparison: it is pure (no new index, protocol or host change) and needs one field on a reader that already exists (`SubmissionService.approvalOf` now also answers the evidence the submission carries). Item (b), `director`, was skipped: no service stores a sign-off record, so reading one means designing a new owner-visible record kind and its permissions, which is not small. Item (c), remote hosts, was skipped: giving a remote host `landingChecks` is a new protocol operation, which needs a protocol version change.
- **What it does** (`landing/landing-gate.ts`, `#claims`, run after every check has its result). Evidence counts only when it names a required check (matched without regard to case or edge spaces) and is bound to the tree the gate judged. Two disagreements: the author recorded `fail` while the gate found `pass`: the check becomes `fail` with `disagreement: "claimed_fail_passed"` ("the author's own evidence for tests on this tree says fail, but the gate found it passing, so the work and its evidence disagree; submit again with evidence that matches"); the author recorded `pass` while the gate found `fail`: the result stays `fail`, with `disagreement: "claimed_pass_failed"` and the plain reason first. Both fields (`claimed`, `disagreement`) are on the entry kept on the request record and the text sent to the author already prints the summary. A claim of `not_run`, for another tree, for a check the project does not require, or against a check the gate could not judge (`not_run`) is not compared. A claim that agrees changes nothing. No claims at all: the result is exactly as before.

## Q02 third slice: the project QA view (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Card Q02 stays planned. Branch `card-q02-s3` off origin/main `5a70b070`. Plain words first: before this, the owner could ask what QA checked on ONE task, but not "what is waiting for QA?" across a project. Now the owner (in any words, in the project in focus) and any reader of the project's tasks see, for each task, its newest code version and whether it waits for QA, has evidence that no longer holds, fails, or passes, with the reasons.

- **Chosen item and why.** Of Q02's Not done list, the project QA view is the one that needs no new stored record, no host or protocol change and no policy decision: it only reads the submissions and the existing QA gate. The review policy (triggers, periodic and incident reviews), verdict revisions citing owner requirements and counting evidence by original source each need a new stored record or an owner-facing product choice, so they stay for later slices.
- **What is built.** `QaEvidenceService.project(by, projectId)` (`submissions/qa-evidence.ts`): scans the project's code submissions (at most 20 pages of 500; `scanLimited` when more exist), keeps each task's NEWEST one (by `submittedAt`, then ID), reads its gate and classifies it: `waiting` (the gate has `no_evidence`: nothing independent, current or stale; a self-check does not count), `stale` (evidence no longer holds, or a re-check is pending), `failing` (failed, blocked, not-run or missing checks, or a superseded decision) and `passes`. Waiting comes first, then stale, failing, passing; at most 200 tasks are listed (`truncated`). A new status kind `qa_project` (`status.ask { kind: "qa_project", projectId }`, status view text with the task title, submission, tree, time, reasons and the four result counts) answers it; chat fills in the project in focus, the interpreter prompt describes it, and `api-v1.md` is regenerated. Read only.
- **Rights.** The owner, or an agent that may read the project's tasks (`task.read`); a task the caller may not read is neither listed nor counted. An unknown project, or one the caller may not read, is `not_found`.
- **Tests.** `submissions/qa-project-view.test.ts` (4 backends: newest-version rule, a newer review is ignored, another project's code is not listed, waiting with a required check also reads missing, the four results stay apart, a changed contract turns a pass into stale, sorting, rights, read twice is the same), `api/start-qa-evidence.test.ts` (+1: the status kind through the API: empty, waiting, failing, passing, another project's agent refused), `api/start-qa-project-chat.test.ts` (chat uses the focused project; none in focus asks which). - **Not done (said plainly).** The review policy (scope, triggers including periodic and incident, required checks, whether independent review gates completion); counting independent evidence by original source (`DeskService.independence`); a reviewer verdict that cites criteria and decision revisions and a rejection that must cite an unmet owner requirement; a team vote never overriding an owner decision in review; automatic invalidation on `contract.set` and decision propagation; other dependencies (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) invalidating evidence. The view does not show older submissions of a task, nor a task with no code submission (a task that was never submitted is not "waiting for QA"), and does not page past 200 tasks. - **Tests.** `submissions/doc-retire.test.ts` on all four backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL): a send that fails after the write, then the same check sent again, delivers one notice; a further repeat leaves one notice and every send carries the same notice ID; the owner's own check and its repeat send nothing. ## Q04 (third slice): team-wide defect risks in chat, and an escalated defect on the Needs-you list (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card Q04 tracks defects and repairs. Two things the owner could not do before are now possible. (1) The owner can ask, in any words, what defects are still unfinished across a project ("what defects are still open?", "which defects wait for my decision?"): the answer counts them as escalated to the owner, repaired and waiting for a check, or open and waiting for a repair, and lists each with severity, cycles used against the limit, task, deliverable and the finding, escalated first, every line citing its records. (2) A defect that escalated after its repair cycles now sits on the owner's Needs-you list like an approval or a question, and the owner answers it there in free words ("let them try the backup step once more"): the system shows the owner what it is about to do and applies it on their word. Card Q04 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Slice chosen, and why.** Of Q04's open items, "what waits for QA" is already answered by Q02's `qa_project` view (reused, not duplicated: the interpreter prompt keeps pointing there for what waits for QA and the new view is the defect half of "team-wide risks"). The two built here share one read of the defect records, need no new record shape, no model and no product choice, and close the gap where an escalation was only a notice that could scroll away. Withdrawing or editing a defect, and gating `done` or an acceptance on open defects, change what other tasks may do and need product choices, so they stay out.
- **Built.** `DefectService.unresolved(by, { projectId?, cap?, escalatedOnly? })`: scans the `defect` records a page at a time (500 per page, at most 20 pages; `scanLimited` says it stopped early and the answer says so), keeps those in state `open`, `repair-submitted` or `escalated`, only where the caller may read the deliverable (the acceptance service's own rule; an agent must name a project; owner sees all), escalated first, then severity, then oldest. Status kind `defect_risks` (`projectId`, defaulting to the project in focus in chat; `StatusService.defectRiskLines`): a counts line and up to 30 defect lines, with the rest counted. Needs-you: a new item kind `defect` (escalated defects, owner only, up to 50, answer choices `accept-as-is` or `repair-again`), answered in place by `needs-you.answer` (`kind: defect`), which calls `defect.override` as the owner with the reason the owner gave or "answered from the Needs-you list", with the defect's revision read just before the change (a change in between is refused `stale_revision`); an item that no longer waits is refused (`invalid_transition`), never decided again. The two choices were added to the chat's list of fixed choices, so the answer need not appear in the owner's words (the item is still matched by the owner's own words and shown first). The interpreter prompt describes both. `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Tests.** `submissions/defects-unresolved.test.ts` (four storage backends): states listed and finished ones left out, order, per-project cycle limit, the owner's view across projects, `escalatedOnly`, the cap against the counts, an agent reading only what it may read and refused without a project, a repair-again returning an item to open with the count kept. `api/start-defect-risks.test.ts` (through `startController`): the chat answer equals the state API's, an empty project says nothing is unfinished, a repaired defect and an open one are not on the Needs-you list, the failed check escalates and it appears there with its choices, another project's agent is told nothing, an agent cannot answer the item, the owner's words are shown first then applied (the failed check stays failed, the owner's reason recorded), the item leaves the list, a repeat and a made-up answer are refused. Mutation checks on the built files (each alone, restored): finished defects counted, project filter dropped, `escalatedOnly` ignored, read right ignored, escalated not first, awaiting-check counted as open, the answer ignoring the defect's state: all caught. Runs (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, sandbox required, offline guard): the two new files, `defects.test`, `start-defects`, `model-interpreter`, `start-qa-project-chat`, `status.test`: 245 of 245. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the Needs-you answer to an escalated defect may use a default reason ("answered from the Needs-you list"), as approvals already do; the owner who wants their own reason gives one or uses `defect.override` directly. Reversible by making `reason` required in `answerNeed`. **ASSUMPTION:** only escalated defects are Needs-you items (an open or repaired one waits on an agent, not the owner). **ASSUMPTION:** the project view lists at most 30 defects and the scan stops after 10,000 defect records (said in the answer); a project beyond that is read through `defect.list` per deliverable.
- **Not done (said plainly).** Withdrawing or editing a defect after it is reported; gating a task's `done` or a deliverable's acceptance on open defects; the P10 conflict return counted as a defect cycle (it is counted in the landing queue's record); escalation of disagreements other than a defect's cycles; periodic and incident-triggered reviews; defects in hand-off packages, retention rules and the web project view; a cross-project (installation-wide) chat view (the owner's Needs-you list is installation-wide, `defect_risks` is per project); a defect's link to Q02 evidence records beyond the evidence references the reporter gives. The Needs-you answer for a defect has no 4-backend test of its own (the service it calls is covered on four backends; the end-to-end test runs on SQLite).

### Q04 third slice review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5 review, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The review found one real problem and two gaps in the descriptions, all fixed. (1) If the owner's answer to an escalated defect was recorded but the reply got lost and the same command was sent again, it was refused as "no longer waits" instead of being answered from what was recorded, unlike approvals and blockers; now the retry gets the recorded answer, and the same command ID with the other answer is refused (`command_conflict`). (2) The `status.ask` description did not name `defect_risks` (the known pitfall; `api.test` checks it and was not in the earlier runs), and its `needs_you` description did not mention held resumes or escalated defects; both now do, and `api-v1.md` is regenerated. (3) The notes said the answer is pinned to the revision "as listed"; it is pinned to the revision read just before the change, now said so.

- **Checked and found sound.** `needs-you.answer` is owner-only and refused from a task credential before anything is read; `defect.override` itself refuses anyone but the owner, so an agent cannot answer its own defect's item. `unresolved` returns nothing for a principal that is neither the owner nor an agent, checks each deliverable's read right (an agent's task credential is held to its task), and only the owner may scan without a project; another project's agent sees an empty answer, never counts (second review: it is now told `not_found`, like `qa_project` and `docs`). The default reason matches approvals; the decision record names the owner as its author. - **ASSUMPTION:** an item is identified by its defect ID, so a proposal shown for one escalation and agreed to after the owner's own repair-again and a fresh escalation of the same defect applies to the new escalation; that needs the owner's own decision in between, and the answer is still the owner's choice about the same finding. ### Q04 third slice second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5 second review, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Two changes. (1) A Needs-you item for an escalated defect now names the escalation it shows: the item carries the defect's `revision`, the chat puts it on the proposal it draws up, and `needs-you.answer` refuses (`invalid_transition`, "it escalated again") an answer whose revision is not the defect's current one. Before, a "yes" to a proposal drawn up for one escalation could, after the owner let the repair go on from elsewhere and the repair failed again, accept the newer escalation as is without the owner seeing it. ### Own-hardware Mac probe: a missing program may report EACCES (2026-11-22)

The Mac runner failed `scripts/wsb-launch-variants.test.mjs` ("a missing program is not found"): launching a program that does not exist gave `EACCES`, not `ENOENT`, because the runner's PATH holds a directory (another user's `.pi/agent/bin`) that the runner user cannot read, and a PATH lookup that hits it reports `EACCES`. The test now accepts `ENOENT` or `EACCES` and still requires a non-zero status, so a launch that succeeds or reports another or no error still fails. No other `scripts/*.test.mjs` PATH lookup assumed ENOENT only (the other ENOENT mentions use fake results or file reads). `scripts/wsb-job-context.mjs` is left alone: `ENOENT` is labelled "not found on PATH", other errors "could not run", which is accurate for EACCES.

- ASSUMPTION: EACCES is a legitimate "not found" result only in this test; production labelling stays as is. No workflow or launch-strategy change.

## P09 sixth slice: the `director` required check is collected at landing (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. A project whose required checks include `director` could land nothing: the landing gate never looked for a director's sign-off and always answered "not run". Now the gate reads the director sign-offs recorded on the code submission the landing lands. The landing goes ahead on that check only when the newest sign-off on that submission says approve, and it counts for the tree being landed only while the patch is unchanged (a work refreshed onto a newer base keeps its sign-off; any other change needs a new one). Card P09 stays planned.

- **Chosen item and why.** The `director` check, not remote-host `landingChecks`: remote hosts need a new protocol operation and a protocol version change, which is not offline-doable as a small slice. The earlier notes said "no sign-off record exists"; that was out of date: Q01b already records a `signoff` submission (role `director`, a `subject`, a decision `approve` or `decline`, copying the subject's tree and patch ID, refused on the signer's own work and for anyone not holding the director role in the project). What was missing was only a way to read them by submission without scanning the whole table, and the gate.
- **What "the director approved this change" means.** The newest `signoff` submission on the landed code submission says `approve`. No new approval path, no new record kind for agents, no new permission: the sign-off is recorded exactly as before. A later decline takes an approval back (as a later review takes back an approval); a later approval, also by another director, replaces a decline. A sign-off never stands in for the `review` check and the review never stands in for it.
- **Built.** `submissions.ts`: each sign-off is added, in the same write, to a per-subject list (record kind `submission-signoffs`, keyed by the subject, the newest 50 are kept and the oldest drops off (review fix below: never refused for size); a repeat of the same command adds nothing; two sign-offs written at the same moment are rebuilt, not refused). `approvalOf` answers `director: { newest, by, signoffId }` only when there is one. Exported `landingDirectorGate(service)` (shared by `api/start.ts` and the tests). `landing-gate.ts`: `directorGate` dependency and `#director`, following the qa/docs pattern: read AFTER the host's run together with the submission; no submission, no reader, an unreadable answer or one for another task, submission or tree is `not_run`; no sign-off is `not_run`; a decline is `fail`; an approval then needs the host's patch ID of the submission's base and tree to equal the submission's claim and the landed change's patch, else `fail` (unreadable: `not_run`). The host is asked for that patch ID when `director` is required too. `api/start.ts` composes `directorGate`. The `workspace.request` description (and `api-v1.md`, regenerated) now says what `director` needs.
- **Tests.** `landing/landing-gate-director.test.ts` (7, the gate alone); `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p09-director.test.ts` (6 tests x 4 backends, real submission service, real gate); `submissions/submissions-p09-director.test.ts` (3 x 4 backends: list, repeat, cap, race, bounded rebuild); `integration/p09-landing-checks.test.ts` extended (the start-level product test: the project requires `director`; refused with no sign-off, refused after a decline, landed after an approval by a director agent). No fixed pauses; the sandbox test skips where it is unavailable, as before.
- **Mutation checks (8, all killed, restored).** Wiring line in `start.ts` removed (the product test fails); a decline treated as a pass; the landed patch not compared; the oldest sign-off deciding instead of the newest; no per-subject list written; a race not rebuilt; the host not asked for the patch ID; the "no sign-off" branch removed.
- **ASSUMPTION (newest wins).** With several directors, the newest sign-off on the submission decides, as with reviews; no quorum and no "all must approve". Reversible: change the reader to require every director's latest to approve.
- **ASSUMPTION (the signer's role is judged when recorded).** A sign-off stays valid if its signer later loses the director role; the sign-off is a historical record, as a review is. A retired signer's sign-off is not undone.
- **ASSUMPTION (sign-off needs no review).** The check reads only sign-offs; whether review is also required is the project's `requiredChecks`, not this check.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) Remote hosts still have no `landingChecks` (needs a protocol version change), so on a remote host a gated landing is refused. (2) Like `review`, `qa` and `docs`, `director` needs a named (or queued) code submission; an owner landing with an empty queue names none and refuses. (3) A sign-off recorded after the gate's last read and before the host writes is not seen (the same window as the other checks). (4) A sign-off that a director gives on a document submission is kept in the list but is never read by the landing. (5) The author's claimed evidence named `director` is compared like the other required checks (already generic); no other change there. (6) Existing sign-offs recorded before this slice are not in the list (it is written from now on) and do not count; a director signs off again.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** (1) Fixed: the sign-off list refused a 51st sign-off (`unavailable`), so after 50 sign-offs a director could no longer record a decline and the 50th approval kept the landing passing; the test asserted that. The list now keeps the newest 50 (the oldest drops off, like the document index), so the newest sign-off is always recorded and decides; the test now records a 51st decline (it decides; the oldest dropped off) and a 52nd approval. (2) Wording: a sign-off that lost a write race was told "another review ... was recorded"; it now says "another sign-off". Checked and left as is: only agents holding `director` in the task's project may sign off, never on their own work; the subject must be a submission of the same task, and the list is keyed by that subject, so a sign-off cannot count for another submission, task or tree; "newest" is the list's order, appended under a revision guard (a sequence, not a clock), and concurrent sign-offs are rebuilt on all 4 backends; sign-offs recorded before this slice are not in the list, so the check is `not_run` (fail-closed) until a director signs off again; `director` was already an accepted required-check name and unknown names are refused when the policy is set.
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Reviewed f9d47278 (origin/main a817c209 had not moved). No code defect found; one test widened. Checked: a sign-off is recorded only by an agent holding `director` with a live grant in the task's project, never on a submission it submitted itself, and a task credential only inside its own task; an `agent.manage` holder creates agents with no grants, so it cannot make a second identity that holds a role in the project. The list is keyed by the subject, so a sign-off on another submission of the task (even one with the very same tree and patch) or on a document submission never counts for the landed one. "Newest" is the list's order, appended under the record's revision (create when absent, update at the read revision) on all four backends, with a lost race rebuilt up to five times; the trim keeps the newest 50 after appending, so the newest entry is always kept and an older approval cannot come back. Every missing or unreadable input is `not_run`, a decline is `fail`, and the patch binding is the one `qa` and `docs` use. The record holds at most 50 entries of about 150 bytes each; a landing that requires `director` makes two more `approvalOf` calls after the host's run (three record reads each: the submission, its reviews and its sign-offs), and every other caller of `approvalOf` now also reads the sign-off list (one read).
  - **Test added.** `workspace-ops-p09-director` (4 backends): an approval on a second code submission of the task with exactly the landed tree and patch, and one on a document submission of the task, leave the landed submission's check `not_run`.
  - **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; all caught).** `directorGate` line removed from `start.js` (the product test fails); the trim keeps the oldest 50 instead of the newest (4); a sign-off that lost a race told as a used command ID, not rebuilt (8); the gate's answer not bound to the submission (1) or to the task (1); the submission's own patch claim not compared (1).
  - **Left as it is (said plainly).** (1) An agent with an `agent.manage` grant can change the roles of existing agents, including giving `director` to a colleague that already has a grant in the project; that is the existing agent-management authority (the same holds for `reviewer` and the review check) and is the owner's choice when granting it, not something this check can see. (2) The owner cannot record a sign-off (sign-offs are agent submissions); a project with no director agent that requires `director` lands nothing until the owner adds a director or drops the check.
  - **Runs (Linux, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`).** `submissions-p09-director`, `landing-gate-director`, `workspace-ops-p09-director`, `landing-gate.test`, `submissions.test`, integration `p09-landing-checks` (sandbox used): 162/162. `api:docs:write` unchanged; `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok.

## Q01b fourth slice: the owner and chat can see what was submitted on a task and where each piece stands (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-q01b-s4`. Plain words first. Submissions and director sign-offs were recorded and read by the landing gate, but the owner had no plain view of them: `submission.list` returns raw records and no status view or chat answer said "was this code reviewed, did the director sign off, what is it waiting for". ### Q01b fourth slice review (Claude agent, clean-context review, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The view could name the wrong submission as the newest, and it showed a reviewer things it may not otherwise read. Both are fixed, with tests.

- **Newest was not always the newest (fixed).** `submission.list` walks the whole submission table in ID order (random), stopping after 100 matches or 2,000 scanned rows. The view read one call, so on a controller with more than 2,000 submissions the "Newest code submission" was the newest of an arbitrary slice, and the partial note said only "older ones may exist". The view now follows the list's cursor for up to 5 calls (bounded: at most 5 x 2,000 rows scanned on PostgreSQL, plus 3 reads per shown code submission), sorts what it read, and when it stopped early says "newer or older ones may exist; \"newest\" here means the newest of those read".
- **A reviewer saw other reviewers' verdicts and the director's decision (fixed).** `approvalOf` takes no caller. A reviewer asked to review a code submission may read that submission only (owner decision), yet the view gave it the other reviewers' verdicts and names and the director's sign-off. Now the review and sign-off state of a code submission are shown to the owner and to the code's author only (the author is already told them when a landing is refused); anyone else sees the submission with a line saying so. ASSUMPTION: the smallest-scope reading of the existing rule; the owner can widen it later.
- **Wording.** An agent's header says "you may read" instead of "on record" (its counts are only what it may read). An approval or approving sign-off adds "An approval counts at landing only while the change's patch stays the one approved", as the gate compares the patch. One prompt example named no task ("is anything waiting for a reviewer?"), which this task view cannot answer; it now names one.
- **Checked and left.** Review state words match `approvalOf` and the gate (`#review`: approved or not required passes subject to the patch; changes/reject fail; none is not run); a decline matches the director check's fail. Report text goes through `quoted` (whole code points, controls and bidi escaped, the cut marked). The `status.ask` summary names the kind; the chat and state API give the same lines (start-level test).
- **Tests.** Two new suites x 4 backends: newest found across list pages (scan pages of 2 rows) and the partial wording past the page bound (pages of 1 row); a reviewer asked to review sees no verdicts or director decision while the author and owner do, with the patch note; the review's giver sees its own review only.
- **Mutation checks (6, built `status.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; all caught, 4 failures each).** One page only; partial never said; the access check removed; the patch note removed; the agent header worded "on record"; the cursor not passed.
- **Runs (Linux, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard).** `submissions-q01b-view`, `start-q01b-view`, `model-interpreter`: 44/44; `status.test`, `api.test`: 286/286. `api:docs:write` unchanged; `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok.

### Q01b fourth slice second review (Claude agent, clean-context second review, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The view is sound: it shows only what `submission.get` allows, the author is the controller-recorded submitter (not a field the agent sets), and its review and director words mean what the landing gate reads. One wording fix and four missing tests.

- **An early-stopped empty scan said "nothing has been submitted" (fixed).** When the bounded scan stopped before the end of the table and had found nothing on the task, the first line still said flatly that nothing was submitted, then added the partial note. On a controller with more than 10,000 stored submissions that is the common case for a task whose rows sit late in ID order. ## Q02 fourth slice: a contract change invalidates QA evidence by itself (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Card Q02 stays planned. Branch `card-q02-s4` off origin/main `de481a70`. Plain words first: until now, QA evidence that no longer fitted a changed task contract was invalidated, and its re-check scheduled, only when someone asked (`qa.evidence.check`). Now changing a task's acceptance criteria, expected result, required evidence or checks through `contract.set` (by the owner, by chat in any words, or by an agent) looks at the task's QA evidence at once: evidence bound to the old contract is invalidated (kept, with its results and reasons), a re-check goes to whoever recorded it and the owner is told, exactly as `qa.evidence.check` does.

- **Chosen item and why.** Of Q02's Not done list this is the smallest complete item that needs no new stored record, no new status kind, no host or protocol change and no policy choice: the first slice's own ASSUMPTION named it ("a later slice can call `check` from `contract.set`"), and the acceptance text says "invalidation schedules revalidation". The review policy, verdict records citing owner requirements and counting by original source each need a new record or an owner-facing product choice; decision propagation reaches tasks through a different path and stays out.
- **What is built.** `QaEvidenceService.contractChanged(taskId)` (`submissions/qa-evidence.ts`): runs the same check as `check` (the body is now `#checkTask`) with the QA service itself as the actor (`service:qa-evidence`, no grants; what changed decides, not who changed it). Its command ID names the contract version and the revision of the task's evidence index, so each change is looked at once, a repeat writes nothing, and a record added later is looked at by the next change. A task with no evidence is not read further. `contract.set` (`api/operations.ts`) calls it after the version is stored, best effort (a failure never fails the contract change; `qa.evidence.check` and the gate still catch it, and the gate never passes stale evidence meanwhile). Chat reaches it through the existing `contract.set` chat operation; the interpreter prompt now says so. No new status kind (the `qa` and `qa_project` kinds already show the invalidated record and the re-check); `contract.set`'s API summary names the behaviour and `api-v1.md` is regenerated after the build.
- **Tests.** `submissions/qa-contract-change.test.ts` (4 backends: no evidence, unknown task, priority change leaves evidence, new criteria invalidate once with the re-check for the recorder and the notice and port told once, a repeat writes nothing, new evidence passes and a later checks change invalidates that one); `api/start-qa-evidence.test.ts` (+1 through the API: priority change leaves it, an author without QA rights changing the criteria invalidates it with `invalidatedBy` the service, the gate shows the pending re-check, a replayed `contract.set` adds nothing; the existing invalidation test now expects the automatic invalidation at the contract change). Mutation checks on the built files, each restored byte-identical (SHA-256): no check made (fails 6 of 9), constant command ID (4 fail), wrong service ID (5), `contract.set` hook removed (2), hook pointed at the wrong task (2). Not killed: removing the "task missing" guard (equivalent: a missing task has no evidence index, which returns first).
- **Not done (said plainly).** The review policy (scope, triggers including periodic and incident, required checks, whether independent review gates completion); counting independent evidence by original source (`DeskService.independence`); a reviewer verdict that cites criteria and decision revisions, and a rejection that must cite an unmet owner requirement; a team vote never overriding an owner decision in review; automatic invalidation on decision changes (a corrected decision still invalidates only when `qa.evidence.check` runs; the gate meanwhile never passes it); other dependencies (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) invalidating evidence; a contract change made by a path other than the `contract.set` operation (swarm child contracts and difficulty changes do not touch the fields that matter, and a task just created has no evidence).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the check after a contract change runs inside the `contract.set` call, not in a background loop: it is cheap (one task's index) and the owner sees the re-check straight away. Reversible: move the call to a queue.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the re-check's `requestedBy` is `service:qa-evidence`, not the person who changed the contract, since the system, not that person, invalidated the evidence.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a failure of the automatic check is swallowed (best effort) rather than reported on the contract change, so a QA fault can never block the owner from changing a contract.

### Q02 fourth slice review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Clean-context review and fixes on `card-q02-s4`; origin/main had not moved (`de481a70`). Plain words first: the change is sound; the tests missed three things it does (a failure of the automatic check never failing the contract change, two checks at the same moment, a repeat at the same contract version after newer evidence went stale), and one existing API test had lost its gate assertion. Tests were added; no product code changed.

- **Checked and found right.** `contract.set` calls the QA service only after `setContract` returned (the version is stored and committed), and only when it did not throw; a failure is swallowed, so it can neither fail nor roll back the change. It is awaited, so the answer waits for one check of the task: bounded by `QA_LIMITS.perTask` (200 records) and `decisions` (20 per record), the same work as `qa.evidence.check`, a few retries at most after a lost race. The actor `service:qa-evidence` is a constant inside the service with no grants, used only as the command's actor and the `invalidatedBy`/`requestedBy` label; service principals are provisioned only by the controller (`provisionService`, called for the dispatcher), so no caller can sign in as it, and command IDs are scoped by actor, so a caller's `qa.evidence.check` cannot reuse or block the automatic command ID. The record shows both: the `contract.set` command under the person who changed it, the `qa.evidence.check` command and `invalidatedBy` under the service. The swallowed failure leaves no log line (as the existing `submitted` hook), but nothing unsafe follows: the P09 landing gate (`gateBound`) recomputes staleness from the contract version in force at every read and binds the contract revision (tested in `workspace-ops-p09-qa.test.ts`: evidence made stale by a contract change, with no check run, refuses the landing), and the `qa` view shows `staleNow`.

A direct `contract.set` operation test: the QA service is told after the change is stored, about that task; a thrown error (at once or later) leaves the answer unchanged; a refused change tells it nothing; a controller without the QA service still changes contracts. `start-qa-evidence.test.ts`: the gate right after the contract change is asserted again (failed, `stale_evidence` and `check_missing`, fields `acceptanceCriteria, checks`, the pending re-check), which the slice had dropped.

Checked: (1) the awaited check runs its reads one after another outside any transaction, so it uses one pooled PostgreSQL connection at a time, and every PostgreSQL call is bounded (`statement_timeout`, `query_timeout`, connection timeout), so a slow or silent server cannot hold `contract.set` forever. Worst case, a task with 200 current records citing 20 decisions each: about 4,400 reads per look at the evidence, two looks for a check that writes, and at most about 27,000 reads when it loses the race three times. That is the same work as `qa.evidence.check`, and it runs even for a priority-only change when the task has evidence. Left as it is. (2) Nothing decides on the stored `current` flag alone. The landing `qa` check (`landingQaGate` → `gate`), the `qa` and `qa_project` views, and documentation verify, impact and landing all use `gate`/`gateBound` or `list().staleNow`, which recompute staleness from the contract in force.
