### CI flake: H12n "two ends of one attempt at once join the first" on Windows Node 24 (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

- **What failed.** Hosted run 45057966643 (commit 65ab7589), windows-latest, Node 24.21.0, shard 1/3, reference store: `a joined stop writes nothing to the attempt: 8 !== 7`. Every other cell passed.
- **Cause: the test was racy; the product is right (kind a).** The test ran its dispatcher with an end-hook limit of 60 ms and then, with the hook still held, did two storage reads and a fixed 20 ms pause before asserting the attempt's revision had not moved. The 60 ms limit starts when the hook is called, so on a slow machine the hook was cut off ("did not answer within 60 ms") between the two reads and the first end's own final write landed on the attempt: one revision higher, taken for a write by the joined stop. The joined stop itself writes nothing: `#stopNow` skips its marker write while `#endingBy` holds the attempt, and `#end` returns the first end. Reproduced locally by raising only the fixed pause from 20 to 120 ms: the same `8 !== 7`.
- **Change (test only, `dispatcher-suite.ts`).** Part one now uses an end-hook limit of 600 000 ms, so nothing but the test's own gate lets the first end go on; the check that a joined stop writes nothing, and that the hook ran once, stays. The gate is released in a `finally` so a failed check cannot leave the end waiting for the long limit. Part two (the hook that never answers: both stops resolve, attempt abandoned, "did not answer within 60 ms" reported, two stops at once) is a separate attempt on a restarted dispatcher with the 60 ms limit, so the timeout path is still proved and no longer races a revision check. The throwing-hook part is unchanged.
- **Mutation checks (each alone, restored).** Marker write no longer skipped while an end is in progress: killed (`8 !== 7`). A second end no longer joins the first: killed (`8 !== 7`). The timeout message changed: killed. The old test with the pause at 120 ms: failed (the repro); the new test passes at any pause under the long limit.
- **Runs.** 30 repeats of the test on reference store and SQLite (60 passes, 0 failures), then 2 parallel loops of 15 under 3 busy-loop CPU hogs (60 passes). Files `dispatcher.test`, `dispatcher.sqlite.test`, `ended-hook.test`, `stopped-early.test`: 248 of 248.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a test-only fix is enough because the product behaviour (joined stop writes nothing) holds under every interleaving seen; a real timer limit stays in part two because the dispatcher has no injected timer for the hook limit, and adding one would be a product change not asked for.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the PostgreSQL file was not run: the changed suite body is shared and the flake is storage-independent.

#### Clean-context review of the H12n flake fix (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

- **Diagnosis confirmed from the code.** `#end` registers `#endingBy` synchronously and calls the end hook in the same synchronous run, so once the hook has been called the entry stays until the first end resolves; `#stopNow` reads it synchronously after `#controlled`, so with the hook held a joined stop has no window to write. Only the first end going on (the 60 ms limit firing) could raise the revision.
- **Fix.** The `try/finally` that releases the gate now also covers the wait for the hook and the first revision read: before, a failure there left the end waiting for the 600 s limit (an unref'd timer), keeping the test process alive. A forced failure of the first check now ends in about 1 s.
- **Mutation checks (built `dispatcher.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256).** Marker write not skipped during an end: killed (`8 !== 7`). Second end does not join: killed (`2 !== 1`). Hook run again by a joined end: killed (`2 !== 1`). End-hook timeout message changed: killed. Timeout not reported: killed.
- **Runs (Linux, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard).** `dispatcher`, `dispatcher.sqlite`, `dispatcher.postgres`, `ended-hook`, `stopped-early`: 360/360. The test alone on reference store, SQLite and PostgreSQL: 20/20 runs, then 3 parallel loops of 20 under 32 busy loops on 32 cores: 60/60. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok.
- **Left as it is.** Part two (60 ms limit, two stops at once) would reject the second stop only if its first read finished more than 60 ms after the first stop had written its marker; both reads start in the same tick, and the old test had the same exposure.

## H12o (automatic release): an approval makes the platform commit by itself (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card H12o commits an approved submission in the task's own checkout, and since the permit slice that commit is a review-gate permit commit when a reviewer approved it. But nothing asked for it: the owner (or an integrator) had to type a `release` with the submission's ID before the reviewed work could land. Now the approval itself asks. When a reviewer approves a code submission, the controller makes (corrected by the review below: a code submission that needs no review is no longer released automatically) the same `release` request the owner could make, under its own service identity, so reviewed work is committed and, with the permit, can land under the default settings. Card H12o stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Slice chosen, and why.** Of H12o's open items this was the smallest complete one that can be built and proved offline with real git: the item "nothing asks for the release automatically after an approval" (Not done 1 of the first slice and of the permit slice). The others need a worker protocol change (a remote host's `release` of a submission), a decision that was already made the other way (committing the landed files in the shared tree is P10c; upgrading an old commit to a permit commit; PLAN.md), or an A06 redesign (the `commitOnce` path).
- **Built.** `WorkspaceOpService.releaseApproved(submissionId, cause)`: the same checks, quiesce, host call and exactly-once `submission-commit` record as the owner's `workspace.request` release (the body of `request` moved into one private method both call), under the identity `service:workspace-release` and the command ID `rel-auto:<cause>`. It never throws. It does nothing when the work is not approved, the task has a live attempt (the release would freeze it), the task is paused, the commit already exists (no host call, nothing made quiet), submissions are not known, or the arguments are malformed. A host that refuses or fails is the recorded answer of that request. `start.ts`: the submission service's recorded-step hook asks it after the landing-queue step, for a code submission and for a review whose verdict is `approve` (the subject is the reviewed submission), best effort (a throw never changes what was recorded). The `cause` is the approving review (or the code submission itself), so a repeat of the same approval does nothing more and a later approval after `changes` tries again.
- **Permit.** Unchanged and decided by the controller from the recorded approval exactly as in the permit slice: a reviewer's approval asks for the permit, the one-agent approval never does.
- **ASSUMPTION (a task with a live attempt is left alone).** The release's quiesce would freeze a running attempt, and a reviewer's approval must not interrupt an author that has started again. So nothing is made then; the next approval, or the owner's own request, does it. Reversible: drop the live-attempt line in `releaseApproved`.
- **ASSUMPTION (one-agent projects).** A code submission that needs no review is released at once too (as the queue already takes it at once). The commit is the platform's own, never a permit commit, so a landing still needs `requirePermit=false` for it, as before.
- **ASSUMPTION (no setting).** There is no owner setting to turn it off: it is the same commit the owner could ask for, in the task's own checkout (the shared tree is not touched), and every landing rule still applies. An owner who wants it off removes the call in `start.ts`.
- **ASSUMPTION (latency).** The release runs inside the review's recording call (a slow host holds that call). A refusal, a remote host or an error leave the review recorded and the owner's own request available.
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-h12o-auto.test.ts` (5 tests x 4 storage backends = 20): a reviewer's approval releases once as a permit commit under the service identity, through the quiesce, repeats and later approvals ask nothing, the owner's request is answered from the record; the one-agent approval without the permit; nothing asked or recorded for unapproved work, a live attempt, a paused task, an unknown or malformed submission or a bad cause, and the next approval then releases; a failing host is the recorded answer, the same approval answered from its record, another approval tries again and one commit is recorded; an approval taken back while the task is made quiet is refused before the host is asked, and a service without submissions does nothing. `integration/h12o-submission-commit.test.ts` (changed, real local worker over real git through `startController`): the reviewer's approval alone made the commit (service identity, one host call, permit marks, `unpermitted` empty); the owner's `release` is then `alreadyRecorded` with no new host call; a stray file in the checkout makes the automatic release refuse (no commit, no record) and the lost-answer and retry steps then run as before.
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, tests run, restored): 7 killed, 1 equivalent.** Live-attempt check removed (4 fail); paused check removed (4); already-committed check removed (4); command ID not including the cause (8); the identity changed (4); the hook never releasing a review's approval (integration test fails); the hook passing the review's own ID instead of the reviewed submission's (integration fails). Equivalent: dropping the "approved" check in `releaseApproved` changes nothing, because `request`'s own approval check refuses an unapproved submission before anything is recorded (kept as defence in depth).
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) A remote host still refuses a release of a submission (no protocol field), so there the approval releases nothing. (2) A task with a live attempt is released only by a later approval or the owner. (3) Nothing commits landed or integrated files in the shared tree (P10c). (4) The old `commitOnce`/`CommitPort`/`CommitGateService` path is still not wired. (5) A commit made earlier without the permit is not upgraded. (6) PLAN.md is still committed and landed. (7) A deliverable accepted through `AcceptanceService` (Q01) is not read as an approval. (8) A failed automatic release is visible only as the recorded request (no notice to the owner).

### H12o (automatic release) review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Clean-context review and fix on `card-h12o-s4`; origin/main had moved (Q01b fourth slice and its reviews) and merged without conflicts.

- **Changed: only a reviewer's approval is released automatically.** The "a code submission that needs no review is released at once" branch is removed, both in the `start.ts` hook (only a review with verdict `approve` asks now) and in `releaseApproved` itself, which now does nothing unless the newest approval is a reviewer's (not `review_disabled_single_agent`, not missing, not the author). It did not let work skip a review at landing: "needs no review" is decided when the code submission is recorded and only when no active agent with the reviewer role and a live grant exists in the project. A reviewer that exists but has not been assigned yet still makes review required, so the case "a reviewer will be assigned later" was never released. It was removed for two other reasons. (1) Under the default landing rule (`requirePermit`) a plain commit can never land, and it stays in the checkout between the landed base and HEAD as an unpermitted commit, so once the project has a reviewer every later reviewed landing from that checkout is refused (old commits are not upgraded, Not done 5). Without the commit the change stays uncommitted and goes into the next submission, where it is reviewed. (2) In the normal flow it did nothing anyway: a code submission comes from the owner of the task's live attempt, and `work.end` opens the submission before it finishes the attempt, so the live-attempt check always skipped it. The owner's own `release` still makes the plain commit for one-agent work, as before this slice. Reversible: restore the `e.kind === "code"` line in `start.ts` and the `reviewerApproved` condition in `releaseApproved`.
- **Checked and left as they are.** An approval taken back by a later `changes`/`reject` between the hook and the host is caught by `#stillApproved` inside the quiesce before the host is asked (tested). A review given during the host's own commit is the same window the owner's request has, and the landing gate reads the approval again after its run. Two approvals at once: the second meets the per-task busy guard before anything is recorded (swallowed), or the existing commit record. An approval of an older submission when the checkout holds newer work is refused by the host ("its files changed") as the recorded answer. The author's own approval is refused by the submission service when recorded and again here. The identity `service:workspace-release` is built only inside the controller, has no grants and goes through no API path, and its command IDs are scoped by that identity, so no owner or agent command ID can collide. The cause is the approving review's submission ID (controller-made, checked against a short safe pattern). A remote host refuses a release that names a submission before anything is sent (`remote/host.ts`), recorded as a refusal with the open marker cleared. The hook runs after the review is stored, and its errors are swallowed; a slow local host holds the reviewer's `submission.record` call for the length of one commit (unchanged ASSUMPTION above).
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops-h12o-auto` test 2 now asserts that the one-agent approval, an approval naming the author, and an approval with no approver ask nothing and record nothing. The owner's own release then makes the plain commit, and a reviewer's later approval asks nothing more (4 backends).
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 7 killed.** Reviewer-only check removed (4 fail). `#stillApproved` during the quiesce removed (4). Live-attempt skip removed (4). Paused skip removed (4). Command ID ignoring the cause (8). Already-committed skip removed (8). The `start.ts` hook no longer releasing a review's approval (the real-git integration test fails).

### H12o (automatic release) second review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Clean-context second review on `card-h12o-s4`. origin/main had not moved (still `1020bc48`), so nothing was merged. No code was changed; one test was added.

- **Safety, checked.** The automatic release is the owner's `release` (one private `#request` both call), so the host's permit decision is the same: a permit commit only when the recorded approval is a reviewer's other than the author. The approval is read three times: in `releaseApproved`, in `#approved` before anything is recorded, and in `#stillApproved` inside the quiesce, right before the host is asked (same base and tree, still a reviewer's). The host commits only when the checkout holds exactly the approved tree on the approved base; anything else in the checkout (the author kept editing, a stray file, a newer submission's work) refuses the release and nothing is committed (the real-git integration test shows it for the automatic release). The commit is made only in the task's own checkout. Landing still goes through the integrator lease, the queue and the landing gate (review, tests, QA, docs, director checks) exactly as before.
- **Identity and command IDs, checked.** Command IDs are scoped by principal (`scopedCommandId` hashes the caller's ID under the principal's ID), so `rel-auto:<cause>` under `service:workspace-release` cannot meet an owner's or an agent's command. The cause is the review submission's ID, made by the controller, not text an agent chooses. An owner could enrol a service principal named `workspace-release`, but a service may hold only recovery actions, so `workspace.request` refuses it at `#authorize` before any replay is looked up.
- **Time limits, checked.** The release runs inside the reviewer's `submission.record` call, after the review is stored. Each git command on the local host stops after 120 s (`GIT_LIMITS.timeoutMs`), and a remote host's workspace request is waited for at most 5 minutes (`workspaceWaitMs`, default 300 000 ms). The call cannot hang forever, but it can be slow.
- **Finding (left as it is, said plainly): a reviewer that records from its own attempt on the task never gets the automatic release.** The author's attempt always ends after its code submission (`work-end` finishes it), so it does not block the release. No code dispatches a reviewer for a code submission yet, and `reviewAssignments` is not wired in `start.ts`. A reviewer records either with its own agent credential, with no attempt (the release runs, as the integration test does), or through the tool bridge from an attempt on the same task (a task credential is scoped to the task the review names). In the second case the reviewer's own attempt is live while it records, so the live-attempt skip always applies. That skip is right: the quiesce would wait for the reviewer's own call in flight, which is waiting for the release. The work then stays uncommitted until the owner's `release` or a later approval made outside an attempt. The owner can ask in free words in chat: the `workspace.request` chat entry describes `release` with `submissionId` (propose, then yes). ASSUMPTION: a release after the reviewer's attempt ends is left for the card that wires reviewer dispatch, since that card decides how reviewers run. It is added to "Not done" as item (9).
- **Interleavings, checked.** A `changes` or `reject` right after the approval: `#stillApproved` refuses inside the quiesce (tested). Two approvals at once: the second meets the per-task busy guard and records nothing (now tested). Approval of an older submission while the checkout holds newer work: the host refuses ("its files changed"). A replayed `submission.record` runs the hook again and is answered from the `rel-auto` record or the commit record.
- **Test added.** `workspace-ops-h12o-auto`: two approvals at once commit once (the host is held open while the second arrives; the second answers nothing and records nothing), and a submissions lookup or a live-attempts lookup that throws answers nothing, never an error, and asks nothing of the host (4 backends).
- **Mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 6 killed.** Reviewer-only check removed (4 fail). The outer catch rethrowing (4, the new test). The per-task busy guard removed (the new test fails). The command ID ignoring the cause (12). Live-attempt skip removed (4). The `start.ts` hook never releasing a review's approval (the real-git integration test fails).
- **Not done (added).** (9) A reviewer that approves from its own attempt on the task gets no automatic release; nothing retries when that attempt ends.

## P10 (tenth slice): the bounds that end a stuck first place are shown to the owner (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Two bounds keep a stuck first place in a landing queue from blocking everything forever: the director is told when the first place has held the branch for four hours, and the controller ends a reserved place that has had no approved submission for twelve hours. Both are checked only when another landing is refused behind that place, and both were invisible: the owner asking "why is nothing landing?" saw the reserved place but not since when it was idle, when it would end, or that the check waits for a refused landing. Now the landing queue view (`landing_queue` in chat, `landing.queue.list` in the API) says so in plain words: for a first reserved place with no approved submission, since when it has had none and the time the controller ends it (or that it is past the bound and the next refused landing ends it, or that the idle time is not counted yet for a record from before it existed); and for an approved first place held past the director's bound that the director was not yet told of, that it has outlasted the bound. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** Of the open items, (a) the `integration` queue showing inside the host's write needs host/git changes, (b) an `add` race judged inside the queue's write cannot be handled soundly for a first assignment (no assignment record exists to carry a revision check, so the check has nothing to compare), and (c) a timer for the idle bound would add a new background loop (a scheduler change with its own failure modes, and release on a clock would end places no landing waits behind). The smallest complete, offline-doable item that most reduces the stuck-submission risk is making the bound visible: an owner who sees "ends at 22:10, checked when a landing is refused" can take the task out at once instead of waiting or guessing. Read-only: no stored record, host or protocol change.
- ASSUMPTION: the view says plainly that nothing ends a place on a clock; making the check run on a tick is a separate, later decision (it changes when places end).
- ASSUMPTION: the lines are shown only to those who may read the queue (owner or integrator), as the view already is; `list` gains `holdMs` and `releaseMs` on `front` (the effective bounds, in milliseconds), so a project-level override added later is shown without a view change.
- **Done.** `LandingQueueOps.list` returns `front.holdMs` and `front.releaseMs`; `StatusService.landingQueueLines` adds the lines; `status.ask` summary, the `landing.queue.list` description and the interpreter prompt describe them (chat reads `landing_queue` for "why is nothing landing?" / "is the queue stuck?" and uses `landing.queue.remove` to let others land at once); `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Tests** (`landing-queue-idle-view.test.ts`, 5 tests on 4 backends = 20): since-when and end time, exactly at the bound (not before), gone after the release; a configured bound in minutes; a record without the idle time (no end time claimed); an approved place just under and at the director's bound and the line replaced once the director was told; a reader without rights is shown nothing. Neighbours: queue release, polish, reservations, status, `start-p10-*` 314/314; all chat 1447/1447; budget/fixed-part files 240/240.
- **Mutation checks** (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical): end bound `>=` to `>`; director bound `>=` to `>`; "already told" condition removed; idle line shown for any first place; end time computed from the wrong bound; `list` ignoring the configured release bound: each failed 4 tests (one per backend). One more (dropping the `idleSince === undefined` guard) is an equivalent mutant (`Date.parse(undefined)` is NaN, so the same branch is taken); the guard only narrows the type.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) A remote host has no `restack` and still refuses a landing `submission`. (2) An H12o release commit is still not a permit commit. (3) The `add` is still judged on the holder read before its write, and a first assignment at a take-out is not guarded (no record to check a revision of). (4) The `integration` operation's queue showing is still not inside the host's write. (5) Nothing commits landed or integrated files (P10c/H12o). ### P10 tenth slice: review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The view's claims were checked against the controller's code. Both bounds use "at or past" as the controller does, and only the owner and integrators see the lines (task credentials and others get nothing). Some wording promised slightly different behaviour than the code has, and one value could make the whole view fail. Fixed:

- **Which landing ends the place.** The view said "a landing refused behind it" ends a reserved place. The controller ends it only when a landing of a submission *queued* behind it is asked for (an owner's unqueued landing ends nothing), and that landing is then judged again and goes ahead, so it is not refused. The lines, the `status.ask` summary, the `landing.queue.list` description and the interpreter prompt now say this.
- **When an old record's count starts.** The view said the count starts at the next refused landing. Any write of the queue starts it (`settled` sets `idleSince` to now), so the line now says "at the next change to this queue, such as a landing asked for behind it".
- **What stops the count.** Approved work coming back drops the idle time, and it starts again if that work goes. The line now says so.
- **Who is told at the hold bound.** When no director can be told, the owner is asked. The line says so and offers landing the task as well as taking it out.
- **A view that could fail.** An idle time near the end of the date range (for example `+275760-09-13T…`) made `new Date(idle + releaseMs).toISOString()` throw, and the whole landing queue view failed. ## Q04 (fourth slice): a defect reported by mistake can be withdrawn (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card Q04 tracks defects. Until now a defect, once reported, could only be repaired, accepted as it is, or left to escalate; a report made against the wrong version, a duplicate or a misreading stayed on the unfinished lists and, once its repair failed, on the owner's Needs-you list. Now the agent that reported it, or the owner, can take it back with a reason (in chat, in any words: "that defect was a mistake, I looked at the wrong version, drop it"). The owner is shown what is about to happen and it applies on their word. The defect ends as `withdrawn`; it leaves the unfinished views and the Needs-you list. Nothing is erased: the report, its checks (a failed check stays failed), its cycle count and any owner decision stay on the record. Card Q04 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Item chosen, and why.** Of the candidates (withdrawal or editing, gating `done` or an acceptance on open defects, the P10 conflict return as a defect cycle, defects in hand-off packages, retention) withdrawal is the smallest complete one: it needs one new terminal state on the existing record, no new record kind, no change to what other tasks may do, and it closes a gap earlier reviews named (a chat report that applied at once with a wrong version had no way back). Gating `done` changes what other work may do (product choice); the P10 count lives in the landing queue (a different record by an earlier ASSUMPTION); hand-off and retention need their own services' shapes. Editing a reported defect is not built: a wrong finding is withdrawn and reported again (the report is immutable evidence).
- **Built.** `DefectService.withdraw` (operation `defect.withdraw`, a chat command, `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated): the reporting agent or the owner, a reason (required, redacted, up to 2000 characters), optional `expectedRevision`. State `withdrawn` (added to `DEFECT_STATES`); `resolution` is `{ kind: "withdrawn", by, at, reason }`. Allowed from `open`, `repair-submitted` or `escalated`; a defect already fixed, accepted as it is or withdrawn is refused `invalid_transition`; the responsible agent (unless it also reported) and any other agent are `forbidden`; another project's agent sees `not_found`. `isFinished` (resolved, overridden, withdrawn) is now the one test used by the owner override (a withdrawn finding is not a "remaining finding" of a later decision and cannot be overridden), `unresolved` (so it leaves `defect_risks` and the Needs-you list) and the `defects` view (counts it as not unresolved, says "withdrawn as mistaken"). A repair or review of a withdrawn defect is refused by the existing state rules. In chat the command is always shown first and pinned to the defect's revision (like review and override); the reason must be the owner's own words (the id comes from the view). The interpreter prompt describes it; no new status kind was added (the `defects` view's description now names the withdrawn state).
- **ASSUMPTION:** only the reporter or the owner may withdraw (the responsible agent may not, so it cannot make findings against its work disappear). Reversible in `DefectService.withdraw`. **ASSUMPTION:** withdrawal is terminal; a wrongly withdrawn finding is reported again as a new defect (reversal would need a new transition). **ASSUMPTION:** the withdrawal is recorded in the defect's own `resolution` (the defect's revision history is the record), not a separate record like the owner's override, since no decision about other findings is involved.
- **Tests.** `submissions/defects-withdraw.test.ts` (four storage backends): authority (another reviewer, the responsible agent, empty reason, stale revision), the recorded resolution and reason, replay of the same command, everything else refused on a withdrawn defect (withdraw, repair, review, override), an escalated defect withdrawn by the owner keeps its failed check and cycle count and leaves the unfinished and escalated-only reads, a later owner override does not list it as remaining, a finished defect cannot be withdrawn, the deliverable list shows the states. `api/start-defect-withdraw.test.ts` (through `startController`, SQLite): the reporter withdraws through the state API, the responsible agent is `forbidden` and another project's agent `not_found`, the owner's chat withdrawal is shown first (an invented reason is refused), applies on their word, the Needs-you list empties, `defect_risks` and the `defects` view say so.

Rejected, withdrawn and released proposals have no kept text left, so only the record goes. Notices already sent to the author (last 100 kept) and the released version's own snapshot are unaffected. An index written before this slice has no `settled` list, so the list begins with the next ended proposal (older ones are not removed). Reversible: raise the constant. This is a removal in the system's own toolbox records, not the owner's data, so it does not go through `retention.delete`.

## T08 (seventh slice): a bound on an author's proposals accepted but never released (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

T08 stays `planned` (not flipped). Branch `card-t08-s7` off origin/main `25ee9c19`. Changed: `catalog/proposals.ts` only (the author index `toolbox-proposer` gains `accepted`, `#unindex(author, id, settle, accepting)`, `PROPOSAL_LIMITS.acceptedPerAuthor` = 20). Tests: one suite and one concurrency suite in `catalog/toolbox-proposals.test.ts` on each of the four backends, and an addition to the composed `api/start-toolbox-proposals.test.ts` (state API refusal and the owner's chat). No new operation, status kind or status wording, so no interpreter prompt or `api-v1.md` change (accepting is already an owner chat command; its refusal reaches chat as the command's own refusal text).

Plain words first. Slice 6 bounded proposals that had ended, but a maintainer's "accept" without a version (the proposal is accepted, release follows later) leaves the pending count and so the 20-waiting cap, and nothing counted it: an author could keep any number of accepted-unreleased proposals, each with its kept text. Now each author may have at most 20 of them. The 21st acceptance without a version is refused (`unavailable`, with words saying to release one by accepting it again with a version); nothing is applied (the proposal stays open and waiting, no notice goes to the author). A release (accept with a version) takes the proposal off the list, which frees a place. Accepting WITH a version is never refused by the bound (it ends the proposal).

ASSUMPTION: refuse, not auto-expire. A maintainer's acceptance is a decision somebody made; discarding it silently after N days or when a newer one arrives would lose that decision and its kept text, and "fail closed" is the smaller, reversible choice (the maintainer releases one or rejects; the bound is one constant). The bound counts only entries that are still accepted-and-unreleased proposals of that author: an entry whose record is gone, ended or not an ID only leaves the list (self-healing, so a list changed by hand cannot block an author for good). The 20 matches the waiting cap.

## Q04 (fifth slice): the landing gate can require "no unfinished defects" (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card Q04 tracks defects, but nothing stopped a task from landing while a defect reported against its work was still open, waiting for a check, or escalated to the owner. A project can now require a new landing check, `defects`, next to `tests`, `review`, `qa`, `docs` and `director`: the work lands only while every defect reported against the task's deliverables is finished (repaired and found fixed, accepted as it is by the owner, or withdrawn as a mistake). A refused landing tells the author which defects are unfinished (their IDs, severity and state, and how many more). The owner asks for it in any words ("don't land anything while it still has open defects"), the change is shown first like any landing change, and `landing_settings` says what the check means. Card Q04 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Item chosen, and why.** Of the open Q04 items (editing a defect, gating `done` on open defects, the P10 conflict return as a defect cycle, hand-off packages, retention), gating is the one with an existing, tested pattern: P09's landing gate already reads QA, documents and director records through one exported reader used by both `start.ts` and the tests. It needs no new record kind, no model and no change to the owner's controls beyond one more name in a list the owner already edits by chat. A gate on the task's `done` status itself would change what every other part of the system may do and needs a product choice; this is opt-in per project (a project that does not name `defects` among its required checks is unchanged) and reversible by removing the name.
- **Built.** `DefectService.landing` and the exported reader `landingDefectsGate(service)` (`submissions/defects.ts`, exported from `submissions/index.ts`; read as the controller at the owner's level like the QA and docs readers): every defect of the task's deliverables, how many are unfinished, and the first five (escalated first, then most severe, then oldest). `LandingGate` takes an optional `defectsGate` and runs the `defects` check (`landing/landing-gate.ts`); `api/start.ts` wires it with `landingDefectsGate(defects)`. `CHECKS` gains `defects` (last), which also makes `integration.set`, the chat's check lists, `integration.default.set` and project creation accept it. Wording: the `landing_settings` view line, the interpreter prompt's list of checks, the `integration.set` field text, `api-v1.md` (regenerated after the build), getting-started and the user guide, the pi-eval task text.
- **The rule.** `pass`: no defect was reported, or all are finished. `fail`: one or more are `open`, `repair-submitted` or `escalated`; the summary says "N of M defect(s) of this task are not finished: <id> (severity, state); ... and K more". `not_run` (counts as failed): the reader is not wired, throws, returns another task's view or an inconsistent one. Read after the host's run, so a defect reported while the checks ran refuses the landing. The check is not bound to the patch ID or tree: a defect is a finding about a version of a deliverable, not about a code tree.
- **Tests.** `landing/landing-gate-defects.test.ts` (the gate alone: pass, fail with the named list and exact "more" count, every not-run path, read after the host's run, a landing with nothing to land); `submissions/defects-landing.test.ts` (four storage backends: the reader through `landingDefectsGate`: none, open, repair-submitted, fixed, escalated first, withdrawn, owner-accepted, bounded list with the exact count, another task's defects left out, unknown or malformed task ID); the end-to-end `integration/p09-landing-checks.test.ts` through `startController` with the real sandbox and a real git repository now also requires `defects`: refused while a reviewer's defect on a deliverable of the task is open (the summary names it, so the wiring was read, not "not collected"), landed once its reporter withdrew it; `status-landing-settings.test.ts` pins the new line; `model-interpreter.test.ts` pins the prompt text.
- **Mutation checks (9, built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; all caught).** `start.ts` without the `defectsGate` wiring (the end-to-end test fails); the check passes with unfinished defects (3 fail); finished defects counted (4); the list unbounded (4); escalated not first (4); another task's view accepted (1); the "and K more" count taken from the list (1); the `landing_settings` name removed (4); `defects` dropped from `CHECKS` (4).
- **ASSUMPTION:** a defect the owner accepted as it is (`overridden`) and a withdrawn one do not block a landing: the owner's own decision stands and a withdrawn finding is not one. Reversible in `DefectService.landing`. **ASSUMPTION:** the check is opt-in (not in any profile's defaults); a project that wants it names it, and since the owner's list replaces the old one the owner says every check the project should require. **ASSUMPTION:** all of the task's deliverables count, whatever their state, so a defect on a rejected deliverable blocks until it is finished.
- **Not done (said plainly).** Gating the task's own `done` status or a deliverable's acceptance on open defects (only landing is gated); a defect's edit; the P10 conflict return as a defect record (still counted in the landing queue); defects in hand-off packages and retention rules (finished defects are still kept without bound); escalation of disagreements other than a defect's cycles; periodic and incident-triggered reviews; the web project view; the link to Q02 evidence beyond references. The end-to-end test runs only where the sandbox works (Linux with bubblewrap), as the other P09 end-to-end checks do; the reader and the gate are covered everywhere.

### Q04 (fifth slice) review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. A clean-context review of the `defects` landing check. One safety problem was fixed: if a record that the task's indexes point at could not be read, the check had skipped it and could pass. It now refuses (`not_run`) instead. Three wording gaps were also fixed. Nothing else changed in how the check behaves.

- **Fixed: fail closed on a missing record.** `DefectService.landing` reused `forTask`, which skips an indexed deliverable or defect whose record is missing (right for a status view, wrong for a gate). It now reads the task's `deliverable-index` and each `defect-index` itself and throws `integrity` for a missing record; the gate turns that into `not_run` ("could not be read"). It also no longer reads each defect's last check record, which the gate never used (up to 10,000 fewer reads for a full task).
- **Fixed: wording.** The interpreter prompt's check list lacked a comma before `defects`; the `landing_settings` status-kind description (which the prompt lists) named the other five checks but not this one; the user guide's director entry said the other checks were "tests, review, QA and documents". All three now name it, and `model-interpreter.test.ts` pins the prompt and the status-kind text.
- **Checked, no change.** The unfinished states are exactly those `isFinished` leaves out (`open`, `repair-submitted`, `escalated`). Reading is complete, with no paging: the indexes are whole records, capped at 100 deliverables per task and 100 defects per deliverable. A new 4-backend case puts one unfinished defect last, behind twelve withdrawn ones on two deliverables, and checks that it is counted and listed. Only the task's own deliverables count; other tasks land through their own gates. A defect against an older version keeps blocking until a check of a newer version finds it fixed, or the owner accepts it or it is withdrawn. That is the defect workflow's own rule, so the check is not bound to the patch, as the slice's notes say. A project cannot get stuck: the owner may withdraw any unfinished defect, or accept it as it is (both work from open, waiting for a check and escalated), and may drop `defects` from the list. An escalated defect is already on the Needs-you list. A defect reported after the gate's read but before the landing's commit is not seen. The `qa`, `docs` and `director` reads have the same short window, and the next landing sees it. `CHECKS` users: `integration.set`/`integration.default.set`/project creation validate against it; stored policies are unaffected (opt-in, in no profile's defaults); the remaining lists that name `qa, docs, director` are submission roles, not landing checks; the project-creation question offers presets only (it never offered `director` either).
- **Tests.** 4-backend `defects-landing.test.ts` gained the ordering-behind-finished case and two fail-closed cases (an index naming a missing defect, and one naming a missing deliverable). **Mutation checks (7, built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; all caught):** missing defect skipped (4 fail); missing deliverable skipped (4); only `open` counted (4); the gate passes one unfinished defect (3); the prompt comma (1); the status-kind name (1); `start.ts` without the wiring (end-to-end, 1).

### Q04 (fifth slice) second review (clean context, Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. A second clean-context review of the `defects` landing check. Nothing was found that would let a landing pass with an unfinished defect through normal use. Two edges of the gate's own checks were tightened so that a malformed answer can never pass. One status line and one stale getting-started sentence were corrected.

- **Fixed: the gate's view check.** The gate accepted any `number` for the counts, so a view with `unresolved` NaN or negative passed (`NaN > 0` is false), and a view listing more items than its `unresolved` count was taken as is. The counts must now be whole numbers, `0 <= unresolved <= checked`, and at most `unresolved` items listed; otherwise `not_run`. `DefectService.landing` never builds such a view; this only closes the gate itself.
- **Fixed: an error that cannot be shown.** Every landing-gate check wrote a failed read as `String(error.message ?? error)`. A thrown value with no `toString` (a null-prototype object) or a `message` getter that throws made that line throw, so the gate's evaluation rejected instead of answering `not_run`. A shared `errorText` now returns a fixed phrase in that case; the 7 call sites (review, qa, docs, director, defects, the host run, the submission read) use it. Messages of ordinary errors are unchanged.
- **Fixed: wording.** The `landing_settings` line said owner-accepted and withdrawn defects "do not count", but the refusal's "N of M" total counts them; it now says "do not block", as the guide and the interpreter prompt do. getting-started still said P09 was planned and a required check was "enforced as far as P08 goes"; it now says the gate runs or reads each required check for the tree that would land on a local host, and that a gated landing on a remote host is refused (the card stays planned until it can).
- **Checked, no change.** Unfinished states are exactly `open`, `repair-submitted` and `escalated` (`isFinished` leaves out `resolved`, `overridden`, `withdrawn`). The 101st deliverable of a task and the 101st defect of a deliverable are refused at creation, and each creation writes the record and its index in one change list (the index under its expected revision), so no defect or deliverable can exist outside the index the gate reads; nothing deletes either record kind. The index is one record per task (no pages or shards), and a deliverable is indexed under the task it was made in. The reader reads at the owner's level, so `#readable` never skips a deliverable. The refusal names defects by ID, severity and state only (no finding text, no deliverable title): a landing agent may see the ID and severity of a defect on an owner-scoped deliverable of the same task, which is less than the `docs` check already shows (obligation titles); accepted. No timeout on the read, as for the other gates (local storage reads). Every list of landing-check names goes through `CHECKS` (`integration.set`, `integration.default.set`, project creation, the chat's settings answers); the other lists naming `qa, docs, director` are submission roles. Stored policies keep their lists; no profile default includes `defects`. The end-to-end test skips cleanly where the sandbox is unusable and fails only with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` on Linux; when it runs it asserts the exact summary naming the reported defect.
- **Tests.** `landing-gate-defects.test.ts`: the exact summaries for "and 1 more" and for exactly five (no "more"), no finding text or title in the summary, six more malformed views (NaN, negative, fractional, too many items), a thrown null-prototype object and a rejected plain string (both `not_run`). `status-landing-settings.test.ts` pins "do not block".
- **Tests run** (slot wrapper, sandbox required, offline guard, tap reporter): landing-gate (3 files), policy (6), defects-landing, start-integration, start-landing-settings, status-landing-settings, model-interpreter, landing-proposal, p09-landing-checks, d01-user-guide, h12s-landing-settings, scripts/d02-docs: 308/308, 0 skipped. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; api docs regenerate unchanged.
- **Own mutation checks (8, built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256; all caught):** items beyond `unresolved` accepted (1 fail); NaN count accepted (1); `errorText` rethrows (1); "and 1 more" dropped (1); the status line back to "do not count" (4); a missing deliverable skipped (4); `repair-submitted` counted as finished (4); `start.ts` without the `defectsGate` wiring (end-to-end, 1).

## Q02 fifth slice: a corrected owner decision invalidates QA evidence by itself (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Card Q02 stays planned. Branch `card-q02-s5` off origin/main `827cfde2`. Plain words first: until now, QA evidence judged against an owner decision that the owner later corrected (superseded, or made a dispute) was invalidated, and its re-check scheduled, only when someone asked (`qa.evidence.check`); the gate never passed it meanwhile. Now the correction itself looks at the QA evidence of every task that relies on the decision: evidence cited against the old decision is invalidated (kept, with results and reasons), a re-check goes to whoever recorded it and the owner is told, exactly as `qa.evidence.check` does.

- **Chosen item and why.** Of Q02's Not done list this is the one the fourth slice named as its remaining half ("automatic invalidation on decision changes"): it needs no new stored record, no new status kind, no host or protocol change and no policy choice, only a call from the decision service's propagation pass into the existing check. The review policy (triggers, periodic and incident reviews, whether review gates completion), counting evidence by original source, verdicts citing owner requirements and invalidation by artifacts or prerequisite tasks each need a new record or an owner-facing product choice.
- **What is built.** `DecisionDeps.taskReached` (`decisions/decisions.ts`): the propagation pass (`#propagate`, run after a decision is superseded, disputed or resolved, and again by `propagate`/`resume`) tells it each task that relies on the changed decisions, after the task's links are marked and it is notified. A failure is swallowed (a QA fault never fails or holds back a decision). `QaEvidenceService.decisionChanged(taskId)` (`submissions/qa-evidence.ts`) runs the same check as `check` with the QA service itself as the actor (`service:qa-evidence`), command ID `qa-dec-<contract version>-<evidence index revision>-<task>` (its own prefix, so it never meets the contract-change IDs); a task with no evidence is not read further, nothing stale writes nothing. `decisionChangeHook` (exported from `submissions/qa-evidence.ts`, used by `api/start.ts` and the tests: one function) reads the QA service when it runs (the decision service is made first) and swallows failures. No new operation or status kind; the interpreter prompt and the user guide now say a correction of a decision the task relies on does it by itself; `api-v1.md` unchanged (no operation changed).
- **Tests.** `submissions/qa-decision-change.test.ts` (4 backends: none/missing/idle tasks, still-standing decision writes nothing, superseded invalidates once with re-check for the recorder and notice and port told once, repeat writes nothing, disputed decision, two notices at once, two tasks at the same index revision each invalidated; plus the hook's own test); `decisions/decisions.test.ts` (4 backends: each reached task told once, a decision nobody relies on tells nothing, a hook that throws synchronously or rejects leaves the decision recorded and propagation done); `api/start-qa-evidence.test.ts` (through the real controller: an unrelated topic leaves the evidence, the correction invalidates it at once with `invalidatedBy` the service, owner notice, gate fails with the pending re-check, a later check and a replayed `decision.record` add nothing; the existing invalidation test now expects the automatic invalidation, so its `qa.evidence.check` after the correction finds nothing left). Mutation checks on the built files, each restored byte-identical (SHA-256): wiring removed from `start.js` (fails 2), QA service never set (2), decision service never tells (6), told the wrong task (6), constant command ID (4), command ID without the task (4, after the two-task test was added; it survived the first version), hook does nothing (3), hook rethrows (1).
- **Not done (said plainly).** The review policy (scope, triggers including periodic and incident, required checks, whether independent review gates completion); counting independent evidence by original source (`DeskService.independence`); a reviewer verdict that cites criteria and decision revisions and a rejection that must cite an unmet owner requirement; a team vote never overriding an owner decision in review; other dependencies (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) invalidating evidence. A decision that evidence cites but the task never linked (`decision.link`) is not reached (the propagation pass follows links); the gate still never passes it and `qa.evidence.check` still catches it. Propagation steps that stay pending (no generation service in the API process) call the hook again on each pass; that is harmless (nothing stale writes nothing). A pass run only by the dispatcher's own decision service (no hook there) leaves it to the API process's pass or an explicit check.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the check runs inside the propagation pass, not in a background loop: it is cheap (one task's index) and the owner sees the re-check straight away. Reversible: move the call to a queue.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a disputed decision counts like a superseded one for evidence (the existing staleness rule already did); the owner's resolution of the dispute does not by itself restore invalidated evidence, new evidence does.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the re-check's `requestedBy` is `service:qa-evidence`, as for contract changes.

- **Review (clean-context, fifth slice).** Fixed: (1) the dispatcher's own decision service (`api/dispatch-compose.ts`, whose `decisions.resume` loop finishes a propagation the API's pass left pending) had no hook, so a task the API's pass could not tell (a notice refused for backpressure, a link-marking fault) was finished by the dispatcher without its QA evidence being looked at, and nothing would look again once the propagation was done; `ComposeInput.decisionTaskReached` now carries the same hook, built once in `api/start.ts` for both services. (2) A failure of the check was swallowed with no trace; `decisionChangeHook` takes an optional error sink and `api/start.ts` passes `onInternalError` (redacted), so a missed invalidation is visible to the operator; a sink that throws is still never the decision's error. Tests: `api/start-qa-evidence.test.ts` (a correction recorded by a decision service with no hook and no generation service stays pending with the evidence current; one tick of the controller's dispatcher finishes it and the evidence is invalidated by `service:qa-evidence` with a re-check for the recorder), `submissions/qa-decision-change.test.ts` (the sink receives the failure, a throwing sink is contained, a working check reports nothing). Checked and not a bug: the hook runs after the decision's own commit (record and resolve commit before `#propagateSafely`), after the task's links are marked and its notice accepted; the only decision changes are `decision.record` (supersede, dispute) and `decision.resolve`, all of which propagate; the reach is the decision's dependents (at most 200 tasks per decision, walked serially as the pass already was; a task with no evidence costs three reads); a committed `qa.evidence.check` always rewrites the evidence index, so a `qa-dec-` ID can never be met again by a later, different invalidation (no wrong replay), and a concurrent check of the same task answers from `lostRace` without a second notice (notices are keyed by re-check ID); the re-check goes to the recorder as for `check` (a removed agent's re-check stays pending and the gate keeps failing, as before); the gate recomputes staleness on every read, so it never passes stale evidence whatever the hook did. Mutations killed (built files, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): dispatcher decision service without the hook, start not passing it, sink not called, hook skipped while the generation step waits (fails the two start tests that rely on the API pass), command ID without the index revision (fails on all four backends).

- **Second review (clean-context, fifth slice).** Fixed: the propagation pass called the QA hook for every reached task on every pass, and the dispatcher passes each pending propagation again on every tick (`decisions.resume` in `dispatch/loops.ts`). So a correction that stayed pending (a notice held back by backpressure on one task) re-read the QA evidence of up to 200 tasks on each tick, and a QA check that kept failing sent up to 200 internal-fault reports on each tick. Now a task's propagation step records `qa: true` once the hook has run (`decisions/records.ts` `PropagationStep.qa`), and later passes skip it. `decisionChangeHook` rejects while the QA service is not attached yet (the step stays open and the next pass looks again, nothing reported). A failed check is reported to the sink and the hook resolves, so each failure is reported once per task and correction. The gate's staleness read and `qa.evidence.check` still catch evidence a failed check missed. Tests: `decisions/decisions.test.ts` (4 backends: a correction kept pending over three passes tells each task's hook once, a task whose hook rejected is told again on the next pass, finishing tells nobody again), `submissions/qa-decision-change.test.ts` (the hook with no service rejects with `unavailable` and reports nothing). Checked and not a bug: a repeat call (API pass, then dispatcher) is idempotent (nothing stale writes nothing; the index revision in the command ID changes after each committed check); a hook failure never stops `resume` or holds a propagation pending (the QA step does not count toward `done`); the sink is `redactedSink` (`api/start.ts`); a 201st task can never rely on a decision (`decision.link` refuses past `tasksPerDecision`), so every dependent is reached; `decisionChanged` writes QA evidence, re-checks and owner notices, never decisions, so it cannot loop back, and propagation holds no lock while it runs; the check runs inside the owner's `decision.record`/`decision.resolve` request, like the notices it follows (the first review's ASSUMPTION), and a correction superseding several decisions at once walks the union of their dependents, as before. Own mutation checks (built files, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): step marker ignored (fails 4), marker never set (4), marker set when the hook rejects (4), hook resolves with no service (1), no-service case reported to the sink (1).

## H12o (sixth slice): the submissions view says whether an approved submission was committed (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Since the automatic release, an approval usually makes the platform commit by itself, but nothing said whether it had: the owner could not tell "approved and committed" from "approved, release refused or never made" without finding the release request. Now the task's `submissions` view tells it, for approved code, in plain words: the commit (short ID, time, and whether it is a review-gate permit commit or a plain platform commit that a landing requiring the permit will not take), or "not made yet" (naming a release request still open on the checkout, or saying the work stays uncommitted until a release request commits it). Card H12o stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** Of the open items (a remote host's `release` of a submission needs a worker-protocol field; `commitOnce`/A06 is a redesign of a gate; PLAN.md and reading a Q01 acceptance as an approval are product decisions), this is the smallest complete, offline-doable one, and it is item (8) of the last slice's "Not done" (a failed or missing release was invisible): a missing view, read-only, no stored field, no change to what lands.
- **Built.** `StatusDeps.submissionRelease` (`commit(submissionId)`, `open(taskId)`, wired in `api/start.ts` to `WorkspaceOpService.submissionCommit` and `openFor`, both of which take no caller and create nothing); `StatusService.#commitWords` adds one sentence to a code submission's line in `submissionLines`. `status.ask`, `submissions` kind text, the interpreter prompt (it also names the `workspace.request` release as the way to commit, proposal first, as the chat entry already says) and `api-v1.md` describe it.
- **Fail closed and private.** The sentence is added only in the branch shown to the owner and to the code's author (the branch for other readers, which already hides review state, is unchanged and reads nothing), and only for code with an approval. A read that throws says "could not be read just now", never "not made yet". A commit recorded before the permit field existed reads as a plain commit (`permitted` absent is not claimed as a permit). Without the dependency (an old composition) nothing is added.
- **Wording.** No existing line's text changed; the sentence is appended after the sign-off/approval-binding text and before the evidence text. Neighbour tests asserting the submissions text were run: 1795/1795 across submissions-q01b-view, start-q01b-view, api.test, all chat tests, status.test, d01-user-guide, h12o-submission-commit and workspace-ops-h12o-auto.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the "not made yet" case for approved one-agent code ("review not required") is told the same way; there the owner's `release` commits it, and the sentence says a release request (the owner's) does.

## Q03 slice 8: a repeat of a QA check makes up the notices and the documentation check its first run lost (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-q03-s8` off origin/main `2a85de66`. Card status is NOT changed (Q03 stays planned).

ASSUMPTION: of Q03's open items this is the smallest complete one that needs no model server, no new record kind, no new bridge tool, and does not change what `done` or a release gate means: the "next slice" note's own leftover "a repeat of `qa.evidence.check` that invalidated nothing new does not re-run the lost-evidence check". It tightens a loss window (a stop between the check's write and its follow-ups) like slice 6 did for the stale-document notice. Documents gating a release or `done` change two gates; own record kinds change every check that reads obligations; reading a document's text needs a decision on formats and what is compared; bridge tools spend the fixed part's budget. Nothing waits on Rob.

- **Plain words.** `qa.evidence.check` writes (it invalidates stale QA evidence and schedules a re-check for each), and only after the write it tells the owner about each re-check and calls the documentation service, which flags documents verified against code whose QA gate no longer passes. A stop between the write and those calls lost them for good: a repeat of the command found nothing stale and did nothing, and no later check would call them. Now a repeat of the same command (same caller, same command ID, which the automatic checks and an agent retrying use) reads the command's own audit entry, takes the evidence it invalidated (at most 50 records) and sends the follow-ups again: the re-check notice (only for a re-check still pending, same text, same notice ID `qa-recheck:<id>`) and the `invalidated` port (the documentation check, whose command IDs are `doc-evidence-lost:<id>` and so do not double). A repeat after some other evidence went stale meanwhile, which replays the write, does the same.
- **Where.** `QaEvidenceService.#checkTask` calls the new `#makeUp` on both repeat paths (`submissions/qa-evidence.ts`); the notice text moved into one helper so the made-up notice reads like the original. No new port, record, operation or stored field: an entry written by older code, or one that cannot be read, sends nothing; the answer of a repeat is unchanged (`replayed` and empty lists as before). Read-only: it writes nothing, and what it sends comes from the stored command and records, never from the caller's words. Another caller sending the same command ID, or a new command ID, is a different command and sends nothing.
- **ASSUMPTION:** every repeat of the command sends again (no stored "sent" marker); the controller keeps one notice per notice ID and the documentation check is keyed by evidence, so a repeat does nothing twice. Reversible by not calling `#makeUp`.
- **Tests.** New `submissions/qa-check-makeup.test.ts` on all four backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL): no evidence invalidated, nothing sent; a check whose sends all fail; another caller's same command ID and a new command ID send nothing; the same check sent again delivers both notices with the original text and runs the documentation hook for both records, the answer unchanged; a further repeat doubles nothing; a replay after other evidence went stale meanwhile still runs the hook; re-checks the new evidence settled are not announced again while the hook still runs.
- **Mutation checks** (built `qa-evidence.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256), each failed the new test on all four backends: no make-up when nothing is stale; a settled re-check still announced; the operation looked up by the wrong ID; the documentation hook not called; the notice ID different on each send; no notices at all; no make-up on the replay path. Survived, judged equivalent: dropping the `state === "invalidated"` check on a listed record (a record in the entry's list can never go back to current).
- **NOT done / leftovers:** nothing re-sends by itself (a repeat of the command is still what makes it up; no sweep); recorded QA evidence on an older code submission after newer code was tested still flags the documents for the older code (needs a per-task code index); everything else Q03 listed (documents gating a release or `done`, own record kinds for support and promotional material, reading the document's text, bridge tools for the docs agent; the D01 user guide's documentation step); the 30-document cap of `task_docs`.

The ports of `qa-contract-change.test.ts` and `qa-decision-change.test.ts` now de-duplicate like the controller (one notice per ID, one documentation check per evidence) because their automatic repeats now send the follow-ups again. **Tests run (through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, sandbox on, forced build first):** `qa-check-makeup` 4/4 backends, `qa-evidence` 8/8, `qa-contract-change` 9/9, `qa-decision-change` 9/9, `doc-auto-checks` 4/4, `doc-obligations` 8/8, `qa-project-view` 8/8, `start-qa-evidence` 7/7, `start-docs` 1/1, `start-docs-verify` 1/1; check:deps, licenses:check, roadmap:check pass.
- **Review (clean-context, eighth slice).** Fixed: (1) the automatic checks did not make up anything after a stop. Their command ID names the evidence index revision and a committed check rewrites the index, so the next `contractChanged` (a replay of `contract.set`) or `decisionChanged` (the next propagation pass, since the `qa` step marker was never set) had a new command ID, found nothing stale and looked up no entry; only two calls at the same moment reached `#makeUp`. Now a call that finds nothing stale also looks up the automatic checks (both `qa-auto-` and `qa-dec-`, same contract version) at the index revision before the current one, the only check that can have written it, and makes up its follow-ups (`#lastAutomatic`). A record added since moves the index on, so nothing is looked up then. The cost is two operation reads per automatic call, plus a bounded make-up (at most 50 records) only right after such a check; `contractChanged` runs once per `contract.set` and `decisionChanged` once per task and correction, never per tick. (2) `#makeUp` now also requires the entry to be a `qa.evidence.check` (the caller's own command ID used for another command first could otherwise be read if its detail happened to carry `taskId` and `invalidated`). (3) The `invalidated` port comment said it is not called for a repeat. The ports of `qa-contract-change`/`qa-decision-change` de-duplicate by notice ID and evidence, like the controller; their assertions still prove that the right records are told and hooked, and that no other notice ID is sent. The notes above say the entry-type mutation failed the first test, but replacing the type check with `true` failed no test. Found outside this slice (not fixed, needs its own design): one `qa.evidence.check` writes 2 changes per record plus the index, and storage allows at most 100 changes per operation (`LIMITS.perOperation`). With 50 or more records stale at once (a task may hold 200), every `check`, `contractChanged` and `decisionChanged` of that task fails with `invalid_command`, so nothing is invalidated, no re-check is scheduled and the owner is not told. - **Q02 batch fix (a check over 50 or more stale evidence records, and a supersede over more than 100 pending re-checks, no longer fail).** The bug (found by the eighth-slice reviewer): one `qa.evidence.check` wrote 2 changes per stale record plus 1 for the index, and storage takes at most 100 changes per operation, while a task may hold 200 records; with 50 or more stale at once every `check`, `contractChanged` and `decisionChanged` failed with `invalid_command`, so nothing was invalidated, no re-check scheduled and the owner not told (the landing gate still blocked, because it reads staleness live: a liveness and visibility bug, not a bypass). `qa.recheck.supersede` had the same limit with more than 100 pending re-checks. Now: (1) a check writes at most `QA_LIMITS.chunk` (40) records per operation and loops (at most 12 chunks, so 200 records fit with room); each chunk is its own command. Chunk 0 keeps the command's own ID (so everything that read that ID still works); chunk n is `<principal>:<sha256 of "<commandId>:chunk:<n>">`. A repeat of the same command finds the chunks already written (they answer as a repeat, their follow-ups are made up by the existing `#makeUp`) and carries on with the next; it continues only after a full chunk (a shorter one finished the first run's work, so a pure repeat still answers as before: nothing written, `replayed`). (2) The answer reports the whole run (all invalidated records and re-checks, including those of chunks an earlier run wrote when the call carried on). (3) The owner notice per re-check and the documentation hook are sent right after the chunk that wrote them, once per record (the ports are keyed by record, as before). (4) The slice-8 "index revision before the current one" lookup cannot work with chunks (each chunk moves the revision). Replaced by a stored marker: the automatic checks write `auto: { id, version, chunks }` into the evidence index in the same operation (absent on any other write of the index: new evidence, a caller's check; read as "nothing owed" when absent). A later automatic call with the same contract version first makes up the follow-ups of every chunk the marker names, then looks for stale records; so the old behaviour (a call after a stop makes up the lost follow-ups; a record added since owes nothing) is kept, and the case a stop in the middle of an automatic check (some chunks written, then the next call has a new command ID because the index moved) is resumed too. (5) `submitted` (supersede) settles at most 80 re-checks per operation in the same way: chunk 0 is `qa-sup:<submission>`, later ones `qa-sup:<submission>:<n>`; it keeps looking until nothing is due. A repeat now also settles re-checks that became due after an earlier call (the old code answered `[]` and left them to the next recorded evidence): only more liveness. ## Q04 (sixth slice): a defect's finding or severity can be corrected before it is finished (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Card Q04 tracks defects. A defect that is real but was recorded with the wrong wording or the wrong severity could only be withdrawn and reported again, which also started its repair count over. Now the agent that reported it, or the owner, can correct the finding text, the severity, or both, in any words in chat ("that defect should say the restore step, not the backup step", "that one is minor, not major"). The owner is shown what is about to happen and it applies on their word. Only the finding and the severity change; the state, the cycles used, the checks, the evidence and any owner decision stay. Each correction is kept on the defect (who, when, the text or severity it replaced, the reason if given), and the defects view tells the owner a defect was edited (how many times, by whom last, and the severity it was reported with). Card Q04 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Item chosen, and why.** Of the open items (editing a defect, gating `done`, the P10 conflict return as a defect cycle, hand-off packages, retention) editing is the smallest complete one that needs no product decision and no new record kind: it is the twin of the withdrawal (same authority, same states, same chat pattern) and closes the gap the fourth slice named ("a wrong finding is withdrawn and reported again"), which lost the cycle count. Gating `done` changes what other work may do (a product choice); the P10 count lives in the landing queue by an earlier ASSUMPTION; hand-off and retention need those services' own shapes.
- **Built.** `DefectService.edit` (operation `defect.edit`, a chat command, `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated): `id`, `finding` and/or `severity` (at least one), optional `reason` (redacted, up to 2000) and `expectedRevision`. Works while the defect is `open`, `repair-submitted` or `escalated`; a resolved, accepted-as-is or withdrawn defect is `invalid_transition`. Who: the owner (not a task-limited credential), or the agent that reported it only while no check of a repair has failed (never once escalated) and when it did none of the work of the repair under check; the responsible agent is `forbidden`, another project's agent or a client `not_found` (the same rules, same code, as `withdraw`). A value equal to the current one is not an edit (only what changed is kept in the entry) and an edit that changes nothing is `invalid_command`. New stored field `edits` on the defect (list of `{ by, at, previousFinding?, previousSeverity?, reason? }`), absent on every defect never edited and read as empty when absent or not a list; at most 20 (`MAX_DEFECT_EDITS`), the 21st is `invalid_transition` saying to withdraw and report again. The audit entry of the command carries the defect, whether the text changed and the new severity (no text). A repeat of the same command ID is answered from its record; another payload under it is `command_conflict`; a pinned edit racing another edit, a repair, a withdrawal or an override applies for exactly one (the rest are `stale_revision` or `invalid_transition`). Records made earlier keep what they saw: an owner decision's `remaining` list and the failed checks are not rewritten. In chat the command is always shown first and pinned to the defect's revision (a model-supplied revision is replaced by the one listed, as for the withdrawal); the corrected finding and the reason must be the owner's own words, the severity is a fixed choice (critical, major, minor) and the ID comes from the view, so a model cannot hand over text or a reason the owner did not say (the proposal shows the severity before anything applies). The interpreter prompt describes it with example sentences; the `defects` status kind's description names the edited line (no new status kind, so `status.ask`'s kind list is unchanged). The user guide has a paragraph ("A defect worded wrongly", bold term `correct`, also in the D01 term list).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the authority is exactly the withdrawal's (reporter under the same limits, owner always), because a reporter who could soften a confirmed or repaired finding could do what the withdrawal rules were written to prevent; reversible in `DefectService.edit`. **ASSUMPTION:** at most 20 edits per defect, each keeping what it replaced (about 40 KB at worst); the number is a constant. **ASSUMPTION:** the reason is optional (an owner saying "change it to minor" gave none; one that is given must be in their words). **ASSUMPTION:** a correction does not reopen or restart anything (no cycle change, no new check): a repair already under check is judged against the finding as now written, and the earlier text is on the edit; the defect's evidence list and `findingEvent` are not editable (they are references, not wording).
- **Tests.** `submissions/defects-edit.test.ts` (four storage backends): arguments (nothing named, empty, too long, unknown severity or field, empty reason), access (another reviewer, the responsible agent, another project's agent, a client, a credential for another task, the owner's task credential), stale revision, no-change refusals, a refused call changes nothing and read views create nothing (revision unchanged), the recorded edit and a replay and a conflicting replay, severity-only by the owner, redaction of finding and reason, a repair under check (reporter allowed, then refused once it did the repair's work, owner allowed), a failed check (reporter refused, owner edits an escalated defect: state, cycles and checks unchanged; an earlier owner decision keeps its text; `unresolved` shows the new text; repair-again keeps the edits and the count), finished defects (withdrawn, accepted, fixed) refused, the 20-edit bound, a hand-edited `edits` value, races (edit against edit pinned, against withdrawal, against an override), and the operation table (arguments, missing command ID, replay, conflict). `api/start-defect-edit.test.ts` (through `startController`, SQLite): the state API (reporter applies, responsible agent `forbidden`, another project's agent `not_found`, bad arguments, views read-only, replay), the chat (a severity change shown first with a model-supplied stale revision, then stale after the reporter edited meanwhile and applied when said again; an invented finding, an invented reason and an unknown ID refused; the owner's own words for finding and reason proposed and applied), an escalated defect corrected by the owner (still escalated, failed check kept, still on the Needs-you list, then finished by a withdrawal and no longer editable), and the defects view lines. `chat/model-interpreter.test.ts` pins the prompt sentence.

### Q04 sixth slice, review (2026-11-22)

- **Authority.** `defect.edit` uses the withdrawal's checks line for line: the owner's own credential (a task-limited owner credential is `forbidden`), otherwise only the reporting agent; reading goes through the same `#load` (another project's agent or a client `not_found`); the reporter is refused once `cycles > 0` or the defect is escalated, and when it is a contributor of the recorded repair version (worked out from the deliverable and that version's record, as the withdrawal does; a missing version record is an `integrity` error, so it does not pass). A severity change cannot open a landing: the `defects` landing check, escalation and the cycle limit read the state only, never the severity (now pinned by a test: after a reporter's downgrade the defect still stops the landing). A reporter correcting a defect whose repair is under check was kept, since the same reporter may withdraw it outright.
- **Fixed: a message that is only "yes" never applied a proposal.** Every intent's evidence had to be at least two words and six characters (`evidenceStrong`, `chat/interpreter.ts`), and the planner (`chat/chat.ts`, the own-words check in `#plan`) applied that to `apply_proposal` and `discard_proposal` too. The real interpreter copies the owner's words as evidence, so for the message "yes" (or "ok", "no") the evidence is that one word and the turn was refused as not in the owner's own words, although the guide says to say yes in any words. Now, for those two intents only, evidence that is the owner's whole own message (ignoring case, white space and punctuation at either end; quoted lines are not part of it) is accepted (`evidenceWholeMessage`). The same word inside a longer message is still refused. Answers to a pending question (`answer` intents) keep the two-word rule; a one-word answer there is still refused (not changed here). `api/start-revoke.test.ts` sent a bare "yes" to a stale proposal and only checked it was not applied: it was refused for its wording before, now for being stale.
