Plain words first. The review's change to the chat's own-words rule (a message that is only "yes" or "no" now counts) was checked from scratch. It is kept, narrowed: such a message names no proposal, so it counts only while exactly one proposal (chat proposals and policy edits together) is open; with several open the chat asks which one (listing them) and does nothing. Before, the model's pick among several open proposals would have been applied on a bare "yes".

- **Safety walk of the relaxed rule.** (a) Quoted material: `splitQuoted` moves `>` lines and fenced blocks out of the owner's text before planning, so `words` never contains them; a message that is wholly quoted has no own text and is refused at `submit` (`invalid_command`, asserted). Quoted text can still steer the model's choice of proposal, which the one-open rule now removes for a bare answer. (b) A message from someone else: `#owner` refuses every non-owner (and task-limited owner) credential before anything is read. Web buttons send `approval.proposal.accept` commands or call `applyProposal` directly, never a bare `apply_proposal` by words, so they are unaffected. (c) Several open proposals: now asked (above); a stale proposal whose apply failed stays `open`, as do coordinator proposals, so this case is common, not rare. `#apply` still refuses another owner's proposal, a discarded one and one drawn up in the same message, and revision pins refuse a stale one. (d) "no": same rule; harmless either way. (e) A model can only claim evidence equal to the owner's whole own text, so it gains nothing over the owner's actual words. (f) `answer` intents still need two words; a bare "yes" to a clarifying question is refused. That is a small chat-control gap, left open (see below). (g) No operation needs an explicit confirmation phrase: every proposal-first operation is confirmed by any owner agreement, so the old two-word rule did not protect high-risk proposals; the shown preview and the pins do. (h) `evidenceStrong` has two other uses (the `answer` check in `#plan`, and every other intent); only apply/discard are relaxed.

### Q03 slice 9 review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5 clean-context reviewer, 2026-11-22)

- **Paging arithmetic and order: correct.** The page is `items.slice(after, min(total, after + 30))`; the "Showing" line appears only for `after > 0`; "nothing comes after" for `after >= total`; the "more" line only when documents remain, with K = min(30, remaining). The order is a total order between asks: `Array.prototype.sort` is stable and the input is the project's stored document index (one ID list, the same on every backend), so documents of equal rank keep the index order and pages never overlap or skip while nothing changes. Access comes before any count: the project view's list refuses a caller who may not read the project's tasks before anything is counted, and the task view checks the task right first; an invalid `after` is refused before any read and says nothing about the project. Chat passes the number through; a non-integer, negative, huge (2^60, 1e21) or text value is refused with the view's own message, as `thinking`'s `after` is (a read needs no own-words check).
- **Fixed: the prompt asked for something a model cannot do.** The interpreter sees only the owner's message, focus, open proposals and pending question, never the view's earlier answer, so "when they end with ... ask again with after M ... ask the same view again with after M" could not be followed: a model asked "show me the rest" had no M. The sentence now gives a rule a model can apply from the owner's words alone: the next or other documents, or the second page, is after 30; the third page after 60 (30 for each page before it); a number the owner gives is used as said ("the documents after 60" is after 60, "from document 61" is after 60). The guide's project paragraph now says the same, plainly: asking for the next ones shows documents 31 to 60; for later ones give the number the view gave or the page, since NimbleNewt does not remember which page you saw last. The task paragraph points to it. The start-docs test comment that said the model takes the count from the view's last line is corrected.
- **Tests added.** `d01-user-guide.test.ts`: the guide's three quoted sentences ("show me the next documents", "show the documents after 60", "the third page of documents") go through the real launcher, the real `ModelInterpreter` and the terminal chat on a project with 61 documents (a stand-in plays the model, applying the prompt's rule, and the test checks the prompt carries the rule); each printed answer holds the state API's own first three lines for after 30 or 60. `status/task-docs.test.ts` (4 backends): after 0 equals the first page; after 1 shows exactly 30 (documents 2 to 31), with no "more" line, in the same order as the first two pages joined; after 29 starts at the 30th; after 1000 says nothing comes after. `model-interpreter.test.ts` pins the new sentence.

### Chat answers slice (2026-11-22): one-word answers to a question, and agreements that name no proposal

Plain words first. Two gaps recorded at the end of the Q04 sixth slice are closed. (A) A one-word reply ("default", "finish") to a question the chat asked was refused as not in the owner's own words. (B) "Yes please" with several proposals open applied the model's pick.

- **(A) Design.** An `answer` intent whose evidence is not a phrase (`evidenceStrong` false) now counts only when (1) the evidence is a stretch of the owner's own text (quoted lines are already gone) and the owner's WHOLE message, (2) the chat reads the question it recorded for that turn (`#choiceSaid`: the owner's own, unanswered, held commands, with its recorded choices and option labels) and the owner's whole message equals exactly one recorded choice, or exactly one option label (the whole label, the part before ": ", or the words in its brackets), ignoring case and end punctuation, and (3) that recorded choice is the one the model reported. Several matches, none, "yes" to a question with no yes choice, or a model claim that differs: refused as before ("not in your own words"). The answer actually carried on is the recorded choice, through the unchanged `#expandAnswer`. Phrases (two words, six characters) keep the old rule. A single "yes" for a single pending proposal is the earlier slice's rule and is unchanged.
- **(B) Design.** For apply/discard with several proposals open (chat proposals and policy edits, read in full up to 100), the chat asks which unless the owner's words single out the model's pick: a word of at least three letters (or any number) that appears in that proposal's summary and in no other open proposal's, or the proposal ID written out. No word list: the open proposals alone decide. "yes please" shares a word with none, so it asks; "the Oak one" picks the proposal that mentions Oak. A pick that is not open is asked about when the words are not a phrase and otherwise left to the stale-proposal checks; 100 or more open ask always (fail closed). One open proposal: unchanged.
- **ASSUMPTION:** option numbers ("2") are not accepted, because the chat does not number its options. **ASSUMPTION:** a yes/no to a question accepts only a literal yes or no among the choices (none of the chat's questions has one); no general agree-to-single-choice word list was made. **ASSUMPTION:** no prompt change: the model already copies the owner's words as evidence and the chat no longer relies on its claim. The guide's "Say yes" sentence gained the two matching sentences.
- **Not done:** a reply by number or by "the second one" in one word; a question whose single choice a bare "yes" accepts; the interpreter does not see an earlier answer (unchanged).
- **Tests:** `chat/chat.test.ts` two suites on 4 backends (agreement among several open: asks, nothing applied, quoted words refused, a word of the other proposal asks, the proposal's own word applies; one-word answer: yes, ok, near-miss, a different claimed choice, a word inside a longer message, a wholly quoted word, a quoted second choice refused, label word answers, second answer refused); `api/start-chat-answers.test.ts` through the running controller and the real `ModelInterpreter` with a deliberately careless stand-in that never receives words the owner did not say.
- **Effect on older tests:** about a dozen existing tests said "yes, do that" with stale or look-alike proposals still open; with several open that now asks, so those tests name the proposal by its ID (or a word only it has) as the owner can. Real owners with leftover open proposals are asked which one until they drop the old ones: this is the intended behavior, not a side effect.
- **Mutation checks (built `chat.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 7 of 8 caught:** model's claimed choice not compared; several matching options accepted; whole-message requirement dropped; a word shared by all proposals counted as naming one; a pick that is not open trusted; an ID written out accepted whatever the words; an already answered question answerable again. NOT caught: the 100-open-proposals cutoff (needs 100 open proposals; fail-closed edge left untested).
- **Tests run (after `tsc --build --force`, stale dist tests removed, sandbox + offline guard, one slot):** every `chat/*.test`, needs-you-answer, every `start-defect*`/`start-defects*`, start-commands, start-revoke, start-jobs, start-chat-answers, model-interpreter, chat-budget, model-budget, workspace-chat, d01-user-guide, scripts/d02-docs: 1563/1563.

#### Chat answers slice: review (clean context, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The review kept the design and narrowed it in five places where the chat could still act on something the owner had not clearly said.

- **Fixed (A), the question answered:** a one-word reply could carry on any unanswered question of the owner, including an older one that a later question had replaced (the model is shown only the one it is waiting on). It now answers only the question the chat is waiting on now (`context.awaiting`).
- **Fixed (A), labels:** option labels can hold names someone else wrote (a responsibility, task or item name in brackets). A word of agreement or refusal ("yes", "ok", "no" and a few like them) now answers only when it is one of the question's recorded choices, never through a label.
- **Fixed (B), contradictory words:** a message that names the model's pick and also points to another open proposal (a word that proposal's text has and the pick's has not, or its ID) was accepted; it now asks, unless the same message also agrees to or drops that other proposal (as in "no Elm, yes Ash").
- **Fixed (B), small words:** a common word ("the", "that", "one", "please" and similar, a short fixed list) that happened to occur in only one proposal's text counted as naming it; such words now name nothing and point nowhere. One older test (`release-owner-words`, "confirm that approval" with two approvals open whose first lines are equal) had passed only because "that" appeared in one of them; it now names the proposal by its ID.
- **Fixed (B), unread policy edits:** a list of policy edits that could not be read counted as none open, so a bare "yes" with one chat proposal applied it. Now the chat asks and accepts only the proposal's ID written out until the list can be read.
- **Kept:** no expiry on the waiting question (an owner's exact one-word answer to the question the chat is waiting on is an answer, however old); the question listing several open proposals now also says the ID names one. The guide sentence says all of this.
- **Tests:** two new suites in `chat/chat.test.ts` on 4 backends (the replaced question, a bare "ok" against a label "(ok)", two labels "(backup)" whichever the model names; unread edits ask and the ID applies; 100 open ask and 99 open apply with the pick named; contradictory words and another proposal's ID ask; one message agreeing to one and dropping the other does both; plain words name nothing).
- **Own mutation checks (built `chat.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 8 of 8 caught:** waiting-question check removed; agreement-word rule removed; 100-open `>=` to `>` (the slice's own uncaught one); unread edits taken as none; plain-word list ignored; several matching options accepted (caught after the test tried both IDs); the same-message exemption removed; the contradiction check removed.

#### Chat answers slice: second review (clean context, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. The second review kept the design and closed one older gap: a message that was only "no" could agree to the one open proposal if the model misread it as a yes.

- **Fixed, a bare "no" read as yes (from the Q04 sixth slice, not this slice):** with one proposal open, the whole-message rule accepted a one-word message for agreeing and for dropping alike, so a model that turned "no" into `apply_proposal` had it applied. The chat now reads that one word itself: a message that is only a word of refusal ("no", "nope", "nah", "cancel", "stop", "never", "don't") never applies a proposal, and one that is only a word of agreement ("yes", "ok", "sure" and the like) never drops one; it asks instead and nothing is done. The two short lists only refuse, never make the chat act, so they are no special phrases; the existing agreement list of the waiting-question rule is now their union (it gained "never" and "don't", which only narrows).
- **Judged and kept, the small-words list:** it only stops common words from counting as naming a proposal or as pointing to another; the rule that decides (a word only one open proposal has, or its ID) is general. It can make the chat ask more often, never act more often.
- **Judged and kept, "no Elm, yes Ash":** each intent still passes its own check against the owner's own words. Which way the owner meant a phrase ("not Ash" read as apply) is the model's reading here exactly as it is with one proposal open ("don't apply Ash"); the chat cannot tell that without guessing at meaning from word lists, and each proposal was shown to the owner before. Only the one-word case above is decided by the chat.
- **Judged and kept, no expiry on the waiting question:** a one-word reply counts only for the newest question still open, only when it is exactly one recorded answer and the model reports the same one; what it resumes is the owner's own held command, which still goes through its proposal or its checks. A phrase answer has never had an expiry either.
- **Usability:** the guide's "Say yes" sentence stays true (a bare yes or no while one proposal is open still works); the new question says what the word was and asks whether to go ahead or drop it.
- **Tests:** `chat/chat.test.ts` new suite on 4 backends ("no", "No!", "nope", "Nah.", "cancel", "don't" read as apply ask and apply nothing; "yes", "OK.", "sure" read as drop ask and keep it; a bare "no" still drops and a bare "yes" still applies); `api/start-chat-answers.test.ts` stand-in that reads "nope" as agreement: asked, nothing created.
- **Own mutation checks (built `chat.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 8 of 9 caught:** refusal-word guard off; drop guard off; same-message exemption given to every proposal; small-words list ignored; waiting-question check off; agreement words answering through a label; 100-open `>=` to `>`; several matching options accepted. Not caught: dropping the whole-message test of a one-word answer, which is equivalent (the recorded-question match already compares the owner's whole message).

## Q02 sixth slice: a reviewer's verdict can cite the criteria version, the decisions and the unmet requirement (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Card Q02 stays planned. Branch `card-q02-s6` off origin/main `07626ec3`. Plain words first: the card says a verdict cites the current acceptance-criteria and decision revisions, that a rejection must cite an unmet owner requirement, and that work bound to a superseded decision fails review. Until now a review (`submission.record`, kind `review`) carried only approve, changes or reject. Now a reviewer may add what it judged against, and the controller checks it.

- **Chosen item and why.** Of Q02's Not done list this is a pure service-level addition with no new stored record kind, no host or protocol change, no new status kind and no product decision. Periodic and incident-triggered reviews need a scheduler and a policy record (a design decision); counting evidence by original source has nothing to count in QA evidence (it is bound to submissions, not desk copies); gating `done` or landing on QA is already done elsewhere (P09). The sentence in the interpreter prompt was not needed: there is no new owner control and no new status kind, so `chat/model-interpreter.ts` and the chat files are untouched.
- **What is built.** A review may carry `criteriaRevision` (the task contract version, 0 when none), `decisions` (up to 20 different decision IDs) and `unmet` (up to 500 characters). Rules (`submissions/review-citation.ts`, called from `SubmissionService.record`):
  - A verdict that cites anything cites `criteriaRevision`; `decisions` or `unmet` without it are refused.
  - The version must be the contract's current one, else `stale_revision` (read the criteria and judge again). Each decision must be one of the task or its project and in force (a superseded one is refused and the current one named); the write checks the decisions have not changed meanwhile.
  - A rejection that cites must name `unmet` (the owner requirement not met); no other verdict may carry `unmet`.
  - An approval that cites must name every decision the task relies on (`decision.link`) and is refused while one of them was superseded (C08: work bound to a superseded decision fails review). A rejection or a request for changes is not held to that (it is the right answer to such work).
  - The checks run when the record is made, after the runner looked for a repeat, so a repeat of the same command after the contract moved on answers the first record. A review that cites nothing is unchanged (nothing extra is stored or checked). Access rules are as before (role title alone grants nothing, no task read is "no such task", no review of one's own work, and a code or QA submission carries none of these fields).
  - Kept on the review record (`criteriaRevision`, `decisions`, `decisionVersions`, `unmet`) and in the subject's verdict list; `approvalOf` answers `cited` for the newest review (the newest decides what is shown); absent fields read safely.
  - Reached through `submission.record` (state API; the op summary and docs name the three arguments), the worker bridge whitelist and the Pi tool schema (three optional parameters; the description is unchanged).
  - **Status line.** The `submissions` view's line for a code submission adds, when its newest review cites: `(it cites criteria version N and decision dec-... vK; unmet requirement: "...")`. Owner and author only (as the rest of that line). Same view, same kind, no new status kind. Guide sentence added to the Submissions bullet.
- **Tests.** `submissions/review-citation.test.ts` (4 backends: reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker thread, PostgreSQL: uncited unchanged, cited kept and answered, repeat after the contract moved, 20 refusals, reliance rules, newest decides, access); `api/start-q02-review-cites.test.ts` (SQLite and PostgreSQL through the composed controller: the owner asks in free words, the stand-in model gets only the message, the real interpreter prompt and chat answer; state API refusals; the guide sentence is asserted); `api/start-q01b-bridge.test.ts` extended (a cited review, a stale one and a rejection with no unmet through the worker bridge); `pi-adapter/src/bridge.test.ts` argument list updated.
- **Own mutation checks** (built files, restored byte-identical by sha256): stale-version check removed; unmet requirement not demanded; superseded-reliance check removed; the whole approval reliance block removed; decision-in-force check removed; status line suffix removed; `approvalOf` not answering `cited`; bridge whitelist without the new arguments; `unmet` not stored; guide sentence changed. All caught.
- **ASSUMPTION:** citing is optional. Requiring it on every review would break every existing reviewer flow and is a policy choice (a project setting could require it later); the absence of a citation is shown as before and is not a failure. ASSUMPTION: a rejection or a request for changes on work relying on a superseded decision is allowed (only an approval is refused). ASSUMPTION: only a rejection carries `unmet`, and only when it cites the criteria. ASSUMPTION: a verdict is not invalidated later when the contract changes (the version it cites stays in the record and the view shows it; the review of the new work comes from a new submission). (Replaced 2026-11-26: an approval now stops counting when the contract's criteria text (expected result, acceptance criteria) or a relied-on decision changes after it; new checks or required evidence do not take it back; see "Q02 stale approvals" below.)
- **NOT done (rest of Q02).** The review policy fields (scope, triggers including periodic and incident, required checks, whether independent review gates completion); counting independent evidence by original source; a team vote never overriding an owner decision; carrying a reviewer verdict over only by unchanged patch-id as a Q02 rule (P09 already binds approvals to the patch at landing); invalidating a cited verdict when the criteria or a decision changes afterwards; dependencies other than criteria and decisions (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) invalidating evidence; requiring a citation by policy; the view does not say that a cited version is no longer the task's current one.
- **Tests run (Linux, slot-wrapped, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, forced build, stale dist tests removed):** all submissions tests, start-q01b-*, start-q02-*, start-submission, start-qa-*, toolbridge/service, status, chat/status, model-interpreter, api/operations, pi-adapter bridge, d01-user-guide, fixed-part-budget. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` pass; API docs regenerated after the build.

Checks of the same record are not repeated.

Clean-context second review and fixes on `card-q02-s6` (origin/main still `f7c8ec08`: nothing to merge).

- **Fixed: an approval went through when a decision the task relies on could not be read.** A link marked `current` whose decision record was missing was treated as in force. Decisions are never removed, so only damaged or partly restored data does this; the approval is now refused (fail closed), as `decision.revalidate` already treats such a link as stale. A storage read that fails throws and records nothing, as before.

Differences, all deliberate: the link's own `superseded` mark also refuses (it is set only when the decision was superseded, which is final, so it agrees); a missing decision refuses here (the guard skips it); the gate topic (implementation hold, planning-only) is not read here, because Q02 asks about decisions the task relies on, not the project's gate. The window between a correction (the decision is marked superseded in the correcting write) and propagation (links marked later by the dispatcher) is covered by reading the decision. A dispute settled by keeping the decision makes it active again and never marks its links, so the refusal clears (tested).

Storage has no "record is absent" check, so a first link (or a first contract) created during the write does not make it rebuild; harmless for safety (a new link can only name a decision in force) and the same as the C08 guard and QA evidence. No existing test or flow records an approval through `submission.record` on a task linked to a superseded or disputed decision (the one test with links and an approval plants the review directly). Pi schema unchanged (19,328 of 19,400; parameter names only: citing is optional, and the refusal texts tell an approver what to do).

## P10 (twelfth slice): an approved first place that never lands is moved to the back after a day (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. A landing queue lands only its first place. If that first place is approved work that nobody lands (its integrator is away, its landing keeps not being asked for), everything behind it waited, and until now the only thing that happened was a notice to the director after four hours. Now, when an approved first place has held the branch for twenty-four hours and approved work of another task waits behind it, the controller moves it to the back of the queue by itself, on the same regular rounds as the other bounds (and at a landing asked for behind it). Nothing is removed: the work stays approved and queued with the same approved base and tree, the next task is first, and the moved work takes its turn again behind the others. The task's holder (while an active agent), the director and the owner are told once. The owner's `landing_queue` view says in plain words, for an approved first place, when the controller will move it and that nothing is removed. Card P10 stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** The release bound for an approved first place is what the slice-11 notes named as still unbounded. The alternative the notes called out, REMOVING an approved first place, would change what lands without the owner's say; moving it to the back keeps every approved submission and only changes the order, which the queue already lets a refresh or a re-approval do. The `add` race on a first assignment still has no record to check a revision of (ninth slice), so it was not chosen.
- **Code.** `LandingQueueService.deferFirst` (`landing/landing-queue.ts`): one recorded command (`landing.queue.defer`, command ID from the queue, the submission and the first place's `since`, so a repeat moves nothing more), judged inside the write: the first place is still that task's entry (same submission, same `front.since`), it has held the branch for the bound, another task's entry waits behind it, and no entry has a landing request `started` or `uncertain` (the first entry's open-request record is read and written back unchanged, as a take-out does, so a landing that begins at the same moment loses the race). The entry's number becomes the queue's next number (its reservation's number follows it); everything else in the entry is unchanged. The audit entry carries the task, the submission, the old and the new number. `LandingQueueOps.#deferFirst` (`landing/queue-ops.ts`): the pre-check on the clock, the move, then the notices (holder through `tell`, director and owner through `escalate` with the new reason `deferred`). Called from `sweepBounds` (the same dispatcher sweep `landing.queue.bounds`, the same 60 s throttle, the same read budget and the same "a task WAITING behind the place is judged on this queue's branch" rule; the result gains `deferred` only when it is not zero) and from `checkLanding` (a landing asked for behind the place is judged again on the queue as it is then, like the idle release). `api/start.ts`: the `deferred` reason is a notice to the owner (never a needs-you) with its own plain text. No new stored field (the move only rewrites numbers the record already has; a record written before this slice reads and writes as before). The `deferMs` option reads as `LANDING_DEFER_MS` when absent; `landing.queue.list` `front` gains `deferMs`.
- **Wording changed.** The `landing_queue` status line (an approved first place: when it is moved, or that it is past the bound; nothing is said when the first-since time is not a real date, as for the hold bound), the `status.ask` summary, the `landing.queue.list` description and result (`api-v1.md` regenerated), ONE sentence at the end of the interpreter prompt's landing-queue paragraph, the user guide's landing-queue paragraph (plus the d01 term "moved to the back of the queue by the controller"). The guide's statement that ending a reservation removes no work is unchanged and still true; it never said an approved place stays first forever.

## Q01b sixth slice: a per-project code index removes the scan bound of the project-wide waiting view (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Branch `card-q01b-s6`. Plain words first. The project-wide "what code is waiting" view (fifth slice) had to scan the whole submission table, which holds every project's submissions in hash order of IDs, and said "only part was looked at" once the controller held more than 10,000 submissions. Now each project keeps a small index of its code, written together with each code submission, and the view reads that when it is complete. Nothing a user sees changes except that the partial notice stops appearing for projects with an index. Card Q01b stays planned.

- **Chosen item and why.** The per-project index, as recommended: it is the only open item that is offline-doable, needs no product decision (the others need the `KIND_ROLES` and project-scoped roles decision, the repository for P08, real check runs for P09, or `reviewAssignments` wiring plus a tool/prompt budget the Pi tool list does not have: 72 characters of room), and it removes exactly the bound the fifth slice documented. No chat, interpreter, prompt, tool or user-guide text changed, so the fixed-part budget is untouched; the view's output is unchanged, so there is no new owner control to make reachable (the existing free-chat view reads the same lines).
- **Built.** Record kind `code-submission-index`, keyed by the project ID: `{ complete, entries: [{ taskId, id, at, by }] }`, one entry per task and submitting agent (the newest; of two at the same instant the greater ID), at most `CODE_INDEX_KEPT` (500) entries, the oldest dropping off and `complete` turning false when it overflows. It is written in the same write as the code submission (`#codeIndexChange` beside the document index), as a `create` or a revision-checked `update`; a write that met another code submission of the same project is built again (the document index's race rule, up to 40 times with a short random wait, then `unavailable`). `SubmissionService.waiting` reads it: complete index: no scan (`source: "index"`, `scanLimited` false); absent, unreadable (not an object of the right shape) or incomplete index: the table is scanned as before (`source: "scan"`), an incomplete index adding its own entries to what the scan found, so the answer is never silently wrong and the partial notice still appears when the scan stops. Entries are only pointers: each is read through `approvalOf`, and an entry whose submission is missing, is not code, or belongs to another project is left out (fail closed). Access rules are unchanged: the owner sees all, an agent only entries it submitted itself, a task credential and strangers get `not_found`. Reading creates nothing (a test checks no index exists after a read of an old project).
- **Backfill.** Bounded and lazy. Nothing is written for old data. The first new code submission of a project with no index seeds it from one scan of the table (the same `WAITING_SCAN` bound, 20 reads of 500 rows): `complete` only when that scan reached the end. A project with old code and no new submission keeps being scanned (`source: "scan"`), exactly as before. An index that exists but cannot be read is left alone by the writer (it could not be revision-checked) and the view scans.
- **Tests.** `submissions-q01b-waiting.test.ts` is now 15 x 4 = 60 (four new service tests on all four backends: the index answers while a small scan bound would have made it partial, one record per project, eight simultaneous code submissions of eight tasks all indexed once, a replay writes nothing more; old data scanned and read, reading creating no index, first new code seeding a complete index; a seed cut short is incomplete and the view uses both sources and still says partial when its scan stops, a damaged index is ignored and not written over; one entry per task and agent, an agent seeing only its own newest code when another agent's is newer, the size limit dropping the oldest and clearing `complete`, entries pointing at nothing or at another project left out). Two earlier tests that needed the scan path (partial wording) now write their code through a writer that leaves no index, the state of data written before this slice (`codeIndexKept: 0`, an injectable option like `docIndexKept`). `api/start-q01b-waiting.test.ts` (start level, SQLite and PostgreSQL): through `startController`, `submission.record` leaves a complete index naming exactly the two submissions, and the free-words chat answer is unchanged.
- **Mutation checks (9, built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256):** seed always marked complete (4 failures); view trusts an incomplete index (4); own-only filter dropped from the index read (10); another project's entry listed (4); unreadable index overwritten (4); newer entry always replaced by the latest write (3); index never written (18); size limit keeps `complete` (4); lost write not built again (4). All caught.
- **ASSUMPTION.** One entry per (task, agent), not per task: an agent's own-code view must show the newest code it submitted even when another agent's is newer, as the fifth slice does.
- **ASSUMPTION.** An unreadable index is never repaired by the writer or the view (no silent rewrite); the view scans. Repair would need an owner-visible decision about what to overwrite, and this case should not occur.
- **ASSUMPTION.** Old projects are not backfilled by a background job: lazy seeding at the next code submission and the scan fallback are the smallest reversible choice.
- **Not done (said plainly).** (1) The reviewer's own "what waits for me" list (needs `reviewAssignments` wiring and a tool or prompt line the Pi budget lacks). (2) A sign-off's patch binding is not shown per sign-off. (3) A project with more than 500 (task, agent) pairs of code, or with old code and no new submission, is still scanned, bounded, and says so. (4) The earlier Q01b items are unchanged: policy for `KIND_ROLES` and project-scoped roles, base/tree/patch-id against the repository (P08), evidence against real check runs (P09), evidence and `submission.get` through the bridge. (5) The task's own `list` still scans by task (not indexed).
- **Tests run** (wrapped in `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, sandbox required, offline guard, after a forced build): every `submissions-*` test, `start-q01b-*`, status tests, `d01-user-guide`, `scripts/d02-docs`: 470 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok; API docs unchanged (no summary changed).

## T08 (eighth slice): the owner's maintainers' view, a read-only status kind (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

T08 stays `planned` (not flipped). Branch `card-t08-s8` off origin/main `a7d40554`. Changed: new `catalog/maintainers.ts` (`toolboxMaintainers`), `status/status.ts` (new status kind `toolbox_maintainers`, `toolboxMaintainerLines`, a `maintainers` port on the `toolbox` dependency), `api/start.ts` (the wiring), `api/operations.ts` (the `status.ask` summary names the kind), `chat/model-interpreter.ts` (one sentence at the end of the toolbox paragraph), `docs/nimblenewt/user-guide.md` (a new section), `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` (regenerated). Not touched: `catalog/proposals.ts` and the bounds from slices 6 and 7, `submissions/*`, `landing/*`, the Pi tool list and its descriptions (no new tool), the chat guards in `chat/chat.ts`.

**What it does.** The owner asks in free words ("who maintains the toolbox", "who can approve the proposals for the lint tool", "…after the first 10") and the status kind `toolbox_maintainers` (`name`, `after`) lists the active agents that hold `toolbox.manage` now, each by its quoted name with its ID. It says whether the right covers every project (then any shared tool) or only named projects (then only tools made for those projects alone, with the project names read from their records), and how many proposals wait for a decision that agent may make (its own never count; a wait of 100 or more reads "at least"). A tool named leaves only the maintainers whose right covers that tool and counts only that tool's proposals. It lists 10 at a time; `after` is how many were already shown, and the answer says "ask again with after N" when more exist, as the docs views do. Nothing is created or changed.

**How the rights are read.** The view reads each active agent as the controller itself judges it (`PrincipalService.current`: the agent's own record, rights given by grant, restrictions, expiry and archived projects), and then asks the same two functions the services use (`maintainsAnywhere`, `mayManage`). It keeps no second list, so a restriction or a taken-back right changes the answer at once (tested). The waiting count calls the existing `ToolboxProposalService.list` as that maintainer, so it is the same set the maintainer would see and may decide, minus its own proposals.

**Access.** Owner only (a task-scoped owner credential is refused too). The service answers `forbidden`; the status layer turns that and an unknown tool into "missing" (`not_found` at the API), so an agent, a maintainer or a stranger is told nothing and not even that the kind exists for them; a task credential is refused at the door. A bad `after` or `name` is `invalid_command`, never guessed. Nothing new is stored, so there is no field to read when absent. The scan reads at most 1000 agents; when it stops there the last line says so.

ASSUMPTION: of the open T08 items the maintainers' view was the smallest complete one that needs no product decision and no change to the proposal bounds, the tool list or the chat guards. A chat ask for a maintainer's revocation was not chosen: a maintainer is an agent, so an owner's chat ask would only duplicate the owner's existing `catalog.revoke`, and a running-call preview would touch the bridge tool and the revoke path. Counting waiting proposals per maintainer by reading as that maintainer was chosen over a second rule so the number can never disagree with what the maintainer may decide. Agents are listed in the order of their record IDs (stable, not alphabetical). Nothing waits on Rob; reversible by removing the `maintainers` port (the view is then not offered).

## H12o (seventh slice): the submissions view says why an automatic release did not commit (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. Since the automatic release, an approval by a reviewer asks the platform to commit the approved code by itself. If the host refused that request (for example a stray file in the checkout), or it failed, the owner's submissions view only said "not made yet; it is committed only when a release request commits it". Now, for the owner and the code's author, the view says that the release the approval asked for was refused, failed or was left unsure, when, and what the host answered. Card H12o stays planned (see "Not done").

- **Chosen item and why.** This is item (3) of the sixth slice's "Not done" ("a failed automatic release is told only as the recorded request"). That note said it needed "a stored last-request index per task". It does not: the automatic release's request already has a fixed command ID (`rel-auto:<approving review>`) under a fixed service identity, and the request's own ID is derived from those, so the view can read exactly that record from the approval it already reads (`approvalOf` gives the review ID). No new stored field, no change to what commits or lands, read-only.
- **Rejected items, and what each needs.** (a) Remote-host release of a submission: needs a new field in the worker protocol and a real remote host to prove it; not provable offline. (b) `commitOnce` / `CommitPort` / A06: a redesign of a gate (the old path would be a second way to commit that must not bypass the review permit), a product and gate decision. (c) The PLAN.md issue (PLAN.md is committed and landed): a product decision about what an approved commit contains. (d) Reading a Q01 acceptance as an approval: a product decision (it would let a different record commit code through a gate that checks reviews). (e) A release retried when a live attempt ends: needs a hook on the attempt lifecycle and changes when platform commits happen; not chosen without a decision. Also not touched, as asked: catalog, the submission index code, landing, the chat guards, the Pi tool list.
- **Built.** `WorkspaceOpService.automaticRelease(submissionId, reviewId)` (no caller, read-only, not an API operation): reads the record at the derived ID and answers its state, times and summary, only when it is a `release` of that very submission; malformed IDs answer nothing. `StatusDeps.submissionRelease.automatic` (optional; absent in an older composition: the old wording stands) is wired in `api/start.ts`. `StatusService.#commitWords` reads it only when there is no commit and no request open, only for an approval that has a review ID by a reviewer other than the author, and only in the branch for the owner and the author (other readers still read nothing). It tells refused, failed or unsure; a finished request that left no commit is not explained (the generic words stand). `status.ask` `submissions` text, the interpreter prompt, the user guide's Submissions bullet and the d01 term list follow.
- **Fail closed.** Any throw in the read says "could not be read just now", as before. A request that is still open keeps the old open-request wording and the automatic record is not read. A recorded commit wins over any automatic answer. The one-agent approval has no review ID, so nothing is read for it.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the host's refusal text (the request's recorded summary) may be shown to the owner and the author in the view, cut to 300 characters, credentials removed, one line, quoted and escaped. (Corrected at review: `workspace.get` needs `workspace.manage`, which an author agent usually lacks, so the author is a new reader of this text.)
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** What the host can answer was checked in `worker/src/workspace/host.ts` and `git.ts`. A deliberate refusal never names a host folder; it may name one file of the task's own checkout (JSON-quoted, at most 40 or 80 characters), which the author works in anyway. A failure (and an unsure end) is a raw thrown error: git's own message (`git.ts` `#run`, 200 characters) or a file-system error, which can name the host's absolute checkout and git folders. So the view now gives the host's words to the author only for a refusal; for a failure or an unsure end the author is told what happened and when, and "What the host said is shown to the owner." The owner sees the words in every case. The reviewer and other agents read nothing (the view test now also checks the reviewer that was asked to review the code, and a composition without `automatic`). The guide says no separate notice is sent. A `done` release with no commit record (the host did not confirm a commit of exactly this submission) keeps the generic "not made yet" words, which stay true. The request states are `started`, `done`, `refused`, `failed` and `uncertain`: a `started` one is open (the open-request words) or, after a restart, turned `uncertain`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** an approval for which the controller refused before recording anything (a live attempt, a paused task, a remote host) still reads as the generic "not made yet" words, because no record exists to read; telling that needs a stored note, which is left undone.
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-h12o-auto-answer.test.ts` (1 x 4 backends): nothing recorded is nothing, reading creates no record, refused with the host's words, another submission or review or a malformed ID is nothing, a failed host, a later approval has its own answer, done. `submissions/submissions-h12o-commit-view.test.ts` (2 new x 4 backends): refused/failed/unsure wording, finished-but-no-commit not explained, open request not asked, recorded commit wins, other readers told nothing and nothing read, a failing read, no records created; the one-agent approval asks nothing. `chat/auto-release-view.test.ts` (through the real chat, the real `ModelInterpreter` and the real status and submission services; 1 prompt test + 1 x 4 backends): in free words the owner is told it was refused and why; the stand-in model hands over no ID and never sees the earlier answer; an agent with no part in the code is told nothing and nothing is read. `integration/h12o-submission-commit.test.ts` (extended, real git through `startController`): the refused automatic release (a stray file) is told with the host's words to the owner, and not to the reviewer.
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the author now sees the host's words only for a refusal that is the host's own answer. Two other kinds of refusal can be recorded for an automatic release, and both are built from an error thrown on the controller's side, so their text is not controlled: an attempt of the task that could not be made quiet (an attempt that starts between the release's check for live attempts and the quiesce; its text carries the checkpoint's or runtime's error, up to 200 characters, which can name a host folder), and the approval re-checked right before the host is asked (any thrown error, a storage error included). `automaticRelease` now answers `hostAnswer: true` only for a refusal recorded as "the host did not do it: ..." (other than the approval re-check, which uses the same prefix) or the fixed "no host" text (now one constant); fail closed. The view gives the author the words only then; otherwise the author is told it was refused and when, and "What the host said is shown to the owner." The owner sees the words in every case. Checked and kept: the host's release refusals (`host.ts #release`, `git.ts release`/staging, `paths.ts`, `names.ts`) are fixed texts, short commit IDs, the submission ID or a JSON-quoted name inside the task's checkout (40 or 80 characters); git's stderr and file-system errors are `unavailable` and rethrown, so they are recorded as `failed`. The derived ID equals the hook's (`releaseApproved(subject, e.submissionId)` with the review submission's ID; `approvalOf().reviewId` is that verdict entry's ID); one record per review, a repeat replays it. The extra read is one record per shown submission, at most 5 per view, and only for approved code with no commit and no open request. The interpreter prompt and the guide sentences stay true. Tests: the service test now covers a quiesce refusal, an approval re-check that threw, no host, a failure and a done request (`hostAnswer` set or not); the view test checks the author is not shown a controller-side refusal's text (the owner is); the real-git test checks the author sees the host's own refusal.

## P09 sixth slice: the landing reads its records again right before the host is asked (read-once windows) (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first. When a landing is judged, the review, QA, document, director and defects records are each looked at once, one after the other. After that the landing shows its lease and its queue place once more and only then asks the host to write. A change that landed in that short stretch (a review taken back, a defect reported, a document flagged, a sign-off declined) was not seen. Now the same records are read once more as the very last step before the host is asked, and a landing whose records changed is refused, saying which check changed. Nothing else changes for a landing where nothing moved. Card P09 stays planned.

- **What was read when (found by reading `workspace-ops.ts` `#request`/`#run` and `landing-gate.ts` `evaluate`).** At the request, before anything is recorded: the lease, the named submission's task, the queue's head. In the quiesce, right before the host: the lease and queue again (`stillLeased`), then the host's one run of the checks, then, only after it, the records in this order: the review's approval, then QA (approval and QA gate), documents (approval and documents gate), director (approval and sign-offs), defects. Then the lease and queue are shown once more, then `port.run`. So the records were NOT read before the start record, and the window was from each record's read until `port.run`: for the review, the QA/docs/director/defects reads, a few awaits plus the lease and queue reads. With a queue the review was already covered by the queue's own check of the approval; without a queue (a landing that names its submission) it was not.
- **Why not storage `check` guards in the start write.** The start record is written before the quiesce and before any gate read, so guarding the records the gate reads inside that write would guard nothing the gate later sees (and the tests may run for minutes in between). The window is after the gate, so the second reading belongs after the gate.
- **Built.** `LandingGate.recheck(record)`: for the checks of the record that passed and are judged from records alone (review, qa, docs, director, defects) it runs the same judgement again with the host report and review state the first judgement kept (in memory, keyed by the record it answered; nothing stored). The tests are not run again and nothing is asked of the host. It answers the checks that no longer pass (as they now read) and the record as it stands (not passed when any changed). A record this gate did not answer throws (the landing is then refused); a landing that requires none of these checks reads nothing. `WorkspaceDeps.landingRecheck` (optional; absent in unit rigs) is called in `#run` as the very last step before `port.run`, after the second lease and queue showing. A changed check refuses the landing exactly like a failed gate: the record keeps the checks as they now read, the author is sent them, and a queued submission stays in the queue with its place and reservation untouched (the existing gate-refusal path). The refusal says "a required check that had passed changed before the landing was made (review failed: ...)". A read that fails is the gate's "not run", so it is refused too; a second reading that throws is refused as "could not be read again ... nothing was landed", with the gate's own answer left on the record and no author notice. `api/start.ts` wires `landingRecheck` to the composed gate. No new stored field, no change to the passing case.
- **Window closed.** A change to the review, QA, documents, director sign-off or defects between the gate's reads and the second reading (which is the last thing before the host is called) now stops the landing before the host is asked and nothing is committed.
- **Window that remains, said plainly.** (1) The second reading is not atomic with the host call: a change in the few awaits between the second reading and the host starting to write is not seen. Closing that needs the host's write to be conditional on controller records, which it cannot be (they are different stores). (2) A change after the host was asked cannot stop a landing already under way; the test states it: the landing is done and the next landing sees the change. (3) The lease and queue are shown once more before the second reading, not after it; the lease is checked by fence by the host path as before. (4) The sub-reads of one check (approval, then its gate) are two reads, not one snapshot, as before.
- **ASSUMPTION.** The second reading re-judges only checks that passed, with the host's first report (the submission's base, tree and computed patch ID never change), so no second host call and no new result can appear where there was a failure.
- **ASSUMPTION.** A read failing in the second reading is a changed check ("not run"), refused; only a fault of the reading itself (an unknown record) throws. Either way the landing is refused and nothing is written.
- **ASSUMPTION.** The refusal sends the author the results (the same text as any gate refusal) because a review or defect change is something the author fixes; a thrown second reading is a controller fault and tells nobody.
- **Start-level wiring (said plainly).** As first written: no start-level test, a removed wiring line not caught. Corrected by the review below: the host's check run is an injection point for the project's required checks (read before it), and `p09-landing-checks` now fails when the wiring line is removed.
- **Tests.** `workspace-ops/workspace-ops-p09-window.test.ts`: 9 x 4 backends + 1 = 37. Nothing changed lands (the host ran the checks once; the records were read again); for each of a review asking for changes (real review record), a defect, a flagged document, a declined director sign-off (real sign-off record) and QA evidence that stopped passing, landing a change right after the gate answered stops the landing before the host is asked, names the check, keeps the other checks as they were, tells the author, and the same landing goes through once the change is undone; a failing read and a throwing second reading fail closed; a tests-only landing reads no record again; a change after the host was asked does not stop the landing (the limit); a refusal keeps a queued submission in the queue and the landing that goes through takes it out; a record the gate did not answer throws.
- **Mutation checks (13, built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256), all caught:** recheck never called (32 failing); changed ignored (28); second-reading error swallowed (4); author not told (20); record not updated (24); review, QA, docs, director, defects each not re-read (4, 4, 4, 4, 12); changed list always empty (28); recheck keeps `passed` true (24); unknown record not a fault (1, after a test was added for it).
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the landing now also reads the project's required checks again as its last step, because they are read before the host runs the tests, which can take minutes. A check the owner added in that time was never judged for this landing, and the landing went ahead. Now it is refused with "the project's required checks changed while this landing was judged (it now also requires defects, which was not judged for it), so nothing was landed ...; ask for the landing again". Nobody is told (the author cannot change the policy), the gate's own answer stays on the record, a queued submission keeps its place, and the next landing is judged under the new checks. A check dropped in that time changes nothing (the landing met the stricter set). A failing read of the policy throws, so the landing is refused ("could not be read again"). `recheck` answers it as `added` and reads no record after it. Checked and kept: the record `#run` gives `recheck` is the object `evaluate` returned (start.ts passes it through unchanged; a copy would make every gated landing refused, which a mutation shows: 41 failing); no await between the second reading and `port.run`; an unchanged state passes identically (same inputs, and `#claims` cannot turn a pass that was not turned before); the changed-check refusal uses the gate-refusal path line by line (`gateRefused`, the attempt told the results on resume, author told, owner told only for `testsNeedOwner`, which cannot be set on a passed record); the only error `recheck` throws itself is a fixed text, and a storage error inside a check is the gate's existing "not run" text (the author already saw those texts from the first judgement). The thrown-path reason embeds `safe(error, 300)` exactly like the existing "required checks could not be read" path. Start-level test: `p09-landing-checks` drops `defects` from the policy, puts it back while the worker runs the checks, and asserts the landing is refused, nothing landed, the author not told and the queue kept; the next landing lands. Removing the wiring line in `api/start.ts` now fails it. Tests: `workspace-ops-p09-window.test.ts` 10 x 4 backends + 1 = 41 (new: a check added after the gate refuses and tells nobody, asked again it lands, a check dropped lands). Own mutation checks (7, built files, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256), all caught: start wiring removed (integration 1 failing); `added` always empty (5); `added` ignored in `#run` (5); `added` inverted (40); judged lookup through a copy of the record (41); policy refusal skipped so records are read (4); author told on a policy refusal (5).
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the earlier note said "a check the owner dropped changes nothing", but the landing still read such a check again, so a defect reported just as the owner stopped requiring the defects check refused a landing that the policy now allows, and the author was told the defects failed. The second reading now leaves out checks the policy no longer requires. Checked and found sound: every refusal in this window (check added, check changed, second reading throws, required-checks read throws) is returned inside the quiet section like the gate's own refusals, so the quiet attempts resume, the request settles `refused` and the task's open request is cleared (`landingUnderway` never sees a `started` landing left over), the lease is not touched, and the queue entry stays (it leaves only on a confirmed `done`). The P10 defer and hold bounds count time at first place, not refusals, so repeated refusals from a policy that keeps changing are bounded by the owner asking again; they move nothing. Both readings get the required checks from the same `integration.effective(projectId)`, which depends only on the project (no per-kind policy), so neither reading refuses wrongly or misses a check. New in the window test (still 41: assertions added to existing tests): a dropped check that would now fail is not read again and the landing goes ahead; a required-checks read that throws in the second reading refuses (host not asked, nobody told) and the next landing goes ahead. Own mutation checks (7, built files, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256), all caught: dropped check read again (4 failing); `added` ignored in the gate (4); recheck not called (36); a throwing second reading let through (8); changed checks never reported (28); author not told on a changed check (20); `added` ignored in the workspace operation (4). Not changed (said plainly): a refused landing whose required checks changed keeps the gate's first record (`passed: true`) on the request, as the fault refusal already does; the refusal summary starts with "the host did not do it:" for these refusals, as it does for the existing lease and queue refusals, although the host was not asked.

## Chat control gap 1: pause, resume and stop by free words (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-22)

Plain words first: the owner can now say "pause Ann", "carry on with Ann", "stop the Garden team" or "what is paused?" in any words. Before, only the typed `/nimblenewt.lifecycle-*` lines (and the web buttons) did this, and the interpreter prompt pointed at "the stop and pause controls" that did not exist in chat. The typed lines are unchanged and stay the no-model fallback.

- **Design.** `lifecycle.pause`, `lifecycle.resume` and `lifecycle.stop` are chat commands (`CHAT_OPS`). The interpreter gives a flat scope: `scopeKind` (task, agent, team, installation) and `scopeName` (the owner's own words); `scope`, `background`, `deadlineMs` and `spendBudget` are not chat arguments. The chat builds the API's `scope` (`#lifecycleScope`): agents and teams by name through the same lookup the `stop_cleanup` read uses (whole word of the message, active agents only; two answers ask which, none says so), a task by exact title in the project in focus (asks for the project if none), the whole installation only when `scopeName` is a word for everything that the owner wrote (`WHOLE_INSTALLATION_WORDS`: everything, all, whole, installation, ...). A bare "stop", or the order word offered as the scope, asks and does nothing. `scopeName` and `reason` go through the existing own-words check; `scopeKind` and `mode` are fixed choices. A reason the owner did not give is recorded as "requested by the owner in chat" (as retirement does).
- **Safety.** Stop and resume: always shown first (one-open-proposal behaviour is the existing machinery: with two open a bare yes asks which). Pause: applies at once, because it only makes things stricter and a resume lifts it (precedent: forbidding best effort and the retirement-free "narrowing" edits apply at once); shown first when the whole installation is meant, when the words are a question or carry no ordering verb (`MOVE_VERBS["lifecycle.pause"]`), or when the message carried quoted text. Background work is never denied by chat. Force Stop, choose, advance and resume-condition are not chat commands (left alone).
- **Read.** New status kind `lifecycle` (owner only, bounded): one task, agent, team or the installation by name; with none named, the installation plus the first 50 active agents that are paused, with who paused them, why and what the runtime reports. A gate the caller may not read is "nothing you may read", never "not paused". Teams and tasks are read when named. It uses `PauseService.gate` (optional addition to the status `pauses` dependency).
- **Prompt.** Net growth 485 characters (156,755 to 157,240): one paragraph (355), three generated operation lines (194), one status line (about 180), minus 245 cut from the retirement paragraph (the examples "retire the old build agent", the release list and "Nothing is deleted..." sentence; the proposal itself shows what is released) and the false line-69 sentence reworded.
- **Guide.** New section "Pausing, resuming and stopping work" (free words first, d01 marker `lifecycle-words`); the typed section now says a typed stop runs at once. `d01-user-guide.test.ts` runs the five sentences through the launcher and real chat and checks each claim.
- **Tests.** `chat/lifecycle-words.test.ts`: 14 cases x 4 backends = 56, real chat + `ModelInterpreter`, stand-in that fails on any text the owner did not say, interpreter never sees an earlier answer, non-owner by chat, API and status. d01: 1 new test.
- **Own mutation checks** (25, built files, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 24 caught; survivor T3 (the "gate may not be read" branch of the status answer): the service's `gate` returns nothing for a reader without rights rather than throwing, so that branch is defensive and not reachable with these services.
- **Not done.** Force Stop / choose / resume-condition by words; teams and tasks are not enumerated by "what is paused?" (named only); a stop's deadline and spend limit are not chat arguments; task scope needs the project in focus; `WHOLE_INSTALLATION_WORDS` is a safety list that makes the chat ask (never refuse for good), an unusual word for everything is asked about once.
- ASSUMPTION: pause of agent/team/task applies at once (stricter-only, reversible); resume and stop are shown first; stop with no mode is a full stop and says so; whole-installation pause is shown first.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-23).** Plain words first: two things were tightened. (1) "What is paused?" was not really owner only: an agent asking the status view directly was told "not paused" about an agent that was paused (the pause service answers "no gate" to a reader without rights, and the answer read that as never paused). The view is now owner only, like the other owner views, and anyone else gets nothing; the test that was meant to show this asked through an API with no status view configured, so it passed without reaching the code, and now asks the status view itself, for an agent with no rights and one that may read agents. The `null` branch for an unreadable gate is removed: the survivor mutant T3 was indeed unreachable (`gate` returns undefined and never throws `forbidden`/`not_found`; `checkScope` throws `invalid_command`). (2) A pause, resume or stop by words took any agent or team named anywhere in the message and only consulted the interpreter's `scopeName` when several matched, so "pause Zed, Ann asked for it" (no Zed) paused Ann at once. The one meant must now be named both in the message and within `scopeName`. New case: 15 x 4 = 60. Merge of origin/main (chat meetings, backups view): import line, describe() and the status.ask summary combined by hand. Both ASSUMPTION lines kept: a pause is stricter-only, needs an ordering verb and the target in one non-question sentence to apply at once, and a resume lifts it; a stop with no mode is what the owner said, is shown first and names suspend as the alternative.
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-23).** Plain words first: a pause by words applies at once, and four ways it could apply when the owner had not given that order are now shown first instead. (1) The pause verb list matched word beginnings, so a verb inside the agent's own name counted ("Parker did well today" holds "park", "Holden" holds "hold") and so did other forms ("Ann is waiting", "Ann holds the lease"): the list is whole words now, and the target's name is blanked out before the verb is looked for (`ownerSaysMove`, pause only; the other moves keep their rule, though a task titled with its own verb, such as "Close the door" for done, has the same shape there and is left for a separate look). (2) A negation, condition or maybe ("don't pause Ann", "if Ann breaks the build, pause her", "pause Ann once she is done") applied at once when the model read a pause: such a message is now shown first (`PAUSE_NOT_PLAIN`, a short list of words such as not, if, when, once, maybe, should; a plain order with one of them is only shown first, never refused). Checked and left as they were: stop and resume are shown first on every path, a stop with no mode says it is a full stop; names in quoted text are not in the words read and quoted text shows any command first; the typed `/nimblenewt.lifecycle-*` lines are untouched; the status view is owner only. ## Chat-control audit follow-up (2026-11-22): the cheap owner-level reachability gaps (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5)

Plain words first. An audit found owner controls the chat could not reach by free words. This slice fixes the cheap ones; each was checked against the code first and each audit claim was true. Not done here: pause, resume and stop by words (a separate slice), meetings, and the low-value items of the audit (role.label, resource.move/scope/unbind, improvement.decide, swarm.cancel, maintenance.request, decision disputes).

- **(a) A read-only `backups` view.** New status kind `backups` (keys `limit`, `after`; owner only; creates nothing). The first page says how backups are set (the schedule and the rules in the backup system's own words, each place copies go to with whether it can be reached, what it holds, its last copy, problem and test, the last test restore, deletes not finished, and what backups leave out), the last failed attempt, and then the backups newest first, 10 at a time (1 to 50). `after` is the name of the last backup shown and gives the next page of backups only (no settings); a name that is no longer there is said so, never guessed. The reads are the same two as `backup.config.status` and `backup.list` (a new `StatusDeps.backups` pair wired in `api/start.ts`; `backupItem` is now exported from `api/operations.ts` so the list is shaped once). A read that fails is one fixed line (the host's error text is not shown); no backups set up, a non-owner and a task credential get "not found" and nothing is read. The interpreter prompt's two backup paragraphs now name the `backups` kind instead of `backup.config.status` and `backup.list`, the K01d paragraph no longer tells the model to take `expectedRevision` from an answer it cannot see, and purge names are said by the owner (`foreignValue` already requires that).
- **The backup scope revision is filled by the system.** `backup.scope.set` now has `revision: "backup-scope"` in the chat table: the chat reads the scope's revision from `backup.config.status` when the message is planned and sets `expectedRevision` itself (a number the model invented that the owner did not write is replaced, as for the other revision kinds), so a change made meanwhile still makes the proposal stale. ASSUMPTION: `backup.config.set`, `backup.target.add` and `backup.target.remove` stay without a filled revision: their `expectedRevision` is optional, the prompt never asked the model for it, and several of them in one message would each pin the same revision and make all but the first stale when agreed.
- **(b) `backup.now` is a chat command** (card K01e's "back-up-now chat command"): `mode: "propose"`, so it is shown first with the reason "a backup copies all your data to this machine and to every place backups go, and takes room and time, so it is shown first" and made only on the owner's yes; the turn's command ID makes a repeat make no second backup. ASSUMPTION: shown first (like the other backup orders) rather than applied at once, as the owner asked for confirmation like other state-changing orders.
- **(c) A read-only `grants` view** (keys `agentId|agentName`, `projectId|projectName`, `state`, `limit`, `after`; owner only). It lists each standing right with its ID, holder, action, where it works (a right for every project also shows in a project's view; a task-only right says so), and whether it is in force or why not (taken back, ended, not started, lapsed from non-use, resting on a right that no longer holds), the basis quoted. State `active` (default) or `revoked`; 20 at a time (1 to 50); `after` is the ID of the last right shown; one look reads at most 2000 records and says where to go on when it stops early. The chat resolves `agentName` (active agents, exact then loose; several ask, none is not found) and `projectName` (the project lookup other commands use); the names never reach the status service, and an ID the owner wrote beside a name wins. The prompt (line about taking a right back) says to read this kind for rights or to find an ID, and that `grant.revoke` takes the ID the owner gives; the guide's rights paragraph no longer says to type `/nimblenewt.grant-list {}` (the typed lines stay in the recovery section for when the assistant is down) and a new short Backups section says what the chat does for backups. ASSUMPTION: the interpreter sees no earlier answer, so the owner reads the ID from the view and says it in the next message (the chat already requires the ID to be in the owner's words); resolving a right from "Ann's right to update tasks" alone was not built.
- **(d) `overview` and `attention` accept `agentName`** (keys now `agentId|agentName`), resolved with the same lookup as `grants`.
- **(e) The prompt names only what the chat can reach.** `wip.backup.get` became "the status kind wip_backup"; the sentence "migration.status, release.rollback.check and release.rollout.status give the detail" is gone (the `release` kind is what the chat reads). Verbs: task.release "Take a task off its agent", resource.bind "Attach a repository or resource", project.plan "Set project due date, milestones", agenda.capture "Save a topic for a later meeting" (these verbs also head the previews the owner reads). `status.ask`'s summary in `api/operations.ts` names `backups` and `grants`; `api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Prompt size: +938 characters** (156,755 to 157,693 at the same base; the two new status lines are 542 of that, the verbs about 60, the rest the hand-written sentences net of what was removed). The Pi worker's fixed part is not touched. Note for later: `acceptedArgs` lists `taskTitle, prerequisiteTitle` on every operation line (about 30 characters each time); trimming it would save far more than this slice adds.
- **Tests.** `chat/gaps1.test.ts` (prompt and guide checks, and on all four backends the real chat with `ModelInterpreter` and a stand-in model that records any value the owner did not say; only `expectedRevision` is exempt, since the system fills it): backups pages, failure line and non-owner, back up now, the scope revision, rights by agent/project/state/page, taking a right back by its ID, 55-right paging, overview/attention by name. `api/start-backups-view.test.ts` runs the same through the started controller with the real backup system. `api/start-k01c.test.ts`'s stand-in now looks for the `backups` kind in the prompt. Mutation checks on the built files (27, each caught, files restored byte-identical by SHA-256): backups owner check, next-page start, default page, settings repeated, host error shown, limit cap; grants owner check, state filter, every-project rights, agent filter, next page, limit; names for overview, attention, ID beside name, ambiguous names, name left in the request; back up now applying at once, not a chat command, no reason, owner check, command ID; scope revision not filled, wrong revision, invented one kept, wrong record, not marked to fill.
- **Review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the views show only what the owner may already read, `backup.now` and the scope revision behave as they should, and three things were corrected. (1) The backups view printed the words of a failed backup as the host gave them; a system error there can carry the folder or file it was about. They now go through the same path removal the backup notices use (the backups folder named in words, any other quoted path written as "(a path)"), for the last backup failure, each place's problem and last problem, and the last test restore. What a target shows was checked: its name, kind and location (the folder, or an https address that `offsiteLocationProblem` already refuses with a user name, password, query or fragment), never the credential's name; the HTTP target's own errors are fixed phrases and a system error is said by its code (`safeMessage`); everything shown passes `shown`/`quoted`, which cut credential-shaped text. A read that throws is the fixed line, with no host words. (2) The grants view said its rights come "in the order they were made"; grant IDs are hashes of the command ID, so the list is by ID; the head line now says "listed by ID". (3) The `backup.now` preview said "copies all your data"; it now says the copy leaves out what the owner chose to leave out of backups and that older backups past the keep rules are removed as usual (that pruning runs right after the backup). Checked and left as they were: `backup.now` goes to `BackupService.backUpFor(commandId)`: one command ID gives one backup, and a backup already running is the answer to a second ask, so two backups never run at once; the chat's confirmed proposal makes none on a second yes. The scope revision is read when the message is planned (`#revisionFor` in the planner, stored in the proposal's arguments), and `BackupScopeService.set` compares it inside its write, so a change between the preview and the yes is refused as stale, never applied over it. Names: active agents only, exact (case-insensitive) then loose, two matches ask, none is not found, as for the environment views; a retired agent's rights are asked for by its ID. Paging: backups after the last name shown, rights after the last ID shown; pages 10 (backups) and 20 (rights), at most 50. Test added: `gaps1` "a look that reads 2000 rights without filling a page stops there" (reference store only: 2001 rights on every backend would take minutes, and the bound is the status service's own count): a holder with no right reads 2000 records and is told to ask after the 2000th ID, and asking after it reads the rest. Own mutation checks on built files (9, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256), all caught: path removal undone (4 failing), backups owner check removed (4), grants owner check removed (4), scope revision not filled (4), `backup.now` applying at once (2), two agents of one name not asked (4), every-project rights not counted (4), the 2000-record stop never said (1, before the new test: 0), eleven pages read instead of ten (1).
- **Second review (clean-context Opus, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the owner could not reach a second page of either new view by plain words. The model never sees an earlier answer, but `after` was the NAME of the last backup shown or the ID of the last right shown, so "show me the next backups" gave it nothing to pass (the paging problem Q03 and T08 already fixed for their views). Both views now page as those do: `after` is how many were already shown, taken from the owner's words by a rule the prompt gives ("the next backups are after 10, the third page after 20"; "the next rights are after 20, the third page after 40"; a number said is used as said). A later backups page starts with "Backups 11 to 20 of 25, newest first." and leaves the settings out; asking past the end says how many there are. The rights view still takes a right's ID as `after`, because a look that stops after reading 2000 records names the ID to go on after, and the owner can say it. The "more follow" lines now say the number to ask after. The guide's Backups section and rights paragraph say how to ask for more ("show me the next backups", "the backups after 20", "what other rights are there?"). Also: when two active agents share a name, the question "Which agent do you mean?" for overview, attention and grants now shows each agent's ID beside the name (before, the two options were the same text). Checked and left as they were: the stand-in model's own-words check exempts only `expectedRevision` (and `after` only in the new paging test, whose value is checked against the prompt's rule); `agentName` and `projectName` must be in the owner's words. Two separate asks for a backup a few minutes apart have different command IDs: if the first is still running, the second's answer is that same backup (`backUpNow` returns the running one), so two never run at once; once it is done, a new ask makes a new backup. The view reads every backup folder's manifest (as `backup.list` does), which the keep rules bound. Prompt size: 157,693 to 158,047 characters (+354 for the paging rule). A cheaper cut for later, not made: `acceptedArgs` puts ", taskTitle, prerequisiteTitle" (30 characters) on 247 operation lines, about 7,400 characters. Tests: gaps1 gains a real-interpreter suite (4 backends) where the stand-in sees only the prompt and the owner's words ("show me the next backups", "the third page of my backups", "what other rights are there?", "the third page of rights") and checks the pages; the paging and past-the-end checks moved to numbers; start-backups-view asks "after 1".
