### Chat answers follow-up (2026-11-22): tests that said a bare "yes" with several proposals open now name the proposal

Plain words first: the exhaustive CI run on main 76b4e27f failed in eleven test files, all for one reason and all the intended behaviour of the chat-answers slice: when several proposals are open, a bare "yes" is answered with "More than one proposal is open ... Which one do you mean?" and nothing is done. These tests open several proposals (proposals from earlier steps, a failed move that stays open for a retry, earlier loop turns) and then accepted with words that fit all of them. No code changed; no rule was weakened.

- **Intended change, test words now name the proposal by its ID (as the slice did):** `setup/provider-secrets` (T4 reserved credential name: the earlier names' proposals stay open, so the yes names its own; the 'backup-signing-key' loop turn failed for the same reason, an asked question instead of the credential-name refusal), `api/start-transfer` (F04m: a failed move's proposal stays open for a retry, so later accepts name theirs), `api/start-release-window` (K07), `api/start-maintenance` (A09), `api/start-integration` (P08b), `api/start-chat` (A09 / U03e), `api/v02c-recovery-ladder` (V02c), `api/start-defined-sources` (H13f), `api/start-activation` (K02), `api/quiet-host-api`, `api/chat-gaps`.
- **No real regression found:** each open proposal in these tests was left open on purpose by the test or by design (a failed apply stays open for a retry).
- **Wording lesson:** the "does this name one proposal" check also looks at the owner's other words. A word that appears only in ANOTHER open proposal's text counts as pointing at that one, and a number counts as a word. "try removing it again" pointed at the move proposal (whose long preview says "never run again") and "yes (0)" pointed at a proposal that mentions 0 records, so both asked which; the tests now say "go ahead and remove it <ID>" and "yes please go ahead <ID>". That a small word or a number of another proposal's text points at it is the chat-answers design and is kept for messages without an ID.
- **Review (clean-context, 2026-11-22).** Plain words first: the eleven test changes only add the proposal's ID to the owner's words and the cited evidence; no assertion was removed or loosened and no expected value changed. T4 is stronger than before the slice's change: the yes now reaches the apply and is refused for the reserved credential name (`credentialName`), with nothing stored. One rule was corrected: the owner's exact ID now names the proposal. In `namesOneProposal` (chat/chat.ts) another open proposal's ID in the message still asks which; otherwise the picked proposal's exact ID, in the cited evidence and in the owner's own message, names it, whatever other words happen to appear in another proposal's text ("again", "7"). An ID counts only whole (`saysId`/`idPattern`: not inside a longer run of letters, digits, hyphens or underscores), so an ID with a character left off or added is no ID. A proposal the same message also answers is still not "another" (as before), a closed proposal's ID is not an open one, and the ID must be in the owner's own words (the own-words guard; quoted text and the model's evidence cannot supply it). The one-word polarity rules now also hold with the ID beside the word: "no <ID>" never applies and "yes <ID>" never drops (the owner is asked, as for a bare word). Tests: `chat/chat.test.ts` "the exact ID of one open proposal ..." (4 backends): bare yes with two open asks; coincidental words without an ID ask; two open IDs ask; three near IDs and cited words that cut a longer word short ask; an ID only in the model's evidence or in quoted text is refused; a closed proposal's ID applies nothing; "No, <ID>." and "<ID> yes" ask; "yes, try again 7 times ...: <ID>, not <closed ID>" applies. `api/start-chat-answers.test.ts` (C) runs the same through the started controller and `ModelInterpreter`, with a stand-in that takes an ID (or an ID with its last character left off) from the owner's words. Own mutation checks on the built `chat.js` (6, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256), all caught: exact ID not winning (5 failing), another open ID not checked first (5), no leading ID boundary (4), no trailing boundary (4), polarity not read beside an ID (4), the message not checked for the whole ID (4).
- **Second review (clean context, 2026-11-23).** Plain words first: the exact-ID rule is kept. Two places where a proposal could be applied or dropped on words that do not say so were narrowed; both only make the chat ask.
  - **Checked and kept.** The ID only says which proposal is meant. Apply or drop still comes from the model's reading, behind the own-words guard (quoted text and the model's evidence cannot supply the ID) and the one-word guard. The old rule already took an ID in the cited words as naming the pick. The new rule only skips the "another proposal's word" check when the exact ID is in the owner's own words. Another open ID is still checked first. 100 or more open still ask (`OPEN_SCAN` is checked before the ID). One proposal open and the trusted path that carries on a question are unchanged. Matching ignores case, as before. The eleven adapted tests only add the ID to the owner's words and the evidence; no assertion was loosened (T4 provider-secrets now reaches the reserved-name refusal).
  - **Fixed, an ID alone:** a message that is only a proposal's ID ("prop-…", "PROP-…?") was applied or dropped, whichever way the model guessed. The model sees no earlier turn, and the which-one question records no answer to carry on, so it could only guess. The chat now asks "go ahead with <ID>, or drop it?" and does nothing. This held before this follow-up too (`evidence.includes(id)`).
  - **Fixed, a word of dropping or accepting beside the ID:** the one-word guard knew only the refusal and agreement lists, so "drop <ID>", "reject <ID>", "<ID>: discard" read as agreement were applied, and "approve <ID>" read as a drop was dropped. The guard now uses `NOT_APPLY` (refusal words plus drop, reject, discard, decline, refuse) and `NOT_DROP` (agreement words plus apply, approve, accept, confirm, proceed), alone or beside the ID. These lists only make the chat ask. `AGREEMENT` (the question-answer label rule) is unchanged.
  - **ASSUMPTION, kept as documented:** a refusal said in several words ("do not apply <ID>", "<ID>: don't do this", "should I apply <ID>?") is the model's reading, with or without an ID and with one proposal open or several, as the chat-answers second review decided. A word-list reading of phrases would guess at meaning and also catch "no rush, go ahead" and "no Elm, yes Ash". This follow-up does not change those messages: the old rule accepted the same ones. Reversible: a phrase guard can be added later.
  - **Guide:** the "Say yes" sentence says to give the ID together with what you want, and that an ID on its own is asked about.
  - **Tests:** `chat/chat.test.ts` (4 backends): the one-word suite adds "Drop.", "reject", "discard", "decline", "Refuse!" read as apply and "Apply.", "approve", "accept", "confirm", "proceed" read as drop (all ask). The exact-ID suite adds "drop <ID>", "Reject <ID>.", "<ID>: discard" read as apply; "approve <ID>", "<ID> accept" read as drop; and the ID alone as apply, upper-case with "?", the ID twice, and "<ID>!" as drop (all ask, nothing applied).
  - **Own mutation checks** (built `chat.js`, each alone, restored byte-identical by SHA-256): 8 of 8 caught. The checks: ID-alone rule off (4 failing), `NOT_APPLY` back to the refusal words (8), `NOT_DROP` back to the agreement words (8), ID not removed before the word is read (4), the whole ID not required in the message (4), another open ID not checked first (5), case-sensitive ID (4), the exact-ID rule off (5).
  - **Tests run (forced build, no stale dist tests, sandbox + offline guard, one slot):** every `chat/*.test` 1552/1552, plus chat.test, start-chat-answers, gaps1, owner-answer and needs-you-answer 201/201; the eleven adapted files 58/58; d01-user-guide 7/7; d02-docs 27/27. check:deps, licenses:check and roadmap:check pass. origin/main had not moved (ec8c9891).

### Prompt headroom (follow-up, 2026-11-22)

The chat interpreter prompt had reached 158,047 characters against a 160,000 cap, with more chat controls queued. Plain words: nothing the owner can do changed; the prompt got 7,179 characters shorter, and its size is now pinned.

- **What was repeated.** The operation list is generated from the chat's own table (`acceptedArgs`). That function adds `taskTitle` and `prerequisiteTitle` (the names the owner may use in place of a task ID or prerequisite ID; the chat looks the title up in the project and asks when it is unclear) to every chat operation, 247 of them, although only 41 take a task ID and 2 a prerequisite ID. Each line carried about 30 characters of them. Now one hand-written sentence says where an argument takes a task ID or a prerequisite ID the owner's own words may be given as `taskTitle` / `prerequisiteTitle` instead, and the lines stop repeating them. A line shows the ID argument the title stands in for, so the model can still see where it applies, and a model is no longer shown a title key on an operation that takes no task (before, 206 lines offered `taskTitle` where it could only fail).
- **Behaviour unchanged.** `acceptedArgs`, the guard that refuses a value that is not in the owner's words, the refusal of unknown keys and the schema check are untouched: the keys are accepted everywhere they were, and an operation without a task still does not act on a task title. Only the generated prompt text changed (the filter in `model-interpreter.ts`, one sentence, and `taskTitle` taken out of the "where a title or a name is listed" examples).
- **Saved.** Operation list 45,586 to 38,184 characters (-7,402); the new sentence costs 223 (net -7,179 in total: 158,047 to 150,868). The status list (30,299 including what follows it) is unchanged.
- **Other duplication looked at, left alone (ASSUMPTION: not worth the risk of dropping what a model needs).** `expectedRevision` is listed on about 110 lines (about 2,000 characters); on the 40 operations whose revision the chat fills itself it is only needed when the owner quotes a revision, but removing it there would hide that key from the model, so it stays. The long verbs (`generation.stream.change` 638 characters, `retention.settings.set` 1,267 with its argument names, `context.route.change`, `network.grant`) each list real switches or settings the model must choose among. The repeated hand-written phrases ("is shown to the owner first and applies only after they agree" 11 times, the policy_edit setting shape 3 times) are about 300 characters each at most and are matched by existing wording tests, so they stay for a card that rewrites that part.
- **Size pin.** `gaps1.test.ts` only checks that the prompt is under 160,000 characters. The new `chat/prompt-room.test.ts` pins the size at 150,868 with a ceiling 2,000 above and a floor 4,000 below, so a card that adds a control sees the pin, and a large cut is checked for dropped controls; moving it is a deliberate edit of `SIZE`. The old 160,000 cap stays as the hard limit (ASSUMPTION: a tighter hard cap than 160,000 is not wanted; the pin is the early warning).

### Chat meetings (follow-up, 2026-11-23): the owner schedules, changes and calls meetings in free words (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5)

Gap 7 of the chat-control audit (2026-11-22) was real: `meeting.schedule`, `meeting.update-schedule`, `meeting.call-urgent` and `meeting.attend.call-now` had no chat route (verified in `chat/commands.ts`: none was in `CHAT_OPS`; only `standup.configure` covered stand-ups), the interpreter prompt did not mention them and the guide had no word on meetings.

  - **What is done.** Four owner commands, all always shown first (mode `propose`, plus an explicit reason in `proposalReason`, so two guards hold each other): `meeting.schedule` (title, agentNames, time, recurrence, timeZone, durationMinutes), `meeting.update-schedule` (a schedule found by `meetingTopic`, then state paused/active/ended, agentNames, time, recurrence, timeZone), `meeting.call-urgent` (title, reason, agentNames, durationMinutes) and `meeting.attend.call-now` (everyone on the project; the chat fills `scope: {kind: "project"}`, never the model). The chat accepts no roster, scope, schedule ID or revision from the model (`MEETING_CHAT_ARGS` in `commands.ts` is the whole accepted list, so the prompt lists exactly these). Agents are named by their names, one by one (exact name, else any part of it, as `meeting.floor.ask` does); a name that fits several asks, one that fits none is refused. The roster is shown on the proposal as names, not principal IDs.
  - **Times.** The mechanism is the one stand-ups and maintenance windows use: the model works out a wall-clock time `HH:MM`, a recurrence (`once` with a date from Now, `daily`, `weekly` with days 0 Sunday to 6) and a zone from the owner's words and the proposal shows them. On top of that, `clockTimeInWords` (new, built on the maintenance-window time reader) refuses an hour the owner's words do not give ("at 9", "9:30am", "half past two", "noon"; a bare number counts only after "at", "from" and the like, so "3 agents" is not 03:00), and a length is refused unless `durationInWords` finds it. A zone is not checked against the words (the owner says "Eastern time", the model says `America/New_York`); it is shown, and when none is named the owner's `meeting.timeZone` setting is read (`settings.effective`) and said on the proposal, or the owner is asked. A one-off meeting also shows the moment in UTC. The proposal says "Check that this is when you meant."
  - **Finding a schedule.** There was no way to list meeting schedules (a stand-up has its own index, other schedules were only readable by ID). New `MeetingService.schedules(viewer, projectId, {limit, afterId})` and read operation `meeting.schedule-list` (project's schedules that are not stand-ups, ID order, 20 by default, 100 at most per page, `next` to continue; it reads at most 1,000 schedule records and says `scanLimited`; a viewer without the right to read the project's meetings gets nothing). The chat matches `meetingTopic` against the titles of schedules that have not ended; several fit: asked, with the titles as choices (the picked title counts as the owner's words, like a meeting or motion pick); none: refused. The revision is read at proposal and again at apply (`revision: "meeting-schedule"`).
  - **Read.** The existing status kind `meetings` now also lists the project's meeting schedules (not ended; stand-ups stay in their own lines): "Title: schedule, every Monday, Wednesday at 09:30 America/New_York, 30 minutes, active. On the roster: ...", citing the schedule and its revision; the status.ask summary names them. It is bounded by `limit` (1 to 50, default 10) and says "There are more meetings than shown"; it is not paged by "after N" (the other `meetings` lines are not either).
  - **Prompt.** One short paragraph plus the four operation lines: the prompt grew from 151,346 to 152,099 characters (+753; the four lines are +435 and the paragraph about +320; the card asked for about 500 at most, and the recurrence formats are most of the paragraph). `SIZE` in `prompt-room.test.ts` was moved to 152,099 on purpose. Guide: new "Meetings" section (four bold terms), checked by a new test in `d01-user-guide.test.ts` (the terms, the claims "shown first", "cannot be undone", "stop at a safe point", and that `meetings` is a real status kind).
  - **Tests.** `chat/chat-meetings.test.ts` on all four backends (7 tests each) and one pure test: real chat plus `ModelInterpreter`, a stand-in model that sees only the prompt and the owner's words (answers only for an operation whose line lists the argument it uses, hands over only the owner's words except a case that invents a value on purpose and is counted), the interpreter sees no earlier answer; scheduling with the applied record checked against what was shown; invented hour, no hour, no zone, no repeat, no names, unknown name, unclear name; update by words, pause, end, nothing to change, ambiguity, unknown; urgent call never applied at once (also in the autonomous profile), no reason, no names, invented length, a given length; call-now with and without participants; status lines, the paged list, stand-ups left out, ended left out, other project left out; a caller without the right sees nothing and cannot schedule or call; an agent session through the chat is refused before any model is asked.
  - **Own mutation checks** (built files, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256): schedule 8 (time check, recurrence required, name ambiguity, names required, zone ask, `agentNames` not accepted, `time` not exempt, names not shown), update 4, call-urgent 4, call-now 4, status read 6, time reader 1, plus the mode checks below: all caught. Four single mutations of a `mode: "propose"` survived because the explicit `proposalReason` line still shows the command first (two independent guards); mutating both at once is caught (4 tests each). The status filter for ended schedules was first uncovered; a test now ends a schedule and requires it to be left out.
  - **NOT done.** (1) Applying `meeting.attend.call-now` through the chat is not exercised offline: the test world has no attendance service, so the test stops at the proposal and its note ("This calls 2 agents: ..."); `AttendanceService.callNow` has its own tests, and the chat only fills `scope` and checks the project has active participant agents (a call-now with a named team is not offered). (2) ~~A one-off date in the past is not refused~~: done in review, see below (the chat does have a clock, `#runner.now()`, as the grant end date check uses). (3) `startDate`, `endDate`, a daily window, `prepareMinutes` and `budgetTokens` of a schedule, and renaming a schedule by chat, are not offered (stand-ups keep their own window controls). (4) Changing a stand-up's schedule still goes through `standup.update`; `meeting.update-schedule` lists only schedules that are not stand-ups. (5) A name that fits several agents asks a plain question (the interpreter sees no earlier answer, so the owner repeats the name more fully), as the other agent-name controls do.
  - **ASSUMPTION:** a schedule needs the owner to say how often (once, every day, certain weekdays) and who attends; the chat asks instead of defaulting to daily, because a meeting set up "at 9" might well be a one-off. **ASSUMPTION:** an urgent call needs the owner's own reason in their words; it asks instead of reusing the title. **ASSUMPTION:** every one of these controls is shown first in every approval profile (a schedule invites agents again and again; a call takes agents away from their work), the smallest reversible choice.
  - **Review (clean-context, 2026-11-23).** Main had not moved (8b1f436f), so nothing was merged. Safety held: all four controls are proposals in every profile by two independent guards (`mode: "propose"` and an explicit `proposalReason` line that returns before any path that could return nothing); a typed line that changes things is refused, an agent session is refused before a model is asked, a viewer without the right gets an empty schedule list, and call-now takes its project from the owner's words, the focus or the only project (else the chat asks) and reaches exactly the active participant agents the service will call (project participants are capped at 50, the meeting roster limit, so a call-now can never be too large). Title and reason are the owner's words (`foreignValue`), the whole message passes the credential check, and the service bounds them (200 and 1,000 characters). Zones are checked with `Intl` (an invented name is refused). Fixed:
    - **A one-off day was the model's.** `date` is exempt from the words check and nothing compared it with the message, so "a retro at 3pm" or "tomorrow" read as the wrong day made a silently wrong meeting, and a day already past was proposed. New `oneOffDayInWords(date, text, today)`: the day written out (the `grantDateInWords` reader), "today"/"tonight", "tomorrow", "the day after tomorrow", "in N days", or the weekday's name within two weeks, with today read on the meeting zone's calendar from the chat's clock; otherwise asked. A moment already past is refused. The prompt now says the date is "of the day they named, from Now".
    - **Weekly days were the model's.** New `weekdaysInWords`: each day must be named (name, short form, plural), or covered by "weekdays"/"workdays"/"business days" or "weekends"; otherwise asked.
    - **Daylight saving.** A one-off time the clocks skip says when it really starts ("that time does not exist that day ... starts at 03:30 local time"); one they pass twice says it starts at the first (as maintenance windows do).
    - **Changing who attends dropped people quietly.** `agentNames` on `meeting.update-schedule` replaces the roster, so "add Bob to the planning meeting" would take everyone else off; the proposal now says "the roster is replaced, not added to" and names who would be taken off. The schedule is now found before the time note, so a change shows the schedule's real zone, days and length instead of "the schedule's own zone"; the "what should change" question no longer offers a title (not accepted).
    - **Calls say how long.** Both calls now say "It lasts N minutes" (30 by default), and call-now says it "calls N agents away from what they are doing".
    - **The meetings status hid schedules.** It asked for `limit` schedules and then dropped ended ones, so ten ended schedules hid every active one (and could answer "No meeting is planned"). It now skips ended ones while reading (up to 10 pages of the schedule list) and takes `after` (how many schedules were already shown; with `after` only schedules are listed). The "more" line names the number to ask for ("ask for the meetings after 10"), a rule the model applies from the owner's words alone; past the end it says there are no more. Planned meetings say "ask for up to 50" when cut.
    - **Prompt.** +118 characters (the `after` rule on the `meetings` kind, +88; "of the day they named", +23; the paragraph's last sentence dropped because the kind now names schedules): SIZE 152,217, set on purpose; the four operation lines have nothing to cut. Guide: one-off day, weekdays, past days refused, roster replaced, how to see more.
    - **Tests.** Two more tests on 4 backends (one-off day: written, tomorrow, Friday, invented, wrong day, past, earlier today, the spring gap and the autumn repeat in America/New_York at fixed instants; weekly days invented, "weekday", "Mon and Thursdays"; status: ten ended schedules then two on, one at a time with "after 1", past the end) and one pure test of both readers; existing tests extended (the real zone on a change, the roster note, a call's length). Own mutation checks on built files, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256, all caught: weekdays always named, "tomorrow" any day ahead, past moment allowed, roster note empty, ended schedules not skipped, daylight-saving gap not said, and two dual-guard checks (call-urgent `mode: "apply"` with its `proposalReason` line removed; call-now `mode: "profile"` with its line removed).
    - **Still not done:** the ones listed above except (2); a one-off day said as "next month on the 3rd" or "the 5th" alone is asked about rather than read.
  - **Second review (clean-context, 2026-11-23).** Main had not moved (8b1f436f), so nothing was merged; the forced build and the API docs were unchanged by the merge step. The helpers were tried directly on the built files with a script (no model) under host zones UTC, Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles, with identical results: "3pm", "15:00", "noon", "midnight", "half past two", "quarter to two" read right, "3 agents" is not a time, "3/4" with no year and "the 5th" are asked about, "in 2 weeks", "Christmas" and "yesterday" are asked about, Feb 29 of a year without one is refused by the date check, "tomorrow" on Dec 31 is Jan 1; the New York spring gap (2027-03-14 02:30 starts 03:30, 07:30 UTC) and autumn repeat (2026-11-01 01:30 is the first, 05:30 UTC) are right. Fixed:
    - **A time without am or pm was taken silently either way.** "at 3" passed the words check as 03:00 or 15:00, and the proposal showed only the 24-hour time. New `clockTimeReading` (`said` / `either` / not given; a leading zero such as `09:30` counts as said): a time read as night-time (before 06:00) from words without am or pm is asked about ("Did you mean 15:00?"), and any other such reading is said on the proposal ("read as 15:00 (in the afternoon), not 03:00").
    - **Which day was taken was hard to see.** A one-off date now shows its weekday and month ("once on 2026-10-30 (Friday 30 October)") and the time note says how far ahead it is on the zone's calendar ("today", "tomorrow", "in 8 days there"), so "Friday" said on a Friday (today or a week on), "next Friday" and "3/4/2027" read the other way round are plain on the proposal.
    - **The meetings status at its page cap.** When the ten-page read stopped first, it claimed more and named "after N" with the same N (all ended, or nothing more among the pages read), so asking again showed the same. It now says "Not every meeting schedule of this project could be read for this answer (it reads at most 1,000 of them, ended ones included), so there may be more than shown" and names no number.
    - **A retired agent taken off a roster was shown by its principal ID.** The roster note now also looks among retired agents, so it is named.
    - Guide: the am/pm rule and how the day is shown. Prompt unchanged (152,217, SIZE as set).
    - **Tests.** Extended on 4 backends (next Friday, the reading of a bare hour asked and said, "3am" and "09:30" say nothing more, the retired agent named) plus a page-cap test with a stand-in schedule source (ten full pages of ended schedules, then of active ones) and pure tests of `clockTimeReading` and the one-off date words. Own mutation checks on built files, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256, all caught: bare hour counted as said (5 failing), night reading not asked (4), leading zero not said (5), weekday and month dropped (5), how far ahead dropped (4), page cap claiming more (4), retired agents not looked up (4), and the dual guard of `meeting.schedule` and `meeting.update-schedule` together (`mode: "apply"` and the `proposalReason` line removed: 12).
    - **Left as it is.** "Friday" may be this week's or next week's (both within two weeks are accepted; the proposal shows which); a weekday name anywhere in the message counts ("a retro on Friday about Monday's outage" accepts a Monday, shown); short day forms that are also words ("sat", "sun") count as days; the roster note names up to 8 taken off and counts the rest. The model works the date out from Now (UTC) while the chat checks it on the meeting zone's calendar, so a model that took the UTC day near midnight is asked, never silently wrong.

### Chat-control gaps, second slice (2026-11-23): settling a conflict between the owner's instructions, role labels and resource detach/move/scope by words (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5)

Gaps 8 and 9 (in part) of the chat-control audit (2026-11-22). `decision.resolve-dispute`, `role.label`, `resource.unbind`, `resource.move` and `resource.scope` were real operations with no chat route, and a conflict between two of the owner's own instructions was not listed anywhere the owner looks.

  - **What is done.** (1) `decision.resolve-dispute`: new Needs-you item kind `dispute` (`status/status.ts`, owner only; text names the topic and both instructions; `members` carries them; answer choices are the decisions' IDs) read through a new `DecisionService.openDisputes(owner, limit)` (scans at most 20 pages of 500 `decision-dispute` records, oldest first, says `truncated`) and wired in `api/start.ts`. `needs-you.answer` answers kind `dispute` with the chosen decision ID (what the web buttons use; the same service call as `decision.resolve-dispute`, owner only). In chat, `decision.resolve-dispute(disputeTopic, choiceWords)` is a proposal in every profile: the conflict is found among the Needs-you items by words from its topic or either instruction, and the instruction that stands by words from its statement; the chat fills `disputeId` and `chosen` from the list. Several conflicts, or words that name no single instruction, ask (choices carry both instructions); none open is said plainly. (2) `role.label(name, label)`: label is the owner's words; clearing (label null) is refused unless the message says clear/remove/reset/drop/delete/unset/default. (3) `resource.unbind(resourceLabel)`, `resource.move(resourceLabel, locator)`, `resource.scope(resourceLabel, access, paths)`: the resource is found among the project's bound resources by its label (several and no label: asked; none fits: refused); the revision is read (`revision: "resource"` in `#revisionFor`); `access` is a fixed choice the words check lets through, so it is held to the owner's words here (write needs writ/edit/modif/chang/full, read needs read/view/look/see/inspect). A resource ID is accepted only when the owner said it or picked it from the choices, and must be bound to the project.
  - **Two guards each.** All five are `mode: "propose"` and also have an explicit line in `proposalReason` (`GAPS_REASON`), so removing either guard alone leaves the command shown first. Only mutating both is the dual failure; a mutation of the mode alone was not caught by the behaviour tests (the reason still shows it) but is by the table test, which also asserts the mode.
  - **Model-supplied values.** `GAPS_CHAT_ARGS` is the whole accepted argument set. `disputeId`, `chosen` and `resourceId` are accepted only to carry the owner's pick from a question the chat asked; the own-words guard refuses any such ID the owner did not write or pick. A revision, project ID and scope are never the model's.
  - **Prompt.** One sentence plus five operation lines: 152,217 to 152,899 characters (+682, under the 700 allowed). `SIZE` in `prompt-room.test.ts` moved to 152,899 on purpose. The Pi tool list is untouched (chat interpreter only).
  - **Guide.** New section "When two of your instructions disagree, role labels and resources", checked by a new test in `d01-user-guide.test.ts`.
  - **Tests.** `chat/chat-gaps2.test.ts` on the four backends (6 tests each, plus one table test): real chat, real `ModelInterpreter`, a stand-in model that answers only for an operation whose line lists every argument it uses, records every value the owner did not say (the cases that invent on purpose are counted), and sees no earlier answer. Conflict made by two stale sessions; item listed with both instructions; proposal shows words, not IDs; nothing chosen before the owner agrees; the chosen one stands afterwards and the item is gone; an invented choice, a made-up ID, no conflict, an unnamed instruction (asked, answer picked from the choices), several conflicts (asked, never the first taken), no fitting topic; the Needs-you answer by ID (owner only, a wrong ID refused, an agent refused); role label set, invented label refused, unrequested clear refused, clear; resources detached, moved, re-scoped with the real revision; invented place, invented access, unknown label, unbound resource, made-up and real-but-unsaid IDs all refused.
  - **Own mutation checks** (built files, restored from git after each; 10, all caught): missing instruction takes the first (4 failing), any words match any instruction (8), own-words guard off for `choiceWords` (4), a resource ID the owner did not say accepted (4; the first version of the test missed it because the bound-list check also stops a made-up ID, so the test now uses a real but unsaid ID), clear without saying so (4), access not held to the words (4), `proposalReason` line removed (4), mode `apply` (1, the table test), stale resource revision (4), `members` dropped from the item (12).
  - **NOT done.** `improvement.decide/group/bring`, `swarm.cancel`, `maintenance.request` (owner), `difficulty.reassign-parent`, `activity.unavailable`: still without a chat route (low value; each needs a name resolver for its target, and the prompt room left is small). The restart sweeps (`lifecycle.sweep`, `handoff.sweep`, `resume.sweep`) are deliberately not given chat routes: they are better run automatically at start (audit gap 10), which is a separate change. Pause, resume and stop were not touched (another slice). A conflict is listed in Needs-you only for the owner and only up to 50 at a time (`truncated` says more). `resource.move` has no `acknowledgeOverlap` by chat: an overlap with another project's binding is refused with the service's reason.
  - **ASSUMPTION:** all five controls are shown first in every approval profile (the smallest reversible choice; a label is cheap to set back, the others are not). **ASSUMPTION:** a conflict's instruction is named by words from the decision's statement (the interpreter's reading of the owner's words, which the Needs-you item shows), not from the old wording; if the words fit neither or both, the owner is asked with both statements. **ASSUMPTION:** an `access` the owner's words do not clearly give is refused rather than defaulted.
  - **First review (2026-11-23, Claude agent).** Checked: every model-supplied value (`disputeTopic`, `choiceWords`, `disputeId`, `chosen`, `name`, `label`, `locator`, `paths`, `resourceLabel`) goes through the own-words guard; only `resourceId` (own check: written in the message or picked) and `access` (own check) are exempt. Dispute membership is fixed when the dispute opens (a new instruction on a disputed topic is refused), and a settled dispute refuses the yes, so a late yes cannot drop an unseen instruction. Agents and task credentials get no dispute items and cannot settle one. The chat never sends `acknowledgeOverlap`. Fixed: (1) `resource.scope` write was let through by a word like "change" in a message that also said "read only" / "not write" / "don't let it change": now refused; (2) words that are one instruction whole beside a longer one containing them ("deploy on Friday" vs "never deploy on Friday") always asked: the whole match is now taken, any other overlap still asks; (3) a dispute about one task did not carry its `taskId` into the Needs-you item, so it was never ranked by the work it holds up or the critical path: now it does. Tests added (4 backends): whole-statement choice and part-of-both asks; a yes after the dispute was settled elsewhere is refused and the other choice stands; a task-scoped dispute carries the task; a successful move; a move onto another project's binding refused at the yes with nothing changed; a stale resource revision refused; write against "read only" words refused (two sentences); "several conflicts" now asserts the question is which conflict (one backend passed by list order before). Own mutation checks on built files, restored byte-identical by SHA-256, all caught on 4 backends: resource ID not in the words, clear without saying so, read-only words ignored, whole-statement preference removed, settled disputes listed, task not carried, several conflicts taking the first. Left as it is: the overlap refusal text names `acknowledgeOverlap` (an API argument; the owner cannot acknowledge an overlap by chat); a task-scoped owner credential reaching the Needs-you list gets the same `forbidden` from the dispute source as from the existing meeting-question source.
  - **Second review (2026-11-23, Claude agent, clean context).** Merged origin/main `9cb4ec3f`, then `32f42c98` (pause, Q02, W04 C, W11); the prompt is now 154,137 (main 153,455 plus this slice 682) and SIZE is pinned there (ceiling 156,137; the 160,000 cap holds). Fixed: (1) `resource.scope` sent no paths when the owner named none, which replaces a path-limited scope with the whole resource ("make Docs read only" on a resource limited to two folders opened all of it, unshown): the chat now keeps the current paths, needs words for the whole resource ("all of it", "whole", "every path"), refuses at once when nothing changes, and the proposal says what the project is left with ("can then only read only the 2 paths below", each path quoted); (2) access polarity in more sentence shapes (`accessSaid`): read is refused for "read and write", "full access", "no longer read-only" or an edit not turned down; write is refused for "read access", "only read it" and the earlier read-only words; "no longer read only" now allows write; the resource's own label ("Read Replica") is taken out before the words are read; (3) a move onto another project's location was refused at the yes with text naming `acknowledgeOverlap`, an argument the chat never sends: the chat now says plainly that nothing changed and what to do (a location that does not overlap, or detach the other project's resource first); the move's proposal shows the whole new location (up to 500 characters) rather than 77; (4) a conflict ranked past the first 50 Needs-you items was reported as "none of your instructions conflict": the chat now says it is not among the items it can read and to answer some first; (5) choice words the owner turns down ("not the SQLite one", "keep never deploy on Friday over deploy on Friday", "instead of", "rather than") or that stand only inside a longer instruction of the conflict now ask instead of choosing; quotes, closing punctuation, case and Unicode form no longer hide a whole instruction ("deploy on Friday."); (6) topic words are matched against the conflict's topic and its instructions (the Needs-you item now carries `topic`), not the line's fixed wording; words that name no topic ("the conflict") ask which one; the meaning says every other instruction of a conflict is dropped (a conflict can have more than two). Tests added (4 backends). Own mutation checks on built files, restored byte-identical by SHA-256, 13 in all, all caught in the end (three first survived and were made to fail by a stronger test or a correct mutation): turned-down choice ignored, label kept as an access word, "read and write"/"full access" ignored, paths not kept, raw overlap text, partial list called none, punctuation kept, "read access" not seen, scope meaning removed, generic topic words used as a topic, move line cut at 400, move locator cut at 77, words inside a longer instruction counted. Checked and left: the dispute scan (at most 20 pages of 500 dispute records, open and settled, plus one read per member of the open ones) runs on every owner Needs-you read and is not cached, the same per-request pattern as the other Needs-you sources; past 10,000 dispute records the list says it may be incomplete. `namesOneProposal` needed no change (a dispute or resource proposal's summary carries its topic or label like any other). Agents and task credentials still see no dispute items; resource choices list only the focused project's bound resources.
  - **Third check (2026-11-23, Claude agent, clean context, on `74f284f4`).** Fixed: (1) write access was still read from sentences that turn writing down ("don't allow writes", "it shouldn't be writable", "revoke write access", "stop it from writing", "writes are not allowed", "switch from write to read", "don't give it full access") and from "change" as the owner's own verb ("change the access to read"): every write word ("read and write", "full access" and "no longer read only" included) must now not be turned down in its own clause, by a word before it (not, never, no, stop, prevent, block, disallow, forbid, deny, remove, revoke, drop, take away, keep ... from, non-) or within the next four words after it (not, off, forbidden, revoked, ...); any turned-down write word refuses write; "change" counts only where it says what the project may do ("let it change", "can change"); the old setting of a "from ... to ..." is ignored. (2) The whole-resource words were found even when turned down ("not the whole thing", "don't open every path"): `wholeSaid` applies the same clause rule and also takes the label out. (3) Choice words beside the other instruction's own words ("keep MySQL over SQLite", "replace SQLite with MySQL", "prefer MySQL to SQLite") now ask which one stands, and more turned-down shapes ask ("never SQLite", "no to SQLite", "anything but SQLite", "SQLite is out", "SQLite should not stand"); a single turned-down place is enough to ask. ## W04 follow-up: bench variant C (2026-11-23, branch `card-w04-variant-c`)

W04's sixth acceptance clause, "bench variant C is run and recorded", was open: `scripts/pi-eval` refused C ("needs W04"), and the bench drives the Pi command line, where the worker's continuation hook does not exist, so C would have equalled B. This follow-up builds part (a), offline; part (b), the real run, is not done.

- **Done (a).** `scripts/pi-eval/continuation-extension.mjs` is a Pi command-line extension with the same decision as the worker's hook, at Pi's `agent_before_settle` boundary (a user-role `custom_message` entry plus `continue: true`). `pi-agent.mjs` loads it when the runner has put a continuation config in the run's environment. The runner (`lib/runner.mjs`) writes the config from the built pi-adapter (`loadContinuationConfig` in `lib/taskset.mjs`: the bound 3, the mark, the nudge words and the cut-off words), reads back the extension's counts (`readContinuation`) and records `nudges` and `continuation: { max, installed, nudges, lengthNudges, endedByReport, errors, logged }` (`installed` only when the extension read the runner's config with its bound; `logged` is the count of the extension's entries in Pi's own log). `taskset.json` variant C is now `"continuation": true` (no `needs`); `run.mjs` no longer refuses it; D is still refused (needs a relaunch driver, as before). `lib/classify.mjs` gained `reportEndsWork`.
- **Tests.** `continuation.test.mjs` (the extension, bad configs, counts-only file, the shipped task set, the built config), `runner.test.mjs` (stand-in agent mode `continued` runs the real extension: continued exactly 3 times, then stops; solves after 2 nudges and is a verified finish; thinking-only and length stops; a blocked report is not nudged; bound 1 and 0; variant A is not continued; an agent without the extension is recorded `installed: false`), and `isolation.test.mjs` (the real Pi against the stand-in server: 4 requests for an announced stop, the nudge in each later one; 1 request for variant A and for a done report).
- **Was not done at the time of part (a) (superseded by the recorded result below; text kept as history).** C has not been run on the Radiance route, so there is no variant C row in `results.jsonl`, and the W04 clause "bench variant C is run and recorded" stays open. This needs the local server (no model calls were made here). The command, from a checkout with the repository built (`npx tsc --build`): `node scripts/pi-eval/run.mjs --variants C --repeats 1 --results /srv/code/worktrees-pi/eval-results` (the Radiance gate waits for an idle server; add `--tasks quote-lines` for one task first). Then record the batch, commit, route and the report here, next to the A and B baseline.
- **Recorded result for (b) (2026-11-25, notes-only card, no model calls; checked against `results.jsonl` and the two batch reports of the bench's results folder).** W04 acceptance met. Clauses 1-5 are covered by offline tests: `packages/pi-adapter/src/continuation.test.ts`, `packages/pi-adapter/src/worker/process.test.ts` (including a restart between nudges, line 752), `packages/controller/src/dispatch/nudges.test.ts`, `packages/controller/src/remote/remote.test.ts`, and `packages/integration/src/w04-continuation.test.ts` through the real sandboxed worker. Clause 6, "bench variant C is run and recorded", is met by the runs below.
    - **What ran.** Variant C on the Radiance route (`qwen3.8-flash-next-iq4r`, thinking medium) from bench commit `f4330e14` (it exists on branch `card-w04-variant-c-run`). `git diff f4330e14 main` over `scripts/pi-eval`, `packages/pi-adapter/src/continuation.ts` and `packages/pi-adapter/src/worker/nudge.ts` is empty, so the bench and the nudge source are the same as main's (checked at main `a66b1bb4`). Batches: `batch-20261124T153731` (27 runs) and `batch-20261125T050221` (`m03h-1` times 3, a rerun after the server answered 502 to all three `m03h-1` runs of the first batch). In all 30 run records the continuation shows `installed: true`, with 0 to 3 nudges per run.
    - **Numbers (re-derived from the run records, equal to the reports).** First batch, 27 runs, 6 contaminated and left out (kind: another checkout), 21 counted. Verified finish: S 6/8 (75.0%), M 2/6 (33.3%), L 4/7 (57.1%; three of the seven are the 502 outage runs). False done (said done, held-back tests fail): 2/21 (9.5%, CI 2.7%-28.9%). The rerun: 3 runs, 1 contaminated, 2 counted: 1 verified finish, 1 false done. With the rerun in place of the three outage runs, L is 5/6 and false done is 3 runs (3/20 on that basis; 3/23 if the outage runs stay counted). Seven runs in all were contaminated and left out.
    - **Result: C does not meet the W01 release gates** (S at least 90%, M 85%, L 70%, false done at most 5%). Those gates are checked for the shipped variant on the real worker by W09; they are not a W04 acceptance item. This result is an input to W09, not a pass, and W09 must not count this C run as its own variant C.
    - **Earlier batch `20261124T052216`** (its nudge named a tool the bench agent does not have) is superseded and kept as recorded; the nudge fix section below explains it.
    - **Limits.** The bench uses a Pi command-line stand-in for the hook, so restart-safe counting and the controller's refusals were not exercised on a real model. One server and one model; repeats of one task are not independent samples; concurrency 3 with the Radiance idle gate off.
    - **The deliverable is narrower than written:** the shipped nudge names no unchecked plan steps (see the Left list of the W04 section: "The nudge names no plan step").
    - The per-batch tables are copied to `evidence/w04-variant-c-batches.md`. The card's status was not changed by this record.
- ASSUMPTION: the smaller of the two options is a Pi extension, not running the bench through the worker process: the worker needs a controller, storage and bridge, and would change what is measured (tools, prompts) besides the continuation; the extension changes only the one thing C is about.
- ASSUMPTION: the extension continues at `agent_before_settle`, Pi's last actionable boundary, so Pi's own retries and compaction have finished first (the analogue of Pi Durable asking `onYield` about a final answer).
- ASSUMPTION: the Pi command line has no `work.end`, so a final report that states done, partial or blocked as its result (the form variant B's prompt asks for) stands in for an accepted work.end and is not nudged; a reply without a stated result is nudged, even if it says it is finished in other words (cost: a nudge, then the agent states its result). An error or abort reply, or a run Pi itself reports as ended by an error or abort (the boundary's `outcome`), is never nudged (Pi's hard exits).
- ASSUMPTION: the nudge words are the worker's own (read from the built pi-adapter), including their mention of `nimblenewt__work-end`; variant B's prompt already tells the agent that on the Pi command line its report replaces that call.
- ASSUMPTION: the counts come from the extension's own file, because the extension is the one place that knows why it continued (a cut-off stop, a stated result); Pi's JSON log also shows each nudge as an `entry_appended` event of the extension's custom type, and the run records that count as `logged` next to it. A run whose extension never wrote counts, or could not read the runner's config, is recorded `installed: false` and is not a C measurement; `report.mjs` names such runs and runs whose two counts differ.
- ASSUMPTION (first review): the agent's sandbox can write the run's artifacts folder (Pi writes its log and the extensions their counts there from inside it, as for `arg-clean.json` since W01b), so an agent that set out to could change `continuation.json` or `agent.jsonl`. It cannot change the decisions themselves (they run in Pi's process, not in a tool), and changing one file without the other shows in the report; the hidden tests and the solution stay outside the sandbox for C as for A and B. Not tightened further: a protected record would need a writer outside the sandbox that sees Pi's boundary, which the Pi command line does not have.
- ASSUMPTION (first review): a plain stated result ("Done.", "Done: ...", "Not done: ...", "Result: partial") is enough to end the continuing, so an agent can end the run early by writing done. This matches W04 itself: the worker gives no nudge after any accepted work.end, and with no task contract (W05) a work.end done is accepted as it is; an early done is scored by the hidden tests and recorded as a false done, not as a finish. Requiring evidence before the done is taken is W05's check, not W04's, and would make C measure W05 as well.
- Limits: this is a stand-in of the hook, not the worker's code path: `turn.continue` refusals (pause, stop, awaiting approval, job running), restart-safe counting and lease checks have no counterpart on the Pi command line. The bound is per run (one request), as the worker's is per turn.
- **Second review (clean-context Claude agent, 2026-11-23).** Merged origin/main `f6ac43e8`. Problems found and fixed:
    - A variant C run whose continuation did not run as configured (not installed, or the counts file and Pi's log disagree) was only named in a note by `report.mjs` and still counted in C's table and gates, so a C that silently ran as B could have shown PASS under C's name. `lib/stats.mjs` now has `continuationOff`: such a run is left out of the variant's rates and fails its gate with the reason; `report.mjs` uses the same check (test in `stats.test.mjs`).
    - No test covered an extension that read a different bound than the runner recorded, nor Pi's log holding other custom entries; both now have tests (`runner.test.mjs`, `classify.test.mjs`); the two mutations they catch survived before.
    - README: the gates section said interface mismatches count as non-finishes only; the code (since an earlier lead decision) also counts them toward false done. Corrected, and the continuation rule added.
    - Checked and left as is: Pi's `agent_before_settle` contract in the installed Pi (handler entries replace the proposed list, so keeping `event.entries` is right; outcome is completed, aborted or error; committed entries are logged as `entry_appended`, so `logged` is real); the classifier ignores the nudge's user-role messages; the regexes the extension runs inside Pi stay in milliseconds on 20,000-character worst cases; the token budget is checked between runs and there is no runner retry, so a nudge only adds to its own run's use within the run's time limit; isolation code is unchanged by the branch and the config holds only the worker's words; `compare.mjs` (informational, no gates) still counts such runs like any other.
    - Mutation checks, each restored byte-identical by SHA-256, all caught: an unconfigured C run counted in rates, a counts mismatch ignored, Pi's error or aborted outcome ignored, the bound off by one, other extensions' proposed entries dropped, the runner's installed flag without the matching bound, any custom message counted as a logged nudge.
    - Variant C has still not been run on the Radiance route; part (b) stays open.

## Q02 fourth slice: the project review policy, its scheduler, and evidence counted by original source (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-23)

Card Q02 and card Q04 stay planned. Branch `card-q02-review-policy` off origin/main `2ff925cb`. Plain words first: a project can now carry a written review policy. The owner says which tasks need independent QA, when a review starts by itself (on each new code submission, every so many minutes, or when an incident is opened in the project), which extra checks the QA gate requires, whether a task may land without independent review, and how many truly independent sources must pass each check. The controller's regular round then creates the reviews the policy asks for, gives each to a reviewer who did not work on the task, and tells only that reviewer. It never pauses, stops, messages or takes work from the agents working on the task: a contributor's running attempt is not touched. Independent QA evidence is also counted by where it came from: a copy of a record and its original, and all records by one agent, are one source.

- **Chosen items.** The two clauses an audit found open: (a) the review policy record with scheduler (this also closes Q04's open clause "periodic and incident-triggered reviews run without interrupting contributors") and (b) counting QA evidence by original source (`DeskService.independence`, previously called only from a test).
- **The record** (`submissions/qa-review-policy.ts`, kind `qa-review-policy`, one per project, id = the project ID). Fields: `scope` (`workClasses` P and/or PC, `taskIds`; empty means all), `triggers` (`onSubmission`, `periodicMinutes` 15 to 43,200 or null, `onIncident`), `requiredChecks` (check names added to the task contract's, at most 20, no credential-shaped text), `gatesCompletion`, `independentSources` (1 to 5, default 1), and `since` (when each trigger was last switched on). Set only by the owner (`qa.review.policy.set`, fields left out stay, a repeated command ID is recorded once); read with `qa.review.policy.get` by the owner or an agent that may read the project's tasks (another project's agent: `not_found`). A project with no record has everything off.
- **Required checks.** The QA gate (`qa.evidence.gate`) adds the policy's check names to the contract's, for a task inside the scope. With the contract naming none, the policy's names are required and every check named in current independent records is still judged, as before.
- **Gates completion.** The landing gate now asks for the required checks with the task: `requiredChecks(projectId, taskId)`. When the policy has `gatesCompletion` and the task is in scope, `review` and `qa` are added to whatever the project's landing settings require (`withPolicyChecks`, order as everywhere). No other landing rule changed; `recheck` asks the same way.
- **Scheduler** (`QaReviewService.sweep`, the dispatcher loop `qa.review.schedule`, also in the maintenance barrier's sweep group; the owner can run it with `qa.review.sweep`). Per policy it (1) settles open requests: done when independent QA evidence was recorded on the request's code submission after the request was made, superseded when the task's newest code moved on; (2) replaces an assignee who can no longer review it (holds the task now, left the reviewers) or leaves the request waiting with the owner told; (3) creates new requests: on a code submission made after `onSubmission` was switched on, for the newest code of each unfinished task in scope each period (`p<n>`, n = minutes since the epoch divided by the interval), and for the newest code of up to 25 tasks in scope for each open incident that began after `onIncident` was switched on (at most 10 incidents). A request (`qa-review-request`, id from project, task, submission, trigger and cause, so a repeated round or a second controller makes it once) names one code submission; at most 100 are open per project, at most 25 are created per round, and a submission that already has an open review is not asked for twice.
- **Who reviews.** From `AgentService.reviewersAvailableIn` (active reviewer agents with a live grant in the project, never the submitter), leaving out everyone who submitted code on the task and the agent that holds the task now; the one with the fewest open reviews first, then by ID. The assignee gets one notice; when nobody is eligible the owner gets one Needs-you notice, and a later round assigns it when a reviewer appears. Notices are repeated by later rounds until they went through (`noticeAt`, `ownerNoticeAt`).
- **Does not interrupt contributors (proved).** The sweep writes only its own records (policy reads, request, request index) and sends one notice to the assignee. Tests: on all four backends a task with a live assignment and attempt gets a review created by a submission, a periodic round and an incident, and the assignment, attempt and task revisions are the same afterwards and the contributor is never told; through the composed controller (`api/start-qa-review-policy.test.ts`) a real admitted attempt of the contributor is still `active` with the same revision after the dispatcher's round created the review.
- **Counting by original source.** A QA record may cite the desk records it was derived from (`sources`, at most 10, each readable by the recorder). The gate groups independent records of a check that passed: two records are one source when the same agent recorded both, or when they cite desk records with the same original (`DeskService.independence`: a copy and a copy of a copy stand on the original); a check passes only when the number of such groups is at least the policy's `independentSources`. A shortfall fails the gate (`fewer_sources`, `shortfalls`, the check reads as missing). Default 1: nothing changes without a policy. A newest `failed` still fails whatever the count.
- **Chat and views.** `qa.review.policy.set` is a chat command (shown first, applied on the owner's yes); the status kind `qa_policy` (`status.ask`, project in focus) tells the policy and the open scheduled reviews 20 at a time (`after` = how many were already shown; `qa.review.requests` pages the same way). The interpreter prompt describes both in one paragraph; prompt growth is 556 characters (SIZE 152,217 to 152,773). The agent bridge tool list is unchanged (no new bridge tool).
- **ASSUMPTION:** one project-wide record with flat fields is enough (no per-task-kind rules); reversible by a later richer scope.
- **ASSUMPTION:** "work kinds" in scope are the two work classes P and PC (the contract's `workClass`) plus named tasks; reviews are of CODE submissions (QA evidence exists only for code).
- **ASSUMPTION:** a trigger starts from the moment the owner switched it on; the backlog is not reviewed backwards. Switching a trigger off and on, or changing the interval, starts it again.
- **ASSUMPTION:** reviewers are agents holding the reviewer role (as `reviewersAvailableIn` judges); agents holding only the qa role are not chosen by the scheduler (they may still record evidence on a request they see). Reversible: widen the port.
- **ASSUMPTION:** an incident review means a look at the newest code of tasks in scope (bounded to 25 tasks per incident), not a review of one named task; the incident ID is the cause.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the periodic trigger skips tasks that are done; an incident trigger also skips only cancelled tasks, so delivered work can be looked at after an incident.
- **ASSUMPTION:** records of one agent count as one source even without citations (the conservative count; an agent cannot make itself several sources).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the policy's required checks apply to the QA gate whether or not `gatesCompletion` is on (the flag controls landing only); a policy change counts from the next gate read and is not bound into the gate's read set.
- **Not done (said plainly).** A review request is not a submission the reviewer is granted access to: it names the code and relies on the reviewer's existing rights (the `reviewAssignments` read-grant of Q01b is still not wired). Closed (done or superseded) requests are not listed by any view; only open ones. A request is not re-notified after assignment except until delivered, there is no deadline or escalation on an unanswered review. A reviewer verdict that cites criteria and decision revisions and a rejection that cites an unmet owner requirement, a team vote never overriding an owner decision, automatic invalidation on `contract.set` and other dependencies (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) are as listed in the earlier slices. Source counting uses desk records the recorder cites; nothing yet makes an agent cite its sources, and evidence copied outside the desk system is not recognised. The policy is not part of hand-off packages, retention rules or the web view. The scan reads submissions page by page (bounded 20 pages) like the project QA view, so a very large installation may see `scanLimited` partial rounds. An owner chat command to run the scheduler now was not added (`qa.review.sweep` is API only).
- **Tests.** `submissions/qa-review-policy.test.ts` (4 backends, 5 tests each: policy record rights, validation and merge; gate with policy checks and source counting; scheduler on submission, periodic and incident with the contributor untouched; nobody eligible, reassignment, repeated notices and paging; landing needs `qa` and `review` for tasks in scope), `api/start-qa-review-policy.test.ts` (composed: chat proposal then yes, view, regular round, rights). Mutation checks on the built files, each restored byte-identical (SHA-256) and each caught: contributor not excluded, notices repeated every round, copy and original counted apart, one recorder counted as several, policy checks not added, gatesCompletion ignored, backlog reviewed backwards, resolved or old incidents trigger, a submission asked for twice, agent may set the policy, superseded never recognised, scope ignored by the scheduler, landing gate asking without the task (13 of 13).

### Q02 fourth slice review: the project review policy (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-23)

First independent review and fixes, on the branch merged with origin/main `db7757ca` (documents only since `2ff925cb`; no conflicts). Plain words: the policy, its scheduler and the source counting did what the card asks; the review tightened six places and added the tests that prove them.

- **Cost of the scheduler (fixed).** The dispatcher ticks every 5 s and ran the round each time, and each project with a policy scanned up to 10,000 submissions on its own (200 policies: two million record reads per tick). Now the dispatcher's call is throttled to once a minute of the controller's clock (`sweep({ throttled: true })`, the pattern of the landing bounds round; the owner's `qa.review.sweep` always runs; the shortest period is 15 minutes) and one round reads the submissions ONCE for every active project (`QaEvidenceService.newestCodeIn`, same bound and order as `newestCode`, which now calls it).
- **Incidents missed on a large installation (fixed).** The incident trigger read at most 10 pages of 200 incident records per project; incident IDs are hashes and resolved incidents are kept until purged, so past 2,000 records a new open incident could go unseen for good. Now one scan per round, for every project with the trigger on, reads as far as the incident service's own list does (100 pages of 500).
- **A contributor's evidence closed the review (fixed).** A request was settled by any evidence the QA gate counts as independent (anyone but the submitter of that submission), so an earlier submitter of the task, or the agent that holds it now, could close the review meant for someone who did not work on it. Now only evidence by a non-contributor (not a submitter of the task's code, not the holder) settles it; the QA gate itself is unchanged.
- **Cancelled tasks (fixed).** An open request of a cancelled task stayed open for ever, counted against the 100 open per project, and stayed on its reviewer's list. Now it is closed as superseded (`settledBy: "cancelled"`).
- **Chat own words (fixed).** `requiredChecks` is on the chat's list of fixed choices (it names landing checks elsewhere), and the words check does not read numbers, so the interpreter could add a check name, an interval or a source count the owner never said (the proposal still showed it first). Now `reviewPolicyForeign` (chat/commands.ts) refuses, with a question, a check name that is not whole words of the owner's message, an interval that is not a length they said ("every two hours", "30 minutes", "hourly", "daily", "weekly") and a source count that is not a number they said. Switches, work classes and task IDs stay fixed choices shown on the proposal.
- **Reads (fixed).** `qa.review.policy.get` showed every named task ID to an agent with the project's task read right even where a restriction hides one task from it; `qa.review.requests` listed a request assigned to the agent for such a task. Both now leave out tasks the reader cannot read (the owner sees all).
- **Owner notice wording (fixed).** "…independently (submission review): the agents that could have worked on it." now says "every reviewer agent of the project worked on the task or holds it now".
- **Checked and found sound.** Owner-only set (agents, task credentials, `notFromTask`); viewers and task credentials refused on reads; the sweep writes only its own records and an inbox notice that wakes nobody (`noticeFromController`), never the assignment, attempt or task; two controllers make a request once (stable ID, command ID `qrr:<id>`, the project index revision serializes creates; on PostgreSQL a concurrent create is `command_conflict` or a replay); a restart mid-round leaves request and index consistent (written in one operation); reviewers are active agents with the reviewer role and a live grant in THIS project (retired and disabled ones are left out, a reviewer of another project is not chosen); a desk-record citation is checked readable by the recorder, an origin is one hop so there are no cycles, citing more only joins sources; the default of 1 source changes nothing (no lookup is made); recheck parity with P09 (an added check refuses, a dropped one is skipped) now has a test.
- **Limits left (said plainly).** (1) Settled requests are kept (they grow with real reviews and submissions, not with time: a periodic request is not repeated while one is open). (2) Contributors are the submitters found by the bounded submission scan; on an installation with more than 10,000 submissions an old submitter may be missed. (3) P09 behaviour, not changed here: a landing whose first judgement required no checks at all is not re-read before it lands, so a policy that starts gating the task during that landing's host run does not stop that one landing. (4) Booleans of the policy are not checked against the owner's words (they are shown on the proposal for the yes).
- **Tests.** Two new tests per backend in `submissions/qa-review-policy.test.ts` (throttle, two projects in one round, contributor and holder evidence leave the review open, cancelled task closed, unreadable cited record refused; landing recheck added/dropped) and chat refusals and acceptances in `api/start-qa-review-policy.test.ts`. 28 of 28 in the slice file, the composed test, and 70 of 70 in the neighbours (QA evidence, QA chat, landing gate three files, chat command previews, prompt room), all alone with the sandbox required. Ten mutations on the built files (holder exclusion, contributor settle, throttle, cancelled, owner-only set, request visibility, one recorder one source, unreadable citation, recheck with task, chat check names), each caught, each file restored byte-identical (sha256).

#### Q02 review policy: second independent review (2026-11-23)

- **Gating with nobody to review (fixed).** With `gatesCompletion` on and no trigger switched on, nothing asked for the independent review a landing now needs, so a landing was refused (the author told) while the owner heard nothing. The scheduler now asks for a review (trigger `gate`) of the newest code of each unfinished task in scope that has no independent evidence from someone who did not work on the task, including code made before the policy; with no eligible reviewer the owner is told, as for the other triggers. Switching gating off and on again asks again (`since.gate` is part of the request's cause).
- **Policy changes mid-round (fixed).** An open request whose task left the scope, or whose trigger was switched off while review does not gate the task, stayed open and kept its reviewer busy. It is now closed as superseded with `settledBy: "policy"`. Limit: a submission-trigger request closed by narrowing the scope is not made again if the scope is widened later (its ID is kept); the next submission is reviewed.
- **Archived or deleted project (fixed).** The scheduler went on creating, assigning and telling for an archived project. It now leaves such a project alone; its open requests continue when it is active again.
- **Two controllers (fixed).** A replayed request creation (another controller made it first with its own pick) was counted and its local pick told, so a reviewer could be told about a request assigned to someone else. A replay is now neither counted nor told; the next round reads the stored request.
- **Notices on reassignment (fixed).** Notice IDs were fixed per request and recipient, so an agent assigned again after someone else (or the owner after a second stretch with no reviewer) was never told again, and the round retried that notice every minute. IDs now carry the start of the stretch (`assignedAt`, or the new `waitingSince`).
- **Cost (fixed).** `reviewersAvailableIn` (reads every agent) was called once per open request per round; now once per worker per project per round.
- **Source counting (fixed).** With `independentSources` > 1, passes older than a newer failure of the same check were counted towards the newest pass. Only the passes newer than the newest non-pass now count.
- **Chat (fixed).** `gatesCompletion` (it can stop every landing of the tasks in scope) was only shown on the proposal. It now needs landing or finishing words in the owner's message (land, merge, complete, finish, done, ship, gate, block, release, integrate, go in/out/live); otherwise it is refused with a question. The prompt is unchanged (SIZE pin unaffected).
- **Checked and found sound.** Periodic buckets are UTC epoch multiples (no daylight-saving effect; a clock set back makes at most a request of an older bucket, deduplicated by the open-request check); the landing recheck passes the task; reads refuse task credentials and viewers; the new tests have no fixed pauses, signals or POSIX paths.
- **Limits left (said plainly).** Raising `independentSources` applies to existing evidence at once (no grandfathering; the gate names `fewer_sources`). The periodic trigger re-reviews unchanged code each period by design. The replay fix has no dedicated test (it needs two controllers racing).
- **Tests.** One new test per backend in `submissions/qa-review-policy.test.ts`; the chat refusal of gating added to `api/start-qa-review-policy.test.ts`; the existing periodic test now expects the switched-off submission request to close.
## K07 quiesce, checkpoint and gate-clean cancel slice (Claude agent, 2026-11-23)

Branch `card-k07-quiesce` off origin/main `2ff925cb`. A clean-context audit named three open K07 clauses: Quiesce without release (and restoring the prior lifecycle state), the Checkpoint, and "cancelled maintenance clears only its own gates". This slice does all three, offline.

- **Quiesce.** When a window is prepared and open, and the embedder gives it a quiesce port (the real controller does): the window records the installation's pause gate as it found it (`active`, or `paused` by someone else), pauses the installation itself when it was active (so no waiting or parked attempt starts or resumes while the release switches), and suspends every `running` attempt with the dispatcher's own Suspend (new calls refused, calls in flight settled, a checkpoint taken), never releasing or force-stopping it. Only a `running` attempt that cannot be made quiet holds the window up (it waits and says which, and ends `deferred` when the window closes); `waiting` and `parked` attempts have no worker, do not hold it, and are counted in the window's one-line summary. Every step is written before the next (the record of what it froze is saved before the freeze; the pause uses a fixed command ID, so a crash between the pause and its record is settled by replay and never pauses twice). A freeze somebody else set is never recorded as the window's and never lifted by it.
- **Put back.** When the window ends in any way (cancelled, committed, reverted, missed, deferred, failed) it releases the attempts it froze and lifts its own pause, in the same sweep (or at the cancel). It finds its own pause by the pause request's operation ID and actor, so a pause already there before the window (the owner's) stays, and so does a pause the owner set after the window's was lifted. A restore step that fails is kept in the record (`quiesce.problem`) and tried again at every sweep; the owner's notice is filed as before. While a window is `activated` (waiting for the release to confirm its start) the installation stays quiet.
- **Checkpoint.** Once quiet, and before the final prepare check and the switch, the window takes a snapshot through a checkpoint port (in the controller: the installation's own backup run, `backUpNow("manual")`, then `verifyBackup` on it) and records its name and manifest digest. A snapshot that cannot be taken, or does not verify, fails the window before anything switches (the owner is told; everything the window held is put back). Nothing new is copied beyond what the backup does (state, configuration and the artifact blobs the backup already holds).
- **Owner reach.** Cancel and the `release_windows` status already reach chat in free words; the status line now says what is quiet (or what is not yet put back) and the checkpoint. The interpreter prompt gained one sentence (about 250 characters; `SIZE` pin unchanged, inside the +2,000 ceiling).
- Tests: `release/windows-quiesce.test.ts`, 11 cases on 4 storage backends (44 runs): running, waiting and parked attempts; the checkpoint order (pause, freeze, snapshot); the hold when a freeze fails, and the deferral at close with everything put back; cancel leaving an owner's earlier pause and another party's freeze; cancel lifting only the window's own pause; the owner lifting the window's pause mid-window; a crash before the pause; a failed restore retried; the checkpoint failing in two ways; no ports = first-slice behaviour. Mutation checks (apply, see a test fail, restore): waiting counted as running; freezes never released; pausing when already paused; checkpoint verification ignored; lifting whichever pause is on the gate; no pause-lifted check; cancel without the put-back; freezes by others claimed as the window's; a failed restore treated as done (9, all caught).
- ASSUMPTION: the window uses the installation-scope pause gate for "dispatch suspended" (the dispatcher already refuses to start attempts under it) rather than a new gate kind. A pause held by someone else when the window opens is left alone, and the owner cannot add a second pause to the same gate (the gate holds one pause), so the window cannot tell an owner pause made during the window from its own; it lifts the pause only if the gate is still the very request it made.
- ASSUMPTION: if the owner lifts the window's pause while the window is open, the window does not pause again against the owner's word: it waits, says so, and ends `deferred` if not cancelled or re-paused.
- ASSUMPTION: a checkpoint failure fails the window (the owner sets a new one) rather than retrying: the common cause (disk full, the backup held for maintenance) is not fixed by waiting a minute.
- ASSUMPTION: suspended attempts are released only when the window ends, not at the activation: the controller restarts into the new release (the launcher runs it at the next start) and its recovery resumes attempts from their checkpoints.
- **First review (Claude agent, 2026-11-23).** Merged origin/main `014db609`. Problems found and fixed, each with a test on 4 backends unless said:
    - An owner's Stop or Suspend of the installation during a window takes the window's pause over (the stop service keeps a pause that is there and marks it taken over); the window's end lifted it anyway, letting new work start under a stop. `PauseService.gateState` now also says `takenOver`, and the window leaves such a pause for the owner to lift (its summary says so).
    - An attempt holds one freeze: a landing or recipe change that lifted the window's freeze and froze again (or froze between the window's look and its freeze) had its freeze lifted by the window's end. The window's freeze reason now starts with `maintenance window <id>:`, the port gives each attempt's freeze reason, and the window lifts only a freeze that still carries it (the others are counted in the summary and kept).
    - While held by one attempt that would not go quiet, every sweep suspended all the others again, each time settling and writing a new attempt checkpoint (for up to a day of sweeps). The attempts already made quiet are recorded (`quiesce.settled`) and not suspended again.
    - An attempt whose start was already under way when the pause closed the gate could become running after the window's one look and run through the switch. The window now looks again after each round of suspensions (up to 4 rounds, as the H12q coordinator does).
    - The checkpoint verified the new backup without a key, so on an installation whose backups are sealed for everything every window failed ("give the passcode"). `backup/checkpoint.ts` (`checkpointOf`): a plain backup is checked in full; a sealed one has its manifest read again from disk and compared with the one written, and the record and status line say its files were not opened (the controller never reads the passcode by itself). Tested on real plain and sealed backups.
