  **Second review (2026-11-24, Claude agent, clean context).** Safe in a running controller: every clock the access check can read there (the loaders' `runner.now()` and the machine's) is the system clock, because the `clock` options of `startApi` (dispatch, notifications, stall, backup) are set only by tests; nothing in the product sets a time source, replays at a recorded time or restores a backup at its old time, so a principal that lost its registered clock (a spread copy, a hand-built service principal, one passed across a process) gets the same answer as one that kept it. Principals built by hand (meeting floor 2026-01-01, maintenance 2026-11-11, the `service:*` readers) have no grants with an end, or are owners, so the time judged at cannot change their answers. Copies checked: `GrantService.explain`, `grantIdsUsed` and the dispatcher's `usedFor` pass an explicit `now`; `policy.evaluate` copies with one grant that has no end; `recovering` makes an owner. One fix: `holdsIn` in `catalog/catalog.ts` (whether an agent is in a toolbox entry's project audience) judged each grant on a spread copy with no time, so in a rig it used the machine's clock while `allows` on the same principal used the rig's (an agent whose grant naming the project ends between the two would drop out of the audience once real time passed it, the same kind of date-dependent test this card is about; in production the same answer). It now passes `now: expiryTime(by)`; a new test in `security/access-clock.test.ts` (fails without the fix). Known and unchanged: "never earlier than `asOf`" is a floor, not monotonic: if the system clock is set back after a principal was loaded, a grant that ended between the two readings holds again until the clock passes its end once more (the old machine-clock behaviour did the same). The cost per check is one `WeakMap` lookup and one clock read, as before. Breakages on built files (each restored, sha256 equal), all caught on `access-clock` and `toolbox-maintainers`: `holdsIn` without the time (1 fails), floor removed (2), loader clock ignored (12), `effectiveOf` not registering (8), an unregistered copy judged at `asOf` only (1), `allowsExactly` back to `asOf` (1). The two files pass 38/38 with the machine clock moved +0, +30 and +400 days.
- **Windows exhaustive failure on main 7c9d6c75, worker package (2026-11-24, card win-shard-hang).** The Windows shard 1 jobs (Node 22 and 24) were reported as a silent stall. They were not: the step durations (55 and 85 minutes) are in the normal range (62-74 minutes on the earlier green runs), and each log ends with a real failure in the worker package, the last package shard 1 runs: `per-job access lists on real NTFS` in `windows-host-real.test.ts` (`wsb start failed (exit null): spawn ...\wsb.exe ENOENT`, "the task ended without reporting an exit code", exit 71 instead of 0). Cause: the test builds its stand-in for the Windows Sandbox client as a plain spread of the real Windows host with a replaced `run`. Since the wsb-repair work every `wsb` command goes through the host's `runWsb` (the scheduled-task launch), and the spread kept the real `runWsb`, so the replaced `run` was never asked about `wsb` and the real task launch tried a real `wsb.exe` that is not installed on the runner. The test only runs on Windows, so no Linux run could show it. Fix: `withRun(host, run)` in `windows-host.ts` returns a copy whose program calls and `wsb` calls both go to `run`; the test uses it. Regression tests (run on every OS) in `windows-task-launch.test.ts`: a copy made with `withRun` never reaches the original's task launch, and a source scan fails if a test that uses the real host builds a stand-in with `...host,` followed by `run:`. Per-call limits were already present (every `wsb` call has `timeoutMs`; the runner's per-file limit stopped the file), so there is no new timeout. **Not proven offline:** that the corrected test passes on a real Windows host; the next Windows exhaustive run shows it. The 161 s the real-host test "the probes also work inside the exact environment" took on Node 24 is a separate slowness, not a failure, and is unchanged.

## Windows AppContainer experiment (2026-11-24, Claude agent; branch `card-win-appcontainer-exp`; an experiment, no product wiring, no plan status touched)

**Purpose.** The Windows Sandbox (`wsb`) backend is dropped: it needs an interactive session, `wsb start` is refused from a service, it needs UAC and it is Pro-only. Owner decision 2026-11-24: for now,
a simpler native baseline that works unattended from a service, with no virtual machine, no UAC at run time, on every edition: a low-privilege AppContainer (LPAC) with no network capability, inside a Job Object
(kill on close, memory and active-process limits), with explicit ACL entries for the container's SID only on a temporary workspace. `experiments/windows-appcontainer/` builds the cheap experiment that proves or
disproves this: a small Rust launcher (`windows-sys` only), a probe that runs inside the container (`probe.mjs`), a harness (`run-experiment.mjs`) and a manual workflow
(`.github/workflows/windows-appcontainer-experiment.yml`: hosted Windows, plus a job for the owner's service runner that runs only when the input `own_runner` is ticked, default off, 45 minute limit). The README lists every Win32 call.

**What was built and checked here (Linux).** The launcher type-checks for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (`cargo check`); it was NOT linked or run (no Windows machine, no mingw linker). The harness logic is tested on Linux with a fake launcher
(`scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs`): argument building and quoting, the matrix, fixtures including a real offline `npm ci` of the tiny fixture package, link planting and its failure, the probe run unconfined (it
reaches every fixture, which proves a Windows denial means something), verdicts, host witnesses, report schema, clean-up and fail-closed paths, and guards on the launcher source and the workflow.
Rust dependencies are outside `licenses:check` (it reads `package-lock.json` only); the one crate, `windows-sys` (MIT OR Apache-2.0), is pinned by `experiments/windows-appcontainer/launcher/Cargo.lock` and built with `--locked`.

**The unknowns, exactly, and what each result would mean.**
1. *Do node, git and npm start under LPAC with only the minimal grants?* Grants given: program install folders read+execute (soft: they may need rights the account lacks), the temp workspace, home and scratch modify, the probe folder read-only.
   Tool probes pass = the minimal set is enough. A tool fails = the "access denied" lines recorded at start-up say which folder or file (a registry key, `%ProgramData%`, a DLL folder) needs a further grant, or whether LPAC is too strict and a plain AppContainer (the cells with the policy attribute off or opt-in) is the usable baseline.
2. *Do all ten containment cases hold?* A case is `pass` only when every attempt got an access-denied code and the host witness saw no change; `weak` when nothing got through but a refusal was another error; `FAIL` is a real leak. Expected: the nine denial cases hold because the container SID has no entry outside its grants.
   `deny-write-protected-name` is expected to FAIL in `baseline-no-protect` (an ACL has no notion of protected names) and hold in the other cells because of the explicit deny entry on `.git`; if the deny entry does not stop a delete or a create inside `.git`, the protected-name rule needs another mechanism.
3. *Junctions and symbolic links.* Junctions (no privilege) are tested; file links only when the account may create them (the run records it). A pass means the target's ACL is judged, not the link's.
4. *Win32k disabled.* Whether Node, git and npm start with Win32k system calls disabled (the cells with Win32k disabled); a launcher refusal at `create-process` or a program that dies at start-up means this mitigation cannot be used for these tools.
5. *Does it work with nobody signed in, and without administrator rights?* Only the own-runner job answers it (a service, session 0). The report records the session id, whether the run was elevated, and every soft grant that was refused with an access-denied or privilege error. If grants on the install folders are refused, the baseline needs a one-time setup step (an administrator grants the container read+execute on the tool folders) or tools copied into a folder the account owns; that is a product decision for later.
6. *Hosted result versus service result.* The hosted runner is an administrator with an open session, so it is only the first answer; it cannot show 1 to 5 for a normal service account.

**What a Windows run still has to show (not testable here).** That `CreateAppContainerProfile` works from a service, that the policy attribute value is accepted, that the job list attribute and the handle list work together, that the output files opened by the launcher are usable by the container,
that loopback is blocked (AppContainers are isolated from loopback unless exempted), that ACL grants and revokes propagate and leave no entries, that an AppContainer child can use a console-less `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` start with files as standard handles, and the numbers (elapsed time, leftover processes).

**ASSUMPTION:** the launcher gives the child only the environment it is told (nothing inherited) and standard input from `NUL`, so an experiment run cannot leak the harness's environment; a real product launcher would decide its own list.
**ASSUMPTION:** a fixed profile name (`NimbleNewtExperiment`) is reused if it exists and is deleted at the end only when this run created it.
**ASSUMPTION:** the LPAC-off cells and the cells with the opt-out flag off and the policy attribute absent are the same configuration; they are run anyway and labelled as such (they show run-to-run noise).
**ASSUMPTION:** the offline `npm ci` uses a local tarball named in the lockfile (with its integrity hash) and an npm cache folder inside the container's scratch folder, not a pre-filled registry cache; a registry-shaped cache is a later refinement.
**ASSUMPTION:** a denial is only `pass` with an access-denied error code; a missing path or a refused connection is `weak`, so a container that merely hides things is not counted as proven.
**ASSUMPTION:** nothing needing real credentials, real customer data or the owner's folders is used: the owner's profile folder is only listed (and expected to be refused); every other path is a fixed fixture under a fresh temporary folder, removed in a finally path.
**Not done:** no product wiring, no change to `containment.ts`, the sandbox launcher or the plan's status; the other agent's `docs/nimblenewt/windows-isolation-plan.md` is not touched here.

**Review (2026-11-24, clean-context Claude agent).** Checked every Win32 call in `win.rs` against Microsoft Learn (UpdateProcThreadAttribute: value sizes, handle list needs inheritable handles and bInheritHandles TRUE, values must outlive the list, Win32k disable = bit 28 of the first DWORD64, job list Windows 10+; SetNamedSecurityInfoW: propagates inheritable entries to existing children, needs WRITE_DAC). Attribute numbers, SECURITY_CAPABILITIES with no capability, the ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS path, the deny-write mask (SYNCHRONIZE and READ_CONTROL removed), canonical order from SetEntriesInAclW, LocalFree/FreeSid on every returned pointer, the single CreateProcessW and the revoke-on-every-exit guard were right; `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` is clean. Fixed: (1) the probe would most likely never have started inside the container: Node canonicalizes its entry file's path at start-up with `lstat` on every ancestor folder, and the fixtures live under the account's profile, which a container cannot read (community report https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/34872 for a different Windows sandbox; unverified for AppContainer), so the probe now starts with `--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` (it imports only `node:` modules); npm does not get them, its start-up is part of the result; (2) when the probe's report is missing, the first lines of the child's error output are kept and shown (`stderrHead`), so one Windows run says why; (3) the probe's entry check compares paths, without case on Windows (a drive letter or 8.3 name in another case would have silenced it); (4) revoke now writes nothing when the DACL holds no explicit entry for the container (idempotent, needs no rights: the harness's clean-up revoke after a dead launcher no longer reports soft grants that never applied as "left"), and a revoke that wrote is read back with GetAce/EqualSid, an entry still there being an error; (5) the attribute-list buffer is pointer-aligned (it was a `Vec<u8>`); (6) a failed wait after the child started no longer prints `childStarted` twice with the second saying false; (7) both workflow run steps write the step summary even when the harness ends non-zero, then exit with its code. **Only a Windows run shows:** whether Node, git and npm start under LPAC with these grants (npm walks ancestor folders itself), whether SetNamedSecurityInfoW's propagation into the workspace follows the planted junctions (that would grant the container its link targets and show as a FAIL of the link cases, never a pass; the targets are fixture folders only), whether the AppContainer network block holds with the runner's firewall settings, CreateAppContainerProfile under the service account, Win32k disable with node.exe, and the time a whole matrix takes (nine cells at up to five minutes each would pass the 40-minute hosted limit if every cell hung).

### Windows AppContainer experiment, round 2 (2026-11-24, Claude agent; branch `card-win-appcontainer-r2`; experiment only, nothing flipped, not pushed)

**What round 1 showed (hosted `windows-latest`, run 45499098682, session id 2, elevated).** The launcher builds, creates the container profile and starts the child, so `CreateAppContainerProfile`, the attribute list, the job and the ACL grants work
on a hosted runner. Node never produced a report in any of the nine cells: LPAC (policy optout) ended in 40 ms with exit 0x80000003 and `WSAStartup: (10107) A system call has failed.` (libuv starts Winsock at start-up; the LPAC has no way to it);
the policy with the opt-in value, and the plain AppContainer, did not end within 300 s; Win32k disabled ended with 0xC0000142 (DLL initialisation failed) after about 20 ms in every cell, so Win32k lockdown cannot be used with Node. Eight cells reported
`grants left: 8` (error 0x20000001: the read-back found the container's deny entry on `.git` still there after the revoke) and one cell left one process.

**Cause of "grants left: 8".** Only the deny entry on the protected `.git` folder survived; all allow entries were removed. The revoke used `SetEntriesInAclW` with `REVOKE_ACCESS`, which did not remove that deny entry (the read-back caught it, as designed).
Fix: the revoke now removes every explicit (non-inherited) allow or deny entry that names the container from a copy of the DACL with `DeleteAce`, then writes it and reads it back (`remove_explicit` in `win.rs`). Every grant in a run's JSON line now also carries
`entriesLeft` (read after the revoke), a new read-only `check --grant ...` command reads the same count for any paths, and the harness (matrix, ladder and firewall) reads every granted path back after each cell or variant, revokes and reads again when anything is left,
and reports both reads. Not provable on Linux: the Windows run shows whether the deny entry is now gone; the Linux tests pin the source shape (hand removal, read-back, `check`) and the harness's handling of entries that stay or go.

**What was added.** (1) Launcher: a repeatable `--capability SID-or-NAME` (string SIDs through `ConvertStringSidToSidW`; the three network capabilities by their documented well-known SIDs S-1-15-3-1, S-1-15-3-2, S-1-15-3-3; any other name, for example
`registryRead` or `lpacCom`, through `DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName`; an unresolvable name stops the run at stage `capability`), and a hang diagnosis taken just before a timed-out job is ended (alive or not, processes in the job, CPU of the process and each thread over two samples one second apart:
no CPU means waiting; it cannot say what a thread waits on). (2) `ladder.mjs` and `--mode ladder`: per variant the steps `cmd.exe /c echo hi`, `hostname.exe`, `node -e "0"`, `node --version`, `node -e "require('net')"`, `node -e "process.stdout.write('x')"`, a file write, `git --version`,
45 s per step (two timeouts skip the rest of a variant). Sixteen variants: plain AppContainer with no capability and with variations (program folders not granted; TEMP and working directory in the workspace; no job limits; `--jitless`; NODE_OPTIONS set; tools copied into the workspace),
plus internetClient, plus internetClient and privateNetworkClientServer, the LPAC with no capability, with registryRead, with registryRead and lpacCom, with the wide set, the opt-in policy value with registryRead, LPAC with internetClient, LPAC with copied tools.
(3) `--mode firewall`: a capability that allows outbound networking is given (`ac-inet-private`), an outbound BLOCK rule scoped to the container's package SID is added with `New-NetFirewallRule ... -Direction Outbound -Action Block -Package <SID>` (exact text in the README and the report), read back, and the container's outbound and loopback
connections are counted by the host's own listeners with and without the rule, while a control outside the container is counted too; the rule is removed in a finally path and its absence read back. (4) The hosted job now runs the ladder, then the firewall experiment, then the matrix at 60 s per cell (round 1's 300 s per cell was spent on hangs); `own_runner` stays off by default.

**What the round-2 run should answer.** (a) Does any program start in a no-capability AppContainer (cmd, hostname), and which node step is the first to fail? (b) Does `require('net')` / Winsock start-up work once the container has internetClient, once an LPAC has registryRead, lpacCom or the wide set, or with the opt-in policy value? i.e. what is the smallest set
that lets node and git run, and does node run at all without a network capability? (c) For the 300 s hang: in the hang report, is the node process alive and idle (waiting: for example on a missing console, a blocked handle or a loader lock) or busy; do `--jitless`, no job limits, TEMP in the workspace, not granting the program folders, copied tools or NODE_OPTIONS change it?
(d) If node needs internetClient to start, can the network still be cut by a package-scoped firewall block rule, for outbound and loopback, with an outside control unaffected? (e) Is the `.git` deny entry gone after the revoke (`ACL read-back ... no entry left` in every cell)? What only a Windows run can prove: all of these.

**ASSUMPTION:** if node only runs with a network capability, the firewall block rule (administrator at install or per run) is the fallback design; that is judged by the firewall result, not decided here.
**ASSUMPTION:** the firewall experiment's clients are `curl.exe` (System32) and node; the evidence is what the host's listeners counted, never what a client printed. A container whose capability alone does not allow the outbound connection makes the result `inconclusive`, not a pass.
**ASSUMPTION:** the hang diagnosis stays small (CPU over one second, thread count) on purpose; it does not read thread wait reasons (that needs undocumented system information calls or a debugger).
**ASSUMPTION:** the capability set "wide" is a guess at the documented LPAC capability names a console program could touch; a name the system does not derive makes that variant `not started (capability)`, which is itself a result.
**Not done:** no change to `containment.ts`, the sandbox launcher or any plan status; no push; the launcher was only type-checked (`cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline`), never run.

### Windows AppContainer experiment, round 3 (2026-11-24, Claude agent; branch `card-win-appcontainer-r3`; experiment only, nothing flipped, not pushed)

**What round 2 showed (hosted run 45504495155).** A plain AppContainer with no capability runs `cmd`, `hostname`, `node -e 0`, `node --version`, `require('net')`, a stdout write and a file write in the granted workspace in every no-capability variant (also with
internetClient). An LPAC with no capability fails (`WSAStartup 10107`, hostname exit 1); an LPAC with `registryRead` (opt-out or opt-in policy), with `registryRead` + `lpacCom` and the wider set run Node. `git.exe --version` failed everywhere (exit 0x80, "could not open
'/dev/null' for reading and writing: Permission denied"). The firewall mini-experiment was inconclusive. Round 1's matrix cells were all `inc` because the probe's report was missing.

**What round 3 changed.**
1. *The probe always ends* (`probe.mjs`): every network attempt has a 3 s limit (socket idle timeout plus a hard timer, `destroy` on every path), tools write to files (not pipes) with a limit each cut down to a 52 s budget, a watchdog prints a partial report naming the
step after 60 s, the harness's hard limit is 90 s per cell, and a progress file gets a line before and after each step; the harness keeps its tail when the report is not complete and the markdown shows it next to the launcher's hang diagnosis. *Cause of round 1's
300 s:* not known. The probe's tools were started with `spawnSync` and Node's default pipes, with limits of 120 to 180 s each, so a few slow or stuck tools exceed 300 s without any single "hang"; `diag-spawn-modes` now starts `node -e 0` from inside the container with files, pipes and ignored handles, and the progress file will name the step if anything still stalls.
2. *Why the firewall run had no capability:* `parseCli` defaulted `--variants` to `all`, and `runFirewall` only used its own default (`ac-inet-private`) when the value was missing, so it took the first variant (`ac-nocap`). Fixed (`all` or nothing means the default), and the verdict is now `inconclusive` when the launcher's line reports fewer capabilities than the variant names.
3. *Git* (`--mode git`, `round3.mjs`). Cause from the sources of git for Windows (`main`): `common-init.c` `init_git()` calls `sanitize_stdfds()` on every start; `setup.c` implements it as `xopen("/dev/null", O_RDWR)`; `wrapper.c` `xopen` dies with "could not open '%s' for reading
and writing"; `compat/mingw.c` `mingw_open` maps "/dev/null" to `nul` and calls `_wopen`. So git itself opens the NUL device for reading AND writing; round 2's launcher gave a read-only NUL as standard input and never tested that. The launcher can now give the child NUL read-write, a real file,
an empty or an open anonymous pipe as standard input, and pipes for output (a launcher thread copies a pipe into the output file). The ladder has 17 variants (standard-handle kinds, the two git.exe programs, copies, `cmd /c`, `MSYS=...`, no `GIT_*` variables, HOME in the workspace, `-c core.fsmonitor=false`, three LPAC variants), each also runs a node script that opens `NUL` and `\\.\NUL` in modes `r`, `w`, `r+` inside the container,
and reads the NUL device's DACL and label by a fixed PowerShell script (is ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES, or the LPAC group ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES, on it?). *The cause on the hosted runner is a measurement of that run, not decided here*; if `r+` is refused for the container and the device's DACL lacks the package group, the fix is outside the container's control (a system object's ACL) and git would need another route (a different Git build, a shim, or running git outside the container).
4. *Configurations* (`--mode cases`): eight cells (`ac-nocap`, `ac-nocap-noprotect`, `ac-inet-private`, `-fwblock`, `-loopback`, `-loopback-fwblock`, `lpac-optout-reg`, `lpac-optout-reg-com`), with a per-cell table, a table with one row per case and one column per configuration and a per-step time table. Block rule (`New-NetFirewallRule -Package`) and loopback exemption (`CheckNetIsolation LoopbackExempt -a -p=<SID>`) are read back before the cell and a cell whose conditions are not confirmed is not run; removal is read back in a finally path.
5. *Junctions and `.git`*: new probes `extra-junction-self-made` (the container makes junctions to the controller's folder, an outside folder and the protected folder and reads/writes through them), `extra-hardlink-read`, `extra-protect-rename-dir`, `-delete-dir`, `-replace-junction`, `-rename-parent` (judged by the host's own view of the folder, each success undone at once, run last), a launcher `grant` command that leaves the entries and an `inheritedEntries` read-back, and `--mode links` (does a grant on the workspace put an entry on the target of a junction inside it? controls: a file and a folder inside the workspace must show inherited entries).
6. *Timing* (`--mode timing`): five container starts against the same program outside, node start, 100 files written, `git init/add/commit` of 100 files (only where `git --version` works inside; outside as baseline) and an offline `npm ci` of 40 local packages, in `ac-nocap` and `lpac-optout-reg-com`.
7. *Workflow*: one hosted step per mode (ladder, git, cases, links, timing, firewall; all after the first with `if: always()`, each with its own limit), job limit 75 minutes, `own_runner` still off by default (its two steps run `cases` and `git`).

**What the round-3 run should answer.** (a) In which step, if any, does the probe still stop (the progress file), and does `diag-spawn-modes` show pipes failing inside the container? (b) Which of the 17 git variants, if any, starts git; does the container open `NUL` with `r+`; is ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES on the device and does an LPAC lose it? (c) The verdict table for the ten cases, the extra probes and the tools per configuration: do the deny-network cases still pass with a network capability (they should leak only with the capability and the loopback exemption and no rule, and hold with the rule), do `git init/add/commit`, `npm --version` and the offline `npm ci` work in each. (d) Does a grant on the workspace reach a junction target; does the container follow a junction to a protected folder; which of create-inside, rename, delete and replace-with-junction on `.git` pass (the contrast cell `ac-nocap-noprotect` shows what the container alone stops), and can the workspace folder itself be renamed. (e) Container start time and the cost of a 100-file commit and a 40-package `npm ci` against outside.

**ASSUMPTION:** a diagnostic probe (`diag-*`) has no verdict (`info`); only cases and extras with an expected outcome are judged.
**ASSUMPTION:** the NUL device's ACL is only read; granting the container rights on a system device is not part of this experiment (it changes a system object and is not something a product could do per run).
**ASSUMPTION:** loopback exemption and firewall rule need administrator rights on the runner; the hosted runner is elevated, the own runner may not be, and a cell whose conditions cannot be confirmed is reported as not run.
**Not done:** the cause of round 1's hang and of git's refusal are not proven (only a Windows run can show them); no change to `containment.ts`, the sandbox launcher or any plan status; no push; the launcher was only type-checked (`cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline`), never run.

### Windows AppContainer experiment, round 3b (2026-11-24, Claude agent; branch `card-win-appcontainer-r3b`; experiment only, nothing flipped, not pushed)

**What round 3 showed (hosted run 45510001368).** (1) The cases mode gave no verdicts: all eight configurations `timed out`, every case `inc`. The progress file shows the probe ran through every step up to `end diag-nul-open` and hung at `start diag-spawn-modes` (the diagnostic that starts `node -e 0` from inside the container with `spawnSync`); the watchdog did not fire (a blocked event loop stops timers) and the report is printed only at the very end, so the computed verdicts were lost. (2) `git.exe` fails in all 17 variants with `could not open /dev/null: Permission denied` (0x80); the NUL device's DACL is Everyone, SYSTEM, Administrators, RESTRICTED, label Low, no ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES, while node's own `fs` opens NUL in r, w and r+ inside the container. (3) `npm ci --offline` fails inside the container with `EPERM ... lstat 'C:\'` raised by node's JavaScript realpath, in the plain and the LPAC container, and passes outside in about 1 s. (4) A grant on the workspace reaches the protected-name folder by inheritance and no junction target (good); the revoke reads back clean. (5) The container start costs about 2.3 s per launcher call. (6) With internetClient and privateNetworkClientServer the container still could not reach the loopback or the outbound listener, with or without the block rule: the rule's effect is unmeasurable.

**What round 3b changed (small and targeted).**
1. *Results survive a hang.* The probe appends one `RESULT` line per step (and one `ATTEMPT` line per attempt of a step that starts programs) to the progress file the moment it has it; the harness rebuilds the report from those lines when the final report is missing or partial and labels the cell `partial: rebuilt from progress`. `diag-spawn-modes` is the very last step; its three modes use an asynchronous `spawn` with a 5 s kill timer, each result written before the next mode; the tools use the same asynchronous call (no `spawnSync` remains in the probe). The four protected-name operations now run before the tools. A worker thread is the watchdog that still works when the main thread is blocked: after the timer's deadline plus 2 s it appends `WATCHDOG`, writes the rebuilt partial report with a direct `writeSync` and kills the whole process (`process.exit` in a worker would end only the worker); the harness's 90 s limit remains the backstop.
2. *npm* (`--mode npm`, `npm.mjs`): the failing call is reproduced alone in the container (`lstat-repro`: every prefix of npm's script path, of the working directory and of node.exe, the JavaScript and the native realpath, the drive root's stat, access and readdir), and 13 variants each change one thing from round 3's call: `--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` by NODE_OPTIONS and by flags, `npm.cmd` through `cmd /c` (with and without the options), npm cache/prefix/logs/user and global configuration and HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA inside the granted home, the project inside the workspace, a `--require` preload that makes `fs.realpathSync` the native one, combinations and the LPAC variants. A variant passes only with exit 0 AND all 40 packages found on disk by the harness.
3. *Git and the NUL device.* New launcher flags `--stdout-nul-rw` and `--stderr-nul-rw` (with the existing `--stdin nul-rw`): variants `all-nul-rw` and `lpac-all-nul-rw`. A new launcher command `open-test` (Rust, no new crate) is run as the child inside the container from a copy in the workspace and opens NUL with `CreateFileW` in twelve combinations (read/write, each access alone, the launcher's own, file-specific rights, with and without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, no sharing, no attributes, `\\.\NUL`), once with an inheritable handle, and with the C runtime's `_wopen` (`O_RDWR`, `O_RDWR|O_BINARY`, read-only, write-only), printing each error. `git.md` then says which combination the container refuses.
4. *Firewall.* The report judges its three assumptions separately (the capabilities open the network; a block rule for the package SID stops it; the rule touches only that container) and states which one fails. One more phase adds `CheckNetIsolation LoopbackExempt -a -n=<profile name>`, reads it back by the package SID and removes it (finally path); the cases mode has the new cell `ac-inet-private-loopback-byname`. A control from a Low-integrity process was not built: it needs a token-based process-creation call, which the launcher's source test forbids by design.
5. *Workflow:* one more hosted step (npm, after the git step, `if: always()`, 15 minutes, 45 s per step); `own_runner` is still off by default.

**Is git inside the container needed? No card needs it (evidence).** A04 (task-plan, "Implement protected filesystem and Git bridge"): the Git bridge gives each checkout *no .git* (its repository lives elsewhere), the controller runs git itself with a fixed environment and command-line overrides, and refuses a checkout holding any Git-named entry; its stated limit is that the dispatcher (H12) must keep the separate git directory outside every sandbox's mounts. H12's acceptance: "a real attempt runs in the selected sandbox with only the checkout mounted and the git directory protected"; `packages/worker/src/sandbox/attempt.ts` refuses a recipe that mounts the git directory or a folder containing it. The containment case `deny-write-protected-name` (`containment.ts`) plants a `.git` folder only to prove it cannot be written. Searching the text of A04, A07, H12 and N06 for git in the sandboxed worker's tools, I found none that lists git among the tools the sandboxed worker itself must run; git is something the controller runs for the worker. So a sandboxed `git.exe` would find no repository anyway (no `.git` in the checkout, none reachable), and git failing to start in the container does not block the design. Git inside the container stays a diagnostic here (it explains why `git.exe` cannot even print its version), not a requirement; if a later card wants `git` for read-only use on a checkout copy, the `open-test` table says which NUL open the container refuses, and the cheapest remedy to try first is whichever launcher flag combination `all-nul-rw` shows to work.

**What the round-3b run should answer.** (a) Do the cases now give verdicts, or at least a rebuilt partial report that names the step that hung (the progress file's `WATCHDOG` line, and whether a worker thread can start and kill the process inside the container)? Do the protected-name verdicts (rename, delete, replace by junction, rename the parent) now appear? (b) Which npm variant, if any, makes `npm ci --offline` pass; which prefix does the `lstat-repro` say is refused; does the native-realpath preload pass (that would show the drive-root `lstat` is the whole cause)? (c) Which NUL open combination does the container refuse, and does `all-nul-rw` make `git --version` pass? (d) Which of the three firewall assumptions fails (round 3 suggests the first: the capabilities alone did not open the network on this runner), and does the loopback exemption by name get applied and read back?

**ASSUMPTION:** `RESULT` lines in the progress file are the single source for a rebuilt report (the same record the final report carries); a step with a start line and no end line is the one that hung, and a step that ended without a `RESULT` line cannot occur and is ignored.
**ASSUMPTION:** the four protected-name operations run before the tools (their verdicts matter most and each undoes itself); the harness's witnesses still report any that failed to undo.
**ASSUMPTION:** the package family name for a container made with `CreateAppContainerProfile` is its profile name, so `-n=<profile name>` is the by-name form; if the tool does not accept it, the report says the add failed and the cell is not run.
**ASSUMPTION:** the launcher copy that runs `open-test` is run from the granted workspace (the container may not reach the checkout it was built in); if that copy does not start, the step is reported, not guessed.
**Not done:** a no-container control from a Low-integrity process (see above); no run on the real service runner; the cause of git's refusal and of npm's `lstat` are shown only by the Windows run; no change to `containment.ts`, the sandbox launcher or any plan status; no push.

### Windows AppContainer experiment, round 4 (2026-11-24, Claude agent; branch `card-win-appcontainer-r4`; experiment only, nothing flipped, not pushed)

**What round 3b showed (hosted run 45517848440).** (A) The cases mode finally gave verdicts in nine configurations. Every containment case passed in all nine (own-folder writes and reads, system folder, host path, symlink read and write, credentials, controller data, hard link read, owner profile, system `Temp`), the loopback and outbound cases were `weak` in the four plain cells without a loopback exemption (nothing got through, but the refusal was not an access-denied code), FAILED (the connection worked) in the three cells WITH an exemption (expected: the exemption is the thing that defeats the case) and passed in both LPAC cells. `deny-write-protected-name` FAILED in all nine cells, including the cells with the deny entry on `.git` (edit, create and delete all allowed), and the contrast cell without the deny entry was identical: the deny entry did nothing. The four `extra-protect-*` operations FAILED too (rename, delete and replace-by-junction of the protected folder allowed; rename of the workspace `weak`, `EBUSY`). (B) Every `tool-*` probe failed with `spawn error EPERM`: node inside the container could not start a child process; `diag-spawn-modes` ended in `EPERM` for "output to files" and HUNG for pipes and "ignore" (the worker-thread watchdog ended the cell at 62 s), although the launcher itself starts node, cmd and hostname in the same container. (C) `npm ci --offline` passes in the container with `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` (variants nodeopts-preserve, flags-preserve, preserve-env-workspace, lpac-preserve-env-workspace) and fails without (EPERM on `lstat 'C:\'` from the JavaScript `realpathSync`). (D) git: every NUL open combination is refused (error 5) in both containers; no card needs git inside the container (see round 3b), so the git question is closed. (E) Launcher overhead is about 2.3 s per start. (F) The worker-thread watchdog fired correctly at about 62 s and the partial reports were rebuilt.

**Diagnosis (A), protected names: what is established and what is not.** Established by the 3b data: the protection did nothing, and the folder itself could be renamed and deleted, so neither the child entries nor the folder's own DELETE right was denied. NOT established: whether the deny entry was never written in a form that counts, or was written and not honoured for this kind of token. The earlier runs only read the DACL back AFTER the revoke, so no run has ever shown the entry. Round 4 therefore (1) records the DACL (SDDL) of the workspace, of `.git` and of `.git\config` after the grants were applied and again after the program ended (`daclsBefore`/`daclsAfter`, the container's SID printed as `<container>`), which shows the entry, its order against the inherited allow and whether anything changed it; and (2) changes the layout so that it does not depend on a deny entry at all. Reasons the old layout could be ineffective, in the order the data can separate them: (a) the deny entry is merged by `SetEntriesInAcl`, whose merge of a deny with an inherited allow for the same trustee is not controlled by the launcher (the new layouts are built entry by entry in a fixed order); (b) an AppContainer's second access check may not treat a deny entry for its own package SID the way a user's does (then every deny layout fails, and only the layout without any allow works, which is why `seal` is the layout of the design rule); (c) the inheritance flags: the entry must be inheritable to files and folders and the folder's DACL must not re-inherit the workspace's modify entry above it (a PROTECTED DACL stops that). The new cells separate (a), (b) and (c): `ac-nocap` (old merge), `ac-nocap-deny-strong` (old merge, every right but read and execute), `ac-nocap-sealed` (hand-built, protected, no write right for the container at all).
The rename and delete of the folder: Windows lets a delete or rename through when the object's own DELETE right OR the parent's delete-child right is held, so both must be absent: the workspace `modify` mask never included delete-child (so the parent is fine), but it includes DELETE and it is inherited onto the protected folder, which is why the folder could be renamed, deleted and replaced. `seal` leaves the container no DELETE on the folder or anything in it. The workspace folder itself (`rename-parent`, `EBUSY` only because the program's working directory was there) needs DELETE on the folder: the new `modify-root` mode grants the folder itself modify without DELETE and everything inside modify with it (one folder-only entry and one inherit-only entry). Junctions: the container cannot create a junction whose target it cannot reach (`EPERM`), but it could create one to a folder inside the workspace (the own-junction probe reached `.git` through it, because `.git` was writable); with `seal` that write is refused because the junction resolves to the sealed folder.

**Diagnosis (B), child programs: what is established and what is not.** The probe's own tool calls used `stdio: ["ignore", file, file]`. libuv opens the NUL device for "ignore" (and for any missing standard handle), and the container cannot open NUL (error 5 for every flag combination, `git.md`): that explains the `EPERM` of the files mode and of every tool, and is the same cause as git's failure. It does NOT yet explain the hangs of the pipes and ignore modes: a start that never returned blocked the thread inside the operating system's process creation (nothing could be learned from the progress file, because the call was synchronous inside the main thread). Suspects, separated by the new ladder: libuv creates named pipes for "pipe" (does the container create one at all: `diag-named-pipe`), libuv assigns every non-detached child to a Job Object of its own that is nested in the launcher's job (job limits all/none/each alone; `detached`), the program's folder (copy in the workspace, install folder, system programs), the container (plain, LPAC), and the system's own CreateProcess (cmd.exe starting node and hostname, no libuv). The progress lines of the step script say whether the call returned; a marker file says whether the grandchild ran.

**What round 4 changed.**
1. *Launcher:* modes `deny-strong`, `seal` and `modify-root` (hand-built DACLs in a fixed order: `InitializeAcl`, `AddAccessDeniedAceEx`, `AddAccessAllowedAceEx`, `AddAce`, `GetLengthSid`); `--dump PATH` and a `dump` command (SDDL through `ConvertSecurityDescriptorToStringSecurityDescriptorW`); the revoke of a seal re-enables inheritance. Still one process-creation call; type-checks with `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline`.
2. *Probe:* tools start from a worker thread (`spawnIsolated`) with standard input from an empty file and output to files; the diagnostic has four modes (files with stdin file, inherit, pipes, ignore), at most 5.5 s each, and runs before the tools; a hung start is a `HUNG` result (counted) and the remaining tools are skipped; when a worker is stuck the probe ends the process by a kill after writing its report. The protected-name case also tries a rename of the config file. The probe's own tools get `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` (the harness's child environment carries it, as the product launcher would).
3. *Harness:* fifteen cells (the nine of 3b plus `ac-nocap-deny-strong`, `ac-nocap-sealed`, `ac-nocap-sealed-root`, `ac-nocap-sealed-root-nolimits`, `ac-inet-private-sealed-root`, `lpac-optout-reg-com-sealed-root`); the table and the per-cell notes name the layout, the workspace entry and the job limits and print the DACLs; `--mode spawn` (`round4.mjs`): 52 steps (a plain or LPAC container, job limits all/none/UI/active/memory alone, node in the workspace or the install folder, cmd.exe, hostname.exe, stdio pipe/inherit/files/ignore, `detached`, `windowsHide`, plus native cmd.exe-starts-a-program steps and a named-pipe step), each a launcher run of 15 s of its own.
4. *Workflow:* the hosted job runs the spawn ladder first, then the cases (fifteen cells, 90 s each), npm, links, timing and the firewall; the smoke ladder and the git ladder are no longer run there (their questions are answered; the code stays); the own-runner job (off by default) runs the cases and the spawn ladder. Hosted limit unchanged (75 minutes); the steps' own limits are 25, 30, 15, 5, 15 and 10 minutes, and the expected total is about 30 minutes.

**Design rule for the product launcher that follows (to be confirmed or corrected by the round-4 run; every line says what it rests on).**
* *Protected names (`.git`, hooks, the like):* give the protected folder a PROTECTED DACL (no inheritance from the workspace) in which the container's only entries are read-and-execute (plus, harmlessly, an explicit deny of write, delete and delete-child, inheritable); never rely on a deny entry on top of the workspace's modify entry. Rests on: Windows' rule that an object's own DACL decides, that a protected DACL stops the workspace entry reaching it, and that the container holds no other allow. Confirmed when `ac-nocap-sealed` passes `deny-write-protected-name`, `extra-protect-rename-dir`, `-delete-dir` and `-replace-junction`; if it does not, the dumped DACLs name the entry that grants the right.
* *The workspace folder itself:* grant modify without DELETE on the folder and modify with DELETE on everything inside (`modify-root`): the agent cannot move, rename or delete the workspace it runs in. Confirmed when `ac-nocap-sealed-root` turns `extra-protect-rename-parent` from `weak` to `pass`.
* *A protected name that does not exist yet* cannot be sealed: create the folder (empty) before the run and seal it, or deny creation in the parent; the product's rule is that the controller creates the protected folders first (A04's checkout has none).
* *Standard handles:* never `stdio: "ignore"` and never a missing standard input (libuv opens the NUL device, refused to the container). Give every child an empty file (or a pipe, if the ladder shows pipes work) for input and files or pipes for output. Rests on the NUL findings (round 3b) and on the files mode's `EPERM`; the ladder shows which of pipe, inherit and files works.
* *Job limits compatible with spawning children:* whichever of `all`/`none`/UI/active/memory-only the ladder shows working with the working stdio mode; the launcher's own job should always keep kill-on-close. If only "none" works, the limits go to a nested job the product creates itself, not to the launcher's.
* *Required environment:* `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` for every node program the agent starts (npm needs it, round 3b), HOME, TEMP and the npm cache inside the granted folders, an explicit PATH of granted folders, no inherited variables.

**What the round-4 run should answer.** (a) In the dumped DACLs, is the old deny entry present and first, and do the sealed folders carry the protected flag (`P` in the SDDL) and no write entry for `<container>`? (b) Does `ac-nocap-sealed` pass the protected-name case and the three folder operations while `ac-nocap` and `ac-nocap-deny-strong` still fail (the layout, not the container, decides), or do all fail (then the dump names the grant that allows)? (c) Does `modify-root` make `rename-parent` pass (`EPERM` instead of `EBUSY`)? (d) In the spawn ladder: which of pipe, inherit, files and ignore work, with which job limits and programs; do the native cmd.exe steps work (then the system's CreateProcess is fine and the problem is libuv's); does `diag-named-pipe` work; where does a hang stop (`hang-in-spawn`: process creation blocked; `hang-child`: the child never ended, with or without its marker)? (e) With the working configuration, do the `tool-*` probes pass in the cases (the cells with `NODE_OPTIONS` set by the harness), and what happens to the cases with the limits off (`ac-nocap-sealed-root-nolimits`)? (f) Is each cell under 90 s now (a hung start costs 5.5 s, not 60 s)?

**ASSUMPTION:** the protected-name layouts are separate cells, each a whole configuration (not a per-case option), so the table reads the same as before and the result of one layout is never mixed with another's.
**ASSUMPTION:** the spawn ladder uses one fixture folder for all steps and a copy of node.exe in its workspace; each step has its own file names, so a hung step cannot disturb the next, and its grants are applied and removed by its own launcher run.
**ASSUMPTION:** a step whose script prints nothing and whose launcher timed out is `hang-in-spawn` only when the progress file shows `before-spawn` without `spawn-returned`; without either it is `no-result`, never a guess.
**ASSUMPTION:** the smoke ladder and the git ladder leave the hosted workflow (their questions are answered; the git ladder's finding is that git need not run in the container); the code, tests and README stay, and either can be run by hand with `--mode ladder` or `--mode git`.
**Not done:** no Windows run was possible here, so the cause of the protected-name failure is not shown, only a layout that avoids relying on it, and the cause of the spawn hang is not shown, only a ladder that separates the suspects; a deny entry's behaviour for an AppContainer's package SID is not documented by Microsoft in the sources read (the DACL dump settles it); no real service-runner run; no change to `containment.ts`, the sandbox launcher or any plan status; no push.

## Windows isolation without Windows Sandbox: plan (2026-11-24, Claude agent; plan only, no code, plan status left alone)

The owner asked for a Windows isolation route that works unattended (a service, nobody signed in, no UAC at run time, at most one admin approval at install) and ideally on Windows Home, because Windows Sandbox needs an interactive session, was refused at `wsb start`, and is absent on Home. [`docs/nimblenewt/windows-isolation-plan.md`](../windows-isolation-plan.md) compares WSL 2 hosting the Linux backend, a native Windows sandbox built like Chromium's and Firefox's (restricted token, low integrity, Job Object, alternate desktop, AppContainer, file permissions), containers (Docker and Podman, whole product or per-task workers), trusted-host mode and their combinations, against the ten containment cases, the cards A03b, G05, G06, Y02, A08c, H12r, H12i, P02, P03, Q01 and Y01, and what can be proven on the owner's PC versus only in CI. Its recommendation is the native sandbox first (WSL 2 later as an optional stronger tier), with an experiment list the Windows-box agent can run without UAC prompts, and a Docker image as a Linux and macOS deployment option only: a container on Windows still needs WSL 2 or Hyper-V underneath. **Not done:** nothing was built or run; every prediction in the document is marked cited, community or unverified. **ASSUMPTION:** lines in the document record the choices made without waiting for the owner.

### macOS shard 1 silent hang (exhaustive run 45513655324 and later): cause and fix

What happened: on macOS shard 1 printed nothing after the root script tests started and was cancelled at the 100-minute limit. The only file added to `scripts/` between de423708 (shard 1 passed in about 50 minutes) and 28cc3207 was `scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs`; its test names never appear in the mac log (a node test file prints only when its process ends), and the log stops at the last file that did end. The stale-dates, windows-host and release-watch changes are not involved: Ubuntu and Windows pass them, and the root checks all finished in 90 seconds.

Cause: the firewall tests listen on a second address, 127.0.0.2. macOS has no 127.0.0.2 on its loopback, so the listen failed (EADDRNOTAVAIL). The harness had already opened its loopback listener and did not close it when the second listen failed, so the test failed AND the open listener kept the test process alive for ever. Reproduced on Linux with an unassignable address: the process never ended (timeout exit 124), and it ends with the fix.

Fix: (1) `ladder.mjs` runFirewall and `run-experiment.mjs` runExperiment close the first listener when the second cannot be made; (2) the firewall tests choose a bindable second address (127.0.0.2, else the machine's own non-loopback IPv4); (3) regression test in the experiment tests (a child process that must end by itself); (4) `scripts/test-shard.mjs` now runs each step through `runStep`: a step that prints nothing for 30 minutes (override: NN_SHARD_QUIET_MS) is reported as STUCK with its step name and the test files still running below it (found with ps, or PowerShell on Windows), ended, and fails with status 124, so a hang names the file instead of a silent cancel. Tests: affected-packages.test.mjs.

Not done: no macOS run was possible here; the Linux reproduction uses an unassignable address. ASSUMPTION: 30 minutes of silence is stuck (the slowest passing shard step prints within a few minutes per file).

## Native Windows plan revision (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-plan-native-windows`; plan text and docs only, no product code, no card flipped, not pushed)

**Why.** The owner decided on 2026-11-24 that Windows Sandbox is not the Windows plan and to focus on the simpler setup. The hosted experiment (`experiments/windows-appcontainer/`, rounds 3b and 4 above) showed on a hosted `windows-latest` runner (a Server edition, build 10.0.26100, interactive session 2, elevated) that the native route is viable there: the sealed protected-name layout passes the protected-name cases, `modify-root` stops the agent renaming its workspace, node and `npm ci --offline` work with `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main`, standard handles must be files (never `ignore` or pipes), git cannot run inside the container (and no card needs it), and the network is none by default. It did NOT show Windows Home or Pro, a non-administrator account, a service in Session 0, or the absence of a UAC prompt for an unelevated install; those are intentions recorded as unproven in A03b.

**What changed (source `scripts/generate_task_plan.py`; `task-plan.json`, `task-plan.md` and the README roadmap are regenerated from it).**
- **A03b** is now "Implement the native Windows launcher (AppContainer, Job Object, ACLs)". Deliverable: the native launcher with the design rules above. Acceptance now names: the ten cases on hosted Windows CI and on the owner's machine with each denial first shown to succeed unconfined; case 9 judged by the refused connection; audit and launch record show the mode and that it is process-level and weaker than Linux's; fail closed, never unconfined; the sealed layout for protected names and `modify-root` for the workspace; files for standard handles (the NUL device is refused to the container); NODE_OPTIONS, HOME, TEMP, npm cache and PATH inside granted folders, with an offline `npm ci` passing; no git in the container; soft grants removed on every exit path with a read-back revoke; Job Object with kill-on-close and the recipe's limits in a form that lets children start; supervisor outside container-writable folders; network none, no loopback exemption, a recipe with a route refused; NTFS only; one documented administrator install step. The Windows Sandbox launcher, its autologon/lock mode, the VM fallback and the session dependence are retired from the card. **Explicitly unproven (an acceptance item that blocks the flip):** launching from the service account in Session 0 with nobody signed in, including after logout and reboot, on the owner's own hardware; the hosted experiment ran in an interactive admin session. Also not claimed: Windows Home (the hosted runner is a Server edition) and Win32k lockdown (Node cannot run with it).
- **G05**: the unattended-identity proof is now about the native launcher from Session 0 on the owner's machine (still unproven until run); adds the protected-name operations on Windows and revoke-after-every-exit checks; case 9 variant; the sign-off records the Windows version and edition and that the Windows boundary is process-level and weaker than Linux's.
- **G06**: names the native launcher as the Windows implementation under test (hosted CI for the automated part, the supplied host for the real part), adds junction-in-workspace and revoke-does-not-follow-junction cases, and records Home or Pro and the service account used.
- **H12r**: title now "Run the worker process under Seatbelt and the native Windows launcher" (the H12b card's cross-reference is updated to match). The Windows half: read-only soft grants for Node and the loaded packages, supervisor outside container-writable folders, the NODE_OPTIONS and file-handle rules, and reaping through the Job Object. The recipe-change-with-restart and refuse-instead-of-unconfined lines are unchanged.
- **H12i**: Windows proof changes from "proxy and grants behave the same on Windows" to "first release gives Windows agents no route; the launcher refuses a recipe with a route with a message that tasks needing the web or a local server wait for a Linux or macOS host". A pipe relay for Windows is a later card, not created here.
- **A08c**: the Windows half is the wider limit set on the Job Object that A03b already creates (kill-on-close, memory, active processes); the card keeps CPU, disk and the macOS mechanism and still records which limits applied. It stays "after the first release".
- **Y02**: Windows runs use the native launcher started from the service account, and the report names the native process-level tier.
- Card IDs, parents and every dependency edge are unchanged. Edges considered: G05 does not gain an edge to A03b (it would delay the Linux and macOS proof; the Windows half of G05 is gated through Y02, which needs A03b); H12i keeps its A03b edge (the Windows refusal is proven on that launcher); A08c keeps A03b (the Job Object is created there); A03b keeps depending only on A03. No card was added: a stronger WSL 2 or container tier exists only as the comparison in `windows-isolation-plan.md` and has no card, so none was kept or invented. Progress records of already-implemented cards (A03's note about the old split) are history and are left as written.
- `docs/nimblenewt/windows-isolation-plan.md`: the seven decisions are marked "decided by delegation, ASSUMPTION 2026-11-25" with a table of the cards each touches, and the owner can overrule any. `docs/nimblenewt/own-hardware-runners.md` has a one-line note that Windows Sandbox is no longer the plan (its job and tests stay only as diagnostics). The Windows Sandbox product code under `packages/worker/src/sandbox/windows*.ts` is untouched; what happens to it (keep as an optional Pro tier or remove) is for A03b's implementer to decide in a reviewed change.

**Round-4 results (hosted run 45525239392 on d5261515, artifact `windows-appcontainer-hosted`; read in the review of this revision).** Cases: `deny-write-protected-name` and `extra-protect-rename-dir`, `-delete-dir`, `-replace-junction` FAIL in all ten cells without the seal (`ac-nocap`, `-noprotect`, `-deny-strong`, the five `ac-inet-private` cells without seal and the two LPAC cells without seal) and pass in all five sealed cells; `extra-protect-rename-parent` is weak in `ac-nocap-sealed` and passes in the four `sealed-root` (modify-root) cells; the container could not create junctions in the sealed cells (EPERM, so `extra-junction-self-made` is inconclusive there; in `ac-nocap` it made one to the writable `.git` and wrote through it); cases 1 to 8 and the hard link, owner profile and system folder probes pass in all fifteen cells; case 9 is weak in plain AppContainer cells (ETIMEDOUT, no connection), FAIL with a loopback exemption, and passes only in the LPAC cells (EACCES); `lpac-optout-reg-com-sealed-root` passes everything but the two git tools (21 pass, 0 weak, 2 FAIL, 1 inconclusive); `tool-node-version`, `tool-npm-version` and `tool-npm-ci-offline` pass in every cell, the git tools fail in every cell. Spawn ladder: files 15/15 and inherit 9/9 work, pipes 0/15 (all `hang-in-spawn`), ignore 0/8 (EPERM), under every job-limit setting (all, none, UI, active-process, memory); the four native steps (the launcher starts cmd.exe, which starts node or hostname) fail with "Access is denied"; the named-pipe diagnostic gave no result. Firewall: inconclusive (internetClient and privateNetworkClientServer did not open the network; the loopback exemption by name did). These numbers are what the card text now cites.

**Review fixes (2026-11-25, clean-context Claude agent).** A03b's deliverable said "a low-privilege AppContainer with no capability"; an LPAC with no capability cannot start node (round 2), so the card now names the measured configuration (LPAC with only registryRead and lpacCom, plain AppContainer as fallback). Case 9 wording "refused connection" became "the host listener sees no connection" (the plain container's attempt times out, it is not refused). New acceptance lines: the case scripts must be shown to run in the container (cmd.exe starting programs was refused in round 4), pipes made inside the container are never used (they hang), a task-folder grant that fails stops the launch (the earlier "grants are soft" contradicted fail-closed), and two more unproven items: a non-administrator account and the controller's channel across the container boundary (H12r says the same). Decision dates in the cards now say 2026-11-25 and "overrulable". This entry's "Why" no longer says Home and Pro were shown. Docs that still described Windows Sandbox or autologon as the plan got a dated note (`g06-evidence.md`, `g01-decision-record.md`, `build-decisions-for-owner.md`, `windows-box-agent-instructions.md`, sections 12 and 13 of `windows-isolation-plan.md`).

**ASSUMPTION:** the seven decisions take the recommended answer, as the owner delegated; each can be overruled by the owner, which changes the cards listed above.
**ASSUMPTION (review):** A03b's container is the LPAC with registryRead and lpacCom, the only configuration that passed case 9 with an access-denied code; a plain AppContainer stays the named fallback. The owner or A03b's implementer can overrule this with a measured reason.
**ASSUMPTION:** native launcher implementation language and layout (the experiment used a small Rust program with one crate, `windows-sys`) is left to A03b's implementer; the card states behaviour, not language.
**Not done / unproven:** Session 0 service launch; Windows Home; real unattended reboot behaviour; a Windows network route; per-agent CPU and disk limits on Windows; the full ten cases on the owner's hardware; no product code, no flips, nothing pushed.

## A03b slice 1: the native Windows launcher, TypeScript side (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b`; offline-testable part only; card NOT flipped; not pushed)

**What was built (all in `packages/worker/src/sandbox/`).**
- `windows-native-plan.ts` (pure, no OS call): turns a launch recipe and command into the launcher command line, using the experiment launcher's measured arguments. The workspace is `modify-root` (modify without DELETE on the folder itself), home and scratch are `modify`, read-only inputs are `rx` (all hard: a task-folder grant that cannot be made stops the launch); each protected name that exists under the workspace is `seal`ed (a PROTECTED DACL with read-and-execute only); the program folders (the Node installation, the packages the worker loads) are `--grant-soft rx`, the only soft grants, and a program folder that is inside a grant already made is skipped, one that contains a task folder, the control folder or the runner's folder is refused. The container is the LPAC (`--aap-policy optout` with only `registryRead` and `lpacCom`); `container: "appcontainer"` is the plain fallback (no policy value, no capability). No network capability or loopback exemption appears anywhere. The Job Object limits are the measured ones (kill-on-close always, 4096 MB, 64 active processes, UI limits). Standard input is a FILE (empty, or the controller's input), standard output and error are FILES: never the NUL device, never a pipe made inside the container. The environment is complete and nothing is inherited: HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA inside the home, TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR in the scratch, `npm_config_cache` in the scratch, PATH of granted folders (program folders, input folders, then System32 which the container reads by the system's rule), `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main` (a recipe's own NODE_OPTIONS follows them), a recipe may not set any variable the launcher sets (any letter case). A recipe with a route is refused (`REFUSED_ROUTE`, typed `invalid_recipe`), and the program path is found only through the recipe's own mounts, `/work`, `/home/agent`, `/scratch` or `/windows`. The launcher's JSON line is parsed, with a typed failure kind for each stage (`container`, `job`, `grant`, `files`, `start`, `launcher`, `revoke`, `filesystem`, `busy`).
- `windows-native-job.ts`: `runNativeJob` (the one routine behind both the runner and the health probe): takes the one run slot (a second run would share the container's SID, so one run's revoke would remove another's grants; a dead holder's lock is taken over), checks every task volume is NTFS before any grant, writes the standard-handle files, runs the launcher, and on EVERY path out (success, failed stage, no answer, launcher that could not be run, timeout) runs an independent read-back (`check`) of every granted path, a second `revoke` and read again if anything is left, and writes a record (`records/<runId>.json`: grants, applied/revoked, soft grants refused, failure, read-back state; no environment values, no file contents; the last 200 are kept). An entry that cannot be removed fails the launch with the typed `revoke` reason and keeps the job folder; `sweepLeftovers` (called by health, and per job folder by `release`) revokes and reads back for every job whose runner is gone and removes the clean folder, reports the rest.
- `windows-native-runner.ts`: the supervisor's runner (placed with the worker's code, outside every container-writable folder): reads the job file, reads the controller's standard input to its end into the input FILE, copies the output FILES back to its own output, exits with the program's exit code; fails closed with a first stderr line `nn-native-failure: <kind>: <words>`.
- `windows-native.ts`: `windowsNativeBackend` (plan, guest view with host paths as on macOS, `health`, `auditDetails`, `descendants`/`startTimes` so the controller's kill finds and ends the launcher and the container's processes, `release` which revokes and reads back after a kill) and `windowsDefaultBackend` (configured from `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_LAUNCHER`, `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_CONTROL_DIR`, `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_CONTAINER`, `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_PROFILE`; never throws; unavailable with a reason when not installed). `health` is a real confined start: it makes the container profile, starts a node program INSIDE the container that must write its own folder and nothing else (outside file, the sealed `.git`, a rename of `.git`) and must not connect to a listener the supervisor opened on the host's loopback (case 9 judged by the host listener seeing no connection), then checks the host's files. A failed probe, a launcher that is not installed, a non-NTFS volume or leftover grants that cannot be removed make the backend unhealthy, and the controller then refuses every launch: nothing runs unconfined.
- The audit and every launch record carry `backendDetails`: `windowsMode: native`, `nativeMode: "native process-level, weaker than Linux"`, the strength, the container and its capabilities, `network: none (no network capability, no loopback exemption)`, the job limits, files for standard handles, soft-grant policy, and the unproven items.
- `SandboxBackend.interactiveInput?: false` (new, optional) and `SandboxLauncher.launch`: a streamed request (a program that talks to its caller over standard input and output, which needs pipes) is refused with a typed `unavailable` reason on the native backend instead of hanging; plain `stdin` text works (it becomes the input file).
- Backend selection: `SandboxLauncher`'s default for `win32` is now `windowsDefaultBackend` (before: no backend); the G05 `windowsEvidenceBackend` is the same native backend. Windows Sandbox is not selected anywhere by default. `windows.ts`, its runner, jobs and the wsb helpers stay (other cards' tests and the owner-hardware diagnostics still use them) and are marked SUPERSEDED in their headers; `windowsSandboxEvidenceBackend` keeps the old G05 variant.

**Tests.** `windows-native.test.ts` (41 tests, 47 after the first review below, 58 after the second; simulated Windows host and a simulated launcher that behaves as the measured one: one JSON line, grants applied and removed, files for handles): the quoting, program mapping, grants and their order, soft only for program folders, environment, reserved names, the whole command line (and that no `nul`, `pipe`, network capability, loopback, Win32k or no-kill switch appears), the launcher's line and typed stage kinds, plan and refusals (route, overlap with the supervisor, links, programs outside the recipe, odd environment names), configuration errors, audit details and the launch record, the pipe refusal, every fail-closed path and the read-back after it, lingering and stubborn entries, NTFS, the run lock, sweep, release after a kill, process-tree lookups, health (healthy; wrote outside; wrote the protected folder; reached the host's listener; launcher missing; not NTFS; container cannot be made; leftovers; busy), the default backend wiring, the runner, stdin reading and the real host's file calls. Neighbours rerun: `launcher.test.ts` (34), `containment.test.ts` (36), `windows.test.ts` (82), `windows-task-launch.test.ts` (34). Mutation checks (each applied, seen failing, restored byte-identical by sha256): route refusal removed; stdin file replaced by NUL; read-back skipped; program folder grant made hard; `interactiveInput` removed; preserve flags dropped; NTFS check removed; a network capability added to the command line.

**The Rust launcher: not productised in this slice.** The TypeScript side is built against the experiment launcher's measured command line (`experiments/windows-appcontainer/launcher`, binary `nn-appc-launcher`, whose `run`, `check`, `revoke` and `info` commands it uses). Productising it is a separate step: a crate under a product folder with its own manifest, the three things CONTRIBUTING.md (D02) requires for a non-TypeScript component, `cargo --locked --offline` in CI, a reproducible Windows build and signing in the install step. ASSUMPTION: the experiment launcher is accepted as the product launcher's contract until then, so its JSON line (`tool: "nn-appc-launcher"`) is what `parseLauncherLine` reads; a renamed or extended product launcher changes only that parser and the argument builder.

**What still blocks the flip (acceptance items not met; the card stays `planned`).**
1. The ten containment cases denied by the real launcher on hosted Windows CI and on the owner's own Windows machine, each first shown to succeed unconfined. The Windows dialect of the case scripts in `containment.ts` still starts programs through cmd.exe, which the container refuses (round 4: cmd.exe started by the launcher was refused when it started node or hostname); they must become node programs run inside the container, and a case whose script cannot run there is inconclusive. Until then the evidence backend reports every case `not_run` or `inconclusive` on Windows. Not done here.
2. Launching from the service account in Session 0 with nobody signed in (after logout and reboot), and from a non-administrator account (no run has ever been made; the hosted runs were elevated). Owner's hardware.
3. The controller's channel to a program in the container (standard input and output, pipes on Linux and macOS): today refused (`interactiveInput: false`), and plain `stdin` text and file output work. Showing a relay across the container boundary can be done on hosted CI. Not done.
4. An offline `npm ci` from a lockfile inside the container through this backend (measured only in the experiment, with the same environment); a hosted-CI step, not done here.
5. The documented administrator install step (not a run-time action of this backend): place the launcher at `%ProgramFiles%\NimbleNewt\nn-launcher.exe` (writable by administrators only), create `%ProgramData%\NimbleNewt\native` for the service account with no entry for the container, create the service account and register the service, grant the account the rights on the task folders' parent. The backend never repeats these; with any of them missing, `health` says which. Documented here and in the code comments only; no installer was written.
6. Windows Home (the hosted runner is a Server edition) and Win32k lockdown are not claimed.
7. The runner and the supervisor placement are checked by path overlap (the task folders may never overlap the control folder, the runner's folder or the launcher's folder); reading the real access list of those folders (that no entry names the container) belongs to the owner-hardware run.
8. Job Object memory and active-process limits are backend settings (defaults 4096 MB and 64 processes, the measured values), not yet a per-launch request field; per-run limits on Windows are card A08c's.

**ASSUMPTION:** one native run at a time (a numbered run lock in the control folder's `locks`, see the second review): concurrent runs would share the container's SID, so one run's program would reach the other's folders and one run's revoke would remove another's grants; per-run profiles can lift this later.
**ASSUMPTION:** the container profile name is one fixed name per machine (`NimbleNewtAgent`), not one profile per run, so profiles do not pile up.
**ASSUMPTION:** a protected name that does not exist in the workspace is not sealed (it is listed in the launch record's `unprotectedSubpaths` as on the other backends); the controller (A04) creates protected folders empty before the run or keeps them out.
**ASSUMPTION:** program arguments are passed as given (the agent sees host paths on Windows, as on macOS; `guestView` says which); only the program itself is mapped from the sandbox's POSIX names.
**ASSUMPTION:** output is relayed when the program ends (files copied back), not streamed live; a program that needs live streaming is the unproven controller-channel item.

**First review of slice 1 (2026-11-25, Claude agent; commit on `card-a03b`, not pushed; card not flipped).** Checked against the card, the round 3b/4 rules and the experiment launcher's source (`win.rs`: its `run`, `check`, `revoke` and `info` commands, `--grant`/`--grant-soft MODE:PATH`, `--stdin file:PATH`, `--env NAME=VALUE`, the JSON fields read here, and that the container's environment is built only from `--env`). Confirmed: every exit path of `runNativeJob` after the first file write runs the independent `check`, a `revoke` and a second `check`; a missing launcher, a non-NTFS or unreadable volume, a failed hard grant, a launcher with no answer, one that cannot be started, and a timeout all end in a typed `nn-native-failure` with no program output; the default `win32` backend is the native one and never Windows Sandbox or an unconfined start; nothing reads the `nn-native-failure` line programmatically, and a failure never returns the program's own output, so a program printing that line cannot turn a failure into a pass (it can only make its own run look failed). Thirteen deliberate breakages of the built files were each caught by a failing test. Fixed, each with a test:
- Read-only inputs and program folders (`checkProgramFolder`) now refuse a trailing dot or space and a short-name (`~1`) part, as task folders already did. Windows reads `C:\dir.` as `C:\dir` and expands `PROGRA~1`, so the plain-text overlap checks against the control and supervisor folders could have been passed by such a spelling (on a real machine the link check's real-path comparison also caught existing ones; now the rule does not depend on it).
- A protected name that is a link or junction is refused at the plan. The launcher sets a seal's protected access list on the path as given and follows a junction, so the seal (and the inheritance given back at the revoke) would land on the folder it points to; the recipe check had refused links at normalisation, and this checks again just before the grants.
- A reused process number no longer keeps a dead run's lock or job folder alive: the lock now records when it was taken, and a live number whose process started after the lock or the status file was written is a later, unrelated process (likely after a restart). Before, such a folder was skipped by every sweep, its entries stayed on the old task's folders, and because every run shares the one container SID, a later run's program would have kept access to those folders. Where start times cannot be read, the number alone decides, as before.
- The job file kept for the sweep is rewritten without the launcher's argument list once the runner has the lock, so the recipe's environment values are not left on disk in the control folder (only the grants remain).
- A launcher answer of `ok` that does not say the program started is now a typed `launcher` failure instead of exit 71 with no reason.
Not changed, recorded: (a) taking over a stale lock is a remove-then-create, so two runners that both find the same stale lock at the same moment could both proceed; one controller starts runners and the busy refusal covers the ordinary case, and per-run profiles (the ASSUMPTION above) would remove the shared-SID reason for the lock. (b) Because the SID is shared, the sweep's revoke of a dead job whose task folders are the same as a live run's removes that live run's entries; the live run then loses access (it fails, it is not widened). (Fixed for the common case: a job folder with no status file, which is what a run refused as busy leaves, never had a grant, so `release` now removes it without a revoke; tested.) (c) Job folders left by a controller that stopped between a clean run and `release` keep only `job.json` (grants, no environment values) and are not removed by the sweep, which cannot tell them from a planned run whose runner has not started yet.

**Second review of slice 1 (2026-11-25, clean-context Claude agent; commit on `card-a03b` after 474f1f84, not pushed; card not flipped).** Read the code and `win.rs` before the first review's notes. Two launcher facts decide most of what follows: the launcher's `revoke` (and its own revoke at the end of `run`) goes through the grant list BACKWARDS, and revoking a `seal` gives the protected folder its inheritance back; and the runner starts the launcher with `execFile`, so a runner that is killed alone leaves the launcher, its Job Object and the program running (kill-on-close fires only when the launcher's own job handle closes; the launcher's limit is `maxRunMs`, 24 hours by default). The controller's kill reaches the launcher only through `descendants`, which returns nothing when the process list cannot be read. The first review's point (b) above ("the live run then loses access, it is not widened") does not hold in that case. Fixed, each with a test:
- **A run whose runner is gone but whose launcher still runs counted as finished.** Lock takeover, the sweep and `release` looked only at the runner's process number.
