After a kill that missed the launcher, `release` revoked under the live program (seal first, so `.git` briefly inherited the workspace's modify entry), and the next run took the lock and started a second program with the same container SID, which could reach the new task's folders (modify on its workspace) and the new one the old. Now `writerAlive` also counts any process the runner started after the lock or status time (bounded by the start of a later process that reuses the runner's number), and a run whose liveness cannot be read (no process list) counts as alive: busy, nothing revoked. `release` reports such a run as a cleanup problem (`releaseProblem`) instead of revoking; the folder stays for a later sweep.
- **The health probe runs in the controller's own process**, and a lock or status file with the host's own process number was always treated as stale. Two backends in one process (two `SandboxLauncher`s) could take over each other's live probe lock and sweep each other's live probe folder. A run in progress in this process is now known by its run id and counts as alive.
- **Stale-lock takeover was a remove-then-create** (recorded but left unchanged by the first review). Two runners that read the same stale lock could both proceed, giving two live programs with one SID, which is wider access, not just a failure. The lock is now the highest-numbered file in `locks`: a run takes the slot by creating the NEXT number exclusively (only one contender can), then backs off if a higher number appeared; release is a separate `<n>.released` file; the real host's `createExclusive` now writes a temporary file and hard-links it into place, so no reader ever sees a half-written lock, and a lock file that cannot be read is never taken over (busy). The cost: a lock file damaged by something else keeps native runs busy until it is removed by hand (it says busy, never runs wider).
- **Entries left by an earlier run reached the next run's program.** Nothing swept before a run (only `health` did), so after a failed `release` the next run's program (same SID) kept the old task's folders. `runNativeJob` now sweeps the other job folders right after taking the lock, and does not start (typed `revoke` failure, no grant made) while any earlier entry is left or another run may still have a program in the container.
- **A seal could be lifted while the workspace entry stayed.** `revokeAndReadBack` sent all grants in one `revoke`, which the launcher processes backwards (seal before workspace); if the workspace revoke then failed, `.git` stayed writable by inheritance. The other grants are now revoked and read back first; the seals are revoked alone, and only once every other grant reads back clean (otherwise they stay, which is narrower).
- **A sweep took a job folder whose runner had started but whose job file was missing as "nothing to revoke"** and removed it. Now that is a problem, never a guess.
- **Windows name quirks.** Device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM0-9, LPT0-9 with the superscript digits, CONIN$, CONOUT$, CLOCK$, with or without an extension) are refused in task folders, read-only inputs, program folders and the program path; Windows opens them as devices, so a grant would land on a device. Case-insensitive comparisons now fold upper case then lower case (`foldWin` in windows-plan.ts), so `C:\Program Fıles` (dotless i) or `C:\Program Fileſ` (long s), which the volume may read as `C:\Program Files`, are refused as overlaps with the supervisor's folders. Whether the NTFS upper-case table maps those letters is not checked here; the fold only refuses more, and on a real machine the link check's real-path comparison catches an existing alias too. Checked and found sound: 8.3 names, trailing dots and spaces, alternate data streams, `\\?\` and UNC, drive-relative paths, forward slashes, and links or junctions in task folders and protected names (round 4 measured that a workspace grant does not reach a junction's target).
Checked and not changed: the program's output handle is opened write-only without DELETE, so it cannot rename or delete the output file in the control folder; a launcher answer can only come from the launcher's own standard output (the program's handles are files, passed by an explicit handle list); records and the kept job file hold no environment values. Recorded, not fixed: (1) the launcher (experiment crate) still revokes a seal before the workspace at the end of `run`; the program has ended by then, but the product launcher should revoke seals last. (2) A controller that stops between `plan` and the runner's start leaves `job.json` WITH the launcher's arguments (environment values) in the supervisor-only control folder until `release`; the same values are on the launcher's command line during a run, visible only to the service account and administrators. (3) The health probe removes its job folder even when its revoke failed; the probe's folders go with it, and the only lasting entry can be the read grant on the Node folder that every run makes anyway. (4) The program can write without limit to its output file on the control folder's volume (disk limits are card A08c's). (5) Per-run container profiles (one SID per run) would remove the one-run-at-a-time rule's reason altogether; the lock and liveness rules above are what make one-at-a-time hold until then. Tests: `windows-native.test.ts` 58 (11 new); neighbours `windows.test.js`, `windows-task-launch`, `windows-real`, `windows-host-real`, `containment-windows-evidence`, `containment`, `launcher`, `windows-redact` 224/224. Mutations on the built files, each seen failing and restored byte-identical by sha256: launcher children not counted; the exclusive create's result ignored; seals revoked with the rest; no sweep before a run; device names allowed; lower case only; the in-process run not counted alive; the release mark ignored; an unreadable lock taken over; and four on safeguards that were already there (a foreign JSON line accepted, an environment name listed twice in another case, a trailing dot allowed in a program folder, a failed run's output returned). No Windows acceptance item is proven by this review; everything above is simulated.

**Third check of slice 1 (2026-11-25, clean-context Claude agent; commit on `card-a03b` after 620d93b7, not pushed; card not flipped).** Re-checked the second review's lock, liveness, revoke-order and sweep changes. Found sound: the numbered lock (only one contender can create a number; the highest number is never removed, so a contender that resumes late on an old listing always finds a higher number and backs off; a crash between the temporary file and the link leaves only an ignored `.tmp`; a damaged holder file keeps runs busy until removed by hand, as recorded); the hard-link create (CreateHardLinkW fails with `EEXIST` when the name exists); the liveness time bounds (CIM start times are local-offset ISO with sub-millisecond digits, which `Date.parse` reads; the launcher starts after the lock and status times); the revoke order at every call site (all go through `revokeAndReadBack`); the sweep and refusal before a run. Fixed, each with a test: (1) **`release` and the health check swept outside the run lock.** A sweep of an earlier, dead run's folder could overlap a new run that applies its grants to the same task folders (one SID): a seal revoke sent late could lift the new run's seal while its workspace entry stayed, leaving the protected folder writable for a live program. Both now take the run slot first (`sweepLeftoversLocked`); while another run holds it nothing is revoked (a started folder is reported, so `release` gives `releaseProblem`, and a later sweep takes it). (2) An exclusive create that throws (not "exists") now counts as busy instead of escaping with the run id still marked as in progress in this process. (3) A test for the late contender's back-off (before it, removing the back-off failed no test). Residual, not changed: a run counts the runner's children only from one second before the lock or status time, so a backwards clock step of more than a second between taking the lock and starting the launcher would make a killed runner's launcher look unrelated. Tests: `windows-native.test.ts` 61 (3 new); neighbours launcher, containment, windows, windows-task-launch, windows-real 186; worker package 754 (752 pass, 2 skipped). Mutations on built files, each restored by sha256: sweep lock ignored, back-off removed, seals revoked though another grant is left, the runner's children ignored, the refusal to start with leftovers removed; each fails at least one test.

## A03b slice 2: the ten containment cases on the native Windows backend (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b2`; offline-testable part only; card NOT flipped; not pushed)

**What was built.** The ten cases of card G05 (`control-write-own-directories`, `control-read-own-decoy`, `deny-write-system`, `deny-write-host-path`, `deny-symlink-read`, `deny-symlink-write`, `deny-credential-read`, `deny-controller-data-read`, `deny-network-loopback`, `deny-write-protected-name`) can now be run on Windows through the native backend. The cmd.exe dialect could not run there (the container refuses `cmd.exe` starting programs, 4 of 4 in the hosted round-4 run), so a third dialect, `windows-node` (now the default on Windows), replaces it for the native backend; the cmd dialect stays for the superseded Windows Sandbox diagnostics.
- `packages/worker/src/sandbox/containment-windows-cases.ts` (new). **The runner** (`WINDOWS_CASE_RUNNER`) is plain JavaScript, node modules only, no child program, no pipe: `node case-runner.mjs case-config.json`, started with the preserve-symlink flags every native run gets, standard handles as files. It makes the attempts of all ten cases in one confined start (the logic is the experiment's `probe.mjs`, cut down to the ten cases), writes one JSON line per case to a file in its own scratch folder as each case ends, and prints `g05-end`. A read counts as `allowed` only when the secret (or the listed name) was really seen. The protected-name case tries edit, create, rename and delete of files in the protected folder, rename of the folder, delete of the folder and replace-with-a-junction (move away, then plant a junction under the name; the second step is marked skippable and is `skipped` when the first was refused). **The host side** (TypeScript, tested on Linux with fakes) decides every verdict: a control passes only if every attempt was allowed and the host sees the files; a denial passes only if no attempt got through, the host's own witness shows nothing changed (outside file, created files, protected folder still a real folder and not renamed/replaced, the listener's connection count), every attempt was refused for an access reason (for the network any failed connect counts, a connection made fails the case) and the same attempts were shown to work without the sandbox (a separate unconfined run on fresh folders, plus the host effect for the write cases and the listener count for the network case). The system folders are not paired (the old rule). Anything that could not run (a link the host could not plant, no unconfined run, a case that did not finish, a launch that failed, a run that timed out, a runner with no result) is inconclusive with the reason, never a pass.
- `containment.ts`: new dialect `windows-node` (default on Windows), `SuiteOptions.nodeExecutable` and `systemPaths` (the latter for tests); the node program is given to the container as a read-only input (`/opt/node`), the runner and its config as another (`/inputs/g05`); the environment passed is empty (the launcher sets its own). ## G05 follow-up: a native Windows report states the weaker boundary (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-g05-weaker`; small fix, card NOT flipped; not pushed)
Finding: the hosted Windows run 45590590268 wrote `containment-win32.json` with backend `windows-native` and `weakerThanLinux: false`, although the plan says the native tier is process-level and weaker than Linux and every record must say so. Cause: `produceReport` set the statement only for macOS, and `assessRelease` refused it for any other platform. Now `statesWeakerBoundary(platform, backend)` (containment.ts) is true for macOS and for every Windows backend except the superseded `windows-sandbox` variant (a virtual machine, which keeps its earlier statement of false), and false for Linux. The validator requires the statement for macOS and native Windows (message: the native Windows boundary is process-level and weaker than Linux's), refuses it for a Windows Sandbox report and for Linux. The schema is unchanged; no committed evidence file exists, and the fixtures of `scripts/y02-checkpoint.test.mjs` and `containment.test.ts` now use the platform rule. ASSUMPTION: a Windows report with no capacity (backend `none`) is treated as native and must state the weaker boundary, since that is what the produced report now says. Needed outside this change: any Windows report already produced by a run before this fix (including run 45590590268's artifact) states false and is refused by the gate; the Windows step must be run again to produce a report. No workflow edit is needed: `exhaustive.yml` and `own-hardware.yml` only produce and read the reports through `containment-evidence.mjs`, which uses the same functions. Cases: macOS, Linux, Windows native and Windows Sandbox each positive and negative in `containment.test.ts`; Windows in the Y02 checkpoint test. Mutation checks: restoring `platform === "darwin"` in the report, dropping the Windows branch of the validator, and inverting the Sandbox branch each failed tests and were restored byte-identical.

### A03b follow-up: two Windows-only test failures (card not flipped)

The exhaustive run on windows-latest failed two worker tests that pass on Linux. Both were test assumptions, not a flaw in the confinement. (1) The launcher test asked a launcher for the "win32" platform and expected the reason to say "native Windows"; on a real Windows host the default backend is the native launcher and the honest reason is that the launcher file was not found (the administrator's one-time install step). The test now builds that backend with a launcher path that cannot exist and accepts either honest reason (off Windows: it exists only on Windows; on Windows: the launcher was not found), so the result is the same on every OS, and a separate case uses an OS with no backend at all. Both still prove that a launch is refused and nothing runs unconfined. (2) The real-host test built its folder from the temporary folder's JavaScript real path; a hosted Windows runner's temp folder is a short name (RUNNER~1), so the host's "is or passes through a link or junction" check, which treats a short name as a link on purpose, correctly said yes. The test now uses the canonical long-name path. In the code, that check became `isLinkOrJunctionWith` (probes injectable): on Windows it normalises both paths and ignores case, and a path that exists but whose real path cannot be read now counts as a link (it previously said "not a link", which failed open; it now matches windows-real.ts). A new test runs the Windows branch on any OS with injected probes (short name, junction higher up, case only, symbolic link, unreadable path, missing path). Four deliberate breakages (case-sensitive compare, fail-open catch, a wrong capacity assertion, no symbolic-link check) each failed a test and were restored byte for byte. ASSUMPTION: the real file calls on Windows/NTFS (hard link, EEXIST, bounded read) behave as Node documents; they were not the cause. NOT verified: the real Windows run itself; the next windows-latest run is the proof.

Review of that follow-up (2026-11-25, Claude agent; card not flipped; not pushed). Found and fixed: the new rule asked an existence check that follows links before the link probe, so a dangling link or junction (its target gone) counted as "not a link"; before the follow-up it counted as a link (lstat said symbolic link). The rule now asks the link probe (lstat, not following) first; only when that probe fails does a missing path count as no link, and a probe failure on a path that is there fails closed. `windows-real.ts` had the same ordering and now uses the same `isLinkOrJunctionWith`. The launcher test expects the reason for its own OS (on Windows: the launcher was not found; elsewhere: native Windows). Checked and not changed: the only production caller of the native host's check is `checkNativeRecipe`, whose paths are already refused as text for "..", a trailing separator, dot or space, a short-name (~1) part, a `\\?\` prefix or a network path, so normalising both sides lets nothing new through; Node's native real path drops the `\\?\` prefix and drive-letter case is ignored. The hosted containment step builds its fixture root with the same `realpathSync.native` (containment.ts), so its folders pass the check as before. The default Windows selection with no backend is still covered by the native-backend wiring test. Tests: injected cases for a dangling link, an unreadable link probe and either separator; a real dangling symbolic link off Windows. Four deliberate breakages of the built file (existence first, lstat failure ignoring existence, real-path failure failing open, case-sensitive compare) each failed a test and were restored byte for byte.

## A03b slice 3: the product launcher crate, the administrator install design, signing and release, contract and CI checks (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b3`; offline-testable part only; card NOT flipped; not pushed)

**What was built.**
- **The product crate, `native/nn-launcher/`** (new top-level folder `native/`, for components that are not TypeScript and not npm packages; `packages/` stays npm-only so the package-boundary check is untouched). The measured launcher source moved with `git mv` from `experiments/windows-appcontainer/launcher/` (history kept): `src/win.rs` (the program), `src/lib.rs` (entry; prints one "Windows only" line elsewhere), `src/main.rs` (the `nn-launcher` binary), `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (the same locked versions and checksums as the experiment's; only the crate's name changed), `rust-toolchain.toml` (exact pin 1.99.1), `.cargo/config.toml` (`/Brepro` for the MSVC target), `cargo-licenses.json`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md`.
- **One source, two builds (ASSUMPTION: the smaller safe path).** Copying 1000 lines would let the experiment and the product drift, and pointing the experiment's many harness paths and tests at a new binary name was the larger change. So the experiment keeps its folder, its crate name and its `nn-appc-launcher.exe`, but `experiments/windows-appcontainer/launcher/` is now a one-file crate depending on `native/nn-launcher` with the cargo feature `experiment`; nothing in the harness changed except that the source-reading tests now read `native/nn-launcher/src/win.rs`. The PRODUCT build (no feature) accepts only the commands `run`, `check`, `revoke`, `info`; grant modes `ro`, `rx`, `modify`, `modify-root`, `seal`; standard input only as `file:PATH`; kill-on-close always. Every experiment option (`deny-write`/`deny-strong` grants, `--win32k-off`, `--no-kill-on-close`, `--keep-profile`, NUL and pipe handles, `--dump`, `grant`, `dump`, `delete-profile`, `open-test`) is refused at the argument check with "not in this build", and the code of `open-test`, the C-runtime declarations and the hang diagnosis (and the ToolHelp import) is compiled out (`#[cfg(feature = "experiment")]`). The code of the other refused options (pipes, NUL, dump) is still compiled in but unreachable: the refusal is at parse time, not by cfg (cutting them out of `run_inner` by cfg would have changed measured code paths for no new safety). The `tool` JSON field keeps the value `nn-appc-launcher` (now one constant `TOOL`) so no recorded run or parser changes meaning; the contract test pins it.
- **Revoke order kept**: `revoke_all` is unchanged (other entries first, newest first; the seals last and only when every other entry is clean); the two-pass source test still passes against the new location.
- **Reproducible build (documented, not yet shown).** Locked dependencies (`--locked`), an exact toolchain pin, `--remap-path-prefix` for the source and cargo folders, `/Brepro` (no timestamp), `codegen-units = 1`, no debug info, no cargo feature in a release. `scripts/native-launcher.mjs record` writes a release record (file name only, size, SHA-256, commit, toolchain, hash of `Cargo.lock`, `features: []`; no time, path or user) and `verify` fails unless a file is exactly the recorded one (and refuses a record that names a feature build). Two builds giving one hash is NOT shown yet: `RELEASE.md` makes it a first-release blocker.
- **Licenses.** `cargo-licenses.json` records the SPDX expression of each of the 10 locked crates (`windows-sys` and its target crates, all `MIT OR Apache-2.0`), read from each crate's own `Cargo.toml` by `npm run licenses:write` when the crates are in the local cargo registry. `npm run licenses:check` now also fails when a crate is missing from the record, a recorded crate is not in `Cargo.lock` (stale), or a license is off the allow list. The experiment crate's own lock file lists the same crates and is not checked separately.
- **Signing and release text** (`native/nn-launcher/RELEASE.md`): Authenticode with a certificate only the owner can supply (the key stays on the owner's token or signing service; nothing secret is stored anywhere), RFC 3161 timestamp, `signtool verify`, hash recorded before and after signing; unsigned builds (hosted CI, own machine) only on the machine that built them and only with the installer's `-AllowUnsigned`.
- **The administrator install** (`native/install/Install-NimbleNewtLauncher.ps1`, README beside it; TEXT, never run). Actions `Verify` (default, read-only), `Install`, `Uninstall`, all with `-WhatIf`. It makes a local standard user `nimblenewt-worker` (member of Users only; right to log on as a batch job; interactive, Remote Desktop and network logon denied; no other right; random 48-byte password made in memory, handed once to `New-LocalUser`, never stored or printed; the worker runs through an S4U task or later a service, so no password is needed), `%ProgramFiles%\NimbleNewt\nn-launcher.exe` (SYSTEM and Administrators full; the account read and execute), `%ProgramData%\NimbleNewt\` (the account read and execute), `%ProgramData%\NimbleNewt\native\` (the account Modify) and `worker.env` with the four `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_*` names. Every access-list line has its reason in the script and in `Verify`; inheritance off; owner Administrators; allow entries only; the entry list is replaced as a whole (idempotent, never additive). The installer demands the file's SHA-256 (and a valid signature unless `-AllowUnsigned`), refuses a pre-made folder under its names that is a link or not owned by an administrator (`%ProgramData%` lets any user create folders), writes a manifest, and `Uninstall` removes only what the manifest names (checked for name and links), refuses a user it did not mark, and stops while the launcher runs.
- **ASSUMPTION (the account form).** A virtual service account (`NT SERVICE\NimbleNewtWorker`, preferred) needs a real Windows service and the product has no service host (the release launcher is a logon-triggered Task Scheduler entry); a group-managed service account needs a domain (not on Home); so a local user with S4U logon is used, with the "log on as a service" right available behind `-ServiceLogon` for a future service host. The service-unit generator (`packages/controller/src/release/service-units.ts`) still makes a logon-triggered, interactive-token task and was NOT changed: running unattended as this account needs an S4U or boot-triggered task, which is a separate change.
- **Contract test** (`packages/worker/src/sandbox/windows-native-contract.test.ts`, 9 tests, every OS): reads the crate's source and the compiled TypeScript and pins the `tool` identifier (one constant in the crate; the parser's literal), every top-level field and every per-grant field `parseLauncherLine` reads against the keys the crate writes, a round trip of a line made of those names, the failure stages the crate reports against the backend's `STAGE_KIND` map, every option and command `launcherArgs`, `grantArgs` and the backend send against what the PRODUCT build accepts (and not an experiment-only option), the grant modes, and that the experiment-only code is behind the feature.

### A03b follow-up: the stand-in container on Node 24 (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-node24`; card not flipped; not pushed)
The exhaustive run on 6ae797af failed six tests in `containment-windows-cases.test.ts` on Node 24 only. Cause: the test's stand-in container (`container-sim.mjs`, which makes file calls fail like the container's) judged the path it was given as plain text. Node 24's module loader reads the runner's own entry file by passing a file: URL object to `fs.readFileSync`, so the stand-in saw `file:///...`, found no allowed folder and refused the loader's read; the runner exited 1 before its first case and every case was inconclusive. Node 22 passes a plain path, which is why it passed here. Fix (test code only; the real runner needed no change): the stand-in now turns a file: URL object, a file: text and a Buffer into the file they name before deciding, so the set of denied paths is unchanged. New test: the same file read as a plain path, a URL object and a Buffer gives the same answer (allowed in the task's folders, refused outside) on every Node version. Checked: with the conversion removed the new test and six old ones fail on both Node 22 and Node 24; two other breakages (protected folder no longer read-only, task folders made read-only) still fail the existing tests. The worker tests pass on Node 22.23.0 and Node 24.21.0 (counts in the commit report). Not covered: the macOS and Windows Node 24 jobs were not available to run here.

### A03b: three Windows-only test failures from the hosted run 45611769590 (card not flipped)

The hosted Windows run (Node 24, shard 1) showed three worker tests failing only there. None hid a product fault; all three were test-side path assumptions. (1) and (2) in `containment-windows-cases.test.ts`: the fake host's table was written with slash paths (`/o/made`), but the host-side witnesses build their paths with the platform's own `join`, which gives `\o\made` on Windows. The fake therefore found nothing, so the confined witness reported that the agent could not write its own directories, and the unconfined proof reported that nothing had changed. In production the config and the witnesses both use the host's join, and the runner reports only attempt names, never paths, so the two sides always agree. The fake now compares paths in one separator form, and a new test runs the same witnesses with `path.win32` paths (a drive letter, backslashes) on any OS. (3) in `launcher.test.ts`: the test put the launcher in `Z:\nonexistent` and the control folder in `Z:\nonexistent\control`, so the derived probe folder (`...\control-probe`) lay inside the launcher's own folder, and the placement check refused it (an honest, fail-closed reason) before the missing-launcher check. The test now puts the launcher in its own `bin` folder, so the missing launcher is what is reported. Because off Windows the default backend answers before reaching either check, `windows-native.test.ts` gains a test with an injected host and win32 paths on every OS: the nested launcher is refused by the placement check, and a launcher in its own folder that is absent is reported as missing. NOT verified: the three tests on a real Windows machine (only the next hosted run shows that); Linux runs on Node 22 and Node 24 only.
