## A03b slice 4: the controller's channel across the container boundary, a file relay (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b4`; offline-testable part only; card NOT flipped; not pushed)

**The question.** A worker that runs inside the native Windows container cannot be given pipes (measured: a pipe made inside the container hangs, 0 of 15; files and inherited handles work, 24 of 24; the NUL device gives EPERM). Until now the backend said `interactiveInput: false` and refused a `stream` request with a typed `unavailable`. The worker's channel to the controller is JSON lines (`@nimblenewt/contracts` `worker-channel.ts`, lines of at most 4 MiB): standard input carries the controller's replies, standard output carries the worker's requests (bridge calls, model calls through the relay, lease renewals, results). The worker's entry reads `process.stdin` through an async iterable and writes through one function (`runWorker({ input, write })`), so the transport can be swapped without touching the worker's logic.

**Design chosen: a file relay held by the supervisor.** The controller side stays on the pipes it already had (to the supervisor, the runner outside the container). The supervisor and the worker talk through two files in a folder inside the task's scratch (`<scratch>\.nn-ch-<run>\to-worker.nnc` and `from-worker.nnc`; the scratch is already container-writable, so no access list changes at all). Why files and not something else: files are the one thing measured to work; polling latency is small against what this channel carries (see "Latency" below); and the worker's code is unchanged apart from its entry.
- **Framing** (`packages/contracts/src/worker-file-channel.ts`). One line per frame: `<seq> <kind> <length>:<payload>\n`. `seq` counts the frames of a file from 1 without gaps (a gap, a repeat or a leading zero is a fault); `length` is the payload's byte length (a half-written frame therefore tells itself apart from a finished one; a reader that gets ahead of a writer simply waits); kinds `m` (one channel message: a JSON object on one line), `a` (acknowledgement, outbox only: the inbox frame number of the last message the worker has taken), `h` (heartbeat, inbox only), `e` (the end; nothing may follow). The decoder fails and stays failed on the first thing that is not a frame: a bad header, a number out of order, a kind this side does not accept, a payload over 4 MiB (failed as soon as its header is read), not valid UTF-8, with a line break, JSON that is not an object, a payload on `h`/`e`, an ack that is not a number, a frame after the end, or more frames than allowed.
- **Ordering and flow control.** Each direction is one ordered file. Controller to worker: the supervisor appends one `m` frame per controller line and counts the bytes the worker has not yet acknowledged; at 8 MiB (twice the longest line, so one maximal line never waits on its own acknowledgement) it pauses the controller's pipe, and resumes on the worker's ack. The pause pushes back onto the controller host's existing pending-write bound (4 MiB, then it stops the worker). An ack must name a message that is still waiting and be newer than the last (otherwise a fault). A lying ack can only let more into the inbox, which the hard cap below bounds. Worker to controller: the supervisor writes each relayed line to the controller's pipe and finishes that write before it takes the next frame (backpressure toward the controller); the worker's file simply grows meanwhile, bounded by the cap, which a timer checks on its own every 100 ms so it holds while a relayed line waits on the controller (a file has no way to push back, which is the one real difference from a pipe). After the program has ended, the rest of the outbox is relayed, but a controller that takes no line for the stall time (60 s) is a fault, so it cannot hold the revoke back.
- **Hard caps** (defaults, set per backend by `channelLimits`): 256 MiB and 2,000,000 frames per file over a whole run, 4 MiB per payload. A file over the cap, a controller that sends more than the inbox may hold, or a line over the bound is a typed fault. These are not A08c's disk limits; they keep this one channel bounded by itself.
- **Polling.** The worker reads the inbox with offsets (first 2 ms, backing off to 25 ms while idle); the supervisor does the same on the outbox. One read takes every complete frame that is there, so a burst costs one poll, and throughput is limited by bandwidth, not by the poll.
- **Close and crash semantics.** Controller closes its input: the supervisor writes `e` to the inbox; the worker's input iterable ends. Worker finishes: it writes `e` and exits; after the program has ended the supervisor reads the outbox to its last frame (nothing the worker managed to write is lost) and only then reports. A frame half written when the program ended is a fault if the program exited by itself with code 0, and only a dropped-frame note after a kill, a time-out or a crash (the exit already says so). No closing frame after an orderly exit is a note. Supervisor crash: its heartbeats (`h`, every 5 s of quiet) stop and the worker ends its input with an error after 60 s without any frame; the Job Object's kill-on-close also ends the program when the launcher goes. Worker crash: the program ends and the controller sees the run end with the supervisor's exit and standard-error tail, as for any worker. Controller crash: its pipes close, the supervisor writes `e`, the worker ends. A write to a closed controller pipe is a fault that ends the program.
- **Trust.** Everything the container writes is untrusted data. The supervisor creates both files itself, with exclusive create, before the program starts, checks each is a plain file with one name, and keeps the handles; it reads the outbox only through its own handle at offsets it chose, and a name that no longer leads to its file (swapped for a link or another file, removed) is a fault, so a link or junction the container plants is never followed and never read or written through. A name that already exists (left by the container) stops the run before the program starts and before any grant is made; the folder is removed and made again, and a folder that is a link is refused. The supervisor forwards only the payload of a well-formed `m` frame, as a line, to the controller's pipe; it never opens, runs, resolves or acts on anything a frame names (a test sends paths, handles and commands in a payload and checks they pass as plain text). A damaged read is dropped whole (nothing of the chunk that held the damage is forwarded) and the run ends as `nn-native-failure: channel: ...` with the program stopped (the launcher process is ended through an abort signal; that its Job Object then ends the program in a real container is unmeasured). The controller's own line stream carries nothing but relayed lines: whatever the program printed on its standard output (still a file) is kept only as a clipped note on standard error. The record (`RunRecord.channel`) holds counts and a note, never content.
- **Wiring.** `SandboxBackend.plan` takes a fourth argument `{ interactive }` (the launcher passes `stream !== undefined`); the native backend then adds a `channel` to the job file and the two file names, last, to the program's environment (`NIMBLENEWT_CHANNEL_INBOX`, `..._OUTBOX`, `..._MAX_BYTES`, `..._MAX_PAYLOAD`, `..._STALL_MS`; a recipe cannot name others). `runNativeJob` makes the files after the lock and the sweep and before the launcher, starts the relay beside the launcher's run, reads the outbox to its end when the program has ended, closes the handles, removes the folder, then does the usual revoke and read-back. The runner (`windows-native-runner.ts`) does not read its input to the end for such a job; it hands the relay the pipes it was given. The worker's entry (`packages/pi-adapter/src/worker/main.ts`) uses the files when the environment names them and standard input and output otherwise. `interactiveInput` is now `true` for the native backend, because the path is wired end to end through `runNativeJob` and tested with the simulated launcher.

**Latency (an estimate, not a measurement on Windows).** The worker's traffic is request and reply (a bridge call, a model call, a lease renewal): the model's own answer takes seconds, a bridge call tens to hundreds of milliseconds. A reply waits for at most one poll on each side (2 to 25 ms, so at most about 50 ms per round trip while idle and about 4 ms when busy). That is small against the calls, so polling is acceptable and nothing here needed lowering the isolation. The idle cost is about 40 polls a second per side, each a size check. If a real container shows worse file latency (caching, sharing) the poll bounds are the knob.

**What a run of it does NOT show (unproven, stays unproven).** Everything above runs on Linux with real files and a simulated launcher; the worker side was also run as a separate real node process over the same files. Not measured: whether the real container can read the inbox and append to the outbox as created by the supervisor (the grant on the scratch folder is meant to give it that, by inheritance; whether files created BEFORE the launcher applies its entry get it is unproven: if not, the files would have to be created after the grant, which the launcher does not allow today), file sharing and caching between the supervisor's handle and the container's, whether a `wx+` handle held by the supervisor and an append handle in the container interoperate on NTFS in practice, that killing the launcher process ends the program through the Job Object when the relay aborts, latency, and everything the earlier slices listed (service account in Session 0, non-administrator, Windows Home, own hardware). The existing hosted run is where the first four can be measured next.
- **ASSUMPTION: the outbox is not append-only for the container.** The ACL modes the launcher has (modify, modify-root, rx, ro, seal) have no append-only entry, and adding one means a Rust change plus a measurement, which is outside this slice. The container can already write everything in its scratch, so the outbox gives it nothing new; the supervisor treats any change other than appending (a shrink, a replaced name) as a fault. A read-only inbox for the container (a `seal` on the inbox folder) was also not used: the supervisor writes the inbox through its own handle, and it is unproven whether a sealed folder would leave the supervisor's account able to write. The container forging its own input harms only itself.
- **Limitation: a long worker run ends at the cap.** A worker that carries more than 256 MiB in either direction over one run ends with a typed fault. Rotating the files would remove that; it is a larger change (new names appear in the container's view) and was left. The cap is configurable by `channelLimits`.
- **Limitation: nothing is forwarded from a damaged read**, even whole frames before the damage in the same read, which is the simpler and safer rule for a run that is ending anyway.

**The service unit (noted, not changed).** `packages/controller/src/release/service-units.ts` still writes a Task Scheduler entry with `<LogonTrigger>` for one user and `<LogonType>InteractiveToken</LogonType>`, which runs only while that user is signed in, with that user's token and profile. Running unattended as the `nimblenewt-worker` account of the installer needs: a principal with `<LogonType>S4U</LogonType>` (no password stored; the account has the "log on as a batch job" right from the installer) and `<UserId>` of that account instead of the signed-in user; a `<BootTrigger>` (and a delay) instead of the logon trigger, so it starts with nobody signed in; `<RunOnlyIfLoggedOn>` off (Task Scheduler: "run whether the user is logged on or not"); no execution time limit (`PT0S`), restart on failure; the working directory, the environment (from the installer's `worker.env`) and the controller's own data folders set explicitly, because an S4U token has no network credentials and no loaded profile unless the folders and variables are given; the task registered by an administrator (the installer step, not the controller). Whether an S4U task can create the AppContainer profile and apply the folder entries in Session 0 is exactly the unproven item from slice 3. A real Windows service host is the alternative (the virtual service account the installer's `-ServiceLogon` allows for) and is a larger change.

**Tests.** New: `packages/contracts/src/worker-file-channel.test.ts` 7 (the framing in any chunking, every kind of damage, the bounds, the worker's end over real files: lines, replies, ack order, the end frame, a damaged inbox, one cut short, a silent supervisor, the size limit, the environment); `windows-native-channel.test.ts` 10 (the relay on every OS with in-memory files: order both ways, a half-written frame waits, a damaged frame, seven kinds of fault, the controller overfilling, backpressure pause and resume with a repeated ack, the heartbeat, the end with orderly and killed exits, a closed controller pipe, a payload that only names things); `windows-native.test.ts` +10 (the plan and its environment, the launcher's `interactive` flag, a conversation through `runNativeJob`, a real worker process over the files, a damaged frame ending the run with the grants still read back, a file filled past the cap and one swapped under its name, names left by the container, the runner for a streamed job, the runner's ports, the real channel files with a hard link, a taken name and a swapped name). One existing test (the launcher's typed refusal of `stream`) now uses a stand-in backend that declares `interactiveInput: false`, since the native backend no longer does. The worker `sandbox` folder: 486 of 486 (0 skipped) on Node 22, and the new and neighbouring files 287 of 287 on Node 24.21.0; contracts 27 of 27; pi-adapter worker folder 60 of 60; `windows*`, `launcher`, `containment-windows*` and `host/process` 336 of 336. `tsc --build --force`, `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` clean; `api:docs:write` changed nothing.

**Deliberate breakages, each seen failing and restored byte-identical (sha256 before and after):** the frame-number check removed (2 tests failed); the outbox name check removed (1); the ack validity check removed (2); the program's standard output forwarded to the controller (1); the relay's fault no longer making the run fail (2); the outbox size cap removed (1); the exclusive create changed to a truncating open (1); the channel environment not set (1); the controller backpressure pause removed (1).

**First review of slice 4 (2026-11-25, Claude agent; card NOT flipped; not pushed).** Problems found and fixed: (1) medium: the outbox's size bound and its name were checked only by the relay's read pass, which waits while a relayed line is written to the controller, so with a controller that had stopped reading, the worker could grow its file (or a sparse jump) without any bound and swap its name unnoticed; a guard timer now checks the size, the name and a shrink through the supervisor's own handle every 100 ms, independent of the reads. (2) medium: `finish` waited on the relay's pending controller write without a bound, so a controller that kept its pipe open but stopped reading held back the revoke and read-back indefinitely; a fault now releases the pending write, and after the program has ended no line taken for `drainMs` (the job's stall time, 60 s) is a typed `channel` fault. (3) low (test gap): the decoder's UTF-8 strictness was untested where it matters (bytes that are not UTF-8 inside a JSON string, an encoded lone surrogate, an overlong form; a lenient decoder still parses them); tests added, also for an escaped lone surrogate and a `__proto__` key passing as plain data. (4) wording: the worker-side comment implied the container's access to the outbox is append-only (it is not: the scratch grant is modify); the Job Object kill on abort is labelled unmeasured. Not a problem: the relay's ack recency check is redundant with removing acknowledged entries (a deliberate removal of it failed no test; kept as defence in depth). Deliberate breakages (built files, one at a time, sha256 identical after restore): the guard timer doing nothing (1 test failed), the pending write not released on a fault (hung test cancelled), the frame-number check (2), the payload bound at the header (2), lenient UTF-8 (0 before the new test), the worker's stall check (cancelled), the worker's cut-short check (cancelled), the hard-link check in `stillNamed` (1), the size cap in both places (2), the exclusive create made truncating (1), the controller line bound (1 + 1 cancelled).

**Second review of slice 4 (2026-11-25, Claude agent, clean context; card NOT flipped; not pushed).** Merged origin/main first (notes conflict only, both sides kept). Problems found and fixed: (1) high: the channel folder is in the task's scratch, where the container has modify rights, and it was removed with the host's recursive `remove` (node `rmSync` recursive) at the end of every run, BEFORE the revoke. A container could put a junction in the folder's place, pointing at a folder only the supervisor may write. Whether node's recursive removal on Windows removes a junction itself or what it leads to was not verified here (node moved `rmSync` to native code in recent versions; no Windows machine to check), so the code no longer depends on it: `ChannelFs.removeFolder` (real: `removeChannelFolderWith` in windows-native-real.ts) looks at the folder without following links; a link or junction in its place is removed itself (unlink, or rmdir when unlink refuses a directory link: neither can remove what a link leads to); a plain folder has only the two channel names removed (a file or a link under those names, never a folder) and is then removed only if empty; nothing is removed recursively; a folder whose real path differs from its name, or that is reached through a link higher up, is left alone. The end-of-run removal now runs AFTER the revoke has been read back, so nothing of the container can change the folder meanwhile; a folder that cannot be removed this way is left in scratch and noted in the run record and on standard error. At the start, a leftover that cannot be removed this way stops the run before the launcher or any grant (it was a recursive remove too). (2) medium: the file-identity check accepted a file number of 0 (a file system that gives none), which would make every such file "the same"; a channel file with number 0 is now refused at creation and never matches. The identity rules are now small exported functions (`channelFileRefusal`, `sameChannelFile`) compared on node's BigInt stats, and tested with numbers that differ only beyond 2^53. (3) low, tests only: the decoder's one-line rule for a payload (`/[\r\n]/`) had no test that reached it (the existing "line break inside a payload" case fails on its length first, and a raw CR between JSON tokens is valid JSON whitespace, so only that rule refuses it); new cases for a raw CR, a raw NUL, and raw U+2028/U+2029 (valid JSON, passed through as ONE line: the controller's `LineDecoder` splits on byte 0x0A only, checked end to end, including a four-byte character split across two writes). (4) low, tests only: no test showed that the relay's timers are gone after `finish` (a leaked guard is inert because it returns early once stopping, and unreferenced timers do not appear among node's active resources); a test now tracks every interval the relay makes, for a clean, a faulted and a stalled end. A test comment that said an open file cannot be replaced under its name on Windows was wrong as a statement (node opens files sharing delete); it now says this is not measured. Checked and found sound: the guard and the read pass can both fault, but the fault is taken once and clears both timers; `Promise.race` against the fault signal lets go of a waiting controller write, and a later rejection of that write is handled by the race (no unhandled rejection); the drain interval is cleared in a `finally`; the frame length is bytes on both sides; an ack must be newer than the last and name a waiting message, so a flood or a forged ack is a fault; the controller sees only the payload of a well-formed `m` frame, after strict UTF-8 decoding and a JSON object check; the worker cannot hang (its stall bound runs on every empty read, and the supervisor's heartbeat keeps a live channel above it). New tests: `windows-native-channel.test.ts` 3, `windows-native.test.ts` 4 (the identity rules; the folder removal with stand-in calls on Windows paths; the same on this machine's real files with a directory link, a junction on Windows; the order of removal against the revoke, a folder left at the end, a leftover at the start), `worker-file-channel.test.ts` cases added to existing tests. **Deliberate breakages (12, each on built files, seen failing, restored byte-identical, sha256 before and after):** the heartbeat not cleared on release (1 test failed); the guard not cleared on release (survived at first: inert; caught after the interval tracking was added); the drain interval not cleared (1); a link in the folder's place treated as a folder (2, including the real-file test, where the files behind the link were removed); the link-higher-up check removed (1); a file number of 0 accepted at creation (1) and matching in `stillNamed` (1); file numbers compared as `Number` (1); the raw CR/LF payload rule removed (1); the frame length counted in characters (1); an ack for a message never sent accepted (2); a relay fault not aborting the program (the affected tests did not finish and were cancelled at the 60-second test timeout). **Still unverified without Windows:** how a real container reads and appends to the files the supervisor created before the grant; node's `nlink`, `ino` (the NTFS file index) and `dev` as seen through `stat` on those files; whether a name node holds open can be renamed or replaced from inside the container; that `rmdir`/`unlink` on a junction there behave as above (the real-file test does create a junction when it runs on Windows); that the Job Object ends every program of the container when the launcher is killed by the abort; and the latency.

### CI typical tier: cancelled at 30 minutes, now five parallel parts (no card; Rob authorized the fix, 2026-11-25, "yes to 2")

**What was wrong.** The `CI` job "typical tier (ubuntu / node 22)" was cancelled at exactly its 30-minute limit on many recent pushes (runs 45613816508, 45596227548, 45590590074, 45577867859, 45543763950, 45525692430 and earlier ones), while other pushes passed in about six minutes. The log of run 45613816508 shows the whole 30 minutes inside one step: the build and the root checks finished at 12:28:08, then the controller package's tests ran from 12:28:09 until the cancel at 12:57:00, still printing passing tests (test number 7465 at 12:56:55). Nothing was stuck: the 30-minute silent-step reporter in `scripts/test-shard.mjs` is not part of this tier (`test-changed.mjs` never used it), so the end was the job's `timeout-minutes: 30`. The controller has 828 test files, about 8,000 tests on the reference store and SQLite; one `node --test` process on a four-core runner needs about 35 minutes for them. Pushes that did not select the controller (here: integration, pi-adapter and worker only: 4.0, 0.4 and 0.7 minutes of tests plus about 1.5 minutes of build and root checks) passed in about six. Whether a push selected the controller depended on the changed paths: any change outside `packages/` that was not documentation selected every package, including scripts' own test files, the experiment folder, `native/`, CONTRIBUTING.md and the other workflows, so a one-line fix to `scripts/*.test.mjs` ran the 35-minute controller suite. The suite grew past the limit around 2026-11-23 (earlier all-package runs fit).

**What changed.** (1) `scripts/test-changed.mjs --shard=i/n` runs one part of the same tier (`tierSteps`, exported and tested): the controller's test files are split into n-1 slices by recorded run time (the same `scripts/shard.mjs` and `scripts/test-weights.json` the exhaustive tier uses), the last part runs every other selected package, and part 1 also runs the root checks and `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs`. A part with nothing to run does nothing and builds nothing. Without `--shard` the behaviour is as before; `--dry-run` prints a part's steps. (2) `ci.yml` has a job `parts` (five matrix cells, `fail-fast: false`, 30-minute limit each, same steps, same network-less run, same action pins and read-only permissions) and a job `test` that keeps the old name "typical tier (ubuntu / node 22)", needs `parts`, runs even when a part failed or was cancelled, fails unless every part succeeded, and runs the generated-plan-files check. (3) `scripts/affected-packages.mjs`: files that no package's sources or tests run, read or import now select no package (the scripts' own tests and the tier's helper scripts, the evidence workflows, CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md; the root checks and `scripts/*.test.mjs` still run on every push and cover them), `experiments/windows-appcontainer/` and `native/` select the worker (and so integration), because the worker's contract test reads them; everything else outside the packages, including `ci.yml` and the scripts that packages run or import, still selects every package. The new test in `affected-packages.test.mjs` fails if a package source or another script names a file on the root-only list, so the list cannot drift into skipping something a package reads. `scripts/ci-workflow.test.mjs` pins the workflow's shape (pins, read-only token, matrix equals the part count given to the script, every part has work, the gate's name and rules).

**Expected effect (estimates from the logs, not measured).** All-package push: four controller slices of about 8.75 minutes plus about 1.5 minutes of build each (about 10 to 12 minutes with the unrecorded weights below), the other packages and part 5 about 6 minutes. A push with no controller change: about 6 minutes, as the passing runs show. A push that touches only root-only files: root checks only (about 3 minutes). `scripts/test-weights.json` lists only 140 of the controller's 828 files (the rest count as the median), so the slices are balanced by count more than by time; refreshing it (`node scripts/test-weights.mjs`, one file at a time, long) would balance them better. NOT done: that refresh, a per-test-file selection inside the controller, caching of `node_modules` or of the build, and any change to the exhaustive tier. ASSUMPTION: five parts (four controller slices) because three would still run about 13 minutes of tests per part plus build on the same runners; the limit stays 30 minutes per part. ASSUMPTION: the gate job is kept under the old name so that any status check that names it keeps working.

**What to look for in the next CI run.** The run on the commit that carries this change selects every package (it changes `ci.yml`), so it is the full test: expect six jobs (five "typical tier part i of 5" and the gate); parts 1 to 4 should each end in about 10 to 14 minutes (their "Typical tier" step prints `TYPICAL TIER (part i of 5)` and `SHARD i/4: about 207 of 828 test files`), part 5 in about 6 to 8; the gate passes only when all five do. A part over 20 minutes means the weights need refreshing. A later push that changes only documentation or `scripts/*.test.mjs` should print `no package is affected` in part 1 and have parts 2 to 5 print `Nothing to run in this part.`

**Independent review (2026-11-25).** Four problems were found and fixed. (1) Medium: the root-only list's honesty test only searched `packages/<fixed list>/src` for the literal file names, so a package test that listed `scripts/` (`readdirSync`), used a template path or a `new URL("../scripts/", import.meta.url)`, or a package.json script naming a root-only file passed it (all four tried, all passed). It now reads every package folder whatever packages exist (sources, tests, package.json, fixtures), and also fails on any directory listing, glob or computed path into `scripts/` or the workflows unless that reader is checked by hand and named in its `CHECKED` list (one today: integration's `fixed-part-budget.test.ts`, which reads `local-host.mjs` and `remote-host.mjs`). (2) Medium: `test-changed.mjs` and `affected-packages.mjs` were root-only, so a change to the tier's own driver (what each part builds and runs, how a package's tests are started) ran no package test on its own push; like `ci.yml` they now select every package. (3) Low: with `--shard`, `run-package-tests.mjs` exited 0 when the package had no compiled tests at all, so four controller slices could pass with nothing run; it now fails as the unsharded run does (an empty slice of a non-empty package still passes). (4) Low: `ci-workflow.test.mjs` now also fails on `continue-on-error` (it would make a failing part count as success for the gate), a matrix `include`/`exclude`, a second plan-files check, a job-level `if:` on the parts, `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` or a secret, takes the package list from the repository, and pins the parts' Node 22.19.0. New tests: the controller slices partition a 840-file list in any listing order, and run-package-tests' empty-package and empty-slice cases. Checked offline: with `--all`, parts 1 to 4 each run 206 of the controller's 824 non-slow test files (513 to 531 recorded seconds each), every file exactly once, none in part 5; npm passes `--shard` through to the runner. NOT verified offline: the hosted run itself (matrix expansion, `needs.parts.result` for the matrix, the gate's name as the required check, run times); the next CI run is the proof, as described above.

### A03b: the own-runner Windows job runs launchers built by CI (no card; Rob authorized the own-hardware run, 2026-11-25; card not flipped)

**What was wrong.** The first own-hardware run (45627037396, input `own_runner`) failed only because its job built the experiment launcher with cargo and the owner's PC has no Rust; Git Bash and node steps passed. We will not ask for a Rust toolchain on that machine. **What changed (workflow `windows-appcontainer-experiment.yml` only).** The hosted job now has a staging step after the product build: both launcher programs (`nn-appc-launcher.exe`, `nn-launcher.exe`) and the product release record go into one artifact `windows-appcontainer-launchers` (7 days), and the job reports their SHA-256 values as job outputs (`experiment_sha256`, `product_sha256`) plus `launchers=ok`, set only when both files exist and the product file matches its release record. The own-runner job now has `needs: hosted` and no cargo or rustup step; it downloads the artifact with `actions/download-artifact` pinned to the full commit of v8.0.2 (the release that pairs with upload-artifact v7), compares each file with the hosted job's output (a value that did not travel inside the artifact), runs `native-launcher.mjs verify` on the product file, and only then places the experiment launcher at the harness's default path and the product launcher in a `verified-launchers` folder, hashing the placed copies again. Nothing starts a launcher before that. Its `if:` is `!cancelled() && needs.hosted.outputs.launchers == 'ok' && inputs.own_runner == true && repository == rkcth/NimbleNewt && ref == main`. Reason: the default needs rule would skip the run whenever an unrelated hosted experiment step fails (a failing case is a finding, not a reason to skip), while `always()` would also run on a cancelled workflow; the `launchers` output makes the own run depend on exactly what it needs (a built, record-checked pair of programs). Unticked, it is still skipped. Permissions stay `contents: read`; the redaction on logs and every other pin are unchanged. **Added to the own-runner job:** the product launcher's `info` and the ten G05 containment cases through the native backend (same commands as the hosted job), run as the runner service, with a redacted `product-info.redacted.txt` and `g05-native/` in the uploaded results. No installer step (that creates an account and changes ACLs and needs its own go-ahead). **Honest limits.** The programs on the owner's machine are the unsigned ones CI built from this commit, not a local build and not a signed release. The pin was resolved with the GitHub API (tag `v8.0.2` is a lightweight tag whose object is the commit `9000827c...`; the same method returns the known upload-artifact v7.0.2 commit `cf430e03...`). Offline verification: the YAML parses and tests pin the shape (no cargo in the own-runner job, pinned download, hash check before the first copy and before any step that starts a launcher, 7-day retention, the `if:`); mutations seen failing and restored byte-identical: a cargo step added, the product hash check deleted, the placed-copy check deleted, `always()` in the `if:`, an unpinned download, 90-day retention. NOT proven offline: the artifact handoff, `sha256sum` and the outputs on the real runners, and what the launcher does as a service. The next own-runner run proves whether the downloaded programs verify and start there, whether the container profile and `info` work with no one signed in (the Session 0 question for the product path), and what the ten cases do as the service account. ASSUMPTION: Git Bash's `sha256sum` is present on the runner (it ships with Git for Windows, which the runner already needs for Git Bash).

**Independent review (2026-11-25).** Five problems were found and fixed. (1) High (the run could never pass, failing safe): `sha256sum "$file"` from GNU coreutils puts a backslash before the hash when the file name contains one, and every `$RUNNER_TEMP` path on Windows does (`D:\a\_temp`); the hosted job would have reported `\<hash>`, which the own-runner job's hex check refuses. Shown with GNU coreutils 9.7 running the workflow's own step scripts with a backslash `RUNNER_TEMP`. Every hash in the workflow is now read from standard input (`sha256sum -b < file`). (2) Medium: the own-runner steps after the check (child-program ladder, product `info`, G05 cases) ran under `if: always()`, so they started even when the check had failed; the verify step now has `id: verify` and those steps run only on `!cancelled() && steps.verify.outcome == 'success'`. (3) Medium (a fail-open in a verification command): `scripts/native-launcher.mjs` compared `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` with `process.argv[1]` as strings, so started through a link or junction it did nothing and ended 0, and `verify` passed without reading the record; it now compares real paths (case-blind on Windows), and a new test runs `verify` through a link (mismatched record: exit 1; missing record: exit 2; matching record: exit 0). (4) Low (a persistent change on the owner's PC): `info --name NimbleNewtProductCheck` and the G05 backend (default profile `NimbleNewtAgent`) each create an AppContainer profile in the runner service's account, and the product launcher never deletes one. The G05 step now uses the CI-only name `NimbleNewtOwnRunnerG05`, and a final step (`always()` once the verify step passed) re-hashes the verified experiment launcher and runs its `delete-profile` for both names (a failure is a warning). (5) Low (defence in depth): the hosted job hashed the launchers only at staging, after the experiment steps had run; each build step now reports its file's hash as a step output right after building, and staging requires the staged copies to match them before it sets `launchers=ok`. Confirmed with no change needed: nothing runs or places a downloaded file before both hashes match (the experiment launcher is copied to the default path only after); the expected values are refused when empty, not lower-case hex or not 64 digits, and compared as whole strings; job outputs are separate from the artifact; extra files in the artifact are ignored (only named files are copied); download-artifact v8 fails on a digest mismatch by default and validates extracted paths; the job `if:` cannot start on push, pull request, schedule, a fork, another branch or unticked; no secrets, `contents: read`; uploaded results are the redacted files. The pin, checked with the GitHub API: `actions/download-artifact` (the `actions` organization's own repository, not a fork), lightweight tag `v8.0.2` = commit `9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333` (a verified merge of PR #493, 2026-10-07, identical to that repository's main today); v8's notes cover v7's direct uploads, and upload-artifact `v7.0.2` = `cf430e03...` as pinned. Mutations, one at a time, each restored byte-identical (sha256 checked): hash check after the first copy, empty-hash tolerance, length check dropped, job `if:` with `always()` (two forms), cargo step, installer step, unpinned download, hash read from the file name, substring comparison, `info` back to `always()`, stage without the build-time comparison, G05 back to the product's profile name, a download with `run-id`: all 14 fail the tests. Only the real run can show that `sha256sum -b` on standard input gives the same value in both jobs' Git Bash, that the artifact hand-off and job outputs work, that `delete-profile` removes both profiles under the service account, and what `info` and the ten cases do with no one signed in.

## A03b session 0 slice: the service-context measurement and Windows AppContainer experiment, round 5 (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-s0`; measurement tooling only; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no product change)

**What happened.** Own-hardware run 45634597880 (the owner's Windows PC, build 26200, node v22.20.0, runner installed as a SERVICE: session id 0, elevated) was the first service-context run. The CI-built launchers matched their hashes. The product launcher's `info` created its container profile, so profile creation works in session 0. But every program started inside the container ended in about 30 ms with exit -1073741502 (0xC0000142, STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED): all fifteen cases inconclusive, node as the first child and node run by cmd.exe failed, hostname.exe run by cmd.exe gave exit 1 with "Access is denied.", and the ten G05 cases on the native backend were 0/10 `not_run` ("the confinement probe failed: exit -1073741502"). cmd.exe itself started. The same launchers pass ten cases on the hosted runner (interactive session 2, build 26100). So either the service context (session 0, a non-interactive window station and desktop) or the OS build (26200) or something on that PC explains it. Plain words: process creation and the container token work from the service; a program that needs the desktop does not get as far as running.

**Research (sources and what each states; details and the ranking are in `docs/nimblenewt/windows-isolation-plan.md` section 12.1).** The closest match is a Microsoft Q&A thread by one asker (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/556403/starting-a-process-in-an-appcontainer-from-a-servi): AppContainer children of a session 0 service ended with 0xC0000142 (cmd.exe worked, powershell.exe and java.exe did not), user32.dll failed to initialise (Process Monitor), a larger non-interactive desktop heap did not help, and granting the AppContainer read access to the session 0 desktop and window station fixed it; a token from a logged-in user also worked. Community, one report, cause presumed. Microsoft's archived SDK blog on 0xC0000142 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/winsdk/what-is-up-with-the-application-failed-to-initialize-properly-0xc0000142-error) names window station and desktop security and desktop heap as the causes and discourages editing system window objects directly; KB 184802 says the same (summary only). STARTUPINFO documents lpDesktop as desktop or station\desktop; NULL or an empty string means "inherit the parent's" (older pages). A service without the interactive flag has a non-interactive station `Service-0x0-<logon id>$`. The window station rights page lists the WINSTA_* rights and the generic mappings. Chromium's design page says its sandbox makes a third, hidden desktop for all targets; nothing was found on how it treats an AppContainer SID. Nothing was found tying builds 26100/26200 to AppContainer children, conhost or CREATE_NO_WINDOW; unrelated 0xC0000142 reports (a missing conhost.exe, SetConsoleActiveScreenBuffer, an OpenAI Codex setup helper) are not evidence here. The claim "a NULL lpDesktop gives the child the service's non-interactive station, whose ACL does not name the container" is an inference from those pages, not a quote.

**Hypotheses, ranked (all unproven).** H1 (most likely) the container's SID has no access to the service's window station and desktop, so user32 cannot initialise; H2 which desktop the child is attached to matters beyond the access; H5 security software or code integrity on that PC; H4 the access control of the program's own folder (hostname.exe's "Access is denied." keeps it alive); H3 the console flag; H6 build 26200 itself. What each outcome of round 5 would mean, and the next slice for each, is the table in the plan (12.1); it is also printed in every round 5 report.

**What was built.**
* Launcher (`native/nn-launcher`, experiment feature ONLY; the product build contains none of it, `cargo check` for the product has no new warnings, the product's dependency list and defaults are unchanged and a test pins that): new options `--desktop MODE` (inherit = lpDesktop NULL as today, empty, winsta0, grant-read, grant-full, grant-station, grant-desktop, new-desktop, new-station) and `--creation FLAG` (no-window = today, detached, none, new-console); new commands `context` (read-only: the launcher's own window station and desktop names, whether the station is the visible interactive one, both DACLs as SDDL, session, integrity RID, elevation, OS version from RtlGetVersion) and `desktop-revoke`. New file `src/desk.rs`. A `grant-*` run adds one explicit allow entry for the container's SID to the DACL of the launcher's current window station and/or desktop (opened by name with READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC) and removes it on every path out (Drop), reading the DACL back (`desktop.objects[].entriesLeft` in the JSON line); `new-*` make objects for the run and close them at the end. Each set-up step prints a before and an after line on standard error; a failed set-up stops the run before anything starts (stage `desktop`). Nothing touches the registry, a service or any persistent setting.
* Harness (`experiments/windows-appcontainer/round5.mjs`, `--mode session0 [--steps ids]`): 78 steps, each one launcher run with a 15 s limit: A the program (cmd, hostname, whoami, a GUI-subsystem wscript.exe, powershell, node installed, a copy of node and of cmd in a granted folder, cmd running node and hostname); B the nine desktop modes with six programs; C the creation flags with three programs and two desktops; D node with no grant on its folder. Every step has an `ATTEMPT` line before and a `RESULT` line after it (console and `session0.progress`) and `session0.partial.json` is rewritten after each step, so a hang loses at most the step it happened in. The report has the context (launcher-side, PE import tables of the programs to see which load user32, security products and Smart App Control state, code-integrity and AppLocker events since the start; all read-only), the steps, the summary, an automatic "what the outcomes point to" list, the printed table of what each outcome means, and the clean-up read-back (the count of entries left on the launcher's window objects before and after).
* Workflow: a session 0 step is second in the hosted job (`if: always()`, 25 minute limit) and second in the own-runner job (gated on the verify step's outcome like every launcher step). The hosted job builds the experiment launcher first, so the new code reaches the owner's PC only through the staged artifact whose hashes are checked; the own runner still builds nothing.
* Docs: README "Round 5" (every new Win32 call is documented, a test pins it), the plan section 12.1, this section.

**What was checked here (Linux, no Windows).** `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` for both crates (the product with the stable toolchain because the pinned one lacks the target; no new warning), `cargo test` for the product and with `--features experiment` (argument tests: the product refuses `--desktop`, `--creation` and the two new commands with any value; the defaults are the product's; the experiment build takes exactly the named values). Harness tests in `scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs`: the steps (unique, each group varies only what it says), argument building, judging (works, no marker, 0xC0000142, hex exit codes, hang, set-up failure), interpretation for each hypothesis pattern, a PE import reader with synthetic images, the context with a fake launcher, the read-only scripts, a full flow with a fake launcher (ATTEMPT before and RESULT after each step, partial files, revoke at the start and the end, everything removed, a launcher that cannot make the container, a dry run, a step that throws), the command line, the progress sink, source guards (desk.rs only in the experiment build, one lpDesktop assignment, one process-creation call, entries removed by Drop and read back, no registry or service calls) and workflow shape guards. A real defect was found by the flow test while writing it: the launcher's `desktop` object overwrote the step's `desktop` field in the record (the summary lost the mode); fixed (`desktopObjects`).

**Not done and not verifiable here (stated plainly).** (1) The launcher changes were type-checked, never linked or run: whether `OpenWindowStationW`/`OpenDesktopW` with WRITE_DAC succeeds on a service's window objects, whether the masks chosen (the documented GENERIC_READ mapping and the full rights) are enough, and what `CreateWindowStationW` does in session 0 are exactly what the run measures. (2) The cause of the 0xC0000142: not decided; H1 is the best fit, not a finding. (3) Build 26200 versus session 0: round 5 on the owner's PC cannot split them alone; the hosted run (build 26100, interactive) already shows the baseline works there. (4) Security-software and event queries need the PowerShell cmdlets and rights of that machine; a failure is recorded as a note, not fatal. (5) A fix for the product launcher is a SEPARATE slice after the measurement (the likely shape, if H1 holds: the launcher makes a window station and desktop per run with an entry only for the container's SID and passes them in lpDesktop). (6) A launcher killed in the middle of a `grant-*` step leaves one entry for a container SID on the runner session's window objects until that session ends or `desktop-revoke` runs (it names no real account); the harness runs `desktop-revoke` at the start and the end.

ASSUMPTION: the round measures the entry levels with the documented GENERIC_READ mappings ("read") and the full rights ("full") rather than guessing the exact minimum; the next round narrows it if "read" fails and "full" works.
ASSUMPTION: `grant-*` touching the runner service's own window objects is acceptable for an experiment because it is one container-SID entry, removed and read back in the same run (and again by `desktop-revoke`); the product fix would use objects made per run instead.
ASSUMPTION: the product launcher is not changed in this slice even though the same defect blocks the product on the owner's PC; no measured fix is proven yet.

**Review (2026-11-25, independent Claude reviewer; branch `card-a03b-s0`, not pushed, no workflow dispatched, card not flipped).** Priority: what the experiment build can do to the owner's PC when it runs inside the runner service's session. Found and fixed (with tests):
1. (High, owner's PC) Nothing stopped the `grant-*` and `new-desktop` modes from adding an entry to `WinSta0` and its desktop when the launcher runs in an interactive session (the runner started with `run.cmd`, or a manual run). Now `deskrules::may_change_launcher_objects` refuses an interactive station (name `WinSta0`, `WSF_VISIBLE` set, or flags unreadable) and nothing is written; those steps report `desktop-setup-failed`. On the hosted runner (interactive) they now report that too; its baseline works there, so the interpretation is unchanged.
2. (Medium, owner's PC, unlikely) `add_entry` merged into a NULL DACL with `SetEntriesInAclW`, which would have replaced "everyone may use this window station" with a DACL holding only the container's entry (other services of the same logon session shut out), and the revoke would then have left an EMPTY DACL. A NULL DACL is now refused (`ERR_NULL_DACL`).
3. (Medium) The revoke removed the container's entries but did not compare the result with the DACL before the grant (`SetEntriesInAclW` writes the canonical order, so a non-canonical DACL could come back reordered). The DACL is now copied before the grant and compared entry by entry after the revoke (`deskrules::compare_acls`, ignoring the unused slack): the same entries in another order are written back from the copy; any other difference (someone else changed it meanwhile) is reported (`matchesOriginal: false`) and never written. `allReverted` now needs that match.
4. (Medium) A step whose launcher was killed (the harness's own limit) left its entry in place for all later steps (measurement contamination and a longer-lived entry); the only revoke was at the end. The harness now runs `desktop-revoke` right after any step of a writing mode that did not report everything reverted.
5. (Medium) A workflow step limit (25 min) killing the harness would have skipped its clean-up. The harness now starts no step that could end after 19 minutes (steps reported `not-started`, a note), and the own-runner job's clean-up step (`always() && verify succeeded`, launcher re-hashed) runs `desktop-revoke --name NimbleNewtExperiment` before removing profiles.
6. (Low) `desktop-revoke` called `CreateAppContainerProfile`, so on a machine without the profile it LEFT one behind; it now derives the SID (`DeriveAppContainerSidFromAppContainerName`, no profile made) and accepts only the SID of one profile (`S-1-15-2-` plus seven sub-authorities; never `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES`, a capability, an account). The same SID check guards `prepare`.
7. (Low, privacy) Code-integrity event messages name files under ANY user profile (the signed-in owner's too, which the harness's own redaction names do not cover) and were stored whole; event texts, security product names and the edition are now bounded and `\Users\<name>` / `/home/<name>` become `<account>` (more is removed for a name with spaces, never less).
8. (Low) `context` and `desktop-revoke` read `GetLastError` after a second call (wrong error code shown); fixed.
9. (Gate) The product contract test's loosened pin (`windows-sys/...` entries of any number) would have accepted any further windows-sys module in the experiment feature; it now pins the exact four, checks that `[dependencies]` is only windows-sys with no optional dependency, and that `deskrules.rs` and `desk.rs` are compiled only with the feature (deskrules also in unit tests).
10. Wording: plan 12.1's table said "H1 confirmed"; now "H1 supported (by this one machine and build)". README notes that a `Service-0x0-...` station is shared by every non-interactive service process of the same logon session.
Checked and left as is: masks match the documented rights (WINSTA_ALL_ACCESS 0x37F, DESKTOP rights 0x1FF, GENERIC_READ mappings as named), entries have no inheritance flags, lpDesktop text `station\desktop`, the wide strings live across `CreateProcessW`, `SetProcessWindowStation` is switched back, every opened or made handle is closed in `finish` (also on panic: `panic = "unwind"` and `Drop`), the PowerShell scripts are fixed and read-only, all SIDs except capability SIDs are redacted in the artifacts, both round-5 workflow steps keep `permissions: contents: read`, pins and the verify gate. Not fixable here: `STATION_FULL` includes WINSTA_EXITWINDOWS for the container on the service station during a `grant-full` step (the children are the harness's own probe programs); a launcher killed by something other than the harness (a runner crash) can still leave one entry until `desktop-revoke` or the end of the logon session. Nothing was run on Windows. 22 deliberate breakages (rules, product refusal, NULL DACL, write-back condition, interactive guard, profile-free revoke, per-step revoke, budget, redaction, interpretation, workflow gate and clean-up, feature pin, module gating) were each caught by a test and restored byte-identical (sha256 before and after). Tests: 442/442 on Node 22 and Node 24 (experiment, native-launcher, affected-packages, ci-workflow, worker windows* and launcher); `cargo test` (product 8, experiment 9); `cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` clean for the product, the experiment feature and the experiment crate; Cargo.lock unchanged.

**Second review (2026-11-25, clean-context Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-s0` after d1186943, not pushed, no workflow dispatched, card not flipped; origin/main fd4babe7 was already the merge base, so no merge).** Checked against Microsoft Learn: GetSecurityInfo (the DACL pointer points into the returned descriptor, freed once with LocalFree; a NULL DACL comes back as a NULL pointer), SetEntriesInAclW ("places any new access-allowed ACEs just before any existing access-allowed ACEs"; it builds a NEW list from the old one), SetSecurityInfo (does not reorder; a NULL pDacl means full access for everyone), SECURITY_INFORMATION (the protected/unprotected flags concern inheritance from a parent, which a window object does not have; DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION alone is used), GetUserObjectInformationW (UOI_FLAGS fills the 12-byte USEROBJECTFLAGS; UOI_NAME is a terminated string; a too-small buffer fails and copies nothing). Found and fixed (with tests):
1. (Medium, owner's PC) The entry was merged with `SetEntriesInAclW`, which rebuilds the whole list (it may merge or re-sort entries), and the order was then repaired by writing the copy taken before the grant back. Two consequences: the write-back could put back a stale copy if something else changed the DACL between the compare and the write (a short window, but on objects shared with other services), and a launcher killed between grant and revoke left a list that `desktop-revoke` could clean of the entry but not put back in its order. Now the launcher inserts ONE allow entry by hand (`deskrules::with_allow_entry`: where SetEntriesInAclW documents it puts one, before the first existing allow entry; every other entry kept byte for byte and in order; refused when an explicit entry for the SID is already there, the ACL or SID is malformed, or the result would not fit), checks it with `IsValidAcl` and writes it in one place (`write_dacl`). The removal (`deskrules::without_explicit_entries`) takes out only explicit allow/deny entries for exactly that SID and writes nothing when there is none. So whoever removes the entry (the launcher at its end or `desktop-revoke` after a kill) gets back the same list. The copy taken before the grant is now only compared and reported (`matchesOriginal`, `orderDiffers`), never written. Both rules are pure and have Rust unit tests that run on Linux.
2. (Low, owner's PC) `desktop-revoke` had no station rule: run in an interactive session (the hosted runner's harness calls it at the start and the end; a runner started with `run.cmd`), it would write WinSta0's DACL whenever it found an entry for the SID. It now applies `may_change_launcher_objects` like the grant: on an interactive or unreadable station it only counts the entries (READ_CONTROL) and writes nothing; `ok` only with none left. No code path now writes a DACL of an interactive window station.
3. (Low) The switch back to the launcher's window station after making a desktop in a new one was not checked; a failure now stops the run (`window objects:` message, `desktop-setup-failed`) instead of starting the child and closing objects from the wrong station.
4. (Low, clean-up) The budget test claimed "19 minutes plus the clean-up fits in 25", counting 6 minutes; by the harness's own limits the clean-up after the last step is 10 minutes (desktop-revoke 60 s, folder read-back 3 x 120 s, events 120 s, profile 60 s), and the step-start check ignored the 60 s desktop-revoke after a writing step. The budget is now derived: 25 min minus that 10-minute clean-up = 15 min, and a writing step reserves its revoke. In the usual run (programs failing within a second) every step still runs; only an all-hanging run loses its last steps.
Checked and left as is: UOI_FLAGS buffer of three u32 and length 12, error mapped to -1 and refused; `WinSta0` compared without case and an unnamed station refused; the changed objects are the process's window station (GetProcessWindowStation) and the thread's desktop (GetThreadDesktop) re-opened by name in the same session, handles closed in `finish` (also on unwind; `panic = "unwind"`); `SetProcessWindowStation` is only around one `CreateDesktopW` call that cannot unwind; objects are made with a NULL SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES (the token's default DACL; a NULL DACL there is refused by `add_entry`); closing the made desktop while the child might still hold it is allowed (CloseDesktop fails only for a desktop assigned to a thread of the calling process; the child holds its own handle); DeriveAppContainerSidFromAppContainerName with FreeSid (via `Sid`), the `S-1-15-2-` plus exactly seven sub-authorities rule; the harness runs one step at a time (spawnSync), revokes after a killed or not-reverted writing step and at the start and the end; the own-runner clean-up (`always() && verify == success`, launcher re-hashed) runs desktop-revoke then the profile deletion; `permissions: contents: read`, action pins and the absence of an installer step unchanged; Cargo.lock files unchanged; the product build refuses every round-5 option and command. Residual: the own-runner job's 45-minute limit is shorter than the sum of its step limits (an all-hanging run could be cancelled by the job limit; the clean-up step is `always()`, and GitHub runs `always()` steps after a cancellation, but this was not measured here); `grant-full` gives the container full desktop rights on a desktop shared with the same logon session's services for the length of one step (UI privilege isolation still separates a low-integrity container from higher-integrity windows); nothing here was run on Windows. 13 deliberate breakages of my own (insert position, the already-present refusal, inherited entries kept, the ACL size bound, the SID revision check, deny entries removed, a write-back added again, desktop-revoke's station rule, a removal that writes with nothing removed, IsValidAcl, the unchecked switch back, the post-step revoke reserve, the clean-up worst case): each caught (6 by Rust unit tests, 7 by the scripts suite) and restored byte-identical by sha256. Tests: 442/442 on Node 22 and Node 24 (experiment, native-launcher, affected-packages, ci-workflow, worker windows* and launcher); `cargo test` product 11, experiment 12; `cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` clean for the product and the product with `experiment`, `cargo check` of the experiment crate clean; `tsc --build --force`, `api:docs:write` (no change), `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` clean.

## A03b session 0 fix: a private window station and desktop for every run (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-ps`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched)

**Why.** Own-hardware run 45650543163 (Rob's PC, runner service, Session 0, build 26200, elevated) showed that AppContainer children from a service fail 0xC0000142 with the service's default window station and desktop, and work when the container has access to a window station AND a desktop. The cleanest working mode was objects made for the run (`new-station`: about 50 ms for node, cmd, powershell, hostname; no change to the service's own objects; clean-up complete). The measurement and the decision are in the plan, section 12.2.

**What the product launcher now does.** Every `run` first makes a private window station (`nn-ws-<random>`) and a desktop (`nn-d`) with the launcher token's default access list plus one explicit allow entry for the container's SID (masks 131967 and 131583, exactly those the experiment applied), reads each access list back and refuses it unless it passes `winobj::private_acl_ok`, passes `station\desktop` as `lpDesktop`, and closes the desktop, then the station, after the child and the grants are done. If anything fails the run stops before any grant, job or child with stage `grant` and a message starting `window objects:` (existing stage, so the backend's typed `grant` failure and the contract tests stay consistent). The process window station is switched only for the CreateDesktopW call and restored at once, checked, with a guard (also on panic). `info` and `check` report `windowStation` (`private`) and `windowStationOk` (made and closed one); `info` fails (stage `grant`) when it cannot, and the backend's health check turns that into "could not make a private window station and desktop for the container (...)" plus a note when it works. The TypeScript parser reads the new fields tolerantly (older lines and wrong types are accepted). The experiment build keeps its own modes; `--desktop private` runs the product path there. The product has no grant mode: it never opens, names or writes the service's own window objects and never touches WinSta0.

**Code layout.** `winobj.rs` (both builds, platform-neutral, Rust unit tests): masks, names, `lpDesktop` text, SID text, the byte-exact entry builder moved out of `deskrules.rs`, and the access-list check. `privdesk.rs` (both builds, Windows): the Win32 calls and the helpers moved out of `desk.rs`. `desk.rs` and `deskrules.rs` stay experiment-only and use them. Cargo features: the product list gained `Win32_System_StationsAndDesktops` and `Win32_Graphics_Gdi` (CreateDesktopW takes a DEVMODEW); the experiment feature lost them. No new crate: `Cargo.lock` is unchanged and valid with `--locked --offline`. CONTRIBUTING.md, the launcher README (section "Window station"), the plan (12.2) and the hosted workflow (`info` must report the private station, in the hosted and the own-runner step) are updated.

**ASSUMPTION: the new objects keep the token's default access list.** The brief allowed "the container only plus the launcher's own user and SYSTEM as needed". The measured configuration used `CreateWindowStationW` with no security attributes (the token's default access list: the launcher's account and SYSTEM, and administrators for an elevated account) and then added the container's entry. An explicit list of only the container and the creator was not measured, so it was not used; instead the list read back is checked for broad groups (Everyone, Anonymous, Network, Interactive, Authenticated Users, Guests, Users, both package groups, any other container or capability) and the run does not start when one is there. If a host's default token list ever holds one of those, `info` says so.
**ASSUMPTION: masks unchanged.** 131967 and 131583 are the measured ones; no smaller mask was guessed.
**ASSUMPTION: an existing name is never adopted.** A name collision (ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) fails closed; names carry 64 random bits.
**ASSUMPTION: `check` does not fail on the station.** It reports `windowStationOk` only, because the read-back after a run must not depend on it; `info` is where it gates.

**Tests.** Rust (both feature sets): `winobj` (measured masks, names, SID text, the access-list check for every broad group, other containers, capabilities, unknown entry kinds, malformed lists; the entry the launcher adds passes the check) plus the existing `deskrules` and `args` tests. TypeScript: the contract test pins the product's windows-sys feature list, that `privdesk.rs` and `winobj.rs` are in both builds, that the product always wants the private station, that it is made before any grant and failure is stage `grant` with `window objects:`, that the code never uses WinSta0, an open by name or a rebuilding entry builder, that every write goes through `give`, the masks, the read-back check, the restore guard, the close order, and the `info`/`check` fields; the backend tests cover the health reason and note; `scripts/native-launcher.test.mjs` pins the two workflow checks.

**Not verified (no Windows here).** The Win32 calls were only type-checked (`cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline`, both feature sets) and never run: that CreateWindowStationW and CreateDesktopW succeed in the product with these exact arguments, that the default token list passes the check on a real service account, that the restore of the process station works, and that node, npm and git run in the container on that PC. The first proof is the own-runner G05 step after this change (a later dispatch, not done here). Not done: desktop-heap behaviour with many parallel runs; a smaller mask; an explicit creator-only list.

### A03b session 0 fix, first review (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-ps`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched)

Reviewed from Microsoft Learn (CreateWindowStationW, CreateDesktopW, SetProcessWindowStation, CloseWindowStation, CloseDesktop, Window Station Security and Access Rights) and the Rust code; no Windows run.

Fixed:
1. (Medium, security check) The read-back check was a deny list of nine groups. It let through other principals a default token access list could hold, such as LOCAL (S-1-2-0, every local logon), CONSOLE LOGON, SERVICE, BATCH, Domain Users (…-513), ALL SERVICES (S-1-5-80-0), the NTLM authentication group or any other account. It also accepted a second allow entry for the container. It is now an ALLOW LIST. The container must hold exactly one explicit entry with the measured mask. Every other allow entry must be SYSTEM, Administrators, OWNER RIGHTS, a logon-session SID (S-1-5-5-X-Y), or the launcher's own token user or owner (read with GetTokenInformation before anything is made). The broad groups and S-1-15-* stay refused even when they are the launcher's own. Anything else stops the run and the message names it.
2. (Medium, correctness) The station was created with dwFlags 0. Microsoft documents that an existing station of that name is then opened ("returns a new handle to the existing window station"), and it does not document ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS for that case. So the "never adopted" claim rested on undocumented behaviour. It is now created with CWF_CREATE_ONLY (1, winuser.h; not in windows-sys 0.59). An existing name makes the call fail. The ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS check stays as a second line.
3. (Low, honesty) `close()` ignored the results of CloseDesktop and CloseWindowStation and reported `closed: true`. A failed close is now kept: `windowObjects.closed` is false and `closeError` is set. `info` reports `windowStationOk: true` only when the objects were also closed. The handle is not retried: the launcher exits right after and the system closes it.
4. (Low, test) The contract test's "own principals before CreateWindowStationW" order check matched the function definition, not the call. It now looks inside `create`.

Checked and left as is:
- **Threads:** no other thread of the launcher exists while the process station is switched. The drain threads start later in run_inner, and `info` and `check` have none.
- **Station close:** CloseWindowStation runs only after the switch back (it fails for the process's own station). If the switch back fails, the run stops and the leftover handle goes with the process.
- **Desktop close:** CloseDesktop runs after the job ended the child. CloseDesktop only fails for a desktop that a thread of the calling process uses, and the child holds its own handles.
- **CreateDesktopW arguments:** pDevmode and lpszDevice are NULL ("Reserved; must be NULL"). The access includes DESKTOP_CREATEWINDOW as the docs require. windows-sys gates CreateDesktopW on the Gdi feature only for the DEVMODEW pointer type. Gdi adds declarations and no code, so keeping the feature is preferable to declaring the function by hand.
- **Entry bytes:** AceSize is 8 + SID length, flags 0, AclSize is recomputed and the revision is kept. The copies are usize-aligned and checked with IsValidAcl.
- **Name randomness:** the 64 bits come from std's RandomState. Its keys come from the OS random source once per thread, and it is a SipHash over the process id and the clock. That is not a documented CSPRNG API, but it is unpredictable without the keys. With CWF_CREATE_ONLY and the read-back, guessing a name gives at most a refused run, never access.
- **Concurrency:** the backend's run lock (windows-native-job.ts takeLock, "one at a time") keeps two runs, which share the NimbleNewtAgent SID, from overlapping.
- **Product refusals and gating:** the product still refuses every experiment option, and `--desktop` is experiment-only. The own-runner steps stay gated by the verify step.
- **Builds:** Cargo.lock is unchanged. `cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` is clean for the product, product+experiment and the experiment crate.

**ASSUMPTION: keep the default token access list and bound it by the allow list, instead of an explicit list at creation.** The default list is the measured configuration. An explicit SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES list (container + own account + SYSTEM) would not depend on the token, but it was never run. The allow list gives the same bound and fails closed. The risk is that a host's default list holds a principal the allow list does not expect. That run stops with the SID named, and info/health report it. If it happens, the fix is an explicit list, not a wider allow list.
**ASSUMPTION: CWF_CREATE_ONLY is safe to add unmeasured.** It is documented since Vista and changes only the case of an existing name.

Open, for the hardware run and the second review:
- CreateWindowStation's page says "Only members of the Administrators group are allowed to specify a name". A non-administrator service account may fail at this step (closed).
- The same page says both that a NULL lpsa gives "GENERIC_ALL access to all users" and that the ACLs "come from the primary or impersonation token of the creator". The read-back is what settles this on real hardware.
- WINSTA_ALL_ACCESS includes WINSTA_EXITWINDOWS and WINSTA_READSCREEN. They only reach the run's own station, but they were not reduced because nothing smaller was measured.
- That a window object is destroyed when its last handle closes is general object-manager behaviour; the API pages do not state it.

Deliberate breakages (16, each caught; files restored with identical sha256):
- **Rust tests:** the SID authority read little-endian; the new allow entry put first; an entry past AclSize accepted; the name without zero padding; LOCAL trusted; a logon SID of any shape accepted; a six-part profile SID accepted; a duplicate container entry accepted.
- **Contract test:** no CWF_CREATE_ONLY; `info` ok without checking the close; the read-back without own principals; the own principals read after the station is made (caught only after fix 4); lpDesktop not from the private desktop.
- **Worker tests:** windowStationError not parsed; the health reason inverted.
- **Workflow test:** the own-runner windowStationOk grep removed.

### A03b session 0 fix, second review (2026-11-25, Claude agent, clean context; branch `card-a03b-ps`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched)

Reviewed from Microsoft Learn (CreateWindowStationW, CreateDesktopW, SetProcessWindowStation, Window Station Security and Access Rights), the measurement file of run 45650543163 and the Rust code; no Windows run.

Fixed:
1. (Medium, security and correctness) **The objects are now created with their final access list; no DACL is written afterwards.** Before, the station and desktop were made with a NULL descriptor and the container's entry was added with SetSecurityInfo. Microsoft documents that NULL default two different ways. The CreateWindowStation page says it "grants GENERIC_ALL access to all users". The window-station security page says the ACLs come "from the primary or impersonation token of the creator". Under the first reading, every run would fail closed at the read-back (Everyone, or a NULL list). Under either reading, between CreateWindowStationW and SetSecurityInfo the object existed with a list the launcher had not chosen, and a handle another account opened then would keep its access after the write. The measurement file does not settle it: the experiment's `new-station` steps record `applied: true` for the write, but they never read the new station's list back. Now `winobj::private_dacl` builds the list: the launcher's token user and SYSTEM with every specific right of the type plus STANDARD_RIGHTS_REQUIRED (0xF037F and 0xF01FF, no generic bits), and the container with the measured masks. It is passed in the SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES of both creating calls, protected (SE_DACL_PROTECTED), with non-inheritable handles. The handles no longer ask for WRITE_DAC. `add_entry`, `write_dacl` and `WRITE_DAC_BIT` (privdesk.rs) and `with_allow_entry`, `names_sid_explicitly` and `ACE_INHERITED` (winobj.rs) are compiled into the experiment build and tests only, so the product binary has no DACL writer. The read-back check stays. The account's entry covers the container's mask. An AppContainer gets only what both its user and groups AND its package SID are granted, so the account's entry has to cover the container's mask, as the token default's GENERIC_ALL did.
2. (Low, defence in depth) **No logon-session wildcard.** The allow list accepted any S-1-5-5-X-Y SID, which includes another user's logon session. The creation list holds none, so a logon SID is now refused and named.
3. (Low) **The container's entry must carry no flags.** Before, only INHERITED was refused. INHERIT_ONLY would make the entry not apply to the object, and OBJECT_INHERIT or CONTAINER_INHERIT would spread it to desktops made later.
4. (Low, diagnosis) **SetLastError(0) right before CreateDesktopW**, so a stale code from the station switch is not read as ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. **An access-denied CreateWindowStationW** now says that Microsoft documents only Administrators may name a window station.

Checked and left as is:
- **Mask mapping:** both masks are specific rights only (0x2037F, 0x201FF; WINSTA_ALL_ACCESS 0x37F and the nine DESKTOP_* rights 0x1FF, both from Microsoft's tables) plus READ_CONTROL. Generic mapping applies only to GENERIC_* bits, so nothing is expected to change between write and read-back. The exact-mask compare is first proven on hardware.
- **Other entry types:** deny entries are passed over (they can only remove access). Object, callback, audit, alarm and label entries in the DACL are refused as not understood. That fails closed, and the launcher's own list has none.
- **own_principals:** the process token (the launcher never impersonates; the objects take the process token's owner). Two-call GetTokenInformation into a usize-aligned buffer. The PSID points into that buffer and is copied (`sid_bytes`) before the buffer is dropped. The handle closes through `Handle`. Any failure stops creation. TokenUser comes first, so own[0] is the account the list is made for. For LocalSystem the user is SYSTEM and the list holds one SYSTEM entry, not two.
- **CWF_CREATE_ONLY = 1:** documented for dwFlags ("the call fails" when the station exists); its winuser.h value is not printed on the page.
- **Station switch:** nothing changed. One thread at that point, Drop guard on unwind (`panic = "unwind"` in the manifest), switch back checked, and the station closed only after the switch back. On a kill, the system closes the handles, and an object with no handle left is destroyed (general object-manager behaviour, not stated on these API pages). Nothing writes to WinSta0 or to the service's objects: the product has no DACL writer at all now.
- **Random names:** RandomState is acceptable. The name is not a secret. Access comes from the creation list. Microsoft documents that only Administrators may NAME a station, so pre-creating a guessed name needs an administrator, and the outcome is a refused run (CWF_CREATE_ONLY), never access.

OPEN, design level (recorded in plan 12.2, residual risk 6): **a non-administrator worker may be unable to make the named station at all.** The design runs the worker as `nimblenewt-worker`, a non-administrator. CreateWindowStation says "Only members of the Administrators group are allowed to specify a name". A NULL or empty name does not help: the system names the station after the caller's logon session, which for a service is its existing station, so CWF_CREATE_ONLY refuses it (without the flag the service's own station would be OPENED). The product code never passes NULL. If the statement holds, every confined run under that account fails closed at stage `grant` with an access-denied message, and `info` and health name it. Unmeasured: the own-hardware non-administrator proof decides it. A failure there is a design decision (for example, an administrator-held component that makes the station for the worker), not a launcher tweak.

**ASSUMPTION: an explicit creation list replaces the measured "NULL descriptor, then add" sequence.** It overrides the first review's ASSUMPTION to keep the default list. That review said the fix, if the default ever surprised, would be an explicit list. The documented default is contradictory, and the window between creation and the write is avoidable. The container's entry and masks are the measured ones, and the account and SYSTEM keep full access as the token default gave them. What changes from the measurement is that no other principal from the default list (for example, Administrators or the logon SID) is on the objects. Nothing measured needed those principals. If the hardware run shows otherwise, the read-back or the child's exit code says so, closed.

Deliberate breakages (14, each caught; every file restored with identical sha256): Rust: SYSTEM added twice for LocalSystem; the container given the full mask; a container mask wider than the account's accepted; only INHERITED refused (inherit-only and inheritable entries pass); the own principals trusted before the broad-group refusal; deny entries counted as the container's entry; the product accepting `--desktop`; the logon-session wildcard back. Contract test: the station made with NULL security attributes; the desktop made with the station's descriptor; the DACL not protected; `add_entry` compiled into the product; inheritable creation handles; the product's create asking for WRITE_DAC.

## A03b worker service unit: the worker as the non-administrator account, S4U and a boot trigger (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-su`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing registered or installed anywhere)

**What was missing.** The only Windows unit the release could print was the controller's: a logon-triggered task of the signed-in user with an interactive token. The worker has to run with nobody signed in, as `nimblenewt-worker` (the standard account the installer makes, whose random password is never stored). Slice 4's notes listed this as "noted, not changed".
