It returns the Task Scheduler XML, the steps for an ADMINISTRATOR, the removal steps and notes. The unit: principal = the account, logon type S4U, run level LeastPrivilege, no password element; one boot trigger with a 1 minute delay and no logon trigger; `ExecutionTimeLimit` PT0S; `MultipleInstancesPolicy` IgnoreNew; `StartWhenAvailable` true; not stopped or blocked on battery; restart on failure 3 times, 1 minute apart (the controller's bound, from `SERVICE_RESTART`); explicit working directory; `node --env-file=<DataDir>\worker.env <remote-worker.mjs> --config <worker.json>`, each argument quoted the way the Windows command line is read. Task version 1.3 (the schema page's version). The environment is only `worker.env`; the host credential is the token file the worker's configuration names, never in the XML. The generator takes paths and names only, so no secret can enter; extra fields are ignored.

So: no network credentials of the account, no EFS files, a non-interactive session. Whether the profile is loaded is not stated there. Every unit's notes say this.

The tests carry the declared element orders and check the unit against them, with a small XML reader of their own (well-formedness, entity escaping, a closing tag for each opening one). They do not validate with a real XSD processor.

Windows paths are written with explicit backslashes (no dependence on the test machine). Mutations (each made a test fail; files restored byte-identical, sha256 checked): S4U to InteractiveToken (2 failures), boot trigger to logon trigger (4), PT0S to PT72H (2), quoting removed (3), 260 limit removed (1), XML escaping of the command removed (1), `$ ; ! #` refusal weakened (1), restart count changed (2), Verify's S4U check changed (2).

- Whether an S4U task of a non-administrator can create the AppContainer profile and the named private window station is OPEN (plan 12.2 risk 6). Plan 12.3 holds the exact own-hardware proof procedure (a probe task with the same principal, then a reboot test, then clean-up), what each outcome means and five fallback designs (an elevated component makes the stations; an elevated one-step launcher; grants on the account's own objects; a real service or a stored-password task; no unattended non-administrator worker). No workflow was added: the installer run needs Rob's explicit go-ahead.
- Restart on failure is Task Scheduler's: it cannot tell exit codes apart and stops after 3 tries. No log file (the worker's own records are the log).

ASSUMPTION: task name `NimbleNewtWorker` (the installer's Verify looks for it). ASSUMPTION: a 1 minute boot delay. ### A03b worker service unit, first review (2026-11-25, Claude agent; same branch; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing registered)

**Found and fixed.**
- (Medium) The account check accepted SID strings (`S-1-5-18` is SYSTEM, and Task Scheduler's UserId accepts SIDs), `LocalService`, `NetworkService`, `DefaultAccount`, `WDAGUtilityAccount` and similar, and a name part looser than the installer's own `-AccountName` pattern (dots, spaces, 63 characters). The name part is now exactly the installer's ValidatePattern (a test reads the .ps1 and pins it), the computer part is NetBIOS-shaped (15 characters, no dots), and SID strings and a list of built-in and well-known names are refused in any case. A renamed built-in Administrator cannot be recognised by name; that is stated.
- (Medium, documentation) Microsoft's "Security Contexts for Tasks" page lists registering an S4U task for a different user's account among the cases where an administrator must supply a password; nothing said so. It is now an OPEN item in the unit's notes (pinned by a test), the README and plan 12.3 (item (c), and an outcome row for the probe registration being refused).
- (Low) Installer Verify: `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName` returns same-named tasks of every folder (an array would have made each check unreliable): now `-TaskPath '\'` and the first result. LogonType and RunLevel are compared as text against the name or the number (`S4U`/`2`, `Limited`/`0`), so an enum or a raw value reads the same. Triggers and actions are filtered for `$null` before a property is read (StrictMode 3). The account must be the bare name or `$env:COMPUTERNAME\<name>` (the earlier `-like "*\name"` accepted any domain's account of that name). Exactly one action, and the worker.env match is case-insensitive.
- (Low, tests) The installer pin now also refuses the CIM and COM registration routes (`Invoke-CimMethod`, `PS_ScheduledTask`, `RegisterByXml`, `RegisterTask`) and any `*-ScheduledTask*` cmdlet other than the read.

**Checked and correct.** Every element, order and value against the XSD on Microsoft Learn (task, registration info, settings, principal and exec are `xs:all`; trigger base is a sequence with BootTrigger's Delay after it; `version` is fixed at 1.3; RestartOnFailure Interval PT1M..P31D and Count an unsignedByte of at least 1, so 1-255; MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew is a schema value and the default; ExecutionTimeLimit is an xs:duration, PT0S is the documented "no limit" setting; Command and WorkingDirectory pathType at most 260, Arguments an unbounded string). `windowsArg` follows the CommandLineToArgvW backslash rules (2n backslashes before a quote become n, 2n+1 escape it; a trailing run is doubled before the closing quote); the reader in the test implements the same rules and now runs a 2000-case generated round trip plus the trailing-backslash case (`--config C:\`). `%` (expanded by Task Scheduler), `"`, control and non-ASCII characters are refused in every path. print-worker refuses root and writes nothing. The controller's unit and golden files are untouched.

**Deliberate breakages (16, each restored byte-identical, sha256 compared):** trailing backslash not doubled; backslash run before a quote not doubled; SID accepted; LocalService accepted; a dot in the name part; Arguments not XML-escaped; logon trigger instead of boot; ExecutionTimeLimit PT72H; LogonType Password; a Password element; HighestAvailable; the OPEN registration note dropped; installer: any task folder; installer: a CIM registration call; installer: wildcard account match; installer: LogonType compared by name only. All caught.

**Only Windows can show:** that the PowerShell 5.1 parser accepts the new Verify lines (checked by eye and by the bracket test only); the actual types and text of `Principal.LogonType`, `RunLevel` and `UserId` returned for an S4U task of a local account; that `Register-ScheduledTask -Xml` accepts the unit without a password (OPEN (c)); and everything plan 12.3 lists.


## A03b reproducibility measurement: a second build from another folder and a PE comparison program (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-repro`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched)

**What was missing.** `native/nn-launcher/RELEASE.md` names reproducibility (two builds of one commit giving one hash) as a first-release blocker, and nothing had measured it. The hosted job built the product launcher once.

**What was built.**
- A new hosted-job step, "Product launcher reproducibility (second build from another folder; a report, not a gate)", right after the product build. It copies the crate folder (without `target`) to a different path with a different folder name outside the checkout, builds there `--locked` with the same pinned toolchain, the same `/Brepro` and the same remap flags (the remap names the second folder, so the path difference should not matter), keeps the same cargo home, and compares the two `nn-launcher.exe` files. It prints one line `reproducibility: A sha256=... B sha256=... identical|DIFFERENT`, a `::warning::` on a difference, a step summary, and uploads both files, a text report and a JSON report under `appc-out/repro/` (artifact `windows-appcontainer-hosted`).
- `scripts/pe-diff.mjs`: a small Node program (no dependency, nothing executed) that reads the PE headers of both files (COFF time stamp, optional header checksum, section table, debug directory entries with the RSDS GUID, age and PDB path), lists the differing byte ranges mapped to those fields and to sections (bounded: at most 64 ranges listed, every byte counted; at most 96 sections, 16 directories, 16 debug entries, a 520-byte path read, 64 MiB per file; every read checks the buffer), says in plain words what a pattern of differences points at, and reports whether either file holds the commit (as text or UTF-16), whether the PE time stamp looks like a build time (within a week of now), and whether either build folder or the cargo home appears in the file (the folder text is searched, only its label is printed). Exit 0 identical, 1 different, 2 usage or unreadable file.
- `scripts/pe-diff.test.mjs` (11 tests, synthetic PE files built in the test, nothing committed): identical, differing time stamp, checksum, debug stamp, GUID, PDB path, `.text`, `.rdata`, `.rsrc` and a longer file; bounded output; 20 malformed inputs (empty, truncated at several points, PE offset outside, 65535 sections, section table past the end, huge optional header size, huge directory count, huge debug size, debug RVA and raw pointer outside, a PDB path with no end); the commit, time and folder search; the program's exit codes and JSON report.
- Shape test in `scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs` pinning the step: after the product build and before staging, `if: always()`, `continue-on-error: true`, a timeout, `set +e` and an `exit 0` ending with no failing exit inside, the second folder outside the checkout with a different name, no shared target folder, no feature, the same flags as the first build, the comparison command and the artifact folder; permissions and action pins are unchanged.
- RELEASE.md and the crate README: what is measured and what is not, and how the unsigned and the signed hash relate.

**Deliberate breakages (7, each restored byte-identical, sha256 compared; each failed a test):** section-count bound removed; COFF time stamp offset moved; exit code 0 on a difference; `continue-on-error` removed from the step; the second build remapping the first folder; the copy including `target`; the 520-byte path bound removed (this one first survived, so a test for a path with no end and a huge stated size was added).

**ASSUMPTION: report, not a gate.** The step ends 0 on every path (a `::warning::` on a difference), with `continue-on-error: true` as a second guard. Reason: reproducibility is not yet known to hold, a failing step would hide the other results of the same run, and the stage step already re-checks the first build's hashes. It becomes a gate only after a hosted run shows `identical`.
**ASSUMPTION: a folder copy, not a second checkout.** The second build uses a byte-for-byte copy of the crate folder (the crate reads nothing outside its own folder: checked, no `../`, `include_*` or build script), so the only difference between the builds is the path and the folder name. A full second `git worktree` was not needed for that.

**Signed against unsigned.** `scripts/native-launcher.mjs record` hashes the bytes it is given. Reproducibility is about the unsigned file; the Authenticode signature changes the file (signature bytes, certificate-table entry, checksum), so the release makes two records (unsigned right after the build, signed after signing; same commit), the installer takes the signed file's hash, and the link between the two is a manual check with `pe-diff.mjs` (only the checksum, the certificate-table entry and bytes after the last section may differ). Nothing links the two records in code; no signed file exists yet. Written into RELEASE.md.

**What the hosted run will show (not yet run).** One of: `identical` (then reproducibility is shown for this one pair of folders on one runner image, not more), or `DIFFERENT` with the regions. Likely candidates if it differs, from reading the build flags and not from a measurement: the PDB path in the debug directory (the linker writes it for MSVC even without debug info, and `--remap-path-prefix` does not reach the linker), a crate-path hash baked into symbol or type names, or the header checksum following another difference. These are guesses; the JSON report names the real ones.

**NOT done / unmeasured.** The hosted result itself; a second runner image or day; the owner's machine; automation of the signed-to-unsigned tie; making the step a gate; any claim of reproducibility.

**Checked.** `scripts/*.test.mjs` 429 tests, 428 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (Node 22); the four affected files 178 pass on Node 22 and Node 24; `npx tsc --build --force`, `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok; `api:docs:write` changed nothing; `CONTRIBUTING.md` names the new script (the d02 docs test passes).

## A03b per-run container profile: one profile for every run, and the question of more than one run at once (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-prp`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows)

**What was lacking.** The native Windows backend made ONE container profile (`NimbleNewtAgent`) and used it for every run. Every run therefore had the same container identity (its SID), so two programs at once would have been able to reach each other's folders, and one run's cleanup would have taken away the other's permissions. That is why the backend ran one confined program at a time behind one exclusive lock.

**What was built (plain words).**
- Every run now makes its own profile, named `NimbleNewtRun-` and sixteen random hex digits (64 random bits, 30 characters; Microsoft allows 64 characters of letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore and space). The backend picks the name; the launcher only checks it. Permissions on files, the private window station's entry and the program's identity all use that run's own SID. After the program ends the launcher takes the permissions back, closes the window objects and the job, deletes the profile and checks that it is gone; the backend reads the permissions back by the run's own SID and, if the launcher's answer did not show the profile gone, asks for the delete itself. Only then are the run's records removed. A delete that cannot be shown is a typed failure (`profile`), the records stay, and the next run or health check cleans first and does not start while the leftover cannot be cleaned.
- Leftovers of a crashed run are cleaned from the backend's OWN records (a file per run in the control folder with the profile name, the run's permissions and folders, written BEFORE the launcher makes anything), revoked by that run's SID, then the profile is deleted and checked. Nothing scans the machine's list of profiles or the registry. The launcher deletes a profile only when it can prove it made it: the name has the exact per-run form, and a record file that the launcher itself wrote (create-new, before it made the profile) holds the same name and the SID the name derives to. A profile with no record, a record of another name, a damaged record, a bad name: nothing is deleted, and the tests show the launcher is not even called.
- The product launcher got tighter, not looser: the only name accepted is the per-run form (the old shared name, the experiment's name, no name at all are refused); `--profile-record` and `--sid` are accepted only on the commands that use them; `check` and `revoke` derive the SID from the name and never make a profile; one command, `delete-profile`, is new in the product, with the proof rule above. No experiment option was added.
- A second, separate setting: `maxConcurrentRuns` (option) or `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_MAX_RUNS` (environment; the operator's own, the installer does not write it), a whole number from 1 to 4. **Default 1, and with 1 the behaviour is the old one** (one slot, a second run busy). Above 1 the backend keeps one slot folder per run and a claim on each run's three task folders: the same workspace, or one inside or around another, is refused as busy (the seal and workspace entries would meet); different workspaces run side by side.
- Because the program folders (the Node installation) and read-only inputs are SHARED, and each launcher reads and rewrites the same folder's access list, two launchers at once could lose an entry or bring back a removed one. The launcher now takes one machine-wide named lock (`NimbleNewtAclWrite`) around every access-list change. This is reasoned, not measured.
- `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_PROFILE` and the `profileName` option are retired: the environment value (the installer still writes it) is read and ignored with a health note; the option is refused. The installer was not changed (a separately scoped file); `DEFAULT_PROFILE_NAME` stays only so the installer and the backend remain pinned to each other.

**The decision on concurrency, from the code.** Reasoned in `windows-isolation-plan.md` 12.4, resource by resource. Per run now: SID, file entries, window station, job, profile, job folder, channel files. Made safe by a claim: the workspace and its seals. Shared and not per run: program folders and read-only inputs, made safe only by the named lock in the launcher, which has never run. So the default stays 1, and more than 1 is an explicit setting that says "UNMEASURED on real Windows" in the audit and health notes.

**ASSUMPTION lines (decisions made without waiting).**
- ASSUMPTION: the shared profile name is retired outright rather than kept as an allowed name for `info`/`check`; nothing is installed anywhere, so no old profile or old job folder needs to be migrated. A job folder written by an older backend (no profile in its job file) is reported as a problem by the sweep, never guessed at.
- ASSUMPTION: "gone" is read with `GetAppContainerFolderPath` on the SID after the delete, treating a failing call as "no profile" (the documentation lists only S_OK and E_INVALIDARG). If real Windows says otherwise every run fails closed with the typed `profile` reason; that is the first thing to measure.
- ASSUMPTION: the launcher deletes the profile itself only when every grant it made is revoked and read back; otherwise it keeps the profile and the supervisor revokes by SID first. Revoking by SID does not need the profile to exist.
- ASSUMPTION: the limit is capped at 4 so a typo cannot open dozens of containers; the cap is a constant (`MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS_LIMIT`) that a later measurement can move.
- ASSUMPTION: with more than one slot, other runs in progress do not stop a new run's start (their claims keep workspaces apart); with one slot a possibly running earlier run still does, as before.
- ASSUMPTION (changed in review): the named lock is `Global\NimbleNewtAclWrite`. The first version had no prefix and called that "per logon session"; Microsoft's "Kernel Object Namespaces" says an unprefixed name is per Terminal Services SESSION, so a launcher from a signed-in session and the worker's session-0 launcher would have held two different locks over the same program folder. A mutex needs no privilege in the global namespace (SeCreateGlobalPrivilege is named only for file-mapping and symbolic-link objects).

**What is NOT done / unverified without Windows.** Profile make and delete cost, the "gone" check, deleting a profile while the folders it used still have handles open, the named lock with two real launchers, desktop heap with several containers, two private window stations at once, whether a non-administrator S4U account may create and delete profiles at all (12.3 asked twice per run now), and everything about concurrency. The code compiles for Windows (`cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline`, product and experiment builds) and the pure parts have Rust unit tests; the TypeScript lifecycle is tested with a simulated launcher on every OS. A single real Windows run of the ten containment cases through the product binary is still the first proof; two at once only after that.

**Checked.** The six affected test groups (`windows*.test.js`, `containment-windows*.test.js`, `native-launcher`, `d02-docs`, `windows-appcontainer-experiment`) 480 pass, 0 fail on Node 22 and on Node 24; `scripts/*.test.mjs` 430 tests (the one failure, CONTRIBUTING.md not naming `profile.rs`, was fixed); `cargo test --locked --offline` (product) and with `--features experiment` 23 pass each; `cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` with and without the experiment feature compiles; `npx tsc --build --force`, `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok; `api:docs:write` changed nothing. 13 deliberate breakages each made at least one test fail and each file was restored byte for byte (sha256 compared): the slot limit ignored, workspace overlap not refused, profile deleted before the read-back, the launcher's "deleted" taken as "gone", read-back without the run's SID, the slot kept when a claim is refused, a dead writer's claim still counting, the profile record written after the launcher ran, the launcher accepting any name, the delete proof skipping the SID, upper-case hex accepted, DACL writes without the machine-wide lock, and the profile deleted although a grant was not revoked.

**Independent review (2026-11-25, Claude agent, same branch; not pushed; nothing run on Windows).** Deletion safety holds: the launcher deletes or revokes only for a name of the exact per-run form (prefix, sixteen lower-case hex digits, nothing else), and the SID is always DERIVED from that name, so no record, path or `--sid` can point it at another profile or another SID (the owner's other AppContainer apps included); a forged record can at most name another `NimbleNewtRun-` profile, all of which are this backend's. Fixed: (1) MEDIUM: a folder claim was written with a plain write, so a runner that stopped mid-write left a half-written claim that every later run counted as held (with the DEFAULT limit 1 too): claims are now created whole (`createExclusive`, as the slot files are), an earlier claim of the same id is replaced, and a claim without a folder list counts as held. (2) MEDIUM: the claim step ran outside the run's try/finally, so a claims folder that could not be made or listed threw out of `runNativeJob` with the slot kept (every later run busy while the process lived); `claimFolders` now never throws (a reason, busy), and the claim and the slot are given back in an inner finally even when the cleanup itself throws. (3) MEDIUM: a runner that stopped after removing both profile records but before removing its status file left a job folder the sweep reported for ever ("profile record missing"), so no run would start again; such a folder is now released (both records absent with a status file means the run was retired: the backend record is written before the status file and removed only after a clean read-back and a profile shown gone), and the two records are removed launcher's first, so a stop between them leaves only the backend's record, which a sweep retires (the other order left a launcher record no sweep looks for). (4) LOW, wording and scope: the ACL lock was said to be per logon session; Microsoft's "Kernel Object Namespaces" says an unprefixed name is per Terminal Services SESSION, so it is now `Global\NimbleNewtAclWrite` (a mutex needs no SeCreateGlobalPrivilege; another account's launcher, or a local account that creates the name first, makes grants fail closed). Not changed, stated: any failure of `GetAppContainerFolderPath` after a successful delete is read as gone (a profile misread as gone has no entries left, since the delete comes after a clean read-back, so the cost is a leaked empty profile; the opposite reading would fail every run closed); a launcher whose `CreateAppContainerProfile` fails for a reason other than "exists" removes its record, which would leave a partly made profile (if Windows ever leaves one) unrecorded; claims whose writer is gone are not counted but not removed either (they accumulate, one per crash); any leftover that cannot be cleaned stops EVERY run, not only runs on its workspace (fail closed, by design). Tests: four review tests; 17 more deliberate breakages each made a test fail and each file was restored byte for byte (sha256): upper-case hex, 15/17 digits, a case-insensitive prefix, the record SID not compared, the record not create-new, the lock removed, the lock without `Global\`, delete before revoke in the sweep, records removed before the delete was checked, the same workspace allowed, the slot not given back when the cleanup throws, the `profile` reason replaced, default limit 2, the claim written with a plain write, a retired job folder not released, the records removed backend-first, a claim error thrown out.

**Second independent review (2026-11-25, Claude agent, clean context, same branch; not pushed; nothing run on Windows).** Read fresh: `runNativeJob` and both finally blocks, the slot and claim code, the sweep's two loops and record order, `windows-native.ts`, and the launcher's `profile.rs`, `args.rs` and the `run`/`info`/`check`/`revoke`/`delete-profile` arms and the ACL lock in `win.rs`. Held up: the slot, claim and in-progress mark are given back on every path out of a run and of a locked sweep (and only by their owner: numbers, claim ids and `LIVE_HERE` entries are the run's own); the launcher deletes only a per-run name with its own record and the derived SID; `info` deletes its throw-away profile on every path after it was made; the mutex is closed on every path and an abandoned one is taken; the TypeScript and Rust names, argument order, reply fields and stage `profile` agree; with limit 1 the slot logic is the one there was. Fixed:
- MEDIUM (default limit 1): the health check's `info` probe writes a profile record in the controller's process; a run's sweep in a runner's process counted that live record as a run in progress, so every run started while the health check made its probe profile failed with the typed `revoke` reason (and a probe profile that could not be deleted refused every run until the controller's next health check). A live record with no grants and no folders reaches nothing and no longer counts; a dead one is still swept.
- MEDIUM (default limit 1): the launcher wrote its record with create-new and then a plain write, so a launcher killed between the two left a half-written record; the backend rightly never acts on a record it cannot read, so that profile name was reported for ever and EVERY run stopped. The record is now made whole (`profile.rs` `create_whole`: a temporary file of its own, flushed, hard-linked to the name, which fails when the name exists; the temporary name removed on every path), with a Rust test on every OS.
- MEDIUM (limit above 1 only): claims covered only the three task folders, so a run whose read-only input was another live run's workspace (or inside or around it, `.git` included) was let through; its grant and revoke rewrite access lists inside that workspace, sealed names included, which is the combination one run's own plan already refuses. A claim now also lists the paths the run grants only to read; an input on another run's task folder (and a task folder on another run's input) is busy; two runs on the same input still run at once. The sweep's per-record claims carry the dead run's grant paths the same way.
- LOW: claims whose writer is gone were skipped but never removed, so each crash left one, and every later run paid one process listing (a PowerShell call) per dead claim, and was busy for each whenever that listing failed. A dead claim is now removed, only while its text is still the one judged.
- Tests: five new review tests (plus two new contract assertions: the lock's take paths, and the whole-record write); one simulated-launcher option (`deleteNotGone`, a self-contradicting answer).
- Docs: plan 12.4 (whole record, claims with reads, probe record, and a paragraph on the operator's way out when a leftover cannot be cleaned: the launcher's own `revoke`/`check`/`delete-profile` with the same proof, then the records, `.sid` first; removing records without those steps is the one thing not to do), launcher README.

Not changed, stated: any leftover that cannot be cleaned still stops EVERY run, including runs on unrelated workspaces (with per-run SIDs that is stricter than needed, but it is fail-closed and the operator's way out is now written down); the claims compare path TEXT (normalised, no short names, no links or junctions, case folded), not file identity, so a `subst` drive or a second drive letter for the same folder is not seen (the controller chooses these paths, not the agent); a run id that differs from another only in letter case would share its claim and job folder names on Windows (run ids are generated); the named lock can be created first by any local account, which then makes every grant fail closed (stated in 12.4 already); a backend record written just before a stop and before the run's status file stays as litter until that job folder is released (nothing was made for it).

Deliberate breakages (19; one at a time, each restored byte for byte, sha256 compared before and after): the run's inner finally without the slot release; without the claim release; the backend deleting the profile although an entry was left (NOT caught at first: test added); the records removed backend-first; the sweep releasing a job folder while the launcher's record is still there; the sweep removing a job folder whose retire failed; retire dropping records next to a damaged launcher record; the status file removed although the profile was not gone; a live probe record counted as a run; inputs not checked against others' task folders (at first a hang, not a failure: the test now fails cleanly); a dead claim removed without comparing its text (NOT caught at first: the race test fired on the wrong claim, fixed); dead claims kept; `deleted` taken as gone (NOT caught at first: no self-contradicting launcher answer existed, added); the locked sweep keeping its slot; the sweep's retire keeping its claim (NOT caught at first: assertion added); the record written with `rename` (replaces an existing record; Rust test); the abandoned mutex not taken and the handle not closed on timeout (NOT pinned at first: contract assertions added); the record written with a plain write again.

**Checked (second review).** The A03b group (`windows*.test.js`, `containment-windows*.test.js`, `native-launcher`, `d02-docs`, `windows-appcontainer-experiment`) 488 pass, 0 fail on Node 22 and on Node 24; `cargo test --locked --offline` 24 pass, with `--features experiment` 24 pass; `cargo +stable check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --locked --offline` with and without the experiment feature compiles with no warning; `npx tsc --build --force`, `check:deps`, `licenses:check`, `roadmap:check` ok; `api:docs:write` changed nothing. What only Windows can show is unchanged (12.4's list), plus: that `std::fs::hard_link` makes the record on the control folder's volume (NTFS supports hard links; the TypeScript side already relies on the same for its own files).

**Why the hosted run failed.** The per-run profile change made the product launcher accept only `NimbleNewtRun-` plus 16 lower-case hex digits and require `--profile-record` on `run`, `info` and `delete-profile`.
