**What changed (only `.github/workflows/windows-appcontainer-experiment.yml`, plus tests).**
- Hosted `info` step and own-runner "Product launcher info as the runner service" step: a fresh name per call (`NimbleNewtRun-$(node ... randomBytes(8) ... 'hex')`), a record file `$RUNNER_TEMP/profile-records/<name>.sid` (the folder is made first; the launcher creates the file create-new, never the folder; the path goes through `cygpath -w`). Both still require `"ok":true`, `"windowStation":"private"`, `"windowStationOk":true`, and now `"profileDeleted":true` and `"profileGone":true` (the fields the launcher's `info` prints). In the hosted step a miss is reported only after the release record and hash output, so the later steps still get their inputs; `profileGone` is the reading the README says is not yet measured, so a failure there is a finding, not a launcher fault.
- G05 ten cases (both jobs): they drive the product through the backend (`containment-evidence.mjs`, `windowsNativeBackend`), which already makes its own per-run names, records, deletes and sweeps. The only fixed name was the retired `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_PROFILE: NimbleNewtOwnRunnerG05` in the own-runner step; it is removed (the backend ignored it and added a health note).
- Own-runner clean-up: the loop that deleted `NimbleNewtProductCheck` and `NimbleNewtOwnRunnerG05` with the experiment launcher is gone. It keeps `desktop-revoke --name NimbleNewtExperiment` with the re-hashed experiment launcher (that call is the experiment launcher's own and keeps its own name). New: if the `info` step was stopped before deleting its profile, the step re-hashes the product launcher and runs `delete-profile --name N --sid S --profile-record P` with the name and record path the info step saved and the SID from the JSON it printed (nothing to do when the JSON says `profileGone`).
- Not adapted, stated: nothing deletes a G05 profile by name from the workflow after a killed run; the backend's own sweep does that at its next start. A leftover is therefore not reported by this workflow.

**What a hosted run will show.** The info step prints one JSON line with `ok`, `windowStation: private`, `windowStationOk`, `profile: created`, `profileDeleted`, `profileGone`. If `profileGone` is false the step goes red after the release record is made (this is the first real measurement of that reading).

**Tests.** `scripts/native-launcher.test.mjs` gains a test that parses every product-launcher call in the workflow (hosted info, own-runner info, clean-up delete-profile): the name comes from a variable generated as 16 hex digits, run/info/delete-profile carry `--profile-record`, delete-profile carries `--sid`, no fixed profile name or `NIMBLENEWT_WIN_PROFILE` remains, and the record folder is made before use. `scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs` pins the new info calls, the extra hash check (six, was five) and the new clean-up. Six deliberate breakages (a fixed name, a dropped record path, an 8-hex name, a delete without `--sid`, the retired env restored, the profile exit moved before the hash output) each failed a test and were restored byte for byte.

## G10, llama.cpp and vLLM measured on a rented GPU (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-25)

- **Built.** `packages/integration/src/g10-engines-live.ts` (the measurement code for both engines: shared head, idle gaps 0/15/30/60/120 s, an eviction ladder, concurrency 1/2/4/8, engine extras), `g10-engines-fake.ts` (scripted llama-server and vLLM stand-ins: slots with a similarity threshold, a host-memory prompt cache, slot save/erase/restore, block-based prefix cache with `cache_salt`, `/metrics`), `g10-engines-live-bench.ts` (the manual run), `g10-engines-live.test.ts` (13 offline tests) and captured responses in `packages/integration/test-fixtures/g10-engines/`. Evidence: `evidence/g10-vllm-run1.json`, `g10-llamacpp-run1.json`, `g10-llamacpp-run2.json` and the plain account `evidence/g10-engines-evidence.md`. The engines are read through their own fields (`timings.cache_n`/`prompt_n`; `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`) and `/metrics`. The code sends only synthetic ledger text, keeps no prompt or answer text, and handles no credential.
- **Result in one paragraph.** On both engines a shared head was reused by other conversations and after idle gaps up to 120 s. vLLM shared it across all concurrent requests; llama.cpp kept a cache per slot, so only one of 2 or 4 simultaneous conversations reused a warm head. Counted as other heads read since the head's last use, it was lost after 4 on llama.cpp with 4 slots and no host cache (kept after 2), after 8 on vLLM (about 5 heads of cache; kept after 4), and after 16 on llama.cpp with its default host cache (kept after 8; the cumulative ladder levels were 8, 16 and 32). Neither engine refused an unknown cache setting. **In run 1 (host prompt cache at its default) a llama.cpp slot erase did not stop reuse of the same prefix** (one observation on this build), which contradicts an assumption of C06's slot hygiene (open follow-up below).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the profile capabilities are not changed to `qualified` by this slice: the qualification test and the C06 profile belong to another card's owner, and the measurement is one run each on one GPU. The numbers are recorded so a later change can cite them. Recommended follow-up (not done): C06 should either set `--cache-ram 0` for shared servers or state that slot clearing is not isolation when the host cache is on.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a rented RTX 3090 (community cloud, $0.22 per hour) replaced the RTX 4090 the task named: no community RTX 4090 was in stock at any attempt; it is the same 24 GB class and cheaper, and speed is not what is compared.
- **ASSUMPTION:** one run per engine configuration, no repeats; the ladder counts other heads since the head was last used (each probe refreshes it), and the exact cliff edge was not searched.
- **Spend and cleanup.** About 31 pod minutes in all at $0.22 per hour (about $0.11; the CLI shows no balance, so the balance was not read and this is price times minutes; the wasted pod's 7 minutes are the operator's record, not in the JSON), four pods created, all deleted; `runpod pod list` showed no pods after every run and at the end. A watchdog and a try/finally in the manual runner deleted the pod on every path; a first pod whose host driver was too old for the llama.cpp image ran nothing and was deleted by hand. No API key, token or configuration file was read, printed or stored.
- **Not done.** Retention past 120 s; other slot counts, unified KV, offload; other models; the real Claude, OpenAI chat and Responses and Strata runs; changing the C06 profiles or the slot-hygiene code; the card is not flipped. G10 stays partly done: Radiance, the hosted OpenAI route, vLLM and llama.cpp are measured; Claude, Strata and the OpenAI Responses route are not.
- **Offline results.** `g10-engines-live.test.ts` 13 of 13 passed under the offline guard before the review (15 after it) (the stand-ins are given as `fetch`; no network): readers per engine (a missing field is "not reported", never a guess), metrics parsing, each phase on both engines, a vLLM without `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` recorded as not reported with no reuse claimed, failures recorded not thrown, the evidence holding no prompt or answer text, no credential header sent, the captured responses re-read.
- **Follow-up (C06) addressed in the section "C06e: erase isolation on llama.cpp" below (it was OPEN when written).** C06's slot hygiene (`inference-cache/adapter.ts` `#call` with `freshSlot: "erase"`, the default; C06 "Limits stated" (3): a call into a slot last held by another project or unknown first clears it and "cannot reuse another project's KV") then sends the call with `cache_prompt: true`. `g10-llamacpp-run1.json` `extras/slot0-after-erase` (host prompt cache at its default) still reused 6,469 of 6,470 tokens after an erase that answered 200; with `--cache-ram 0` (run 2) the same step reused 0. So on a llama-server with the host cache on, the erase does not prevent a call from being served a prefix another project already sent (prefix match only). Unaffected: the `reuseOff` path (`cache_prompt: false`: 0 cached in both runs). Also affected: the llama.cpp profile's tuning list (no `--cache-ram`) and its retention text (silent on the host cache). Options for C06's owner: require or recommend `--cache-ram 0` for a llama-server shared by projects, or treat a host-cache server like `freshSlot: "off"` (reuse off on a holder change), or record that erase is not isolation there. One run per setting; a repeat on the target build should come first.
- **Independent review and fixes (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-25).** Merged origin/main ecb4ba7a (notes conflict, both sides kept). Recomputed every figure in `g10-engines-evidence.md` from the three JSON files and the four fixtures. Corrected in the note (the data is unchanged): the ladder now states other heads since last use throughout (llama.cpp run 2 was "lost at 8 others since the last probe": it was 4 since, 8 in total; run 1 "kept through 16 others" was 8 since last use; the notes' result paragraph used cumulative totals and said the head "survived more conversations than the cache holds", true only for llama.cpp with the host cache); run 2's restore row is 6,470 of 6,471 (not 6,474); idle prompt sizes; cost about $0.11 (not $0.12); the Radiance comparison (its marker survived 0, 15, 30 s and was lost at 60 s, not "0, 60 and 300 s"; Radiance accepted every cache field, its 400 came from the `logit_bias` stand-in); the vLLM 15 s slow first token is no longer attributed to the proxy, and the other variation of vLLM first-token times with full reuse is stated; "empty slot" and "one after another" (not recorded) narrowed; run 1's JSON carries the earlier combined check `restoreBroughtTheHeadBack: false`, said; "one run per configuration, no repeats" stated at the top; vLLM had served calls before its run (`metricsAtStart`), said; the C06 remark rewritten as an observation naming the exact code assumption, with row citations. Code: `evictionRun` records `cliffOtherHeadsSinceLastUse` and `lastKeptOtherHeadsSinceLastUse` (the docstring had said only a missed probe re-reads the head); vLLM `cache_salt` values are new per run (they were constant; harmless while each head carries a nonce, but now independent of that). Tests (15): the idle order (each gap between its warm call and the next, nothing sent in it, one head per gap), the since-last-use figures, per-run salts, time to first token at the first non-empty content with a controlled clock, and a test that recomputes the note's ladder, concurrency, erase and idle figures from the committed evidence. 11 deliberate breakages, all caught, build output restored by sha256: cached read from `prompt_tokens`, cliff from the total, concurrency serial, idle gap skipped, constant salt, prompt text in the evidence, metrics delta reversed, first token not taken, one head for every gap, the same other head repeated in the ladder, the prime call inside the timed group. Hygiene: no key, token, pod id, proxy address or host address in the diff or fixtures; `pod.dataCenterId` is null.

### A03b: the installer's first real run found a -WhatIf failure (card not flipped)

**What the owner saw.** On a real Windows machine (Windows PowerShell 5.1, elevated, StrictMode 3 in the script): `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Install-NimbleNewtLauncher.ps1 -Action Install -LauncherPath .\nn-launcher.exe -ExpectedSha256 <hash> -AllowUnsigned -WhatIf` printed `What if: Performing the operation "Retrieve the value for property 'ProviderPath'" on target "InputObject: C:\nn-test\nn-launcher.exe"` and then failed with `The property 'Hash' cannot be found on this object` (PropertyNotFoundStrict).

**Root cause, as far as it can be known without Windows.** The script is `[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]`, so `-WhatIf` sets `$WhatIfPreference` for every command it calls. Windows PowerShell 5.1's file-hash cmdlet is written in PowerShell; its own steps (a member read of `ProviderPath`) honour the preference, so it printed the question and returned nothing, and `(...).Hash` failed under StrictMode. The message names a read step of that cmdlet, so this is the best reading; it was not reproduced here (no PowerShell on this machine). The same class of risk applies to any read-only cmdlet written in PowerShell or a CDXML module, so all result-dereferencing reads were wrapped, not just the hash.

**Why nothing caught it before.** (1) The Linux tests read the script as text: they cannot run PowerShell, and the earlier hosted-workflow tests only pinned that the step contained `-WhatIf`. (2) The hosted step did already call the installer with a launcher path, a hash and `-WhatIf` under `shell: powershell` (5.1), so it should have reached the hash; why it did not report red is not known from the repository: the hosted runs so far went red earlier (the product launcher info step) and the installer step's own result was not examined or recorded in these notes, and the step ran the script in-process (`& $f`) rather than as the owner did, as a separate `powershell.exe -File` with a relative path. ASSUMPTION: the difference of invocation, or an unread result, explains it; the new step removes the difference instead of guessing which it was. (3) The first slice never ran on a real machine at all (README: "written, not run").

**What changed.** `Get-Sha256Hex` (.NET only, `finally` disposal, upper-case hex) replaces every file-hash cmdlet call (Install: source, placed file, re-hash after copy; Verify). `Invoke-Read` (sets `$WhatIfPreference = $false` inside its own scope) wraps every read-only cmdlet whose output is used, in Install, Verify and Uninstall. `-LauncherPath` is made a full path once, so the .NET calls and the cmdlets agree about a relative path. State-changing calls stay inside `ShouldProcess`. The hosted step "Installer script" now builds the owner's command from the product `nn-launcher.exe` (hash computed with .NET in the step, not with the installer's helper) and runs it under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (relative path, `-File`) and PowerShell 7, fails on a non-zero exit, a missing dry-run line, error text (`PropertyNotFound`, `Retrieve the value for property`, `Exception`) or an account/folder left behind (read-only checks), then runs Verify under 5.1 with and without `-WhatIf`. It is a gate for this check only. Action pins and permissions are untouched.

**Tests.** `scripts/native-launcher.test.mjs`: no file-hash cmdlet in the installer; the helper's shape; every read cmdlet is inside `Invoke-Read` (line scan); changes stay inside ShouldProcess; the workflow's required dry-run lines are lines the installer prints; the workflow step runs both shells with the real path and fails on errors. `scripts/windows-appcontainer-experiment.test.mjs`: one matching test. Ten deliberate breakages (stripping the helper, reintroducing the cmdlet, unwrapping a read, defeating `Invoke-Read`, no disposal, dropping the pwsh run or the launcher path, `continue-on-error`, a cmdlet in the helper) each failed a test; files restored by checksum.

**Not done / only a Windows run can confirm.** That the repair works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 (the new hosted step is the first check); that the exact dry-run text is as predicted (the required lines come from reading the script, not from a run; if the first hosted run shows different wording, adjust the list); that `Get-LocalUser` and friends behave under PowerShell 7's compatibility layer; that the Verify exit code is 1 on an empty machine as designed.

### A03b: the standard-account probe script (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-probe`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows or PowerShell)

**What was lacking.** Plan 12.3 asks two questions that only a task run as the NON-administrator S4U account can answer: can it create the container profile, and can it make the private window station. The owner will run the real `Install` and `Verify` next, and needed one script that answers both, with a plain verdict and a block to paste back.

**What was built.** `native/install/Probe-NimbleNewtWorker.ps1` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 syntax, StrictMode 3, `-WhatIf`, one question). It refuses unless elevated, the installer's manifest is present and has the installer's schema, the account exists, is enabled, carries the installer's marker, matches the manifest's SID and is not in Administrators (an unreadable group fails closed), the launcher has the manifest's hash, no path is a link, and no task named `NimbleNewtProbe` exists. It writes `probe-inner.ps1` (create-new, ASCII, hashed before and after) into the control folder, registers the task from XML it generates itself (S4U, LeastPrivilege, no password element, no trigger, `PT10M`, an Exec of `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ...`), starts it, waits on the task state and the result file with a deadline, reads the result as data, prints the verdict and a paste-back block, and in a `finally` stops (if running) and unregisters that exact task name and deletes the files it made by exact name. The inner program (as the account, Session 0) writes `probe-result.json` after every step and in a `finally`: the token facts (user, SID, system and administrator flags, integrity level, session id, groups), the profile and temp folders, `whoami /user /groups /priv`, then the launcher's `info` and `check` and, only if `info` left a profile behind, `delete-profile` with the launcher's own proof. Hosted workflow: a step parses the script and its inner program with PowerShell 5.1 and runs the `-WhatIf` path with a made-up manifest (plus three refusals) and asserts that no task or file appeared.

**Decisions made here (ASSUMPTION lines).**
- **ASSUMPTION:** the OUTER script generates the per-run name (8 random bytes from `RNGCryptoServiceProvider`, lower hex) and passes it to the inner program, instead of the inner generating it: the outer then knows the exact record file name for clean-up even if the task dies, and prints it. The format is the launcher's (`NimbleNewtRun-` and 16 lower hex digits).
- **ASSUMPTION:** no contained `run` is attempted. The launcher's `run` needs `--stdin file:`, `--stdout`, `--stderr`, folder grants and finite job limits, all of which the worker's backend writes per run; a hand-made one would be a second implementation and its result would not show the product path. `info` plus `check` are the probe; the ten G05 cases through the backend stay the next step.
- **ASSUMPTION:** `check` is given `--grant rx:<install folder>` (read only; it only counts entries for the container's derived SID on that path) and `--sid` from `info` as the launcher's own cross-check.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the probe process's own window station name is not read. It needs a compiled helper (Add-Type writes into the account's temp folder, which an S4U profile may not have) or hand-built reflection code that cannot be tested here; `info` reports `windowStation` and `windowStationOk`, which is the question. The profile and temp folders are reported instead (they show whether a profile was loaded).
- **ASSUMPTION:** the inner program stays modifiable by the account (the control folder gives it Modify on everything inside, and an administrator-created file inherits that), so the outer script hashes it before the task starts and after it ends and prints both results. A change by the account between the two would be shown, not prevented.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a leftover record file is kept (and said so) when the launcher could not prove the profile was deleted; it is the proof `delete-profile` needs. A leftover `probe-result.json` of an earlier run is overwritten by name.
- Exit codes: 0 a result was obtained (the verdict may be a negative finding), 1 no result or an error, 2 refused before any change, 3 the task or a file is still there.

**Tests.** `scripts/nonadmin-probe.test.mjs`: 25 tests on Node 22 and 24. They pin the shape: ASCII; brackets and strings (the checker moved to `scripts/ps-brackets.mjs`, shared with the installer's test); 5.1 syntax; no automatic-variable names; no password parameter, secure string, credential or `schtasks`; one Register call with `-Xml` and `-Force:$false`; only Register, Unregister, Start, Stop, Get-ScheduledTask and Get-ScheduledTaskInfo, each naming the constant task name and no wildcard; the unregister in a `finally` guarded by "this run registered it"; every change after the ShouldProcess question; the refusals (administrator, manifest, hash, links, overrides without `-WhatIf`) and that the manifest keys the probe reads are those the installer writes; the task XML parsed with a small reader (S4U, LeastPrivilege, no Password, no Triggers, PT10M, the Task Scheduler schema's order, escaping of `&`); the command-line quoting and the safe-path pattern with bad examples; every read cmdlet inside `Invoke-Read` and no `Get-FileHash`; the bounded wait; the verdict rows against plan 12.3's table; the launcher flags against `args.rs`' own rules (`--profile-record` only for info and delete-profile, `--sid` only for check and delete-profile, no `run`) and the JSON fields and stages against the launcher source; the installer's control-folder rights the probe relies on; the hosted step; the README, plan, CONTRIBUTING and these notes. CONTRIBUTING.md accounts for the new `.ps1` (d02's rule). Deliberate breakages: see "Checked" below.

**Not done / only a real run can show.** That any of this runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the hosted step is its first parse and `-WhatIf` run; Linux only reads the text); that `Register-ScheduledTask -Xml` accepts the S4U principal without a password (the open item (c)); that `Get-LocalGroupMember -SID` works on the owner's machine (an orphaned-SID bug in Windows PowerShell 5.1 can make it fail, which the script treats as a refusal, not a pass); the exact task result codes in the meaning table (common values only); whether the token's integrity level appears in `WindowsIdentity.Groups` (also in the saved `whoami /groups` text); whether `info` under S4U creates the profile and the station (the question itself); a reboot test; Windows Home; Task Scheduler restart behaviour.

**Review (2026-11-25, Claude agent, independent review and fixes; card NOT flipped; not pushed; nothing run on Windows or PowerShell).** Read as Windows PowerShell 5.1 code, outer and inner, against the owner's two lessons (a `-WhatIf` leak into reads; a property that the object does not have under StrictMode). Found and fixed:
- HIGH, the script could not have started: `"(stage $stage: $err)"` in `Get-Verdict` is a parse error in PowerShell (`$stage:` is read as a drive-qualified variable; "':' was not followed by a valid variable name character"), so the whole file fails to parse. Now `$($stage):`; a Linux test rejects `$name:` followed by a non-name character in the probe and the installer (the hosted parse step would have caught it, but it was never dispatched).
- HIGH, Ctrl+C could leave the task: the `finally` used `Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object` and value-returning helpers before `Unregister-ScheduledTask`. Microsoft's about_Try_Catch_Finally says a `finally` runs after Ctrl+C but the pipeline is stopped, and reports describe output inside it ending the block. The clean-up now uses only .NET and the Task Scheduler COM interface (`Schedule.Service`: `GetTask`, `Stop(0)`, `DeleteTask(name, 0)`, read back with 0x80070002 as the only "gone"), each step in its own `try`, no cmdlet, no function call, no pipeline (a test enforces this). The flag is set BEFORE `Register-ScheduledTask` (a stop right after it still removes the task), and the task is removed only if its XML carries this run's random name. Closing the window still skips the clean-up (stated).
- MEDIUM, the account could change the program between the hash check and the start (it has Modify below the control folder). `probe-inner.ps1` is now created in one call with a protected DACL (`D:P(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;0x1200a9;;;<account SID>)`, read and execute only) through the .NET Framework `FileStream` constructor that takes a `FileSecurity`; the DACL and the control folder's delete-child rights are read back before anything is registered. The script therefore requires Windows PowerShell 5.1 (refuses 7 outside the test mode).
- MEDIUM, the administrator check: `Get-LocalGroupMember` on 5.1 fails for a whole group with an orphaned or cloud member, which refused the probe on such machines. A second, independent reading (the account's own groups through the WinNT provider) is added; either naming Administrators refuses; both unreadable refuses.
- MEDIUM, invalid-probe detection: .NET's `WindowsIdentity.Groups` leaves out the integrity label and deny-only groups, so `integrityLevel` was always empty and a UAC-filtered administrator token looked clean. The inner program now reads `S-1-16-*` and `S-1-5-32-544` from `whoami /groups` by SID (not localized); the verdict is `invalid probe` also for a different user SID than the manifest's, High or System integrity, the launcher's `elevated`, or a listed Administrators SID.
- MEDIUM, over-claiming: a registration error that names a line and column of the task text (a fault in the script) was labelled plan 12.3 (c); it is now `task text refused (a fault in this script)`, and (c) says when it holds. OK no longer says "Risk 6 does not bite" in general: it says this machine and build only, whether the per-run profile was deleted again, and that the ten cases, the reboot, restarts and other editions are not shown.
- LOW: the default wait (240 s) was shorter than the task's own worst case (420 s with the pipe and kill waits), so a slow `info` could be stopped mid-call; now 480 to 900, default 540 (under `PT10M`). The task state and last result are read from the COM object (documented TASK_STATE numbers) instead of the CIM enum. A result counts only if it names this run's random name; its size is read inside the `try`; it is read with `-Encoding Ascii` (written ASCII by another account). The `profiles` folder is the worker backend's too (`windows-native-job.ts`): it is removed only if this run made it.
- Confirmed, not changed: `check --grant rx:<install folder>` writes nothing (win.rs `check`: `sid_for_entries` only derives the SID for a per-run name, `explicit_count` reads with `GetNamedSecurityInfoW`); `delete-profile` runs only with the launcher's proof (name form, record, SID); no password anywhere; `Register-ScheduledTask -Xml` takes a string; every launcher and whoami call has a bounded wait and a kill, with both pipes drained; the inner file and the result are ASCII on both sides; `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8` covers the deepest value (5 levels).
- Only a real Windows run can show: that the file parses and runs under 5.1 (the hosted step parses it and runs `-WhatIf`), the COM calls and the `FileStream`/`FileSecurity` constructor as written, the WinNT group reading, the Task Scheduler's answer to an S4U registration without a password, and everything the probe itself measures. Tests: `scripts/nonadmin-probe.test.mjs`, 29 tests.

### C06e: erase isolation on llama.cpp (follow-up of G10; card not flipped)

- **What the code assumed.** C06 "Limits stated" (3) said a call into a slot last held by another project or an unknown holder first erases the slot (`/slots/N?action=erase`) and then goes out with `cache_prompt: true`, so it "cannot reuse another project's KV". G10 measured that on a llama-server with its default host prompt cache (`--cache-ram` at its default, prompts kept beside the slots) the erase answered 200 and the next call still reused 6,469 of 6,470 tokens another project had sent (`g10-llamacpp-run1.json`, row `extras/slot0-after-erase`); with `--cache-ram 0` the same step reused none (`g10-llamacpp-run2.json`), and `cache_prompt: false` reused none in both runs.
- **What changed.** (1) New endpoint option `hostPromptCacheOff` (true or false; an attestation that the server runs with `--cache-ram 0`). The controller cannot detect it: the committed `/props` and `/slots` fixtures do not name the setting, so it is a deployment fact set with the other endpoint options (`slots`, `slotSave`, ...), not a chat setting. (2) The llama.cpp profile carries `eraseIsolation: "attested" | "unattested"`. (3) In `CacheAdapter` a call that crosses a project boundary (previous holder another project, or unknown: a start, a release, a slot-less call, a restart) is **erased and then reuses** only when the endpoint is attested; otherwise **no erase is sent and the call carries `cache_prompt: false`** (no reuse at all). Same-project calls are unchanged (they reuse; measured working). Other profiles (vLLM with its `cache_salt`, Claude, OpenAI, Radiance, Strata) are not touched: they set no `eraseIsolation`. (4) `CallResult.isolation` records the mode of every call into a named slot: `same-project`, `erase-host-cache-attested-off`, `erase`, `cache-prompt-off-host-cache-not-attested`, `cache-prompt-off-configured` (`freshSlot: "off"`), `cache-prompt-off-erase-failed`; the unattested mode also adds a `skipped` line that names `--cache-ram 0`. (5) The llama.cpp profile's tuning list gains `--cache-ram 0` for a shared server, its retention text and caveats say whether the host cache is attested off, and the tuning text states what was measured (one run, this build) and what was not (other builds and values, a second run). (6) The `LlamaSim` stand-in can model the host cache (`hostCache: true`): a prompt leaving a slot (by overwrite or erase) is kept beside the slots and a `cache_prompt: true` call reuses it.
- **Default behaviour before and after.** Before: every llama.cpp endpoint with slots erased a foreign or unknown slot and reused, with the leak above on a default server. After: an endpoint that does not say `hostPromptCacheOff: true` sends the first call across a project boundary with `cache_prompt: false` (one re-read; no erase request) and its later same-project calls reuse; an attested endpoint behaves as before. A project that is the only user of its server loses only the first call's reuse after each hand-over or restart.
- **ASSUMPTION:** option (a) from the task, chosen because the endpoint options are already the place for server facts and the change is two small branches. The conservative reading is kept: without the attestation the controller assumes the host cache may be on. `freshSlot: "off"` keeps its meaning and wins over the attestation.
- **ASSUMPTION:** `hostPromptCacheOff` is not an owner chat control: like `slots` and `slotSave` it describes how the server was launched, is supplied in the endpoint configuration when the engine is connected, and cannot be learned from chat; the profile's retention text, caveats and tuning list name it so an owner who is asked about the server can be told what to set. No interpreter prompt or control list enumerates endpoint options (checked), so none changed.
- **Not done / limits.** (a) One run per setting on one build; a repeat on the target build should come first, and the attestation is only as true as the launch command. (b) A later call of the same project is sent with `cache_prompt: true`; with the host cache on, the server may serve it any prompt another project left in the host cache that matches the new prompt further than the slot's own (for example a new conversation of the same project in the same slot whose head another project sent; not only tokens beyond the project's earlier prompt). The measured leak was the shared head at a hand-over, which this closes; the same-project case was not measured and is not closed without `--cache-ram 0` (see the review below). (c) The ledger (R05) totals are unchanged; the mode is in the call result and its `skipped` text only. (d) No real server was touched (no model calls); the evidence is the committed G10 JSON, and the tests use the stand-in modelled on it.
- **Tests.** `adapter.test.ts`: 5 new tests (cross-project call unattested sends `cache_prompt: false` and reuses nothing though the host cache holds the head, with a control that the stand-in leaks after an erase; same-project reuse; attested erase path with `cache_prompt: true`; unknown holder counts as cross-project; every mode named, vLLM unchanged; profile text and option check); the existing slot tests now run attested. 8 deliberate breakages (attestation ignored, unknown holder as same project, mode not recorded, profile always attested, `cache_prompt` always true, wrong mode label, same-project mislabelled, stand-in forgets the host cache) were each caught and the files restored byte-identical (sha256).
- **Independent review and fixes (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-25).** Branch was level with origin/main (318ee722); no merge needed. Every route by which a llama.cpp call could carry `cache_prompt: true` after another project or an unknown holder used the server was listed: first call after a start, after a release, after a restart, a slot-less call, a plain call, `freshSlot: "off"`, a failed erase and the attested erase path were correct. Found and fixed: (1) **medium, from C06:** a call that named a slot but was sent **without** `id_slot` (a project that requires isolation, whose call carries no cache settings; or a slot at or above the configured count, which `slotChoice` drops) was recorded as that slot's holder, kept only that slot's turn, and did not forget the other holders, although the server placed it anywhere. So the slot it really landed in kept its old holder, whose next same-project call went out with `cache_prompt: true` onto the other project's prompt (for an isolation-required project: other projects sped up by its prompt; for an out-of-range slot on an attested server, an erase was also sent to a slot that does not exist). Now the adapter works out the slot the request will really name (`#namedSlot`: plain, isolation required on a backend whose isolation is `none`, or outside `slotCount`, a new profile field) and treats every other call as slot-less (the server's turn, every holder forgotten, no erase). (2) **medium, from C06:** `slot("save")` wrote whatever the slot held into a file under the caller's marker without checking the holder; a restore of that file then makes the caller the holder and its next call reuses with `cache_prompt: true`. A save is now refused (never thrown) unless this project is the slot's recorded holder (save and restore are not yet wired into the dispatcher, so this was latent). (3) **low:** the isolation mode was missing for slot-less calls, the retry after a refusal (it kept the first attempt's mode) and llama.cpp without `slots`; new modes `cache-prompt-off-no-slot`, `cache-prompt-off-isolation-required` and `reuse-slots-not-configured` (no hand-over protection at all without `slots`, stated, unchanged behaviour). (4) **low, text:** the same-project residual is now an owner-visible caveat of every unattested llama.cpp profile, and an isolation-required call on an unattested llama.cpp says other projects may still be sped up by its prompt (before, the llama.cpp text implied full isolation). The stand-in's host model is documented as leakier than measured: it would have served the kept head to the empty slot 1, where run 1 measured 4 tokens.
- **Decision on the residual (ASSUMPTION, recorded for the lead).** Same-project calls on an unattested server keep `cache_prompt: true`. llama-server has no request field that turns off only the host prompt cache: `cache_prompt: false` is the only per-request control and it also turns off the slot's own reuse, so the conservative alternative is no reuse at all on every default server until an owner attests. Reasons for keeping it: only identical tokens are ever reused (the other project's text never reaches the call; what leaks is timing), C06's standing lead decision (1) accepts that timing side channel on shared local backends by default and removes it per project with `isolationRequired`, the measured hand-over case is closed, and the residual is stated in the profile caveats, the tuning list and here, with `--cache-ram 0` plus `hostPromptCacheOff` (or a server of its own) as the way to remove it. If the owner wants the stricter reading, it is a one-line change in `#call` (reuse off for every call on an unattested endpoint).
- **Attestation: who can set it.** Endpoint options, `hostPromptCacheOff` like `slots` and `slotSave`, come only from the controller's start options (`dispatch.cache.endpoints`, read by `dispatch-compose.ts`); they are not stored settings, no command or chat control writes them, and the launcher does not set them today. So no agent or task-scoped credential can set the attestation. A wrong `true` brings back the measured run 1 reuse across projects at every hand-over (a test shows it); a wrong `false` costs one re-read per hand-over. Chat reachability: no endpoint option is an owner chat control (none is wired to the launcher at all), so this one is consistent with them; when endpoint cache configuration becomes an owner setting, all of its options, this one included, belong in the chat controls.
- **Review tests.** `adapter.test.ts` +5: a golden replay of the committed G10 extras rows (run 1 `slot0-after-erase` 6,469 of 6,470 after an erase that answered 200, run 2 0; the stand-in replays the sequence: run 2 exactly, run 1 never less than measured and different only at `slot1-same-head`), the unattested adapter never sends run 1's shape (erase then `cache_prompt: true` into that slot) across a boundary while the attested one sends run 2's, a wrong attestation reproduces the leak; calls sent without `id_slot` (isolation required, slot out of range, the retry after a refusal, no `slots`) recorded as no holder with their modes; save only by the holder; the residual caveat. One expectation of the earlier mode test changed (a slot-less call now records `cache-prompt-off-no-slot`). 15 deliberate breakages, each caught and restored by sha256: unknown holder as same project, attestation default true, mode labels swapped, `cache_prompt: true` after a cross-project call, `id_slot` not pinned, the erase-failed path sending `cache_prompt: true`, the attested path skipping the erase, `--cache-ram 0` missing from the profile, an isolation-required call keeping the named slot, a slot outside the count kept, the save guard removed, the retry's mode not recorded, the stand-in forgetting the host cache on erase, the unslotted mode not recorded, the residual caveat dropped.
- **Second independent review and fixes (Claude agent, 2026-11-25, clean context).** Branch level with origin/main 318ee722. Found and fixed: (1) **medium, introduced by C06e on the new default:** on an unattested endpoint a call across a project boundary sends no erase, and the old holder was only replaced when the call completed. A call that failed or was cut off after the server had read it (an error status, a lost connection, Pi's abort during prefill) left the **previous** project recorded as the slot's holder although the slot might now hold this call's prompt; that project's next call then went out as `same-project` with `cache_prompt: true` over the other project's prompt. Before C06e the default erase path deleted the holder first, so this was a regression of the default (and it was already open in C06 on the `freshSlot: "off"` and erase-refused paths). Now the holder is forgotten as soon as a call crosses a project boundary, before anything is sent, and only a call that completes records its project. (2) **low:** the plain retry after a refused `id_slot` forgot the holders only after it was answered, so a retry that threw left them in place; they are now forgotten before it is sent. (3) **low:** a restore that failed or was cut off kept the slot's old holder although the file may already have been loaded; the holder is now forgotten before a restore is sent and recorded only when it completes. Checked and found sound: `#namedSlot` matches what `prepare` really sends (plain, isolation required on a backend with isolation `none`, a slot outside `slotCount`; an agent-supplied `id_slot` in the body only ever reaches the slot-less path, which forgets every holder); slot-less calls take the server's turn; the save guard is checked inside the slot's turn; a restore cannot reach another project's file through the adapter only as far as the dispatcher resolves the marker for the project (unchanged C06 duty), and the file name must match `nn-[a-z0-9]{8,40}.bin` (no path); every llama.cpp route records exactly one mode and none claims more than it gives; vLLM, Claude, OpenAI, Radiance and Strata take none of the changed branches (all are unslotted and set no `eraseIsolation`; Strata's unguarded save is unchanged). The `hostPromptCacheOff: true` added to the dispatcher, pi-fetch and h12e tests was checked by removing it: four tests then fail only where they expect reuse or an erase at a hand-over (the intended change), so the attestation keeps them testing what they tested; a pi-fetch test of the **default** endpoint (hand-over sent with `cache_prompt: false`, no erase, same project reuses afterwards, host cache on) was added because none existed. **Wording corrected:** the earlier review called the profile caveats "owner-visible"; today nothing outside `inference-cache` reads `profile.caveats`, `tuning` or `CallResult.isolation` (no API, chat control or ledger field), so the residual and the `--cache-ram 0` advice are findable in the code and these notes only. Tests: `adapter.test.ts` +6 (a failed or cut-off call across a boundary for each of attested/unattested, status/throw, erase/off/erase-refused; a retry that throws; a failed restore; a call refused before writing; a wipe by another slot's retry while a call runs; turn order of a slot-less call between slot calls), `pi-fetch.test.ts` +1. 14 deliberate breakages, each caught and `adapter.ts` restored by sha256: the hand-over delete removed, the retry forgetting after its answer, the restore pre-delete removed, the save guard admitting an unknown holder, the guard moved to restore, a failed restore recording its holder, a restore ignoring a wipe, a failed call recording its holder, a call ignoring a wipe, a slot-less call taking only slot 0's turn, slot turns not chained, the server's turn not waiting for slot work, `slotCount` ignored, the save guard removed (four of these were uncaught before the new tests).
- **OPEN for the owner (not changed here).** (a) The same-project residual on an unattested server: this review agrees with keeping reuse (consistent with C06 lead decision (1), which accepts the timing side channel on shared local backends by default and removes it per project with `isolationRequired`); the stricter reading is the one-line change named above. (b) The text that tells an owner to run `--cache-ram 0` and set `hostPromptCacheOff` is not shown anywhere an owner reads yet; when endpoint cache configuration becomes an owner setting, the profile caveats and tuning list should be shown with it. (c) llama.cpp **without** `slots` but with `slotSave` still saves any slot unguarded (no holder is ever known there; the profile already says such a server has no hand-over protection); refusing every save there is the consistent choice once save is wired into the dispatcher.

### A03b: the owner's first real Verify found a wrong property name (branch `card-a03b-vp`; card not flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows)

**What the owner found.** After a real Install, `-Action Verify` (Windows PowerShell 5.1, StrictMode 3) printed `PASS  the account exists` and stopped with `The property 'PasswordNeverExpires' cannot be found on this object`. The script read `$user.PasswordNeverExpires` on the object `Get-LocalUser` returns. That object has AccountExpires, Description, Enabled, FullName, PasswordChangeableDate, PasswordExpires, PasswordLastSet, PasswordRequired, UserMayChangePassword, LastLogon, Name, SID, PrincipalSource and ObjectClass (Microsoft's documentation for Get-LocalUser); `PasswordNeverExpires` is a parameter of the command that creates a user. Under StrictMode 3 a missing property throws.

**Why nothing earlier could see it.** The dry run (`Install -WhatIf`) never reads an account. The hosted `Verify` runs on an empty machine, where `Get-LocalUser` finds nothing, so the script stops at `FAIL  the account exists` and never reaches the line that reads the account's properties; the text-only Linux tests checked the shape of the script, not the names a command's result has.

**Done.**
- The line prints `password expires: never` when `PasswordExpires` is empty, else the date. Install makes the user with the never-expires switch, which leaves `PasswordExpires` empty. ASSUMPTION: this is information only (no PASS/FAIL line): the installer's header and README never say the password must never expire, and an administrator may apply a policy later.
- Audit of every property read in the script (Install, Verify, Uninstall, helpers). Changed: (1) `$user.PasswordNeverExpires` (wrong name, the owner's failure); (2) `(Get-LocalGroup -SID ...).Name` now `Get-Prop`; (3) the worker task's action `Execute`, `Arguments`, `WorkingDirectory` (printed, and `Arguments` in the boot check): only the exec action type has them, a COM-handler or e-mail action throws under StrictMode, now `Get-Prop`; (4) Uninstall's manifest fields `schema`, `account`, `accountSid`, `installDir`, `dataDir`, `controlDir`, `launcher`: a damaged or foreign manifest (or an empty file, which makes the object empty) threw an unhelpful error, now `Get-Prop` and the account name and SID are validated (a short pattern and a local SID, `S-1-5-21-...`) before any use. Checked and left as they are (documented on every object of their kind): LocalUser Name/SID/Enabled/Description/PasswordExpires, LocalGroupMember SID, Get-Acl AreAccessRulesProtected/Access and its owner and rule methods, access-rule IdentityReference/FileSystemRights/InheritanceFlags/PropagationFlags/AccessControlType, the signature's Status, the task's Principal/Triggers/Actions and the principal's UserId/LogonType/RunLevel, a trigger's CimClass.CimClassName, file items' FullName, user profile SID, hashtable keys of the plan, SecurityIdentifier Value, and the intrinsic Count of arrays.
- `Get-Prop $object 'Name'` is the one new helper: null object or absent property gives null; it uses `PSObject.Properties[...]`, Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatible. `Get-Sha256Hex` and `Invoke-Read` are unchanged and no file-hash cmdlet is used.
- Hosted workflow step "Installer Verify against a real throw-away account (hosted runner only)", after the G05 step: it refuses unless `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is `true` and `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT` is `github-hosted`; makes `nnprobe` plus six random characters with the installer's own marker (read from the script), a random password made with .NET and never printed, the same flags Install uses, and the Users group; runs `-Action Verify -AccountName <name>` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and requires `PASS  the account exists`, the marker PASS line, `password expires: never` (this also tests, on a real machine, that the switch gives an empty PasswordExpires), `account rights:` (the runner is elevated, so the LSA code is compiled and read too), `RESULT:` and exit 1 (no files are installed), and no `cannot be found on this object`; removes the user by exact name in `finally` and fails if it is still there. It is not in the own-runner job. Action pins and permissions are unchanged.
- Linux tests: every `$variable.Property` and `(command ...).Property` is checked against a documented-name table written in the test (a wrong name fails it), dotted reads of optional properties are forbidden, a new variable from `Get-LocalUser`/`Get-ScheduledTask`/`Get-AuthenticodeSignature` must be added to the table; ten deliberate breakages are caught (the installer file's SHA-256 is compared before and after: the breakages are made on a copy in memory). Shape tests pin the new workflow step (hosted-only guard before anything is made, random name, no password printed, removal in `finally`, never in the own-runner job).

**NOT done / what a real Windows run must still prove.** Uninstall has still never run: the manifest reading with `Get-Prop`, the profile removal (`Win32_UserProfile`), `Remove-LocalUser`, the link-safe removal and the folder removal are text-checked only (the manifest validation is new, so a real Install then Uninstall is the proof). The hosted step reaches the account lines only; the Files/access-list/launcher/manifest/worker-task lines of Verify after a real Install are still unproven on any machine (the owner's run will show the next one after the account lines). The throw-away account on a hosted runner is an administrator-run machine: whether a standard user's Verify prints the same is unproven.

### A03b: a real Install, Verify and Uninstall on the disposable hosted runner (branch `card-a03b-hri`; card not flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows)

**Why.** The owner's first real runs found two faults (the hash cmdlet under -WhatIf; a property that does not exist on a user object) that the text tests, the dry run and Verify on an empty machine could not reach. The rest of Verify and ALL of Uninstall have never run on any machine. A GitHub-hosted Windows runner is a disposable elevated virtual machine, so the whole life cycle can be proven there at no risk to the owner.

**Done: the hosted step "Installer real Install, Verify and Uninstall (hosted runner only)"** (workflow lines: one new step `installer_real` and its follow-up `installer_real_cleanup`, inserted between the launchers upload and the last artifact upload; nothing else in the file was edited). Windows PowerShell 5.1. ### A03b: the home case tool bug, CreateProcessW error 203 in every step (2026-11-25, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-home3`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows)

**Evidence.** The hosted run 45739585162 (artifact `windows-appcontainer-hosted`, folder `home/`) ran the tool: the de-elevated child was not elevated, medium integrity, session 2; WinSta0 could be opened with WINSTA_CREATEDESKTOP and with WRITE_DAC; the temporary station entry was written and removed (`entries left 0, same as before`); the private desktop was made. But all 28 program steps in every group failed with `create-process: CreateProcessW failed: 203` (ERROR_ENVVAR_NOT_FOUND), so nothing was learned about any option.

**Cause.** The home steps (`home.rs`, `step_run`) gave the program an environment of only SystemRoot, windir, TEMP, TMP and PATH. Windows refuses to start an AppContainer program with an explicit environment block that has no `LOCALAPPDATA` (it places the container's TEMP and TMP from it, then rewrites them to the container's own folders). The other modes that work (the product's run, the experiment's rounds) send HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP, TMP, PATH, SystemRoot and windir. Sources: several independent projects report this exact error and fix (for example a Microsoft Q&A thread on CreateProcessW 203 with LPAC, and GitHub changes that add LOCALAPPDATA); Microsoft's CreateProcess page does not document it. The rest of the call was checked and matches the working path: the block is UTF-16, each entry and the block are NUL-ended, `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` is set, and the working folder and command line are built as in the product.
ASSUMPTION: LOCALAPPDATA is the cause (the reports say removing only it reproduces 203 and adding it fixes it). If a new run still shows 203, the next suspects are the inherited handle list and the working folder.

**Change.** `homerules::home_env(sys, ws)` builds the step environment: SystemRoot, windir, ComSpec, PATHEXT, LOCALAPPDATA, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, HOME, TEMP, TMP (all user folders point into the step's work folder) and PATH. The environment-block builder moved from `win.rs` to `args.rs` (both builds, UTF-16 via `encode_utf16`, same behaviour) so a Rust test can reach it on Linux. `home.mjs` now prints the real error code and a "TOOL BUG, NOT A POLICY VERDICT" paragraph when every program step of every group failed in `create-process` with the same error, marks such groups `not-measured` (not `fails`), says "No option was measured" when no program started in any step, and says "No option worked" only when programs did start. README (`What a result means...`) says the same.

**Tests.** Rust: the block is UTF-16, sorted case-insensitively, one NUL per entry, double-NUL ended (empty block: two NULs); the home environment holds every required name with the work folder as the only user folder. JS: three new tests (the tool-bug report and its limits, the verdict wording, a source-shape test that the step uses `home_env`, that the block builder is UTF-16 and NUL-ended, that `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` and the block go to `CreateProcessW` and `win.rs` has no second builder). Nine deliberate breakages, each caught and restored by checksum: no LOCALAPPDATA in the step, LOCALAPPDATA dropped from `home_env`, final NUL missing, Unicode flag dropped, sort removed, differing errors still a tool bug, groups still saying `fails`, error code not printed, bytes instead of UTF-16.

**Only Windows can show:** that the hosted run now starts the programs (no 203), and then what each option really does. If any other CreateProcessW error appears in all steps, the summary now says so instead of reading as a verdict.

## K04 standby replication and recovery watermarks (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26): built ahead, card not flipped

Owner guide: docs/nimblenewt/standby-recovery.md. The card is built ahead of its dependency root (Y03) and its status is left alone.

**What exists.**
- `storage/postgres/replication.ts`: only ordinary SQL on ordinary connections. `probeNode` (role, writable or not, system identifier, write-ahead-log position, received position, last replay time), `readStandbyLinks` and `measureLag` (bytes not yet on the standby's disk, bytes on disk but not applied, flush and replay lag from the primary, sync state), `promoteStandby` (`pg_promote`, refuses a node that is not a standby), `findWritablePrimary` (first node that is writable, with what was found at each, an unreachable node named), `readControllerState` (reads the controller tables on a standby without writing), `synchronousSettingsText` (text for the operator; nothing is changed).
- `recovery/` (new): `manifest.ts` (the recovery manifest folder: counters, every record with its revision, every artifact file; the manifest file is written last, whole or absent, own checksum plus a checksum for each sidecar), `assess.ts` (the comparison of a node with a manifest), `promotion.ts` (`promoteDatabase`, the only way in: refuses with reasons and changes nothing, or promotes the database and says `controller: "not_promoted"`), `watermarks.ts` (`measureLoss`), `capability.ts` (optional standby configuration, `verifyStandbyInstallation`), `restored.ts` (`reportRestoredStore`: the SQLite recovery path, a restored backup measured against the manifest), `source.ts` (read access over any store's snapshot). Exported as `recovery` from the package index.
- `storage/postgres/testing/replica.ts`: a real PostgreSQL primary and a real streaming standby, both disposable embedded servers on loopback. The standby is a copy of the stopped primary's folder started with `standby.signal` (the embedded binaries have no `pg_basebackup`), so it is PostgreSQL's own physical streaming replication. The documented shared test server at /srv/code/test-postgres was not used: its role cannot create replication slots and it is one server; nothing of it was touched.

**Acceptance, clause by clause.**
- Distinguish database failover from controller promotion: `promoteDatabase` returns `database: "promoted"`, `controller: "not_promoted"`; the test reopens the store on the promoted node and finds the epoch and holder unchanged, then takes the epoch as a separate step and sees the old epoch refused (`stale_epoch`).
- Configured synchronous and asynchronous loss: real pair. Asynchronous: the standby is stopped, three more commits are acknowledged, the primary is crashed, the standby is promoted; all three are lost, counted, with a loss window in milliseconds. Synchronous: every acknowledged commit survives (lost 0); a commit waiting for the stopped standby is cut and is `uncertain_commit`; after promotion it is absent and sending it again by operation ID admits it once (a second send is a replay). Also: with the standby stopped a synchronous commit is not answered and completes when it returns.
- Writable-primary reconnection: `findWritablePrimary([old, standby])` skips the dead node, picks the promoted one, and a store reopened there works; the old handle's calls fail, not hang. A store opened on a standby reads but a write fails (`unavailable`, "cannot set transaction read-write mode during recovery").
- No custom replication protocol: a source scan of the replication and recovery code (no replication connection, no protocol code, no `START_REPLICATION`, no WAL copy tool, no raw sockets) and the one role-changing call is `pg_promote`.
- Lag and loss window: lag read from the primary (zero when caught up; with replay paused the standby shows flushed but unreplayed bytes; a stopped standby shows no link); the loss window comes from acknowledged writes against survivors.
- Missing blobs or workflow state prevent promotion: real standby, manifest from the primary. A file missing on the standby host, a file with the right name and wrong bytes, a record the standby never received, counters behind: each refused, the standby still in recovery afterwards. With the file present the promotion goes through.
- Backups independently restorable: a backup made beside the standby verifies and restores into the reference store and SQLite after both servers are stopped; the backup folder holds nothing of the replication or the manifest.

**Tests.** `recovery/recovery.test.ts` (17 after the first review, the manifest, comparison and restored-backup report on all four backends, tamper cases, loss measurement, config, the order of every refusal with the steps stood in for, the protocol scan) and `storage/postgres/standby.test.ts` (8, real pair).

The capability is a library the recovery endpoint will use. Writing the manifest on a schedule and shipping it with the artifact files to the standby host is not scheduled by anything yet.
- The standby here is on the same machine over loopback. A real network (latency, a partition that is neither up nor down, a standby on another host with its own disk and clock, a slot or archive setup, TLS, a pooler) is not shown. Replay lag in milliseconds is read from PostgreSQL's own sampling and is not asserted to a value.
- Promotion does not fence the old primary: it only refuses when the old primary's address is given and it still answers and is not in recovery (writable, or read-only only by default). Fencing is K05. An unreachable but running old primary (a partition) is not detected here; the result's notes say the old primary did not answer.
- A removed record or blob after the manifest was written shows as missing and blocks (by design; write a new manifest after retention).
ASSUMPTION: the manifest covers every record (name and revision) and every artifact blob; "workflow state" is read as the controller's records and counters, because the controller keeps all workflow state as records.
ASSUMPTION: no override for a refused promotion exists in K04; an owner choice to accept a known loss belongs to K05's consent flow.
ASSUMPTION: `PostgresStorage.open` on a standby is left as it is (it opens read-only usable); choosing the node is `findWritablePrimary`'s job.

### K04 first review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-26)

Read the code against each acceptance clause and ran it. Fixed:
- **Medium: the public `promoteDatabase` options carried a `steps` field** (probe, state, promote, writable-primary) that a caller could set to replace any check, so passing an argument could get past a refusal. It is gone: `promoteDatabase(options)` always uses the real steps; the tests use `promoteDatabaseWith(options, steps)` from `recovery/promotion.ts`, which the recovery index and the package exports do not offer.
- **Medium: an old primary that answers but is read-only only by default was treated as safe.** `findWritablePrimary` calls it `read_only`, and the promotion went ahead, but `default_transaction_read_only` does not stop a session that asks for read-write (the controller's store does), so that would have left two primaries. The promotion now probes the old primary itself and refuses any old primary that answers and is not in recovery; a node of another cluster is still refused. An old primary that does not answer now adds a note (it may be running behind a partition) instead of nothing.
- **Medium (test strength): the real-pair case "a file with the right name and the wrong bytes" used an empty store,** so it was a second missing-file case. It now writes wrong bytes of the right size at the blob's path and asserts `blob_corrupt`.
- **Low: `replayWaitMs` was not checked** (NaN made the replay wait never end, since no time is later than NaN). Now whole milliseconds from 0 to 600000, else refused. A standby that stops answering, or is promoted by something else, during the wait now gives a refusal instead of a stray error.
- **Low: `readRecoveryManifest` did not check field shapes.** The self-checksum shows only that the text is unchanged, so a manifest with no `watermark` that still matched its checksum skipped the epoch and counter checks, because a comparison with undefined is false. Now the watermark, both sidecar entries (file name must be the fixed name), every line of both sidecars and the row counts are checked, else `RecoveryManifestBad`.
- **Low: the manifest swap order and its comment.** The comment said an existing manifest is "replaced only when the new one is whole", but the old files were deleted before the new ones were put in. The swap now removes `manifest.json` first and puts the new one in last (a crash leaves no manifest, refused, never a mix), and the comment and owner guide say so.
- **Low: `readControllerState`'s `pageSize` went into the SQL text unchecked.** Now a whole number from 1 to 10000.
- **Low (harness): nodes started by `pg_ctl` are daemons.** A test that times out (its `finally` never runs) left them running until the next run's sweep, and the sweep does not run on Windows. Every node still running is now stopped (immediate) when the process exits.
- **Test added on the real pair:** with replay paused (received ahead of replayed), `promoteDatabase` is refused and the node stays a standby.
- **Guide:** a "What is not here yet" section (no chat, status or API reach until K05, no automatic failover, one machine over loopback only) and the old-primary and manifest-swap rules as they now work.

Checked and found right: the one role-changing call is `pg_promote`, and `promoteStandby` refuses a node that is not in recovery. The order is manifest, standby, old primary, replay, comparison, and only then promote. The epoch and holder are unchanged after a promotion, and the old epoch is `stale_epoch` once a new one is taken. Uncertain commits on the real synchronous pair are resolved once by operation ID. Schema names are checked by pattern and quoted. No password appears in any probe, reconnection or refusal message: tried with a refused port, a bad port, a malformed host and an unknown host. Tombstones are left out of the manifest. Backups are untouched by the manifest and replication, and still restore on their own. Nothing in K04 is an owner control, so nothing needs chat reach yet (K05 owns the recovery chat and endpoint). No new dependency. api-v1.md is unchanged.

Fourteen deliberate breakages were each caught by a failing test, and each file was restored and its checksum confirmed: a manifest read failure ignored, a read-only old primary accepted, the old primary's system identifier not compared, the replay wait skipped, comparison problems ignored, the epoch not compared, an older revision accepted, the manifest self-checksum skipped, the watermark shape not checked, artifact blobs not listed, the restored report always complete, lag reading the replay position as the flush position, the low-level promote accepting a primary, a standby taken as writable for reconnection.

Still open, not changed here: `freePort` closes its probe socket before the server binds, so another process could take the port in between (the start would then fail loudly, not silently). In the synchronous test, "lost 0" alone would also hold for a fast asynchronous pair; the synchronous guarantee is shown by the commit that waits (`SyncRep`) and by `uncertain_commit` when the primary is cut during that wait. A standby restarted with no primary reports no received position, so replay of its local WAL is not waited for. That only makes the check stricter (it reads less than the promotion will hold), never looser.

### A03b: the home desktop in the product launcher (2026-11-26, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-homeprod`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; no workflow dispatched; nothing run on Windows)

**What is done.** The product launcher (`native/nn-launcher`) now has a second window-object mode for the common one-account PC. When the NAMED private window station is refused with error 5 and the launcher is NOT elevated, it makes ONE private desktop `nn-hd-<64 random bits>` on the user's own interactive window station `WinSta0` (`privdesk.rs`, `create_home`), created with its final protected access list (the same descriptor, mask and read-back allow list as the private desktop), with nothing written to WinSta0's access list, no station switch, no station handle closed, `lpDesktop` `WinSta0\nn-hd-<hex>`. The rule that chooses (`winobj::try_home_desktop`), the station rule (`may_make_home_desktop`: visible interactive `WinSta0` only; a service's station fails closed), the name, the mode names and "a home run needs `--ui-limits`" (`home_needs_ui_limits`) are pure functions with Rust tests on Linux. The elevated named-station path is byte-for-byte the same code. There is no fallback to the inherited desktop: a failed home desktop is a typed failure (stage `grant`, "window objects: ...") and nothing starts. The mode is reported: the launcher's line has `windowStation` `private` or `home-desktop` (set when the objects were made or refused, so an early failure claims neither), `privateStationError` (the named station's refusal when the home desktop was used) and `windowObjects.mode`. `info` and `check` ask the same question, so `info` reports `windowStation:"home-desktop"`, `windowStationOk:true` on success. TypeScript: `WINDOW_STATION_MODES`, `isWindowStationMode`, `privateStationError` in the plan parser; health refuses a mode it does not know and gives a note for the home desktop; a run with an unknown mode is a typed `launcher` failure; the run record keeps `windowStation`. Hosted workflow: the de-elevated cross-check step now prints the mode and a notice or a warning (a report, not a gate; the step still ends with `exit 0`).

**The exposure, stated plainly.** The home desktop closes what belongs to the desktop (windows, foreground, cursor, screen pixel; measured). It does NOT close the station's clipboard and atom table: the clipboard open succeeded (contents never read) and a global atom add worked; a keyboard hook is installable on the container's own desktop only. The job's clipboard limits did not block the open in the one measured run. Reasoning and the table: plan 12.5.1.

- ASSUMPTION: the home desktop is tried only for a NON-elevated launcher (`elevated` from the token) refused with error 5. An elevated launcher that was refused stays a failure, so the measured elevated paths cannot change mode by accident.
- ASSUMPTION: the home desktop is made only on a visible interactive `WinSta0`. The evidence is from signed-in sessions; a non-elevated launcher in a service's station fails closed (not measured).
- ASSUMPTION: a home run without `--ui-limits` is refused by the launcher (the backend always passes it); the named-station path keeps accepting what it accepted.
- Owner decision (2026-11-26, "Let's require someone to be logged in"): the SUPPORTED Windows configuration is the worker running as the signed-in user, non-elevated, in the home desktop mode; the elevated named-station mode is an optional stronger path. Windows work stops when nobody is signed in; logout and reboot are handled by the existing suspend and resume paths, TO BE VERIFIED on Windows, not proven. An unattended Session-0 service identity is not a requirement. Generated files and the task-plan acceptance text were not edited here: the lead narrows G05/A03b through the generator.
- Owner decision (2026-11-26, "The clipboard is fine"): the shared clipboard is an ACCEPTED exposure of the home desktop mode, recorded as a decision, not an open item; no separate mitigation is built.
- A stale contract test (the experiment feature list in `Cargo.toml`) was already out of date on main; it now pins the current list.

### A03b home desktop in the product: first review (2026-11-26, Claude agent; branch `card-a03b-homeprod`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; nothing run on Windows)

**Problems found and fixed.** (1) Medium-low: the mode choice used `is_elevated()`, which reads "could not query the token" as "not elevated", so a launcher of unknown elevation that was refused the named station with error 5 would have taken the home desktop. The choice now uses `elevation()` (`Option<bool>`; None when the token cannot be opened or queried) and `try_home_desktop` needs `Some(false)`. The JSON line's `elevated` is unchanged (`is_elevated()` is `elevation() == Some(true)`, the same value as before). (2) Low: the home desktop's station rule accepted any visible WinSta0, including session 0's (the services' session, no signed-in user; never measured, and outside the owner's "someone signed in" configuration). `may_make_home_desktop` now also takes the session id and refuses session 0 and an unreadable session. (3) Low: the backend's health note said "each run gets a private window station and desktop" when `info` named no mode at all; that note is now given only for `windowStation:"private"`, and a launcher that names no mode gets a note saying the mode is not known.

**Checked and found right.** An elevated launcher never reaches the home desktop; only the refusal of CreateWindowStationW itself (error 5) can lead there (errors before that call, and later errors of the named desktop, leave the station error 0); the inherited desktop is never used (lpDesktop is always the made one, and `run_inner` refuses a run without it); the home desktop is created with the protected creation descriptor (own user, SYSTEM, the container's one entry with mask 131583), never written afterwards and read back with the same allow list; its handle is created non-inheritable and the child's handle list holds only the three standard handles; on every error after creation `Drop` closes it; on a run it is closed after `run_inner` returns, i.e. after the job handle (kill-on-close) was dropped; the process's own station handle is neither switched nor closed. The station name is read as UTF-16 up to the first NUL and compared case-insensitively with `WinSta0`; USEROBJECTFLAGS is 12 bytes with dwFlags third. The elevated workflow gates still require `windowStation:"private"`; the de-elevated cross-check runs under `set +e`, `continue-on-error: true` and ends with `exit 0`. The product's `create_home` matches the experiment's measured `prepare_home` creation (same descriptor, rights and read-back), with the visible-flag and session checks added.

**Left as they are (noted).** The experiment build's `--desktop private` also falls back to the home desktop when run non-elevated (its line then says `home-desktop`); no current experiment step runs `private` non-elevated. The standard-account probe (`native/install/Probe-NimbleNewtWorker.ps1`) treats only `windowStation:"private"` as OK; a home-desktop success would read as "(e) info failed elsewhere", but its S4U task runs on a service station, which the home desktop refuses, so it reports "(b)" as before. The raw output of the owner's home-probe run is not stored in the repository, so the numbers in plan 12.5.1's table (495/28 windows, 0x20327, 0xf00ff) could not be checked against the source here; the clipboard statements agree with the recorded owner decision. The home desktop is refused without `--ui-limits` only after it was made (it is closed again and nothing starts).

**Tests.** Rust: unknown elevation does not lead to the home desktop; session 0 and an unreadable session are refused; a station name with a trailing NUL or a desktop path is not WinSta0. TypeScript: the contract pins `elevation()` (three-valued, None on both failures) and the session check before CreateDesktopW; health with no mode named claims no mode. Fifteen deliberate breakages, each caught and restored by checksum: home desktop for an elevated launcher, unknown elevation as not elevated, any error leading to the home desktop, session 0 accepted, WSF_VISIBLE unchecked, a home run without UI limits, default descriptor at creation, no read-back, run without the UI-limit rule, two-valued elevation in the run, an unreadable token read as not elevated, health claiming `private` with no mode, an unknown mode accepted for a run, `inherit` added to the mode list, health accepting an unknown mode.

**Only Windows can show:** everything about the real calls: that the product's `info` and a full `run` work on the owner's PC in this mode, that TokenElevation reads `false` there, that `ProcessIdToSessionId` gives a non-zero session, and the open points listed in the slice entry above.


### A03b home desktop in the product: second review (2026-11-26, Claude agent, clean context; branch `card-a03b-homeprod2` from `card-a03b-homeprod`; card NOT flipped; not pushed; nothing run on Windows)

**Problems found and fixed.** (1) Low-medium (documentation honesty): the container's desktop mask 131583 was never decoded in the documents. It is 0x201FF, READ_CONTROL plus all nine `DESKTOP_*` rights, including `SWITCHDESKTOP`, `HOOKCONTROL` and both journal rights (it is not 0x2013F). On the home desktop `SWITCHDESKTOP` matters because the desktop is on the visible WinSta0; what stops `SwitchDesktop` is only the job's `JOB_OBJECT_UILIMIT_DESKTOP` (documented, not measured). Plan 12.5.1 and the README now say so; a Rust test pins the decoding, and the job's UI-limit word is a named constant (`winobj::JOB_UI_LIMITS`) with a test that it holds the desktop bit. The mask was NOT narrowed: the product's set is the set the experiment measured, and changing it needs a Windows run. (2) Low: after a timeout or leftover processes the launcher called TerminateJobObject (which returns before the processes are gone) and closed the window objects at once; the comment said the job "has ended the child by then". It now waits up to 5 s for the job to be empty (`winobj::wait_job_empty`, bounded, unit tested) and reports `jobProcessesAtEnd`; the comments and documents say that `windowObjects.closed` is about the launcher's handle (CloseDesktop does not fail because another process uses the desktop; the desktop goes with its last user). (3) Low: CreateDesktopW OPENS a desktop whose name exists (documented) and does not document ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS; the code and documents now say the refusal rests on that code AND the read-back. (4) Low: the health reason for a failed home desktop said "could not make a private window station and desktop"; it now names the home desktop and carries both refusals. (5) Documentation: the figures of 12.5.1 (495/28 windows, 0x20327, 0xf00ff, 14 desktop steps) now say they come from the owner's `home-probe` output pasted into the working session on 2026-11-26, not stored in the repository; the two masks are decoded.

**Checked and found right.** Error and early-return paths of `create`, `create_named` and `create_home`: every handle is set into the struct before a later check and closed once by `Drop` (`close` is idempotent); the home path never holds or closes the process station handle; a killed launcher leaves no window object (handles close with the process, kill-on-close is always on in the product) and writes no access list anywhere; the profile it leaves is the existing sweep's case. The launcher's own user is not locked out (it gets DESKTOP_FULL, a superset of the container's mask; CreateDesktop's own requirements, CREATEWINDOW and READOBJECTS/WRITEOBJECTS with READ_CONTROL, hold). Administrators and OWNER RIGHTS are tolerated by the read-back but never created; for a non-elevated token Administrators is deny-only and the owner is the same user, and neither can admit the container. The container's SID exists before the desktop (the per-run profile is made first), and the read-back checks every entry. JSON: an older launcher's line parses (no new required field), an unknown mode is refused by health and fails a run, `jobProcessesAtEnd` is additive. The hosted cross-check is `set +e`, `continue-on-error: true`, `exit 0`, and prints only the redacted line and the mode and error fields.

**Tests.** Rust: mask decode, UI-limit word, the bounded job wait. TypeScript contract: the wait comes after leftovers are ended and before the objects are closed; the UI-limit word is the constant; a home run without the limits is refused. Backend: the failed-home-desktop health reason. Documents: provenance, decode, the documented-only status of the switch limit. Thirteen deliberate breakages, each caught and restored by sha256 (desktop bit dropped from the UI limits, WRITE_DAC added to the container mask, the wait waiting on an unreadable count, the wait one poll too long, no wait, the literal UI word, objects not closed after the run, a home run without the limits, the health reason for the home desktop, the dropped named-station refusal, the plan's provenance removed, the switch limit claimed as measured, the README's decode removed).

**Only Windows can show:** that the product's `info` reports `home-desktop` with `windowStationOk:true` (which also shows that CloseDesktop succeeds on the new desktop's handle), that a product `run` starts cmd, hostname and node there, that `JOB_OBJECT_UILIMIT_DESKTOP` stops `SwitchDesktop` on WinSta0, and what `jobProcessesAtEnd` reads after a timeout.
