### C06 follow-up: no retry without the isolation setting (2026-11-26, Claude agent; branch `card-c06-saltfix`; fix in 98328a28; card not flipped; not pushed; no server contacted)

- **The finding (G10 close, first review).** When an endpoint refused a cache setting, `CacheAdapter.#call` sent the same messages again with no cache settings. It did this for every project, including one that requires isolation. On vLLM, isolation is `request-salt`, so that retry dropped `cache_salt`, the thing that keeps the project apart. The plain call could then reuse another project's cached prefix, or leave this project's prefix shared.
- **What changed.** If the server refuses a cache setting and the project requires isolation (`CacheContext.isolationRequired`), the adapter no longer retries. It returns the refusal with the server's status. The error message is in plain words: "The server refused the setting that keeps this project's cache apart from other projects (…). This project requires isolation, so the call was not sent again without it. To run it, use another route (a server that accepts the setting, or one of the project's own), or, if the project does not need to be kept apart, turn off its isolation requirement where the controller is configured." (wording as corrected by the first review below) The same text goes in three places: the body's `error.message`, the new `CallResult.isolationRefused` (with the server's own text, the status and the settings the refused call carried) and the result's `skipped` list, which is where the adapter already records what was left out. The outcome is `unknown`. Projects that do not require isolation keep today's retry. Through `piFetch`, Pi is answered with this plain-words error instead of the server's own text (`isolationRefusedMessage` is exported).
- **Other places with the same pattern.** The rule is on the isolation requirement, not on the backend, so it covers every profile that sends something to keep an isolated project apart. **llama.cpp without slots:** an isolated call carries `cache_prompt: false`. A plain retry would leave that field out, and llama-server then reuses (its default), so this was the same flaw. **llama.cpp with slots:** a refused `cache_prompt` was already returned as an error, and it now carries the plain-words record too. **Strata:** a plain retry would drop `strata_checkpoint: false`. **Claude, OpenAI, Radiance and generic** send an isolated project no cache setting at all, so nothing can be refused and nothing changes. C06e is not weakened: `hostPromptCacheOff`, erase-or-`cache_prompt: false` on a project boundary and the slot holders are untouched, and the slotted rule (a refused `cache_prompt` is never retried) is unchanged. No other code retries without a cache field. The `g10-engines-live*` probes are hand-run measurements, not production calls. vLLM calls made by the dispatcher are observed only, not routed through the adapter, so there Pi's own request with the salt is what is sent, and there is no retry.
- **Tests.** In `adapter.test.ts`, one new test uses the real `CacheAdapter` against scripted servers. vLLM refusing `cache_salt` (a 400, and a FastAPI-style 422): the isolated project gets the error, and the server sees exactly one body, which carries the salt. A non-cache 400 comes back as it is. A project without isolation (unset or false) is still retried. The same checks run for llama.cpp without slots and with slots (`cache_prompt: false` refused) and for Strata (`strata_checkpoint: false` refused; a non-isolated pinned call is still retried). Claude with isolation required sends nothing, so a 400 mentioning `cache_control` is returned as it is. In `pi-fetch.test.ts`, one new test: an isolated project on a slotted llama.cpp gets the plain-words 400, and exactly one call with `cache_prompt: false` is sent. 11 deliberate breakages were applied to the built files, and each failed at least one test before being restored by sha256: never decline, decline any error, decline every project, decline only on request-salt backends, the server's body kept, a retry sent after declining, the message missing from `skipped`, the kept settings empty, the message losing "not sent again without it", the record not returned, and Pi given the server's text.
- **Not done.** No new owner control. (Corrected by the first review: there is no existing owner control for a project's isolation requirement either; it is the composer's `dispatch.cache.isolationRequired` hook, which no production code supplies yet, so the message now says "where the controller is configured" rather than naming an owner action.) The refusal is recorded on the call's result. No separate activity entry was added, because the dispatcher records no other adapter result in an activity entry either.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the rule applies to every backend's refused isolation setting, not only vLLM's `cache_salt`, because a plain retry drops the protection the same way on llama.cpp and Strata.
- **First review and fixes (2026-11-26, Claude agent, Opus 5.5; not pushed; card not flipped; no server contacted).** (1) **Completeness.** Every place in `packages/`, `scripts/`, `benchmarks/`, `experiments/` and `prototypes/` that sends a cache field was listed (`cache_salt`, `cache_prompt`, `id_slot`, `strata_checkpoint`, `strata_prefix`, `cache_control`, `prompt_cache_key`, `session_id`, slot actions). The only code that sends a call again without a cache field after a failure is `CacheAdapter.#call`, now guarded. `profileFor`'s isolation wrapper and `piCachePolicy` drop fields before the first send (by design, for isolation). The pi-adapter's `cache-shaping.ts` only applies the policy's payload hook and never retries. Pi's own retry (pi-ai `isRetryableAssistantError`) restarts a turn only on transient-error words (overloaded, rate limit, 5xx, network); the plain-words message contains none of them, and its SDKs do not retry 400 or 422, so exactly one call reaches the server. The G10 benches (`g10-engines-live.ts` "retry-without-setting", `g10-radiance-*`, `g10-hermes-route.ts`) are hand-run probes with no project and no isolation context. In the dispatcher, only a slotted llama.cpp with shared state goes through the adapter; vLLM, Strata and unslotted llama.cpp calls are observed, which means they are sent once as Pi built them (with the salt), and Pi then gets the server's own error, not the plain words (low, stated). (2) **Detection.** A refusal is a 400 or 422 whose text (message plus FastAPI `detail`) names one of the profile's fields as a whole word, and only when the call carried settings. An unrelated 400 that happens to name the field would block the isolated project with this message, and the server's own text is kept beside it (`error.server`, `reason`). **Fixed (low):** a given `isolationRequired` hook that answered undefined or null (a JavaScript caller, or a project it does not know) counted as not required; now any answer other than `false` counts as required, and a hook that throws fails the attempt. With no hook at all, no project requires isolation, as C06 lead decision (1) says; this was not changed, because isolation by default would turn reuse off for every project on llama.cpp, Radiance, Strata, OpenAI and Claude. That is a product choice, recorded here for the lead. (3) **Text.** **Fixed (low):** the message named an owner action ("mark the project as not requiring isolation") that has no control. **Fixed (low):** the server's quoted text was already redacted and limited to 300 characters. Control, line-separator and direction-changing characters are now made single spaces (in `failureMessage`, so fallback and slot reasons get the same treatment). Host names in the server's text are not removed by `redactText`. The existing non-isolation error path already gives Pi the server's whole text, so this is not a new exposure. **Fixed (low):** `skipped` was built with a nested condition that would have dropped the refusal message whenever the host-cache caveat applied (unreachable today); both are now added independently. (4) **Tests.** `cache.test.ts` +1: the hook fails closed, both synchronous and promised; false shares; a throwing hook rejects; with no hook a project shares. `adapter.test.ts`: the new wording, `error.server`, and a server text with NUL, CR/LF, U+202E and U+2028 that comes back as one plain line of 300 characters. 12 deliberate breakages of the built files, each caught and restored by sha256, on Node 22 and Node 24: the flag never honoured; a hook's undefined treated as not required; the hook's answer never carried; 422 not a refusal; the message losing "not sent again"; an isolated slotted llama.cpp retried plain (with the slotted `cache_prompt` guard removed); Strata isolated retried; vLLM isolated retried; pi-fetch giving Pi the server's text; the character stripping removed; the message missing from `skipped`; and the non-isolated plain retry removed (caught by the `g10-radiance-live` integration test). Interpreter prompt unchanged; `api-v1.md` unchanged.

## Q03 claims slice: capability claims checked against a capability register and the document's own text; support guidance and promotional assets as their own kinds (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26)

Branch `card-q03-claims` off origin/main `fda74a46`. Card status is NOT changed (Q03 stays planned). This answers the flip audit's finding on the clause "no unsupported marketing capability claims": before this slice nothing read a document's text, the claims were only what the recorder listed, and support guidance and promotional assets were obligations with an audience rather than their own kinds.

Plain words first. Every claim a document makes now names a capability from the project's **capability register**, and the register says whether that capability is `supported`, `experimental` or `unsupported`. The register starts with the controller's own labels, taken from the code that states them (Claude and Strata prompt caching are experimental, from `cacheMaturityOf`, the same function the cache profiles use; an unattended Windows worker is unsupported, by the owner's decision of 2026-11-26 that Windows needs a signed-in user). The owner or a director agent can rate a capability or add one. When a document is verified, the controller also reads the document change's text, when the change names an artifact this controller stores. It splits the text into sentences and looks for the names of experimental or unsupported capabilities. A sentence that names one without a label in the same sentence is flagged; for an experimental capability the label is "experimental", "not measured", "beta" and similar, or a negation, and for an unsupported one only a negation counts. Any flag refuses the verification. The refusal is kept on the record, shown first in the owner's docs view with each flag's rule and the quoted sentence. The scan does not try to understand prose: it matches known names, and the rule for every flag is stated.

- **What is built.**
  - `submissions/doc-claims.ts` (pure): the built-in register, `effectiveRegister` (a project entry with the same ID replaces a built-in one, as a recorded decision), `checkDeclared` (the record's claims), `scanText` (the text), `cleanText`, and `artifactDocumentReader`. The cleaning: NFKC; zero-width characters and soft hyphens removed, so a name cannot be hidden by splitting it; direction marks and overrides removed; other control characters turned into spaces; HTML tags and Markdown marks turned into spaces; then the text is redacted, cut on whole characters (200) and JSON-quoted in the owner's line. Six rules, each with a sentence the owner reads: `claim_without_capability`, `unknown_capability`, `unsupported_capability_claimed`, `experimental_claim_unlabelled`, `unsupported_mention`, `experimental_mention_unlabelled`. Sentences end at `.`, `!`, `?` followed by a space, or at a line break, so each bullet line is its own sentence. Names match case-insensitively as whole words, with spaces, hyphens or nothing between their words. "no" or "without" counts as a negation only directly before the name (at most two words between), so "There is no unattended Windows service" passes and "No setup needed. Claude caching saves money" is flagged. The words of a name are blanked before the label search, so a name such as "nobody signed in" is not its own negation.
  - The reader reads only the artifact the document change recorded: the digest must be `sha256:` plus the artifact's manifest digest (as the tool bridge records it), and the artifact must belong to the same project. Text files are chosen by name, read in path order, at most 50 files, 256 KiB each and 1 MiB in all, and decoded as strict UTF-8. Anything else is listed as skipped and never guessed at. A damaged blob is the artifact service's `integrity` error. It is wired in `api/start.ts` only when the controller has an artifact store.
  - `DocObligationService`:
    - `record`: every claim now needs a `capabilityId` the register knows. A new `kind`: `document` (the default; older records count as this), `support_guidance` (audience `support`) or `promotional_asset` (audience `promotional`). The last two need a `channel`, and a promotional asset has a `mediaType` (`text` by default). A change of kind or media type makes the record unverified again, like a change of claims.
    - `verify`: runs the claim check after the existing QA and evidence checks. When a check flags something, `verified: false` is returned with the flags; the record keeps `claimCheck` (when, who, which document change, whether the text was read, at most 20 flags plus a total), its state is unchanged and nothing is settled. A replay is answered from the command's own audit entry. A passing verification keeps the maturity of every capability the document claimed or named (`verification.claims`). A promotional text asset cannot be verified until its text has been read.
    - `setCapability` and `capabilities` are new. Only the owner or a director may rate a capability; the docs agent that writes the claims may not. A lower rating flags documents that were verified while the capability was rated higher, with the new reason `capability_changed` and one update task per capability for the document's keeper. Asking again finishes the flagging and repeats nothing.
    - `release` now counts flagged documents by kind (`byKind`) as well as by audience.
  - State API: `doc.capability.set` and `doc.capability.list` are new. `doc.obligation.record` takes `kind`, `channel`, `mediaType` and `claims[].capabilityId`. `doc.obligation.verify` returns `verified`, `scanned` and `flags`, plus `shown` lines when refused, so the chat says why. `api-v1.md` was regenerated.
  - Owner chat: `doc.capability.set` is a chat command and is always shown first. The proposal says what the capability is rated now and whether that is the controller's own label, how many kept documents claim or name it, and what follows (a lower rating: those verified under the higher rating go stale with update tasks; a higher one: documents may claim it, and one refused can be verified again). The capability ID, maturity, kind and media type come from views or fixed lists (`DOC_EXEMPT`); a name, note or channel must be in the owner's own words. The `docs` view lists documents refused for their claims first ("CLAIMS REFUSED ... "), labels each kind (promotional asset with its medium and channel, support guidance with its channel), shows each claim's capability, and ends with a line for the capability register (maturity, who set it or that it is the controller's own label, and how many documents). The interpreter prompt describes the register, the kinds, `doc.capability.set` and the refusal in a few sentences; nearby wording was shortened to make room. The prompt is 155,905 characters, under the 156,560 ceiling; `SIZE` was not moved.
- **Tests.** New: `submissions/doc-claims.test.ts` (pure: the built-in labels, the scan rules and their negations and labels, hostile text, the declared-claim rules, the reader's bounds and refusals). The hostile text covers zero-width-split names, U+202E overrides, NUL and BEL, an injected instruction, HTML and script tags, a secret-shaped token, an over-long sentence, and a cut beside a surrogate pair; the same input gives the same flags in the same order. New: `submissions/doc-claims-service.test.ts` on all four backends (reference, SQLite, SQLite on a worker thread, PostgreSQL). It covers who may rate, the kinds and their fields, a promotional text that cannot be verified without its text, a refusal kept and replayed with the same flags, a labelled text verifying, an image checked on its declared claims only, a downgrade flagging the two verified documents with assigned update tasks and the repeat flagging nothing, a rating back up flagging nothing, a declared claim refused after a downgrade, and a release counted by kind. Changed: `submissions/doc-obligations.test.ts` and `doc-auto-checks.test.ts` (claims name a capability, the register entry is set, a document text port), and `api/start-docs.test.ts`. The running controller now stores real artifacts for every document change, so the landing page's text is read. Dora's change naming Claude caching with a U+202E override is refused; the owner's docs view, asked by chat, shows the refusal first with the cleaned sentence and ends with the register. The owner rates Claude caching supported by chat, sees the consequence on the proposal, a made-up name is refused, and after applying, the same change verifies.
- **Deliberate breakages.** 15 changes to the built files, each run against the targeted test files and restored byte for byte (checked by sha256), on Node 22 and Node 24. Each one alone: experimental labels ignored; zero-width characters kept; direction marks kept; "no" before a name not counted; an experimental label accepted for an unsupported capability; an unsupported declared claim not flagged; the reader not checking the digest; `verify` ignoring the flags; a promotional text no longer needing its text read; the docs role allowed to rate; a rating back up flagging documents; an unknown capability recorded; support guidance for any audience; a replay forgetting the refusal; the docs view hiding the refusal. All 15 were caught. The support-audience one was caught only after a test for it was added: the first run found that gap.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a claim must name a capability ID (the clause says a claim references a capability the record marks supported), and the register is per project, starting from the controller's own labels. Claims recorded before this slice have no ID; they are flagged `claim_without_capability` the next time the document is verified, so the keeper re-records them. A document verified earlier stays verified. Reversible: making `capabilityId` optional again restores the old rule.
- **ASSUMPTION:** "their own record kinds" is a `kind` on the one obligation record (`document`, `support_guidance`, `promotional_asset`, each with owner, audience, version, implementing tasks, state, and a channel or media type where it applies), not three storage kinds. Every existing check (impact, release, landing, retire, notices, views) reads the one index, so all three are flagged alike with no second copy of that logic. Reversible: a later split can move records by kind.
- **ASSUMPTION:** only the owner or a director agent rates capabilities, not the docs role, so the agent writing a claim cannot rate it. Nothing waits on Rob: an owner who prefers otherwise can rate by chat.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the built-in entries are the three the code and the owner's decisions state today: Claude and Strata prompt caching (experimental, from `cacheMaturityOf`; they become supported by themselves if that function ever reports them measured), and the unattended Windows worker (unsupported, from the 2026-11-26 decision). Other maturity labels in the code (provider kinds marked "unmeasured", the roadmap's planned cards) were not turned into entries. Their names are too general to scan for without many false flags ("OpenAI-compatible"), and a planned card is not a user-facing capability. A project adds what it needs.
- **ASSUMPTION:** "nearby" means the same sentence; a label in the next sentence does not count. This is conservative and easy to explain. A false flag is cleared by writing the label into the sentence, or by the owner rating the capability; a missed claim needs wording the name list does not cover.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a promotional asset of text (the default) cannot be verified until its text is read, because the clause is about marketing. User and developer documents and support guidance are scanned when their text can be read, and are checked on their declared claims when it cannot (the refusal and the view say whether the text was read). A controller with no artifact store therefore cannot verify a promotional text; that is said in the refusal.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a refusal for claims is a write (the record keeps `claimCheck`, and its revision moves), not an error. The owner sees it in the docs view without asking again, and the chat result says "Not verified" with up to five flags.
- **Not done:**
  - Images, video and audio are not read: their declared claims are all that is checked.
  - Formats other than plain text, Markdown and HTML (PDF, Office files) are skipped by name.
  - Synonyms and paraphrases that are not in a capability's names are not found ("cache with Anthropic's models"). A capability's `names` list is the only vocabulary.
  - Negation is simple (since the first review: it must stand within 8 words of the name, and "not just/only/merely/simply" is no denial; a negation that far away still lets a sentence through, and one 9 words away does not count).
  - The scan runs only when a document is verified. A text changed later and never re-verified is not scanned, and the impact and release checks do not read text.
  - A capability rated lower flags only documents verified under the higher rating; an unverified document that names it is caught when it is verified.
  - Taking a project entry away, to fall back to the built-in label, is not a control: rate it again instead.
  - The chat verify path (`doc.obligation.verify` by chat on a verified document) still needs the document change named, as before.
  - The rest of Q03's open list: documents gating a release or a task's `done`, bridge tools for the docs agent, the D01 guide's documentation step, older-code QA evidence.
- **Runs** (after `npx tsc --build --force`, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` and the offline guard, on Node 22.23.0 and Node 24.21.0, the same counts on both): submissions and status in full, 719 of 719; chat in full plus `api.test`, `start-docs`, `start-docs-verify`, `start-release-docs`, `start-qa-evidence`, `start-commands`, `start-status`, `start-acceptance`, `start-defects`, the landing-gate files and `workspace-ops-p09-docs`, 1877 of 1877; `scripts/*.test.mjs`, 497 of 498 (one platform skip: "off Linux"). PostgreSQL included, nothing else skipped. `check:deps`, `licenses:check` and `roadmap:check` passed; `api-v1.md` was regenerated and committed. No model was called.
- **First review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-26).** Problems found and fixed, each with a test:
  - *Medium.* The document reader read an artifact that names no project for any project (its project check passed when the artifact had none), and a document submission's `artifactId` is not checked against the project when it is recorded. It now refuses an artifact with no project; every publishing path names one.
  - *Medium.* A file named as text that was not read (over 50 files, over 256 KiB, over 1 MiB in all, or not UTF-8) was skipped silently, so a document could pass with its claims in a large or UTF-16 file. Each is now a `text_unread` flag naming the file and why; the verification is refused until the text is split or saved as UTF-8.
  - *Medium.* A director could rate one of the controller's own labels higher (Claude caching `supported`), and an override's `names` replaced the built-in names, so the scan could be narrowed to nothing. Rating a built-in label higher is now the owner's only (a director may still rate it lower), and an override always keeps the built-in names.
  - *Medium.* A lower rating flagged only documents that had declared the capability or named an unsupported or experimental one: the text scan did not record supported capabilities, so a document naming a supported capability in its text was missed when it was rated lower. The scan now records every capability named (supported ones are still never flagged).
  - *Medium.* Sentences: hard-wrapped Markdown and text split a sentence at each line break, so a label on the next line was a false flag and a name broken by the wrap was missed; HTML tags were spaces, so a heading and the next paragraph were one sentence. A line break inside a paragraph is now a space (a blank line, a list item, a heading, a quote, a table row, a code fence or a setext underline still ends a line), HTML block tags end a line, and HTML character references are decoded (`Strata&nbsp;caching`). Plurals (`Windows services`) and possessives (`Claude's prompt caching`) of a name are found.
  - *Medium.* A negation anywhere in the sentence labelled it ("Don't worry: Claude caching halves your bill" passed), and "preview" or "beta" anywhere labelled an experimental capability. A negation, "preview" and "beta" now count only within 8 words of the name, and "not just" and the like are not denials. "Experimental", "not measured", "unmeasured" and "untested" still count anywhere in the sentence. Every place a name stands in a sentence needs its own label.
  - *Medium (robustness).* The "no/without before the name" test ran on the whole sentence before every match: about 1.5 s per 256 KiB file of repeated names, allocating gigabytes of short-lived strings. It now looks at the 120 characters before the name (about 50 ms). Measured on the built code with 256 KiB inputs: repeated names, unclosed tags, `&#` runs, long space runs, wrapped lines, possessive runs, all under 0.5 s; no pattern backtracks badly.
  - *Low.* `doc.obligation.verify` returned every flag (tens of thousands for a file of short sentences); it now returns at most 20 with `total`, like the record and the replay.
  - *Low.* A flag's file path reached the owner unquoted and unredacted; it is now cleaned of control and direction characters, redacted, cut and JSON-quoted (`file "index.html"`).
  - *Low (chat).* The owner's chat found a capability only by its exact ID. It is now found by its ID, name or scanned names in the owner's words ("Claude caching"), words that fit more than one are asked about, and a new capability named in words with its name gets an ID made from them.
  - Checked and found sound: only the owner or a director rates (a task credential is refused by the operation, tested; the docs role is refused by the service; host, client and service principals are refused); the chat command is a proposal applied only on the owner's yes, with the consequence shown; the digest and the project are checked before any file is read; quotes are cleaned, redacted, cut and JSON-quoted; replay answers from the command's own audit entry; the new record kind `doc-capabilities` needs no backend change (all four backends run the service test).
  - Limits that remain (honest): names are the only vocabulary (no synonyms or paraphrase); look-alike letters from other scripts (Cyrillic "а") are not folded, only NFKC forms; a Markdown link splitting a name (`[Strata](url) caching`) is missed; a negation within 8 words that is about something else still lets the sentence through; text inside code fences is scanned like prose; documents verified before this slice keep their verification and carry no record of capabilities, so a later lower rating does not flag them (they are flagged at their next verification, `claim_without_capability` for each old claim); a director who also holds the docs role could still rate a project capability they claim (role assignment is the owner's).

- **Second review (clean context, Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-26; not pushed; card not flipped; no model or network call).** Probed on the built code with about 45 inputs, one route each. The problems below were found and fixed, each with a test:
  - *Medium (scanner).* Names were hidden from the scan, and text a reader sees went unread, by: look-alike letters from other scripts (Cyrillic `а`, Greek `ο`, Latin `ɑ`, `ı`); combining marks (`Stráta`); format characters other than the listed zero-width ones (tag characters U+E0000 to U+E007F, invisible operators U+2061 to U+2064, the combining grapheme joiner, variation selectors); Hangul filler characters used as spaces; a hyphen at a line wrap (`Stra-` / `ta`); Markdown or inline HTML inside a word (`Stra**ta**`, ``Stra`ta` ``, `Stra<b>ta</b>`, `Stra<!-- -->ta`); a Markdown link or reference link over a name (`[Strata](url) caching`, `[Strata][1] caching`); a reference without its `;` (`Strata&nbspcaching`); an `<img alt>`, `title` or `aria-label` (removed with the tag); an HTML comment holding `>` (the rest of the comment, "not", stayed in the text as a negation). Now: names are matched in a *matching form* (NFKD, every combining mark and format character removed, filler characters made spaces, a fixed table of Cyrillic, Greek and Latin look-alikes folded to ASCII, a hyphen and spaces between letters joined). The quoted sentence stays the cleaned one. Comments are removed whole, by search (an unclosed one ends the text, as a browser reads it). A tag or Markdown mark between two letters joins them. Link addresses and reference labels are dropped. Shown attributes are scanned as sentences of their own (so a tooltip cannot label the sentence beside it). `;` is optional on a reference. Every format character and variation selector is removed from what the owner sees (tag characters can carry text the owner does not see), in quotes and in file paths alike.
  - *Medium (labels).* A label was a regex hit anywhere, so "non-experimental", "not experimental", "no longer experimental", `x.io/experimental/notes`, the word quoted (`the "experimental" tag`) and `x.io/beta` all labelled a capability, and a negation inside a link (`x.io/not-a-scam`) denied one. Labels and negations are now whole words of the prose. A word inside a link, path or address does not count, and neither does a word in quotation marks. Hyphenated words are split ("experimental-only" still labels). A label with "not", "no", "non", "never", "nor", "isn't", "aren't", "wasn't" or "hardly" one or two words before it is taken back. A negation that takes back a label ("is not experimental", "isn't beta") denies the label, not the capability. A nearby negation must also be in the same clause: the window stops at `;`. "Not yet measured" is a label. Declared claims use the same rules.
  - *Medium (authorization).* An agent holding both the docs and the director roles could rate a capability (a project one, as `supported`) and then verify a document that claims or names it. This was listed as a limit by the first review; it is now closed at verification. Each capability the document claims or names is flagged `capability_rated_by_writer` (shown as `capability register (offline-mode): ...: "offline-mode was rated supported by agent:bo"`) when its project rating was set by the agent that submitted the document change or keeps the document, and that rating is above `unsupported` (for a controller label: above the controller's own rating). The owner or another director rating it clears the flag. A self-set `unsupported` needs nobody.
  - *Medium (consistency).* `verify` read the register but did not guard it. A rating lowered while the document was being read and checked could commit a verification recorded under the old rating, after the lowering had already looked for documents to flag. The verification now carries a `check` on the register's revision, so it is refused with `stale_revision` ("verify again"). Remaining window: a project whose register record does not exist yet (only built-in labels) gets no guard on its first rating.
  - *Low (robustness).* Measured on the built code, 256 KiB inputs: with a full register (100 capabilities of 10 names), a file of short sentences took about 1 s before this review (5.2 s per MiB); the scan ran inside the verification with no break between files. Capabilities are now first looked for in the whole text (only those named anywhere are tried sentence by sentence), an ASCII sentence skips the matching-form work, and the verification yields between files. Now: 1 MiB of short sentences with the full register takes 0.09 s. The worst 256 KiB case measured is about 0.6 s (repeated look-alike names, full register). With the built-in register every case is under 0.3 s. No pattern backtracks badly (unclosed comments, `](` runs, `][` runs, `&nbsp` runs, `a- ` runs: each under 60 ms).
  - *Low (replay).* A repeat whose audit detail could not be read (a transient read error between the runner's own lookup and the detail) was answered `verified: true` with no flags. Now the record answers when it still tells: the refusal for this document change, or the verification with it. Otherwise the answer is `unavailable` ("ask again"), never "verified".
  - Checked and found sound: `doc.capability.set` refuses task credentials (operation), host, client and service principals, the docs role and other projects' directors (service); only the owner raises a controller label; an override keeps the controller's names; `doc.capability.list` and `doc.obligation.verify` keep their reader and keeper rules; the chat proposal is shown first with its consequence, applies only on yes, asks when words fit several capabilities, and needs a new capability's name in the owner's words; every document text reaching the owner is cleaned, redacted, cut and JSON-quoted; the downgrade flagging is idempotent and is finished by a repeat; the service test runs on all four backends. The prompt is still 155,905 characters (unchanged).
  - Limits that remain (stated): synonyms and paraphrase (the register's `names` is the vocabulary, and the owner or a director can add up to 10 names per capability); a name spelled with letter spacing (`S t r a t a`) or digits for letters; a negation within 8 words in the same clause that is about something else ("Strata caching halves your bill and you will not need setup", "Never pay full price: Strata caching ...", "Strata caching cannot be beaten") still lets the sentence through. This is the cost of a word-window rule, and closing it needs a reading of the grammar the scan does not attempt. Look-alikes outside the fixed table (Cherokee, Armenian beyond a few letters, mathematical letters NFKD does not fold) are not folded. Code fences and tables are scanned like prose (conservative). Documents verified before this slice carry no capability record, so a lower rating does not flag them until their next verification.
  - *Deliberate breakages.* 15 new ones, different from both earlier lists. Each was a change to the built files, run against the one test file that should fail, then restored byte for byte (checked by sha256). Each one alone: look-alikes not folded; combining marks kept; format characters kept in the cleaned text; HTML comments kept; Markdown link addresses kept; a tag inside a word made a space; shown attributes dropped; a label never taken back; words inside links counted; a negation of a label counted as a denial; a negation in another clause counted; the whole-text filter run on the unfolded text; a self-rated capability not flagged; the register's revision not guarded; an unreadable replay answered "verified". All 15 were caught. Two ("words inside links", "another clause") were missed at first: whole-word matching already rejects most link words, and the test had a negation only after the name. Cases for a label after a hyphen in a link and a negation in the clause before were added, and both were then caught.
  - *Runs* (after `npx tsc --build --force`, through `/tmp/nn-slot.sh` with `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1` and the offline guard; Node 22.23.0 and Node 24.21.0, same counts on both): `doc-claims`, `doc-claims-service` (reference, SQLite, SQLite worker, PostgreSQL), `doc-obligations`, `doc-auto-checks`, `doc-retire`, `api/start-docs`, `api/start-docs-verify` and `chat/prompt-room`, 44 of 44. Per the owner's rule of 2026-11-21 for reviewers, only the changed test files and their neighbours were run. The whole submissions, status and chat suites and `scripts/*.test.mjs` (no script changed) are left to the exhaustive CI run. `check:deps`, `licenses:check` and `roadmap:check` pass. `api-v1.md` is unchanged (`api:docs:write` produced no diff). ## H12n real-dispatcher settle test (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26)

Plain words first. When an agent ends with `work.end { submit: true }` while one of its tool calls is still running, the controller cuts that call before it stages the work. If the cut call could have written to the checkout, the work must not be submitted: the ending becomes a plain end with a `release_failed` blocker. That rule was tested only with a stand-in for the dispatcher (`work-end/work-end.test.ts`). Nothing tested the real binding, `dispatcherEndingPorts.settle` in `packages/controller/src/work-end/ports.ts`. With that binding broken so that it never reports a write, or so that it counts calls that had already ended, all 78 tests in `work-end`, `api/start-work-end` and `dispatch/turn-end` still passed. Slice 1's "Remains" item 5 (a real-dispatcher test with a call in flight) was not built. It is built now. Card H12n is not flipped (it waits on Q01b).

- **Test** (`packages/controller/src/api/start-work-end-settle.test.ts`, SQLite and PostgreSQL; PostgreSQL is left out in the typical tier like its neighbours). It uses a composed `startController` with a remote host connected. The host is offered the attempt and accepts it. A tool call is begun on the host and never reported, the way a call stays in flight when the host's worker is killed mid-call. Then the agent asks `work.end { submit: true }` and the dispatcher's tick completes the ending through the real binding.
  - (a) A `write-file` call in flight is cut `uncertain`. The ending is `ended` / `release_failed`, its summary is `release_failed: 1 write call(s) had to be killed (w1: its outcome is not known); the work was not submitted`, and an open `runtime_hold` blocker on the task carries that summary. Nothing is staged and no submission is recorded.
  - (b) `read-file` and `grep` calls in flight are cut `cancelled`, and the submit goes through: staged once, with one code submission naming the attempt. Two earlier calls of the same attempt are not counted: a write the host reported done, and a write it reported `uncertain` before the ending began. Neither was in flight when the settle began. There is no blocker.
  - (c) Read-only or write comes from the controller's own catalogue (`policy/catalog.ts`: `read-file` and `grep` are `inspect`, `write-file` is `workspace-edit`). The test sets no classification. It checks the operation records' `readOnly` before the cut and their state after it.
  - (d) After (a), the owner asks the chat in free words ("what is holding up Order seeds 1? did it get submitted?", and in other words "Order seeds 1 - why is it stuck"). A stand-in model picks the existing `task` view by the description the interpreter's prompt gives it ("how one task is going and what blocks it") and copies the title from the owner's words. The answer says "It is held up by a technical problem: release_failed: 1 write call(s) had to be killed (w1: its outcome is not known); the work was not submitted ...". `status.ask` (the browser's source) gives the same lines. No control was added.
- **Bug found and fixed (chat, not the binding).** The interpreter's prompt offers the `task` view as `task(taskId|taskTitle)`, but the chat resolved a task title only for its other task views. So "how is <title> going" reached the status service with `taskTitle` and was refused (`taskTitle: is not a field of this command`). The owner could not reach the task view by name. `chat/chat.ts` now resolves the title for `task` the same way as for `attempt_endings` and `work_report`: one exact title in the focused project decides, several or partial matches are asked about, and an ID given beside a title wins. The settle binding itself showed no bug.
- **Observed, not changed.**
  - (1) After `release_failed` the attempt ends with the agent's own result, so `done` is `succeeded`. This is by design (the card: "turns submit into end", a plain end), and the blocker is what holds the task.
  - (2) The `attempt_endings` view says "It left no blocker." for such an attempt. That view lists only the W03/W05/W10 blockers read from the dispatch record. The `task` view shows the `release_failed` blocker.
  - (3) A local executor that honours the stop signal ends `cancelled` and is not counted as a write, even for a write tool (the dispatcher's meaning of `cancelled` is "no effect"). Only a call that does not stop in time, or one no running executor owns (the remote case tested here), is cut `uncertain`. ASSUMPTION: this matches the card ("kill hung calls"). A write executor that can be stopped part-way must not report the stop as `cancelled` after it has written.
- **Breakages** (built files, each run against the new file, then restored and its sha256 compared). All 12 were caught:
  - M1: the binding never reports a write.
  - M2: it counts calls that were not running when the settle began.
  - M3: its running set takes every call.
  - M4: the dispatcher's recovery cuts every local call `cancelled`.
  - M5: the recovery cuts every local call `uncertain`.
  - M6: every call is read-only.
  - M7: no call is read-only.
  - M8: the catalogue classes `write-file` as `inspect`.
  - M9: the ending ignores killed writes.
  - M10: the settle leaves in-flight calls that no executor owns.
  - M11: the chat does not resolve a title for the `task` view.
  - M12: the binding counts a `cancelled` call as a write.
  - M1 and M2 were also run against the three existing suites, which still passed all 78 tests (the gap the audit named).

## Q02 stale approvals: an approval stops counting when a decision it relied on or the criteria change after it (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26)

Card Q02 stays planned (not flipped; a later audit decides). Branch `card-q02-stale-approval` off origin/main `61cad655`. Plain words first: a flip audit found that an approval recorded BEFORE the owner corrected a decision the task relies on kept counting. The check (`readApprovalReliance`) ran only when a review was written; `SubmissionService.approvalOf`, which the landing gate's `review` check, the landing queue, a release, the status views and chat read, never looked again. Under the default profiles (tests and review required) code approved before a correction still landed. Now an approval is judged again every time it is read, and stops counting when what it was judged against changed.

- **What is built.**
  - Each new approval keeps what it was judged against (`judgedAgainst` on the review record, `basis` in the subject's verdict list): the task contract version in force at the write (cited or not; the write now also carries a revision check on the contract, so a contract change racing the approval lands strictly before or after it) and each decision the task relied on (`decisionId@linkVersion`, from the same reads `readApprovalReliance` already made, which now returns them).
  - `approvalOutdated` (`submissions/approval-standing.ts`) says why an approval no longer counts, in plain words: a relied-on decision superseded (by which decision, at what time), disputed (since when; waits for the owner) or unreadable (fail closed); the task relying on a decision it was not judged against (a new link, or the work revalidated against the correcting decision: the approval was given on the old one); a cited decision no longer in force or at another version; the contract's criteria text (expected result, acceptance criteria: `APPROVAL_CRITERIA_FIELDS`) changed since the version it was judged against (which fields, the version numbers, when the current version was stored).
  - `approvalOf` calls it for the newest approval (its own or carried by an unchanged patch ID) and answers `approved: false`, `newest: "approve"`, `outdated` (review, approver, time, `because`) and a `reason` that ends "a reviewer has to review it again against the current decisions and criteria". Because every reader goes through `approvalOf`, all of them see it: the landing gate's `review` check fails with the reason in its summary (and the author's refused-landing text carries it), `landing.queue.add` and the landing refuse it (`review_invalid`, with the reason), a release refuses it, the chat's approved-code lookup does not offer it, the review waiting view puts it back to `needs_review` (not "changes asked").
  - Nothing is written at the correction, so nothing can be missed by a failed hook or a pending propagation; a new review judged against the current decisions and criteria restores the approval; a dispute the owner settles by keeping the decision restores the old approval (nothing it was judged against changed).
  - Approvals recorded before this change have no basis and are judged by their time: a link made after the approval is a new dependency; the contract version in force then is found by walking stored versions back by `changedAt` (at most `APPROVAL_CONTRACT_WALK` = 20 reads; past that, or with a version missing, it does not count: fail closed).
- **Owner reach (nothing new to approve).** The `submissions` view (owner and author) says, for such code: "approved by X at T, but that approval no longer counts and the work does not land on it: <what changed, when>. It waits for a reviewer to review it again against the current decisions and criteria (a new approval restores it)". `landing.queue.list` adds `held` for the first ten entries that would not land now, and the `landing_queue` view says "it does not land now: <reason>". The interpreter prompt names both in one clause each in the status kinds' descriptions (+197 characters: 155,097 to 155,294, ceiling 156,560; the pin comment says so). User guide: one sentence in each of the Submissions and Landing queue bullets (asserted by the end-to-end test). `submission.record`'s `verdict` and `landing.queue.list`'s result docs say it; `api-v1.md` regenerated after the build.
- **ASSUMPTION:** a change of the contract's version alone does not take an approval back; only a change of the criteria text (expected result, acceptance criteria) does. New checks or required evidence leave it too, unlike QA evidence: the landing gate runs the contract's checks itself (`tests`) and the QA gate judges evidence (`qa`), and the existing P09 flow sets the test command after the review (`integration/p09-landing-checks` failed when checks counted). A new priority, budget, difficulty, class or permission leaves it. Reversible: add fields to `APPROVAL_CRITERIA_FIELDS`.
- **ASSUMPTION:** the check runs when an approval is read, not as an invalidation write at the correction: it is the smallest change that every consumer passes through, it cannot be lost to a failed or pending propagation step, and it is undone by a later review without any record to clean up. Cost: one reliance read, at most 50 decision reads (deduplicated), one contract read and one or two version reads per approved submission read (more only for an approval recorded before this change).
- **ASSUMPTION:** a dispute settled by keeping the decision restores the earlier approval; a decision revalidated to a correcting decision does not (the approval was judged against the old one).
- **ASSUMPTION (changed by the first review):** for approvals with no basis (old data) times are compared as instants (`Date.parse`, not as text, so a time written without milliseconds is read right), and a link or contract version stored at the approval's very millisecond, or a time that cannot be read, counts as made after it (fail closed: the order cannot be told). New approvals use the recorded basis, so time plays no part. Clock steps backwards on the controller between an old approval and a later link remain a residual risk for old data only.
- **Tests.** `submissions/approval-stale.test.ts` (4 backends x 2 tests): approval keeps its basis; supersede after the approval (before and after propagation marks the link) gives `approved: false` with the plain reason, a failing landing `review` check, a held queue entry and a refused `checkLanding`, the waiting view back to `needs_review`; revalidation keeps it stale; a new review restores it in all of them; priority-only change and new checks or required evidence leave it, a criteria change and an expected-result change take it back, a cited review against the new version restores it; dispute holds it and settling by keeping restores it; a new link, an unreadable decision, a superseded or re-versioned cited decision each take it back; carry-over by unchanged patch ID still works for unchanged decisions and stops by the same rule; a request for changes is unaffected; old approvals without a basis judged by time (contract walk, priority-only change, contract made after, unreadable version, walk limit, link after). `api/start-q02-stale-approval.test.ts` (SQLite, PostgreSQL, composed controller): real `contract.set`, `decision.record`, `decision.link`, landing branch and automatic queueing; the owner's real correction; the owner asks in free words and the stand-in model gets only the message; the chat answer, the author's own view and the `landing_queue` view say why; `decision.revalidate` keeps it stale; re-review restores; a priority change leaves it, a criteria change takes it back; the guide sentences. The vote test (`qa-leftovers.test.ts`: a majority of reviewers and an adopted meeting vote cannot override an owner decision) is unchanged and passes.
- **Own mutation checks (built files, each alone, restored byte-identical by sha256): 15 of 15 caught** by the two new test files: relied-on superseded/disputed decision ignored; a link made after the approval ignored; disputed treated as in force; the link's own superseded mark not read (survived the first run; a test of a marked link with an active decision record was added); cited decision version not compared; criteria change ignored; the old-approval walk taking the current version; `approvalOf` not applying the check; basis not kept in the verdict list; relied-on decisions not recorded in the basis; waiting view showing "changes asked"; status line wording dropped; queue `held` not computed; queue view reason dropped; uncited approval recording contract version 0.
- **Not done (said plainly).** No re-review request is scheduled when an approval stops counting (QA evidence schedules a re-check; for reviews the owner and author are told through the views and the refused landing, and the reviewer is not notified); a queued entry whose approval stopped counting stays in the queue (the landing refuses it with the reason; it is not withdrawn by itself, so a first place can hold the branch until it is reviewed again or taken out; the existing P10 bounds still apply); the queue view reads the approval of the first ten entries only; an approval given under `review_disabled_single_agent` (no reviewer) is not a review and is not covered (as the sixth slice recorded); dependencies other than criteria and decisions (artifacts, prerequisite tasks) still do not take an approval back; director sign-offs are not re-judged.
## P02 open clauses: workspace admission, the initial working state, proposals never cover a push, merge or deployment, and three workspace tests (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26)

A flip audit of P02 listed six offline items as open. This slice does all six. The card is NOT flipped: it depends on Y02 (planned, owner/Windows).

**1. The workspace admits only repositories in the task's access scope.**
- `ProjectResourceService.workspaceAdmission({ taskId, projectId, folder })` (`packages/controller/src/projects/resources.ts`) is for code that builds the services. It takes no caller's rights, only reads, and never pins. It answers `{ admitted: true, binding }` or `{ admitted: false, reason }` in words the owner can be told as they are:
  - A task that names a repository (or holds a pin) is admitted only on the binding the dispatcher pinned it to, at the location version it was pinned at, and only when `folder` is that binding's location. It is refused before the pin, after a move (until `checkout.repin`), after an unbind, and after the task is re-pointed at another repository.
  - A task that names no repository is admitted only when `folder` is the location of a repository bound to the task's project.
  - In both cases the binding must give write access to the whole repository. Read access is refused ("an agent's workspace is written in"), and so is a path-limited scope ("a workspace holds all of it").
  - The location is compared exactly as written (it stays opaque to the controller). A moved, unbound or re-pointed checkout, or too many records to look through, becomes a refusal with what was found.
- `LocalWorkspaces` takes an optional `admit` hook (`packages/worker/src/workspace/local-host.ts`). It is asked at every `ensure`, before a checkout is made or handed out again, with the folder the host would use. A refusal or a throw opens nothing (fail closed), and the refusal is the error message. A binding narrowed between attempts refuses the next hand-out, but the checkout and its work stay where they are. The landing, refresh and quarantine operations still find the checkout, because the controller judges those.
- `scripts/local-host.mjs` (the product host on this computer) wires `admit` to `services.resources.workspaceAdmission`. Tested end to end in `u14b-local-host.test.ts`: once the project's access is narrowed to reading, the next attempt fails. The tick's `skipped` entry and the attempt's recorded outcome both say "the workspace was not opened: the project has read access only to repository "garden", and an agent's workspace is written in; give the project write access to it first". No agent ran and no checkout was made.
- The chat prompt says, in one sentence, why such an attempt fails and what fixes it (bind with write access).
- The other end-to-end tests of the local host (`g09c`, `h12t`, `p02b`, `t02d`, `u14b`) now bind their repository with write access, as setup readiness already told owners to ("project.create, then resource.bind for its repository"). `u14e` already bound it through the chat.

**2. The initial working state is recorded with each attempt.**
- `GitBridge.startState` returns the checkout's base, its HEAD, the tree of the checkout as it stands, and the files that differ from HEAD or are untracked, with their status. The tree is written through a private index, so the checkout's own index is not touched. It uses the same neutral attributes as `doneState` and `stage`. Ignored files are not part of it.
- When `ensure` hands a workspace to a named attempt, `LocalWorkspaces` writes `<task>/starts/<attempt>.json` once. It sits beside the checkout and outside the sandbox mount. It holds the attempt, task and project; the time; base, HEAD and tree; up to 500 changed or untracked files (all of them counted); a sha256 digest over base, HEAD, tree and every listed file with its status; and the identity of the admitting binding (resource ID, repository ID, location version). The record is built in a private file and hard-linked into place. A crash therefore leaves either no record or a whole one, and a resume of the same attempt keeps the first record. Each later attempt gets its own record. `LocalWorkspaces.startState` reads a record back.

**3. An accepted proposal never authorizes a downstream push, merge or deploy.**
- `NEVER_PROPOSED` (`packages/controller/src/policy/load.ts`) now also holds `push`, `merge` and `deploy`, the catalogue's classes for `git-push`, `git-merge` and `deploy`. Approvals of these never become a standing-rule proposal, in development or testing.
- A proposal stored before this change is refused by `accept`, by `acceptBySwitching`, and by the step that finishes a half-made acceptance. The reason reads "proposal … is for pushes; a standing-rule proposal never authorizes a push, a merge or a deployment. Allow it yourself instead (a grant you make, or the task's instruction), or dismiss the proposal". So is a stored proposal whose grant would not be exactly `approve.class.<its class>`, such as a wildcard or another class. Dismissing still works.
- The chat prompt says proposals never cover these.
- The A07b tests and the two chat approval tests that used `git-push` as their example class now use a database update (`mutate`), a send and a publication.
- Toolbox (T08) proposals are separate records and were not changed. Their suites were run (see below).

**4.-6. Tests** (`packages/worker/src/workspace/p02-workspace.test.ts`):
- **Interruption.** A second host process takes the next attempt, writes an untracked file and is killed with SIGKILL. A restarted host (a new `LocalWorkspaces` over the same folders) hands the next attempt the same checkout, with the first attempt's changed and untracked files and the killed one's untracked file. That attempt's start record and `doneState` list all three, and none of it reached the shared repository.
- **Restack plus landing gate.** Landing checks run on the approved tree. The landing branch then moves, the approved change is re-applied (P10), and a landing that names the tree the earlier checks ran on is refused with nothing written. The checks run again and see the re-applied tree (the head's new file and the approved change together), and that landing lands.
- **No metadata pollution.** The shared checkout has its own setting, five hooks that leave a mark if run, and an `info/exclude` line. Then the full set of workspace operations runs: ensure, progress, doneState, submitView, stageWork, integration, landing checks, landing, refresh, a second attempt and quarantine. Afterwards `.git/config`, `.git/hooks`, `.git/info` and `.git/worktrees` are byte for byte the same, no worktree was added, no hook ran, and nothing was put under `.git/nn`.

**ASSUMPTION:** a task that names no repository is admitted on any repository bound to its project with write access to all of it. The host still uses the project's first listed local folder, so a task cannot yet choose between two bound repositories of one project without naming one.
**ASSUMPTION:** a read-only or path-limited binding refuses the workspace, rather than opening a read-only or partial copy. An agent's workspace is a writable copy of the whole tree and its work lands there. A read-only analysis workspace is a later card's design.
**ASSUMPTION:** a start record that cannot be written refuses the workspace (fail closed), so no attempt starts without a record of what it started from.
**ASSUMPTION:** answering a proposal by switching to the derived profile stays an owner's profile decision for proposals of other classes, as A07b and A07c specify. The derived profile's own table, shown in the switch preview, lets pushes and merges run in free environments; that is the profile, not the proposal.

**Not done:**
- A remote worker host (`scripts/remote-host.mjs`) asks no admission. It takes its folders from its operator's own configuration, has no controller records, and the worker protocol carries no admission call.
- The start records stay on the host. No controller view or chat status shows them yet, and a review reads them only through `LocalWorkspaces.startState` on the host.
- A standing grant for `approve.class.push`, `merge` or `deploy` made by an accepted proposal before this change is not revoked or ignored by the engine. No such grant can be made any more, and no installation predates the change.
- The host keeps one shared folder per project, so a task that names a second bound repository of its project is refused rather than given that repository.

**Tests.** Node 22 and Node 24.21.0, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, the same counts on both: controller policy 211, projects 490 (with the new `p02-workspace-admission.test.ts`, 16 = 4 suites on four backends), chat 1737, status 243, catalog (T08 toolbox) 188, workspace-ops 553; worker workspace 187 (185 pass, 2 Windows-only skips; the new `p02-workspace.test.ts` is 6); integration 19 (the local-host tests above plus h12m, h12q, p09); `scripts/*.test.mjs` 498 (497 pass, 1 skip). No failures.
**Mutation check.** 16 deliberate breakages, each restored with its sha256 checked, and all 16 caught: write access not required; a path-limited scope admitted; a pinned task opened on any folder; the folder of an unpinned task not compared; a named repository admitted before its pin; another project's task admitted; the host ignoring a refusal; the host treating a failing check as admitted; a start record overwritten on every hand-out; a start record that cannot be written ignored; the start state leaving out untracked files; the start tree taken from HEAD; push proposed again; a stored push proposal accepted; a half-accepted merge proposal finished into a grant; and the product host (`local-host.mjs`) asking no admission (caught by u14b).

**Fixed.**

Refresh, reapply, release, quarantine and restack write only the task's own checkout and are not asked. Lower-case IDs keep `<attempt>.json`. The record names its attempt either way, and `startState` reads it back by ID. Tested.

Owner chat grants (`policy_edit`) are the owner's own path and are unaffected. The refusal names the owner's own way first.

**Still open, for the flip audit.**

This is silently open, not fail-closed: it uses the folders its operator configured, for any task the controller sends it. The protocol has no admission call. ## P02 remote hosts: workspace admission before work is sent to a remote worker host (Claude agent, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-26)

The P02 first review left one medium item open: a remote worker host (`scripts/remote-host.mjs`) asked no admission and used the folder its operator configured for any task the controller sent it (silently open). This slice closes it on the controller side. The card is NOT flipped (it depends on Y02).

**How it works.**
- **The host says which folder it uses.** For each project in its `projects` setting whose folder exists, `remote-host.mjs` announces `repo:<projectId>:sha256:<digest>` in the capabilities' existing `workspaces` list. The digest is sha256 of the folder exactly as written in the host's configuration. The path itself is never sent (`remote/workspace-declaration.ts`: `workspaceDeclaration`, `declaredFolders`, `folderDigest`). The protocol has no new field: an older controller reads the entry as one more workspace name, and an older host announces none. The list holds at most 20 names, so a host with more projects declares 20 and logs the others, and those others get no workspace work.
- **The controller asks the project's access scope.** `ProjectResourceService.workspaceAdmissionByDigest` matches the digest against the locations of the repositories bound to the task's project (compared as written), then judges the match with the same `workspaceAdmission` the local host uses: the pin, the location version, write access, all paths. `remote/workspace-declaration.ts`'s `hostWorkspaceAdmission` turns the answer into plain reasons. A host that declares no folder for the project gets: "host:X does not say which folder it uses for project P, so no workspace is opened there (a host older than this controller says nothing: update it; otherwise set the project's folder in that host's configuration and bind that folder to the project with write access)". A folder that is not bound gets "...bind that folder, written exactly as in the host's configuration, to the project with write access first (resource.bind)". Read-only, path-limited, other-repository and two-folder declarations each get their own reason.
- **Where it is judged** (`RemoteWorkerService`, new dependency `workspaceAdmission`): the dispatcher's look at each host (`refusals`), `candidates`, `place`, the re-check when the host reads its offer (an offer refused there is withdrawn and the attempt ends with the reason), and the target of a move (`relocate`). Every remote attempt opens a workspace on its host (`remote-host.mjs` calls `LocalWorkspaces.ensure` for each order), so every attempt is judged.
- **Before the pin.** The dispatcher looks at hosts before it writes a repository-naming task's checkout pin. `workspaceAdmission` refused such a task as "not pinned yet", so the look passes `beforePin`: the task is judged on the binding its pin would take now. `place`, which runs after the pin, judges the pin itself. Tested by narrowing the binding between the look and the placement: the offer is refused and nothing reaches the host.
- **Integration and landing again (TOCTOU).** `askWorkspace` checks again, with the host's current announcement, before it sends an `integration` or a `landing`. A binding unbound, moved or narrowed, a host that came back with another folder or none, or a check that cannot be read, all answer `ok: false` "nothing was sent to host:X, so nothing was written to the shared repository: <reason>". Nothing is listed for the host.
- **Not judged** (as on the local host, which judges only `ensure`, integration and landing): refresh, reapply, release and quarantine write only the task's own checkout. Done checks (`verify`), looks (`observe`), conversation-store transfers and thinking purges open no workspace, so an older host still takes them (tested with a thinking purge). WIP restore (P02b) never reaches a remote host: `wipBackupRouter` already refuses it with its own reason. A remote release of an approved submission is already refused (H12o).
- **Wiring.** `dispatch-compose.ts` always gives the product's admission. `RemoteStartOptions.workspaceAdmission` lets code replace it. The controller and integration tests that are about other cards and run scripted hosts with no shared repository pass `async () => []` there (21 controller files and 3 integration files, the same way they already pass `placementPolicy`). The tests that run the real host program (`l05e`, `l04e`) and the H12m remote workspace test now bind the shared folder with write access, and H12m declares it. `l05e` first shows the real program refused for its unbound folder (nothing offered, the plan says why), then binds the folder and runs.
- **Owner reach.** The reasons reach the owner through the views that already exist: the dispatcher's plan (`skipped`), the blocked notice after a few ticks, the ended attempt's outcome and the placement history. The interpreter prompt's P02 sentence gains one clause: "on a remote host it is the folder that host's configuration names (an older host names none: update it)". The prompt is 155,722 characters, under the 156,560 ceiling, and the pin is unchanged.

**ASSUMPTION:** the host declares a digest, not the path, so no remote machine's paths are recorded on the controller (the capabilities field is documented as names, never paths), and every entry fits the field's 120 characters. The owner therefore binds the folder with the text the host's operator wrote. The refusal says so. ASSUMPTION: this reuses the existing `workspaces` field rather than adding one, because the controller refuses unknown capability fields: a new field would make a newer host unable to connect to an older controller.
**ASSUMPTION:** a host that declares nothing for the project is treated as not admitted for workspace work (fail closed). Every remote attempt is workspace work, so an older host gets no attempts until it is updated, but it still answers non-workspace requests.
**ASSUMPTION:** when no host may open the workspace, the attempt waits with every host's reason and the owner is told after a few ticks. This is the existing H07e behaviour for lasting refusals. The attempt is not failed: binding the folder lets the same attempt start (tested).
**ASSUMPTION:** an admission that cannot be read during the dispatcher's look is reported and the placement judges it again, the existing rule for a host that cannot say. At delivery the offer is held. At `place` the error refuses the start. For an integration or a landing it refuses with nothing sent.
**ASSUMPTION:** refresh and reapply are not judged. They read the shared repository into the task's own checkout but write nothing shared, which matches the local host. A later landing of that work is judged.

**Not done.**
- The host's own side still trusts its configuration. A remote host that lies about its folder could open a workspace elsewhere. The controller cannot see another machine's disk, so the protection is against misconfiguration and unbound folders, not against a hostile host (which holds the code anyway).
- A host can declare at most 20 projects (the field's existing limit). More would need a protocol change.
- Start records (P02) on a remote host stay on that host, as on the local host. No controller view shows them.
- Not run on Windows or macOS here. The remote host is Linux only, and the change has no paths, signals or locale use on the controller.

**Tests.** Base origin/main ff3ba6f9. `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npx tsc --build --force` clean, no stale dist tests, `api:docs:write` unchanged (no API change), check:deps, licenses:check and roadmap:check ok. Node 22 and Node 24.21.0, `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, offline guard, `/tmp/nn-slot.sh`, the same counts on both, no failures: controller remote 1,066; projects 494 (with the new four-backend digest suite: 20 = 5 suites × 4 backends); dispatch 1,604; workspace-ops 553; the composed remote set 191 (every `startController` remote test, the new `api/start-remote-admission.test.ts` with 6 tests, and `chat/prompt-room`); worker 861 (859 pass, 2 Windows-only skips); `scripts/*.test.mjs` 499 (498 pass, 1 skip; the new remote-host declaration test); integration remote set 12 (`g09-remote-updates`, `h07b`, `h12k`, `h12m`, `k01i`, `l04e`, `l05d`, `l05e`, `w12-remote-anchor`). No known flake was hit.
**Mutation check.** 18 deliberate breakages on the built code and the host script, each restored with its sha256 checked, all 18 caught on both Node versions: the dispatcher's look not judged; the placement not judged; candidates not judged; delivery not judged again; a move's target not judged; integration and landing asks not judged; the landing ask not judged; an unreadable admission sending anyway; an older host admitted; two declared folders taking the first; a refusal ignored; a digest matching any repository; the look before the pin passed on as strict; an unpinned named task admitted without the look; the host declaring nothing; the host declaring the raw path; the poller announcing no declaration; the product wiring no admission.

## P02 remote hosts first review (Claude agent, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-26)

Reviewed `3206e2b7` (merged with origin/main `2d15b370`, no conflicts). The card is NOT flipped.

**Found and fixed.**
- (Medium) An integration or a landing that passed the check stayed listed for the host by host ID, not by session. A host that restarted with another `projects` folder, and reconnected before `waitMs` ran out, read the request in its new session and would have written to the new folder without a new check. Now `askWorkspace` keeps the folder the host declared for the project with the request, and `workspaceRequests` refuses the request ("nothing was sent to host:X ...: it reconnected declaring another folder / no folder ...") when the host's declaration now differs, or cannot be read, before listing it. A reconnect with the same folder still gets the request. Tested in `api/start-remote-admission.test.ts`.
- (Low, tests) Three breakages of my own were not caught: an answer of the folder admission that is not a clear `admitted: true` admitting; an admission that cannot be read when the host reads its offer delivering the offer; and a lookup error in `workspaceAdmissionByDigest` thrown rather than refused. New tests: `remote/p02-workspace-declaration.test.ts` (declaration parsing, malformed answers, reason cut, throw passed on, none and two folders refused without asking), a delivery test where the admission cannot be read (held, neither delivered nor withdrawn, delivered once readable), a malformed project ID refused, and a composed test for a folder with letters outside ASCII and mixed case (the host's digest and the controller's match), a lower-cased folder refused and another project's declaration not taken.

**Checked and found sound.** The only production construction of `RemoteWorkerService` is `composeDispatch`, which always wires `hostWorkspaceAdmission` over `workspaceAdmissionByDigest`; `RemoteDeps.workspaceAdmission` absent means not judged, but only tests construct the service directly. A non-function override fails closed (the call throws, every check point refuses or holds). The 24 test-file edits are the same one-line `workspaceAdmission: async () => []` in tests about other cards (capacity, placement, quiet hosts, contracts, releases, wake); the real product admission runs in `start-remote-admission` (8 tests) and the `l05e`, `l04e` and `h12m` integration tests. A host with no announced capabilities is already refused by `capabilityReasons` at every point, including `#ask`. Declarations are scoped to the task's project; the 20-entry cap keeps the configuration's order and the projects past it get no workspace work; trailing slash, case, symlink and relative differences are refused (the host requires an absolute folder; comparison is as written); the remote host is Linux only. Reasons quote no host-supplied text (host IDs and project IDs are checked shapes; labels are the owner's). `reapply` and `refresh` only fetch from the shared repository into the task's own git directory, as on the local host.

**Stays open.** The host still trusts its own configuration: the controller cannot see a remote disk, and a nonce or challenge would be answered by the same host software, so it adds nothing against a host that reports wrongly. This is a plain limit; the existing placement policy (which hosts may hold a project's data and credential) is the owner's lever. The interpreter prompt is now 156,530 characters after the merge, 30 under the 156,560 ceiling: the next card that adds prompt text must raise `SIZE` on purpose or make room.

**Mutation check.** 13 new breakages, each restored with its sha256 checked, all caught on Node 22 and Node 24.21.0 (three of them only after the new tests): the reconnect check skipped; another project's declaration taken; the same folder twice counted as two; a malformed answer admitting; an unreadable admission at delivery delivering; the digest compared without case; the controller digesting the location as latin1; a lookup error thrown rather than refused; the host cap at 21; the host declaring folders that do not exist; a move judged on the source host; the request's declaration recorded wrong; an empty declaration asked rather than refused.

A host that restarted with another `projects` folder (or none) could have gone on opening the task's workspace there. The shipped `remote-host.mjs` keeps its held attempts in memory, so after a restart it holds nothing and this path is not reached by it, but the protocol allows it. Now `accept` in a new session judges the folder the host declares now: a refusal answers `unavailable` with the reason and changes nothing (the attempt is not ended, so binding the folder or restoring the host's configuration lets the next accept go through), and an unreadable admission answers `unavailable` too. The handshake (`reconcile`) still says "reaccept" for such an attempt; the accept that follows refuses with the reason.
- (Low, tests) Five branches had no test that failed when they were broken: the request check when what the host declares cannot be read as it reads its requests; an admission that cannot be read at `place` (after the dispatcher's look passed); the same at a move's target; the owner's hint for a digest that matches only an unbound repository or a non-repository resource; and the host digesting its folder exactly as written (no trailing-slash or `.` tidying). New tests: `remote/p02-reaccept.test.ts` (5 suites × 4 backends), one new suite in `projects/p02-workspace-admission.test.ts`, and an assertion in `scripts/remote-host.test.mjs`.
- (Prompt room) The P02 clause is now "; remote: its config folder; update old hosts" (45 characters, 60 fewer). The prompt is 156,470 characters, 90 under the 156,560 ceiling, so C08's task override (~64) fits. `SIZE` is unchanged.

**Checked and found sound.** Every way work reaches a host: offers (delivery and accept of an offer are judged), `place`, `candidates` and `refusals` (the look, before the pin), relocation (target judged), integration and landing asks (judged, the declaration kept with the request and compared when the host reads it). A repeat of the same request ID joins the first entry with its declaration, a withdrawn one is refused, and an evicted one is judged again as new. `runScript` needs the session that accepted the attempt. `verify`, `observe`, conversation-store transfers and thinking purges open no workspace on the host (it calls `ensure` only for an order). WIP restore never reaches a remote host. A controller restart loses in-memory offers and asks, which are made again through `place` and `askWorkspace` and judged there. Digests: `resource.bind` stores the locator as written (no trim and no Unicode normalization; control characters refused), and the host digests the configured text as written. So NFC against NFD, case, trailing slash, `.` segments, Windows-style paths (not absolute on the Linux host, so not declared), newline or NUL (not a folder, or refused by bind) and over-long paths all fail closed, with the "written exactly as in the host's configuration" hint. Two projects bound to the same folder are declared and judged per project. A path-limited or read-only binding is refused. With several repositories, the digest selects the one at that location. Refusal texts carry only checked-shape host, project and attempt IDs, the owner's labels and internal error text; the only host-supplied data used is the hex digest matched by a regular expression.

**Stays open.** The host still trusts its own configuration (unchanged from the first review). The 20-project cap. A folder typed in another Unicode form than the host's configuration is refused until bound as written (usability, fail closed).
